en: The preface to this compilation was begun in the spring of the Renchen year at Falin Temple in the northern frontier.
Its carving and completion were finished in the summer of the Jiawu year at Zongjian Hall in Bolin, the capital. Now...
The title is *Zongjian Fali* (The Forest of Dharma in the Mirror of the Lineage).

This identifies the ground of realization. As for the compilers of the texts, they all paired Nan Yue and Qing Yuan as counterparts; this cannot avoid errors. Now, I have followed the *Tongyao* (Essential Compendium).
Nanyue returned to Nanyue; Qingyuan returned to Qingyuan. Since the lineages have been made clear, readers will naturally be free from errors.
The confusion between "Tianhuang" and "Tianwang" has led to endless disputes between the two houses, remaining a case of doubt for all eternity. [If one wishes...]
It is truly difficult to interject with further analysis; moreover, why should one engage in deep discussion regarding a doctrine that has already fallen?
For now, I shall enclose these two characters within a black circle, leaving them for future authors to address.
Matters must necessarily follow antiquity. The errors regarding the Five Patriarchs of the Dongxia lineage began only in recent times;
previously, no one had mentioned them, and thus I had not heard of them. How could I now dare to arbitrarily add or delete anything? I have respectfully followed such works as the *Huìyuán*.
I hope this may spare me from the reproaches of former sages and the incurrence of transgressions.
From Mazu Daoyi, the first successor under Nanyue, down to Wufeng Xuelin Gaoyu;
and from Shitou Xiqian, the first successor under Qingyuan, down to Zhinan Cheshuangguan Yin: after these, the recorded sayings (*yulu*) became numerous.
Truly, there is still much that remains incomplete.
Since the Song and Yuan dynasties, the one thousand seven hundred *gong'an* (public cases) that have been transmitted are known to all;

whenever the subject is mentioned, this specific number is invariably cited. Furthermore, it is not realized that beyond these there exists other wondrous enlightenment, which has caused the insights of the ancients to be buried and lost.
The spirit of the worthy [master] is truly lamentable. Consequently, two thousand five hundred and sixty-four cases have been added.

As for the *Lianzhu* (String of Pearls), it consists solely of verses; as for the *Tongyao* (Essential Compendium), it consists solely of *nian* (critical comments). To divide them into these two branches inevitably means that each retains its own particular perspective. Upon examination...

There have also been sighs that while one aspect is grasped, another is lost. Now, all have been collected together, so that one may hope to see them clearly at a glance, as if observing things through a transparent flame.

Among the various regional *yulu* (recorded sayings) and *nian-song* (verses on cases), there are many that have not yet been widely circulated; these have now been extensively sought out and gathered.

As for the *lu* (records), even those consisting of fragmentary chapters and broken slips must be carefully collated and recorded three or more times before being included in the collection to be made public for future generations.
Regarding cases within the *gong'an* that appear ambiguous, I do not dare to hastily add my own conjectures, lest I be ridiculed by the various quarters of the monastic community. For instance:

Regarding the "Oil Cakes" (youci) kōan: one version attributes it to Ehu, while another attributes it to Nanyuan; it is uncertain which is correct. For now, both are included among the records of the ancient worthies.
Other cases should be understood accordingly.
Gong’an were originally intended to refine one’s insight; yet some, instead, use their own preconceived notions to force-fabricate interpretations of the gong’an.

Although such people may momentarily impress others as heroes, I fear that the ancients of old would shed tears for them. Therefore, all instances of forced fabrication and decadent frivolity are here excluded from this collection.
The verses and commentaries were collected as they arose, rather than strictly following the chronological order of the practitioners.
This work was first carved at the capital with over two thousand five hundred cases;
it was carved a second time at Lian’an, with an additional one hundred fifty-odd cases added, totaling two thousand seven hundred and twenty cases.
As for the collation of the *gong'an* cases, there are inevitable differences—some major, some minor—in the arrangement and ordering of the volumes.

This work was completed in a mere two years; consequently, many records of venerable masters from deep mountains and remote valleys that have not been transmitted to the world must necessarily be missing.
I respectfully await future scholars to supplement these omissions.

When the World-Honored One Śākyamuni Buddha was first born, he pointed with one hand toward heaven and with the other toward the earth, walked seven steps,
and gazing in the four directions, declared: "In all that is above heaven and below heaven, I alone am the Honored One."
Yunmen Wenyan said, "If I had seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to the dogs, so as to ensure peace throughout the world.
Xuedou Xian said, "I would have immediately overturned the meditation seat.
Fayan Wenyi said, "Yunmen’s momentum was indeed great, yet he lacked the principles of the Buddha-dharma. At that time, an elder remarked, "I thought there was no one [who could surpass him]."

Proof. Xuedou said, "The hook is in the ground of non-doubt. Langye Jue said, "Yunmen may indeed be said to 'offer this profound mind to every dust mote and land'; this is what is called repaying the Buddha's kindness.
Yunfeng Yue said, "Although Yunmen possesses a strategy for settling chaos, he lacks the way to emerge from it himself. Fachang Yu said, "Yunmen..."
"A fine blow! But it was too late. Before he had even left the Tuṣita Heaven, a single thrust under his heels would have been appropriate.
Nevertheless, it is like drawing one's bow after the thief has already fled. Tiantong Hua said: "Although Yunmen’s words have circulated, they cannot avoid falling into his trap.
Gao Feng Miao said: "The World-Honored One is much like a sacred tortoise dragging its tail; he brought about his own destruction."
This was the omen. Although Yunmen fully upheld the true command, he was merely increasing the ignorance of others for their sake.
At that time, he should have simply drawn a circle on the ground, written the character "ding" (T) within it, and then extended both hands to show it;
this would surely have caused it to melt away like ice and crumble like a fortress. Nantang Yu said: "Yunmen’s fine staff is truly startling."
It cannot be avoided that he would have wounded his own edge and committed a blunder with his hands. Had he seen [the Master] at that time, he need only have said, "Wash the basin! Wash the basin!
If this old fellow had known how to act appropriately, he would surely have withdrawn in secret, avoiding falling into disgrace in broad daylight.

Tiantong Wu said: "I am not like Yunmen, who was so greatly startled and made such a fuss. At that time, I would simply have stepped forward and placed my hand upon my forehead, saying: 'Wash the basin!'"

"A cat. Look at where his face is turned. Xiqia Cheng said, "If one had encountered such a statement at that time, one should simply step forward with palms joined and say, 'Long life to the Great King!'"

Pointing to heaven, pointing to earth, his words ring out clearly; sending messages and transmitting words, he departs from the painted hall. The messenger still possesses great spirit; the host must surely be extraordinary.
(Quán Dàdào) The founding of the base and the establishment of the enterprise were the affairs of former kings;
the upright governance and the maintenance of fullness are the concerns of later emperors. Swords and halberds have all been turned into agricultural implements.
At this moment, who can report the sounds of peace?

(Foyin Yuan) As beautiful as Xi Shi leaving the golden palace, As coquettish as Yang Guifei descending from the jade tower, She still half-conceals her face with a lute, Yet her grace becomes all the more enchanting for those who cannot see her. (Fujian Qin)

A single fire casts a golden bullet; perfectly round, it costs nothing in tongs or hammer. Picked up and cast from the crest of a ten-thousand-fathom peak, it strikes down the white phoenix from the edge of heaven.
(Cishou Shen) A stone tiger from a thousand years ago gives birth to a qilin;
its single horn and entire body shine with five colors. The golden lock and jade gate are completely pulled apart.
Severed. Within the realm of Vairocana, the dust and smoke of the drums rise.
(Xuedou Zong) As soon as this old fellow was born, he was already in a hurry; taking seven steps, he acted like one deranged.
He has deceived countless foolish men and women, opening their eyes wide as they enter the cauldron of boiling oil. (Jingshan Gao)
From of old, a wealthy house produces a pampered child; as soon as it emerges from the womb, it begins to strike about wildly.
Only when its skill is exhausted beneath the twin trees does it finally realize that for forty-nine years it has been in error.
(Lan’an Shu) Bathing an infant beneath the tree of no-sorrow, at the clear dawn the rose opens with dew. Turning aside, the monk meets him face to face.
[The place: Later, the donkey and horse emerge from the womb.
(Tiantong Jing) Never having entered the belly of Māyā, with both hands one knows not where they are placed;
emerging from the right flank, the realm of Māra appears—fit only for lamentation, unfit for looking upon. (Tianmu Li)
Taking seven steps, he walked about as if in a daze; pointing to heaven and pointing to earth, he was not clear.
Since right and wrong have already fallen upon the ears of bystanders, even if one were to wash them until the year of the donkey, they would still not be clean.

(Xutang Yu) From birth, I have regretted being of the same lineage [as him]; though my heart and liver are cast of iron, they too should be consumed. I return to you the One Honored One of the Three Realms.

Internally: Alas, today and again tomorrow! (Jiā'ān Zhēn) The poisonous seeds and poisonous flowers of Vairambha wind bloom; they add another cup to Yunmen’s drunkenness. Today at Kēqiáo the weather is foul;
thin mist and sparse rain wash over the yellow plum blossoms. (Jièwēng Chún)
Māyā gives birth to an infant today; from the heavenly palace she has descended to the earth. This is no phoenix egg hatched from a hen’s nest;
it is clearly an elephant cub born from a donkey’s womb.

(Qianyan Chang) Suddenly hearing the plaintive cry atop the imperial tower, her jade hairpin snaps and her heart grows weary. Though she does not issue a general amnesty, [the world is already transformed].
Guest: There is indeed a thieving mind here, nodding its head in secret.
(Shilangru) Like metal leaping from the furnace, it is inherently inauspicious; the forging of Ganjiang brings calamity upon the Red Eyebrows.
One who restores order to heaven and earth may be called a sovereign, yet there are numerous precedents for the clandestine seizure of a kingdom. (Guantaoqi)
The moon rises over the mountain city as warhorses gallop in haste; After the rain has passed, the new waters hold the fragrance of lotus flowers.
From this point on, autumn is at its finest upon Lake Dongting; Amidst the sounds of misty waves, the fishermen vie with one another.
(卄/昂) Xi Sen says to himself, paces to and fro, Stirs his own heart of longing and acts as his own matchmaker. It is not that he lacks his own kin and bone.
Meat. Who has brought charcoal into the midst of the snow?
(Han Songcao) Before the Great Cause is achieved, he first establishes his own integrity. For three months in Xianyang, the fires blaze a deep crimson.
To the very end, he does not forget the image of a fallen state. What face does he have to show to Jiangdong? (Lü Yujiao)
One digs a deep pit oneself and buries oneself alive; a stench of blood soaks the earth as the corpses lie exposed.
Though one may be called most honored and great among men and gods, it is like a straw sandal breaking at the base of a fence.
(Falin’s Verse) On the eighth day of the twelfth month, when the morning star appeared, the World-Honored One suddenly attained great enlightenment and said: "How marvelous! One..."
"All sentient beings possess the wisdom, virtues, and marks of a Tathāgata; it is only because of deluded thoughts and attachments that they are unable to realize them.
Boshan Lai said: "Fundamental ignorance is itself immovable wisdom; immovable wisdom is itself the fundamental [wisdom]."
"Regarding 'Ignorance' (avidyā): here one must possess a separate eye. Old Gautama’s ice melts and his fortress crumbles. Tianzhang Yu said:

"How great and small [in stature] Śākyamuni has made this talk into two separate pieces! Had there been someone at that time who dropped a single word, it would have spared the descendants of later generations from copying patterns and drawing models.
Nevertheless, even so, I cannot allow myself to bow before this Śākyamuni! [He lets out a shout.]
"Hai! Yuedi Zhi said: "Sitting for too long on the Snowy Mountains leads to fatigue; empty flowers fall in confusion from a single ladle.
It is only fitting to pour this foul water upon oneself. Why? Because those wondrous lines from his six years of practice do not match the preceding sounds from the lower ground.
Daolin Lu said: "One eye is opened, but one mouth is lost."
When Gautama lost his eyes, there was but a single branch of plum blossoms amidst the snow;
now, thorns grow everywhere, yet one laughs at the spring wind for its chaotic blowing. (Huitang Xian) Heaven covers and earth sustains;
formed into a mass and rolled into a lump, it pervades the Dharma-realm without limit, and when analyzed down to the subtlest atom (*paramāṇu*), it has no interior.
When the profound mysteries are exhausted, who can distinguish between front and back? The Buddhas and Patriarchs come to repay their karmic debts of speech;
go ask the old master Nanquan. Everyone eats but a single stalk of vegetable. (Hongzhi Jue) Entering the mountains—what do you seek to plot?
Coming out of the mountains—why do you do so? Had you known the affairs of today earlier, you would regret not having been more careful.
In the beginning, (Wuzhun Shanfan) raised his head and saw the stars, suddenly awakening to the Way. On Yellow Clay Mountain, wild mugwort grows;
Old Lady Li makes her own clothes, cutting not red silk but fragrant soap. (Yutang Yi).
The golden bell strikes through the night at the nine-layered city walls; returning after six years, his emaciated form is transformed.
Waiting until the eyes and minds of sentient beings are awakened, the Snowy Mountains remain as ever, green and towering.
(Xutang Yu) Six years on the Snowy Peaks, the Way was finally perfected; he struck out the ghostly eyes of the past. With a face full of shame and confusion, there is no place for attachment.
At this very place, even now I am terrified at the sight of the morning star.
(Jingsou Jue) Two thousand years ago on the eighth day of the twelfth month, the Yellow-Faced Gautama’s two eyes were wide open.
Having consumed too much salt over *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, his six years of asceticism only served to increase his thirst. (Yuejiang Yin)
For six years I hid away in the Snowy Mountains; with ash on my head and dust on my face, I was ashamed of my own countenance.
This morning, suddenly beholding the appearance of the morning star, I finally realize that until now I have been deceived by my own eyes.
(Iron Mountain Ren) My home is in the deep mountains, yet I sought mountains elsewhere; my eyes opened, where could I place this shame-faced countenance? With earnest care, I pity you, O Prince.
Intoxicated. The moon fills the lotus robes, frost fills the braids.
(Yulim Xu) Today is precisely the eighth day of the twelfth month. The old Śākyamuni’s eyes are blind. During broad daylight under the blue sky, he was bewitched by a ghost;
at night, facing the bright stars, he scraped his eyes. (Chaozong Ren)
Every day one lifts the eyes and beholds the stars; how can one speak of renewal so abruptly? Now I ask the Old Man of Vulture Peak:
how many more hairs of eyebrows does he have left? (Liu Ji Qian) He came into the mountains after six years of arduous practice;
at midnight, the bright star split his cheeks with laughter. Truly, the skull has been dried out.
It is exhausted. For what reason has this calamity been provoked? (The Sound of the Dharma Forest) The World-Honored One ascends the seat.
Mañjuśrī strikes the gavel and says: "Observe closely the Dharma of the Dharma-King; such is the Dharma of the Dharma-King."
The World-Honored One then descended from his seat.

Bājī Chè said, "The bustling crowd fills the earth and pervades the heavens. Shílínzé said, "Among the assembly it is said that when the World-Honored One entered the forest, he did not stir a blade of grass;
when Mañjuśrī entered the water, he did not stir a ripple. Thus, naturally, the seas were calm and the rivers clear."
Shaking his hand, he laughed loudly and said, "You have erred! Tell me, what is the principle here? 'Turning over the seas and mountains to seek a true friend;
overturning heaven and earth to bring about peace. Tiantong Wu said, "Mañjuśrī is much like one who mistakes the shadow for the head;
the World-Honored One, too, has his feet off the ground. Yunmen Wenyan said, "At that time, he should have snatched [the whisk] away."
[The Master] sets aside Mañjuśrī’s mallet and lets out a shout, saying, "Watch this Old Man of the Yellow Face—what move will he make?
Boshan Lai said: "The World-Honored One pulls the golden needle; Mañjuśrī draws the jade thread across. To sew together the seas and mountains, one must indeed be such a person. But tell me:
before he had even ascended the seat, where was the Dharma of the Dharma-King? Baoren Xian.
Yun said: "Although the World-Honored One was head-on and tail-on, he did not realize he had been put to work by Mañjuśrī.
Guxiu Yao said: "The World-Honored One was threading a needle within the light of a flash of lightning; Mañjuśrī was writing characters upon the tongue of a fierce tiger.
Even if one were to employ both 'letting go' and 'seizing' in unison, one would already have fallen to the third or fourth level. Is there anyone who can act as the master for these two elders?"
How extraordinary! The lutes and songs meander away, dispersing with the clouds; the cuckoo vainly transmits its cry through the secluded garden.
A million numinous mountains are like reeds and hemp; as the wind moves and the clouds gather, they already form a dense veil.
Had it not been for the old Manjusri at that time, Gautama would have repeatedly scattered sand. (Foyin Yuan)
The moon in the heart of the waves is utterly cold; the clear pool surely does not permit the dragon to coil there.
How many unreturned travelers are there across the Five Lakes, yet they are caught by others holding fishing rods.

(Shangfang Yi) A single orb of bright moon reflects the heart of heaven; the living beings of the four seas receive its illumination. Why need one wait for the western wind to shake the cinnabar peaks?
Cassia. Once more, from the azure heights, the autumnal sounds of the ninth month are sent forth.
(Fujian Qín) Do you see this single thread of true wind? The subtle Mother of Transformation sets her shuttle to the loom; she weaves an ancient brocade containing the image of spring.
Alas, what can be done about the Lord of the East leaking its secrets? (Tiāntóng Jué)
Silken edicts and sealed memorials issue forth from the imperial pavilion; In his strategic counsel, he was like Zhang Liang borrowing the counting sticks of Liu Bang.
It was not for the casting of seals nor the melting of them again; The beacon fires of the Six Kingdoms were still far from extinguished.

(By Zhuan’an Fan) A beautiful woman of the South is seen within a painting; The first touch of the frost-tipped brush leaves her morning makeup unfinished. Do not trouble yourself to apply rouge and powder to her face.
Color: Beyond the window, plum blossoms brush against the cold shadows.

(Lingtíng Tǐng) In the secluded valley, jade branches open, bearing dew; Spring holds within it reds and purples, piling up like brocade. Who would have known that they would encounter the "flower-rush" rain?
Faded petals fall, filling the green moss with drifting blossoms. (Hánsōng Cāo)
The World-Honored One was questioned by a rishi possessing the five supernatural powers (pañcābhijñā): "The Tathāgata possesses six supernatural powers, while I possess five;
what is this one [additional] power? The World-Honored One called to the rishi, and the rishi responded, "Yes. The World-Honored One said, "That one power—ask me about it."
Mingjue Xian said: "The Old Barbarian [the Buddha] originally did not know there was such a 'penetration' (abhijñā); he instead struck the correct with the deviant. Langye Jue said:
"That the World-Honored One did not know may be called striking the deviant with the correct;
that the Five Penetrations did not know was truly striking the correct with the deviant. Cuiyan Zhi said: "The Five Penetrations asked thus; the World-Honored One answered thus."
Yaoqie could not fathom that one stroke. Yunfeng Yue said, "The Great Gautama was exposed by the outsider.
Someone from the sidelines, unable to accept this, came forward; Yunfeng wanted to ask him, "What is that one stroke?"
Gunanmen said: "It is easy to summon a snake; it is difficult to send it away. When the World-Honored One was pressed by the immortal, he had no way to turn back.
Taking the wrong for right, why did he not strike him immediately upon being questioned?

Had he done so, the immortal would have known his home at once and would have cast off his five supernatural powers all at once. Would he not then have become a carefree immortal on level ground? — Chongxian.
Qiyun said: "The old barbarian knew very well that there was one such thing, yet his mouth was simply too narrow. Pingtianben said:
"When the World-Honored One was lightly nudged by the immortal, he was driven straight to calling a bell a jar. Langshan Yu said: [He remained silent.]
The World-Honored One went to the nest to plunder; it was like pushing a boat downstream. As for that one stroke, it remains truly beyond comprehension.
You ask why? Because this question is personal: "The ridge-plum and river-willow share the fragrance of spring.
Without needing further search for the stolen goods, the thief’s own body has already been exposed in the hall. (Changling Zhuo)
That one phrase—ask me! At the dark portal hangs a hairless lock; with a casual pull, it opens.
Three wives sit facing one another. *Du!* (Duanqiao Lun) Drunk, he rides a white crane up to the Silver Palace;
in a dream, he spans a blue phoenix into the Vermilion Hall. When the wine is sobered and the eyes open, all is gone.
I see it: along the stream, peach and plum trees by the eastern wind.
(Zhongfeng edition) That one stroke—do you ask me? A monkey climbs a tree to steal wild fruit; though he chews it in his mouth, it is neither sweet nor fragrant.
Within the eyes and within the ears, there is nothing but fire. Suddenly, one bumps into the gardener; there is nowhere to hide.

(Sanyi Yu) Once, when a non-Buddhist asked the World-Honored One, "I do not ask for words regarding existence, nor do I ask for words regarding non-existence," the World-Honored One remained seated as he was.
The non-Buddhist praised him, saying, "The World-Honored One is greatly compassionate; he has cleared away the clouds of my delusion and enabled me to enter. He then prostrated himself.
He then departed. Ānanda asked, "What realization did the outsider have that he claimed to have entered [the path]?
The World-Honored One said, "He was like a fine horse that moves at the mere sight of the shadow of the whip."
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said: "The Great and Small World-Honored Ones were both led away by Ānanda with a single statement.
He further spoke these words: "What is it that you ask? When the monk Fayen Yi was requested for instruction, before he had finished his discourse, Fayen said, "Stop!
Stop! Do you intend to understand this from the point where the World-Honored One remained silent for a long time? The monk attained realization through this. Xuedou Xian said: "Wrong!"
If you do not distinguish them correctly, it is like chasing the shadow of a whip; it is as they say: "Once the clouds of delusion have cleared, one will certainly see the Buddha.
Would you allow that such a person is a fellow practitioner? If you were to understand this together with me, then all the masters of the world would be companions to external paths.
"If each [of them] were not a seal of realization, then the monks of this eastern land would not be the equals of the non-Buddhists (tīrthikas) of the Western Heavens.
Cuiyan Zhi said: "The World-Honored One was smeared right in the face by the non-Buddhist.
As for that non-Buddhist saying, 'Let me enter,' he had not yet even dreamed of it. Since he never dreamed of it, why did he instead attain awakening? Langye Jue.

The Cloud (Yunmen) said: "Vaguely resembling a melody, it was just barely fit to hear; yet it was blown by the wind into another tune. Yangqi Hui said: "The World-Honored One set aside his own way to follow others;
the non-Buddhist merely used the occasion of the feast to offer praise. Weishan Zhe said: "The non-Buddhist harbors a precious mirror within his breast;
the World-Honored One personally held it aloft for him. Thus, the myriad phenomena were made manifest and brilliant, and all things appeared with perfect clarity."
Furthermore, Ānanda obtained the golden bell and struck it once more, so that the fourfold assembly heard it together. It was much like two dragons playing with a pearl;
it only serves to increase the arrogance of those who possess wisdom. Yunju Qi said: "Where is the point of awakening for the non-Buddhists? Someone in the assembly said:
"When the World-Honored One remained silent for a long while—that is precisely where the whip is raised. Can you understand it this way? Zhaojue Qin.
The Master said: "Wait for him to ask. Whether he asks 'Is there a word? or 'Is there no word?', strike him at the sound of his voice.

When Ānanda asked, "What has the outsider realized? the Master likewise struck him at the sound of his voice. To kill a person, one must have the sword that kills; to give life to a person, one must have the sword that gives life.
Jingshan Gaofeng, having finished citing Xuedou’s words, said: "The heterodox and the orthodox are clearly distinguished."
"It is exactly like the shadow of a whip. Xiu of Qingshan said, "The two elders were precisely critiquing from within the shadow of the whip.
After a long silence, he said, "Thirty years hence, this story will spread widely. Nanjian asked, "Gautama has been far too negligent!"
"If it were this mountain monk, I would have overturned the seat along with him. Nevertheless, those who understand me are few, while those who laugh at me are many.
Furuo Zhi said: "The two venerable masters Xuedou and Miaoxi swallowed the Buddhas and patriarchs in their spirit and their names resounded through antiquity and the present."

Examining this from the perspective of the future, even a single stroke of the thirty blows would not have been spared for him. Why? Because it was improper to falsely distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox based on the mere shadow of the whip.
Ten-thousand-fathom cold pools are clear to the bottom; At night’s stillness, the scaled fish swim toward the light.
With a single pull of the rod, they follow the hook upward; The vast waters disperse the moonlight’s brilliance.
(Baiyun Yuan) Snow covers the lofty trees, all of one color; Clear light reflects above and below, containing the empty azure. A woodcutter stands at the river crossing.
Cold. Looking as far as the eye can see, the cold moon shines white for whom?
(Cheng Kumu) The World-Honored One is just like a bronze mirror; hung in the void, the autumn moon is pure. Without partiality inside or out, it makes one’s gall-bladder shiver with cold;
high and low, each and every thing reflects one another. (Fujian Qin)
Revealing his shadow while hiding his body, he questioned the World-Honored One: "Gautama, not a single stroke was added to the dot.
From this point, the clouds of delusion began to unfurl and roll away; tenfold spirit diminished by eight parts.

(By Fodeng Xun) Before the skull of delusion and enlightenment, why labor further to raise the whip? Merely maintaining the precepts of chickens and dogs, one does not study the Zen of the Patriarchs.

(Gushan Gui): The World-Honored One’s single eye penetrates the three realms; the heretics’ pair of eyes pierce the five heavens. The floral intent is at its peak of richness as the peach-cheeked face smiles;
the springtime radiance does not reside in the tips of the willow branches. (Xuechao Yi):
Holding a brick yourself, you toss it into the air; inevitably, you strike your own head with it. It is painfully clear that you suffer this pain yourself and find it hard to describe;
it is your own doing, so rub it and go back home. (Duanqiao Lun) The wild birds warble their frequent songs;
the Eastern Emperor secretly turns the spring of the kalpa-pot. Before the forest flowers have even bloomed, they have already become a tangle.
Relying on this, there remains a lingering fragrance that coldly intoxicates people.
(Huanji Ting) On the ninth day, the thatched gate is spread with green mats; the wine banner is rolled high for the chrysanthemum spring. Since Yuanming departed, there has been no news;
there is only the lingering fragrance left to coldly intoxicate people. (Falin Yin)
The World-Honored One was asked by a non-Buddhist practitioner what dharma he had taught yesterday. The World-Honored One replied, "I taught the dharma of certainty.
The practitioner asked, "What dharma did you teach today? The World-Honored One replied, "I taught the dharma of uncertainty.
The practitioner asked, "Why was it certain yesterday but uncertain today? The World-Honored One said, "Yesterday was certain; today is uncertain."
Wuzu Ke said: "How could the World-Honored One take the property of another and use it as his own?
Weishan Zhe said: "How great the World-Honored One is! He is knocking on the upper story while standing on the lower. Daopei said: "I am not like this.
If asked why yesterday he spoke of the fixed Dharma and today he speaks of the unfixed Dharma, I would simply say: 'This is not within your realm. Jianfu Huai said: "The World..."
The Venerable One was cornered by the non-Buddhists purely by chance. Nevertheless, right and wrong had not yet been distinguished.

The Longhua School says: "The Yellow-Faced Gautama followed the heterodox and pursued the evil; though the non-Buddhists may have resonance within their words, alas, they lack the sinews in their eyes."
The ancient mirror has from the start been free of a single speck or trace; it distinguishes beauty and ugliness before one’s eyes as they arise.
Now that the mirror is shattered, there is no light or shadow; the wind rolls over the waters of the Chang Jiang, their color turbid.
(The Poison-Coated Whip) Having traveled dozens of stages through Jiangnan, the morning breeze and waning moon enter Huaqing. Upon Chaoyuan Pavilion, the west wind blows.
Urgent. [The sound of rain] enters the Changyang Palace and becomes the sound of falling rain. (Chu Shi Qi) The World-Honored One commanded Ānanda to go and ask Devadatta:

"Are you at peace within the hells? He replied: "Though I am in the hells, it is as joyful as the third dhyāna heaven. He further ordered Ānanda to ask whether he would seek to emerge from there. He replied: *Note:

This passage appears to be a fragmentary excerpt from a collection of Chan or Buddhist verse and prose, likely from the Ming dynasty, featuring the poet-monk Chu Shi Qi. The final response to the question of seeking emergence is left incomplete in the source text.*
"I shall wait for the World-Honored One to arrive and then emerge. Ānanda said, "The Buddha is the Great Teacher of the three realms;
how could he have any portion [of karma] leading to hell? He replied, "Since the Buddha has no portion leading to hell, how could I have any portion leading out of hell?"
Cuiyan Zhen said: "The words of the Master come directly from his own mouth. Jingshan Guangzuo said:
"Since there is no part that comes out and no part that goes in, what do you call Śākyamuni? What do you call Devadatta? And what do you call hell?
Do you understand thoroughly? He carries his own jar to buy village wine, yet returns wearing his robe."
[He] acts as the host. Tianning Qi said: "Miaoxi’s critique in this manner is like confusing 'diaodao' for 'xiangsi' or 'yulu' for 'cancha.
He fails to realize that Śākyamuni is Śākyamuni, Devadatta is Devadatta, and hell is hell."
It seems there is no way to engage with this. A night of falling flower-rain; a mountain stream filled with the fragrance of water. Fulong Chang said:
"To remain unshaken in the face of peril is the mark of a true great man. Wanfeng Zang said:
"Since he is the Teacher of the Three Realms, why does he have no portion of entering hell? Only when Ānanda directly receives it can he attain it."

How laughable is Devadatta! Though he entered the Nāraka hell for ten minor kalpas and attained the wondrous bliss of the third dhyāna, he still had to blow on his own body hair to return to the bird’s nest.

(Zhandang Zhun) If one can truly resolve to go over a precipice ten thousand fathoms high, one knows not where to find one's whole corpse; driven by the winds of karma, one is blown back to life once more.
Xing asked, "What time is it now? (Xu Tangyu: Water-moon, empty flowers, the sky within a mirror;
Where the cinnabar elixir is perfected, all are immortals. Let the small boat drift wherever the wind blows;
It remains only by the shallows amidst the reeds. (Bao Puliàn)
Waste fields and barren lands have no one to till them; once tilled, there is immediate strife and death.
It is better to entrust them all to you completely, so that the spring breeze may continue to grow its creeping vines as before.
(Lüyùjiāo) The Mountain Man of Huáyuè loves deep sleep; his pure heart is never moved by profit or fame. He alone finds joy within the world of his dreams.
Great! The rocks crumble and the pines wither; too lazy to record the years.
(Qing of Jingtang) Once, when the World-Honored One was about to debate with the Brahmin Dīrghanakha, the latter made a preliminary agreement, saying:
"If my doctrine falls into error, I shall cut off my own head to apologize. The World-Honored One asked: "What is the fundamental tenet of your doctrine? He replied: "My doctrine holds that all..."
"Non-acceptance is my tenet. The World-Honored One asked, "Do you accept this view? Zhi then shook his sleeves and departed.
While traveling halfway home, he attained a realization and said to his disciples, "I shall return and cut off my own head to apologize to the World-Honored One.
A disciple said, "It would be fortunate indeed to achieve victory before the assembly of devas and humans; why should you cut off your head? Zhi replied, "I would rather [die] while still alive..."
The wise man cut off his head before him; he did not achieve victory before the ignorant man. He then sighed, saying: "My doctrine has failed in both places.
If this view is accepted, the point of defeat is gross; if this view is not accepted, the point of defeat is subtle."
All humans, devas, and those of the two vehicles do not know where my doctrine falls; only the World-Honored One and the great bodhisattvas know where my doctrine falls.
Returning before the World-Honored One, he said, "Since my doctrine has fallen into defeat at both ends, I shall cut off my head to apologize.
The World-Honored One said, "In my Dharma, there is no such thing. You should turn your mind [toward the truth]."
He turned toward the Way; thereupon, together with five hundred disciples, he left the household life at once and realized arhatship.
Lingyu Jiao said: "In a state of dazed confusion, he was carrying a load of buckets when he dropped one; he did not know its weight."
Suddenly picking up his staff, he said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! Falin-yin said: "Tell me, did the Brahmin realize it while on the road?
If this were today, you would have had to strike him down and drive him out immediately."
If this view were to accept [anything], it would destroy the family lineage; if this view does not accept [anything], with whom would one debate?
When the carrying pole snaps, both ends are released; within a single hair-tip, the universe appears. (Tianyi Huai) Accepting nothing at all, he displays the family style;
with a single word, both sides are shattered and both ends are empty. Having snatched back the returning light, the red banner is seized.
At this point, one finally believes that what was said before words has fallen into one's own school [of thought].

(Fundamental Awakening, Part One) When the World-Honored One was preaching the Dharma for his mother in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, King Udayana missed the Buddha and commanded a craftsman to carve a sandalwood image.
When the World-Honored One descended, the image also came out to welcome him.
Falin’s *Yinyun* says: "The Great and Small World-Honored Ones were possessed by a malevolent spirit;
the Mass of Purple Golden Light illuminated the mountains and rivers. In heaven and among men, their majestic spirit was abundant.
Once, he commanded Mañjuśrī to lead his retinue to the city of Vaiśālī to inquire after Vimalakīrti. (Xutang Yu)
The clouds atop the ridge peak never rest; the water flowing at the bottom of the ravine is too busy. Upon a single blade of grass, the divine transformation is complete;
across the great earth, no one has eyes to see it. (Muyun Men) Zhang Sengyao painted the form of a dragon on a wall.
He succeeded in painting the dragon, yet he did not capture its spirit. When the wall was broken and he looked in astonishment, there were no two [dragons].
Such is the case. Soaring and ascending depend entirely upon the one who dots the eyes.
(Ordinary Transformation) A sandalwood-carved body of purple-gold; meeting him with such extraordinary spirit and vigor.
How shameful that Gautama’s clear and blind eyes have, for no reason, been covered by yet another grain of dust. (Observing the Spiritual Mechanism)
The World-Honored One called out three times; the image also responded three times. The World-Honored One said, "The Buddha of True Non-action truly resides within my own body.
Daoyi of Miaogushan remarked, "For whose family concern is the World-Honored One? He then shouted, "You all must by all means avoid identifying with that which is bright and lucid!"
The true Buddha, unconditioned, resides within my own body; three calls and three responses—how profoundly alert!
If a person does not awaken to this fundamental source, they will wander through kalpas of dust and mist, identifying with consciousness and spirit.
(Daming Zhi) When the World-Honored One was caused by the Gandharva King to play music, the mountains, rivers, and great earth all became the sound of the lute. Kāśyapa...
He rose to dance. The King asked, "Kāśyapa, are you not an Arhat whose outflows are exhausted? How can there still be residual habits?
The World-Honored One said, "In truth, there are no residual habits. Do not slander the Dharma. The King then stroked the lute three more times.
Kāśyapa also performed a dance three times. The king said, "Kāśyapa, is it not true that you have danced?
The World-Honored One replied, "In truth, I never danced. The king said, "How can the World-Honored One speak falsely? The World-Honored One said, "I do not speak falsely."
"You play the lute; do the mountains, rivers, the great earth, the grasses, and the trees not all become the sound of the lute?
"Yes," said the King. The World-Honored One said, "Kāśyapa was also like this; in truth, he never performed a dance. Thereupon, the King believed and accepted it.
Xiu Shan-zhu asked Chengyuan: "When the Gandharva King plays music, it causes Mount Sumeru to tremble and the waters of the ocean to surge in waves.
How do you understand Kāśyapa’s dancing? Yuan said, "In a past life, Kāśyapa was once a musician;
his habitual tendencies have not yet been eliminated. Xiu asked, "And as for Mount Sumeru trembling and the waters of the ocean surging in waves—how do you explain that?"
Yuanxiu departed. Fayan Yi stepped in and said, "This is precisely habitual tendency.
Huanji Ji said, "Some say that Śākyamuni used medicine to remove the illness, while Chengyuan used the illness to remove the medicine; they have not even dreamed of the Gandharva King.
Huangbo Qi said, "If it were I, the mountain monk, when asked whether Kāśyapa was an Arhat, I would..."

Since his outflows are already exhausted, how could there still be any residual habits? Moreover, he even rose to dance. It was merely by using one wedge to extract another that he caused the Gandharva King to fall into successive doubts and be put to death.
Gently plucking a single string, its sound vibrates through the three thousandfold world-systems and the great chiliocosm. Fortunately, Kāśyapa understood the hidden intent;
he was willing to let his silken sleeves be stained by the spring mist.
(Tuduo Ce) There is a three-foot sword fit for an audience with the state of Zhao, yet without eyes that see a thousand li, it is difficult to perceive a hanging thread. Lofty and majestic!
Majestic! The Great Master of the Three Realms. (Xu Tangyu) The moon reflects off the plum blossoms, white;
the wind drives the willow catkins wild. Human sentiments are like the horse’s jaw; the traveler’s road is like a sheep’s gut.
(From the *Yujü Qián*):

At the assembly on Vulture Peak, there were five hundred bhikṣus who had attained the four dhyānas and possessed the five supernormal powers (*pañcābhijñā*), yet had not yet attained the patience of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*).

By means of their supernormal power of knowledge of past lives (*pūrvanivāsajñānābhijñā*), each of them individually beheld their own past lives, [seeing how they] had killed their fathers and committed harm.
The mother and the assembly harbored doubts within their minds and were unable to penetrate the profound Dharma.
Thereupon, Mañjuśrī, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, took a sharp sword in his hand and pressed it against the World-Honored One. The World-Honored One said, "Stop, stop!"
"Do not commit an act of rebellion. Do not harm me; I shall surely be harmed. To be harmed while practicing the good—to be so harmed—is [the true state].
Mañjuśrī has been devoid of self and person from the very beginning; it is only because of the internal mind that one perceives a self and a person.
When the internal mind arises, 'I' am inevitably harmed, and this is precisely what is called 'harming. Thereupon, the five hundred bhikṣus realized their own original mind."
"A dream is like an illusion; within a dream or an illusion, there is no self, no person, nor even parents who give birth or are born.
At this, the five hundred bhikṣus praised in unison: 'Mañjuśrī, the Great Wise One, has profoundly penetrated the very source of the Dharma.
Though he personally grasps a sharp sword and presses it against the body of the Tathāgata, the sword and the Buddha are likewise identical—a single mark, without distinction.'"
"There are two: the signless and the unarisen. Within these, how can there be killing? Tian Tong Jie said:
"To act for others, one must act thoroughly; to kill a person, one must see blood.
Manjusri exhausted every ounce of strength from his wrists, yet he still did not know where this sword came from; it has brought shame upon the Old Man Shakyamuni, whose entire body is but a mouth.
Unable to resolve this through analysis, five hundred bhikṣus attained enlightenment in such a manner—yet they entered hell as swiftly as a shot arrow.
Suddenly, if one were to kick over the great ocean and topple Mount Sumeru, Yunmen’s fan would leap up to the Thirty-three Heavens and strike Indra on the nose;
a blow from the carp of the Eastern Sea would cause rain to pour down like an overturned basin. But what then?
After a long silence, he said: "Since I first mastered the Three Platforms, every beat has been nothing but song. Wanfeng Zang said:

"If I were the World-Honored One, I would wait for Mañjuśrī to arrive and strike him dead with a single blow of my staff, so as to spare the bhikṣu from circling around in the realm of formlessness and non-arising. Nanshan Bao said: "The World-Honored One was struck by Mañjuśrī..."
*Sat*. This means you must cast out all the old, stagnant goods you have accumulated from the very beginning.
If it were not for these five hundred bhikṣus who are so skilled at "untying the wrist," even if Mañjuśrī had hands all over his body, he could not have gathered them up.
Nevertheless, this may suffice within the gate of Gautama; however, within the gate of the patch-robed monks (*naṃseng*), not even a single drop is of any use.
From the very beginning, Buddhas and Patriarchs have always been at odds. Where the electric wheel turns, it is straight as a bowstring.
If the Golden-haired Lion could understand this pressure through harmony, the Qilin in the moon would laugh until they pierce the heavens.
(Xiatang Yuan) When Mañjuśrī pressured the Tathāgata that day, the five hundred śrāvakas had their eyes opened wide. If you wish to understand the Buddha of the Tathāgata...
So it is. Within the green serpent’s casket, wind and thunder roar.
(Fundamental Awakening I) Emerging from the casket, the green serpent’s breath spews rainbows; it shifts the mountains and seas by tens of thousands of layers.
Had there not been a guest with a grievance at that time, why would one appeal to the presence of the Sovereign regarding points of difference? (Green Rain on the Banana Leaves)
The World-Honored One, in response to King Prasenajit’s question—“In the noble ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), is there the conventional truth (*saṃvṛti-satya*)?
If one says there is not, then wisdom should not be twofold; if one says there is, then wisdom should not be unitary.

The World-Honored One replied, "It is the stupa of the Buddhas of the past. Ānanda asked, "As for those Buddhas of the past..."
"Who is your disciple? The World-Honored One replied, "He is my disciple. [The monk] said, "It should be so.

"If I were Ānanda, when the World-Honored One said, 'Wait; this is my disciple,' I would simply ask the Buddha, 'Whose disciple is he?
As soon as I was about to open my mouth, I would have prostrated and departed. Lianfu Ce said:
"If Ānanda had seen at that moment that he was his disciple, why did he not immediately perform three prostrations? This would have forced the Yellow-Faced Old Man to find no place to stand."
At the place where the World-Honored One was seated, he saw two men carrying a pig past him. He then asked, "What is this?
They replied, "The Buddha possesses all-encompassing wisdom; yet you do not even recognize a piglet. The World-Honored One said, "One must still ask it as it passes by."
Taizai Xuan said, "Had it not been for the World-Honored One’s question, I would have almost forgotten. Dizang En said, "This old man was also without cause;
I have added one complication upon another. Suddenly, the two of them burst into loud laughter and carried the pig away.
What a scene of utter embarrassment! Shouchang Jing said, "The gentleman assists in the perfection of others' virtues."
Wanfeng Zang said: "Carried forward, he has already fallen. Zifú Lǔ said: "The gentleman is moved by profit.
Lǜyǔ Jiāo said: "The World-Honored One is much like one who invites a thief to ruin his house.
Even if those two had waited for the question and struck him with a single blow of the staff, saying, 'Why do you not offer a rebuttal?'—how could the World-Honored One have reached a settlement?"

"Is it impermanent? The World-Honored One likewise did not answer. [The interlocutor] said, "World-Honored One, you possess all-encompassing wisdom; why do you not answer me?
The World-Honored One replied, "All that you ask is mere conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*)."
Gaofeng Miaoyun said: "The heterodox scholars may have spoken like those who are mute, yet the World-Honored One’s silence was like thunder.
To see it clearly here is precisely to increase frivolous proliferation (*prapañca*). Why? Listen closely, listen closely! Baiguangming said:
"The heterodox scholars asked about the Dharma twice, which has already become frivolous proliferation; the World-Honored One did not answer twice, yet the frivolous proliferation remains abundant."

the long sword leaning against the sky chills those who approach. Yuan-an Yue said:
"If I were Kāśyapa, seeing him speak in such a manner, I would have laughed once more. Let us see how this old fellow will finally settle the matter. Chong-hua Neng.

the Red-Browed One ultimately did not strike the poor man’s house.

Power. In the space between her brows, joy beholds a single dot of spring.

she does not see the noble lady atop the palace. (Nan’an Yi) With high hair-knots and cloud-like tresses, her palace makeup is complete.
To a single melody in the spring breeze, she sings of Du Weiniang. Siming has seen this so often that he regards it as nothing.
Incident: He was so distressed that he killed the Governor of Suzhou (Shi Gongben).
The Lord rises early; the minister rises early. As the moon sets over the vermilion court and dawn approaches, he hastens with his golden belt to the audience before the Sovereign.
The imperial incense burners drift in the mist; the palace chambers are deep and secluded. At the Wumen Gate, all is still as the first moon rises.
From the halls comes the cry of a phoenix.
(Riding the sound of the lion) Once, when Mañjuśrī arrived at the place where the Buddhas had gathered, each of the Buddhas returned to their own realm, leaving only a single woman behind.
While in samādhi, Mañjuśrī wondered, "How is it that this woman is able to approach the Buddha’s seat while I cannot?
The World-Honored One said, "Simply awaken this woman and ask her yourself. Mañjuśrī then circumambulated the woman three times.
He snapped his fingers once. He then supported her up to the Brahma Heaven, yet despite exhausting all his supernatural powers, he could not release her from her samādhi.
The World-Honored One said, "Even if there were hundreds of thousands of Mañjuśrīs, they too would be unable to release this woman from her samādhi.
Below, past lands as numerous as the sands of forty-two Ganges Rivers, there is the Bodhisattva Vimalacitra who can release this woman from her samādhi. It was necessary...
Wuming emerged from the earth. The World-Honored One commanded her to come forth; Wuming then snapped her fingers once, and the woman thereupon arose from her samādhi.
Cuiyan Zhi said: "A monk goes to stay in a temple; when a thief strikes, one does not guard one's own home. Wuyun Feng said:
"Not only can Mañjuśrī not emerge from this samādhi, I fear that even the Tathāgata could not emerge from it.
Cuiyan Zhen asked a monk: "Why was Mañjuśrī unable to emerge, while Wuming was instead able to emerge? Yingshao [commented].
When Wufang was questioned, he pinched his knee with his hand and walked away. Zhen laughed and said, "He is not yet a man who sells spoons and chopsticks.
