Pogong Miaoxiu said: "For forty-nine years, this old fellow has been topsy-turvy, speaking crosswise and speaking vertically, all in the vain hope of being diligent at the very end; yet he did not realize that he was deceiving hundreds of millions of others."
The assembly has remained until now fallen beneath the Iron Ring Mountains (Cakravāḍa), with no means of liberation. Qinghuazhen said:
"If I, this mountain monk, had been there at that time, I would have simply and lightly patted the World-Honored One on his back and said: 'Old man, do not let your mind rest.'"

Not only does this cause Gautama to stand with his face covered in shame, but it also spares the hundreds of thousands of humans and devas from merely listening to empty sounds by means of their ladles.
Chongxian remarked: "Lacquer cuts itself because of its hardness; grease burns itself because of its brightness.
The Yellow-Faced Gautama remains unchanged until death—how firm and resolute he is!"
Patting his chest, he addresses the assembly, deceiving the infants; yet how can his body move when his steps do not? For three thousand years, he has received echoes and sustained emptiness;
the spring breeze remains as it was, and the grass grows lush and green.
(Changling Zhuo) The wind shakes the willow threads as Pāpīyas dances; the rain moistens the flower cheeks as Nanda and Ānanda grieve. Where is the Yellow-Faced Gautama?
Go away! To cause people to arrive here and merely knit their brows—(Wuzu Fan)—under the twin śāla trees, he rubbed his chest with his hand;
speaking of existence and talking of non-existence, he prattled of empty liberation.
If one says that Gautama once entered extinction, it is a mistaken teaching that makes the weeping birds laugh at the spring breeze—(Xuzhou Du).
This decrepit Gautama knows no shame; even as he departs, he still displays his elegance. Striking his chest, he shows the assembly where he has gone:
a single cry from a weeping bird, and the mountains grow even more secluded.
(Wanshan Ning) On the day of the World-Honored One’s nirvana, Kāśyapa arrived last. The World-Honored One then revealed his two feet from within the coffin.
He showed it to him. Kāśyapa then prostrated and requested that the Tathāgata cremate himself with the fire of samādhi.
Immediately, the golden coffin rose up from its bed of seven treasures, circumambulated the city of Kuśinagara seven times, and returned to its original place.
There, he manifested the *tejodhātu-samādhi* (fire-element samādhi) and consumed himself by fire.
Chengshan Qian said: "The Yellow-Faced Old Man has been showing off for forty-nine years, yet he is still not satisfied.
At the very end, he once again puts on all these various displays; truly, he does not know life from death.
Nevertheless, even grinding one's bones to powder would not suffice to repay him."
He attained nirvana before even leaving the royal palace; why was it necessary for his golden coffin to expose his two feet?
This caused Kāśyapa’s eyebrows to knit in frown, while Ānanda overturned the *yaṣṭi* pillar at the gate.
(Fujian Qin) As he was about to depart, he would not yet rest; once his two lotus-feet were revealed, they could no longer be withdrawn. To this day, his bones and joints remain joined with his hair.
The Aperture: Exposed to the spring breeze atop the hundred grasses. (Xutang Yu) Seven steps taken leave behind traces;
the coffin reveals the twin feet—how easily can they be gathered? A light rain sprinkles flowers like a thousand drops of tears;
thin mist enshrouds the bamboo like a mound of sorrow. (Gao Feng Miao)
As soon as he opened his mouth, he was struck down; at the moment of death, he again exposed his hidden flaws. Throughout his life, his vast spirit could not be restrained;
even in the coffin, he went mad. (Lingji’s Contemplation):
Before the World-Honored One left Tuṣita Heaven, he had already descended into the royal palace; before he emerged from his mother’s womb, his work of saving sentient beings was already complete.
Tianye Zhuyun said: "Do not wait for right and wrong to enter your ears; those who were once close friends may turn into enemies.
Bunet Yuu said: "In the land of Silla, fire burns; in the region of Wu and Yue, stone men have their feet scorched.
Master Zhi discards the scissors from the end of his staff and knocks down the walls where Fenggan used to dwell in Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai. Fenyang Wude..."
Suddenly, from within the sub-temple, there emerges a flat-headed wild duck of Gaoyou. Upon meeting anyone, it bows its head and says, "Master, Master.
Then, looking left and right, it says: "Since Xuansha departed, there has been no news;
on every branch, red and white flowers alike do not bloom."
A sharp blade may have honey upon it, yet there is no need to lick it; do not taste the water of a household tainted by *gū* poison.
By neither licking nor tasting, one commits no offense; composed and clad in brocade, one returns to one’s own home.

(Dahui Zonggao) Without leaving Tuṣita, he descended to the royal palace; he immediately stepped onto the mountain of blades and entered the boiling cauldron. He casually seized the "white-thief" (the thief who steals unseen).
Thief! Your eyes are filled with exposed evidence and stolen goods.
(Xiatang Yuan) Your flesh and bones were once starkly bare; today your face has grown a thousand layers thick.
You should be counted as one more who has "lifted the head and covered the tail," winning the race for the bell after the *śrāmaṇera* meal. (Huican Ti)
When the sun rises, the heavens rejoice; when clouds arise from the earth, sorrow is born. How can it be that humans do not age, remaining like water flowing forever?
(By Qian Yan-chang) Silk strings vibrate beneath the night moon; emerald sleeves dance in the spring breeze. In this very state of carefree wandering, who can share in it?
(Shuzhong Yun) For a thousand years the soul of Shu still harbors resentment toward whom? Its cries, dripping blood, fall upon the flowering branches.
On a night of bright moon and eastern winds across the mountains, it is precisely the moment when the sorrowful person cannot sleep. (Tianye Zhou)
This refers to applying rat poison. A beautiful woman, resentful, ingests it; once ingested, she immediately becomes insane. Whether her hair is disheveled or not, her feet are surely bound.
(A Han-era metaphor from various sutras).
At the beginning of the sutra, a monk asked Dizang Chen: "The character 'mi' (rice) lacks the 'mu' (wood) radical; it is not the character 'ba' (eight). I wonder what kind of character it is.
Dizang said: "Look at the footnote below. Gunanmen said: "The character 'mi' itself is the footnote."
Because characters are not it, yet without them it is not formed. The myriad phenomena of the universe are clarified herein.
Even if one were to skillfully explain a thousand kinds of wonders, it would be neither the *upāya* nor the sutra.

(Piyun Ji) The golden words of our Buddha are a deep ocean of meaning; opening and closing [the teachings] depends solely on awakening to the true mind. The wondrous point is marked at the very beginning.
Memorandum. A secret emissary, the clay ox, chants day and night.
(Yunju You) The character "yi" is not formed; the eight strokes are not right. The *śakrāloka* eye cannot peer into it.
Re-extracted upon the tip of a single hair, the wrathful Nanda and Tāta lose their majesty. (Jingshan Gao)

Bird tracks are half-revealed upon the gray moss; tadpoles swim together in the spring waters. If you do not believe, accept, and practice this, you will not avoid rising from your seat [in the midst of your studies].
(Shi Ming) Do not seek the original truth in the title of the scripture;
why search for the Dharma King’s body within a pile of paper? Before the Sanskrit case has been opened, you must take it up as your own responsibility.
Go! Spare yourself from being a man who merely traces the lines and counts the characters.
(Jue'an Xiang) The character "with" (*yi*) does not form an eight; it is not so. The spring breeze brushes the railing, yet the flowers still sleep.
Where has the Prince gone, that he has not yet returned? The fragrant grasses grow lush and thick, filling the earth with sorrow. (Juelang Sheng)
The characters do not form a word; eight strokes fail to complete it. At first glance it seems like "豈" (qǐ), yet upon close reading it is like a "bean" (dòu).
It would be better to suit both parts by cutting the lapel and extending the sleeve. (Sānyíyú) / From of old, one plants trees to enjoy the cool breeze;
though the tree grows tall, one still laments the darkness in the guest window. One exerts all effort to push it open, yet cannot.
Depart! It will cause people for a thousand ages to expend their deliberations.
(Qian Chu-ne) Even Cangjie found it difficult to create [the characters], and Kumārajīva found it difficult to translate. When the Muni held it up, he himself did not recognize it first.
(Seng Ying-shi) After Ānanda finished begging his food at the Śūraṅgama Sūtra, he...

Begging for alms has no fixed method; yet when asked by one with ill intent, the almsgiver’s compassionate heart pities the guest in his moon-like face and *kāṣāya*, while her feelings are captivated by the lady with brows like mountain peaks.

In her coquettish charm, she promises to share the flowers reflected in the mirror to avoid laughter; in her radiant beauty, she leaves behind hairpins compared to jade, feeling shy before their fragrance.
Had it not been for the parrot calling out the man’s name, who would have believed that such tenderness was but a dreamland? (Seeking a response from within)
In the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, the Buddha said to Ānanda: "When I do not see, how is it that you do not see the place where I do not see?
If you could see my non-seeing, then it would naturally not be the characteristic of that non-seeing. If you cannot see the ground of my non-seeing,"
Spontaneity is not a thing. How could it not be you? Boshan Lai said: "The entire earth is this Śākyamuni; Ānanda touches the nostrils of Śākyamuni.
The entire earth is this Ānanda; Śākyamuni tears open the breast of Ānanda. Now tell me, where does one turn?
"I see it. Where would I not see it? If you can plant an eye here, the Yellow-Faced Old Man has deceived others and, moreover, deceived himself.
Miaowei Jun said: "The World-Honored One’s words here contain two points of defeat.

If you can examine them through and through, you will stand alone by the side of the Pond of Mandarava Lotuses; if you cannot examine them through and through, you will be like a pair of solitary wild geese crashing into a net."
The earth soars high;
the whole elephant and the whole ox are no different in intent. From of old, all masters have shared this same model.
If you wish now to see the old Gautama, every land and every speck of dust lies halfway there. (Xuedou Xian)
The pillar before the hall has long been pregnant; the child born is truly remarkable. Before it can speak, it composes a rhapsody;
with a single stroke, it wins the title of Grand Marshal. (Baizhang Yuan) He speaks of departing from the hundred negations while maintaining the rules;
yet when not a single dharma is mentioned, one still falls into the trap. In Vimalakīrti’s silence, he was once sealed in speechlessness.
Mouth. In the vast silence of Magadha, the door is just now being closed.
(Fujian Qin) On the day a novice first sells flowers, she hides her teeth with a coy bashfulness; yet when her countenance grows old, it is stripped bare with nothing left to conceal.
Yet one laughs at the white clouds dispersing in vain; One knows not where the bright moon has fallen—to whose house?
(Chongjue Kong) The vast ocean is drained dry, and the great void is filled. The nostrils of the patch-robed monk are long; the tongue of the ancient Buddha is short.
A strand of pearls passes through nine curves; a jade ring turns but once. Meeting directly beneath, they do not recognize each other; Only then does one believe that this person is truly such.
Joining Companions. (Hongzhi Jue) Through the forest, one faintly hears the sound of looms; One knows there are people living in the green mists.
But when one actually enters the gate and sees for oneself, It turns out to be nothing more than a child’s play. (Jiandang Ji)
Smooth stones are not jade; clear waters are not gold. Great Yu channeled them westward, while Bian He wept as he sank into the earth.
How beautiful and how vast! Erroneous in antiquity and ground down in the present. (Xutang Yu):
A hundred knots of sorrowful entrails—parting is difficult. A mute man eating bitterness—to whom can he speak? If there are words, they can only be told to the East.
Feng: "How can one untie the knot in the center? (Zhanran Cheng:
"A home with jar-windows and rope-doorposts, a dwelling of commoners and slaves; raising poles and hacking wood is but a vain clamor.
To know that where purple canopies gather like clouds, a single sword can slay the serpent of the White Emperor. (Lingrun Ji:)
In the *Śūraṃgama*, the Buddha commanded Mañjuśrī to go and protect it with this mantra.
Cease seeking it upon palm leaves or birch bark; its patterns follow the form and thus defile it. How could the *Uṣṇīṣa* Dharma be fathomed by ordinary sentiments?
The heart of the mantra must be transmitted and upheld by one of great wisdom. How could a red furnace allow spring snow to remain? In a black marsh, there is only the sorrowful sight of staining.

Plain silk. Once you have realized it, all mountains will be your native village; whether moving forward or retreating, there is a path that naturally transcends the forked ways. (Spontaneously seeking to receive the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.
The Buddha said to Ānanda: "If you can transform objects, you are identical to the Tathāgata."
If one can turn things around, one is immediately a Tathāgata. When spring warmth comes, mountain flowers bloom everywhere.
One naturally possesses a pair of hands for the destitute; they have never easily performed the Three Terraces dance.
(Baizhang Yuan) The color of rain blends with mist across the four quarters; how can one peer in before the eyelids have even opened? To casually pierce through the Vajra [mind]—
The boundary is vast and open, without the toil of paths or crossroads.
(Or-an-ti) Where others dwell, I do not dwell; where others walk, I do not walk. It is not that it is difficult for me to live together with others;
it is simply that the monastic and the lay must be clearly distinguished. (Ci-shan-ying)
Yao’s robe-hanging in non-action; Yu’s guiding of the waters; Lun Pian’s carving with skilled hands;
Ji Chang’s shooting with sharp arrows—they each perfected their capacities and occupied their respective stations. As for man and thing, which is this and which is that?
(De Wei-yu) In the fields, green snail shells form the bones; before the steps, red amaranth leaves serve as flowers. The body and belly of the earthworm are nothing but [insects].
Crab. Jellyfish eyes are all shrimp. (Duanliu Du) *Śūraṃgama Sūtra*:
"When seeing sees, that seeing is not seeing. Seeing is already apart from seeing; seeing cannot reach it."
Nengren Gui said: "The falling flower has the intention to follow the flowing water; the flowing water has no mind to cherish the falling flower. Hansong Cao said:
"Of the thirty-six meritorious ministers of Emperor Shizu, how can the Cloud Terrace compare to the height of the Fishing Terrace?
Miaowei Jun said: "The World-Honored One was like a small child eating a plum; he hurriedly bit into the red part, and suddenly his finger was bitten through."
The head—directly it causes blood to splash up to the Brahma Heaven.
Upon the stringless lute lies a song of no partiality; once played, it rolls on and on. The flowing water over broken cliffs has few who understand it.
Six times six does not equal thirty-six. (Miaofeng Shan)
Leaning on a slender cane, he reaches the heights where wind and mist mingle; He begs the traveler for a broader field of vision.
One knows not by how much that vision is broadened— The white birds have flown away, and the azure sky remains.
(Puweng Xian) Rain washes the pale red of the peach blossoms tender; Wind shakes the light green of the willow filaments. Within the shadows of white clouds, the strange rocks stand.
Dew. Amidst the luster of green waters, ancient trees are clear.
(Qian’an Guang) The Persian from the bottom of the sea has lost his gold; the double-blind old woman searches for it in the grass. At night, she feels her way and finds pine needles and thorns;
she runs all through the eastern village crying out to sell needles. (Tianru Ze)
The mountains are resplendent; joy follows our travels. Throughout the night, the scenery reflects upon the azure stream.
The moon sets, the watches of the night end, and dawn breaks at the horizon. Drunk, we support the Lord as he ascends the high tower.
(Yinshan Xian) A single expanse of tidal sound descends upon the Stone Head. Parting at the river pavilion brings sorrow to the traveler. How pitiable, the willow threads—ten thousand strands.
A foot-measure, as if tying away a boat on the spring river. (Lingrun’s Mechanism) The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*’s "Seeking the Mind in Seven Places":
the seven places of seeking the mind are easily established; when one investigates and pursues them, the case becomes clear. It is all because the internal thief is difficult to guard against.
Avoiding chaos, he turned heaven and earth to see the Great Peace.
(Wan’an Yan) Blowing on the chaff to find the grain results in nothing but fuss; not because of one matter does one grow one bit of wisdom.
(Beijian Jian) He sought him in seven places beyond the heavens; a beam of light shot directly at Ānanda’s shoulder. Gautama was truly too fond of his son.
Urged on by all, the eel is forced onto the bamboo pole.
(Jue'an Xiang) The vast ocean is sucked dry to reveal the coral; he goes straight for the pearl beneath the jaws of the black dragon.
For over thirty years he has sought the ocean treasury, yet he did not know his own body was dwelling upon a mountain of jewels. (Yujì Qián)
In the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, the eight ways of returning are used to discern seeing;
brightness, darkness, form, and emptiness cannot be returned. That which cannot be returned is beyond all climbing and grasping. It carves out the void of space to form its boundaries and shores:
one layer of water separates it from one layer of mountain. (Wan’an Yan)
*Śūraṅgama Sūtra*: Ānanda and the great assembly have recovered their fundamental, wondrous mind.
They search east, west, south, and north for empty space; from the ends of the earth to the furthest reaches of the heavens, no news can be obtained.
Their strength is exhausted and their spirits weary, yet there is nowhere to find it. The ten-thousand-year-old pine remains upon Mount Zhurong. (Wan’an Yan)
It accords with my former aspirations; now they are fulfilled. This jade is truly marvelous; I only fear it may not be jade.
(Beijian Jian) *Śūraṃgama Sūtra*:
"The wondrous nature is perfectly luminous, transcending all names and marks."
Luyan He said: "Is not the wondrous nature itself the name? Is not perfect luminosity itself the mark?
How then can you explain the principle of being free from all names and marks?"
One coin as capital, ten thousand coins in profit; the wealthy feel they lack, while the poor have more than enough.
A few grains of medicine to transform the bones and seize the essence—let him yield to Pan Lang, riding his donkey backward.
(Wan’an Yan) The golden platter cannot be moved; it rolls and turns, difficult to stay still. After waiting for a long while, it is perfectly bright and clear like a dewdrop.
(Bei Jian Jian): Zi, Chou, Yin, Mao; Bing, Ding, Jia, Yi. The small month has twenty-nine days; the large month has thirty.
The sea deity knows its value but not its price; it remains among humanity to illuminate the night. (Mu Yun Men)
*The Śūraṅgama Sūtra*: "All things that can be returned are naturally not you; as for that which cannot be returned, if it is not you, who else could it be? Nengren Gui said:
"I have always regretted that when spring departs, there is no place to seek it; I did not know it would turn and enter right here. He gave a shout and said:
"Thirty years from now, do not say that Nengren has corrupted the children of others! Hansong Cao.
It is said: "Originally intending to flee to dwell within a famous mountain, I have instead emerged from that mountain back into the human world.
Returning, returning, returning—after this return, there is no further return. A solitary idler between heaven and earth: last night a great tiger was bitten by a leopard;
its fur and skin have fallen away, yet its body remains fundamentally striped. (Jue'an Xiang)
The sun is warm and the breeze gentle; the scenery is even more extraordinary. Flower upon flower, grass upon grass, the whole mechanism is revealed.
A gust of fragrant wind rises from the wisteria, drawing wandering bees to fly everywhere.
(Xinwen Ben) Who else is it that does not return to you? Withered red petals drift onto the fishing rocks. The sun slants, the wind has stilled, and no one is there.
Sweeping away, the swallow flies back to the water’s edge.
(Tianmu Li) The wutong leaves fall in the midst of the third autumn; The wild geese’ wings flutter as they fly freely away. Vast and boundless, the land of Chu cannot hold their flight;
They now follow the cold moon to roost upon the marshes. (I’an Yan)
The days grow long and the smoke vanishes; the ancient halls are cool. In this era of Great Peace and no affairs, the wine banners are fragrant.
Who knows whose power it is that lets the cattle loose and the horses return? A full heart of tranquil and simple conduct remains.
(Zhengxinxiu) My native land is lost and all things have changed; Upon the misty waves of the river, I return under the bright moon. A wild song awakens the birds on the sandy islets.
The wild geese all fly deep into the reeds.
(Master Qu Ji) A solitary boat is moored idly at the bend of the Mi-lo River; all day long, the misty rain gathers in dense layers.
After the morning breeze scatters them across the heavens, he with the frost-white brows gazes alone upon the crystal platter. (Yue Dezu)
*Śūraṅgama Sūtra*: "The six dissolve and the one perishes.
The faculties and objects, bondage and liberation, share the same source. When they cease at a single point, the six functions are abandoned.
Grasping a single strand of red thread, the nostrils of one's birth are pierced all at once. (Wan'an Yan)
The six faculties are of no use, for faith does not penetrate; all at once, they are entrusted to the spring breeze. A single curl of incense smoke lingers idly through the clear day;
though the hundred birds do not come, the flowers are naturally red.
(Beijian Jian) *Śūraṃgama Sūtra*: Ānanda and the great assembly again addressed the Buddha, saying: "If this wondrously bright, truly pure, and sublime mind is originally..."

Coming and pervading everywhere, it is thus: even down to the great earth, the grasses, the trees, and all wriggling, sentient beings—their fundamental source, true suchness (*tathatā*), is precisely the true body of the Tathāgata’s attainment of Buddhahood. Since the Buddha-body is truly real, how could there further exist hells, hungry ghosts, or animals?
Before the Double Sword Peak lies the ruins of an ancient temple; the Celestial Honored One was originally but a single Muni.
In times of difficulty, one can only share the incense and lamps—do not listen to idle people prattle about right and wrong.
(Wan’an Yan) Three snakes and nine rats occupy a single mu of land; carrying staff and wood wherever they go, they perform their play upon meeting the stage. (Beijian Jian)

"Ānanda, you need only discard that which arises and ceases and maintain the true permanence. When the light of permanence manifests before you, the sense organs, objects, consciousness, and mind will naturally dissolve away.
Lingyan Zuyuan gave a shout and said, "The Yellow-Faced Old Man [the Buddha] sells flour while mixing it with bran; for two thousand years, this has been rare!"
People offer their price. Since Tianning has opened this shop, it is difficult to allow the goods of the traveler to remain stagnant for long.
This morning, they have all been displayed before you at once. Those who understand the times and master change, please take a full load and depart. Should you be slow-witted, however—
Holding up his staff, he said: "The movements of the market fluctuate morning and evening; do not say I did not tell you so.
*Śūraṅgama Sūtra*: 'If that which is capable of deliberation is your mind, then you are mistaking a thief for your son.'"
Xiu Shanzhu said separately: "If you can push it down to its bottom and find it is not your mind, then you are merely mistaking the son for the thief.
Tiantong Jue said: "Now, even as you push it down, whether it be the son or the thief, you are buying a hat to fit the head; eating fish, you remove the bones."
Baoshou newly said: "The World-Honored One knew only the first, but not the second;
Longji knew only the second, but not the first. Here it is not so: that which can be inferred may be the mind, and it may also not be the mind.
Why? Morning after morning is the fifteenth day of the first month; night after night is the Lantern Festival."
*Śūraṅgama Sūtra*: You should know that empty space arises within your own mind, like a single fragment of cloud appearing within the vast clarity of the great sky;

how much more so the various worlds within that empty space? If even one person among you gives rise to true realization and returns to the source, this emptiness of the ten directions will completely vanish and perish.
Wuzu Yan said: "When one person gives rise to the truth and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions is touched and struck at every turn. Zhaojue Qin said:
"When one person gives rise to the truth and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions is like adding flowers to brocade. Dongshan Daowu said:
"When one person gives rise to the truth and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions is opened wide with eight characters," and he then spread his two hands.
When one person gives rise to true awakening and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions vanishes. Try asking:
how does Yangqi’s chestnut compare to Yunmen’s fried cake?
(Nun Wuzhuo Chi) Drifting in a daze, weary with thoughts; after drinking a bowl of strong tea, the eyes open wide. The imperial transformation pervades the four seas and five lakes.
Within, there is not a single thing that is dust or defilement.
(Pak Ong-hyeon) Once accompanying the mountain clouds back to the evening hues, still attending the setting sun as it drifts upon the autumn sounds.
Though there are countless masters of brush and ink in this world, not a single stroke of this heart-wrenching scene can be painted. (Gyogwang Seong)
Gripped, it becomes a fist; opened, it becomes a palm. A single cloud in the vast void does not depart from its original source. It awakens and develops the ignorant masses.
Looking down, he uplifts those who have lost their way; the Persians from the South Sea enter the Great Tang. His eyebrows rest only above his eyes.

(Muyunmen) The moon touches the heavens, its momentum unassailable. When spring comes, it paints the emerald waves in the heart of the water. Upon the level fields and manors, travelers bustle to and fro;
only when they are pushed over do they realize the path is uneven. (Guantaoqi)
*Śūraṃgama Sūtra*: "To establish a knowing within seeing is the very root of ignorance;
to have no seeing within seeing is itself nirvāṇa—taintless, truly pure. How could any other thing be admitted therein?"
The site of enlightenment is like a cloud; Śākyamuni the Old Man has laid his entire body down. How shall the descendants of later generations receive this succession?
Do you wish to understand? The Way of Penetrating the Profundity is not the world of men; where can one seek it amidst these mountains that fill the eye?
Before the eyes of one with clear vision, there is darkness for three feet; among guests there is no host, and within the host there are guests.
The yakṣa brandishes the *kīla* staff and strikes down the single wheel of the moon from the treetop.
(Tianru Ze) *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*: Bhadrapāla enters the bath and suddenly awakens to the cause of water.
A monk who has realized the matter can digest one [portion]. On the long couch, he stretches out his legs and lies down; within his dreams, he speaks of awakening to perfect penetration.
Having washed with fragrant water, he spits right back in the face.

(Xuedou Xian) When the dust is washed away and the body touched, both are empty and still. Wondrously realizing the secret perfection, he transcends view and thought. A white jade boulder without flaw, yet in vain it receives...
A blemish! To be smeared with filth within the Assembly of Perfect Penetration (*Lengyan*).
[In the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*,] the Buddha said: "Pūrṇa, as you have said, it is fundamentally pure and serene; how then do mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise?
Have you not constantly heard the Tathāgata proclaim that the nature of awakening is wondrously luminous, and that fundamental awakening is inherently bright?"
Subtle! Pure and fundamentally luminous, pervading the entire Dharma-realm, mountains, rivers, and the great earth all appear therein.
When the nature-awareness, wondrous and bright, mistakes the reflection for the light itself, the eyes and ears then follow the body and its form. (Wan’an Yan)
Pervasive and pure, there is no room for anything else within it. Mountains, rivers, the great earth, and the myriad phenomena are all arrayed therein.
(Beijian Jian) In the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva accomplishes the thirty-two transformation bodies and attains the fourteen dharmas of fearlessness.

How excellent is Avalokiteśvara! The revolving of hearing is liberated from sound; Whether the dog barks or the donkey brays, whether it ceases or not— In both the mundane and supramundane worlds, he is as agile and lively as a leaping fish.

Wisdom. One does not meet Buddha-wisdom; it exists only when it exists within the assembly. It is merely the hidden sprout and concealed claws. In the Great Peace, there is a place of seeing. Without sparing one's eyebrows, I present this to all of you: wait for someone to ask, and answer immediately as the words come forth. Pō'ān Xian said: "Ultimately, what is Buddha-wisdom? He then offered this verse: Ultimate reality is not a matter of seeking; The true source is originally complete. When the great function is fully displayed, The ten directions are all clear and bright. If you wish to see the Buddha, Do not look for him outside yourself. If you can see him within yourself, Then he is right here before your eyes. If you do not understand this, You will wander through birth and death. If you understand this, You will transcend the world of suffering. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be grasped by the mind. If you can let go of the mind, Then you have met the Buddha. If you grasp at the mind, You are far from the Buddha. If you can let go of both mind and Buddha, Then you are free from all constraints. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be sought through effort. If you can abandon effort, Then you have attained the Way. If you rely on effort, You are lost in delusion. If you can abandon both effort and delusion, Then you are at ease in the midst of the mundane. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be realized through views. If you can abandon views, Then you have seen the truth. If you cling to views, You are trapped in ignorance. If you can abandon both views and ignorance, Then you are liberated in the midst of existence. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be attained through speech. If you can abandon speech, Then you have entered the silence. If you rely on speech, You are caught in the net of words. If you can abandon both speech and the net, Then you are at peace in the midst of the world. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be understood through intellect. If you can abandon intellect, Then you have reached the ultimate. If you rely on intellect, You are bound by discrimination. If you can abandon both intellect and discrimination, Then you are at rest in the midst of phenomena. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be cultivated through practice. If you can abandon practice, Then you have fulfilled the path. If you rely on practice, You are burdened by toil. If you can abandon both practice and toil, Then you are at ease in the midst of activity. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be maintained through mindfulness. If you can abandon mindfulness, Then you have attained non-action. If you rely on mindfulness, You are distracted by objects. If you can abandon both mindfulness and distraction, Then you are at ease in the midst of the senses. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be known through consciousness. If you can abandon consciousness, Then you have realized the unborn. If you rely on consciousness, You are immersed in the flow of birth and death. If you can abandon both consciousness and the flow, Then you are at ease in the midst of the six realms. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be attained through attainment. If you can abandon attainment, Then you have realized the unconditioned. If you rely on attainment, You are bound by the fruits of karma. If you can abandon both attainment and karma, Then you are at ease in the midst of the three worlds. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be sought through seeking. If you can abandon seeking, Then you have realized the non-seeking. If you rely on seeking, You are lost in the cycle of samsara. If you can abandon both seeking and samsara, Then you are at ease in the midst of the four modes of birth. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be grasped through grasping. If you can abandon grasping, Then you have realized the non-grasping. If you rely on grasping, You are bound by the fetters of attachment. If you can abandon both grasping and attachment, Then you are at ease in the midst of the five aggregates. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be realized through realization. If you can abandon realization, Then you have realized the non-realization. If you rely on realization, You are bound by the duality of subject and object. If you can abandon both realization and duality, Then you are at ease in the midst of the six sense bases. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be manifested through manifestation. If you can abandon manifestation, Then you have realized the non-manifestation. If you rely on manifestation, You are bound by the appearances of form and sound. If you can abandon both manifestation and appearance, Then you are at ease in the midst of the eighteen elements. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be attained through attainment. If you can abandon attainment, Then you have realized the non-attainment. If you rely on attainment, You are bound by the distinctions of gain and loss. If you can abandon both attainment and distinction, Then you are at ease in the midst of the twelve links of dependent origination. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be understood through understanding. If you can abandon understanding, Then you have realized the non-understanding. If you rely on understanding, You are bound by the delusions of ignorance. If you can abandon both understanding and delusion, Then you are at ease in the midst of the three poisons. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be practiced through practice. If you can abandon practice, Then you have realized the non-practice. If you rely on practice, You are bound by the habits of affliction. If you can abandon both practice and affliction, Then you are at ease in the midst of the eight winds. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be preserved through preservation. If you can abandon preservation, Then you have realized the non-preservation. If you rely on preservation, You are bound by the clinging to self and dharmas. If you can abandon both preservation and clinging, Then you are at ease in the midst of the four nutriments. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be maintained through maintenance. If you can abandon maintenance, Then you have realized the non-maintenance. If you rely on maintenance, You are bound by the continuity of the life-stream. If you can abandon both maintenance and continuity, Then you are at ease in the midst of the four foundations of mindfulness. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be cultivated through cultivation. If you can abandon cultivation, Then you have realized the non-cultivation. If you rely on cultivation, You are bound by the efforts of the path. If you can abandon both cultivation and effort, Then you are at ease in the midst of the seven factors of enlightenment. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be perfected through perfection. If you can abandon perfection, Then you have realized the non-perfection. If you rely on perfection, You are bound by the attainments of the stages. If you can abandon both perfection and attainment, Then you are at ease in the midst of the eightfold noble path. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be attained through attainment. If you can abandon attainment, Then you have realized the non-attainment. If you rely on attainment, You are bound by the fruits of the vehicles. If you can abandon both attainment and fruit, Then you are at ease in the midst of the three bodies of the Buddha. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be realized through realization. If you can abandon realization, Then you have realized the non-realization. If you rely on realization, You are bound by the distinctions of the teachings. If you can abandon both realization and distinction, Then you are at ease in the midst of the three mysteries. This is called the Buddha’s wisdom. It is not something to be manifested through manifestation. If you can abandon manifestation, Then you have realized the non-manifestation. If you rely on manifestation, You are bound by the appearances of the lands. If you can abandon both manifestation and appearance, Then you are at ease in the midst of the three secrets. The Lotus Sutra: If there are sentient beings who hear this chapter on Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, you should know that the merit of such people is not small.

Constantly stirring the white days while seeking flowers in the alleys; I spend all my gold for the price of wine. Wearing my robe inside out, I clap my hands high;

When Vimalakīrti, with the assistance of Subhūti, entered Vimalakīrti’s house to beg for alms, Mañjuśrī took the bowl and filled it with rice, saying:
"If you can regard food as equal, then all dharmas are also equal; if all dharmas are equal, then [regarding food is equal]..."
The food is also equal. Only when you beg for alms in this manner may you accept the food.

Even if those six heterodox teachers are your teachers, and because of them you have left the household life, and wherever those teachers fall, you also follow them in falling—only then may you accept the food.
You have entered into various false views and failed to reach the other shore; you dwell among the eight difficulties and have not attained freedom from them;
you are identical to afflictions and remain apart from the dharma of purity. Yet, you have attained the samādhi of non-contention—may all sentient beings also attain this concentration.
Those who give to you are not called fields of merit; those who make offerings to you fall into the three evil realms.
You act with one hand in concert with the various Māras and are a companion among all weary laborers. You are no different from the various Māras and the afflictions (*kleśa*);
you harbor enmity toward all sentient beings, slander the Buddhas, and destroy the Dharma. You do not enter [the path].
“As long as there are those who count as a multitude, you shall never attain parinirvāṇa. If you can accept this, only then may you take this food.
When Subhūti heard this, he was utterly bewildered; not knowing how to respond, he set down his bowl and wished to leave.
Baofeng Qing said: "The meaning of 'a bountiful year' belongs to Māṭhika; however, Subhūti was so preoccupied with gazing at the heavens that he lost his oar.
Consequently, when food reached his mouth, it was snatched away by another. Guangyin Biao said:
To seal the mouth of Chi-shuo and seize the eloquence of those who engage in strife—such that none dare to oppose—is what is prized in clear discernment.
Why did the Venerable One not, at that time, take a single morsel of food and wait for him to speak thus, thereby immediately silencing his mouth?
"Lest this fellow should fall into the thicket of complications. Nevertheless, looking at it now, it seems as though he has already lost the first move to him on the cold ground.
It is clear that old Śūnyatā-janman (Śāriputra) is made to laugh to death. Lin Youhui said:
"Everyone says that Subhūti could not pick up a scorpion’s tail upside down or pull a tiger’s whiskers against the grain; consequently, when the food reached his mouth, he was caught by it."
People snatch it away, yet they do not realize that the Venerable One was merely setting down his bowl before departing;
this was no act of ill will. Boundless and limitless, there is no need for deliberation: the ebb and flow of the tide are inherently level.
Whether clear or turbid, shallow or deep, bitter or bland—the single flavor is distinct and clear. (Baoning Yong)

With wrong views, one takes refuge in non-Buddhist teachers; falling together with such a teacher—how could there be any doubt about this? Relying on you, may your alms bowl be filled with fragrant rice;
at noon, when the sun stands high, my belly is truly hungry.

(Zhang Wujin) Entering the forest without stirring the grass, entering the water without disturbing the waves—the cauldron of boiling oil has no place that is cool; close your eyes and leap across the Yellow River.
(Gushan Gui) Sitting alone, who can know my intent?
Green mountains face the setting sun. The flowers must bloom throughout the night; they do not wait for the morning breeze to blow. (Jingshan Gao)
Walking alone on the street in broad daylight; lying down alone in the house at night. The mountain is high, yet it does not obstruct the flight of white clouds;
the bamboo is dense, yet it does not hinder the flow of the stream.
(Zhao Tang 1) Vimalakīrti: Prajñāpāramitā is the mother of Bodhisattvas; she accommodates all dharmas without any mark of discrimination.
All dharmas are free from the marks of discrimination; they abide in suchness according to the various marks mentioned above.
Within the scenery of spring, heaven and earth are vast; boundless rivers and mountains unfold like a painted scroll.
(Yangshan Qin) Vimalakīrti manifested illness in Vaiśālī, and the Buddha commanded Mañjuśrī to go and inquire after him. Mañjuśrī said: "That superior man is difficult to..."
To respond appropriately, he has profoundly realized the true nature of reality (*dharmatā*) and skillfully expounds the essential teachings. His eloquence is unimpeded and his wisdom is unhindered.
He fully knows all the ritual methods of the bodhisattvas and has entered every secret treasury of the Buddhas.

Having subdued all demons, he sports with supernatural powers (*abhijñā*); both his wisdom and his skillful means (*upāya*) have already reached the further shore. Nevertheless, you must now receive the Buddha’s command.
He went there to inquire after his illness.
Guishan said, "The gate of the layman is high; it may be called standing like a wall ten thousand fathoms high, where water cannot leak through.
To conceive a thought is to err; to stir a single thought is to create a barrier. If you neither conceive nor stir, you fall into the realm of non-action. How then do you enter?"
After a long silence, he said: "Step back! Step back!
Sitting coldly in the city of Vaiśālī, a hundred ailments broke out all at once; unable to have Mañjuśrī come, I nearly met my end."
(Jingshan Gao) manifested illness in the Vimalakīrti-style abbot’s quarters; even Mañjuśrī found it difficult to draw near. Looking at it, there is no medicine that can cure it;
simply avoiding certain foods is the best remedy. (Zhe’eng Yan)
Feigning illness has been incurable from the start; Mañjuśrī specifically applied the needle and the awl for him. The matter was stripped away, leaving a mouth three feet long;
when questioned, he remains as before, like a drumstick.
(Wuzu Fan) Hand holding a whisk, seated upon a Huchuang chair; eyes like falling stars, hair like hoarfrost. All day long he speaks not, yet constantly reveals [the truth].
Illness! He has gouged out healthy flesh to form a sore.
(Shuai’an Cong) Wrinkling his natural eight-character brows, who knows of these ailments?
Mañjuśrī draws out the needle from the *gāohuáng* (the vital point between heart and diaphragm)—this too is like treating a dead horse with medicine. (Zhōngxuān Fù)
Sitting upright in the master’s chamber, he misapplies his mind; how can a single tree form a forest?
Unaware that the illness lies deep within the vital organs, he is struck by Mañjuśrī with a single needle.
(Xiaoweng Kan) Vimalakīrti and Mañjuśrī: from the root of non-abiding, all dharmas are established.
I-an Kwon said: "A needle hidden in the eye; breath exhaled from the ear.
From my youth until now, I have never uttered empty words. I turn over the ocean floor to plant green pines;
I bump into Li San-heok on the street—you go west and I go east. (Ji Suwang)
Without deficiency and without remainder, without necessity and without fixity. Dharmas and dharmas are perfectly interfused; in every instance, they are manifest.
Taking non-abiding as the root, their wondrous harmony is immeasurable. Establishing all dharmas, even the sands of the world cannot fathom them.
*Du du!* A fine bird does not perch upon a tree without shadow. (Zhúlàng)
Vimalakīrti enters nirvāṇa without severing the afflictions (*kleśa*).

Born in the morning and dying by evening, this occurs millions of times; how many times in a single day do they meet face-to-face? When the battle lines are drawn and the banners unfurled, he comes forth;
when a single finger moves, the guest’s play is revealed. (Baizhang Yuan)
When the thirty-two bodhisattvas had each finished speaking, Mañjuśrī said, "Regarding all dharmas, there is no speech, no discourse, no demonstration, and no cognition;
it is free from all questioning and answering—this is the entrance into the gate of non-duality.
Mañjuśrī then asked Vimalakīrti, and Vimalakīrti remained silent. Mañjuśrī sighed in admiration, saying, "To the extent that there is not even a word or a letter..."
"Truly entering the gate of non-duality.
Baofu Zhan said, "Vimalakīrti’s single silence did not yet exit the gate of transformation. He also said, "The great and small Vimalakīrtis were pinned down by Mañjuśrī with a single sitting;
to this day they cannot rise. Baoren Xiu said, "If you want them to rise, what difficulty is there? He then gave a slap.
After Xuedou Xian finished citing Mañjuśrī’s words, he asked, "What did Vimalakīrti say? After a long silence, he said, "He has been thoroughly exposed.
Lanxi Jue said, "Mañjuśrī’s praise was well-intentioned, yet it was still like divining with a ladle while listening for an echo. Vimalakīrti remained silent;
you all must not praise a tortoise for striking a tile. Dayang Jingzhen said, "The Dharma-gate of non-duality is silence."
Yet it was not silence. If it had been silence, then Mañjuśrī would have spoken redundantly; if it had not been silence, Vimalakīrti’s entire display would have been in vain.
Baoneng Xiu said: "To sacrifice one's own person for the sake of the assembly inevitably brings disaster from one's private door;

how could Mañjuśrī’s piercing critique have been tolerated once the flaws were already exposed? Even if Tiantong says, 'He dwells amidst the secular dust yet has no trace of vulgarity,' it still does not suffice."
"This is like covering one's nose while stealing perfume. Qingshan Xiu said: "What connection is there between groping for something in speech and silence?
If you can recognize the source before all the bodhisattvas have even opened their mouths, only then will you know that speaking is itself silence, and silence is itself speaking.
All the bodhisattvas have never uttered a single word, yet the old Vimalakīrti’s voice was like thunder. Do you understand? Long.

"The elephant’s trampling is not something a donkey can endure. Boshan Lai said: "To build a plank road openly while secretly crossing at Chen-cang—were one to deliberate upon this in terms of speech or silence, how would it differ from placing a foot in a bowl?
Although these two great masters differ, their application of makeup and powder is so seamless that not even a drop of water can pass between them;

When begging for alms along the streets of the city of Vaiśālī, and when gathering robes and washing my feet in the Jeta Grove, Subhūti has, without cause, praised me as marvelous.
How could such words be so? (From the *Ratnapatra-sūtra*):
"Vajra, you should abide thus; you should thus subdue your mind."

How rare, how rare is the Buddha! The wondrous principle reaches the ultimate nirvana. How does one dwell in subduing [the passions]? Subduing them through faith is difficult. The two laws are wondrous among all dharmas;
the teachings and parables of the Three Vehicles are vast. Excellent! Now listen attentively, so that the six thieves may be spared from obstruction.
(Boatman Fushi): Seven hands and eight feet, divine heads and ghostly faces; they cannot be opened by the blow of a staff, nor severed by the edge of a blade.
They leap and bound throughout Jambudvīpa thousands of times, yet at every turn, they do not depart from the Hall of the Empty King. (Yezhu Chuan).
Severing the torrential flow that comes from the teachings; following the current does not necessarily mean drifting away in a vast rush.
The green mountains hold fast the momentum of those about to fly; the blue seas surely know the height from which they come.
(Xinwen Ben) Vajra: All marks whatsoever are empty and false. If one sees all marks as non-marks, then one sees the Tathāgata.
Lai Fayan Yi said: "If one sees that all marks are non-marks, then one does not see the Tathāgata. Baohua Ren said:
"The Great and Small World-Honored Ones embraced bridge pillars to bathe; I, however, am not like them. If one sees that all marks are non-marks..."
"Characteristics. This means seeing all characteristics. Nevertheless, while it is easy to see the Tathāgata, it is difficult to see all characteristics as non-characteristics.
Miaowei Jun said: "The great and small jewel-flowers only know how to leap within straw sandals; they do not understand seeing all characteristics as non-characteristics."
"Study further for thirty years.
Where there is form or seeking, it is all delusion; where there is no shape or mark, one falls into partiality and desiccation.
Magnificent and profound, how could there ever be idleness? A single path of cold light pierces the great void. (Yeyu Chuan)
Reflecting in the woods and reflecting in the sun, all are one and the same red. Blown down and blown open, it is all but the wind.
A pity that those who would pluck the fragrance do not see; in an instant, it is all entrusted to the wandering bees.
(Xinwen Ben) Vajra: All worthy sages are distinguished by means of the unconditioned dharma (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*).
Qianyan Chang said: "The World-Honored One has two tongues; ignorance has but one tongue.
All worthy sages are without distinction, for they all rely upon the unconditioned."
A single piece of gold forms ten thousand vessels; all depend on the artisan’s wisdom. Why must it necessarily be the city of Vaiśālī for everyone to speak of non-duality?
(Juehai Yuan) "The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom. When cold, one turns toward the fire; when hot, [one seeks the shade].
Seeking coolness; when vigorous, one performs walking meditation (*caṅkrama*); when weary, one sleeps. One looks up at the sky and opens the mouth to draw breath.
(Baoning Yong) Vajra! All Buddhas and the *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* dharma of all Buddhas.
All emerge from this sutra. A monk asked Shoushan, "What is this sutra? Shoushan said, "Lower your voice. The monk asked, "What is upholding it?

Above. At the heart of the great ocean’s waves, the Buddhas and Patriarchs extend their compassion; truly there is skillful means. Every word is proclaimed without departing from this sutra.
Entrust yourself to the source from which this sutra emerges, and you shall immediately board an iron ship amidst the clouds. Be careful not to misunderstand. (Yeyu Chuan)
Water flows from Mount Kunlun and rises as clouds; fishermen and woodcutters ask about its origin.
They know only that the surging waves and mountain crags are vast, yet they refuse to cast their lines or wield their axes.

Sitting quietly in the mountain hall at night, there is no speech; Silent and vast, it is fundamentally natural. For what reason does the west wind stir the woods and fields?
A single cry of a cold wild goose resounds through the long sky. (Yemuchuan) One should give rise to the mind without dwelling anywhere;
Vast, penetrating, and perfectly luminous, it is true in every place. Directly beneath, the crown of the head opens to the Right [Eye].
The Eye: Throughout the sands of the great trichiliocosm, his entire body appears.

The moon is bright and the stars are few; crows and magpies fly southward. Circling the tree three times, there is no branch where they may perch.

A lone spear and a single horse traverse the winds and dust; willow colors and flower smoke dare not approach his person. With a single blast of the Qiang flute, the courage of Liaodong is lost;
where the wheel of frost appears, it brings even greater sorrow to men. (Yinyuan Qi) Vajra:
If one is treated with contempt by others, this is because that person’s karmic offenses from previous lives should have caused them to fall into the evil realms. By virtue of [the present...]

Choushou (Chou) comments: "If one holds that there are phenomena external to the mind, one should fall into the evil realms; yet by clinging to oneself, one is instead despised by others."
"Vile! Boshanlai said: "How many people have you bound and killed? How many people have you liberated? You are both female and wearing yellow;
if one judges you by cause and effect, you will enter hell as swiftly as a shot arrow."
A bright pearl held in the palm; those with merit are rewarded. Whether beautiful or ugly, none can approach it—it possesses no artifice at all.
Since there is no artifice, Pāpīyān loses his way. "Gautama, Gautama, do you recognize me? (The clarity of awakening is manifest.
Who does not know that water does not wash water? The whirlwind is eternally still, yet it rushes about incessantly. If one could [read] the calendar for a thousand years...
Calculate it! You will avoid being pushed off the palm of the patrol officer.

thus they overturn the mountain of transgressions of their predecessors. (Zhang Wujin)
Succession upon succession of merits and faults; the sticky persistence of cause and effect. Beyond the mirror, Yanruo Duo runs wild; struck by the staff, Paozhuo falls.
When Paozhuo has fallen, they come to offer congratulations, yet he says, "I have been neglecting you all along.
(Tiantong Jue) The warbling of secluded birds amidst crimson and green; a single couch of warm breeze startles one from midday sleep. A dancing sleeve and a single shirt enter the marketplace.
In the marketplace, Lord Zhang drinks the wine while Lord Li is intoxicated.
(Shi Yu Fang) Though his native land does not employ him, the Chanyu eats snow and swallows felt with ease. For ten years in the desert he has borne the Han insignia;
his loyal spirit needs no crane to carry his letter. (Ju Zu You)
Vajra! The *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* attained by the Tathāgata is, within it, neither real nor false;
*bodhi* is neither real nor false.
How many men can truly be called "great men"? Only those who do not return to the Cinnabar Valley for the golden pheasant.
The phoenix soars; the azure pool reflects the empty jade hare.
(Fohui Spring) Life’s journey is like a dream or drifting clouds; with no worldly possessions, I have severed ties with my kin.
I have preserved but a pair of blue and white eyes, laughing at the countless people who come and go. (Yefu Creek)
The flavor of salt in water; the blue pigment within the lacquer. That which the Tathāgata has attained is accomplished by a single stroke.
How laughable that even the dexterous hand of Wei Zhiyao never once managed to capture the true likeness of Master Zhigong.
(Muyun Men) Vajra: The past mind cannot be apprehended; the present mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended.
It is so. In the Nantang Hall, Jingju recounted how Deshan went to Tanzhou to visit a tea lady for refreshments. The lady asked, "The three minds cannot be apprehended;
which mind does the Venerable Senior refresh? Deshan was speechless. Tonight, I shall provide a substitute response for Deshan. Wait—
He said, "The three minds are unattainable. He simply replied, "Hush, hush! An old woman must not be so impolite.
Is it not too rigid to act like this? To which [the Master] replied, "No, it is not. Old woman, from where have you obtained such news?"

Is it not too weak to act in such a manner? At that time, when he said, "The three minds cannot be apprehended," you should have pointed to whichever mind [he was referring to] and simply told him, "Give me a pair of warm ones in exchange. (Falin’s Pronunciation) Mañjuśrī asked the lady Āmrapālī: "What is the meaning of birth? The lady said:

One can clearly know that the four conditions of earth, water, fire, and wind have never attained self-existence; yet, through their conjunction, they are able to function according to what is appropriate, which constitutes the meaning of "birth. Again, he asked: "What is the meaning of death? The woman replied: "Death takes 'not dying' as the meaning of death. He asked: "How is it that death takes 'not dying' as the meaning of death? The woman said: [She continued: "The nature of all dharmas is originally non-arising. Because there is no birth, there is no death. Since there is no death, this is called 'death. This is why death takes 'not dying' as the meaning of death. He further asked: "If all dharmas are originally non-arising, how can there be birth and death? The woman replied: "It is like the empty space within a vessel. When the vessel is broken, the space is not destroyed; when the vessel is formed, the space does not arise. Birth and death are also like this. They are merely names provisionally established by the power of causes and conditions. Apart from these causes and conditions, there is no separate entity of birth and death. Therefore, although we speak of birth and death, in reality there is neither birth nor death. He again asked: "If there is no birth and death, how can one attain liberation? The woman replied: "Liberation is simply the exhaustion of delusion. Delusion has no location; it is merely a false designation. If one realizes that delusion is fundamentally non-existent, then liberation is attained. Liberation is not something to be sought externally; it is simply the cessation of the mind's grasping. If the mind does not grasp at anything, then the nature of liberation is revealed. He further asked: "If there is no liberation, who is it that attains it? The woman replied: "Who is it that asks? If you can understand this person who asks, then you will understand liberation. He asked: "How can I understand this person who asks? The woman replied: "This person who asks is originally non-existent. It is because of the deluded mind that one falsely perceives a self. If you can realize that the deluded mind is itself non-existent, then there is no one to ask and no one to answer. This is called attaining liberation. He further asked: "If there is no one to attain liberation, for whom is there suffering? The woman replied: "Suffering is the mind's own projection. It arises from the mind and returns to the mind. If you can realize that the mind is originally empty and quiescent, then suffering is extinguished. Suffering is not something external that can harm you. It is only because the mind grasps at phenomena that suffering arises. If you do not grasp, there is no suffering. He further asked: "If there is no suffering, what is the meaning of Nirvana? The woman replied: "Nirvana is the extinction of the three poisons. Greed, anger, and ignorance are originally non-existent. If one realizes that the three poisons are fundamentally empty, then there is no greed, no anger, and no ignorance. This is Nirvana. Nirvana is not a place to be reached; it is simply the mind's return to its original source. He further asked: "If there is no place to reach, how can one enter Nirvana? The woman replied: "To enter Nirvana is to enter the gate of non-duality. There is no subject who enters and no object to be entered. If you can realize that the mind is originally non-dual, then you have entered Nirvana. He further asked: "If there is no entering, how can one abide in Nirvana? The woman replied: "Abiding in Nirvana means abiding in the nature of reality. The nature of reality is eternally quiescent and unchanging. If you can abide in this quiescence without wavering, then you are abiding in Nirvana. He further asked: "If there is no abiding, how can one manifest the Buddha-way? The woman replied: "Manifesting the Buddha-way means manifesting the wisdom of the Buddhas. The wisdom of the Buddhas is the wisdom of the ordinary person. There is no difference between them. If you can realize that the ordinary mind is itself the Buddha-mind, then you have manifested the Buddha-way. He further asked: "If there is no manifestation, how can one turn the wheel of Dharma? The woman replied: "Turning the wheel of Dharma means teaching and transforming sentient beings. Sentient beings are originally non-existent; they are merely names. If you can teach and transform without grasping at the existence of sentient beings, then you are turning the wheel of Dharma. He further asked: "If there is no turning, how can one enter Parinirvana? The woman replied: "Entering Parinirvana is the ultimate extinction of all conceptualization. All conceptualization is originally empty. If you can exhaust all conceptualization, then you have entered Parinirvana. He further asked: "If there is no entering, how can one benefit others? The woman replied: "Benefiting others means responding to conditions with compassion. Compassion is originally non-existent; it is a response to the suffering of others. If you can respond to conditions with compassion without grasping at the existence of others, then you are benefiting others. He further asked: "If there is no benefiting, how can one uphold the Dharma? The woman replied: "Upholding the Dharma means upholding the true nature of all dharmas. The true nature of all dharmas is the nature of emptiness. If you can uphold this emptiness without grasping at it, then you are upholding the Dharma. He further asked: "If there is no upholding, how can one protect the Sangha? The woman replied: "Protecting the Sangha means protecting the harmony of the community. Harmony is originally non-existent; it is a provisional establishment. If you can maintain harmony without grasping at the existence of the community, then you are protecting the Sangha. He further asked: "If there is no protecting, how can one cultivate the Bodhisattva path? The woman replied: "Cultivating the Bodhisattva path means cultivating the six perfections. The six perfections are originally non-existent; they are practices performed for the sake of sentient beings. If you can practice the six perfections without grasping at the existence of sentient beings, then you are cultivating the Bodhisattva path. He further asked: "If there is no cultivation, how can one attain Buddhahood? The woman replied: "Attaining Buddhahood means realizing the nature of the mind. The nature of the mind is eternally pure and luminous. If you can realize this purity and luminosity, then you have attained Buddhahood. He further asked: "If there is no attaining, how can one save sentient beings? The woman replied: "Saving sentient beings means leading them to realize the nature of the mind. The nature of the mind is the same for all. If you can lead others to realize this sameness, then you are saving sentient beings. He further asked: "If there is no saving, how can one be called a Buddha? The woman replied: "A Buddha is one who has awakened to the truth. The truth is originally non-existent; it is simply the cessation of delusion. If you have awakened to this cessation of delusion, then you are a Buddha. He further asked: "If there is no awakening, how can one be called a Tathagata? The woman replied: "A Tathagata is one who has come from whence they came. Whence did they come? From the nature of reality. Where do they go? To the nature of reality. If you can realize that coming and going are both within the nature of reality, then you are a Tathagata. He further asked: "If there is no coming or going, how can one manifest various transformations? The woman replied: "Manifesting transformations means responding to the capacities of sentient beings. The capacities of sentient beings are infinite. If you can manifest transformations according to their capacities without being bound by them, then you are manifesting various transformations. He further asked: "If there is no manifesting, how can one preach the Dharma? The woman replied: "Preaching the Dharma means transmitting the mind-seal. The mind-seal is originally wordless. If you can transmit this wordlessness through words, then you are preaching the Dharma. He further asked: "If there is no preaching, how can one be called a teacher? The woman replied: "A teacher is one who points out the way. The way is originally non-existent; it is simply the path of liberation. If you can point out this path without grasping at it, then you are a teacher. He further asked: "If there is no pointing out, how can one be called a patriarch? The woman replied: "A patriarch is one who transmits the Dharma-eye. The Dharma-eye is originally blind. If you can transmit this blindness without losing sight of the truth, then you are a patriarch. He further asked: "If there is no transmission, how can one be called a successor? The woman replied: "A successor is one who upholds the lineage. The lineage is originally non-existent; it is simply the continuity of the Dharma. If you can uphold this continuity without grasping at it, then you are a successor. He further asked: "If there is no succession, how can one be called a disciple? The woman replied: "A disciple
