Holy Sages of Manifested Transformation.
As Śāriputra entered the city, he saw the girl Candrottarā from afar as she was leaving.
He thought to himself, "I wonder if this sister has attained *kṣānti* (receptivity) upon seeing the Buddha; I shall test her. He then asked, "Where are you going?
The girl replied, "Just as Śāriputra is going, so am I. Śāriputra said, "I am entering the city, while you are leaving the city. How can you say 'just as'?"
Śāriputra departed in such a manner. The woman asked, "Upon what should the disciples of the Buddhas rely for their dwelling?

Śāriputra replied, "They should rely upon the Great Nirvāṇa for their dwelling. The woman said, "Since they rely upon the Great Nirvāṇa for their dwelling, then I am just like Śāriputra, departing in such a manner."
Taisuī Zhe said: "One person enters the city; one person leaves the city. Why then do you say that Śāriputra went in such a manner?
If you can know the destination of these two people, then throughout the twelve periods of the day, every movement and action will be nothing other than abiding in Great Nirvāṇa.
If you do not yet know this, your karmic consciousness will be vast and茫然 (mángmáng—vast and bewildered), with no fundamental basis to rely upon. Dongchan Guan said: "Śāri..."
"Śāriputra dwells by relying on the Great Nirvāṇa; he sits within the deep pit of liberation.
If the girl Candrottarā were to go as Śāriputra does, she too would be following the heterodox and pursuing evil. Zhaojue Qin said:
"Dwelling in non-dwelling, acting in non-acting, seeing in non-seeing, and employing in non-employing—under each person’s heels, all is vast and identical to the great void."

It is like ten suns shining simultaneously; light radiates wherever they touch. If you understand it thus, then you will realize non-arising together with Candrottarā and attain the stage of non-retrogression.
Whether going, coming, or staying, there is nowhere that you are not within great liberation.
You have, at once, pierced the nostrils of all Buddhas of the three periods of time. What need is there to speak of Śāriputra “going thus”? Dharma.
Linyun said: "It is a pity that Śāriputra was so thoroughly outwitted by this woman. When she asked, 'Upon what should the disciples of the Buddhas rely for their dwelling?

he should have simply said, 'Dwell as the girl Candrottarā dwells. Would that not be like getting a person's head and returning a person's ox, or getting a person's head and returning a person's horse?"

Faintly veiled by mist, deeply locked in fog. How could Śāriputra know this path? Even if one were to crash straight into the City of Nirvana, one could not avoid being led away by him in such a manner.
The Maiden Candrottarā is truly pitiable; she loves to paint her brows with blue pigment.
(Buddha-Wisdom Spring) The original, true substance penetrates the very source; entering and exiting follow the same path through this single gate.
Having already dwelt in the Great Liberation of the Tathāgata, the supreme treasure in one’s palm illuminates heaven and earth. (Yuánwù Qín)
Meeting, they beat drums and play the lute; it must be that they are both masters of their craft.
When the song ends, one knows not where they have gone, as the setting sun slants across the evening clouds. (Shi’an Shao) The great earth is utterly free of even a speck of dust;
facing south, one looks at the Big Dipper. When the rooster is married, it flies after the rooster; when the dog is married, it runs after the dog.
(Śuexuan Jin): Once, when Śāriputra was in the room of Vimalakīrti, a heavenly maiden scattered flowers. She asked him, "Why do you not transform this female body?
He replied, "For twelve years now, I have sought the mark of a woman and have been unable to find it."

"It has been attained. What, then, could it be transformed into? At that moment, the goddess used her supernatural powers to transform Śāriputra into a goddess and herself manifested in the form of Śāriputra, asking: "Why do you not transform away this female body?
Śāriputra replied with the appearance of the goddess: "I do not know by what transformation I have been changed into a female body. The goddess said: "Śā..."
“Śāriputra, if you were able to transform this female body, then all women would likewise be able to transform theirs.
Just as Śāriputra is not a woman yet manifests in a female body, so it is with all women; though they manifest in female bodies, they are not women.
At that moment, he withdrew Śāriputra’s body, restoring it to its former state, and asked:
"Where now is the physical form and appearance of a woman? Śāriputra replied, "The physical form and appearance of a woman exists nowhere, nor does it not exist.
The goddess said, "All dharmas are likewise thus: they exist nowhere, nor do they not exist."
Baizhang Yuan said, "I am not your equal. Qingshan Xiu said, "Śāriputra had good intentions but did not receive a good reward.

Everyone says he was turned by the heavenly maiden from his female body; however, according to my own view, let us not say the heavenly maiden could turn Śāriputra alone—she could even turn all the men on this great earth into female bodies. As for oneself..."
The female body cannot remain; why? Since it has been said that for twelve years one sought the mark of a woman and could not find it at all, where did you see Śāriputra transform his female body?
Śāriputra has already perfected the seeds of the outflows; having transformed his physical form, he knows nothing at all. A single thread runs through the common path—it is no other thing.
At midnight, the barbarian monk walks through the snow and returns.
(Zhengtang Bian) Śāriputra asked Subhūti: "Is preaching the six *pāramitās* within a dream the same as when one is awake?"
This was a different matter. Ti said, "The meaning of this is profound and subtle; I am unable to explain it. There is the Great Being Maitreya in this assembly;
you should go and ask him. Pu did not go to ask Maitreya. Maitreya said, "Who is named Maitreya? Who is Maitreya?"
Xuedou Xian said: "If, at that time, he had not let him pass, but instead had pressed him further, asking, 'Who is Maitreya?
Who is the one called Maitreya? then ice would have melted and walls would have crumbled. Zhaojue Qin said:

"Whether the discourse on the six *pāramitās* in a dream is the same as or different from that when awake—lower your voices, lower your voices! This meaning is profound and subtle; I am unable [to fathom it]."
It is said: "There are thorns in the soft mud. Within this assembly is the Great Being Maitreya; you may go and ask him.
How can one argue by passing the matter off to another? Śāriputra asked Maitreya: "Taking error for error—who is named Maitreya, and who is the actual Maitreya?
His face is three inches thick. It is further said: "Do you understand thoroughly yet? A single phrase meets the occasion; myriad conditions [fall away].
[The verse] "Dormant Excision. Gunanmen said: Rising early, even before the fifth watch, there are still travelers on the night road.
The Dharma preached in dreams is no different from when awake; Marvelous function and spiritual powers do not go beyond this very source.
Who is it? What is its name? It is all Maitreya. Where the auspicious light arises, the Heart-Jewel appears. (Zhaojue Qin)
When Subhūti preached the Dharma, Śakra rained down flowers. Maitreya asked: "From where did these flowers come?
Did you obtain them from heaven, from the earth, or from among humans? Śakra replied to each that it was not so. Maitreya then asked, "Where, then, were they obtained?
Śakra raised his hand. Maitreya said, "So it is, so it is."
Yunmen Wenyan said: "When Śakra raised his hand, how was it? Were your four elements and five aggregates the same as or different from the Old Śākyamuni?
Tianning Qisong said: "A vast marsh hides mountains; a mist can subdue a leopard.
Letting Suṇṛta pass by—what has the Venerable One been using all along to preach the Dharma? He too deserves a squeeze."
Subhūti was sitting in meditative seclusion within a rocky cave when the devas rained down flowers and offered praise. Udāyin asked, "Who is it raining flowers?
And why are they offering praise? The deva replied, "I am a Brahmā deity. I revere the Venerable One for his excellent exposition of the Prajñāpāramitā.
Udāyin said, "I have never uttered a single word regarding the Prajñāpāramitā. The deva said, "It is so. The Venerable One has no teaching; I..."
This is "no hearing. That there is no speaking and no hearing is the true teaching of Prajñāpāramitā.
Xuedou Xian said: "To avoid clamor and seek a place of stillness—there has never been such a method in the world. He sat in meditative equipoise (dhyāna) within a mountain cave.
He was also defiled by that same group of fellows. Furthermore, there was an old fellow who could not hold his ground;
when asked who he was, he had already revealed his defeat. "I revere the Venerable One for his eloquent exposition of Prajñāpāramitā"—suddenly, foul water was splashed over his head.
He further said, "I have never uttered a single word regarding Prajñāpāramitā"—he is running through the weeds. The Venerable One has nothing to say.
[He] was then silent. [The Master] said, "Your consciousness is so fond of likes and dislikes; you all seem like this sort of person. Where would there be a 'today' for you?
He then summoned the assembly again, saying, "Xuedou is fortunately a man of no affairs. What do you seek by coming here?
With his staff, he drove them all away at once. Qingshan Xiu said: "Mingjue is like someone who has just plugged a leaky hole. It is empty."
Even if one strikes the bottom of Brahmā’s realm, it will not fail to strike the leak in one’s own house.
Have you ever struck it? Because King Aśoka asked Piṇḍola: “I have heard that you, Venerable One, have personally seen the Buddha; is this true?
Piṇḍola raised his hand to his eyebrows, remained silent for a long while, and then said, “Do you understand? The King said, “I do not understand. Piṇḍola said, “The Anavatapta Lake.”
The Dragon King once invited the Buddha for a meal; at that time, I was also included among his retinue.
Fengyang Zhao (Zhao of Fenyang) spoke on his behalf, saying, "On the contrary, it is you, Venerable One, who have troubled yourself. Cuoyan Zhen said, "Tell me, where did you see him?"
Even if the snow is ethereal and the lake’s light is tranquil, do not speak of dreams. Baoning Yong spoke on his behalf, saying, "Rare indeed!
Rare indeed! Yunju Yuan said on his behalf, "Wang [the King] suddenly spat right in his face.
Liangshan Yuan said, "The Great King asked with such gentleness, yet the Venerable One accepted so hastily. If one examines this closely, it is nothing short of a failure."
Pause. Where is the point of leakage? "The talent of the Guoqing is noble; the child of a wealthy family is spoiled. Huanglong Yun said:
"The Venerable One attained the great capacity and manifested the great function; he did not come in vain having personally seen the Buddha.
Nevertheless, it was thanks to King Aśoka’s letting him off. Had he not let him off, he would have ended up losing his eyebrows. Miyin Ming said: "The Venerable..."

This person has observed a single fast for King Yama and, through cultivation over many kalpas, has almost exhausted his outflows. Yet, upon encountering a yellow oriole, he needlessly uses a golden pellet;
what a pity! As the sound of the Dharma-forest emerges, the King’s voice says: "I thought the Venerable One had personally seen the Buddha."
The ancient style of the assembly on Vulture Peak has been cast off from this point onward; its momentum is inexhaustible. Before Mount Jindou, it is once again revealed:
do not mistake the *fú* plant for the Heavenly Hero. (Zhengtang’s Discernment) The Venerable One personally saw the Buddha come;
raising his eyebrows, he broke into a smile. From antiquity to the present, there is not a hair’s breadth of separation.
Agreed. Who in heaven or on earth can accompany him? (Fozhao Guang) Raising his eyebrows with his hand:
"The thousand sages have never known him from the beginning; the assembly at Vulture Peak remains as it was.
What need is there to speak of today or yesterday? (Yuelin Guan)
Raising his eyebrows, he answered the question; having personally seen the Buddha, he did not deceive. To this day, he continues to receive offerings throughout the four worlds;
spring rests upon the plum branches, cold with lingering snow. (Tiantong Jing) A single word from the Sovereign issues forth like imperial edicts;
the Venerable One’s eyebrows part in eight directions. The winds clear across the four seas, and the misty waves subside.
Tranquility. The azure sky is boundless, the waters have no shore.
(Wuzhun Shanfan) When the Venerable Aṅgulimāla had not yet left the household life, he was a non-Buddhist practitioner who followed the teachings of Kauśika.
Desiring to ascend the throne as king, Kauśika used the thumbs of a thousand people to fashion a flower crown; he had already obtained nine hundred and ninety-nine.
He was missing only one finger. He then intended to murder his mother to obtain it. The Buddha then manifested as a śramaṇa walking ahead of him.
Vīrūḍhaka released his mother and pursued the Buddha. Unable to catch up with him, he called out, "Gautama! Stop! Stop! The Buddha said, "I have long since stopped; it is you who do not stop.
Upon hearing this, Vīrūḍhaka’s mind suddenly opened to awakening. He then went forth under the Buddha and entered the monastic life.
Aṅgulimāla was fierce and bold, full of martial vigor; Gautama said, "Stop, stop! Cease this storm! To kill a man and become a Buddha—this is like pinning it to one's head.
Turning rain and overturning clouds happens in an instant.
(Shushan Ru: To seek from others is a futile toil; the fault lies in the excessive proliferation of words. Having slaughtered his entire family, he still [continues].

Kill! Who could possibly do anything to you? (From *Yeyun Nan*) When Aṅgulimālya arrived at the house of an elder carrying his alms bowl, he encountered the elder’s wife in the throes of a difficult labor.

The elder asked, "O disciple of Gautama, what dharma do you possess that can alleviate this difficulty of childbirth? Aṅgulimālya replied, "I have only recently entered the Way; I do not yet know this."
The Dharma-master said, "Wait until you have gone to ask the Buddha and returned to inform me. He then returned and reported this to the Buddha. The Buddha said, "Go quickly and tell her:
'I have followed the Dharma of the Worthy and Holy Ones since time immemorial; I have never killed a living being. Kūṭadanta received the Buddha’s words and went to announce them.
Upon hearing this, his wife gave birth immediately.
Tiantong Muan said: "The World-Honored One moved the flowers and gave them along with the butterflies; Angulimala carried the spring water back with the moon.
The parturient woman: clouds rest idly on the mountain peak. The unenlightened elder: the water flows at the bottom of the ravine. Too busy! There is an offense within the case."
The four of them have all been released according to the Vinaya. As for the infant born at the bottom, how can one argue about it?
Entrust him to the blind village elder; let him do as he pleases, whether he drills tortoises or beats tiles. Guangjiao Yu said:

"When Aṅgulimāla held his almsbowl and arrived at the gate of the elder’s house, the moon was in his hand as he cupped the water, and the fragrance filled his robes as he played with the flowers. He encountered the family in the midst of a perilous crisis."
"Gautama’s disciples—what dharma must they possess to be able to escape the perils of childbirth? This matter arose from a request for instruction. "I have only just entered the Path;

wait until I return to ask the World-Honored One. You must take care not to fall into error. Upon his return, he reported the matter to the Buddha in full detail, which was very much like feigning clarity.
"Go quickly and report: 'Since I followed the Dharma of the Worthy and Holy Ones, I have never killed a living being. A flushed face is not as good as the spoken word."
Directly. He took the words and went to inform her; it was not that he was soft or stubborn. When his wife heard this, she gave birth at that very moment; she believed half of it then.
Today, I have fully exposed the innermost heart of the ancients. Yet there remains one point of confusion that has not yet been pointed out.
Which point is it? To deliver a message and transmit words is merely the "great majority"; once one enters their realm of function, it is immediately—
Applying the paste, they simultaneously embroidered the patterns of mandarin ducks. Is it not so that the colors are grasped as they arise?

Tandu Yi said: "The World-Honored One used the wind to fan the fire; the Venerable One followed human sentiment by bending his ways. His wife was able to give birth. How many people would not have been unable to reconcile this?
Alas! The arising of things must have a beginning; the coming of honor or disgrace must reflect its cause."
Virtue has its origins in antiquity. Tianjie Minyun said: "The Elder [Śāriputra] opened up a path and set a trap, intending to ensure that no one in the world could walk upon it;
the World-Honored One released the iron gate of the Yellow River, causing all nine bends and three curves to flow backward.
But tell me, as for the portion belonging to Aṅgulimāla, what was it like? "The vast, surging waves make it difficult to send a message. From...
Instructed to dot her forehead, she stays overnight at the Dragon Gate;
the Lady Chang’er within the moon does not paint her brows. She takes only clouds and mist for her gauze robe;
unaware that her dreams have followed the blue phoenix away, she still returns home with flower branches covering her face. (Zhuan’an Gui)
Before the mountains of Huayin lies a well a hundred feet deep; within it, cold spring water pierces the bones with its chill.
Whose young daughter comes here to reflect her image? She does not look at anything else, but gazes upon the collar of her robe.
(Jingshan Gaofeng) Colorful banners and divine flags chase the morning breeze; the cock-crowers urge the drumming of the drums. The bronze ewer’s water is long-leaking—when will it end?
Rest! To urge one another thus is but to hasten old age.

(Nansou Mao) As the stars turn and the frosty wheel of time pierces the bones clear, a vast expanse of cold azure drenches the void and its spirit. A sound is passed through the empty valley, yet leaves no trace;
let the hound Han-ku bark as he will beneath the bright moon. (Baopu Lian)
Smoke and clouds seal the ancient cave, leaving the first-time visitor lost. I ask the elders of the three households: "The spring light is shared by half a lamp.
(By Xiu of Qingshan) Master Yan lies high upon the Fu-chun磯 (磯), while Master Xie hides deep within the Rose Cave. Do not say that in this vast silence there is no news.
Penetrating. A stone woman sings out from amidst the clouds in a dream. *Du!* You should know the propriety of ritual! (Fully endowed) There is ice clutching a frog;
fire flies as butterflies. Willow catkins grieve for the frost; lotus flowers cherish the sun.
Desiring the peace of the state of Yan, the Crown Prince went to Qin as a hostage. (Three are suitable for the basin.)

The ancient road across autumn cannot be traversed; for what reason does the traveler wander so solitary? A single cry from a lone wild goose in the frosty sky—vast clouds and mountains double the melancholy of my heart.
(By Buyun Fu) Eight hundred peaks join the clouds, yet the snow has not yet melted;
as the sun rises high, the trees of Qin harbor their sorrow at the distance. In one night in Chang’an, the flowers have blossomed.
All spent. The spring breeze of the second month is like a pair of scissors.
(Jie Yanxiu) Ten thousand *li* of clear light embrace a void so azure; it wells up as a single sphere of ice-cold crystal. At the end of the melody, the person on the opposite bank is gone;
only the stars remain, falling into the cold of the river. (Falin Yin’er)
The Dharma of the Sages and Worthies comes to us through non-killing; once we meet, our hearts are moved with sorrow.
Unaware that the night has deepened in the upper quarters, one becomes accustomed to hearing the tenth watch of the "South of the Dream" (Nanke).

Prince Nanda dismembered his own flesh and returned it to his mother; he dismembered his own bones and returned them to his father. Thereupon, he manifested his true body and, exercising great supernatural power, preached the Dharma for his parents.
Foyuan said: "Since the flesh has returned to the mother and the bones have returned to the father, what do you use as a body?
If a student can see into this point, they will sweep away the five aggregates and swallow up the ten directions."
The flesh and bones have all been returned to his parents; one does not know which of them is Nanda. With a single flip of the head, he turns over upon a single hair-follicle;
across ten billion hair-follicles, there is not the slightest error.
(Jingshan Gao) The original body of Prince Nanda stands firm, independent, and untainted by dust. As clouds disperse and waters flow, heaven and earth—
Pure. Between the fences, yellow leaves vie for the spring.
(Zide Hui) Bone returns to the father; flesh returns to the mother. The sun sinks in the west; the waters flow east. After a long while, he said: "Dew.
(Beijian Jian) Not relying on the womb is not yet kinship. Caoshan’s single laugh stirs up the wind and dust. Last night, from where did the jade flute come?
Awakening. Disturbing the dreamer within the deep inner chambers.
(Jue-lang Sheng) On a cool night, frost flies as heaven and earth turn autumnal; withered leaves fall, revealing the river's flow. All at once, the body is revealed within the golden wind;
when the moon sets, it cannot be sought in the clear pool. (Li-shan Ning)

The young crows cry out as the jade screens are left empty; a new coolness fills the pillow with a single breeze. Having awakened, the sounds of autumn are nowhere to be found—only moonlight amidst the fallen wutong leaves on the steps.
(The character for "screen" [屏] contains the radical for "moon" [月] and "earth" [厂].
The Seven Sage Sisters traveled together to the Śītavana charnel ground. One sister pointed to a corpse and said: "The corpse is here, but where is the person?"
At that place, one elder sister said, "What is this? What is this? The other sisters observed closely, and each attained realization.
Moved by this, Śakra devānām indra scattered flowers and said, "I pray only that you, Noble Sister, may tell me what you require; I shall provide for you for the rest of my life. The woman said:
"In my home, the four requisites and the seven treasures are all fully provided. I require only three things: first, a single rootless tree;
second, a patch of ground where neither sun nor shade exists; and third, a mountain valley that does not echo when called.
The commentary states: "I possess everything that is required; however, as for these three things, I truly have none to offer."
The woman said, "If you do not possess this, how can you understand how to save others? She then went with him to inform the Buddha.
The Buddha said, "None of my disciples understand this meaning; only the great Bodhisattvas understand this meaning."
Huanglong Xin said: "If the tree seed did not exist, how could there be a bountiful provision? Since there is a bountiful provision, the mind does not issue forth in vain.
Now, if one seeks [the fruit] while lacking the root seed, with what will one respond? Baofeng Wen said: "Did Śakra understand or not?
If he did not understand, why did he scatter flowers and request the gift? If he did understand, it is further said that 'in truth there was nothing. These three..."
"How do you clearly discern the universal substance so as not to fail the Holy Woman? Sanfeng Zang said:
"The Holy Woman was thoroughly deceived by Śakra. Fuyan Rong said: "The Seven Virtuous Women were much like buying iron and obtaining gold, or digging stone and finding jade.
While it is not that they lacked the attainment of the Way, how could one help but regret being smeared by Gautama? Song’an.
The Master said: "Three things—Śakra has long since brought them forth. It is a pity that the Seven Virtuous Ladies missed them.
The ground where neither yin nor yang exists; the mountain that does not echo when called; the rootless tree—all of you must grasp them.
O Seven Virtuous Ladies, you are too coy and foolish! You paint your brows with rouge. If the Goddess of Spring did not possess these three things, how could she have enticed the celestial flowers?"
Flying about in disorder. (Fujian Yongqin) The corpse is here, but where is the person?
A swift thunderclap splits the mountains, the wind shakes the sea. When clouds fly and rain disperses, it is the moment of meeting;
from within the eyes of the skull, radiance is emitted. (Longya Wencui)
A single stalk of a rootless tree; the mountain elder does not trouble himself with weeding or hoeing. He smashes a thousand-year-old peach pit; there is no need to climb a tree to seek fish.
(Mong’an Yue San) A single plot of ground where neither yin nor yang exists;
clearly, he buys at a high price and sells at a low. There is nowhere for a corpse to be buried alive; it is laid bare.

With three heads and two faces, it does not belong to a single mountain valley; it penetrates through a thousand gates and ten thousand doors. At the clear dawn, a single cry of the cuckoo urges people:
"It is better to go back home."
The seven treasures and eight jewels are available for your needs; yet these three things have never existed from the outset.
If you can extract them from within non-existence, there is no need to see a Buddha to ask how it is.
(Tianmu Li) An old woman east of the city was born at the same time as the Buddha, yet she did not wish to see him. Whenever she saw the Buddha coming, she would immediately turn away.

He tried to avoid it. Nevertheless, when he looked back toward the east and west, everything was entirely Buddha; he then covered his face with his hand, and even within the ten fingers of his palm, everything was entirely Buddha.
Xuedou Xian said: "Although she is but an old woman, she truly possesses the deeds of a man of honor.
Since she knows that retreating would be somewhat difficult, she cannot help but swallow her words and endure her breath. Now, if you do not wish to see the Buddha, I grant you this;

however, you must strictly avoid covering your face with your hands. Why? Because those with clear eyes are watching. Do not think that under Xuedou’s gate, I am teaching you to act like an old woman."
Vasanti. Fuyan Rong said: "The old woman did not wish to see the Buddha; her natural bearing was such that everywhere, east and west, was entirely the Buddha.
Her natural bearing was such that she perceived this: the old woman is the Buddha, and the Buddha is the old woman.
Otherwise, there would be cold and heat to shorten your lifespan, and there would be ghosts and spirits to envy your blessings. Huangbo Qi said:

She did not wish to see the Buddha; when the wind subsided and the waves grew calm, everything was the Buddha. "When the water rises, the boat floats high. But tell me, where does the old woman’s seductive charm reside?
If one does not sleep in the same bed, how can one know there is a hole in the lining of the quilt? Qinghua Yan said:
Xuedou lost one eye; he simply did not realize that his old wife still carries the scent of cosmetics.
If he sees an "Old Man with a Yellow Face," he immediately avoids him; but if he encounters mountains, rivers, and the great earth, where can he possibly go to avoid them?
"Is there anyone who can speak up for Xuedou? Wenfeng Yu said, "The old woman is far too boastful;
she does not realize that even she is merely fleeing from her own shadow under the sun."
With eyes open, it is present; with eyes closed, it is present. There is no way to avoid it. Take the wrong for the right.
A majestic qilin has but a single horn. (Uncovering the chamber:

The Sage Mother of the Eastern City sits upon a lotus pedestal; the true eye of all sentient beings in the great earth is opened. Born together with the Buddha, they yet harbor aversion toward what they see.
Buddha. It is difficult for one body to become two Tathāgatas.
(Xutang Yuyuan) In my whole life, I never wished to meet a Buddha; yet at the tips of my ten fingers, his azure countenance appears.
After wind and rain have passed over the peach blossoms along the road, where can horse hooves avoid the remaining petals? (Shishi Hui)
Palely painted brows, she dances beneath the moon; her refined charms exhausted, who can behold her?
Her jade-like countenance is desolate, tears streaming down; a single tree of pear blossoms bears spring rain.
(Falin’s Verse) The youth Sudhana went to Mount Wonderful Peak to visit the Bodhisattva Meghashri. He searched in the four directions for seven days before finally seeing him.
While walking in meditation on a distant peak, Fengri Yue said:
"I searched everywhere for it, but in the end, it could not be seen. If there is a Way, there is no seeing; this is true seeing.
Furthermore, since the Dharma-body of the Way is formless, what is there to see? To understand it in such a way takes sixty kalpas over three lifetimes."
"Not even dreamed of. [The Master] struck the desk once and said: "In this place is Maitreya;
there is no gate and no Sudhana. Song-an Zheng said: "Sudhana was actually quite close at the point where he sought him but could not see him.
Yet when they meet on the distant peak, what connection is there? To pass judgment in such a manner—thirty years from now, the various quarters will surely examine it."
The grass grows lush upon the peak of Goryeo-san; though we follow step by step, no trace remains.
If you say you have personally beheld it on another mountain, the single sail has already passed to the east of Haemun Gate.
(By Byeolsan Ji) A vast mist hangs over the lush green grass; for seven days I lingered there, but news could not pass. One step further on the tip of the staff, and I have personally stumbled.
Feet. At the sea gate, waves roll over white duckweed in the wind.
(Ji Tianxin) Vast and distant, the path through clouds and mountains reaches its end; hesitating, there is no way to find the tracks.
It is faintly like a melody just barely fit to hear, yet it is blown by the wind into another tune. (Zhanran Cheng)
Gazing at the wind and parting the grass, the path reaches its end; looking in all four directions, there is only vast emptiness. Do not be surprised that the Cloud of Virtue has nowhere to be found;
it is simply because you have arrived personally at the Wondrous High Peak. (At this moment, recite:

"When a single thought does not arise, one can behold the essence directly; yet here and now, the clouds remain ten thousand miles away. When the waves of the third level surge high, the fish transform.
Dragon: "Foolish people vainly bail out the water from a night pond" (*Daolin zhi*).
When Sudhana visited the sage Vidhura in the country of Nalasa, immeasurable sages praised him with one voice.
He descended from his seat and took [Vidhura’s] hand; Buddha-fields appeared before him, and he awakened to true, pure wisdom, attaining mastery over its expansion and contraction. He attained...
Regarding the Dharma Gate of the Invincible Banner, Shigan Fui said:
"Among the assembly, it is said that the Seer Vimaka exchanged a single black bean for Sudhana’s eyes.
Little do they know that the Seer Vimaka was thoroughly hoodwinked by Sudhana; even until now, he has been left behind."
It cannot be grasped with the hands. Is there anyone today who can act as the patron for the Seer Vimokṣa?
The ancient road is level and plain—do not wander astray. With clear moonlight and a wind of liberation, they stir the ten directions.
The events of that day between the Seer Vimokṣa and Sudhana are as fine as Pan Lang riding backward on his donkey. (Oran’s Verse)
Subhūti (Sudhana) later went before the pavilion. Maitreya snapped his fingers once, and the gates of the pavilion opened.
Once Subhūti had entered, they closed again. He saw hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of pavilions;
in each pavilion stood a Maitreya leading his retinue with a Subhūti standing before him. Maitreya snapped his fingers again and said, "Excellent!"
"O man! Such is the nature of dharmas.
Wondrous-Intent (Miao-yi), the Youthful Innocent (Dong-zhen), has finally gathered [the fruits]; Sudhana, having reached this point, has ceased his southern journey.
Suddenly and completely he enters the treasury of Vairocana; I regret visiting the mountain hermitages to see bhikṣus. (Zhang Wu-jin)
On the solitary peak of the Wondrous Summit, there is no teacher; wandering through a hundred or ten cities, Sudhana lost his way.
If the pavilions appear again at the snap of a finger, though one has clear eyes, they have never been opened.
(Oran Tiyi) The question was distinct and the answer upright; they are like two swords leaning against the cold sky. Once the gate of the pavilion is opened—
Afterwards, his face was filled with shame and embarrassment, finding no place of rest.
(Zhe-weng Yan) When Sudhana first visited Mañjuśrī and proceeded in succession until he reached the pavilion, he returned outside the City of Universal Gates wishing to have an audience with him.
Mañjuśrī extended his hand across more than a hundred *yojanas* and stroked the crown of Sudhana’s head; immediately, he beheld the atoms of dust.
Shushi knew this and immediately accepted and practiced his teaching.

Later, when Shanglan Chao asked about the reason why Sudhana, after meeting Mañjuśrī, nevertheless traveled southward, Lan replied: [The text continues with the answer: "Because he had not yet exhausted his karmic conditions. (未盡其機也)

"Learning relies on entering the inner chamber [of the master's room] to know how to penetrate all quarters," it is said. When he arrived at the city of Sumā, why did Maitreya again send him to see Mañjuśrī?
Lan said: "The Way is vast and boundless; one never meets with it exhaustively. Touzi Qing said: "Indeed, the Way has neither delusion nor enlightenment; realization is triggered by the teacher.
One does not abide in the states of sage or ordinary person, but adorns them with wondrous practice. For this reason, Mañjuśrī sent him away."

Ascending Mount Sumeru, one meets the Master by the seashore; in the marketplace, one pays homage to the Friend. Whether on the mountain of blades, in a house of debauchery, in the shackles of punishment, or within the royal palace;
whether as a young girl or boy, or as the noble Queen Gopā; with Maitreya snapping his fingers or Samantabhadra beholding him in person—having seen Mañjuśrī once more, what further need is there?
One knows for certain that those who understand the universal path realize existence; the Way is vast and boundless, its luminous traces never obscured.
Having exhausted all subtleties through exhaustive investigation, one still wonders why there is yet another person who does not investigate. After a long silence, he said:
"With a head full of white hair, he leaves the mountain valleys; at midnight, he pierces the clouds to pass through the marketplace."
The sun rises high in the sky, its light spreading above and below; the source of the Kunlun flows into the rivers and streams.
Clouds linger upon the spring mountains as the wind never ceases; geese depart for the south as heaven and earth turn autumnal.
(Touzi Qing) Fifty-three guides who point the way have wandered through over a hundred cities by habit; their straw sandals are worn through—what have they accomplished?
What can compare to returning home and putting an end to questioning the way?
(Tieshan Ren) Vast and boundless, he travels south within a dream; fifty-three encounters spring from the tips of his fingers. The Bodhisattva’s arms are long, yet the sleeves of his robe are short;
Śāriputra’s feet are thin, yet his straw sandals are wide. (Dachuan Ji)
Throughout his life, he carried his wooden board and displayed his cleverness; having finished his study session and returned home, one asks: "What is it like?
Having traversed all one hundred and ten cities, where one knows many people, there is much contention.
(Xiaowen Kan) Fifty-three men strung together on a single thread; though the child is small, his courage is like heaven's. Vast and boundless are the misty waters, without weight or measure.
Counting it, one buys the scenery for no price.
(Beijian Jian) Having traveled through the clouds and mists of the South, I have gathered rare treasures to fill my boat. With a snap of the fingers, the wind-sail reaches the shore;
In an instant, it is all turned into great coins of light. (Wuzhun Fan)
Sudhana went to the Buddha’s assembly to visit Samantabhadra. He saw him seated upon a red lotus throne atop a white elephant king;

with single-minded devotion, he drew near to pay his respects and inquire about the essentials of the Dharma. With wisdom and compassion perfected and his practices and vows fulfilled, Sudhana immediately attained the Buddha-virtue of the "Dust-like Samādhi" that manifests as identical to the ocean of fruition.
Beating the drum and playing the lute, they return to their own home. The wooden boy can clap his hands; the stone woman knows how to brew tea.
Clouds disperse to reveal the moon at the edge of the sky; spring comes and flowers bloom upon the trees. When Śāriputra has finished his pilgrimage, the black bean has not yet sprouted.
(Enkyōchū) A butcher named Kwang-ak slaughtered a thousand sheep daily. One day, he set down his butcher’s knife and said, "I am counted among the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa.
The World-Honored One said, "So it is, so it is."
Huguo Yuan said: "That butcher put down his knife at that moment and was finished. It leaves people with nothing but doubt.
He then said, 'I am counted among the thousand Buddhas,' which makes those looking on laugh to death. Dongshan Jue said:
"Nowadays, the monastic communities assume that Guang'e was a past Buddha who temporarily manifested as a butcher. For now, let us rejoice that there is no connection whatsoever."
It is said that this man who did not blink when killing people cast down his butcher’s blade and became a Buddha on the spot; yet, rejoice, there is no connection here.
Again, it is said that upon casting down the butcher’s blade he declared, "I am counted among the thousand Buddhas";
yet, how distinct this one Buddha is—rejoice, there is no connection here. Do you wish to recognize Guang'e? "The peach blossoms by the roadside after wind and rain—" Horse!
Where do the hooves avoid the remaining crimson? Tianzhang Yu said: "How magnificent is this butcher with the broad forehead!
Once this knife has entered his hands, he comes and goes with vast and sovereign ease. It is a pity he was once rendered dull by the World-Honored One;
thus he could not help but strike a blow that leaves no room for negotiation. Do you wish to recognize this butcher? His spirit and bearing are not derived from heaven or earth. He wished to—
"Do you recognize the World-Honored One? Pushing a boat downstream requires little effort. Chengshan Huiquan said:
"This butcher truly possesses the deeds of a great man. Yet, if one examines him closely, he is merely a blind donkey following the herd.
Have you not heard it said: 'A man of integrity has his own ambition to soar to the heavens; how could he walk where others have trodden?'"

In the past he was a butcher’s knife; today he is a Buddha. This morning he is a Buddha; as a Buddha, he can be a knife. Being able to be a knife and being able to be a Buddha—there is no distinction between them.
Then one beholds the white jade tuft between his eyebrows.

(Yuanwu Keqin) At the moment he laid down the butcher’s knife, even a blow from a staff could not turn him back. The clouds depart for the imperial capital; the waters return to flow through the Yangtze and Han rivers.
(Tuianxiu) Returning from a dream, she rises late; at the dressing table, she adjusts her disheveled hair and arranges her flower-ornaments.
The Consort’s jade-like countenance is truly unbearable to behold—why need one re-plant eyebrows upon the eyes? (Zhengxinxiu)
When the Mahāsattva Vasubandhu descended from the palace of Maitreya, the Mahāsattva Asaṅga asked him:
"The Sūtra states that four hundred years among humans constitute one day and night in that heaven.

During a single period, Maitreya brings five hundred billion devaputras to the realization of the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti). I wonder what Dharma he teaches. Vasubandhu replied: "He teaches only this:"
This single dharma is merely that its Sanskrit sounds are elegant and refined, causing people to delight in hearing it.
Jianfu Hui said: "Maitreya has already spoken erroneously; Vasubandhu has already transmitted erroneously.

Today, this mountain monk, following the error with the error, shall annotate and break it open for you. After a long silence, he said: "Listen attentively, listen attentively! What follows is a long text. [It is] entrusted..."
Regarding this, Yunmen Cheng said: "Vasubandhu was mistaken in applying names and phrases.
If this were the Dharma expounded in the Inner Court, it would require the further closing of the room in the kingdom of Magadha and the silencing of the mouth in the city of Vaiśālī.
Why? Because the myriad pipes have hearts but cannot hear; the solitary cliff has no ears, yet it knows the sound. Lingyan Chu said:
To follow the error with the error is not without its purpose. Jianfu’s approach is this very Dharma; even the foot of the character "Xuan" (玄) has never been moved.
What more need be said of the "long passage below"? He then held up his staff and said: "Look! Look!
This Elder of the Wooden Seat [takes] ten billion sets of four continents, ten billion Mount Sumerus, ten billion fragrant seas, and ten billion vessel-worlds..."
Within the intermediate realms, all the suns, moons, stars, and the myriad phenomena of the universe; bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, humans, devas, asuras, hell-beings, and animals;
sentient and insentient beings, those with four legs or many legs—all are melted together into a single scroll of the *Vimalaprabhāsa-sūtra*.
For you all, it shall preach day and night, burning brightly and without ceasing. Within this assembly...
"Is there anyone here who has realized the patience of the non-arising of dharmas?
If there is, come forth and receive this blow! The Brahma Viśeṣacintin said to the Devaputra Avaivartika:
"I have never seen you in this Buddha-field. The Devaputra replied: "I too have never seen myself in this field."
Tiantong Wu said: "These two fellows each demarcate their own territory and establish their own boundaries;
each remains invisible to the other, and each claims supremacy for themselves, regardless of the ugliness of those looking on. Dayu Peng said: "I have never seen you, nor have I ever seen myself.
This pair of unperforated iron hammers is difficult to penetrate through examination. Had I seen them at that time, I would have given each of them—"

For two thousand years, the Māra King Bāṣpaccheda, leading his retinue, followed the Bodhisattva Vajrasama for a thousand years, seeking the place where he arose [from meditation], but could not find it.
Suddenly, one day, he saw him and asked: "Upon what do you rely to abide? For a thousand..."
For years I have sought the place where you arise, but I could not find it. Zhi said, "I do not dwell by relying on dwelling, nor do I dwell by relying on non-dwelling; I dwell in this manner."
Fayan Yi said: "When the Demon King could not see Jingang Qi, Jingang Qi immediately followed him.
But did Jingang Qi, in turn, see the Demon King? Jingshan Hongzhi said: "Since he could not find the place where [the mind] arises, what is it that has been following him for a thousand years?
Jingang Qi speaks thus; they are mutually deceiving one another. Fayan’s critique is likewise."
"This is like looking through a hole to drive in a wedge. Is there anyone here now who knows where Miaoxi originated?
He gave a shout and said, "Why speak in your sleep? Dongchan Yue said, "Wealth and honor are easy; poverty and hardship are difficult. Empty space has no mind, yet walls have ears.
These two old fellows cannot be without fault. But tell me, where does the fault lie? The path begins from the level ground."
Dangerous! People are busy within stillness. Yunmen Xinxin said: “Jingang Qi is far too prone to leakage.
Since he does not abide in either existence or non-existence, why was he seen by the Demon King? Zifú Lùzhēng said: “For a thousand years he could not find his point of origin;
for what reason did he suddenly see it one day? Is it not because Jingang Qi leaked through?”
"Lao-mo! Is this not the King of Māras suffering from blurred vision?

A monk who had entered meditative absorption was asked by an outsider: 'The Wheel-Turning King is of the lineage of sentient beings; he is neither a Buddha nor an Arhat, yet he does not receive a future body.
What is the meaning of this? The monk remained in absorption and questioned Maitreya; once Maitreya had finished answering, the monk emerged from his concentration.
Dingyue said, "It is like a potter molding clay to form a vessel.
Fenyang Zhao’s response was: "This merely exhausts the Venerable One with his往返 (coming and going) of spiritual function.
Falin Yin said, "Why did the outsider not wait until the monk emerged from samādhi and simply say, 'This merely exhausts you, Upāsaka'? Now, thirty blows are sent to you."
If one were to compare this to the Inner Court of Tuṣita Heaven, how would one reconcile it with the monks who observe?

When the Great Being Shanhui of the Twin Trees was invited by Emperor Wu of the Liang Dynasty to lecture on the sutras, the Master ascended the seat, struck the lectern once with a ruler, and immediately descended.
The Emperor was stunned. Master Zhigong then asked, "Does Your Majesty understand? The Emperor replied:

"No. Master Zhi said. After the Great Being had finished preaching the sutra, Fenyang Wuye Shao remarked, "He preached it very well. Baizhang Fengyan said, "Both of these great beings were caught in a single indictment by Emperor Wu.
Benjue Yi said, "The Great Being was already a tangle; Master Zhi added another layer of commentary."
"Do you all wish to hear it now? After a long silence, he said: "Two different parts; they are subsumed under the preceding category. Qingshan Xiu said:
"Of these three great elders, one possessed the strategy for stabilizing the state, and another possessed the wisdom for securing the realm."
One person possessed talent beyond measure; it is a pity that Emperor Wu was unable to fully realize it. Nevertheless, sovereigns naturally possess the strategy to uphold heaven;
without moving a blade of grass or a grain of dust, they establish peace.
He did not lodge this body within the Twin Trees, but instead stirred up dust and ashes in the land of Liang.
Had he not met the Elder Zhigong at that time, he too would have been a sorrowful man departing his country.
(Xuedou Xian) How could the Great Being have ever known how to preach the sutras? Zhigong’s skillful means merely assisted him; with one sweep of the hand, everything upon the desk was gone.
Take it! You will simply cause King Liang to glare with bulging eyes.
(Baizhang Yuan) Two mouths, clearly visible, yet not a single tongue—let me decide for you whether they are born together or die together.
Nalaka eats thorns upon his crown; blood flows from beneath Vajrapāṇi’s feet. (Dongshan Kong)
One day, the Great Being saw Emperor Wu but did not rise. The ministers asked, "The Great Being sees the Emperor;
why does he not rise? The Being replied, "If the ground of Dharma were to move, all things would be unsettled."
Tianning Qi said: "From morning until evening, Shoushan has walked about countless times.
If it were the ground of the Dharma, who would dare to move even a single blade of grass? He added: "I do not speak this way;
if I did, Great Master Fu would sit there and be unable to rise. Qingshan Xiu said: "If Chu-shih speaks thus, one may rise but cannot sit; there is one who can rise."

"Come forth and meet me, you who have attained the seated state! [The Master] lets out a shout and says: "Though he possesses a pair of hands that seek the ultimate, he has never once bowed before an ordinary person.
The State of Liang causes the State of Wei to grieve; crossing the river and plunging into the water, they follow the current unseen. Although there is not an inch of ground upon which to dwell—"
Movement! Alas, how can one contend with the autumn upon half a tree in the Twin Groves?
(Touzi Qing) One day, a Great Being, wearing his patched robe, a crown, and sandals, went to have an audience with Emperor Wu. The Emperor asked, "Are you a monk?"
The scholar pointed to his crown and asked, "Is this the Way? The master pointed to his straw sandals and said, "Is this the mundane world?
The scholar then pointed to his patched robe.
Fenyang Wude said: "The Great Being possesses many abilities. Wuzu Fayan said: "It makes those looking on laugh to death. Foxin Cui said:
"If you wish to recognize the essence of the sages of the Three Teachings, look to where Emperor Wu asked his question.

If you wish to recognize the function of the sages of the Three Teachings, realize it at the point where the Great Being pointed. Even if you clearly distinguish essence from function, a patch-robed monk..."
"Your Excellency, it is far too late. Wufeng Fu said: "If Emperor Wu had been a masterful ruler, he would have immediately driven that blue-eyed barbarian out of the country.
Why? Because the laws contain explicit provisions for the investigation of strange speech and foreign attire."
Shifeng Xun said: "When Great Master Fu shook out his three hundred and sixty joints, Emperor Wu’s single word 'Ya' caused it all to melt away like ice and crumble like tiles."
Clad in tattered rags, cold as a fragment of cloud; feet in morning sandals, head crowned with a hat.
To make the three houses follow the same track—grinding sand will never form a ball.
(Xiaowen Kan) Neither Confucian, nor Daoist, nor Chan; this fabricated practice is truly pitiable. One wastes a lifetime, failing in all three.
It is finished. More than eight hundred years have passed since then. (One-Nap Jie) The Great Being composed this verse:
"Night after night, one embraces the Buddha in sleep; morning after morning, one rises together with him. Whether rising or sitting, we are always in each other’s company."
Like a form and its shadow, they are inseparable. If you wish to know where the Buddha has gone, it is simply this sound of speech.
Xuansha Shibei said, "The Great Being merely recognizes that which is bright and lucid.
Xuedou Xian, regarding the phrase "If you wish to know where the Buddha has gone," instead said, "Three lifetimes, sixty kalpas," and then added, "No monk in the world can leap out of this."
"Even for one whose mouth hangs on the wall—if they have another aperture—once they have been examined through, [the Master] strikes again.
He further said, "Xuansha was also 'beating the grass to startle the snake. Jiufeng Qin said, "The Great Being perceives difference within a single dharma."
Jiufeng was not like this: "Every night when exhausted, I sleep; every morning when awake, I rise.
Dongshan Cong said, "Jiufeng is a man of great power; his words do not issue in vain. Dongshan, however, was not like this either: "When weariness comes, I simply sleep."
Upon waking, he immediately arose. But tell me, do you monks still sleep during the day?
Even so, after thirty years, do not mix mud with water. Fachang Yu said: "Dafu Bodhisattva was like one spreading a vast net across the heavens to catch dragons and strike phoenixes;
alas, even the horned and scaled, the feathered and the winged, were all trapped within it."
There is no path. If they were truly numinous birds or extraordinary beasts, they would certainly have a separate way of life.
Baoning Yong said: "Xuansha said that the Great Master only recognized this 'bright and numinous' state. Dongshan said, 'You monks, do you still sleep during the day?
Regarding these two turns of phrase, who says there are no immortals in the world? One must believe that within the alchemical casket [there is another realm]."
There is another day. Again, he composed a verse:
When it is time to sleep, one sleeps; when it is time to rise, one rises. Washing the face, the skin becomes radiant; sipping tea, the beard is moistened.
The great ocean stirs up red dust; from level ground, waves arise. A-ha, a-he-he! Ra-li-li, ra-li!

Who possesses the melody of the Dan-yu to trade for a city of illusory silver? After a long silence, he said: "Having once suffered the bitterness of snow and frost, one is startled even by the falling of willow blossoms. (Tianyi Huai)
A pavilion every five *li*, a post station every ten *li*—the eight directions are vast and majestic;
those who come and go have no detours. Do you not see? On the road to Mount Tai, there is a straightforward old woman, accustomed to pointing out the way before others.
(Cao Yuanjin) The Great Being’s Verse: Empty-handed, yet holding a hoe; walking, yet riding a water buffalo. As people pass over the bridge, the bridge...
Flowing water does not flow.
On the sixth month’s upper *fu*, and on the mid-autumn of the eighth month, when a person is at rest they do not speak; when water is level it does not flow.
(Xinwen Ben) When a fish swims, the water becomes turbid; when a bird flies, feathers fall. The Great Being lies across [the path], yet he does not suffer from the axe or chisel. (Muan Yong)
The dog runs, shaking its muzzle; the monkey worries, raking its head. Outside the gate of Ruiyan, the water has flowed westward since ancient times.

(Duanqiao Lun) Twisted and gnarled, the withered tree has long been combed by the wind; unassailed by snow or rain, its flowers are even more red. Though the seasons do not follow it, it still forms buds.
My son, it is difficult to discuss the merit of transformation with one’s mother.
(The waters soak through; the spirit-tree has no roots, yet moss grows long upon its stones. Its dense, flourishing leaves burst forth like jade flowers. After many years, it bears a golden fruit;
without waiting for the wind to blow, its fragrance comes of itself. (The illusory clouds are employed.)

A Verse by the Great Being: Mount Sumeru is the father of the mustard seed; The mustard seed is the grandfather of Mount Sumeru. Mountains and rivers are level and plain; I strike the ice to brew tea.
It is no easy matter for Mount Sumeru to contain a mustard seed; Yet for the mustard seed to contain Mount Sumeru is as simple as nothing. The long river is churned until it becomes butter.
Curd. Gently striking through the Patriarch’s barrier. (Yuánwù Qín) The Great Being’s verse:
There is a thing prior to heaven and earth; formless, it is fundamentally still and vast. It is the lord of the myriad phenomena;
it does not wither along with the four seasons.

Wuzu Yan said: "The ancients could truly be described as 'adding flowers upon brocade'; it is indeed extraordinary. The *Bailian Qu* follows the capacities of later students and likewise provides a verse:
'Within existence there is non-existence; within non-existence there is non-existence. Within the subtle there is subtlety; within the coarse there is coarseness. Baoshou Fang said:
"'There is a thing prior to heaven and earth'—what will you use for eyes? 'Formless and fundamentally still and vast'—" [He] raised his whisk.
The Master said: "This fellow can act as the lord of the myriad phenomena. When the sun rises at the edge of heaven and the moon descends, what then?
It does not wither along with the four seasons. "You may deceive the ancient masters of past generations, but I, this mountain monk, am not like that.

There is nothing prior to heaven and earth; that which has form is fundamentally desolate. I do not act as the lord of the myriad phenomena; I constantly wither along with the four seasons. —Chengshan Jia (城山洽)
[The Master] said: "For a Great Being to advocate such a thing is to lead people to make their living inside a ghost cave.

Here it is not so: 'There is a thing prior to heaven and earth; there is no time when it is not silent and vast. It can act as the lord of the myriad phenomena, yet it also withers along with the four seasons.
Fusong woke up and said: "If I were to meet Baohua today, I would give him thirty blows of the staff, and he would never again [claim otherwise]."
Abundant. Why is this so? Have you not seen how the Way of the gentleman grows while the Way of the petty man wanes?

With faces like the earth and heads like ash, they are unstained by dust; in the flower-strewn streets and willow-lined alleys, they delight in the true nature of heaven. When the golden cock crowns at dawn, the dream of the jade tower ends;
with a single tree in bloom, there is the spring of vast kalpas. (Zu’an Jian)
There are willows hanging over the banks of West Lake in Suzhou; there are willows in Changzhou as well. In whose house are there not a few?
How shameful to face others with such grandiose talk! (In the region of Ningyuan:
An old man of Xinzhou, seeing the Venerable Buddhāpālī while he was traveling through the mountains, asked him, "Where are you going?"
Liyun said, "I am going to Mount Tai to pay homage to Mañjuśrī. Weng asked, "Great Virtue, upon returning from seeing Mañjuśrī, will you recognize him?
Liyun had no reply.
Fenyang Zhao spoke on his behalf, saying, "Today is a day of great fortune. Yunmen Cheng spoke on his behalf by performing three prostrations. "Old Man! [he added].
"If you ask further," [the Master] turned his body, pulled his staff, and departed. Falin-yin spoke on his behalf, saying: "Since childhood, Falin has consumed sweet chrysanthemums.
When the Old Man of Mount Tai asked the Venerable Buddhāpālī from where he had come, Pālī replied, "I have come from the Western Country. The Old Man said:
"Did you bring back the *Buddhōṣṇīṣavijaya Sūtra*? Dali replied, "I did not bring it back. The old man said, "What benefit is there in coming empty-handed? Dali then returned.
T'ai-yang Xuan asked, "What words could have been spoken at that time so that he might have met Mañjuśrī and avoided returning to the West?"
The Heavenly One then extended both hands as if imitating him. Falingyin said: "Amoghapāśa.
Regarding the Elder of Mount Tai (Wuzhuo), because he delighted in traveling to Wutai, the Elder led his ox to drink water and brought him inside.
He asked, "Where have you recently come from? Wuzhuo replied, "From the South. He asked, "How is the Dharma maintained in the South? He replied, "It is the Age of Dharma Decline (Mofa)."
A monk who had only slightly observed the precepts asked about the size of the assembly. The Master replied, "Sometimes three hundred, sometimes five hundred.
The monk then asked how the community was being maintained there. The Master said, "Dragons and snakes are mixed together; ordinary people and sages dwell side by side.
The monk asked again, "How many people are in the assembly? The Master said, "Three before three, and three after three."
Fenyang Shanzhao said in his place: "I know you. Xuefeng asked: "What is the meaning of 'three before, three after'?
Lingyun Qian said: "A fish in the water; a bird on the mountain. Xuefeng asked: "What does that mean? Lingyun said:
"High enough to shoot at; deep enough to fish in. Jingshan Daoyuan said in his place: "If the Master conducts the monastery in this manner..."
Truly, it is not easy. Tiantong Jie said: "The three-threes before and the three-threes after—how can one speak of this?
After a long silence, he said: "Bamboo shadows sweep the steps, yet the dust does not stir; the moon pierces the bottom of the pond, yet the water leaves no trace. Chang'ung Jing said:
"Whether three hundred or five hundred—copper coins or iron coins—it is sufficient to count to a hundred. The three-threes before and the three-threes after..."
Third: Radishes and taro are piled shallowly to fill the carrying pole. Suddenly, eyes open everywhere; one will surely clap their hands and laugh aloud.
But tell me, what is it they laugh at? Not laughing at the "bāchā" (the raw meat), they laugh at the fabrication.
Although those who laugh are still rare, if someone were to ask Tiantong how many followers he has, I would simply say: "The newly built Miaoyan Monastery is praised as number one."
All gathered together within the painted scene;
the sacred monastery extends throughout the realms of sand. Everywhere before one’s eyes, Mañjuśrī engages in conversation. Yet, beneath his words, one does not know how to open the Buddha-eye;
turning back, one sees only the verdant mountain crags. (Mingzhao Qian)
A thousand peaks winding and curling, their color like indigo; who would say that Mañjuśrī is here in conversation?
How laughable are the many followers at Qingliang—three times three before and three times three after. (By Mingjue Xian) How laughable are those three before and three after!
At the outset they spoke to one another in a babble of words, yet it was precisely because of Wuzhuo that [the truth] became clear.
I see it. From this point of cool serenity, one may enter the realm of contemplation (Foyin Yuan).

Three times three before, and three times three after—all piled at once upon the head of the carrying pole. When one arrives home and examines them closely, the bundles before one’s eyes are still all loose and hanging down.

To inform the assembly of monks, listen attentively: the boat follows the current, while the stone sinks.

(Prajñā-rū) Sitting for long becomes weary; one longs for an old friend. Meeting under the blossoms, we discuss our idle sentiments. Who would have known that the traveler’s road extends to the ends of the earth?
Far away. Having drunk the dregs of the vessel, he is still not sober. (Chen-chu-ne) Meeting on a distant road, he is but dust in one’s eyes.
Bowing his head in worship, he obscures his true nature. Rising up, he does not see the face of Mañjuśrī.
The Great Tang is shattered; there is not a single person remaining. (Xiuyan Rui)
While the Old Man was drinking tea with Wuzhuo, he picked up a glass cup and asked, "Is there such a thing as this in the South?
Wuzhuo replied, "No. The Old Man said, "What do you usually use to drink your tea? Wuzhuo was speechless.
Dongshan Jia, on behalf of [the questioner], spread out both hands. He further said: "Setting aside 'existence' and 'non-existence' for a moment, can you perceive this which is being borrowed?
Caoshan Chang, on behalf of [the questioner], said: "I have long received the Great Being’s brandishing of his sword; why then does he remain within a single speck of dust?"
Changqing Lingmo said: "A deluded guest like this advising the host. Fenyang Wude said: "Thank you for your inquiry.
Baoshou Xingyan’s new verse says: "It turns out you have never been to the South. Then he further says: "No, no."
Having branched off from the south, you have traversed many paths; at every place where you drink tea, they use glass vessels.
How is it that you have just now arrived at Qingliang Temple? When questioned, it turns out they know nothing at all.
(Zhengjue Yi) A precious glass cup is held up for you; though the flavor of the tea is rich, the dream does not awaken. Ask further: how many "threes" are there?
The assembly contends; they teach others without distinguishing victory from defeat.
(Xiang Tianqing) Gazing at Wutai, his thoughts linger on and on. Under the bright sun and clear sky, he is deluded by ghosts.
Most painful of all is this one thing difficult to comprehend: when drinking tea from a crystal cup. (Xiang Tan Yong)
As the sun was setting, Baizhang Zhi said, "I wish to stay here for one night; would that be possible? The Old Man replied, "You still have a mind of attachment;
you may not. Baizhang said, "I have no mind of attachment. The Old Man asked, "Have you received the precepts? Baizhang replied, "I have received them long ago.

white clouds fill the eyes as one lies amidst the wild grass. (Daowu Zhen)
Three by three, before and after—thank you for the Master’s guidance. Dragons and snakes leap about; tigers glare with fierce intent.
Attempting to calculate it measure by measure, what could one possibly discuss? To try to hold the reins over Juntai is in vain; how could even an elephant king withstand such trampling?
(Touzi Shu) When Wuzhuo asked the Old Man, "Is this not Mañjuśrī? the Old Man replied, "How could there be two Mañjuśrīs? Wuzhuo...

The boy pointed behind the Vajra and said, 'Look! Look! As the Master turned his head, the manifested temple vanished."
Xianyan Zhiyun said: "The boy is not practicing the samādhi of invisibility; with what face would you see him?
Though the pavilions have their names, they lack all substance. Let us ask the stubborn child about the very beginning of his creation.
Suddenly pointing at Vajra, he looks behind him; in old age, one is often mocked by ghosts. (Foyin Yuan)
The temple plaque suddenly gleams at the tip of my finger; even the Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara cannot behold it.
Since I first glimpsed the back of the Vajra, I have been carving wild characters right up until now.
(By Zhengjue Yi) With a free hand I wrote the plaque for this mountain temple; the two characters I inscribed are even more distinct. How can I bear to look back toward the high crags?
Gazing out, a single floating cloud settles into the evening.
(By Zhì of Xiányán) Suddenly entering the bend of Peach Creek, The boat returns in profound stillness. All worldly possessions have been cast adrift; Looking around, the waters stretch on and on.
The sword has long since departed; you, O fool, need no longer seek it with such urgency.
(From the *Daxi deng*) The Treasure Master Baozhi of Jinling asked a foreign monk: "I have heard that you, Venerable One, once called me a butcher."
"Have you ever seen me kill a living being? He replied, "I have. Zhi said, "There is the seeing of seeing, the seeing of non-seeing, and the seeing of neither existence nor non-existence.
If it is the seeing of seeing, that is the view of an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*). If it is the seeing of non-seeing, that is the view of a *śrāvaka*.
If it is the seeing of neither existence nor non-existence, that is the view of a non-Buddhist (*tīrthika*). I wonder, Venerable Sir, how do you see? The monk said, "You have this..."
[The question: "Is this right view?
Fenyang Zhao’s record of his response says: "Your coming from the West was not in vain. Falinyin’s record of his response says:

Tianmu Li said: "The Great and Small Zhigong both fell into error regarding the objective realm. I, this mountain monk, am not like that;
sometimes, because of a fine moon, I open the door and gaze at the peak ahead."
Master Zhigong spoke these words: "All day long they pick up incense and choose fire, yet they do not know that their own bodies are the *dharmadhātu* (the site of enlightenment).
Master Xuansha Bi added his own comment: "All day long they pick up incense and choose fire, yet they do not know what the true *dharmadhātu* actually is. Yuanjue Zhen asked:
"Regarding the words of these two venerable masters, is there any distinction between them as being intimate or distant? Xuedou Xian said:
A pair of iron hammers without holes. Zhaojue Qin said: "All day long he picks up incense and selects firewood, yet he does not know he is picking up incense and selecting firewood.
Tiantang Jue cited Master Zhigong’s words, saying: "What limit is there for these fellows who dally with their spirits?"
Citing the words of Xuansha, [Zhaozhou] said: "How extraordinary! An eighty-year-old old man enters the examination hall;
this is truly no mere child’s play. Tell me, where does the point of benefit and harm lie? Whether one has wisdom or lacks it, there is a difference of thirty li.
Baoren Xiu said: "The body is the *dharmadhātu*. Before the skull, one sees countless ghosts. If it is a true *dharmadhātu*, what prevents one from penetrating through?"
"Accepting this as the bottom line: Although it is so, when a Chu person loses an arrow, a Chu person finds it;
yet this is not as good as when a person loses an arrow and that same person finds it—this is still truly 'finding' it. The *Longchi Chuan* says: "In my old age, I have no affairs;
all day long I do nothing but handle incense and choose firewood. Gunanmen said: "Every day you all handle incense and choose firewood; do you see the Jewel?"
Even Master Zhigong had none. If you see him, you deserve a blow of the staff.
Atop the mountain of the five aggregates is the ancient Buddha hall; pick up the incense and choose the fire—this is how to take it up. Why must you seek sages and saints outside?
All day long, there is nothing that is not the site of enlightenment. (Benjue I)
The rustic style of this humble home is far beyond the ordinary. All achievements of the Great Peace are now forgotten. Where can one find that single expanse of the Imperial Wind?
Swallows dance and orioles sing as the days grow ever longer.
