The Sage of Manifestation, the Great Master Huisi of Mount Nanyue, was prompted by Master Zhigong to convey this message to him: "Why do you not go down into the mountains to teach and transform sentient beings?
Why do you merely gaze at the clouds and the Milky Way? The Master replied: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have all been swallowed by me in a single mouth."
[The Master] swallowed it all up. Where else would there be sentient beings left to teach?
On behalf of Master Ji, Wuzu Zhiyuan delivered a message, saying: "Try explaining the principle further. Baoci then pressed him, asking:
"Tell me, was that a word from the mountain top or a word from the foot of the mountain? Xuedou Xian said: "What stench of excrement is there?"
Qi. Cuiyan Zhi said, "Sida saw only the sharpness of the tip of the awl, but did not see the squareness of the chisel's head.
Tiansheng Tai said, "Sida only knew how to open his mouth; Baogong tripped right on level ground. Yunju Shun said:
Before Master Sida delivered his message, he was still slightly superior [to others]. Langye Jue said, "To test a person at the point of ultimate certainty.
Bajiao Che said, "Take another step forward," and further said, "Though it is entering the mud and entering the water, how many can grasp it?
Baoning Yong addressed Sida differently, saying, "Tell the Dharma Master to shut his dog’s mouth!"
Yunju Zhuang said, "To bury both these fellows in a single pit would not be considered excessive. Nevertheless, one must not act with such haste.
After a long silence, he said, "The clouds go toward the imperial capital; the waters flow back to the Yangtze and Han rivers.
Shilin Ze said, "One man drags through mud and water; the other folds his hands and withdraws his feet. Xu Liu, carrying only a single plank, meets with the censure of others."
He inspected them and called to the assembly, saying: "Master Baogong Sida is right now upon this mountain monk’s staff;
his eyebrows are knotted together as they manifest their spiritual powers. Do you see? He picks up a flute with no holes and, facing the wind, blows both ends at once.
Chushi Qi, acting on behalf of Master Zhizhou, further said: "He has been seen through. Longxiang Yin.
It is said: When Dashi was pressed by Master Zhi, he was driven straight back three thousand li.
Master Min of Pingyang said, "Master Zhi’s message was not a kind one. Although Dashui was a man of true substance, he could not avoid falling into his trap.
He paused for a long while and then said, "I do not concern myself with whether this is flourishing or not."
There is no matter at hand; let it be as it is, with harmonious clouds occupying Lake Dongting. Qixia Chengyun said:

"Sida sat high atop the peak of Mount Nanyue, considering himself a man of antiquity from the era of Fuxi and Huangdi. Yet, when Zhigong gave him a light squeeze, he was immediately seen flustered and scrambling.
Huangbo Qi said: "The clam and the crab-heron grapple with one another, and both fall into the hands of the fisherman. Tianmu.
The Vinaya says: "I thought there was something truly great about you;
with a single gulp, you have swallowed the Buddhas of the three periods of time. Your teeth are like sword-trees, your eyes like bells. There is no need for phoenix-glue to mend a severed string;
one only requires a connoisseur to listen with an attentive ear. (Xutang Yu)
The Buddha swallows sentient beings in a single gulp; not even a hair’s breadth remains, yet the Way persists.
When the sun and moon are just raised upon the tip of the staff, the three thousand worlds and the mountains and seas are stirred into darkness.
(By Nianlin Ying) Eyes fixed on the misty heavens, lying amidst white clouds, one knows not that there is a world beneath the mountain. From where could there be any further sentient beings?
The Buddhas of the three periods swallow it all in a single mouth.
(One Primordial Awakening) At once, Qingxiu sings a song of Great Peace. A single hair is cast into the great forge’s red furnace;
try to pick out the ashes from within, and the crimson flames already surround you. (Monguan Yue)
The Verse of the Great Being Du Shun of the Myriad Years: A cow in Huai Prefecture eats the grain; (Ciming says: "The worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.

A horse in Yizhou has a bloated belly; (Ants carry a bowl to deliver it. The whole world seeks a physician; (Donkey's head and horse's horn. To cauterize the left flank of a pig; (Painting a tiger results in a wildcat.)
Xiangtian Xian said: "This single verse is like a ten-thousand-fathom silver mountain where there is no place for you to set foot;
it is also like a cluster of thorny jujube fruits where there is no place for you to insert a needle. This old monk, not sparing a hair on his eyebrows, shall provide a commentary for each of you:
'The ox in Huai state eats the grain'—this is 'Shang Daren. 'The horse in Yizhou has a bloated belly'—this is 'Qiu Yiji.'"
The world seeks a physician; he transforms three thousand people. He cauterizes the left shoulder of a pig.

Among the seventy scholars, some say, "The Master acting thus is like washing away mud with more mud. To them he says, "You young students, your nine sons and eight daughters, Jia Zuoren—his propriety is well known."
A single rain, a single shade, yet the wind is not yet harmonious; spring is dissipated amidst this lack of joy.
The peach blossoms have already vanished into the flowing stream, leaving Master Liu to suffer much in his desolation.

(Xinwen Ben) The barbarian wife holds a three-foot jar of fermented vinegar; when the village elder hears its sourness, his face wrinkles a hundred times. It draws forth the beggar to shrug his shoulders.
Cold. It stands solemnly like a single painting by Wu Daozi. (Yangxi Sen) Flower branches and grassy vines unfold before the eyes;
Small white and long red blooms are like the cheeks of a girl from Yue. Pitifully, at the close of day, their fragrance falls away;
They marry the spring breeze without the need for a matchmaker. (Nan’an Yi)
Hanshan Baidai of Mingzhou carried a cloth bag and a mat upon a staff;
inside were contained an alms bowl, a water jar, wooden sandals, fish, rice, vegetables, meat, tiles, stones, wood, and earth. Amidst a great crowd, he shook them down and said, "Look! Look!
Then, picking each one up and showing it to the people, he asked, "What do you call this?"
Langye Jue said: "Maitreya Bodhisattva. Zhaojue Qin said: "That which is familiar is difficult to forget.
Since Maitreya is not it, and the Cloth Bag is not it, let both right and wrong be forgotten. Gold is produced in beautiful waters; the supreme treasure fills the bag."
Buying high and selling low—if you understand how to deliberate on this, there is no need for three prostrations. To explain the definitive meaning and annotate the Mahāyāna:

it is like a firefly’s glow in the moonlight or a lamp beneath the sun. With a cloth bag as a pillow, one sleeps a single slumber; leaning against the mountain, the mountain colors are layer upon layer of azure.
(By Yanxuan Zun)
It is nothing but a single cloth bag. What marvel could there be within it? When weary, it serves as a pillow;
carrying it along causes no hindrance. Sometimes opened in a bustling market, it is mostly for one’s own trade.
(Baizhang Yuanwen) Heaven cannot cover it; earth cannot bear it. It encompasses heaven and earth, all returning to the cloth bag. At the crossroads of the street—
Wide open; taking up everything as one pleases according to others' tastes.
(Lingyuan Qing) Reluctant to skillfully paint eyebrows at the dressing table, the jade hairpin is snapped in utter folly.
The innermost thoughts have been fully expressed, yet few can understand them; Only the clear breeze and bright moon know. (Shi Quji)
Pudeng was standing on a main thoroughfare. A monk asked him, "What are you doing here? The Master said, "I am waiting for someone. The monk said, "He has arrived.
The Master took a tangerine from his bosom and handed it to the monk. As the monk reached out to receive it, the Master withdrew his hand and said, "You are not that person.
On another occasion, seeing a monk walking ahead of him, the Master patted him on the back.
[The monk] went down. The Master turned his head back and said, "Bring me that one-copper coin.
Niu of Guizong spoke differently, saying, "Go back and come again. Baoshou Fang said, "This monk was indeed a man of the house;
it was only that he still lacked something. When [the Master] said, 'Wait for someone,' he should have immediately said: 'If so, then please [wait for me].'"
The Master went on ahead. If he had further offered a tangerine, one would have been well-advised to clap one's hands and laugh loudly, then shake out one’s sleeves and depart.
Xixia Cheng said: "The Cloth Bag encounters people and immediately begins to show off; if he had not obtained a tangerine," [he would have had no reason to act thus].
How many have been deceived by this monk? You are not that person. Drawing the bow after the thief has fled; picking it up and walking away, setting it down and resting.
That drowsy master of meditation—his cleverness turns into clumsiness. How could he know the intent of the Buddhas and Patriarchs?
His skirt and tunic are patched a hundred times over. Sometimes standing alone—who is there to understand him? Return home!
Ah! A single sky of bright moonlight. (Buddha-huiquan) Behold this dull Pu-tai!
His eyebrows are coarse and his eyes are large. All day long he is on the street, yet he has no goods to sell in the market.
A-he-he! Return! Pay back the debt with the principal. (Baoning Yong) Patting the back to seek money is a lapse;
turning the head and shifting the brain obscures the true mechanism. Alas, no one recognizes him in the bustling market;
empty-handed, he returns home carrying a cloth bag on his shoulder. (Fozhao Guang)
To turn one's head is already too late; it is just as it was before one turned their head at all. Having failed to find even a single coin, there is no place to turn;
yet you still labor in vain—deceiving whom? (Beijian Jian) When meeting someone, he begs for a single coin;
yet the bag in his hand contains the wealth of a rival state. It is not that his descent into this world was late; it is that he detested the Buddha and refused to become one.
(Huanxi I) Before Pudu was about to pass into *parinirvāṇa*, he sat upright on a flat rock at the eastern corridor of Yue-lin Monastery and spoke this verse:

"Maitreya is truly Maitreya, Manifesting in thousands of billions of bodies; From time to time he reveals [himself]. [Tiantong Jue comments: "He breaks through the gateway of the face. ["He strikes right at the nostrils. ["From time to time he reveals..."]
The people of the time (raised their eyes high). The people of the time all failed to recognize [him] (they avoided him face-to-face).
He passed away peacefully. Tiantong Jue said: "The stubborn布袋 (Pūgaku) blocks the streets and cuts through the alleys; there is truly no place to avoid him. Can you discern this?
'To see the cheek from behind the head—do not associate with such a person. Jingshan Ji said: "Maitreya has three hundred and sixty..."
The joints of the bones and the eighty-four thousand pores of the skin have all at once been scattered into the laps of everyone present.
Do you recognize them or not? [He] plants his staff and says: "In the heavens there is no Maitreya; on the earth there is no Maitreya. Baoshou Xin says:
"The entire great earth is a pavilion; throughout the entire dharma-realm is Maitreya. Why is it that there is recognition and non-recognition?"
"I do not know. Nevertheless, let us wait until tomorrow. Jin-su Yuan said: "This fellow has given himself away without being struck.
I, this mountain monk, have recently seen injustice on the road and wished to provide him with a thorough critique. Maitreya is truly Maitreya—do not show off so much!
To manifest a thousand or ten billion bodies—this wild fox spirit! 'Constantly revealing it to people at all times'—what a waste of effort!"

The people of that time did not recognize him at all. One must by no means suppress the noble to make them base. There was once someone who saw injustice on the road and said, "I want to question him.
As soon as he opened his mouth, Bagu Daoshi struck him over the head with his staff before he could even formulate a thought.
Next, for one and a half coins, he finds three or two pieces of copper. Who would have known that within this tattered cloth bag are many Maitreya Buddhas?
(Xiatang Yuan) That madman on the banks of the Changting River—dragging his staff, turning his head, whom is he waiting for? I tell you, that person was originally not...
In this regard, you must know that there is a time of "turning the body" (transformation).
As the Venerable Bhadra said when discussing the aggregation of subtle particles with the Dharma Master Sheng: "The subtle particles of form have no self-nature."

He asked, "What is meant by 'emptiness'? The other replied, "This merely clarifies that the emptiness of form in the cause has been attained, but it does not yet clarify the emptiness of form in the fruit.
Sheng asked, "What is the emptiness of form in the fruit? The other said, "Because a single atom is empty, many atoms are empty;
because many atoms are empty, a single atom is empty. Within the emptiness of a single atom there are no many atoms; within the emptiness of many atoms there is no single atom."
Yanguan said: "Form and emptiness in the cause, and form and emptiness in the fruit—these are all dreams within a dream.
Fenyang Zhao said: "Stop this entanglement."
Numinous light fills the eyes, crowding the mountains and rivers; within this illusory realm, phenomena abound. Having realized the wondrous essence, one knows that conditions do not obstruct;
yet clinging emotions are worn away by the objects themselves. (By Shuangquan Qiong) Form is emptiness, emptiness is form;
form is emptiness, emptiness is form. Obstructing the pass at Tongguan, the road is impassable. The kalpa-fire blazes forth, reducing even a hair-tip to nothingness.
All exhausted. The green mountains remain as before amidst the white clouds. (Tianyi Huai):
Within this majestic appearance there is no mark of emptiness; in the bright clarity of space, all forms and colors are cut off.
Directly beneath, form and emptiness are not two; the name "form" originally does not belong to me. (Lingyin Ben).
Venerable Prajñātāra said to King Vimalakīrti: "When in the womb, it is called the body; when dwelling in the world, it is called a person;
in the eye, it is called seeing; in the ear, it is called hearing; in the nose, it distinguishes fragrance; in the tongue, it engages in discourse; in the hand, it grasps."
Moving and rushing upon the feet, it manifests everywhere, encompassing the entire Dharma-realm; yet when withdrawn, it is contained within a single minute speck of dust.
Those who recognize it know it as Buddha-nature; those who do not recognize it call it the vital spirit.
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "Ultimately, what is the Buddha-nature? What is the vital spirit? Tianning Weiqing said:
"At the beginning of the letter, he tells his mother to be diligent in her rest; at the end of the letter, he tells his mother not to doze off.
Do you recognize your mother’s face? Her jade countenance is desolate, tears streaming down; a single tree of pear blossoms bears spring rain. Yingshan Yuan said: [He remained silent.]
At that time, they called it "Buddha-nature. The Venerable One’s face was already three feet thick;

yet he further spoke of its functions in eight locations, corrupting the men and women of many households. Nevertheless, compared to those who merely dabble in the spirit, his hands and feet were still somewhat superior.
Dongshan Ying took up his whisk and gave a single sweep, saying: "This is the Buddha."
"What do you call the spiritual essence? He then waved his whisk and said, "This is the spiritual essence.
"Then what do you call Buddha-nature? He waved the whisk twice in succession and said, "Do not speak of dreams before a fool. He then cast down the whisk.

Setting aside these difficulties of right and wrong, the weeds are deep and the path is blocked; taking north for south, they assume false names and usurp others' places, utterly shameless.
How much less can they endure further talk? They deceive countless foolish men and women, mistaking the saddle-bridge for the lower jaw. (Fragrant Banner Sea)

In antiquity there was a King of Diverse Views who clung to delusions and gave rise to heterodox opinions. The Venerable Prajñātāra served as his counselor to open a single thread of understanding for him:

"The Buddha-nature is like empty space, constantly manifesting through its eight gates. While glory and splendor have their periods of flourishing and decline, the Great Way undergoes no further change."
Change and non-change: Qingliang truly requires the rhinoceros fan.
(Nantang Jing) While in the womb, it becomes the body; following conditions to manifest its innate truth.
Seeing clearly the events of that time, day and night it radiates light and turns the wheel of Dharma. (Layman Liu Xingchao, Eight)
A famous man in this world, I now know him to be the body of Śākyamuni. How pitiable are those who are restless and muddled;
each and every one of them buries a priceless treasure.
What is in the eye is called seeing. Last night at the third watch, a flash of lightning struck, shattering the root of delusion until not a single thing remained; only then did I realize.
The body sits within the Palace of the Sovereign of Space;

what is heard at the ear is called "hearing. How can it be that dullness and deafness fill the universe? Who would know that when drums resound and bells ring in the night, every single one opens the gates of myriad wonders?
Discerning fragrance with the nose: one has personally smelled it within the sandalwood grove; penetrating the earth and perfuming the heavens, it is known only by oneself.
Meeting face-to-face, it is difficult to recognize. Discussing with the tongue:
through skillful means, one must open the gate of great giving. If you are a true connoisseur and the two meet, what need is there for labor?
Whether remaining silent or speaking much,
whether grasping with the hand, releasing, or clenching— everything depends on him. He laughs at the old master Pang who said in his day,
"Carrying water and hauling firewood is not what is marvelous."
Running about with feet bare, one tramples upon the grass sandals until no trace remains. I now clearly inform you:
from this point on, there shall be no returning;
once you have returned, you will attain it. A *brahmin* poem says: When the body of a *brahmin* dies, his soul meets King Yama. Having read through the books of a hundred kings...
He could not avoid being beaten and interrogated.
Fengxue Zhao said, "A single invocation of 'Namo Buddha,' and all have already attained the Way of the Buddhas. Qianyan Chang said, "This is simply a ready-made saying;
Fengxue used it at the right moment. Ji’ansi Da said, "The worldly air of the Brahmin has not been cleared away."

Fengxue has not yet escaped the burden of his one-sided board. But tell me, what excellence does Jiangshan possess? One who does not revere the Goddess of Fortune—who would begrudge the Woman of Darkness?
Zen Master Fenggan of Tiantai said to Hanshan and Shide, "Come with me; let us go tour Mount Wutai."
"You are one of my own kind. If you do not go, you are not one of my own kind. The Mountain asked, "Why would you go to travel?
The Master replied, "To pay homage to Mañjuśrī. The Mountain said, "Then you are not one of my own kind."
Cuiyan Zhi said: "This is very much like Biancai meeting Xiao Yi. Baoshou Fang said: "The manifest bestowal and the sudden withdrawal belong to him;
it was Fenggan who secretly lowered the hook and the awl. Yet, were he in the gate of a patch-robed monk, he too would have to eat a blow of the staff.
Lingxi Yu said: "Rising early in the fifth watch, there are still travelers on the night road."
When Chan Master Hanshan of Tiantai was visited by Zhaozhou, they were wandering in the mountains when they saw the tracks of an ox.
Hanshan asked the Elder, "Do you recognize this ox? Zhaozhou replied, "I do not. Hanshan pointed to the tracks and said, "These are the tracks of five hundred arhats wandering in the mountains.
Zhaozhou asked, "If they are arhats, why did you call them oxen? Hanshan replied, "Heaven! (Cangtian).
“O Blue Heaven! Zhou He laughed loudly. Shanshan asked, “What are you doing? He replied, “Blue Heaven! Blue Heaven!
Shanshan said, “This little fellow indeed possesses the strategic insight of a great man.”
Lingyan Zhu said: "Hanshan was like carving a cave in empty space;
Zhaozhou’s eye-light shatters the four worlds, yet even with all his might he could only say, 'I do not know. As for these two men, both equally crying out, 'Heaven!
Heaven!'—is there any difference between them or not? A monk cried out, "Heaven! Heaven! Lingyan said, "I recognize you."
The monk hesitated to speak. Yankuan, however, said, "Heaven! Heaven!
Hanshan, having foreseen that Guishan would come to Guoqing Temple to receive the precepts, went with Shide to Songmen to welcome him.
As soon as Guishan arrived, the two men emerged from both sides of the path and let out three roars like tigers.
Guishan stood motionless, unable to respond. Hanshan said, "Since our parting at Vulture Peak until this very day, do you still remember us?
Guishan remained silent. Shide picked up his staff and said, "Old brother, call this..."
"What does he do? Guishan again had no reply. Hanshan said, "Stop, stop! There is no need to ask.
Since his departure, he has already served as a king for three lifetimes; he has forgotten it all."

Yongning Ding said: "These two wind-whipping, madness-inducing fellows have exhausted their spiritual powers and exhausted all their wiles, yet they still cannot get out of the circle of Mount Gui. He then offered this verse:
One lift, one press—a smile for the clear breeze; the wild crane, heartless, mingles with the azure sky. Alas, how they are utterly heedless!
Yet they lean upon one another and gaze back and forth amidst the white clouds.
A poem by Hanshan says: If you know how to catch a mouse, it does not require a white cat with five spots. If you can awaken to the nature of reality, what need is there for brocade robes?
Pearls may enter a straw mat; Buddha-nature dwells in thatch huts. This whole crowd of people who grasp at appearances—none of their mental efforts will ever connect with the truth.
Sengjian said, "How wonderful! This Tiantai mountain has been defiled by that fellow.
Once, while the monks were roasting eggplants, Hanshan took an eggplant skewer and struck one monk on the back.
As the monk turned his head, Hanshan held up the skewer and asked, "What is this? The monk replied, "This madman! Hanshan—
He then turned to a monk beside him and said, "Tell me, how much salt and sauce has this monk cost me? Baofeng Wen said:
"Hanshan beat that monk; truly it was because he had cost so much salt and sauce. Is there not some other principle at work here?"
Huanglong Qing said: "Hanshan only knows how much salt and sauce that monk has spent; he does not know that he himself has scattered even more.
Where is the place where it was scattered? After a long silence, he said: "The ten directions of the world are in a state of chaos;
one day they are gathered back, and the five flavors are complete. Shilin Ze said: "A large tree is wrapped in a large hide; a small tree..."
Regarding "The Little Leather Wrapping": since the monk has already been inspected by Hanshan, Hanshan himself ought to be inspected by someone.
Chengshan Jia stepped forward and, seizing a string of eggplants, struck him, saying, "I do not even recognize an eggplant."
Hanshan said: "Red dust arises from the bottom of the well; white waves rise upon the high peak. The rock-mother gives birth to a rock-child;
turtle-hair grows inch by inch. If you wish to study Bodhi, simply look at this model."
Dongshan Cong remained silent for a long while and then said, "Do you know where he has gone? If you do not know, look!
Subhūti has entered the Sangha hall. Take care."
A verse by Hanshan says: "My mind is like the autumn moon, Its light shining brightly upon the azure pool. Nothing can be compared to it;
How am I to describe it? Baofu Quan said:
"My mind is like a lantern, Lit from within and without, glowing red. Something can indeed be compared to it; Come [and see]!"
At dawn the sun rises in the east. Lingxi Yu said: "Whether great or small, Hanshan has failed to recognize his own goods as he stepped out the door;
he deserves thirty blows with the staff.
When Shigede was sweeping the ground, the temple master asked him, "Your name is Shigede? It was because Fenggan picked you up that you returned here."
"What is your ultimate name? De put down his broom and stood with his hands joined in *añjali*. The master asked again. De picked up the broom, swept the floor, and left.
Hanshan beat his breast and cried, "Heaven! Heaven! De asked, "What are you doing? Hanshan said, "Did you not hear it said:
'When a member of the eastern family dies, the western family offers condolences'? The two of them then performed a dance.
Laughing and weeping, he departed.
Lingyan Chu said: "The abbot asked for but one name, yet Shide presented forth the clan names and personal names from throughout immeasurable kalpas all at once.
The abbot was truly one whose wondrous wisdom is perfectly luminous, yet he could not discern [the truth] beneath it. Cold.
Although Mount [Shan] has once again provided commentaries on the *Mātṛkā* (alphabet) of all arts, how many people have understood it through laughter or weeping?
Those who do not recognize their own names may well remain in doubt.
The great earth is covered in dust and never clears; I know not what dharma will bring peace. It would be better to have a broom cast from iron;
sweeping until the year of the donkey, it only becomes deeper.
(Meigu Yue) When the Great Master Zhiyi of Tiantai was reciting the Lotus Sutra on Mount Nanyue, he reached the "Chapter on the Bodhisattva Medicine King" and realized it was true.

Diligence is called the true Dharma-offering to the Tathāgata. Thereupon, he awakened to the *dharmapuṇḍarīka-āvartadhāraṇī-samādhi* and personally beheld the assembly on Vulture Peak as solemnly present and undispersed as ever.
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "Now, for those who have not yet attained the *pratyutpanna-samādhi* (revolving dharani), do you still see the assembly on Vulture Peak?
If you see it, by what do you take it as proof? If you do not see it, this is true diligence; this is called the true Dharma-offering to the Tathagata. Lingyan Zuyou said:
"Ten thousand miles of clear waves, profound stillness and immovable; the precious moon soars through the void, its light swallowing all."
When the herd of elephants is exactly like this, what do you call the *svādhiṣṭhāna-dhāraṇī-samādhi*? Suddenly, a bolt of lightning strikes;
a fierce wind rises from all four directions; clouds disperse and stars fly; the waters dry up and the moon falls. Where has the assembly on Vulture Peak gone?
If you all wish to recognize the Wise One (*Jñānin*), look at the peach blossoms by the roadside after the wind and rain—the horse’s hooves [trample them down].
Where can one avoid the fading red?
The World-Honored One rises with serene composure from samādhi; the Master awakens at the time of Bhaisajyarāja’s diligence.
On Vulture Peak, the people have not yet dispersed; were it not for Nan-yueh, who would know this? (Yang Wuwai)
Where the mountain stream ends, the evening sun slants low; Upon the river, winter winds fill the sands with snow.
This is the old road through Jiangnan; Through mist and across the water, one sees the plum blossoms.
(Luoyue Ying) Exhausting all family wealth and personal riches, One offers only the True Dharma to the Tathāgata. The path of former times—where is it now?
Standing here, wherever the eye falls, the Spirit Mountain (Ling Shan) rises in verdant mounds.
(Tianmu Li) One should offer the True Dharma to the Tathāgata. Flowers bloom in secluded crags and perilous places;
one night a wild wind blows them nearly all away, and countless fallen petals dot the moss. (Xutang Yu)
The *Fahua zhi* states that when Prime Minister Lü Xugong asked the Great Being about the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma, the Master replied:
"Originally there is not a single thing; a single flavor, however, becomes true."
Zifu Yu said: "Since there is not a single thing, what 'one flavor' could possibly be taken as real? This [view] may indeed deceive the public regarding the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma.
If anyone asks Zifu about the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma, I would say: 'From the beginning, every single thing is already manifest;
do not take this one flavor to be the truth. Sanmei Zhen said: 'To recognize one flavor is to fall into delusion.'"
Regarding "inside the pit": if you do not recognize even a single flavor, you fall into the pit at Zifu. Recognizing it is [the way]; not recognizing it is [the way].
Zhi said that when King Jixian questioned him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
the Master replied: "Within the shadows of the green mountains, a surge of azure rises; the precious pagoda chants aloud, shaking the morning breeze. Zhi then said, "Please have Fahua burn [this]."
[The Master] incenses [the altar]. The Master says: "Do not seek it from the precepts; do not seek it from the Buddha. Jiang Tianquan says:
"Both guest and host have fallen into error. [Jiang] waits for a clarification, saying: "Please burn incense. [The Master] does not answer, saying:
"Do you still want to seek a second offering? [Jiang] waits for Zhiyan to say: "Do not seek it from the precepts; do not seek it from the Buddha..."

He continued to press him. Why did he not answer? That old fellow who was previously so full of doubt—should anyone now ask about the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, I would strike them thirty times across the back with my staff. As for those who requested incense, today I let them go. And why? Because...

"Compassion for the wounded tortoise and leniency toward the soft-shelled turtle both depend entirely on oneself. Chan Master Zhenzhe said: "If Wang Zhi had simply covered his ears and walked out at that time, would you say he approved of it or not?

He then offered this verse: The tortoise was wounded, yet the turtle was spared; Both stem from what is within me. If Wang Zhi had then covered his ears and departed, Would you say he approved of it, or did he not?
A traveler in the southland, night after night, asks for a boat home. In a dream, a single "a" sound; pushing the oars, he crosses to the other side.
The mountain’s reflection was never seen by the eyes; The chanting of the pagoda was never heard by the ears. If you understand this, there is no need to create further interpretations.
On the tip of a single hair, realize the absolute truth. (Four: Sailing the Seas)
Zhiyan asked because he had been questioned by Xu Yue, the Assistant Instructor at the National Academy, regarding the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West.
The Master said, "The one on the eastern side of the street. Zhiyan said, "I do not yet understand. The Master said, "Three kinds of people do not understand."
Donglian Yong said: "At that time, Xu Yue waited at the eastern side of the street; he performed a prostration and then departed.
Not only did he act as a clever practitioner, but he also spared Zhiyan from a second ladle of foul water. Puming Yu said:
"Is 'the eastern side of the street' the meaning of the West [coming from India] or not? If it is, why are there three types of people?"
"No. Xu Yue did not advance further and said, "Old man, you speak too much. He watched to see what further tricks Zhiyan would perform.
Because a monk asked Zhiyan, "Does the Buddha exist in this world? the Master said, "Wen-shu is here in the temple."
Zifu Yu said: "The earthworm has passed through your eyes; the frog has leaped into your skull.
You cannot avoid it, nor can you approach it. Only Mañjuśrī in the temple is absent. Sanmei Zhen said: [He is present.]
The eyes have been pierced through; the skull has been shattered through. Since there is nothing to avoid, nor anything to approach, tell me:
does Mañjuśrī still exist within the monastery?
Zhuyan asked, "Is the Master an ordinary person or a sage? The Master then raised his hand and said, "I do not dwell here.
Luan Yuan remarked, "'I do not dwell here'—Zhuyan was off by a hair's breadth. Why did he pointlessly raise his hand? I..."
In this place, one washes the cap-sash in clarity and washes the feet in turbidity; one laughs at the refined elegance of the boy. I do not dwell here;
"saint" and "ordinary" are but redundant words. Deep in the forest, the autumn night is cold; leaves fall, their sound like rain.
(厂阿[蠢-春+者]) Once, while the First Patriarch of the Western Heaven,
Venerable Kāśyapa, was treading mud, a novice monk asked the Patriarch: "How can you do this yourself?"
Wuzu said, "If I do not act for him, who will act for me?
Fayen Yi said, "Had I seen him at that time, I would have dragged him away to tread in the mud.
Wuzu Jie said, "Kāśyapa and the śrāmaṇera spoke the truth well. Dongshan Jia said, "Do you want some tea? Baofu [said], "..."
Ningyong said: "Even so, bystanders will laugh. Xishan Yin said: "The Great and Small Honored Ones are extremely skilled at mixing mud and water."
Kāśyapa was once asked by a non-Buddhist practitioner, "What is this 'self of the self'? The Patriarch said, "The one who seeks the self is your self.
[The practitioner] said, "This is my self of the self; where is your self? The Patriarch said, "You ask me while you yourself seek it."
Muzhi Cheng said: "The Great and Small Venerables only know how to pelt sparrows on the ground; they cannot look up and shoot a vulture from the sky.
When [the student] asked, "What is 'this'? [Muzhi] struck him with his staff as he spoke. When [the student] asked, "Where is my self? [Muzhi] likewise struck him with his staff as he spoke.
Not only did he pull out the seeds of his wrong views accumulated over kalpas, but one can also see the function employed under our Ancestor’s gate.
The circumstances were different.
The Second Patriarch, Venerable Ānanda, asked Kāśyapa, "Elder brother, apart from the golden-brocade *kāṣāya* robe that the World-Honored One transmitted to you, what else did he transmit?
Kāśyapa called out, "Ānanda! The Patriarch responded, "Yes. Kāśyapa said, "Throw the door open! (or, "Turn the door upside down! and passed away.
It was previously hung upon the banner-pole.
Fenyang Zhao said, "Without asking, how could one know? Wuzu Ji said, "Exposed. Cuiyan Zhi said, "A thousand-year-old tree without a shadow;
a bottomless boot of the present age. Letan Qing said, "Before the banner-pole has even fallen, [he] has already pierced through it."
The skulls of all people have been exchanged for their own eyes. Once the flagpole has fallen, where will you see the Old Śākyamuni?
Yunju Zhuang said: "If you understand it before the flagpole falls, you bury the ancestral tradition.
If you understand it after the flagpole has fallen, you betray yourself. Now tell me: apart from the golden threads, what else is there ultimately?"
What was transmitted? A three-faced wildcat treads upon the moon; a two-headed white ox grasps smoke in its hands. Han Yue Zang said:
"As for what the World-Honored One transmitted—tell me, was it outside the golden brocade *kāṣāya*, or inside the golden brocade *kāṣāya*? *Psh!*
Beyond the golden robe, what transmission remains? Overturn the old monastery pole before the gate. Do not take its acquisition as a supreme omen;
For hundreds or thousands of years hence, let it be shown to others. (Cao Tang Qing) Flowers and leaves join in their fragrance;
there is surely a time for this. Kāśyapa resisted the summons and divided the robes. Now, do not inquire about that time.
Matters: "The traveler on the road has his mouth as a monument" (Zhengjue Yi).
Raising the golden robe, he topples the banner-pole; at every step, he treads upon green waters and blue mountains (Min Gufo).
At the gate of Nanda, he topples the banner-pole; beyond the transmission of the golden robe, what else is there to transmit? A natural outsider, a teacherless one.
Realization. Alas, how can one compete with the time before Vipaśyin Buddha?
(Zhang Wujin) Only when mind and mind illuminate each other do they truly know one another; the golden-colored dhūta distinguishes right from wrong.
Viewing the five-li signpost from outside the city walls, if the person present refuses to acknowledge it, whom else can one blame? (Daochangru)
Upon the lapis lazuli hall, he bestowed the golden robe; the fragrant blossoms of the *dì* and *è* joined in excellence, a rare occurrence of two.
The flagpole outside the gate was cast down, sparing those in the north and south from questioning the wind and the banner.

(Shàngfāng Yì) Beyond the transmission of the golden robe, what else is transmitted? It is reported that the flagpole has been toppled before the gate. How laughable, the people trampling the greens! Their clothes are stained with mud.
Intoxicated. The peach and plum trees fill the valley, yet they speak not of themselves.
(Shijiaming) Two thousand years since the Tathāgata’s secret entrustment, all that has been personally received has become nothing but a wave of rumors.
Until now it has remained a mere public proclamation; the bannerpole still leans against the gate as before. (Da Hong’en)
Casually indulging in idle talk about the golden robe, one immediately topples the flagpole right before one’s face.
From this point on, the natural order of kinship turns meaningless; its cold radiance still chills those who approach it.
(Xiatang Yuan) The younger brother responds to the elder’s call, yet the image cannot be painted. Who would be willing to travel within? Since the house was broken and the people gone...
Later, until the present day, matters have further evolved. (Moon Forest Guan): The plumage of the kingfisher, the horns of the qilin;
brother responds as elder calls younger, shaking the seas and mountains. When the road is far and the night long, do not carry a torch;
topple the monastery banner pole right before the gate. (High Plateau Spring)
Wild shops and mountain bridges follow the horse’s hooves; as one travels on and on, the peach and plum trees naturally form a path.
Who would have known that beyond the willows drooping over the ancient bank, there is yet another spring breeze dancing amidst the azure heights?
(Zundao Qi) The Third Patriarch, Śaṇavāsa, asked Venerable Guptaka, "How old are you? He replied, "I am ten years old."
7. The Patriarch asked, "Is your body seventeen and your nature seventeen? He replied, "Master, your hair has turned white;

is it the hair that has turned white, or is it the mind that has turned white? The Patriarch said, "My hair alone has turned white; my mind has not. [The monk] said, "My body is seventeen, but my nature is not seventeen."
Tiantong Wu said: "The great and small patriarchs split the discourse into two pieces. Jiang Tianquan said:

"Since the Third Patriarch was already skilled at analysis, Guṇamati’s analysis was even more skillful. If this were my land, they would only have the lot of being masters of the Dharma or their slaves."
In the empty forest, the cold moon; over the blue waters, the cool clouds. Beneath the crags, a pure breeze; a single stream of autumnal sounds.
(Zha) The Fourth Patriarch Upagupta went to visit an elderly bhikṣuṇī. As soon as he entered the gate, he accidentally broke her alms bowl.
The nun said, "When the Buddha was in the world, the group of six bhikṣus were extremely coarse in their conduct. When they came to me..."
"Even a layperson would not act like this. How can a Venerable One who succeeds to the Patriarchal seat engage in such coarse behavior? The Patriarch remained silent.
Fenyang Zhao spoke on his behalf, saying, "I already knew it was an error. Falinyin said, "If even the Patriarch was like this, how much more so in these present times? He then laughed heartily.
When the Fourth Patriarch asked the Fifth Patriarch, Tiṭṭhaka, "Do you leave home for the sake of the body, or do you leave home for the sake of the mind?
he replied, "As for leaving home, it is to be without self and without the notion of self; therefore, the mind is neither born nor extinguished.
That the mind is neither born nor extinguished is the eternal Way; thus, all Buddhas are also eternal. The mind has no form or appearance, and its essence is likewise so. The Patriarch said, "You..."
"When one attains great enlightenment and the self-mind becomes luminous, one saves sentient beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges within the Buddha-dharma.
Bacao Che said, "For example, although lutes, zithers, and harps possess exquisite sounds, if there are no skilled fingers, they can never produce them."

The Seventh Patriarch, Venerable Vasumitra, was once requested by Buddhadasa to engage in a formal debate on doctrine. The Patriarch said, "O Benevolent One, where there is debate, there is no true meaning;
where there is true meaning, there is no debate. If you intend to debate for the sake of meaning, it will ultimately not be a discussion of true meaning.
Buddhadasa, realizing that the Patriarch’s principle was superior, submitted with sincere reverence.
"Samādhi True Cloud" says: "If one were to claim that meaning is superior in this manner, then everyone in the Eastern Land could become a patriarch.
I wonder if even Buddha would have been moved to admiration? Meiche Xing said: "Although the Seventh Patriarch did not engage in doctrinal debate, he could not help but move his lips.
That Nanquan deeply understood and was moved to admiration was also merely seeking it upon the tip of another's tongue."
It is clear.
The ninth patriarch, Buddhamitra, spoke in verse: "Neither my parents are my kin; who is the most intimate kin?
Neither the Buddhas are my path; who is the supreme path?"
Yun’gai’s original saying was: “My parents are not my kin; there is no one who is not my kin. The Buddhas are not my Way;
there is no one who is not my Way. The Patriarch attained the first phrase; Yun’gai attained the second phrase.
If someone can add a third phrase, I will grant them a place of equal authority, a three-way division of power. Mianjie said: “My parents are not my kin—[in] the eye...”
Severing all subtle dust, the Buddhas are not my path; even iron eyes and copper pupils cannot see through it.
Your words are intimate with the mind—like a mosquito biting an iron nail. Your practice merges with the Way—pervading above, below, and in the four directions.
To repay this profound kindness, I shall simply speak these words: "Blooming red lotuses emerge from within the fire. Fulong Chang said: "Parents are not my..."
"Parents are not my kin; that which is not my kin is the Buddhas. The Buddhas are not my Way; the Way is also not mine.
The Patriarch could not attain the first phrase; Yun-gai could not attain the second phrase.

Even if one’s body were crushed into a thousand peaks like fine dust, how could it stop at merely having one's head split into seven pieces? Huiyun Guang said: "Parents are not my kin"—this is the most intimate kinship.
"Those Buddhas are not my Way; this is the ultimate Way. The Patriarch attained the first half of the sentence, and Dong'an attained the second half.
Is there anyone who can utter the complete sentence? [He] then gave a shout.
The place of vision is solitary and perilous; the ground one stands upon is high. Urgent as a spark from flint, sharp as a blade. Arriving at the house, one asks for the way: "Where is the house?
He overturns the chessboard and casts off his robe. (Xiatang Yuan) For half a lifetime his feet never touched the ground;
he knew he had traversed the ends of the earth. Having obtained the seal of the winter melon, it remains to this day.
Staring with wide eyes and mouth agape.
(Songyuan Yue) If parents are not one's kin, who then is kin? Two eyes shining brightly, framed by two eyebrows.
Unrecognized atop the Han-yuan Hall—this is precisely the moment of meeting at Mount Min and Mount Emei. (Shixi Yue)

When parents are not kin, who is most kin? The Chang Jiang rolls on, its waves like silver. A single sail hoisted high beyond the misty waves— Only then does one believe that纵横 (zōnghéng, "transverse and longitudinal") is not the mundane dust. even if you were to open your eyes with prideful spirit, how could that compare to not being deceived by the Old Barbarian? (Jingshan Gao)
Without waiting for the seven-point interrogation, one sees nothingness immediately. A monkey swings on a swing over the water;
the Prince of Silla shoots a single arrow. Keep your eyes wide open and see clearly: it pierces through the face of the Persian. (Shiming) The Second Patriarch, for no reason, went to Shaolin;
he stood in the snow before the courtyard until it reached his waist. Even if you were to find the "mind that is not," [it would be of no use].
There is. Yet one has not escaped having one’s entire body submerged in the mud.
(Shuan-an Yan) To bend one’s will and follow the superior is truly difficult; amidst the snow, he severed his arm, gazing up at the lofty cold.
When the iron ox is whipped into motion beneath Xiong Peak, a single draught dries the Yellow River to its very bottom. (Huo-an Ti)
Dharma sat facing the wall for nine years; amidst the deep snow, he found one. He found one.
The myriad phenomena of the universe were split asunder. (Nirvāṇa is total non-attachment.
In the deep night of Chang’an, the snow falls vast and white; seeking peace of mind, one becomes all the more restless. Even if one opens the living path before words—
Eyes! How could you know you have already been deceived by that old barbarian?
(Xian-an Guan) From level ground, a heap of bones rises without cause; one carries their living body to be buried in the snow.
Even if you were to find the Dharma for settling the mind, bring me back my mother-born arm! (Yin-shan Can)
Seeking the mind, one finds no trace; recognizing the time, it is the ordinary. From this point on, there is no need for idle days;
when spring comes, the accumulated snow melts of its own accord.
(Lingsou Yuan) A night of golden wind hastens one toward old age; it blows down the wutong leaves—whom shall they leave to sweep? Suddenly, they fly upon Wuyulu Peak.
Feng. The Persian picks it up and treats it as a treasure.

(Huimen Sheng) The Third Patriarch, Master Sengcan, asked the Second Patriarch: "I, your disciple, am afflicted by a chronic wind ailment; I pray that you, Master, will absolve my transgressions. The Patriarch said:

"Bring forth your transgressions so that I may absolve them for you. The Master replied: "I have searched for my transgressions, but they are utterly unobtainable. The Patriarch said: [They are unobtainable].

"I have finished confessing my transgressions with you. You should now abide in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. The Master said, "Now that I have seen the Upādhyāya, I already know what the Sangha is.
But I do not yet understand what is meant by 'Buddha' and 'Dharma. The Patriarch said, "This very mind is the Buddha;

this very mind is the Dharma. Buddha and Dharma are non-dual; the Jewel of the Sangha is likewise so. The Master said, "Only today do I realize that the nature of transgression exists neither within nor without."
In the interim, it is just like the mind itself; the Buddha-dharma is non-dual.
The Patriarch [Baizhang] held him in high esteem. Langye Huijue said: "He still lacks the ability to say, 'What is this so-called Dharma? and 'Where does the Brahman reside?

Liangshan Guan, at the point where one seeks after transgression and finds it utterly unobtainable, asked: "Where has the nature of transgression gone? He further said: "Not only the nature of transgression, but even the seeker..."
Nor does he see anything existing. Yunju Qi said: "The Second Patriarch deeply esteemed him. Did he approve of his understanding of the Buddha-dharma?
Or did he approve of his exposition of principles?"
The offenses have no root; the nature is already empty. Where the wind of arising should blow, no wind arises.
To this day, the waters of the mountains and valleys flow as a single stream into the sea.
(In the Buddha-land, white) the flute without holes and the felt clappers—though the five notes and six scales are all-pervasive, people of this age do not recognize the yellow scroll.
Chuo laughed and said, "I am ascending the precious hall.
(Wuzu Yan) "Wind-illness entangles my body; I seek the offense but cannot find it. Nine myriad miles of journey, spreading wings that touch the clouds.
(Min Gufo) "The whole body itching with a foul odor, I beg someone to scratch me. Scratching deep into the bones, the body is already weary. Suddenly, he scratches right where it hurts."
It is finished. The itchy spots of a lifetime are all at once eliminated.
(Shui’an Yi) Transgressions as vast as the heavens have no door for repentance; red and raw, they permeate one’s life and cannot be cured. Already, all four corners have been stepped upon;
let future generations do as they please with their needles and awls. (Wumen Kai)

A wind-illness entangles his body and life, beyond the reach of medicine; poverty-stricken, he suffers robbery—how truly pitiable. Who would have known that when seeking the source of the crime, there is nowhere to be found?
This is precisely the moment the thief returns to an empty house.

(Great Rest and Humility) His entire being is illness, bone adhering to skin; throughout the world, no one recognizes him. Even if one were to repent for every root of transgression, [it would be in vain].
Understood. Yet, one still loses both eyebrows. (Chijue Chong) Ten thousand miles the sky opens, a gale blows;
clouds push the moon’s carriage forth, shrouded in mist. Deep autumn, deep river—what clear shadows!
Dewdrops fall upon the lotuses, red on both banks. (Wuyi Lai)

The Third Patriarch’s *Inscription on Faith in Mind* says: "The ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes discrimination. Simply do not harbor hatred or attachment, and all will be transparently clear.
Baoen Xiu said: "When the Patriarch spoke the word 'dislikes,' he had already fallen into hatred and attachment himself. Yet he then said, 'Simply do not...'"
"Hatred and love are transparently clear and manifest; how could this be anything less than raising one's voice in an attempt to stop an echo?
Deshan Huibian said, "The Ultimate Way is most difficult; it requires discernment. If there were no hatred or love, how could clarity be seen?
Fochuan Yiyun said, "The Patriarch has opened up the eight characters and handed them over with both hands. Nevertheless, the direct approach is indeed so."
Direct and straightforward! Yet how extremely paradoxical it is. I, this mountain monk, shall provide you with another path: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes picking and choosing.
Simply do not harbor likes or dislikes, and it will be transparently clear. After a long silence, he said: "Investigate! (Chán).
The Third Patriarch said: "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth.
When you have ascended the peak, your footsteps are wide; when you find a place to linger, linger there.
Where the pine forest is lush and reflects the crimson clouds, to raise your eyes and seek it out is to be deceived. (Cloud Pines Chapter)
Since coming forth, he has trailed his staff beyond a thousand peaks; who recognizes that this dappled beast is a tiger? Grasping the sound of pines, it finds no place of attachment;
with the breeze, it blows through the crimson blossoms of the emerald peach trees.
(Moon, Cliff, Screen) The Third Patriarch said: "Two arise from one; do not even cling to the one. When the one mind does not arise, the myriad dharmas are without fault."
Yuan Jieying suddenly picked up his staff and said, "The Third Patriarch Master has arrived!
By means of the Samādhi of Non-attachment and the Samādhi of the Seal of Wisdom, he moves Mount Sumeru into the eye of a mustard seed.
Seeing that you people do not understand, he transforms into the Samādhi of Vigorous Display, pierces through your nostrils and eyes, and runs inside the pillar. He struck the ground with the staff.
The Third Patriarch said, "The six sense-objects are not evil; they are identical to perfect enlightenment.
Xuedou Xian said, "This staff is a sense-object. What fault is there? Since there is no fault, you ought to distinguish the host."
Thus it is said: "Upon a heap of refuse appears the sixteen-foot golden body. Set that aside for a moment. "On the bare flesh-ball, one stands ten thousand fathoms high.
This too is letting pass another point. Even if they come from the eight directions and the four quarters, it is exactly right to strike them down with a single blow.
Gunan said: "Although Xuedou’s staff is well able to act as the master for the Patriarchs,"
For now, you have not yet even touched the ground with your heels.
The Fourth Patriarch Daoyin, the Great Master Physician, visited the Third Patriarch and asked, "I pray that the Honored One will, out of compassion, grant me the Dharma-gate of liberation.
The Patriarch said, "Who has bound you? The Master replied, "No one has bound me. The Patriarch said, "Why then do you seek it further?"
"Are you liberated? The Master attained great enlightenment.

Before Niu-t'ou was born, the plum had already ripened. He strolled leisurely among men; the pond was formed beneath the moon. Though the imperial summons arrived three times, he lazily kept his eyes closed;
at the peak of White Lotus, the light rays intermingled. (Yun-yen, because of this).
Who binds? There is no one to bind. Why then seek further liberation? It is not necessarily the geese of Right Army (Wang Xizhi) that are the cranes of Master Zhi.
(Shitada Kō) The Fourth Patriarch resided at Mount Pòtóu in Qí Prefecture; disciples gathered like clouds. He restrained his mind and did not sleep, so that his ribs never touched the mat.
One day, while seated, he addressed the assembly, saying: "During the Wude era, I traveled to Mount Lu.
Looking toward Mount Poutou, I saw purple clouds like a canopy, with white vapors dividing crosswise into six paths. Do you understand?
Hongren said, "Is this not the Dharma that the Master will later bring forth as a separate branch? The Master said, "Excellent. Emperor Taizong of the Tang dynasty had long admired the Master.
The Way. Though summoned three times, he did not go. He was granted purple robes. The stupa of Ciyun;
the master of great medicine. One gazes up at him in reverence; the two peaks stand towering high. Lazy Rong could not obtain the almsbowl from the Western Heaven;
it was bestowed directly upon the child on the road to Huangmei. (Yang Wuwai)
Seeking a teacher beyond the islands, he returned having untied his bonds; beneath the Double Peaks, he was uniquely secluded and extraordinary.
He then took his robe and bowl as a matter of human courtesy, begging them from a young child at Huangmei.
(Foguo Bai said: "The notoriety of one's fame is known to obstruct the Way; I fear that even a formal lineage may burden a person. Do not be sparing with the novice who asks for the Dharma."
The tongue: A hundred-year journey as a guest must share the same dust.
(Juefan Hong) Firmly declining the purple-clay edict from the Phoenix Palace, this ancient hammer brings disgrace to the ancestral wind.
Sitting firmly at the twin peaks where not a blade of grass grows, he kept the pine branches that obstruct others out of affection. (Wumen Kai)
Purple clouds fly over the peak of Pòtóu; three times he declined the celestial decree, aging in the azure mists.
Though this滞貨 (stale merchandise) has no practical use, it should not be handed over to a small child.
(Mù of Shàoshì) Having attained freedom from the deep pit of liberation, he brandishes his staff alone, flaunting his elegance. Unwarrantedly, he brings trouble upon the one who planted the pine.
Old age. The consciousness of karma is vast and boundless, refusing to rest.
(Nuonan Zhao) Beneath Mount Poutou, he seeks a shortcut; he entices the children on the Huangmei road.
Again he travels south to visit Niushou Peak, deceiving the flowers and birds into losing all hope of his return. (Dianniu You)
The Fourth Patriarch presented the Fifth Patriarch with this verse: "The nature of the lotus seed exists; Depending on the ground, the lotus is born.
When the great condition unites with this nature, Birth after birth, it is non-birth."
This minor messenger was born with a majestic bearing; his nature is empty, extinguishing both the internal and external—the True Doctrine.
The Patriarch Pòtóu personally encountered him, fanning up the Vairambha wind that covers the earth.
(Mò'ān Huì) When the Fifth Patriarch, Master Hóngrěn, was planting pine trees on the Western Mountain in Qízhōu, the Fourth Patriarch said: "I wish to transmit [the Dharma]..."
"I give this Dharma to you. You have already reached old age; if you were to come again, I would still be too late for you. The Master then went to be born into the Zhou family.
When he was seven years old, he met the Patriarch at Huangmei. The Patriarch asked, "What is your surname?
The Master replied, "I do have a surname, but it is not an ordinary surname. The Patriarch asked, "What surname is it? The Master replied, "It is Buddha-nature. The Patriarch said, "You have none."
"What is your surname? The Master said, "Because its nature is empty, it has none.
"How old are you for planting pine trees? How young are you for transmitting the robe? The former body and the latter body are one dream and two awakenings.
White lotuses bloom atop the mountain peak; the bright moon shines coldly for a thousand years. (Yang Woei II)

Rising at dawn, they go forth to work; planting pines is their delight. How many were planted in the past? Now they fill the crags and valleys. The white-haired man has gone and the young children return;
they bring laughter to the thousand-year-old cranes upon the treetops.
Long, white hair hangs down as he descends the green mountains; Returning after seven years, his former countenance has changed. The man has become young again, yet the pine trees are already old;
From this point on, right and wrong shall fall back into the world of men.

(Buddhist Country’s Bai) Who is the prior incarnation? Who is the subsequent one? In vain do you compare names for their novelty or antiquity. Do not ask the neighbor about where they have gone or come from.
The matter: "I am that person of old, yet not that person of old.
(Zu Yinming) The fruit ripens at Huangmei; the white lotus blooms. When asked about Buddha-nature alone, its essence differs from the ordinary womb.
The robe is passed to one who departs for the Southern Ridge; the pines grow old on the Western Mountain as I return. What purpose is served by these two borrowed skin-bags? A single flask of wind.
The moon is limpid and free of dust.
(Tiantong Jue) Planting pine trees that fill the mountains; turning over in the dark. Although he obtained the robe of faith, when has he ever known his father’s face?
(Shitoku Kaoru) For many years his livelihood has been by the spade; ten thousand pines lock in the azure mist. The dream is shattered at Caoxi—the world is vast;
returning again, he is not worth half a coin. (Shōshitsu Mokushō)
The planted pines grow naturally enough; yet one stubbornly follows others into the fire pit. Having exchanged this skin-sack, quickly turn back your head;
as before, the nostrils do not dispute by even a hair’s breadth.
(Shishi Hui) One plants several hundred green pines by hand; hungry one eats, thirsty one drinks, all as it is. Without cause, borrowing the path, once again [one is met].
Seen. Yet it was passed down by others as the Chart of the Patriarchs. (Tuiwengxiu) An old man who went to plant pines returns to transmit the joy of the Dharma to a youth.

He has his mother’s face but no father’s surname; this numinous sprout beyond the kalpas does not violate the spring. (Shu’anan) *Note: This is a Zen verse commentary on the "Chart of the Patriarchs" (Zutangji).
The text plays with themes of lineage, transmission, and the paradoxical nature of spiritual inheritance.*
A thousand mountains have been planted with no empty space left; yet one branch still remains by the side of the mattock.
Had it not been for the deception of Zhou’s daughter, how could the robe and bowl have reached your transmission?
(Zhongfeng Ben) On the day of planting pines within Mount Pòtóu, while lodging by the banks of the Zhúgǎng River, the Great Dharma hung by a single thread over the nine heavens.
The Tripod. Who can understand the affairs of coming and going?
(Yuan-an’s verse: A newborn calf has no fear of tigers; casually it comes to strike the He-shan drum—this too is suffering. Within the Apang Palace they boast of immense wealth;
there are countless gates to many pavilions. Having walked just three or five steps over there, the Persian suddenly—
He encountered the deity Jīvaka, who said: "The nature of all things is empty; because there is no self, there is no 'I'. (Nan-an Yi).
The Fifth Patriarch’s verse of entrustment to the Sixth Patriarch says: "When sentient beings come to plant seeds, fruits arise according to the ground.
Since insentient things have no seeds, they lack nature and thus have no arising."

Only eight months had passed since he trod the pestle when, in the middle of the night, his robe and bowl were mistakenly passed on. The discourse on the wind and the banner fell, and all who heard it perished;
from ancient times to the present, resentment has been drawn into this act of white-robed theft.
(Muan Hui) When the Great Master Huineng of the Sixth Patriarch heard that the Fifth Patriarch of Huangmei was departing for an audience, the Patriarch asked him, "Where have you come from?"
The Master said, "Lingnan. The Patriarch asked, "What do you seek? The Master replied, "I seek only to become a Buddha.
The Patriarch said, "People of Lingnan have no Buddha-nature; how can you become a Buddha? The Master replied, "People may be from the north or the south, but how could it be so with Buddha-nature?
The Patriarch rebuked him, saying, "Go and work in the stable! One day, the Patriarch ordered each of them to present a verse. Shenxiu wrote his on the wall:
The inscription on the corridor wall read: "The body is the Bodhi tree; the mind is like a bright mirror stand. At all times, diligently wipe it clean; do not let it gather dust.
The Master (Huineng) offered a different verse: "Bodhi originally has no tree; the bright mirror is also no stand.
Fundamentally there is not a single thing; where, then, can dust gather? The Patriarch silently recognized his potential.
A stone falls at his waist; the mortar and pestle ring out. Old Lu finds the heavy inconvenient, not the light.
Though he inherited the robe and bowl of Huangmei, it is still dozens of stages away from Caoxi.
(Yang Wuwai) The Sixth Patriarch was no true man in those days; he asked another to write on the wall while he himself plastered over it. Clearly there is a verse, yet he says there is none.
The object, however, accepted another’s single almsbowl (Sixin Xin).
An old yellow plum wrapped in osmanthus leaves is not planted upon the ground of yin and yang. How could bees and butterflies know the distance of its fragrance?
Its traces are hard to find as it departs and returns. (Dongshan Yan)
At midnight at Huangmei, he gave the instructions in error; as soon as he caught a glimpse of a star, he began to act recklessly.
At the head of Dayu Ridge, he dropped a great heap of dung, leaving his descendants of later generations stained by it.

(Muan Yong) Casting down the axe for gathering firewood, he went straight into the millhouse to pound grain. With one step, he trampled all the way to the bottom, and the message of Huangmei was thus communicated.
(Buddha-Zhao Guang):
One should give rise to the mind by abiding nowhere; at one stroke, the great earth, mountains, and rivers sink away. From this, a separate opening unfolds to the ends of the world;
in Xin Prefecture, a bundle of firewood is as precious as gold. (Po’an Xian)
The four-line gāthā cannot be read; three times it was transmitted, yet from the start it was non-existent.
Thorns grow along the path of Caoxi, reaching all the way down to this day halfway there.
(Miaofengshan) There is no tree of Bodhi and no stand for the mirror; this foul mouth has been clearly split open by a ghost. Fortunately, I am selling firewood and have nothing to worry about.
The Liao people are stubbornly obstinate, bringing disaster upon their own bodies. (No gate opens.
Not acting as woodcutters, they act as millers; they test the quality of the grain solely by their physical strength.
Whether they tread upon it or not, the rice and the bran alike reach the alms bowl. (Xiyuan Hui)
The seven hundred eminent monks gathered for the Chan assembly; their eyes empty the four seas, their noses reach toward heaven.
If Huangmei had been without partiality or crookedness, how could there have been a robe or bowl passed down to you?

(Chijue Chong) Carrying a load of firewood on his shoulder, his eyes are empty before him; entering the road to Huangmei, his artistry is exhausted. He has sold off the branches and leaves of the forest.
Exhausted. In Lingnan there is no ground for planting the spring breeze.
(Zhongfeng Ben) Huangmei’s entrustment was too hurried; at midnight, he crossed the river in sorrowful silence.
Thinking no one knew his whereabouts, the thief has already revealed himself along with the stolen goods. (Xin’an Chou)
