*Ji*: "The sound of the watchtower shakes as the moon passes over the Cangzhou.
(Ge Lu Tan) "The new moon reflects in the clear stream, its circle complete above and below; cold clouds sweep it away as it falls into the distant sky.
At the top of the city wall, three drumbeats resound in the darkness; the myriad phenomena of the universe rest upon the pillow. (Sanfeng Zang)

The Sixth Patriarch was at Fǎxìng Monastery when a wind blew the banner atop the pagoda finial. Two monks engaged in debate; one said, "It is the wind that moves," while the other said, "It is the banner that moves.
The Master said, "It is not the wind that moves, nor is it the banner that moves. It is your own minds, O worthy ones, that move."
Xuefeng Yun said, "The great and small patriarchs have the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake;
they deserve twenty blows of the staff. While serving him, the Venerable Fu gnashed his teeth. Xuefeng said, "I say this, yet they also deserve twenty blows of the staff.
Baofu Zhan said, "The heart of a thief is naturally apprehensive; this is also like Xiao He establishing the laws. Wuzu Jie said, "What is the point of all this?"
Baling Jian said: "The Patriarch said, 'It is not the wind moving, nor is it the banner moving. Since it is neither wind nor banner, where does one apply [the mind]?
If there is anyone who can act as the Patriarch's advocate, let them come forth and meet with Baling."
Xuedou Xian said: "The wind moves, the banner moves. Since it is both wind and banner, where do they land?
If there is someone who can act as a patron for Baling, come forth and meet Xuedou! Letan Qing said: "It is not the wind moving; it is not the banner moving.
If you are a person of keen intelligence, you should take this up immediately by letting go at the precipice, without looking back or ahead."
"Previously, when you were born, you were deluded and bewildered; your mind was stirred by others. But now, is there anyone who can act as the master for the Patriarch?
If there is, come forth and meet with this old monk. Tiantong Huo said: "One blind man leads a crowd of blind men;
together they pull each other into a fiery pit. Huanglong Xin said: "It is not the wind moving, nor is it the banner moving. An eye that sees clearly—"
"One cannot deceive him by even a hair's breadth. Benevolent One, your mind has been stirred; for now, proceed slowly. Where did you see the Patriarch?
He then cast down his whisk and said, "Look! Jingshan Daowu, having finished citing Xuefeng’s words, said: "Do you wish to recognize Monk Fu?
A rhinoceros develops its horn-patterns from gazing at the moon. Do you wish to recognize Xuefeng? An elephant is startled by thunder."
"Entering the Tusk. Zhongfeng Ben said: "Tasting a single morsel of the tripod, one comes to know all its flavors. 'It is not the wind moving, nor the banner moving;
it is the mind of the wise man that moves'—this may be called tasting a single morsel of the tripod.
It causes people to involuntarily feel revulsion and vomit. Tianning Qi said: "'The wind moves, the banner moves, the mind moves'—I have already removed these for you. Turn toward what?"
"Where can one see the Patriarch? Jingshan Xiu said: "The Great and Small Patriarchs have wrongly provided annotations for people;
they deserve thirty blows of the staff. Longchi Chuan said: "It is not the wind moving, nor the banner moving, nor the mind moving.
When a monk asked, 'What, after all, is it that moves? Longchi called to the monk. As the monk stepped forward, Longchi struck him."
[The Master] gave a slap and said, "I only permit you to know; I do not permit you to understand. He gave another slap and said, "Go!
Nuo’an asked, "The great patriarchs strike three thousand times in the morning and eight hundred times in the evening. Jin-su Yuan said, "Do you know where the patriarchs have landed?
At the beginning of the letter, he teaches his mother to be diligent in her rest; at the end of the letter, he teaches his mother not to doze off; in the middle..."
A single phrase does not form a complete text; boundless longing flows as tears amidst the flower rain.
It is neither the wind nor the banner; it is a black cat with spotted markings on its face.
The traveler at night covets only the bright moon, unaware that he has fallen into the cold water while still wearing his clothes. (Fachang Yu)
Vast and wide stretches this imperial post road; from dawn until dusk, it has never barred the passage of people.
It is not that my whole family fails to advance, but alas, thorns grow before our gate.
(Baoning Yong) East, west, south, and north—there is no empty space; in the four directions and above and below, each acts according to their lot. All kinsmen together are but one.
Body. Having traveled to the ends of the earth, there is no companion.
(Third Patriarch’s Ancestral Hall) It is neither wind nor banner; white clouds still cover the green mountains.
In recent years, grown old and utterly lacking strength, I have stolen a moment’s leisure from the midst of busyness. (Xuefeng Yuan)
Diving straight down into the vast blue ocean to seize the pearl from the black dragon’s jaws—when face-to-face it is presented, is there anything to be seen?
If one does not open the true eye upon reaching this point, the disease of the vital organs will be difficult to revive. (As for the "Dharma Hall," it is said:
Pointing out that both the wind and the banner are not [the truth], and directly stating that even the movement of the mind is likewise not [it], last night there was a single expanse of cold stream.
The moon pierces through the old green peaks of my home.
(Fuxincai) Dreaming of wandering atop Mount Huading past the Vermilion Hills, I tread upon cold clouds and lean against a stone pavilion.
Eagerly gazing at the waterfalls cascading down the cliffs, I did not realize my body was already at the head of the emerald river. (Changlingzhuo)
"It is neither wind nor banner, nor is it mind. Even the profoundness of Caoxi is not truly profound.
When Nanda the Wrathful tosses and turns away, one cannot seek him even by analyzing him into pervasive atoms.
(Huanglong Zhen) "It is neither wind nor banner; it is the movement of the mind. It is like borrowing Mazu to scratch where it itches. Who can catch the solitary crane beyond the heavens?
Marrow. Who can understand the glue for mending broken strings?
(Chongjue Kong) When the waves are still and the wind is calm, it is truly a fine sight to behold. The autumn river is crystal clear and the azure sky is vast.
Fishermen vie with one another to cast their lines; they do not see the icy moon dipping into the cold water. (Chang’an Chong)
The great ocean’s waves surge; the waters of a thousand rivers flow backward. Within the palaces of the Dragon Kings, not a single person is seen wandering.
(Ying’an Hua) It is not the wind or the banner that moves; Heaven gave birth to the Old Lord Li. From the hair upon his head at birth, every inch was as white as silver.
(Xuetang’s Verse) After Zhang Qian toppled Mount Kunlun, How many have plumbed the source of the Mengjin? How laughable are those who do not know heaven and earth;
To this day they still insist there is a "Heavenly Ruler" (Qiankun). (Kentang’s Supplement)
It is not the wind, nor is it the banner; the General rides his horse out through Tongguan Pass. Annan and the northern frontiers have all been brought under his rule;
from time to time he lights his lamp and gazes upon his sword. (Tianmu Li) A single moon over Chang’an;
the sound of pounding clothes in ten thousand households. The autumn wind cannot blow it away; it is all the longing for the Jade Gate.
(Gufeng Shen): "The wind and the banner stir the mind; with one appearance, it is passed over. Knowing only how to open the mouth, one does not realize the conversation has fallen away.
(Wumen Kai): "The earth spirit returns to the earth; the heavenly spirit returns to heaven. With earnest courtesy, they see him off with precious horses and gold coins. (Wuzhun Fan).
A trace of private affection brings but shame; it has already leaked out to you, my lord. Amidst longing thoughts, it is now the third month of spring;
whether flowers fall or bloom, all is but sorrow. (By San-yi Yu) At dusk, faint clouds wander across the Milky Way;
the cry of geese startles a world of autumn. The trees are a thousand fathoms high as the west wind blows.
Urgent! Red and yellow blink and chase the flowing water.
(Tianye Zhoushou) Yuyang Chongju, having finished citing Baoling and Xuedou, said: "It is neither wind nor banner; there is nowhere for attachment. It is wind and it is banner;
there is nowhere to be attached. Even a swift falcon that reaches for the heavens loses its tracks; even a golden-maned lion crouching on the ground is thrown into confusion. A-ha!
Hehe. Whether one awakens or not, it makes me long once more for Master Xie Sanlang: "A single thread of line, fishing alone in the cold river rain.
The Sixth Patriarch’s verse says: "Stolidly, I do not cultivate good; carefree, I do not commit evil. In profound stillness, I sever both seeing and hearing."
Vast and expansive, the mind is free from attachment.
The *Shouchang Jing* says: "Stolidly not cultivating goodness, one shatters the void into fragments; Leisurely not committing evil, one turns and topples the Palace of the Empty King.
In profound stillness, seeing and hearing are severed; The entire Dharma-realm of the ten directions shares a single gate of compassion."
Vast and expansive, the mind has no attachments. Startled awake, a gnat swallows the Five Peaks. Is this meaning not similar? Alas!
The long river flows eastward day and night; the waters of the sea have never decreased nor increased.
A monk asked the Sixth Patriarch, "Who will obtain the robe and bowl of Huangmei? The Master said, "The one who understands the Buddha-dharma shall obtain them.
The monk asked, "Will you yourself, Reverend, obtain them? The Master said, "I shall not obtain them. The monk asked, "Why do you not obtain them?
The Master said, "Because I do not understand the Buddha-dharma."
Fenyang Shanzhao said: "Only then do we know that the secret intent is difficult to transmit. Cuiyan Zhi said: "If you understand it, there are two heads;
if you do not understand it, there are three heads. How, then, can there be a way to emerge? Jingshan Daokai said:
Do you see the Patriarch yet? If you do not see him, I, Jingshan, shall point him out for you. "Bamboo, bamboo—leaves have withered.

Suddenly a gale arises; it is just like the tattered cassock of Master Wang in the corner by the wall of the eastern corridor of the thirty-six cloisters at the Great Xiangguosi Temple in the Eastern Capital. After all, what is it? Return.
While drinking tea in the hall, Tianning Qi said: "The staff strikes the head of the stone man; *bò bò*, he discusses the actual matter.
Yunju Zhuang said: "Setting aside for a moment whether one has attained it or not, or whether one understands it or not—why has the life-force of the Patriarch fallen into the hands of this monk?"
Picking it up with the hand of faith, one sees its uniqueness; within this, there is no effort to convey the message.
Huangmei did not permit the transmission of this principle; at midnight, he once entrusted it to Old Lu.
(Da-hong En) Chopping like a nail, cutting like iron—great skill appears as if clumsy. Holding up a single phrase: "If you do not understand the Buddha-dharma, let the leaves fall as they may."
The flowers bloom; one need not inquire whether it is spring’s chill or autumn’s heat. Parting ways—through all eternity, the moon in the empty realm above the cold pond.
(Yuánwù Qín) Not understanding the Buddha-dharma of Huangmei, one remains wide awake even with eyes closed in a dream.
There is not a single ounce of gold here, yet the common man sells three sheng of wine. (Xuěān Jǐn)
The Patriarch did not understand Zen; Confucius could not read characters. Striking the head of a stone man with a staff—*bò bò*!—he discussed the actual reality.
(Gao Feng Miao) Because Wōluén had a verse, the Sixth Patriarch [responded]: "Wōluén has his skills; he can sever a hundred thoughts. When facing objects..."
If the mind does not arise, Bodhi grows day by day. The Master replied separately: "I, Huineng, have no clever artifice; I do not sever the hundred thoughts.
When facing objects, the mental states arise; how then could Bodhi grow?"
Tiantong Jue said: "The sunflower turns toward the sun; the willow catkins follow the wind. Baoshou Xin said:
"As soon as one speaks of the three unbroken lines of Qian, there are already the six broken lines of Kun. How does one complete a hexagram?
If you wish to know where the lines and images are clearly revealed, look only at the palms of King Wen."
The Sixth Patriarch addressed the assembly, saying, "I have an object that has no head and no tail;
it has no name and no character; it has no back and no face. Do you all recognize it? At that time, Shenhui of Heze stepped forward and said, "It is the fundamental source of all dharmas;
it is the Buddha-nature of Shenhui. The Master struck him with a staff and said, "You talkative śrāmaṇera! When I call it..."
If one cannot even manage a single thing, how much less can one realize the fundamental Buddha-nature?
Even if this person were to cover his head with a thatched roof in the future, he would merely become a follower of the school of intellectual understanding.
Fayan Yi said: "The ancient masters' bestowal of predictions was never mistaken. To take intellectual understanding as the core principle today is precisely what Heze [Shenhui] did.
When a single speck of film clouds the eye, illusory flowers fall in confusion. The novice Shenhui lost his money and incurred punishment; he saw only the chisel-head."
"Square! Not seeing the sharpness of the tip of a needle. A great man! Little Śākyamuni! A single strike of an iron whip shatters the coral.

(Yuánwù Qín) "A painter uses five colors to paint empty space; one must know that as soon as the brush touches the paper, the original track is lost. Furthermore, there was Wú Dàodì of the Táng Dynasty..."
My son, throughout your life you have exerted your efforts in vain upon paper.
(Cishou Shen) An iron shackle without a hole must be carried by someone; it brings trouble upon descendants that is no small matter.
At midnight, suddenly forgetting the three-foot cloth, one instead covers a shameful face with empty hands. (Falin Yin)
One day, the Sixth Patriarch said to his disciples, "I wish to return to Xinzhou. You should quickly prepare the boat.
The disciples asked, "Master, when will you return from here? The Master replied, "Leaves fall and return to their root; when I come back, I shall have no mouth."
Fayun Xiu said: "Not only was there no mouth when he came, but there were also no nostrils when he went. Baizhang Yuan said:

"The Patriarch may truly be called one who is skilled at borrowing a hand to perform a fist-punch. There are certain fellows who often say, 'The words are still ringing in my ears,' yet they fail to see that it has been said:
'Ziqi departed and did not return; how lamentable this vast expanse! One does not know who among heaven and earth understands.'"
"Who, moreover, is this sound? Wuzu Yan said: "The Patriarch’s saying like this still lacks awakening.
A segment of emptiness atop the mountain of the five aggregates: when coming, there is no mouth; when going, there is no trace.
If you wish to clarify the principle of 'leaves falling and returning to the root,' only at the very end can you reach this school. (Benjue 1)
Once the leaves have fallen and returned to the root, a single drop from Caoxi is profound. Few people reach this mountain retreat; truly, one must be a fellow traveler to appreciate it.

(Longmen Yuan 2) Having returned to the root and attained the essential meaning, what more is there to discuss? At the mouth of the cave, the Qin man’s gate is half-shut; when the flowers fall, they simply follow the flowing stream.
Far away, empty space alone holds the gathering of vast wild clouds.

When the clouds disperse, the sky naturally widens; when the leaves fall, they return to their root. Turning my head toward the misty waves, the sound of fishermen’s songs passes by the distant village.
(Xingzong Yue) The source rises in the southern heavens, at the very end of the sky. Before setting out, one has already arrived in New Prefecture.
Coming with no mouth, departing without a companion—how much more so this autumn with its whistling yellow leaves. (Xu Tang Yu)
*Zongjian fali*, Volume Six;

Compiled by Jiyun Tang.
A collateral branch of the various patriarchs:
Chan Master Faron of Oxhead (a successor of the Fourth Patriarch Xinxing). When the Fourth Patriarch arrived at the mountain, he entered the hermitage and saw tiger tracks;
he immediately made a gesture of fear. The Master said, "The Master still has this. The Patriarch asked, "What is this?"
"Ma. At these words, the Master attained realization. Thereafter, the hundred birds no longer brought flowers.
Xuedou Xian, acting on behalf of Huairang, merely made a gesture of fear. He also said: "It would have been better to let it pass.
A monk asked, "Why did the hundred birds bring flowers to Niutou before he had seen the Fourth Patriarch? Nanquan Puyuan replied, "Because he was treading step by step upon them."
The Buddha’s Staircase. Zhaozhou said, "Sufficient firewood, sufficient water. Dayue Zhe said, "One's hair stands on end with cold.
Falin Yin said, "The mountains and rivers of Han land remain. Again he asked, "After seeing [the Buddha], for what reason do the hundred birds not come?
Quan said, "Even if they did not come, they would still fall short of Old Master Wang by a single thread of the Way. Zhaozhou said, "Sufficient firewood."
[The guest] says: "Satiated with water. Miaoyan says: "Sweat pours from his forehead. Linji says: "In the palaces of Qin, the plants and trees turn autumnal;
atop the peak of Niutou, heavy clouds lock the summit. Sitting alone in vast stillness, this body is entrusted here;
though the hundred birds do not come and spring passes away again, one does not know who is the person who reaches the hermitage. (Mingjue Xian)
Purple qi mingles and permeates the white clouds; Having met the Master of the School, the path from delusion was pointed out.
The hundred birds carrying flowers in their beaks are in vain sorrow; They do not see the former master within the hermitage.

(Yang Woei) Flowers fall and flowers bloom, and the hundred birds grieve; Before the hermitage, the things remain the same, but the master is no more. Though the Peach Blossom Spring is but a few paces away, there is no one to seek it out.
A solitary place; with a single oar, the fisherman in his straw cloak returns in silence.
(Zhang Wujin) A single bed, desolate beside the green shade; by day the pine door is locked, deep and cold.
Lazy Rong has reached the state of ordinary nature; where can one find the birds bringing flowers? (Zu Yin Ming)
In the vast stillness of wind and moon, one reclines amidst mists and clouds; from this point on, the hundred birds no longer offer flowers.
Benevolence and righteousness are severed at the threshold of poverty; worldly sentiments lean toward those who possess wealth.

(By Meng’an Xin) It is because of the moon that water reveals its stillness; it is because of the absence of clouds that the heavens first appear lofty. Sitting alone upon a solitary peak, there is no need for further [explanation].
Question: At this time, it is difficult to attach even a single hair’s breadth [of conceptualization].
(Bieping Yin) Before the rain, one sees neither flowers nor leaves among the branches; after the rain, there is utterly no flower beneath the leaves.
Fluttering butterflies pass over the wall; one knows not to whom the spring colors now belong. (Gufeng Shen)
Catching the horse’s bridle, he rides away; empty-handed, he returns on foot. Along the path before the silent hermitage, the flower-bearer bird does not fly.
(Tieshan Ren) The moon fills the ponds, the green fills the mountains. He comes and goes daily amidst the myriad flowers. Once he has trod upon and severed the path of his coming—
On the Road: On the ridge, there are no clouds; the pines are naturally at ease.

(By Lǎnmù Chéng) Chan Master Xuānguó Xuāntíng of Xuānzhōu (he was a successor of Níutóu Wéi). Once, when a monk asked the Fifth Patriarch, "What is the meaning of the True Nature’s Dependent Origination?
the Patriarch remained silent. At that time, the Master [Xuāntíng] was standing in attendance and said, "The Great Master has just given rise to a single thought."
When asked, "At the very moment of questioning, this is dependent origination within the true nature," Sengdà attained great enlightenment.
Jìngshān Gǎo said, "Even before a single thought has arisen, at the moment of questioning, there can be no lack of dependent origination. At that time, a monk said:
Before a single thought has arisen, what do you call "conditioned origination"? Miaoxi said, "I also want you to speak in just this way.
Tianning Qi said, "A Kunlun slave wearing iron trousers; strike him once and he takes a step forward."
Lingyan Chu said: "Everyone says that Huangmei 'levels the high by descending to the low,' yet they fail to realize that the path ahead is far too perilous.
This monk merely looks toward the summit of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff and advances; how could he know his own body is already in the Imperial Capital? Regarding the Chan of Ting:
Miaoxi had one person for whom 'pointing was not reaching' and another for whom 'reaching was not pointing.'"
When a monk asked Chan Master Tianzhu Chonghui (who was a successor of Niutou Wei), "Before Bodhidharma came to this land, was there still the Buddha-dharma or not?
The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment whether it existed before he came, what is the matter right now?
The monk said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "The eternal sky: one morning’s wind and moon. The monk was speechless.
The Master spoke again, saying, "Ācārya, do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "How is it from your own side?
What does it have to do with whether or not that Dharma came? When he came, it was very much like a fortune-teller."
"Seeing that you do not understand, I have used the divination chart to pierce through it for you. From the moment signs of good or bad fortune arise, they are entirely within your own sphere;
look at them all yourself. The monk asked, "What is one who understands divination? The Master said, "The very moment you step out the door, you have already missed it."
Who has set foot upon the eternal vast sky? Once wind and moon have ceased, do not pick them up again.
With a single punch, he knocks down the fortune-teller; beyond the gate, all is naturally vast and open.
(Yunlin Lu) When a monk asked Tianzhu, "What is the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū? the Master said, "Since the beginning of vast kalpas..."
"It has never been obstructed. If it is not the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū, what is it?
[The student] asked, "Why is the Buddha-dharma not manifest before me? The Master said, "It is precisely because you do not understand that it does not manifest.
If you were to understand, there would be no Buddha to be realized."
Pou Xi once said: "To overturn the celestial gate and kick over the terrestrial axis is certainly not impossible;
yet, how regrettable that this monk remains long stuck and unpenetrated, failing his own potential and exhausting his mental and physical strength."
Chan Master Xuansu of Helin in Runzhou (a successor of Niu-tou Wei) was once asked by a monk who knocked on the door.
The Master asked, "Who is there? The monk replied, "I am a monk. The Master said, "Not only monks; even if a Buddha were to come, he would not be admitted.
The monk asked, "Why would a Buddha not be admitted? The Master said, "Because there is no place for him to lodge."
Baoshou Fang said: "Huelin speaks thus; I thought he was standing atop a high, towering peak, yet I did not realize that this monk has long since pushed him down into a ten-thousand-fathom abyss."
In the tenth month, the clear frost falls thick; standing before the wind, the cold pierces to the bone. Having no place at all to rest, I wave my hands and depart from Chang’an.
(Songyuan Yue) To say "a Buddha comes" is not even acceptable; every joint of one’s bones is pure gold. There is no need for three prostrations to realize this.
All is understood. Cranes cry out in the empty mountains; bamboo fills the groves.

(Self-Composed Reverence) I close my door at midday and sit alone constantly; In the empty hall, I occasionally roll back the night-bright curtains. Too weary to follow worldly affairs, I have forgotten the coming and going of guests.
The falling leaves and golden winds bring the stern message of frost. (Phantom Dwelling in the Courtyard)
The sturdy barrier is firmly held; though struck, it cannot be penetrated. Even Buddhas and Patriarchs are not permitted entry.
If you are a true offspring of the golden-maned lion, you will turn back and soar across the great void.
(Yishi Yuan) Chan Master Guishan Daoyin of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou (successor of Helin Su). Mazu sent a messenger with a letter to him.
In the letter, he drew a circle. When the Master opened the seal and saw it, he placed a single dot within the circle and then sealed it back and returned it.
Upon hearing this, National Teacher Zhong said, "Master Qin was still deluded by Master Ma."
Baofu Zhan said, "Where is the place of delusion? How can one avoid being deluded?

Xuedou Xian said, "Setting aside the fact that Jingshan was deluded, if he had presented [the matter] to the National Teacher, what other skillful means would the National Teacher have employed to avoid being deluded?
An old master said, "At that time, he should have sat [in silence] and let it rest. Others have also said, "He should simply have drawn a line through it."

If it were like that, it would simply be a lack of shame. How dare you claim that the teachers of the world all possess the vajra-eye and can extensively manifest supernatural transformations; even so, could they escape it? I want everyone to know where Xuedou stands.
When Jizhe the Horse Master sketched it out at that time, he was already deluded from the start. Wuzu Ji said, "Two colors, one match.
He also said, "With three people pointing the way, what do you intend to do? Weishan Zhe said, "Do you recognize the path of Mazu?
A single drop of ink forms two dragons. National Teacher Daoyuan said that even Master Daoqin was still caught by the Horse Master.
[The Master] was perplexed. It could be said that "a thousand miles share the same breeze. Have you not heard the saying: "Holding a night-bright talisman in hand, how many know when the dawn breaks?
Jingshan Hongdao said: "Mazu [said it was] a bitter cold in mid-winter; Guoyi [said it was] gradually warming in early summer.
Although the cold and heat differ, neither missed their proper season. Why did the National Teacher say that Master Qin was still being deceived by Master Ma?"

"Delusion! A lotus leaf moves without wind; there must surely be a fish swimming beneath. Tianning Qi said: "If one places a dot within the perfect circle (*yuanxiang*), the sun and moon lose their light and heaven and earth fall into darkness.

At first, you were not deluded by Master Qin; rather, Master Ma was deluded first, and his error has extended even to Old Nanyang. What a mess! After a long silence, he said: 'Throughout my life, I have laid my liver and gall out for others.'"**Note:** The final phrase "xiang...

appears to be an incomplete fragment. Based on the context of Chan records, it likely refers to the famous verse by Linji Yixuan: "The whole body is the Buddha" (全身是佛). Thus, the full line would read: "Throughout my life, I have laid my liver and gall out for others; my whole body is the Buddha. I have translated this based on the standard textual tradition.
"Consciousness is like being unacquainted. Guonan said: "Guonan has thirty blows. One blow for Master Ma, who should not have been deluded by himself;
one blow for Master Qin, who should not have been deluded; and one blow for Xuedou, who should not have judged it as delusion.
Furthermore, there is one more blow to gently reveal the truth to all of you. Chongxian Qi said: "Master Ma’s weeds..."
I offer my greetings. Master Daoqin’s myriad characters are full of twists and turns; though his exchanges are without error, they only serve to make the path increasingly circuitous.

Everyone says that National Teacher Zhong was still deluded by Master Mazu, yet they fail to realize that when a word is transcribed three times, it can turn from "crow" (wū) and "yes" (ān) into "horse" (mǎ).
When Mazu tested Jingshan at that time, he subtly revealed his secret mechanism;
unexpectedly, however, the old man of Nanyang leveled a pitfall upon flat ground as if it were a trivial matter. (Foyin Yuan) Words of delusion have their origins;
a spiritual communion across a thousand li is like casting a mustard seed into a needle’s eye. Who would have known that he could cause the clouds to pass through?
I believe it not; even stones nod their heads. (Zhaojue Zong) To delude oneself and others is no trivial matter.
Not missing the proper season, one attains a single excellence. Treading upon the grass rope, every bone trembles—simply because at the outset one was bitten by a snake. (Yunlin Lu)
Once, Mazu dispatched Zhizang to ask the Master, "In the twelve hours of the day, what do you take as the objective realm?
The Master replied, "I shall have news for you when you return. Zhizang said, "I am returning right now.
The Master said, "Deliver this message to Great Master Mazu: he must go back and ask Caoshan."
Yunju Zhuang said: "Master Ma was like one who deployed his troops to provoke a battle; Guoyi may be called one who produced a stratagem when encountering a crisis.
Although this monk was skilled at conveying messages, he was nonetheless laborious and without merit. He suddenly picked up his staff, drew a line, and said:
"When the three-tiered waves are high, the fish transforms into a dragon; yet the fool still scoops water from the night pond. Benjueyi said: [The same].
Mazu secretly passed the golden needle; Jingshan clearly threaded the jade thread. Were it not for this monk, how could one recognize the full manifestation of the literary brilliance?
Look closely: the beautiful maiden has already returned to the celestial expanse, while the simpleton still crouches by the fire.
National Teacher Yi received the Emperor’s personal veneration during the reign of Emperor Daizong of the Tang dynasty. One day, while in the inner palace, he rose as the Emperor approached.
The Emperor asked, "Why do you rise, Master? The Master replied, "How can a donor regard me, a poor monk, within the context of the four modes of deportment?"
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "If one does not look toward the four modes of deportment, how then can one see Guoyi?
Standing outside the deportments, the whole body is within them; though repeatedly bestowed with dragon sleeves, they cannot conceal the shame on the face."

(West Rock Hui) The Sovereign of Ten Thousand Chariots is the Teacher of the Nation; In his daily life, he never departs from the four modes of deportment. Mountains stretch long and waters flow far, yet we but remember him in vain;
Yellow leaves blow in the wind, but the man has not yet returned. (Xianji Yun)
When Chan Master Daolin of Niaoke (National Teacher No. 1, successor to Xuanqin) was about to depart for other regions to study the Buddha-dharma, his attendant said, "I am going away.
The Master said, "As for the Buddha-dharma, I, this old monk, also have a little bit of it. The attendant asked, "What is the Master’s Buddha-dharma?
The Master picked up some cloth-pelts, blew upon them once, and the attendant attained great enlightenment.
Daguang Xiu said, "It is a pity that this monk takes the sounds and colors from another’s lips to define his entire life;

he does not realize that his own radiance covers heaven and earth. Shending Yin, having cited this, then plucked a tuft of cloth from his own body and blew upon it, saying, "Do you understand? In the future, do not let me down. Jingshan Guangzhao said, "Da..."
Shan’s critique in this manner has not even seen Bird Nest (Niaoke) in his dreams. Tianning Qi said:
"If the attendant had simply shouted at the moment the feather was picked up, he would have avoided being scrutinized by those in all quarters.
For me to speak thus is also to increase delusion for the sake of others' idle affairs."
White phoenixes soar through mist and clouds, controlling the bird’s nest; the pearl of the black dragon shines upon the ancestral mountains and rivers.
The original intent of picking up the cloth-hair—that essence and function of Vairocana—is more than a mere trifle. (Master Kefu):
When Niaoke picked up the cloth-hair and blew upon it, a single beam of cold light met the setting sun. Though this was the heart-mind of an old woman, it was no small matter.
[Shimen Yi]: "All things! Awakening has come, yet one is still halfway home. Without wind, ripples rise all around; the azure topknot and silken patterns are seen with the True Eye.

Just as the Yellow River is locked by three layers of ice, one beholds the dragon coiled within the Nārāyaṇa cave. [Yunju You]: "All things! Awakening has come, yet one is still halfway home. Without wind, ripples rise all around; the azure topknot and silken patterns are seen with the True Eye.
Just as the Yellow River is locked by three layers of ice, one beholds the dragon coiled within the Nārāyaṇa cave."
Niaokuo blew on a cloth-hair; the red sun was high at midday. Because King Zhao delighted in swords, the people of the entire state wore blades.
(Zhenjing Wen) Old and decrepit, forgetting artifice—this is Niaokuo. By the misty vines upon the West Lake, he blew a tuft of cloth-hair; there was not much more to it.
"Son! Though he has iron eyes and copper pupils, what can he do? (Bao Feng Qian) It is difficult for even a speck of gold-dust to pass through his eyes.
Once awakened, the person of today is the person of antiquity. To gather up the entire earth is like grasping a grain of millet;
within a single hair-tip, the whole body is manifested. (Fo Jian Qin)
A single puff of cloth-hair: immediately one knows where one returns. Cold light pervades the earth; the needle and hammer are revealed alone.
(Chu Fang’an) Riding horses gallop about in the morning breeze; the general issues his command east of the city.
Picking up the golden arrowhead—a touch of subtle skill—he pierces the single dot of red at the heart of the flower. (Tudu Ce)
In the long forests, the secluded birds chirp in vain; tender willows dance against the wind like emerald waves. Who among the wealthy and noble in the spring city does not enjoy this?
It leads one to take a leisurely stroll up the slopes of the imperial grove.
(San-yi-yu) From the beginning, there has never been a mark of axe or hatchet; let him remain a man of the mountains in his true colors. To create complications outside the season is senseless.
This brings calamity down upon one’s door from out of the blue.
(Xiaoru Yuan) When Bai Juyi asked Master Niaoke, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? the Master said, "Commit no evil;
practice all that is good. Bai Juyi said, "Even a three-year-old child knows how to say that. The Master said, "A three-year-old..."
"The child may be able to speak it, but an eighty-year-old man cannot practice it.
Falin-yin said: "Having left the brothel but not yet repaid his debt for wine, he does not accord with others himself.
A man like Ji-e now sits upon the ground of clarity; let us call him Niaoke and have him explain the Buddha-dharma for us."
Can it be so? Evil has no appearance; goodness has no form. Both are nurtured and grown from the field of one’s own mind. Without moving a blade, they are lightly pierced through;
awakening and affliction are equal to space. (The Infinite Life Sutra)
Chan Master Daoming of Mount Meng in Yuanzhou (a successor of the Fifth Patriarch Huineng) once pursued the Sixth Patriarch, Lu Xingzhe, as far as Dayu Ridge.
The Patriarch placed his robe upon a rock; when the Master attempted to lift it and found it immovable, he said, "I have come for the sake of the Dharma."

"It was not for the sake of clothing that I came; I pray that the Master will grant me instruction. The Patriarch said, "At this very moment, when you are neither thinking of good nor thinking of evil—what is your original face, Layman Ming?

The Master attained great enlightenment and prostrated himself, saying, "Beyond these secret words and secret meanings you have just imparted, is there any further intent? The Patriarch said, "I shall now explain it for you."
This is precisely what is not secret. If you reflect back upon yourself, the secret is right there with you.
Falin said: "The practitioner is profoundly without coming or going; yet, when struck lightly by this fellow Meng Babang, he immediately urinates on the spot.
Since those two thousand years have passed, we do not know where the robe and bowl at the head of Dayu Ridge have gone.
Is it still there? To this day, there are infinite, limitless monks, each of whom stares wide-eyed, desiring nothing but to see their original face.
Truly, they are laughable beyond measure.
Precisely at such a time, throughout kalpas one has never been deluded. Step by step one traverses the triple world, returning home forever free from doubt.

(Longmen Yuan) Majestic and sublime, the wondrous form is beyond the slightest trace; good and evil are both forgotten—can it even be seen? Ten thousand miles of clouds have cleared, and the celestial realm is revealed.
Pure. The sea-mind is waveless, the moon-disk solitary.
(Fóxìng Tái) At nightfall, he transmitted the robe to Old Lú. What a pity for the old, ancient fellow from Huangméi! He said, "When I tell you to stop chasing people, do not chase them further.
Indeed, he fell from his high standing once and returned. (Xuěxī Jiè)
Eighteen beauties enter the embroidered chamber; before the lamp, there is no leisure to discuss the heat and cold. This elegance cannot be transmitted through words;

it truly depends on our own independent mastery. (By Liu Yuxi) National Teacher Huian of Songshan (who succeeded the Fifth Patriarch Ren) was asked by Tanran: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
[The student] asked about "intention. The Master said, "Why do you not ask about your own intention? [The student] asked, "What is one's own intention?
The Master said, "Observe the secret functioning. [The student] asked, "What is the secret functioning? The Master indicated it by opening and closing his eyes.
Nevertheless, one knows where to return upon hearing the words.
Achan said, "To know where to return upon hearing the words means that a monk has already been carrying his own self on his back.
He then joined his palms and said, "I, Achan, do not dare hope for you all to meet with National Teacher An."
Holding up a lamp to seek fire, one searches outside; yet the clear indication is that it resides within one’s own body.
Suddenly, the Eye of Correctness opens at the crown of the head—neither from oneself nor from another.

(Lingjiu Cheng) Regarding the Venerable Puzhao Duo of Mount Song (who was a successor of National Teacher An): There was once a temple on Mount Song that was extremely efficacious. In its main hall, there was only...
He set up a single hearth. The Master struck it three times with his staff and said, "Tsk! This hearth is merely composed of clay and tiles.
From where does the sacred come? From where does the numinous arise? Yet you thus slaughter living beings! He struck it another three times, and the hearth collapsed.
After a short while, a figure in green robes and a tall cap appeared, prostrating himself and saying, "I am originally the deity of this temple. For a long time..."

He was receiving the retribution for his past karma. Now, having heard the Master’s teaching on the Dharma of non-arising (*anutpāda*), he has attained liberation from this place and been reborn in heaven.

The Master said, "This is your own original nature; it is not something I have forcefully asserted. A monk asked, "I have long served at your side, yet I have not received your skillful means (*upāya*).
What principle did the stove-god realize that he was immediately reborn in heaven? The Master said, "I simply told him:"
"This is composed of mud and tiles; there is no other principle to it. The monk pondered this.
The Master asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Why do you not understand the nature that is inherently present?
The monk prostrated. The Master said, "Falling! Falling! Broken! Broken! Later, someone reported this to National Teacher An, who sighed and said, "This..."
The Son of Heaven has realized that all things and the self are as one;
fortune, misfortune, majesty, and sternness do not reside in the spirit. To whom does he offer these leftover cups and cold roasted meats?
Since his departure, there has been no news; yet the village elder still beats the sacrificial drum. (Longmen Yuan)

Relying on the hearth for spiritual power, one does not become spiritual oneself. Where the traces of spirituality are severed, there is but a heap of dust. The wild old man does not come to beat the sacrificial drum;
striking the right cause while departing from the heterodox is a different kind of spring.
(Fodeng Xun) The nine-headed *zhēn* bird soars through the heavens with its poison; the world-protecting Nārāyaṇa possesses eight long arms. Water flows out from the edge of the rock.
Cold. The wind comes from within the flowers, carrying fragrance. (Nanyue Sheng) Struck by him once, one must bow the head;
in vain one wears the scholar’s cap like a refugee of Chu. Behold the clouds parting to reveal the mountains and peaks;
the sound of the stream is unceasing as the water flows on. (Puci Yun)
Because a monk who had broken the stove came from the place of Niu-t'ou, the Master asked him, "From which Dharma assembly have you come?
The monk stepped forward, joined his palms, circumambulated the Master once, and departed. The Master said, "There should be no such person under Niu-t'ou."

The monk then passed to the left of the Master and stood with his hands joined in *añjali*. The Master said, "As expected, as expected. The monk then asked, "How is it when responding to things does not depend on another?
The Master said, "How could it not depend on another? The monk said, "In that case, one follows the correct path back to the source.
The Master said, "What is there to follow when returning to the source? The monk said, "Had it not been for you, Master, I would have nearly made a mistake."
[The monk] committed an offense. The Master said, "This is still the principle [you held] before you saw the Fourth Patriarch. After seeing him, bring it here.
The monk then circumambulated the Master once and departed. The Master said, "The Way of accordance with correctness has been thus from ancient times to the present.
The monk bowed and withdrew.
Han Lei said: "Puo-zao [the monk who broke the stove] acted with spontaneous freedom; seizing and releasing according to the occasion, he was truly a master craftsman of the school.
This monk was accustomed to being a guest and knew how to advance and retreat appropriately;
one could say he had personally seen Niutou. However, when scrutinized, both have been exposed. But where exactly did they expose themselves? Sanmei Zhen said: "This fellow!"
Even a mere technician would dare say he has come from Oxhead. As for Old Man Pòzào, he broke his staff at that time.
Chan Master Sōngshān Jùjí (a successor of Pòzào Duò) was once asked by a monk: "What is a person of great cultivation?"
The Master said, "Carrying the pillory and wearing the shackles. The monk asked, "What is it like for one who performs karma?
The Master said, "Practicing meditation and entering samādhi. The monk was speechless. The Master then said, "If you ask me about good, good does not arise from evil. If you ask me about evil..."
Evil does not follow from good; therefore it is said that good and evil are like floating clouds, arising and ceasing without a fixed location.
When Monk Qiwu later heard this account from Puozaodu, he remarked, "This man has realized that all phenomena are unborn."
Jianfu Huai said: "In front, the official path does not admit even a needle; behind, private carriages and horses pass through. Zhaojue Qin said:
"When you exhaustively examine goodness, from where does goodness come? When you thoroughly investigate evil, from where does evil arise?

If someone asks, "What is a great practitioner of cultivation? simply say: "Cultivating dhyāna and entering samādhi. If they ask, "What is a person of great karma? simply say: "Carrying [the burden]."
"Shackles, bands, and locks. Tell me, are these the same or different? Jingshan Daowu said: "Alas, how can one help it? One is merely creating deluded thoughts before the skull.
Wushi Daowu’s words for the "before" state are: "Lying across the body, facing the universe. His words for the "after" state are: [omitted].

Barefoot upon the mountain of blades, bound in chains and bearing the cangue to invite one’s own transgressions; entering meditative absorption and falling into a deep pit—when both ends are cast off, there is no longer anything to rely upon.
A solitary idler within heaven and earth. (By Bieshan Zhi)
Chan Master Weizheng of Zhongnan Mountain (a successor of Huairang of Mount Song, the Northern School) once encountered the following event: Emperor Wenzong of the Tang dynasty was fond of clams.
One day, among the imperial provisions, there was one that could not be split open. The Emperor considered this a marvel and burned incense to pray to it.

Suddenly, it transformed into a Bodhisattva, complete with all the features of a Brahma-like countenance. The Emperor immediately placed it in a casket made of *suvarṇa* and sandalwood and covered it with fine brocade.
The Xingshan Temple was bestowed [upon him]. Thereupon, the Emperor questioned his ministers: "What auspicious omen is this?

They replied that Chan Master Weizheng of Taibai Mountain had a profound understanding of the Buddha-dharma. The Emperor summoned the Master to question him. The Master said: "No phenomenon occurs without a corresponding cause;
this is intended to awaken Your Majesty’s faith. He cited the Sūtra: "By whatever form one should be delivered, that very form shall appear."
The Master spoke the Dharma for the Emperor’s body. The Emperor said, “Your body is already manifest; yet I have not heard you preach the Dharma.
The Master asked, “Does Your Majesty regard this as permanent or impermanent? Do you believe it or not? The Emperor replied, “This is a rare and marvelous thing;
I believe it with deep conviction. The Master said, “Your Majesty has already heard the preaching of the Dharma. The Emperor was greatly pleased.
Jiannanyin said: "The clam preaching the Dharma is precisely it; Weizheng’s commentary refuting this is not correct.
'The species of snails, conchs, and clams / Are the heart of the Great Tang Emperor. / If one’s preferences are deep faith, / Then [recite] Namah Avalokiteśvara.'"
(Xiyuan Hui) Mixing water with mud—how busy he was! He was exposed by that fellow, a truly outrageous matter.
Though he may have tacitly grasped the King’s intent, he has already cast his entire body into the cauldron of boiling oil. (Beihai Xin)
Within the oysters and clams lies the response-body (*nirmāṇakāya*); yet even further, his preaching of the Dharma is not the ultimate truth.
The Great Being of Potalaka is like a prince of Tang; his piercing gaze leaves no one without the kindness of a single night’s lodging.
(From *Xianji yun*) Having turned back from the depths of the boiling cauldron, though the revolving mallet strikes him and he cannot open [the shell], suddenly the Bodhisattva bursts wide open.
Manifesting thus, there is no need for further doubt or suspicion. (3 Yuan 2) This very old man was not a true hero in his prime;
he spoke of the Dharma with deluded words, muddling things up himself. Nevertheless, he deceived the Son of Heaven of Tang and made the blue-eyed barbarian of the Western Heavens laugh to tears.
National Teacher Huizhong of Guangzhai in the Western Capital (the successor to the Sixth Patriarch Huineng) was once asked by Emperor Suzong, "What Dharma did you receive at Caoxi?
The Master replied, "Does Your Majesty see that single cloud in the sky? The Emperor said, "I see it.
The Master said, "Nail it down! Hang it up!"
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said: "Better that good things not exist at all. Qingshan Xiu said:

"Fortunately, the National Teacher’s response did not involve the 'leaving' or the 'subtle,' nor did it fall into the path of principle. This may be called transcending the present and surpassing antiquity, walking alone across heaven and earth.
Had Suzong been able to turn his body and apply a sudden pressure, who knows how he would have rolled up that single sheet of cloud? A Hall.
The wind is cool and serene; the meaning of a thousand ages is clear and distinct. Baiya Fu said:
"Does the National Teacher’s saying like this derive from Caoxi, or does it not derive from Caoxi?"
Where there is no opening for a mouth, yet one opens it; when the intention is to return, one returns immediately. Zhaozhou does not reside within the realm of clarity;
this is not yet the time when the wild goat hangs from its horns.
(Cishou Shen) When Emperor Suzong asked National Teacher Huairang, "What is the Ten-Body Tamer? the Master stood up and said, "Understood."
Mo said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Hand the pure pitcher to this old monk.
Bearing snow and containing frost, it leans half against the fence; within its slanting shadow, the immortal form is revealed.
Spring has arrived in the village ahead last night, yet the old monk in his bamboo cottage still knows nothing of it. (Xinwen Ben)
Quietly she pours the *tusu* [milk] with intent; the young gentleman knows nothing of its meaning. When applying makeup, she can only smear the "pardon-powder" (*shuǎfěn*);
let others criticize her as being too vulgar. (Jiāshuǐ Jiá) National Teacher:
When Emperor Suzong asked, "What is the Samādhi of Non-contention? the Master said, "Donor, you have stepped on a *vimala* [lotus]."
Lu climbed onto the master’s head and asked, "What is the meaning of this? The master said, "Do not mistake it for your own pure *dharmakāya*.
Lu asked again, but the master did not look at him at all. Lu said, "I am the Son of Heaven of the Great Tang;
why do you, Master, utterly refuse to look upon me? The master replied, "Do you see the empty sky? Lu said, "I see it. The master said, "Does it blink its eyes?"
"Your Majesty, no.
Jingshan Daokai said, "If you wish to see the National Teacher, he is right within your own eyes. You miss him when your eyes are open;
you miss him when your eyes are closed. Since he is within your eyes, why do you miss him? Miaoxi spoke thus.
The Way—how much has been missed!
Even "Teacher of a Nation" is but a forced designation. Nanyang alone was permitted to spread his illustrious reputation.
Having supported the true Son of Heaven of the Great Tang, he once trod upon the crown of Vairocana. (Xuedou Xian II)
An iron hammer shatters the golden bones; between heaven and earth, what else remains? The ocean of three thousand lands is serene and clear at night;
one knows not who has entered the blue dragon’s cave.
The author’s pure regulations have no peer in the world; once he grasped the golden awl atop the Dragon Pavilion.
How excellent that he pierced through the crown of Vairocana, until even Mañjuśrī smiled and nodded his head.
(Wuwei Xiu II) The precious moon contains the void as it aligns with the many peaks; who can distinguish their heights amidst the thin mist? Mount Sumeru is smashed to pieces by Yanguan.
The drum beats; Vairocana is brought down beneath the wind.
At every step one treads upon the crown of Vairocana’s head. This is neither one's own pure body, yet one wondrously enters the gate of emptiness and attains the mark of emptiness.
It is the liver and gall of the Patriarchs, the very spirit of the Buddhas. (Fujian Qín)
The National Teacher, upon seeing Nanquan enter, asked, "Where have you come from? Nanquan replied, "From Jiangxi.
The Master said, "Have you brought back Mazu’s true portrait? Nanquan said, "This very one is it. The Master said, "What about the one behind him? Nanquan then withdrew.
Changqing Ling said, "It is very much like not knowing. Baofu Zhuan spoke differently, saying, "He has simply not reached this place of yours, Master.
Wuzu Ji said, "The Master is well-acquainted with this path. Yunju Xi said, "Changqing and Baofu both support him from behind;
as for Nanquan’s 'resting,' does he support him from the front or from behind?"
The heavens are filled with clouds. Nanquan builds a high tower at the bottom of a well; the National Teacher peers over his shoulder inside a lacquer bucket.
Beyond this, two by two and three by three, they support those in front and those behind—this is truly picking up horse dung in Yangzhou and going to Suzhou to sell blended incense.
The National Teacher had previously attained the supernormal power of knowing others' minds through the Tripitaka Master Dairi. Emperor Suzong ordered the Master to verify this.
The Master asked, "Have you attained the power of knowing others' minds? He replied, "I dare not say so. The Master said, "Tell me, where am I right now?
He replied, "You are the National Teacher of the entire realm; how could you go to Western Sichuan to watch the boat races? The Master [laughed].
After a long time, he asked again. Tripitaka said, "How can you, the teacher of an entire nation, go to Tianjin Bridge to watch monkeys being played with?
When the Master asked for the third time, Tripitaka hesitated, not knowing where to turn.
The Master rebuked him, saying, "You wild fox spirit! Where is your 'knowledge of others' minds' now? Tripitaka had no reply.
A monk once asked Zhaozhou, “The National Teacher was not seen for the third time; I wonder where the National Teacher is?
Zhaozhou replied, “He is inside the nostrils of the Tripitaka Master. Later, a monk asked Xuansha, “Since he is inside the nostrils of the Tripitaka Master, why is he not seen?
Xuansha said, “It is precisely because he is too close. Yangshan Huiji remarked, “The first two times were still within the realm of conceptual involvement (*shé*).”
The object and the mind. Later, he entered the samādhi of self-enjoyment, which is why [the Master] did not see him.
Faling Yin said, "It is easy to see the National Teacher, but it is difficult to see Yangshan. Xuansha Shibei asked, "Do you say that you saw him during those two previous occasions?
Later, Xuedou Xian said, "Defeated! Defeated! Baizhang Yuan said, "The National Teacher was right here."
"What difficulty is there in seeing the nostrils inside the Tripitaka Master’s nose? One simply does not realize that the National Teacher is within the eyes of the Tripitaka Master.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "As for whether the Tripitaka Master sees the National Teacher’s nostrils or not—Baoci then said, 'He saw them on the previous two occasions;
why did he not see them later? Now tell me, where does the point of significance lie?"
Gao Feng Miaoyun said: "The lifelong skills of the Great and Small National Masters were all thoroughly exposed by this barbarian monk.
Nevertheless, it was fortunate that they encountered a sagely sovereign who provided witness. Baen Xiu said: "If it were within one's own eyes, what would be difficult to see?
One simply does not realize that the Tripitaka Master’s entire body is the National Master. Nevertheless, even he could only speak half of it."
If one wishes to realize the Way in its entirety, the Tripitaka Master had already met the National Teacher even before he departed from the Western Heavens.
Fochuan Zong said: "The Tripitaka Master waited for the National Teacher to say, 'Where is he right now? and simply clapped his hands and laughed loudly;
this would have made it impossible for that National Teacher of a kingdom to provide any explanation. Longchi Zhen said:
"Let us set aside for a moment the fact that the Great and Small National Teachers were driven by the Tripitaka Master into having no place to hide.

But as for why they were not seen during the third time—Longchi said: 'Not only did the Tripitaka Master fail to find them, I dare guarantee that the National Teacher himself did not even know where they had gone. He then laughed loudly. Xianyan Jian said: "At that time..."
Waiting for the National Teacher to question him, [Yunmen] said, "Those who confess are exempt from punishment.
That Heart-Knowledge Tripitaka Master was far too coarse; the monkey watched as the boat was rowed away.
Facing the National Teacher, he could not be found—simply because he had been deceived by his own eyes all along. (Yezhu River)
Responding to the myriad capacities of beings, there must be a specific method. I do not yet know where to seek Nanyang.
Since losing the monkey, he has not performed on the bridge for a long time.

(Lan’an Shu) Concealing the blade and avoiding the arrow, the paths are a thousand differences; for ten thousand ages, the old master has been indulgent. It is truly wonderful that the heron cannot be found.
Abiding in the place, deep in the night, he dwells with the moon amidst the reeds.
(Iron Mountain Ren) When Master Guishan received a letter sent by Mazu via Xitang Zang, the Master asked, "What Dharma does your teacher preach?
Zang walked from west to east and stood there. The Master said, "Is that all? Is there something else? Zang then walked back from east to west.
He stood up. The Master said, "This is Master Ma’s; what about yours, worthy one? Zang replied, "I have already presented it to the Master."
Baofu Zhan said, "The Great Xitang has obscured Master Mazu by no small amount.
Falin Yin said, "Baofu only knows that Xitang obscured Master Mazu; he does not realize that the National Teacher himself has obscured even more."
The National Teacher asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From the South. The Master said, "What Dharma do the teachers of the South use to instruct people?
The monk replied, "The teachers of the South say that once the winds and fires [of death] have dispersed, it is like a snake shedding its skin or a dragon changing its bones;
one's original true nature remains perfectly intact and undestroyed. The Master said, "Alas! Alas! How bitter! The South... [text ends]
Fangzhishi said, "The Dharma you preach is half-existent and half-extinct. He asked, "I wonder, Master, with what Dharma do you instruct people?
The Master replied, "In this place of mine, body and mind are as one; there is nothing else outside the body.
Fangzhishi said, "How can you, Master, equate this bubble-like, illusory body with the essence of the Dharma? The Master said, "Why have you entered onto a deviant path? Fangzhishi said:
"In what place does such-and-such a person enter onto a deviant path? The Master said: "Have you not seen it taught in the scriptures:
'If one sees me by means of form, or seeks me by means of sound, this person follows a deviant path and cannot see the Tathāgata'?"
Yunmen Wenyan said: "Body and mind are as one; there is nothing outside of them. Where, then, could the mountains, rivers, and the great earth exist? Shending Yanzhen said:
"The National Teacher’s way of speaking leaves the head but lacks the tail. As for what was previously said about 'body and mind being as one,' where has that gone?
Jingci Chang said: "If that monk had waited at that moment for the National Teacher to say..."
"To see me by means of form, or to seek me by means of sound—such people walk upon a deviant path and cannot perceive the Tathāgata.
Yet [the National Teacher] merely said, "Alas! Alas! Half-living and half-extinguished, the Great and Small National Teachers [failed to resolve this].
Dongchan Guanzhuo said: "The National Teacher and that monk met through form and sound; they met apart from form and sound. If one were apart from form and sound, how would this differ from Nanquan?"

Now you understand that consciousness is half-arising and half-ceasing. If it were identical to form and sound, then the saying, "Seeking form through the eyes and sound through the ears is to practice a deviant path," would be contradicted.
Is there no one who can act as a master for the National Teacher? I must ask you this:
since body and mind are one and there is nothing outside the body, why is this bubble-like, illusory body not the same as the Dharma-body? Yuan Jieying said:
The Great and Small National Preceptors previously said that one does not construct villages in front nor shift shops behind;

since they taught that body and mind are as one, why did they further say that seeing with form and seeking with sound is practicing a deviant path? Wherein lies the intent of the National Preceptors?
A monk asked the National Teacher, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The ten thousand bodhisattvas in the Mañjuśrī Hall.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion."
At that time, vegetables were cheap; radish heads covered the ground. One could buy one for a single coin, and those who obtained them ate their fill with contented sighs.

(Fujian Qin) Seeking the Truth, I mistakenly entered the Isle of Penglai; the fragrant breeze never ceases as the pine flowers age. Where have you gone, gathering the mushrooms, that you have not yet returned?
"Come. White clouds fill the ground, yet no one sweeps it.
(Jik-dam-sim) The National Teacher was asked by Military Commissioner Yu, "How do you practice while residing at White Rock Mountain?

The Master called to his attendant boy, rubbed the boy's head with his hand, and said: "When it is clearly awake, speak directly as being clearly awake; when it is vividly distinct, speak directly as being vividly distinct. He then pointed toward...
Later, do not allow yourself to be deceived by others.
Baofu Zhan said, "The National Teacher was caught on the spot; he was left with his hands flustered and his feet in disarray. Falin Yin said:
