Once, when an ancient master did not go to the hall, his attendant requested that he attend. The Master said, "I have eaten my fill of oil-cakes on my estate.
The attendant said, "The Master has never gone out. The Master said, "Go and ask the estate manager. Only then did the attendant go out.
The Gate. Suddenly, the master of the estate arrives to thank the Abbot for coming to the estate to eat oil-cakes.
Jingshan Daokai says: "The Abbot did not attend the hall; the master of the estate thanks him for his deigning visit.
Once a word enters the gates of officialdom, nine oxen cannot pull it out. Xidun Chao says: "One person sees the hare and releases the hawk; the other takes what is wrong and makes it right."
Wrong! You may call them a pack of Puzhou men. Although this master of the monastery is indeed clever, he cannot help but move when pulled by the nose.
If I were the master of the monastery, I would simply let out a cold laugh in the face of that ancient worthy; I guarantee that the old fellow would be left with his face full of shame.
Nearby, it is on the edge of the lips; far away, it is in a land of river sands. How many people in the world do not get to eat oil-cakes?
(Gushan Gui) Riding a tiger through the marketplace, holding a torch to steal a pig: the master sleeps with eyes wide open, while the neighbor cries out that a donkey is lost.
(Wan’an Yan): Asafoetida has no true essence; mercury has no falsehood. The decrepit Master of Goose Lake—his conduct may be known. (Zhuan’an Gui):

The Queen Mother of the Penglai Immortals feasts at the Jade Pool; the immortal maidens lose their way across the waters while seeking her traces. It is only fitting that the woodcutter transmits the news.
Arrived! It turns out he was all along to the west of the desk mountain.
(Shi Zhao-ye) Since when did the ancient worthies ever move their lips? How many know how they ate their oil-cakes to satiety?
Now, reflecting in this cold stillness, I write my sorrows in secret—whom can I send them to? (Ken-tang Chong)
Having eaten the oil-cake, he did not attend the vegetarian feast. The Master of the Hermitage came specifically to thank the Teacher:
"He has searched through thousands of mountains and ten thousand waters, yet his eyes remain unopened as he kicks away his straw sandals.
(Wuzhuo’s General Verse): Zhang San is not yet dead; Li Si comes to demand his life. He brings trouble upon those in the eastern and western villages—Chen Liu and Wang Ba.
The official sale has exhausted my fields and gardens.
(Lüshi of Meng’an) Willow colors on the eastern street trail misty green; Peach blossoms in the western lane reflect one another in red. Looking left and right, I can never look enough;
All at once, they are entrusted to the east wind. (Yishi of Nan’an)
The people of Qin are accustomed to playing with the ball of Chu; they deceive the infant, chasing it in two directions.
Without the eastern wind to keep the rhythm, they will surely leave the scene in disarray upon the riverbanks.

(Apánzhū) Learning to play the lute, one uses a cotton bow; writing characters, one imitates the *kōudǒu* script. Heaven and Earth leak its primordial essence; children and grandchildren ruin their own hands.
Seeking like-minded companions within the kingdom of Campā; the red-haired Persian pounds grain in a wooden mortar.
(Jie Yanxiu) The hibiscus remains silent as dreams drift in a daze; the powdered butterfly steals the fragrance at its whim. There is no help for it, as the song from the painted tower begins again;
the yellow oriole refuses to roost upon the high branch. (Xue Qijing)
Half the rose trellis fills the courtyard with fragrance; with each passing breeze, it grows cooler.
Where last night’s fallen petals drifted and scattered, they have provoked the wandering bees to fly up and down in wild frenzy.

(Falin-yin) Shuttling the door to ply one's trade with feigned innocence—press once more, and the thief’s true form is revealed. If you can seize both the person and the stolen goods together, then...
"Defeated! Master Jiao, please excuse my coming to your door. (Three circles) An ancient worthy said:
"This one plot of land has been entrusted to you for how long now? I shall stand here on this very spot and wait for you to grasp it."
Fayan Yi said: "The mountain monk sits here now, waiting for you to grasp it. Is there any principle [to be found]? Which is intimate? Which is distant?
Try to judge for me. Zhaojue Qin said: "How much time has passed since this plot of ground was entrusted to me?
Today, before the assembly, I shall offer a celebratory confession. Huiyun Sheng said: "Three..."
This old man has cast his body among things; his compassionate heart is truly excessive. Yet, alas, the winds and waves seem difficult to reconcile.
I, this mountain monk, am otherwise. This very plot of land has been entrusted to me for how long! I am weary and wish to go to sleep.
Shishuang Zun said: "This one piece of ground has been entrusted [to you] for how long! Why is it that none of you can tread upon it?
It is simply because it is too clear; this very clarity causes what is attained to be delayed."
An ancient worthy was once asked by a monk, "The yang returns at the beginning of winter; the days grow longer by one thread. I wonder, how much does the Buddha-dharma grow?
The worthy replied, "It grows by one thread. He then asked another ancient worthy, who replied, "One thread grows."
Jianfu Can said: "Traveling the mountain path together as one, each person perceives the mist and clouds differently. Gaofeng Miao said:
"To strike a blow right in the nest—this returns to the two elders' own fundamental tongs and hammers. If you speak of the length or brevity of the Buddha-dharma, you have not yet seen it in a dream.
Today, if someone were suddenly to ask, "West Peak, how long is the Buddha-dharma? I would simply say: [The original text here implies a response that cuts off the inquiry].
He said to him: "Ten thousand *li* from east to west, eight thousand *li* from south to north. Xiang Tianxian remarked:
"Although these two elders possess the skillful means to patch up empty space, their red thread has not yet been severed; they merely make their livelihood out of long and short.
If someone were to ask such a question today, I would simply say to them: 'Do not compare lengths with a jade thread.'"
"Let us take this golden needle and embroider it for you to see.
An ancient worthy wrote the character for "mind" (心) on his gate, wrote the character for "mind" on his window, and wrote the character for "mind" on his wall.
Fayan Wenyi said: "On the gate, simply write the character for 'gate' (門); on the window, simply write the character for 'window' (窗); on the wall, simply write [the character for 'wall'] (壁)."
"Wall-character. Xuangjue then said: "Do not write the character 'gate' above the gate; do not write the character 'window' above the window; do not write the character 'wall' upon the wall. Why?
Because the meaning of the characters is already manifest. Longtang Zhu said: "Write the character 'window' above the gate;
write the character 'wall' above the window; write the character 'gate' upon the wall. Why? [Because] the East..."
The mountain stream flows westward; clouds rise from the southern peaks and the northern peaks. Baiyan Fu said: "The Elder commits the slander of contradiction;
Fayan commits the slander of superimposition; Xuangjue commits the slander of negation; Longtang commits the slander of frivolous proliferation.
These four fellows have been found guilty and their cases closed. Is there anyone who still feels dissatisfied? Come forward and try!"
"Strain your eyes to look at one head. Shengkeyu said: "Building a ten-thousand-li wall reaching from the sea to Mount Dai, firmly consolidating the old mountains and rivers;
Zhong Kui pastes the door-god at midnight, pasting until dawn to look at his own self. Laughing, he points to the image of the door-god himself."
One does not even know that one is oneself a gate-guarding deity.
(Tian'an Sheng) Everything rises higher and higher; reaching the very peak, it is difficult to turn back. Strike a thought and look closely:
why was it established in such a manner at that time? (Lanfang Da)
Let the myriad phenomena be subject to the True Eye; what need is there to debate right and wrong?
Who can lightly raise a single arrowhead and, having straightaway shattered the three barriers, return with the song of victory? (The Great Play) An ancient worthy said:
"The Patriarch faced the wall for nine years in search of one who could understand him. If you understand it in this way, you will eat iron.
"The staff will have its day. Furthermore, another veteran elder said: "The Patriarch sat facing the wall for nine years; how can you not feel shame?
If you understand it in this way, you must buy straw sandals and travel on foot for thirty more years."
Langya Jue said: "Since that is not so, tell me: what was the meaning of the Patriarch’s wall-gazing? After a long silence, he said:
"If you wish to avoid incurring karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the True Dharma-Wheel of the Tathāgata.
Tiantong Jie said: "The two elders were merely knocking on bricks and beating tiles; Langya Jue painted a tiger and ended up with a wildcat. If you all wish to see the face of the Patriarch—"
What is the underlying meaning? A bottomless pit is difficult to fill.
An ancient worthy said: "The Buddha-dharma is vast indeed; it is simply a toothache. Jingshan Hongzhi said:
"I told you not to travel the road beneath the mountain; now you truly hear the heart-rending cry of the monkey. Sheng.
Fayun said: "If one were Tao Yuanming, one would have knit one's brows and returned home immediately.
An ancient worthy said: "That which is long is the long Dharmakāya; that which is short is the short Dharmakāya."
Tiantong Jue said: "Tell me, what does the Śūnyatā-deva call when he speaks of the Dharma-body? After a long silence, he said:
"One must not shorten the ducks or cut the cranes, nor level the mountains or fill the valleys."
An ancient worthy asked, "Three years ago I took the life of one person, and today I am filled with sorrow and anxiety night and day.
How can I avoid this [karmic retribution]?
Lü Yujiao said, "Fortunately, there is no corroborating witness. Falin Yin said, "His breath has not yet ceased."
An ancient worthy did not speak of the Dharma for others throughout an entire summer retreat. A monk sighed and said, "I have merely passed this summer in vain.
I do not dare hope that the Master will preach the Buddha-Dharma, but it would be enough for me to hear even two words of the True Cause."
Upon hearing this, an old master said, "Dharma brother, do not speak so hastily. If we speak of the true cause, there is not even a single character.
Having finished speaking, he tapped his teeth and said, "Just now, I spoke without reason; it was not right to say such a thing.
An old master in the neighboring wall heard this and said, "What a fine pot of soup that has been defiled by a single pellet of rat droppings!"
Baoci then questioned him, saying: "Tell me, is this a word of praise or a word of refusal?
If it is praise, why did he say, 'It has been defiled by mouse droppings'? If it is a refusal, what fault is there? Can you verify this? Cui峰 Xian said:
"In whose household are there not one or two grains [of rice] in the pot? Falín Yīn said: "One who confesses is exempted from punishment."
Huanglong Qing said: "The two old masters saw only the sharpness of the chisel's tip, but not the squareness of the chisel's head.
As for this monk, he dares not hope that the Master will preach the Buddha-dharma; even to hear the two characters of 'the True Cause' would suffice. Is this so, or is it not?
Those who investigate the profound mysteries must possess the eye that penetrates all quarters; they should skillfully discern the ancient and the modern within words. — Jingshan Xiu.

It is said: "This assembly has created trouble where there was none. The elder administered medicine according to the illness; the thread went out and the silk came in, and the needlework was sewn so that no seam was visible.
Yet, alas, they have still not realized the final phrase. As for the elder next door acting in this manner—how is he to be understood?
The Three Ministers must all be exhorted together.
Throughout the summer, he prepared a single pot of soup. Even at Mount Fuyan, they would not yet allow him to vie for equality.
Do not say it was defiled and no one saw; the single eye of the neighboring wall-dwelling Chan master is clear.
(Zhengjue Yi) During the long summer there was no other pursuit; he prepared a single pot of soup. Its flavor was quite fragrant, yet it left a stain upon the firm ground.
The mouth is the gate of calamity; the tongue is the axe that hews the body. To add three catties of iron is solely because one gazes upon the rusted bolt.
(Cishou Shen) The clear, cold stream weeps in the autumn ravine; as soon as one understands the vast ocean, one sets sail. It is said that Xu You once washed his ears here.
[The Master] said: "How pitiful that Chao Fu further whipped his ox!
(Xutang Yu) Once a word has been uttered, even four horses cannot overtake it. Having spoken the Way, how can one regret it?
Coldly exposed by others, he clenches his jaw; his mouth is too weary to open. (Wumen Chan)
An ancient worthy kept a young attendant who was entirely ignorant of proper etiquette. When a wandering monk arrived at the hermitage, he instructed the boy in the morning and evening rites.
Later that evening, seeing the elder returning from outside, the boy went forward to offer his greetings.
The old master was astonished and asked, "Who taught you? The boy replied, "The head monk in the hall. The old master immediately summoned that monk and questioned him:
"Head monk, what kind of mental conduct is this of yours to frequent the homes of others?
This boy has been raised by me for two or three years; he is naturally pitiable. Who taught you to corrupt him and dress him up in such a way?"
He departed in haste. At twilight, drenched by the rain, he was chased out by him. Fayen Yi said:
"The ancients revealed such a fragment of their family style; how extraordinary! But tell me, what was the intent? Falin Yin said:
"Why did that monk not then turn back and say: 'If so, then the hermitage...'"
The Master should indeed leave the hospital; let us see how he will arrange his affairs.
An ancient worthy, when asked by a monk, "What serves as the vessel for crossing over birth and death? replied, "When the year ends, do not burn paper money."
When the year ends, no money is burned; rat holes are pierced by snakes. Even if one attains profound realization, they face each other across the Western Heaven.
(Cao Yuan Sheng) An ancient worthy, when asked by a monk, "What is it like when the year is exhausted and the age comes to an end? the Worthy said, "Every household looks out upon the wilds."
Fox cub! Every household watches this wild fox cub. He holds his iron flute crosswise and blows it in a chaotic, disordered fashion. Having finished blowing, he knows not where he has gone;
the evening sun is already hanging low over the western tips of the willow branches. (Songyuan Yue)
Every household looks upon the wild fox cubs; though many see them, those who truly recognize them are few. A hundred monsters and a thousand demons have all left their tracks behind;
the spring breeze has already reached the ten-thousand-year-old branch. (Huisou Guang) An ancient worthy offered this saying:
"A single thatched toilet is erected in the middle of the crossroads, yet it is strictly forbidden for anyone to defecate there."
Later, when a monk brought this up to Nantang Jing, Nantang said, "You have already defecated; what more do you want me to defecate?
When Xiu heard this, he burned incense, looked toward Nantang from afar, and prostrated in gratitude.
The Fifth Patriarch Jiao said: "Nantang knew it and yet committed the offense; this old master was caught in a single instance.
Examining this from the start, it does not go beyond the understanding of 'passing excrement.'"

An ancient worthy said: "When the sun rises, the light of the mind shines; when the heavens are overcast, the nature-ground is dark. Those who do not know heaven and earth fail to realize that the Way of firmness possesses both Qian and Kun.
Nan-shi Xi said: "To speak in such a manner—those who have attained thorough awakening throughout the past and present are as numerous as rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds. To misunderstand it is..."
[They] are like rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds. With a whisk, he draws a line and says:
"The Anavatapta Lake is forty yojanas deep and forty yojanas wide."
An ancient worthy once had a statue of a holy monk being dripped upon by a leak from the roof. Someone asked him, "Since this is a holy monk, why is there a leak?
The Worthy had no reply. Tiantai Shaodai remarked, "Being free from outflows (*anāsrava*) does not constitute being a holy monk. Falin Yin remarked, "The Elder understands clearly."
With a thatched roof over his head, he had five thousand disciples in coarse woolen robes.
An ancient worthy composed a verse: "A single void atop the mountain of the five aggregates; Entering and exiting through the same gate, yet we do not meet.
For immeasurable kalpas, I have lived in a rented house; To the very end, I did not know the true host."
An elder said: "Since you did not recognize him [the Buddha], whom did you ask when you first rented [this robe]?
Because of this, when an ancient worthy was asked by a monk, "What is it like before an ancient mirror has been polished? the Worthy said, "No effort is applied.
The monk asked, "What is it like after it has been polished? The Worthy said, "It does not reflect."
The *Longchi chuanbie* (The Transmission of the Dragon Pond) says: "How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? He replied, "One sees brightness but does not see darkness.
"And how is it after it has been polished? He replied, "One sees darkness but does not see brightness."
An ancient worthy asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From East River.

The Master said, "With twin streams and solitary pines, the smoke clear and the moon white—where is the master of the seat, the Upādhyāya? The monk said, "As soon as I arrived at Dong'an, I was met with this question."
The Master said, "To record the sword and carve the boat; to break the pearl to seek its reflection—is this not your realm, Reverend? Go and drink tea.
[The monk] asked, "Who is the true master of Dong'an? The Master said, "A colt on the road cannot surpass a Huailiu steed."
The monk prostrated. The Master said, "A foreigner beating a drum—there is no rhythm at all in his dancing.
Xianyan Jian said, "The ancient worthy sold rice with the husks still on; this monk has stolen the weeds and claimed them as his own. If he were the true master," [he would have been different].
Neither of us yet knows where we are.
The sun’s staff rises with the dawn over the azure peaks; ten thousand valleys and a thousand crags reveal a vast and open atmosphere.
Who would have thought that wind and clouds possess such shifting moods? In an instant, rain and mist fill the mountains and rivers. (Yongning Ding)
There were two ancient masters who lived in hermitages for ten days without meeting. One day they encountered each other.
The master of the upper hermitage asked, "I have not seen you for a long time; where have you been? The master of the lower hermitage replied, "I have been in my hermitage building a seamless stūpa.
The master of the upper hermitage said, "I also wish to build one. Please lend me the mold for the stūpa so that I may see it. The master of the lower hermitage... [proceeded to give it].
The Master said, "Why did you not speak sooner? It has just been borrowed by someone.
Fayen Yi further questioned him, saying, "Tell me, was it borrowed from him or not?"
A seamless stupa-casket that neither hand can lift; it has been borrowed by someone and remains unreturned to this day.
Before one has even finished searching, how many have already been known among gods and men?

(Yue’an Guo) It was just right when it was borrowed away by someone. Do not say that the neighbor’s house will not admit you; it is perfectly round and seamless, making it difficult to set down a brush.
There are merely one or two layers of mist and clouds. (Shílín Gǒng)
An elder master was visited by a monk who came to pay his respects. Finding that the master was not present, the monk went to see the attendant.

The attendant asked, "Have you yet paid your respects to the Master? The monk replied, "No. The attendant then pointed to a dog and said, "If you wish to see the Master, simply prostrate yourself to this dog.
The monk was left speechless. Later, when the ancient worthy returned and heard of this, he asked, "What do you say to this?"
To avoid being speechless, Yunmen Wenyan said, "If you wish to examine the master, first examine the disciple.
Falin Yin spoke on his behalf, saying only, "Wait until the Master returns; do not say that I was speechless."
While the Head of the Assembly was reciting the name of Amitābha, his junior attendant called out, "Preceptor! When the Preceptor turned around, the junior attendant did not respond.
This occurred several times, until the Preceptor rebuked him. The junior attendant said, "How many years has it been since you have called him that he responds?
But as soon as I call him, he flies into a rage."
Shi’an Fēngdài said in his stead, “I am not as good as you. Fālín Yīn said in his stead, “When you were committing evil, did you give rise to a realization?
When the monk entered the underworld, he saw Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, who asked him what kind of practice he had cultivated throughout his life. The monk replied, ‘I recited the Dharma...’”
In the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, it is said: "Stop, stop! There is no need to speak; my Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive. When asked, "Will you speak or not?
the monk remained silent. Baoshou Xinda said in his place: "Why must it be proclaimed again? Guizong Rou said in his place: "This time I shall return. (He then departed.)
"Please circulate this. Lüyùjiāo said: "In that case, one may turn it over for merit as the occasion arises.
Fālínyī spoke on his behalf: "Great Being, do not forget these words after thirty years."
An old master was asked by someone: "Fish take water as their life; why then do they die in water?
Tianlong Ji said, "Why does it not go to the shore to die? Lüyùjiāo said, "There is nowhere to go.
Yú'ān Jí said, "It is afraid of rotting away. Fālín Yīn spoke on his behalf, saying, "The boatman's son."
While he was away, a monk from Yun’gai Mountain requested tiles for the construction of a hall. Someone asked him, "Since you are already at Yun’gai, why do you need to beg for tiles?
The monk had no reply.
Lü Yujiao spoke in his place, saying: "In spring, there are not three days of clear weather. Falinyin spoke in his place, saying: "Your efforts have been in vain.
A person from Goryeo came to Qiantang to carve a sacred image of Avalokiteśvara; when it was lifted onto the boat, it could not be moved at all.
Consequently, he was invited to enter Kaiyuan Temple in Mingzhou to receive offerings. Later, someone raised this question: "There is no land where you do not manifest your form;
why then does the sacred image not go to the kingdom of Goryeo?"
Changqing Ling said: "Though his manifestation is universal, seeing the image gives rise to partiality.
Fayan Yi said: "Do you recognize Guanyin yet? Xia'an Yu said: "Sentient beings are inverted; deluded about themselves, they pursue external objects. Falin Yin spoke on their behalf, saying:
"Do not say that this mountain monk’s command does not go forth."

There was a monk who, while reciting a scripture with a boy, instructed the boy to place it inside a case. The boy asked, "Where shall I place that which you, Venerable Sir, have been reciting? The monk had no reply.
Xikenshen said: "Why does this monk not speak? Look at his mess! It may be so, but it is like a *gāmbhārī* fruit before the wind and a *nārikela* fruit under the sun.
Falin Yin spoke on his behalf: "This lad is so dull-witted!"
The Librarian asked a monk, "Why do you not read the scriptures? The monk replied, "I do not know how to read. The Librarian said, "Why do you not ask someone else?
The monk held out his hand and asked, "What kind of characters are these? The Librarian was speechless.
Master Falin’s commentary says: "The former words do not accord with the subsequent speech.
A precious sword in the sleeve brushes against the stars; a numinous talisman behind the elbow illuminates the eight directions.
Having turned the pivot of the sun, let the world below remain vast and boundless. (Shuan-an Yan)
Standing like cranes, crawling like snakes, their momentum never ceases; the Brahmī script of the Five Indias brings grief to ghosts and spirits.
None among the disciples of Confucius recognize it; the blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head. (By Hui of Yukan) An elder asked a presiding master:

"Regarding the commentaries and sub-commentaries that explain the meaning [of the sutras], how do they differ in their breadth and brevity? The master replied: "The sub-commentary explains the commentary."
The Sub-commentary (Shu) explains the Sūtra. On the previous day, [the Master] asked, "What does the Sūtra explain? The Host had no reply.
Falinyin spoke on his behalf, saying: "Does the one who gave you food to eat at the foot of the mountain possess eyes, or not?"
A lifetime’s accumulated karma is suddenly either partial or complete; opening the mouth, all is revealed—every word is profound.
When pressed to the point where the patterns intertwine and the corners join, the green mountains are locked in emerald, and the drifting mists are severed.
(Suan Ding) A monk from Liutong Monastery in Taizhou was about to board a boat when someone asked him: "Since you possess the six supernatural powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), why..."
"Rent a boat. The monk remained silent.
Tiantai Shao (Tianxi Shao) of the Song dynasty said, "I did not wish to startle the assembly. Lüyù Jiao (Lüyù Zhao) of the Song dynasty said, "When reason prevails, one follows it."
Falin’s voice echoed through the ages, saying: "In the past, when someone asked me such a question, I answered just as I have today.
A monk living in a hermitage in Guangnan encountered a great king on a hunting expedition. When the attendants announced, "The Great King is coming; rise! the monk said:
"It is not only when the Great King comes that you do not rise; even when the Buddha comes, you do not rise. The King then asked the monk, "Is it not true that he is your teacher?
The monk replied, "Yes. The King said, "If so, why do you not rise upon seeing your teacher? The monk was speechless.
Fayan Yi’s successor said: "It is not yet sufficient to repay his kindness. Baoning Yong’s successor said:
"My acquaintances fill the world, but today I have met one such person. Tianning Qi said: "If you wish to observe the teacher, first observe the disciple.
Bairan Fu’s successor said: "If the son is not honored, the father will not be revered. Hezhu Qian said: "Today I have come out for a small matter."
A great encounter. Lü Yujiao said in his place: "This is not my humble way of seeing it. Falin Yin said in his place:
"The officials have troubled you today to provide this testimony."
When a monk arrived, Caoxi’s robe-and-bowl attendant held up the robe and said, "This is that which could not be lifted at the head of Mount Dayu.
The monk asked, "Why is it now in your hands, Venerable? The attendant was speechless.

Yunmen Wenyan said, "Both [sides] fail to understand. He further provided a substitute response for the point where there is no speech, saying, "To hear from afar is not as good as arriving in person.
He also said, "This is a lion cub. Tianye Zhuan said, "The one who carries his life is caught on the hook.
He also said, "The Great Master entered extinction long ago. Falin Yin provided a substitute response, saying, "A fellow who shifts the tray while eating his meal."
There was a practitioner who followed a Dharma Master into the Buddha hall. He spat toward the Buddha. The Dharma Master said, "Practitioner, you lack propriety;
why do you spit at the Buddha? The practitioner replied, "I thought this was not a place where there is a Buddha, so I came here to spit on someone.
The Dharma Master had no words.
Guishan Lingyou said, "The benevolent person is actually the non-benevolent person; the non-benevolent person is actually the benevolent person.

Yangshan Huiji, acting on behalf of the Dharma Master, simply spat at the practitioner. If the practitioner had anything to say, Yangshan would have told him, "Bring me back to the place where there is no practitioner.
Zifu Daolun, acting on behalf of the Dharma Master, simply struck him. He further remarked, "This only saves half."
Tianye said, "Close the dog's mouth during the day. Falin said, "When there is no Buddha, what is the use of spitting?
The attendant at the Si-zhou Pagoda locked the door at the proper time. Someone asked, "Since you are the Great Master of the Three Realms," [why do you lock the door?]
"Why was the disciple locked up? The attendant had no reply.
Fayan spoke on his behalf, saying, "The disciple locked him; the Master locked him. Fadeng spoke on his behalf, saying, "Give me back the key!"
The Elder replied on his behalf: "The lock of Jizhou; the lock of Qianzhou. Falin Yin replied on his behalf, merely handing over the key and saying: "Receive it securely."
The intent behind locking the gates at this very moment is profound. When questioned, one clearly distinguishes the false from the true.
Who would have known that upon the peach and plum trees in the third month, the reds and whites are but the manifestation of the spring?

(Zhiguanhui) There was a practitioner of the Way sitting with his back turned before the Buddha Hall. A monk said, "Practitioner of the Way, do not turn your back on the Buddha. The practitioner of the Way replied:
"Virtuous One, according to the fundamental teachings, the Buddha-body pervades the Dharma-realm.
Where could you possibly sit? The monk had no reply.
Fayyan spoke on his behalf: "I recognize you. Falinyin spoke on his behalf: "You have come before this mountain monk once again to act like a fool."
At Yantai, the mountain master arrived at Yuan Tongyuan to visit. The First Seat asked, "Yuantong has no path;
how did the mountain master manage to arrive? The master was speechless.
Gui-zong Rou spoke on his behalf, saying: "Unexpectedly, we meet again. Fa-lin Yin spoke on his behalf, saying:
"In the official records, why is there a surname but no given name?"
Someone asked a monk, "What kind of lamp do you light? The monk replied, "A perpetually burning lamp. [The person] asked, "When was it lit? The monk said, "It was lit last year.
[The person] asked, "Where is the perpetual burning? The monk was speechless.
Changqing Lingmo’s verse says: "If it were not like this, I would know you do not allow yourself to be deceived. Fayan’s alternative verse says:
"Profit moves the gentleman. Falin Yin’s verse says: "How many people have you questioned thus far?"
Laozi, Li Dan, the Pillar Scribe, said: "The Dao is profound and still, as if perhaps existing. I do not know whose son it is;
it is like that which precedes the Emperor.
Gao Feng Miao remarked: "Alas! This fellow has wrongly added a footnote. 'Profound and still, as if perhaps existing'—I do not know..."
"Whose son is he? He is the Elder Vimalakīrti within the city of Vaiśālī. The Old Master said:
"When those of superior capacity hear the Way, they practice it with diligence; when those of middling capacity hear the Way, they are as if it exists and yet as if it does not."
"The man of inferior capacity hears the Way and laughs at it. Jianfu Can said:
"The man of superior capacity hears the Way and practices it with diligence; what a state of frantic urgency! The man of middling capacity hears the Way and is as if it exists, as if it does not;
he still has some measure of discernment. The man of inferior capacity hears the Way and laughs at it—this, however, possesses the spirit of a patch-robed monk."
[The Master] sighed. "Three types of people have been simultaneously settled. Now tell me, which of these is worthy of receiving offerings from devas and humans?
Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty visited Xiangguo Temple and asked a monk, "What sutra are you studying?
The monk replied, "The *Benevolent Kings Sutra* (*Renwang Jing*). The Emperor said, "Since this is my sutra, why is it in your hands? The monk was speechless.
Xuedou Xian spoke on his behalf: "The August Heaven has no partiality; it aids only virtue. Tianning Qi said:
"If you ask Yongzuo, he will simply hold the sutra over his head with both hands and say, 'Ten thousand years! Ten thousand years! Xuexuan Cheng said: "The words of the King are like fine silk;
once they issue forth, they are like coarse thread. Bairan Fu said: "I am not like that old scholar Xuedou. I would wait—"

The Emperor asked, "I have merely received this specifically for Your Majesty’s circulation. If it were another king who was a true master of the Way, how would he respond when asked what the single phrase for circulation is?
He then joined his palms and said, "The *Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā-sūtra*, Fascicle Two."
Shifeng Xunda said, "I, this humble one, have today a share in expressing gratitude. Falin Yin said on his behalf, "Your Majesty’s words in years past were not as ambiguous as they are today."
The Emperor Taizong visited the Kaibao Pagoda and asked, "Who are you? The monk replied, "I am the master of this pagoda.
The Emperor said, "Since this is my pagoda, why do you act as its master? The monk was speechless.
Cui Feng Xian spoke on behalf [of the assembly], saying: "The entire nation knows this. Xiao An Yu spoke on behalf [of the assembly], saying: "Who dares to move it?
Fa Lin Yin spoke on behalf [of the assembly], saying: "At the time of Longguang Buddha, one would have completely forgotten it."
When the monk came for an audience with the Emperor Taizong, the Emperor asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Wo-yun Hermitage on Mount Lu.
The Emperor said, "I have heard that where the clouds rest deeply, one does not pay court to the sovereign. For what reason have you come here? The monk was speechless.
Cui Feng Xian’s turn of phrase was: “It is difficult to escape the ultimate transformation. Baoshou Fang’s turn of phrase was: “An unlearned dead man. He also said:
“I especially thank Your Majesty for your inquiry. Furi Zhe’s turn of phrase was: “It is simply because we parted at Vulture Peak.”
Master Falin’s verse says: “This poor monk has large eyes; thank heaven for the eyebrows that shield them. I ask the traveler deep in the clouds:
how shall you answer when asked about the peace and prosperity? The vast transformation is impossible to evade;
across ten thousand miles of distant sky, but a single speck of cloud. (Beijian Jian’er)
Not turning away from the imperial countenance even at a distance of a few inches, my stubborn resolve still recalls the old mountains.
If you would truly grant yourself to the state, we shall together enjoy the years of Great Peace.
Beneath the White Cloud Rock, he does not crave leisure; he simply wishes to strike open the golden lock and gate. It is not that he has no mind to escape into transformation;
for the most part, he intentionally seeks to behold the countenance of Yao. (At this point, the Emperor recited:
The Emperor Taizong, upon being informed by a monk that the Tripitaka had been consumed by fire, wished to request its imperial restoration. The Emperor summoned him to inquire about the past.
"Previously, Fotuo Moteng was not burned; why is it that today he is burned? The monk had no reply. Cui Feng Xian spoke on his behalf:
"Your Majesty does not forget the entrustment. Bai Yan Fu spoke on his behalf: "I know Your Majesty does not begrudge the precious treasury.
Lü Yu Jiao spoke on his behalf: "The imperial decree does not fail to reach its destination. Fa Lin Yin spoke on his behalf: [He remained silent].
"The Mātanga of old; the Mātanga of today.
When the monk entered to have an audience with Emperor Taizong, he addressed him, saying, "Does Your Majesty still remember this humble monk? The Emperor asked, "Where did we last meet?
He replied, "We parted at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, and it has been until this very day. The Emperor asked, "By what means [did you come]?"
[The Emperor] asked for verification. The monk had no reply.
Cui-feng Xian spoke on his behalf, saying: "This poor monk has come specifically for this purpose. Chong-hua Neng spoke on behalf of the monk, picking up his whisk.
Bai-yan Fu spoke on his behalf, saying: "I thought Your Majesty had forgotten. Fa-lin Yin spoke on his behalf, saying: "Salt."
Tea, cloth bags, and money—someone has returned them all.
Two thousand years since our parting at Vulture Peak; that we meet again, O Holy Sovereign, could it be by mere chance?
Gently scooping up clear spring water to wipe my aged eyes, I push aside the clouds and mist to behold the blue sky. (Shixi Yue)

One day, Emperor Taizong held up his alms bowl and asked Prime Minister Wang Sui, "Since it is something that cannot be lifted at the head of Mount Dayu, why is it now in my hands? Wang Sui had no reply.
Ciming Yuan spoke on behalf [of the Emperor], saying: "Your Majesty possesses great power. Falin Yin spoke on behalf [of the Emperor], saying:
"Today, this subject shall settle the case of Mount Dayu.
The entire earth is gathered back into the space of my grasp; what difficulty is there in lifting up the alms bowl? To whom can the message within this be entrusted?"
It is truly so. The autumn waters, autumn clouds, and the chill of an autumn night.
(Yunna Qing) Emperor Taizong once dreamed of a divine being who exhorted him to arouse the *bodhicitta*. The following day, he questioned his court ministers, "How does one arouse the *bodhicitta*?
None of the ministers could provide an answer.
Cui Feng Xian’s commentary states: "Truly unheard of in antiquity or today. Bie Feng Yin’s commentary states: "The words of a king are like a fine thread;
their execution is like a heavy cord. Fa Lin Yin’s commentary states: "The Vinaya contains explicit regulations."
How is the wondrous mind of Bodhi brought forth? Responding to ten thousand occasions throughout the day, it is fundamentally never mistaken.
To turn one’s head and glance at it even for a moment—suddenly, the entire great chiliocosm is the Imperial House.

(Songyuan Yue) Ten thousand miles of songs of praise proclaim the Sage’s transformation; with gentle breezes and timely rains, woodcutters and farmers rejoice. Had it not been for the three shouts at Mount Song, [the world would have remained in darkness].
Afterwards, when there are no more elephants, who will know true Great Peace?

(Shuangshan Yuan) To give rise to the Bodhicitta is not difficult; it lies within a single thought-moment of the Sovereign. Sages have transmitted this to one another, all following the same principle;
may the enduring reign of the state remain as secure as Mount Tai. (Xin’an Chou)
When National Teacher Jì presented the "Diagram of the Three Realms" to Emperor Taizong, the Emperor asked, "In which realm do I reside? Jì had no reply.
Lüyǔjiāo said, "It is entirely within the transformative nourishment of Your Majesty. Fālín yīn spoke on his behalf, saying, "This time, this poor monk shall never again present such a diagram."
When Emperor Taizu of the Ming dynasty was at Tianjie Temple, he heard the sound of a fish-drum. He asked a monk, "Whose meal for the monastics is this?

The monk replied, "None. The Emperor said, "Whose vow is being fulfilled? The monk replied, "None. The Emperor said, "If there is truly nothing at all, then you ought to sit in silent seclusion facing a wall to investigate your original nature. Why do you chatter on like this?"
Qixuan said: "The intent of the Iron-Wheel King pervades the entire realm; even if a thousand sages were to appear, they could not shift it by so much as a hair’s breadth.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of this profound stillness? Xuan said, "Moving! Moving!"

The Garrison Commander of Qiantang was stationed at the border as a local commander. Whenever he saw a monk, he would question him; if they reached a mutual accord, he would invite the monk to stay the night.
One day, two monks arrived, and he asked, "Where have you recently come from? They replied, "From the place of Master Mazu in Jiangxi.
The Commander asked, "What kind of skillful means does Master Mazu have? They said, "He says, 'Ordinary mind is the Way; this very mind is Buddha. Upon hearing this, the Commander immediately...
He was ushered out. Two other monks arrived and questioned him as before. When the monk said, "Neither mind nor Buddha," he was again ushered out.
Both the "is" and the "is not" were requested to be expelled; towering ten thousand fathoms high like a standing wall, his lifelong heart and gall were laid bare before others.
Tilting. Acquaintances are treated as if they were strangers.
(Wuji Pai) Beneath the azure oil-canopy banner, you have established meritorious deeds; in both strategy and tactics, you alone are seen by me.
Since you first came with a sincere heart to serve the state, the sounding of the *diaodou* drums at the frontier has never been heard. (Xutang Yu)
Cutting through the Han, carving the clouds upon a thousand-fathom cliff—lofty and upright, truly a place where even birds find it hard to perch.
Let the migrating geese and flying monkeys pass as they will; they only add to the evening’s cry of the cold cicadas.
(Dào Lǒngxīng) The natural bone and structure of this being defy kings and lords. It did not dwell in Qin, nor did it remain in Han. Countless falling flowers are swept away by the wind.
All spent; the remaining fragrance fills the ground—who will gather it?

(An Old Poem) When Layman Han was asked by the assembly to serve as the presiding mourner for Sanping’s passing, he covered the *caopao* gong with a handkerchief, placed a single sword across its top, and set it before the shrine, saying:
"If you can speak the Way, you may act as the presiding mourner. The assembly was unable to respond.
[The Master] said, “Yes. The officer then kicked over the cooking cauldron and wept, crying out, “Heaven! Heaven! My late teacher is far away! Luoshan Xian remarked, “Alas!
How extraordinary, how extraordinary! The six hundred or so disciples under Sanping have all been swallowed up by this worldly fellow.
Had Old Teacher Chen been there at that time, he would have simply covered [the officer’s] head with a three-foot length of cloth.”
Transversely across [the altar] lies a blade with its edge exposed; lifting up the mourning curtain, he sits in the hall. Observe this man of the Han family:
he cannot help but act as the presiding mourner, yet he cannot help but refrain from acting as the presiding mourner. To advance toward him, there must be ritual propriety.
Tui-zhi (Han Yu) was required to observe the proper rites.
While he was composing his "Discourse on the Non-existence of Ghosts" late at night with his brush in hand, he suddenly saw a ghost appear and say:
"You claim there are no ghosts; here I am!"
Dongshan Yanguan, acting as the representative, made the gesture of a sparrowhawk and said, "Gu-gu-ku. Lingyin Yuan, placing his hand upon his forehead, asked, "What is it like?
Falin Yin, acting as the representative, merely called out, "Quickly bring paper and brush!"
Once, an elder had a monk entrusted with his alms bowl who was bitten by a dog while at his home.
The elder then pointed to the *kāṣāya* the monk was wearing and said, "A dragon will not swallow even a single thread worn by it;
the Great Master wears the full dharma robes—why, then, has he been bitten by a dog? The monk was speechless.
Baohua Ren’s substitute said: "Before examining the soil on the mountain peak, one first observes the master beneath the eaves. Guanzhi Li’s substitute said:
"The mountain monk’s year of birth falls under the *kan* hexagram; his destiny is beset by the 'double death' (*chongsha*) star. Falin Yin’s substitute said: "Layman, you have been so ungrateful!"
A donor entered the monastery and offered "money according to seniority" for the community of monks. The administrative monk said, "Place one portion before the Holy Monk (the Buddha).
The donor asked, "How old is the Holy Monk? The monk had no reply.
Fayan Yi’s substitute said: "One knows it immediately when the heart's aspiration is fulfilled. Baoning Yong’s substitute said: "I only fear that the donor’s power may not reach [the goal].
Tianning Qi’s substitute said: "The alms bowl has no bottom. Baoshou Fang’s substitute said:
"If it is so, then the assembly shall not receive even half a coin today. Guanzhi Li’s substitute said: "Just now..."
What was formerly one part has now become two parts. Falingyin (Fa-lin-yin) said on his behalf: "It can be digested; it can be digested.
A certain official entered the Tianwang Monastery in Zhenzhou and, upon seeing the divine image, asked the monastery director, "Who is the merit-donor for this?
He replied, "The Guardian King of the State. The official said, "Does he protect only this country, or does he protect all others as well?"

The Master said, "In Qin it is Qin; in Chu it is Chu. The Official asked, "On the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month, when the city of Zhenzhou is broken open, where will the Heavenly King go? The Master had no reply.
Falin’s verse says: "Official, you have no use for me here. The green mountains daily rub against the heavens;

The flowing waters year by year wash the heart of the sea. When the wild waves have subsided and not a drop remains, One searches in vain for the mud and water that once permeated the whole body. (Qingshan Ding)
Once, there was a man riding a donkey who asked a group of monks where they were going. The monks replied, "To the site of enlightenment (the *bodhimaṇḍa*).
The man said, "Where is it that is not the site of enlightenment? A monk struck him with his fist and said, "This fellow has no sense!
You ride your donkey right into the site of enlightenment and do not dismount. The man was left speechless.

Baoneng Xiu said: "Everyone says this fellow has a head but no tail; he can act, but cannot carry through. What they fail to realize is that this monk’s earlier words do not accord with his later ones.
Since one knows that every lifting and placing of the foot is itself the site of enlightenment (dōjō), how can there be such a discrepancy?"
Why do you not realize that riding a donkey or mounting a horse is nothing other than Buddha-work? Wansong wishes to settle this unresolved case;
let me further provide a detailed analysis for you. You lack the spirit to take a blow—O monks of Maoguang and Duzhen, you have already failed to exert yourselves to the utmost;
how can you afford to miss the mark? The site of enlightenment is but one; the Buddha-dharma is fundamentally not manifold. I leave it to you, O *śrāmaṇera*.
"Dao," he said, "Oṃ sarva. Longtang Zhu remarked, "This monk is far too coarse; he is beating people about haphazardly within the Dharma hall.
Falinyin merely laughed and said, "I did not expect that even those who have left the household life could possess such vulgar habits."
On the road to Linyang, there was an old woman who made her living selling cakes. When Deshan first left Sichuan, he went to her to buy some cakes for his morning meal.
The woman pointed to his carrying pole and asked, "What texts are on the head of this venerable monk?
Deshan replied, "The *Commentary on the Blue Dragon*. The woman asked, "Which sutra does that commentary explain? He said, "The *Diamond Sutra*. The woman said, "I have a question for you."
If he replied that he had received some refreshments, [the Master] said, "If you did not receive any, then go elsewhere to buy some.
The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* states: "The past mind cannot be apprehended; the present mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended.
I do not know which mind the Venerable One intends to refresh. The Master remained silent.
Tiantong Wu said: "If I were Deshan, I would simply say, 'The monk in my belly is hungry; select the largest ones and bring them here quickly.
Once they had been brought, I would shoulder them and depart immediately. This would ensure that the old woman was left in a state of total doubt."
Qixia Chengyun said, "Today this mountain monk is weary. Falin Yin stepped forward and said on his behalf, "This *dianxin* (refreshment) is only fit for old ladies to eat."
A certain old woman had supported a mountain hermit for twenty years, constantly employing a young girl to serve him.
One day, she ordered the girl to embrace the hermit firmly and asked, "At such a moment as this, what is it? The hermit replied, "A withered tree leans against a cold cliff;
throughout the three months of winter, there is no warmth. The girl returned and reported this to the old woman. The woman said, "For twenty..."
After receiving offerings for a year, she obtained a common man and consequently sent him away, burning down the hermitage.
Tiantong Jie said: "This old woman’s inner chamber is deep and secure, impenetrable as a watertight seal;
yet she leans toward scattering flowers upon withered wood and igniting flames within cold crags. This monk stands solitary and remote, accustomed to entering surging waves, sitting at ease."
He cuts off the surging tide; in the end, not a single drop remains upon his person. If one examines this closely, there are certainly two people who have been shackled and bound.
Yet, as for the Buddha-dharma, you have not even seen it in a dream. Lian-an asked: "To suppress the weak and assist the strong has been the way since ancient times.
To wear long robes and peddle prettiness makes it difficult for false teachings to be supported. In years past, I myself was once..."
The old woman changed his very eyes. The monk missed the mark; yet, upon careful examination, it was actually the old woman who missed the monk.
Clapping her hands, she laughed heartily and said, "Thirty years from now, I shall reveal this to you all.
Kongdong Ci said: "Among the assembly, Dao'an said, 'The abbess has not yet attained it. The old woman was a master."
To express it in such a way reveals only the sharpness of the tip of a needle.

Little do they know that the old woman did not understand the master of the hermitage’s place of enjoyment, nor did the master of the hermitage understand the old woman’s sphere of activity. This pair of clumsy fellows—twenty blows each!
"Why is this? At Lion Rock, rewards and punishments are clearly distinguished. Dongta Xi said: "The abbot’s wall is several *ren* high and its joints are not permeable;
the old woman crossed the double barrier in secret, wishing to explore the springtime colors within the inner gate.
Had it not been a truly extraordinary event, how could we have seen such a dark meeting with bright entry? Lüyǔjiāo said: "The woman held fast; the old woman [was trapped]."
"Burning the hermitage—what does that have to do with the monk? As for the saying, 'A withered tree leans against a cold cliff;
throughout the three winters there is no warmth'—how would you respond? He spread his hands and said, "How very clear!
Mingshi Xi said: "The old woman stands atop a high peak; it is difficult to descend from there. The abbot walks along the bottom of a deep sea; it is not easy to climb up."
Examining this from the perspective of the future, neither of the two is resolved. Tell me, how shall we settle this? [He strikes a circular shape with his whisk and says:
"Fortunately, a single plot of wild ground remains; year after year, the grass grows green of its own accord."
One does not see the spots of man; one sees the spots of the tiger. Calculating this, do not wish to see the spots of man.
Once the tiger’s spots are seen, one can avoid them entirely; only the spots of man are most difficult to avoid.
(Huo’an Ti) The iron wall bursts open, clouds scattering in fragments; from the Black Mountain rolls forth the full orb of the moon. Within this, light and darkness contend with one another.
In the realm beyond the heavens, who can discern the one who peeks out? (Vast Hall, O Fool! The poor man constantly envies the wealthy;
the wealthy do not deceive the poor. Do not trust that which is "straight among the straight"; you must guard against benevolence that is not truly benevolent.
(Xianji Yun): For twenty years I have lacked the eye; burning down this thatched hut was done in vain. The spring warmth is not much to speak of;
these words of truth may also serve as a teacher. (Hengchuan Gong)
Amidst ten thousand flowers, his body remains unstained; how many people in Jambudvīpa has he brought to their downfall?
If you wish to know the conduct of this monk, there is a steel needle within a ball of soft cotton. (Wu Yi arrives. When adversaries meet, each possesses a unique skill;
how could such divine strategy be known to outsiders? As they turn upon one another to cause harm, the resentment is difficult to resolve.
Understood. A most venomous heart conceals its mechanisms in the dark.

(Yongjue Xian) Clouds fill the deep crags, flowers cover the outskirts; the transformation and nourishment of heaven and earth are truly abundant. People of this age see only the splendor of the crimson gates;
who recognizes that the price of dwelling in seclusion is many times higher? (Tianmu Xiu)

Displaying clever schemes on the edge of a precipice—this is the most groundless way to trap a tiger. Do not say it is easy to cast one's body across; you must know that it is difficult to keep a live sparrow.
(Dading Xin) The old woman burned the hermitage; fine flowers are hard to grasp. Stealing fragrance and pilfering jade—how could she deceive Heaven? (Juelang Sheng)
Holding fast at the secure barrier, one proceeds upward; one does not bring pure integrity into the dust of the world.
Borrowing a modicum of "harmonizing with light," one loses both the lady and the army.
(Tian’an Sheng) The thief does not become wealthy; the incense-burner does not remain poor. How many seekers of the Way encounter the Flower Spirit beneath the moon?
(Ji Shui Guang) Who knows the mechanism of leaving one’s station? The venomous dragon was pulled out at Poonahsi. Splitting open the ocean waters, the subtlety of *śamatha-vipaśyanā* is revealed;
not seeing the tail is even more extraordinary. (Sheng Ke Yu)
I once marveled that the Marquis of Liu resembled a beauty; naturally, the Red Emperor’s soul was lost to him. With one blow and one shoe, they sang in response to one another;
though the fires of kalpa burn through them, no trace can be found.
(Mok Liji) Where a single sail opens, another sail opens; the waters are emerald and the sands bright, with moss upon both banks. Each displays their elegance as they return to their separate homes.
Pu: "Let the gulls and herons doubt and suspect as they will.
(Non-rhyming tone) At this very moment, when people-seeing and sentient-being-seeing occur, the pillar enters the lantern; the mountain gate emerges from the Buddha hall.
(Han Guan’s Metaphor):
Seeking the profound in the land of Han, he dwells in the region of Shu; from Eastern Wu and Western Chu, letters of state are sent in succession.
Without discussing matters of war or human affairs, he entices Kongming to emerge from his thatched cottage. (Ancient Sail, Favorable)
Xing is at the southern edge of heaven; the two wheels of sun and moon draw each other into darkness.
One who does not know the ancient brocade *huíwén* (reversed-text) pattern mistakenly calls this "Yunmen’s Six Not Included.
(Falin-yin) Once, while staying at Āmrapālī, a monk visited Mihu and entered the hermitage. He asked the lady, "Do you have any kinsmen? The lady—
[The Master] said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "Where is it? Ba said, "Mountains, rivers, the great earth, whether grass or trees—all are my attendants.
[The monk] said, "Have you come here as a nun? Ba said, "What do you see me as?"
Baizhang said, “A worldly person. Nanyue said, “You cannot be a monk. Baizhang said, “Do not confuse the Buddha-dharma, Master.
Nanyue said, “I am not confusing the Buddha-dharma. Baizhang said, “If that is so, does this not constitute confusion?
Nanyue said, “You are a man and I am a woman; how could that be confusion?”
The Dou family can brew wine that dispels sorrow; it dispels the sorrows of anyone who suffers them.
Look at me and you—we are both desolate, simply because night follows upon night and morning follows upon morning.
(Tie Rong and Xuan Er) I urge you not to provoke the tongue of an old woman; once provoked, her clamorous chatter will never cease. Moreover, there is the formidable Mother of Liangshan.
The "Insect" (Chong): Having found a path, he plunders house after house.
His skirt drags eight folds of Xiang River water; his topknot binds a single mass of Wushan clouds. He sells himself until his entire body is full of charm;
how many people pity him, and how many loathe him? (Tian'an Sheng)
