The First Generation after Dajian:
Chan Master Huairang of Nanyue in Hengzhou (the successor of Dajian Huineng). When he first visited the Sixth Patriarch, the Patriarch asked, "Where have you come from?"
The Master said, "I have come from Mount Song. The Patriarch asked, "What thing is it that comes like this? The Master replied, "To describe it as a thing is not to the point.
The Patriarch asked, "Can it be cultivated and realized? The Master replied, "There is nothing that cannot be cultivated and realized; yet it cannot be defiled.
The Patriarch said, "This very state of being undefiled is what all Buddhas protect and keep in mind. Since you are thus..."
"It is so. I am also like this. [Chē* dù] Lìcān said: "Nanyue Daoxuan’s saying that 'it is like one thing' is simply not the case.
How thick-skinned must you be to say, 'The Sixth Patriarch also said I am like this'?"
The jade lies within the pond; the lotus emerges from the water. Though defilement cannot sever it, this is merely a comparison.
If you, Great Master, can thus take this up, then one night on Mount Dongting, the autumn wind will rise.
(Foyin Yuan) Coming and coming from the summit of Song, if you come in such a manner, not a single thing is fit, for you are already covered in dust. Return at once to Nanyue to grind bricks.
A fragment. It is observed that the wind-chasing steed has returned.
(Foguo Bai) "To describe it as a single thing is not correct; only after eight years did the firewood-seller reach accord. For the most part, there is not much to imitate;
how could one exhaust it throughout kalpas? (Puweng Xian)
Setting out directly from Mount Song, one wanders freely through the vast expanse of heaven and earth. Since not even a single thing exists, how could there be anything like it?
A long sword leaning against the sky chills those who approach. (The Boundless Lineage) Majestic is the wondrous tracelessness of daily life;
the moment one stirs so much as a hair’s breadth, it becomes dust. The silver moon reflecting in the water sinks into the night.
The *pò* (soul) lingers on the fragrance of flowers as the butterfly’s soul becomes intoxicated with its scent.
(Yanshan Qin) Having come from afar, his spirit is most exalted; when questioned, it is like frost upon snow.
He has already stood outside the Gate of the Great Sun—why need he stir the fire or heat the water again? (Hanshan Qing)
"What thing comes like this? "The magpie pecks at food near the birth-pavilion; If one stirs it casually, it flies away in haste.
The pillar vainly dwells in the womb of the stone woman.
(Han Guan’s Metaphor) Nanyue [Huiyong] once asked Mazu, who was then residing at the Chuanfa Court and spending his days in seated meditation: "Virtuous One, why do you sit in meditation?"
"What do you seek? he asked. [Nanquan] replied, "I seek to become a Buddha. The Master then took a brick and began grinding it in front of the temple.
The Patriarch asked, "What are you doing by grinding this? Nanquan said, "I am grinding it to make a mirror. The Patriarch said, "By grinding a brick, how can you make a mirror?
Nanquan said, "By sitting in meditation, how can one become a Buddha? The Patriarch asked, "How then is it so? Nanquan said, "It is like a bull pulling a cart; if the cart does not move..."
"Whether it be driving a cart or driving an ox—it is the same. At these words, Mazu awakened to the essential meaning.
Falin Yinzhen asked, "Did Mazu awaken through the driving of the cart, or through the driving of the ox? Thereupon, he clapped his hands and laughed heartily.
Polishing a brick to make a mirror—this is to long for what shares the same sound. When asked, he clearly reveals his original mind.
As soon as the wooden man is called, he turns his face and points; the earthen ox plows forth ancient gold.
(Fenyang Zhao) Polishing a brick to make a mirror is not difficult; suddenly light arises, illuminating the great thousandfold world. How laughable to sit in meditation seeking the Buddha!
This person has, until now, applied even more lashes to the ox’s back.
(Foyin Yuan) Grinding a brick to make a mirror; playing *dalu* at the banquet table. All fish and dragons know that water is their life.
(Mingu Fo) Pain in the hindbrain of the cart-ox leads to further lashing; casting away the gold to embrace a glazed brick. Following evil and pursuing the heterodox until this day.
"Day. This is a mistaken transmission regarding the Buddha and the mind.
(Xiaoweng Kan) Throughout my life, I have laid bare my heart and gall toward others; my transgressions fill the heavens and are no light matter.
Having brought disgrace upon Master Ma by following his chaotic lead, I have continued to mistake the zero point on the scale until now. (Songyuan Yue)
All phenomena forgotten, a hundred thoughts reduced to ashes. In an ordinary moment, he suddenly pulls [the ox] back by the nose. A single point of mirror-light shines like the sun;
it truly causes the heart-mind of the wooden man to open. (Xueyan Qin) A dragon-riding steed with the feet of a thoroughbred is trapped by a salt-cart;
before meeting Sunyang, it still lags on the road. He pulls it free from the head-rope and gives it a lash.
*Ti*. The wind-whirled hooves rustle as flashes of lightning drive on.
(Pingyang Mien) When a monk asked the Master of Nanyue: "When a mirror is used to cast an image, once the image is formed, where does the light of the mirror go?"
The Master said, "When you were a young boy, where was your true appearance? He replied, "Even after the image was completed, why does it not reflect anything?
The Master said, "Although it does not reflect, one cannot deceive it by even a single point."
Fayan Yi distinguished them by saying, "Which one, Venerable Sir, is the image cast by you? Baoshou Fang simply said, "How great are Nanyue and his commentaries;
they are not easy to explain. Xuefeng, however, was not like this: he was like casting an image in a mirror.
Once the image is formed, where does the light go? Waiting for the other’s eyes to flicker with doubt, he struck him across the spine.
The eyes within the skull are still visible; the dragon’s roar from within the withered wood is even more wild.
When the void is shattered, the realm of light is exhausted; herein there is another matter for deliberation.

(Cishou Shen) The question probes the profound, and the answer is even more mysterious. To strike a blow upon one's own person is the height of elegance; if you wish to know it, not even a single point can be concealed.
The place: several peaks above the river are so green they seem about to float.
(Opening the Secluded Room) Twisted ancient trunks are entwined with moss; under the clear sun, jade-like blossoms unfold.
I have always lamented that when spring departs there is no place to find it, yet I did not know it had turned its course and entered here. (Raising the Snowy Blade)
Because Mazu was spreading his teachings in Jiangxi, Nanyue dispatched a monk to investigate him.
He instructed the monk, saying: "When he ascends the hall, simply ask him, 'What is it? and remember whatever words he says. The monk went there and asked exactly as instructed.
Mazu said, "Since the time of chaos, for thirty years, salt and soy sauce have never been lacking. The monk returned and reported this to Nanyue.
The Master deeply approved of this.
Jingshan Hongjue said, "Yunmen was not like that: when he saw an inauspicious dream at night, he wrote 'Great Auspiciousness' over his gate.
Tianning Weiqing said, "If I were the Great Master, as soon as I saw that monk come forward, I would step down from my meditation seat, seize him, and give him a severe beating."
He gave him a meal and instructed him to return and report this to Nanyue, so as to manifest that his own lineage had a reliable source and that his own eyes were clear.
As for Jingshan speaking in this manner—how is he the same as Mazu or different?
It is like writing Lu Tong’s poem on the lunar eclipse upon a black-lacquered screen. Fulong Chang said: "Upon the back of a broken donkey..."
This brings about a swarm of flies. Dajue Sheng said, "The meaning yields a bountiful harvest," yet he still leaves Mazu with the burden of implicating Nanyue, which remains hanging over his heart.
For thirty years in confusion, there has never been a lack of salt and sauce. Mazu of Jiangxi and Huairang of Nanyue—(Gushan Gui) saw them clearly and recognized them intimately;
yet even bringing this up still involves the journey. Even if one does not err by so much as a hair’s breadth.
This is the very person who licks his fingers after picking up food. (Jingshan Gao) When the family is poor, even the children suffer;
when affairs are urgent, one cannot rely on others. Opening the mouth reveals the tethering rope; such negligence brings trouble upon the neighbors.
(Or the essence of the hermitage:
Verifying the right and the wrong amidst the flash of a stone-fire; casually picking out the grit from one’s eyes.
Since then, there has never been a lack of salt and sauce; I dare guarantee that he has not yet reached his home. (Mukan Egen)
Since the plums are already ripe, when would one go out to pick them again? To let their fragrance pervade the entire land, a fierce wind is sent to blow.

(Snowy Flames Auspiciousness) The will to sweep away the smoke of war has not yet ceased; the clear sky and bright sun cause men to grieve. In an era of Great Peace, there is no need for the General’s armor.
Seal. Drawing the sword and hanging the halberd, one finally reaches the head.
(Wu Yi Lai) Coming from Mount Zizhu, he does not deceive himself. Exquisite flowers blaze, the grasses grow lush;
amidst them, how many idle sentiments there are! Aside from Mount Heng, who else could know them? (Chi Ping Jing)
The Second Generation after Dajian (Nanyue Huairang):
Chan Master Mazu Daoyi of Jiangxi (Heir to Nanyue Huairang). A monk asked the Master, "Why do you say 'this very mind is Buddha'?
The Master said, "To stop a small child from crying. The monk asked, "After the crying has stopped, what then? The Master said:
"It is neither mind nor Buddha. [The student] asked, "Setting aside these two types of people, how would you instruct someone else?
The Master said, "I would tell him it is not a thing. [The student] asked, "What if someone who has already realized this were to come? The Master said, "I would have him realize the Great Way."
Huangbo Qi said: "To say 'this very mind is Buddha' is to place a head upon one's own head. To say 'neither mind nor Buddha' is to bind oneself with no rope.
'Neither mind, nor Buddha, nor thing' is like washing clods of earth in the mud. After a long silence, he said:
"The land is vast and the people are few; those who meet are rare."
A million brave soldiers set forth; the General hunts at Weicheng. Unconcerned with the strength of his bow and arrows, the slanting Milky Way and the first moon have just risen.

(Cui Zhenyan) There is no need for rabbit horns to exist; there is no need for ox horns to be absent. Where existence and non-existence are not [the ultimate] state, the fragrant scent fills the road.

(Qing of Caotang): The wind is fierce and the leaves fall frequently; the mountain is high and the sun sinks quickly. Those within the hall do not see [the outside]; beyond the window, the white clouds are deep.
(Zhuo of Changling)
The plain zither is strung in the fifth month; flowing water and falling flowers lie deep. In silent listening, the subtle sound penetrates to its depths—cool and clear, the music of antiquity.

(By Fuxincai) The spring light of the third month is harmonious and warm; The brocade-like mountains and rivers are the same everywhere. At dawn, mist rises from the green tiles on the Cold Food Festival.
Rain. The crimson curtains are rolled up by the clear breeze of apricot blossoms.
(Cishou Shen) It resounds when struck, yet there is no sound to be heard. In the bitter cold, it is moist with sweat; in the scorching heat, it is as pure as ice.
Try asking the travelers passing along the road: "How many stages from here to Chang'an? (Huanglong Zhen)
The iron ox plows through the void of the heavens; peach blossoms fall petal by petal from the deep source. Once the people of Qin departed, there has been no news;
for a thousand ages the colors of the peaks and ridges have grown ever more fresh.
(Xuedou Zong) "This very mind is Buddha"—the eyebrows drag upon the ground. "Neither this mind nor Buddha"—the two eyes are crossed. Within the dream of the butterfly, ten thousand homes.
Li Zi Gui: On the branch, the moon at the third watch. (Xiatang Yuan) A cluster of human dwellings, a village beyond the islands.
Falling flowers and flowing water as the moon turns yellow. When the hundred rivers reach the sea, they must stay;
after all, how could there ever have been another source? (Tieshan Ren)
When a monk asked Mazu, "What is the Buddha? the Master said, "The very mind is the Buddha.
Gao Feng Miao said: "Among those who deliberate on this, all claim that the mind is fundamentally the Buddha and that there is no mind apart from the Buddha;
thus they say 'the very mind is the Buddha. Alas, alas! If one holds such a view, by tomorrow or the day after, one will be eating iron [in hell]."
The staff has its own share. Since it is thus, how should one act? A bamboo shoot emerges askew, pressed down by a rock; a flower grows upside down, suspended from a cliff.
"This very mind is Buddha"—an iron ox has no bones. A fierce dragon plays in the sea; a magnificent hawk soars toward the heavens. The Western River is sucked dry.
Not yet extraordinary; a lotus born from fire, its fragrance wafting.
(Nantang Jing) "The very mind is the Buddha. A dragon enters a snake’s den. To emerge as a general and enter as a minister, to bring peace to the realm and stabilize the state.
(Shitou Hui) "The very mind is the Buddha. The Lady Chang’e does not paint her brows; once she is stained by rouge and powder, her beauty turns into ugliness.
(Tianmu Li): "The mind itself is Buddha.
Aconite, frost, and wolf-poison can raise the dead and restore life without requiring even a single dose. (Huanxi Yi):
Hard as pure steel, yet soft as mud; sweet as mountain honey, yet poisonous as aconite. Swallow it whole, and swallow it whole again.
Vomit it out! You’ve cheated the horse-sieve of Jiangxi (Zhongfeng Ben).
"Zhi-hu-zhe-ye-yi-an-zai"—these seven characters are what defines a scholar.
If there is even the slightest bit of instability, the Iron Mountain stands face-to-face, its form towering and steep (Ban’an Dan).
"Whose family’s rice? Hanging an empty bag. He pointed it out to a young boy and told him to look; when he untied it, he saw only ashes.
At that moment, his life-root was severed.
(Kaishan Jian) When a monk asked Mazu, "What is the Buddha? the Master said, "Neither mind nor Buddha."
Jade from the Azure Sea, jade-discs from Mount Jing—shining across heaven and earth, who can truly discern them? With a sharp blade, one cuts down the rootless tree;
ten thousand layers of peaks withdraw their mists and fogs.
(By Yuanwu Qinquan) Having sold all his fields and gardens, he is utterly poor; he knows not where he may find a place to rest his body. Wandering aimlessly atop the tower, he is unrestrained.
Inspecting, he blows his iron flute across Lake Dongting.
(Kaishan Xian) The scenery and air of the second month are floating; young gentlemen roam the imperial streets.
Sitting cross-legged upon silver couches, they tilt their cups in joy; three children play with horse-globes. (Muan Zhong)
Neither Buddha nor mind—this is called severing emotional attachments. On the profound path, like a bird’s track, hasten back home. With the *śakrāloka* eye, preserve the transformative pivot.
Do not linger guarding the cold crags while the strange grasses grow green.
(Nanyuan Sheng) Mazu said, "Neither mind, nor Buddha. Directly beneath this, there is no further nest or burrow. This year’s walnuts on the tree are superior to—
Last year’s tangerines. (Zhengtang’s Discernment) When all beings on earth attain perfect enlightenment, hundreds of thousands of Buddhas fall into hell. Cease this frequent raising of such talk;
I fear the Old Man of the Yama Family might find out. (Zhongfeng’s Version)
Once Mazu was with Baizhang, Nanquan, and Xitang as they attended him while enjoying the moon. The Master asked, "At this very moment, how is it?
Xitang said, "It is precisely the time for making offerings. Baizhang said, "It is precisely the time for practicing cultivation.
Nanquan brushed his sleeves and departed. The Master remarked, "The sutras have entered the canon; Chan has returned to the sea. Only Puyuan alone transcends the mundane world."
Cuiyan Zhen said: "Shendeng Shuweng says it is simply because his 'old woman’s heart' is too earnest.
Cuiyan is not like this. He lowers a ten-thousand-li hook to detain a thousand-li black steed; he spreads a sky-reaching net to strike the great fish leaping through the waves.
Is there anyone? If there is, come forth through the waves and meet me. If not, then return to the base of the cliff and wait for the moon to brighten. Lectan.
Qingyun said: "If it is right, it is entirely right; if it is wrong, it is entirely wrong.
Shending’s ‘motherly heart’ is so earnest that it is much like gold sand mixed together, where jade and stone are difficult to distinguish.
As for Mazu’s final words being spoken in such a manner, wherein lies the motherly heart? Without understanding this meaning, one’s practice is but bitter toil. Kaifu Ning said: "Mazu, Great..."

The Master casually unrolls and rolls up [the scroll]; his wondrous hand is natural. This too is like being so intent on watching the wild geese in the clouds that one loses the boat at the ferryhead.
If anyone can examine this and discern it, they will "wear fur while wandering through a mass of fire" and "bear horns while wallowing in the mud.

Should your vision still be dim and hazy, I shall provide you with a commentary: "The Sutras enter the Canon and Chan returns to the Sea"—yet even this is not yet the personal realization of a patch-robed monk.
At last, he brushed his sleeves and walked away, saying, "Go back! He shattered the heavy gates and opened them wide.
Is there anyone who has seen Master Ma? After a long silence, he said, "Enough, enough! Every night in Chang'an, every house has its moon;
in some places there is song and dance, in others there is sorrow. Huguo Long said, "The Foal tramples everyone underfoot. A single blow must be met with a single palm."
Blood! Each of the three great elders displayed their own family style, yet unconsciously they turned it into a display of overzealous, sentimental concern.

The monastic community discusses this at length, all saying that the story of "gazing at the moon" is extraordinary. But when examined closely, it is truly intolerable. Why? Because these three men took a tortoise and turned it into a turtle.
Lingyuan Yue said, regarding the point where offerings are most appropriate: "It is like hoping for plums to quench one's thirst."
Regarding the place where practice is exactly right, he said: "Gold does not trade with gold. Regarding the place where he shook out his sleeves and departed, he said:
"He has only attained a single peg. Regarding the place where he alone transcends all things, he said: "Oṃ maṇidhāri hūṃ phaṭ. He further said:
"This lot of broken-down fellows—every one of their nostrils has been pierced through. Where, you people, will you go to breathe?"
Wushan Dao said: "Baizhang’s West Hall [disciple] reached the point of speech but not of practice;
Nanquan reached the point of practice but not of speech. Both must receive a blow of the staff. As for Mazu speaking thus, is there any distinction of superiority or inferiority?
He drew a circle with his whisk and said, "Fortunately, it is as clear as a mirror; why use a hook that is bent? He struck the whisk.
The Sutras have entered the Canon; Chan has returned to the Sea. Only Puyuan alone transcends the mundane world.
(Tut! There is only the moon reflecting on the wall; there is no wind blowing through the leaves.
(Zhaojue Zong) The Sutras have entered the Canon; Chan has returned to the Sea. I bow my head in refuge and join my palms in veneration. Master Wang transcends the mundane world.
Twenty years ago he came thus; now all his idle splendor has vanished. (Tiantong Jue) At Guoqing, the talent is noble;
in a wealthy house, the children are pampered. Let everyone lend a hand; let neither side yield to the other.

(Jingshan Gao): At the ancient ferry, where there is no wind, the hook is cast straight down; the intent of the silk line lies in catching the whales and turtles. Under Mazu’s words, the family’s ugliness was exposed;
for a thousand ages, descendants have wandered amidst the weeds. (Zantang Shen)
The various sons manage their households, each growing fat; among them, one alone is truly pitiable. With a basket full of ink, no one will buy it;
at midnight he carries it back home to dye his robes black. (Da-xie-qian) Each son has established his own livelihood;
from of old, filial piety arises on both sides. Greedy for a night’s pleasure, the whole family gathers.
Joyful. At the break of dawn, he hurriedly struck the fifth watch.
(Wuzu Fan) To the bottom of the source, they are all one family. His noble bearing outshines the four neighbors.
He pulls the rope from the puppet stage; suddenly, a parrot flies over Xiqin. (Wuyi Lai)
To hide a mountain in a marsh is to hide a boat in a lake; throughout the world there is nothing hidden, as it penetrates the nine schools of thought.
With both hands flung open, one follows the steps in joy; carefree and unimpeded, the three realms cannot detain one.
(Feiyin Rong) Walking together under the moon, we speak of daily life: filial piety is tender and charming, while rebellion is wild. At daybreak, one knows not where one has gone.
"Go! You will grieve the night traveler until the end.

(Huishan Haichao) When a monk asked Mazu, "Leaving behind the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations, I ask the Master to point directly to the meaning of the Westward Transmission," the Master said, "I am weary today and cannot explain it for you. Go and ask Zhizang. The monk went and asked him.
The monk went to ask Zang. Zang said, "Why do you not ask the Master? The monk replied, "The Master told me to come ask you.
Zang said, "I have a headache today; I cannot explain it for you. Go ask your elder brother Hai. The monk went to ask Hai.
Hai said, "When I arrive at this point, I too do not understand. The monk returned and reported this to the Master. The Master said, "Zang’s head is white; Hai’s head is black."
Taisu Zhe said: "This monk asked in such a manner, and Master Ma answered in such a manner; it transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations.
Brother Zhizanghai does not understand this at all. Do you see? It is not without reason that it is said: 'The colt tramples the people of the world to death.'"
Wuzu Yan said: "As for Mazu’s place of shamelessness and embarrassment, he could only say, 'The head is white, the tail is black.
This monk carried a load of bewilderment and exchanged it for a lack of understanding. Had his eyes been like shooting stars, how many people would have lost their money and suffered for it!
Gao Feng Miao said: "Mazu and his son shared one gate; they were no ordinary ones."
Truly, he has a serpent’s heart within a Buddha’s mouth; he is also well-versed in the *Liùtāo* (Six Tactics) and *Sānlüè* (Three Strategies).
Were it not for the work of Zhuge Kongming, this monk would surely have lost his life. The *Longchi Chuan* says:
"The three great elders were brought to such domestic chaos by this leg-picking fellow that even now father and son remain at odds. Is there anyone who can mediate this? [He] threw down his staff.

Regarding the "Cane" (zhàng): Lingyan Chu said, "To encounter great favor without being startled, and to face great chaos without being terrified—were it not for one who has mastered the great principles of the world and grasped the transformative nurturance of Heaven and Earth, they would still be unable to deploy their strategies from within the tent to secure victory a thousand *li* away.
How, then, could they dare hope for the peace of the world through profound reverence? The Ma family, father and son, were like those pushing aside a million [soldiers]."
When a great army of heroes is brought to submission with a mere cough or a spittle, by what artifice is this achieved?
"The head at the source is white; the head at the ocean is black. Even a monk with clear eyes cannot comprehend it. A colt tramples all people underfoot.
Linji was not yet a thief who steals in broad daylight. Beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations, in all of heaven and earth, only I know.

(Xuedou Xian) The two goddesses of the Xiang River possess the rank of immortals; they lean with smiles against vermilion gates and fragrant thoroughfares, a single stroke of crimson suffusing their cheeks.
Red. Even more so, it possesses a color of utter naturalness.
(Fujian Qin) The four lines and hundred negations are all cut off; the "Spring Breeze" and "Snowy White" melodies sing ever higher.
On a night of clear wind and bright moon without a cloud, who would trade a "blowing-hair" sword for a precious blade? (Nanhua Bing)
A short cap, light robes, and a narrow waistcoat; she dances through all eighteen variations of the *huguā* flute. When the music ends and the wine is spent, she has still not returned;
upon her return, the moonlight blends with the clouds in white purity. (Xiatang Yuan:

The path of a hundred negations is cut off, penetrating the subtle and minute; when the four phrases of emotion are forgotten, the supreme faculty is awakened. Though the bamboo is dense, it does not hinder the flowing stream.
It passes. How could the height of the mountain obstruct the flight of white clouds?

(Zuanjian of Zu’an) That medicine produces illness was witnessed by the sages of old; that illness produces medicine—surely who else could it be? Whether with white hair or black hair, there is the son who sustains the family.
With a phrase or without a phrase, there is the pivotal mechanism that cuts off the stream. Majestically sitting, he brings his tongue to a standstill.
On the road, one should laugh at the ancient sage of Vaiśālī (Hongzhi Jue).
In the flower groves, the spring breeze fills the sleeves with fragrance; red and white blooms stand in equal measure. How much more so for those who are full of sentiment:
a single flute call from the wheat fields passes over the wild pond (Qingxi Xin).
I have trodden upon the highest peak of a thousand crags; my life’s journey grows ever more clumsy, and I am utterly incapable of anything.
What need is there to argue pointlessly about severing ties? Now I see that my old friends are but a single climbing vine.
(Mu Chen Min) The remaining flowers have fallen away, and the birds’ cries are mournful; a singular spring sorrow follows the tangled threads. As I lie upon this empty bed, my heart is broken.
All severed. How could the General who campaigns north of the frontier know? (Ziqiao) The lush greens and fading reds press upon the imperial city.
One cannot bear the warbling of the coquettish oriole outside the curtain. For what reason is Lady Chen’s heart as cold as iron?
She still laments that at Changmen Gate she does not see spring. (Jingtang Qing)
A lone spear and a single horse enter the heavy city; The thunder of gongs and drums resounds in the four directions.
Unaware of the wild wind, heaven and earth grow dark; Turning my head, there is nowhere that does not move me to despair.
(Falin, Rhymes 2) The wind whistles and the rain whistles; As spring ends, the cuckoo calls from its old branch. Across the bank, the cloud shadows are cold and desolate.
Severed. A single red sun half-crosses the bridge.
Once, while Mazu was strolling with Baizhang on a mountain excursion, they saw wild ducks fly past. The Master asked, "What is that?"
He replied, "A wild duck. The Master asked, "Where has it gone? He said, "It flew away. The Master then pinched the staff-bearer's nose.
In his agony, the bearer let out a cry: "Ai-ya! Ai-ya! The Master said, "And yet you say it flew away.
At these words, the staff-bearer attained awakening.
Zhongfeng Ben said: "To set a brocade trap to ensnare beasts, or to dangle fragrant bait to catch fish—only a skilled craftsman can do this.
Mazu intended to capture a bird; he plunged deep into the wild weeds and exhausted all his strength, yet he only managed to break through half of an iron net.
Was he truly a skilled craftsman? Baoshou Fang said: "The Great and Small Mazu may be said to have failed in their efforts."

Wang Shi, however, what he has obtained does not exceed this wild duck. If he were a magnificent falcon soaring toward the heavens, Master Ma, would you yourself still be free from concern? Or would you not?

The wild duck—where does it go? When Master Ma saw it coming, he spoke with it; they exhausted their discourse on the sentiments of mountain clouds and ocean moons, yet as before, it did not understand and flew away. [Master Ma] then seized it and said, "Speak!
Speak! (Xuedou Xian). The flowing water has east and west; the reeds have no front or back. A sandbird suddenly flies by; the fisherman is startled by the night song.
Who says the bright moon has nowhere to be found? It turns out it is right here upon the autumn river.
(Shangfang Yi) A flock of wild ducks flies by, their momentum impossible to hold; in a flash they pass, and the high autumn is already here.
Grasp their sound and you will seize the lifelong pain; do not trouble yourself with a short rope to tie their snouts. (Fodeng Xun)
A wild duck flies across the sky; Zhang San meets Li Da. A solitary boat is moored on the bank; a yellow ox is unyoked from the millstone.
(By Baiyang Shun) The lamp of the mind cannot be handed over; the seal of the patriarchs is likewise difficult to transmit. The wild duck flies away—his nose is twisted until it is pierced.
(Heikō Kō) When Mazu returned to the attendants' quarters after a mountain excursion with Baizhang, Baizhang wept bitterly. A fellow practitioner asked him, "Are you grieving for your parents?
Baizhang replied, "No. [The practitioner] asked, "Have you been scolded by someone? Baizhang replied, "No. [The practitioner] asked, "Then why are you weeping?"
Zhaozhou said, "My nostrils were pinched by the Great Master until they hurt unbearably. [The attendant] asked, "What was the cause for this lack of accord?
Zhaozhou said, "Go ask the Abbot yourself. The attendant went to ask Attendant Hai, who was weeping in his quarters.
When asked why he was weeping over a lack of accord, the attendant replied, "It is because he understands; you should go ask him yourself. The attendant then returned.
The Master said, "The Abbot said you understand; let me ask you something. Baizhang then laughed heartily.
His companion asked, "Just now you were crying; why are you laughing now? Baizhang replied, "Just now I was crying; now I am laughing."
Sanfeng Zang said: "His paired sandals head toward the celestial court;
With every thought, his spirit is wounded. Unawares, he turns and laughs anew. Clouds atop the ridge never rest at ease;
Water in the ravine flows with too much haste. (Longmen Yuan)
Sometimes laughing, sometimes weeping; sorrow and joy entwine, urging one on in secret. How can this principle be explained to others?
To mend a severed string, one must have *luán* glue.
(Jingshan Gao) Sometimes laughing, sometimes weeping—the melody is so high that those who can harmonize are few, difficult to restrain. A single stream of pure sound penetrates the nine heavens.
O Celestial One! Who in this world can follow in the fragrant tracks of those who preceded them?
(Miaofeng Shan) One cannot weep enough; one cannot laugh enough. I shall empty my belly and pour out my heart to tell you: that father and son are not kin is something known only by the ignorant.
A three-catty iron behind the head as he lifts it up.
(Songyuan Yue) The chessboard is transformed; the medicine is countered. Swiftly seizing the moment, no further stratagems are required. To strike the painful spot again is like a sharp awl.
When the eyes first open, the nose-tip hangs down; shame covers his entire face, impossible to conceal. He laughs and weeps, flaunting the moon.
Like eyebrows. (Meiguku Etsu) Mazu ascended the hall;
as soon as the assembly had gathered, Baizhang stepped forward, rolled up his sitting mat, and bowed. The Master then descended from his seat.
Xuedou Xian said: "Everywhere people say this is extraordinary. But when it is raised in such a manner, is it actually appropriate?
If it were appropriate, it would be like a water jelly using a shrimp for eyes. If it were not appropriate, then why praise it in vain?

Among the assembly, there are some who rush forward in a disorderly fashion to ask, 'What was the intent of the ancient? Furthermore, there are those who are so old in years that they do not even recognize what is good."
"Evil! [The Master] replied, "I thought you were a guest from Xiantuo. He further said, "Come again before my seat tomorrow; alas, alas!
Had I seen him come out then and roll up his mat, I would have kicked him right in the chest so that neither those sitting nor those standing could rise.
This was simply to ensure that future generations would have a different way of life, sparing them from being thus left stranded by such dull-wittedness. Is this not so?"
A man of such heroic spirit! Baizhang Quan brought forth Mazu’s words, saying: "My failure to guide you might still be excusable, but your failure to respond is far too extreme.
Huanglong Xin said: "When Mazu ascended the hall, Baizhang rolled up his mat. Later generations, unable to grasp the wind from which this came, all say that no trace was left behind.
Little do they realize that it was precisely within the peach-blossom waves that the sail should have been set."

At the head of Qīlǐ Tān, it is even more worthy to cast one’s line for fish. Now there must surely be some fellow who can distinguish between sinking and floating, and discern the shallow and the deep.
Come forth and try to determine the currents; is there anyone? If not, then simply take up the fisherman’s flute and blow it idly by the seaside.
Dàyuè Zhì said: "The light of dawn has not yet parted, and all gaze expectantly; yet when the day breaks, they still search."
Constantly.
When Mazu ascended the hall, Baizhang rolled up his mat; the orthodox command was not followed, and what was crooked was forced straight. (Xuedou Xian):
Mazu ascends the hall, Baizhang rolls up the mat—when one person gains half a catty, it is returned to him as eight ounces. Even if one were to patch the seams...
Completely absent. One cannot help but stand by and clap one's hands. (Quán Dàdào):
When a million heroic troops face each other in formation, who is it that knows how to turn back the drums? If the general’s head is not fierce, he will bring disaster upon his three armies;
alas, there is nowhere for the true command to be carried out. (Fóyìn Yuán).
Yesterday the east wind was unexpectedly fierce; peach blossoms fell in disarray like red rain. Last night the east wind went mad again;
they cover the ground, yet no one knows where they have gone.
(Baiyun Cuan) Ascending the hall and rolling up the mat is peerless; the bright sun rises in radiance, pervading everywhere. How laughable—sudden thunder startling the universe!
The universe. An object in a well does not raise its head. (Seal of the Ocean-Mudra) A wild duck flies by;
the tip of the nose cracks open. Unrolling the mat once more to display one's ugliness and clumsiness—even if you were to sit alone atop the Great Hero Peak.
It is also like a second moon in the sky. (Yang Wuwe) Deep in the night, he recognizes the path home;
Without waiting for dawn, he passes through the pass. A three-foot Mo-ya sword rests horizontally in his hand;
To this day, he sits firmly atop Mount Daxiong. (Shangfang Yi)
Rolling it up, the majestic eyes are revealed; brought forth, they are presented face-to-face once more.
With the tip of the nose completely stripped away, who could possibly look upon it? Taking hands, we return together to walk side by side.
(Chu Fang’an) A colt gallops a thousand miles; as the mat is rolled up, he follows in pursuit. In one night the autumn wind arises; everywhere the yellow chrysanthemums bloom.
The Stone [Name] Ghost hangs up the face of Nāṭa; barefoot, he stands firm upon Mount Sumeru. He whips up the iron ox on the banks of the Yellow River;
at the bottom of the great ocean, he devours the coral. (Xuedou Zong)
The wind stilled, the Five Lakes broaden; I lower my sails to gaze at will. The ripples follow the water’s tranquility; their silken hue chills the observer.
I raise my oars to linger by the cloud-hidden cove; I shift my boat onto the emerald bay. Its fame and splendor illuminate the ancestral realm; for a thousand years, let all people behold it.
(Lóngmén Yuǎn) Vast and surging, the long river meets the azure sky; A single sail hoisted high, one immediately rides the wind. How joyful!
Without expending the slightest effort, The home mountains ten thousand *li* away are reached in an instant. (Kāishàn Qiān)
A single handle of the blade of dispassionate snow—when facing its edge, who would dare to offend even a hair’s breadth?
Master Ma and his son personally wield it; blood sprays across a thousand mountains as the wind howls in fury.
(Wuzhun Shanfeng) The great general ascends the altar, a wind from all eight directions; banners are furled, drums silenced, and the four camps are empty. The atmosphere of peace is as clear as...
It is granted. Only then do we see the merit of the King’s generals in not having to fight.

(Hanshan Qing) Peace has no outward form in this brocade imperial realm. At dawn, the Son of Heaven ascends the Phoenix Pavilion. With upright demeanor and trailing robes, he returns to the position of Sage Ruler;
there are worthy lords who harmonize the soup and manage the state. (Gumei Lie)
When Mazu saw Nanquan passing out food, he asked, "What is in the bucket? Nanquan said, "Shut your mouth.
Tianjing Xin remarked, "Mazu did not know what he was asking; Nanquan did not understand what he was answering."
"If you understand this, the descendants of Jiangxi will not be reduced to sweeping away the dust, and Mazu will find peace.
The head monk asked, "How has the Master’s health been lately? The Master replied, "The Buddha of the Sun's Face, the Buddha of the Moon's Face."
Zhaojue Qin said: "If one knows where this public case lands, one can stride alone across the vermilion heavens.
If one does not know, one will often stray from the path before the withered tree and the cliff. He is a master of his own house;
at such a point, one must possess the skillful means to drive the plowman’s ox and snatch the hungry man’s food before one can finally see his horse."
When the Great Master was dealing with people, it was not like this; there was no way through at all. When people arrive here, how can they attain peace and stability?
Chongqing Gu said: "At that time, it is a pity the head monk let him off. Had he not let him off, he should have said to him: 'I knew well enough, Master, that your illness lies in the vital organs.
Bairyam Pu spoke on behalf of the head monk, saying: [He should have said: "I knew well enough, Master, that your illness lies in the vital organs."
It is no wonder the physician said that you, O Monk, do not know how to observe dietary restrictions.
Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha—what things are these Five Emperors and Three Sovereigns? For twenty years, I have endured bitter hardship.
For your sake, he went straight down into the Azure Dragon’s cave. Worthy of being recounted: let no clear-eyed monk treat this with levity.
(Xuedou Xian) The Face of the Sun, the Face of the Moon. The stars shift and the constellations turn; the Persian who lost the dawn cannot find his head.
(Cuiyan Zhen) A young lord suddenly goes wild, piercing the clouds at midnight to enter the inner chamber. The two hundred and eight Xiannü goddesses perform a hundred kinds of [graces].
Skillful! Above the eyes, embroidered mandarin ducks are stitched.
(Yehhyunjun) Sun-faced Buddha, moon-faced Buddha; night after night, morning after morning, how fine are these sights! A colt tramples all people underfoot.
Xuanyuan shatters the cave of spirits.
(Yang Woei-wei) Sitting upright upon the meditation cushion, threading the needle’s eye. A gust of western wind arrives; two or three leaves fall.
(Baoning Yong): The sun’s face, the moon’s face—stars streaming, lightning rolling. Like a mirror facing its image without partiality, like a pearl on a platter turning of itself.
Do you not see the gold that has been refined a hundred times before the forge and hammer? Or the single thread of silk after passing through the blade and the ruler? (Tiantong Jue)
The sun’s face is to the east, the moon’s face to the west; who says they fall naturally into the stream before us?
The mountain peach blossoms have fallen and spring has departed, yet the cuckoo still cries upon its branch.

(Shangfang Yi) The colt from Shifang possesses a fierce and wild spirit; he tramples upon the crown of Vairocana and walks thereon. Just as he suffers from a pain in his spleen, he turns his head back.
Painful! Even in the midst of illness, there remains a clever mind (Zhang Wujin).
A young maidservant paints her brows like a silkworm; before the phoenix-mirror stand, she speaks as if demented.
She says her own jade-like countenance has no peer, yet she goes to the rack to put on her silk robes (Wuzu Yan).
Willow colors on the eastern street drag along misty green; Peach blossoms in the western lane reflect one another in red.
Looking left and right, never weary of the sight, All at once, they are entrusted to the east wind.
(Fojian Qin) The golden crow has just sung and the sun is at its zenith; The royal road is level and smooth, opening everywhere. But alas, the colt was born too... [bold]... 早 (early).
Early! Treading upon the Great Void as before. (Zhengjue Yi) Sun-face, Moon-face;
the lightning in the void. Although it cuts off the tongues of all monks under heaven, even so, it clearly only says half the story. (Yudao Po)
Strike the yellow oriole; do not let it sing upon the branches. When it sings, it startles my dreams, preventing me from reaching Liaoxi.

(Dian Niuyou) She opens her face in laughter within the vermilion mirror; she stretches out her legs to sleep within the white jade basin. In general, such moments in human life are difficult to find.
Together. When we have gathered in a circle, let us simply remain in that circle.
(Fóxìng Tàiyán) Few have reached the ancient hall; who knows of one sitting upright upon the *pútán*?
Had it not been for the monastery master conveying this news, how could the cold light shine ten thousand miles away? (Zhōngjì Néng)
The sun-face and moon-face stand out so prominently they are difficult to distinguish; as one prepares to lift the eyes, two fragments appear in the air.
(Wuzu Fan) Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha—Flying Eagle Peak joins with the three regions of India; South High Peak faces North High Peak.
Six bridges span the green willows hanging down; (entering the snow) who would have thought the flickering lamp-shadows would stir up war?
Battle-horses gallop in confusion, coming and going again. When the candles are extinguished, everyone returns at once;
from the watchtower, the sound of the horn blares forth once more. (The stone streambed is worn smooth.)

Wearing the southern cap yet speaking the language of Chu, he did not forget the sounds of his native land. Whether in moments of haste or in times of distress, there was no way to gauge the depth of his character.
Have you not seen how, over thirty years, his talk of salt and sauce has been a source of many hardships and long reflections?

(Tian Shui Guang) Having learned the art of the elegant man who adorns himself with powder, he once dressed up in two ways at a single stroke; yet when his head and face were changed, no one recognized him.
Consciousness was originally Li Erniang of the Eastern Village (Rao’an edition).
She dug wells and plowed fields; she went out to work and returned to rest. Without knowing or perceiving, she followed the patterns of the Emperor.
Singing divine hymns and dancing at the village shrine, she spontaneously set her own tune, making old man Wang of the Eastern Village laugh to death (Qingyun Qi edition).
A single hair is wound into an ice-silk knot; it is transparent on all four sides, entirely without trace. The message has been exhausted for the earless stone man;
the mud ox gives birth to the Iron Kunlun. (Falin’s Verse) Mazu addressed the assembly:
"Generally speaking, any words or phrases belong to the school of Deva. Take this very thing as the master."
Jieyun Qu said: "Sometimes this mountain monk does not deliberate upon a single phrase as being a single phrase;
sometimes he does deliberate upon a single phrase as being a single phrase. He suddenly took up his staff and said, "Master Mazu has arrived!"
Again, he strikes once and says: "The matter arises from the specific circumstances; as it is passed along, the discourse becomes difficult to clarify. He leans on his staff and says:
"Like a jade turning and a pearl revolving—look with your own eyes! Where there is entanglement, there is no entanglement;
simply take this one thing as the master. He lets out a shout: "A single sword leaning against the heavens—the stars and constellations grow cold! (Shixi Yue)
Amidst wind and snow filling the heavens, he sets out on his journey. A lone horse, its body crossing over the heads of a hundred weeds.
Hearing that foxes and rabbits are cunning upon the plains, he frequently casts his hawk-like gaze upon the Wu hooks [swords].
(Tian'an Sheng San) Entirely relying on his three-inch tongue to act with mastery, the six states shall join in celebrating peace. A great golden seal, worth a *dou*, hangs from his elbow.
Later on, Su Qin was originally the old Su Qin.
The pines are straight and the thorns are crooked; the magpies screech and the crows caw. Originally there is no intention, yet it cannot be said they are without feeling.
Desiring that fish and dragons may know their own natures and destinies, he repeatedly stirs the vast ocean with his broken chopsticks.
When a monk came to visit Mazu, the Master drew a circle and said, "If you enter, I strike; if you do not enter, I strike.
As soon as the monk entered, the Master struck him. The monk said, "Master, you may not strike me. The Master leaned his staff against the wall and ceased.
Xuedou Xian said, "Both are incomplete. He leaned his staff against [the wall] and, as soon as the monk hesitated, struck him across the back with the staff.
Yunju Zhuang said, "Although the Master’s command was carried out, alas, he stirred up waves where there was no wind.
Since this monk has already received the blow, there is indeed no way for him to justify himself. Furthermore, how do you understand the principle of why he desisted?"
Baoshou newly says: When released, the soldiers follow the general’s turn; when withdrawn, the horses listen to the sound of the gong.

Since we are discussing the opposing of forces, there is no lack of mutual attack. Each possesses a singular capability, yet it is only the divine steed that is permitted to maneuver the strategy within the tent and decide victory a thousand *li* away.
Why is this? It is solely because one seeks the tranquility of the state; in the end, one does not prize the rank of a marquis.
The gate-head responds to the void as it may; how could one avoid transgressing unless one is cautious from the start?
Having snatched away Mazu’s thorny staff, he sits watching the world vie with one another in their distinctions.
(Xiaoyan Bao) An iron chain hangs high, impossible to climb; where the nightingale cries, the night is just ending. At this moment, the moonlight is without sentiment.
"Limit. How many have ever crossed the Jade Pass? (Fushan Chu).
Mazu drew four lines before a monk—making the top line long and the bottom three lines short—and said, "You must not say that one line is long and three lines are short.
Apart from these four lines, please, Master, give me your answer. The Master [remained silent].
He then drew a line on the ground and said, "One cannot determine its length or shortness; I have answered you.
Nan-yang Chung remarked, "Why not ask the old monk? Wei-shan Kuo said, "Borrowing a grandmother’s robe to bow for her birthday.
Feng-hsiao Miao said, "After three transcriptions, the characters *wu* and *yan* become *ma*. Hsi-feng said, "I could have laughed at this, but I restrained myself."
[The Master] could not restrain himself. He corrected the words for everyone’s sake. After a long while, he called to his attendant and said, "Remember this clearly.
One day Mazu asked Baizhang, "Where have you come from? [Baizhang] replied, "From behind the mountain. The Master said, "Did you encounter anyone there?
[Baizhang] replied, "I did not encounter anyone. The Master said, "Why did you not encounter anyone? [Baizhang] replied, "If I had encountered anyone, then..."
He presented this to the Master. The Master asked, "Where did you get this news? He replied, "It is Huaihai’s fault.
The Master said, "In fact, it is the old monk’s own fault."
Guoqing Ying said: "Since people do not see [him], for what reason does each person carry a burden of transgressions? Shifeng Xun said:
"Setting aside for a moment whether one encounters him or not, tell me: who is this person? If you can recognize this person,"
Mazu and Baizhang shared a karmic connection regarding the straw sandals.

Under the third generation of the Sixth Patriarch, there was the Great Wisdom Chan Master Baizhang Huaihai of Hongzhou (the single successor of Mazu). He visited Mazu for a second time; while standing in attendance, he said:
The Patriarch held up the whisk at the corner of the meditation seat. The Master said, "Is it used as this, or apart from this?

The Patriarch placed it back in its original position and asked, "After you have departed, how will you instruct people when you open your two flaps of skin [your mouth]? The Master took the whisk and held it up.
The Patriarch said, "Use this very thing, yet remain detached from using it. The Master hung his whisk back in its original place.
The Patriarch let out a thunderous shout, and the Master attained great enlightenment on the spot. One day he said to the assembly, "The Buddha-dharma is no small matter.
In the past, when I was struck by a shout from Master Ma, my ears were deaf for three days straight. When Huangbo heard this account, he involuntarily stuck out his tongue.
Fenyang Shanzhao said: "If one has attained awakening, that is the end of it. Why speak of being deaf for three days? Shimen Tong said:
"If one were not deaf for three days, how could one have attained awakening? Fenyang said: "My way of speaking is half a month’s journey behind Shimen’s.
Xuedou Xian said: "Nowadays, there are many who enumerate its branches, but few who investigate its source."
Few [understand]. Everyone says that Baizhang attained great enlightenment under the shout; but is this actually the case? However, there are differences between "diao" and "dao," or "si" and "ru.
If one is a person with clear eyes, they cannot be deceived for even a single point. It is just as Mazu said:

After that, with two pieces of skin opened up, what would you take as a person? Baizhang held up his whisk. Was this like a worm boring through wood, or was it like the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching?
If you all wish to understand why [Baizhang] went deaf for three days, know that refined gold from a great forge remains unchanged in color.
Donglin Cong said: "When speaking, one does not avoid having one's tongue cut; when tending the furnace, one does not avoid being struck by flying sparks."
How could the Buddha-dharma ever be bent to conform to human sentiments? Today at Donglin, we go to contend for the pearl within the lair of the blue dragon.
It was not without reason that Baizhang’s great wisdom caused him to be deaf for three days;
how could Shenzhao of Fenzhou and Shimen escape being two blind men? Have these three old fellows ever attained enlightenment? After a long silence, he said: "Ancestors and fathers..."
"Not understood. The calamity will extend to one's descendants. Lectan Ying said: "Assembly, tell me:
when Mazu at that time shouted, was it because Baizhang had awakened, or because he had not awakened? Today, this mountain monk will not spare his eyebrows to explain this for you.
After a long silence, he said: "Three before, three after. Yun’gai Zhi said: "To manifest a great capacity and reveal a great function..."
As for this function—who other than Mazu could have performed it? To "employ this function and yet remain apart from this function"—only Baizhang grasped its essential meaning.
Why was he deaf in both ears for three days after being struck by Mazu’s single shout?
"If you do not enter the startling waves, it is difficult to encounter the fish that satisfies your heart. Huanglong Xin said: "Huanglong saw injustice and wishes to question Xuedou. Since—"
This is great refined gold from the forge; it should not change its color. Why was there deafness for three days?
"From before, no one has recognized the sweating horses; it is only to re-examine the merit that covers the age. Zhaojue Qin said:

"In that case, when masters join together to proclaim the Way, it is certainly permissible for each to have an 'eye' for guiding others. However, they must first clarify the meaning of Mazu and Baizhang."
The pivot. Have you not yet clearly realized his great function? Do you all know that one shout? It is truly like a crashing thunderclap;
those who hear it lose their courage and their very souls. To understand it is to experience three days of deafness. It is just like striking a "poison-coated" drum;
those who hear it lose their bodies and forfeit their lives. Holding up his whisk, he said: "If someone were to ask, 'Is this function itself separate from this function? Master Huo—"
Sheng immediately struck him. Following this, he gave a shout and said again, "Do you still see Mazu and Baizhang?

Ruigan Yun said, "Without the eye that distinguishes dragons from snakes, it is difficult to shoulder the true lineage. Without the ingenuity that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs," [one cannot succeed].
It is difficult to definitively judge between ancient and modern times. Mazu’s single shout did not merely cause Baizhang’s deafness for three days;
it reached all the way to the oceans of worlds atop the King of Cloud-Canopies (Fudǎngwáng), shattering the ear-doors of both sages and ordinary beings alike.
When listening is not authentic, one calls a bell a jar. Do you all know where this falls? The clouds have gathered and the rain has cleared; the vast sky is wide open. A pair—
"The mandarin ducks cannot be painted. Yūan Ān-yú said: "Mazu the Great Master fused heaven and earth and commanded divine strategies.
Baizhang wielded authority beyond the pass, and Huangbo immediately seized the banners and drums; wherever they turned, there was no enemy.

Thus one knows that functional application (*jìngyòng*) is the divine marrow of the successive patriarchs and the tongs and hammer for the myriad species. Fenzhou said: 'Once you have attained awakening, then...'"
Let us not speak of "three days of deaf ears. Shimen said, "If one were not deaf for three days, how could one attain awakening?
To judge it in such a manner—would the ancients have accepted it? This old monk, disregarding the smell of raw meat, shall attempt to settle this for you.
"Beacon fires rise over the towers of Yuyang; within the melodies, every sound is a cry that breaks the heart. Nan’an leaned back, held up his *ruyi* (ceremonial fly-whisk), and said:
"A sacred vessel cannot fail to be profound; only then can it possess spiritual resonance.
O copper plate, O copper plate, if you truly possess such spirit, I pray you may illuminate the form of my beloved a thousand miles away. He struck the *ruyi*.
Treading upon the bow of the boat, he holds his fishing rod; with waves rough and winds tight, it is difficult to catch fish.
Turning back to reflect on how clouds become rain in many places, one sees only the four quarters vying to emerge from the mountains.

(Cuiyan Zhen) A single shout—those who can discern it in the monastic forests are rare. Deafness prevails throughout ancient and modern times, yet they stubbornly apply needles and awls. The lantern strikes its palms and laughs aloud.
A laugh. The incense burner lowers its head and yet frowns.

(Haiyin Xin) Failing to clarify great wisdom, one seeks it further. Following one another, they are unable to employ it freely. When waves are severed and currents cut off, the whole body is manifested.
Deaf for three days, who can know the sound? (Zhaojue Zong)
The sentiments of a guest turn with every step one takes; though possessing great majestic radiance, it cannot be manifested.
Suddenly, a shout deafens both ears; Nata’s eyes open and Huangbo’s face appears.
(Zhenjing Wen) A wooden horse tramples the people of Jambudvīpa; an earthen ox drinks dry the waters of the vast ocean. Thunder fills the sky, and the mountains and peaks tremble.
Crushing it down—look, look! Waves surge upon level ground.

(Baoning Yong) The rain has cleared, yet the drifting clouds have not yet returned; from the clear sky, suddenly comes a clap of thunder. The plum on the ridge has already received the news of spring;
it is not like the mountain peach that blooms all at once. (Shangfang Yi)
A single shout from Jiangxi shook heaven and earth; this total exertion of great function was a total annihilation. For three days his ears were deaf as the wind passed through the trees;
it brought misfortune upon Huangbo, causing him to lose his descendants.

(Gushan Gui) Under the hooves of the colt, the family tradition was lost; from that time forth, news has been communicated across the four seas. From amidst the flames of a raging fire, he fished [the pearl] out.
The Moon: Majestically sitting alone atop Mount Daxiong, (Jingshan Gaofeng) father and son meet;
their affinity is one of kindred spirit. The precious sword of Longquan is ground once more.
To clarify Mazu’s shout of that day, the mountains and rivers of the great earth all go deaf. (Cishou Shen)
A sudden clap of thunder shatters the moon over the clear pool; for three days thereafter, one remains deaf.
Having cast off the fatal malady of the *gāohuáng* (the incurable spot between heart and spine), the monastic groves from this point forward possess their own ancestral style.
Father and son together wander through the weeds; before the assembly, they handle the matter with some sense of shame. A sudden clap of thunder—a shock that startles the heavens.
The earth is directly rendered a vast ocean where not a single drop flows.
(Lan’an Xu) Where the shout ceases, the angry thunder is withdrawn; the family style is utterly lost, leaving nothing behind.
Even if one were to gather up the spoils of war, it would all be destroyed by song and dance. (Shí’ān Shì)
On the winds and waves of the worldly path, I have not seen you; my grieving heart writes in secret—whom can I discuss it with? A sudden thunderclap has just echoed and a clear breeze has arisen;
under the bright sun, the heavens are filled and the stars are distributed.
(Muan Yong) Refined gold does not change its color; why was he deaf for three days? Once a single character enters the gates of officialdom, even nine oxen cannot pull it out.

(Kentang Chong) The heart of the flower is radiant, smiling at the spring sun; The posture of the willow is seductive, following the rain and wind. Precious indeed are these two things that may be compared:
The flushed cheeks when drunk, and the waist when dancing. (Haizhou Ci)
Raising its head and horns, it plays in the spring tide; its remaining tail still burns with lightning-fire.
With a single clap of thunder, behold the transformation: Mount Sumeru leaps five times into the clouds.

(Jingminglian) A single sound of "poisoned lacquer" causes all who hear it to perish; skulls lie scattered everywhere with no place to hide. Extending his three-inch tongue, he brings peace to the nation.
A sword, for a thousand autumns, as chilling and white as frost.
(Yinyuan Qi) Seeking to lure heroes to Maling, he repeatedly reduced his fires while secretly adding troops.
When the firelight revealed the character "heart" on the wooden plaque, Only then did he sigh that his empty fame had been built by a mere youth. (Huatang Yan)
If you walk, I walk; if you run, I run. With a single shout from the Venerable Yang, all traces of him are forgotten.
The mountains and seas are overturned, and the currents flow backward; who among the shrimp, crabs, fish, or dragons dare even look?
(Falin, Verse Two) Hand in hand, we travel the long road as guests; donkey-load and horse-carriage meet in equal measure. At the parting of ways, a single word breaks the heart.
At Chushi, he played the flute horizontally across the wild pond.

Once, when Mazu sent three jars of sauce to him, Baizhang ascended the hall, finished opening the letter, and then picked up his staff, pointing at it and saying, "If you can say something, I shall not break these.
The assembly remained silent, so the Master broke them open and returned to his quarters.
Three bottles of sauce sent as a message to Tongyuan: at that moment, the assembly was startled as it shattered. Between paternal kindness and filial piety, who could entrust them to one another?
Do not say the Chan school is too heartless. (Benjue I) When the command is issued, who dares to violate its sharp edge?
The battlefield is solemn and silent; the eight directions have surrendered. It is only regrettable that we did not encounter the capture of the bandit.
Hand. Shu Ta has achieved a magnificent success. (Lin Ya Qi) In the five watches of night at Jiangcheng, the sound of the horn is early.
Its melody passes on as the east wind pierces the door at dawn. Within the curtains, the beautiful lady sleeps most deeply;
her dream follows the flowing water past the Penglao Islands. (Bai Yu Si)
Baizhang was asked by Yunyan, "For whom do you toil so busily every day? The Master said, "There is one person who needs it.
Yunyan said, "Why do you not let him do it himself? The Master said, "He has no livelihood of his own."
Yunju Zhuang said: "To know how to wield it, one need not have a frost-sharpened blade; to prolong one's life, why necessarily require the nine-fold elixir?
Jingshan Xiu said: "Everyone says that Baizhang swallowed the Buddhas and Patriarchs and his eyes covered heaven and earth, yet he could not avoid dragging through mud and water.
Little do they realize that one who was once a wanderer has particular compassion for travelers, and one who loves wine naturally cherishes those who are intoxicated."
When the assembly had gathered in the hall, Baizhang struck them all at once with his staff to disperse them. He then called out to the great assembly;
as they turned their heads, the Master asked, "What is this?"
Huangbo ascended the hall. Just as the assembly had gathered, he struck them all at once with his staff and dispersed them. He then called out to the great assembly;
the assembly turned their heads, and Huangbo said, "The moon is like a drawn bow; little rain, much wind.
Xuedou Xian said, "If it were Xuedou ascending the hall, as soon as the assembly had gathered, he would strike them all at once with his staff and then simply stop. Tiantong Jue said, "Below..."
"Acting as a matchmaker to seek a dove; using a straight hook to fish for a carp—each has their own means of engaging with things and benefiting living beings.
But what about one who cannot be confined by cages and cannot be turned back by calls? [With this, he struck the incense stand once with his staff]."
A monk asked Baizhang, "What is the extraordinary matter? The Master said, "Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak.
The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
Tiantong Huo said, "Great or small Baizhang, his answer was not yet complete. Jingshan Ji said, "Baizhang merely..."
It is better to be honored where there is no Buddha. Once someone asked Jingshan, "What is the extraordinary matter?
He simply replied, "All of you shall become Buddhas. If the person then prostrated, he would further say, "Just cultivate a heart of resolve, and you will certainly not be deceived."

The ancestral domain is where celestial steeds gallop; the gates of transformation unfold and roll up along different paths. Like a flash of lightning or a spark from flint, they exist as shifting mechanisms;
yet it is laughable that people come to stroke the tiger’s whiskers.

(Xuedou Xian) How could such great capacity and great function be in vain? Sitting alone on the majestic peak, he possesses his own sovereign authority. Were one to err even slightly in transmitting the King’s decree...
As for this person, they must receive three thousand blows upon the crown of their head.
(Baizhang Yuan) *Zongjian Fali*, Volume Nine;
*Zongjian Fali*, Volume Ten.
*Jiyun Tang* (Collection Hall), compiled by Dajian [Huineng], Third Generation, Baizhang:
Whenever he ascended the hall, there was always an old man who followed the assembly to listen to the Dharma. One day, when the assembly had withdrawn, only...
The old man would not step back. The Master asked, "Who are you? He replied, "I am no human being. In the past, during the time of Kāśyapa Buddha, I once lived on this mountain.
When a student asked me, 'Does a great practitioner of the Way still fall within the realm of cause and effect?
