Why? Because he has a place of abiding. The verse says:
Called a thief by others, he swallowed his words and drew in his breath. Though the words were harsh, they were truly a fine flavor.
Not walking where the Tathāgata walks, this man possesses a will that soars toward the heavens.
While Nanquan was sitting in the abbot’s quarters, he asked Liangqin, "Is there still a Buddha within the empty kalpa?
Qian replied, "There is. The Master said, "Who is it? Qian said, "Liangqin. The Master asked, "In what land do you dwell? Qian was speechless.

Dongshan Ying’s successor turned his body and walked away. Haimen Yong said, "If Master Liang had been able to snap his fingers lightly at that moment, he would have ensured that Old Teacher Wang did not look on with indifference."
Nanquan addressed the assembly: "Since my youth, Master Wang has raised a water buffalo.

If I intend to pasture it east of the stream, I cannot avoid consuming the king’s water and grass; if I intend to pasture it west of the stream, I likewise cannot avoid consuming the king’s water and grass.
It is better to simply accept things as they are; then, nothing at all can be perceived."
Yunmen Wenyan said, "Tell me, does the ox enter from within or from without? Even if you can explain clearly where it enters, I shall further ask you:
where is the ox? Zhao of Mount Guishan said, "Yunmen only knows how to seek the ox; he does not know how to pass the halter through its nostrils.
He then took up his staff and said, "The nostrils of the Buddhas of the three periods and all the old monks of the world—"
"Everything has been pierced through at once by this mountain monk’s staff. Now tell me, where is the mountain monk’s own nostrils? After a long silence, he said:
"To charge another with a crime and then sentence them for that very crime. Changqing Ling said:
"Tell me, does Nanquan act for others in the beginning, or does he act for others in the end? Xuedou said: "Pierced through all at once. Yunfeng Yue said: [The same].
What need is there to speak of mere fragments? The entire universe—earth and sky, form and emptiness, light and darkness, the sentient and the insentient—is all contained within this mountain monk.
To let go is to have a place to follow conditions; to hold fast is to leave no door for escape. But tell me:
is letting go better, or is holding fast better? Zhaojue Qin said: "Harmonizing with the light, following along with things, and mingling with the dust of the world."
To avoid the sharp edge of the blade while maintaining mastery over gathering and releasing—this is Nanquan’s fundamental fodder.
Since my youth, I have raised a water buffalo. Sometimes it stands alone on a solitary peak; sometimes it wanders freely through the bustling marketplace.
Whether by the eastern or western stream, it has consistently broken through the dust and pierced the mark. But tell me, where is it now? Tiantong.
Jie said: "Nanquan was like one sketching from a model; Changqing was like one sifting through sand to find gold; Yunmen’s nostrils were already pierced."
Xuedou settles the case based on the facts. He takes up his staff and asks, "Where is there yet another? He then throws down the staff.
Lingyin Yue said, "Master Wang has indeed emptied his heart and poured out his guts, yet he has not yet succeeded in changing customs.
As for me, I have raised only a single donkey, which has been toppling eastward and staggering westward all along. When the time was right, he—
The sun travels by no means less than a thousand or ten thousand *li* in a day; yet when it is contrary, it does not move even a single step.
Tell me, how far apart is this from the Water Ox of Master Wáng? After a long silence, he said: "The fisherman dances his oars; the rustic old man sings his song."
Tiantong Ju said: "Nanquan’s 'tending the ox' is truly extraordinary;
it is simply that at every point there is no way to provide a defense. Why is this so? Because he accepts whatever is allotted to him.
Baolin Xiu said: "Nanquan’s water-buffalo has no nostrils. How can you lot of fellows pierce it? Therefore, Old Shengmo..."
The Human Path. It is identical with all things and encompasses all; it cannot be grasped by any means. Yet tell me, after one has "accepted a little according to one's lot," what then?
"The weeds, grass, and tares worry about being weeded and mowed; hooves, horns, hide, and fur seek their accustomed time.
Gunanmen said: "Nanquan only knew how to seek people among the weeds; alas, he needlessly grew horns, drawing in all [others]."
The Great Master rolled right into the weeds. Have you not yet attained a state of absolute purity? Do you see where Nanquan let go?
"To offer this profound mind to every dust mote and land—this is what is called repaying the Buddha's kindness."
Hanging willows darken the head of the stream; Whether east or west, they are free. Several times I have slept drunk upon a cow’s back;
A few notes of the horizontal flute, one wheel of autumn.
(Lan’an Shu) The Water-Ox of Nanquan is naturally so; According to its lot, it undergoes change. With a great laugh, heaven and earth—
Narrow. There is no further dharma to transmit to others.
(Yuelin Guan) Not letting it flow east or west along the stream, accept a little according to your lot. Cold and warmth are known only by oneself; to whom can this be clearly explained?
(Mu’an Yong) It is better to accept things as they come; to call this an ordinary matter is already a mistake. Amidst the green grass by the stream, his horns are revealed;
in the rain and mist, to whom does that single straw cloak belong? (Tieniu Yin)
At Nanquan, the Water-Ox forgets the whip and halter; north, south, east, and west are all one family. The royal tax has been paid in full and on time;
the cowherd plays his flute as the distant mountains slant away.
(Liyun Tianmu) It is not as good as simply accepting things as they are; when thirsty one drinks and when hungry one eats, for this only oneself knows. Treading through the springtime mist and rain.
Sufficient! Stretching across the universe, by whom else could it be?
(Lian’an asked. Harmony, harmony, harmony! How far east and west? How far south and north? Return, return!
To avoid the wind and the rain. Plow and weed in due season; let us feast in our granaries. (Yangxi Sen)
Nanquan said to a monk, "What a fine wind there was last night. The monk replied, "What a fine wind there was last night.
The Master said, "It blew down a pine tree right in front of the gate. The monk said, "It blew down a pine tree right in front of the gate.

He then said to another monk, "What a fine wind there was last night. The monk asked, "What kind of wind was it? The Master said, "It blew down a pine tree right in front of the gate. The monk said, "It was that."
"What is 'What pine'? The Master said, "One gains, one loses.
Cuiyan Zhen said, "There has been much deliberation among the assembly. Some say that because he answered according to the facts previously, he is said to have 'gained.
Later, it was improper for him to ask, 'What wind? Therefore, he is said to have 'lost. However, they only know of the uniformity of carriages and writings."
What is this blending of mud and jade into one place? Do you not know the source of the Way? Do you not understand the depth of principle? Do you wish to comprehend it?
When meeting a swordsman on the road, you must present your sword; unless you are a poet, do not offer your verse. Zhaojue Qin said:

In general, responding in verse requires seizing the opportune moment to distinguish the dragon from the snake and differentiate the monastic from the lay. This is what is meant by "beating the drum and playing the lute;
meeting, two masters of the same house. As for Nanquan’s saying that one gains and one loses—dare I ask, which one gains and which one loses?
Here, one must be a person of the highest caliber to succeed. Do you understand? The Goose King.
Zhe-lu was not originally of the duck species.
When Nanquan visited Baizhang, Baizhang asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "I have come from Jiangnan.
Baizhang asked, "Have you brought the portrait of Great Master Mazu with you? The Master said, "This very one here. Baizhang said, "What about the one behind him? The Master— [text breaks off].
He shook his sleeves and departed.
This very act of facing the wind from all eight directions is it. The talk of shaking one’s sleeves moves heaven and earth; how admirable is Old Teacher Wángshān selling himself!
He acts neither as a lowly man nor as a noble one. (Lóngmén Yuǎn)
The elder brother is difficult for the elder brother; the younger brother is difficult for the younger brother. Mazu’s true essence is precisely this:
it shakes the eighteen rapids of the West River, and though there is no wind upon the surface of the water, waves arise of their own accord.
(Stone Creek Moon). Nanquan asked Shenshan, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from pounding rice. The Master said, "Do you pound with your hands or do you pound with your feet?"
The mountain remained silent. The Master said, "Ask me, and I will tell you. The mountain then asked, "Is it struck with the hand, or struck with the foot?
The Master said, "Take this clearly to heart; later, when you meet someone with clear eyes, present it to them."
Yunyan Cheng spoke on his behalf, saying: "Only one without hands or feet understands how to strike. Baoning Yong spoke on his behalf, saying:
"The Master possesses all-encompassing wisdom.
While Nanquan was inspecting the hall, he led an ox into the hall; the Head Seat stroked the ox's back with his hand.
[The Master] descended. The Master then ceased [speaking]. Zhaozhou placed two bundles of grass before the Head Seat.

Guoqing Ying said: "Zhaozhou and Nanquan are much like peddlers selling goods from Yangzhou inside their own house. As for the Head Seat acting in such a manner, one can only say his courtesy is known."
"Properly provide and look after the fodder and materials. Why must the skin and hair be uniform?
This provokes those who merely resemble the herd, causing their true horns and peaks to remain incomplete.
(From *Bǎoyèyuán*) Nanquan asked the *vina* (steward), "What are you doing today during the communal labor (*pusqing*)? He replied, "Grinding. The Master said, "The millstone follows..."
"You are pulling hard. You must not move the central pivot. He remained silent.

Baofu spoke on his behalf, saying, "Up until now you have been pulling the millstone; now it seems you cannot do it. Fayan spoke on his behalf, saying, "If that is so, then you are not pulling at all.
Zifu Yu spoke on his behalf, saying, "The Master has already moved; how can one prevent others?"
[The Master] moves. Jiang Tianquan speaks on his behalf: "If I were here, I would drag him here and grind him.
Jian Nan-yin raises [the point]: "One must not touch the central tree. The first offender’s crime is doubled. Previously you were dragging [him], but now that does not accord with your former words;
it does not match your subsequent speech. If this is so, then he is not being dragged. Thank you for your diligent labor. (And) harmonize.

Already having stirred up contention, he forbids others from stirring it; like a leper dragging along his companions, if I were there, I would have pulled him in and dragged him across the floor, thrusting his head into a basin of glue, saying, "What a fine central pillar!"—unprovoked, Nanquan has torn it to shreds.
Even those who avoid the stench of leftovers still partake in a portion of it; you must not touch the center.
Xinshuzi then said, "Seal the dog's mouth! Thus he managed to cause Master Wang to have his mouth rendered mute.
Nanquan asked Grand Master Lu Xun, "When you go there, what will you use to govern the people? He replied, "I will govern the people with wisdom."
The Master said, "If that were so, then the living beings there would all be plunged into misery.
Shending Kui replied, "He possesses both literary talent and military strategy; his belly is full of armor and weapons.

While it is not that he lacks the ability to serve the sovereign and benefit the people, Lu Xun cannot yet be considered a guest under the Gate of the Patriarchs. To truly possess the claws and fangs of the ultimate path of our school—"
It is said that living beings have fallen into a state of misery; Master Wang, you must look after them before it is too late.

Again, he offered this verse: "Living beings are in a mire of suffering; I shall raise the dead and restore life. I will extract the grit from their eyes And pull out the nails from behind their heads. Reflecting back, I see how plain ink was once dyed with sorrowful silk;
From of old, those who carve ornate patterns have lost their virtue."
Nanquan, Luzu, Shanshan, and Guizong—these four were departing from Mazu’s place.
As they parted ways on the road, the Master (Nanquan) thrust down his staff and said, "If you can speak, you are hindered by this; if you cannot speak, you are also hindered by this.
Guizong pulled the staff and struck the Master once, saying, "It is just this! Teacher Wang speaks thus."
"What is obstructed and what is unobstructed? Lu Zu said, "This very phrase is widely disseminated throughout the world.
Xuedou asked, "Is there anything that is not disseminated? Lu Zu said, "There is. Xuedou asked, "What is it that is not disseminated?
Lu Zu made the gesture of clapping his hands.
A difficult elder brother and a difficult younger brother—first, second, third, and fourth—born of the same mother, each one resembling the other.
Carrying their staffs with them, they perform on whatever stage they encounter. Do not say there is any obstruction; a single phrase spreads through heaven and earth.
(Fojian Qín) Obstruction and non-obstruction: when the dragon roars, the mist rises. Spreading and not spreading: a fly clings to the horse’s tail. North, south, east, and west.
"Thousand li, ten thousand li—how eminent! (The Perfect Enlightenment is Manifested).
While Nanquan was drinking tea with three others, Luzu lifted up his tea bowl and said, "When the world was first formed, there already was this.
The Master said, "People today recognize only this, but do not recognize the world. Zong said, "It is so."
The Master said, "Brother, do you not share this same view? Zong then picked up his cup and said, "Can you say anything before the world was formed?
The Master made a gesture of clapping his hands, and Zong made a gesture of receiving the clap with his face.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Luzu sifts soil and raises dust; Nanquan mixes mud and blends water; Guizong stirs up fire and scatters ashes;
Shan-shan sits watching success and failure. Do you understand? When arrow-points meet, there is no yielding;
four people together lift a single cup."
Nanquan said: "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know that there is; the black oxen and white cows, however, do know that there is.
Daowei Zhi said: "Since the Buddhas of the three periods do not know that there is, when have the black oxen and white cows ever even dreamed of it?
You must clearly realize that there is a person above who knows that there is, before you can attain it. But how is it that one knows?"
Some people drink the official wine and lie upon the official streets; they die where they stand and are buried where they fall.
Upon the battlefields, there are countless heroic men, their corpses piled as high as mountains and heaped like peaks. Boshanlai said: "The hands span the earth; the tail reaches to heaven."
Master Wang acted among those of different species. The Buddhas of the three periods did not know he existed; he gathered the bright moon atop the shadowless tree.
The black oxen and white cows, however, knew he was there; they clipped the white clouds within the valleys where no one should be.
Who knows this meaning? None but the long-intoning one. Yuan-an Meng said: "I must ask everyone: how [do you understand]?"
"This black slave and white ox know something of this matter. Another replied, "The land of Jambūdvīpa has lapis lazuli ground;
before the Lion Rock, the water and grass are fragrant. The Hermitage Master said, "If you speak such words as these, there will come a day when you shall wear iron bits and carry a saddle."
The Buddhas of the three periods do not know it exists; each one faces south and gazes at the Northern Dipper.

The dark-brown ox and the white cow, however, know it exists; they wear horns, hold up their heads, and roar like lions. They tread upon the four corners of the earth, yet remain perfectly round; an eight-cornered millstone rolls through the empty sky.
If you try to seek it out, you will be struck across the spine and dragged away; you may grasp the nostrils, but you lose your mouth. I ask you, Puhua—what is this?
A headless donkey. How does it compare to Zi Hu’s single dog?
(Yuánwù Qín) The Buddhas of the three periods do not know its existence; old and decrepit, it wanders abroad.
Its eyelids cover all five Sumeru mountains; it performs somersaults within the great ocean. (Jìngshān Gǎo 2)
The dark-skinned slave and the white ox, conversely, know that there is [Buddha-nature]. The waterfall does not flow; the green mountains run.
How laughable, the Master Wuzhuo of no cause—mistaking a winnowing basket for an ironing board.

The bird from beyond the passes nests on the southern branches; the horses of Ji province neigh in the northern wind. The tawny slave and the white ox—by even an inch they have never passed one another.
Ten thousand mountains are all cut off at once; ten thousand streams flow entirely toward the east. As soon as the Heavenly King joins his palms, Nātha smashes the imperial bell.

(Or the essence of the hermitage: Wavering and hurried, tangled and disheveled; a hundred things cannot be grasped, nothing at all can be endured. In silence, one knows for oneself that the ground is secure;

Trusting fully, they eat their fill. (Tiantong Jue) The village elder sacrifices to the river god;

(Puk-ung Hyeon): The Way of the noble man declines; the Way of the petty man grows. Those with merit are punished; those without merit are rewarded.

"One must not slander the King and the Master. [The host] said, "How would I dare slander the Venerable? The Master then sneezed and asked, "How many were there?

Thirty coins buy a thatched sickle; meeting face-to-face, he holds up the first tally.

a solitary wild goose descends gracefully toward the distant sky. (Like a place of practice.)

The Master replied, "I shall become a water buffalo on the mountain below. The monk asked, "May I follow you there?
The Master said, "If you would follow me, you must bring back a blade of grass."
Within the categories, it is difficult to discern; one must be clear and distinct. Wearing horns and shrouded in fur, one has not yet awakened.

wait until mealtime, prepare the food, eat it yourself, and then bring a portion up to me on the mountain. After a short while, the monk ate it himself, then smashed all the cooking utensils and lay down on his bed.
When the Master waited and saw that he had not returned, he went back. Upon arriving, he saw [the monk].

The monk lay down. The Master also went to one side and lay down. When the monk got up and left, the Master remained behind and said, "When I lived in the hermitage in the past, there was a clever practitioner; even until now, I have not seen him."
Wuzu Ke said, "This too is a poor man thinking of his old debts. Cuiyan Zhi said, "These two fellows:
they do not reach the village in front, nor do they reach the inn behind. Gao Feng Miao said, "Although Nanquan steps firmly at every pace,"
One cannot help but follow others in their rising and falling. Even if this monk were able to eat his fill and sleep soundly, he would certainly not know that rice is made from grain.
If there were so much as a single word of falsehood in Gaofeng’s announcement, he would fall forever into the Hell of the Plucked Tongue.
Yuanmiao Yu said: "The monk's demeanor at that time was truly lovely. After Nanquan had passed away, one might well have thought of this gentleman; alas, it was too late to see him.
Why did he not, when the monk came down the mountain, dig a pit and bury him?
Would that not have settled the matter according to the facts? A monk remarked, "An old fellow with a big mouth! Yuanmiao then gave him a blow of his staff and drove him away.
[The Master] came out. Yun’an Yue said: “Although Nanquan possessed the mechanism for trapping a tiger, he still did not exhaust his skill.
At that time, seeing him sleeping soundly with his head on the mat, one should simply have let out a great laugh; this would surely have left that fellow in a state of doubt.”
Shengke Yu said: "What is this talk of 'not seeing the Way for twenty years'? When the cauldron and bowls were smashed, it had already vanished long ago.
Quan went and lay down beside him; he was merely chasing tracks and seeking shadows. To raise such a case after twenty years—how pitiful!
What is the meaning? From before, no one has recognized his merit from shedding sweat on the battlefield; he simply wishes to once more discuss his epoch-making achievements.
The "blow-off-hair" sword is sharp; the waves against the current are clear. The spirit and ambition of a man do not conform to common sentiment.
You campaign in the north, I strike at Qin in the west. For ten thousand generations, may we together enjoy peace and prosperity. (Nantang Jing)
Short trousers, long tunic, and a white ramie headcloth; with a wheezing sound, he hurriedly pushes his wheel beneath the moon.
Meeting him on the road in Luoyang, everyone is a merchant engaged in trade.
(Xutang Yuyi) A single lump of gold—a blunt hoe—summons the ghosts of broad daylight to come and steal it. Since he departed, there has been no trace.
Traces. Wherever the eye turns, the green mountains are all sorrow.
(Zhongfeng Ben) The young lords of the Five Tombs need not boast of their wealth; the high monk with his hundred patches does not disdain poverty.
When spring arrives after the second month in Jiangnan, the yellow orioles sing throughout the villages of apricot blossoms. (Shanfu Zheng)
While Nanquan was admiring the moon, Zhaozhou pointed at it and asked, "When did you come to be like this?
The Master replied, "Twenty years ago, Old Wang also came this way. Zhaozhou asked, "How about right now? The Master then returned to his quarters.
Tiantong Jue said: "Set aside for a moment what was twenty years ago; how about after twenty years? Do you still know where Old Wang’s footsteps lie?
No spirit bed in the inner room; the whole family does not wear mourning. Zimei Zhou said:
"In this place of Leping, we do not concern ourselves with whether it is twenty years ago or twenty years later. It is precisely at the eighth..."
"What about the fifteenth night of the month? After a long silence, he said: "Better to cut out one's tongue than to violate a taboo.

The sword falls into the cold pond; vainly one carves marks upon a drifting boat. Frost-flakes and surging waves bring sorrow to men. The old fisherman has finished his casting and returns to the deep cove;
A pair of mandarin ducks alight by the river crossing. (Shangfang Yue)
The new moon’s reflection sinks into the abyss of the azure sky; the dragons and serpents at the bottom of the water are startled and cannot sleep.
Suddenly their heads and horns collide, and flying smoke and drifting mists fill the plains.
(The Ancient Sailboat) Nanquan, along with Guizong and Magu, went to pay homage to the National Teacher. On the way, the Master drew a circle on the ground.
Xiang said, "If you can express the Way, you may go. Zong then sat down right in the midst of Xiang. Gu stepped forward and performed a woman’s bow.
The Master said, "If that is so, then you shall not go. Zong asked, "What kind of mental activity is this? Thereupon, the Master called out to him by name and they returned together.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "If I had seen him at that time, I would have given each person a blow of my staff, just to ensure peace throughout the world.
Yunju Xi said, "Recently, Nanquan wanted to pay his respects to the National Teacher; why did he instead call him back?
Tell me, what was the meaning of the ancient one? Baoci then raised the question: "As for Nanquan speaking in such a manner..."
These are words of acceptance; these are words of non-acceptance. Wuzu Yan said:
"The three men are the Samādhi of the Wisdom Torch and the Samādhi of King Śrīsaṃbhava. Jianfu Xing said: "Emperor Wu sought immortals but did not find them;
Wang Qiao sat upright and ascended to heaven. Nevertheless, among the three, some have seen the National Teacher, while others have not.
The Master’s Bottom Line. Nanhua Ying said: "Discerning the melody when the strings are moved belongs to Magu Guizong;

seizing the drum and capturing the banner is especially fitting for the old man Nanquan. It reaches the point where those who travel together do not walk in step, and where one sides with principle rather than kin.
Where the white clouds end, there is green mountain; the traveler is further beyond the green mountain. Tiantong Jue said: "I, when..."
At that time, as soon as he saw [the monk], he immediately rubbed away the circular mark.
Not only did he break through Nanquan’s old nest, but he also left Guizong with no place to rest his body. Magu could not display his skillful means;
Nanquan said, "In that case, you do not go. "Indeed, indeed," [said] Tianbao Shu. "The three great elders displayed their skillful means in such a manner while on the road."
The two of them—when will they ever meet the National Teacher? Zhongfeng Ben said: "Nanquan drew a line in the ground to make a prison;
Guizong fell into a pit and a ditch; Magu was respectful yet lacked propriety. Examining them closely:
one person’s eyes look down upon the four seas; another’s tongue reaches up to the Brahma Heaven; and another enters hell as swiftly as an arrow. —Xiaoyan.
Baoyun said: "Before the three elders had even set foot on the road, their nostrils were already in the hands of the National Teacher.

Yet, as soon as they reached mid-journey, they were seen playing with the 'fragrance of gruel and rice. Qingshan Xiu said: "Although these three great elders were born of the same root, they did not die of the same root;
each has his own way of manifesting himself. However, among these three men, there is one who is worthy to be a teacher—if one were to select him..."
"It is so; I grant you the eye of discernment. Tianjing Xin said: "One person buys a hat to fit the head;
one person takes a mistake as a success; one person looks at the tower and strikes the tower; there is yet another whose forehead breaks into a sweat."
The archer shoots his arrow at the monkey; why does it circle the tree so straight? Of the thousands and tens of thousands, who has ever hit its mark?
Calling out to one another, come back home! Do not ascend or descend upon the road to Caoxi. Again he said: "The road to Caoxi is level and plain;
for what reason, then, should one not ascend or descend? (Mingjue Xian)
Vast and boundless, the great earth is covered in snow a foot deep; rivers and lakes form a single expanse, impossible to distinguish.
An old fisherman, clad in his rain cape, returns under the moonlight—who would say that the traveler’s path is cut off in the night?

(By Baoning Yong) Skillfully seizing and boldly grasping, how bitter and arduous! Who can discern the distant from the near within this? As falling flowers and fragrant grasses lie empty at the forked path.
On the road, fine rain and slanting winds obscure all people.

(Min Gufo) Nanquan, Magu, and Guizong—though their eyes of the Way were originally not obstructed—they went to pay respects to the National Teacher to behold his physical excellence, yet they labored in vain, reaching only halfway. (Shushan Ru)
Carrying a flower drum in hand, he reaches the foot of the city wall; wearing his hemp sandals backward, he passes through the narrow gate.
Smiling, he writes ancient characters upon firewood; everyone comes to walk with him in the twilight moonlight.

(By Yuet Tang Chang) Having finished his meal at a rustic inn, he casually asks for directions. As a master of the Way, he always carries his staff and wooden clappers with him. Whenever they meet, people all say: "Retire from office."
Go! How could one ever have seen a single person beneath the forest?
(Nirgrantha) A golden needle embroiders a jade mandarin duck; the stone maiden holds it forth without concealment.
Just as the wooden man casts a sidelong glance, to this day they remain paired but never become a couple. (Wan’an Rou)
Three children embrace a flower drum, beating it so that the south stirs and the north moves. The handle of the Dipper hangs low at night as heaven is about to dawn;
the sound of the flute disperses before the Jade Tower.
(Nanxun’s Inquiry) Nanquan asked the Dharma Master, "Can you lecture on the sutras for me? The Master replied, "For your sake, O Monk..."
Jiā was expounding on Chan. Another person, acting as the *upādhyāya*, was lecturing on the sutras. The Master said, "One must not trade golden pellets for silver pellets.
Fālínyī spoke on behalf of the monk, saying, "I did not expect that even within the School of the Patriarchs, there would still be such twisting and squeezing of the nostrils."
The ball rolls on the platter, and the platter rolls the ball. In this moment of direct encounter, one transcends and lets go; this is the "good view.
The people of the world know its value but do not know its price; to pick it up with the hand as it comes is no difficult matter.
(Zhengtang’s Discernment) Nanquan said: "Old Wang is selling his body; is there anyone who will buy it? A monk stepped forward and said:
"I will buy it. The Master said, "Neither as something expensive nor as something cheap—how will you buy it? The monk had no reply.
Zhaozhou spoke on his behalf, saying, "Next year, I will make a robe of cloth for the Master. Wolong Qiu said, "The Master belongs to me.
Heshan Yin spoke on his behalf, saying, "What kind of principle is that? Mingzhao Qian [spoke on his behalf].
A monk beside him who was bidding said, "It is well-placed; let us go.
Xuedou Xian said, "Although these masters compete to buy it, they still do not understand how to surrender their strategic advantage. But tell me, would Nanquan have consented?
Even Cuifeng intended to offer a price that would leave Nanquan with no way to advance and no way to retreat. After a long silence, he said, "There is room elsewhere."
"The Master may not have it. Yinjing Cen said, "I have my share in repaying his kindness. Yunju Zhuang said, "The nose-rope is in my hands.

Xiaoyan Bao said, "Today this mountain monk offers a brand-new price, so that the old fellow can neither belong to another nor belong to himself. I wait for him to say, 'Do not treat it as precious...'"
"What would you do if they treated you as a lowly person and asked how much they should pay for you?
Just say, 'Please, Master, return to the Abbot’s quarters for a moment of tea. Yuan’an Meng said: "Cui-feng could only serve as Nanquan’s slave.

But as for this situation where there is no door to enter and no path to retreat—does it still allow for Cui-feng? Gu-nan Men said: "When the various elder masters handle the case in this way, does it still..."
"Do you agree with Nanquan’s intention? [The monk] did not realize that Nanquan was comparing himself to others;
it was out of compassion that he spoke such words of "falling into the weeds. At that time, had he been asked in this way, he should have simply said, "If so, then the Master and I emerge as equals.
By thus revealing his own skillful means, he would not have rendered Nanquan's single act of Dharma-giving in vain. Do you understand?
"Zhaozhou said: 'Moziqi has gone and will not return; how deeply lamentable! One knows not who else in heaven and earth can be a true知音 (zhīyīn—'one who understands').
Longchi Zhen said: "The Master's three and a half lines—whom does he ask to write them? Tianmu Lü said: "Master Wang merely seeks someone to set a price on his words;
little does he realize that his maidservants and slaves will bring this upon themselves for a thousand ages."
The King is old and clearly intends to sell himself; in an instant, he entrusts [himself] to another. Piteous, the world vies to offer its price.
(Foyin Yuan) Though the transaction is completed, the contract is not genuine.
(Xiyuan Bao’s continuation) Nanquan has opened his shop on a grand scale; rare and precious goods are sent out to dominate the market. Although many vie to purchase, the price offered—
Too little. To this day, the whole world debates this point.
(Yexuan Zun) When an old man sells himself, it is difficult to set a price; whether high or low, it is not easy to find a fitting recompense.
Had he not felt regret at that time, he would have been brought back and entrusted to the garden keeper. (Haiyin Xin)
Neither noble nor base; high and low are separated by a mere hair’s breadth.
When benefit and harm are clearly explained to others, do the clever monks see or not?
(Ding of Daitang) Old in years yet high in spirit, coming and going without measure, he travels by night in his haste and loses his torch. *Tu!* Smash the ghosts to pieces!

The Gatekeeper. *Sili sili, sulu sulu.* (Dream-Monastery Vinaya) Once, when a monk came to inquire after him and stood with his hands joined in greeting, Nanquan said, "Too worldly. The monk then pressed his palms together in a formal gesture of reverence.
Nanquan said, "Too monastic. The monk was speechless.
Jingshan Daowu said: "Joining the palms is too monastic; crossing the hands is again worldly.
When it is neither of these, there is no place for your venerable self to rest. Having no place to rest—therein lies the core. *Oṃ suru suru siri siri ha.*
Lately, the royal decrees have become somewhat strict; it is not permitted to jostle for position or snatch away trade.
Tianning Qi said: "To clasp the hands is too worldly; to join the palms is too monastic. Neither monastic nor worldly—who would dare assign a name?
Even to examine this closely is merely to set up a target and invite an arrow. Tell me, where does it land: on the monk’s side, or on Nanquan’s side?"
Palms joined in reverence is the way of the great monk; hands crossed is the way of the laity. With hands cast loose as one steps out the gate, the mountains are blue and the waters are green.
Changing one’s pace and shifting one’s body, this is the ancient wind: the wooden man joins in singing the song of non-arising.

(Da Hongshui) Moving north, south, east, or west, there is no place where one does not find benefit. This makes people deeply love Old Nanquan. His eyebrows are knotted together as if in mutual entanglement.
It is like this: "The nostrils reach the heavens, yet they pass through nothing. (Longmen Yuan).
Once, when Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "Where does a person who truly knows go?
the Master replied, "I go to become a water buffalo at the house of a lay donor in front of the mountain. Zhaozhou said, "Thank you for the instruction. The Master said, "Last night..."
"The third watch moon shines upon the window.
Yunfeng Yue said, "Had it not been for Nanquan’s later words, we would have ended up breaking down the city of Caizhou.
Jingshan Daokai said, "Yunfeng lost one of his eyes; he did not realize that it was precisely because of those later words that [the city] was broken down on the spot."
Caizhou. Dongshan Ying said: "Yunfeng looks at the tower and strikes the tower; Jingshan uses a wedge because of a hole.
If judged by the eyes of a true monk, I dare say that both have not even dreamed of it. But tell me, what excellence does Dongshan possess?
After a long silence, he said: "A lion does not eat the remains left by a hawk; a swift falcon does not strike a dead hare."
Tugging out the nostrils—where is it? Mud and water are tossed about at will. As the sun sets, he sits astride his donkey and rides away;
then again, a sliver of moon rises over the Eastern Mountain.
(Baoning Yong) What is seen with the eyes is but the ordinary. It does not startle, yet it endures for a long time. It remains through the night at the cold window.
The moon, as before, shines upon the thatched hall at the third watch.
(Gushan Gui) Measuring the body to cut the robe, gauging the water to drive the pestle—not a hair’s breadth of error. Yet, for now, stay outside the gate.
(Jingshan Gao) Becoming a water buffalo in the donor’s house, you come and go as you please; you never encroach upon the people’s crops.
Sowing grain—why must it be Nanquan facing Zhaozhou? (Zhao Tang’s first verse:
He pulls open the locks of the golden hall and strikes the bell of the jade tower. The traveler who, greedy for his journey, has not yet returned, needlessly seeks his own tracks.
(Mu’an Yong) Elegant and slender, her sash is fragrant;
I long for you as I catch the morning breeze. The water-lily flowers blush at being face-to-face; I turn my steps to tread upon the fragrant thicket. (Xiāoshān Shù)
There is one who, weary of this body, lies upon an ivory bed; taking a step, he pulls at the hem of my robe as we reach the painted hall.
Had there not been three feet of cloth to cover my face, I would have nearly put that ungrateful lover to shame.
(By Buryak Pu) Nanquan sent a letter to Zhunyu, saying: "Principle changes according to phenomena; vastness is not external. When phenomena accord with principle..."
The monk asked, "What is 'the vast expanse is not within'? After Master Zhenju finished reading the letter from Sengda, he asked, "How is it that 'the vast expanse is not without'?
Zhenju said, "To ask one and answer a hundred is no hindrance. The monk asked, "How is it that 'the silent stillness is not within'?
Zhenju said, "To perceive sounds and forms through opposition is not the mark of a master. The monk then asked Changsha, "What is 'the vast expanse is not without'?"
Sandeng stared at him with wide eyes and asked, "What is 'solitude that is not internal'? Sandeng closed his eyes and stared back.
The monk then asked Zhaozhou, "What is 'vastness that is not external'? Zhaozhou made the gesture of eating a meal. [The monk] asked again, "What is 'solitude that is not internal'?
Zhaozhou made the gesture of wiping his mouth with his hand. Upon hearing this, the Master said, "These three men..."
"It is not a mistake for you to be my disciple," said Zhaojue Qin.
"Although Nanquan had the karmic conditions to raise such sons, alas, he loved his children so much that he failed to see their ugliness.
Little did he realize that among these three, one had eyes but no feet, one had feet but no eyes, and one had both feet and eyes."
They both lack eyes. Nevertheless, both may serve as teachers for Nanquan. Why is this so? Because their understanding of principle and phenomena is clear.
Once, when a monk asked Nanquan, "Before one's parents were born, where was the nose? the Master said, "Father..."
"The mother has already given birth. Where are the nostrils?
Guoqing Ying said, "When going, the nostrils reach toward heaven; when coming, the feet tread upon solid ground.
Why seek someone’s judgment? After a long silence, he said, "Were it not for Yang Deyi, who would have seen Ma Xiangru?"
Under Nanquan’s assembly, the head cook prepared two portions of food and went to the garden to oversee the grounds.
When it was time for the gardener to spread out his alms bowl, a "Buddha-remembering" bird suddenly began to sing. The gardener struck the bowl once; as the bird sang again, he struck it once more.
When the singing ceased, the gardener asked the head cook, "Did you hear that? The cook replied, "I did not understand. The gardener struck the bowl again.
[The Master] said, "Stop. Falingyin took his place and said, "Hitherto there have been two parts; why must there now be three?
Will this not leave the head gardener speechless? [The Master] said, "Not so. Pour the food out before the birds and see what the head gardener does then."
One day, while Chan Master Zhichang of Guizong on Mount Lu (a successor of Mazu) was weeding, a monk who was a lecturer in the sutras came to visit him.
Suddenly seeing a snake passing by, the Master cut it with his hoe. The monk said, "I have long admired Guizong;
I never expected you would be such a coarse practitioner. The Master replied, "You are coarse, and I am coarse. The monk asked, "What is this coarseness? The Master held up [his hoe].
He picked up his hoe and asked, "What is the subtle? The Master made the gesture of slaying a snake. The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall follow it.
The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment following it, where did you see me slay a snake? The monk was speechless.
Xuefeng asked Deshan, "What was the meaning behind the ancients' act of beheading a snake? Deshan struck him. Xuefeng immediately ran away.

Deshan called out, "Wait, monk! Xuefeng turned his head back. Deshan said, "In the future, when you attain realization, you will finally understand that this old fellow’s heart is one of thoroughgoing, compassionate concern.
Cui峰 Xian said, "Guizong only knew how to guard the beginning, but could not protect the end. Deshan..."
Could he truly act according to his command? Not yet having clarified the matter of "slaying the snake," he said, "Everyone, look! Today at Cuifeng, I shall slay three or five.
With his staff, he struck them and dispersed the assembly.
The great function moves freely in all directions like a flash of lightning; even the Śakrāloka eyes are as if smeared with glue.
Deluded followers scramble with their lips and teeth in their dreams, yet they recall following him—following along with him.
(Haiyin Xin) Performing somersaults upon a ten-thousand-fathom pole, casting the fishing hook into the heart of the great ocean waves: his great substance returns to its very flesh and bone.
"Excellent! Without applying rouge and powder, one is still elegant.
(Nanhua Bing) When Prefect Li Bo questioned Guizong, saying, "I do not ask about the Three Vehicles or the twelve divisions of the teachings;
what is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master then held up his fist and asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said:
The well-read scholar did not even recognize his own fist. He said, "I truly do not understand. The Master said, "If you understand, it will be of use to you on the road;
if you do not understand, it will merely circulate as worldly convention."
Falin-yin said: "Guizong only knows that others are 'cuo-da' (scholars); he does not realize that he himself is an even greater 'cuo-da.
He then held up his fist and said: 'This is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. If you understand it, you may freely enjoy it on the road and let it circulate as worldly truth.
If you do not understand it, then enjoying it on the road and letting it circulate as worldly truth will all remain separated from you by three layers of dust. Suddenly—"
One person said, "This is a fist. Falin remarked, "It is simply that you wish to speak this way. Jinshan Quan said, "The Prefect is acting foolishly;
Guizong is talking too much. You have not yet even dreamed of the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West."
Guizong addressed the assembly: "I now wish to speak of Chan; all you sons, come forward together. The great assembly approached, and the Master said:
"Listen to the practice of Avalokiteśvara, which skillfully responds to all places. A monk asked, "What is the practice of Avalokiteśvara?
The Master snapped his fingers and said, "Do you all hear it? They replied, "We hear it. The Master said, "A whole crew of fellows—just like that!"
"What is it that you seek within? With these words, he struck him with his staff and drove him away, then returned to the abbot’s quarters with a great laugh.
Wuxue (Wumen) transcended by a mere snap of the fingers; the faculty of the ear was purified. Penetrating beyond both hearing and non-hearing—how wondrous is the practice of Avalokiteśvara!
The tip of the staff points out the Vajra King; it serves as a bridge across perilous paths.
(Yuanwu Keqin) Once, while Guizong and Nanquan were traveling together, they took their leave of one another during a tea ceremony.
Nanquan said, "Regarding the dialogues we have previously discussed, brother, we both already know them. However, if someone should suddenly ask about the ultimate matter hereafter—"
"How is it? The Master said, "This patch of ground is excellent for pitching a hermitage. [The monk] said, "Setting aside the pitching of the hermitage for a moment, what is the ultimate matter?
The Master then kicked over the tea kettle and rose, saying, "Brother, finish your tea."
"I have not yet drunk the tea," [Nanquan] said. The Master said, "This talk of yours would not even digest a drop of water.
Nanquan then desisted.
Wuzu Jie said, "Nanquan only knows how to be a guest; he does not know how to be a host. Guishan Zhe said, "Nanquan..."
When Quan met the strong, he became weak; when Guizong met the weak, he became strong. For thirty years they traveled together, yet in the end, the matter could not be settled through deliberation.
Even so, he was still one hair’s breadth behind Old Master Wang. Zhaojue Qin said: [The text provided ends here.]
Who would not be struck with awe by such startling words? Some say that Nanquan’s attempt to engage Guizong failed, which is why he was rebuked.
Little do they realize that "the traveler is still beyond the green mountains. Jiangshan, not sparing his eyebrows, provides this footnote for you all:
Nanquan poked his head out too far; Guizong stood as steep as ten thousand fathoms.
Tell me, is there still a way to emerge? A shout will surely leave you deaf for three days.
Tiantong Hua said: "Nanquan’s journey was too hurried; Guizong pierced through where it was thinnest.
Although these two elders revealed the true eye of Mazu, they have not yet dreamed of the ultimate matter. Why? Because their homes are in the eastern provinces."
Guizong asked his junior attendant as he was taking leave, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to study the 'Five Flavors' Chan in various quarters.
The Master said, "In various quarters there are the Five Flavors of Chan; here, I have only the One Flavor of Chan. A monk asked, "What is the One Flavor of Chan?
The Master struck him. The monk said, "I understand! I understand! The Master said, "Speak! Speak!"
"Come! As soon as the monk opened his mouth, the Master struck him again.
Huangbo Yun said, "Of the eighty-four *śāstṛ*s that Great Master Mazu produced, every one of them was dripping wet;
only Guizong was slightly better. Cui峰 Xian said, "What is there in using strength to deceive the weak?"
[The Master said: "Difficult! Why do you not study the 'one-flavor Chan' that I have here? Just tell him: 'Withdraw! Wait until he picks it up.
Some blind fellows merely go on shouting "HŪṂ, HŪṂ. Under Xuedou’s gate, who would dare [to speak thus]? Zhaojue Qin said:
"Had it not been for Huangbo’s profound discernment of the situation, it would have resulted in laboring in vain. Tianjing Xin added: "A different matter."
Yun said: "It was precisely because Huangbo deeply discerned the subtle nuances that he labored in vain. Zifu added:
"Guizong was fortunate in having this single flavor of Chan; it was only through groundless talk of 'too much salt' and 'too much vinegar' that it ended up becoming five flavors."
Nowadays, there are those who take their leave to study the "five-flavor Chan," merely saying, "Be careful on the road.
If one were truly a man of substance, they would surely have a different way of life. After Tianning Qi finished citing Huangbo’s words, he said:
"What do you mean by 'it is but a trifle'? It is simply not yet so. Here, I have only the 'one-flavor Chan'—and with that, I overturn the meditation seat! Thus he was seen.
Not taking it up, one contemplates it from a thousand miles away.
The five flavors and the single flavor—once tasted, one must let out a sigh.
When the command is issued at the peak of the Golden Wheel, the chilling clear breeze is truly fearsome. (Shijianming)
I brew fragrant and pure wine, yet its price remains low; to this day, few travelers tread the official road. The single flavor of returning to the source is like continuous bitterness;
how many young monks of the monastic groves have missed their chance?
(Changling Zhuo) Plum blossoms in the snow, mountains in the mist—easy to behold, difficult to paint. Had you not entered the ranks of the worldly, you would have known better.
Yan Duo-mai (Sheshua) painted peonies. (Xuegu Yong) While Guizong was plastering a wall, Bai Sharen came by.
The Master asked, "Are you a scholar of the noble kind or a scholar of the petty kind? He replied, "A scholar of the noble kind.
The Master then struck the mud-tray once. Bai then passed him the mud. The Master took it and used it immediately.
After a long silence, he said, "Could you be the quick-witted Minister Bai? The man replied, "I dare not say so. The Master said, "You have only a share of 'passing through the mud.

Three sounds open the universal gate; the weary souls in the sea of suffering cannot be called back.

"Every touch of the eye is Bodhi; scattering sand is showing you three things even more extensively.
When patch-robed monks meet, they laugh 'he-he'; spring birds warble as they scold falling blossoms.

He hurriedly chased them with his staff, saying, "This lot of fellows—there isn't a single one among you who has any wisdom! You've kicked over my marker and taken the vegetables back!"
Yunju Zhuang said: "Suppose there were a monk who pulled up a single stalk of vegetable; would he have grasped Guizong’s meaning?
He took up his staff, struck the incense table, and said: "Guizong the Master has arrived! He leaned the staff against it and descended from the seat.
Guizong was once asked by Li Bo, the Regional Inspector of Jiangzhou: "I have heard that Mount Sumeru can contain a mustard seed; I do not doubt this.
But as for a mustard seed containing Mount Sumeru—is this not mere idle talk? The Master said, "People say that you, the Prefectural Governor, have read ten thousand scrolls of books, is that so?
Li replied, "I dare not say so. The Master said, "Suppose your body were as small as a coconut; where would those ten thousand scrolls of books be?"
"Where does one place it? Li bowed his head and remained silent.
"Letting go, the sun and moon shine; grasping firmly, heaven and earth are dark. If you do not turn back upon this single stroke, thorns will grow everywhere."
The dragon palace and the ocean treasury are not vast; the spark from flint and the flash of lightning are not swift. Have you not seen?
Beneath Mount Zixiao, by the side of the ink-well, the Eight Divine Horses followed like the wind, yet could not catch up.

(Fohuiquan) With ten thousand scrolls of poetry and books, his head and horns emerged all at once. As soon as he stepped across the gates of the school, he deployed his strategic prowess. Ancient Guizong was truly...

One day, National Teacher Qian’an of Yanguan in Hangzhou (a successor of Mazu I) called to his attendant, saying, “Bring me the rhinoceros fan.
The attendant replied, “It is broken. The Master said, “The fan is indeed broken; now bring me back the rhinoceros. The attendant was speechless.

Xuedou Xian said: "I want the horns and head that are incomplete. Shishuang Chu, representing his contemporaries, said: "If it were returned to the Master, then there would be none at all. Xuedou said: "The rhinoceros calf is still here.

His horns have grown anew. I ask you, venerable Chan practitioners, to offer a turning word. He then asked: "The fan has been broken; now give me back the rhinoceros.

"Two. Alas, one still does not know where the rhinoceros is! I, this mountain monk, wish for all of you to know my view as well:

Infinite cool breezes and its horned head have all followed the clouds and rain, vanishing beyond pursuit.

The marvel lies in a single point of penetrating clarity in autumn.
(Tiantong Jue) The bright moon shines with cold radiance; the pure breeze never ceases. Salt Officer’s boundless intent—what need is there to seek the rhinoceros?

The rhinoceros horn fan has its origins. Time and again it is raised, time and again it is set aside. Lotus leaves tilt in disorder as pearls glisten;
after one more rain, [it rests] by the head of the emerald stream.
(Lan’an Shu) Holding up the teaching beyond the norm, those who recognize it are rare. Even heroes reach this point and are utterly deluded. Suddenly, both eyes are opened wide.
"Blind! (Bilu Meng) The myriad phenomena and the ten thousand forms all trigger the supreme mechanism.

He said, "This is the livelihood of the house of ghosts. After a long silence, he said, "Though the Sword Pass is perilous, traveling at night is even more so.
Daimai Tai offered this in his stead: "The text below is long; it shall be entrusted to a future day. Jingshan Guangzhen offered this in his stead: "Two different segments;
they are gathered back into the preceding section."
Yanguan addressed the assembly: "Take empty space as the drum and Mount Sumeru as the mallet. What kind of person can strike it?
Nanquan said, "Old man Wang does not strike this broken drum. Fayan Yi said, "Old man Wang does not strike it.
Xuedou Xian said, "Those who strike are many; those who listen are extremely few. Now I ask: who is it that knows how to strike?"
"Do not slander the Salt Commissioner. Nanquan said, "Master Wang does not beat this broken drum. Fayan said, "Master Wang does not beat it;
since neither of the two can be helped, one is even more *malāra* (foolish). He further said, "Master Wang does not beat it;
does he still approve of those from other quarters? [The Master] provided a substitute response: "A thousand-year field has eight hundred owners."
Yellow Dragon Xin said: "Nanquan and Fayen only know how to look ahead; they cannot look behind.
For instance, when Yanguan said, 'Take empty space as the drum and Mount Sumeru as the mallet,' where is the place it is broken?
Can you still discern this? Even if you can clearly discern the place where it is broken, I will further ask you: 'Where is the drum? " Tian.
Tonghua said: "Nanquan’s Dharma-eye is much like eating a plum; one bites only at the red skin. Today, this mountain monk goes to meet Yanguan:
taking empty space as the drum and Mount Sumeru as the mallet, whenever there is a beat, I shall strike."
"Do not ask who it is. He then took up his staff and struck the ground once. Tiantong Jie said: "Yanguan set fire after drawing water;
Nanquan stirred up chaos until the stars flew; Fayen buried his troops to provoke a fight.

Each of these venerable masters exerted their own hand, yet not a single person among them was truly enlightened; they were merely following the crowd to carry the drum. Xiangfu provides a direct shortcut for you all."
The Way: take empty space as the drum and Mount Sumeru as the mallet. The lacquer bucket goes into the hall. Tianning Qi said:
"Tell me, where is his point of breach? Will you ever dream of it, even in a donkey’s year? Baoshou Xin’s substitute verse says: "Listen."
Nengren Jian said: "The two venerable masters follow each other's rhythm like a dance in the forest of mulberry trees;
one might say they are harmonious in their accompaniment. Nevertheless, they cannot avoid turning at the heels of others. Today, Dayuan wishes to meet with Yanguan."
"Taking empty space as the drum and Mount Sumeru as the mallet. [The Master] suddenly picks up his staff and strikes once, saying:
"Be careful not to hear it! Old Wang of Nanquan was groundlessly following Yan-guan to serve as a music official.
The command of the Western Patriarch is strict and prohibitive, sparing him from the mistaken joy of the Chan assembly. (Nanyuan Sheng)
The National Teacher exerted great effort to set up the face-drum; it is still superior to ten thousand cases of "poisoned lacquer.
Nanquan was no skilled hand at striking—until this day, the world has not ceased its cries of grievance.
(Bya-phyug-pa) Under the assembly of Yanguan, there was an administrator who one day suddenly saw a messenger of the underworld come to summon him. He then said: "I..."
Jia said, "My body is occupied with official duties and I have not had the leisure to practice. May I request permission to be excused for seven days? Is this possible?
The messenger replied, "I shall wait to report this to the King. If he grants permission, you may come after seven days; otherwise, you must arrive in an instant. Having spoken, he vanished.
After seven days had passed, Jia returned, but in the end, he could not find the monk anywhere.
Dongshan Jia spoke on his behalf, saying: "He has been found by him. Tiantong Wu raised this for inquiry, saying:
"Why was the first messenger of death seen, while the second messenger of death was not seen?"
Take off those worn-out straw sandals; cast down that broken wooden ladle! I tell you, King of Ghosts: what kind of handiwork are you performing? (Lian-an asked:
When the wind blows, the fire’s power is not great, yet it topples the green vines within the blue rattan. When the smoke has ended and the ashes have flown away, one forgets to eat.
"O Great King, you have committed a grave offense against the *maitrā* (the compassionate one).
(The Han Guan Analogy) A monk asked the Abbot of Yanguan, "What is the Dharmakāya Vairocana?
The Master said, "Bring me the pure water pitcher. When the monk brought the pitcher, the Master said, "Put it back in its original place. The monk asked again. The Master—
[It was] said: "The ancient Buddha passed away long ago.

Do you understand? The clouds at the peak of the ridge are never idle. —Wuwei Zhe of Mt. Gui.
The Master said: "I, this mountain monk, am not like that. If someone suddenly asks me, I simply say: 'The assembly, return to the hall.
If one can gain realization under the gate of Daowei, then the ancient Śākyamuni was not first and the new Maitreya is not later.
But as for the turning-around phrase—how do you speak it? Next year there will be fresh branches again; the spring wind’s vexation shall never cease."

Since this monk did not realize the Master's underlying intent, the National Teacher’s [teaching] was established in vain. Yunmen said, "There are no traces. This does not even support the National Teacher.
Xuedou said, "Pointing with one finger to heaven and pointing with one finger to earth—how could there be 'no'? This also supports him.
The National Teacher did not rise. Taking his whisk, he drew a single stroke and said, "All the preceding complications are cut off at once.
Now tell me, ultimately, what is the Dharmakāya Vairocana? He threw down the whisk and descended from his seat. Falin Yin said:

Selfless. As birds travel through the void and fish move within the water, they forget one another across rivers and lakes; as clouds and sky fulfill their purposes, they find their own will.

Not yet having recognized the father and son, the needle and the magnet, the water and the milk remain as they are. *Du du!* You yourself deserve thirty blows.

Wearing lotus robes and eating pine needles, dwelling amidst the deep clouds—this was surely a mistaken perception of that former year. To bury one’s life is for the mind to be Buddha;
for ten thousand years and a thousand ages, it shall not become dust.

A smile. Who would have believed that for half a lifetime I kept watch by a solitary lamp?

Daming was asked by Layman Pang: "I have long heard of Daming; I wonder if the plum has ripened yet?

[This is] a refutation. For others, the plum has been ripe for a long time.

"Hen. (The same as above regarding Damei. Jia then asked, "I do not know which of these two is intimate and which is distant.

At that moment, hearing the shout, he struck them both at once with his staff. This not only severed the entanglements of the two men, but also established him as a patriarchal master of the world.

losing one and replacing it with another—this very day is the first of the fourth month; of the three hundred and sixty days of a year, every single day...
"The alms bowl and the basin are both wet twice. *Chang*. Gu Nanmen said: "Cui Feng, after getting drunk, asked for another cup;

Where skill and clumsiness cannot reach, Yan-guan has a way of manifesting himself. These are the words of the Master himself, spoken from his own mouth: "The rooster and dog barking at their neighbors. (Chang-er of Yue-tang). Through events, wisdom grows;
by recognizing him, one falls into entanglement. Turning the body over, one travels with dawn; the entire family becomes wealthy and noble. All vie to lift him up and offer him praise.
One sinks into oneself; who can emerge from this state of inversion, compliance, right, and wrong? Grasp it so that you may let go and act.
With both hands supporting the plow, the water rises above the knees.
