The rat’s voice then said: "It is this very thing; it is not another. You must protect and maintain it well; I am about to depart. Xuedou Xian remarked:
"This fellow was coarse and reckless while alive, and he remains dull-witted even after death. 'It is this very thing; it is not another.'"
"What kind of thing is this? Is there still a place to hand it over, or not? Some people do not understand how to cut off Daimei’s heels;
they merely say, "He was too hasty in his progress. Baofeng Wen said: "Since it is not some other thing, what thing is it?
Dizang En said: "What kind of talk is that? Xingshan Guang said: "This fellow, at the moment of death..."
It is like water dripping from the mouth; it is this very thing and nothing else. How could it be anything less than vast and profound? Alas!

When the Master first attained the Way, he said, "The mind is itself Buddha. Finally, when instructing his disciples, he showed them that "things are not other things," thereby exhausting the source of all dharmas.
Penetrating the bones of a thousand sages, true transformation does not shift; how could it hinder appearing and disappearing?
(Yongming Shou) Chan Master Lingmo of Wuxie Mountain in Wuzhou (a successor of Mazu Daoyi). When he first visited Shitou, he asked:
"If our words accord, I shall stay; if they do not, I shall leave. Shitou remained seated on his mat. The Master then departed. Shitou called out, "Dharma-heir! The Master—
Turning his head back, Tou said, "From birth until death, it is only this very thing. Why turn your head and shift your gaze?
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment; he then broke his staff and settled there.
Dongshan Jia said, "At that time, had it not been for our late master Wuxie’s great capacity to bear it, it would have been difficult indeed.
Nevertheless, even so, one still traverses the journey. Changqing said, "Dangerous! Xuanguo said, "What is it that constitutes 'traversing the journey'?
A monk said, "Because he realized it within the three-inch space while on the journey, he is thus traversing it. Xuanguo said, "Is it because..."
"Is it that he realized himself? Or did he realize the 'three inches'? If it were himself, why would he become 'three inches'?
If it were 'three inches,' why would he attain awakening? Tell me, what was Dongshan’s intention?
Cuiyan Zhi said: "Shitou took his seat; Wuxie turned his head. Shitou calling him back was already doing too much."
Fengyue said: "This fellow, Daoshou, cannot sit still nor hold himself steady; he is like a man carrying a wooden board.
Having let him go, he then calls him back, being clouded over by it and claiming, 'I have attained enlightenment here.'"
"A donkey-year dream. Master Guishan said, "Wuye left right then and there; this can be called cutting off the tongues of everyone in the world.
Since he was called back, he was already quite muddled. To break the staff is like drawing a bow after the thief has passed.
But as for Shitou taking his seat—what was his intention? Dizang En said, "Just..."
It is fitting to go this way, but it is not fitting to come this way.
Whether on the road or at home, how shall one respond? Do not seek the former master with a single standard. His majestic bearing was like that of a king;
yet he could not avoid being half-lacking in a skull. (Longmen Yuan)
As he was about to leave, he called out in a loud voice and brought [the master] back; at that moment, his mind’s eye opened all at once.
If you wish to know that this does not rely on the power of cultivation, let life and death drift slowly as they come and go. (Becoming a withered tree.
Chan Master Baoji of Panshan in Youzhou (a successor of Mazu Daoyi). Initially, when he first attended Mazu, he served as a street-walker. One day...
As he went out the gate, he saw people carrying a funeral procession. A ritual singer was shaking a bell and chanting: "The red wheel is certain to sink in the west;
I know not to which direction the soul has departed. The filial son weeps with bitter grief. At these words, the Master suddenly attained awakening.
Yunju Zhuang said: "Big and small Panshan recognized only that which is 'brightly manifest and spiritually alert.
If there were such a person here, they would surely have a different way of life. But tell me, what kind of way of life is it? A pair of mandarin ducks is embroidered for you to behold;
the golden needle is not handed over to anyone."
In response to this deep sorrow, one immediately accepts it. Where, ultimately, does the soul go? In a state of leaping joy, the whole body is naturally revealed;
only then does one know that throughout the entire realm, nothing has ever been hidden.
(Haiyin Xin) I wonder where the soul goes: with no place to rest, it is revealed in its majestic dignity. Like water flowing from the side of a rock.
Cold. The wind comes from within the flowers, bringing fragrance.
(Yuelin Guan) Suddenly hearing mournful wailing beneath the curtain, it instantly causes Tiantai to face Wutai. Wind and moon remain as one across past and present;
though one has a mouth all over one's body, it is difficult to open. (Shui'an Yan)
The sound of the *xiè* song is choked with sobs, its cadence long and drawn out. Hearing this mournful wailing, one’s bowels are suddenly rent asunder.
As before, the crimson sun sets behind the western mountains; within the great trichiliocosm, there is no place to lodge such desolation.
(Tianmu Li) The *xièlù* dirge is sorrowful and truly pitiable; the white poplars and crimson banners flutter away. Amidst the sounds of lamentation, there is nothing that can extinguish it.
Breath. Striking the south, movement occurs in the north.
(Beijian Jian) One day, while in the marketplace, Panshan saw someone buying meat and said, "Cut me a piece of the finest.
The butcher set down his knife and, with palms joined, said, "Prefect, that piece is not the finest. The Master attained great enlightenment and returned.
He presented this to the Patriarch, who gave his seal of approval:
"This matter is clear and not hidden; in every head and every object, they naturally accord.
A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them— Yet they follow the warbling orioles as they fly over the low wall. (Nan-hua Bing)
By the river’s edge, I see off a guest boarding a small boat; Facing each other, an old fisherman silently casts his hook.
With a single pull, a scaled jewel ascends to his hand; The distant mountains layer upon layer, the waters flow on and on.
(Miaofengshan) A half-acre wasteland pond opens like a mirror; The light of heaven and the shadows of clouds linger together. The singing oriole awakens the beautiful woman.
Dream. An old friend came up from Hancheng.
Panshan said, "If you say 'this very mind is Buddha,' at present you have not yet entered the profound mystery.
If you say 'neither mind nor Buddha,' this is still merely pointing to the ultimate track."
Tiantong Jue said: "Having money, one does not know how to spend it; knowing how to spend it, one has no money. How can one attain perfection?
To marry a young wife, one must be a white-haired man. Baolin Xiu said: "In these times, the pathhead cannot be realized in its entirety.
'Neither mind nor Buddha' lacks the divine function. If you wish to attain perfection, there is no way other than this."
In winter one turns toward the fire, and it is only in the sixth month that one begins to sell ice; thus it is said: "To marry a young wife, one must be a white-haired man.
But then, how do you explain the line about "tuning the lute and the harp"? An old husband and a short-lived wife, each tormenting the other in turn.
Panshan said: "In the three realms there is no dharma; where can one seek the mind? The four elements are fundamentally empty; upon what does the Buddha rely to abide?
The celestial sphere is unmoving, silent and wordless. Face-to-face presentation—there is nothing more. Take care.
When there are no dharmas in the three realms, where can one seek the mind? With white clouds as a canopy and flowing water as a lute, one or two strains go unappreciated by anyone;
after the rain has passed, the autumn waters in the night pond are deep.
(Cui Feng Xian) The green bamboo sits within the hall facing the window; the dark mountains screen the gate opposite the door. There is yet another thing worthy of admiration.
In this place, the night is deep and the flowing water murmurs *chan-chan*.
(Fujian Qín) In the Three Realms there is no dharma; where can one seek the mind? The mountain’s appearance after rain, the pine’s resonance in the wind.
Lying across or sleeping on one’s back with nothing else to do— Let the moss at will cover the ground. (Foxing Tài)
The mountain cottage is free of dust and exceptionally clear; pomegranate flowers bloom, shining through the curtains.
The shade of the locust trees covers the ground at high noon; as I awaken from my dream, a warbler sings out once.

(Opening the Secluded Room) The willows hang low, about to hide the crows; after the ritual of the earth, the eastern wind sweeps away the falling petals. Where shall I go on horseback to invite my friends?
Fine. Looking at the mulberry and hemp plants to the south and north of the mountain, (Yuguku Kun) the old fisherman on the river casts his line.
His livelihood is wherever he may be; there is no need to return home. Deep in the night under the moon, he indulges in clear dreams;
the wind presses the light clouds as they skim the water. (Ungwa Hee)
Panshan addressed the assembly: "The moon of the mind is solitary and perfect; its light swallows the ten thousand phenomena. The light does not illuminate objects, nor do objects exist.
When both light and objects are forgotten, what is it then?"
Dongshan Liangjie said, "If light and objects have not yet been forgotten, what else could it be? Yunmen Wenyan said, "Even if you were to act in this way, you would still be halfway;
this is not yet the path of total transcendence. After a long silence, he said, "The Flower-Peak of Tiantai.
Jingzhao Daoyuan said, "A white heron descends the field—a thousand dots of snow; a yellow oriole perches on a tree—a single branch of blossoms. Qinghua said, [silently].
Zenghe gave a shout and said: "When a character is transcribed three times, 'wu' becomes 'ma. Dongming Jian raised the question:
'When light and its object are both forgotten, what is it? [Zenghe] shouted once and said: 'What is this? 'Before light and its object are forgotten, what is it?
He then raised his whisk and said: 'What do you call this thing? Again, he gave a shout."
The light does not illuminate the object, nor does the object exist; when both light and object are forgotten, there remains yet another trace.
The hundred birds do not come as spring has already faded; falling flowers and flowing water wind around a solitary village.
(Kentang Chong) It cannot be depicted, it cannot be painted; the Sleeping Dragon is forever wary of the clarity of the green pool. To attempt to direct the mind toward it is ultimately difficult.
Meeting. The adept must be startled in secret. (Songyuan Yue) Jade dew falls silently upon the shadowless tree;
golden wind stirs subtly at the night-bright curtain. The wooden man whips up the clay ox as it bellows;
the azure dragon is not permitted to lie in the green abyss. (Xiaoyin Yin)
Panshan said: "O virtuous Chan practitioners, it is like throwing a sword into the air; one need not deliberate over whether it reaches its mark or not.
This is because the empty wheel leaves no trace and the blade remains unimpaired. If you can act thus, then mind after mind is without knowing.
The whole mind is the Buddha; the whole Buddha is the person. When person and Buddha are without distinction, only then has one begun the Way."
Jingshan Daowu, under the phrase "In mind after mind there is no knowing," said: "Tsk! Within the treasury of our King, there is no such sword. Yufan Yuanwu said:
"If one speaks of a son of the robe in his true colors, in reality there is no such sword; yet if one speaks of a son of the robe in his true colors, in reality there *is* such a sword.
A monk standing by laughed derisively and said: "Have you not seen Panshan say: 'Students weary their bodies'?"
It is like a monkey grasping at shadows. Yuanwu said, "Tsk! I knew you were sitting in a ghost cave.
Panshan said, "One may study the Way within this: it is like the earth supporting a mountain, yet not knowing the mountain's towering loftiness;
it is like a stone containing jade, yet not knowing the jade's flawlessness. If one is thus, this is called 'leaving home' (renunciation)."
Xuedou Xian said: "Walking three thousand miles by day and eight hundred by night—this is what I habitually employ;
set it aside for a moment. In what place, you all, do you see Panshan? Jingshan Guangzhao said:
"If one can act thus, it is like pressing on the eyes until flowers appear. Cuiyan Zhongzhe said: "To see Panshan is easy; to see Jingshan is difficult."
"Mountains are difficult. Lingyan Chu said: "Whether with eyes open or closed, where is it not Panshan?
After a long silence, he let out a shout and said: "Drowsy fellows! Are you awake yet?"
The mountain is already solitary and steep; few travelers reach it. The jade is already flawless; its authenticity cannot be distinguished.
(Huanglong Xin) The mountain forgets its solitude and steepness; the jade is without flaw. Everywhere there is a source of immortals—that is my home.
It is laughable that Ge Hong never awakened to this truth, traveling far to Qu-lou to inquire about cinnabar. (Tianmu Li)
Panshan said: "The path that goes upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages.
Ciming Huiyuan said: "The path that goes upward—the thousand sages do not affirm it. Langye Huijiao said:
"All the excellent causes and conditions from the lectures and praises above. Yangqi Fanghui said: "It is stuck on the mouth. Jingshan Daokai said: "Upward."
"The single path. The hot bowl makes a ringing sound. Tiantong Jie said, "The path beyond this is to dig into the earth to seek the heavens.
Jianfu Can said, "The path beyond this has not been transmitted by the thousand sages. *Svāhā* to the profound truth of the Vinaya.
"The path beyond this has not been ignited by the thousand sages. *Suru-siri svāhā*. If you all understand it in this way, [you are mistaken].
*Kalā kalā.* Tianning Qi said: "All the great elders have exhausted their powers to clarify only the path leading downward.
As for the path leading upward—when will you ever see it in a dream? Pingyang Min said: "Panshan said, 'The path leading upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages.
Why do you cry out in grievance while carrying the stolen goods? Ciming said, 'The path leading upward..."*
The "one path upward" has not been so for a thousand sages. Do not falsely claim to have reached clarity. Jingshan said:
"The one path upward is like the sound of a hot bowl clinking. Closing one's eyes and leaping over the Yellow River. Qianyan said: "The one path upward is beneath your feet;
it is like joining bamboo poles to point at the blue sky. The former Elder said: "The one path upward is to tread through worn-out straw sandals; it is like a monkey climbing up a tree in reverse."
“‘The tree’—these five Chinese characters have been accounted for by this mountain monk all at once. After all, what is the path that leads upward?
Holding up his staff, he rose and said, “Return to the hall for tea. Kaisan Jin said, “The path that leads upward.
After a long silence, he said, “When the roof leaks, one watches the stars while sleeping. Tianjing Xin said, “The path that leads upward.”
Falling into pits and ditches; inauspicious dreams at night; writing on the wall. Guangjiao Yu said:
"The one path above—three lifetimes, sixty kalpas. Falin Yin said: "The one path above—tut!"
The path beyond Mount Pan—how can it be described? Rarely is a traveler seen, for their ears have been pierced. When the mouth is applied, there is no place to bite;
only then does one know that the thousand sages could not transmit it. (Baiyun Yuan) It is not that it cannot be transmitted;
it is simply that the ocean-mouth is difficult to express. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, an iron boat is launched. (Jingshan Guangzhao)
Not transmitted by a thousand sages until this day, it is peerless when brought forth from the mouth.
At the foot of Mount Dongting, in the heart of Lake Tai, travelers on the road chatter in vain.
(Songyuan Yue) When Panshan was about to pass away, he addressed the assembly, saying, "Is there anyone who can paint my true likeness? The assembly presented what they had written.
Zhancheng presented [his work], but neither was approved. Puhua came forward and said, "I have painted it. The Master asked, "Why do you not present it to this old monk?
Puhua then performed a somersault and left. The Master remarked, "This fellow will go on to act like a madman from now on."
Baofu Zhan said, "Puhua’s eccentricity was no small matter; Panshan’s ugliness and clumsiness were even more so.
Changlu Liao shook his body and said, "I am killed by this joy! If one did not possess eyes that pierce through heaven and earth, how could one see this whole piece of refined gold and uncut jade?
He spoke again, "I have made a copy of Puhua’s likeness based on the original; tonight I shall unfold it for you to see."
He caused the great assembly to gaze upon him, then performed a somersault and returned to the hall.
Xiqia Cheng said, "If it had been Great Master Linji, not a single one of thirty blows would have been spared. Fortunately, we encountered Panshan who let him go.
But tell me, where did that blow land? If you say 'right here,' I would split your back with a blow; I know your stick is blind."
"Acting in disorder. Guoqing Ying said: "Tsk! One person transmits the false, ten thousand people transmit it as true.
Your Master’s true ugliness and clumsiness are unfit for presentation; exhausting body and mind, you make people laugh to death.
Do not seek even a thread of meaning therein; the White-Nosed Kunlun celebrates the New Year. (Longmen Yuan)
Utterly ice-cold and empty, there is no shadow or image. Turning somersaults upside down, it is difficult to imitate.
After the rains have ceased atop a thousand peaks following the Huangmei season, the moon of cassia rises once more from the sea.
(Xue’an Jin) This clear, wondrous, and strange face born of one’s mother—how could a brush of exquisite painting ever depict it? This fellow has transmitted it perfectly.
It is like this: as the saying goes, "Painting a tiger only results in a wildcat. (From *Bǎoyè Yuán*).
Chan Master Bǎochè of Mágǔ in Púzhōu (a successor of Mázǔ) went to Línjì and asked: "The Great Compassionate One has a thousand hands and eyes."
"Which one is the true eye? Jie said, "The thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion. "Which one is the true eye? Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
The Master stepped forward, dragged Jie down from his meditation seat, and sat back down himself. Jie stepped forward and said, "How do you do?
As the Master hesitated, Jie gave a shout, dragged him off the seat, and sat back down. The Master then went out.

Master Shengying said: "Virtuous one of Chan, regarding these two venerable masters, what is their underlying intent? Nowadays, everyone speaks of 'illumination' and 'function. But what bowl are they illuminating?
Everyone only knows how to mount their own horse to go catch the thief, or take up their own sword to go kill the thief;
these two men, however, were uniquely able to seize the thief’s horse to catch the thief and take the thief’s sword to kill the thief. Nevertheless, even so—"
This is so. Linji gained the advantage, yet he lost the advantage. Yangshan Qin said:
"Though these two elders displayed their myriad hands and eyes all at once in such a manner of vigorous exhortation, how could they avoid being both blind men?"
Tell me, can anyone discern this? *Xia!* (A blind eye). Tianning Qi said: "The two elders exchange roles as host and guest;
their wielding and seizing are worth observing, like a fierce flame burning through the sky or a sudden thunderclap shaking the earth.
Nevertheless, what connection does this have with the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion? One sees only the surging waves, but fails to see the Palace of the Sea Dragon."
For many years on the frontier, I heard only his name; today before the ranks, I behold him face to face. Mounted alone on a single horse with a solitary spear, he fought for several bouts.
It was well that he saw the opportunity and loosed a single arrow.
(Bao-ning’s Valor) Meeting on a narrow path, it is difficult to turn back. A clash of arms in the space of a breath; banners and drums flash and swirl, utterly beyond measure.
Bian: Let me ask, who was the victor? (Purongping):
When the bandits’ ranks met at midnight, they scrambled for flags and drums to seek advantage;
suddenly, at dawn, they saw one another again, and with faces full of shame and humiliation, each returned home. (Bieshanzhi)

Reversing the rudders and hoisting the sails to play with the sea breeze, he overturns the axis of the earth to display his heroic prowess. He plucks out the color of the pearl from beneath the dragon’s chin;
with a single bowl, he gathers back the two venomous dragons. (Lian’an asked:
Drunk to satiety under the moon atop the willow tower, they sing to their fill the breeze beneath the peach-blossom fan. The cups and tally-sticks are interlaced beyond measure.
[The Master] said: "Looking at one another, we are all flushed with wine.
(Jiayin’s Commentary) Magu and Nanquan, two or three people, went to visit Jingshan. On the road, they encountered an old woman.
They asked her, "Which way does the road to Jingshan go? The woman said, "Go straight ahead. The Master said, "The water ahead is deep; can you cross it?"
"No," the old woman said, "my feet are not wet. He asked again, "The rice on the upper bank is so excellent, while the rice on the lower bank is so poor;
why is that? The old woman said, "It has all been eaten by crabs. The Master said, "The grain is fragrant. The old woman said, "It has no scent.
He asked again, "Where do you live, old woman? The old woman said, "I am right here. The three of them then arrived at the inn.
The old woman brought a bottle of tea and three cups, saying, "If the Master possesses supernatural powers, then please drink the tea.
While the three men looked at one another, the woman said, "Watch as this old crone displays her own supernatural powers," whereupon she poured out the tea and departed.
Chengtian Yi said: "The old woman was like a valiant cavalryman facing the enemy; yet, alas, she poked her head out too far.
Magu and the other two were like veteran generals patrolling the borders; they were more than capable of holding their ground. But when examined closely, they still lacked one move."
Meeting on the road through Shaanxi was no ordinary encounter; banners and spears were cast down as they spoke with ease.
But when the conversation reached the affairs of the Central Plains, you climbed the high ridge while I waded through the river.
(Qingshan Ding) Magu, holding his staff, went to Zhangjing; he circled the meditation seat three times, struck it once with his staff, and stood firm.
Dongshan stood up. Jing said, "It is so, it is so. He went to Nanquan and did the same; Nanquan said, "It is not so, it is not so.
The Master asked, "Jing says it is so; why does the Monk say it is not so? Nanquan replied, "Jing is indeed right, but you are wrong.
This is driven by the force of the wind; in the end, it will lead to ruin."
Changqing said in place of Dayu: "Where are the Buddha-dharma, body, and mind? Again, in place of Dayu, he said in response to Zhangjing’s "This is you;
it is not": "What kind of mental activity is this? Baofu Zhan gave a different response:
he simply shook his staff once and departed. He also said: "Zhangjing and Nanquan can truly be called 'one is'."
First, it is not so. Furthermore, it is said: "Magu’s words were somewhat like a melody, barely fit to be heard, yet they were blown by the wind into another tune.
Yunju Xi said: "Zhangjing did not necessarily say it was right; Nanquan did not necessarily say it was wrong. It is also said:
At the outset, it would have been just right for Magu to simply take his staff and go out. Xuedou Xian, acting on behalf of both [Nanquan and Mazu], said "Wrong" in both instances.
Guizong Zhe said: "When Zhangjing said 'Right,' he fell into Magu’s trap; when Nanquan said 'Not Right,' he also fell into Magu’s trap.
If someone were to come before you today in such a manner, you should simply say: 'He has not yet arrived.'"
"Here, thirty blows are well-deserved. Letan Qing said, "Zhangjing says 'it is,' and he too deserves thirty blows;
Nanquan says 'it is not,' and he too deserves thirty blows. Why? Because whether it is 'is' or 'is not,' the wondrous meaning is fully revealed;
Zhangjing and Nanquan have both suffered a defeat. Shengmo Guang said, "It is non-existent."

However, it is not that there is no true right; this right has no master. All myriad virtues return to the same source, yet the owl and the cock merely waste their efforts in a cycle of day and night.
I have no three inches of tongue to call a turtle a soft-shelled tortoise; Kāśyapa would not consent, so let him frown as he pleases.
Tianning Qi said: "The bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip; the sweet melon is sweet from stem to blossom."
This is a mistake, that is a mistake—cut off all such grasping at once! The waves of the four seas have smoothed over, and the tides of the hundred rivers have ebbed. The ancient strategy is lofty;
in each of the twelve gates there is a path, yet it is empty and desolate. It is not desolate. Those who practice should seek the medicine for those who are already healthy.
(Cuifeng Xian): "Zhangjing says it is right;
Nanquan says it is wrong. Who can penetrate the waves against the current? Pity this fellow, skinless and bloodless;
he is given a green dragon but does not know how to ride it. (Nantang Jing)
"It is so, it is so. Let loose the true turtle-nosed one of the South Mountain. It is not so, it is not so. Turn back the wind-chasing steed of a thousand miles.
In the end, it will meet with ruin—how pitiable! The throat is choked and there is no breath to draw. No breath to draw? There is still a nose."
Zhaozhou hangs a gourd on the eastern wall; laughable indeed is Vimalakīrti’s discourse on non-duality.
(Qionggu Lian) The mechanism of wondrous transformation flashes like lightning; life and death surge forth together before one's eyes. A bright pearl has its own price as a bright pearl;
do not try to catch sparrows with it at the edge of the fence. (Muan Yong)

One day, while Magu was fanning himself, a monk asked, "The nature of wind is eternally abiding and nowhere is it not pervasive. Why, then, does the Master still wave his fan? The Master said, "You know only that the nature of wind is eternally abiding; you do not yet know that it is nowhere not pervasive. The monk asked, "What is meant by 'nowhere not pervasive'? The Master again waved his fan. The monk bowed, and the Master said: [The Master said: "I have already spoken for you. The monk remained silent. The Master said, "If you had been able to speak at that time, you would have been like a dragon soaring through the clouds. But because you were unable to speak, you are like a snake crawling in a grassy ditch. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "It is like a person who has lost their way and wanders about in confusion. The monk asked, "How can one avoid wandering in confusion? The Master said, "If you wish to avoid wandering in confusion, you must first abandon your own mind. The monk asked, "What is the abandonment of one's own mind? The Master said, "If you wish to abandon your own mind, you must first realize that there is no such thing as 'one's own mind. If you realize there is no 'one's own mind,' then you will naturally abandon it. If you abandon it, you will naturally find peace. If you find peace, you will naturally be free from all afflictions. If you are free from all afflictions, you will naturally attain liberation. If you attain liberation, you will naturally realize the Way. If you realize the Way, you will naturally manifest great compassion. If you manifest great compassion, you will naturally benefit all sentient beings. If you benefit all sentient beings, you will naturally fulfill the Bodhisattva path. If you fulfill the Bodhisattva path, you will naturally become a Buddha. If you become a Buddha, you will naturally turn the Wheel of Dharma. If you turn the Wheel of Dharma, you will naturally save all sentient beings. If you save all sentient beings, you will naturally enter Nirvana. If you enter Nirvana, you will naturally transcend birth and death. If you transcend birth and death, you will naturally abide in the state of eternal bliss. The monk asked, "How can one enter Nirvana? The Master said, "If you wish to enter Nirvana, you must first realize that there is no Nirvana to be entered. If you realize there is no Nirvana to be entered, then you will naturally enter it. If you enter it, you will naturally be free from all conceptualization. If you are free from all conceptualization, you will naturally be free from all attachment. If you are free from all attachment, you will naturally be free from all grasping. If you are free from all grasping, you will naturally be free from all delusion. If you are free from all delusion, you will naturally be free from all suffering. If you are free from all suffering, you will naturally be free from all birth. If you are free from all birth, you will naturally be free from all death. If you are free from all death, you will naturally be free from all transmigration. If you are free from all transmigration, you will naturally be free from all karma. If you are free from all karma, you will naturally be free from all causes and conditions. If you are free from all causes and conditions, you will naturally be free from all phenomena. If you are free from all phenomena, you will naturally be free from all names and forms. If you are free from all names and forms, you will naturally be free from all distinctions. If you are free from all distinctions, you will naturally be free from all duality. If you are free from all duality, you will naturally be free from all extremes. If you are free from all extremes, you will naturally be free from all views. If you are free from all views, you will naturally be free from all attachments. If you are free from all attachments, you will naturally be free from all obstacles. If you are free from all obstacles, you will naturally be free from all hindrances. If you are free from all hindrances, you will naturally be free from all fetters. If you are free from all fetters, you will naturally be free from all bonds. If you are free from all bonds, you will naturally be free from all attachments. If you are free from all attachments, you will naturally be free from all desires. If you are free from all desires, you will naturally be free from all cravings. If you are free from all cravings, you will naturally be free from all passions. If you are free from all passions, you will naturally be free from all afflictions. If you are free from all afflictions, you will naturally be free from all delusions. If you are free from all delusions, you will naturally be free from all ignorance. If you are free from all ignorance, you will naturally be free from all obstructions. If you are free from all obstructions, you will naturally be free from all defilements. If you are free from all defilements, you will naturally be free from all impurities. If you are free from all impurities, you will naturally be free from all stains. If you are free from all stains, you will naturally be free from all turbidity. If you are free from all turbidity, you will naturally be free from all confusion. If you are free from all confusion, you will naturally be free from all distraction. If you are free from all distraction, you will naturally be free from all agitation. If you are free from all agitation, you will naturally be free from all restlessness. If you are free from all restlessness, you will naturally be free from all instability. If you are free from all instability, you will naturally be free from all wavering. If you are free from all wavering, you will naturally be free from all fluctuation. If you are free from all fluctuation, you will naturally be free from all change. If you are free from all change, you will naturally be free from all transformation. If you are free from all transformation, you will naturally be free from all arising and ceasing. If you are free from all arising and ceasing, you will naturally be free from all coming and going. If you are free from all coming and going, you will naturally be free from all entering and exiting. If you are free from all entering and exiting, you will naturally be free from all dwelling and departing. If you are free from all dwelling and departing, you will naturally be free from all staying and leaving. If you are free from all staying and leaving, you will naturally be free from all abiding and moving. If you are free from all abiding and moving, you will naturally be free from all fixed positions. If you are free from all attachments to places, you will naturally be free from all attachments to things. Cuiyan Zhi challenged him, saying, "As for Shan’s speaking in this manner, does he thereby avoid being at fault? If he avoids it, he has not yet attained [the Way]."
"The eye is present; it cannot be avoided. This also contradicts his previous statement.
While Xishan was eating his rice, Nanquan gathered up the leftover rice and said, "Leftover rice. The Master said, "Non-arising. Nanquan said, "That is still just the branch.
After he had walked only a few steps, the Master called out, "Elder! Nanquan looked back and asked, "What? The Master—
He said: "Do not say this is secondary.
Shending Kui said: "When monks have enough porridge and enough rice, they should simply stop. What is the use of that which sticks to the teeth?
Give twenty blows of the staff to each of these two fellows. Is there any fault in such a judgment? Examine it!
Even upon attaining it, one receives thirty blows of the staff.
The ancients patrolled the hall and personally "weeded" the living. Crossing water requires a boat; plowing is not easy. Do not say that non-arising is still merely secondary;
if even a hair’s breadth is not resolved, confusion will run rampant. (Zhimen Zu)
"Before birth, one verse relied on those of the same lineage; apart from the pipes, the pure tones were naturally sublime. A night’s west wind could not blow them away;
the plum blossoms played their music, falling all the way to the clouds.
(Shendingshui Gui) One day, while Shanshan, Guizong, and Nanquan were walking along a path, they encountered a tiger. Each passed it by its side. Nanquan said:
He asked Guizong, "What was that tiger you just saw like? Guizong said, "It was like a cat.
He then asked the Master, and the Master said, "It was like a dog. The Master then asked Daquan, and Daquan said, "It was like a tiger."

Daguang Zhiyun said: "These three old fellows huddle together and chatter in their sleep. If you wish to attain thorough penetration all at once, you must investigate this tiger. He then offered a verse:
A single tiger, three people see it differently; each establishes their own school of style according to their high or low station.
Because they fail to gain strength on this path, they pass their floating life in vain within a dream.
One thing with two names—how truly marvelous! Among these three people, which one can serve as the teacher?
Without the Vajra-eye upon the crown of the head, who could discern that which transcends both the vertical and horizontal?
(Kai-xian Ying) Five times five is twenty-five. A tiger is originally a tiger; a dog and a cat can never be spoken of at the same time.
Close the gates at night; lock the doors early. You must believe that sharp fangs and claws are to be feared. At the head of every household’s door lies the road to Chang’an;
these are all the paths for examination candidates ascending to the imperial court.
(Fujian Qín) Master Xiāoyáo of Yúnzhōu (a successor of Mázǔ I), because Monk Lùxī said: "The mind clings to conditions moment by moment."
"His mind is eternally tranquil. The Master said, "Yesterday there was also someone who spoke like that. [Xuefeng] asked, "What did he say? The Master said, "I do not know.
[Xuefeng] said, "Please tell me, Reverend. The Master struck him over the mouth with his whisk. Xuefeng shook out his sleeves and departed.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "O Great Assembly! Even if you were to fix your eyes upon the crown of your heads, you would still fail to discern him.
Jiangshan Qin said: "Although this old monk lacks eyes upon the crown of my head, I can still verify that his bones have been exposed.
How is this to be seen? A venomous snake in an ancient tomb wears horns upon its head; a fierce tiger on the Southern Mountain has a tail like a forked tongue."
Chan Master Huizang of Shigong in Fuzhou (a successor of Mazu Daoyi) was formerly a hunter.
While pursuing a deer, he encountered Mazu, who asked him, "Have you seen the deer pass by? The master replied, "I am a hunter.
Mazu asked, "Are you skilled at archery? He replied, "I am. Mazu asked, "With a single arrow, how many do you shoot? He replied, "I shoot one. Mazu said:
"You do not understand archery," [the Master] said. He asked, "Does the Upādhyāya understand archery? The Patriarch replied, "I understand archery.
He asked, "With one arrow, how many can you shoot? The Patriarch replied, "I shoot a whole flock. He said, "Since both parties possess life, how can you shoot a whole flock?
The Patriarch said, "Since you know this to be so, why do you not shoot yourself? He replied, "If you were to command me to shoot myself, it would simply be impossible."
Regarding the point of entry, the Patriarch said, "This fellow’s ignorance and afflictions have been dormant for kalpas, but today they are suddenly extinguished.
The Master then cast down his bow and arrows and entered the Patriarch’s service to leave the household life.
Qingliang Qin said: "How is it that one arrow shoots a flock? Truly, even the life-force of the trichiliocosm does not require more than a single arrow.
Xuedou Xian said: "Master Mazu’s 'one arrow for a flock' is like shooting at a target by chance;
what use is there in such a thing? It is not as good as Shigong’s 'one arrow for one.'"
"A fine hand indeed! Today, Cui-feng emulates the deeds of the ancients; he intends to release an arrow. He shouts loudly, 'Look at the arrow!
and then says, 'It has hit. Cui-yang Zhi said: "Mazu’s one arrow hitting a flock was still not yet excellent.
This mountain monk’s one arrow shoots all moving beings and sentient creatures; there is none that does not hit. Nevertheless, even so, it only says..."
He attained half; the other half he left for the senior monks to explain.
Once, when a monk asked Shigong, "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them? the Master said, "This person has no birth and death."
Yuánwù Qín said: "Do you recognize that one? A swift falcon soars toward the heavens; a bewildered bird perches upon the fence.
Tíngjì Xìn said: "Great as Shígǒng was, he looked only to his haste and failed to notice he was about to lose his footing."
The deep orchids in the spring valley invade the traveler’s robes; along the fragrant path, the withered blossoms scatter as the woodcutter returns home.
He wishes to take his axe-handle to fashion another, yet the year draws to a close and the branches and leaves drift away on the clouds.
(Qingshan Ding) Whenever Shigong saw a monk, he would draw his bow and aim an arrow at him. One day, Sanping arrived; the Master said, "Look!"
[Zhao]zhou drew an arrow. Baopeng then pushed aside his chest and said, "This is the arrow that kills people. What about the arrow that gives life?
The Master then tapped the bowstring three times. Baopeng then prostrated himself.

The Master said, "For thirty years I have drawn my bow and set my arrows, yet I have only managed to shoot half a sage. He then snapped the bow and arrow in two. Later, Baopeng recounted this to Dadian.
Dian said, "Since it is a 'living man's arrow,' why did you identify it on the bowstring? Ping had no reply.
Dian said, "Thirty years from now, it will be difficult even to bring up this story."
Yunmen asked Changqing, “How can one avoid being called ‘half a sage’? Changqing said, “If you do not offer a counter-price, how can one distinguish the true from the false?
Yunmen said, “Entering the water, one sees the tall man. Shoushan Nian said, “Everyone says that Sanping hit the mark;
is he not being treated with due respect? After a long silence, he said: ‘The mechanism is not the work of Han Guang.’”
Do not treat this matter with indifference. Xuedou Xian said: "It would not have been difficult to first break it apart; however, Sanping had already realized it within himself.
Even so, if the old master wishes to bring Sanping back to life, he cannot avoid drawing his bow and setting his arrow. Zhitai Ai said:
"If one does not truly strike the tiger, one’s labor is in vain and the feathers will simply fall to the ground. Gaofeng Miao said: "A stone..."
Gong drew his bow with such intensity that he seemed as if no one else existed; Sanping received the arrow, turning cleverness into clumsiness.
Even so, what of the "half-sage"? When the falling flower has the intention to follow the flowing water, the flowing water has no heart to cherish the falling flower.
Zhongfeng Ben said: "To pierce the hundred-step willow and penetrate the nine-layered drum is indeed a matter of keen eyes and nimble hands."
"It is as if a half-saint possessed the art of invisibility; thus, Shigong’s skill was exhausted.
Gushan Xian said, "To bare one's chest to meet an arrow truly displays the bearing of a great man. Yet, he recognized only the 'killing arrow';
when asked again about the 'life-giving arrow,' how much time had already been wasted! Shigong acted like a physician treating a dead horse. Although he managed to save him..."
"It is merely half a person. Falingyin said: "It is also said that one arrow shoots one person.
For thirty years, there has been but one bow. With this single bow, the bowstring is fixed across the realm;
yet who would have known that though the 'Half-Sage' offered his submission, the message was not conveyed through the surrender of the jade tablet and the leading of the sheep? (Zhengjue Yi)
Stringing the bow and setting the arrow is not for naught; though many hit the mark, their lives remain incomplete. When the semi-sage strikes the pivot, there is no other intent;
why must one of high merit be depicted in the Lingyan Gallery?
(Fohuiquan) Stringing the bow and setting the arrow for thirty years, he shot Sanping, yet half remained incomplete. How can this compare to the ten thousand people pointing all at once?
The place: A solitary wild goose falls into the autumn sky as the sun slants down.
(Foguo Bai said: "He could have split the arrow aimed at his chest; why did he remain only half a person? It is because he understood the path; therefore, he did not preserve his whole body."
(Lingyan An): Recognizing the speckled [arrowhead], he hurriedly drew the bowstring. A single shaft roared through the wind, startling the heavens. Come forward and observe closely:
who could have shot through the stone of Lantian? (Xinwen Ben)
Shigong asked Xitang Zang, "Do you understand how to seize empty space? He replied, "I can seize it. The Master said, "How do you seize it?
Xitang made a gesture with his hand as if grasping at empty space. The Master said, "You do not know how to seize it.
Xitang then asked the Master, "Brother, how do you seize it? The Master grabbed Xitang by the nostrils and pulled them. Xitang let out a cry of pain and said:
Dasha gripped the man’s nostrils so firmly that he nearly pulled them off. The Master said, “Only by grasping space in this manner can you succeed.
Baoshou then remarked, “If I were in the position of Xitang, when [the Master] asked, ‘Can you grasp space? I would have also said, ‘I can grasp it.’”
[The Master] said, "I have attained it. [The monk] asked, "How did you seize it? [The Master] immediately kicked Shigong down with one foot.

Baoyan Fu said, "Turning heaven and earth upside down is not impossible; however, at that time, if Xitang had stepped forward and struck him right across the face with his palm, what would have happened then?"
Whenever Chan Master Hong'en of Zhongyi in Langzhou (a successor of Mazu I) saw a monk, he would clap his hands and pucker his lips, saying, "Wu-ye!
Wu-ye! When Yangshan arrived, he walked from east to west and from west to east, and finally stood in the center.
The Master asked, "Where did you obtain this samādhi? Mountan said, "I learned it from the seal-imprint at Caoxi.
The Master asked, "Whom did you attend? He replied, "I attended Yi Suojue.
The Master then asked, "And where did you, Reverend, obtain this samādhi? He replied, "I learned it from Great Master Ma."
Langye Jue said: "Do not speak of sorrow to one who is already sorrowful. Falin Yin said: "It makes the bystanders laugh to death.
Caoxi’s transmission of the seal was mistaken; Changjing’s reception of it was coarse.
One might have thought the barbarian’s beard would turn the world red, but it turns out there is yet another red-bearded barbarian. (Zhengjue Yi)
Yangshan was skilled at questioning; Zhongyi was skilled at responding. Turning back and turning over, every beat was a command.
(Cishou Shen) Once, because Yangshan asked how one might attain the vision of one's nature, the Master said:
"Suppose there is a room with six windows. Inside there is a monkey, and outside there is a monkey who calls out 'Singing-sing' from the east. The monkey—
The monkey immediately responded. Thus, he was called through all six windows and responded to each. Daban Shan bowed and said, "I have now understood everything through the Master’s metaphors.
However, there is one further matter: when the inner monkey is dozing and the outer monkey wishes to see it, what then?
The Master descended from his meditation seat, took Shan’s hand, and danced with him, saying, "A langur! (xing).
Xinghua said, "I have met you. Xinxiang Xian said, "Do you all wish to see these two elders? I shall also give you a parable.
Zhongyi was very much like a goldsmith; Yangshan brought a piece of gold and had the goldsmith appraise its value. The goldsmith..."
They settled the price in full. As they were about to complete the transaction, the seller of the gold further offered to add extra weight on the scale.
Although the goldsmith was secretly pleased, he could not help but harbor suspicions in his heart. Why? If this were not a spy, it must surely be stolen property.
Yunju Xi said: "If at that time Zhongyi had not received that single phrase from Yangshan, where would Zhongyi be now?"
Chongshou Chou said, "Is there anyone who can definitively grasp this principle?
If one cannot definitively grasp it, it is merely the activity of playing with one's own spirit and vitality. Where, then, does the meaning of Buddha-nature reside?
Baoci Su then said, "If it were not for Yangshan, how could we have seen Zhongyi? But tell me, where was it that Yangshan saw Zhongyi?"
Regarding the "Village Head" (Yichu): Dongta Ming says, "Whether 'large,' 'small,' or 'medium' village head—these are erroneous names and phrases.
They are also called 'Buddha-nature,' and they are also called 'monkeys. Then, clapping his hands and laughing 'he-he,' he asks: 'What kind of talk is this?
Cuiyan Zhe says, "Whether 'large,' 'small,' or 'medium' village head, once pressed by Yangshan, he could not avoid being flustered and bewildered. As for Cuiyan, however—"
But how can one clearly see the Buddha-nature? A blow across the back! Why avoid the monkey’s greed for sleep?
It tires the six gates with their incessant calling.
Sleeping frozen in a snow hut, the night crumbles away; deep and secluded, the wattle gate does not open at night.
One observes the shifting transformations of the withered gardens as the spring wind blows up the ashes from the *lǜ* tubes.
(Tiantong Jue) Every person has an old monkey; from evening to morning, it never ceases its antics. When called, it immediately knows where to land.
In the eighth case, a golden ball was rolled upon flower-bricks (Cishou Shen):
"A single room contains all in its emptiness, facing six windows; The monkey remains, peerless and alone. When thoughts are forgotten and anxieties severed, the monkey dies;
The whole land is at peace, and the six kingdoms submit. (Nantang Jing)

A single room is desolate; five windows are wide open. In the center, Mount Yangshan rises and acts of his own accord, handling a single monkey that performs a thousand kinds of antics. "Washing basin! Washing basin! I know you. (Wanshan Ning).
Chan Master Changxing of Letan in Hongzhou (a successor of Mazu Daoyi) was once visited by Nanquan, who saw the Master sitting with his back to the wall.
As they sat, Huìquán patted the Master on the back. The Master asked, "Who is it? He replied, "Pǔyuàn. The Master asked, "How are you?
He replied, "I am as usual. The Master said, "Why do you trouble yourself so much?"
Facing the wall amidst a precarious heap, he leads guests past it. When asked who it is, he asks further, "How is it?
To say that the ordinary is already a matter of much concern is to find even more matters when examining one's own household affairs.
(Xiyan Hui) National Teacher Wuye Dada of Fenzhou (successor of Mazu I). A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Do not..."
"Do not engage in false conceptualization. Furthermore, when a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? the Master said, "The very mind is the Buddha.
Xuedou Xian, regarding the phrase "do not engage in false conceptualization," said, "It blocks the nostrils. Regarding the phrase "the very mind is the Buddha," he said:
"The tongue is stuck. Zhaojue Qin said: "At this very moment, the tongue is stuck and the nostrils are blocked.
Is there still any place to turn the body and breathe?—[he] strikes. Gunan Men said:
One turn of phrase binds oneself without a rope; one turn of phrase fails to distinguish gold from brass; one turn of phrase is like mountains piled high and peaks heaped up.
There is yet another turn of phrase that will be realized thirty years hence.
The King’s majestic authority—whom would dare to rival it? A mere hair’s breadth of movement and the iron wheel follows.
People of the time see only the sharpness of the needle-point; how many can see the needle within the point?

(Lan’an Puhui). Wuye addressed the assembly: "If there is even a single hair’s breadth of sentiment regarding sainthood or ordinariness that has not been exhausted, one cannot avoid entering the womb of a donkey."
"Entering the womb of a donkey or a horse.
Baizhang said: "Even if one were to exhaust all traces of holy and ordinary thoughts down to a single hair’s breadth, one would still not avoid entering the womb of a donkey or a horse.
Qingshan Xiu said: "They have not yet reached total exhaustion; today I shall pick them up all at once."
[He] stops them. "Do you all still see even a single hair-tip? He lets out a shout and says: "Above all, do not try to pierce the tortoise shell or strike the roof tiles.
Why is Wuye so urgent? Why is Baiyun so solitary? One thought the barbarian’s beard was red, yet there is another red-bearded barbarian.
(Nanyuan Sheng): A single path as straight as a string;
heart and hand are even more intimate. Only when the arrow pierces the shadow of the red sun does one see the man who shoots the eagle. (Gushan Gui)
Chan Master Dayi of Gehu in Xinzhou (a successor of Mazu Daoyi) was summoned to the Linqide Hall by Emperor Xianzong of the Tang dynasty to debate the Dharma.
A Dharma Master asked, "What is Chan? The Master pointed at the empty space with his hand. The Dharma Master had no reply.
The Emperor said, "The Dharma Master has expounded infinite sutras and treatises, yet he cannot cope with this single point."
Expounding principles and discussing the truth before the Purple Palace, the great meaning of Gehu needlessly fatigues the spirit.
Since the Buddha-nature has always been difficult to name and far removed, how can it compare to the King’s intimate, silent realization?
(Tianmu Li) Furthermore, Gehu asked the eminent masters: "In walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, what ultimately constitutes the Way? There was...
One said, "Knowledge is the Way. The Master said, "It cannot be known by intellect, nor can it be recognized by consciousness.

How then can 'knowledge' be the Way? Another said, "Non-discrimination is the Way. The Master said, "One who is well able to discern the characteristics of all phenomena remains unmoved within the primary truth (paramārtha).
How then can 'non-discrimination' be the Way? Another said, "The four dhyānas [are the Way]. The Master said... [text continues]
"The eight dhyānas are the Way. The Master said, "The Buddha-body is unconditioned and does not fall within the realm of numerical categories.
How could the four dhyanas and eight dhyānas be it? The assembly all remained speechless.
Jingshan Hongdao said: "If you scold me, I will let you have your way; if you spit at me, I will let you have your way. Tianning Weiqing said:
"When a monk stays overnight in a temple, he cannot prevent himself from being robbed by a thief."
At Geohu, [Baizhang] cited Emperor Shunzong’s question to Chan Master Śrī: “How can all sentient beings in this great earth see their nature and achieve Buddhahood?
Śrī replied, “The Buddha-nature is like the moon in the water: it can be seen, but it cannot be grasped. The Master said:
"The Buddha-nature is not something seen by looking; it must be seen directly. How can one grasp the moon in the water? The Emperor then asked, "What is this Buddha-nature?
The Master replied, "It is not separate from what Your Majesty has just asked. The Emperor then attained a silent realization of this.
Yingshan Yin said: "If you say that what is not separate from what Your Majesty has asked is itself Buddha-nature, then the eyebrows of Guyu must also stand upright.
Why? Because you only understand that the eyes are horizontal; you do not know that the nose is straight. Falin Yin said:
"The master shows courtesy to the servant."
One falls because of the ground and rises because of the ground; to seek to rise apart from the ground is illogical.
Though the words of one who does not depart from what was asked may seem intimate, if one remains attached to them, it is still not correct.
(*Mirror of Withered Meditation*) Zen Master Foguang Ruman of Luojing (a successor of Mazu Daoyi), when asked by Emperor Shunzong of the Tang dynasty: "From where does the Buddha come?"
"Where did he come from? Where does he go when he passes away? Since it is said that he is always present in the world, where is the Buddha now? The Master replied:
"The Buddha comes from the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) and passes away into the unconditioned. The Dharma-body is equal to empty space; it is eternally present in the realm of no-mind."
The Emperor was greatly pleased.
The Dharma-body is vast and great, equal to empty space; why need one compare its arising and ceasing for similarities or differences?
After wind and rain have passed over the peach blossoms by the roadside, where can a horse’s hoof avoid the remaining red petals? (Yuejiang Yin)

Chan Master Mengxi (a successor of Mazu Daoyi) asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Dingzhou. The Master said, "What extraordinary events have occurred recently in Dingzhou?
The monk said, "I have been staying at the guest quarters there, but I have heard only that salt is expensive and rice is cheap;
there are no extraordinary events at all. The Master said, "It is just like this here as well. We offer monks coarse porridge and plain rice, which is different from anything else."
There is nothing extraordinary here. What more do you seek by coming to this place?
Her elegant and simple adornments are perfect in every detail; her brows are refined and her eyes beautiful, all clearly distinct.
Fortunately, she is untainted by the breath of passion; like a brocade flower, she adds layer upon layer. (Pingxiang)
Chan Master Weikuan of Xingshan in Jingzhao (a successor of Mazu Daoyi) was asked by a monk, “Does a dog have Buddha-nature?

The Master said, “It has. The monk asked, “Does the Master have it too? The Master said, “I do not. The monk said, “All sentient beings possess Buddha-nature; why then do you, Master, lack it? The Master replied, “I am not a sentient being. The monk said—
"If it is neither a sentient being, is it perhaps the Buddha? The Master said, "It is not the Buddha. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, what is it?
The Master said, "It is also not a thing. [The monk] asked, "Can it be seen or conceived? The Master said, "It is beyond the reach of thought."
To perceive it such that it cannot be deliberated upon is called "inconceivable.
Regarding this, Fa-lin-yin separately states: "If it were a Buddha, then it would exist."
Setting aside that monk’s question and removing Chángzhōu’s answer: "Singing freely, I return home; the pure breeze pervades the six realms.
(Wǔzǔ Yǎn) He tears apart the nostrils of Mount Sumeru and tramples the universe of the great ocean underfoot. Before him, the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are all— [The text ends here.]
"My children and grandchildren" (Chuanfang).
When a monk asked the Master of Jingzhao, "Where does the Way reside? the Master said, "The Way is right before your eyes. The monk said, "Why do I not see it?
The Master said, "Because you have the notion of 'I,' you therefore do not see it. The monk said, "If I have the notion of 'I,' then I do not see it."
"Does the Master still see? The Master said, "With you and me, we look back and forth and do not see. [The monk] asked, "Without me and without you, do you still see?
The Master said, "Without me and without you, who is there to seek to see?"
Shendǐng Guīyún said: "The capital treats a three-year-old child with such pity that it would not begrudge even two eyebrows. In the end, this is laborious toil without merit;
these monks and nuns only understand seeking through side-gates, unaware that they themselves dwell in the Imperial Capital.
Let me ask: when there is neither person nor self, who ultimately is it that seeks an audience? He gave a sudden shout and said: "Vipaśyin Buddha has long since set his mind upon this."
Even until now, the wondrous has not been attained. Again, he composed a verse:
"There is not a single thing to compare or discuss; The nostrils still rest upon the upper lip. The warm sun melts the snow from the mountain crags;
On what mountain are the pines and cypresses not lush and green?"
Chan Master Caotang of Jingzhao (a successor of Mazu I) once visited Haichang. Chang asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master said, "From the Dharma-hall. Chang said, "What kind of place is this? The Master said, "A thief does not strike the house of a poor man."
Fenyang Wude succeeded him; with a harmonious tone, he struck the staff.
Having found Peach Blossom Spring, one may well avoid the Qin; the flowers of Peach Blossom Spring smile most sympathetically.
Since falling away beyond the realm of heaven and earth, who has cared for the sounds of wind and rain, waxing and waning? (Qingshan Ding)
Chan Master Zongyin of Sanjiao Mountain in Tanzhou (a successor of Mazu Daoyi) addressed the assembly:
"If we discuss this matter, as soon as you raise your eyebrows, you have already missed it. Magu then asked, "I do not ask about raising the eyebrows;
what is this matter? The Master said, "You have missed it. Magu then overturned the meditation seat, and the Master struck him.
Changqing Lianzong said, "Silent. Baofu Zhan said, "Drawing the bow after the bandit has already fled.
Cui峰 Xian said, "These two fellows have heads but no tails; their eyebrows have not even blinked. Why speak of missing this matter?
Shortly thereafter, a monk asked, 'Why do the eyebrows not blink? Cui Feng struck him immediately."
Zhaojue Qin said: "To call this 'this matter' is already like gouging a sore on good flesh; how much more so to say that as soon as one raises one's eyebrows, one has already missed it?
While Mazu and Cuifeng’s 'drawing the bow after the thief has fled' are indeed so, [it is still not enough]."
There was yet another. Suddenly grasping his staff, he descended from the seat. Tianbao Shu said: "The two elders exchanged verses in this manner;
it was indeed like thunderclaps and rolling lightning, or the splitting of rocks and the collapsing of cliffs. Yet, as for this matter, there are ten thousand miles of white clouds."
Gunanmen said: "If the triangular eyebrows were not like those of Cui Peak, they would surely have been struck down as two separate pieces.
Now, when there is a question, he strikes one straight across the back; what eyebrows is he looking for? Guangjiao Yu said:

"The two great elders were much like a hungry hawk dividing meat or a fierce tiger snatching food. Although they competed with each other in their bids, they could not avoid being laughed at by bystanders."
Observe! Today this mountain monk beats the drum and ascends the seat; you all have crowded upward, yet none dare to stir.
Without the use of weapons, take it for granted that under the wind and rain, all under heaven shall enjoy peace. Amidst this, there is mutual jostling and pressing.
If you say he missed the mark, you are deceiving an ordinary person. If you say he did not miss the mark, after all, what do you call this "this matter"?
[He] let out a shout and descended from his seat. Xiangweng Yun said: "Sanjiao kills people without using a sword;
Xuedou brings people to life without using a blade. Magu splits the sea to swallow dragons; this monk hides his mechanism to trap tigers. Taichun now...
"What have you been doing all day? The wind at the peak is somewhat stiff;
each of you, please take care of your eyebrows. Let go and you will find stability; treading firmly on the four corners, you emerge directly before the sun. Humans and devas do not understand it.
(Tianzhang Yu) The true command is majestic and stern, allowing no compromise; as the stars shift and the constellations turn, its trace cannot be found. The General raises his spear at the head.
The horse; a swirling mass of murderous qi, rolling black winds.
(Dai Tangding) A divine steed gallops across the ranks of dragons and serpents. Swift as lightning, fast as a shooting star, none can equal its pace. Banners and drums are all seized at once;
the beauty remains still on the far side of the river. (Dao Longxing)
Warm breezes and slanting sun lead my solitary staff; on the stony path, who pities the emerald grasses covering it? Having sought my home and garden, spring has already departed;
gazing to the limits of the clouds and mountains, the greenery layers upon layers.
(Xuerenqi) Sanjiao said: "In preaching the Dharma, one must respond to the time and the season. A monk asked about the four yellows and four reds.
"How is it at that time? The Master said, "Carried on the tip of a staff for three months. [The monk] asked, "Why is there so much air stored in his belly?
The Master said, "What can one do about a single rope? [The monk] asked, "How can he get the air out? The Master said, "Wait until the skin is pierced through."
Standing firm on level ground, one still refuses to rest; following the flower-shadows and willow-paths as the seasons flow. Let it fill the belly until there is no idle air left;
only then does one believe that this person has attained true freedom.

(會麼):** A standard phrase used to test the student's realization. * **The verse:** This is a *jìngjué* (頌絕) or verse-commentary on the preceding dialogue. The sentiment reflects the Chan ideal of direct transmission and the rarity of meeting true practitioners. The final couplet is a common lament in Chinese poetry regarding the difficulty of maintaining friendship or spiritual connection over time.

* **Cánlǎng Jiàn (禪朗鑑):** The author of this commentary. The character *jiàn* (鑑) means mirror, suggesting a reflective or critical appraisal of the dialogue. The term *cánlǎng* (禪朗) likely refers to a specific lineage or style of Chan practice.
