Xuedou Xian said, "The eyes of a patriarch must reach such a state. It is like a golden-winged bird cleaving the sea to seize and swallow the dragon directly.
There are some fellows whose eyes cannot distinguish east from west and who do not even know when their staff is upside down; they simply go on talking about 'illumination.'"
"Simultaneously, both person and environment are stripped away. Guishan Zhe said: "Wujiao is much like Guli exerting the majesty of splitting Mount Taohua;
the Azure Dragon displays the momentum of seizing the Black Pearl. It leaves heaven and earth discolored and the sun and moon their radiance hidden.
He then held up his staff and said: "Do you all recognize Wujiao? If you do, lay this staff across your knees."
The Mohe sword alone dominates the world. If you do not yet recognize this, there are eyes upon the staff as clear as the sun.
(He strikes the meditation staff. Baizhang Yuan said: "Among the assembly, some discuss it, saying: 'The staff is in Wugou’s hands;
what difficulty is there in using strength to overwhelm weakness? Alas! Such a perspective as this is difficult even for water to dissolve. Therefore it is said: *Tí*..."
The supreme flavor of ghee is prized by the world; yet when encountered by such people as these, it turns instead into a poisonous drug.

Do you recognize the *vibhītaka* tree? Horizontally grasping the Mo-ye sword, he maintains the full and correct mandate; throughout the realm of Great Peace, he slays the dull and obstinate. Zhaojue Qin said:

"Xuedou clearly distinguishes between the ancient and the modern, and discerns the heterodox and the orthodox. If one does not know 'there is,' how could one understand such a statement? Nevertheless..."
It is so. You have only seen where Wujou let go; you have not yet understood where Wujou held fast. Do you wish to know where Wujou held fast?
It is such that even Śākyamuni and Maitreya would still be his servants, not daring to look upon him with a direct eye.
If one were to act strictly according to the command, everyone throughout the entire earth would have to receive a blow of the staff. Tianmu Li said:
"Everyone says that Wugou’s application [of the staff] was like a thunderclap at the end of a ritual;

yet they fail to realize that their very lives and natures fell into the hands of the two monks, like defeated generals casting aside their spears and scattering across the field. Yunju Zhuang said: "A precipice on level ground."
Standing alone and lofty amidst the level plain, everyone in all directions knows only that Wujou possessed the means to transcend the school and surpass the pattern;
yet they do not know Wujou’s thoroughgoing, compassionate heart (*lǎopóxīn*). Do you understand? Striking the head of a stone man with a staff—*bò bò*—he speaks of actual reality.
Yuan’an Yu said: "Wujou simply continued to act according to his mandate; Maitreya and Śākyamuni stand [in awe]."
"Downwind! Let me ask you, Xuan-shao, do you find it sweet? If you find it sweet, you blind the eyes of all people in the world.
If you do not find it sweet, you blind Wujou’s own eyes. Even if you were to accept both 'sweet' and 'not sweet' together, that would still be like a blind donkey following the great herd.
Ziguoxiu said: "Wujou exhausted his methods, yet he did not care for the common folk. So too was it with Cui-feng."
This is merely following the red lacquer and filling in the ink. Although Zhaojue’s black and white were refined and precise, he only knew where Wujiao held fast;
he did not understand where Wujiao let go. Do you wish to know where he let go? Where the bamboo is dense, it does not hinder the flowing stream from passing through.
How could the height of the mountain obstruct the flight of white clouds?
Naked, one thrusts against the white blade; from death, one finds life once more. A single arrow loses its own track; ten thousand chariots all lose their ruts.
(Zhuan-an Gui): A blazing fire brooks no landing for mosquitoes; the great ocean cannot tolerate a corpse lodging therein.
Even one with three heads and six arms—facing such a wind, there is none who does not raise the flag of surrender. (Jing-shan Gao)
Holding the Mohe sword in his grasp, he sits upon the high seat. Should you attempt to charge forward, you will lose your life.
Even if your spiritual spark were as swift as a flash of lightning, in the end you could not avoid dwelling in sickness amidst the reeds.
(Lan’an Xu) Two blades with hidden points face the sun; to hesitate over whether to strike or touch is to lose one's body. He is accustomed to seizing the initiative before the move is made.
[The Master] said, "Hand! You should not, without fault, ensnare an ordinary person.
(Huanki Ting) Wujou asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "Dingzhou. The Master said, "How is the Dharma-way in Dingzhou compared to here?
He replied, "It is no different. The Master said, "If it is no different, then go back there immediately," and he struck him. The monk said:
"There is an eye at the tip of the staff; one must not act with haste. The Master said, "Today I have struck one," and he struck three more times.
The monk then went out. The Master said, "The staff was originally meant for someone to eat [the blows].
The monk replied, "But the handle of the ladle is still in the hands of the Master. The Master said, "If you want it, I shall give it back to you. The monk approached.
The monk previously snatched the staff and struck the Master three times. The Master said, "What a pity! What a pity! The monk said, "There is someone here who has eaten [of the Dharma].
The Master said, "Roughly, roughly; you have struck a man. The monk bowed, and the Master said, "And yet, you go away like this?
The monk laughed loudly and departed. The Master said, "You deserve it! You truly deserve it!"
Kaixian Jin said: "Clouds move and rain falls; thunder roars and lightning sweeps. Binding the tiger and releasing the tiger; entering the grass and emerging from the grass.
When Wugou met this monk, it can be called the mutual exchange of host and guest, where yielding and seizing are clearly observable.
Why, then, did he say, 'I can handle such a thing'? Tell me, was he approving him or not? Zifukuang said: "A lot of money."

A skilled merchant; long sleeves facilitate a fine dance. Adapting to the times and gauging the situation, his steps accord with the compass and square. He is adept at discussing how the body flies upon the palm;
when others discard it, he takes it up. Yet, overall, he still lacks one move. Huànqìtíng said:
"How many people are there who beat bricks and strike tiles against Xuedou’s verse? They do not realize that Xuedou’s life-vein lies within the staff of Wugu."
To call out is easy; to send away is difficult. Examine closely this shifting of the spiritual pivot: though the kalpa-stone is solid, it may still be destroyed;
the depths of the blue ocean must surely dry up. Old Wugu: how many such ways are there? Handing him the handle of the ladle is truly reckless.
(Manifesting Clear Awareness) The mutual seeing is not in vain; it is clearly entrusted to you. When you are drunk, I shall support you up; when I fall, you must support me back up.
Alternating as guest and host, we shall proceed together into the imperial capital. Singing loudly and laughing in the nine thoroughfares, [we are] among the people of heaven.
In this interval, there is only you and I.
(Fóxìng Tài) Wind upon wind and rain upon rain, my voice turns to silence; beneath the trees, wandering silken threads of thought never sever their affection.
The flying blossoms are swept upward to the upper pavilion; the beautiful woman idly leans against the jade balustrade. (Sānfēng Zàng)
Thief robbing thief; mechanism meeting mechanism. The celestial pivot turns and the stars tremble; the terrestrial axis is upturned and the seas and mountains shift.
(Eh! When the dragon and serpent battle, heaven and earth shake; the boiling cauldron’s cold sound penetrates the boundaries of the world.
(Yuan’an Fu) Chan Master Shijiu (a successor of Mazu Daoyi) went to visit Mazu. Mazu asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Wujiao."
The Patriarch asked, "What have you been saying lately, Wujiu? The Master replied, "How many people are utterly bewildered by this?
The Patriarch said, "Setting aside their bewilderment for a moment, how about that one silent word? What is it? The Master then stepped forward three paces.
The Patriarch said, "I have seven blows to send to Wujiu; would you accept them? The Master said, "Venerable Sir, please eat them first."
"Such-and-such will later agree.
Zhaojue Qin said, "To fish out one or half a person from within a thicket of weeds—what common ground for conversation is there?
Nevertheless, even so, he still lets one move pass. Tianjing Xin said, "These two fellows: if they succeed, they do so together."
Success or failure, both result in ruin. Look closely: it is all like a beggar demanding an old debt.
Shijiu’s foot was set too late; Mazu’s mouth opened too early. To seek money at the crossroads, one must beat him with a wooden mallet. (Yuedang Chang)
Shi Jiu was asked by a monk, "What is the pearl in Dizang’s hand? The Master said, "Do you still have one in your own hand?
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Do not deceive the assembly. He then offered this verse: Failing to recognize the treasure within oneself.

Following along, he perceives external objects; like one fleeing from his shadow at midday, or a man who loses his head in a mirror, he greedily gazes at the moon in the sky and loses the oar in his hand.
On the path beneath the stone mortar mountain, his plans for returning home grow ever more remote.
A brilliant light before one’s face—clapping hands, we laugh at ourselves. But tell me, what is it that we laugh at?
Because we have failed to benefit others (Fodeng Xun), we have lost our own treasure.
Why need one inquire about external dust? When all conditions are completely shattered, only then does one see the person of original nature.

(Tu-du-ce) The Chan Master of an Ancient Temple (a successor of Mazu I): When Danxia came to visit and stayed overnight, at dawn when the congee was ready, the attendant served only one bowl to the Master and kept one bowl for himself, paying no heed to Danxia. Danxia then took a bowl for himself as well.
As he was eating gruel, the Master said, "Rising early at the fifth watch of the night, there are still travelers on the road. Yunxia said to the Master, "Why do you not instruct your attendants?
How can they be so discourteous? The Master replied, "I do not wish to defile the men and women of this household upon this pure ground.
Yunxia said, "In that case, you old fellow, you have not even questioned their transgression."
A fledgling emerging from a phoenix’s nest has no weak wings; a guest lodging at the Dragon Gate would never hesitate. Let the moss and lichen be swept away by the pines and wind as they will;
this ancient temple has never been subject to dust. (Mu Chen Min) A wealthy house has a pampered child;
a powerful army has no feeble generals. An earthen ox swallows the moon; waves rise ten thousand fathoms. A stone shoot sprouts forth.
A single stalk rises ten thousand fathoms high. (This is the mastery of adapting to changes through skillful means.
One day, while Master Benxi Chan (a successor of Mazu Daoyi) was sitting in meditation, Layman Pang arrived.
As soon as the Master looked up, the Layman drew a circle on the ground with his staff. The Master stepped forward and trampled it. The Layman said, "Is it so? Or is it not so?"
The Master also drew a circle. The Layman stepped close and stepped right over it. The Master said, "Is it thus, or is it not? The Layman threw down his staff and stood there.
The Master said, "When you came, you had a staff; when you go, you have none. The Layman replied, "It is naturally perfected as it is;
to look askance at it in vain is superfluous. The Master clapped his hands and said, "How marvelous! How marvelous! It is entirely nothing."
[The monk] attained it. The Master picked up his staff and walked away. The Master said, "Watch the path! Watch the path!
Each presented their own insight, exchanging sharp spiritual sparks that were as swift as a flash of fire beyond reach and a flash of lightning beyond penetration.
He cast down his staff and stood there—not acting with careless haste. He picked up his staff and walked away—not acting with hurried urgency. Herein lies where one may find application.
A single eye—this allows you to see Master Pang in person.
(Shixi Yue) Raising a brush to paint, one plays with the restless spirit; wiping away traces and removing footprints, one sees the person anew.
Reaching the place where the water ends and the mountains exhaust themselves, the clouds disperse across the sky and the moonlight shines bright. (Xiatang Yuan)
Nineteen paths of level ground; in the end, not a single game is the same. Wishing to distinguish the order of the players, one must observe their tracks with a sidelong glance.
(Zhengjue Xian) When Benxi was asked by Master Pang how he understood the meaning behind Danxia’s striking of his attendant, the Master said, "Old man, old man."
The Great Master, seeing that the man was being critical, said, "I am asking you because we were fellow students under the same teacher.
The Master replied, "If that is so, bring it up from the beginning and let us deliberate together. The man said, "You are a venerable elder;
it is not fitting for you to speak of right and wrong regarding others. The Master said, "I take pity on your advanced age. The man said, "A grave offense, a grave offense!"
A pair of iron hammers like balls of cotton; a pair of crows like white cranes. Suddenly meeting on a narrow path, one cannot help but take what comes.
(Fojian Qin) Chan Master Luyuan of Shaoyu (a successor of Mazu Daoyi) ascended the hall and said: "The direct meaning from the West—how could it not be difficult to speak of?"
"None among the great assembly have been able to speak of it. Come forward and try to speak! A monk stepped forth;
as soon as he had prostrated himself, the Master struck him, saying, "What kind of time is this for you to show your head?"
A later person cited this to Changqing. Changqing said, "No problem, no problem. Baofu Zhan spoke on his behalf, saying, "It was for the sake of the Master’s not sparing his own life.
Chengtian Zong said, "The Dharma-treasury is not easy to uphold; these two old fellows could not support it.
I say that if this monk had not stepped forward, the staff would have been eaten by the source of milk himself."
Guishan Lingyou said: "If this monk had possessed the true eye, as soon as he opened his mouth, he should have been told: 'Old Monk, do not show off so much.
Not only would he have exposed Luyuan’s deception, but he would also have cut off the tongues of everyone in the world."
Guangyin Biao says: "If this monk were a true man, as soon as [the master] raised his staff, he should have seized it and, pushing him back a step, said:
'The Master must also take half for himself. This would have left the old fellow utterly crestfallen."
The Patriarch’s intent in coming from the West—how could it be easily measured? To lift one's eyes is already to err in receiving it.
If you, O *śrāmaṇera*, do not understand the proper timing, you will open your eyes wide and enter the cauldron of boiling oil.

(Cishan said: "What is the true meaning of that which came from the West? Most who raise their voices to proclaim it pity those who remain halfway. To entice a thief home is to bring ruin upon oneself."
The bandit believed that he was wearing an amulet for warding off weapons on his person.
(Zhao Shanqi) When Layman Ruyuan was a *śrāmaṇera* under Master Yangshan, he recited the scriptures with a loud voice.
The Master scolded him, saying, "This *śrāmaṇera* recites the scriptures as if he were weeping. Layman Yangshan said, "Huiji is simply like this; I wonder, how about you, Master? The Master—
He then looked back. Shanshan said, "If it is like this, how does it differ from weeping?

The Master then ceased; arrow-points met, sword-blades crossed. Stars shifted and the Dipper turned; images were exchanged and hexagrams drawn. Turning his head, the evening clouds had not yet merged;
raising his eyes, the new moon ascended the treetops. (Adapting to change through skillful means)
The elephant king looks back; the lion turns its paws. Like jade turning and pearls revolving, the mountains are green and the waters are azure.
The voice of the kalaviṅka bird is already marvelous while still within its shell; when it emerges from the flock, it truly possesses wings that can seize the wind.
(Yuan’an An) Zen Master Qifeng (a successor of Mazu I), when asked by Layman Pang, "How many *li* is it from here to the mountain peak? the Master replied: [The text ends here].
[The Master] asked, "Where have you come from? [The monk] said, "One could say he is so stern and rigid that one cannot even question him.
The Master said, "How much is it? [The monk] said, "One, two, three. The Master said, "Four, five, six. [The monk] said, "Why do you not say seven?
The Master said, "As soon as there is seven, there is eight. [The monk] said, "It is so; it is so. The Master said, "Add as many as you wish. [The monk] said, "I cannot enter the hall."
In the Hall, the Master said, "Bring me back the master of this moment, the Old Pang. [Pang] said, "Why do you lack spirit?
The Master said, "What a fine inquiry! Yet you have not questioned the right person. [Pang] said, "I thought as much; I thought as much."
Tiantong Hua said: "To arouse the great potential and manifest the great function, it is not merely a matter of lightning-fast sparks or a flame passing through the wind;
one must require that the level ground be as steep and precipitous as a solitary cliff, and that the rugged heights be as flat as a plain.

Observe how these two elders entered the tiger’s den and penetrated the profound source, until they reached the state of interlocking patterns and free-swinging mastery, attaining great sovereignty. For what reason?"
"I have never been to Mount Kōmyō. As for Master Seijū’s saying, 'Return to me, at such a time, the master of Layman P'ang,' Master Shisho said, 'Why trouble yourself with such spirit?
Here at Kueizō, I intend to set up an eye so that everyone may have a sudden flash of realization. After a long silence, he said:
"The bamboo shadows sweep the steps, yet the dust does not stir; the moon pierces the bottom of the pond, yet the water leaves no trace."
One day, Qifu Peak was walking alongside Layman Pang. The Layman took a step forward and said, "I am one step stronger than you, Master.
The Master replied, "There is no 'back' or 'front'; old man, you wish to be first. The Layman said, "'The bitter within bitterness is not yet this one phrase.
The Master said, "I fear you will not be satisfied. The Layman said, "If the old man is not satisfied, Qifu Peak is capable [of it]."
"What are you doing? the Master asked. The scholar said, "If I had a staff in my hand, I would strike you without weariness.
He then slapped the Master once and said, "Not very good. Only then did the Master pick up his staff, whereupon the scholar seized it and said, "This fellow has suffered a defeat today.
The Master laughed and said, "I am clumsy; you are clever. The scholar then clapped his hands and went out, saying, "An equal meeting an equal."

Jiao Jiangtianquan said: "In yielding there is seizing; Master Pang knew only how to retreat behind the waters. In losing there is winning; Master Qi was accustomed to reducing the number of cooking fires.
Although they both emerged from the school of Master Ma, in the end they have not yet beheld Master Ma’s face."
The silk line is drawn in and released amidst the misty waves; Sitting steadily upon the jetty, he lowers his fishing hook.
This true, wondrous secret has not been transmitted through antiquity; Reeds and flowers reflect the moon as autumn fills the heavens.
(De-shi-xin) Chan Master Shuilao of Hongzhou (a successor of Mazu I) asked Mazu, "What is the very meaning of the coming from the West?"
The Patriarch then stepped on him right at the chest and knocked him down. The Master attained great enlightenment; rising up, he laughed heartily and said, "How extraordinary!
How extraordinary! Hundreds of thousands of samādhis and immeasurable subtle meanings—all are recognized by finding their source upon the tip of a single hair."
Langye Jue said: "Great assembly, you tell me: did Shaokang still attain enlightenment or not?
Tiantong Jue said: "Master Mazu should not have let him go. When he rose up and spoke thus, he should have simply asked, 'From where did that single hair-tip come?
Had he hesitated for a moment, Mazu would have given him another kick. Lianhua Wan said: "A buttress."
"Life brings forth arrows. Gushan Puhui said: "A beggar sees a small profit;
a colt gives one kick, and the donkey falls to the ground. Laughing loudly, he gets up; the sheep bleats and the dog barks.
(Yexuan Zun) "When kicked down once, it is enough for a great laugh; all former skills and wiles were merely labor in vain. Yet the serpent’s head must still be rubbed hard."
Itching. Myriad upon myriad, ten thousand upon ten thousand, emerge from a single hair-pore.
(Baiyun Yuan) Shuilao took up the opportunity and penetrated the Patriarch’s intent; the colt’s single kick revealed the root source.
The void collapses with no intervening space; he then steers an iron boat across the vast blue sea. (Zhaojue Zong)
The bamboo tubes must have already fermented it to perfection; do not begrudge the slanting of your cap within intoxication.
The *túmí* has its own subtle fragrance, yet this is wine after all—it is not the flower.
(Lǎn’ān Shū) They say spring has arrived beautifully, but the wild winds are far too unruly. They blow the flowers away with the water, overturning the fishing boat.
(Xue’an Jin) Tearing a piece of tattered ramie cloth, he mends a pair of tattered ramie trousers. He chases the deer of the South Mountain and outpaces the hares of the North Mountain.
He spins cotton and eats tofu; ever since he turned the winnowing fan upside down, his two legs have remained as stiff as vinegar until now.
Jiexu Xie arrived with water and mud, drew a circle on the Master’s shoulder, and placed it there. The Master pushed it away three times, then drew another circle and pointed at the monk.
The monk bowed; the Master struck him, saying, “You fraud who deceives others!”
Baoning Yong bowed at another monk’s feet and spat upon them before departing. He then offered this verse:
To kick away and to bring forth the fist is but the ordinary; How can one avoid seeing the stars of Shen and Shang? Relying on the public standard for measurement, there is no partiality;
The short remains short, and the long remains long.
When Shuilao was asked by a monk, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? the Master said, "If there is movement, a shadow appears; if there is awakening, ice forms.
Zifu Yu remarked, "If there is movement, a shadow appears, but when there is no movement, it cannot be that there is no shadow. If there is awakening, ice forms..."
When one is unaware, ice cannot be absent. It is said that even the eyes of a śramaṇa cannot perceive it, let alone its movement.
The Water-Bull sleeps on the open ground; why trouble him with the short flute or further lash him with a whip?
Free and easy beneath the long forest, a single day passes like a hundred years. (Yugu Zhi)
Chan Master Zhentu of Yangqi in Yuanzhou (a successor of Mazu I). A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master held up his rosary. The monk was at a loss. The Master said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not. The Master said, "I have studied under Shitou.
[The monk] asked, "What realization did you gain from seeing Shitou? The Master pointed to the deer in the courtyard.
[The Master] asked, "Do you understand? [Wu Yi] replied, "I do not. The Master said, "He has attained freedom:
Dew wets the earth and clouds gather, not yet withdrawn at dawn; the evening glow still lingers atop the cassia branches.
After the night-owl cries from the western peak at midnight, one smiles to watch the moonlight float upon the surface of the sea. (Wu Yi arrived.)
One day, when Chan Master Taoyu of Fuyong in Piling (a successor of Mazu I) was serving food, he arrived before Pang Gong.
As the master was about to receive it, the Master withdrew his hand and said, "To receive food with a conceptual mind is what Vimalakīrti rebuked.
Having set aside this single instance, layman, do you still find it acceptable? Pang Gong replied, "At that time, wasn't Subhūti a master of his craft? The Master said, "That is not the point."
Regarding another matter: it is said that when food reached his mouth, it was snatched away by someone. The Master then proceeded to distribute the food.
The Duke said, "One phrase is unnecessary. Zhaojue Qin remarked, "Shanxian is a master; Fuyong is extraordinary. They were all completely accounted for by Pang Gong in a single indictment."
It is understood. As for the statement that "it cannot be resolved by a single phrase," tell me, what is that phrase? "Sitting upright, receiving offerings;
may the donor always be at peace."
Furong asked because of the question from Master Pang: "Does Mazu transmit his point of truly benefiting people to you, my teacher?
The Master said, "I have not yet seen him; how could I know his point of being real? Furong said, "Even this very seeing and knowing has no place to be sought.
The Master said, "Layman, you must not speak of it in a one-sided manner. Furong said, "One..."
The challenger lost his point once again. "If one proceeds with two directions or three directions," he asked, "can the Master still open his mouth?
The Master replied, "It is truly impossible to open one's mouth; this may be called 'reality' (shí). The official clapped his hands and departed.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Why did Furong not say, 'I entrust it to you'? When [the student] asks, 'What is the point of true reality?', he should have given him a slap.
When the student's eyes flicker and move, he should give him another slap.
Why? It is simply to cut through all this tangled undergrowth. Fochuan Zong said: "These two fellows are nothing but dung-collecting mules."
How strange! Although one may cast the fishing line in secret, one cannot deceive the wild mountains.

One day, while Master Fubei (a successor of Mazu Daoyi) was serving tea, Ling Xingpo arrived. The woman asked, "To whom do you entrust that phrase which cannot be spoken even with one's full strength?

"A snowball! A snowball! Old Pang’s clever device is beyond recovery; neither in heaven nor on earth does he know his own whereabouts.
Within the eyes and within the ears, there is absolute detachment. Absolute detachment! Even the blue-eyed barbarian monk finds it difficult to discern.
(Cui-feng Xian) It falls amidst the snow; no hand or foot is offended. Even with an iron tongue driven into place, it is difficult to bring it to the mouth.
A palm-snowball is swung and comes crashing against the face; it strikes the back of the Vajra-brain. (Yun-jue Wu)
Three feet of cold light pierce the Dipper and Ox; where Moye is raised, ghosts and spirits tremble with dread. The barbarians do not recognize the General’s command;
having mistakenly entered the heavy encirclement, blood flows from their necks.
(At the head of the Yezhu River: Above is vast and boundless; below one’s feet is vast and boundless. To remain fixed is easy; to turn away in a flash is difficult. The Vajra Jewel Sword.
It chills the bones. Do not look outside the words of the critical pivot. (Moon over Shixi). Master Pang said:
"Having sons, I do not marry them off; having daughters, I do not give them away. All together in a circle, we speak of the discourse on non-arising."
Yang Wuweï said in another version: "When a son grows up, he must marry; when a daughter grows up, she must wed.
What leisure do you have to further discuss talk of non-arising? Baizhang Yuan said: "Although these two men differ in their tone of voice, their tongues are nonetheless one and the same.
Today there is a person who marries his sons and weds his daughters, yet whenever he encounters a monk, he joyfully speaks of non-arising."
A story. Regardless of how many thousands of autumns humanity may endure, one only perceives that heaven and earth are as large as a grain of millet.
Wealth and nobility, glory and splendor—they are merely the "hu," "zhe," "ya," and "er" within the vast void. Only the green mountains facing one's door remain;
they are, in truth, a single scroll of painting. Then, with his whisk, he drew a stroke through the air.
Gathering the sentiments of mountain clouds and ocean moons: the circle is complete, the nose straight, and the brows arched.
With a whisk of tortoise hair and a staff of hare horns, one strikes the void until it rings out with a *pao pao* sound.
(Shixi Yue) Spring comes and flowers bloom; autumn passes and leaves fall. Father and son are gathered as one; what good or evil could they possibly distinguish? (Kuchan Jing)
Not saying it is so; not saying it is not. A raised eyebrow, a blink of an eye—deceit within, releasing folly. Father’s kindness, son’s filial piety: there is no other matter;
the whole family is simply seeking advantage. (Nun Xianlin Ying) Master Pang said:

"The mind is as such, and the environment is also as such. There is neither reality nor unreality. Whether there is something, I do not concern myself with it; whether there is nothing," [I do not concern myself with it].
"Indeterminate. Not a sage or a worthy, but an ordinary person who has finished their business.
Jingshan Daowu said: "Pure white, vast blue. Water cannot moisten it; fire cannot burn it. What is this?
You must not ask about it. To ask would blind your eyes. [He struck the incense stand once with his staff.]
[The Master] said, "Down! Tianning Qi said: "If you wish to become an ordinary person who has accomplished their task, you must advance three more steps. Falin Yin said:
"If you wish to become an ordinary person who has accomplished their task, you must retreat three steps immediately. Jianfu Ru said:
"Chushi said, 'If you wish to become an ordinary person who has accomplished their task, you must advance three more steps. But how do you advance? Five!"
Old Clouds, the waters of the Nine Rivers, roll up and spread out, appearing and disappearing within the great void; yet ultimately, they remain within the transformative influence of our Sovereign.
Pang Gong said: "The ten directions gather together as one; Each and every one studies non-action (*wuwei*). This is the field for selecting Buddhas;
With an empty mind, one returns having passed the imperial examination."
Tiantong Jie said: "The ten directions gather together as one—a wall of iron, a mountain of silver. Each and every one studies non-action, while the sun and moon shine upon them.

This is the field for selecting Buddhas, where dragons and snakes are intermingled; with an empty mind, they return having passed the imperial examination, where ordinary beings and sages dwell together."
Suddenly picking up his staff and holding it crosswise, he said, "Pang the Layman is sitting right here.
Do you all see him? He then threw it down and said, "Three lifetimes, sixty kalpas."
The *fuhou* turban is covered in dust, the boots are worn through; in the field where Buddhas are selected, there are not two such men.
If you say, "With a mind empty, I have passed the imperial examination and returned," I shall strike a blow upon your head that you will find difficult to let pass.
(Fohuiquan) Wind, moon, mountains, and rivers share one family; who comes to settle dragons and snakes beneath the words? Taibai never even climbed it.
[The Master] said: "Your Excellency, last night the tip of the brush spontaneously produced flowers.
(Xinwen Ben) "Having exhausted his entire livelihood, he sells a colander; among the band of pickpockets, he seeks advantage. Looking at his skills, they are merely like this;
yet he says, 'With an empty mind, I have passed the imperial examination and returned. (Fozhao Guang)
Master Pang said: "To protect life, one must kill; only when killing is exhausted does one dwell in peace. If you understand the meaning within this, an iron boat will float upon the water.
Master Zhaojue Qin said: "But tell me, what is it that is killed? To kill the life-force of sentient beings is the view of ordinary people. What is killed?"
"The six thieves and afflictions" is the view of a lecture master. "Killing the Buddhas and killing the patriarchs" is the view of a great icchantika.
Within the domain of a patch-robed monk, what exactly is it that is killed? Jingshan Yan said: "One only knows how easy it is to open one's mouth;
one fails to realize how long one's tongue is."
One day, Master Pang said, "Difficult, difficult! Ten loads of sesame seeds spread out upon a tree. Dame responded at once, "Easy, easy!
The meaning of the Patriarch lies at the tips of the hundred blades of grass. Lingzhao said, "Neither difficult nor easy;
when hungry, one eats; when tired, one sleeps."
Jingshan Daokai said: "These three worldly fellows travel together but not in step; they gain together but do not lose together.
Nevertheless, it makes the bystanders laugh to death. Dajue Sheng said: "I would give thirty blows to each of these three worldly fellows. Why? Because—"
"What is this 'what' that exists? To speak of the difficult and the easy—right now, is there anyone who can transcend the difficult and the easy?
Even if there were, it would still be like a fan in the middle of winter. Lian’an Guang said: "Though the family may be prosperous, it is the son who gives rise to filial piety."
A state’s hegemony produces strategic ministers; if order and peace remain as they are, it would be a pity to grant them thirty [miles].
To avoid the division of borders and the drawing of lines, the man at the mouth of the pass mutters on and on without ceasing, yet he takes his colander as a companion for his travels.
He has a daughter whom he refuses to marry; in years to come, she will surely become an old spinster. (Lan’an Shu)
Enemy upon enemy, face to face they all behold one another. Playing a lute without strings, its pure sound resounds through the ages.
(Xianchan Guan) Three pack-animals cross the bridge together; one stretches, one bends, and one stoops. Their reflections in the water divide their lengths.
Short. It would make bystanders laugh to death; [this] bundle seems like it wants to whistle.
(Mengan Lü) Master Pang threw his entire household estate into the Xiang River, while his daughter Lingzhao daily sold a colander in the marketplace.
With her hair bound in a bun like a massed cloud, her graceful form is full of charm. She carries several bamboo sieves balanced on the tip of her staff.
Entering the marketplace, how could she expect no one to ask about her? Should she encounter a true connoisseur, he will certainly not let her off easy.

(Yuanzhao’s version: "Her father cast his livelihood into the waters of the Xiang River; it has burdened his daughter to sell sieves along the streets. It is not that their family is poor, but rather because of the son...")
Suffering. How many people can truly understand this mind?
(Wuji Pai) The father has already returned home with his heart having attained the highest degree; the daughter follows suit in painting her brows like a moth.
Within the household, there is only the affairs of the household; where could one find spare money to buy a colander? (Wuliangshou)
Master Pang happened to be selling a colander when he fell down the bridge. As soon as Lingzhao saw this, she also went and collapsed beside her father.
The Master asked, "What are you doing? She replied, "Seeing my father fall to the ground, I was there to support him. The Master said, "Fortunately, no one saw us."
Master Pang falls; Lingzhao helps him up. Since both have failed, what is there for the one? (Guoqing Ying) The Layman falls to the ground; Lingzhao helps him up.
This is the trickery of a beggar—what point is there in seeking it? (Tiantong Hua) Filial piety hides rebellion;
one’s own ugliness cannot be concealed before others. This life’s close kin are, from a former existence, bitter enemies.
(Nan-sou Mao) Master Pang falls to the ground;
Lingzhao helps him up. Several hundred years have passed since then, yet the pure breeze has not ceased.
It has not ceased. A thousand-foot carp from the Eastern Sea leaps [through the clouds]. (Yi-an Shen)
Pang Gong asked Lingzhao, "The ancients said: 'Clearly, clearly, atop the hundred blades of grass; clearly, clearly, the meaning of the Patriarchs. How do you understand this?
Lingzhao replied, "Old and decrepit as you are, why do you utter such words?
Pang Gong asked, "How about you? She said, "Clearly, clearly, atop the hundred blades of grass; clearly, clearly, the meaning of the Patriarchs. Pang Gong then smiled.
Ten thousand *li* of cloudless sky, the Milky Way stretches across; The profound path of the Great Square is traversed with ease.
Father’s wisdom and capacity are rare in this world; A halo of light emerges from atop the daughter’s head. (Or:
The essence of the Hermitage) Pang’s family reputation endures for a thousand ages; They respond to one another on the difficult and the easy. Among them, Lingzhao is slightly superior.
"Son, the Patriarch’s meaning is clear upon the tips of the hundred grasses.
(Cheng the Head Seat) When Master Pang was about to enter extinction, he said to Lingzhao, "Observe the sun for its time; report to me when it is noon.
Lingzhao quickly reported, "The sun has already reached midday, yet there is an eclipse. As the Master went out the door to observe, Lingzhao immediately ascended her father’s seat.
She sat with palms joined and passed away. The Duke smiled and said, "My daughter’s skill was this swift; she has extended [my life] for another seven days.
At home, there was a full troupe of musicians performing a newly composed tune unlike any other: "Clearly one laments parting, yet it is a joy to meet again."

(Xiyuan Hui): A stage of dancing and acting, the whole family in joy; drums and music resound through the heavens as they perform at will. Once the theatrical robes are cast off, who can recognize them?
Without cause, they laugh the Yellow Fanchoe down. (Beihai Xin)
When Pang Gong was about to pass away, Yu Gong, the Governor of Longzhou, went to inquire after his illness. Pang Gong said, "I only wish that you would empty all that exists;
be careful not to fill what does not exist. Dwell happily in this world, for everything is like a shadow or an echo. Having spoken these words, he leaned his head upon Yu's knee and passed away.

If you wish to know the place where the source is exhausted, who can point out the way for those lost? Beyond the setting sun and the roosters and dogs, the peach and plum trees naturally form a path.

(Xutang Yu) When the old woman Pang entered Lukun Temple to perform a vegetarian feast, the *vina* (chant leader) requested that she provide the intent for the dedication of merit. The old woman took up her comb.
Pointing it toward the back of her hair-bun, she said, "This is my dedication of merit," and then she departed.
Laywoman Pang shifted the comb to the side of her bun; such elegance as this is peerless in all the world.
When all matters are settled with impartial justice, the rector need not record them on his brush. (Cishou Shen)
The *vinaya-dhara* addresses the assembly with a solemn proclamation; In return, he is laughed at by his mother-in-law.
He turns his tooth-comb back and re-ties his sandals; Yet when they meet, they still deliberate in error.
(Da Tang Ding) — Fourth generation under Dajian.
Chan Master Xiyun Huidi of Huangbo in Hongzhou (a successor of Baizhang Hai) ascended the hall and said:

"All of you here are nothing but dregs of wine and vinegar. Traveling as monks like this, where else could you find your place today? Do you know that within the Great Tang Empire there are no Chan masters?
At that time, a monk asked: "As for the various quarters gathering assemblies and opening the halls for teaching, why..."
"Why do you say there is no teacher? he asked. [Yangshan] replied, "I do not say there is no Chan;
I simply say there is no teacher. Miaoyan asked Yangshan, "What do you say to this? Yangshan said, "The king of geese chooses its milk; it is inherently not of the same kind as a duck.
Miaoyan said, "This is indeed difficult to distinguish. Wuzu Ji stepped forward and addressed the monks, saying, "Thank you, Master, for explaining the principle so well."
Shimen Cong said: "Huangbo’s instruction was indeed extraordinary; yet as soon as he was pressed by Puna, he lost one of his eyes.
Cuiyan Zhen said: "The masters of all quarters say that Huangbo sat upon this monk;
others say that Huangbo was brought up by this monk until he could not even analyze it. Why is this so? Cuiyan [speaks] now..."

As he was about to raise an objection, [the Master said]: "A misty leopard’s fur is so thick and lustrous that it never stoops to eat; a bird in the courtyard nurtures its courage, waiting until the end to startle people.
Cheng Tianzong said: "The eye of the Fifth Patriarch shines forth, piercing through the four worlds; yet even to see Huangbo would still not be sufficient."
If one wishes to uphold the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, one must be a master of the Huangbo lineage.
Wuishan Zhe said: "Do not blame him for his former abundance of spirit; he once trod upon the highest pass. Fachang Yu said:
"I want one who has no Zen to serve as National Teacher. Jingshan Gao said: "Tell me, is this a sentence of clarified butter, or is it a dose of poison?"
[This is a] phrase. Tiantong Wu said: "Huangbo was much like one who has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake.

At that time, when [Nanquan] asked, 'What about those in all quarters who guide disciples and lead assemblies? why did he not strike him with a blow of his staff in unison with the sound? Dongshan Ying said:
"Although Huangbo’s eyes covered heaven and earth and his breath swallowed the universe, he was nonetheless far too noisy. Still...
"Is there anyone who knows the place where E-luo was beheaded? After a long silence, he said, "Dangerous. Zifu Guang said, "Huangbo’s words here bring tears to his eyes and pain to his bowels.
Those who do not understand might think he is overstepping the various quarters [of the Chan school]. If that were so, it would be a profound injustice to the ancients.
Let me briefly reveal a glimpse of my own view from Mount Bian. After a long silence, he said, "A short song cannot be made long."
Teacherless adepts fill the Great Tang; those who merely consume dregs of wine cannot understand. Passing idly through the bamboo temple, spring is already deep;
falling petals scatter in disorder, staining the hue of the moss.

(Fohuiquan) Branches diverge and silks are dyed in great confusion; leaves cluster and flowers link, ruining the ancestral school. Skillfully grasping the compass of creation, one transforms the world.
The Handle. Water and clouds are the tools for the potter; he screens out the trivial and cuts away the coarse wool.
With a star-weighing mirror and a jade-ruler golden blade, Old Huangbo perceives even the finest hair of autumn. Sitting firm in the spring breeze, he allows nothing to rise high. (Tiantong Jue):
Only by putting on clothes upon one’s body can one avoid the cold; merely speaking of food at the mouth will never satisfy one’s hunger. An old woman within the Great Tang Empire.
Chan. Today I have annotated it through and through for you.
(Jingshan Gao) A body that transcends the phenomenal world encompasses the universe; where sage and ordinary being reach their limit, not even a speck of dust can enter.
The spirit of a monk ought to be thus: who on the field will be the one to seize the banner? (Xuedou Zong)
Proclaiming the wondrous meaning amidst a thicket of brambles; emitting rays of light within a garden of caltrops. Of thousands of words and ten thousand phrases, no one understands;
yet again, following the warbling oriole over the low wall.

(Huitong Dan) At the Gate of Ghosts, even ghosts are startled by the posted talisman; yet another sight of the hair-tip Broom Star. If one can pass through this barrier, one’s credentials will be verified.
Correct. Deep in the night, he walks the imperial street with his hand extended.
(Zhong’an Kong): It is not that there is no Chan; it is simply that there is no teacher. A cat has a grinding muller tied to its tail.
Deep in the night, it kills the mouse by the bedside. Who among the travelers on the road would know of this? (Zhongfeng Ben).
Year after year, year after year, he devours dregs of wine; Deluded by flowers, intoxicated by willows, a mere scoundrel.
He has exchanged his two eyes for donkey dung; Smiling as he departs, he offers one final solemnity.
(Zibao Ke) In joyful spirit, his small boat hoists full sails; A favorable wind from every side leaves no obstruction. The sound of the flute plays the plum blossoms to their end.
**Tiao:** The setting sun brings forth the tide; May is cold.
(Daliang Bei) Within the Great Tang Empire there is no Chan master. In the midnight frosty sky, the moon’s reflection lingers.
When the watch has passed and footprints are few, One takes up a silk fan to shield the flowering branches. (Falin Yin)
When Baizhang asked Huangbo, "Where have you come from? the Master replied, "I have come from picking mushrooms at Mount Daxiong.
Baizhang asked, "Did you see a tiger? The Master then let out a tiger's roar. Baizhang raised his axe and made a gesture as if to strike him.
The Master then gave Baizhang a slap. Baizhang laughed heartily and went back. Upon ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying, "Mount Daxiong..."
"Below there is a great beast; you all must watch out for it! Today, Old Man Baizhang has been personally struck by its fangs.
Yangshan asked, "What would you have done, Master Weishan? Weishan said, "At that time, Baizhang should have simply struck him down with one blow of his axe."
Yangshan asked, "For what reason has it come to this? Yangshan said, "It is not so. Muzhou asked, "How so? Yangshan said, "Baizhang only knows how to ride the tiger's head;
he does not know how to grasp the tiger's tail. Muzhou said, "My son, you have a truly perilous statement.

Wuzu Jie remarked, "Baizhang is much like a thief whose heart is filled with trepidation; Huangbo is one who finds it difficult to forget what he is well-versed in. Yunmen added, "The tiger’s tail is indeed dangerous."

Juzhuang said: "To claim that Baizhang lacked the 'trap for tigers' and that Huangbo possessed the 'surpassing of the master'—such theorizing is like piercing one's brain into a vat of glue. He drew a stroke with his whisk and said:
"Splitting open the towering beauty of Mount Hua, releasing the Yellow River in its ultimate clarity. Chuan'an Cheng said: "Baizhang had the 'trap for tigers'..."
As for this "function" (*jī*): Huangbo possessed the utility of "biting the arrowhead. Had they encountered one another suddenly and directly, it would have been enough to behold his brilliance.
Alas, he failed to guard his conduct to the end, which caused matters to remain unresolved throughout past and present. Lin Youhui said:

"Everyone says that Huangbo’s functional capacity surpassed his master [Nanquan], and that Baizhang praised him deeply. Little do they realize that this old thief harbored ill intent; he dug a deep pit..."
A pitfall. Even if one possesses the fangs and claws of Huangbo throughout one’s entire being, in the end, one cannot leap out.
When the tips of arrows meet, there is naturally no discrepancy; it is only right that a natural son serves his father.
To gather up the entire earth, not a single inch of soil remains. A three-foot Great Sword settles dragons and snakes. (Zhiguanhui)
Because Baizhang asked Huangbo, "Dharma-heir Yun, it is no easy matter to clear the fields," the Master replied, "I have been working alongside the assembly.
Baizhang said, "It must have been troublesome for you to perform such labor. The Master replied, "How would I dare refuse the toil? Baizhang asked, "How much field have you cleared?
The Master took his hoe and struck the ground three times. Baizhang then gave a shout, and the Master covered his ears and departed.
Langye Jue said: "Baizhang’s single shout cast its line into a ten-thousand-fathom abyss;
Huangbo’s covering of his ears stood alone atop a thousand peaks. Weishan Zhe said: "Huangbo’s cultivation of the fields was not in vain;
Baizhang’s governance of the monastery did not issue empty commands."
When we meet and converse, our principles are not deficient; yet in an ordinary moment, we turn away and part. In the end, water must flow back to the sea;
in the final analysis, clouds surely seek the mountain to return.
(Longmen Yuan) Once, when Huangbo saw six newly arrived monks, five of them prostrated themselves, while one raised his sitting mat and made a gesture.
Yuanxiang said, "I have heard there is a very fierce hunting dog. Xuedou said, "It comes seeking the sound of the antelope. Yuanxiang said, "The antelope has no sound for you to seek.
Xuedou said, "It comes seeking the tracks of the antelope. Yuanxiang said, "The antelope has no tracks for you to seek.
Xuedou said, "It comes seeking the footprints of the antelope. Yuanxiang said, "The antelope has no footprints for you to seek."
Xun said, "In that case, he is a dead langur. The Master then ceased speaking. The next day, he ascended the hall and said, "Yesterday’s monk Xun, the langur—come forward!
The monk immediately stepped out. The Master said, "Yesterday’s koan was not yet finished; I, the old monk, simply ceased speaking.
What do you have to say about it? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "I took you for a genuine patch-robed monk."
"Originally, he was merely a scholar-monk," [Baizhang] said, and drove him out with his staff.
Cui峰 Xian said: "If there are neither sounds nor traces, where will the hunting dog go to seek and pursue?
Is it by means of the absence of sound and trace that one perceives Huangbo? O Zen adepts, if you wish to understand the mechanism for trapping a tiger..."
"One must be a monk of genuine substance. Nanmen of Goun said: "Huangbo had bait on the hook; this monk followed the hook straight up.
Nevertheless, since he was a hunting dog, why did he fail to recognize the antelope even when it came right before him?
At that time, when Huangbo said, "The antelope is silent—go find it," [the monk] should have immediately seized him and said, "This old fellow, from the very beginning..."
He has come and remains right here. Even if Huangbo possessed the "trap for tigers" ruse, where else could he have deployed it?
Longhua Ti said: "At that time, when Huangbo said, 'The wild sheep has no sound;

you must seek it,' one should have simply replied, 'No need for further examination,' and then swept the sleeves and departed. Even if Huangbo’s entire body were eyes, he still would not have been able to discern him."
While Huangbo was prostrating before the Buddha in the hall of Yanguan, the future Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang dynasty was there as a śrāmaṇera.
He asked, "If one does not seek the Buddha, does not seek the Dharma, and does not seek the Saṃgha, what is it that you, Elder, are seeking when you prostrate?"
The Master said, "Do not seek it by clinging to the Buddha; do not seek it by clinging to the Dharma; do not seek it by clinging to the Sangha. Always pay homage to such matters.
Zhiyi asked, "What is the use of paying homage? The Master then struck him. Zhiyi said, "That was too coarse.
The Master said, "What place is this for speaking of coarse or fine? He then struck him again.

Beneath one’s knees, yellow gold is precious; within the palms of one’s hands, heaven and earth are vast. One rejoices in the meeting of wind and clouds; the four seas are all chilled by the surging waves.

(Hui of Xiyuan) Thunder roars and lightning flashes as the full mechanism is unleashed. It is precisely at the moment when the hidden dragon sleeps soundly. Suddenly, awakening from the dream, the springtime resentment stirs.
Severance. The morning breeze blows the rain across the stream before me. (Clouds of Leisure) Huangbo said:
"Since Master Bodhidharma arrived in China, he has spoken only of the One Mind and transmitted only the One Dharma."
The Buddha transmits the Buddha, not transmitting any other Buddha; the Dharma transmits the Dharma, not speaking of any other Dharma.
The Dharma is the ineffable Dharma; the Buddha is the ungraspable Buddha. The Buddha is precisely the fundamentally pure mind.
Suiryaku Un said: "Huangbo was breathing through the nostrils of Master Bodhidharma; he thought there was no one to examine him.
This mountain monk is not suppressing his majestic brilliance; I simply wish for the household to be peaceful and the door to be secure."
Huangbo was the head seat under Nanquan. One day at the time of the midday meal, he took up his bowl and sat in the place of honor reserved for Nanquan.
When Nanquan entered the hall and saw him, he asked, "Venerable sir, how many years have you been practicing the Way?
The Master replied, "Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja. Nanquan said, "Even so, you are still but a descendant of Old Master Wang. The Master then took up his bowl and moved to the second seat.
Quán (Huangbo) stopped.
Wúguān Yòu said, "He who deceives his enemy perishes. Yǎngshān said, "Not so; one must know that Huangbo possessed the mechanism for trapping tigers.
Wúguān said, "Your insight has grown this far. Cùfēng Xiǎn said, "What a pity for Old Wang!"

The Master [Zhaozhou] saw only the sharpness of the tip of the awl. Had I been Nanquan at that time, I would have waited for him to say "before King Wei-yin," and then immediately taken the seat in the second position, leaving Huangbo unable to rise for the rest of his life. Even so, however...
One must also rescue Nanquan. Yunfeng Yue said: "Everyone says that Huangbo possesses the mechanism for trapping tigers and Nanquan possesses the function of killing tigers;
yet they do not realize that this old thief has years but no virtue. Even his eating and sitting do not accord with his proper station.
If one were under Yunfeng’s gate, what need would there be to speak of anything prior to King Weyin? Furthermore...
"If there were someone greater than Master Wangluo, one would simply have to give him a blow with the staff and drive him out. Jingshan Daowu said:

"Why wait for him to ask how many years he has been practicing the Way? As soon as he entered the hall and saw that he was occupying the seat of the presiding master, [Wangluo] took his bowl and sat in the second seat.
Even if Huangbo possessed the 'trap for tigers' device, where could he possibly have applied it? Baohua.
Renyun said, "There is gathering and there is releasing; host and guest alternate. Huangbo was certainly a master;
he not only knew how to ride the tiger's head, but also understood how to gather in the tiger's tail. Nanquan was an even more skilled hand.

When Yaoshan remarked, "He who seeks to deceive the enemy perishes," it was like pouring oil onto fire. Yangshan said, "One must know that Huangbo possessed the mechanism for trapping a tiger"—this is truly chilling.
Each of the four elders occupies his own domain, each claiming supremacy for himself. If one fully upholds [the Dharma], all fully uphold it;
if one fails, all fail. Today, I have bound these four elders together into a single mass and cast them before you.
Is there anyone who will come to the rescue of these four elders? Lingyin Li said:
I shall simply take these two fellows and place them beneath my words as a footnote. Is there anyone here today who can occupy the seat of this mountain monk?
If there is, then this mountain monk will hold out his bowl and return to the abbot’s quarters; let us see how they handle the final tally.
When old age comes, who will remember one another? Before others, each pretends to be alert and wise. Yet, none shall escape being buried together in the same pit;
how many today still possess clear vision? (Longmen Yuan) "Vipaśyin Buddha is my descendant.
When Old Wang spoke those grand words, Huangbo recognized the opportunity and distinguished the host.
(Ban): A model for a thousand ages, he established the lineage of the School. (Shushan Ru):
Clearly stirring up a vat of excrement, yet burning musk incense so it wafts exquisitely. One never perceives any of that fragrance;
one sits entirely within the vat of excrement. (Mongan Yue)

"Once upon a time, military banners were advantageous; why now have you fallen into unrighteousness? It is largely due to the intensification of warfare that, in the end, the dignity of the King has been compromised.
(Dao Lǒngxīng) One day, Huangbo clenched his fist and said, "All the old monks of the world are right here. If I were to let go..."
"A single thread of the Way. It runs seven ways long and eight ways cross from here. [The Master said: "If you do not let it pass, it does not take more than a pinch.

A monk then asked, "What is it like when you let the single thread of the Way pass? The Master said, "Seven ways long and eight ways cross. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when you do not let it pass? The Master said, "Universal."
When a monk asked Yunmen Wenyan, "What is it that is seven times free and eight times unrestrained? Yunmen said, "Think of me; I am old.
