[The student] said, "Body. The Master said, "Earth, water, fire, wind, sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. [The student] said, "These are the five aggregates (*pañcaskandha*).

The Master said, "These are distinct from the five aggregates. A single expanse of clear sky is still a cataract; a thousand waves surging together do not constitute a great tide. When both paths are cast aside, there is no 'sentient being' (*nirmanas*)."
It is said: "In every place, the spring breeze causes the willows and peach blossoms to bloom" (Xueguan Yin).

One day, Chan Master Nirvana of Baizhang in Hongzhou (a successor of Baizhang Hai) addressed the assembly, saying, "When you have finished clearing the fields for me, I shall preach the Great Meaning for you.
When the monks had finished clearing the fields, they requested the Master to preach the Great Meaning.
The Master opened both hands and showed them to him. (According to an examination of the *Quan shu*, the "Liu stele" version is the correct one.
Baizhang Wenduan said: "Baizhang’s exposition of the Great Meaning ended right here. At that time, those who had already undergone a second interview with Mazu [were present]."
"Where has he gone? If you say he still remains, you cannot avoid painting legs on a snake. But tell me, how do you perceive the place where Old Man Baizhang stands? He then said:
"When guests arrive and there is no tea or refreshments, mugwort soup shall serve as the ritual offering.
Wuqiao Zhe said: "Baizhang expounded the Great Meaning; it may truly be said that such was rarely heard in antiquity or today, illuminating the past."
[The previous master] cut off [the lineage]. Daowei, however, was not like that; he simply said, "You have labored hard clearing the fields; please return to the hall to rest.
He caused all the patch-robed monks under heaven to lose their edge and be rendered tongue-tied. Why? A crane with its nine peaks finds it difficult to spread its wings;
a horse without a thousand-li stride vainly pursues the wind. Tiantong Huayan said: "Baoyun wanted to see how Mazu responded to Baizhang’s second visit."
This is truly laughable. One must laugh for thirty years. Furthermore, one must laugh for another thirty years over the question: "How does one know where Baizhang stood?
When guests arrive and there is no tea or refreshments, offering mugwort soup in place of formal hospitality—this too merits thirty years of laughter.
Three laughs thus amount to ninety years. Is this because you find Baiyun’s critique to be incorrect, or is it...?
There is another principle here that you all must discern. This mountain monk hands over his staff with both hands.
If you have not yet attained this, how many times have you returned home drunk under the bright moon, led out by the sound of pipes and songs before the painted hall?
"Spreading both hands at that moment, he spoke: 'The Great Meaning shall circulate and fill the world.
Do not say, "Entering a wild field, one does not pick," for now everywhere the weeds are rank.

(Muan Zhong) The Great Meaning opened the fields to establish the ancestral foundation; the clear title-deeds were shown for transmission and maintenance. The descendants are unwilling to abandon what their ancestors left behind."
Karma. Begging for alms, year after year, one serves upon the roads and byways.
(Lan’an Xu) When the communal labor to clear the fields is complete, everyone is covered in water and mud. With both hands outstretched, do not ask anyone;
last night at the third watch, the moon fell to the west. (Cian Yuan)

Stale goods from many years past, he seeks to unload; with clever makeup and flowery words, he speaks to all people. But when it comes time to bring them forth and sell them in the open market, the price demanded reaches the heavens—who would dare approach?
(Gao Feng Miao) He clears away the thickets, breaks through the desolate wastes, and shatters literary artifice;
wearing his hat and donning his raincoat, he stands upon the ancient site of practice. The Great Meaning has always been such that nothing can cover it.
[The Master] covered [his head]. "Why trouble yourself to stretch out your hand to deliberate further? (Shijian Le).
Chan Master Congshen of Zhaozhou Guanyin Monastery (a successor of Nanquan Yuan). When he first visited Nanquan, Nanquan asked, "Are you a novice with a master, or a novice without a master?
The Master replied, "A novice with a master. [Nanquan] asked, "Which one is your master?"
The Master approached him personally and said, "It is a severe cold in the middle winter; I trust that you, O Venerable One, are enjoying a myriad blessings.
He then permitted Quanqi to enter his room.
Understanding how one grasps a single blade of wild grass and calls it the sixteen-foot golden body, one realizes that every point is the Way;
the pupil of the eye is the person before you. (Yan Ruru) I ask: what is the master?
Stepping forward with hands clasped to exchange greetings of cold and warmth, one simply knows the North Star and its surrounding constellations.
Gong: "The Yellow River is seen to be thoroughly turbid at its source.
(Bao-ye-yuan) One day, Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "What is the Way? Nanquan replied, "Ordinary mind is the Way. Zhaozhou asked, "Can one still direct oneself toward it?
Nanquan said, "To intend to direct oneself toward it is already to deviate. Zhaozhou asked, "If one does not intend it, how can one know it?"
"This is the Way. Quan said, "The Way does not belong to knowing, nor does it belong to not-knowing. Knowing is deluded cognition; not-knowing is indeterminate (avyākṛta).
If one truly penetrates the Way that is free from doubt, it is like the great void—vast, open, and expansive.
How could one forcibly impose distinctions of right and wrong? At these words, the Master realized the principle.
Guishan Lingyou said: "It is not so, yet it is also not otherwise. When it is neither so nor otherwise, what then? He held up his whisk and said:
"The whale swallows the ocean until its waters are exhausted, revealing the coral branches. Lingyin Wuzhuo said:
"Under the blue sky and bright sun, what is there to awaken to? Psh! Psh! The dragon pearl is smashed within the azure dragon’s lair."
Jingshan Xiu said: "The ancients have already laid bare their hearts, livers, and five viscera all at once.
A soaring falcon that cleaves the clouds should seize the moment; a weary fish trapped in a shallow pool merely exhausts itself stirring the waves in vain. Duli Mai said:
"To speak in such a manner is truly like throwing bricks and tiles into a bustling marketplace. Only those who actually experience it will understand. Zhaozhou.
Since this has already been struck, it is like obtaining a lamp in the darkness or finding a treasure while poor. Even grinding one's bones to powder would not suffice as recompense;
a single phrase, when clearly realized, transcends billions of worlds.
If you say that the ordinary mind is the Way, you are adding branches to the branches already growing upward.
It is as if one has stripped off the undershirt that clings to the skin; come here and let me place eyebrows upon your eyes!
(Gushan Gui) I urge you not to weary your spirit in vain. To call it "ordinary" is to distance yourself from it further. It is utterly bland and lacks all flavor.
The Flavor. Each time it is raised, it is new.
(Jingshan Daokai) The sun lingers long and the flowers are in full bloom; white clouds and flowing water dwell together in harmony.
On the road to Chang’an, human traces are rare. Nanquan fell to the secondary level. (Cishou Shen)
The profound path is not traversed by penetrating the subtle; when the Way accords with the ordinary, the supreme faculty awakens. At the top of the shadowless tree, the spring colors dawn;
the golden rooster cries upon the branch where nothing sprouts.
(Zu’an Jian) Having realized the ordinary, one reaches one’s native land; yet many people of this age fear falling into the ordinary. Of the youth, there are but ninety days remaining.
Day after day, one gets drunk a hundred times over without end.
(Xue’an Jin) Once, when a monk asked Zhaozhou, “What is the crown-mark of Vairocana? the Master said, “I left home as a youth;
my eyes have never seen double.”
Tiantong Hua said: "Big or small, Zhaozhou’s words are one-sided and withered. If someone were to ask Tiantong, 'What is the crown-mark of Vairocana?
I would simply say: 'The large is large; the small is small. Tiantong Jie said:
"If you look for it within Zhaozhou’s words, you will sit and kill all the monks under heaven. If you look for it within Ying’an’s words, you will run and kill them."
As for the patch-robed monks of the world, I, this mountain monk, am not like that. If someone were to ask me, I would simply say: "A brick with deer-prints.
When a monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is a pure monastery? the Master said, "A girl with horned hair.
[The monk asked,] "Who is inside the monastery? The Master said, "A girl with horned hair is pregnant."
Crossing arms over the chest and cradling the belly to conceal the dragon seed; cutting open the gallbladder and exposing the liver to touch the phoenix embryo.
Do not say this child is easily obtained; you must know he comes from the depths of a grieving heart.
(Fenyang Zhao) The girl with the horned hair-head reveals her true nature; the pure monastery was built for the sake of others. The worldly do not understand those beneath the forest trees.
I fear that without money it will be difficult to buy a crimson skirt.
(Fujian Qin) Who knows the autumn colors of the vast void? The beautiful lady in the painted pavilion spreads her smiling brows.
Regretting her own beauty yet unseen by others, She frequently plays her jade flute in the breeze. (Lishan Ning)
The brush touches the crimson and green with no hesitation; as the hand moves, a landscape painting is instantly formed.
Hung in the hall for all to see, who knows where the true effort lies?
(Liyun Si) Once, a monk asked Zhaozhou: "Before the world existed, this nature already existed. When the world perishes, what becomes of this nature?"
"It is indestructible. "What is this indestructible nature? The Master said, "The four great elements and the five aggregates. [The student] said, "These are still subject to destruction.
What is the indestructible nature? The Master said, "The four great elements and the five aggregates."
Zhaojue Qin said: "A thousand-fathom deep pool is clear to its very bottom.
Regarding Zhaozhou’s response when a monk asked: "If someone from outside the Buddhist fold were to suddenly ask you, Master Zhaozhou, what Dharma you teach, how would you answer?
The Master said: "Salt is expensive; rice is cheap."
Salt is expensive and rice is cheap; all things are manifest. If you wish to deliberate upon them, it is like pulling an arrow from the back of your head.
(Lan’an Xu) Once, a monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is it to leave the household life? The Master said, "Not treading upon high fame, nor seeking gain by any means."
Yun-cang Xian said: When a monk asked this, Zhaozhou replied that it was "extremely ordinary" and that there was "nothing extraordinary.
Although it is thus, there is a thorn in the soft mud; one must take care not to tread upon it.
For those who have left the household life, the three miserable realms are forever severed; their bodies feel no cold and their bellies suffer no hunger.
With a bamboo staff, they strike the waning moon atop the mountain peak; blowing their iron flutes backward, they chant new poems. (Wu Yi arrives.
Once, when a monk was taking his leave, Zhaozhou asked him, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to various quarters to study the Buddha-dharma. The Master then held up his whisk.
He said, "Where there is a Buddha, do not stay; where there is no Buddha, run past quickly. Even if you encounter someone three thousand li away, do not speak of this mistakenly.
[The student] said, "If that is so, then I shall not go. The Master said, "Plucking the willow blossoms. Plucking the willow blossoms."
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell; an iron weight has been eaten through by worms. Where there is no Buddha, run past quickly;
you will bump into the broken stove at Mount Song. When meeting people three thousand miles away, do not speak of this in error."
Two stone men whispering to one another: "If it is so, then I shall not go. These words have already spread throughout the world:
"Plucking the willow flowers, plucking the willow flowers. Oṃ maṇidhāri hūṃ phaṭ. Tiantong Jue said:
"To sink into emptiness or linger in traces, to mishandle the hand or wound the blade—none of these constitute the conduct of a patch-robed monk. You must simply not enter into the paths of others."
In the marketplace, one does not ascend another’s bedchamber; in the center, one does not establish the mysterious;
in the periphery, one does not cling to things. Only then can one hold fast or let go with freedom. After Lingyin Yue finished citing the words of Jingshan, he said:
"The Elder Dahui exerted his full strength, yet he could only reach this point. Do you know where Xiangshan lands? An iron mountain collapses and crushes a silver mountain."
The platter turns the pearl, and the pearl runs upon the platter; the dense mandarin ducks are embroidered idly, yet the golden needle is never shown to others.
Tianning Qi said: "The Great Ancestor Miaoxi sang this before; Tianning, his distant descendant, hums it after. In front of the gate, watercress is planted;
from the watercress grow chopsticks. From the chopsticks, lotus flowers bloom; upon the lotus flowers, knots are formed."
The Papaya. Suddenly the papaya fell to the ground, scattering countless white sesame seeds.
Why? It was simply to enter the beat. Baoshou Xin said: "A brand-new iron caltrop; it penetrates straight through two layers of barriers. To penetrate those two layers of barriers:
at the mountain pass, the moon remains curved as before. Falin Yin, having finished citing the words of Jingshan, said: "Jingshan..."
Old Man Shan has let Zhaozhou down no small amount. Faling does not fear the scrutiny of the various quarters, yet he too is dragged out and searched.
Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; the sparks have entered his trousers. Where there is no Buddha, one must run past in haste; he meets with calamity and carries misfortune.
Do not err in citing this beyond three thousand miles. At the crossroads of the street, evil gathers once more. If it is thus, then—
He departs! He makes Old Lady Wang of the Eastern Village laugh to tears. "Picking the willow flowers, picking the willow flowers. The poisonous snake in the ancient tomb has horns upon its head;
the fierce tiger on the Southern Mountain has a bushy tail. To speak thus is merely to do injustice to Miaoxi. (He lets out a shout and says:
"In vain one takes this unreturned intent / And tells it to those who wish to travel."
Few are those who have severed the three barriers; facing the blade, who can manifest their full majesty? At the place where willow blossoms are plucked, who beholds them?
The wind carries them across the sky, flying like snow. (Fohuiquan) The green mountains are no different [from before];
white jade is without flaw. Vastly flows the water; in confusion, the yellow chrysanthemums. Where there is a Buddha, even a hair’s breadth...
Not established at all. Where there is no Buddha, ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences arise. A traveler who has not yet returned to Chang’an;
seeking the stream, he still plucks the willow blossoms.
(Tiantong Jue) Unable to bear the bitterness of snow and frost, fearing to see the willow flowers fall; having broken through Zhaozhou’s barrier, the pure wind fills the vast expanse.
(Yuanwu Keqin) does not travel the bird-path nor dwell in the marketplace; with eyes blurred by wine, he rubs them and sleeps in broad daylight.
Though it is said that when meeting people he never errs in his responses, plucking the willow blossoms is but the season of spring. (Boshan Liangjie)
At long pavilions and short pavilions, their parting words were endless; unable to restrain their separation, they chanted poems of entwined branches.
(From the *Jianan Lu*) A monk once asked Zhaozhou, "Among the three bodies, which one is the original body? The Master replied, "None is lacking, and none is superfluous."
Yishan Nu said: "When Master Zhaozhou, whether great or small, was pressed by someone with a single squeeze, he was immediately unable to provide an explanation.
If anyone were to ask such a question today, I would simply rise from my seat and stand with my hands folded. I would wait for their eyes to flicker and shift."
He struck him across the spine.
Once, a monk asked Zhaozhou, "I have heard that you personally met Nanquan; is this true?
The Master replied, "In Zhenzhou, they grow large radishes."
Dongta Xi said: "If someone were to ask Dongta, 'I have heard that you, Master, personally saw Longchi—is this true? simply tell them: 'You may ask whatever you wish.

Then, after they have finished their prostrations, let them withdraw. Qinglong Cao said: "Zhaozhou was able to silence the mouth of that single monk, but it would be difficult to silence the mouths of all people in the world."
Tao Qian planted only willows at Pengze; Pan Yue cultivated only flowers at Heyang.
How can these compare to gazing upon the river in the evening, where several peaks of azure green belong to the fishermen’s homes?
(Haiyin Xin) Even the Ancient Buddha of Zhaozhou spoke much; radishes grow in the fields of the provincial capital. Many monks throughout the world gnaw upon them.
Biting through—between the teeth, it slips past Old Nanquan. (Wenshu said: "I have visited Master Nanquan Wang;
the radish of Zhenzhou has no secrets of its own. He picks it up and blocks the mouth of right and wrong;
this "Snowy Melody" and "Spring Tune" is not the *Chuci*. (Jingshan Daoyuan)
"Great radishes grow in Zhenzhou; there is a reason why master and disciple are in accord.
Maitreya is in Guanyin Temple; Zhaozhou is to the west of Dongyuan.
(Gushan Gui) "Green comes from the indigo plant; ice is born from water. Not a step can be taken; ten thousand miles of white clouds. (Huan'an Ti)
A mere pittance of livelihood on the lips; when ignited, it rushes like the wind and whirls like lightning.
Do not vainly say the radish of Zhinzhou is large; when have you ever truly seen Old Nanquan?
(Shi’an Shao) Fuzhou lychees, Qingzhou dates—among all things, nothing surpasses a good source. That which is selected from within the furnace is not [the true one].

Refined gold. Those stored in silk-lined boxes are not the ultimate treasure. Zhaozhou originally intended to settle the conflict of arms, yet he only provoked smoke from the beacon fires to drift aimlessly in the void.
(San Yi Yu) Once, when a scholar asked Zhaozhou, "Is it true that the Buddha does not go against the wishes of sentient beings? the Master said, "Yes. The scholar said, "I..."
Jiawu asked, "May I seek the staff held by the Master? The Master said, "A gentleman does not take away what another cherishes.
Jiawu said, "I am no gentleman. The Master replied, "Neither am I a Buddha."

Yishan Nu said: "Zhaozhou, the ancient Buddha, was free in both bestowing and taking away. Were it not for one of transcendent capacity, one would inevitably run headlong into the thicket of right and wrong.
Haimen Yong said: "Why did Zhaozhou not then offer him [the staff] with both hands?

Had he waited until the other was about to receive it, he would have struck him across the spine. This would not only have brought lifelong joy to the man, but would also have benefited future generations."
Know that we monks have a distinct function:
when the opportunity arises, we act without hesitation. A bright pearl rolls across a lapis lazuli platter;
Old Zhaozhou is a village schoolmaster. A single staff is carried by two men. (Shi’an Shi)

Capturing the drum and seizing the banner was expected of Zhaozhou; yet even in opening new frontiers and expanding territory, his strategy remained deficient. One does not know the location of the acupuncture points until the illness has been long-present;
it is difficult to determine where to apply the moxibustion upon a scar already scorched by fire.
(Supplemented by Songshan) Zhaozhou went to visit Baizhang. Baizhang asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From Nanquan. Baizhang said, "Nanquan recently..."
The Master asked, "What words did Dayu have to show his disciples? The Teacher said, "A person of no affairs need only depart in silence.
[The questioner] said, "Setting aside the phrase 'in silence' for a moment, how would you speak the phrase 'in a state of total blankness'? The Teacher took three steps forward.
The Master (Zhaozhou) gave a shout. The Teacher (Linji) made a gesture of shrinking his body. The Master said, "Excellent, profound stillness.
The Teacher then went out. Langye Huijue said: "The old man Zhaozhou gained his claws and fangs within the lion’s den.
Zhaoguo Qian said: "When masters meet, neither can easily grasp the other; they are utterly still and silent. Advancing or retreating, one cannot squeeze them."
It was completed; the clay figure could not be finished. The great road cannot be traversed by running through the grass. Master Ming of Pingyang said:
"The thief is a petty person, yet his cunning exceeds that of a gentleman. Nevertheless, there is one true thief and there is one grass-thief.
It is within the gate; it is outside the gate. One does not act like Lord Ping who offended the Ox and Dipper constellations.
A lion’s roar versus a jackal’s howl. Plucking out the pupils from the eyes of Li Lou. One hand contracts, one hand extends. Double Ninth is definitely the ninth day of the ninth month.
Turning over the seas and mountains to seek a true friend. Bare bones, the two elbows exposed. (Xiatang Yuan)
A government official once asked Zhaozhou, "Does the Master enter hell? The Master replied, "I shall enter hell at the very end.
The official asked, "Why would a great spiritual teacher enter hell? The Master said, "If I do not enter, who will transform and guide you?"

Fuyan Rong said: "The old fellow Zhaozhou’s hands and feet are not like others; not only does he drag people down when entering the water, but he is also able to seize the banner from their very face.
Nevertheless, he could not avoid being exposed by the pillar."
A single iron hammerhead, protruding without a hole; even Xiantuo with his azure eyes knits his brows.
His house has a path that reaches through the heavens; how could one know it by chasing after scents or seeking out sounds?
(Tianguzhao) Zhaozhou addressed the assembly: "As for the word 'Buddha,' I do not like to hear it."
Huànjué Ān said: "Everyone, you must by all means avoid understanding it in this way. Since you do not understand it in this way, how then do you understand it?
He then offered this verse: "The single word 'Buddha' I do not care to hear; Last year was as it is, and so is this year’s spring. In this year’s spring, the Great [Dharma] descends."
Snow. The black lacquer bowl at the tomb on land turns into a white bowl.
The blue sky holds thin clouds; the evening breeze is cold. Intoxicated, I take up the jade zither and play beneath the moon.
I thought my melody was so lofty that no one would recognize it; who knew I had been deceived by my own fingers? (Luryan Ho)
Zhaozhou’s evening discourse: "Tonight I shall answer questions. Anyone who can ask a question, please come forward.
At that moment, a monk stepped out and bowed. The Master said, "I intended to throw a brick to draw out a jade; instead, I have drawn out a mere brick."
Jue Tieci asked Fayan, "What was the intention of the former master? Fayan said, "It is like the state appointing a general;
when someone is asked who can go, if someone comes forward and says, 'I can go,' you must say, 'You cannot go.
[Fayan] said, 'I understand. Changqing Ling asked Jue Tieci, "As soon as that monk came out and prostrated..."
"Why do you take it to be a brick? Jue said, "Just now, someone over there asked the same thing.
Qing asked, "What did you say to him? Jue replied, "I said the same thing to him. Baoshou Zhao said:
If one shoots at a tiger without hitting it truly, one’s efforts are in vain and the arrow feathers sink into the earth. Baoci then said, "Where does it become a brick?
The masters of the Zen groves say that as soon as it comes out, it becomes a brick. But consider this:
when one goes in and out, walks, stands, sits, or lies down every day, can it all be bricks? Tell me, was this monk who came out possessed of the eye, or not?

Cui Feng Xian said: "A person of keen intelligence, upon hearing this mention, will immediately know where it lands. Even so, though it be thus, to let it pass would be to overlook the iron hammerhead.

Now, the words of a patriarch are never uttered in vain; one who comes forward must surely be a master of the craft. Why, then, does he 'throw a brick to draw out a jade'? Do you wish to recognize Zhaozhou?
No one has recognized his past labors on the battlefield; he simply wishes to reassert his merit that covers the age."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Everyone says that Zhaozhou attained a mechanism that transcends the crowd; his provisional arrangements during his lifetime were indeed free and easy.
Yet this monk wishes to beat the rhythm and knock at the gate, failing to manage his maneuvers even within a flash of lightning.

Zhaojue’s iron hammerhead is able to take what is near as a metaphor so as not to let the ancestral wind fall; Fayen possessed the talent for universal discernment and would have known where it fell."
[The Master] said, "I venture to ask you all: since you are masters of the school, why is it that when you throw a brick, you only draw out a cinder-block?
How many people understand the probing pole and the shadow-grass? It is just like a general’s banner on one side; whether slaying generals or establishing camps, it all depends on me.
Riding an iron horse backward, I ascend Mount Sumeru. (Cishou Shen)
A thousand-year-old field has eight hundred owners. Who can, when the opportunity arises, discern its origin? Zhaozhou wished to provide an answer; he threw a brick to draw out the tiles.
Old Jue spoke of the essential point, like the ceremony of enfeoffing a general. Whether one can go or cannot go is distinguished by black and white beneath a single word.
Here, higher than peaks ten thousand fathoms tall, without moving a single hair, he captures Buddhas and Patriarchs. (Yuanyu Qin)
Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "The Way is not outside of things; that which is outside of things is not the Way. What is the Way that is outside of things? Nanquan struck him.
The Master seized the staff and said, "In the future, do not strike people in error. Nanquan said, "Dragons and snakes are easy to distinguish;
a patch-robed monk is difficult to deceive."
Cui Feng Xian said: "Zhaozhou is like a dragon without horns, or a snake with feet. At that time, he did not care; 'exhausting the law leaves no people.
He must have been beaten with a staff and driven out. Gunan Men said: "Nanquan truly loved his son so much that he did not notice his ugliness.
If he were such a person, why would he wait for others to drive him out? He would have covered his own nose and left on his own."
With supple coils, he conceals his edge as he enters the fray; he captures them all and opens wide their eyes.
A hero who decides life and death in a single stroke, possessing both the talent of a civil official and a military general.
(Baoning’s Valor) To distinguish the true gold, one must recognize it in the fire; the eye upon the staff is as bright as the sun. When rewards and punishments are clear, rites and music follow.
Complete. A master and his son are truly hard to find.

The sweet and sour flavors are natural from the start; with leaves and branches intact, each fruit is round. The people of Jambudvīpa have not yet known it;
the legend of the *āmra* fruit is surely a hollow transmission. (By Baoning Yong) No solitary peak stands alone;
the perilous pass is fundamentally steep. The Old Man of Zhaozhou is as flawless as jade. Pointing directly at the head, he reveals it within the hall.
At the bottom, he sweeps away the vast flowers before the eyes. (Snow Hall’s Verse):
One Buddha within the hall, twice emitting rays of light; intending to repay the high price, there is no doubt in his measure.

He has mistakenly spent three or five hundred iron coins. (Hàn Guān Yù)
When Zhaozhou heard the novice shout "Attendance is dismissed," he said to his attendant, "Tell him to leave.

If you understand it here, you will see Zhaozhou. Falinyin said: "If you understand it here, you betray Zhaozhou. Tianzhi Wei said:
"Under the blue sky and bright sun, a thunderbolt startles the multitude; he carves out the five viscera and the heart-liver to give to others and explain them."
"Adhesive removes the bonds. This is truly regrettable; planting thorns at the very gate causes so many people to be unable to advance or retreat.
Is there anyone who can get out? (He lets out a shout.)
Having entered the gate, one remains outside it. Speaking to the person, they do not understand; so one raises the voice even higher: "My ears are deaf.
(Gushan Gui) The wind whistles through the pines, the rain sighs through the cypresses. A lion bites a man; a hunting dog chases a clod of earth.

The monk said, "From the Buddhas above down to the ants below, all possess Buddha-nature; why then does the dog have none? The Master said:
It is because he still possesses the consciousness of karma. Furthermore, a monk asked, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature?
The Master said, "Yes. The monk asked, "If it has it, why does it enter this skin bag? The Master said, "Knowing it and yet deliberately transgressing."
Cuiyan Zhi said: "To speak of existence and to speak of non-existence—these two colors are but one match.
What about now? Zifu Guan was asked by a monk: "Why does the dog have no Buddha-nature? Guan said: "It bites anyone it encounters to death. The monk asked:
"For what reason, then, do you also say it has Buddha-nature? Guan said: "Upon seeing its master, it wags its tail."
It is said that the *karmic consciousness* remains; who would say its intent is not profound? When the ocean dries up, its bottom is finally seen; when a person dies, their mind is not known.
(Zhenjing Wen) Releasing both existence and non-existence, then gathering them both back in—Master Zhao’s mechanism is peerless in the world. Try ascending to the high point of the sea gate.
Gazing afar, a thousand rivers and ten thousand streams all flow eastward.
(Puyong Ping) The Buddha-nature is clearly manifest, transcending existence and non-existence; why use a gourd to hang vinegar? Thin mists and light smoke cannot remain;
my small boat has already passed Lake Dongting. (Xiatang Yuan)

When Lord Zhang drinks village wine, Lord Li remains drunk and does not wake; facing south, he looks at the Big Dipper. (Shi’an Shao) The dog has no Buddha-nature.
On the road of expectant gazing, one meets Zihu; when the nature of karmic consciousness is present, it suffers a single bite. Great!
Throughout the land there is not a single blue-eyed barbarian; the dog has Buddha-nature. The spring breeze stirs a thousand willow trees;
knowing yet deliberately transgressing—how pitiable! Each one looks south to see the Northern Dipper.
(Wuan Quan) The dog has Buddha-nature; the dog lacks Buddha-nature. A straight hook originally seeks the fish that take the bait; chasing the scent, it searches for...
Incense, clouds, and water travelers; a clamorous and chaotic jumble of distinctions. Levelly displayed, grandly unfurled—do not blame me for failing to be careful at the outset.
Pointing out flaws to return the Zhao jade; the King of Qin did not recognize Lord Lin Xiangru. (Tiantong Jue) The dog has it:
the old woman selling fans covers her hands with them every day. The dog does not have it: planting melons, one first gets to eat the gourd.
Heaven-endowed nature has always been different for each. Lu Tong did not drink Liu Ling’s wine.
(San Yi Yu) Once, when a monk asked Zhaozhou, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature? the Master said, "No."
Zhaozhou’s drawn sword: its cold frost and radiant flames blaze on high. If you intend to ask "How is it? your body shall be split in two.
(Wuzu Yan) With great strength, advanced age, and even bolder courage, the clear wind follows the tiger and the clouds follow the dragon; how many snarling beasts seek out the sound?
Traces: A horned antelope hanging from a branch leaves no track.
(Baofeng Xiang) Zhaozhou’s dog has no Buddha-nature; ten thousand layers of green mountains conceal an ancient mirror.
The barefoot Persian enters the Great Tang; the eight-armed Nalakūvara executes the true command. (Chouyan Yun)
On the day of Yi-ji, the Great Man Qiu appeared; the forest became his enemy. His sharp fangs were like swords and halberds; there was a reason for his taking life or sparing it.
(Nanyan Sheng) He split horse and man with a single stroke; blood surged from the void like billowing waves. Thousands upon thousands of people vied [to see].
Look! Who can understand the parting of the eyelids and the bristling of the hair?
(Zhong’an Kong): The dog has no Buddha-nature; the old oyster spits forth a bright pearl. In Western Sichuan the cuckoo cries; in Jiangnan the partridge calls.
(Wenshu Dao) Zhaozhou’s dog has no Buddha-nature. In the void, he digs out the mirror from the Qin era;
its radiance is so total that not even a speck of a star is seen, yet it shines through clearly above, below, and in all four directions. (Shui’an Yan)
The Great Tamer of Persia drinks a hundred cups; pausing, he grips the tiller as the leader of ten thousand men. With the wind against him, he passes through the Yellow Ox Gorge;
he takes no account of the Qutang and Yanʼyu rapids. (Dongshan Kong: "A dog has no Buddha-nature.
When the planet Rāhu enters one's destiny, it is not that one kills people; rather, one is surely killed by others.
(Nan Shuji): Twenty-four states of iron are cast into a single hammer, which is flung onto the main street;
no one can step upon it. (Lang’an Ran)
The single word "non-existence" has killed countless people; how many heroes have their corpses strewn across the road!
(Iron Mountain Ren) A beautiful maiden of sixteen delays her embroidery; beneath the purple *zhijing* flowers, the yellow oriole warbles.
How pitiable are these boundless sentiments of spring’s end—all contained within that moment of silence when she sets down her needle. (Ottang Ren)

Zhaozhou said, "The dog has no Buddha-nature. The fullness of spring’s colors spreads across rivers and lakes; How many are there who pluck leaves and seek branches, Needlessly leaving the flowers of Luoyang strewn along the road?
(Gao Feng Miao) A single glance at the long river reveals a vast expanse of cold mist;
In the midst of the current, my four quarters are utterly bewildered. What a pity that the bright moon is already deep into the night.
Down below, no one asks for a ferry at the riverhead.
(Han-shan Qing) Every household has a piece of cloth to cover their shame; once cast aside, it can serve as rain and dew.
I alone find it strange that in his day, Old Zhaozhou Threw away his cap and put on his trousers. (Shi-yu Fang)
From what place does the autumn wind arise? Whistling, it sends forth the flocks of geese. Coming this morning into the courtyard trees, The solitary traveler hears it first.
(By Zhuone) The back of Stone Beam Bridge is as slippery as moss; A single stream of the Milky Way rushes straight down. Shoes of travelers from ancient times have trodden it, yet not...
Tired. How many people have gathered the falling blossoms of the waterfall? (Qing of Jingtang) Zhaozhou ascended the hall and said:
"The golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; the wooden Buddha does not pass through fire; the clay Buddha does not pass through water."
"The True Buddha sits within the house. Jingshan Daokai said:
"Venerable Zhaozhou has emptied his heart and soul; he has finished reporting this matter.
Is there anyone here who knows how to acknowledge this kindness and repay it? Yangshan Qian said: "He reveals the true body of the Tathāgata and elucidates the direction [of the Way]."
Regarding the ultimate principle: Zhaozhou was indeed a masterful hand; however, he was not right to needlessly create complications. My own view is otherwise:
the golden Buddha passes through the furnace, the wooden Buddha passes through the fire, and the clay Buddha passes through the water; as for the true Buddha, it is silent.

Be careful not to fall into words. Suddenly, if someone were to come forward and say, "Saying it this way is precisely forcing a fabrication," [the Master] would strike his knee once and say, "I thought there was no one to witness this."
A clay Buddha does not cross water; divine light illuminates heaven and earth. If one stands in the snow without ceasing, who would not polish away their falsehoods?
(Cui-feng Xian III) A golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace;
when people come to visit Zi-hu, there are several characters upon his signboard—where is the pure breeze not present?
The wooden Buddha does not pass through fire; I often think of the one who broke the hearth. When the staff suddenly struck him, I finally realized I had betrayed myself.
The wooden Buddha does not pass through fire; before the Terrace of Ambrosia I met Bodhidharma. Alas, the people of Luoyang have yet to arrive;
for nine years he sat in vain and coldly facing the wall. (Sengsheng Changsan)

The golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; sitting here, I sigh for those weary lives rushing along the roads. Had one not looked at the painting on the Huashan wall, how could one have known of Fan Lang riding his donkey backward?
The clay Buddha does not cross the water; a single ray of numinous light illuminates heaven and earth. How admirable is the old, ancient peg of Xuansha!
He did not want the South Mountain, he wanted the turtle-nosed snake.
The forms of the three Buddhas are all unreal; the pupils in their eyes are the people before one’s own face.
If you can believe in the treasure within your own house, the warbling birds and mountain flowers are the same springtime.
(Yayufuan) The clay Buddha does not cross the water; when the Vairambha wind suddenly rises, the great earth is pitch black and vast—how would a patch-robed monk dare to look?
(Third Verse by Gao Feng Miao) A golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; An iron-wrapped night-bright pearl— With one blow, both are ground to powder. Where is its pure radiance not present?
The wooden Buddha does not fear the fire; he pulls open the locks of the golden hall. Within and without, all obstructions are severed; yet people of this age still remain bashful and hesitant.
Zhaozhou was once asked by a nun, "What is the meaning of the most profound mystery? The Master pinched her with his hand.
The nun said, "The Master still has this. The Master replied, "Rather, it is you who have this."
Falin’s Record of Sounds says: At that time, he waited for him to say, "The Master still has this remaining. Why did he not simply stop right then?
He allowed him to harbor doubt for thirty years.
Dense, deep, and profound—the meaning is most far-reaching. How many people have mistakenly deliberated over it in their cold indifference?
If a nun can understand Zhaozhou’s meaning, even an iron heart would break with grief.
(Cishou Shen) A hard-headed fellow wrapped in cotton-wool; the elegant old Zhaozhou of Hebei. Salt where it is salty, salt added where it is bland.
Water. A laugh breaks out from the carriage eaves and never ceases.
(Zhengtang Bian) A fierce tiger hides deep within the shallow grass thicket; how many times has the bright moon entered the misty vines?
Even if one possesses the Vajra-eye upon the crown of the head, one cannot avoid stumbling past him right before one’s own eyes. (Gao Feng Miao)
A monk once asked Zhaozhou, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The one outside the wall. The monk said, "I am not asking about that Way.
The Master said, "Which Way? The monk said, "The Great Way. The Master said, "The Great Way penetrates Chang'an."
Wushi said, "As for the Way, Shixi was not like this. When someone asked him, 'What is the Way?
he simply replied, 'Yesterday someone came from Sian; today he is going out to Guangde. Now tell me, is this the same as Zhaozhou’s [response], or is it different?
After a long silence, he said, 'Look under your feet. Tianqin Rui said, "This monk only knew how to ask for directions; he did not know [the Way]."
He missed it right before his eyes. Zhaozhou was greedy for ferry-crossing tolls; who could have foreseen that he would lose the fare?
Daci Xun said: "If someone were to ask me today, 'What is the Way? I would simply say, 'From Fuchun to Tianmu is one hundred and twenty li.
Now tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different? He then let out a long sigh.
The house style of Old Zhao does not deceive; when asked about the Great Way, he points to Chang’an. Who can return home with level steps?
Most labor in vain, creating difficulties for themselves. (Shui’an I) The Great Way penetrates to Chang’an;
his words are upright and his speech is likewise upright. When the year ends and the snow melts away, spring comes and it is as cold as before.

The Master said, "What did you say? When the monk asked again, the Master said, "Vipaśyin Buddha has long since set his mind upon it."
"Up until now, he has not attained the subtle.

as soon as he heard him ask, 'Why do you not appear? he struck him immediately, causing him to reflect deeply upon his pain. He managed—

Zhaozhou ascended the hall and said: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes picking and choosing. As soon as there is speech, there is picking and choosing;
there is clarity. I, this old monk, do not abide within clarity. Do you still harbor any attachment or protection?
At that time, a monk asked, "If you do not abide within clarity, what is it that you protect? The Master replied, "I do not know either."
[The monk] said, "If the Master does not know, why are you not in the state of clarity? The Master said, "It is fine to ask such questions, but after bowing, withdraw."
Cui Feng Xian said, "Zhaozhou retreated three thousand li. Tiantong Jue said, "This monk was indeed 'cut and smoothed' (refined), yet he could not perceive the opportunity and adapt.
Zhaozhou was also 'chiseled and polished,' yet he nearly failed to resolve the matter through mutual engagement.
Among the assembly, people merely say that he had reason to withdraw; little do they realize that [Zhaozhou] was exerting his full strength to sustain the Dharma. Do you understand?"
"Have you all understood? A scorched brick strikes one who is frozen to the very marrow. Tiantong Wu said:
"Master Zhaozhou was quite like someone pushing away evil while distancing himself from it. Why did he not provide the fodder that is his due? Gunan Men said:

"Zhaozhou valued what is fundamental, yet he did not realize he had instead turned it into something extraneous. Nevertheless, without the strength of the Five Dings, the road of the Silkworm Clan cannot be traversed."
"Open up! You people, you must ask whether he is very protective or not protective, and you must also receive the 'Gunan' staff.
I now guarantee this matter for you; it shall never be in vain."
The Ultimate Way is not difficult: speak with integrity and act with integrity. One may have many aspects, yet two are never of two kinds.
The sun rises at the edge of heaven; the moon descends before the railing. The mountains are deep and the waters cold. When the consciousness of the skull is exhausted, what joy can stand?
When the dragon roars from the withered wood, the moisture has not yet dried. Difficult, difficult! Discernment and clarity—you must see for yourself. (Cui Feng Xian)
Most simple and most easy; identical to heaven and identical to earth. When the discernment is clear and plain, why harbor such protection and attachment?

"The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes picking and choosing. Is this the nest of common people?"

he too deserves twenty blows. These blows must have their due recipient; if you cannot discern this, let this story circulate widely for now. He then offered a verse: The old monk’s answer was like a stone wall; Five years passed before he could speak.

The Master said, “Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored. The monk said, “This is still discrimination.
The Master said, “You slave! Where is the discrimination here? The monk was speechless.

it is simply that one must loathe discrimination. If you understand it in such a way, even after ten thousand years you will not have glimpsed it in a dream."
As deep as the ocean, as firm as a mountain. A mosquito or a gadfly playing with a fierce wind in the void;
an ant trying to shake an iron pillar in the heart of the waves. To pick and choose—this is like a drumhead spread before the window.
(Cui Feng Xian) The round autumn moon stamps its seal upon the heart of heaven; before every object there is a wheel. The toad that has entered its hole has no way out.
On the road, one accuses the Way of being uneven.
(Baiyun Yuan) A single pulse passes through Chang’an right before the gate; the traveler vainly laments the hardships of the journey. This is not to boast of cleverness before others;
with a golden hammer, he shatters ten thousand layers of barriers. (Wuan Quan)
People are as stubborn as iron; the laws of the state are like a furnace. When the grain is ripe and brought to the threshing floor, they do not pay their taxes.
There are worms in the rice; there is bran in the wheat. You tenant farmers! The Supreme Way is without difficulty—if you understand this, it is not difficult at all.

Water cannot wet him; wind cannot penetrate him. With the gait of a tiger and the stride of a dragon, ghosts cry out and spirits weep.
With a head three feet long, who could this be? Facing one another, they remain silent as he stands alone on his single foot.

Yet alas, people of this age fail to see them. (Foyan Yuan)

The Master looked at him and said, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Go ask Yunju.

Gutang said: "At that time, had I been asked, 'Who is it that brushes away the dust? I would have immediately snatched the broom and given him a thorough beating.

Cui峰 Xian said, "All you Zen adepts, is there anyone who recognizes Zhaozhou? Come forth and let us deliberate together."
If you have not yet been able to discern this clearly, it is best to start from the beginning so that I may break it open for you: four times nine is thirty-six. *Shou*. Gu Nanmen said:

I return to you Zhaozhou’s "Have you finished eating your gruel yet? Having set aside that monk’s "I have finished eating my gruel," Cui峰 (Cui Feng) [responds].

Tell me, has he ever given any indication? Black beans have always been good for making sauce; a bhikṣuṇī is certainly a shigu (nun).
Old fellow Dahui has teeth like a forest of swords and a mouth like a blood-basin; it turns out he was all along right here—washing the bowl.
How could such talk ever have been fully articulated? Today, Longan does not begrudge his lips and teeth; he speaks it through clearly and directly:
Having eaten the congee, one washes the bowl. "Zhaozhou hangs a gourd on the eastern wall.

Probing the principles of things, she has established her household; Gathering the opportune moments, she immediately recognizes the Mind. Thank you, O Spring Wind, for your impartiality;

Yet among those who received the prophecy on Vulture Peak, none had ever experienced such a sequence as this. (Zhengjue Yi)
The young gentleman in brocade sits amidst a cluster of flowers; the melodies of phoenix pipes and crane flutes have not yet ended.
Yet one laughs at the peach tree for its greed to bear fruit—how many times has it been wronged by the wind of the fifth watch?

they do not realize that the mud beneath their feet is deep. Were it not for Old Man Zhaozhou, who could have manifested such great merit from his labors?

Do you understand? When the clouds have gathered and the rain has cleared, the vast sky is wide open; a pair of mandarin ducks cannot be captured in a painting.

a solitary cloud, a wild crane. A-he-he! (Yun’gai Zhi) Zhaozhou addressed the assembly:

This is still not yet ten-fold perfection or complete stability. O Great Assembly, do you recognize the Eye of Heaven and Earth? From the beginning, it has never borrowed the power of the three luminaries;
it shines through mountains and rivers with the brilliance of ten thousand bushels of gold.
One day, Zhaozhou struck a fire-pot and asked a monk, "I call this fire; what do you call it? The monk was speechless.
The Master said, "Failing to recognize the profound principle, one's efforts at meditative stillness are but toil in vain."
Fadeng Qian said, "I am not your equal.
Zhaozhou’s eyes emit light that pierces through the four quarters of the world; placing a handle upon a bowl remains a topic of conversation to this day.
(Old Monk Zheng):
Directly beneath, right and wrong cannot be grasped. At that place where they cannot be grasped, one should take it up with confidence. Last night the wooden man delivered a message:
The Persian from the South Sea has passed through the Great Tang. (Wayan Xuan)
Once, two monks vied with one another, each refusing to accept the position of the first seat. The administrator informed the Master, who said, "Let both be the second seats.
The administrator asked, "Who then shall serve as the first seat? The Master said, "Bring some incense.
When the administrator replied, "The incense is ready," the Master said, "The fragrance of the precepts, the fragrance of concentration, the fragrance of wisdom, and the fragrance of liberation."
Tiantong Hua said: "Zhaozhou’s single blow was indeed enough to startle the multitude and stir the assembly.
Yet, when scrutinized, it is merely washing clods of earth in the mud. If one were under the gate of Jianfu, there would be no need for such mutual deference;
there is someone for the first seat, someone for the second seat, and someone for the third seat. Nevertheless, even so, one cannot avoid following [the path]."

The headnote refutes this. The first seat cannot be pierced even by one with iron eyes and copper pupils; the second seat is like the "spring breeze and white snow," for which no one can join in the song;
the third seat is the true body and mind, identical to Bodhidharma. But tell me: is it the same as Zhaozhou, or is it different?
Yuan'an Meng said: "Zhaozhou established this seat; originally, he placed [the student] upon the rank of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, causing Heaven..."
In the monasteries below, no one dared to sit in the seat of authority; from this point on, the rules and regulations fell into decline, and even until today they have not been restored.
Is there anyone who will rectify the discipline for the sake of the Dharma community? Do not hesitate to decline; please come forward and meet me.

After receiving the offering, the Master descended from his meditation seat, circumambulated it once, and said, "Tell the old woman that the turning of the *Tripitaka* is finished.
When the messenger returned and reported this to the woman, she said, "I came to request the turning of the complete canon; why have you only turned half of it?"
Baoci then said: "Where is it that there is a deficiency of half a *piṭaka*? Tell me, with what kind of eye did Nanapo speak in such a manner?
Jingshan Daowu said: "Among the assembly, they deliberate, saying: 'What is that half-*piṭaka*?'"
Some say he circumambulated once more; some say he snapped his fingers; some say he cleared his throat; some say he let out a shout; some say he clapped his hands.

Even if all the elder monks in the world were likewise to circumambulate it a hundred thousand million times, the same would hold true.
Regarding the old woman’s share, she can only obtain half of the *piṭaka*.

Even if the mountains, rivers, the great earth, and the myriad phenomena of the forest—including every blade of grass and tree—were each to possess the mark of the broad and long tongue, speaking with one voice in different mouths from this day until the end of the future, regarding the old woman’s share, they would still only obtain half of the *piṭaka*. Do you all wish to recognize the old woman?
"Behold the embroidered mandarin ducks; she does not hand the golden needle to others. Tianning Qi said:
"This old woman says that Zhaozhou only managed to turn over half of the Tripitaka, playing with the false while taking it for the true.
