The spiritual mechanism of a thousand *li* is not easily encountered. When a dragon gives birth to a dragon’s offspring, do not be complacent.
Zhao’s family seized the "Jade of Ten Thousand Cities," while the Lord of Qin and Liangxiu both lost their lives.

(Cui Feng Xian) Among the myriad trees, some wither and die according to the seasons; yet the cypress in Zhaozhou’s courtyard flourishes forever. Not only does it withstand the frost, it maintains its integrity.
Its joints; how often it produces pure tones facing the bright moon.
(Huanglong Nan) In the deep courtyard, its coiled roots possess a profound green hue. The old monk has long pointed this out to those in the lineage of Chan.
Year after year, its frost-defying integrity remains unchanged. When will the carrying down of its pure breeze ever cease? (Zhengjue Yi)
The courtyard cypress of Zhaozhou is a bitter ordeal for the patched-robed monk; like a well-sweep at the mouth of a well, it cannot be swallowed whole.
(Yexuan Zun) The courtyard cypress of Zhaozhou stands tall and dense; dewdrops and the clarity of the wind add to its verdant hue.
One cannot seek it by plucking leaves or tracing branches; its coiled roots endure through ten thousand ages, ultimately without end. (Damingxiu)
The cypress trees beneath Zhaozhou’s courtyard stand in dense rows; plucking leaves and tracing branches has continued from antiquity to the present.
If a monk with clear eyes were to look upon them, the meaning of the Patriarch who came from the West would surely sink into oblivion.
(By Yang Wuweī) A single hare lies across the ancient road; as soon as the blue hawk sees it, he seizes it. The hunting dogs that followed lacked the necessary skill.
Nature. Seeking emptiness at the old site of the withered stump.
(Chengtian Zong) Su Wu did not bow; Han Xin faced the court. If you understand it thus, ten thousand miles of distance.
(Mannan Cheng) Zhaozhou’s courtyard cypress—speaking to the Chan guests. A black-lacquered screen; pine and ivy brighten the window-frames. (Furi Cai)
A hundred treasures of light cluster at the invisible crown of the head; this great divine mantra is most wondrous and miraculous: *gate pārasaṃgate*.
A stone man loses his black hen at midnight. (Zhengtang Bian):

His brows are like snow across the riverbank; his eyes contain the autumn of the Yellow River; his mouth is like the surging waves of the sea; his tongue is a vessel that rides the current. These are the hands that dispel chaos.
The strategy for Great Peace: Old Zhaozhou, Old Zhaozhou. The bustling monastic forests have not yet ceased their clamor;
it is merely a waste of effort. The carriage is built to fit the ruts; fundamentally, there are no clever skills involved.
Filling the valleys and leveling the ditches—(Hongzhi Jue)—the cypress tree in front of the courtyard is a fine great coffin. Someone buys it, yet no one carries it away.
(The Parable of the Han Pass) Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Where have you set out from? The monk replied, "Xuefeng. The Master said, "What words did Xuefeng use to instruct people?
The monk said, "He usually says, 'The entire world of the ten directions is a single eye of the śramaṇa. You all..."
"Where are all these people going to defecate? The Master said, "If you, O Ācārya, return, take a spade with you.
Baofu Zhan said, "To the south there is Xuefeng; to the north there is Zhaozhou.
Cui峰 Xian said, "Since this monk did not come from Xuefeng, it is a pity for Zhaozhou’s spade. Langya Jue said, "Among the assembly, some have said:"
"I am sending a spade to bury Xuefeng. If you say, "I am sending a bowl," then he would say, "To hold porridge and rice.
Do you still see this in a dream through such deluded interpretations? It is not the hand of Monk You; it is merely a vain attempt at painting in colors. Qinghua Yan said:
"If it were this mountain monk, seeing that the Dharma brother was returning, he would have sent a spade with him.
When asked why he did not take it, he would simply say: 'The Master cannot do without it here.
Falin Yin said: "This monk came directly from Xuefeng; for what reason did Cuipeng say he did not come from Xuefeng?"
If you can speak this way, you will not have disgraced Zhaozhou’s spade.
Yet, looking south toward Xuefeng, it is still ten thousand li away; traveling north, you have not yet stepped through Zhaozhou’s Barrier. You have deceived him with that single blunt spade;
for over two hundred years, it has gone and has not returned. (Zhengjue Yi)
The path across the stone bridge is as slippery as moss; the winds on the Min Ridge are so high that the frost does not melt.
Everyone we meet speaks only of their travels—how many among them have ever reached Xuefeng?
(Fohuiquan) Where does one defecate at Xuefeng? Zhaozhou sent a spade. A śramaṇa’s single eye is left in such a state of disorder.
A-he-he! The drum rolls in the land of Great Tang; in the land of Silla, the dance sways.
(Biefeng Yin) A single eye across the great earth—who would dare to defecate within it? An axe was sent away, who knew it would reach Xuefeng?
(Hengchuan Gong): Looking up, one stirs up dust; holding a torch against the wind, one harms no other, yet brings ruin upon oneself.
I yield this to the man at Zhuxuan who sleeps high on his pillow, watching the white clouds age as frost burns the trees. (Shiyu Fang)
The spring colors of the Five Tombs are ten times more lush; The east wind vexes all, blowing without end. A drunkard calls out to the traveler on the riverbank who will not return;
The cry of the cuckoo ceases at the tips of the green willow branches.
(By Tian Duo'en) Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Have you ever read the Lotus Sūtra? The monk replied, "I have. The Master said, "The patched robe hangs in the void."
"Idly, they falsely name themselves 'aranyas' (forest-dwellers) to deceive and delude the people of the world. How do you understand this?
A monk prepared to prostrate himself, and the Master said, "Have you come wearing your patched robe? The monk replied, "I have come wearing it. The Master said, "Do not delude me.
The monk asked, "How can one avoid being deluded? The Master said, "Do not take my words as authoritative."
Cui峰 Xian said: "Big and small Zhaozhou, you have the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake. If you can discern this, you will see through Zhaozhou;
if you cannot, each of you will simply wrap yourselves tightly in your patched robes—do not delude yourselves, Cuipeak!"
Gounan said: "As for Zhaozhou asking in such a manner and this monk answering in such a manner—does this mean the monk is confusing Zhaozhou, or is Zhaozhou confusing the monk?"
A monk once asked Zhaozhou, "What is it like when the black bean has not yet sprouted? The Master said, "It is good for making sauce.
Zhaozhou’s livelihood is so capable that he is always busy; the whole black bean enters the sauce vat.
Today, there are those who come to sift and grind it, making a resonant *dang-dang* sound within a broken sand pot. (Wanfeng Wei)
Zhaozhou asked the head monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come to deliver a birth. The Master said, "Why did the crows fly away? The monk said, "They were afraid of me.
The Master said, "After ten years as an administrator, how can you speak such words? The head monk then asked, "Why did they fly away?
The Master said, "The head monk has no murderous intent."
Killing mind, killing mind. The moon falls into the cold pond; the autumn waters are deep. One must haul up the golden tortoise and swallow the hook.
How pitiful—few know the truth face-to-face.
(Lüyu Jiao) While Zhaozhou was strolling in a garden with an official, a rabbit saw them and bolted in alarm. The official asked, "The Master is a great virtuous one."
Knowledge. When the rabbit saw him, why did it run away? The Master said, "This old monk loves to kill.
With the poisonous and fierce hearts of yakṣas and rākṣasas, Flower Peak is as steep as a cliff and the sea is as deep as an abyss.
Having already displayed the edge of his sword before people, he hesitates once more at the Black Cloud Peak. (Lüyu Jiao)
Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "What is it to walk among those of different species? Nanquan patted the ground with his hand and brayed like a donkey.
Zhaozhou then gave him a kick and returned to the hall, saying, "Regret, regret! Nanquan sent an attendant to ask, "Regret for what?"
The Master said, "I regret not having given him another two kicks.
Tianjing Xin said, "Nanquan was short of one move by Zhaozhou; Zhaozhou lost one turn of the mechanism to Nanquan. How do you understand this?
'A thousand-year-old scrap of paper is good for compounding medicine.'"
His merit eclipsed the Three Kingdoms; his fame was established in the Eight Array Diagrams. The river flows on, yet the stones do not turn—his lingering regret was the failure to swallow Wu.
(Qie Shunuo) Emperor Han Gao toiled in the affairs of war;
his imperial enterprise flourished as many heroes rose. Yet he still lamented that the four quarters lacked stalwarts.
The Scholar returns to his hometown and sings the "Song of the Great Wind" with sorrow.
(Jueyuan Yin). *Zongjian Fali*, Volume Seventeen;
*Zongjian Fali*, Volume Eighteen.

In the *Jiyun-tang*, compiled by the fourth generation under Dajian [Huineng], it is recorded that Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "Does it accord with the bright side, or does it accord with the dark side? Nanquan then descended from his seat and returned to the abbot's quarters. The Master [said]:
The Master said, "This old fellow was rendered speechless by my single question. The Head Seat said, "Do not say it was because the Abbot had nothing to say;
rather, it is simply that you, Senior Seat, do not understand. The Master then struck him with his palm, saying, "This blow should have been taken by the old Abbot himself."
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said: "The real thief has fled; the officer searching for stolen goods receives a beating. He also said:

"If Nanquan had not acted decisively when it was time to decide, he would have instead invited chaos. Yunju Shun asked: "How do you all understand this? Some immediately say, "The Head Seat fell into his trap.
But if you understand it in that way, how can it be right? I, this mountain monk, say: Zhaozhou was very much like a bystander.
If there were no one present, the great matter would already be as clear as the bright sun; yet it must be made ten times more perfectly complete.
The head seat in the hall is as black as lacquer—on a cold day, for whose sake does he take this "dark blow"? (Baoning Yong)
Zhaozhou went out and encountered an old woman on the road. He asked her, "Where are you going? The woman said, "I am going to steal Zhaozhou’s bamboo shoots.
The Master said, "What would you do if you suddenly encountered Zhaozhou? The woman gave him a slap. The Master then desisted.
Cui-feng Xian said: "A fine slap! Would there not be another two slaps even further beyond the point of examination?
Wuzu Yan said: "Zhaozhou has already ceased; how shall one deliberate upon this? Baiyun reveals a message so that all people may know it together."
Although the old woman exercised her rightful authority, she did not resolve the matter in her lifetime. Zhaozhou was struck twice; he clenched his teeth with determination.
The old woman’s path departed as light as a leaf; Zhaozhou’s lofty reputation remains as heavy as a mountain for a thousand ages. Nantang Yu said:
"I thought the barbarian’s beard was red, yet there is another red-bearded barbarian. Longchi Chuan said: "Zhaozhou..."
"Rest! Is this an affirmation or a negation? Gunanmen said: "Today Zhaozhou has gone out a little and encountered something great.
Yuanzhao Sen said: "Do you recognize Zhaozhou? Clouds drift in threads; the wind blows gently.
I tell you, traveler, do not go up the mountain peak. Oufeng Cheng said: "The thief is a petty person, yet his cunning surpasses that of the gentleman."
Drawing the bow to shoot straight ahead, its momentum is difficult to withstand. The principle of the "tiger-trapping" mechanism is most profound.
Though one may covet another's single grain of rice, who would have known they would lose half a year’s worth of provisions?
(Haiyin Xin) Those who reach the tiger’s den or the demon’s palace are rare. When the old woman stumbles, people harbor doubts. No one knows that Zhaozhou received a slap of the palm.
Meeting. Even until now, it has become a source of contention. (Yū Dàpó) Departing is as heavy as a mountain;
arriving is as light as a single feather. There is no separate path for going and coming; under the overturned canopy, we meet anew at white hair.

(Hexiang Yuan): Along the way, valiant troops invade the frontier river; smoke and dust block the roads, cutting off all passage for men. To stabilize the realm, we rely on the presence of Zhang Liang;
from atop the city walls, the painted horns sound the Chu songs. (Xuedou Zong)
Spurring on his horse with a lash, he ascends the wine tower; how does this compare to sitting on the ground and watching Yangzhou?
Right and wrong, long and short—all have been settled. A rat’s theft can never equal a dog’s pilfering.

(Wuzhun Shanfu) Why is it that when facing the field of practice, one lacks the skill of a master? It is simply because there is another way of life. To yield to others is not the mark of a foolish man.
The woman: "The most venomous tiger has no teeth or fangs. (Jiukuida) Whips and maces brandished together, their strength resists the extraordinary;
Stars fly and lightning rolls, their likenesses difficult to match. His name shall be depicted on the Qilin Hall, yet his family mountain remains as it was;
Fragrant grasses shroud the mist as birds cry out in disarray. (Yuzhi Long)
Zhaozhou addressed the assembly: "Reading the sutras is within birth and death; not reading the sutras is also within birth and death.
How, then, do you all manage to escape? A monk then asked, "What about when neither is retained?
The Master said, "If it is real, then one may. If it is not real, how can one possibly escape birth and death?"
Studying the sutras is still within birth and death; sitting inside a grain basket, there is nothing to eat. Not studying the sutras is also within birth and death;
amidst a heap of brocade robes, there is nowhere to wear them. Suddenly, a crow or a magpie lets out a single cry; turning the body, one leaps up, and the whole family rejoices.
Do not hesitate! Now it is cast before the assembly: even the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot lift it.
(□□□) Once, a lay practitioner asked Zhaozhou, "Venerable Sir, you are advanced in years; how many teeth do you have? The Master replied, "I have only one.
The practitioner said, "If you have only one, how can you eat? The Master said, "Although there is only one, it goes down with every bite."
"Chewing upon it.

Or, as Master An said: "Zhaozhou opens his mouth, and naturally, everyone below chews upon it. This supreme achievement eclipses the Buddhas and Patriarchs, while its Way-shade protects humans and devas.
I, this mountain recluse, shall once again speak a verse to glorify this great event.

The Great Function is fully manifested as the ancient Buddha’s fang-tooth; it illuminates heaven and mirrors earth, with nothing else. Riding upon inspiration by the sun’s side, one establishes meritorious deeds;
its literary brilliance and natural flow belong to the true lineage.
A monk once asked Zhaozhou, "What is it like when one is clear and pure, free from a single speck of defilement?

The Master said, "That is still just a hired laborer for someone else. Mianjie said, "This monk set up a point of inquiry that was truly steep and perilous; yet, alas, Zhaozhou had a way to lift him up."
"A technique that reaches the very vitals. Although it is so, everything still falls into the hands of Tiandong. After all, how is it?
[He] lets out a shout.
Zhaozhou said, "For twenty years, this old monk has not mixed his mind with anything; only the morning and evening meals have been mixed."
Regarding the place where the mind is applied:
Having passed through the Jade Pass, the army has long since returned; yet he still beats the drums before others.
He merely says the horse walks upon fragrant grass, unaware that his own body is already trapped within a heavy siege. (Wuwen Can)
Zhaozhou asked a newly arrived monk, "Have you ever been here before? The monk replied, "I have. The Master said, "Go and drink tea.
He asked another monk, and the monk replied, "I have not been here before. The Master said, "Go and drink tea.

Later, the courtyard steward asked, "Why do you tell those who have been here to go and drink tea, and those who have not been here to go and drink tea as well? The Master called out, "Steward! The steward responded. The Master said, "Go and drink tea."
He assented. The Master said, "Go drink tea.
Baofu Zhan said, "Zhaozhou was accustomed to taking advantage of the situation. Kaifeng Ning said, "Under Zhaozhou’s gate, no distinction is made between high and low;
a single bowl of coarse tea is offered universally. Only those who have tasted it know that it is within the cold ashes."
The Ninth Transformation: Perfume Penetrating the Vase. If you have not yet discerned the beginning and end of this matter, I cannot help but provide another annotation.
Myriad thousands upon thousands in the north, south, east, and west—did Zhaozhou’s reception of guests come for nothing? Do not disdain its plainness and lack of flavor;
he was simply accustomed to roasting all sesame seeds at once. (He strikes the meditation seat once with his whisk.)
"Once arrived, it is the same as not yet having arrived; Zhaozhou thus maintains his family tradition. Lately, the royal decree has tightened its defenses;
from now on, no human sentiments shall be tolerated.
(Foyin Yuan) The dragon-spring sword in its precious casket emits a night-light; it hangs silently and long in the empty hall. If noble guests from the four quarters should come...
I visit you; after the tea is finished, let us cease our talk of long and short. (Daopei Xiu):
The pearl of the black dragon is flawless, the jade is without blemish; carried by horse and donkey to the house of the Imperial Son.
Having been there, one need not hesitate—let us together share this single bowl of tea. (Luohan Nan)
The old man of Zhaozhou has a warm heart; with a single cup of coarse tea, he tests those who walk the path.
Turning his head, he sees where the bridge by the roadside has broken—the white artemisia and red smartweed reflect the slanting sun.
(Zhe’ung Yan) “Drink tea and go. The night rain hastens the crimson onto the flower pistils; swarms of wild bees fly in pursuit of their shadows. Who knows how many...
Knowing where to return, he goes to drink tea; a thousand-year-old withered tree suddenly blooms. The *subing* bird still cries out until its throat bleeds at midnight.
On the eastern wind, the golden saddle is far away on the winding road.

(Bao Puliàn) I have heard of the hand of Ren Gong, skilled at fishing; how can it compare to a single hook in the moonlight over the Western River? Time and again, fish and dragons swallow it, yet cannot hold it.
Attained. A single note from a Qiang flute emerges from the Cloud Tower; let it wander at ease. Gathering up the fishing line, one attains freedom.
*Du!* (Da Ding Xin).
Once, when a monk asked Zhaozhou, "All phenomena return to One; where does that One return? the Master said, "I am in Qingzhou."
He made a cotton robe for his neck that weighed seven *jin*.
Zhaojue Qin said: "The three eyes of Maheśvara are clearly illuminated in a single phrase; like the rivers flowing to the sea, a thousand paths share the same track."
Although it is thus, there is yet one more point. Suppose someone were to ask, "Where does 'all returns to one' go?
You should simply say, "When hungry, eat; when tired, sleep. Yuansou Duan said, "Zhaozhou’s words are fine, but they nonetheless fail to meet the challenge of the situation.
Zhongfeng, however, was not like this: "The myriad dharmas return to the One; where does the One return? In the fourth year of the Zhida era.
"The floodwaters of the Western Mountains surged and overflowed; in a single night, they swept away three stone bridges.
The stone lions at the mountain gate let out great roars, and the mountains, rivers, and the great earth all shook.
You lot, you sleepyheads—what do you know of east, west, south, or north? Yangshan Qian said, "Master Zhaozhou’s red thread beneath his heels remains unsevered."
When questioned casually, they simply try to patch the east with the west. Daolin was not like this: "The myriad dharmas return to the One;
to what does the One return? He struck him across the back thirty times. Although this was indeed excessively harsh, it nonetheless brought a moment of total exhilaration.
Holding up his staff, he said, "Is there anyone here now who would ask such a question? Then, leaning the staff against himself, he said, "Let it go."
One step further. Gao Feng Miaoyun said: "Zhaozhou was muddying the waters;
not only was he unable to sever this monk's state of doubt, but he also deceived the monks of the world, causing them to die within the thicket of entanglements. West Peak, however, is not like this.
If someone were to ask such a question today, I would simply say to him: 'A dog licks a hot oil cauldron. Tian.
Jiesheng said, "If you want my head, they will chop it off and take it; if you want my skin, they will flay it and take it; if you want my heart, they will carve it out and take it.

Fortunately, there is no method by which one can withstand a thief who steals in broad daylight. Bianshan Yuan said, "The snipe and the clam contend with one another, and both fall into the hands of the fisherman."
Unraveling the folds, he once encountered the ancient master; how many know the weight of the seven-pound robe?
Now cast into the West Lake, who shall receive this load of pure breeze? (Cui-feng Xian) When asked, he answered intimately with his cloth robe;
he pointed out Qingzhou as his old haunt. The bright moon hangs in the sky, sinking the great fishhook.
Soaking. The whale and the crocodile have no choice but to swallow the hook.
(Zhaojue Zong) At midnight, in pitch-black darkness, a thief was caught. When a light was lit to examine him, it turned out to be Old Wang.
(Gushan Gui) casually lifts up the seven-pound robe; how many practitioners of Chan apply their minds to investigate it?
They all make their nests in Qingzhou, unaware that the spring colors lie in Jiangnan. (Yuan’an Yan)
In the cauldron of boiling water, there is no cool ground; the Yellow River flows with its bottom rolling up. A vajra is difficult to thrust through;
a lantern-ball hangs behind the head. (Oran’s essence:
On all four sides, the great waves are ten thousand fathoms deep; there is no road to heaven and no gate to earth. Within this, the principle is surely difficult to grasp.
The plaint is not for one who grieves, yet it breaks the soul.
(Gao Feng Miao) The axe has rotted the branch, the game unfinished. Celestial fragrance blows as cranes descend upon the jade altar. The black and white pieces on the board are lightly turned over;
with sleeves brushed, the jade pendants grow cold at Cangwu. (Zhongfeng Ben)

The virtue of the Zhou dynasty can be used for self-preservation; the benefits of the Zhou dynasty can be used for universal salvation. When the platter is lifted and the contents revealed, who is there with whom to reach accord?
Fresh flowers, lush grass, verdant wu trees, and crimson cassias—(A Marvelous Omen from Heaven!)—the shadow of the Long River drenches the autumn sky.
Frost-touched leaves rustle, their very form filled with sorrow. Suddenly, an old man sings by the new waters.
[The Master] commands: "The waves stir, and the gulls by the moon take flight. (This is the manifestation of the present.
Once, when Wang Gong, the Military Governor of Zhending, brought his sons into the monastery, the Master sat and asked, "Great King, do you understand?
He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Since childhood I have observed the fast; my body is already old, and I lack the strength to greet people."
He descended from his meditation seat. The King treated him with even greater courtesy and respect. The following day, he ordered an attendant to deliver a message;
the Master descended from his meditation seat to receive it. An attendant remarked, "When the Great King arrived, the Master did not descend from his meditation seat;
why then do you descend when this general arrives? The Master replied, "This is not something you understand. When those of the highest rank arrive..."
Receive those of superior rank upon the meditation seat; receive those of middling rank after descending from the meditation seat; receive those of inferior rank outside the triple gate.

To sit cross-legged to welcome a guest of high status, or to face a banner while seated on a curved bench—this is not a matter of eccentric custom, for they dwell in a land of ritual and righteousness.
(Xiyuan Hui) A broken-legged Zen chair joined with split firewood; it is still fit for reclining one’s head while greeting noble guests.
One clearly knows that though their lands are vast and their wealth smoke-filled, they cannot compete with the bone-deep poverty of others. (Shixi Yue)

How can a human king compare to the honored Dharma King? Without descending from his meditation seat, he receives those of the highest capacity. Do not say there is still a gap between sovereign and subject;
one must first distinguish host and guest before entering the mountains.
(Yuepo Ming) Once, when an attendant reported, "The Great King is coming," Master Zhaozhou said, "Ten thousand blessings to the Great King. The attendant replied, "He has not yet arrived."
The Master said, "He says he has come again.
Huanglong Nan remarked, "Every step reveals it; a seer is rarely encountered. The attendant only knows how to announce a guest, unaware that he himself is in the imperial capital.
Zhaozhou entered the weeds to seek the man, not realizing his entire body was covered in mud and water. — Baiyun Yuan.

The Master said, "Although the attendant was at a loss for what to do, how could he avoid the King’s command? Now that the King’s command has been issued, how do you express the phrase 'the seas are calm and the rivers are clear'?
The rustic old man knows nothing of the labors of Yao and Shun; he merely beats the drum loudly to sacrifice to the River God.
Jingshan Xiu said, "The attendant reports to the guest, yet does not know who this guest is. Zhaozhou is a shrimp."
He yielded to his son and, without realizing it, struck out and lost his own eyes. But tell me, what was the meaning behind Jingshan’s doing so?
A patrolman violates the curfew. Furiritsu (Furizhi) said: "Today the Imperial carriage has arrived in person. Suppose an attendant were to announce, 'Long live the Emperor!
and you immediately gave him a slap across the face, saying, 'Do not deceive this mountain monk. Why? Because the Heavenly Majesty is never far from one."
The countenance is but a few inches away; how could there ever be even a moment’s distance before the Most Honored One?
When the message is delivered and the words have been conveyed, one joins the palms, lowers the head, and bows. Yet facing him, there are those with both the "blue" and "white" eyes;
right before one's face, they have missed the old man who dwells on the mountain. (Chu’an Fang)
Fine steeds and common mules fill the roads; who dares to distinguish their quality by their coat?
Had there not been the discernment of Bo Le at that time, the thousand-li wind-chasing colt would have been lost.
(Cishou Shen) Xu You washed his ears at the stream; Chaofu did not drink the water from which oxen drank. The attendant personally entered the Imperial Capital. Zhaozhou...
It is simply within the weeds. (Nanyuan Sheng) Coming, the palace follows the person;
going, the music fills the road. The attendant is as white-haired as when he was new;
Zhaozhou meets him with an open carriage as if they were old friends. (Biefeng Yin)
Spring mountains cast their reflections upon a river of crimson; The orioles and willows harbor deep affection for the jade steed.
Do not regret that this is not the brushwork of an immortal; It is simply because you are currently within a painting.
(By Buryan Fu) When Zhaozhou arrived at the place of Master Yian, he asked, "Is there anything? Is there anything? The master raised his fist. The Master said:
"The water is too shallow; this is not a place to moor a boat. He then departed. Arriving at another hermitage, he asked, "Is there anything?
Is there anything? The master also raised his fist. The Master said, "You can bestow and you can seize; you can kill and you can bring to life. He then paid his respects.
Zhiti Ai said: "Zhaozhou saw only the sharpness of the tip of the awl. Yunju Shun said: "At that time, Zhaozhou was full of self-importance.
Even so, his nostrils were nonetheless in the hands of the two hut-keepers.
Longmen Yuan said: "The hut-keepers both raised their fists equally; why did Zhaozhou accept one and reject the other?"
"Do you wish to recognize Zhaozhou? [He] struck the left side of the meditation seat once. "Do you wish to recognize the Second Hermit? [He] struck the right side of the meditation seat once.
After a long silence, he said: "Easy to open the mouth from beginning to end; difficult to preserve the heart through the cold of winter.
Guo of Mount Huangbo said: "A thousand kinds of grasses weep in the dew; pines of one kind chant in the wind. Why is it that he accepts one and not the other?"
One who is willing to see through this point here—neither Śākyamuni before nor Maitreya after—cuts off the essential ford;
heaven is eternal and earth is long-lasting. If it were otherwise, I would provide a commentary for you. After a long silence, he said:
"If it were not so, how could one know that it is so? Zhaojue Qin said: "The life-vein of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, the tongs and hammer of the successive sages; it changes the North Star."
Shifting the stars, startling heaven and shaking the earth—there are people of this sort who have not yet emerged from their own nests;
they merely say, "The tongue is in Zhaozhou's mouth. Little do they realize that their own very life has already fallen into the hands of another.

If you can grasp the supreme lineage of the school and meet the two hermit masters, you will then be able to distinguish dragons from snakes and discern the monastic from the lay. This is precisely the time to apply yourself with vigor.
Do you still know where Zhaozhou fell? Be careful not to be vague or superficial. Lian’an Guang said: "The embroidered mandarin ducks are displayed for you to behold;
I do not hand the golden needle over to others. Lianfu Ce said: "Zhaozhou put on a pair of straw sandals and traveled everywhere;
he did not fear killing people with his doubts, yet he ended up exposing his defeat in the hands of the two庵主 (hermitage masters)."
Looking left and right, he said: "Where is it that he fails? Two rows of solitary wild geese fly high, striking the earth;
a pair of mandarin ducks stand alone by the pond. Yun'an Yue said: "The water is too shallow; it is not a place for mooring a boat."
There is resonance within words; one who can both release and seize should immediately prostrate. Within the phrasing, the sharp point is concealed.
Nowadays, there are certain masterless orphaned spirits who do nothing but calculate gain and loss; they not only miss the mark of the ancients, but also bury their own selves.
Do you know where this falls? In a great furnace, refined gold remains unchanged in color.
Question and answer have always been of one essence; do not be negligent regarding this primary point. The General naturally possesses a glorious reputation;
even if he does not receive a fief, he remains free from worldly cares.
(Foji Yu) A scale without stars is level at both ends; when lifted up, it must be seen clearly. If you attempt to dispute over fractions within this state...
Two: Knowing that he has mistaken the zero-point on the scale (Fóxìng Tàiyī).
Tiger-striding and dragon-galloping across the nine realms, he knows how to stir wind and thunder from level ground. In a casual call, he summons the Master of the Hermitage;
instantly, the waters of a thousand rivers flow backward. (Fóxīn Cáiyī)
Passing the hand over the chest, they weep for their lord: "The coffin has not yet emerged, but the corpse leans out.
It would be better to dig deep and bury it; one can guarantee eating tender eggplants next year.
(Xiatang Yuan) Banners flash as they rush to and fro; many who gaze from afar give rise to doubt and suspicion. At this moment, if only Fan Gong were here...
A single step, and the two gates of Hongmen open. (Wuzhun Shanfan) North of the River and south of the River, all are within the imperial domain.
The wheel of transformation shines upon all without partiality. Yet the frontier flute remains beyond the eastern breeze;
When the stone woman hears it, her brows are filled with laughter. (Wuqu Kong)
Short oars and light sails, familiar with the raging waves; Going east or stopping west, one finds carefree ease.
Leaving or staying does not go beyond the reed-flowered shore; Those who seek it on dry land only weary themselves.
(By Baegun Hyu) Willow trees by the Yangtze River dance in the wind; Pine trees on the ridges are cold with the dew. In recent times, worldly affairs have become increasingly harsh.
Furthermore, every person has a particular fondness for the purple silk crown.
(Huishan’s Sea) One kind of upright fist, two kinds of responses. A donkey’s lips and a horse’s muzzle have no cause [for existence].
Having won a thousand fathoms of silk at the Wu Gorge, one lowers the fishing hook across the four seas and five lakes. (Falin’s Sound Two)
A lone steed and a single blade to establish great merit; in both strategy and tactics, you alone are peerless.
Having brought order to both north of Ji and south of Jing, your heroic fame shall forever settle the River Fen.
Once, while Wenyuan was prostrating before the Buddha in the Buddha Hall, Zhaozhou saw him and struck him with his staff, saying, "What are you doing?
Wenyuan replied, "I am prostrating to the Buddha. Zhaozhou said, "Why bother prostrating? Wenyuan said, "Even prostrating is a good thing.
Zhaozhou said, "A good thing is not as good as having nothing at all."
Zhongfeng’s original text says: Wenyuan said, "To prostrate before the Buddha is a good deed; it does no harm to be pliant and yielding.
Zhaozhou said, "A good deed is not as good as having none at all. The conversation has already fallen into error. Do you wish to know where the old man Zhaozhou fell into error?
Wait until he strikes his own skull open, and then I shall tell you.
Wenyuan’s cultivation of practice does not fall into emptiness; from time to time he gazes upon and pays homage to the purple-gold countenance.
Although Zhaozhou’s staff is short, it cleaves through the myriad peaks of Mount Hua.

(Jingshan Gao) Knowing only to gaze upon and pay homage to the purple-gold countenance, one is unaware that the crown of one’s head has been struck by a thunderbolt. One’s lifelong heart and gall have been shown to others.
Tilting. To recognize someone is the same as not recognizing them.
(Mongan Cong) Once, when a monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is Zhaozhou? the Master said, "The east gate, the west gate, the south gate, and the north gate."
Jingshan Hongdao said: "This monk asked Zhaozhou; Zhaozhou answered Zhaozhou. 'If you get a horse from someone, give a cow back to that person.
When people are level, they do not speak; when water is level, it does not flow. Do you understand? When the favor received is deep, one should withdraw first;
when the realization gained is profound, one should stop right then. Tianning Weiqing said: "Everyone says this monk’s spiritual powers leap beyond Zhaozhou."
The barrier cannot be passed. A true man of great character should resolve the matter decisively before the assembly.
If, before the bow has even been drawn and the arrows exhausted, one simply folds one's hands and surrenders, why not utter a turning phrase to make him pay tribute?
Tell me, what kind of phrase could be uttered? Qingshan Xiu said: "This monk’s formulation of a question is truly extraordinary. He has not yet understood."
Who would dare enter the tiger’s den and stroke its whiskers? To say he understands—how could he ever be willing to let it rest at that?
Within the phrase, the pivot of function is presented, coming straight at one's face; the *śakrāloka* eye is utterly free of even a speck of dust.
The gates facing east, west, south, and north stand opposite one another; infinite hammer-strokes cannot pry them open. (Cui Feng Xian)
The four walls and gates stand firm at Zhaozhou; Swords and spears were nearly raised beneath the city. Where now are the general’s warhorses?
Wild weeds and idle flowers fill the earth with sorrow. (Zhaojue Zong) A single strike from the golden mallet in his sleeve opens it wide;
East, west, south, and north, all traces of dust are gone. To the south of the Stone Bridge lies Mount Tai.
The Road. I tell you, traveler, go back and return.
(Puyongping) Old Zhaozhou of the south, north, east, and west—when he sees someone riding a horse, he rides a cow.
Seeking the way home beneath the clear breeze and the moon, one asks Kong Qiu before the gate of the Master. (Xiatangyuan)
A monk once asked Zhaozhou, "Does a newborn infant possess the six consciousnesses? The Master said, "Hitting a ball on a swift current.
Later, that same monk asked Touzi, "What is the meaning of 'hitting a ball on a swift current'?
Touzi said, "Thought after thought, there is no lingering."
Falin’s *Yinyun* says: "The upper line is insufficient; the lower line has a surplus.

The six consciousnesses have no merit in extending this single question. A master has already discerned the origin of the matter together with you. In the vast expanse, a ball is struck upon swift waters;
its falling place does not linger—who can perceive it? (Cui-feng Xian)

What is called consciousness possesses the six [consciousnesses]; eighty-four thousand [dharmas] are not enough. A newborn infant still prattles; it is like hitting a ball against a rushing current, striking it right in the mouth.
(Baizhang Yuanwen) At dawn, amidst the vast expanse, one strikes a ball. From birth, thought after thought leaves no trace.

If you know that once it hits the ground, there is no track left behind— (White Cloud Yuan) The morning sun is vast and boundless as one strikes a ball. From birth, every thought-moment does not linger. If you know that upon hitting the ground, there is no trace—
Traces. At the beginning, Yunmen’s "The six do not contain it" (Cishou Shen).
When a monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is your surname, Master? the Master said, "It is in Changzhou.
[The monk] asked, "How old are you? The Master said, "It is in Suzhou."

There is one in Suzhou; there is one in Changzhou. One must believe that these are the words of a patriarch coming from the mouth of a patriarch. How could the Ancient Buddha of Zhaozhou have been in vain?
When the world perishes, he does not decay. If you can investigate the source and root herein, you will certainly face south and look at the Big Dipper. (Cui Feng Xian)
There is one in Changzhou; there is one in Suzhou. With a tongue that flaps and lolls, he roars the lion’s roar. The Mountain of Longevity is high, and the Sea of Blessings is deep.
Eighty-one, nine times nine. If you can immediately turn the light back within yourself, your name shall remain imperishable for ten thousand ages. (Fujian Qín)
In Suzhou there is it, and in Changzhou there is it. In the third month, the *shàogū* birds cry out in Jiangnan.
How laughable is this man who has years but no virtue; when pressed by others, he forces a distinction.
(Tuingeng Ning) Zhaozhou asked a presiding master, "What sutra do you lecture on? He replied, "I lecture on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*. The Master said, "Ask one..."
"Can you grasp the meaning? he asked. "I can," the monk replied. The Master kicked into the air and blew a blast, saying, "What is the meaning of this?
The monk said, "There is no such meaning in the sutras. The Master said, "You empty-headed liar! This is the meaning of the five hundred strongmen lifting the rock; you do not recognize it."
The Elder Master spoke on his behalf, saying: "The Master deceives me and deceives the great assembly. Cui-feng Xian spoke differently, saying:
"The Master is accustomed to seizing such opportunities.
With one kick, he causes the axis of the earth to overturn; with a single blow, he turns the pivot of heaven. The lecturer does not recognize the perfect sphere."
**The Meaning.** Emptiness: abandoning the mountain in front and passing the mountain behind.
(Guītáng Jūshì) Lifting the stone: from the beginning, the meaning has not been the same. In the depths of the surging waves, he displays his spiritual powers.
The lofty standard does not reside on the reed-banked shore; Pair after pair, they follow the morning breeze. (Dìng of Dàitáng)
A monk once asked Zhaozhou, "I have long heard of the Stone Bridge at Zhaozhou; having arrived here, I see only a small footbridge.
The Master said, "You see only the footbridge; you do not yet see the Stone Bridge. The monk asked, "What is the Stone Bridge? The Master replied, "It carries donkeys and it carries horses."
Chengshan Huiquan said: "The old fellow’s final statement, 'Saving the donkeys and saving the horses,' was both a reward and a punishment for him.
If you can discern this here and now, your lifelong study of the Way will be complete; otherwise, even when drinking water, you must guard against choking."
Standing alone and precarious, the Way is lofty; to enter the sea, one must still hook the giant turtle.
It is laughable that the old man of Ganki, a contemporary, could say that even splitting an arrow is but a futile effort. (Cui Feng Xian) His conduct is that of a being of a different species;
his mind is true, and his speech is intimate. Following the current, he spontaneously attains the wondrous; reaching the shore, he is not lost at the ferry crossing.

(Tianning Lian): The long whale has already surged over the cresting waves; the lame turtle still grinds through the mud by the bridge. Whether crossing horses or crossing donkeys, it is difficult to comprehend;
beneath the shadows of green willows, the paths diverge east and west. (Dizang En)
Once, a monk said to Zhaozhou, "I have come from Chang'an carrying a single staff, yet I have never encountered a single person.
The Master said, "This is simply because your virtue, Great Virtue, has a short staff. The monk was speechless.
Tongan Xian said to the monks from other regions, "In this old monk’s place, I have never seen such a person. He then spoke on behalf of the monk, saying, "He is not short either.
Tiantong Wu spoke on behalf [of the monk], saying, "It is my fault; I did not expect to lightly offend the Master."
Falin bowed three times in his stead.
Once, when a monk asked Zhaozhou, "How should one apply the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day?
the Master said, "You are driven by the twelve hours; I am the one who makes use of the twelve hours."

To cause one to be summoned at the twelve hours of the day only to be sent away again; to rely on official authority and exploit power to deceive others—vast and empty, with no foundation to rely upon.
(Jingshan Gao) The bell marks the end of evening, the cock heralds the dawn; why should Zhaozhou trouble himself with idle vexation? He tears asunder the void into two.
At the edge of the world, a miraculous herb grows from the incense burner of an ancient temple.
(Xue’an Jin) The elders of the local district are at peace; Zhaozhou’s timing is most elegant. If there is wine today, drink until drunk today;
when tomorrow’s worries come, then worry about them tomorrow. (Yean Xuan)
Heaven comes, dragons come; spirits come, ghosts come; wind comes, rain comes; donkeys come, horses come. He was nearly dead—once gone, he does not return.
(The Han Guan Metaphor) While Zhaozhou was drawing water at the well-house of Nanquan, he saw Nanquan passing by and immediately leapt up to hang from the pillar.
The Master stepped back and said, "Save me! Save me! On the steps leading up from the spring, the Master said, "One, two, three, four, five.
After a short while, the Master went back and bowed in thanks, saying, "I just now thanked the Master for saving me."
Zhaojue Qin said: "One person follows error with error; another looks at the tower and strikes the tower.
Although this is so, a father conceals for his son—the straightforwardness lies right therein. Jingshan Ce said: "Zhaozhou hangs up a sheep to sell dogs;
Nanquan has years but no virtue. When the master of the case acts according to the occasion, he can only pull over the ladder to teach this fellow."
A lifetime of setbacks—do you understand? Only by raising a child does one come to know a father’s compassion.
These casual arrangements are by no means in vain; waves upon level ground are about to submerge the heavens.
Yet, strike the ladder a few more times, lest you lose your footing and fall into the Yellow Springs. (Fóxìng Tài)
Once Zhaozhou was passing through the hall when he called out to his attendant. The attendant responded, "Yes. The Master said, "What a magnificent hall of merit! The attendant had no reply.
He who first responded from within the hall did not realize that the consciousness of karma is vast and boundless; yet, although the merit has already been accomplished.
It is so. Yet, alas, at the beginning he did not emit light. (Gushan Gui) What a magnificent hall of merit!
It is entirely composed of past Buddhas; their bodies are adorned with the marks of a hundred blessings, fashioned not from carved sandalwood.
"Daily incense smoke, nightly lamps—look at them; they are nothing more than dried radishes. (Jingshan Daoyuan) Once, while traveling, Zhaozhou arrived at Linji.
Just as he had finished washing his feet, Linji asked him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Zhaozhou replied, "It happens to be the time when this old monk is washing his feet. Linji then stepped forward and assumed a posture of listening.
The Master said, "If you understand, then you understand; why do you keep at this 'feeding'? Jie then returned to the abbot's quarters.
The Master said, "After thirty years of traveling as a pilgrim, today I have mistakenly provided a footnote for others."
Fayun Xiu said: "Among the assembly, some deliberate, saying that Zhaozhou did not recognize Linji as a thief, but rather provided him with a footnote.
At that time, Linji made a gesture of listening; why did Zhaozhou not simply strike him across the ear?
If you deliberate in this way, you have never even dreamed of Zhaozhou’s recognition of Linji. Little do you realize that both were but old men."
"Thief! You must know that there is one true master. I dare ask you all: who among you is that true master?
Jiaozhongguang said: "Linji possesses the eye for testing people; Zhaozhou has long been satiated by the monastic community.
When they casually reveal a glimpse of their style, it is naturally head-to-tail correct. Do you understand? If you do not, the flowing water shall surely pass on to other mountains."
No foot-washing station is provided here; listening from the side at such a time is no mere matter of snatching at scraps.
When the two elders Zhaozhou and Linji met, what need was there to labor over adding footnotes?
(Gushan Gui): One man’s eyes were like drum mallets; another’s head was like a wooden ladle. These two old men, shameless as they are, persist to this day.
There is nowhere to rest or settle. (Jingshan Daokai) Once, when a monk was taking his leave, Zhaozhou asked him, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "To Xuefeng.
The Master said, "If Xuefeng were to suddenly ask you, 'What words or phrases does your teacher have? how would you answer? The monk said, "In that case, please let the Master say it for me."
The Master said, "In winter it is cold; in summer it is hot. He asked again, "If someone were to ask you about the ultimate matter, what would you say?
The monk was speechless. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "I have come directly from Zhaozhou myself;
I am no mere messenger. Later, that monk went to Xuefeng. Xuefeng asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Zhaozhou. Xuefeng asked about Zhaozhou...
"What words did Zhaozhou have? The monk recounted the previous story. Feng said, "It must have been I, Zhaozhou, who was at fault.
When Xuansha Beicheng heard this, he remarked, "How great Zhaozhou is! He does not even know his own defeat. Yunju Xi said:
Where exactly was Zhaozhou’s point of failure? If you can discern it, that is the eye of a true elder.
When a monk approached, Zhaozhou turned his face to the wall and wrote Sanskrit characters. The monk spread out his sitting cloth, performed three prostrations, and the Master turned his body away.
The monk gathered up his sitting cloth and departed. The Master said, "Suffering! Suffering! The monk laughed heartily.
Suffering upon suffering! To whom can one speak to trigger the mechanism? It must be like a crossbow bolt weighing a thousand *jin*.
When the thirty-three heavens strike the Imperial Bell, the mountains, rivers, and great earth all break into dance.

(The Ox-herder’s Wanderings) Suffering within joy, joy within suffering—this monk from Zhaozhou lacks realization in both cases. Even if one were to suddenly penetrate the very source, it would still be so.
This is washing dirt with mud. (Fozhao Guang) Not failing to recognize the foremost tally before one's eyes;
when the occasion arises, his fists and kicks are never given as mere trifling responses.
A scorched brick strikes the frozen ground to its very bottom; Red-Eye bumps into a firebrand. (Yanshi Kai)
When Zhaozhou was serving as the head cook at Nanquan, he happened upon a communal work period for picking vegetables. He then called out from inside the monks' hall, "Put out the fire!
Put out the fire! The assembly all rushed together to the hall, but the Master had already closed the door; the crowd was left speechless.
Nanquan then threw his key and entered through the window. The Master then opened the door.
Yishan Nü said, "I do not learn from Nanquan's way of adding oil to the lamp and fuel to the fire; at that time, I would have seen him close the door."
He picked up a clod of earth and wrote two characters, "Seal" (fēng), upon the gate, leaving Zhaozhou with no way to emerge until this day.
When Zhaozhou arrived at Huangbo, Huangbo saw him coming and immediately closed the door to his quarters; the Master then took a torch and...
Inside the Dharma Hall, [Vzhou] cried out, "Save me from the fire! Save me from the fire! Huangbo opened the door, seized him, and said, "Speak! Speak!
The Master replied, "To draw the bow after the thief has fled.
Baofu Zhan said, "Huangbo has a head but no tail; Zhaozhou has a tail but no head. Wuzu Jie.
Yun said: "Huangbo only knows how to buy cheap; he does not know how to sell dear. Zhaozhou brought blessing out of misfortune.
Cui Feng Xian said: "Truly it is laughable! One must laugh for thirty years. Suppose a monk were to ask, 'What is there to laugh at?
I would laugh at him for drawing his bow after the thief has already fled. Nantang Yu said: "Beating the watch-sticks at the double gates—Huangbo went too far."
The embankment: biting the barb and breaking through the barrier—Zhaozhou was always adept at finding such opportunities.
Although neither side was harmed, it broke through the nostrils of Cui Feng. Gu Nanmen said: "Xuedou’s laugh is excellent;
it is simply that he did not fail to follow the pulse of Zhaozhou’s words. After all, how is it? Thief! Thief!"
