The Fourth Generation Descendant of Dajian (Da Jian):
National Teacher Yunji of Zhongnan Mountain (Dharma Heir of Nanquan Puyuan). Initially, he visited Nanquan and asked, "The *maṇi* jewel is not recognized by people;
it is personally held within the *tathāgatagarbha*. What is this *garbha*? Nanquan replied, "Old man Wang."
"That which comes and goes with you is the casket. The Master asked, "When there is no coming or going, what then?
Quan said, "That too is the casket. The Master asked again, "What is the pearl? Quan called out to the Master. The Patriarch responded. Quan said:
"Go! You do not understand my words. From this point on, the Master entered the realm of faith.
At the place where Cui-feng spoke of "one who comes and goes," he said, "A fellow of the weeds.

At the place concerning one who neither comes nor goes, he also said, "Adding frost to snow. Regarding the question "What is the pearl? he gave a separate response: "Dangerous! He also said, "A hundred-foot pole."

To employ such stratagems at the outset is not the mark of a masterful hand. If you can apply a single eye here, allowing guest and host to interchange roles, you will be able to penetrate deeply into the tiger’s den.
If it is otherwise, then even if the Master and Patriarch were to attain enlightenment, it would still be a case of a dragon’s head and a snake’s tail.
Baizhang Yuan said: "A single mani-jewel at the edge of the clouds was nearly falling into a ten-thousand-fathom deep pit;
it was only thanks to the old hand of Nanquan that he personally lifted it up. Now tell me, where is this jewel now?"
"The Sea God knows its nobility but not its price; it remains in the human world to illuminate the night. Jingyin Chengyun said:
"Nanquan’s responses to the occasion—his granting and withholding—are indeed worth observing. Yet, in the end, he has still not extracted the pearl from it.
Even if you say, 'I do not understand your words,' that is precisely where it is hidden. After all, where is the pearl? Is it that the Sea God knows it?"
"Do you not know its price? This is merely the 'New Wife Chan' of recent times; there is no need to bring it forth. [He] struck the meditation seat and said:
"The pearl and the casket have both been ground to powder by this old monk in a single squeeze.
What more do you all seek here? [He] struck once more. Zhaojue Qin said: "Nanquan, for a time, extended his hand; he could withdraw and release, capture and let go."
"It is not that it does not exist; however, you have simply not yet seen the matter that lies above this.
For instance, if the entire earth is the *tathāgatagarbha*, where would you place the pearl? If the entire earth is the *maṇi* jewel, where would you place the *garbha*?
If you can clearly find a way to turn yourself around, I will grant that you possess one eye. Nantang Yu said, "Now tell me, Master—"
When the Patriarch attained enlightenment, after all, whose power and grace did he inherit? If you can apply your eye here, you will see that from beginning to end, everything is upright.
Gunan said: "Nanquan uses far too many words. Had he been asked, 'What is the treasury? he should have simply said, 'Do not seek it elsewhere. When asked, 'What is the pearl?
he should have smashed it to pieces with a single blow. That would have been a true master. Li.
An Guang said: "I, this mountain monk, am not like that. What is the casket? A cotton-wrapped stone. What is the pearl?
An iron-bound lump of clay."
An old fisherman deep within the dark blue waves; casting bait and pulling line, his strength is spent.
Under a clear breeze and bright moon on a single boat, he knows not that his body is within a crystal palace.

(Fohuiquan) Distinguish right from wrong; clarify gain and loss. Responding to the mind, it is as clear as pointing at one's own palm. Whether coming and going or not coming and going—it is simply this.
This is the treasury. The Wheel-Turning King rewarded those who served it with merit; the Yellow Emperor obtained it through the formless (Wangxiang).
Turning the pivot and engaging the mechanism—this is true skill. A clear-eyed monk must not be negligent.
(Tiantong Jue) The gray falcon pursues the hare; the black dragon sports with the pearl. Penetrating the unblinking blue eye, how could the hand that illuminates objects be empty? Coming and going...
No coming or going; a deceptive smearing within the grass. At the top of a hundred-foot pole, one enters the tiger’s den;
clearly, the moon rises upon the long coral.
(Yuánwù Qín) To gather it is easy; to see it is difficult. To see it is easy; to employ it is difficult. If you can see it and employ it, these two are no different from one another.
Leisurely holding a flute to return home, he blows it deep into the night past the Muzi River bend.
(Duan’an Yan) Clearly the moon rises over the tall coral trees; a single stretch of splendor illuminates the great void.
All sentient beings of the vast earth enjoy this together, yet within the Tathāgatagarbha, it has been non-existent from the beginning. (Songyuan Yue)
In ancient times, people sang both the melody and the sentiment; nowadays, those who sing only produce sound.
I wish to explain this to you, but you do not understand; try asking Yang Qiong about these words.
(Haizhou Ci) The light of the wild waters shakes across ten thousand acres of peril; upon the branches of the coral tree, the moon hangs low. Before the dais, the dew-pillar has no [support].
The nose. He instead uses the spring breeze to paint the brows of the distant mountains.
(Lingyan Chu) Chan Master Yidu of Xiangyan in Dengzhou, under Nanquan, ascended the hall. "Speech is slander; silence is deception.
Beyond speech and silence, there is something more. This old monk’s mouth is too narrow; I cannot explain it for you."
Lingyin Yue said, "Tell me, was that speaking or not speaking? After a long silence, he said, "Go drink tea.
Tianmu Li said, "If one were to cause tears to fall repeatedly, even the vast ocean would surely dry up. Benjue Wei said, "Xiangyan’s tongue dragged on the ground;
Songyuan wrongly added a footnote. Qingfu simply sits on the ground watching Yangzhou."
When Master Rizhao (a successor of Nanquan Yuan) was visited by Yaxi for an interview, the Master made a gesture of rising.
Yaxi said, "This old mountain ghost still sees me here. The Master said, "Forgive me, forgive me; just now I failed to respond properly.
As Yaxi was about to offer further words, the Master gave a shout. Yaxi said, "When facing a great battle array, it is indeed difficult to resist. The Master said, "It is."
Is it so? Xī said, "No, no. Zhaozhou said, "Pity these two fellows;
they do not recognize the turning phrase. Xianyan Zhi said, "Expanding to fill the six directions, yet withdrawing and concealing within the profound.
Even granting this to those two elders, if they wish to leave behind the livelihood of the ghostly realm, they have still not quite reached it."
Dividing lands and establishing borders, the hegemonic enterprise was accomplished. Among heroes, who does not admire Huan and Wen?
Since swords and halberds have become farming tools, are the mountains and rivers of Qi and Jin divided or not?

(Tianmu Zhi) Upon seeing the master at work, he displays his profound mechanism; hand and eye, body and soul, possess a majestic power in all eight directions. Without harming the nature of things, he exerts his new strength.
Verse: Master and guest exchange roles; the reward is at the thatched gate.
(Hongding Jiao) The Prefect of Xuanchuan, Layman Lu Xun (who visited Nanquan Yuan), asked Nanquan:
"In my home, I have a large stone which I sometimes sit upon and sometimes lie upon. Now I intend to carve it into the image of a Buddha. Would this be permissible?"
Nanquan said, "Attaining, attaining. The Master asked, "Is it not that nothing is not attained? Nanquan said, "Not attained, not attained.
Yunyan Cheng said, "When sitting, one is a Buddha; when not sitting, one is not a Buddha. Dongshan Liangjie said, "When not sitting, one is a Buddha; when sitting, one is not a Buddha.
Baofu Zhuan said, "Nanquan was looking at the tower and knocking down the tower—Yunyan and Dongshan."
One up, one down. Wuzu Ke said: "Nanquan only understands shifting the wind; he does not understand changing the customs.
Yunyan and Dongshan are dreaming within a dream. Tiantong Ju said: "Shifting function to accord with the position; shifting the position to accord with function."
This returns us to Master Dongshan and his son; tell me, what was Nanquan’s intention? Truly, it is like a needle that cannot pierce through. Gaofeng Miao said:
"This is precisely what is meant by 'The sage has no fixed mind; he takes the minds of the common people as his own.'"
Dawe Lun said: "This great official possesses a single piece of fine stone; had he not met Nanquan, his purity would have nearly been lost.
Falin Yin said: "To return to a person with the very way that person used—Nanquan did so, yet he nonetheless missed the mark regarding Official Lu Xuan."
To attain or not to attain—Heaven is vast, the earth is narrow. Whether sitting, reclining, or walking, there is no need for weariness or doubt.

(Zhenru Zhe) Nanquan’s attainment is attainment; how does it differ from non-attainment? A refined person, a noble gentleman—his deportment is never errant. (Huanglong Zhen) Attainment before, non-attainment after:
who knows that the single thread consists of two five-hundred pieces? The rain falls through the cypress trees, the wind plays upon the pines.
The *se*. A person on the other side of the mountain listens to the lyrics of the *zhègū* bird, mistakenly taking them for the eighteen variations of the frontier *jiā* flute.
(Shi’an Shao) Sitting and reclining through several springs, half-sealed by moss and half-enveloped by clouds;
without edges and without seams, difficult to grasp or lift up—one vainly speaks of one’s liver and entrails to others. (Xianji Yun)
Held in both hands, it is difficult to cover; as before, with both hands, it is returned. Under a single pillow of pure breeze, sleep is deep and heavy;
a bird picks up a falling flower by the path at the crag.
(Nuo-an Zhao) By the willow-lined stream, green threads hang down; on the branch, the yellow oriole warbles its song. How many, in their greedy play, do not realize—
Spring. In vain it causes thousands upon thousands of fallen petals.
(Gao Feng Miao) Lu Jue asked Nanquan, "Dharma Master Zhao is truly extraordinary; he understands that heaven and earth share the same root and all things are one body.
Nanquan pointed to the peony in front of the courtyard and said, "Great Officer, when people of this age see this single stalk of flowers..."
"It is like a dream.
Baoning Yong struck his palms together and said, "Who has reached such a state?
Huanglong Xin asked a monk, "When Nanquan spoke thus, how could one see it as being of one body with me? The monk held up his sitting mat. Huanglong—
Xuedou said: "To raise it is easy; to see it returned is difficult. At the summit of Vairocana’s head, the celestial wind is cold;
towering down directly into the Azure Dragon’s cave, who would dare look upon it? Zhaojue Qin said: "Lu Guo grasps the golden lock; Nanquan opens it wide with eight characters.
It reaches the point where the seven treasures and eight jewels are arrayed before one's eyes. He then held up his whisk and said: "Heaven and earth are one..."
"Pointing at it—ten thousand things are but one horse; his whole body is a mouth, yet he cannot be fully analyzed. Jingshan Daoyuan said:

"If you look from the perspective of principle (*li*), not only would Nanquan not be able to deceive the Great Officer by even a single point, you yourself would not have even touched a single hair on the back of his heels.
If you look from the perspective of phenomena (*shi*), not only would the Great Officer not be able to deceive Nanquan..."
"Not a single bit [of it] can be grasped; one has not even dreamed of the stench of his sweat.
Or if someone comes forth and says, "Great and small, Mount Jing-shan speaks of principle and speaks of phenomena," you simply tell him:

"Just understand it within the context of principle and phenomena. Tian-ning Qi said: "If you understand it on the basis of the same root and single substance, you fall into the trap of Master Zhao. If you..."
To reconcile this through phenomena and principle is to fall into the "wisteria vines" of Wondrous Joy (Abhirati);
there is no freedom whatsoever. As for Nanquan speaking thus, how ultimately should one understand it? "Where the level marshes end, there are green mountains;
the traveler stands even beyond the green mountains. Yuan'an Mengju, having finished citing Xuedou’s verse, said: "The Great Officer dreams within a dream. Nanquan..."

In the spring dream, one divines the dream; Xuedou was skilled at tracing the source of the dream. Mountains and rivers within a mirror, seeing and hearing within a reflection—smash the mirror, brush away the reflection.
What a pity that single branch; having plucked it toward the frosty sky and the moonlight, you come again to search for it in the clear pool.
Is it not said: "The moon has fallen and night is deep; who knows where we shall meet?"
Seeing, hearing, perceiving, and knowing are not each separate; mountains and rivers do not exist within the mirror.
On a frosty sky, the moon has fallen and night is half spent; who shares this cold reflection in the clear pool?
(Cui-feng Xian) The mountains are moist, the stones harbor jade; the forests are lush, the depths conceal pearls. Seeing this single flower is like a dream—vividly, its roots...
Fundamentally, they do not follow divergent paths. Master Wáng, casting aside all formal constraints, calls out to the indolent Gentleman Lù right in the midst of the bustling capital (Yuánwù Qín).
He illuminates the root of creation where the subtle and the manifest depart;
though they enter and exit in profusion, he perceives their gateway. Roaming his spirit beyond the kalpas, he asks: what is it?
There is. Cast your eyes upon the sound before you and know that the wondrous exists. The tiger’s roar is a whistling breeze blowing through the crags;
the dragon’s cry is a lingering mist that darkens the cavern clouds. Nanquan has shattered the dreams of the age.

If you wish to recognize the majestic Honored One who succeeds to the throne, (Hongzhi Jue), know that heaven and earth share the same root from the beginning; you should not come again to ask others. Thus, you obtain Nanquan’s direct pointing.
Showing it plainly: "Ordinary flowers bloom; it is spring within a dream.
(Gushan Gui) Pointing out that the deep crimson is the same as of old, there is no longer any premature loveliness among the fragrant clusters.
Nanquan departs with the spring in his smile, leaving behind only the lingering red to intoxicate the bees. (Xinwen Ben)
The road to the mysterious pass of the Jade Cave is long; how could the coiled peach be an ordinary fragrance?
Hidden away, it is not permitted for the human world to see it; one only fears that the spring breeze might leak its scent.
(By Jeong-dang Beon) Heaven and earth share the same root as a single body; it is difficult for a painter to paint, and difficult even to sketch. Nanquan shifts his step and moves his form.
In this place, it draws forth the yellow oriole to alight upon the willow branches.
(Xiaoyan Wei) The nest knows the wind; the burrow knows the rain. The magnet attracts the needle; the tide rises at the sourness. Send word to all people: do not be reckless or crude.
The tiger has its missing tooth; the horse has its white hind hoof. How can east and west be so closely entrusted to one another?
(Qian Yan-chang) The lake’s light is limpid, reflecting the clouds and mountains. The young lord roams the flowers, gazing at will. Suddenly he hears a call and turns his head to look;
only then does he realize he has reined in his horse and arrived at Chang’an. (Lin Gao-yu)
Lu Yeng asked Nanquan, "Master, in my home I have been raising a goose in a jar.
It has now grown large and I wish to take it out, yet I must not break the jar, nor may I harm the goose.
I do not know what expedient means there might be. Nanquan called out, "Dafu! Lu Yeng responded, "Yes? Nanquan said, "It is out."
Gao Feng’s Miaoyun said: "Nanquan is a decrepit old man; his hand and eye are not intimate. Even if he manages to produce something, it is still dead merchandise.
If it were Gao Feng, I would simply say to him: 'Great Master, have you ever shown this to anyone? As soon as he attempts to offer a rebuttal, I would strike him out with a flurry of blows.
This is not merely to strip him of his 'fowl-smelling cloth robe,' but to cause the patch-robed monks of the world—"
Each monk has untied the glue and cast off the bonds; they have lived their lives in joy and liberation. Master Yingshan Yun said:

"If the Great Official had not encountered Old Teacher Wang, he would not have avoided the breaking of the bottle and the injury of the goose. But tell me, what is it like after he has been called forth?
Ten-thousand-li eagles fly together as far as the horizon; thousand-year-old cranes soar in unison."
Lu Yèng asked Nánquán, "What is the purpose of Mahākāruṇika Bodhisattva employing so many hands and eyes?
Nánquán replied, "It is like a state employing a high minister; what is he for?"
Cui-feng Xian commented: "This does not equal what the Great Official asked. Bao-ning Yong commented: "It was still not beyond his capacity.
The hand-eye of Great Compassion came forth with intimacy; the old Wang responded to the occasion, arranging host and guest. He turned the spearhead back—how swift!"
"Convenient. From this point on, the six realms shall be free from the dust of affliction.
(Yuan'an Xuan) Lu Jue asked Nanquan, "Disciple, I have come from the Six Realms; do they still possess bodies there?
Nanquan said, "Remember it clearly and present it to a master. Lu Jue said, "The Master is inconceivable; wherever you go, you are in the world."
Regarding the "attainment of the realm" (dhātu-siddhi), it is said: "What has just occurred is entirely a matter within the domain of the Great Officer.
Falingyin remarked: "The old man Nanquan possesses only the sword that kills; he simply lacks the sword that gives life.
This is why Layman Lu Guanyou died once and never lived again. Why not wait for him to say, 'Master, you cannot [do this]'?"
When his contemplation reached its consummation throughout the worlds, he gave a shout, saying, "I thought you were a man of great caliber.
Lu Guen turned his head back toward him from that very spot. Who, ten thousand generations hence, would dare regard him as a mere worldly fellow?
The beautiful lady saw an object through her gauze curtain; pointing, she asked the Immortal Lord what it was. The Immortal held it in his hand and went out the door to look;
his cloud-robes were further brushed by the clear breeze.

(Two Hidden Mysteries) Though the *jiao* wood lute is said to be a wondrous instrument, its silk strings possess an even more profound resonance. One who understands the lines knows a true connoisseur capable of striking it.
Praise! How could their meeting be anything less than a mustard seed fitting through the eye of a needle?

(Xuzhou Sheng) Lu Jue asked Nanquan, "I, your disciple, also have a slight understanding of the Buddha-dharma. Nanquan then asked, "How do you conduct yourself throughout the twelve periods of the day?
Jue replied, "I am not attached to even a single thread. Nanquan said, "You are still a man standing on the steps. Jue said, [and Nanquan struck him].
How is this seen? It is said: "A ruler who possesses the Way does not employ ministers of mere worldly wisdom.

When the birds are exhausted, the fine bow is hidden; when the clever hare is dead, the swift hound is cooked. Seated upon the throne for ten thousand years, how could a man of wisdom allow his emotions to be entangled?

With no arms or armor beyond the frontier, the Vermilion Mountain resounds with the cry of the phoenix. Within the transformative influence of the King’s governance, the four seas and the eight wildernesses are all contained. Let it hang down...
The Duke bows in homage to enjoy the Great Peace.
(Adapting to change through skillful means) The skull stands up in joy; the withered tree roars like a dragon. In vain do we speak of spring having arrived, for the water still forms ice.

With a chest and mind broad and open, one does not lean upon the sparse fence; with eyes squinting slightly, do not allow yourself to become fettered. The man at the steps—does he know, or does he not?
Clouds unroll over sea and mountains as ghosts lower their voices in rain; orioles, fond of spring flowers, sing from near and far.
(Tian'an Sheng) When Lu Guo went to offer condolences upon Nanquan’s passing, the monastery head asked him, "Why do you not weep for the late Master?
Guo replied, "If you, Monastery Head, can speak [the truth], then I shall weep. The head was speechless.
Changqing Ling said, "Tell me, is it appropriate to weep or not? Faling Yin, acting on behalf of the Abbot, simply made the sound of weeping.
When the lay practitioner Ganji of Chizhou (who had met Nanquan Yuan) was opening a reception hall, someone asked him, "Lay practitioner, regarding this reception hall..."
Yi Gan said, "It is like feeding a donkey or feeding a horse.
Langlang Jue said, "Quickly bring the food! Wuzu Yan said, "May the practitioner always remain as he is today."
Gaofeng Miaoyun said: "Langya’s style is indeed beautiful, yet it is merely a matter of frantic fabrication; it is unfit for offering.
Wuzu did not discern the wind of his coming, serving him only a bowl of bland vegetable soup—what a pity that so much salt and vinegar was wasted!"
It is like feeding a donkey or a horse; one simply serves the leftovers of the soup and rice, there is no need to laboriously pick them out.
But tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different? You must be able to determine this. Even if you were to consume ten thousand taels of gold daily, it would still be so;
otherwise, even when drinking water, you must guard against choking. Ji Shuǎng said: "If one has nostrils, they will surely take this food and eat it."
"Not inferior. Do you recognize Ganqi? "Habitually passing before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, hand in golden whip, celebrating peace.
When Ganqi entered Nanquan’s hall to host a vegetarian feast, Huangbo was serving as the Head Seat. Ganqi asked for funds, and Huangbo said, "Funds..."
"The two kinds of giving—material wealth and the Dharma—are equal and without distinction. Gan said, "If you speak thus, how can you consume my offerings?
He then carried the money out. A short while later, he re-entered and said, "Please accept these material gifts. Baizhang replied, "Material wealth and the Dharma are equal and without distinction.
Only then did Gan present his offerings.
Cuiyan Zhen said: "The practitioner Ganqi is a clever fellow who has slipped his footing; as for Huangbo’s bestowing of wealth, when did he ever dream of it? Yunju Yuan said:
"Big and small Huangbo were both had their 'one eye' changed by Ganqi. Jingshan Guangzhao said:
"In a single stroke, they followed the heterodox and pursued evil; Yunju and Luohan were only slightly better. Lingyin Huiyue [concurred].
Yun said, "This is all like covering one's ears while stealing a bell. One fails to realize that Ganqi has both gathering and releasing; the Head Seat was thoroughly awake from start to finish.
When the clouds gather and the rain clears, the vast sky is wide open—a pair of mandarin ducks cannot be captured in a painting.
Mingzhao added a supplement, saying: "The attendant requested the distribution of alms twice—was this a good intention or not? Huangbo [remained consistent] from beginning to end."
The answers were generally ordinary; why then would one be accepted while another was rejected?

Throwing it out and scattering it about, they presented their skills to one another. Before the gates of hell, with the eyes of a ghost, one peers through the skull to see beyond the liver and gallbladder;
atop the crown of Maheśvara, there is yet another layer of clarity. (Xutang Yu)
When Gan-zhi’s host arrived at his residence, he asked, "Where are you from? The host replied, "Yao-shan. Gan-zhi asked, "Have you brought medicine with you?
He replied, "I do not know what illness there is. Gan-zhi joyfully took one hundred ounces of silver and offered it to him.
He further said, "If there is someone in the mountains, this object shall be returned. The host subsequently returned to the mountain and delivered the letter. Yao-... [text ends]
Deshan asked, "Why have you returned so quickly? The host immediately recounted their previous conversation. Deshan said, "Hurry and send him back;
your son has already encountered bandits. The host then sent him back. Ganyue said, "There was someone in the mountains; give him an additional hundred taels as an offering."
Tongan Xian said, "Had I known the practitioner would ask such a question, I would never have said that Yaoshan had come.
Xuefeng Kung said, "The old fellow Yaoshan was himself too timid. Had it been Xuefeng, he would have simply taken him in. Why?"
Furthermore, he taught Gan-zhi, who remained in doubt for thirty years. Tiantong Muan said: "The practitioner uses a shrimp to fish for a giant turtle;

the master of the transformation (the donor) greedily craves the bait while forgetting the hook. When Yaoshan lost his sheep, he only then mended his fence; thus, gain and loss cannot help but be half-and-half.
Although Tong’an had a plan to enter the earth, he lacked the stratagem to pierce the heavens. If I, this mountain monk, were to provide the offering...
As for the master of the retreat, he should give a single shout at that moment and depart; this will ensure the attendant remains in doubt for half his life.

Longtang Zhu said: "If I were the host of the retreat, I would wait until he had offered me several ingots of silver, then stretch out my hand and say, 'The attendant must take another three doses before it is finished.
This way, I can guarantee he will empty his purse to make the offering, while his very life-roots remain in my hands."
In the inner quarters, Ganqi asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Mount Gui.
Ganqi said, "A while ago, a monk asked Mount Gui, 'What is the meaning of the West? Mount Gui held up his whisk. How do you understand this?"
[Guishan] said, "To borrow events to clarify the mind and to attach to objects to manifest principle. Danxia Zhitian said, "It would be better for you to go back to Mount Gui now.
Upon hearing this, Baofu raised his hand and then covered it with his hand. Qingshan Ding said: "Danxia’s blinding of the monk’s eyes is certainly not without merit;
however, as for that monk—did he come from Mount Gui, or did he not come from Mount Gui?"
What is the meaning of the Patriarchs’ intent from the West? The plum blossoms by the stream have already bloomed in abundance.
The single pivot of the ultimate path is realized beyond words; before the wind, I recall the Elder Vimalakīrti from afar.
(Hongfazhe) One day, Gānzhì entered Nánquán’s hall to serve congee and requested that Nánquán recite the liturgy. Nánquán then struck the gavel.
He said, "I request that the assembly recite the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra for the sake of this cat.
He then sweetly brushed out his sleeves and departed. Later, after the morning gruel, Yunquan asked the head cook, "Where has the Master gone?
The cook replied, "He left right then and there. Yunquan immediately smashed the cooking pot.
Yunmen Xinyun said: "The old fellow Nanquan cannot avoid rising and falling along with others;
even if he were to smash the cooking pot, it would still be like drawing a bow after the thief has fled. Yuan'an Meng said: "A rabbit conceives a fetus; a clam holds the bright moon."
"Thirty blows were sent to strike Xuedou; Six 'Non-receptions' thoroughly exposed Yunmen. Nüwa melted stones to patch the heavens;
the First Emperor drove mountains to block the seas. Nevertheless, thirty years hence, every time one drinks water, one will choke.
Mingzhao added: "When the boat cannot be saved, break the scoop."

Meeting on divergent paths, the verse has already been answered; idly blowing the *qiāng* flute toward the marshes, the fisherman greedily watches the herons at the river’s edge, unaware that his skiff is drifting with the waves.
(Xuefeng Yu) High-sounding verses and loud laughter, a wild nature; Pan Lang rides his donkey out from his native village, startling the herons on the sand in the evening sky.
Wild geese slanting away toward the sea gate in two or three rows.
(Zantang Zhun) When needle points meet, there is already conflict; it brings trouble upon Nanquan for beating the rice-pot. Do not say that you let him off lightly this year;
for the most part, those with offenses are dealt with according to different statutes. (Xiaoweng Kan)
One day, Chan Master Lingxun of Mount Furong in Fuzhou took his leave of Guizong. Guizong asked, "Where are you going?
The Master replied, "I am going back to Min. Guizong said, "You have been here for many years; finish your preparations and then come back."
The Master spoke to his disciple of the supreme Dharma of the Buddha. As the Master was tying his robes to depart, Xuefeng Zong said, "Come closer.
The Master then drew near. Zong said, "The weather is cold; take care on your journey. Upon hearing these words, the Master suddenly forgot all his previous understanding.
An eighty-year-old woman learns to paint her eyebrows; with a foolish heart, she wishes to compare herself to her youth.
One morning, when the mirror on the stand is shattered, she finally realizes that everything she has done before was wrong.
(Cishou Shen) One day, Fuyong visited his fellow practitioner, Master Shixing. As Shixing ascended the hall, he held up his staff with his right hand.
He leaned his staff against the left side and, after a long while, said, "If it were not for my elder brother Fuyong, this would be difficult to fully comprehend.
He then descended from the seat.
Huanglong Nan said, "The true nature cannot be put to use, so he simply stops; yet he takes the Buddha-dharma to be a matter of personal favor, leading to..."
This will cause people a thousand years hence to treat it as a source of ridicule. Furthermore, tell me: where does the point of profit or harm lie?

Qinglong said: "Although the true nature indeed encompasses both human sentiment and the Buddha-dharma all at once, it is much like selling lychees before a person from Fujian—it cannot avoid drawing the laughter of bystanders."

Exhausting my aged spirit in attendance, I find the cups and dishes more refined than ever before. Who would have known that the wine of a village inn is difficult to persuade the people on the imperial terrace to accept?

In the fifth month, the fierce heat is at its peak; sweat flows down one’s back beyond description.

Jiada. One day, Linji had a monk seize him and said, "If you do not come in this way at all, how will you respond?

Pinch the nostrils once; the sourness departs by ninety percent. Had it not been for the Great Compassion Temple where he could hide, where else would Puhua be seen?

In swift waters, fish move with difficulty; when the wind is high, birds do not perch. Worldly sentiments observe the cold and warmth;
human faces follow the rise and fall [of fortune].
(Songyuan Yue) One evening, Puhua entered Linji’s hall and ate raw vegetables. Linji said, "This fellow looks very much like a donkey."
The Master then let out a donkey’s bray. Ji said to the steward, "Prepare a fine supply of fodder. The Master said, "The people of Shaoshi do not recognize me;

Meeting within the grass, two red-browed warriors; their clash is as swift as flight. Their banners east and west are exactly alike;
let us ask, who shall return victorious? (Shangfang Yi)

A starving donkey with raw vegetables on its head; Linji caught him before his hall. With ears pricked and a long bray, he followed the kicks and trampling, unaware that his karmic debts must be cleared by borrowing from another.

At the foot of the steps, he lets fall the bell of the kalpa’s beginning; in sumo, he calls out the name of the horse-driver.
When the five blows come down, there is no place for snow; yet he says, "He is not an official. (Tianmu Li) A refined hero, a refined talent;
in the greasy alleys and song-towers, they indulge in banquets. By the time the cups run dry, the moon has also vanished.

(Byu-byan-phu) One day, Puhua went with Linji to a donor’s house for a meal. Linji asked, "A hair swallows the vast ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru.

Ji said, "That was too coarse. The Master said, "What kind of place is this, where you speak of coarse and fine?
Ji stopped. The next day they went to a meal together again. Ji said, "How does today's offering compare to yesterday's? The Master kicked over the dining table again.

Regarding "coarse and fine," Jie then stuck out his tongue.

Seizing clouds and grasping mist without stirring a ripple; like two tigers competing for food, capturing them alive without harming a single life.

Here, if someone were suddenly to ask: "A hair swallows the vast ocean, and a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru—is this due to supernatural powers and wondrous methods, or is it simply the natural state of things?

Island. When there is spirit, add more spirit; where there is no elegance, there is elegance nonetheless. Nanhua Ying said: "Linji calls forth face-to-face;

Without dismounting, each went on his own way. Zhaojue Chengruo said: "If refined gold is not tempered a hundred times, how can its brilliance be seen?
If a supreme treasure is not appraised for its price, how can its authenticity be known? It was not that Linji was incapable of testing Puhua."

Emerging once and submerging once; going forth and returning once—snatching food from the mouth of a fierce tiger or scratching an itch on the head of a venomous snake—even so, it does not yet measure up to the deeds of a great man.
These two elders were famous throughout the universe and their reputation was heavy in their own time;
how could this mountain monk keep his three inches [of tongue] tightly sealed? Letting both pass by, for they were playing with the false as if it were real; letting neither pass by.

[Zhaozhou] said, "It is wrong. You have struck him too severely. "If you people were to deliberate upon this as a matter of the Buddha-dharma, the entire school of Bodhidharma would be wiped out like dust.
Nantang Yu said, "Cui-feng’s saying such a thing also deserves twenty blows. Have you not heard it said:
'When the real thief has fled, the officer who searches for stolen goods receives the beating'? Qingshan Xiu said, "One person..."
One possesses the hand that seizes the dragon; the other has attained the mechanism for trapping the tiger. Both are masters of the craft. But tell me:
who is the one trapping the tiger, and who is the one seizing the dragon? Gunanmen said: "Linji’s single staff is usually used to strike horizontally or vertically.
Why, then, does he stick out his tongue here? *A single note of the Hsiang flute at evening on the deserted pavilion; you head toward Xiao.*
I traveled from Xiang to Qin.
To recognize true gold, one must place it in the fire; through repeated smelting, its fineness or coarseness is revealed. When trading on the high road, there is no yielding;
the price of a fine object has always been exceptional. (Haoyin Xin)
Drawing back a crossbow capable of lifting a thousand *qun*, the trigger is released; it pierces clouds and penetrates stone like a flash of lightning.
Without the strength to lift a cauldron or pull down a mountain, how could one easily ride a black steed across a thousand *li*?
(From the *Yujü Qian*) The black dragon surges forth; the Bohai Sea is vast and boundless. Its breath steams over Yunmeng, its waves shake Yuyang. The clouds suddenly darken.
The sun and moon have lost their light; who says that Puhua was mad? (Tianshui Guang) Chaff and husks are cast upon Yao and Shun;
cicadas and wrens laugh at the Kun and Peng. Under the pressure of stones, bamboo shoots emerge askew; Hanging from the cliffs, flowers grow upside down.
Chopping wood for the hearth; roasting a hen that crouches beneath. With a single crash of thunder, heaven and earth split asunder; not permitted to sing of Great Peace upon the broad royal road.
(Sanji Fu) Meeting by chance, they specifically unfold the karmic conditions; appearing and disappearing with ease, their wondrous function is complete. A kingfisher tramples over lotus leaves.
Rain. A heron pierces the mist of the bamboo grove.
(Lang Shan Yu) When Puhua was about to enter extinction, he said to people, "I beg you for a *zhidu* (straight robe). When people offered him clothing, he would not accept any of it.
Linji sent someone to deliver a coffin for him; the Master laughed and said, "Linji’s brat is so talkative."
He accepted it and then took leave of the assembly, saying, "Tomorrow at the eastern gate, I shall depart from life. The people of the commandery followed one another to escort him out of the city.
The Master spoke in a stern voice, "The burial today does not accord with the principles of the *Qingwu* (the art of geomancy); tomorrow at the southern gate, I shall pass away."
The people followed him accordingly. He further said, "It will be auspicious for me to depart through the West Gate tomorrow. As days passed, the people gradually became fewer.
On the fourth day, he personally carried his coffin outside the North Gate, entered it while ringing a bell, and passed away. The people of the commandery rushed out of the city.
When they lifted the coffin to look inside, it was already gone; only the sound of wooden clappers (*diao*) was heard fading gradually into the air, its origin unfathomable.
"The wind has blown until nothing remains. One coffin, carried by eight men; they carry it out beyond the walls of Zhenzhou City.
Let him follow the wooden clappers as he distinguishes himself. (Beijian Jian)
"Having scooped up empty space to make it one's neighbor, one then hides one's body within the Big Dipper.
This plunderer of emptiness—what a lot of fuss! He still uses an empty coffin to deceive later generations.
(Dongshan Yuan) Chan Master Liangshui of Shouzhou (successor of Magu Che) went to visit Magu. Upon seeing him coming, Magu took his hoe and went away.
"Clearing the weeds. When the Master arrived at the place where the weeds were being cleared, Gu did not look back at all; he simply returned to his quarters and shut the door.
The next day, the Master went again, and Gu shut the door once more. The Master then knocked on the door. Gu asked, "Who is it?
As the Master was about to state his name, he suddenly attained enlightenment. He said urgently, "Master, do not deceive Liangsui. Had Liangsui not come..."
He paid his respects to the Preceptor. He had almost been led astray by the sutras and treatises for his entire life.
Upon returning to the lecture hall, he said to the assembly, "What all of you know, Liang-sui knows entirely; what Liang-sui knows, none of you know."
Yunmen Wenyan said, "There is already a wave against the current. To have now attained entry is the meaning of going with the current;
it is also called the occasion of 'releasing both. He further asked, "What is the place where Liangsu knows? Donglin Yan said:
"What is it that Liang-sui knows? [The Master] said, "A cormorant speaking to a crane. Lingyin Yue said, "To act for others, one must be thorough;
to bite into raw iron, to go against the current, and to drive a stake into empty space."
Throughout my life, I have cast my heart and courage open to others; how many people are there who have reached this gate?
Since our parting, the old acquaintances of the capital city see only warm smoke and slanting sun as dusk falls again.

(Longmen Yuan) Seeking words and chasing phrases leads to endless complications; it is only because one has been deceived by the eyes from of old. If you can let go with an open hand, you will be able to return to your original home.
The kingdom—darkly contemplating how many paths there are at the crossroads.
(Danxia Chun) Having personally arrived at Peach Blossom Spring, the scenery is secluded; a single jar of bright moon is as profound as autumn.
Reflecting back on the day spring ends at the cave entrance, countless red blossoms are carried away by the flowing water. (Cheng Kumu)
Meeting is like encountering a living enemy; it stirs ten thousand measures of grief throughout one’s entire being.
Since I have no longer sought [the truth] from others, this time I am ashamed to look upon my head in the mirror.
(Wenyi Run) Chan Master Chuwai of Qianzhou (a successor of Xitang Zang). A monk asked: "Regarding the three vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, what is their underlying principle?"
"Attaining the wondrous—does this accord with or differ from the intent of the Patriarchs? The Master said, "You must discern it beyond these six propositions;
you must not turn according to their sounds or appearances. The monk asked, "What are the six propositions?
The Master said, "'It is speech,' 'it is silence,' 'it is neither speech nor silence,' 'it is both,' 'it is neither,' and 'how would you do it? The monk was at a loss.
Luan Yuan said: "This monk can truly be called one for whom 'calamity does not enter the door of the cautious family.
Yet his final utterance of a single mantra cannot help but draw laughter from onlookers. Only that this monk was at a loss for words makes him slightly superior."
The world was in turmoil, all vying to make Qin their emperor; yet Luan of Lu would rather die than submit as a subject.
How much better to sit beneath a thatched eave by the green peaks, taking a long nap with both legs stretched out.
(Zifuxu) Master Chao of Jinzhou (a successor of Zhangjing Yun) invited Master Mi for a meal but did not arrange any seating. When Master Mi arrived, he unfolded his sitting mat.
While prostrating before his sitting mat, Master Mi descended from the meditation seat. Mi then sat upon the master’s seat, while the master withdrew to sit on the floor.
When the meal was finished, Mi departed. An attendant said, "The Master is revered by all people; today your seat has been usurped by another.
The Master replied, "If he returns after three days, I shall accept him as my successor. Three days later, Mi returned.
Later, when the result arrived, he said, "The other day I encountered bandits.
Because of this, a monk asked Jingqing, "What was the meaning of your encounter with the bandits the other day? Jingqing replied, "I saw only the sharpness of the tip of the awl."
"One does not see the square head of the chisel. Yuyan Meng said: "At that time, as soon as Master Mi arrived, he sat down on the ground.
He left Jinzhou with no way to ascend to heaven and no way to enter the earth, sitting straight through until the appearance of Ruci Tathāgata.
'I shall come again at that time to meet him,' he thought, and then, striking his forehead with his hand, he cried out: 'Cat! (Baohua).
Enxian said: "In Jinzhou, [Mihuai] lost his position; Mihe encountered bandits; the scale-hook was driven with nails—this was simply a matter of pulling it straight.
It is a pity that the attendant lacked quick wit. Had he been a true man, when Master Mi said, 'The other day I encountered bandits,' he should have asked, 'What did you lose, Master?
Had he been able to utter such words at that time, not only would Master Mi have held him in high esteem,"
Fu. Zhishi Jinzhou retired from his post as was his right.
Regarding the Venerable Master Gaoji of Hexing Prefecture (the successor of Zhangjing Yun): A monk asked, "What is the Way? What is Chan?"
The Master showed him with a verse, saying: "The named is not the Great Way; right and wrong are both not Chan.
If you wish to know the meaning herein, yellow leaves stop the crying for pennies."
Zifu Yu said: "The Way cannot be established without Chan; Chan cannot be practiced without the Way. Nowadays, those who follow the 'barbarian masters' do not understand how to adapt and transform.
It is not that they fail to strike with a single blow to the end; rather, from within their cosmetic makeup, they produce endless four-character and six-character prose.
They cannot avoid the fate of having their fingers bitten by the Duke of Ji. I, this mountain monk, shall provide yet another path: when there is a name, there is greatness."
The Way—both right and wrong are equally Chan. If you can realize the meaning within this, your labor in burning paper money will be in vain.
Chan Master Bimoyan of Mount Wutai (a successor of Mazu Daoyi, lineage of Yongtai Tuan) constantly carried a wooden pitchfork.
Whenever he saw a monk approach, as soon as the monk prostrated, he would thrust the fork into the monk’s neck and say: "Which demon or sorcerer taught you to leave the household life? Which..."
"A demon has been bewitching you to make you travel on foot. Whether you can speak or not, you shall die at my hands.
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Hearing this, Heshan Tong went to see him. Before he had even prostrated himself, he threw himself into the Master's embrace.
The Master then patted Tong’s back three times. Tong clapped his hands and said, "Brother, you have deceived me from three thousand *li* away."
"I have come. You have enticed me from three thousand *li* away.
Baofu Zhan said, "To hesitate when one ought to decide brings about further disorder. Shoushan Nian said, "A thousand hearings are not equal to one seeing.
Fayan Yi, for the sake of Su Dao, spoke on behalf of the monk, saying, "Beg for our lives! Beg for our lives! This was reported.
Cishi then spoke on behalf of the monk: "The old fellow has managed to let go of his staff. Fadeng Qin spoke on behalf of the monk:
He simply extended his neck to show it. Wuzu Ji said: "Had I seen him at that moment, I would have snatched the staff away, struck him across the face with it, and knocked him down.
Then I would have lit a fire and examined whether his face was thick or thin. Mingzhao Qian said: "I, for my part..."
At that moment, seeing Yi on the verge of speaking but before he had spoken, [Dongshan] first gave him a slap. Langye Huijue said:
"The thunder was very loud, but there were no raindrops at all."
Severing the heavy ford, it is difficult for one to pass. To lift the staff, one must believe the skull is dry. Only after reaching Mount Huo will you know the essential point;
dying together and living together is not yet sufficient to observe.

Above. One breath draws the vast ocean dry to its very depths.

He then asked, "What is the great meaning of the coming from the West? Huangbo immediately—
He struck him hard. Thus he asked three times and was struck three times. Finally, he took his leave from the seat, saying, "I have come to ask questions and received only blows.
Regretting my own stupidity and ignorance, I shall now go on a pilgrimage to various regions. He addressed Baizhang, saying, "Although Yixuan is a junior, he is truly extraordinary.

"Go to Dayú. The Master then went to visit Dayú. Dayú asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from Huangbo.
Dayú asked, "What instructions did he give you? The Master said, "I asked him about the true meaning of the West [India], and three times I was struck for asking three times."
He did not know where his fault lay. Wuzhuo said, "Huangbo’s heart is so earnest and compassionate that he has exhausted himself for your sake, yet you still seek out his faults.

Wuzhuo then grabbed him and said, "You bed-wetting little ghost! Just now I asked you where your fault was; what about now?"

The Master struck Yuyi three times under the ribs. Yuyi pushed him away and said, "Your teacher is Huangbo; it is none of my business."

Spreading throughout the world:
sleep-filled eyes, three times struck, yet will not open. Suddenly, a wild leap and a roar like thunder.

"If you hear it said 'taking away the person but not the environment,' simply add two phrases to the environment. If you hear it said 'taking away the environment but not the person,' simply add two phrases to the person.
To clarify the fundamental principle (gangzong) of Linji, you must recognize the two words 'sometimes'."
Only then can you attain it. Sometimes the person is taken away but the environment is not; how do you comprehend this? Sometimes the environment is taken away but the person is not;
how do you take responsibility for this? Sometimes both person and environment are taken away; how do you withstand this?
Sometimes neither person nor environment is taken away; how do you proceed within this?
The wine from earthen jars is ripe and all are drunk; The smoke thickens above the forest as the flowers glow crimson.
At midnight, without lamps, the incense chamber is still; A swing hangs suspended in the bright moonlight. (By Fojian Qin, No.
4) When the oriole meets the warmth of spring, its song flows smoothly; When a person encounters times of peace, their smiling face unfolds. Several times the fallen petals have followed the water.
Go! A single long blast of the flute emerges from the clouds;
his majestic spirit rolls like thunder, and his chilling majesty pursues the frost and snow. When the General’s command is issued, the barbarians of Jing are struck down;
a single stroke of the divine sword leaves a trail of blood for a thousand li.
The Son of Heaven of our sagacious court sits in the Hall of Distinction; the living beings of the four seas all rest in peace. A gallant youth of youthful years overturns his golden goblet;
the peach blossoms filling the courtyard are as red as brocade.
As the King wields his sword, the will is that of the Sovereign; held crosswise, its hair-cutting blade—whom would dare oppose?
Punishing the guilty and consoling the people manifests the Great Function; mountains and rivers do not alter their ancient boundaries.
(Pingyang Min 4) At the capital court, one desires to behold clarity and purity; feathered dispatches fly like stars down to the Phoenix City. The three divisions are unified into one.
The earth is settled; oxen are released and horses returned to joy in the peace of the realm.
How could one dare to snore beside the Cloud Terrace? Once the Golden Wheel is rolled forth, the ten thousand nations are subdued. The altars of state have already followed the funeral bier away;
in the palaces of Qin, there is no longer any Ziying to return.

With hands folded in ease, he transforms even the remote frontiers; carriages and books, jade and silk, all share in the patterns of civilization. Joyful is the age of Shun, where heaven and earth are vast;
boundless is the sky of Yao, where sun and moon endure long.
Flowers and willows fill the planting beds; the breeze intoxicates the wandering traveler. Sparse shadows slant across the ground; the solitary guest alone remains sober.
(Tianmu Xiu, 4) Removing his hat, he forgets to tend the hoe; Lu Fu already has a husband. The five horses hesitate; why is the Magistrate so foolish?
They ravaged Chu and whipped its corpses; their actions were perverse and their methods inverted. I shall surely avenge them. Qin has sent forth its armies.
Peach blossoms line both banks; with chicken and millet, I invite my guests. The path through the cave mouth is narrow—who would ask for the way across?
He cleaves open the Nine Cauldrons and brings forth the divine elixir. Radiant and glorious, it reflects the sun and illuminates the casket.
The Lord of Waters sighs in secret; the mountain sprites clamor at night. The great sword is ground once more; brandished to the left and whirled to the right.
White clouds drift as they please into the valleys; why need the bright moon reach the mountains? Look, look! For ten thousand ages, forever beyond pursuit. (Tan Jiren)
Linji said: "A single shout distinguishes guest and host; illumination and function proceed simultaneously.
Zhaojue Qin gave a shout and said: "Now tell me, is this the guest or the host? Is it illumination or function? Do you understand thoroughly?
When the momentum of a thousand peaks reaches the mountain range, it stops; when the sound of ten thousand streams returns to the sea, it vanishes. Yufeng Xin said:
Master Linji proclaimed the "one step beyond" of the Buddha King of Emptiness; this may be called "building villages and changing inns," or "secretly inscribing talismans.
Yet, what if one suddenly encounters a tongueless person who cannot be shouted at? Furthermore, how is it when both guest and host are hidden?
Both illumination and function are blind; the Buddha-dharma has no spiritual efficacy. He further composed a verse:
Peach and plum blossoms bloom in the days of the third month; The garden is filled with green and white, drenching people in chill. On the branches, spring grows weary as a light rain blows;
The remaining red petals on the ground are hard to bear looking upon.
Under the assembly of Linji, two fellow students questioned one another. One said, "Setting aside the capacities of the middle and lower grades, please, elder brother, speak a single phrase.
The other said, "As soon as you attempt to ask, you have already missed it. The first replied, "If that is so, then I shall pay my respects to you, elder brother.
The second said, "You thief! Hearing this, the Master ascended the hall and said, "If you wish to understand the host and guest of Linji..."
Verse: Ask the practitioners of the second dhyāna within the hall.
The beautiful woman whispers in private, lingering in the courtyard. She turns her gaze as the golden cage parrot listens;
Fearing that the bird’s cries might reveal her secret heart, She plucks fragrant rice with her hands and whispers in secret. (Weian Xuan)
Linji addressed the assembly: "Sometimes there is first illumination and then function; sometimes there is first function and then illumination; sometimes illumination and function are simultaneous;
and sometimes illumination and function are not simultaneous. When there is first illumination and then function, there is a person present.
When there is first function and then illumination, there is a Dharma present. When illumination and function are simultaneous, one drives the plowman’s ox and robs the hungry man of his food."

"Beating the bones to extract the marrow; striking with the needle and awl with merciless force. When illumination and function do not arise simultaneously, there is questioning and answering, establishing the guest and establishing the host, blending water and mixing mud.
To respond to the occasion and engage with beings—if one is a person of transcendent capacity, they would seize the moment and depart before the question is even raised;
this would still leave something to be desired."
Fenyang Shanzhao said: "First illumination, then function—let us deliberate on this together. First function, then illumination—only then can you be considered a person.
Illumination and function simultaneous—how will you withstand this? Illumination and function not simultaneous—how will you find a place to settle?
Langye Huijue said: "First illumination, then function—this reveals the claws and fangs of the lion. First...

Using the subsequent illumination: even if one employs the majestic power of a king of elephants, illumination and function are simultaneous, like a dragon obtaining water, bringing forth rain and surging clouds.
When illumination and function are not simultaneous, it is like lifting up an infant or looking down with pity upon a young child.
This is how the ancients established the Dharma gates; whether it is appropriate or inappropriate is as follows: if it is appropriate, it is like Ji Xin mounting the nine dragons—
[The Master] said: "A palanquin. It is not fitting to act like this. When Xiang Yu lost his horse Zhi, was there anyone who could vent his indignation on behalf of Langye?
If there were none, I, this mountain monk, shall go forth myself. He struck his staff and descended from the seat. Jingshan Gao said:
"If one employs illumination first and then function, it blinds the eyes of all people. If one employs function first and then illumination, it opens [the eyes of one person]."
It cuts through the eyes of all people. If illumination and function were simultaneous, then one would be half-open and half-blind.
If illumination and function were not simultaneous, then one would be either fully open or fully blind. Among these four statements, one contains both guest and host;
one contains the guest but lacks the host; one lacks both guest and host; and one is fully endowed with both guest and host. This is the present moment.
Perhaps there might be someone among the assembly, a person who refuses to be deceived, who would step forward and say:
"What kind of place is this, where you speak of existence and non-existence, of illumination and function, of host and guest?
Seizing him by the chest and dragging him down from the meditation seat, you should give him a thorough beating! Yet, one cannot blame him."
It is difficult to perceive even within the flash of lightning; by the time one reaches the point of the needle and the awl, it is no longer fit for use.
If one attains a heroic and spirited lion cub, they will cast aside the trigger-mechanism and employ their function to illuminate what lies before them.

(Xiu Si of Qing Shan) A white staff meets the head—the pivot of killing and giving life. Turning the body and exhaling the breath, the vision is slow. The fishing line is cast in vain at the hook’s tip.
The bait: leave the wind and waves to you; the handle is already held.
With a harmonious sound, all deliberation is cut off. Bright moon and clear breeze—how could they ever be concealed?
If you are a guest beneath the gate of the Patriarchs, you shall take this up even if your entire body is crushed to pieces.

Sometimes there is wind and rain, sometimes it is clear; if one understands the cause in this way, there is no need for listening. It is laughable that people of this age lack the capacity for understanding;
they mistakenly take a solitary state and chant it toward others.
The three mysterious halberds and armor are worn backward; who can discern the duality of light and dark? Should one attempt to meet their sharp edge, the steed snatches them away.
If one were to exert the strength that could uproot mountains, (Pingyang Mien) would first act and then reflect.
He releases the hawk with its string cut; as the child looks on, the great wind has already swept it past.
(Heavenly Eye Xiu, No. 4) First illuminate, then act;
it makes people feel the itch where they ache, scratching them until they are overjoyed, with a heavy blow behind the head.
Illumination and function occur simultaneously; like thunder crashing and lightning flashing, wind and rain come from all eight directions, leaving no place for one to take shelter.
If illumination and function do not occur simultaneously, then let one go ahead and grope about. Once you recognize this grandmotherly heart, every single step will be a living resource.
Linji was once asked by a monk, "What is the 'hair-cutting sword'? The Master said, "A disaster! A disaster!
The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.

The sword is hidden in its scabbard, its coldness overwhelming and chilling to the bone. If you intend to ask further, you will linger and pass beyond the southern peaks; yet you still wish to press forward while seeking retreat.
Later, his majestic influence would circle the mountain streams and pools for a thousand ages.
(Touzi Qing) When Linji arrived at the place of Master Sanfeng Ping, Ping asked, "Where did you set out from? The Master replied, "Huangbo."
Zhaozhou asked, "What have Huangbo been saying lately? The Master replied, "Last night the Golden Ox was covered in mud and filth;
even until now, no trace of him can be seen. Zhaozhou said, "The autumn wind blows through the jade flute; who is it that knows this melody?"
The Master said, "Directly penetrating ten thousand layers of barriers, not dwelling beyond the azure heavens. Huangbo Ping said, "These words are far too lofty.
The Master said, "A dragon gives birth to a golden phoenix chick; it shatters the emerald lapis lazuli. Ping said, "Sit for a while and drink some tea."
Qingshan Ding said: "The 'white-handed thief' (the master of stealth) can indeed be considered difficult to resist even when facing a great battle array.

But as for the tea of Sanfeng—is it nectar or is it poison? Hongfazhe said: "To scratch an itch on the head of a venomous dragon, or to cast one's body across the mouth of a fierce tiger—this is certainly not impossible.
However, as for striking the joints, knocking at the gate, breaching the tower, and leaping over the hearth—"
This still leaves one move behind Sanfeng.
When Linji posed his question: "One person is atop a solitary peak with no way out;
another person is at the crossroads with no front or back. Which one is ahead? Which one is behind?"
Wutian Huiyun said: "There is yet another person who is neither on the solitary peak nor at the crossroads.
Why does the old fellow Linji not know him? Having said this, he descended from his seat.
When Linji arrived at Huayan in Xiangzhou, Huayan saw him coming and crossed his staff horizontally while assuming the posture of one who was sleeping.
Linji said, "Do not doze off. Huayan said, "A skilled Chan guest is indeed quite different from others. Linji said, "Attendant, bring some tea for the Master to drink.
Huayan called out, "Venerable Vihārasvāmin (the rector), arrange the third seat!"
Chengtian Yi said: "The East Pavilion of the Avatamsaka Sutra is grandly opened, yet Linji merely plays the lute and sings of the fish.
If you wish for this story to spread far and wide, you must simply be given a beating with a staff and driven out."
The clay ox chews the moon as it sinks into the cold pool; the wooden horse neighs in the wind as Mount Tai awakens anew. Looking up and down, heaven and earth are entirely non-dual;
in an instant, they cause the grasses and trees to harmonize with the springtime warmth.
(Qingshan Ding) Once, when a monk came to visit Linji, the Master extended both hands. The monk remained silent. The Master asked, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not understand."
The Master said, "It is a whole, unbreakable sphere; I give you two coins.
Jiang Tianquan said, "To let it go is perilous; to pull it back is even swifter. To speak thus is called 'white-handed thievery'; it is only suitable for Linji."
Wind-swept and leaning gracefully against the crimson balustrade, she half-sells her coquettish modesty, chilling those who would fain be drunk.
Yet the fair-faced young man has not yet offered his praise; with ten parts of tears, she pours forth her own heart.
(Qingshan Ding) One day, Linji said to the two senior monks Puhua and Kefu, "I wish to establish [the Way] here."
"The *Huangbo Zongzhi* states: 'The two of you may now take my robe. The two men then respectfully departed.
Three days later, Puhua came back up and asked, 'What did you say three days ago, Master? The Master then struck him."
Three days later, Kefu came up and asked, "Master, why did you strike Puhua the day before yesterday?
The Master struck him as well.
Changlu Ren said, "Puhua and Kefu must not be let off; it would have been improper for Old Man Linji to let them go."
If it were just Chan’an, he would have spent his entire life carrying a shoulder-board with no one to complete the task.

Nevertheless, even though this is so, you must know that beyond the distant mist and waves, there is another way to deliberate. Mishong Deng said: "Killing and giving life are in one's hand; bestowing and taking away depend on the occasion.
It is not that he lacked [this capacity], but had Linji wished to establish the school of Huangbo, I would dare say it was 'not yet. I, too, wish to..."
Within this, the tenets of Caodong are established. At Qingliang’s gate, one faces the Xiaoxia Peak; at every moment, the golden needle passes through in secret.
Whether you have attained realization or not is of no concern. When the month has thirty days, it is the "great month"; when it has twenty-nine, it is the "small month.
At every hour, the jade thread is drawn across horizontally. Nor does he bid you come up or go down. At just such a time, one moves with measured steps, bowing and turning.

There is nothing that is not the mechanism of mutual interpenetration; every movement, turn, and action is entirely the principle of subtle density. There is no need for the labor of digging into the earth to seek out the heavens;
naturally, the sound accords with its resonance. Nevertheless, though it is thus, only when the minister is able to retire from his position can he truly attend upon his sovereign.
Only when you can turn yourself around will you be fit to approach your father. But how do you express this one phrase of turning? "Next year there shall be new branches;
the spring wind’s vexation shall not cease until the end. Pingyang Mian said: "It is a pity that these two men, having been so deeply respected, were allowed to depart.
Linji did not cut them off decisively on the spot, which causes later generations to look toward the three days prior."
"Three days later, he will toy with his own spirit. Today, I, this mountain monk, shall utterly exterminate him for him.
I, this mountain monk, also wish to establish the school of Tiantong right here. How shall it be accomplished? Is it best to depart with respectful greetings now?
Or is it to come back up after three days? Or is it to go from east to west? Or is it to remain silent for a long while?
Did he remain silent? Or did he shake out his sleeves and leave the hall? Or did he circumambulate the seat three times and perform a woman’s bow?
Or did he raise his eyebrows, blink his eyes, point a finger, and clench his fists? Or did he overturn the Dharma-seat and shout to disperse the assembly?
All the actions performed above were merely playing with the vital spirit; ultimately, how does one bring forth that single hand?
"Eyes, together with this mountain monk, establish the fundamental tenet. Do you understand? A crane has nine peaks, yet its wings find it hard to soar;
a horse lacks the thousand-li stride, so its pursuit of the wind is in vain. Gunanmen said: "The orthodox lineage of Hebei was like lightning striking;
yet Kefu and Puhua merely failed to fight on the field and instead raised their troops from behind the lines. They sought to surpass Linji, but they had not yet attained it."
Today this mountain monk wishes to establish the school of Linji at this very mountain.
Suppose someone were to step forward with single-minded directness and ask, “What did the Master say?”—I would strike them across the spine with my staff.

Or suppose a second person were to step forward and ask, “Master, why did you just strike that monk?”—I would likewise strike him across the spine with my staff. [Suddenly] he picks up his staff and says:
The eyes upon the tip of the staff are as bright as the sun; to recognize true gold, one must look within the fire.
Once, when Magu asked Linji, "Of the twelve faces of Avalokiteśvara, which is the front face?
the Master descended from his rope-cot, seized him, and said, "Where has the twelve-faced Avalokiteśvara gone? As Magu turned his body and prepared to sit down, [the Master struck him].
The Master brandished his staff and struck him. Gu stepped forward and seized the staff; they grappled together and entered the abbot’s quarters.
Great Compassionate Avalokiteśvara reveals his true face; the official permits not even a needle, yet a single thread passes through.
A rat drags a gourd—how busy it is! A ghost contends over a lacquer bucket—no one sees it. (Gushan Gui)
Obscuring the foremost move right before one's eyes, they pull and drag, presenting their skills to one another.
One does not know that, apart from the hand of Wang Wei, who else could paint it so perfectly?

(Jingshan Daoyuan) Habitually riding spirited steeds and competing in colorful boats, each displays their own elegance in the moment of action. Brandishing whips and dancing with oars, all people [witness the spectacle].
Seeing this, how could one know that the wondrous place grants freedom?
(Nanshi Xu) When Linji heard Deshan instructing the assembly, saying, "If you can speak it, thirty blows;
if you cannot speak it, thirty blows," he said to Luopu, "Go and ask him why, even if one can speak it, there are thirty blows. Wait—
Yishan struck him. [Baofu] caught the staff and gave it a shove, watching to see what he would do. Baofu asked as instructed. Yishan then struck him.
Baofu caught the staff and gave it another shove; Yishan then returned to his quarters. Baofu went back and reported this to the Master (Dongshan).
The Master said, "I have always suspected this fellow. Nevertheless, do you recognize Deshan?
As Pufu hesitated, the Master struck him.
Yantou Quanhuo said, "Deshan usually relies only on the single staff before him; even if a Buddha were to come, [he would strike him with it]."
[He] struck him. "Even since his arrival, I have struck him; yet how regrettable that there is still this slight discrepancy! Ziyun Qi said:
"As for Linji’s statement, 'I have always suspected this fellow,' was this an expression of approval or disapproval? Or is there some other principle involved?"
Wujindu said: "How could a crossbow of a thousand *jin* pull its trigger for a mere mouse?

It is not that [the speed of] rushing currents passing a blade or blazing flames overtaking the wind does not exist; yet, had the two elders scrutinized this thoroughly, they would have deserved thirty blows themselves."
Why is this? If the head does not lead with vigor, it brings misfortune upon the entire army.
The Xiongnu chieftain prides himself on skills that surpass others; the minor general’s instructions for his departure seemed authentic.
Upon reaching the enemy, he indeed achieved a small victory, yet upon returning, he could not avoid losing his entire body. (Haixin Xin)
It is like a young parrot in a golden cage, bound as if by a single green robe of red jade.
Although it has learned to speak the words of humans, when questioned, it fundamentally knows nothing at all.
(Fojian Qín) Linji asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Dingzhou. The Master raised his staff; the monk hesitated, and the Master [struck him].
[The Master] struck him. The monk refused to accept it. The Master said, "In the future, you will encounter those with clear eyes. Later, the monk went to visit Sansheng;
as soon as he brought up the previous conversation, Sansheng struck him. The monk hesitated, and Sansheng struck him again.
Tiantong Hua said: "If Linji and Sansheng had possessed a 'turning-over' phrase at that time, the descendants of later generations would not have been reduced to nothingness.
He suddenly took up his staff, said, "There is yet another one—where does it go? and then struck the ground once with it.
Yuan'an Yu said: "The spring on the bamboo leads down through the bamboo; the flowers east of the ravine bloom red west of the ravine.
Guangjiao Yu said: "Everyone says this monk lacks vigor. Had he waited for Linji to raise his staff, he would have immediately overturned the meditation seat.
Not only would he have cut off Linji's tongue, but he could also have been a fellow student of Sansheng. Little do they realize that both these elders...
He was seen through by him.
The Han Emperor looked on from afar with pity for his slender willow camp; indeed, when the tally arrived, he could not help himself. Alas for the guests of the Jinwu Guard who come and go;
having lost their tally, they further suffer the loss of their troops. (Bailin Ge)
Linji addressed the assembly: "Those who seek the Dharma do not shrink from losing their bodies or forfeiting their lives.
At the place of my former teacher, I asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma three times and was struck three times, like being brushed by a bundle of mugwort.
Now, if I were to think of another blow, who would be willing to deal it? A monk stepped forward and said, 'I will deal it. The Master [raised] his staff."
Dudu gave [the staff] to the assembly. As the assembly reached out to receive it, the Master struck him.
Cui峰 Xian said, "To let go was perilous; to pull back was too hasty.
Wuzu Ji said, "Linji is much like a poor man thinking of his old debts. Chengtian Zong said, "But tell me, what is this staff Linji uses today?"
"Is this the same as the staff he received back then, or is it different? If you say they are the same, you betray Huangbo.
If you say they are different, you wrong Linji. But if his full potential were exhausted [in that moment], tell me, on whose side would it lie?
He then took up his staff and said, "Step back! Step back! Tiantong Huo said: "The underlying meaning of Linji receiving the staff three times—"
