Afterward, the chaos follows the names as they fall to the ends of the earth.
(Ci-hang Pu) It is as if one reaches for the heavens to demand a high price, yet remains vaguely bound to the earth to repay the debt.
When one finally steps out to look at the river’s head, two children are playing with a ferry boat. (Yun-han Yin)
A single glance requires no laborious application of rouge and powder; Xuan Sha’s broom brushes on the蛾眉 (arched brows).
Knowing only how to conceal Lingyun’s ugliness, he fails to realize that once the eyebrows have fallen away, one knows nothing at all.

(Puweng Xian) Upon seeing a peach blossom, he immediately dodges and retreats; Iron Encircling Mountain has sunk him so there is no way out. Leaning against walls and huddling by sides, he knows only too well [the futility of his efforts].
Little. Once spring arrives, the soul is severed once more.
(Muzhou of Shaoshi) On the Flower-Falling Terrace, brocade is spread anew; Before the Agate Steps, vermilion sand is laid down.
Humanity and righteousness are entirely severed where there is poverty; Worldly sentiments lean toward those with wealth. (Wumiao of Gaofeng)
Wandering aimlessly for willows, my feelings are restless; Treading upon peach blossoms, my eyes alone are red. Blown weary through the gardens, spring has already faded;
How can I bear the eastern wind drumming from across the shore?
(Falin’s second rhyme) A fierce tiger blocking the path, I am startled in secret; Meeting on a narrow road, how could we contend? My bitter heart, piece by piece, leaves no witness.
He cried out: "Outside the mountain ranges, one hears especially the sound of wailing in grief.
Because Changsheng asked Lingyun, "What was it like before the primordial chaos had divided? the Master replied, "The pillar is pregnant."

[The student] asked, "What is it like after this division? The Master said, "It is like a fragment of cloud appearing in the vast void. [The student] asked, "As for that vast void itself, does it still receive the appearance of clouds or not?
The Master did not answer. [The student] asked, "If that is so, then living beings do not come forth? The Master likewise did not answer.

[The student] asked, "When one reaches the state where there is pure clarity and no trace of clouds, what is it then? The Master said, "That is still merely the flow of eternal constancy (*zhenchang liuzhu*)."
[The student] asked, "What is this 'true, constant flow'? The Master said, "It is like a mirror that is always bright. [The student] asked, "I do not yet know:
is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "There is. [The student] asked, "What is this thing beyond?
The Master said, "Break the mirror and then I will see you."
Bazhao Che said, "Meeting face-to-face, it is simply that—enough. He further asked, "What is the point of breaking the mirror?
Baizhao Yuan said, "If you do not break the mirror, how can there be a meeting? Taiyang Xuan said, "It has already been broken right now. Furthermore, how do you meet face-to-face?
He then said, "The illumination is exhausted and the essence has no dependence; throughout the entire body, it is difficult to discern. Kaifu Ning said:
The entire world of the ten directions is a single mirror. How can one speak of the principle of "breaking it"?

Even if you have eyes that see clearly and hands that act with immediacy—such that both light and mirror are forgotten, like a hen brooding her eggs, where pecking and hatching occur simultaneously—you are precisely the one who deserves to be struck by Baozi’s staff.
Why? Because Zen practitioners who merely play with shadows are as numerous as hemp and millet. Zhaojue Qin said: "One."
One person is skilled at questioning; another is skilled at answering. Let us set aside for now the idea that they are like glue and lacquer meeting, or water and milk blending together.
But tell me: when the mirror is shattered, how do they see one another? After a long silence, he clapped his hands and said, "Finished. Tiantong Jue said:
"Whether divided or undivided, the jade mechanism moves in the night. Whether struck or unstruck, the golden shuttle is cast in secret. It is directly a single color, pure."
Qing said, "I have not yet attained the tenfold perfection; I sit steadily for now. But tell me, after the mirror is shattered, where do we meet?
"In the clear autumn, after the old hare has swallowed the light; at the moment the azure dragon sheds its bones from the limpid waters.
Huanglong Zhong said, "According to Muan’s realization, what need is there to speak of whether the primordial chaos was divided or undivided, or whether the mirror was shattered or not shattered?"
Even if you were to understand it at the place where a pillar conceives, it would still be but a single cloud dotting the vast clarity of the sky. Do you truly comprehend this?
Wait until empty space falls to the ground, and then I shall speak to you.
A golden rooster pecks at a jade egg; a phoenix chick flies forth. Entering the door, it lets out a long cry; returning home, it dons its brocade robe.
(Fujian Qín) At midnight, frost gathers and the stars grow cold; the vast sky clears of clouds as the mountain moon sets. Among all those who receive the blow upon the blue heavens—

Know this! When the Azure Dragon sheds its bones, who can perceive it? When the Golden Phoenix bursts through the jade lock-gate, when the Qilin snaps the golden tether—far beyond the kalpas, who could possibly restrain it? North, south, east, and west, it stands utterly transcendent.
(Chengtianzong) Once, when a monk asked Lingyun, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? the Master held up his whisk and said, "He has appeared."
"How is it after the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master also held up his whisk. The monk did not accept this. He went to Xuefeng and recounted the previous conversation.
Xuefeng asked, "Do you accept him? The monk said, "I do not. Xuefeng said, "Ask me, and I will tell you.
The monk asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? Xuefeng held up his whisk. [The monk asked again,] "How is it after he appeared in the world? Xuefeng...
He set down his whisk. The monk bowed, and Feng struck him. Later, the monk went to Xuansha and recounted the previous conversation.
Xuansha asked, "How do you understand this? The monk said, "I do not understand. Xuansha said, "Let me give you a parable: Suppose a man buys a plot of land;
he has already completed all the legal contracts for its boundaries to the east, west, south, and north. Yet, in the center of it, there remains a tree."
It was still within my reach.
When Yunmen Wenyan held up two upright whisks, he said: "The front one is it; the back one does not hit. Guishan Zhe said:
"This monk has drawn a bow and prepared two arrows, intending to overturn the world. Yet, when he reached the presence of Xuansha..."
Beforehand, not a single skillful maneuver could be deployed. Why? Because "Though the crane has the Nine Gao heights, its wings find it hard to soar;
though the horse lacks the thousand-li stride, it vainly pursues the wind."
A monk asked Lingyun, "What is it to sit upright and contemplate the true mark? The Master said, "Losing a coin in the river, one must fish for it in the river.
Losing a coin in the river, one must fish for it in the river. When brought forth, it is used freely and expansively throughout the world; with the clouds, one buys up the Southern Mountain."
The ground is shallowly sown and deeply weeded, plowed at will. (Buddha-mind is merely...
When Lingyun was asked by a monk, "What is it to return to the root and attain the essential meaning? the Master said, "Long ago I forgot;
I do not recall the arising of dust."
The family is ruined and the people are gone; on what can one rely? Without mind and without possessions, I seek a place to return.
For ten years I have forgotten the path by which I came; though I briefly recall this moment, I know nothing at all.
(Touzi Qing) Lingyun asked a monk, "Where are you going? He replied, "I am going to Xuefeng. The Master said, "I have a letter to send to Xuefeng."
Feng asked, "Have you attained it? The monk replied, "Please, then. The Master took off one sandal and tossed it before him; the monk then departed.
Upon arriving at Xuefeng, Feng asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Lingyun. Feng asked, "Is the Master well?
He said, "I have a message for him to deliver. Feng asked, "Where is it? The monk took off one sandal and tossed it before Feng; Feng then ceased questioning.

Taisu Xiu said: "Since Xuefeng was unable to discern the true nature of the monk's message, and this monk, moreover, only knew how to imitate a model and leave him stumped, had Lingyun suddenly said at that time: 'I have a letter to send him.'"
The monk said, "I request [instruction]. Lingyun merely took his seat. How could that monk have failed to communicate clearly?
A true man acting for others should not leave another unable to utter a single word. Baryak Pu said: "That monk and Lingyun communicated on equal terms;
he sent it back in its original seal, not daring to add a single character of his own. Yet, how regrettable that Xuefeng’s letter was also received."
[This is] understood. It is simply that one does not open the seal to look inside; one knows what kind of mental activity Xuefeng possessed.
When a monk asked Lingyun, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? the Master said: "The donkey's business is not yet finished, and the horse's business has already arrived."
The donkey’s business is not yet finished when the horse’s business arrives; as soon as the sound of the bell ceases, the drum beats on.
The Patriarch loves to eat *harō* rice; to the north lies Wenshu at Mount Wutai.
(Fohuiquan) Going eastward one sees no benefit in going west; in the south they sell cheaply, while in the north they sell dear. Calculating the river in thousands across and hundreds up and down.
Sha. Ninety-nine turns into eighty-two. (Baoning Yong) The shade of pines extends beyond the path;
sparse rain falls at no fixed hour. How many cycles of rise and fall have there been in the affairs of the world? Yet those who dwell among the mountains remain unaware.
(Meng’an Cong) Chan Master Huìjué of Guāngxiào Monastery in Yángzhōu (a successor of Zhòuzhōu Shèn) went to Fǎyǎn’s place. Fǎyǎn asked, “Where have you recently come from?
The Master replied, “Zhòuzhōu. Fǎyǎn said, “I have heard that Zhòuzhōu has the ‘Pine Tree’ koan; is this true? The Master said, “Yes.”
"No," he said. "Everyone who comes and goes says there is. How can you, Venerable Elder, say there is not? The Master said, "The former master truly did not say such a thing.
Do not slander the former master, Reverend. Nanquan said, "A true lion cub!"
Jingshan Hongzhao said: "If you say these words exist, you miss Jue’s Iron Ladle;
if you say these words do not exist, you miss Fayan. If you avoid both sides, you miss Zhaozhou.
Even if you do none of these things and have another way of penetration, you will enter hell like a shot arrow. Gushan Huiguo said: "Jue’s Iron..."
"This is called 'attaining without emptiness. It is simply that he never once dreamed of Zhaozhou. Xiaoyan Bao said: "Fayan lost one of his eyes at that time.
For Jue to speak in such a manner is also to fail to support Zhaozhou. Falin Yin said:
"He flees from the pit only to fall into the moat."
Few know that Zhaozhou had no words; those who see him are rare north and south of the river. Where are the peach blossoms of the mountain temple now?
Meeting him, one can only cherish the poems of Master Bai.
(Da-hong Sui) Scorched by the sun and buffeted by the wind, his solitary shadow remains—Zhaozhou once pointed to the tree leaning against the courtyard. The Great and Small Qingliang of Shengyuan.
Old man! You have not yet understood that the former master did not lack these words.
(Zhengjue Yi) Who says the former master lacked these words? The scorched-tail tiger is originally a tiger; the hornet does not cling to its old nest.
How could a fierce general die at home? Watch closely! Look back! If you understand how to cut off the flow, where will you go?
Depart! A pure breeze rises with every step you take. (Huitong Dan) What is most precious about a celestial messenger?
It lies in being able to respond well in debate. Not only will you remain unsullied, but the state’s altars of soil and grain may yet be preserved.
(Seal: As Accomplished) One path leads to Xiangxiang, one to Qin. A single word at this parting makes one deeply sorrowful.
Since the mountains and waters divided their domains, who among travelers can avoid asking for the ford? (Cai Shangrong)
Venerable Yanyang of Xinxing in Hongzhou (a successor of Zhaozhou Shen), while studying under Zhaozhou, asked:
"What is it like when one brings nothing at all? Zhaozhou said, "Set it down. The Master said, "When I bring nothing at all, what is there to set down?
Zhaozhou said, "If you cannot set it down, carry it away. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Regarding the "Superior Fruit," under the first question, the commentary states: "Cradling the stolen goods while crying out for innocence. Under the subsequent statement, the commentary states:
"Alas! Alas! Master Xiangyun said: "Zhaozhou was forging iron at the furnace; Yan Yang brought disaster upon himself.
Although he attained awakening, it would have been better had this good thing never happened."
Not a single thing can be brought forth; the two shoulders cannot bear the weight. Suddenly realizing one's error beneath a word, the heart is filled with boundless joy.
Once malice and evil are cast from the mind, even snakes and tigers become friends. Though many hundreds of years have passed, the pure breeze has not yet ceased.
(Huanglong Nan): Shifting high to occupy the low, he wields his sovereign authority; the gates of liberation open—how pitiable!
Without the true, wondrous secret of the King of Emptiness, one is dragged along by sounds and forms as they arise. (Zhenjing Wen)
It does not hinder one’s progress to yield the first move with subtlety; yet when one realizes the mind is coarse, there is shame for having struck one's own head.
When the board is broken and the axe-handle at the waist has rotted away, one washes clean the ordinary bones to roam together with the immortals.
(Tiantong Ju) Presenting the pivot face-to-face is no ordinary matter; where the slightest hair is exhausted, it is as heavy as a mountain. The heart-wrenching melody is like being in person—
Listen! The flowing water and mournful wind need not be plucked [on a lute].
(Tudu Ce) Suddenly administering a needle to the vital point below the gallbladder, at that moment there was nowhere for the whole body to lodge.
Hehe! Laughing, he entered the realm of Yan Yang; with snakes and tigers as neighbors, he cannot be sought. (Mianjie)
The earth swallows the vermilion, turning it to red soil; the granary lacks a single grain of rice, and the husks lie overturned in the mortar.
This "red poverty" makes it impossible to survive, yet others come to point a finger at one’s stolen goods.
(Zhongfeng Edition) Fragrance wafts from the cassia seeds under a full moon; raindrops fall upon the lotus as autumn reaches its midpoint. Let the seasons pass as they will outside the gate.
Change. Securely wrap yourself in your patched robe and cover your head.
(Hengchuan Hongguang) Though the remaining light is fine, the sun flows toward the west. Why toil so busily like a horse or an ox? I tell you: you cannot carry your heart and liver with you;
when you come, hang it high upon the tip of a tree branch. (Meiweng Daoguang)
Chan Master Xinjian of Wuzhou (a successor of Zhaozhou Sheng) never kept a śrāmaṇera throughout his life. A Dharma Master once said, "Master, you are advanced in years;

why do you not seek out a śrāmaṇera to attend to you? The Master replied, "If there were one who was blind in the eyes, deaf in the ears, and mute in the mouth, please find such a person for me. The Master was speechless.
Shi’an Fēng said: "It is a pity that this *zuǒzhǔ* (abbot) has a beginning but no end; he fails to manage human affairs, causing Xīnjiàn to suffer a lifetime of grievance.
If Dèqìng were acting as the *zuǒzhǔ*, when [Xīnjiàn] spoke in such a manner, he would simply say:
"There is one elder whose eyes are not blind, whose ears are not deaf, and whose mouth is not mute—do you still want him? He would wait until [Xīnjiàn] was unsettled, and then...
He lets out two sighs. Observe how he brings it to a close!
Chan Master Duofu of Hangzhou (a successor of Zhaozhou Congshen) was asked by a monk, "What is the single grove of bamboo at Duofu?
The Master said, "One stalk, two stalks, leaning. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Three stalks, four stalks, curved."
One stem, two stems, leaning askew; sparse shadows stir like dragons and serpents. My mind suspects the birth of dark specters; my failing eyes see empty blossoms.
Three stems, four stems, bending and curving; they restore to me a grove of bamboo. At times they draw in the pure breeze; fallen leaves fill the mountain valleys.

Chan Master Fushí of Zhāngzhōu (succeeded Zihu Zōng), who lacked the talent for meditation, ascended the hall and said: "This mountain monk has opened a divination shop; it can determine people's poverty or wealth and settle their life or death.
At that time, a monk stepped forward and said: "Setting aside life and death, and poverty and wealth, [what about that which] does not fall into the five [aggregates]?"
[The student] said, "I am practicing. I request that the Master guide me directly. The Master said, "Gold, wood, water, fire, and earth.

Bodhidharma’s coming from the West was merely divining for you; fortune and misfortune lie with you and do not depend on another. Within this, one simply relies on the hexagram lines to make a judgment;
how could there be such things as partiality toward the familiar or the distant? (Benjue I)

Metal, wood, water, fire, and earth—these are the numbers of the sequence from beginning to end: five, six, four, three, and two. In the first hexagram-line, the White Tiger transmits its influence. Bitter, bitter!
To obtain this hexagram in a divination means a lifetime of poverty; distant friends will not come, and the sick will die.
(Lan’an’s *Xu*) Metal, wood, water, fire, and earth—the great beast is originally a tiger. It is laughable that General Li [Li Guang] let his arrows go to waste at Lantian.
When the monk Zuo Huo came to visit Master Ruyong Yuan (a successor of Zihu Zong), the Master clapped his hands three times and said, "A fierce tiger stands in the gateway;
who is there to oppose it? Huo replied, "A swift hawk soars toward the heavens; who can catch it? The Master said:
Each was difficult to withstand. Nanquan said, "Stop for now; this public case has not yet been resolved.
The Master brandished his staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters. Nanquan was speechless. The Master said, "This fellow is dead!"
Zhaojue Qin said: "When strength rivals and power is equal, it is a fine match indeed; when eyes meet and hands respond, neither side gains any advantage.
At the end, it is a pity to let him go. When he returns to the abbot’s quarters after his dance, you should clap your hands three times and then sweep your sleeves and depart.
In this way, not only will both beginning and end be complete, but you will also avoid being subject to others' criticisms and annotations. Nevertheless, even so..."
Huikong was speechless. "Can he even turn over on his side? He speaks idly of rising early; there are still travelers on the road at night.
Daoyi Zhi said: "In strength there is one even stronger; in all the world, there is originally no number one person."
Do you understand? He has no skill at all; Pāpīyān has lost his way. Here, there is no place for you to apply your understanding.
One day, when the Chan Master Sītishan Shiti (he was a successor of Zhuyou) saw an attendant carrying an alms bowl toward the hall, he asked, "Where are you going?
The attendant replied, "I am going to the hall for the midday meal. The Master said, "How could I not know that you are going [to the hall]?"
[The Master] said, "I am going to the hall for the midday meal. [The attendant] asked, "Aside from this, what else would you say?
The Master said, "I am simply asking you about your fundamental matter. [The attendant] said, "If the Master asks about my fundamental matter, I am indeed going to the hall for the midday meal.
The Master said, "You do not fail in being my attendant."
Tiantong Jue said: "To let him go would be unacceptable. Now I must twist his nose until it aches and beat him until his bones protrude;
only then will he be spared from following the herd of blind donkeys. Thus it is said: 'On level ground there are countless dead men;
one who penetrates the thorn forest is a true master. But tell me, has this monk just now penetrated it or not?"
"Much emptiness is not as good as a little reality. Qinghua Yun said, "Having entered this gate, you must ensure your ground is stable and secure so that you can withstand the hammer and tongs.
Only after a hundred smeltings and a thousand beatings will you remain unchanged from beginning to end. As the saying goes: 'If you wish to recognize true gold, look for it in the fire.
Shiti’s acquiescence was like Lu Gong looking at his own reflection in a mirror. Why did he not give him thirty blows right then?"
A blow! Even if he were to encounter a hundred flavors of exquisite delicacies, he must first spit them out before he can succeed.
Father and son walk together through the weeds; they gallop like shooting stars and roll like lightning, with a clap of thunder.
They deceive countless men of heroic spirit, who mistake the saddle for the bridge and spend their entire lives in error. (Xin’an Chou)
Chan Master Liao Ran of Mount Moshan in Junzhou (a successor in the lineage of Guizong Changxia and Gaoyuan Yu) was once asked by Guankxi, "What is Mount Moshan?
The Master replied, "It does not reveal its crown. Guankxi asked, "Who is the master of Mount Moshan? The Master replied, "Neither male nor female.
Guankxi then shouted, "Why do you not transform yourself? The Master said, "I am neither a spirit nor a ghost; why should I transform?"
"What is it? At this, Xi bowed in submission. He served as the head gardener for three years. Zhaojue Qin said:
"Suppose someone were to ask me, 'What is Mount Mo? One looks out and sees nothing. What is the Master of Mount Mo?
He is fit to be a teacher of Buddhas and patriarchs. Why not transform yourself? You, Upāsaka, must transform yourself. [He] intended—
As he hesitated, [Dongshan] struck him across the back with his staff. Now tell me: was it Moshan or Jiangshan? When the opportunity arises, there is no partiality;
to hesitate is to be separated by a thousand mountains. Faling Yin said: "If Guanyin were still here, one would do well to devote oneself to him for three years."
Tiantong Jue said: "It is neither the form of male nor female; it emerges from the measure of existence and non-existence. It penetrates before all maneuvers and transcends above the three realms.
Exhausted yet penetrating, simple yet appropriate: the pines hold the wind and the night is cold; the stream carries the rain and the spring rises.
Lingyin Li said: "Moshan plays with the false as if it were real; he always finds this opportunity. Guankui..."
To recompense both the root and the branch, one fills one’s belly and forgets a hundred hungers; even until the phrase "soaking the hemp" is inverted and stripped away.
Before the point of a flying arrow, who can bite its tip? Do you wish to know where Mount Moshan lands?
When the great garuḍa wishes to spread its sky-reaching wings, who pays heed to the surging clouds across the six directions?
Neither male nor female, solitary and serene; the true body majestic and grand—who can reach it? Not a single word is transmitted, yet the eyes of a thousand sages behold it.
The wind stilled in the nine heavens, the moon curves its arc.
(Zidehui) Neither male nor female—this is the Master of Mount Mo. From antiquity to the present, majestic and grand, he is ever revealed alone. Ever revealed alone—he is seen!
His pure reputation spread far and wide throughout the world.
(Yuelin Guan) Chan Master Dao Wu of Guannan in Xiangzhou (a disciple of Yanguan An who constantly followed him at Guannan) was waiting outside the mountain gate with one foot raised,
wearing a leopard-skin loincloth and holding a *jiaoluo* staff, when he saw Zhaozhou approaching.
He then gave a loud shout of acknowledgment and stood there. The Governor said, "Wait upon me with careful attention. The Master gave another shout of acknowledgment and departed.
Fengshan remarked, "The Great and Small Guannan have needlessly handed over their defeat to others. Nevertheless, do you know Zhao?"
How could one from this province fail to fit within the great circle? In the Liangshan marshes they call themselves heroes, yet upon closer inspection, they are all but unprincipled men.
One blows a flute with no holes; another strums a lute with no strings. One tune, two tunes—no one understands them. After the rain has passed, the night...
The pond water is deep in autumn. (Qian’an Guang) Daowu performs a dance;
it has no set notation. If you seek it through hearing, I dare not grant you permission.
(Ye’an Xuan) Guannan sometimes held a wooden sword upon his shoulder and performed a dance. A monk asked, "Where did the sword in your hand come from?"
The Master then threw it to the ground. The monk picked it up and placed it back in the Master’s hand.
The Master asked, “Where did you get this? The monk had no reply. The Master said, “I grant you three days to produce a turning word. The monk still had no reply.
The Master then placed the sword on his shoulder and performed a dance, saying, “Only by acting like this can one succeed.”
Yunfeng Yue said: "False teachings are difficult to support. Longchi Chuan said: "Originally, even a wooden sword can kill people.
This monk once suffered the single blow of Daowu; it was not merely for three days, but until this very day he has never regained his breath.
Had he been a master of the Way, as soon as he saw the sword cast upon the ground, he would have picked it up and placed it upon his shoulder."
He performs a dance once. When the monk asks, "Where did you get this sword? he simply hurls it to the ground, waves his hand, and walks away.
Later, when a monk from Guannan asked, "What is the house style of the Master? the Master descended from his meditation seat and acted like a woman.
Baizhang bowed and said, "Thank you for coming from afar. I have nothing worthy to receive you as a guest.
The Azure Dragon lies coiled in the sea while auspicious clouds rise high; looking in the four directions, all streams return to the source like the tide.
When the wooden man comes to inquire about the affairs of the Western Palace, he returns the favor with a single peach from the Eastern Garden. (Touzi Qing)
The harvest is bountiful and the times are clear; rites and righteousness abound. Meeting one another, we accompany each other with wine and song.
Unable to drink with open hearts amidst the banquet, how can we bear this sky of wind and moon?
(Dong-sou Ying) In the famous garden, a hundred flowers bloom in profusion; the cuckoo’s cry urges on the wild chatter of swallows. Ten thousand bushels of springtime radiance cannot be hidden.
Abiding, I feel pity for the rare encounter with the Spring Lord.
(Qingmen Forest) Chan Master Juzhi of Jinhua, Wuzhou (successor to Chang of Damei under Tianlong).

When he first resided at his hermitage, a nun wearing a bamboo hat and carrying a staff circled the Master three times and said, "If you can speak the Way, I shall remove my hat. She asked this three times. The Master—
The Master had no reply, and the nun departed. The Master said, "It is already somewhat late; why do you not stay for a while? The nun replied, "If you can speak the Way, then I shall stay.
Again, the Master had no reply. After more than ten days, Tianlong arrived. The Master recounted the previous events to him.

Tianlong raised one finger and pointed it out to him. The Master attained great enlightenment. Whenever there was an inquiry or a question, he would only raise one finger. Addressing the assembly, he said, "I have attained..."
"Zen of the Single Finger of Tianlong: its benefits are inexhaustible throughout one's life.
Xuansha Shiguan said, "Had I seen him at that time, I would have broken off his finger.
Changqing Huiheng spoke on his behalf, saying, "Fine food is not for the hungry man to eat. Caoshan Benji said, "Juzhi was crude in his realization; he merely recognized..."
When one attains a single opportunity and a single realm, it is all the same—clapping hands and patting the palms. This is the marvel of that West Garden.
Baoci then raised the point, asking: "Tell me, has Jushi realized yet? If he has realized, why was his acceptance so crude and reckless?
If he has not realized, it is also said that 'a finger-pointing Zen' is inexhaustible. Tell me, what was Caoshan’s intention?
"How so? Yunju Xi said, "As for Xuansha speaking in such a manner, does he approve him or not?
Jingshan Gao cited the verse by Laye: "Juzhi’s single finger—I tell you: A hawk born this morning soars to the heavens.
Were it not for the strength to lift the tripod and pull the mountain, The black steed of a thousand li would not be easy to ride. He then said, "Juzhi..."
Langya could not provide an exhalation for him; he was nearly buried and lost. Miaoxi followed later with his own commentary:
"Juzhi’s single finger—only when one has eaten their fill of rice do they rest. Tied ten thousand strings of cash at the waist, riding a crane up to Yangzhou.
Lingyin Yue said, "Tell me, what is this 'one-finger Chan'? He then held up his whisk and said, "See!"
"Mò. If you can see this, you may walk hand-in-hand with Juiti. But if it is not yet so, I cannot help but speak another verse:
'One move higher, one step wider; cutting off the barrier of Buddhas and Patriarchs, they lose the path they came by.
Píngyáng Mín said: "Lángyá and Miàoxī merely cheered from their seats while watching the game; they did not understand."
Capturing the banner on horseback—do you all wish to know? Is it not clear where the single finger falls? Furthermore, listen as this mountain elder recites a mantra to make up for any deficiencies:
"Who does not possess the Zen of a single finger? The subtle turning of the vital pivot rests with the celestial dragons."

Eight panels of silk skirt dip and trail upon the ground; her twin eyes, painted on, rival the beauty of Chang’e.

The Way. How many travelers halt their horses to gaze?

There was once a youth named Jue-zhi who, whenever he saw someone asking him a question, would simply point his finger upward.

One day, the Master secretly tucked a knife into his sleeve and asked the boy, "I have heard that you understand the Buddha-dharma; is this true? The boy replied, "Yes. The Master asked, "What is the Buddha?"
A young boy pointed his finger at him. The Master cut off the boy's finger with a knife. The boy cried out and ran away. The Master called to the boy; the boy turned his head back.
The Master asked, "What is the Buddha? As the boy raised his hand, he no longer saw his finger, and he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
The *Qingbo Ge* says: "Juzhi obtained Tianlong’s single finger, yet for his entire life he carried a board and failed to realize it.
When the boy raised his finger later, Juzhi again had that finger severed for him. Why did he not have severed his own finger at that time, thus sparing himself from carrying a board for a lifetime?"
A single finger-joint of Jufu; a single hair plucks out nine oxen. The Flower Peak reaches the heavens in azure green;

the Yellow River flows from its very depths. Cut off the finger—suddenly turn the head. Before the green bamboo hat, there is no limit to affairs; beneath the green straw raincoat, everything ceases at once.
(Shantang Chun) Juti left Old Tianlong at a loss; holding aloft his sharp blade alone, he tested the young boy.
With but a slight lift of his hand, Guli split the myriad peaks of Mount Hua. (Wumen Kai)

if you are not a poet, do not offer your poem. Lian-an Wen asked, "Tell me, does this constitute succeeding Linji, or does it not?

Between the edges of a blade, there is not even enough space for a person to set foot. At the moment when Great Enlightenment (Dajue) and Xinghua’s staff and shouts were exchanged, how could there have been any room for thought, mind, or intellectual interpretation?

This is the principle of how Linji received the painful blows from Huangbo. He suddenly picked up his staff and said:

Too solitary, too remote; the sun blazes high. A raw jade and unrefined gold—what need for weeds?

Habitually casting aside the three-inch blade, one’s fate of floating or sinking is settled. If one merely encounters a fish, why need it be in the deep?
Ever since the candle was blown out at Longtan, Only the waning moon remains, piercing the heart of the lake.

When Emperor Zhuangzong of the Later Tang returned to the Wei-fu Palace after his visit to Hebei, he summoned Master Xinghua and asked him, "I have obtained a treasure upon taking the Central Plains, yet no one has ever offered a price for it. The Master said, "Please let Your Majesty show me this treasure.
The Emperor extended the two ends of his *pòtóu* (head-wrap) with both hands. The Master said, "Who would dare to offer a price for the treasure of a sovereign?"
Jiashan Baocai then said: "Now tell me, did Xinghua approve of Zhuangzong or not? If he approved, where were Xinghua’s eyes?
If he did not approve, where lay Zhuangzong’s fault? Cui峰 Xian said: "To the point."
What the Venerable One has attained can only be observed from the side. Were it not for one who is a master capable of transforming others, they would often have to pay a high price for it.

"At that time, Xinghua made one move that could be called 'drunk with wine. How would you judge it today? Huanglong Xin said: "Xinghua..."
He manifested for a single lifetime, acting according to the capacity of his audience. Alas, how could he have known that this Son of Heaven would be buried and forgotten?

At that time, he should simply have said: "The pearl of the oyster has been recovered, yet it is of no use. He should have taught him to find another livelihood in the future, so as to avoid mutual stagnation.

Now, if someone were to ask me, how would I appraise its value? —Xiaoyan (Xixian) Chan Master* *Note: The original text contains the name "Xiaoyan" (笑巖), which refers to the Ming dynasty Chan master Xixian Zhixian (西溪智賢). This commentary reflects his pedagogical style.*
Baoyun said: "A true king can indeed produce, speak, and act with mastery. Xinghua, a master of clear eyes, was also well able to distinguish and repay his debt while sharing the seat.

If I were to act as a catalyst for transformation, I would wait until the Emperor had fully extended the legs of his official head-wrap, and then say directly:

"Your Majesty, how can you preach the true formula while selling counterfeit medicine? In that instant, I would cause him to exhaust all views of subjectivity and objectivity and forget all attachment to precious things.

Not only would this lead the Sovereign to attain great liberation, but it would also spare the world from merely receiving echoes within the gateway of light and shadow, allowing them instead to find their livelihood there.

Boshanlai said: "A jade disc of a foot in diameter, or a pearl bright enough to illuminate an entire carriage—compared to the radiance of the Central Plains, these may perhaps not even be worth a fraction.
Mañjuśrī’s precious crown cannot conceal it; Vimalakīrti’s room of ten feet square cannot contain its manifestation;
and Xinghua, in the end, could not offer a price for it. Even so, who says that gold is like mere dross? Ping.

After a long silence, he said, "Pity that three-foot dragon-whiskers are called nothing more than a piece of ordinary tattered cloth."
The treasures of a sovereign king are indeed difficult to repay; Xinghua manifested form and speech as a single stroke of genius.
With both hands he spread out the ends of his official cap, and the imperial edict hung suspended from the Phoenix Pavilion.

A treasure of the Central Plains appearing at Xinghua—this single segment of radiance is difficult to price. His imperial enterprise can serve as a teacher for ten thousand generations;
like a golden wheel, his majesty governs the four quarters of the world (Tiantong Jue).

Shoushan Nian said: "Look at how Xinghua employs [the shout] in this way; why does he let him pass?

"Which one is the master? Nevertheless, you must still be careful. He further said, "Both have faults; both are without fault.

Not using the Makara gate to bar the heavy doors; light and darkness are divided by a single shout. The yellow bird calls back the woodcutter from his dream;

Tiantong Hua said: "Among the assembly, some deliberate that 'escaping into the ancient temple' refers to one's own self prior to the empty kalpa;

This cannot help but invite the derision of bystanders. If one were to ask me, the mountain monk:

His vital strength was not yet declined, so he was able to capture him alive.

The Senior Monk Ding (the Dharma heir of Linji Xuan) was returning from a meal at the Prefectural Office when he sat down on a bridge.
Three presiding masters arrived; one of them asked, "What is it like to reach the very bottom of the deep waters of Chan?
The Master seized him and prepared to throw him over the bridge. The other two masters hurried forward and pleaded, "Stop, stop! Do not take offense at our interruption."
[The Master] sat. He said, "I hope you will show me some compassion. The Master replied, "If it were not for these two presiding masters, I would have driven them to their ultimate exhaustion.
Ling'an asked, "The very life of the Venerable Ding is now in the hands of the two presiding masters."
When the Venerable Huo (the successor of Linji Xuan) arrived at Baizhang, Baizhang said, "Dharma brother, may I ask you something?
The Master replied, "Fortunately, this is not a matter of words; why must you prattle on? Baizhang said, "Having secured Annam, you still worry about the north of the pass.
The Master thrust open his chest and said, "Is it thus? Or is it not thus? Baizhang said, "Nevertheless, it is difficult to grasp. He wanted—*yào*.
Furthermore, it is difficult to conceive. The Master said, "If you know, you have attained it; if you know, you have attained it.
Yangshan Huiji said, "If there were someone who could discern where these two men have fallen, they would be truly extraordinary.
If one cannot distinguish this, it is much like losing one's way at midday. Jiangshan Zhiqin said, "Baizhang sat alone atop the summit of Mount Daxiong."
The wind of coughing arose; Zen travelers from the four quarters retreated upon seeing the precipice. For what reason did Upper Seat Huo arrive?
He went straight until his bow was broken and his arrows exhausted.
When Upper Seat Huo arrived at Deshan, as soon as Deshan saw him, he descended from his meditation seat and made a gesture of unfolding his sitting mat. Master—
[The Master] said: "Setting this aside for a moment, suppose you suddenly encounter a person for whom mind and environment are as one;
what would you say to them so as not to be censured by those of all quarters? Sanshan said: "That would still leave them three steps behind where they were yesterday.
You must act as a true master yourself. The Master then gave a shout. Sanshan remained silent. The Master said: "I have stuffed the throat of that old wild fox!"
Huishan Daoyou said, "Although Master Huo gained the advantage, what can he do? It is like covering one's ears while stealing a bell.
Jiangshan Foyin said, "With a single shout, Master Huo made guest and host clearly manifest. Deshan’s 'No Words' has spread throughout the world; Old Huishan..."
This son is adding frost to snow. Examining his conduct from beginning to end, he must not be let off. Thereupon, he threw down his staff.

One day, while Chen Cao, the Prefect of Muzhou (also known as the Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; see the entry on Muzhou Ming), was ascending the tower with his subordinates, he saw several monks passing by.
An official remarked, "Those coming here are all traveling monks. The Prefect said, "They are not."
He asked, "How do you know it is not? The Official said, "Wait until he comes; I shall examine him. After a short while, the monk arrived before the tower.
The Official suddenly called out, "Upādhyāya! and the monks all raised their heads. The Official said to the assembled officials, "I told you so."
Taisu Zhe said: "The Minister may truly be said to hold the sun and moon of Confucius in his hands and wear the golden seal of Vairocana at his waist.
Not only are the Confucian scholars struck with awe, but even the monastics are left at a loss. Have you not heard it said that when the opportunity arises, he is like a flash of lightning?"
"Only then can he avoid dwelling in sickness amidst the reeds. Tiantong Jue said, "Minister Chen Cao was a 'white-clawed thief' (a master thief);
he could not deceive Changlu by even a single point. Gushan Yong said, "This monk’s reason is difficult to vindicate; though he is dead, one does not offer condolences for him.
The Minister presses his sword against the gate—who would dare look at him with a direct eye? Tongxuan Qi said, "The Minister may indeed be called..."

Skilled at discerning good and ill fortune, he changes people’s very eyes in the midst of the clamor. Although this monk raises his head and calls it marvelous, it is a pity that he remains equally subject to grievance.
With a single word one leaves the nest; with a thousand births one emerges from the entanglements. Last night the wind and snow were fierce; the tree broke before the cliff.
(Xuetang’s Verse): Having grasped the foremost mallet of Mount Sumeru, how could those with copper heads and iron brows contain him?
As the salt and plum, the oars and rudders, and the rain that nourishes the world—who else could it be but this man? (Fufan’s Seal)
Jixian once appraised Uqiu Zi; though he followed his every transformation, the changes were so subtle as to be indistinguishable, and he utterly failed to escape.
He was bested by one gazing from a high tower, whose vision was so piercingly clear it could discern the finest autumn hair.
(Xutang Yu) The Minister asked a monk, "May I ask you something? The monk replied, "Shut your dog's mouth. The official then—
He pinched his own mouth and said, "This one [the speaker] has committed a transgression. [The Master] said, "One who knows their fault must surely reform it.
The Official said, "May I beg the *ācārya* for his mouth so that I may eat rice?
He thus poured out all the matters concerning the gate; he simply wished to walk together through the weeds. Grasping arms, there was no need for further admonition.
Entrustment. With heels planted on the ground, one moves freely in all directions.
(Suan-an Ding) While at the Shangshu Study, he held up a sesame cake and asked a monk, "Is there such a thing as this in Jiangxi and Hunan?"
[The Master] asked, "What did the monk just eat? The official replied, "He struck the bell to thank for the resonance.
Yingshan Yin said, "This monk is like a swift falcon soaring toward the sky; he arrives with great speed and ease. Yet, alas, in the end, he falls into its net.
As for saying 'he struck the bell to thank for the resonance'—how would you respond to this? Why does he not say 'grass'?"
The rebels were utterly defeated.
The Minister asked Muzhou, "What sutra are you studying? Zhou replied, "The Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
The Minister said, "It was translated during the Six Dynasties; which dynasty’s version are you studying? Zhou held it up and said, "All conditioned phenomena..."
Like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, or a shadow—wondrous as the translations transmitted from the Six Dynasties. Yet, to the very end, one has not awakened to the aperture of that time.
One must believe that the aged phoenix in the branches, when spring arrives, instead calls out like a yellow oriole. (Zhengtang Bian)
*Zongjian fali*, Scroll Twenty-Six;
*Zongjian fali*, Scroll Twenty-Seven.
Compiled by Jiyun Tang.
Chan Master Huiyong of Nanuan in Ruzhou (the successor of Xinghua Jiang), the seventh generation descendant of Dajian, ascended the hall and said:

"Those from all quarters possess only the eye of 'simultaneous pecking and hatching,' but they do not possess the function of 'simultaneous pecking and hatching. A monk then asked, "What is simultaneous pecking and hatching?"
The Master said, "A master of the Way does not wait for the pecking and the hatching; when the pecking and hatching occur simultaneously, both are lost.
The monk said, "This is still not where I was asking. The Master said, "And how would you answer where you were asking? The monk said, "Lost. The Master then struck him.
The monk did not accept this.

Cuiyan Zhen said: "To calculate strategy within the tent is to decide victory a thousand *li* away. Although Nanyuan deployed his full capacity against the enemy, alas, the terrain was vast and the men were few.
Weishan Zhe said: "Nanyuan held high the patriarchal seal, seizing and relinquishing as the occasion required.

This monk was well able to face the front and resist the attack, yet how could he avoid his strength being exhausted and his stratagems coming to an end? Is there anyone present now who possesses the original [capacity]?"
“Is there any patch-robed monk here? Come forth and meet with Dayang! It is not for the sake of stirring up a clamor;
it is because I value that the ancestral wind not fall into decline. If there is none, then today Dayang is much like one who seeks battle but achieves no merit. Yunju Wu said:
"What is the eye of simultaneous pecking and hatching? If the eye attains clarity, its function is naturally complete. It is also said: "The master does not peck and hatch;
he loses [the opportunity] when pecking and hatching are simultaneous. Why does he not peck and hatch? Therefore it is said:
"If the child lets out a roar, the mother perishes immediately. Can you still see this clearly? Falin-yin said: "This was all a temporary arrangement devised by Nan-yuan."

It is indeed extraordinary; yet, alas, the striking monk does not grasp it. This monk exerts himself to the utmost for the sake of the assembly, striving with reckless disregard for his own person, but he cannot avoid falling into a pit or a trench.

If one were to wait for him to say, "I possess only the eye of simultaneous pecking and hatching, but I do not possess the function of simultaneous pecking and hatching," then one would simply say, "Shut that prisoner's mouth!
Even if Nan-yuan were to employ his full mechanism of granting and seizing, it would still be so.
"Three thousand *li* apart—if the son lets out a roar, the mother perishes immediately and everything returns to the son; throughout the ten directions, all is unobstructed.
When the Great Function manifests, the principle is natural; why must you stir the mind to create artificial forms? If you still do not understand, here is Yunju’s staff. (Yunju Wu)
Do not treat the Buddha-dharma as mere human sentiment; exhaustively examine the "ghost-eyes" of all quarters.
Even if one is a master who does not wait for the "pecking and hatching," one still mistakenly fixes upon the markings on the scale-pan.
(Xiaowen Kan) It is easy to summon a snake, but difficult to dismiss it; once dismissed, who knows it might turn back again? Having recognized this snake, one must be able to transform it.
He manifested a transformation; thus, he lowered his staff and sent him down to the high sandbar (as recorded in the *Wuming Jing*).
Later, while at the assembly of Yunmen, that monk heard two monks raise this story. One monk asked, "At that time, why did Nan-yuan’s staff break?
Suddenly, the monk attained enlightenment. He then hurried back to pay his respects, but the Master had already passed away.
He then went to visit Fengxue. Fengxue asked, "Are you the monk who at that time asked the former master about the story of the 'simultaneous pecking and hatching'?
He replied, "I am. Fengxue said, "How did you understand it then? He replied, "It was as if I were walking within the shadow of a lamp. Fengxue said, "You have understood."
Langye Jue said: "This monk understands how to hoist the banner of surrender, but he does not understand how to seize the sword and halberd.
Cuiyan Zhen quoted Fengxue’s words, saying: "At that time, had I waited for this monk to attempt to offer a rebuttal, I would have struck him across the mouth with my sitting cloth."
Jingyin Cheng said, "The entire army achieved victory; it was like grass bowing before the wind. Nan’uan’s lion-like pounce on the rabbit likewise exerted his full strength.
Wuwei Zhongzhe said, "Great indeed was Fengxue, yet he used foul water to douse others.
Daopi was not like this; at that time, I was as if walking within the shadow of a lamp, and I could have simply said to him: 'First...'"
"The Master’s flesh is still warm! You have such a view as this! With his staff, he struck him down from the Dharma Hall, sparing him the shame of betraying Nan-yuan.
Dongchan Guan said: "To uphold Nan-yuan's school, one must credit Fengxue.
While people everywhere often say that he approved of this monk, they fail to realize that this monk was actually pushed by him into a ten-thousand-fathom pit."
[The Master] said: "Li'an asked, 'When the total capacity meets and overcomes [the opponent], it is like grass bowing down before the wind.

To uphold the supreme纲宗 (gāngzōng) of the lineage, one must indeed be an old man like Nan-yuan. This monk later attained enlightenment; he only knew how to surrender and submit, but did not understand how to seize the banner and slay the generals.
At that time, Feng-xue should have waited for him to say 'Yes,' and then struck him out with a continuous series of blows. This monk—

One might as well establish a separate life-span [for this teaching], so as to spare future generations from groping for it within the shadows of a lamp. [The Master] suddenly brandishes his staff and says:
"If there is anyone today who can act as the patron for this monk, come forth and meet with this staff! If there is none, today we have lost ground."
Simultaneity and the sequence of pecking and hatching do not occur at the same time; even sparks from flint and flashes of lightning are still too slow.
Now you have already realized how one walks within the shadow of the lamp; to let this slip by is not to seize the advantage.

(Yangshan Qin) Sacrificing one's life to leave the Phoenix Palace, one seeks the Dragon Court to serve the state. How can one merely emulate those scholar-officials who grow old behind a window, studying but a single classic?
(Chuyuan Yin) Nan-yuan ascended the hall and said: "Upon this lump of red flesh, one stands ten thousand fathoms high.

A monk asked, "Is it not you, Master, who said that upon this lump of red flesh one stands ten thousand fathoms high? The Master replied, "Yes. The monk then overturned the meditation seat. The Master—
The Master said, "This fellow is like a blind donkey causing chaos. When the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.
Jingshan Daoyuan said, "I now guarantee for you that this matter shall never be in vain. Tiantong Huayan said, "This too is like inviting a thief to ruin one's house;
had it not been for this monk’s daring to pull at the tiger's whiskers, how could we have seen Nan-yuan’s sweat?"
The horse’s merit is great. Although this is so, let us further provide another path: Upon the bare flesh-ball, it stands ten thousand fathoms high.
If a monk comes forth, strike him across the spine. Why? Because it is the sword that kills and the sword that gives life. Lingyin Yue said:
This monk has a single-minded resolve and a small heart with great courage. Even Nan-yuan was a karmic connection for him as a foster child. Tian-ning Qi said:
"This monk dares to scratch an itch on the head of a venomous snake and strip off the scales from under the chin of a blue dragon.
Who would not admire his great courage? It is only that at the end, he lacked one move. Since leaving the cave, there has been no rival; he has gained the advantage."
When one encounters others, be generous toward them. Yunju Zhuang said, "Under a heavy reward, there will surely be brave men.
Qingshan Xiu said, "This monk was on the verge of completing a nine-cubit mountain, yet he lacked the final basket of earth.
Zhufeng Kun said, "This monk is like one who has climbed a hundred-foot tower; he is missing only a single step. Baoying, though he exerted his utmost strength...
To hold it up is still to dabble in the perils atop the pole;

to cradle the sun and moon in one’s palms, to cover gold coins with the tongue, to stand like a sheer cliff ten thousand fathoms high, and for the radiance of the hair-tip to pierce through to the Brahma Heaven—all these are but further complications.

(Gushan Gui): Upon this lump of red flesh, one must act with intimacy. When host and guest each have their own logic, neither can prevail. Two hunchbacks meet; nowadays, there are no upright people in the world. (Jingshan Gao): Upon this lump of red flesh, one must act with intimacy.
When host and guest each have their own logic, neither can prevail. Two hunchbacks meet; nowadays, there are no upright people in the world.
Within the flash of lightning, the monastic and the lay are distinguished; without violating even a hair’s breadth [of the rules], they cause the entire lineage to be extinguished.
(Mukan Egen) The sun and moon lose their light as the air of slaughter floats; the celestial war-drums resound as the *pīxiu* beasts go to battle.
With cries of victory, the true frontier generals are captured; which young man would not lift his head? (Xutang Wuyi)
Once the golden shaft was drawn, he secretly marveled at its wonder; shifting his stance, he encountered the thunderbolt mechanism once more.

Chu Hsiang used the extraordinary to flee the Red Emperor; the Han army seized the momentum to invade the entirety of Qi. Striking when the enemy did not expect it, attacking where they were unprepared—lost in Dongyang, yet gained in Xi.
Such are the wiles of these two men from Puzhou; let them go on deceiving one another face-to-face with their reflections. (Tian'an Sheng)
The setting sun over the level sands in the great wilderness to the west; the stones upon the ridges are high and then low again.
Gū Láng, in his arrogance toward the enemy, forgot to look back; he fell into the other's ranks and lost his way at the end of the path.
Nányuàn asked a monk, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "Wáng Shàngshū and Lǐ..."
The Vice President asked, "What is the meaning? The Master said, "The ox-head faces south; the horse-head faces north.
Jingshan Daoyuan said, "The first answer was appropriate; the second answer was not.
Mingyin Huai said, "When Miaoxi spoke thus, did he satisfy Nan Yuan’s intent or not?"
A monk asked Nan-yuan, "The sun and moon alternate in their passing, and cold and heat shift in succession. What is that which does not involve cold or heat?
The Master said, "Purple silk tied around the forehead, embroidered skirts at the waist. The monk said, "I have now understood the higher mechanism."
"How do those of middling and inferior capacity understand this? The Master said, "Hide yourself within a charcoal storehouse.
Huiqiu Long remarked, "The question already possesses the essential principle, and the answer likewise startles the multitude.

Nevertheless, Nan-yuan only knew how to observe the faculties and respond to the occasion, administering medicine according to the illness; Huiqiu provides yet another path. What is it that does not involve the cold?"
Regarding "The Heat": "Deep within the snow of the village ahead, last night a single branch blossomed. The upward-turning mechanism has now been made clear;
how shall those of middling and inferior capacity understand it? "Buying a hat to fit the head. Kongsheng said:

"Although Nan-yuan’s 'upward' presentation was fully raised without involving the subtle and mysterious, it was nonetheless clever yet迂 (yū—pedantic/roundabout) and added much rouge and powder. Today..."
A question was asked: "The sun and moon alternate in their passing, and cold and heat shift in succession. What is it that does not involve itself with cold and heat?
The mud-judge in the village of three households has already been understood regarding the upward-moving pivot; how, however, can those of middling and inferior capacity comprehend this?
Matters of great importance cannot be entrusted to you; minor affairs each must attend to themselves.
With a purple silk head-wrap and embroidered waist-skirt, her grace and elegance surpass those of the state of Qin.
A jade flute tucked away so no one can see it, she blows forth the spring of the Phoenix Tower deep into the night. (Xuetang Xing)
When a monk came to visit Nan-yuan, as soon as he entered the abbot’s quarters, Nan-yuan pointed his finger and said, "Defeated!
The Master picked up his staff and handed it to the monk; as the monk was about to take it, the Master struck him.
Yunfeng Yue said: "This monk has light upon his head, yet he does not know that beneath his feet he is as black as lacquer.
Even if you were to strike out in the ten directions, it would still be right to give him three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred in the evening."
A monk asked Nan-yuan, "What is it like when an ancient hall is restored? The Master said, "The roof tiles of the bright hall reach down to the eaves.
The monk said, "In that case, the adornments are fully complete. The Master said, "When the grass is cut, the snake’s head falls off."

Zhaoqing Ting said: "The poor man thinks of the treasure place, yet points his finger toward the conjured city. Should he suddenly wander off, losing both home and livelihood—what will become of him in the end?
You must know that the man who weeps over his jade has, for no reason, brought about utter ruin."
The mechanism of giving and taking—how can it be fathomed? To produce understanding based on mere words is truly pitiable.
When a spring breeze rises at dawn, it blows down three or four branches of the courtyard flowers.
(Haixin) Re-establishing the ancient hall, one discerns the wind that has come; tiles set upon the double eaves display a majestic air. It is no wonder that many have such intentions before others.
Qi! There is no such thing as a "home" within his breast.
(Xichan Ji) Nan-yuan was once asked by a monk, "Where have all the sages of the past gone?
The Master said, "If they do not ascend to heaven, they enter hell. The monk asked, "And what about you, Master? The Master replied, "Do you know Old Bao-ying?"
"Where does it land? The monk hesitated. The Master struck him across the mouth with his whisk and said, "Do you know who it is that eats the whisk?
He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The command should have been yours to carry out," and struck him once more with the whisk.
Cui Feng Xian said: "The command has already been carried out; furthermore, the whisk does not know its place of origin.

Xuedou uttered the word "blind," which was intended to add frost to snow. Huanglong Xin said: "A flaw in a white jade disk can still be polished away, but a malady in the vital organs is most difficult to treat.
This monk held the command in his hand; for what reason could he not carry it out? His transgression lies therein."
"Wherein does it lie? Jingshan Daowei said, "To weigh Linji’s Three Mysteries and Three Essentials, one must still look to Nan-yuan.
Why did Cui-feng say, "The whisk does not know its place of origin"? Miaoxi said, "Blind!"
"Furthermore, we must both see each other. Dongchan Guanzhen said, "The Master should have had that monk go;
why did you go yourself? A dull-witted person would simply say, 'The whisk is in Nan'yan's hand.
If it were so, not only would you be suppressing your own majestic light, but you would also fail to recognize Nan'yan. Xingkong said, "Although Nan'yan ordered you to go yourself, he intended—"
"Furthermore, that striking monk does not hit the mark. Tianning Qi said: "Although Cui峰 was a master with clear eyes, he still did not know where Old Baoying had landed.
Since he did not know where he had landed, why did he say, 'The whisk does not know its place of origin'?
He possessed only one eye. Miaoxi said 'blind'—this too is like a family member of the East dying."
The attendants from the western quarters assisted with the mourning.
The Master of the Southern Courtyard asked the monk, "What is your name? He replied, "Pusan. The Master said, "What would you do if you suddenly encountered a piece of excrement?
He replied, "I do not know. The Master then struck him.
Two pieces of dung, fused into a single mass; they smoke the heavens and scorch the earth—who can smell them?
For ten thousand ages, the monastic forests have used this as a point of discussion.
(Xishan Liang) Attendant Shoukuo (successor of Xinghua Jiang) asked Deshan: "Where have all the sages of the past gone? Deshan...
Xuefeng asked, "How? How? The Master said, "An imperial decree summons the flying dragon horse; a lame turtle sticks its head out. Sansheng stopped.
The next day, after bathing, the Master passed him tea. Sansheng patted the Master on the back once and said, "What about yesterday’s case?
The Master said, "This old fellow only begins to see clearly today. Sansheng stopped again.
[The monk] departs. Cui峰 Xian said: "Even refined gold must undergo a hundred smeltings; it requires the hammer of one's own true portion.
Since Deshan has already compared himself to others, this monk likewise suffers a grievance. He drew a line with his staff and said: "As for the previous case—"
[The Master] set it aside. "Where have all the sages above gone? As the assembly hesitated, he drove them out all at once.
Huanglong Nan said: "Deshan feigned deafness and dumbness; although he secretly gained the advantage, Kuo Gong covered his ears while stealing the bell."
Alas, how can one help but be ridiculed by onlookers? Taisuī Zhe said: "If one does not ascend the Dragon Gate, how can one know the vastness of the blue sea?
Even if the waves surge a thousand fathoms high, what can be done if the Dragon King pays no heed? Yunju Yuan said: "In general, for every guest there must be a host; they must be kindred spirits.
Only those who share in life and death together are fit to face the enemy. Kuo the Attendant alone—

Standing atop a rocky crag, he turns his body and strokes the tiger’s whiskers backward; Vajra Zhou sits calmly in the heart of the great ocean waves, reaching back with his hands to seize the horn of a qilin.
He draws up battle lines before Mount Dantaka and contends for the spearhead within the kingdom of Campā.
Clearly there is both loss and victory; tell me, who gains and who loses? Lingyin Yue said: "The one in front..."
This is a precipice ten thousand *ren* high; behind it lies the "blade-edge" facing the front. How can one enter the gate of Deshan? Ba’en Xiuyun said:
"It is not merely a matter of stealing the bell. It is like plucking the pearl from beneath the chin of a black dragon at the bottom of a ninefold abyss while the dragon is asleep;
were it to wake, one would surely be ground to powder. He further said: "Using a decoy to seek a pigeon; clinging to the capital to seek profit."
Indeed, he could not escape his trap. Suddenly, someone asked Wansong, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? Wansong slapped him across the face and said, "Right here!
This was enough to make even a soaring dragon and a lame turtle shrink their necks and clench their hooves;
it left attendant Deshan with no way to defend himself and his tongue tied. Do you recognize this old fellow Deshan? In his youth, he once settled the matter of dragons and snakes.
The Battle Lines. "In my decrepitude, I still listen to the songs of a young child. Boshanlai said: "Deshan’s single staff was, in ordinary times, dripping with blood.
Why, then, is it not used here? Do you understand? He draws the transverse bone from within the dark;
he sits upon his own tongue in the midst of clarity. Gunanmen said: "To cast one's body across the mouth of a fierce tiger; to rub oneself against the head of a venomous snake."
Itching! One out, one in; one push, one shove—it is indeed a fine hand. Cui-feng speaks thus:
setting aside all the sages of the past, where have this band of fellows gone? "Pitiful are the countless tide-players."
"In the end, he still falls back into the tide and dies. Pujilong said, "The Daoist Master has exhausted his moral resources; the mechanism of 'the mountain collapsing on the tiger' is profound.
Yet he does not realize that his heart, liver, and five viscera have already been completely torn out by this fellow Meng Bala.
Is there anyone who can cast a single eye of discernment before this mechanism?"
The spirit of the upright man and loyal minister is most heroic; a single word to aid the state makes even death seem light.
Unlike those who are sycophantic and seek only security, they do not spend a lifetime coveting favor and greedily pursuing glory.
(Foyin Yuan) When the cloud-bird spreads its wings, the heavens lose their luster; yet the frog at the bottom of the well still clamors "du-du-du. Suddenly, the sun turns and leaps forth.
Come! A thousand peaks, ten thousand peaks, all starkly protruding. (Baizhang Yuan) When meeting face-to-face, the adept knows;
herein, even the sparks of flint and flashes of lightning are slow. The strategist who masters the mechanism has profound intent;
the general who deceives the enemy lacks foresight. A shot that hits the mark—whom else could it deceive? Seeing the jaw behind the head—who is there?
Difficult to offend. With eyes beneath his brows, he gains the advantage.
(Tiantong Jué) A stubborn-skinned tiger lies in the forest glades; let others do as they please, even if they drip oil upon him. His belly is full because he has once feasted on meat;
though called out repeatedly, he lazily refuses to lift his head. (Wuzhun Fan)
Habituated to battle, he deeply conceals the trap for tigers; how could he dare to violate the heavy encirclement when pursued to the end?
Even if he manages to preserve his body intact, his banners and spears are shattered and his majesty lost.
(Han-shan Qing) The bright moon shines upon the traveler on the road; abrupt peaks and low valleys become level in a single sweep. The wind sweeps the scattered clouds back to the mountain peaks.
All is exhausted; it is only because Hua Shan remains green. (Lian-an asks:

By imperial decree, the Flying Dragon is summoned to display great merit. With his five-clawed hooves he tramples, swallowing the barbarians with his breath. The King’s designs have already established a legacy for a thousand years;
those who were arrogant and defiant merely indulged in their own ferocity. (Fu-shan stores:)

Shoukuo arrived at Lumeng. One day, while seeing the Chan Master Chu engaged in conversation with a monk, Shoukuo came down from the mountain and asked, "What are you doing all day long, looking so disheveled and distracted?
Chu replied, "Did you see me looking disheveled and distracted, Master? Shoukuo gave a shout; Chu also shouted. Both men then ceased speaking.
The Master said, "Venerable elders, you should look at these two blind men," and immediately after, he gave a shout.
He then returned to his quarters and ordered an attendant to invite the Master up, saying, "Just now, the old monk and Chan-jiao had a meeting as host and guest;
where was there any failure? The Master replied, "I see only that your illness has grown deeper. The Master [Baizhang] said, "The old monk himself—"
"Upon seeing Xinghua arrive, you will understand. The Master said, "When the Abbot visited Xinghua, I was his attendant;
I remember what was said at that time. The Gatekeeper said, "Please quote it for me. The Master then quoted:
Xinghua asked, "Where have you come from, Reverend? The Abbot replied, "From Wutai. Xinghua asked, "Did you see Mañjuśrī? The Abbot—
