(Zhang Wujin) Whose daughter is so exceptionally beautiful? This horse-herder is a hundred times more clever. How laughable, that appointment by the Jinsands;
from beginning to end, the union was never realized as a pair. (Huan’an Ti)
Fengxue was once asked by a monk, "The summer retreat is over; please, Master, offer words of commendation for our labor. The Master said:
"The sleeves are rolled up and the dragon cave’s rain is swept away; the cup floats as ripples surge, and blossoms overflow from the alms-bowl bag."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Fengxue’s application was appropriate for the matter at hand; he was indeed elegant and refined. Yet, he only managed to speak of a phrase from 'on the road.
Suppose someone were to ask Daolin: 'The summer retreat has concluded; please, Master, offer a word of recommendation. He would reply:
'By the side of the Hall of Four Cuts, auspicious vapors soar; on the banks of the Three Xiang Rivers, the lofty banner is seized.'"
A monk asked Fengxue, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "What is not the Buddha?
The monk said, "I do not yet understand; I beg the Master to point it out again. The Master said, "My home is east of the Sea Gate; the sun of Fusang shines there first."

Falin’s *Yinyun* says: "The arrow that pierces the willow—Fengxue was not without skillful hands; yet, even so, he still falls short by three paces when it comes to blending with the light and mingling with the dust.
A single ray of white hair between the brows—throughout kalpas, where could one know how to hide it? The eternal night is vast and silent, yet the heavens have not yet dawned."
Dawn. You must still rub your forehead and gaze toward Fusang.
(Baoning Yong) Words that cut through iron value being direct and appropriate; turning one’s head is more than just being separated by Fusang.
Most pitiable is passing before the Xuande Gate, yet going further to seek Bianliang among others. (Zuan Rui)
Fengxue went to Huanglong. Huanglong said, "The stone horn pierces the path through the clouds; what is the meaning of these hanging branches?
The Master replied, "Red clouds enshroud the jade image; the peaks embrace the valleys and plains. Huanglong said, "If that is so, then I shall follow you.
The Master said, "Master, speak softly."
A priceless bright pearl hangs in the dark; at nightfall, one would try to pierce a wooden man.
Who knew that it was instead seen by the earthen ox, who swallowed it into the abyss of crimson mists and azure waves?
(Touzi Qing) Once, when Fengxue was with Zhen Yuantou, they were reciting the *Lotus Sūtra* together. While making their inquiries, the Master asked Zhen, "What is this?"
The World-Honored One speaks what is not spoken; Kāśyapa hears what is not heard. Zhen said, "The magpie cries atop the tree, yet its intent lies within the hemp field.
The Master said, "Why do you perform such foolish merit? Why do you not investigate the words and phrases?"
He then asked Nian Fahua, "How do you understand this? Nian said, "Moving one's countenance to reveal the ancient road;
not falling into the silent mechanism. The Master turned to look at Zhen and said, "Why do you not observe the words spoken by Nian Fahua?"
Gao Feng Miaoyun said: "In years past, when I was attending my former teacher, I too was once asked this same question.
As soon as I attempted to offer a word in response, I was struck with a severe beating of hot sticks that left me in unbearable pain for three days.
If you, Great Assembly, truly wish to discern the relative superiority of these two elders, simply look at the place where Master Miaozuo received his beating."
When a monk asked Fengxue, "What is the Way? the Master said, "Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion.
The monk asked, "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, "Ask the City God."

Touzi said, "The blue sky. He pointed to the Way, saying it is realized by one's own practice within oneself. When asked about the ultimate resolution of awakening, he answered by upholding the fundamental principle:
"If it is not you yourself, your progress is in vain. Why is this? Because the path that leads upward is one where even the thousand sages do not travel.

In the mere interval of a deliberation, the journey is ten thousand miles. For this reason, auspicious purple clouds welcome the Dragon Palace, while the halls are shrouded in mist and the moss-covered steps are deep.
Within the inner chambers, incense smoke lingers as the people are silent. At such a moment as this, would you allow anyone even the breath of a sigh?
If there were even the space for a breath, that journey would again be ten thousand miles. Thus, I offer this verse:

The deep palace and forbidden halls are shielded by layered enclosures; the curtains are still, and purple qi hangs from the eaves and pillars. Moss covers the ground, blocking access to the imperial audience;
let your family members show you the way, and do not hesitate.
Fengxue was once asked by a monk, "What is the student’s own self? The Master said, "It is your own self.
The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
Tianbao Shu said, "'It is your own self'—this is pouring water on water. [If I were there,] I would have struck him across the spine with a staff, right through to the bone and to the marrow."
Fengxue was once asked by a monk, "When the deer of the world form a herd, how does one shoot the leader among them?
The Master said, "The fishing boat has reached the banks of the Xiao and Xiang rivers; with a choked breath and in despair, one asks the white gulls."

In the Forbidden Palace and inner chambers, the hearing and sight are perilous. Thinking with partiality, he stands alone as the crimson decree descends. The clouds sever the Han lands; the marshes stretch far away.
At twilight on the ridges, the gibbons howl as the solitary moon follows.

(Touzi Qing) The Emperor is distant and heaven is high; one reviles the Most Honored One. Only by chance did I meet a man of state, and the silken decree was bestowed. The imperial edict proclaims that all under heaven shall return to the Sovereign.
Transformation. When the winged species [geese] pass through Yanmen Pass, they carry reeds in their beaks.
Regarding the Wind Cave, when a monk asked, "The ancient melody has no rhyme or meter; how can one harmonize it? the Master said:
"The wooden cock crows at the hour of Zi; the straw dog barks as the day breaks."
Jingshan Hongdao said: "To answer a question in such a manner, one has not yet become a true descendant of Linji.
Suppose someone were to ask Jingshan today: 'The ancient melody has no rhyme or meter; how can it be harmonized? I would simply say to him: 'The wooden cock crows at midnight;
the straw dog barks when dawn breaks. Nantang Yu said: "The beginning was not reached, and the end went too far."
To see the principles from beginning to end, one must achieve the resonance of metal and jade.
Qingshan Xiu said, "Even the Elder Miaoxi has not yet become a true descendant of Fengxue. When someone asked Qingshan, "The ancient melody has no tune;
how can it be harmonized? he simply replied to him: "At dawn, the straw dogs bark; at midnight, the wooden roosters crow."
Moonlight on ancient crags locks heavy clouds; Withered trees welcome fragrance, lingering with spring at evening. Last night the stars and river crossed the Southern Dipper;
The golden crow followed the phoenix across the celestial wheel. (Touzi Qing) Brightness and darkness are twin mechanisms of killing and life;
In the cold breeze of the azure oil, all distinctions of high and low cease. Before the frost, the ancient tune of a thousand peaks—
At dawn, the Lady Chang’e within the moon is lost amidst the dew. If one is not a true connoisseur, it is in vain to lean over and listen;
one merely hears the orioles falling by the western stream.

(Companion to my partner) The plum blossoms emit their fragrant scent in the sixth month; the willow catkins fly wildly during the three cold days of winter. If you can sing of non-action within the midst of nothingness—
Upon emerging, one finally realizes that [the sounds] were originally not in the *gong* or *shang* registers.
(Jiashui Qia) Fengxue was asked by a monk, "What is the point of intimacy for a student?
The Master said, "On the southern side of Mount Sumeru they beat the drums together; before Mount Helan they kick the leather ball."
With kindness, he once extended a question to an old man: "Singing at the East Mountain, chanting at the North Mountain.
To play with the tide, one must be a traveler of the Wu River; For parting words, let them belong to a man of Hanland.
(Touzi Qing) Fengxue ascended the seat within the yamen of Commissioner Li in Yingzhou and said: "The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs is like this..."
It is like the mechanism of an iron ox: when it departs, it is sealed; when it remains, it is broken. As for neither departing nor remaining—is it the seal, or is it not the seal? Can anyone say so?
At that time, the Elder Lupi came forward and asked, "The student possesses the mechanism of the iron ox;
I pray the Master will not apply the seal. The Master said, "I am skilled at fishing for whales."
Nichei was like a vast expanse of water, yet he sighed at how his own progress was like a frog’s stride, mired in the mud and silt of a pond.
As he stood there reflecting, the Master shouted, "Elder, why do you not offer a word? Nichei hesitated. The Master struck him with a whisk and said, "Do you still remember the *huatou*?
Try to bring it up. Just as Nichei was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him again with the whisk. The Abbot said, "I know for certain now."
"The Buddha-dharma and the royal law are the same. The Master asked, "What principle do you see?
Muxi replied, "To hesitate when one ought to act results in disorder. The Master then descended from his seat.

Zhaojue Qin said: "Fengxue donned the armor of the Three Mysteries and deployed the four types of guest-host relations; he clearly raised the banner of faith and secretly arrayed his ranks against the enemy.

When it came to Lupi, as soon as [Fengxue] mounted the iron ox, he seized him instantly, thereby enabling the herdsman to know his way home—what is called the dragon’s gallop, the tiger’s stride, the phoenix’s flight, and the peacock’s soaring. Even so, Chongning was waiting for him."
The Way possesses the pivot of the "iron ox. To strike the spine with a staff—why? Because it is the "sword that kills" and the "sword that gives life.
Ba’en Xiuzhuo said: "When Fengxue asked, 'Governor, what principle have you seen? at this point one should have cleared Lupei’s grievance. Tianning Qisong said:
"It is like the spark struck from flint or a flash of lightning; whether one grasps it or not remains to be seen."
To escape mourning is to lose one’s life. Fengxue stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, cutting off the tongue of Lupi.

If Lupi were a man of true caliber, he would not have been subject to the scrutiny of the Herdsman; yet as soon as Lupi spoke of "the Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs being like the mechanism of an iron ox," Fengxue burst into loud laughter.
Had Lupi hesitated for a moment, Fengxue would have struck him once and departed. Without cause, he invited the Master [to speak].
"Without bearing the seal, leaning on another's gate and walling by another's side, one is nonetheless called a 'lord' by the people of the age.
Now, if there were someone to act as the master for Fengxue, I would ask him: 'Where is the Mind-Seal? Qingshan Xiu said:
"One who seeks a decisive victory does not spare his own head. Lupi was also a fierce general, daring to come and seize the command."
The banners and flags were arrayed. Alas, the battle formation of Fengxue was already set; you had no gate through which to enter and no path by which to exit.
Were it not for one who has donned the armor and spears of the Three Mysteries and carries the Seven Matters upon their person, who could act thus?
Nevertheless, had there not been the Herdsman at that time, how could the movement have been brought to its conclusion? Boshan Lai said: "Fengxue held the mud seal in his hand."
One may seal it and remain within it, or one may break the seal; Lubo does not apply a seal—this is precisely the mechanism of the Iron Ox.
It is a pity that it is so utterly parched; had it possessed even a trace of moisture, one could have guaranteed that his mud seal would have rotted away.

Píngyáng Mín said: "Fengxue holds the mandate, and the Herdsman knows the homecoming. This may truly be called the galloping of dragons, the bounding of tigers, the soaring of phoenixes, and the flitting of peacocks."
Morning and evening, at one and the same time; once in a thousand autumns, perhaps one may encounter it. As for Lupi’s failure to maintain his integrity, where exactly did his transgression lie?
Dajue Sheng said: "Fengxue’s true command was fully exercised; Lupi withdrew from the field to sell out his own ranks. He yielded entirely to the Herdsman by a single move. Why is this so?
Even if Boya had the melodies of the High Mountains, if he did not meet a connoisseur, they were but in vain."
Having captured Lu Po, he mounts the iron ox; the three mysteries and the armor and weapons have not yet been easily requited.
By the waters that flow toward the sea at the foot of King Chu’s city, with a single shout, he once caused them to flow backward.

(Cui Feng Xian) The spearhead stands like a sheer cliff—the mechanism of the iron ox; the ten directions are traversed as the precious sword is brandished. In one stroke, the rebel armies are all ground to dust.
Shattered! The victory songs are sung in unison as all returns to Great Peace.

(Bao Ning Yong) The legacy of the successive sagely emperors never permits a single lapse. One attempts to mount an iron ox, only to have it suddenly struck through the head and broken. Lupei hesitated when he ought to have severed [the doubt];
lightning-swift and star-flying, he was captured alive. A shout brings forth a pivot like a thunderclap; the spears of the Three Mysteries.
Jiashan shook the entire forest;
Yuanwu’s "iron ox" mechanism—sealing and breaking through, penetrating beyond the crown of Vairocana’s head—to sit upon the tongue of the transformation Buddha.
Fengxue held the scales; Lupi suffered defeat. Under the staff and the shout, it was like lightning or a spark from flint, vividly clear.
The bright pearl is clearly visible in the bowl; yet to raise one's eyebrows is already to miss it.
(Tiantong Jue) A crimson flame reaching to the heavens; stones are scorched and gold flows. Those near and those far—everyone is made to burn their heads.
When the celestial winds blow even more fiercely, the wreckage is all too plain to see across the vast blue seas. (Xiansheng Cheng)
Fengxue ascended the hall and said: "If you establish even a single atom of dust, the state will flourish and the country will prosper, yet the village elders will frown.

If you do not establish even a single atom of dust, the state will perish and the country will fall, yet the village elders will be at peace. If you can understand this clearly, then you, O *śrāmaṇera*, have no share in it; it is entirely the old monk’s.
If you do not understand this clearly, the old monk is, in fact, you, O *śrāmaṇera*. You, O *śrāmaṇera*, and the old monk are also able [to be thus]."
He can awaken all people under heaven, and he can also blind all people under heaven. Do you wish to recognize the *jueluo* (the teacher)?
He gives a single clap to the right and says, "It is here. Do you wish to recognize this old monk? He gives a single clap to the left and says, "It is here."
Yunmen Wenyan said, "Here it is easy; there it is difficult. Langye Huijue said, "Guessing with a ladle while listening to an empty sound.
Baizhang Fenggan said, "Is it immediate? Is it not immediate? After a long silence, he said, "The heart does not betray others;
the face has no color of shame. He struck the meditation seat once. Wuzu Fayan, having cited this, said, "Peace and tranquility..."
Not so. If you establish a single speck of dust, the grass before the Dharma Hall is a fathom deep; if you do not establish a single speck of dust, it is like adding flowers upon brocade.

Why is this? Have you not seen it said: "Nine times nine is eighty-one. When the poor fellow has finished his punishment, he intends to stretch out his legs and sleep, but the mosquitoes, gadflies, and fleas come crawling out.
Tiantong Huo said: "Big or small, Fengxue did not understand the turning phrase."
Lingyin Yue said, "The sour stench of Great and Small Fengxue still lingers. Ba’en Xiu said, "Yunmen adds a point to an arrow;
Langye pulls out the wedge from behind the head. This is also like a single speck of dust causing the fall or rise of a house or nation;
yet in truth, how has the central tree ever moved even slightly? Wushi Dao said, "Fengxue is very much like..."
This diviner: before the money for the divination has been cast, all good and ill fortune lies entirely within one's own person;
once the money is thrown down, all misfortune and blessing, good and ill, lie entirely upon the shoulders of another.
Now tell me, when he strikes his left hand once and his right hand once with his palm, what is his meaning?
Let the country elder not knit his brows; instead, let him plan to establish a foundation for the state and its heroes.
Where now are the strategists and the fierce generals? Only the pure wind across ten thousand *li* knows them alone.

(Cui Feng Xian) To establish a state, he still lets the country elder rejoice; his majesty extends beyond the borders without raising a speck of dust. His纵横 (*zōnghéng*, strategic maneuvers) are unfathomable, and he is both civil and martial.
Martial. How many people are there in this vast and boundless universe?
(Baizhang Yuan) With hair as white as snow, he rose by the Wei River to cast his line. How does he compare to those who starved to death on Mount Shouyang?
It is all within a single speck of dust that manifests various transformations; both lofty fame and meritorious achievements are difficult to erase. (Tiantong Jue II)
How much joy, how much sorrow? Behold the two brows of the rustic elder. The realm is peaceful and stable, as clear as a mirror;
the waters recede and the mountains stand bare—a single expanse of autumn.
Behold, both released and both gathered again; some voices of joy, others of sorrow. All sages and worthies vanish like a flash of lightning;
the great chiliocosm is but a bubble in the sea. (Xueyan Qin) Home and nation clearly attain freedom;
prosperity and decline are entirely gathered within a single speck of dust. The general’s warhorse sleeps just as it lies.
Ripe. Let the wild weeds fill the earth with sorrow.
(Zhuwu Jian) The gates and the mountains and rivers cost much deliberation; a single speck of dust vainly compares rise and fall.
How can it compare to the bottom of a thatched hut against green peaks, where the pine wind enters one’s dreams in the bright day? (Weizhong Fu)
On both banks, lotuses vie with the rosy clouds; the wind and moon of this world belong to the fisherman’s house.
The fishing rod is gathered in, the rain-cloak is cold; in silent stillness, the autumn river rolls its waves.
(Falin Yin) Fengxue went to attend Nan’uan. Nan’uan asked, “Where have you recently come from? The Master said, “From the South. Nan’uan said, “In the South, one—”
"How can one deliberate upon the staff and the shout? The Master said, "Deliberate upon them as something extraordinary. [The monk] said, "It is not so here.
The Master asked, "In what way, then, do you deliberate here? He replied, "Under the staff, there is the patience of non-arising;
facing the critical moment, the teacher is not seen. At this, the Master attained realization.
Jingshan Daowu said: "At that time, Fengxue should have fully spread his sitting cloth and paid him three prostrations;
otherwise, he should have overturned the meditation seat. He then turned to his attendant and said: 'Tell me, was Fengxue right to prostrate at that moment?'"
Xian-dao overturned the meditation seat; this was called "the bandits were utterly defeated. Gao said, "Look at this blind fellow making such a mess," and he struck him.
Qing-shan Xiu said, "Wu of Feng-xue was not without realization, but alas, he fell into the secondary position."

If I, this mountain monk, were Nan-yuan, when he asked, "How do you deliberate here? I would have struck him across the spine with my staff, ensuring that he would become thoroughly proficient and well-versed.
A shout like a probing pole in the grass; the bloodline of no-master penetrates the crimson thread.
Failing to recognize General Li in the open field, one merely practices the single arrow that pierced the willow branch.
(Nanyuan Sheng) A lion teaches its cub to turn back and leap; seizing the moment, it displays its sharp edge. Yet, one laments the primordial chaos (*hundun*) once more.
Chiseling away. The wild deer marks its branch, recalling the Ancient Sovereign.
(South Gate) Where teacher and disciple merge, it is like a mustard seed meeting a needle; the mountains are not yet high, the seas are not yet deep.
Behold the furnace and bellows of the master at work—able to refine that inauspicious metal that leaps from the forge. (Rufeng Gao)
Fengxue was once asked by a monk: "When speech and silence involve transcendence and subtlety, how can one pass through them without transgression? The Master said:
"I always remember that within the third month in Jiangnan, where the partridges cry, the hundred flowers are fragrant."
Cui Feng Xian said: "Someone once asked me this. I replied to him, 'I would slit open his belly and gouge out his heart.
But what about that? He further said: 'Blowing fire with the wind is a matter of a different caliber; sparing the turtle while injuring the tortoise must surely have its master.
Wuquan Shou said: "The fine scenery of Jiangnan truly deserves to be like this. For a thousand years, those who come to view the sights have only increased people's restlessness. If...
Or perhaps it is not so; there will be new branches again next year. The spring wind that causes such vexation has not yet ceased.
Gushan Gui said: "Tell me, is this a transgression or not? Nanhua Bing said: "When Fengxue enters the forest, the grass does not move."
Entering the water without stirring the waves; within the eyes, Mount Sumeru is overturned; across the eyebrows, the worlds are laid horizontally. In the end, where does it all fall?
Only the Old Barbarian (the Buddha) is permitted to know; the Old Barbarian is not permitted to understand. Yunju Yuan said:
"Furthermore, rejoice that the world is at peace. After Xichan Xu finished citing the words of Xuedou, he said: "One person is like the warm harmony of early spring;
another is like frost added to snow. Although the responsive mechanism of their coming is not obscure, their methods of bestowing and revoking are worth observing."
What can be done about the question posed by a monk who has not yet emerged? Once, a monk asked Xiangyun: "I have said to him: 'Where the clay ox roars, a thousand peaks are exquisite;
when the wooden horse neighs, ten thousand trees turn autumnal. He further said: 'The lion yawns and the elephant king looks back;
thirty years hence, it will be a mixture of mud and water—do not say you saw Xiangyun come. Donglin Yan cited this.
Cui-feng finished speaking and said: "The Emperor’s decree within the realm; the General’s command beyond the frontier. Tian-tong Jue said:
"Barely exposed, perfectly round—truly without seams or joints. But tell me, is it Feng-xue who is without seams and joints, or is it Cui-feng?
Do you understand? Blending with the light yet stirring up trouble; scraping and polishing until the house is complete. Tian-tong Jie said: "Feng..."
The Patriarch Xuefeng sold white flour mixed with chaff and husks, thereby leading later people astray;
they merely pursue intellectual principles deep within the "Hundred Flowers" and wander about in crowds outside, beating around the bush. Jing Mountain was not like this.

When someone asked, "How can one pass through the state of speech and silence, which involves transcendence and subtlety, without falling into error? he would immediately reply to him: "Set aside that question for a moment."
Zhongfeng Ben said: "This monk’s place of inquiry is like a great flood reaching the heavens; there is nothing that does not lie within the waves.
Although Fengxue is indeed one who enters the water without drowning, how can he avoid being entirely contained within it?"
Where the partridges cry, a hundred flowers are fragrant. Clapping my hands, I let out a hearty laugh.
Recalling the places I traveled in years past, I see someone being sent off into the setting sun at a mountain valley.
(Haiyin Xin) Where the partridges cry, the hundred flowers are fresh. In this land by the river, the path has always been level and clear. To report to those on their way who have not yet returned:
Guest: "Excuse me, sir; my family is not at home. (Baofeng Ming) Within the shadows of colored clouds, a celestial being appears.
Holding a red silk fan, they shield their face. You must quickly fix your gaze upon the immortal;
do not look at the fan in the immortal’s hand. (Fojian Qin)
Suddenly stepping out the door, one first sees the path; Just as the foot is set down, one has already boarded the boat.
The secret instructions of the immortals are truly worthy of treasuring; Though father and son are close, they cannot be transmitted.
(Miaoxi Gao) Fengxue was asked by a monk: "From the ancients of old, seal after seal has been in accord. What is this 'accord'?"
"Eyes. The Master said: "Those who dabble lightly in the Way understand the shifting of opportunities. Cast aside the handkerchief for wiping away tears;
when the mirror is set before the hall, ugliness cannot escape. A single opportunity is presented, and the soul trembles with fear.
If you meet this with the skill of Chaozong, you will immediately attain a world-surpassing elegance. (Han Lei Jian)
When a monk asked Fengxue, "What is the Buddha? the Master said, "The bamboo-stem whip beneath the Zhangling Mountains.
Daofeng Qing remarked, "He is like one who controls a thousand-li horse and looses a 'piercing the willow' arrow; yet, alas, he labors in vain without merit."
Bamboo-ribbed whips beneath Mount Zhānglín; branches and joints sparse by the ancient stream. To understand the Master’s opening of the True Eye:
a full orb shines at midnight, illuminating the autumn sky.
(Hǎiyìn Xìn) Bamboo-ribbed whips beneath Mount Zhānglín; water lies in the deep ravine, the moon is in the heavens. A fine steed knows not where it has gone.
Depart! Ānanda remains as before before the World-Honored One.
(Zhenjing Wen) At the foot of Zhulin Mountain, bamboo whips; pulled forth from the cold crags, they still bear the smoke.
Supported across the broken bridge, they once proved their strength; Now they are not worth half a coin. (Shangfang Yi)
Chan Master Tiehu An of Yingqiao in汝州 (a successor of Nanyuan Yong), while tending the fire, was asked by Minister Zhong, "How can one escape from the burning of the three realms?
The Master used his incense spoon to poke at the fire; as Zhong hesitated, the Master called out, "Minister!
At this, Minister Zhong attained realization.
Loudly stirring the fire, he summons the Minister of Works; the flames blaze toward heaven, driving him right across his face.
Yet, he remains able to sit steadily right here, letting the snow fill the streets outside his gate.
(Yemuchuan) To burn through the three realms and seek liberation—spring has come, and now spring is seen to depart. It is that he does not see the coming of spring.
Go! When the sun rises in the east, it sets in the west at night.
(Xianji Yun) Chan Master Guijing of Xingyang in Yingzhou (a successor of Xiyan Ming): He went to visit Xiyan and asked, "What is it like when one intends to ask but does not ask?
Xiyan struck him immediately. The Master remained silent for a long while. Xiyan said, "If you call this a staff, your eyebrows and beard will fall off."
Upon hearing the Master’s words, he attained great enlightenment.
Baofu Zhan said, "Even so, how many hairs are there on your eyebrows? Kaifu Ning said, "Xingyang indeed possesses the mechanism for trapping tigers;
Xiyuan unwittingly threw himself into his deep pit. If one can discern this, one will personally [attain it].
Wearing the Vairocana seal, he plucks the tiger’s whiskers right before its face. Yet, such is the case when one's insight has not yet reached full perfection.
When the staff-head possesses eyes as bright as the sun, you must recognize true gold by looking within the fire.
Chan Master Shoushan Shengnian of Ruzhou (the successor of Fengxue Zhaoyin), the ninth generation descendant of Dajian Huineng. Once, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while the mother-in-law leads it. The monk asked, "In what phrase is this statement contained? The Master said:
"Neither the Three Mysteries can encompass it, nor can the Four Propositions include it. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this?

The Master said, "Heaven is long and earth is enduring; the sun and moon shine together. On another occasion, because a monk asked, "When the daughter-in-law rides the donkey, the mother-in-law leads it—what is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "A centenarian grandfather loses his father. The monk asked, "How could a centenarian grandfather have a father?"
"Father? The Master said, "You understand. He added, "This is solitary sitting, where there is neither high nor low; from the beginning, not a single dharma has been given to anyone.
Yungan Yu said: "Qin Shen is profoundly silent; the lacquer-cocked head is like a Great General removing fleas. Guangxiang.
One might say: "To respond to the occasion and engage with others is indeed swift and nimble, yet it cannot avoid the laughter of onlookers.
Grasping the muzzle with the hand and treading on the tail with the feet; looking up at the sky while listening to the flowing water.
At dawn, he is sent out by the roadside; at night's quiet, he returns to his thatched hut. (Daowu Zhen)
The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads; Old Wang pilots an iron ship through the air. A sail is hung at the bottom of a well where the wind is fierce;
atop the summit of Mount Sumeru, the waves overflow the heavens. (Seal of the Ocean-Print) The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads;
her face is like the full moon and her eyes are like lotuses. She further takes the hem of her gauze sleeves to lead [him] along.
A single segment of elegance pervades the great thousandfold world.
(Cishou Shen) The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. Her natural elegance is spontaneous;

Water flows from the high plateau, its waves lapping against the sky; in the four directions, above, and below, all dust and smoke have vanished.
Clearly, what a truly excellent message! Yet it seems few people of this age reach that state.

While he was waiting for [the monk] to gaze greedily at the heavens, [Ciming] gave him a finger. As the monk hesitated, [Ciming] drew his sword and struck him down.

If one were unable to set it aside for even a single day while sleeping or eating, how could one spend their entire life awaiting the world with weapons? Why such fear?

It is fit for song, yet unfit for song; a blade of grass and the golden body—what can be done? An ordinary person of this world truly lacks merit;

With a pillow-sack, one finds freedom in deep sleep; let others’ clamor and chatter be as they may. Even with coarse clothing and simple food, there is no lingering thought;

Not so. Where, then, does delusion reside? For now, let us set aside the matter of delusion; take up that which is awakened and look at it.

"Three times three before, and three times three after. (Yuangwu Qin)

Old age; withered flowers are again driven by the wind of the fifth watch.

the Master said, "From where did you, Prince, receive such news? Prince Li let out a shout. The Master said, "A jackal howling."

Blowing against the wind, blowing with the wind; with iron eyes and copper pupils, who dares to peer?

A scorched brick strikes a frozen surface through to the bottom; a red-eyed man bumps into a firebrand.

Hard as a ball of cotton, yet soft as an iron stake; it cannot be bent by curving it, nor broken by twisting it. It does not violate the void and the mysterious.

Yong gave a shout and said, "Wild fox spirit! The Master pointed his finger and said, "You grinning, swaggering fellow—do you think you can get away with that again? Yong... [remained silent].

Little does he know that though gold dust is precious, when it falls into the eye it becomes a cataract.
Even if he were to emerge from it, nothing could save him except for an iron boat floating upon the water. Tianning Hong said: "Although Ciming possesses [this power]..."
A means of arising from life and returning to death; it is much like staring-eyed eyes within a coffin. Again, he offers this verse:
Holding fast the barrier gates, he passed through the Chu camp; The general’s single arrow shattered the heavy city. Now the four seas are as clear as if washed away;

"Lightning-flash dullness! Langye has a phrase that settles heaven and earth. Everyone, raise your eyes high!

"Ground! You have not yet escaped the trap of imitating patterns and copying forms. I shall grant you and the three elders a single verdict. Pingshan has the phrase that settles heaven and earth.
Thereupon, he descended from his seat.
Langya ascended the hall and said: "All of you who are here with me for this summer retreat, I shall point out five kinds of illnesses for you.
First, you must not go to a place ten thousand *li* away where there is not a single inch of grass. Second, you must not sleep alone on a solitary peak.
Third, you must not draw bows and set arrows. Fourth, you must not seek refuge outside of phenomena. Fifth, you must not remain stuck."
Regarding life and death: why is this? If one is obstructed in even a single place, it is difficult to save oneself; only when one is unimpeded in all five places can one be called a true guide.
You people, if you encounter those of clear vision and authentic practice while traveling to various regions, convey a message to me, so that the ancestral wind may not fall into decline.
If you are merely ordinary practitioners, then cease your efforts. Why? Because you are naked.
In the heart of the kingdom, one boasts of fine finery; I suspect you are utterly unaware of the times.
A cricket treads upon two [dangao] gourds; a mute man has a dream and laughs to himself. Laughing until dawn, to whom could he tell it?
A crow understands how to cry out like a qilin. (Zhengtang’s Discernment)
Langya pointed out five kinds of illness; though the world’s skilled physicians find it difficult to prescribe the medicine, I shall smash them all for you right here and now.

"The essence is originally pure and tranquil; why do mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise?"

"The beginning was not reached, yet the end was excessive. Wuzu Fayan said: "Though gold dust is precious, when it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract.

'Flowing on and on, transparent and clear, with no front or back; when picked up, it sometimes becomes two pieces.

When clarity is manifest, the essence of non-transgression is fully revealed. Advancing with resolute vigor, one must deliberate upon this.
Beauty and ugliness depend solely on encountering the ancient mirror; turning one's head, the face is covered in shame and dismay.

(Lingyin Yue) sets no pits or snares;
he brandishes no gleaming blade. With a single arrow he pierces the willow; his divine eyes do not blink.

Knowing the place where his mother’s heart breaks, let even the iron-hearted weep as if pouring forth water. (Zibao Ke) Langye addressed the assembly:
"Those who come in this manner, arrange them in the upper section. Those who do not come in this manner, [arrange them] in the lower section."
"Registering for lodging. When one comes as a person of the highest caliber, they cross the river alone in silent solitude.

Anan resided at Faju Monastery.
At Langye, he addressed the assembly: "To advance is to die; to retreat is to perish. To neither advance nor retreat is to fall into the realm of non-action.
Why is this so? Though Chang’an is pleasant, it is not a place for long-term residence."

The Master said, "Zhaozhou once studied under Nanquan. [The monk] said, "I do not yet understand. The Master said, "This winter there will be much snow and rain;
what can a poor family do about it?"
Baoshou Fang said: "Langye’s response to this question may be called the great opening of the treasure storehouse;

yet, alas, he did not meet a discerning eye, so his achievement was wasted in vain. Nevertheless, were it not for the wild geese arriving last night, how could one have seen the autumn at the sea gate?"
Langya addressed the assembly: "Do you remember when a monk asked an old master, 'What is the Buddha? The master replied, 'Neither a grave mound nor a tree.
Do you all understand? If you do not, I shall provide a further commentary: 'Neither a grave mound nor a tree'—it is like a fence of thorns."

No mound is raised, no trees are planted; thorns and *luán* bushes are used as markers. The dry heavens serve as the canopy, and the thick earth serves as the basin. There, souls and spirits are gathered together;

the worthy and the foolish share but one coffin. Scorched by the sun and buffeted by the wind, there is no barrier or enclosure—through a thousand autumns and ten thousand springs, it remains forever vast and desolate.
Chan Master Shouzhi of Dayu in Ruizhou (Suzhou), a successor of Fenyang Wude Zhao (Pingyang Min), addressed the assembly: "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know that there is [something]."

"The wildcat and the white ox, however, do know it exists. He then picked up his whisk and said, "The wildcat and the white ox are both here, emitting light and shaking the earth. Why is this so? Because there are two distinct parts."
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "If Dayu had not spoken those subsequent words, he would have surely been replaced in his very eyes by a cat and an ox.
Even so, he still could not avoid being like a weight dipped in vinegar. Yuan'an Yuyu said:
"When Dayu brought up the cat and the ox, had you ever even dreamed of them?"
Daiyu was once asked by a monk, "If the entire body is the eye, where is the mouth? The Master said, "Three leaps.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The seasonal rhyme of the lyrics has ended; the melody of the song arises toward spring."
Yuanwu Keqin’s *Blue Cliff Record* commentary states: "Although Dayu indeed possessed eloquence like a cascading river, alas, this monk had no eyes.

Ying’an Hua said: “These are fine words, yet they have no point of origin. If anyone can discern this, I will give you one or two taels of gold.
Guding Ming said: “When a master acts for the sake of others, it is like a household with *gū* poison that places poison in their food and drink;
they never fail to seek to sever the life-root of people. Nevertheless, how many are there who can be considered enemies? Neng... [text ends]
Renjian said: "If you do not call it 'a single stalk of leek,' you will enter hell as swiftly as an arrow shot. But how is it in the end?
If you can simply serve the rice into the bowl of no-mind, someone will naturally come forward to carry the broken-legged cauldron."
The complete mechanism of killing and enlivening is presented face-to-face. All of you gather together to eat a stalk of greens.
Later generations do not understand this meaning; they merely wander aimlessly, picking up firewood from the wilds.
(Songyuan Yue) Hard as cotton, soft as iron—when you drink water, everyone must beware of choking. It is laughable how the old fool at the riverbank remains so ignorant.
To this day, striving for cleverness has instead resulted in failure. (*Kuchan Jing*) The golden and green glazed tiles of the palace eaves reflect upon the high mountains.

the General holds his mirror and weeps over his frost-white hair. (*Tie Rong Yi*)

"The old fellow Dayú’s proclamation of this matter can truly be called exhausting [the truth]."

when set down, one moves with sovereign ease. When neither picked up nor set down, what is it called? He laughs heartily and says: "What is it?"
"A dry piece of excrement.
Dayu asked an attendant, "After you have finished your salutation, you stand to one side—what is the principle behind that?
The attendant said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Stand over there. The attendant immediately moved over. The Master said, "Pointless, pointless!"
Tianning Qi said: "Those who complete themselves are few; those who ruin themselves are many. Guangyin Biao said: "An attendant is indeed difficult to find.
How can this be known? Were it not for the wild geese arriving last night, how could one perceive the autumn at the sea gate?"
When a monk asked Dagu, "What is the Buddha? the Master said, "A saw cutting a weight.
A saw cutting a weight has no seams or gaps; it is blown by the wind and baked by the sun from morning until night.
Although one is not permitted to engage in idle deliberation, let the four worlds be weighed and lifted as you please. (Baiyun Yuan)
Holding a golden whip in hand, he strikes the iron ox; He roams at will throughout the great trichiliocosm.
Meeting him upon the banks of the Ganges as numerous as its sands, He recognizes silently without a word, nodding his head of his own accord.
(Baoning Yong) Sawing apart the scale-weight: this comes from an old poem by Du Fu: "Scented rice, the parrot's seedlings pecked at until bare; Green phoenix trees, where the phoenix has grown old."
Huangzhi. (Huaiyu proclaims:
"The crosscut and the scale-weight are clearly distinguished; touching them can still shatter one's eyes. This was personally forged in a red furnace;
throughout antiquity and today, how many have been awakened? (Guangyan Lamp)
Chan Master Quanju of Fahuas Monastery in Shuzhou (a successor of Fenyang Shanzhao) arrived at the place of Langye Huijue. Langye asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
The Master said, "The Two Zhe. Langye asked, "Did you come by boat or by land? The Master said, "By boat. Langye asked, "Where is the boat now?
The Master said, "At the foot of the stairs. Langye asked, "How do you express the phrase that does not involve the journey? The Master remained seated.
Gives him a blow with his staff and says, "Fabricated old fellows are as numerous as hemp and millet. He brushes out his sleeves and departs. Lang asks an attendant, "Who was this person?
The attendant replies, "It was Master Jue. Lang says, "Could it be Master Jue, my junior uncle?
My late teacher instructed me to seek him out. He then descends to the guest hall and asks, "Is Master Jue here?"
"Uncle Master, do not take offense at my slight discourtesy just now. The Master shouted. He asked again, "Elder, when did you arrive at Fenyang?
Lang replied, "I arrived at such-and-such a time. The Master said, "I have heard your name in Zhejiang long ago.
It turns out your understanding is merely this; how then can your fame spread throughout the world? Lang then prostrated himself and said, "I am guilty, sir."
[This was] passed over. Jingshan Daokai said: "The guest is the guest from beginning to end; the host is the host from beginning to end.

When these two great elders suddenly encounter one another, host and guest interchange, directly revealing the very marrow of Linji’s mind. Had it not been for one who has thoroughly realized the stage beyond, [this would not have occurred].
Bi: "To possess the true eye that transcends ordinary sentiment, one cannot yet avoid engaging in calculations of gain and loss.

Yunmen Xincheng said: "A fist coming and a foot going is the fundamental tongs and hammer. If you were to use a broken basket filled with water to extinguish a fire, it would make the bystanders laugh until they die.
Thirty years from now, someone will explain this through and through. Dongshan Huo said: "I strike upon the tongues of these two venerable elders."
Only by swinging over this swing can one speak a way that transcends ordinary circumstances;

not only will one not be entangled by right and wrong, but one will even employ right and wrong themselves to perform the work of a Buddha. Otherwise, you would go to West Qin while I remain in East Lu.
Yunyan said, "The Senior Monk [Dongshan] may indeed be described as 'carrying his bamboo pole with him, performing as the occasion demands.
Nevertheless, had there not been Langye’s accompaniment of song and beat, how could he have produced the 'Yangchun' and 'Bai-xue' melodies?"

When scolding one another, there are no kind words; when striking one another, there are no skillful fists. How much better it is when the wind is calm and the waves are still, with the bright moon filling the boats upon the river.
(Da-hong En) Having seized the pearl of the black dragon, he returns at once; the petty-rooted demons all fall into doubt and suspicion. He picks it up and hurls it into the vast waves.
[Verse] Wash our hands; let us all go home together. (Jingshan Gaofeng) The fisherman is carefree, drifting east or west as he pleases.
He plays his flute horizontally, its tones uneven. In the still night under the bright moon, the fish do not bite.
Reclining in his small boat, he enters the Wuling Brook. (Meng’an Xinxin)
Water does not wash water; gold is not bartered for gold. One obtains a horse by mistaking its coat color; one delights in the lute by tuning its silk strings.

From the binding of cords and the drawing of trigrams, such were the many affairs; yet they utterly lost the true simplicity of Pangu’s heart. (Xinwen Ben) The celestial *qiao* drums resound amidst the crimson dust;
swords and spears cover the earth, yet one can extricate oneself from them. Interlocking horns and mottled patterns appear wherever one turns.
Entering. A silver mountain and iron wall are the thoroughfare.
(I’an Gwon) Black mist swirls and splashes against the face; holding a jade scepter, he sighs at the vastness. Within the flash of lightning, one must pass through the eye of a needle;
layer upon layer of thread-ends cannot be untangled. (U’ung Sin)
To exhaust [the enemy] means meeting one’s match at the frontier pass; even more startling is the surrender of terms and the hoisting of the flag of submission.
All see the clear construction of the plank road, yet they do not know of the secret crossing at Chen’ang.
(Lian’an asked: "Clouds follow the dragon, wind follows the tiger; when the North Mountain is sunny, the South Mountain rains. To let go is for the bright moon to soar into the void.
Seizing Mount Sumeru and propping it up upside down; light and darkness intermingled, striking and singing raised together. Infinite fish and shrimp strain their eyes;
by riding the whirlwind, they win the right to spread throughout the universe.
(By Baiyu Si) Holding the divine talisman upside down behind the elbow; drawing the precious sword horizontally and hanging it from the brow. Everyone, cast it forth before the assembly!
Look! The Buddha’s mouth and a serpent’s heart rolled into one mass.
(Eyu Lang) Later, Langye brought this up to Ciming. Ciming said, "Master Ju’s insight is barely enough for his own sake;
as for you, you have fallen into negligence—how can you lead others?"
To record his merit, he was ranked in the Hall of the Ancients and discussed military affairs; yet he intended to carry out this very counsel.
One night, the autumn wind stirred homesickness, and the eight thousand disciples returned together to till the soil. (Liran asked:
"The Lotus Sūtra says to the assembly: 'If Śākyamuni had not appeared in the world and Bodhidharma had not come from the West, the Buddha-dharma would have pervaded the world.'"
Tánxuán’s mouth did not open.
Jìngshān Gǎo said, “The heart of a thief is naturally timid. Yù’ān Méng said, “The Great and Small Fǎhuá [masters] have the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake.
Zhǐhǎi said, “Since it is called ‘discussing the profound mystery,’ why does he say his mouth does not open? Thereupon—

Striking the desk with his hand as if using a *yongyi* (mind-at-will) staff, he said: "If you listen with your ears, you will never understand; only when you hear with your eyes will you truly be intimate [with it].
When a monk asked Fahu, "The matter of birth and death is great; I pray that the Master will save me," the Master replied, "I have lost my boat in Lake Dongting."
The boat is lost within Lake Dongting; the barefoot Persian sleeps at the bottom of the water. No one in the entire world can call him back;
the spring breeze blows him into the village of apricot blossoms.
(Xue’an Jin) Nanyue Bajiao Daogu Chan Master (successor of Fenyang Zhao) was walking in the mountains with Ciming when they encountered a...
At the Dragon Pool of the Poisonous Dragon, the Master took Ming with him to bathe. As Ming pulled back his arm to leave, the Master undressed and leaped in.
A thunderclap followed immediately; a foul wind blew and rain fell, shaking the trees and forest. Ming crouched in the grass, thinking the Master must have died.
After a short while, the sky cleared and the sun shone; the Master then extended his neck out from between the waves and said, "Ha! (or "Phat!").
Liran asked: "Guaquan was prepared to stake his very life to test the monks of the world, yet he was exposed by the old fellow Ciming. Daofeng Zhen said: "One man found life within death;
the other crouched in the grass. Both were exposed by the monks of the world. Zifukuang said: "Guquan sold..."
[The Master] plays with the words. Had there not been the testimony of Ciming, this would have been nothing more than idle labor.
When Guquan arrived at Ciming’s place, Ciming asked: "White clouds hang across the valley mouth;
from where has the man of the Way come? The Master looked left and right and said: "Where was the fire last night that burned out the ancient tomb? Ciming said: "Not yet. Further...
Dao said, "Make the sound of a tiger. Ming clapped his sitting cloth (zuoju) once. The Master caught it and pushed Ming onto the meditation seat (chanbed).
Ming then made the sound of a tiger. The Master laughed loudly and said, "I have seen more than seventy virtuous teachers (shanzhishi)."
"Today, for the first time, I have met a true master.
Tiantong Hua said: "If those two old fellows had stepped upon Linji’s 'upward' path at that time, we would not have even food to eat today.
Do you know where Jianfu has landed? Longxiang Yin said: "One person attained it."
The substance cannot be used; one person can use it, but not the substance. How would you dare to call yourself a descendant of Linji?
If you can examine this through and through, not only will you complete the ancient sages' old stories, but you will also spare me from being left stranded today by my late teacher, Wuchuan.
He brandishes his staff and strikes it once, saying: "The eyes upon the tip of the staff are as bright as the sun. If you wish to recognize them—"
"Examine true gold in the fire. Tianning Qi said, "To apply such terminology is an error. At that time, how could Ciming have tolerated this madman speaking like this?
He should have given him another blow of his sitting mat and watched what kind of trick he would perform.
As soon as his eyes flickered, he would have driven him out with a blow of the staff. If the Dharma-lineage of Linji had not fallen into desolation, [this would not have happened]."
When the two armies clash in battle, banners and spears stand upright and drums lack mallets. Not a hair’s breadth is transgressed against the General’s command;
each holds fast to their own single-legged mechanism. (Xiatang Yuan) A scholar and a warrior meet by chance;
they exhaustively discuss heroes, yet each is different. Together they go to Chang’an to pay court to the Sage.
Master, your name shall ultimately reach the heights of celestial wisdom.
(Xu Tangyu) Behold two tigers ascending a high mountain; their horns rising and falling are no ordinary sight.
Snatching and jostling one another with great spirit, the pure wind and bright moon stir the human realm. (Fuyan Rong)
Chan Master Tiansheng Haotai of Anjishou (successor of Fenyang Zhao). A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "A black-lacquered holy monk.
"A black-lacquered holy monk is truly extraordinary; do not defile him with pigments and colors. People join their palms and burn incense, yet they do not [see him].
Respectfully. Heshan and Shide smile while knitting their brows.
(Haixin Xin) When Tiansheng arrived at Langye, Langye asked, "To bury the troops and provoke a battle is not yet the mark of a master. With a single horse and a lone spear, he requested an audience.
The Master pointed at Langye and said, "If the general's head is not fierce, it will bring misfortune upon the three armies. Langye struck the Master.
The Master also struck Xie with one sitting-cloth (zuoju). Xie caught hold of it and said, "The previous sitting-cloth was the enforcement of this mountain monk’s command;
where does the sitting-cloth of the Senior Monk (shangzu) fall? The Master said, "I humbly pray you will accept my offering.
Xie pushed him away and said, "At the fifth watch, rising early, there is yet another traveler at night. The Master said, "A thief!"
After he had drawn his bow, Xie said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea.
Bairan Fu remarked, "When these two elders meet, it can truly be called meeting a fellow from one's own hometown and speaking the dialect of that hometown.
Nevertheless, while their true character is indeed authentic, they cannot help but carry a touch of formality."
Chan Master Fayan Yuanjian of Fushan in Shu State (dharma heir of Xueyan Chongxian). A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "A pile of bones rising from level ground."
Tender grasses line the slanting paths; mountain springs carry their azure currents. Wen Cheng once sought the waters of the Wei River; Zhuang Zhou was ashamed to serve as a court official.

(Touzi Qing) A mound of bones rises from level ground; in the third month of spring, thunder shakes the earth. One hears only of those who have gone a thousand li away; not one person is seen returning.
(Original Enlightenment I) A heap of bones rises from level ground; the golden-haired lion roars. Who knows this flavorless discourse? It blocks the mouths of the multitude.
(Kṣitigarbha’s Grace)
Stale goods do not enter the market; what need is there to discuss the state of the times? For those who have a fixed price to pay, Heaven will come to their door of its own accord.
(Yuan Chu Dan) Fushan was asked by a monk: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he inherit? The Master said: "Eighty..."
The old man rolled a ball of embroidered silk and said, "In this way, a single phrase suddenly opens the ancestral lineage;
the weapons of the three mysteries shake the monastic forests. The Master replied, "Li Ling was originally a subject of the Han court."
Touzi said: "The waters are deep and the fish hide; the leaves have fallen and the nests are sparse.

He then offered this verse: Rootless grass within the moon; Withered tree blossoms before the mountains. After the wild geese return from the desert passes, In whose house do the mortars and pestles fall?
Moss covers the ancient hall; the Milky Way hangs low with the handle of the Dipper. The golden rooster has just announced the dawn; the jade maid descends the steps late.

(Tianning Lian) Shun’s eyes had double pupils as he succeeded the Emperor Yao; His glorious fame resounds through the ages like the Xiao Shao music. Hearing the sound, one forgets the flavor—what does this accomplish?
Matters. Without access to the imperial power amidst the weeds and thickets, [I am] arrogant.
(Accompanying my companions) Fushan addressed the assembly: "Fenyang has three kinds of lion's phrases: first, transcending the school and differing from the eye;

second, matching brows and following in the same tracks; third, being like an echo or a shadow, a sound heard from afar. If one transcends the school and differs from the eye, their insight surpasses that of the teacher; such a person may be considered [a true successor]."
Only when one has planted the seeds of virtue is one fit to receive the transmission. If you walk side by side with the Master, your views will become equal to his;
if you fall short of even half the Master’s virtue, you are like a jackal relying on the power of its shadow and echo—how can such a different species be distinguished?
Therefore, the former masters gave this entrustment: "If you should meet [the Master], you must examine him with extreme care; do not investigate superficially or with negligence."
Tiger-like strategy and dragon-like tactics possess subtle mastery; transcending the teacher, why should one rely on a teacher? To stroke a tiger’s whiskers backward is but a trivial matter;
to rub an elephant’s trunk at will is a display of ease. Victory over the enemy is indeed a complete triumph; losing the mechanism of the game, one nevertheless occupies the initiative.
Born with such extraordinary nature, who can share it? To Huatuo alone is granted the attainment of the One Mystery. (Pingyang Min)
A monk asked Fushan, "What is the path that leads upward? The Master said, "In the first month of spring, it is still cold.

"In the first month of spring, it is still cold. "From beginning to end, there are ten thousand kinds and a thousand variations. "Last night, empty space fell to the ground; together with the breeze..."
(Leaning against the railing. Chan Master Daguang Tanying of Jingshan in Runzhou (a successor of Shimen Cong) said: "The seven Buddhas are the subjects of one's nature;
the myriad dharmas are the slaves of one's mind. But tell me, where is the master? He then gave a shout himself and said, "The seven Buddhas have already..."
With his head poking out from below, he again assented, saying, "Each shall attend to their own duties.

Duanyuan Lun said: "To call the Seven Buddhas 'servants of nature' and to point to the myriad dharmas as 'slaves of the mind'—Daguan claims for himself a path of transcendence, yet when he himself shouts and himself assents, this is merely the business of slaves; where is the master?"
When have you ever seen this in a dream? Does the great assembly wish to see it? [He] sweeps once with the whisk and says:
"At dawn, a breeze of spring stirs; throughout the gardens, flowers of a hundred varieties bloom."
A monk asked Jinshan, "What is the long Dharmakāya? The Master said, "A six-foot staff. The monk asked, "What is the short Dharmakāya?
The Master said, "A three-inch counting-stick. The monk said, "In that case, the Dharmakāya has two forms.
The Master said, "There is still more—squareness and roundness."
Liran asked: "The ancients' single-period arrangements can indeed be called 'treading firmly on all four corners of the ground.
Yet when examined closely, these too were merely elaborations following the flow of the discourse. Suppose someone were to ask this mountain monk, 'What is the long Dharma-body?
I would reply, 'A six-foot staff. If they then asked, 'What is the short Dharma-body? I would strike them across the spine. If that is so, does it not follow that there are two Dharma-bodies?"
He threw down his staff and said, "The army follows the seal; the general pursues the talisman. Tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different?
He then offered a verse:
Roaming amidst the waves of ten thousand layers of the long river, The moon follows the fisherman onto his small boat. Whether the fishing rod is cast or retracted depends on me.
[The Master] gestured with his hand, saying: "Do not calculate the labor;
you may rest as soon as it is convenient. When the Commandery Governor Li Zunxū (who is mentioned in the *Shimen Cong*) came to take leave of Jǐan Shàngzuò, the Governor asked:

"You recently departed from Shangdang and have now arrived at the Central Capital. Just as we were about to engage in conversation, you suddenly turn back your tiger-patterned staff to point toward the azure of Yunping."
Jiao visited the clear stream at Xueling. He asked, "I do not know how matters are here and there; what is it like?
Jian said, "The sharp sword sweeps away [all things], leaving heaven and earth pure; the frosty blade is just raised, and the Ox and Cow constellations grow cold.
Wei said, "It happens to be a day when my ears are deaf. Jian said, "A single arrow brings down two eagles. Wei said, "Why, Master, did you say that?"
Wuzhu was sleeping wearing straw sandals. Xuanjian gave them a flick with his sleeve. Wuzhu lowered his head and said, "Today, you may truly be called 'subdued' (jiangfu).
Xuanjian replied, "Puhua has come out of the Sangha Hall."
Lotus flowers bathe in the waves as the clear river recedes; red smartweeds sway in the wind as wild geese cast oblique shadows.
Gazing alone upon the river at evening, to whom does this boundless autumnal scenery belong?
(Ssan Ding) Yang Wenyong Yi, the Imperial Secretary of the Song Dynasty (seen by Guanghui Lian), whose courtesy name was Dainian, asked Guanghui: "I once..."
He asked the Chief Attendant Yunyan Liang, "What is it like when two great tigers bite each other? The Attendant said, "A unified whole.
He [Dongshan] said, "I simply keep watching; I wonder if speaking thus is acceptable? Huaihai said, "It is not so here.
The Master said, "Please, Reverend, give another turn of phrase. Huaihai made a gesture with his hand as if pulling a nose.
He said: "This beast is leaping about once more. The Master had a realization, and there was a verse that said: An octagonal millstone runs through the void;
A golden-maned lion transforms into a dog. If you wish to hide your body within the Big Dipper, You must join your palms before the Southern Dipper.
Master Mei Gaorun said: "The observer is a single mantra that causes the heavens to rotate leftward and the earth to rotate rightward.
Nevertheless, where there is a pond, there is a moon; in whose hearth is there no smoke? Let the Great Year speak as he may and attain enlightenment as he will."
To direct one's efforts toward the vast emptiness of "zhi-hu-ye-zhe" (the particles of discourse)—how can this compare to your own ability to recognize a single phrase?
But tell me, what is that one phrase? (He lets out a shout.)
The Inner Secretary (Neihan) clings to the Southern Dipper and leans upon the Northern Dipper; with vast wisdom, he turns the celestial pivot and overturns the earth’s axis.
Vast and silent through the ages, who can know him? A severed string must be joined by phoenix-glue.
(Shiyan Lian) The white stones lie stark and clear, concealing their beautiful jade within. Though the Way of the Gentleman is obscured, the Gentleman finds joy therein. (Xutang Yu)
Prince Wen asked Guanghui: "I have heard that you, Master, have said that all sinful karma arises from wealth and treasures, and thus you urge people to distance themselves from them.
Yet, the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa take wealth as their very lifeblood, and states gather people through wealth.
Since the teachings speak of two kinds of giving—material and Dharma—how can you urge people to distance themselves from wealth and treasures?"
Huì said, "The iron cage-top atop the flagpole. The Master said, "The horse from Haitan is as large as a donkey.
Huì said, "A chicken of Chu is not a phoenix of Mount Dan. The Master said, "Two thousand years since the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, and the bhikṣus have little sense of shame."
A yakṣa’s head, a bodhisattva’s face; a ghost pounding grain, a Buddha leaping over a wall. Sharing the same gate yet not knowing each other at the door;
surpassing the past and transcending the present, yet lacking even an inch of merit. A lamp-wick, a *zhī* plant, a broken stone, and a leg; Bian Que and Lu Yi vie for mastery.

(Or-an-ti) Having already known that the guest-dream lies within the mists and clouds, who would begrudge the cries of monkeys in the night rain? In vain do you say that news from Heng and Xiang has been cut off;
for more than a year, rows of wild geese have passed by Badong. (Tie-rong-yuan)
Duke Wen asked Ciming, "What is the one phrase for an elder to benefit others? Ciming said, "The cutting edge.
The Duke said, "A bride in a long skirt running through the mud. Ciming said, "Who could equal a scholar like you? The Duke said, "An adept! An adept!"
[The Master] said, "I shall give you thirty blows. Layman Gong clapped his hand on his knee and said, "What kind of place is this?
Master Ci clapped his hands and said, "You cannot let him off either. Layman Gong laughed heartily.
The breeze is gentle and the sun is warm; spring is at its peak. The willow colors are like gold, and the shadows of the flowers are thick.
Entering the old site of my former travels in Peach Blossom Spring, One peak locks another in a continuous chain.
(By Baiting Yong) He thrusts his whole body into the lair of the azure dragon; He pulls out several coral trees. He strikes down the ordinary brushwood and weeds.
With the price paid, he exchanged money for wine and became intoxicated on the Flower Street.
(A long whistle in the bright moonlight.

Chan Master Yangqi Fanghui of Yanzhou, the twelfth generation descendant of Great Mirror [Baizhang], (who was a successor of Ciming Yuan), was once asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said:
A three-legged donkey walks by prancing on its hooves. [The Master] said, "Is it not just this? The Master replied, "Elder of Hunan.
Tiantong Hua said, "Great and small Yangqi have split their speech into two pieces. Tell me, where does Jianfu’s eye for guiding others lie?"
Regarding this point: Jingshan Xiu said, "Whether great or small, Yangqi was caught by this monk’s single question; he could not help but reveal both his hands and feet.

Yunmen Xin said, "If you wish to understand where the three-legged donkey falls, you must first run through the womb of a donkey and the belly of a horse once; only then will seeing Yangqi not be difficult."
A three-legged donkey trots on its hooves; the two rivers south of the Yangtze are hot again in autumn. The northwest wind fears the early cold of frost;
I shut my door, sorrowful to see the willow petals fall. (Wan’an Yan) When the Dharma appears, the crafty arise;
when a buttress is raised, it invites the arrow. Who has personally seen the three-legged donkey? If you have personally seen it, then explain!
The face of Kālarī Nanda. (Fozhao Guang) A three-legged donkey trots along on its hooves;
it stirs up a clear breeze that chills to the bone. It tramples through Vairocana’s light until the shadows are severed;
there is no need to stir waves upon level ground. (Yue’an Guo)
A single arrow shoots down the wild geese at the edge of heaven; thousands and ten thousands gaze upon it with fixed eyes.
They do not know from where this arrow comes; when has the Elder of Hunan ever seen it?
(Zhong’an Kōng) The east wind warms the flowers, their colors lingering; everywhere, butterflies fly over the walls. The kitchen wife hears nothing of the Son of Heaven.
Imperial Decree: In Taiping, doors are never closed day or night. (Addressing the wind-signal:
I force myself to drink the wine purchased from the market; I am ashamed to look upon the books I have already read. Idle flowers fill the ground once more— How can my sorrowful longing be described?

(Yue-Rong Xuan): Once, when Yangqi was holding a memorial vegetarian feast for the anniversary of Ciming’s death, the assembly had gathered. Before the portrait of the deceased, the Master clenched both fists and placed them upon his head;
he then drew a line with his sitting cloth, struck a circular mark, and burned incense. He then withdrew three paces.
He stepped forward and performed a woman’s bow. The Head Seat said, “Stop making such a fuss. The Master asked, “What about you, Head Seat?
He replied, “Venerable Master, stop making such a fuss. The Master said, “A rabbit eating cow’s milk. The Second Seat stepped forward, drew a circle in the air, and then burned incense.
He also withdrew three paces and performed a woman’s bow. The Master stepped forward and assumed a posture of listening.
Shi [the Master] was about to deliberate on his response. The Master gave him a slap and said, "This lacquer bucket! You are acting in disorder.
Faling Yin said, "To hesitate when one ought to act resolutely brings disorder upon oneself."
A single stage of puppetry, carved from wood; half divine forms, half ghostly shapes. When the singing and drumming cease, day has not yet dawned;
a lingering cold moon still hangs in the sparse lattice window. (Xutang) Yangqi listened to the shifting currents and sealed a thousand variations;
through ancient times and today, he causes people to admire the true artist. He simply held the Three Seals of the Patriarchs.
It is so; it does not hinder the tangled confusion that is like hemp fibers. (Guantang Jushi) Yangqi ascended the hall and said:
"Heaven attains the One and becomes clear; Earth attains the One and becomes tranquil; a sovereign attains the One and governs the world.
What can a patch-robed monk do by attaining the One? After a long pause, he said: "The mouth of the alms bowl faces heaven."
Miaoxi Gaoyun said: "The old fellow Yangqi is much like someone who has drowned an entire boat of hemp and then comes back to sweep out a small scoop.
Fulong Chang said: "Big or small, Yangqi finds it difficult to forget what he is familiar with. As for a patch-robed monk who has attained it—how would he act?
He struck the ground once with his staff, let out a shout, and descended from the seat.
When the alms bowl faces toward the heavens, the worlds of the ten directions are but a single lump of iron.
Shaolin’s wall-gazing for many years was in vain; it only adds more grit to the eyes of the patch-robed monks.
(Baiyun Yuan) When a patch-robed monk applies a squeeze, the mouth of the alms bowl opens wide. Under the Yangqi school, all under heaven merely gaze at plums to quench their thirst. (Songyuan Yue)
Once, when a monk asked Yangqi, "What was the meaning behind Bodhidharma’s wall-gazing at Shaolin? The Master said, "The man from the West did not understand the language of Tang.
The man from the West did not understand the language of Tang. He sat upright and majestic before Mount Shaoshi, yet he was still struck on the teeth by Bodhiruci."
[Fragmentary] To this day there is a principle that cannot be proclaimed. (Fóxìng Tǎi) The Westerners do not understand the language of Táng;
the thunder from a drought shakes through the great thousandfold world-system. For nine years he faced the wall with no one to understand;
the jade hare and golden crow whirl within the fire. (Wú'ān Quán)
Once, when Ciming ascended the hall at Yangqi, the Master stepped forward and asked, "When a solitary bird warbles its song and leaves the clouds to enter the tangled peaks, what then?
Ciming replied, "I am walking through the wild weeds; you, too, have entered the deep village. The Master said, "The official does not allow even a needle to pass;
