Baizhang Le said: "Huanglong has all along possessed the hands and feet of one who bites pigs and dogs. Today he has been brought down by this monk.
Since a crossbow capable of pulling a thousand *jin* does not fire at a mere mouse-trap, why did it hit the target?"
Huanglong invited Heyoshan Huipu to visit him. Huipu was well-versed in the sutras and śāstras; he was known as a "Tiger of Meaning" throughout the two rivers. Huanglong asked:
"Ānanda asked Kāśyapa, 'What did the World-Honored One transmit to you besides the golden robe? What is the underlying meaning of this karmic occasion? The Master said:
"Venerable sir, when you left Sichuan, did you ever go to Yuyuan? He replied: "I went there. The Master said: "Did you [ever ask him]?"
"Will you stay for the formal registration? [The guest] said, "I shall depart this very night. The Master said, "At the Dharma site of the Wise One (Zhihui), Guan Yu offers a ritual feast.
What harm is there in staying for a while to form a karmic connection? The guest remained silent for a long time, then repeated his previous question. The Master lowered his head.
The guest hurried out, greatly astonished, and said, "The tigers of meaning from the two rivers cannot withstand a single spit from this old man."
A single spurt from Huanglong cuts through all hesitation; it brings laughter to the onlookers, yet remains a source of sorrow.
The lovely maiden has already returned to the celestial realms, while the foolish lad still dwells by the fire.
(Dun’an’s Verse) A pagoda in the mist is like a dream; mountains amidst the trees seem ready to move. At the place where the grassy stream halts its flow, a solitary city is faintly visible.
(Hongqiu Yu) Huanglong addressed the assembly:
"One person studies the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* in the morning and contemplates the *Prajñāpāramitā* in the evening, diligent day and night without a moment's rest.
There is another person who neither practices Chan nor discusses doctrine; he takes up a tattered mat and sleeps in the sun."
Thus, these two people arrived together at Huanglong; one was conditioned and the other was unconditioned.
Which of them would he settle? After a long silence, he said: "Gongde Tian and the Woman of Darkness—a wise host accepts neither."
Píngyáng Mǐn said: "This mountain monk’s Chan is not like that of the petty householder Hónglóng.
Thus, when these two men arrived together at Néngrén and settled down side by side, why was this? 'The sea is vast, so let the fish leap; the sky is wide, so let the birds fly.'"
Chan Master Cuiyan Zhenke of Hongzhou (a successor of Ciming Huiyuan) was spending the summer retreat with Attendant Tongshan at Jinkuan.

The Master prided himself on having personally seen Ciming and believed there was no one in the world who could satisfy his mind. Attendant Tongshan knew that the Master had not yet attained full penetration.
One day, while walking together in the mountains, the attendant picked up a piece of tile or rubble, placed it upon a flat rock, and said to the Master: "If you [can understand] toward this..."
"If you can utter a turning word here, I will grant that you have personally seen Ciming. The Master looked left and right, intending to respond;

Shanzhao rebuked him, saying, "To hesitate while pondering and to stop the mechanism of thought means your intellectual consciousness has not yet penetrated it. When have you ever even dreamed of it?"

The surging tide rages at the ferryhead; the short oars and narrow boat cannot cross it. If you could release the hook and turn back, I would teach you how to make the waves of the four seas clear and still.

(Duchao Fang) When Cuiyan’s Head Seat was unwell, [Cuiyan] asked him, "Is this an illness of the physical body, or an illness of the Dharma-body? The seat replied, "It has been so since early morning."
The attendant asked about the master’s appearance. The Master said, "Washing clods of earth in the mud. The attendant said, "The Master is accustomed to using this device.
The Master said, "Last night the crown of Śakra fell to the ground; why did it fall? The attendant was speechless.
The Master said, "Clouds rise on the southern mountain; rain falls on the northern mountain."
Layer upon layer of misty waters, layer upon layer of clouds; the waters submerge the cross-ponds, and the paths cannot be distinguished.
How laughable are the travelers wandering on the road, lost in the vastness, forgetting the spring of their native garden.
(Shengyi) A single leaf of the paulownia tree is scorched by the frost, turning into a lute with its tail half-charred. Who would blame it for its stringless sound being severed?
Song: "The wind and rain stir up the surging waves. (Han Guanshu).
Chan Master Wuzhen Daowu of Tanzhou (a successor of Ciming Huiyuan). A monk asked: "What is it like when one understands immediately upon encountering [the situation]?"
The Master said: "A rat carries a grinding muller on its tail.
Shending Kui said: "If you understand it immediately as being utterly still, the deep pool will not permit the blue dragon to coil within.

To seek the underlying cause beneath these words is already to become a wretched lacquer bucket. Even if there are no clouds for ten thousand miles, the clear blue sky must still receive a blow of the staff. End.
In the end, what of it? From now on, if you do not return, you shall surely attain it; who can vie for the misty scenery of the Five Lakes? Again, he offers this verse:
For the Way-man, going and staying, there is no fixed home; why trouble him by adding legs to a snake? Fortunate indeed that his single body is as light as an arrow;
how could he bear the addition of shackles upon his cuffs?
Having traveled as a guest through the hardships of the northern lands, the wanderer vainly sings the *zhègū* lyrics.
Clearly one knows the moon is upon the plum blossoms; yet by the time one sees the blossoms, it is already too late.
(Yuan’an Zheng) A fine hawk soars high, exhausting the limits of space; white clouds drift deep into the distance, infinitely vast. Ten thousand oxen could not drag back this pure wind.
Turning, as if traversing the roads of one’s native land—how many layers? (The conditions cease with the conditions.
Chan Master Fang of Jiangshan in Yuezhou (he was a successor of Langye Huijue). A monk asked, "What is the Venerable One of Immovability?
The Master said, "Wearing only his cotton robe, he passes through the marketplace. The monk said, "I do not yet understand. The Master said, "Riding a donkey, he tramples it to pieces."
Dongtingbo said, "Having passed through the three-tiered waves, listen intently for a single clap of thunder. The Master said, "Stretching out one's hand, one cannot see one's own palm.
Dongtingbo said, "Do you still permit this student to advance further? The Master said, "To address the void on purpose.
Dongtingbo said, "Beneath the roll of thunder, a small drum is difficult to sound. The Master said, "On a flower-patterned ball, there is no need to embroider red."
The banner says: "Thirty years from now, these words will circulate widely. The Master then struck him.
The guest remains the guest from beginning to end; the host remains the host from beginning to end. How can the Unmoving Honored One be touched without there being a place where he stops?
Brightly clear at the head of the bustling market; deeply plunging across the bottom of the sea. The featherless iron falcon sweeps through the moon’s gloom;

the swift hawk pierces the clouds as the sky breaks into dawn. One device treading upon another; the arrowhead meeting the arrowhead. How does this compare to casting wide one's eyes beyond the heavens?
Do not let right and wrong enter your ears. (Tian'an Sheng)
The Immovable Honored One is lively and agile; the jeweled platter rolls and turns as spring returns to the valley. Departure and stay are like the bright moon reflected in a cold pond;

unfolding and rolling are like colored clouds drifting through the azure void. Clouds hang over ten thousand li, the wings of a p’eng bird spread wide; a crane with a thousand-year span unfurls its feathers. How mistaken!
The pure breeze from all eight directions—how vast and empty it is! (Yuan’an Fu)
Chan Master Tan of Xingjiao Monastery in Xuanchou (a successor of Langye Huijue) ascended the hall. The Xuedou emissary Shengzong came forward and asked:
"Before the Buddhas appeared in the world, everyone’s nostrils reached the heavens; after they appeared in the world, why is there not a trace of news?
The Master said: "Before Chicken Foot Peak, the wind is still. Shengzong said: "Not yet—speak further!"
The Master said, "Great snow fills Chang'an. Zong said, "Who understands this meaning? It makes me remember Nanquan.
He then brushed his sleeves, returned to the assembly, and did not prostrate. The Master remarked, "Xin Xingjiao has lost ground today," and immediately retired to his quarters.
He sent someone to invite Zong back, saying, "Just now, I missed the mark with a single turn of phrase before the assembly of devas and humans."
The Master asked, "Why did you not prostrate yourself earlier? You even covered it over! Zong said, "A great man has gold beneath his knees;
how could he be willing to prostrate before an eyeless old monk? The Master said, "I have another saying. Zong then proceeded to explain his previous words.
When he reached the place where the Master was staying overnight, the Master said, "I have thirty blows to give you; go and strike Xuedou with them.
Zong then prostrated himself.
Lian’an asked, "The guest is always the guest from beginning to end, and the host is always the host from beginning to end. Suddenly, guest and host exchange places."
It cannot be said that there is nothing gained and nothing lost. If you say Xingjiao was the host, how could it be that Shengzong refused him?
If you say Shengzong was the guest, why did he instead send the staff to strike Xuedou? Do you understand?
"Were it not for the wild geese last night, who would have seen the autumn at the sea gate? Yishiyuan said: "Xingjiao’s letting go was perilous; this monk..."
He received it far too quickly. As for the intent behind saying, "Thirty blows are sent to be struck at Xuedou," how is it?
As soon as the antelope hangs its horns, the hounds find no trace.

Facing the light, one cannot cease; what can be done about it? Good words, on the contrary, cause many to fail their examinations. When the principle is grasped, the silken line is cast down once more;
from the Three Stages of the Dragon Gate, wind and waves arise.
(Sanzongzang) In the silent night of cold winds and deep snow, the tiger roars and the monkeys wail, lending no voice to one another. East and West Heaven alike beg for [instruction].
A command! Who else would boast of such a high price before others? Messenger! Messenger! Do you know or not? Year after year, the flowers fall beneath the Breast Peak (Nanyue).
(The mountain stores them. The Dragon Gate opens wide to admit the talented;
how joyful it is that another now sits upon the Tiger’s Head. Letting go was too late; gathering was too soon.
Swiftly, look back: a crescent moon at the sea-gate in autumn.
(Tianzhangyu) The wild geese arrive, vainly spreading characters from the clouds; The fish depart, needlessly overturning flowers upon the water.
This night, the moon is bright and all gaze toward it; One knows not whose house the bright moon will fall upon. (Tiefanzhou)
Chan Master Wenyue of Yunfeng on Mount Nanyue (a successor of Dayu Zhi) ascended the hall and said:
"All of you who come up here in this manner are much like thrusting your heads into a vat of glue. To go down in this manner is also to trip upon level ground.
Even if you neither come nor go, I shall strike you three thousand times in the morning and eight hundred times in the evening."
Baoshou said, "The old fellow Yunfeng is much like a mirror on a stand;
he only knows how to reflect others, yet he does not realize that even before he had stepped out of his own abbot’s quarters, he had already been 'eaten'."
Yunfeng was once asked by a monk, "Is there Buddha-dharma on the mountain peaks and rocky precipices? The Master said, "There is.
The monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma of the mountain peaks and rocky precipices? The Master said, "A monkey climbing a tree upside down."
Jingshan Daowu said: "If a person can believe, accept, and put this into practice, the task of a lifetime of study is finished.
Yunfeng was once asked by a monk, "What is the Dharma-gate of the mind-ground? The Master said, "It is not obtained from others.
The monk asked, "When it is not obtained from others, what then? The Master said, "From here to Hengyang is not far."
Jingshan Daowu said, "Yunmen was not like this. What is the Dharma-gate of the mind-ground? It is not obtained from others.
When it is not obtained from others, what then? Look beneath your feet. Falin Yin said, "Borrowing someone else's chopsticks to eat one's own meal."
Jinmingjin said, "Jinming does not think so. What is the Dharma-gate of the mind-ground? It is not obtained from others.
When it is not obtained from others, what then? [The Master] struck him across the back with his staff.
Chan Master Jingduan of Xiyu Shizi in Anji Prefecture (a successor of Longhuayue under Guinyin Cong) was visited by a nun.
The Master said, "Come back at the third watch of the fifth watch tomorrow morning. Early the next morning, the Master sat with his face smeared with red powder.
The nun entered, saw [the scene], and was startled; she then attained awakening.
Among the monks, the women were filled with shame and confusion. The "man among women" accepted it with a single smile.
From this day forward, such an ugly state is difficult to conceal; there is no need for rouge and powder to adorn the face. (Chaozong Ren)
In old age, I feel my passions have grown idle, as if utterly alone. At the fifth watch, I apply my makeup to join the nuns.
Though I have already fallen into the trap of the war-fires, can the powder on my face and the rouge on my lips be washed away?
(Shan-ci Ji) Thirteenth generation descendant of Dajian.
Chan Master Shouduan of Baoyun Monastery in Shuzhou (a successor of Yangqi Hui) addressed the assembly: "This matter is like standing atop a ten-thousand-fathom cliff.
Everyone knows that if one lets go of their hands, they will fall straight to the bottom; yet, they simply cannot relinquish their lives.
Today, Fahua, without moving a single hair’s breadth, shall lead you all to the very bottom. He then cast down his staff.
When about to cast one's body from a perilous height, who would not frown at such deliberation? Without moving a single hair, one reaches the very bottom;

the eyelids open wide to cover Mount Sumeru. (Xutang Yu) Having exhausted every word to describe the fine flavor of the lychee, he pities his child and unconsciously harms his own elegant phrasing. He goes further, taking the peeled fruit and placing it before others.
Lips. When they reach the mouth, who can afford to investigate? (Sixth Verse, Snow) Bāiyún ascended the hall and said:
"If you can truly achieve a single instance of breaking into a sweat, then even upon a single blade of grass you will manifest jade towers and crystal palaces.
If you have not yet achieved a single instance of breaking into a sweat, then even if there were jade towers and crystal palaces,"
Yet it is covered over by a single blade of grass. How can one get out through the sweat? Naturally there is a pair of poor hands;
they have never easily performed the *San-tai* dance.
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "It can certainly be believed that a jade palace and a crystal hall manifest upon a single blade of grass;
yet the jade palace and crystal hall are themselves covered by that single blade of grass—do not let him deceive you. Jingshan speaks thus for those who have already broken out in a sweat once;
as for those who have not yet broken out in a sweat once, do not even so much as touch it. Tian: [This is the name of the person who requested the commentary.]
Ning Qi said: "If you cast aside even a single blade of grass, where are the jade towers and crystal palaces?
Reaching the end of the land of Wu by the river, across the shore are many mountains of Yue. Xiaoyan Bao said: "Both Baizhang and Dahui were skilled at suppressing and elevating;
they were certainly not lacking at that time. Yet, alas, there is still the stench of sweat hitting one's nose! Furi Xi said: "Longan..."
Not so. There is no need for you all to break a sweat; simply eat when hungry and sleep when weary.
In the rain and mist year after year at Jingu Valley, who can understand how a single blade of grass dances in the spring breeze?
The courtyard flowers stir up boundless sorrow, weeping to death the crimson *jiangli* on both banks of the river. (Tianshui Guang)

When the nine variations are completed, the melody is formed; when the three endings are finished, the ritual is fully realized. Through this, the *Guofeng* (Air of the States) is rectified, and the King’s transformation naturally becomes harmonious and prosperous.
(Jue Yuan-yin) White Cloud ascends the hall:
The ancients have left behind a word or half a phrase; when one has not yet penetrated them, one strikes against an iron wall.
It is similar. Suddenly, one day, if you see through it, you will finally realize that your own self is originally an iron wall.
Now, how will you penetrate it? He said again: "An iron wall, an iron wall."
Shilín said, "Báiyún has seen through the iron wall; he has lost a pair of eyes.
Fúlóng let out a great shout and said, "What use is an iron wall? Bǎozhǎng snapped his fingers once and said, "Reduced to a hundred fragments!"
Baibyun said to Dongshan Yan, "There have been several Chan practitioners coming from Mount Lu;

when I instructed them to speak, they were able to speak, and when I asked them to clarify, they were able to clarify. They can even compose verses on ancient cases, yet it is simply not yet there. Yan harbored this doubt for a long time.
He then attained enlightenment, saying: "From this moment, a single body broke into white sweat;
I clearly realized a load of pure breeze. Foyan Yuan said: "When I served my former teacher, he cited this causal occasion and said to me:
'In the study of the Way, you must let go all at once before you can attain peace and joy. Great assembly, do you see it? He then offered this verse:"
If you can let go, how refreshing! If you cannot let go, it is like an ox pulling a plow.
It is laughable that the ancient masters of all quarters beat the drum and preach Zen without end—without end! They are not afraid, yet they are truly lamentable.
To be able to tread upon the crown of Vairocana and travel thereon, even without speaking, one naturally transmits it throughout the world. Well done, great brother!
Seeking out the Peach Blossom Spring, he wished to escape Qin; Unexpectedly, he was again invaded by bandits.
Now, as a lone horse passes before the wind, His resentment for the fallen state and ruined home grows ever deeper.
(Su Hongli) Upon being visited by Circuit Intendant Guo Gongfu, Baiyun raised his staff and addressed the assembly: "Last night, while upon my pillow, I composed this mountain..."
Verse. In response to the great scholar Gongfu, I speak this for the assembly; I ask that you clearly present it to all quarters hereafter.
This verse is not merely for the sake of the great scholar Gongfu, but is intended to strip away the flesh-and-blood undershirt from every nostril-wielding monk in the world.
It says: "The Great Man Above, Qiu Yi Ji, transformed three thousand disciples, seventy..."
"O scholar! You are but a small creature. As for the eight or nine children, their fine cultivation of benevolence allows one to know the rites.
Huìtán received [this teaching] and said: "The Old Man of White Clouds intends to strip away the flesh-and-blood sweatshirt from all the monks in the world."
Little do they realize that they are merely adding a "hawk-scented robe" to all the monks of the world.
Baoyun ascended the hall and, citing a koan to bestow upon the assembly, remained silent for a long while before saying: "The mouth is fit only for eating food."
Baoyun cites an ancient precedent; it is truly extraordinary. One’s mouth is fit for eating rice, yet few people know this.
All you venerable Chan masters, do not hesitate: once you are full, you naturally forget a hundred hungers.
(Duan’an Yan) Baoyun was once asked by a monk: "A single shout distinguishes guest and host; illumination and function operate simultaneously. Setting aside these two paths..."
"Please, Master, speak another way. The Master then shouted. The monk said, "I have long harbored doubts about you, Master. The Master then struck him.
The monk said, "A true master of our school. The Master said, "Not even that is necessary. The monk bowed.
Fulong Chang said, "This monk has long been suspicious of the Master: does he accept this statement or not?
Baiyun then struck him. Was this a reward for him or a punishment? If one seeks to select a Buddha without such an eye, what would even a thousand years of effort avail?
Baibyun ascended the hall and said: "Within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the expanse of the universe, there is a single treasure hidden within the mountain of form.
Great assembly, your eyes are above your nose and your feet are below your belly; tell me, where is it?
After a long silence, he said: "I know not where human faces have gone, yet the peach blossoms remain as they were."
A clear stream flows past the head of the green mountain; sky and water are pure and fresh, a single color in autumn.
Thirty *li* from the dust of the world, white clouds and crimson leaves drift together in leisure.
(Quánshíwò) The immortals do not dwell fixedly in the east or west; they reside only amidst the vast, misty purple mists. One knows deeply that these sacred traces cannot [be grasped].
Seeking. As soon as you intend to seek him out, he is already separated by a thousand peaks.

(Lindundun) Baiyun ascended the hall and said: "If one can utter a single phrase completely, one may take the Buddhas and Patriarchs as one's teachers; if one cannot utter a single phrase completely..."
"To serve as a teacher for humans and devas—how do you speak on this today? He then said: "Where there is water, it contains the moon;
where there is no mountain, it does not bear clouds.
Nan-yueh Chih said: "I, this mountain monk, am not like that. One phrase speaks it all: 'To serve as a teacher for humans and devas. One phrase.
"The Way is neither exhausted nor can it be fully given; one takes the Buddhas and Patriarchs as teachers. But for now, how do you speak of it?
He then said: "A torch before every door. Huitan responded: "If there were a single word, it would betray the Buddhas and Patriarchs;

if there were not a single word, it would deceive the gods and humans. To say the Way is exhausted or that it is not exhausted—to try to save oneself in either case is insufficient. How then do you all fare?"
After a long silence, he said: "Scoop up the water and the moon is in your hand; pluck the flowers and their fragrance fills your robes.
Baoyun entered the hall. Seeing the assembly gathered, he took up his staff and asked, "Does the great assembly understand?
He then struck the ground with it once and said: "Two rows of tears upon the coral pillow—half are for thinking of you, half are for resenting you."
How many times have I been drenched by water and dragged through the mud? Old in years and solitary at heart, I do not realize it myself.
The traveler does not return; I gaze on in vain longing. A stream flows through the valley, and falling petals drift along with it.

(Wuan Quan) Stepping from the painted hall upon her tilted golden lotus, she has grown weary of applying rouge and powder, much less anointing herself with incense. To a single melody of spring wind, there is no one to hear her.
Meeting. Tired, leaning against the balustrade, my heart nearly breaks. (Renzi Lin). Baiyun Zhi resided at Yuan Tong and addressed the assembly:
"Difficult, difficult, difficult—it is difficult to dispel emotional attachments. When emotion is exhausted, the perfect luminosity is a single cold pearl.
Even using skillful means to dispel emotion is still not it; to further eliminate those skillful means is utterly groundless. Great Assembly, emotion..."
"How can one dispel it? He descended from his seat, packed his bag, and departed.

Upon arriving, he paid his respects and said: "Master Duan may truly be said to have 'left his country with a body as light as a leaf,' yet his high reputation remains as heavy as a mountain for a thousand ages.
Although I, this mountain monk, am a descendant of his lineage, we travel the same road yet take different paths. With these words, he stepped forward.
He did not move his body. Why? Because where others dwell, I do not dwell; where others walk, I do not walk.
It is not that he finds it difficult to live with others; rather, for both the ordained and the laity, one must be clear and distinct.
Great assembly, tell me: whose is this—Endu’s or this mountain monk’s? He lets out a shout and says: "Let it cool down and then look!"
Baibyun was asked by a monk: "The old year has already passed and the new year has arrived; what is the meaning of 'non-transmigration'?
The Master said: "Eyebrows are above the eyes."
Having finished fishing, I return and do not moor my boat; as the moon sets over the river village, it is precisely the time for sleep.
Even if a night wind should blow me away, I shall remain by the shallow waters amidst the reeds.
(Gyotei Chūni) Falling leaves have already followed the flowing water; the spring breeze has not yet allowed the hundred flowers to bloom. The face of the green mountains remains as it was before.
It remains throughout the day, stretching across to face the setting sun.
A gentle breeze spreads warmth as it plays upon the bright sands; beyond the outskirts, crows in black plumage dot the emerald clouds. Vastly, smoke coalesces as the thousand peaks fall silent;
atop painted towers, the sounds of flutes and drums mark the presence of human dwellings. (Sharp as a spearhead.)
Baibyun addressed the assembly: Golden buds cluster thick, fresh with the morning dew; Gathered to brew fragrant tea, we celebrate this auspicious day.
Why need one insist upon wine for the floating cup? A mere trace of pure fragrance is enough to intoxicate the soul.
Liaoyuan Yuyun said: "The Old Man of Baiyun was much like a clever wife who makes noodles without flour;
it is a pity that those who can appreciate the flavor are few. Kaimu, imitating him, also composed a verse: "On the Double Ninth, the yellow chrysanthemums have not yet bloomed."
There is no need to recall Meng Jia’s hat falling; it is enough that the green mountains remain ever before one's eyes. It does not hinder the flowing waters from going forth without limit.
Yuan’an added: "Baiyun Kewen’s opening of blessings is much like Xu Liu carrying a single plank—each sees only one side."
Jingshan’s perspective is something I wish everyone to know together. The shifting of seasons and the changing of the times are but ordinary occurrences.

Once the Double Ninth Festival has passed, the first yang-energy of spring returns. Human affairs naturally give rise to thoughts of today; yet the chrysanthemums still bear the fragrance of last year.
Chan Master Renyong of Baoning in Jinling (a successor of Yangqi Hui) addressed the assembly:
"Śākyamuni Buddha preached the Dharma for forty-nine years, yet never uttered a single word. Upagupta’s chamber was filled with tally-sticks, yet he never ordained a single person.
Bodhidharma did not dwell at Shaoshi; the Sixth Patriarch did not reside at Caoxi. Who, then, is the successor?"
"Who among the many is the first to awaken? Since it is thus, let him who has no wound not inflict one upon himself.
Striking his knee and looking at the assembly, he said, "I am glad that the world is at peace."
Baoshou Fang said: "Baoning says that since one has no wounds oneself, one should not inflict injury upon them; yet he does not realize that he has already gouged out his own flesh.
He also says that all under heaven is at peace; yet he does not realize that he has already incited rebellion himself."
The smoke warms the earth’s rich loam as farming labors begin; a fresh plow breaks through the spring fields after the rain.
The plains stretch far and wide, a boundless expanse of green, where wild grasses and idle flowers bloom in succession. (Xutang Yu) Baoning ascends the hall:
The wind whistles through the branches, the rain breaks up the clods of earth; at dawn, upon the pillow, the song of the oriole shatters into fragments. The frog...
The earthworms chirp all at once; neither Miaode nor Kongsheng understands. They do not understand. Three form a group, four make a troop;
deep and mysterious, drifting and soaring, they go from village to village ahead and behind, gathering peaches and plums in clusters of two and three.
Nantang Yu said: "Baoning is much like a stylish young scholar of twenty-eight; he has consistently peddled his charm within the Chan school, which is truly fit for public admiration.
Yet, beneath the gate of the patch-robed monks, he is precisely the one who deserves a blow of the staff. Why? 'The grain does not flourish in the glare of the sun;
They compete to plant peach and plum trees in spring. This causes those who plow with all their might To become, for the most part, flower-sellers.'"
Nengrenjian held up his staff and said: "It is not so here. White clouds serve as a canopy; flowing water acts as a lute. One tune, two tunes—no one understands them.
After the rain has passed, the spring waters in the night pond are deep. Yuan'an Ji said: "The calligraphy of Wang Xizhi penetrates the stone by three inches;
the literary brilliance of Li Bai and Du Fu shines with ten-thousand-fathom radiance. Old Baoning may indeed be said to have [attained this]."
Perfectly good, perfectly beautiful. Yet, when examined closely, it cannot avoid making the nostrils of the patch-robed monk burst with laughter.

Why? Because, for the time being, there is no principle of Buddha-dharma here. As for Puci, what does he do? He sits upright upon the meditation cushion and threads a needle through the eye of a needle.
A gust of west wind arrives; two or three leaves fall. Longchi Wei said: "Baoning’s approach was like this."
The Way, though its elegant style and transcendent character manifest both principle and phenomena, cannot avoid taking its footing in the midst of a hundred flowers vying for splendor.

If it were like the bright moon in an autumn sky, with trees shedding their golden leaves, a thousand mountains baring their bones, and ten thousand waters clear and still— therein, one would still not know where the news lies.
Baoning addressed the assembly: "The Great Square has no exterior; the Great Circle has no interior.
With neither interior nor exterior, saints and ordinary beings are gathered together. Even tiles and pebbles emit light, and Mount Sumeru is pulverized.
All immeasurable Dharma gates and hundreds of thousands of samādhis—hold up his staff and says—are all right here. Do you understand? *Suru suru, sili sili*."
Lingyin Yue said, "This old fellow is much like one whose karmic consciousness is vast and murky; he is helpless against the boat.
Break the scoop! Gulin Mao said, "Lingyin has torn out his heart and liver, yet he still has not seen Baoning.
Today, this mountain monk shall once again bring it forth: when all dharmas are realized as being of one suchness, even the golden circle and the thorny chestnut are cast aside."
This is "Seeing the Great Sage at Sizhou.
Baoning ascended the hall and said: "If I speak of the Buddha-dharma to provide for the assembly, you will inevitably lose your eyebrows and whiskers.
If I speak of worldly dharmas to provide for the assembly, you will enter hell as if shot by an arrow. Setting aside these two paths, tell me: what do you say?"
What could possibly be said? A three-inch tongue has no place to use; a pair of empty hands cannot form a fist.
Master Shishuang said, "Big or small, Baoning was originally a coward. This mountain monk, however, is not so.
If I speak of the Buddha-dharma to provide for the assembly, it is like a dragon finding water; if I speak of worldly dharmas to provide for the assembly, it is like a tiger leaning against a tree.
"Mountains. If one departs from these two paths, how then? "From of old, no one has recognized the sweating horses; they only desire to re-discuss the merit that covers the age.
Baoning ascended the hall. A monk rose and bowed, then reached into his robe with his hand, making a gesture as if presenting an object.
The Master made a gesture of offering. The monk again made a gesture of offering. The Master looked to his left. The monk again made a gesture of offering. The Master looked to his right.
The monk again made a gesture of receiving an object. The Master pointed straight down with his hand. The monk hesitated. The Master said, "There is only this;
there is nothing else. The monk drew a line in the air with his hand. The Master said, "As expected. The monk returned to the assembly. The Master laughed heartily.
The jade from Mount Jing gained a value twice as high; even when meeting people, it still wishes to conceal its radiance.
The *wǔshū* stone merely presents itself in vain, only to perish by the "smile-knife" of the King of Chu.
(Jiān’ān Yí) Bǎoníng ascended the hall and, pointing upward with his hand and then pointing downward, said: "This is Śākyamuni. He then raised his fist.
[The Master] said, "This one is Kāśyapa. [He] joined his palms and said, "This one is Ānanda. [He] extended his hands and asked, "What is this?
[The monk] was put to such shame it was enough to kill him.
Xue’an Song said: “Baoning indeed acts in this way, yet he cannot avoid the futility of sweating his horses in vain.
According to Panshan, however, it is not so. Pointing up with his hand and pointing down, he said: ‘This is not Śākyamuni. Raising his fist, he said: ‘This is not Kāśyapa.
Joining his palms, he said: ‘This is not Ānanda. Then, opening his hands, he said: ‘Tell me, what is this?’”
"What? He shook his hand again and said, "When speech does not hit the mark, it is all idle talk.
Baoning addressed the assembly: "The three realms are but mind; the myriad dharmas are but consciousness. Clouds arise beyond the railing; raindrops fall before the eaves.
The mountain stream is as deep blue as indigo; the mountain flowers bloom like brocade. If one does not investigate the source at this very moment, [it will lead directly to... "
Wait until the future to ask Maitreya;
Spiritually resonant, it does not involve past, present, or future. The entire triple world is but a single point of mind: Outside the railing, the spring wind and spring butterflies dance;
Before the gate, the willows by the door sing at dawn with the oriole. (Danxia Chun)
The Chan Master Yushan of Chaling in Tanzhou (a successor of Yangqi Hui) was instructed by a visiting transformation-monk from Mount Lu to contemplate the question:
"How does one advance further atop a hundred-foot pole? Fodeng replied, "Agh! For three years he did so. One day, while crossing a bridge on a donkey, he stepped upon a plank and fell;

at that moment, he attained sudden great enlightenment. He then composed a verse: Atop a hundred-foot pole, How can one advance further? Agh! If you wish to know the meaning of this, Look at me as I fall.

I possess a single bright pearl that has long been locked away by the dust of worldly toil. Today, the dust is cleared and its light shines forth, piercing through the myriad peaks of mountains and rivers.
For this reason, I shall no longer travel to distant lands.
Jianfu Can said: "Master Yu caught a mere glimpse before the donkey and behind the horse, and immediately began to boast and flaunt it as his lifelong study of the Way.
He brandished his staff, struck once, and said: "Today, Kaixian has smashed him to pieces with a single blow!
He looked to his left and right and asked: "Is there anyone here who does not agree? He then leaned his staff against the wall.
Descending from his seat:
"He lost his footing on the stream bridge; both eyes have gone dry. He mistakenly took fish-eyes for bright pearls.
Even if dust were cleared away and light were born, it would shatter mountains and rivers—there is nothing to be seen in a dream. (Wuzhun Shanfan)
Wearing a straw rain-hat, riding a donkey across the waters of Xi; the morning rain makes the moss as slippery as mud.
It matters not that a single step breaks the bridge over the stream; turning my head, the green mountains appear low on the horizon.
(Da Wei Lun) A single stumble results in total disarray; the road to Cha Ling turns circuitous. Yet one takes a muddy pellet and mistakes it for a night-shining pearl.

(Ge Lu Tan) The Layman Sun Bi-bu (who had met Yangqi Hui) was one day attending to a legal case when Yangqi arrived. As the official was presiding over the judgment, he said, "I am bound by royal affairs;
how can I escape them? Yangqi pointed at him and asked, "Do you understand thoroughly? The official replied, "I look forward to..."
The Master pointed it out, saying, "This is the profound and vast vow of Bi-bu to benefit all living beings. The Official asked, "I do not yet understand how this is so.
Qi showed him by means of a verse, which said: "Manifesting in the body of a civil official, He widely propagates his compassionate vows, profound and deep.
When he points again for the sake of men, Under the staff, blood flows profusely. The Official attained realization.
Beneath the staff, blood flows profusely; true brass cannot rival gold. The mandarin ducks are personally embroidered by hand—there is no need to seek a golden needle further.
(From *Xuetang Xing*; *Zongjian Fali*, Volume 31)
*Zongjian fali*, Scroll 32, Compiled by Jiyun Tang;
the Thirteenth Generation after Dajian [Huineng].
Chan Master Huitang Zuxin of Huanglong in Longxing Prefecture (a successor of Huanglong Nan) was once asked by Huang Shanggu to point out the direct shortcut.
The Master said, "As for what Confucius said—'Have you disciples thought that I am hiding something from you?
I hide nothing from you'—how would you explain this? As the official was about to respond, the Master said, "Not so, not so. One day...
While traveling through the mountains, it happened that the rock-orchids were in full bloom. The Master asked, "Do you smell the fragrance of the *mugichika*? He replied, "I do.

The Master said, "Is there anything I have hidden from you? The man was suddenly relieved and prostrated himself, saying, "The Master possesses such a compassionate, grandmotherly heart (*rōbada-shin*).
The Master replied, "It is simply because I wish for you to reach your home."
His home dwells in the land of white clouds; north, south, east, and west, the paths are vast and dim. Time and again he wished to return but could not;
suddenly he heard the secluded fragrance of mountain osmanthus wafting forth. (Stone Creek Moon) The waves of the Sea of Learning have not yet subsided;
how many times has he troubled his immortal sandals to ascend the forested peaks? The celestial fragrance blows down upon the autumn wind.
Old age; unaware, we have been led together to the Hall of Broad Cold.
(Gong of Shilin) By the waters and beneath the trees, my former way of life remains; returning home in a dream is not yet truly home.
Last night, as the moon shone bright, the impulse to return stirred; a gust of western wind brings the osmanthus flowers. (Gang of Xueji)
The fragrance of the osmanthus flowers—I have no secrets to hide. After a single heap of fire, when has anything ever been concealed?
At night deep, there is no need to light a lamp; there is plenty of bright moonlight right before one’s bed.
(Zhuan’an Cheng) Huitang was discussing the *Zhaolun* with Xia Yi and Gongli. When they reached the passage on "taking all things as oneself,"...
Sentient beings and insentient things abide together as one body. At that time, a dog was lying beneath a fragrant table. The Master took up his ruler and struck the dog;
he then struck the fragrant table and said, "The dog has sentience and thus departs; the fragrant table is insentient and remains."
"How can the sentient and the insentient become one body? Gu Li was unable to respond. The Master said, "As soon as thought is involved, it becomes an extraneous dharma.
When have you ever realized that the myriad things are yourself?"
Suiyan Yun said: "The old fellow Huanglong was not sparing in his compassion. You all stand here like those who enter a mountain of jewels and return empty-handed.

If you wish to understand that the myriad dharmas are yourself and that sentient and insentient beings share one body, then kill the sentient dog and smash the insentient incense table; gather them all up completely and give them to him."
Tied into a bundle, it is cast into the great ocean of the East; naturally, it becomes vast and unencumbered.
Nevertheless, you must further know that there is a single aperture at the crown of the head before you can attain it. (He raises his staff and strikes the incense table. *Alala, alala!*
My feet and knees ache from climbing mountains; my tongue slips as I drink water. At the crossroads stands the Stone Gandang;

facing the moon and the wind, I blow the *chich-ba* (flute). Píngyáng Mín said: "There is no doubt that nails can be pulled out and wedges removed, yet Ruìyán unfortunately suffered a wound to his blade and met with a mishap in his hand.
How about this: let the sentient dog continue to keep watch, while the insentient incense table..."
"Keep this for future use. Do you all wish to understand how the myriad dharmas are of one essence with your own sentient and insentient nature?
Listen then, as this staff exerts its power for you. (He strikes the incense table once.)
In Huìtáng’s room, he held up his fist and showed it to the assembly, saying: "To call it a 'fist' is to encounter [the obstacle of affirmation];
not to call it a 'fist' is to turn one's back [on the truth]. I wonder, what shall we call it?"
Naked, with no place left to hide; before Huanglong spoke, he had already entrusted it.
If you bring your intellectual views to the gate, he has his own path that reaches through the clouds.
(Daochanglin) Backing or touching—people find this difficult to understand; rely on you to look closely. As soon as a single cloud emerges from the cave, it conceals the mountain before one’s eyes.
(One: Xuechao) One day at mealtime, Huìtáng heard the sound of the wooden board and called for the attendant who strikes the board, saying, "Give him five blows.
A short while later, when the bell rang, he again called for the attendant who strikes the bell, saying, "Give him ten blows. Then he laughed heartily. Just as the assembly...
Once everyone was seated, the Master entered the hall and struck the gavel, saying: "The assembly has finished their meal; now let us return to the Abbot’s quarters. Yongning Ding said:
"The attendant eating the staff is naturally a story that travels the world. But one must ask the old fellow Huanglong."
"Have you been able to get some rice to eat yet?
Chan Master Yun’an Zhenjing Kewen of Baofeng in Longxing Prefecture (a successor of Huanglong Nan) went to study under Huanglong, but they did not reach accord.
He then visited Xiangcheng Shun, who asked him, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Huanglong. [Xiangcheng] asked, "What has Huanglong been up to lately?"
Ji asked, "What words did he say? The Master said, "Recently, the local government commissioned Huanglong to serve as abbot.

Huangbo, the Elder, gave a test statement: 'Reciting hymns on the bell tower; planting vegetables under one's own seat. He declared that whoever could provide a response that met the standard would be invited to take up the position.
Sheng, the Head Seat, replied, 'A fierce tiger sits blocking the road. Huanglong then ordered him to go and reside there."
Cheng said, "The Head Seat Sheng would have been able to dwell [in the Dharma] had he only produced a single turning word; as for Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma, he has not even dreamed of it.
At this, the Master attained great enlightenment, finally understanding Huanglong’s point of application.
The Stone Daring at the Crossroads. Having been away from home for a long time, one forgets the native land.
The carp is ultimately more delicious in the Southland; the *cóng* leaves float upon the waves as the tangerines turn golden.
(Sanyiyu) Baofeng, because Huanglong Nan said, "I just had my attendant roll up the curtain," asked him, "When it is rolled up, it is like..."
"What? he asked. "When the curtain is lowered and one sees through the whole world, what then? He replied, "Water cannot leak through.
"When it is neither rolled up nor let down, what then? He was speechless. "How about you? the Master asked.
The Master said, "Only then would the Abbot have had his attendant carried down to the Nirvana Hall. Longhuo shouted, "The people of Guansi truly have no brains! Thereupon—
He looked toward a monk beside him; the Master then pointed at him and said, "This monk has not even dreamed of it.
Long laughed.
Bairyam Pu said: "When Huanglong said, 'He has nothing to say,' how would you have responded? As for students of the present day..."
Ten pairs of five cloths were offered to him, yet he did not roll them up nor let them go; when they were worn, they fell over.
This Bao Feng was not like that. Bao Feng said, "Only when the Master takes the place of the attendant and descends to the Nirvana Hall can it be done.
As for the teachers nowadays, they are either shouting insults or wielding blind staffs. This Huang Long, however, was not like that. Now tell me: how is it?
Where are the essential points regarding this father and son? Face-to-face, seizing the moment, swift as thunder and lightning. "He returns home;
his family is wealthy and his children are charming. Nevertheless, this still cannot withstand the cold laughter of the bystander-monks.
Baofeng addressed the assembly: "This morning is the first day of the ninth month; the frosty air of last night was cold.
You should know that every path outside the gate leads straight through to Chang'an. He gave a shout.
Suiryak Un said: "Old Jingning was urinating and defecating upon the pure ground. Where did the entire assembly go at that time?
This mountain monk dares to add his dog's tail to the fox fur. Today is the first day of the ninth month; the mountain wind blows cold against the face.
Beyond a thousand miles, those who know the sound hear the white geese announce peace. It is so, yet one has not yet seen the action."
Within the household, one does not see the Way; as soon as there is right and wrong, the mind becomes chaotic and lost.
When Baofeng returned from Xiangcheng, he visited Huanglong. Huanglong asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master. Huanglong said, "It happens that I am away. The Master asked, "Where have you gone? Huanglong replied, "To Tiantai."
While on a communal work assignment (fusshō) traveling the mountains of Nanyue, the Master said, "If that is so, then this student has attained mastery.
[The monk] asked, "Where did you get those shoes on your feet? The Master replied, "I purchased them at Mount Lu for seven hundred and fifty coins.
[The monk] said, "When have you ever attained mastery? The Master pointed to the shoes and said, "When have I not been masterful? The monk bowed in acceptance.
Zifu Guang said: "Huanglong attacked where he was not defended; Baofeng held where he was not attacked. War chariots approached the ramparts and fire-arrows drifted through the air.
As the opposing hands met, victory or defeat was difficult to decide. A stray boat suddenly called out, and the response came with the sound.
One vessel of the Jingman was seized. Now tell me: on whose side—guest or host—did this rest?"
Baofeng ascended the hall and said: "Within the school of the patch-robed monks, there is nothing that is not a transmeasure realm and sovereign meditative concentration.
He let out a shout and said: "Is this not a transmeasure realm? He then cleared his throat once and said:
"Is this not sovereign meditative concentration? He laughed heartily: "Ha! Ha! Ha! To offer this profound mind to the dust-motes and lands—this is what is called repaying the Buddha."
[Zhaozhou] said, "Thank you. Yunju Zhuang said, "Jingshan does not do it this way. He picked up his staff and said, "When attained in the mind, every matter is unimpeded;
when applied in the hand, every dharma is perfectly accomplished. He leaned on the staff and said, "That family has its own path that reaches through the heavens."
"One does not walk where the Tathāgata walks.
When the various mountains gathered at Baofeng, Chan Master Yuan of Foyin arrived late. Baofeng asked, "Why did you come so late, Yunju?
Yuan said, "Because I was wearing straw sandals and had to pass through the belly of Guizong, that is why I was late. The Master said:
Yet he was swallowed up by Guizong. Yinyuan said, "What can be done? He cannot spit it out. The Master said, "If he cannot spit it out, then let him shit it out.
Yongning Ding said, "If I were Baofeng, as soon as [Yinyuan] said 'it passed through Guizong's belly,' I would have grabbed him by the collar."
Let us say, for a moment: how many hairs are there on the gallbladder? Even if Foyin exhausted all his skillful means, he would not be able to act or maneuver [to reach them].
Regarding Baofeng Huayan’s six verses, the Verse on the Non-obstruction of All Phenomena says: "All phenomena are non-obstructive; as one wishes, they are naturally so."
Holding a pig’s head in his hand while reciting the pure precepts, he left the brothel before repaying his wine debt.
At the crossroads, he untied his cloth bag and pointed toward the sea, saying:
"It is not so here; all things are unimpeded, as free and sovereign as one wishes. Food is no concern."
I sleep soundly and am too lazy to undo my belt. When I see evil, I do not feel anger; when I see good, I do not feel attachment.
Throughout my entire life, I have never known how to fabricate strange wonders. Now tell me: is it I who am right, or is it Baofeng?
Baofeng addressed the assembly: "The Ascetic’s Rock is shrouded in moss; the Pen-Throwing Peak is entangled by vines and ferns.
In the Arhat Hall, three novices are ordained each year; at Guizong Temple, one drinks tea after the session of inquiry."
When a monk asked Tiandong Hua, "What is the principle of this? Tiandong said, "He is a man from Guansi who likes to tell stories of monks from Sichuan.
Baofeng ascended the hall and said, "Under the gate of Dongshan, if you wish to walk, you walk; if you wish to sit, you sit. Within the alms bowl..."
Defecating into a clean water jar and spitting therein—practicing while clinging to the Dharma is like a donkey dragging a millstone.
Jingtang Qing said: "I have heard it said that the people of Guansi lack brains; it turns out they are simply here for no reason."
He utterly shattered and destroyed, one by one, all the precepts established by the World-Honored One over three great *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas. Then he let out a shout.
At that time, had anyone been able to deliver a shout in response, it would have not only demonstrated the correctness of their eye of study, but also [validated the master's own realization].
Furthermore, let us allow Dongshan to proceed as a master of his own caliber; he would not dare to urinate or spit recklessly upon pure ground.
[The Master] suddenly picks up his staff and asks: "Is there anyone who would champion the cause of injustice for Dongshan? He then leans the staff against the wall.
Comparing this to the case of Zhang Qiu and the rabbit, it too was an encounter with failure.

When a monk visited Master Hongying of Lengtian in Longxing (a successor of Huanglong Nan), he rose from his prostrations and lowered the corner of his *kāṣāya*, saying, "When one has stripped off the clothes and cast aside the armor, what then?
The Master said, "Fortunately, the smoke of war has ceased; the bow-tips rest against the wall."
[The Master] hung [the robe] up. The monk then pulled up his upper *kāṣāya* and asked, "When one is readjusting their armor and robes, what then?

The Master said, "Had you not reached the banks of the Wu River, I would have known you would not be willing to rest. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "You have terrified me! The monk clapped his hands once.
The Master said, "This too is finding life within death. The monk bowed. The Master said, "I thought this was the time for withdrawal."
The one with the talent to "break Zhao like a swallow" was originally a smuggler of private salt.
Ying Shan-yun said: "The General’s command has unjustly caused the subordinates to be killed. Why did that monk not simply say 'thief, thief' and come out?
Ru-an Zhang said: "That monk charged through the front lines to resist the enemy, unaware that a spear had struck him in the back of the head."
Although Letan was able to deploy a long snake formation, alas, he lacked the means to capture them alive.
Looking to his left and right, he said, "Is there anyone here who, disregarding danger and ruin, would enter directly with a single blade?
If not, watch as this mountain monk snatches food from the mouth of a starving tiger! He then took up his staff and drove them all out at once.
He broke Zhao and gathered Yan, possessing the talent of a sovereign; he supplied the strategic pivot and seized the turning point, bringing forth the winning tally.
With his whole body full of courage, he was ready to charge at the vanguard; having fought out of a heavy encirclement, he was encircled once again.
(Xueguang Yin). When Master Qingxian of Longqing (a successor of Huanglong Nan) was inquiring after him, Long said, "Based on what you know—"
[The Dragon] saw [the Master]. [He said,] "I can only reach the upper end, but not the lower end. The Master said, "I can reach both the upper end and the lower end.
The Dragon asked, "What is the upper end? The Master said, "The wind passes over; the tree head shakes. The Dragon asked, "What is the lower end? The Master said, "Cut by knife, hewn by axe.

The Dragon said, "I, the old monk, am not like that. The Master said: *Note: This dialogue is from the *Wumen Guan* (Gateless Barrier), Case 14, concerning the encounter between Master Xuefeng Yicun and the Dragon King.*
"What is the beginning? Long said, "The hair is disheveled and the ears are prominent. The Master asked, "What is the end?
Long said, "Tightly lacing my straw sandals. The Master said, "Thank you for answering my question. Long then gave a shout.
People of that time see only the white reed flowers; they do not see the red blooms of the *liǎo* grass opening.
If you ask about the clear meaning at the top of the tree, last night the western wind reached the *wú tóng*.
(Iron-like Mechanism, Xìn) Longqing asked Huanglong, "When you attained the seat and donned the robes, how did you provide for others afterward? The Master said, "When encountered..."
"When it is square, it is immediately square; when it is round, it is immediately round. Long said, "Speaking like that, you still have traces of your lips and teeth remaining.
The Master said, "I am exactly like this. But what about you, Reverend? Long said, "Come closer and I will explain it to you in detail.
The Master clapped his hands and said, "That which I have been using for thirty years has been caught out today! Long gave him a reprimand.
He laughed loudly and said, "In one sense, they are both spirits.
Sanmei Zhenyun said, "Longqing only knew how to defeat Huanglong; he did not know that he himself was defeated by Huanglong.
Sanmei, speaking thus, still has lips and teeth. This is precisely the provision made over thirty years. You should also examine this.
Chan Master Xiansha Hechen Minghui of Fuzhou (successor of Huanglong Nan). A monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "A private road for carriages and horses. The monk took a step forward. The Master said, "The public office does not admit even a needle."
To respond to the occasion is simply to perceive the occasion itself. Skillfully setting the trap, one escapes the trap.
Just as one might intend to gallop the *huālóu* horse for a thousand li, the golden whip is snatched away by me and brought back home.
(Sixth Snow, Yinyuan) Huangbo Jicui Yong Anzhu (successor of Huanglong Nan) asked a monk, "Shenqi, it has been a long time since we last met; what have you been doing?"
[Qichun] said, "Recently I saw that Master Wei has found a place of peace and happiness. The Master said, "Try to explain it to me and let us see.
Qichun then related what he had attained. The Master said, "You are Wei, but you are not yet [the true] Wei. Qichun could not fathom this.
He returned and told Wei, who said, "You are not [Wei], yet you are never not [Wei]. Qichun’s doubts grew deeper. He went to Jicui to question Master Nan, who laughed heartily.
Upon hearing this, the Master composed a verse, saying: "Light and darkness intermingle; the pivot of killing and giving life. The realm of the Great Man is known by Samantabhadra.
Born from the same root, yet dying on different branches— The old veteran in the hermitage is made to laugh to his heart's content."
Yangshan said: "These three old fellows have needles within their cotton and thorns within the mud; there is no lack of clear rewards and hidden punishments.
Yet, as for the very core of a monk, it is worlds apart from this—why? Because it is improper to speak of right or wrong."
Chan Master Wenhui Huixian of Changqing in Fuzhou (a successor in the lineage of Fushan Yuan and Jingyin Zhen). A monk asked:

"Having left the precious monastery of the Abbot and ascended to the practice site of Yanqing, what is the Venerable One of Immovability? The Master said: "A solitary boat carrying the bright moon. The monk asked:
"What if you suddenly encounter a situation where both oars and rudders have been set aside? The Master said: "The fisherman is especially..."
Ai Su Lu-hua. Ying Shan Yin commented separately:
"If someone were to ask me, 'What is the Immovable Honored One? I would simply tell them:
'Burn incense and pay your respects.'"

Chan Master Fayan of Dongshan in Qizhou (successor to Baiyun Chuan), the fourteenth generation descendant of Dajian, went to study under Baiyun Shou. He presented the koan regarding the "mani jewel" asked of Nanquan for inquiry.
Baiyun rebuked him. The Master attained realization and offered this verse of karmic resonance: "Before the mountain..."
"A single patch of idle land; with palms joined in earnest, he asks his patriarchal grandfather: 'How many times have you sold it only to buy it back?
It is because of your love for the pines and bamboos that they draw in the pure breeze. Yun gave his approval.
Miaoxi Gaoyun said: "A patch of vacant land before the mountain—originally remembered by me. Joining my palms, I earnestly ask the patriarch:
it is simply because the deed is not clear. Several times he sold it, yet he bought it back; difficult indeed for the broker.
Out of pity for the pines and bamboos that draw in the pure breeze," he gave a shout and said: "The beggar sees only small profit. *Wen* (Record)
Fengyu Zhen said: "If you sell it and then buy it back yourself, I will not ask about that. But tell me, everyone:
ultimately, what do you call this single patch of idle land? Even if you can explain it clearly, I still wish to ask you for the deed."
Fields before the mountain are sold and bought; the pine and bamboo’s cool breeze evoke deep self-pity. It is laughable how one boasts of wealth and honor in a dream;
once awake, it is not worth half a coin. (Duan’an Yan) “Dieing with resolve, I see the white clouds;
a cup of poisoned wine is filled to the brim. Had you not drunk it, you would have returned empty-handed.”
Departing, my fields have no way to avoid being submerged by the land.
(Zhuwu Jian) When human relations gain wealth, they immediately boast of their strength; yet the pure breeze of pines and bamboo cannot be concealed.
How can this compare to sitting beneath the north window in the age of Fuxi, where one discards his robes and lies high to take in the lingering cool? (Lian’an Wen)
Loving others, he endures wind and snow; alone and desolate, he grasps his fishing rod. The night is still and the clouds part, revealing the solitary moon.
That which is unbearable to behold is yet fit to be gazed upon. A pure breeze descends; the moonlight is fading.
Casting his line, he dozes off while leaning against the balustrade. (The heavens are vast.)
Dongshan said: "This old monk has traveled for over ten years and studied under dozens of spiritual teachers (kalyāṇamitra), thinking that he had finally reached a definitive understanding.
Yet, upon arriving at the assembly of Fushan Yuanjian, I could not open my mouth again.
Later, I went to Baiyun, where by biting into a single iron sour dumpling, I truly found all flavors complete. But tell me, what was the stuffing?"
How can one express it in a single phrase? The cockscomb flower blooms, enchanting the early autumn. Who could dye its purple filaments?
Sometimes the wind stirs and they lean against each other repeatedly; It is as if they are vying with one another incessantly before the steps.
Lingyin Yue said, "Dongshan’s speaking in such a manner still lacks awakening.
Baiyun’s 'iron sour dumpling' is difficult for a monk to bite into; yet if one suddenly manages to break it apart, one lets out a great lion's roar."
(Chengyuan Guo): Returning from a military expedition, Dongshan addressed the assembly: "I have been away on expedition for half a month; my eyes could not see the bridge of my own nose.
I lost the Zen of the Patriarchs and picked up a piece of old junk. Now tell me, where shall I put it? One part I offer to Śākyamuni."
