The attendant said, "Who says that the harmonious blending is merely a single color? The purple swallows chatter; the yellow orioles sing. Who says that the 'guan-guan' call is merely a single sound?
Tianwang Hai said, "Great or small, Taiping (the Great Peace) needlessly creates complications. Today, Dizang (Kṣitigarbha) gathers them all back into one place."
Do not allow for analytical discrimination. The peach blossoms are red; the plum blossoms are white. The news from the tips of the branches has been fully revealed.
The purple swallows chatter; the yellow orioles sing. Within this very life, everything is presented face-to-face. One sees only the imperial wind forming a single expanse;
one knows not where the capital city lies.
Tàipíng was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Eating rice, one bites upon grit;
eating rice, one bites upon grit. The third tooth is hidden and lost. Once the spring breeze has passed, even the staff blossoms."
Chan Master Fuyan Qingyuan of Longmen in Shuzhou (a successor of Wuzu Faian), who was known as Cishou Shen, frequently sought instruction from Wuzu.
Whenever he asked a question, Wuzu would simply say, "I am not as good as you; you understand it well yourself. The Master’s doubts grew even deeper, and he continued to seek resolution from him.
The Head Seat Yuanli led the Master by the hand, guiding him around the incense burner several times as they walked.
He said, "You understand this well enough yourself. The Master replied, "I hope you will grant me some instruction; why do you mock me so?
Yuanli said, "Only after you have attained enlightenment in the future will you understand the significance of today’s events."
I do not understand; it is not as you say. Dharma’s gate is missing two teeth. Throughout the hall, there is the boundless wind of white arum flowers.
Clearly, they do not arise from the autumn river. (Xuetang Xing) I do not understand; it is not as you say.
Within the sandalwood grove, the fragrant breeze arises. A single song of the fisherman passes over the Xiao River.
Xiang. The sound of churning the vast blue ocean has not yet ceased.
(Ding of the Dumb Hall) For a single day, Longmen was not at peace. A monk asked, "When birth and death arrive, what then?
The Master said, "Mount Huankong. The monk asked, "Is it only this, or is there something else? The Master said, "It is in Tongcheng County. The monk reported this to others.
He paid his respects to the Head Seat (Shouzuo). The Head Seat said, "Brother Yuan, it has been thirty years since we last met; this time, I have come to see you through.
Jianfu Xingyu remarked, "The Head Seat pays his respects to one who was a fellow student of the late Master; it is a pity he died stuck beneath the words."
Longmen addressed the assembly: "A thousand explanations and ten thousand expositions are not equal to seeing one face in person.
Even without speaking, it is naturally clear. There is the analogy of the Prince’s precious sword; the analogy of the blind men feeling the elephant;

the matter of beckoning across the river in Chan studies; the matter of meeting at Wangzhou Pavilion; and the matters of deep mountains and rocky cliffs—all of these are seen through direct encounter."
It does not lie in mere explanation.
Rather, one should discern right from wrong within the human realm. Life and death swirl turbidly before the eyes like eyebrows;
it is not by recounting the events of years past that one comes to know them across ten thousand ages and a thousand autumns. (Xutang Yu)
Longmen addressed the assembly: "Heaven attains the One and becomes clear; Earth attains the One and becomes tranquil; the Sage attains the One and brings peace to the world.
When a patch-robed monk attains the One, calamity descends upon his person."
Shi’an Fēng said: "The Old Man of Longmen attained it—indeed he did—but he could not avoid being timid.
Deqing, however, is not like that. Heaven attained the One and became clear; Earth attained the One and became tranquil; the Sage attained the One and governed the world.
When a monk attains the One, the water reaches the channel."
Chan Master Qing Su of Jiuzheng’s Jiuding Monastery (a successor of the Fifth Patriarch Yuan) was once visited by Governor Lü, who came to behold the Great Image.
The Governor asked, "Since this is a great image, why does it carry two pillars upon its shoulders? The Master replied, "There are no idle hands on board a ship."
Shou then performed a prostration.
Zhaojue Qin said, "I feared I had killed everyone under heaven. Jianfu Xing said, "I thought there was no one," and he also said:
"I originally had some remaining strength. Daomiao Guo said:
"To shoulder the whole body [of the Dharma]—the light of the text is brilliant, illuminating the auspicious city. If one has not yet beheld its profound wonders, one asks others;
were it not for Jiuding’s ability to discern, one would almost mistake the markings on the scale. (Xuànjiàn Héng)
Jiuding Qin arrived while the Master was with Lao Su. The Master asked, "When the sword is at the throat during a dance, what then?
Qin replied, "I humbly pray that you will graciously accept this. The Master scolded him, saying, "Old thief! Go die! You ask me! Qin then restated his previous question.
The Master joined his palms and bowed, saying, "Yipo.
Zifu Yu said, "Even the Elder Qin is not sufficient to verify this; can the Old Man of Jiuding verify it or not?
Zifu also spoke for him, saying, "I humbly pray that you will graciously accept this offering."
The Head Seat Yuanli (who was a successor of the Fifth Patriarch Xuedou Yan) was once asked by a monk, "The sutras say to cultivate all wholesome dharmas;
what are wholesome dharmas? The Master suddenly stood up and said, "Above is heaven, below is earth; those sitting in the middle sit, and those standing stand.
What do you call 'wholesome dharmas'? The monk had no reply, and the Master struck him with his palm.
Jianfu Xingyun said: "The Way of the Great Assembly has no crosswise path; it is only right that one should proceed directly.
I dare say that when bowing to the Head Seat, the Head Seat’s nostrils fall into the hands of this monk. If anyone can examine this and see through it, they may roam freely throughout the world."
The Elder Fashu (who was a successor of the Fifth Patriarch, Yuan) arrived at the seat of Donglin Du.

Seeing that he had attained the essence of the straightforward and substantial, one day [Fashu] took up a branch of flowers, circled Lin’s meditation seat once, and with his back turned, inserted it into the incense burner, saying, "Venerable Master, tell me, what is the meaning of this?
Lin offered several responses, but none were in accord. After more than two months, Lin finally...
He asked the Master, saying, "Please try to explain it to me. The Master replied, "I simply took some flowers and placed them in the incense burner;
why does the Master himself suspect there is something amiss?"

Xiaoyan Bao said: "When Elder Chuo took a flower and inserted it into the incense burner, although there was originally nothing of great significance, since the abbot had already opened the hall and gathered the assembly, how could he avoid having some personal interest involved? Tell me, where exactly lies this point of interest?"
Liran asked, "What would you do in this situation? Yizuo replied, "That wild fox spirit!
Had I been Donglin at that time, I would have struck him across the back with my staff and driven him out, so as to avoid this mutual dulling of one another. What business is there here?
He then sighed twice and said, "From ancient times to the present, everyone says that Chan Master Chushi drove away the plowman’s oxen and snatched food from the hungry."
Regarding "human food": there are those who give freely and those who snatch it away; they can kill and they can bring to life.
When examined closely, such a person is like one who has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake. Shigan Fuyou said, "This will lead people to ruin."
A fine steed from the stable, unrivaled in its excellence, neighs against the wind and with the wind. "Come here, O Bole," it cries, as its value increases;
it shall surely earn a wondrous name that fills the imperial capital.
(Soyam Min) Yu Daopo of Jinling (a disciple of Baiyun Yuan who met Langye Huijue while selling oil-cakes) once heard a beggar one day.

She sang out: "Were it not for Liuyi transmitting this letter, by what means could I have reached Dongting Lake? Suddenly she attained great awakening; she threw the plate of steamed cakes to the ground.
Her husband looked on from the side and said, "Are you mad? His wife slapped him and said, "This is not within your sphere of understanding."
He went to visit Lang-xia. As Lang-xia looked at him, he recognized his profound realization and asked, "Which one is the 'person of no station'?
Ba replied instantly, "There is a person of no station who has six arms and three heads;
with great effort and wrath, he splits Mount Hua in two, so that the waters of Wan-nian flow on, unaware of spring. From this, his reputation spread far and wide.
The sound of song drifts from the springtime of Dongting Lake. A sorrowful person hears it and their soul fades away in secret. They weep and laugh; they rejoice and then grow angry.
Riding backward upon a lame tortoise, they chase after the qilin.

(Mei Fengren) The bright moon soaring through the void is utterly beyond kinship. The pure wind shaking the earth reaches into the poverty of one's very bones. In tattered sleeves, one is lost within the dragon cave.
Rain. How can the rivers and lakes bear to see those who mark the boat?
(Tong Qiuyu). Whenever a monk arrived, the Daoist nun would say, "Child, child. If the monk hesitated, she would immediately shut the door.
Fodeng Xun went to test her; when the nun saw him, she questioned him as before. Fodeng said, "Where is your father? The nun turned around.
Baizhang bowed to a pillar lamp stand and immediately tripped over it, saying, "I thought there was something truly extraordinary here. He then walked out.
Baizhang stumbled up and called out, "Son! Son! Come back; I cherish you! But the lamp stand paid him no mind.
Baiyan Fu said: "The numinous tortoise bearing the diagram naturally incurred the omen of its own destruction.

While the old woman is indeed to be pitied, although He Shan holds the iron tally in his grasp and is skilled at sweeping away the smoke of war, he only knows how to strike openly and does not understand how to attack in secret."
Why does the one with eyes extend a single hand from the mountain to look?
Liuyi’s delivery of the letter was known only to himself. To gain an advantage is to suffer a loss; husband and beloved son were both cast aside.
In deep sorrow and profound pity, he begs for an adopted child. (The Laughing Old Man is worthy.)
Suddenly meeting face-to-face with that iron mask, the whole family is lost and he calls out for his child.
A lion turning over, baring its fangs and claws—yet this still falls into the second gear of that fellow. But tell me, who is he? (Tudu Ce).
Chan Master Fuxin Benchai of Shangfeng in Tanzhou (a successor of Huanglong Qing under Huichang Xin), while observing a monk at the neighboring desk:

While reading the *Extensive Record of Cao-Dong*, I came upon the passage where Yaoshan returns from gathering firewood. A monk asks him, "Where have you come from? Yaoshan replies, "I have come to fetch firewood.
The monk points to the sword at his waist and asks, "What is that thing making such a 'miao-peo-peo' sound? Yaoshan draws the sword and makes a gesture as if to strike.
At this, I suddenly felt a surge of joy; I slapped the monk sitting at the adjacent desk with my palm, pulled back the curtain, and hurried out.
Langshan Yu said: "This monk knows only to greedily gaze at the fine scenery, unaware that he is in the imperial capital.

If he had ascended the peak, he could have been called a fine horse that, upon seeing the whip, pursues the wind for a thousand li. Even so, though it be thus, he has not yet even begun to meet Yaoshan. He then offered this verse:

Upon hearing it once, he was immediately startled and shook the multitude; with his feet following their own accord, he trampled the springtime of the great earth. From this point on, there was no need for even three inches of iron;
within the realm of Vairocana, he raised clouds of dust.
Chan Master Dongshan Huikong of Xuefeng in Fuzhou (a successor of Letan Qing) was asked by a monk, "How was it before the Master had seen Caotang?
The Master said, "It is present in Jiangnan. The monk asked, "How is it after having seen him? The Master said, "It is absent in Jiangbei."
It exists in Jiangnan, but not in Jiangbei. In the vast void, the Old Lord (Laojun) draws talismans;
his true spiritual efficacy eradicates a hundred monsters and spirits, scaring the bearded Li Si on the street to death. (Submitted by Xuejian.
Chan Master Yuanming Daomin of Yuandao Monastery in Jiangzhou (a successor of Leduan Qian under Donglin Zong) was [honored] by the Vice President of the Department of State Affairs, Fan Chong.
When Zhi Xu was serving as the Governor of Yuzhang, he went to pay his respects. After the tea had been finished, [Xu] said, "I am advanced in years;
having fallen among those in the ranks of the purple and gold [robes], I have drifted somewhat far from this matter. The Master called out, "Director of the Imperial Library! [Xu] responded, "Yes?
The Master said, "How could there be anything so distant? [Xu] leaped with joy and said, "I beg the Master to grant me further instruction. The Master said, "From here, go to Hongdu."

There were four stages. The Duke stood there pondering. The Master said, "If you see, you see immediately; if you deliberate, you have already missed it. At these words, the Duke attained a sudden realization.
Yingshan Yin said, "The Elder Yuan-tong has a wondrous medicine in his bag that can raise the dead and restore life in an instant."

Engraved. Although the Vice President of the Left has entered this province, he is not far from these matters; yet, alas, his local accent is still easily recognized, and he remains utterly bewildered regarding his homeland and state.
Chan Master Shao Long of Huqiu in Pingjiang (16th generation descendant of Dajian; successor to Yuanwu Keqin) visited Yuanwu. Yuanwu said: "At the moment of seeing the seer..."
"Seeing is not seeing. Even seeing is already free from seeing; seeing cannot reach it. He raised his fist and asked, "Do you see this?
The Master said, "I see. Yuanwu said, "This is like placing a head on top of a head. The Master attained sudden realization and prostrated himself. Yuanwu scolded him, saying, "What have you seen?
The Master replied, "The dense bamboo does not hinder the flowing water from passing through. Yuanwu nodded in approval.
Yunhan Man said: "To see what is not seeing is like placing a head upon a head; it is like water flowing through dense bamboo, where clouds fly and lightning dances.
Even so, Upper Seat Man still will not grant his assent. Juewang Qiu said:
"Foguo picked up a bundle of rotten vines, thinking no one would recognize them. Yet how could he have known? The 'Sleeping Tiger' has a personal touch and keen eyesight."
Yang cut him off. "Even so, why did you not wait until before he had even raised his voice and then give him a shout? This would have forced the old fellow to seal his mouth and tie his tongue.
You are busy adding head to head; you boast of your mastery of the scriptures and travel to all quarters. Be free from such concerns—do not say that he is without it."
[The Master] uses [it]. When a sleeping tiger bares its fangs, who dares to face it?
(Muyun Men) To kill, one must still use the sword that kills; the iron walls and silver mountains vanish on the spot. A master hand need not press down heavily upon the blade;
the entire army has already crossed at Lintao. (Xiaohan Yu)
A single punch shatters the backbone of empty space; tigers roar and dragons cry throughout the Great Tang.
By day, the lion’s den is overturned in alarm; a thousand demons and a hundred monsters all hide away.
(Muan Hui) When a monk asked Master Huqiu, "What is the meaning of the ninety-day restriction of the feet? the Master said, "When principle prevails, one follows it."
[The student] said, "As for those whose six sense organs are incomplete, can they still be restrained? The Master said, "They have passed right through the nostrils.
[The student] said, "Today this student has encountered a great calamity while only making a small exit. The Master said, "A surrendered general is not executed.
[The student] said, "If that is so, then the Master is letting me go as I please. The Master said, "Letting prisoners stay too long fosters their cleverness."
Severe frost and bitter snow come and go; Flakes of falling flowers dot the stone platform. Entrust this to the temple boy to sweep away quickly;
Do not let the poet-guest take it back in his sleeve again.
(Shengke Yu) When [Zhao] Shengke arrived at Daxin’s place, Daxin asked, "What kind of monk are you? The Master replied, "A traveling monk. Daxin asked, "What..."
The village monk asked, "What kind of donkey’s feet and horse’s feet are you practicing? The Master said, "What does the barbarian from Guangnan say?
Why not speak out loud? Xinxin replied, "He actually has a bit of the scent of a patch-robed monk."
Nanyue Ji said: "It is a pity that Huanglong did not provide the fodder appropriate to his own station at the end.
Had he provided the fodder appropriate to his own station, the Dharma-lineage of Linji would not have fallen into such desolation."

In this land of travelers, I feel but vain desolation; though many old friends remain at the ends of the earth, there is no place to express my noble sentiments. We may now discuss our past conversations once more.

The remaining snow has not yet melted from the rocks, yet the plum blossoms have already broken forth in spring. Pausing here with a distinct sense of purpose, we come to continue our shared path of refined culture.
(Virtual Hall Fū) Meeting by chance, when did we expect such new laughter and speech? In the autumn wind, a guest at the pine pavilion, my body alone.
Leaning on the railing, I remain silent regarding the affairs of my entire life; Meeting until old age, it is but another person. (Bao-ye Yuan)
Chan Master Dahui Pu-jue Zonggao of Mount Jing in Lin’an (a successor of Yuanwu Keqin), while serving as the head of the assembly at Yunju, gave a small-scale sermon (*xiaocan*).
Zhaojue Yuan asked: "When the sword is suspended from the brow, what then? The Master replied: "Blood splatters against the Brahma Heaven.
Yuanwu, from beneath the seat, beckoned with his hand, saying: "Stop, stop! That question was excellent; the answer is even better."
Qi! Yuan then returned to the assembly. From this, the Master became renowned by that name.
Longxiang Yin said: "How extraordinary, how extraordinary! Among these seventeen hundred spiritual friends, the vital energy remains stern and majestic."
Who would have known that two hundred years later, in the city of Jinling, we would again encounter such a master?
He is like a lute made of lion-sinew: once it is played, all other strings snap. He is like a "poison-smeared" drum: once struck, all who hear it perish.

You, members of this assembly, should attend upon and serve him without weariness or fatigue; each, according to your faculties and conduct, shall become a vessel for the Dharma. Nevertheless, there is...
The clouds and billows reaching the heavens can accommodate fish that swallow boats; there is a wind of ninety thousand *li* that can support wings that hang from the sky.
On a day when Great Wisdom was in the celestial realm, he heard Yuanwu ascend the hall and cite a monk’s question to Yunmen: "What is [the meaning]?"
"The place where all Buddhas emerge" is the gate; it is said, "Walking upon the water of the eastern mountain.
If one were Tianning, it would not be so. What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? He simply says to him: "A fragrant breeze comes from the south;
the halls and pavilions grow cool. Upon these words, the Master’s continuity of past and future was severed.
Jingshan Xiu said: "When Zhaojue held this up in such a manner, it was like leaving the Cao family gate from Zhengzhou.
When Miaoxi attained enlightenment, it was like looking toward Changlu from Zhenzhou. Jingshan’s own realization is something I wish for all of you to know together:
where the Buddhas manifest their bodies, there is absolutely no need for deliberation. In the morning we ate white congee; now our bellies are hungry again."
The myriad virtues do not belong to oneself; where, then, are the ten bodies concealed? A fragrant breeze rises from the palace halls; the days of transformation are truly long and expansive.
(Gong of Shilin) All Buddhas walk upon the water atop Dongshan; amidst leisure, there is nothing to do, and the day is especially long. A fragrant breeze sweeps in, coming from nowhere.
It is done. Without intending to cool others, people are cooled of their own accord.
(Ge Lu Tan) Amidst the fragrance of peonies, the breeze is graceful; within the shadows of pear blossoms, the moon is full.
The host lies drunk upon the pillow of Xihuang, gazing directly at the reflection cast by the pearl curtains. (Qian Ren Gang)
On the day of Dàhuì’s formal opening of the hall, after he had descended from the seat, the Vice Minister Fēng Gōngjí asked, "Master, you often say that one is not such a 'little insect.
Why then have you failed today? The Master said, "The entire great earth is this very Upāsaka Gǎo.
How do you see it? As Fēng hesitated, the Master struck him with his palm.
Pingyang Mian said: "Feng Jichuan may indeed be said to have a method for wielding the adze; yet, alas, he has no success in carving the plaster.
If it were this mountain monk, I would say: 'The entire world is this very Seat-Holder Gaofeng—how do you see it?
Then, as soon as he makes a movement or a sound, I would immediately shout. Would this not increase [his realization]?"
"Colorful officials and attendants! Nevertheless, one must still rouse Great Wisdom (Mahāmati). If someone were to question this mountain monk right now, what would I say to him?
'Clouds unfold as the moon in every house; spring comes with flowers everywhere.'"
Dahui asked a monk, "The Way does not require cultivation; it simply requires that you do not defile it.
What is this 'undefiled' Way? The monk said, "I dare not say. The Master asked, "Why do you dare not say? The monk replied, "For fear of defiling it.
The Master shouted loudly, "Attendant, bring the dustpan and broom! The monk was left bewildered, and the Master struck him.
Baiyan Fu said: "Let us set aside for a moment the fact that this monk was about to complete a mountain nine fathoms high, yet lacked the final basket of earth.
But as for Dahui speaking in such a manner—has he truly escaped being at fault? If I were that monk..."
When he was asked, "What is the state that is unstained? he simply took a basin of water, placed it before Miaoxi, and departed.
Later, when Mahamati asked about the state when both mind and dharmas are forgotten, the Master replied: "The hand of an old woman selling fans."
Shading from the Sun:
An old woman selling fans shades herself from the sun with her hand. A single style of Chan flows from the house itself.
Tell this to the traveler who has not yet returned home; why must you go outside to eat *pōzhā*? (Yuepo Ming)
Dahui asked Miaozong, "The ancients did not leave their quarters; why was it that they ate oil-cakes on the altar?
Miaozong said, "Only when you, Master, let me pass may I dare to communicate the message. The Master said, "I have let you pass; try to speak.
Miaozong said, "I, too, let you, Master, pass. The Master said, "What about the oil-cake? Miaozong remained silent.
[The Master] gave a shout and then departed.
Tianshuzhi said, "Old man Dahui was again failing to cut off what needed cutting off.

If it were this mountain monk, when he asked him why Gu De did not leave the abbot's quarters, I would have asked him, 'Why are you eating oil-cakes at the village? When he replied, 'Wait, let the Master release me...'"
Only after this time did he dare to pass along word of his condition; [the Master] then struck him a blow across the spine. Why? Because to let him go would have been unacceptable.
Dahui ascended the hall and said: "In the Jeta Grove, he was never born; beneath the twin śāla trees, how could he ever have died?
To see Gautama as neither born nor dead is to add yet more grit to one's eyes."
Baohua Ren said: "Although the Old Man of Jingshan blocks the essential ford, it is as if he sees only the sharpness of the tip of the awl.
Caoxi is not so: in the Lumbinī Garden there is birth that is not born; beneath the twin śāla trees there is extinction that is not extinguished."
"Seeing Gautama through birth and death—clearly, foul water is being splashed right in one's face! Since there is no dust in your eyes, why use water to splash them?
If you were to benefit others and assist living beings, you could not lack even a single ladleful at the very beginning.
He then looked left and right, gave a shout, and said: "Why is it that each and every one of you is dripping with water?"
Dahui asked a monk, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. How do you understand this? The monk said, "I understand.
The Master said, "You have understood the seven generations of ancestors in your house. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "Just now you said you 'understand'."
"Drink it now! It is not mind, not Buddha, not a thing—what is it?
When the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.
Ruiyan Yun said, "The Elder Dahui holds fast to this one point; even if one were to take the great void as..."
[The Master] opens his mouth. [He says: "Mount Sumeru as the tongue—its function is likewise difficult to fathom. Examining this closely, one cannot avoid having gain and loss.
If that monk had been a true person at that time, seeing him ask such a question, he would have simply said to him, 'Three watches have passed beyond the Iron Ring Mountains.
Would this not have illuminated the past and cut off the future? He strikes the whisk and says: "The staff transforms into a dragon and departs; the deluded ones..."
A man was bailing out a pond at night.
Dahuì said to Zisháo, "You only know 'investigating things' (gewù), but you do not know 'things being investigated' (wùgé). Sháo then asked, "What is 'things being investigated'?
The Master replied, "Have you not seen it recorded in a minor history? There was a person of the Tang who plotted with An Lushan."
As for the rebel: this man had previously served as the governor of Langzhou, and a portrait of him was there.

When Emperor Minghuang visited Shu, he saw it and, in a fit of rage, ordered an attendant to strike the head of the image with a sword. Since the former governor resided in Shaanxi, his head suddenly fell to the ground.
Upon hearing this, Lord Dong grasped the profound meaning and said, "Zishao [Zhaozhou] says 'the pattern of things' (gewu), while Miaoxi [Dongshan Liangjie] says 'things patterned' (wuge).
If you wish to know the single thread that runs through all, it is simply two times five hundred. The Master approved of this.

Baoshou said: "Although Miaoxi Zishao’s discourse was as vital as a gale and rarely encountered throughout the ages, he only knew how to follow the pattern of painting a gourd. Here, it is not so. If someone asks, 'What is the realization of things?
I would say: 'This jade ruyi is what Minister Tao sent. Do you understand? A single red sun dawns beyond the heavens."
"Fools all look into the mist. *He lets out a shout.* "The principle is investigated and the object is investigated;
the lantern stumbles, the pillar’s skin is pierced, and blood flows everywhere. Donning the dragon’s scales, he penetrates the Dragon Gate;
seizing the tiger’s cub, he enters the Tiger’s Den. With a single arrow at the heavy barrier, he displays his full majesty—this makes the clouds laugh to death."
A single saying on the collapsing gate: (A wall ten thousand fathoms high).
The rain has ceased and the clouds have vanished; the colors of the clearing sky are profound. The young gentleman out for spring strolls tipsy at the spring pavilion.
Whom can he speak his boundless elegance to? A single cry from a bird, and heaven and earth turn autumnal. (Tianyu Bao)
Dahui asked the assembly about the story of Xiangyan climbing the tree: "How do you understand this?
A monk replied, "Singing the *zhègū* [partridge] song in the spring breeze. The Master said, "Touzi Shouzhuo said, 'I do not ask about the tree;
bring me a phrase from beneath the tree. How would you respond to that? The monk said, "I have already told the Master just now. The Master said, "Excellent."
"Singing the *zhègū* [partridge] song to the spring breeze—this is the language of the tree above and the language of the tree below.
When the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. Dazhu said: "What a pity that this monk had a dragon's head but a snake's tail!

'Singing the *zhègū* song to the spring breeze—this is the language of the tree above and the language of the tree below'—he should have simply said, 'If you doubt, seek another teacher. I dare guarantee that at Mount Jing, the ice will melt."
It shattered like a collapsing wall. Every time Dahuai raised his bamboo stick to question his students, he would say: "To call it a 'bamboo stick' is to hit [the mark];
not to call it a 'bamboo stick' is to miss [the mark]. You cannot utter a word; you cannot remain silent. Speak quickly! Speak quickly! From...
Thirteen people attained the Dharma through this.
Yunmen raised his bamboo whisk; ordinary beings and sages alike hid their traces. Anger was born outside the Diamond Gate;
faces turned crimson within the stable of wooden horses. (Nun Wuzhuo)
A three-foot rattan snake with a mouth reeking of raw flesh; it once swallowed thirteen men of exceptional brilliance. Dust covers the four walls and the lanterns are black;
the old tail is scorched yellow, its eyes glaring with rage. (From the *Zhuyou Jian*) At Jingshan, he tested those who came to study with his bamboo switch;
if you hesitate for a moment, I know you have already fallen into the two or three [stages of delusion]. Even the spark of flint and the flash of lightning are still [but fleeting traces].
Dull! Stop using mouse-like tricks to display such foolishness.
(Shi’an Yu) Dahui asked a monk, "The Fifth Patriarch Yuan said, 'Zhaozhou’s 'the dog has no Buddha-nature' is ten thousand times better than a cat.
What is the meaning of this? The monk replied, "The wind blows and the grass bends. The Master said, "You haven't spoken nonsense either."
"But how do you understand this? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "You are merely those who parrot words," and struck him out.
"A dog is ten thousand times better than a cat; a golden-maned lion is rolled up in the grass. When the grass falls and the wind blows, there is no confused talk.
"Miaoxi is very much like a white-thief; those who merely parrot words deserve a beating. *Suru sili hūṃ*."
*Phat.* (Three times, rinse the bowl.

Dahui, because he did not understand the dialogue regarding "the phrase with existence" and "the phrase without existence"—the story of the rattan leaning against the tree—once asked Zhaojue, "When you were at Wuzu at that time, you asked about this very dialogue; I do not know what Wuzu said. Zhaojue...
He smiled but did not answer. The Master questioned him repeatedly. Huairang said, "I asked the Fifth Patriarch about this.
The Patriarch said, 'It cannot be traced; it cannot be painted. I also asked, 'What is it like when the tree falls and the vines wither?
The Patriarch said, 'It has come along with you. At that moment, the Master was suddenly set at ease.
Flowers bloom upon the bamboo, thorns arise; floating fluff forms moths, and the engraved script is deep. After Mi’s life ended, only regret remains;
the Píngyǔ Isle is desolate, its weeds casting dark shadows.

(Sān Fēng Zàng) To inquire of the matters transmitted from the patriarchs, one grows weary before the wine-cup with long discourse. Though one may be quite capable of succeeding in the Hall, [the task remains vast].
Joyful! One cannot bear to converse with Xihuang (the Sage of the Great Xia).
Chan Master Heshang Huairang of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou (a successor of Zhaojue Qinquan), whose posthumous name was Xia Tang, was once asked by Emperor Xiaozong:

"The other day, while asleep in a dream, I suddenly heard the sound of a bell and woke up. I do not know whether the dream and the waking state are one and the same. The Master said: "Your Majesty asks..."
Regarding that which is within the dream and that which is upon awakening: if you ask about that upon awakening, it is currently nothing but the rambling of one who is still asleep.

If you ask about that within the dream, there is no difference between dreaming and waking; who then could make a distinction? A dream is itself an illusion. To know it as an illusion is to be free from it.
To leave illusion behind is awakening; in awakening, the mind is unmoving. Thus it is said: "If one can turn things over, one is identical to the Tathāgata.
The Emperor asked, "Since illusions and dreams are not real, from where does the sound of the bell arise? The Master replied, "It arises from the place where Your Majesty asks.
The Emperor was greatly pleased.
Nanyue Ji said: "If Xiatang had not had these later words, he would have been nearly exposed by Emperor Xiaozong.
Falin Yin said: "How well Great and Little Xiatang articulated the principle!"
Xiatang asked a monk, "The entire Tripitaka is but harsh speech. What is your original body, Vairocana?
The monk replied, "Tiantai’s communal labor and Nanyue’s mountain excursions. The Master gave a different answer:
"Lake Anavatapta is forty yojanas deep and forty yojanas wide."
The almanac of years is brought forth for use; victory and defeat are mostly deduced from the palm.
The sun receding and the moon rising present distinct images—who else could have established these laws of the primordial heaven?
(Suan Ding) One day, Xiatang struck the drum and ascended the hall, yet he remained hidden within the curtains. The attendant monks could not find him. A monk [asked]:
The monk said, "No. The Master pulled back the curtain and said, "It is right here; why do you not see it? The monk had no reply.
The Master said, "A great axe chops at the three gates."
Chitan Zhu said: "He sat hidden within the tent, yet he granted that Xiatang was already right here. Can this be called 'entering the grass'?
As for the great axe striking the three gates—it shall be debated again after thirty years."
Chan Master Anmin Huazang of Jinling (a successor of Yuanwu Keqin) went to visit Fojian Keqin and asked him, "Foguo had a phrase that he never spoke of to anyone;
has he ever spoken it to you? The Master replied, "Shut your dog's mouth! Fojian said in a stern voice, "That is not the principle.
The Master said, "No one can snatch away your salt and tea bag. [Fojian] was at a loss.
“Why do you cry out? Jingian said, “If Foguo had not explained it for you, I would have explained it for you.
The Master said, “If you, Reverend, have doubts, seek another teacher. Jingian then let out a great laugh.
The old fisherman loves to pursue the waves like thunder; he casts his iron net down, covering the heavens. The golden-scaled leviathan plays with the bait, its fins flickering and snapping;
through a thousand layers and ten hundred folds, it breaks them all open.
(Jian’an Yi) Chan Master Fozhi Duanyu of Yuyang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture (a successor of Zhaojue Qin), while ascending the hall, said: "It is easy to fill a vast chasm."
A leaking cup is difficult to fill; yet if one maintains a firm grasp, there is neither difficulty nor ease. If one sets aside the entire earth, there is ample room;
if one lets out even a speck of dust, there is no way to pass. If you do not set it aside and do not let it out, where will you tread?
Sharing the same sincerity and common joys and sorrows, one must know that drinking water nourishes the body.
The place attained is solitary and precarious; its application is vast and wide. The entire body is fashioned into a solid sphere of purple-gold.
When the bee in the lattice thinks of next year’s nest, do not bore into the old site amidst the flying dust.
(Bījaśrī) Chan Master Cihang Jǐngyuán of Hùguó Monastery in Tāizhōu (successor of Zhāojié Qín) ascended the hall and said: "Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvaranirghoṣa..."
That previous group of fellows was off by seven or eight; after King Weyin, that next group of fellows missed by two or three;
yet this present group of fellows sits and stands with such solemnity. Tell me, is this being off by seven or eight?
"Having fallen twice and thrice, will you still be able to attain liberation? [The Master] raises his whisk and says: "Hūṃ, hūṃ!
In the deep shade of the thickets and bamboos at Little Plain, the clear, rushing stream sounds like a lute.
Having happened upon the broken bridge under the bright moon, the old monkey cries out in the desolate silence of midnight. (Fenxiang Jixiang)"
Chan Master Ren (Suzuki Shōkei), successor of Zhaojue Qinqin, ascends the hall at the Rantang Hall of Zhong Tianzhu in Hangzhou Prefecture:
"The springtime has already passed its halfway mark; the weather for nurturing flowers is perfectly harmonious.
Upon the branches of the *haitang*, the song of the oriole is fine—do you, followers of the Way, perceive this? Even so, how shall one pass through sound and form?"
Born upon the Way: the golden-reined horse neighs in the fields of fragrant grass; the jade-towered person is drunk beneath the apricot blossoms of spring.
Her youthful countenance vies with the richness of the three months; yet she draws her green woolen shawl over herself, no longer visible.
Pretending to take up a golden hairpin to smooth her fluttering tresses, her figure appears as a shadow beyond the curtain within the painted hall. (Pingxiang)
Chan Master Shouxun Fendeng of Heshan in Anji (heir to Taiping Qin): Once, while Yuanwu was traveling with him on a mountain excursion, they happened upon a deep pool.
Yuanwu pushed the Master into the water and immediately asked, "What was it like before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master replied, "The pool is deep; the fish gather. Yuanwu asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master replied, "The tree is tall."
Zhao Feng asked, "What is it like when seeing and when not yet seeing? The Master replied, "Stretching out one's legs is precisely within drawing them back.
Wuzhuo then praised him.
Nantang Yu said, "Heshan, you have attained it; you have attained it. Yet you cannot avoid being mired in water and mud. Yuanwu was indeed high, but [Nantang's critique] was also high.

Alas, how can one help but employ the mind and put it into practice? Although this is so, "If you do not enter the startling waves, you will find it difficult to encounter the fish that satisfies your heart.
When a monk asked, "What is the matter that transcends [the ordinary]? the Master said, "If the great ocean were to know contentment, the hundred rivers would surely flow backward.
The monk bowed, and the Master said, "This is what you have studied for thirty years, Upāsaka Xu."
Never willing to encounter the sharp edge of worldly affairs, his carefree traces are free from the burden of ornaments. Clad in coarse, shaggy robes, he sits in the *kijū* posture;
against the wind, he empties the fragrance of his precious casket.
(Pingxiang) Chan Master Mingbian of the Main Hall at Daochang Monastery in Anji County (a successor of Longmen Yuan). In his room, he questioned students regarding earthworms.
Why does the earthworm transform into a lily?
Having stayed in a guesthouse in Bingzhou for ten years, my heart longs to return day and night to Xianyang.
Without cause, I have crossed the Sanggan River once more; Now I remember Bingzhou as my true hometown. (Cen Yuanji)
When the earthen dragon and the lily flower transformed, I asked him about it, but he knew nothing from the start.
Generally, when people meet, jealousy arises; there are few with beautiful brows in this world.
(Tianye Zhou) Chan Master Yue’an Shanguo of Daming in Tanzhou (a successor of Dongshan Yan’s lineage at Kaifu Ning) ascended the hall. [He said: "Xi Zhong fashioned..."
A chariot has one hundred spokes; remove both ends and take away the axle. Holding up his staff and drawing a circle, he said, "Do not mistake the zero point on the scale.
He struck it once and descended from his seat.
The Sea God knows its nobility but not its price; it remains for the human world to illuminate the night.
The blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head—who would have known that its function leaves no seam or crack? (Moon Forest Guan).
Shangshu Mojiang, Layman of Fenning in Hongzhou (disciple of Dongshan Yan, who saw Daisui Jing), was an official in Western Shu. He went to pay his respects to Nan... [text ends]

Nantang consulted him regarding the essentials for resolving his doubts. Nan-tang instructed him to maintain a state of alertness toward the source of goodness. After a long time without any breakthrough, he happened to enter the latrine;
suddenly, the stench was so foul that he covered his nose with his hand, whereupon he attained realization. He saw clearly how Nan-tang had been acting for him and presented this verse:
"From the beginning, my natural grace has loved elegance; I have often laughed at those who seek it outwardly."
"Ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences—nowhere to be found. Once attained, it has always been at the tip of the nose. Tangke approved of this.
Yingshan Yun said, "Although the Minister (Tangke) reached this through diligent effort, if one examines him closely, he still carries a trace of foul odor.
Why? Because he fell down right at the edge of a latrine."
The lay practitioner Wu Juhou (who had studied under Yuan Tong Min), holding his official insignia, returned to Zhongling.

He visited Yuan Tong and said, "In the past, when I went to the provincial examinations, I passed through Zhaozhou’s barrier. I once asked the former abbot, Elder Ne, about the matter of 'passing the barrier,' and he replied, 'Go ahead and take up your official post.
Now, it has been more than fifty years without my realizing it. Yuan Tong said: [He continued: "Have you ever..."
"Do you understand the matter of passing through the barrier? The Master said, "I have passed straight through eight times, yet I always maintain this thought;
however, I have not yet reached a state of complete liberation. Tongdu handed him a fan and said, "Please use this fan. The Master immediately waved the fan.
Tongdu said, "Where is there anything that is not liberated? The Master suddenly attained realization and said, "Please grant me the final word. Tongdu, however—
[Changsha] waved his fan twice. Master Gong said, "Intimate! Intimate! Tong said, "The tongue of the Jiao barbarian reaches three thousand li. Yingshan Yin said:

"If Yuancong had not followed up with these subsequent words, he would have failed to avoid leaving Master Wu in a state of dull stagnation, merely playing with his vital spirit at the point where the fan was waved—what end could there have been?
As for saying, 'The tongue of the Jiao barbarian reaches three thousand li,' what does this mean?"
The Essential Meaning.
On the anniversary of his death at Tiger Hill, Chan Master Tian Tong Ying’an Tanhua (successor of Huqiu Long), the seventeenth descendant of Dajian, offered incense and said: "Even..."
This old monk of no intelligence, who has encountered birth and death and met with calamity, has exhausted every artifice, yet he could never find a place to settle.
From that time on, he laid down his weapons; he puts on clothes and eats food according to his lot.
For twenty years he has sat upon the wooden stool, hanging up sheep and selling dogs—what evidence is there that this has any basis? Nevertheless, once a year he burns incense.
"Xiangri (Fragrant Sun). For a thousand ages, it causes people's resentment to deepen.
Juewang Li said: "From the beginning, there has been much spirit; at the end, all deliberation ceases.

The old man Ying’an was so thoroughly pierced through the nostrils by Huqiu that he had nowhere to vent his breath. Having endured this for years and months, he finally found relief upon a single incense offering.
Announcing it to the gods and the ghosts—this is truly like carrying stolen goods while crying out for innocence. It makes people laugh. But tell me, what is there to laugh at?
Hanging up the head of a sheep while selling dog meat.
"Dog meat and sheep heads, calling for the Patriarch; putting on clothes and eating rice, simply following the times. The bloody battles on the desert sands are now forgotten;
raising up the deep-seated enmity, one does not let it go. (Muyun Men) "Words spoken do not enter; he displays his transcendence.
He has already passed through by borrowing this path from before. Dog meat and sheep heads are found everywhere."
Sold! To this day, there are those in the world who are confused by this.
(Mifeng’s Secret Transmission) Ying’an ascended the hall and said: "Sitting in a wall for nine years ruined the descendants of the East;
returning to the West with a single shoe left the Old Man of Yellow Face at a loss. He drew a line with his staff and said: "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; a single horse—"
"Three Tis (寅) arise. Yunhanman said:
"The ancient path of the stone ox spans heaven and earth; a single horse and three tis trample over demons and Buddhas.
Do you know where this old fellow lands? A sword leaves its precious scabbard because of injustice; medicine comes forth to save the sick."
The Golden Pitcher.

Ying’an addressed the assembly: “It is like a fine horse that gallops at the mere sight of the shadow of a whip. At that time, Fozhao Guang stepped forward and said, “One who sees the shadow of the whip is not a fine horse.
The Master [Ying’an] then ceased speaking.
The second head, with flames swifter than the wind, cannot bear the sorrow; it can only endure the grief.
After one long cry that shakes its mane, ten thousand horses fall silent as the battle is won.
(Beijian Jian) Truly a fine steed, how could it suffer the whip? Leaping into the air, it surges ahead of all men. Its fame is inscribed across the seas, and all people praise it.
Noble! How regrettable that Han’s sorrow turns toward the past. (Yuan Shu Zong) Ying’an said:
"Before the fifteenth day, one draws water and sets fire; after the fifteenth day, magpies chirp and crows caw.
On the fifteenth day itself, the wind is calm, the waves are still, the state is prosperous, and the people are at peace. There is a single phrase that reaches [the truth].
"You have silenced my mouth; I have not a single word to give you. You have blinded your own eyes! At the crossroads stands Pan Siliang:
his hair uncombed, his face unwashed—know him as either a sage or a commoner."
Tianzhen then said: "The old fellow Ying'an seems to rely on his wealth to bully the poor; he has not failed to show off his cleverness. Haimen, however, is not like this:
before the fifteenth day, light is not separate from darkness; after the fifteenth day, darkness is not separate from light.
On the very fifteenth day, light and darkness are suddenly forgotten, and past and present are transcended beyond all dependence. In what direction, then, will you all turn?"
Investigate this thoroughly. [The Master] strikes the whisk and says: "In leisure, one finds no accord with the joy of forest and springs; sitting long, one hears only the sound of wind and rain.
Ying’an addressed the assembly: "The phrase that cannot be uttered even with one’s full strength does not lie at Tiantai; it must surely be at Nanyue."
When you scold one another, let it be; I spare you the binding with thorns. When you spit at one another, let it be; I spare you the splashing of water.
Suddenly, you grasp the head of a snake. Clapping hands, "Luo-luo-li-li! (Kentang Chong).
After Jīvaka departed, there has been no news. The sick press against the gate day after day in their distress. The hundred herbs know for themselves that they lack consciousness.
[The speaker] was weeping profusely at the base of the fence. (Xutang Yuyuan) Sheng'an addressed the assembly:
"Zen, Zen! Do not torment one another further. Those who sit, let them sit; those who sleep, let them sleep.
All of you shall be at peace and happy. There is no dharma to be transmitted. Zen, Zen! The Five Ranks of Dongshan, the Three Mysteries of Linji—Dadian."
Thirty nights have passed. Feet tread the earth; heads touch the heavens. Meditating and meditating—worth not even half a coin. When the ocean dries up, its bottom is finally seen;
when a person dies, the skin of their feet wears through.
Quanshi Le said: "The old fellow Ying’an’s mouth is like a hanging torrent, yet he can only speak half of it.
Today, I, this mountain monk, shall proclaim this remaining half before the assembly, without concealment or reservation.
I wish to walk hand-in-hand with this old man. Zen, Zen! Like fire catching or oil being fried; when hungry, eat; when weary, sleep. A divine immortal!"
The secret essence is not transmitted from father to son. Chan, Chan! The most subtle within the subtle, the most profound within the profound.
If Bodhidharma had not come to the Eastern Land and the Second Patriarch had not gone to the Western Heaven—Chan, Chan! Yellow chrysanthemums bloom like gold coins; a tiger wears a paper cap.
Dongba wears a cloth shirt. Huizhou Yuan said: "The Patriarch of Hua held this up in such a way that it might be called emptying his belly and pouring out his heart.
Yet, alas, those who recognize this kindness are few. Since I am a descendant in his lineage, I cannot avoid meeting him face-to-face.

Zen! Zen! The tea is ready and the incense is burning; beneath the clear wind and the moon, one sleeps on a stone pillow amidst the clouds. From the very beginning, there has been no handle to grasp."
There is something truly worthy of transmission: Chan, Chan. A single phrase, already perfected, splits asunder the Three Mysteries. The flowing water reaches the sea;
the moon never leaves the sky. Chan, Chan. In Guanzhong they use iron coins; if you do not sleep on the same bed, how can you know there is a hole in the lining of the quilt?
Chan Master Fozhao Deguang of Yuwang in Mingzhou (a successor of Dahui Zonggao) was summoned for an audience by Emperor Xiaozong of the Song dynasty.

When the Master recited the verse of Lingyun—“Up until now, there has been no further doubt”—the Emperor asked, “Where is it that he has no doubt? The Master replied, “That is precisely where he has no doubt.”
The Emperor said: "Empty-handed, he leads an iron ox;
amidst the leisure between ten thousand affairs, he probes the Chan school. How could the Six Dragons rest midway? Empty-handed, he leads the ox past the Celestial Gate.
The Purple Palace lies deep within the Sublime High Peak. (Guitalu Jushi)
When Emperor Xiaozong questioned Fozhao about what Śākyamuni Buddha accomplished during his six years in the mountains, the Master said:
"I thought Your Majesty had forgotten.
After six years of diligent toil, what was ultimately achieved? I ask the King: do you remember? Although one may know the answer directly, it is difficult to withstand [the challenge].
**Hui (諱):** In the end, it can never be glossed over.
(Beijian Jian) A great root, a great vessel, and great cultivation; With a sudden turn of the pivot, one reaches the ultimate source. For ten billion years there has been but one Buddha;
The Snowy Mountains have never separated him from the Dragon Palace. (Shiyan Lian)
Chan Master Yan of Wan’an at Donglin in the Nine Rivers region (a successor of Dahui Zonggao) addressed the assembly:
"Sitting upon the Buddha’s throne and hacking off the Buddha’s feet, he shows no respect for Confucius of the Eastern House, yet turns westward to practice ritual and music."

Kengtang Chong said, "To enter the mud and enter the water is not non-existent; yet how can one say the former master was not like a cicada clinging to a withered tree, weeping until its tears were spent without looking back?
He struck the meditation staff and said, "Truly, there is one who does not look back.
I, Jingci, prostrate three times to you within this incense burner."
Chan Master Shiyi of Jingci Water Hermitage in Hangzhou (a successor of Fozhi Yu) posed this question within his quarters:
"Why does the barbarian from the Western Heaven have no beard?"
The cowherd boy lost his tattered straw raincoat; drifting away for many years, it is rarely seen.
Picking it up and draping it over the fence-top, he draws the crows to fly around the tree.
(Ding of Baichuang) Chan Master Xiangtang Xingji of Guoqing Temple in Taizhou (the successor of Huguo Yuan), ascended the hall. "Perfect Penetration does not open the gate of birth..."
A medicine shop that sells nothing but dead cat heads—truly, who would not be struck with cold sweat all over their body upon encountering such a thing?
Panshan Song said: "At this Panshan, we do not open a pharmacy for the living, nor do we sell dead cat heads."
Holding but a single unperforated flute, he blows it against the wind, severing the autumn of the Chu River.

At Jiaoshan Pujisi, Chan Master Huan’an Shiti (the successor of Huoguo Yuan)—when asked by Ge Xinzhai: [The master] replied: "A single branch of the unperforated flute; blowing against the wind, it cuts through the autumn of the Chu River. At Jiaoshan Pujisi, Chan Master Huan’an Shiti (the successor of Huoguo Yuan)—when asked by Ge Xinzhai:
A husband and wife were fighting. Their son was summoned to serve as a witness. When asked to testify for his father, he did so; when asked to testify for his mother, he did so.
The Master said, "The small emerges and meets the great," and then offered this verse: Eight-armed Nātha with three eyes, Beating the drum with twin mallets at the prow of the ship.
The giant turtle swallows it all in one gulp—the azure seas are emptied; The winds clear across the four hundred provinces of the universe.
In the cycle of birth and death, we pity ourselves as sharing the same chamber and burrow; for what reason are we separated midway by passes and mountains?
One morning, suddenly attaining the realization of one’s own child, only then does one realize how difficult it is to uncover what has been covered.
(Xuetang Xing) *Zongjian Fali*, Volume 34.
*Zongjian fali*, Scroll Thirty-Five, Compiled by Jiyun Tang;
under the lineage of the Great Mirror (Dajian), Eighteenth Generation.
One day, while serving Chan Master Mian Xianjie of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture (who was a successor of Ying’an Hua), the Master attended him.
The Master asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master replied, "A broken sand pot."
The King of Awakening (Jue Wang) established a distinct verse: "A bucket with its band removed;

A young gentleman of the Five Tombs in his prime, Delighting in the spring breeze as he gallops on horseback, Sparing no golden coins for pellets, Striking the yellow oriole beneath the sea-blossom trees. (Shuang Shan Yuan)
White jade carved into clay pellets; yellow gold cast into iron *Kunlun* mountains. A thousand-year-old滞貨 (stale goods) no one buys;
inevitably, they now burden one's descendants. (Great Rest and Humility) A thousand pieces of gold spent until nothing remains;
for food and clothing all day long, one must take from others. This is not the true chivalry of the Five Tombs.
Bones. Turning one’s head, one still clings to the old turban.
(Yuehan Qian) The Eye of the True Dharma has never uttered such words; how could a broken sand pot have spoken this? A lifetime of indulgence in wine makes resentment hard to erase;
treading on the moon and wading through flowers, one passes through distant villages. (Zhao’an Fan)
When sorrow comes, not a single word can bear the heat; after intoxication, a thousand cups are not considered too much.
Turning over the sand basin, the eyes are extinguished; half a window of frost-moon amidst the misty vines.
(Lian’an asked: "The hair-tip star is now present at the gate; a hundred monsters and a thousand demons are all transformed into grace. Chew thoroughly the red steel until it is crushed."
A lump of clay. It turns out to be a bottomless broken sand-basin. (Nanyue Jue) The great chiliocosm is pitch-black and vast.
For years, the Dharma-eye has not been fit for inspection. I bring forth this broken basin; it cannot be struck through.
Let the ancients and the present-day alike compete to bore into it. (Muyun Men)
Mimian was once asked by a monk, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master said, "A straw sandal has no thread.
The monk asked, "As for your saying, 'Breaking a sand pot,' what does that mean? The Master said, "I have never moved my tongue.
The monk said, "These words have already spread throughout the world. The Master said, "Guessing with a ladle while listening to empty sounds."
Nanyue Ji said: "One turn of phrase secures the state; one turn of phrase ruins the livelihood and destroys the family.
If anyone can examine this thoroughly, I, the mountain monk, grant them a secure seat in the ancestral hall."
Mimian addressed the assembly: "In a year of three hundred and sixty days, tonight is precisely the moment of transition.
To shift one's body and change one's step requires nothing more than this; throughout the six directions, the pure breeze continues to blow without ceasing."
Zudeng Shao said: "I, Huqiu, am but a humble descendant of his lineage, yet I shall attempt to imitate him.
Three hundred and sixty thousand days in a hundred years—counting them forward or backward, there is neither beginning nor end. This evening we gather together; the New Year approaches.
With a single crack of a firecracker, who knows when it will cease? Is there anyone here who can link arms with the Patriarch? If there is, let a solitary wild duck fly forth!"
The ground rises high. If there were not [this], a pair of mandarin ducks would stand alone in the pond.
Chan Master Yian Youquan of Huazang in Changzhou (a dharma successor of Wuan Quan) once sat through the night until dawn.

When the one who distributed gruel arrived, he forgot to open his alms bowl. A neighboring monk touched it with his hand, and the Master was awakened by this. He composed a verse, saying: "Black lacquer..."

Kunlun holds his fishing rod; the ancient sail is hoisted high as he descends the surging rapids. Amidst the shadows of reeds, he plays with the bright moon, drawing the blind turtle up onto his fishing boat.
Clouds deepen, the river is cut off, and the sail is drawn alone. It is a pity that the neighboring monk pulls the rudder around.
Only then can one believe the matter of the Perfectly Bright One’s snap of the fingers; it turns out this saying is not empty.
(Guītáng Jūshì) Cen Master Yànfǎng of Jìngcí Monastery in Hángzhōu (successor of Wàn’ān Yán), addressed the assembly: “Observe the direction and you will know where he has gone.”
The traveler does not arrive at any direction; the heel of his straw sandals suddenly breaks.

His whole body is already in the Imperial Capital—how can it be said that observing the directions does not occur within the directions? The moment one opens their foul mouth, they become perverse and distorted.
The traveler wishes to seek the road to Chang’an, yet before they know it, their whole body is in the Imperial Capital. (Closing the Room / Opening the Door)
The Nineteenth Generation Dharma Successor of Dajian (Baizhang), Chan Master Zu'an of Wulong in Kuizhou (a successor of Tiantong Jie), was serving as an assistant seat at Lingyin Monastery.
A practitioner of the Way requested instruction, saying: "I cannot catch hold of this monkey; I pray you will grant me your guidance. The Master said: "Why use 'catching'? It is like the wind."
Blowing upon the water, patterns naturally form.
Jue Wang remarked, "Pobian’s response to the question required no effort at all; the seeker, in seeking further instruction, brought about his own defeat."
Furthermore, I ask you all: where is the monkey right now? Jiang Tianhai said, "Tell me, before the wind has even arisen, where are the ripples?
*Duh!* It would have been better to stop this imprisonment and let go of such cleverness.
The Most Benevolent Son of Heaven harmonizes the Jade Candle; the winds of the universe are clear across eight hundred provinces.
Without the slightest blade being raised, the King’s transformation spreads everywhere; the One Man sits upright, hands folded, within the Dragon Pavilion.

(Pingyang Min) Only when dwelling in a great state does one truly know nobility; when the waters reach Xiao and Xiang, they flow with singular clarity. Suddenly, the wind sweeps across the rivers and lakes.
Sweeping away all in a single breath, he blows through the ice of spring until it melts.
(Lianwen) Seizing the throat and holding the strategic pass, the rushing torrent crossing the blade depends entirely on the person. To speak of the Way is merely ordinary speech;
all artifice is utterly extinguished, leaving only the intimacy between father and son. (Muyun Men)
The Sword-Trees, Knife-Mountains, and the Realm of Rākṣasas; the Cauldron-Broth, the Furnace-Coals, and the Ghost-Gate Barrier—Yama the King ultimately does not subject one to these tortures;
