under the Great Mirror (Dajian), Twenty-Fifth Generation.
Chan Master Shiwu of Wansong Peak at Dengwu in Suzhou (a successor of Qianyan Chang) went to visit Qianyan.
Qianyan asked, "With what do you come to meet this old monk? The Master raised his fist and said, "I meet the Abbot right here.
Qianyan said, "Once dead and burned, where will you find a place to settle your body and establish your life? The Master replied, "The bubble arises and the bubble perishes; the water remains."
The wind ceases and the waves subside; the moon reflects upon the pool.
The wind rises high and the moon grows cold as the azure sky stretches wide. Suddenly the Milky Way pours forth its jade-like essence;
In an instant, all becomes a single color. One lake ripples, one lake is spring. (The Gate of Wisdom Opens)
The "Warm Spring" melody is sung forth, awaiting those who understand; the "White Snow" is presented, and the meaning grows ever deeper.
In vain do they say the trapped fish seeks only the pond; naturally, the secluded bird delights in the lofty forest.
(Byun-an Yong) The frosty wind is piercing and impossible to turn back; before it enters the silk robes, the bones are already cold. One cannot obtain even a fraction of the "Warm Spring."
Power. Striving for mastery, he lets out a long啸 (shout) while leaning alone against the railing.
(Quan Jianxu) Holding up his fist to meet him, he turns away before realizing he is stuck in deep mud.
Even if he were to leap out from a lotus root, it would not equal following the Vajra Precious Sword. (Qiushan Kui)
Wanfeng asked Yanguan, "It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha, and it is not an object; what is it?

The Master drew a circle with his sitting cloth, crossed his hands, and stood there. One day, while they were working together to cut pine trees, the Master picked up a round stone, made the gesture of offering a pearl, and said, "I ask the Master to set its price. Yanguan replied, "It is not worth half a coin. The Master said:
"Blind! Yan said, "I am blind, and you are blind too. The Master said, "Blind! Blind!
Standing alone on a solitary peak, he reaches throughout the nine provinces; presenting pearls and offering stones, he blinds both eyes. Without wind, white waves toss heaven and earth;
with one shout, the waters of the West River flow backward. (Fushan Zhu)
Wanfeng, because of this, ascended the hall and raised the koan: "When the lotus leaves move without wind, there must be fish swimming.
The Master let out a shout, shook his sleeves, and departed. Yuyan presented a verse, saying: "Deep green chrysanthemums fill the eyes; autumn is here.
Baizhang sits upright atop the azure peak. Lightly he brings forth the phrase 'no guest, no host. With one shout, the waters of a thousand rivers flow backward."
Beneath the pines for a thousand years lies the *fuling* fungus; how can it compare to the brilliance of a precious jewel?
How joyfully one hears the fierce tiger’s roar in the mountains, yet it does not hinder the swimming fish as they travel through the seabed.

(Muyun Men) Master and disciple are both utterly extinguished; with heads held high and horns upon their brows, their spirit rushes on with martial vigor. They kick over Mount Kunlun, leaving no trace behind.
Mutually. Earth-shaking winds and thunder darken the seas and mountains. (Zifu’s Contemplation).
The twenty-sixth generation descendant of Dajian (Nanyue Huairang), Chan Master Baozang Puchi of Dengwei in Suzhou (successor of Wanfeng Wei). The verse of entrustment from Wanfeng says: Dayu.
Pain beneath the ribs; the fists are clenched. The Three Essentials and Three Mysteries transcend both the orthodox and the biased.

Among the lions within the cave of Linji, the lamps continue their blazing flame, transmitted through ancient and modern times. When Feng was about to enter extinction, someone asked him, "How many disciples in your assembly have attained the Dharma?
Feng showed them this verse: "Compassion without thought; The flower blooms and the fruit ripens. *Inga* (the cause).
The ground is clearly distinguished. The Jewel of Wisdom offers this entrustment:
"The eyes of the bed-wetting ghost-child have opened; three fists beneath the ribs—truly magnificent!
To spend one's father’s money is not to be a good son; bring forth the path of the living mechanism. (Muyun Men)
The Eye of the True Dharma has been completely extinguished. What school is this, propping up and supporting? Who knows that from nothingness, much trouble arises?
To stir up trouble in others’ households—their transgressions are beyond measure. (Zifu’s Contemplation) In old age, he lowers his line to catch the crimson fish;
leisurely, he takes a gāthā as a fragrant treasure. As for the Buddha-dharma, there is not much to it—it is like wetting one’s bed.
Son, the practice of divination by stalks has long deceived later generations.
(Nanshan Duan) From antiquity, the gates of generals have produced heroic talents; inheriting the family’s reputation, they deploy the Six Tactics.
It reaches the point where the tiger tally hangs from their elbows, their towering presence surpassing all lofty standards. (Keda Yan)
When Lord Zhang drinks wine, Lord Li goes mad; a fist struck beneath the ribs cuts off both the orthodox and the deviant. Within the lion’s den there is no other beast;
the succession of fragrant blossoms and the continuation of the flame are transmitted through all time.

(Fushan Zhu) One verse has been passed down to this extraordinary age; lamp after lamp continues the flame throughout the myriad peaks. The lion cubs, generation after generation, remain rooted in the source.
The Pulse: The sun and moon shine together, illuminating the ancient spring.
(Pingshan Gao) Linji’s single Eye of the True Dharma is taken up and entrusted to this person. A single bright moon shines through past and present;
ten thousand households and a thousand lamps share one reality. (Nanzong Chuan)
A crimson fledgling peers from the phoenix’s lair, catching a glimpse of a single speck. The total mechanism of "yes" and "no" rivals the spiritual mountain;
soaring beyond the clouds, the golden light appears. The inexhaustible lamp of mind illuminates the end of night.
(Hèyá Wù) — The twenty-seventh generation under Dàjiàn.
Chan Master Xubai Huichan of Dongming in Hangzhou (a successor of Baozang Chi) attained a realization upon seeing a pine tree. He reported this to Baozang, who rebuked him.
One day, Baozang asked, "The mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way. How do you understand this?"

The Master approached to inquire after his well-being and stood with palms joined. Huizang rebuked him, saying, "After all this time you have been here, is this the kind of understanding you have attained?
The Master was filled with indignation; by the second day, he suddenly penetrated to the very source of the Dharma.
He then presented a verse, saying: A single fist shatters the great void; The billions of Sumeru mountains leave no trace.
I ask you, who is the master within? From the Fusang tree rises a single red orb.
As for Jin-su riding upon the clouds, although the great and small treasuries employ harsh tongs and hammers, they are truly steeped in a heavy stench. If it were Jin-su,
he would wait until the other’s eyebrows twitch and then strike him across the spine with a staff, making him thoroughly bare and clear,
bringing him lifelong joy.
The Buddha-dharma is truly as deep as the ocean; To try to fathom it with a conch-shell is but a waste of effort.
With sharp horns he turns his body and emerges; He can pierce empty space with a single needle.
(Muyun Men) He drags down the idle root of one's own self; A single blow penetrates the celestial wheel and the summit barrier— Stark, towering, solitary and eminent.
Zhuo! When he seizes the claws and fangs right in the hall, (Zifu’s Gaze)—he shatters empty space, vividly and clearly manifest.
His entire being surges forth, beyond all acceptance or rejection. Vast and open, he stands alone, revealing no private intent;
from the heavens above to the human realm below, there is nowhere to hide. (Guyun’s Mirror)
Gripping the three passes firmly, how could one relax? Suddenly bursting through, the vast void is shattered. Everywhere the mother’s face is revealed;
only then does one believe that all previous efforts were in vain. (Ming Gaofeng) Ten thousand miles of long winds unfold the Six Tactics;
breaking the passes and striking the joints depends on the hero. With a fist of emptiness, the family reputation is overturned.
A shake; a single shout as lofty as the sun and moon.
(With An-gui) Thoroughly testing people is no mere matter; how could one allow them to wander about on the periphery? When a single function flashes forth, the skull dries up;
it falls crashing into the void, and the sun shines brightly. (Su-an Ren)
Suddenly twisting the mother’s nose, one finally believes that today his power and function are complete.
He shatters empty space and overturns the mountains and seas; a solitary radiance shines brightly from the deep abyss.
(Lingchang Yun) Twenty-eighth generation after Dajian.
Chan Master Yongci Haizhou (d.u. of Yishan in Jinling (a successor of Dongming Xian) first visited Taichu Yuan.
Yuan asked, "Before your parents were born, what was your original face?
The Master walked from east to west and stood with his hands folded. Yuan said, "Not it, not it. The Master replied, "Two eyes facing two eyes. Yuan—
He nodded in agreement. He visited Dongming Xian again and asked, "Who is worthy to wear the markless field-of-merit robe?
Xian struck him with his palm. The Master said, "What is that? Xian struck him again. The Master said, "Even if one strike does not serve as a single strike, what then?
Xian struck him once more. The Master said, "The old monk's reputation is not in vain. He then unfolded his sitting cloth, prostrated three times, and departed.
He paid his respects. Not long after, he opened the Dharma at Ilsan. Myeongjeon sent a monk with his robe and whisk, offering a verse that said:
"Entrusted to the boat of Compassionate Sea; I seek you, yet find no one to repay me. On the day after next year’s New Year, the western wind will smile and nod its head.
The following year, Dongmyeong passed away exactly as predicted.
From where have you returned to lodge in the thatched hut? The Old Lord has mistaken you for the ancient Gautama.
With one sudden shower of rain, the flower-like countenance fades; atop the ethereal peak, the azure mist drips down.
(Muyun Men) Seeing that heaven and earth are as vast as a bushel, how could they become blurred the moment one stirs them? The eye-sight is expansive, transcending all quarters.
[Seal] "Externally: Only now do I believe that previously I was no true man.
(By Guàn of Zífú). Zen Master Bǎofēng Zhìxuān of Gāopíng Temple in Jīnlíng (the dharma heir of Hǎizhōu Cí), the twenty-ninth generation descendant of Dàjiàn, relied upon Hǎizhōu at Yìshàn.
Having attended him for many years, he had seen through the principles with precision and practiced them with stability. Zhou bestowed upon him a verse, saying:
"Delusion and enlightenment are like clouds in the sky; The azure heavens are bright and pure, utterly without trace. The manifest world is revealed within it."
Killing and bringing to life are both spontaneously manifest when brought forth.
The sky is naturally azure and the water is naturally clear. A silver hook suddenly catches the man crossing the river; the oars turn back upstream to the village bank.
Having found the way home, his face is full of spring. (Zifu’s Contemplation)
Baofeng invited Tianqichai to take part in the examination. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Beijing.
The Master said, "Is there another place you have gone to? He replied, "I have wandered freely wherever I pleased. The Master asked, "Have you ever been to Sichuan? He replied, "I have.
The Master asked, "How is the landscape of Sichuan compared to here? He replied, "Though the mountains and rivers differ, the wind and moon are the same. The Master [nodded].
[The Master] held up his fist and said, "Is there this? [The monk] said, "No. The Master said, "Why then is it not there?
[The monk] said, "It is not my realm. The Master said, "What is your realm? [The monk] said, "Even the Buddhas cannot recognize it; who would dare to arbitrarily assign it a name?
The Master said, "Are you not then clinging to emptiness? [The monk] said, "I will never make my living inside a ghost cave."
Ji said, "Among the ninety-six kinds of non-Buddhist paths in the Western Heaven, you are the foremost. Rui shook his sleeves and departed.
Jinguang said, "Bao Feng’s response to the occasion was subtle and dense; he buried him alive face-to-face. This was not just Master Tianqi."
"I almost lost one of my eyes! Nevertheless, what is the foremost among the ninety-six kinds of non-Buddhist paths?
After a long silence, he said: "Even the Buddhas cannot recognize it; who would dare to force a name upon it?"
Why do these verbose words refuse to clear away? A single blow—the high mirror can judge it for itself.
Though the non-Buddhists of the Western Heavens received his prediction, that fish which has passed through the net cannot be summoned back.
(Muyun Men) When he lets loose a single thread, the needle comes and goes; he severs the dark ford, and the fish thrash its gills. It sucks dry the millions of gallons of Lake Tai.
Recently, surging waves have overflowed the heavens, their roar like thunder.
(Zifu Guan) Elegant and refined in every direction, the masters of the Great Way turn back immediately upon being confronted head-on.
Who among them knows this realm? From time immemorial, even all Buddhas have been unable to recognize it. (Guyun Jian)

The ordinary world of wind and moon—its realm is profound and deep. Even the Buddhas do not know it; who then can be its true connoisseur? The peach blossoms are in full bloom as the spring wind blows far away;
from a thousand miles away, this longing stirs the traveler’s heart. (By Quan Jianxu) At that moment, the staff and the shout were administered.
With the keen eyes of a hawk and the clear vision of a dragon, the hand was applied with personal intimacy. To be touched by it is to feel one's entire being chilled through to the marrow.
Bones. A place where one would not expect to be startled, yet it startles (the fist-stone and the lush waters).
Under the Great Mirror (Dajian), in the thirtieth generation, Chan Master Tianqi Benrui of Jingmen at Jingling (Succeeding Baofeng Xuan) addressed the assembly: "In the world there is no dharma. Out.
There is no dharma in the world. If one can penetrate this "no-dharma," one returns home to sit in peace. Qingshan Xiu said:
"The Patriarch Qichu simply wanted to exhaust the Dharma without regard for whether there were any people left. I, his unworthy descendant, do not act in such a way.
There is no dharma in the world, and there is no dharma beyond the world. If one can penetrate this 'no-dharma,' it is precisely the right time to practice."
Feet. Huìtán received [the transmission] and said: "Of these two great elders, one was skilled at gathering but not at releasing; the other was skilled at releasing but not at gathering.
I, the unworthy one, shall add mud upon the earth. There is no dharma in the world, and there is no dharma beyond the world.
To one who penetrates this "dharma-less" state, thirty blows of the staff are well-deserved. Why? Because it is the "sword that kills" and the "sword that gives life.
Tianqi ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the essential teaching of Gao Feng? The Master said, "The stone horse neighs in the wind beyond the mundane world;
the golden rooster cries out before the imperial palace. The monk asked, "What is so extraordinary about this? The Master said, "If you do not encounter..."
"One who knows the sound merely exerts themselves in talk about the 'cold of the year'. [The student] asked, "What is it that has been transmitted from patriarch to patriarch?
The Master said, "The mud ox at the bottom of the sea tosses white waves; the stone woman in the forest fans the clear breeze.
[The student] asked, "Who is it that enjoys this when the entire great earth is fully revealed? The Master said, "Li Erge of the eastern village."

Chengtian Yi said: "As for profound discourse that enters into principle, it is certainly not lacking. However, if the Great Ancestor Tianqi wishes to uphold the essential tenets of Gao Feng, he still lacks one crucial point."
One day, Tianqi raised the topic for the two senior monks, Puzhao and Taichu, saying: "Setting aside the Three Mysteries above, one must resolve the final point.
Taichu asked, "What is the final point? The Master said, "The wind blows through the willows by the wall;
the sun shines upon the elms by the stream. Puzhao said, "In the low places of the green mountains, one sees the vastness of the sky. Red... [text fragment]
When the lotus opened, he smelled the scent of the water. He made a retching sound and said, "This is truly playing with a bundle of straw.
The Master asked, "What about you? Tai made a retching sound, then rose from his seat and returned to his place.
The *Shichesheng* (Stone Cart Vehicle) says: "One belch, and there is nothing to be reckoned; one belch, and the body rises to its place.
Let those with the eye of discernment examine this.
Zen Master Fashou Daoji of Tianting Monastery in Xiuzhou (the seventh generation descendant of Huading Duxia and successor to Ji’an Zu), due to Lu Wutai.
The questioner asked, "Was there originally anything to be changed before the drawing? The Master said, "If there were nothing, with what would you draw?
The questioner asked, "What is it like after the drawing? The Master said, "Originally, there was not a single stroke. The questioner said, "There are currently sixty-four hexagrams;

how can you say they do not exist? The Master said, "Layman, do not become attached to words. The questioner said, "I ask the Master to set aside words and manifest a single line for me to see. The Master—
He summoned Wutai. Wutai responded, "Yes. The Master said, "From where does this single line arise?
Puming replied, "Whether before or after the drawing, whether discussing existence or non-existence, it has no connection whatsoever with the Great Changes (the *I Ching*).

Even if a single call and a single response were as clear as the lines and images themselves, that would still not be the ultimate standard for a monk. Before the drawing, there was already [the line]."
"Why not simply call out 'Is there a change? and wait for him to respond? Then you could say, 'There has always been a change.
Master Lu would surely have a different point of entry here, which would spare us much further complication."
Living in a dilapidated wall and a broken house within the secluded forest, with doors left unshut throughout the past and present;
turning north to face south, one meets shadows and echoes—how pitiful that what is but a few inches apart is separated by a thousand fathoms!
(Yulin Xiu) On the throne of the Sage of the Eight Trigrams, they discuss the Cook; in the courtyard of the Master, Confucius is refuted. They dwell together precisely because they do not [conflict].
Consciousness—instead, strike the golden hammer behind the head.
(Yichuyuan) Chan Master Wumen Juexue Zhengcong of Longquan on Guanzilizhen in Suizhou, the thirty-first generation descendant of Dajian (successor to Tianqire). He went to visit Tian.
Qi attended him for a long time. One day Qi asked, "What is it like when one is in the world yet forgets the world?
The Master said, "To realize that things are not things. Qi asked, "What is it like when one is mindful yet forgets mindfulness? The Master said, "In the mind, there is no mind.
Qi asked, "What is it like when both mind and things are forgotten? The Master said, "Mount Hua rises steeply; Mount Taihang’s peaks are jagged. Qi [was enlightened].
He then presented this verse: "Breaking through emotion, emotion is broken; breaking it, one returns to emotion. Tracing is severed, there is no self-interest—refined within, most refined.
Knowing this within, I now spare nothing; I entrust the entire basket to you, O benevolent one, to carry forth."
Yunhanman said: "To understand that things are not things is like gouging a sore on healthy flesh; to have no mind within the mind is like driving a wedge into one's own eyes.
Had it not been for this final phrase, I would almost have called him a scholar-monk."
Meeting you now is already like casting a hook in the dark. I have told him all my private secrets.
When both mind and objects are forgotten beyond heaven and earth, how could Mount Hua ever shift with the four seasons? (Punching the stone and pouring water.
Wumen asked a monk, "What is your original face? The Master said, "The Fragrant Pavilion of Stone. [The monk] said, "Then..."

The ancient cloud-peak summit is difficult for people to behold; By chance, it is swept by the wind and reflects the evening glow. The hundred birds have not yet returned and the sky is already dark;
Deep in the night, as always, they roost amidst the reeds.
Wen Yin Tianqi asked, "Suffering and pleasure are both caused by the mind; why then do we grasp at them externally? The Master said, "It is simply because you do not understand.
He asked, "Right and wrong are both matters of circumstance; why then do we falsely accept them? The Master said, "You have mistaken the zero point on the scale.

He asked, "Delusion and awakening are both functions of the person; why then are they not mastered? The Master said, "Had you known early on that the lamp is fire, would you have sought it in the four directions?"
The sound of the bell reveals the *uttarāsaṅga*; who on this great earth does not rub their eyes?
Having clearly grasped the meaning of the lamp-light, what can be done against one who turns the clouds and overturns the rain?

(Muyunmen) In the spring garden, flowers are in full bloom like surging waves; they dally with butterflies vying for beauty, their fragrance overwhelming the nose. As the sun sets behind the thatched eaves, the color of the sky...
Late evening. A single wheel of frost-moon shines upon the pond.
(Zifu Guan) Where there is water, it contains the moon from heaven; no mountain lacks the clouds from the mountain peak. For what reason do people of this world follow after deluded men and women?
They mistakenly take Zhang Lang for Li Jun. (Xuchunuan)
The Weaver Girl comes out at night, her shuttle and thread clumsy; / Without cause, she dabbles in cleverness by the River of Magpies.
/ Though she tries to veil her gauze sleeves with thin mist, / Before she has even begun to dance in the spring breeze, her elbows have already pierced through.
(By Chuan Jianxu, the thirty-second generation under the Great Mirror [Dajian Huineng])
Chan Master Xiyuan Yuexin Debao of Beijing (dharma heir of Longquan Cong) went to Guanziling to study under Juexue.
While washing vegetables, he suddenly noticed a single leaf being carried by the water, spinning in circles; though he tried to catch it, he could not. At that moment, he attained realization.
Carrying his basket back, he encountered Juexue, who asked, "What is this? The Master replied, "A basket of vegetables. Juexue said, "Why not say something else?"

The Master said, "Please ask another question. The student departed. One day, as the student was taking his leave, the Master raised a whisk and said, "If you can utter a single phrase regarding this, you may go forth as one who has transcended the ordinary. The student was speechless. Thereafter, he returned to study under him once more.
[The Master asked: "In learning, everyone has parents. Where are your parents now? The Master said: "A single fire has consumed them. [The monk] said:
"If that is so, then you have no parents? The Master said: "They exist, yet even the Buddha’s eye cannot see them.
[The monk] said: "Do you see them? The Master said: "I do not see them either. [The monk] said: "Why do you not see them? The Master—
[The Master] said: "If you see it, it is not the true parent. Xue said: "Excellent! Thereupon [the Master] gave his seal of approval.
"Picking it up from the water and burning it in the fire; with head emerging beyond the heavens, one is naturally carefree.
Turning back to reflect, before the pivot of the mechanism was understood, there was not even a single hair’s breadth—yet that single hair is indeed a single hair. (Pingyang Man)
A single leaf of vegetable suddenly drifts with the current; Joyfully leaping, he returns home to offer it all as a tribute.
The parents' entire bodies are red and raw; Only this blind donkey can truly uphold the ancestral legacy.

(Lian'an asked: "A single stem, round and turning; a single tip, fresh and new. Carrying his basket back home, he has no intention to display his meaning. Clouds gather and rain disperses across the river sky.
At dusk, a single spark on the red furnace is like a light flake of snow.
(From the Xiao’an edition) Where the hand cannot reach, one sees a single stalk of vegetable; where a single flame consumes, all is penetrated without obstruction.
The original true parents are ground into a hundred fragments in a single mouth. Though they may move freely in all directions—seven ways and eight ways—they remain entirely without seams or cracks.
(Guyun Jian) A single hair-tip, perfectly revolving, is Mount Sumeru; held up in the hand, the smiling eyes return. Do not say that one's own kin cannot be found.

When Xiangyan was asked by a monk, "What is the matter that you benefited from in years past?
the Master held his whisk upside down and looked at the monk, saying, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I have already recognized what you are doing, Master. The Master [nodded].
The Master said, "Tell me, what was Huang Siniang of Jingzhou seeking when she prostrated before the Buddha? The monk had no reply, and the Master struck him out.
Jin-su Cheng remarked, "Question and answer were clear to both parties; who would have known that at the final squeeze, it was like falling into an abyss?"

"A pit ten thousand fathoms deep; even to this day, one cannot rise from it. He summoned the assembly and said, "Can you still save him? Do not say, 'It is fine to draw the bow after the thief has passed.
Xiaoyan went to Xiong’er Mountain to pay homage at the ancestral pagoda. A monk of the temple scolded him, saying, "The pagoda is empty; why do you, you fool, prostrate yourself before it?"
The Master pointed to the stupa with his finger and asked, "Is this an empty stupa? He replied, "It is. The Master said, "The Patriarch has departed.
[The monk] said, "He took his sandals and returned to the West. The Master cried out, "Alas! Alas!"

Dongmingji said: "Let us set aside this monk for a moment. As for the fact that Old Man Xiangyan saw the Patriarch bowing yet did not see the Patriarch bowing—if you say he saw him, Xiangyan spoke thus; if you say he did not see him, Xiangyan also spoke thus.
Ultimately, how is it? After a long silence, he said: "The rain from the previous ten days does not cease at the eaves; a flash of lightning..."
The thunder continues into the latter part of the night;
atop the high Xiong’er Peak, wild goose shadows shiver in the cold. The mournful wind sweeps through until the weeds grow rank and long. Three thousand miles away, there is no one to know me;
blood splatters as the cuckoo cries, its tears still un-dried. (Lian’an asked.)
A hook with bait is cast upon the silken line; Thrown into the heart of the waves, the fish does not swallow it. Returning home, I sing to myself as the mountains remain green;
Looking back, how laughable—the depths of the water and clouds.
(Meiguk Yeol) Xiaoyan ascended the hall and held up his staff, saying, "Is there anyone? Is there anyone? At that time, a monk came forward and prostrated. The Master said:
He struck him across the spine and said, "Why are you so talkative? He replied, "I have not yet uttered a single word; why do you call me talkative?
The Master struck him again and said, "A second offense will not be tolerated."
Sanfeng Zang said: "Jùn is indeed extremely sharp, yet he cannot avoid being caught up in busyness. Yìzé Rěn said: "The mechanism is steep and keen;
the command is severe and cold. To act as a teacher in such a manner is truly direct, yet it is a pity to encounter someone like Meng Bāláng."
Do not say that one has already taken responsibility before opening one's mouth; when have you ever even dreamed of where the blow from the staff falls?
At that time, had it been this mountain monk, I would have waited for him to strike me across the back and then said, "Why such excessive talk? and immediately overturned the meditation seat.
If you were to teach directly, this old man would have no opening for speech throughout his life.
There is no need for the meeting of host and guest; one who personally seizes the divine mechanism cuts off the path of men. Amidst the snowy night, the plum blossoms lead the way in early spring;
though the fragrant herbs fill the garden, they do not know it is new. (Safuku Zō)
A perilous pass atop ten-thousand-fathom peaks; even a hair’s breadth separates one from a thousand mountains.
If the traveler does not understand the strategy for opening the gate, the scenery before their eyes remains distinct from the world.
(Han Song Cao) Xiangyan saw a monk standing upright with his staff planted in the ground and asked in a loud voice, "Virtuous one, do you recognize the lineage of the ancestors?"

[The monk] asked, "Does the meaning of the Esoteric Teachings (Mikkyō) rely on verbal discourse? The Master replied, "If it is esoteric, it is not discourse; if it is discourse, it is not the meaning.

After [the monk] withdrew, he placed his staff across his shoulder, stood upright with one foot raised, and asked, "What is this meaning? The Master wrote the character for "one" (*ichi*) on the ground.
[The monk] drew a line on the ground with his staff, standing upon it with a stride as wide as two shins, and again placed his staff across his shoulder.
Pressing his hand against the master’s abdomen, he leaned forward to look at him and asked, "What is the meaning of this? The master wrote the character *jia* (嘉) on the ground.

The monk immediately planted his *xi* staff in the earth, placed both hands on his hips, lifted one leg high, and with gritted teeth and glaring eyes, assumed the posture for subduing demons, asking, "What is the meaning of this? The master wrote the character *zhi* (之) on the ground. He—
The Master pointed his fingers toward heaven and earth, circled them once, and asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master wrote the character *you* (尤) on the ground.
He stepped forward and performed a woman’s prostration. The Master pointed his fingers at two monks and wrote the character *can* (蠶) on the ground.
While he was still circling three times, he performed a prostration and stood to the Master’s right. The Master [wrote] on the ground...

He wrote the character for "Buddha" (佛) on top [of the character for "Māra" (魔)]. When the man approached and spoke, the Master said, "Even if you reach this point, you must still encounter 'Māra' within 'Buddha';
only then will it be so. The man sighed and said, "Aha! Are you truly a Mahāyāna *sarvajña* (all-knowing) superior being?
He prostrated himself and departed. The Master looked at the assembly and said, "This is the manifestation of the Vajra-transformation presented by the noble and holy ones."
Samādhi. The Samādhirāja Samādhi. He used this to test me; yet he, too, will have his own new realization. Xiangweng Yun said:
"The way these two men respond with such vinegar-like acerbity is much like carving out auspicious patterns and dragon motifs from a block of raw iron.
There is both the provisional and the real; there is both killing and giving life. If you can examine this thoroughly, you may understand."
This means that the patch-robed monks of the Eastern Land laugh to death the non-Buddhists of the Western Heavens. Should this not yet be so, he takes up his staff, draws a line, and says:
"The Fairy of the Colored Clouds fans her crimson gauze."
Having traversed a thousand mountains, my straw sandals are worn through; Leaving things to their natural course, I pass these good years with ease.
The field of practice is secure when examined with plain honesty; The life-force of the Vulture Peak hangs by a single thread.
(Muyun Mon) When a monk asked Xigyan, "If a single word expresses it all and allows for no further speech, what then? the Master said:
The cuckoo calls by the banks of the Wuling Creek; ten li of peach blossoms are dyed crimson with its blood.
The cuckoo cries out by the banks of the Wuling Creek; ten thousand words and a thousand phrases, yet no other sound.
If one turns back and realizes it is better to return home, all travelers from the ends of the earth will set their course back toward the journey’s end. (Yuan’an Yun)
Whose peach and plum trees vie in fragrance and beauty? The cuckoo calls out again and again, summoning the traveler home. Once I trod the path by the banks of the Wuling Stream;
the spring colors within the cavern were unlike those of the human world.
(By Yue of Luan) Words exhausted and principles fully expressed, the tongue goes dry. Coral from the bottom of the sea supports the moon. Amidst the cries of the cuckoo, the flowers fall.
Red. How many masters have fully divulged this? (Cheonan Seung) When two guests entered the gate, Soram laughed and said:
"Thick pines and tall bamboos—I suddenly see the Master. He then asked, "What is the style of a man of the Way? The Master replied, "Thick pines and tall bamboos.
[The guest] asked, "What is the underlying meaning? The Master said: [Note: The text provided ends abruptly with "The Master said," suggesting the dialogue continues.]
I find it insufficient for my own viewing; I leave it here for guests to behold.
What is the significance of these luxuriant pines and tall bamboos? Their sturdy nodes are not merely defiant against the cold of winter.
They draw in the distant wind to purify the six directions. Do not regard their sound and form as something trivial. (Meo Won-deok)
Chan Master Wuhuan Xingchong of Mount Jing in Hangzhou (the ninth generation descendant of Huding Duxia, successor to Juewei Kong) returned after compiling the *Record of Wuqu*.
Wuqu asked, "What have you been doing all this time? The Master replied, "Xingchong has purchased a plot of land and obtained the original deed;
I request the Master’s signature. He then presented the record for his inspection. Wuqu—
When he received it, [Nanquan] said, "This is mine; yours is that. The Master said, "Preceptor, do not encroach upon another's stall and snatch away their trade.
Nanquan immediately threw down the staff and went out. The Master then departed.
The ancient forest is like clouds. If I were Guishan, when the Master said, "This is mine;
this is yours," I would have immediately prostrated and said, "Today, I see that the Master has grown old."
Meeting one another, each displays their own family style; the ancestral legacy is inexhaustible for descendants to use. In the boundless great ocean, the carp leap at will;
across the ten-thousand-li expanse of the long sky, the wild geese fly freely.
(Tianfeng Xingwu) When a monk asked, "What is the school of Deva? the Master said, "A single character does not bear a stroke. The monk asked again.

Filling the void of space, there is no one to offer a price. Meeting him unexpectedly, one is left in a state of agitation, "seven up, eight down.

The great wealthy man must return to the elder’s house; naturally, there is a livelihood wherever one goes.

(Ji'an enters) The fish swimming beneath one's feet remain entirely unaware; out of pity for the *guan-er* birds, how can they be so deluded? How many have betrayed righteousness and forgotten their kindness!

Under the thirty-third generation of Dajian [Huineng], at Longchi of Jingxi, was Chan Master Hanyou Zhengchuan (the successor of Xiyuan Bao). Once, upon hearing the crackling sound of lamp-flames, he attained enlightenment.
Upon hearing the sound of an explosion, he attained a realization. He then traveled to the capital to seek verification from Xiangyan.

Xiangyan said, "Recite everything you have previously realized, one by one. When the Master had related his words halfway through, Xiangyan kicked out a shoe and said, "Speak a single phrase regarding this!
The Master was unable to respond. He returned to the hall and did not sleep the entire night; the next morning, he was still standing there waiting.

He stood beneath the eaves. When Yunyan saw him, he called out to the Master. The Master turned his head back; Yunyan then lifted one foot, assuming the posture of an asura obstructing the sun and moon.
The Master suddenly felt a sense of liberation.
In the stillness of night, the lamp-flower roars a single sound; upon the lapis lazuli palace, the whole body is revealed.
The Great Spirit splits asunder the colors of Mount Hua; the barefooted Persian travels on a roadless path. (Lian’an asked:
When the two pieces of skin are just opening and closing, a dead snake suddenly stirs and comes toward a person; at daybreak, the poisonous breath finally revives.
Awakened! The upraised-foot asura—how strange! (At the Ancient South Gate) A flash of lightning reveals the distinction between man and machine;
a thunderclap in the clear sky is too solitary and perilous. Turn your head and gouge out the eye at the crown of your skull;
the golden lock of the mysterious pass is instantly reduced to ashes. (Huishan Xian)
Kicking out his sandals, he cuts them off clean; where the asuras obstruct, the whole mechanism is alive. His entire being is revealed, difficult to conceal;
with a single umbrella, he returns home, bearing the thousand mountains upon his strength.
(Guyun Jian) Suddenly he severs the throat—look! It is as if it were difficult to breathe or turn the body. Turning his head, a thunderclap strikes again.
Sent off. He smashes a single sphere of empty space.
(Suanren) The earthen ox strides up to Mount Tai; Treading through the layered peaks, the mist and rain clear away.
If a pure breeze did not arise from beneath both armpits, How could one have personally reached Mount Chicheng? (Miaoyunxiong)
At Longchi, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Coming? The Master said, "The deer sleeps alone north of the house.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The roosters crow together west of the stream."
Jiashan Yu said: "Although my grandfather’s response was like striking two birds with one stone, it could not help but cause this monk to mistake east for north.
This unworthy grandson would have answered differently. To the question 'What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? he would simply have said:

'Facing the vast waters of the river, watch the boats passing by morning and evening,' and further added: 'I do not understand. Then he would have pointed and said: 'Within the reeds on both banks, the clear breeze [blows].'"
[The Master] cited the "White Heron. Miaowei Jun said: "The ancients brought forth the mechanism for trapping a tiger;
it was indeed extraordinary. Yet, how can one help it? This monk from Youzhou is still tolerable, but the most painful part is 'Silla.
Before those with clear eyes, this is nothing but a laughingstock. But tell me, what is there to laugh at? Wait thirty years and you shall see. Pingji Pu said: "If you say..."
These two lines constitute the meaning of the Westward Journey. One is liable to receive an iron staff for them. Yizhi then said:
"The Patriarch’s eyes looked toward the southeast, but his intent lay in the northwest. When someone asked Zifu, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? he simply replied: [the same].

The mountain clouds are white as the curtain rolls up; the courtyard is deep with yellowed rock leaves. Waiting for the clouds, one does not understand; with a single ladle of cold stream water, one sits facing the moon upon a pine ridge.
To the north of the house, a deer sleeps alone; to the west of the stream, the roosters cry in unison. This very meaning of the Western Arrival is known only to those who have truly realized it.

(Longchi Wei): The frost beneath the tongue is cold enough to chill those nearby; idle words and superfluous talk, however, possess a lingering sentiment. With whom can one enjoy the morning breeze and the waning moon?
They disperse into the tall willows, becoming the sound of rain. (Meigu Yue):
One day, while at Longchi, due to a certain matter, [Zhaozhou] put on a tight-fitting shirt, lifted a chair, and performed a woman’s bow.
He said to Xiu of Qingshan, "Master Xiu, wait; let me bow to you as my teacher. Xiu laughed and presented this verse:
"The wooden man raises his voice with a laugh; Who recognizes him even as he puts on clothes? Yesterday I observed him and saw he was a man; Today..."
In the morning, he turned back into an old woman. The Master said, "This verse is very much to my liking.
Falinyin said, "Although the verse of the Great Ancestor of Qing Shan is excellent and beautiful, it truly does not fully capture the intent of the Ancestor Huan.
It cannot be discussed further; let us light a lamp and see how thick his skin is. Did the Ancestor Huan truly have such an intention back then?"

At that moment, the host and guest are fully present within the shadow-grass; illumination and function are gathered together as the wooden man performs his rites. Overturning [the world], it is fundamentally neither male nor female;
a flash of lightning in the blue sky, a mustard seed meeting a needle’s eye. (Daofeng Zhen)
Meeting face-to-face, there is no need for reproach; originally it is neither I nor another. A single regretful matter throughout my life:
I mistakenly called Master Zhang by the name of Mistress Li.
(Falin’s Record) When a monk asked Longchi, “What is the extraordinary matter of the Buddhas and Patriarchs? the Master replied, “A shrimp catching a dragon.”
The monk said, "If that is so, then it is not extraordinary. The Master said, "A cat catching a mouse.
The monk bowed. The Master then shouted. The monk said, "Why does the Master not let me pass?
The Master said, "I have business; you may go now."
Dongming Ji said: "The Goose King selects milk; he has never been of the duck kind.
To enter the realm of another's mechanism is too solitary and perilous. Striking face-to-face, one encounters his downward blow.
Swords and halberds mistake the body, and one grows old in vain. How many have ever passed through the Jade Pass? (Lian'an asked.)
A single word before the wind settles the fundamental principle; whether spoken in Han or Hu language, it is surely understood.
At the end, he once more raises the command of a thousand ages; a solitary lamp beneath the setting sun, veiled in mist.

(Shan Ci Ji) It is difficult for one to penetrate the Dragon Gate of ten thousand fathoms. When the golden-scaled fish intends to leap, it stirs the waves. With lightning and thunder escorting it, it burns once more.
The tail; raw blood flows empty, leaving dark stains upon the stone. (Nanjian Zhen) A wondrous frog captures the great beast;
fully upholding the profound essentials, he shakes the family tradition. Like lightning and sparks from flint, no trace can remain;
with a single shout, he instantly makes the universe empty. (Zuan Rui)
When a monk asked Longchi, "What is the Zen of the Tathāgata? the Master held up his fist. The monk asked, "What is the Zen of the Patriarchs?
The Master likewise held up his fist. The monk asked, "Are the Zen of the Tathāgata and the Zen of the Patriarchs the same or different?
The Master again held it up and said, "It is either a fist, or else it is a palm."
Baoneng Xiu said: "If someone were to ask Baoneng today, 'What is Tathāgata Chan?'—the mountain gate is the answer.
'What is Patriarchal Chan?'—the Buddha hall is the answer. Are Tathāgata Chan and Patriarchal Chan the same or different?
Simply say: 'It is difficult to deceive those with clear eyes.'"
Ascending the hall at Longchi: All phenomena are not existent; all phenomena are not non-existent. If one can realize it in this way, it is like pressing a gourd against the water.
The shimmering lake light is even more favored in the clear weather; the misty mountain colors are likewise marvelous in the rain. If one were to compare West Lake to the Western [Paradise]...
My son, whether lightly adorned or heavily made up, you are always suitable.

At the summit of Shuangjing, first shout; at Shiyuan Rock, let [Pai] leap as he pleases. At Mingyue Pool, the earth is overturned and heaven is tilted.
Among these four lines, one possesses the "sword that kills" but lacks the "sword that gives life";

In times of great peace and no affairs, the sword is drawn from its scabbard; in times of affliction, the blade enters the sheath.

Han said, "I ask the Master to provide one phrase that transcends sound and form. The Master replied, "The entire mountain is covered in snow.
Puming used this case, saying: "This monk thrust himself against a blade; that he survived is no small feat of skill.
Old Man Nan exhausted every bit of salt and sauce, yet in the end could not find what satisfied his heart. Is there anyone here who can point to something else outside of sound and form?"
"Speak one phrase! After a long silence, he said, "Above all, do not say, 'The whole mountain is covered in snow. Ōuan Yan said:
"This old fellow from Xingshan is accustomed to using official property to oppress ordinary people.
Is there anyone here who can vindicate the monk’s grievance? Come forth and meet Ōuan’s staff!"

Suddenly beholding the remaining firewood, my dream was abruptly cleared. My private estate is utterly exhausted, and my body finds no ease.

Chan Master Wufeng Ruxue of Daming Mountain in Tanzhou (a successor of Tiantong Wu) was asked by a monk, "For what purpose did Śākyamuni appear in the world?
The Master said, "A poor man thinks of his old debts. The monk struck his sitting mat and departed.
The Master said, "You foolish fellow, you leave again like that!"
Falin’s *Yinyun* says: "As for the place where Old Śākyamuni dropped his joints, Wufeng need not trouble himself to examine it.
Today, there are thirty blows; let them be stored away for now. Why? Because within the Way of Benevolence and Righteousness," [it is so].
Eight thousand round-trips of questions regarding the single transmission; A cascade of jade is cast forth, yet few can fully comprehend it.
It deceives wandering scholars into composing empty rhapsodies, While they vainly inherit the wild eccentricity of the rustic elder.

(Pure as a Wheel of Snow) Having forged a backbone of pride, one cannot bear the sorrows of the world; The azure waters and the vast sky share a single hue in autumn. One’s livelihood follows its own course, following its own measure.
Sufficient. Why need one seek further in haste?
(Kedayan) Amidst the reeds, the moon’s reflection is round and full; take care, old fisherman, as you hold your fishing rod.
At the moment the line is cast or retracted by hand, all is white and vast, then again black and vast. (Nanzong Chuan)
Thoroughly impoverished to the very marrow, he enters the marketplace of the world. Myriad threads of emotion lock his face in shame.
How many times have we spoken to the depths of our innermost hearts? These matters of the mind can only be erased within dreams.
(Falin Yin) When the Five Peaks was in Guanzhong, a lay practitioner asked him, "What do you do while staying in Guanzhong? The Master replied, "A bamboo bed."
"Sleeping high on my pillow, I await the clouds," he said. "Is this not killing people with boredom? The Master replied, "Five white birds cry out at the fifth watch.
Faling said, "The Five Peaks are rushing toward their destination; the Layman has taken a wrong path. Both are expressions from beyond the passes. If you wish to advance—
What about it? Xuedou has spoken his piece, and then he says:
"Where the frost flowers drift, the night grows cold; the oil lamp is exhausted, yet the兴致 (xìngzì) is not yet ended. Three children sit facing one another;
at leisure and with nothing to do, they play with two balls."
Wufeng was asked by a monk about Mañjuśrī giving rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma. Before the question had even ended, the Master said, "Venerable sir, you ought to receive my prostration.
As the monk prepared to open his mouth, the Master covered it with his hand.
Falin-yin said: "The five peaks are but a single-time provisional arrangement; though their granting and revoking may be observed, they cannot avoid being a singular, deliberate fabrication.
He further composed a verse:
"A crow seeks to perch upon the branches of the wild weeds; A gust of western wind rolls white sand. Opening one's eyes, one knows not where [it goes]."
Depart! Last night at the frontier passes, the *huqia* flute was sounded.
Chan Master Fazang (Dharma-Treasury) of Hanshan Three Peaks (a successor of Tiantong Wu) ascended the hall and said: "Year after year, winter is cold and summer is hot;
day after day, the night is dark and the day is bright. Even if one were to master these twelve hours, look and see—how many people could there possibly be?"
