With no scriptures at the head of his staff and wearing only his kashaya robe, how could he have the leisure to dally with a dead snake?
Hearing that the news of spring has arrived early at Donggao, he follows the wind and rain once more to plant mulberry and hemp.
Sanfeng ascended the hall and said: "All of you here are guests from under the patriarchs' gate; there is no need to ask 'how is it?
[He] let out a shout and said: 'Family disgrace must not be broadcast abroad.'"
Family scandals are groundlessly broadcast abroad; they carry wine and duck, walking in a procession.
Seeking the head and horns beneath the gate of the Patriarch, they are laughed at by Old Lady Li of the East Village. (Falin’s Verse) Three Peaks ascends the hall:
"Those who have traveled on foot throughout the four worlds under heaven—if they have a mouth capable of eating rice, they can lift their feet."
There are those who do not even arise from their seats; with mouths agape, what would they eat? After a long silence, he said: "Ask the various quarters.
The spring light of ninety days rests upon a cold pillow. The east wind shifts the moon onto the crimson balustrade.
Clearly discerning that white hair still pities its youth, the tears of unending sorrow have not yet dried. (A)
Chan Master Pōshān Hǎimíng (Successor of Tiantóng Wù) of Shuāngguì on Liángshān in Kuizhōu. A monk asked: "What is the meaning of 'One and Six open Heaven'?
The Master said: "The mountain hermitage is cold where the bamboos are dense. The monk asked: "What is the meaning of 'Two and Five form Nature'?
The Master said: "The lotus blooms with fragrance in the water palace."
Answering the question as it arises in the hand; wrapped in paper and bound with hemp, who would dare look?
Lightly treading his feet past the Dragon Gate, he stirs up wind and thunder that pierce the very marrow of one’s bones.
(Dun’an Tao) Shuanggui ascends the hall: Inside the jar of sour vinegar, there are many mosquitoes and gnats; upon the back of a broken donkey, there are plenty of flies. I...
In this place, there is nothing to swallow and no place to settle. There are blows from fans and smoke from incense. Those who are greedy for life and fearful of death need not come to my gate.
A dragonfly pierces the moon in the broken waves; the clear light is dispersed, yet it remains perfect above and below. Fish and dragons swallow and spit out their very lives;
following the wind and clouds, the waves overflow the heavens.
(Suan Ding) Shuanggui ascends the hall: "The bright stars in the sky suddenly emerge; Śākyamuni loses one eye. Turning back to look at the six..."
Regarding the four modes of birth, each one is like an insect gnawing at wood.
Faling Yin said: "Shuanggui only sees Śākyamuni; if you wish to see the six realms and the four modes of birth, you are still separated by eighty thousand miles.
Yongning Ding said: "It is not that Shuanggui has stripped others of their brilliance for the sake of people; it is simply that..."
To judge others by one's own standard:
When a monk asked the Double-Pine Master (Shuanggui), "What is it like when one eats all day long without ever chewing a single grain of rice?
The Master said, "A single magpie with nine tails."
The gate opens; the great mansion provides a place to rest. Drifting and solitary, one suffers as one seeks again. Waiting until reaching home, one inquires once more for news.
The oriole moves to the lofty tree; listen to its cry.
(Sulan Ding) Zen Master Fiyin Tongrong of Mount Jing (successor of Tiantong Wu) ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said: "Before the sound, there is a phrase."
"Son, you must want everyone to know.
Shengfaraoyun said: 'Jingshan is much like a leper leading his companions. Falinyin said:
'The old fellow Jingshan lures people into breaking the law.'"
Peach-like cheeks glow red as the sun shines upon them; willow-like brows sway green like fine silk in the breeze.
A palindrome poem seals a thousand drops of tears, sent merely to convey longing—may my husband understand.

(By Sheng Faring) It is entirely because of the moon over Huai that it may shine upon the spring of Yingyang. A single arrow pierces through the heavy gates; though his merit is great, he does not seek to establish a monument.
(Deqing Qi) When spring arrives, peach blossoms overflow the source of the stream; the scenery possesses a world of its own.
The old fisherman fears to speak of it to others, lest he invite idle sorrows upon his descendants. (Falin Yin)
Jingshan ascends the hall: This matter is spontaneously perfected within every person; there is no need for laborious effort or the cultivation of causes.
On the road of conceptual proliferation, errors abound; to directly accept it as it is, that is the true person.
Deqing Qi said: "I wish to ask the Elder of Mount Jing: if it is already primordially manifest, why must one further 'directly take it upon oneself' (diti chengdang)?
Before you can even deliberate, I shall give you a slap across the face. Falin Yin said: "I will tell you a parable for you.
Suppose there is a good man, with a line of characters engraved upon his face that reads, 'So-and-so.'"
"Do you think this person still possesses eyes or not?
In the fields beyond the outskirts, the harvests are abundant; within the chamber, every chest and casket contains jade ornaments.
I urge the impoverished son not to be startled: now, with both hands, I entrust them to him. (Deqing Qi)
A trace of rouge glows through her cheeks; in embroidered robes and brocade tunic, she smiles at the spring breeze. Her grieving heart is entirely knotted with longing;
she seals her message to be sent eastward across the mountains of Wu and the waters of Chu.
(Falin’s Verse) A monk asked Jingshan, "How can one clarify such a matter that is so headless and brainless? The Master said, "You..."
Before he had even reached the point of being head-over-heels, the monk was already standing in the field. The monk prostrated; the Master said, "The head and brain have emerged.
Shengfa Rong remarked, "This monk has his ox-head on his back and refuses to acknowledge the stolen goods. Jing Mountain strikes the watch-sticks at the main gate and catches the thief face-to-face."
At dusk, the noble scholar’s spirit stirs as he embraces his lute; through the night he sits by the moon at your humble abode.
Do not say it is bland and lacks flavor—a single cup of clear soup serves as tea.
(Deqing Qi) Jingshan asked Lingji: “Before the World-Honored One had ascended the seat, and before Mañjuśrī had struck the gavel—tell me, what was it?”

"Is there the Buddha-dharma or not? Before the question had even finished, the Master hurriedly brandished his staff and said, "Tell me, right now—is this ascending the seat or not ascending the seat?
As the student attempted to respond, the Master struck him directly and sent him back.

With a body ten thousand fathoms tall, he plays amidst the perilous crags; a single hair stands upright, overturning the five Sumeru mountains. Even Buddhas and patriarchs find it difficult to glimpse him;
the entire world is desolate, yet all belongs to him. The sun surges from the east, the moon sinks in the west—what prevents him from manifesting his true function wherever he is? (Yi-ce Ren)
A monk asked Jingshan, "What is the master’s household style? The Master said, "There is little rice and no salt.
The monk asked, "If a guest should suddenly arrive, how will you receive him? The Master said, "I have no leisure to worry about hunger."
Chao-an Ding said: "Although our late master was a gentleman who remained steadfast in poverty, how could one bear such extreme destitution?
If someone were to ask me, 'What is the house style of Fuyan? I would simply say: 'A single piece of plain cloth for clothing; three full meals a day.'"
If a guest should suddenly arrive, how would you receive them? "Iron-nail rice and wooden-splinter soup.
Suppose someone from the sidelines were to come forward and say, "For the Master to answer in such a way is much like a beggar suddenly becoming wealthy.
Have you not heard it said: "To know contentment is honor; to know sufficiency is wealth"? How can one blame this old monk?
Chan Master Tongcheng (successor to Tiantong Wu) of Jinsu Shiche was asked by a monk, "What is it to be the master within the dust?
The Master said, "Washing one's hands and seeing the blue sky. The monk asked, "What is it to be a guest who comes from beyond transformation?
The Master said, "One blow leaves a mark on every inch of skin."
With disheveled white hair, he leaves the mountain valleys; Rushing home at dusk, he does not follow the usual path.
A single wheel of the jade hare rises over the eastern ridge; In vain one hears the heart-rending cries of the monkeys.
(Suanan Ding) Chan Master Chaozong Tongren of Baohua on Gan Prefecture (Successor of Tiantong Wu). A monk asked: "What is the ancient Buddha?"
Regarding family style, the Master said, "Baohua Temple is one that has existed for a thousand years. [The monk] asked, "What is the brand-new decree?
The Master said, "I am the one residing here today. [The monk] asked, "Are there any distinctions of superiority or inferiority between the Buddhas of the past and the Buddhas of the future?
The Master held up his whisk and said, "Realize it in the middle."
A thousand-year-old temple from the Tang Dynasty; its orderly traditions and regulations—how could they be desolate?
If one directly perceives the intent of past and present, a single unfolding of spiritual awareness soars to the heavens.

(Shu Pung-heung) The *kāṣāya* robe upon the plowed fields—a thousand-year-old temple. In meeting and assisting beings, it remains the same across past and present. A room full of orchids and fragrant herbs, he extends his hand.
[He] attained it. "The cold plum’s fragrance disperses amidst the white clouds" (as straight as a string).
When Baohua asked a monk, "Why does the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net still linger in the water?
The Master said, "It is their daily meal. [The monk] said, "Just take enough to satisfy yourself. The Master said, "What can you do when you are submerged head-first?"
"Samādhi is like a cloud of true reality. At that time, why did the Jewel Flower not lend him a single thunderclap to prevent him from being submerged head-first?
Nevertheless, it is precisely in this everyday meal that one sees where the old man stands.
The Layman Baohua asked, "If the moon is missing one segment, can it be restored? The Master said, "It can be restored. The Layman asked, "With what will you restore it?
The Master said, "I shall simply use that which is missing to restore it."
Carrying snow to fill the well—the effort was not in vain. Body and mind endure the vicissitudes of cold and heat.
The vast, silent night holds a void-like azure; the clear light of the universe is swallowed in a single gulp.
(Suan Ding) *Zongjian Fali*, Volume 37.
*Zongjian fali*, Scroll 38, Compiled by Jiyun Tang;
under the Sixth Patriarch, the thirty-fifth generation.
Chan Master Wanyu Tongwei of Longchi (successor of Tiantong Wu) ascended the hall and said: "To open one's mouth is to create a double wedge;
to remain silent is to lose the fundamental source. You must know that this matter—who would dare to exhaust its description? He raised his whisk and said:
"If you can recognize the old Manjusri within this, you may take it for granted that there is no need to cross over to another peak."
Plum blossoms fill the trees outside the courtyard; willow branches line the embankment in a thousand green stalks.
To know the true message of this matter, listen suddenly to the single cry of a bird upon a branch.
(Iron Mechanism’s Seal) When a monk asked Longchi, “What is it like when the tree withers and the leaves fall? the Master said, “The path of the ants is difficult to find.”
Migrating birds easily find their nests;
a western wind suddenly rises, cold and whistling. Reed flowers on both banks cover a small boat;
unmooring it, one can return to one’s native land, where a single orb of bright moon shines as serene as autumn. (Péifēngzé)
Longchi was once asked by a monk, "When the sun has set behind the western mountains, what is the situation within the grove?
The Master said, "The tiger walks the path of the woodcutters; the birds roost on their old branches."
Sitting alone amidst the secluded bamboos, the frosty moon is cold. From where has this lute-player come to linger here with such joy?
High mountains and flowing waters—few are those who understand; wild geese alight upon the level sands—who can play them?
(By Songruo Zhao) Chan Master Hongjue Daomin of Pingyang, Yuezhou (successor of Tiantong Wu). A monk asked: "At midnight on the Snowy Mountains, one beholds..."
"Star Bright. This very morning, the Way was first perfected through Right Awakening (Sambodhi). What is the matter before Mount Sambodhi?
The Master said, "At this time, one drives sturdy oxen over the autumn ridges. "What is the matter of the causal conditions for transcending the world?
The Master said, "On what day will you ride the returning phoenix atop the Mountain of the Way? "What is the matter of the present moment? The Master said, "Look beneath your feet."
Extinguish the lamp of inexhaustibility; hold the Linji staff upside down. Upon the post-houses of the four seas, the traces of two shimmering swords remain.
The affairs of the mountain front are causes for future days; sons and grandsons run hither and thither across the south and north of the river.

(Most Lazy Root) The literary grove cannot contain the penetration of the Jade Hall; the imperial decree descends amidst the dripping of the water-clock. Purple qi soars through the void into the celestial expanse.
Outside. At the base, from beneath his feet, a high wind rises. (Purple mists congeal at dawn. The Five Ridges vie for supremacy;

winding and undulating, they emerge, giving birth to this great man, whose peer there is scarcely in the world. A single cough or a spittle falls into the Nine Heavens, where it follows the wind to produce pearls and jade.
When the Way of Perfect Enlightenment was first accomplished, he drove the sturdy oxen across the autumn fields. Have you not heard? Constantly...
The mountain holds treasures that endure as the legacy of the state; though all sons run to and fro in vain, only the virtuous mother provides solace.

(Facing the Green Mountain) The immortal transcendent hums a chant of the five clouds; able to ride the golden dragon across the vast four seas. Beneath his feet, the talented scholars are as pure as snow;
with pine blossoms covering the ground, he surpasses both fisherman and woodcutter. (Minggaogong Peak)
Pingyang ascended the hall and said: "Baizhang attained the great capacity; Huangbo attained the great function.
But what did that other person attain? [He] let out a shout and said: 'Transcending the standards of past and present, I do not share your table. He struck his staff down."
Chengtian Yi said: "Píngyáng was destined to share the wind and moon with Bǎizhàng and Huángbò; to divide their territories would not mean he failed to attain them.
Even if he had attained them, it would still be like one who has retreated fifty paces laughing at another who has retreated a hundred.
Fālín Yīn said: "I am not like Píngyáng. Bǎizhàng attained the Great Mechanism and Huángbò attained the Great Function; furthermore, there is..."
What does a person gain? A thief in an empty house. Again, he offers this verse:
Before the wind, a single melody travels, stifling the clouds; The ocean waters surge with waves, and the trees raise their voices. Vast and boundless, heaven and earth never cease;
Who is there that can truly ask for one who knows this?
Píngyáng addressed the assembly: "Tonight, I shall teach everyone to attain thorough enlightenment. Are you willing to accept it in this way?
After a long silence, he said: "Do not force the noble to become the base."
Sōng further addressed them, saying: "The Venerable Master Hongjue was like a golden-winged garuḍa cleaving the ocean to seize and swallow the dragon directly.
Tonight, I, your unworthy descendant, shall likewise cause everyone to attain thorough enlightenment. Will you accept this in such a manner?
After a long silence, he said: "A single film before the eye; empty flowers fall in confusion. He then offered a verse:
The ice-cold wheel hangs bright as the heart of heaven; the great earth, mountains, and rivers receive its illuminating presence. Shattering the universe, one beholds it face-to-face;
its radiance extends ten thousand miles, overflowing with pure clarity.

Píngyáng asked: "Suppose there is a person who attends court in the morning and recites scriptures in the evening, never departing from Chan and the teachings. Suddenly, they are struck by lightning—what then?
He answered on his own behalf: "The peach pit is smashed to pieces, revealing the old kernel within."
Failing to distinguish north from south is still falling into views; when the paths of sage and ordinary are severed, dust still remains.
With one blow behind the head, everyone turns over at once; liberated from all dependence, one stands peerless.
(Guanming of Gu'an) One day, Pyeongyang led a donkey around the hall once and commanded the assembly to offer a word; none were in accord, so he himself acted as the donkey.
He brayed and went out.
Weng Zhen said, "Both the Great and Small Pinyangs were skilled at acting among heterodox species; however, they lacked the marks of a great man.
Had I been there, I would have stuffed grass into their mouths and struck them twice upon their backs. If they had—"

He further brayed like a donkey. He struck the wooden board three times, pulled him out of the hall by his rope, and showed him that even with such "pervading-the-heavens" skills, there was no place for him to stand. He then offered this verse:
A thousand-year-old ancient tree has long since become a spirit; it deliberately accompanies this fellow of a different species. Taking steps at ease, it trills its song with artful skill;
though there is no one to join in, it spontaneously brays like a donkey.
One night at Pingyang, [Nanquan] entered the hall and shouted loudly, saying, "I just lost a cow from the pen!
Let everyone join me in a communal work assignment to go up the mountain and search for the cow. As soon as a monk stepped out, the Master lowered his head and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
The ancient Xuezhe said: "In the pen at Pingyang, although the ox is not seen, its head and horns are nonetheless fully manifest.
A water buffalo of Cuiyan is always within the pen; it simply has no tracks to be found. I dare ask the assembly: [Where is it?]
Since it has always been within the railing, why is there no trace of it?
Evening *chan* at Pingyang: Pines are straight, thorns are crooked; cranes are white, crows are black. A large month has thirty days;
a small month has twenty-nine. Everyone knows this. But suppose someone calls you from behind—then you turn your head around. Now tell me: where did you go when you turned?
"What side of affairs does he clarify? The bag’s belly is wide; Vajrapāṇi’s board is broad. Xinfan Lan said:
"This old fellow’s teeth do not even clench against the wind; he merely talks to himself.
Had he stopped right there at 'What side of affairs does he clarify? it would have left people with lingering doubts. Yet he goes on to say, 'The bag’s belly...'"
The breadth of Kuan’s Vajrapāṇi [icon] is vast. How is this different from teaching people how to climb trees or providing ladders for thieves to pass over?
Does it not seduce and corrupt the men and women of families? Then he took up his staff and said: "Is there anyone here who cannot bear this? Come forward! I am precisely about to ask you:
turning your head and shifting your gaze—what kind of matter does that clarify?"
Chan Master Shiqi Tongyun of Xuedou (successor to Tiantong Wu) ascended the hall. "The capital is very noisy; my kingdom is at peace," he said.
Holding up his staff, he added, "One cannot say that this staff is not at peace. He then tapped it and said, "Lower your voices!
Lower your voices!"
In the city of Chang’an, the smoke and people are still; in my country, all is tranquil while affairs multiply.
If you are a true offspring of the golden-maned lion, you will perceive the paradox even three thousand miles away. (Peifeng Ze) Xuedou ascended the hall:
At the beginning of the month, at the full moon, the moon is round, the moon is waning—a single phrase fully raised, and ten thousand functions are stilled.
Xuezhao struck the staff and said, "Look, look! It is being cast down! *Du!* Jiang Tianquan said:
"The pointing out at Vulture Peak and the painting at Caoxi are both not as good as this one-time revelation by the old fellow Xuedou.
Yet, alas, all the people in the great earth have understood it entirely upon the staff."
Chan Master Mochun Tongmen of Helin in Runzhou (successor to Tiantong Wuzu). A monk asked, "Before the World-Honored One held up the flower, and before Kāśyapa smiled, what was the meaning?
The Master said, "What bowl are you looking for? The monk asked, "And after Kāśyapa smiled, what then? The Master said, "A total failure."
Eighteen infants emerge from the painted hall; the elders do not recognize such a display.
Meeting people, they vainly claim to seek out friends; a heart as pure as ice is entrusted to the wild pond.
(Ming Gaofeng) No sand enters the eyes; no water enters the ears. Eight *liang* together with half a *jin*; one fall brings another rise.

If one attempts to deliberate upon it, it is separated by ten thousand miles. Fallen flowers abound amidst wind and rain; fragrant and moist, the oriole perches on its branch. (Facing the green mountains:
A single, perfectly round heart of primordial antiquity—who was it that skillfully chiseled it, thereby losing its true purity?
Though one may possess the power to mend the heavens with refined stones, there is nothing to be done against the Lord of Spring as he dallies in early spring. (Miaoyun Xiong)
Gunan ascended the hall. Throwing down his staff, he said, "This falling is not something other. Then, raising it up and performing a dance, he said, "Moving freely in all directions, it is not dust.
Do you see how the mountains, rivers, and the great earth fully reveal the body of the Dharma King?
He then struck the incense table and said, "A single piece of elm or paulownia wood; when struck, its sound kills people."
Before the phoenix-mirror stand, she skillfully paints her brows; She applies her own rouge and powder, claiming herself most exquisite.
Passing through curtains and doors, her elegance excels; The fragrance of *suheta* incense blows across her face.
(Suan-an Ding) Gu-nan ascends the hall: "The great ocean does not harbor corpses; empty space is not stained by the five colors; it is like a great mass of fire."
In the midst [of emptiness], there is no hiding of mosquitoes or gnats; within the dharma of non-abiding, there is no establishing of delusion or enlightenment.
For all you people who strive to study Chan and awaken to the Way, it will take sixty kalpas over three lifetimes.
Yongning Ding said: "If Guinan did not establish the four prohibitions, how could one reveal that the heels of one's own self are floating?"
Pressing on and pressing on—without cause, waves rise from level ground. A single bubble in the vast ocean contains a hundred rivers.
If you ask for the precise meaning of the middle stream, ten thousand brooks and a thousand ravines all flow from the abyss. (De-shi-xin)
Chan Master Tongxian of Fushishi Baoen Temple in Wujiang (a successor of Tiantong Wu) went to Tiantong to pay his respects. Tiantong again appointed him as an attendant.
One day, encountering snow, Tiantong asked, "This fine snow—why does it not fall elsewhere?
The Master replied, "It is simply because there is not an inch of earth upon the great earth. Tiantong said, "Since there is not an inch of earth, where, after all, does it fall?"
The Master said: "The front mountain and the back mountain;
atop the oriole’s nest, one wanders at night. Witnessing the corpse-smeared ground, one immediately understands; within the cool serenity of the hall, one personally sees through it.
The hawk from Silla has a smile filling its beak. (Lingchang Yun)
A lone flute is blown in the desolate, empty courtyard; the sound of the wind suits me as I lean upon my pillow. With a solitary lamp, dreams are severed and fragrant tears fall;
I write my sorrowful heart in secret—whom can it be sent to? (By Zixiu Man) As soon as one crosses the Clear Barrier, both eyes awaken.
Beneath the Linglong Rock, there is no distinction between the intimate and the stranger. A breeze arises from the corner of the hall, cool as...
Washing. "The Six Heavens send down flying flowers, renewing the world.

(Quanchi Wo) Regarding the "Requiting Kindness" [Kannon] case, when a monk asked, "If one clearly does not violate the command, is it still permitted for another to attain enlightenment? The Master said, "That still falls into the second rank.
The monk said, "It is easy to open a mouth from beginning to end, but difficult to preserve a heart through the cold of winter. The Master said, "Go out and reflect on this yourself."

Depart! The barbarian cavalry have needlessly entered the imperial city. Advancing and retreating, they vainly prop themselves up; yet the commander-in-chief in the central courtyard can enforce his orders.
Without moving a blade or a spear, he establishes a time of Great Peace. (Huguo Yue)
Ascending the hall to give thanks for the patronage: The crow flies and the hare runs as swiftly as a shuttle; how could light and darkness ever obscure him?
Within this, there is originally nothing to be said; yet to say "there is nothing to be said" already constitutes much. Holding up his whisk, he said:
"Is this 'having something to say' or 'having nothing to say'? He then threw down the whisk.
No sooner is the foul mouth opened than matters are as tangled as hemp. Dwelling neither in East Lu nor West Qin, what need is there to deliberate further on existence or non-existence?
One merely smears on rouge and powder to boast before others. (Suan Ding):
Regarding the meaning of the "Broken Sand Pot" asked by a monk at Baen Temple, the Master said: "Scattered and fallen apart, filling [the void]."
Ditches and ravines. Here the monk had an awakening:
"Scattered and dispersed, they fill the ditches and ravines; in one's old age, one adds footnotes for others.
Had I been by his side in those days, both would have been buried in a single pit. (Pingji Pu)
Chan Master Tongqi of Linye (successor to Tiantong Wu) ascended the hall and said: "I have a single phrase that pervades heaven and covers the earth.
I present it to you all; do not attempt to deliberate upon it. What phrase is this?"
Zifu Yu said: "This fellow who hides his head but reveals his tail has already been exposed. You have also asked, 'What kind of phrase is this?
Suppose someone were to suddenly overturn the meditation seat—how would you evade it?"
Tongxuan ascended the hall and said: "The Dharma-body, the Reward-body, and the Transformation-body are all threaded together on a single string. Nevertheless, this is far too simple and direct;
it spares everyone from groping about in the dark. May you all be happy! He struck the meditation staff and said:
"The auspicious qilin has but a single horn."
At the clear dawn, a beautiful woman emerges from her inner chamber; In the breeze, her hairpins and bracelets ring out in distinct notes of *gong* and *shang*.
Her rainbow-robes are tied with knots of crystalline purity; O Chang’e within the moon, do not claim to be her peer. (Suan Ding) Regarding the "Penetration of Mysteries":
A monk asked, "What is it to have not a single thought arise? The Master said, "A hundredfold fragments. [The monk] said, "If..."
"How can one go to the place where the life-root (jīvitendriya) is severed? The Master said, "Cease applying effort.
Luan Yuan said, "At the moment the life-root is severed, it naturally ceases. Even if you apply effort, it is like a single thought not arising;
yet, is this truly capable of shattering everything into a hundred fragments?"
Master Lin Gao Benyu (succeeded by Xiu of Qing Shan) of the Bamboo Grove at Jingkou addressed the assembly: "Pressing oil from within stone;
taking fire from within water. This is not a matter of laboring with physical movement; it is simply a matter of revealing [the truth] directly before one's eyes.
Master Zhaozhou was far too clever—be careful not to say that his 'Qingzhou cloth robe weighs seven pounds.'"
On the bamboo bed, with a high pillow, there is truly nothing to do; outside the door, one knows not from where the wind comes. Suddenly it awakens a dream of an autumn night:
the bright moon rises before the window upon the solitary peak. (Tieji Xin) At Zhulin, a monk asked:
"The flowers bloom on the withered tree before the Hall of the Bright Moon—is this a phrase of the guest or the host?"
The Master said, "A barren woman weeps for the blue sky.
Shengfa Rong remarked, "Although the Old Man of Lingao does not fail to respond to the incoming stimulus,
if one wishes to 'sever the nails and cut through the iron' or 'raise the dead and restore life,' he still lacks one move."
Zhulin asked a monk, "When heaven does not cover and earth does not support, where can one find a place to settle the body and establish one's life?
The Master struck him and went back into the abbot’s quarters. The next day, the monk asked again, "Yesterday I was given a blow; is the Master still in pain today?"
The Master struck him out again.
Chengtian Yi said, "Jiashan’s tactical maneuvers are truly not unworthy of being a 'Dragon Gate' of a generation;
yet, when examined closely, he cannot avoid blinding the eyes of the entire city of Ruzhou."
Chan Master Yulin Tongxiu of Xitianmu in Hangzhou (Successor of Qingshan Xiu). A monk asked: "In the past, the High Ancestor said:
'The mud ox at the bottom of the sea swallows the moon and runs; the stone tiger before the cliff cradles its cub and sleeps; the iron snake drills into the diamond eye;
Kunlun rides an elephant led by a heron. What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "A fine son, after all..."
Not using one's father’s money;
a fragrant elephant cuts through the current. River water becomes pearls; a tiger gives birth to three cubs—eventually there will be leopards and hares.

The waves at the bottom of the sea surge upward as the Dragon Chart emerges. A heron stands amidst the snow—how does it differ from the bright moon? Since ancient times, High Peak has been as pure as...
Granted. To speak at random, the eastern neighbor has an abundance of wealth.
(Most Lazy Root) He alone has established a family fortune of ten thousand acres, not seeking the ancestral estates. How could he borrow even a fraction from the five carts?

Within this, the Great Dharma is currently employed; one phrase serves as the title for a case that endures for a thousand ages. Good lad! From lamp to lamp, the flame continues—this is a living burial.

The Hall. (Ming Gao Feng) Ten-thousand-hu measures of bright pearls cannot be exhausted; five carts of book scrolls have no end to their use. The two eyes, east and west, share the same springtime command;
for a thousand years, the wind of propagation and recitation has prevailed. (Master Han Jing)
Both giving and taking are brought under the power of his grasp; the divine child vies for the "money that stops crying. His glorious reputation reaches Wu and Yue;
his lofty spirit shakes the mountains and rivers and the heavens of the Five Peaks.
(Zi Ning Xiao) High-seated and following in the footsteps of ancient masters, the Western Peak rises from the earth with even greater brilliance. Picking up pebbles and rubble, they become pure gold.
How could he ever be willing to ask others about Shi Chong? (Returning with the Hermit) River-like eyes and sea-like mouth;
his entire being is a blade’s edge. His stratagems overflow like the heavens; his whole body is a display of dynamic power. He lays it all out upon the platter.
A fine young man! When the treasure-trove is opened, who recognizes the gift?
(From the *Nanzong Chuan*) The Iron Ox roars wherever it goes amidst clouds and waves; across ten thousand li of mountains and rivers, the purple qi rises high.
Within this, the world is concealed within the cosmos; for a thousand autumns, no one shall call him but a child. (By Park In-ui)
An exceptional man should exert himself; why boast of his ancestors' vast fields and manors? With ten thousand scrolls stored within his breast, there is no end to his wisdom;
let his sons carry his fame far across the four seas.
(Zonglinxiang) Because the autumn colors were magnificent at Tianmu, he addressed the assembly: "I, this mountain monk, can preach a fine discourse on the Buddha-dharma. It hangs—"
Upon the Huayu Bridge, the assembly each looked for themselves. After a long while, he said: "Bai Le once visited three times;
who could have added a thousand pieces of gold? You offered it to me, but you did not accept it; I returned it whole, leaning against a withered vine."
Huishi Qi said: "If Sun Chudang were here today, he would simply say, 'Old Monk, you must personally undergo one round of punishment.
Why is this so? It is because it is improper to treat the property of the monastery as one's own private gift."
Tianmu addressed the assembly: "An old window and a dilapidated house; a paper screen and a blue lamp.
Is there anyone here who has caught even a hint of its flavor? The wind has grown sharp tonight; it will snow by three parts."

Yongning Ding said: "Everyone says that Tianmu is the teacher of the entire nation; yet, when one looks closely, it is like a beggar picking up a Kaiyuan treasure that cannot be used because its inscriptions are incomplete."
A monk asked Tianmu, "What is the fundamental matter? The Master said, "He manages the household smoke, whether it rises high or low.
Shengfa Rong remarked, "Tianmu only knows that this monk manages the household smoke, whether it rises high or low; he does not know himself."
Having forgotten the length of the ladle’s handle, she is unaware that her beauty could topple a kingdom.

Tipping her jade phoenix hairpin askew as she emerges from the silken curtains, she occasionally opens a golden mirror to examine her complexion, still adjusting her fresh makeup and entrusting a painter to draw her brows. (Jian’an Yi)
One day, Tianmu asked Dai Tingcheng, "From where does a cloud arise? He replied, "It arises from where you, Master, have questioned.
The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, am at fault.
Yongning Ding said, "The old man Tianmu was like one who sets up a target only to draw an arrow upon himself. Peifeng Ze said, "Iron."
A whole ball is stuffed into the mouth; who is there to swallow it?
When a monk asked Tianmu why drums are beaten and bells are rung, the Master said, "To change people's eyes."
Huishi Qi said: "If I were the officiating monk, I would simply prostrate and return to the assembly. Let us see how this old fellow can be brought to his end.
Chan Master Tongwen Ruo’an of Lian’an, Hangzhou (successor to Xiushan), was asked by a monk about the thousand hands of Avalokiteśvara.
"The eye is not merely the 'correct eye. The Master said: 'Lowering the fishing line at a rapid current.

Lowering the line in swift waters, a thousand eyes are bewildered; following the waves eastward, one casts again to the west. The golden-winged bird seizes and snaps it, and the vast ocean is exhausted.
Thunder and rain roar as they pass through the nine ravines. (Tianli Zhen)
A thousand-fathom line casts into the azure waves; The swimming fish, upon seeing it, dart like a shuttle.
Infinite intent follows the flowing current; How can one do anything about this clear, true eye?
(Xuchun-yunduan) Yanling did not accept the Han dynasty’s fief; At the rapids, he opened the true eye. Suddenly, a scaled dragon is seen breaking through the waves.
Come! The fishing line pulls the very heavens and earth around.
(Beiming Zhan) I am too weary to roll embroidered balls in the streets; instead, I come to the broken shore to cast my golden hook.
The swimming scales chase the waves as misty billows stretch to infinity; the fisherman need only lean against his moon-laden boat. (Nishan Wei)

Sitting on a fishing rock by the ancient bank, the breeze is clear; The rapids are high and the current swift, the waves fly like birds. The thousand eyes of Great Compassion have been blind from the start;
Returning empty-handed, he carries a boat full of bright moonlight.
(Keda Yan) Even if Lord Ye possessed the skill to dot the pupils, He could not dot the eye at the back of Great Compassion’s head. Just as he has descended onto the swift-water rapids—
Fishing. The ten directions tremble as they watch the flying dragon.
(Miaowei Jun) When Lia’an escorted Master Xueqiao to the mountain gate, he saw a dog barking. Xue said, "This fellow has no Buddha-nature, going here and there.
The Master replied, "But you have scratched the Great Master’s itch. Xue laughed loudly; the Master also laughed loudly.
They smiled and departed.
Sanmei Zhenyun said: "Since there is no Buddha-nature, why did they happen to scratch the itchy spot?
One must know that in the smiles of these two great elders, each harbors a kind of 'white-handed' theft."
Liyuan was asked by a monk, "What is it like when you do not recognize the one facing you? The Master said, "A blade or an axe cannot cut it open.
Falingyin said, "The old monk is the old monk; you, O *śrāmaṇera*, are you yourself. Can you borrow even a single point from me?"
"If the Acharya has no share, it shall all go to this old monk. Ten people, five pairs, all say this is far too much fabrication.
Today there are seven blows; for now, let them be sealed and sent to the storehouse, to await thirty years hence."
The golden hammer behind the head is used for coarse matters; Emperor Wu once yielded to the blue-eyed barbarian.
The great battle at Mount Yan has its inscription engraved anew; he has completely reclaimed the old imperial capital.
(Haihui Xing) From the days of Sun and Wu, hardships arose; they sucked abscesses and shared wine amidst the ranks. Tens of thousands of heroic soldiers were like fathers to them.
"Son, we share life and death at the frontier pass.
(Shengfa Rong) At Li'an, when a monk asked, "What are the three kinds of illnesses of the Dharma-body? the Master said, "Scorching a scar.
The monk asked, "What are the two kinds of light? The Master said, "If you look at them, you will go blind."
Falin-yin said: "If you do not leap over several times beyond the other side of Wei-yin, you will inevitably encounter obstructions wherever you go.
The three kinds of illnesses and two kinds of lights have already been cast aside; yet what do you call this 'Dharmakāya'?
Although Chuiyu is indeed his true bone-and-flesh descendant, he has truly never caught even a whiff of his sweat-smelling breath."
Wait until I have toppled Mount Daren and sucked dry the spring of the Dharma-rain; at that time, I shall speak to you again slowly.
The Master of the Realm has never had a fixed method; he simply stirs chicken dung into hemp sugar.
A single dose of empty space cures all illness, which is even superior to the nine-fold refined incense that passes through the bottle. (Shengfa Rong)
Master Liran was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice.
To penetrate the heavy barrier is not difficult; at Hanyuan, do not ask about Chang'an again.
How lamentable are those travelers who, on mistaken paths, greedily pursue their journey—still facing a thousand mountains and ten thousand peaks. (Meigu Yue)
Liyuan Yin came for a second audience. The Master asked, "Where have you been staying lately?
Yin replied, "Xinghua. The Master struck him. Yin said, "This old fellow still holds such a view. The Master struck again.
Yin said, "If you act as a teacher in this way, you will blind people's eyes. The Master struck once more and said, "Today I shall blind yours."
"One. Yinyue said, "I have already admitted defeat. The Master then sighed. Yinyue said, "Heaven! Heaven!
The Master sighed again. Yinyue then departed.
De’an Xin said, "There is the host within the guest, and the guest within the host; they exchange roles to meet the occasion, yet it is one scene of admitting defeat."
"Nevertheless, at that time, he further bestowed [the Dharma] upon thirty others; how could this not illuminate the past and enrich the future?
Later, when Li’an asked a monk, 'All sentient beings practice the way of filial piety; why then does the earth-owl eat its mother?
The Master replied, 'An enemy meets a narrow path.'"
Huangbo Zhenjue said: "The Master threw a ball of ice into a cauldron of boiling water; he snatched a live sparrow from the jaws of a tiger.
Not only did he change the eyes of all quarters, he has gone on to blind the eyes of everyone in the world."
Liyuan asked a monk, "A person of great ultimate penetration is fundamentally liberated from birth and death; why then is their life-root not severed?
The Master said, "A snail has swallowed a duck."
The snail swallows the duck; illumination and function are complete as guest and host. With a single word, the fundamental principle is settled;
the thousand-jin trigger is released like a crossbow.
(Langye Zhen) At Lian’an, when a monk asked, "What is it like when one is utterly destitute and bare-boned? the Master said, "I have a piece of tattered robe."
"I will give it to you right away. The monk hesitated. The Master said, "It cannot be worn.
Miaowei Jun remarked, "This monk was poor and met with robbery; he is utterly without recourse.

The Old Master read the wind and set his sails—his mastery of seizing and releasing is truly worth observing. Yet, when scrutinized, there is still one move missing. Let those with eyes discern this!"
Not necessarily does what is in the heart match what is in the mouth; when one arrives, those who know them become enemies instead.
When meeting people, speak but three parts of the truth; let guests form a group and fall short by two counts.
(Xiao’an Yù) Master Tōngjì of Lùluó Mountain on Nanyuē (Succeeded by Qiāngshān Xiū). A monk asked: “What is that which transcends the Buddhas?”
Transcending the patriarchal phrase, the Master held up his staff and said, "Realize it right here. The monk then shouted. The Master struck him.
As the monk prepared to offer further words, the Master chased him out with a continuous succession of blows.
The staff-tip points to the moon in the mid-heavens; within the pond, the wind wafts the fragrance of the lotus.
If you ask for the phrase that transcends the patriarchs from the West, it is but a vain labor to expend one’s own critical judgment.
(Wu Shiwei) A single phrase fully presented transcends Buddhas and patriarchs. To again provoke a living snake requires hands that are not naturally nimble. The traveler truly does not...
To explain the return journey: It would be in vain to have the Lord of Spring repeatedly pluck the willows.
(The Integrity of the Cold Pine) When asked about the verse of the Ancestor from Yue, he flung out an iron steamed bun. Having caught even a trace of its flavor, one is satiated and cannot stop.
This thought is truly serene, as misty vapors swirl around the green creepers; A shadow hangs suspended from the overhanging cliff, flickering and vast.
It overturns the idle nests of Buddhas and Patriarchs, Bestowing upon the wandering traveler a value many times greater. (The snow-wheel is pure.)
A monk asked Nanyue, "What is the place where a student establishes their body and sustains their life?
The Master said, "Wait until I have a place to establish my body and sustain my life, and then I will tell you."
Shengfayong said: "Although Nanyue gained strength while on the road, alas, he spent his days in petty toil.
If one wishes to return home and enjoy peace and prosperity, it will take sixty kalpas over three lifetimes."
Nanyue was once asked by a monk, "If one holds a sharp sword in hand, why does the monkey not die?
The Master said, "It is entirely due to its own power.
Tieji Xinda remarked, "So it turns out the Master is also merely making his living right here."
Jiang Tianquan said: "Relying on the power of the sharp sword, the monkey dies; relying on the power of the monkey, what is the use of the sharp sword? Let those with eyes discern this."
Nanyue was asked by a monk: "Having bitten through the sour iron dumpling, why are there still hungry people on the road?
The Master said, "We travel the same path, yet take different tracks.
Zifu Yu remarked, "This fellow dares to call himself a Chan guest; why not further say, 'In that case, it is the same as the Master'?"
This refers to a future life. It is taught that Nanyue had his share of the monastery divided.
Chan Master Tongshou of Yangshan Songji (succeeded by Xiu of Qingshan) ascended the hall and said: "The gate faces a thousand peaks of azure; Along the stream, a path winds through seclusion.
If you seek further for the profound and wondrous principle, It is like stirring the embers to search for floating bubbles."
Chengtian Yi said: "Yangshan’s teaching in this manner, though born of a most earnest and compassionate heart, cannot help but fail his former sages and bring ruin to his descendants."
Yangshan was asked by a monk, "The twenty-five sages were originally without superiority or inferiority; why did he single out the faculty of the ear as the perfect penetration?
The Master said, "Cuiwei died of frostbite."

At the mountain’s end, one doubts there is a path; yet as one turns around the stream, the scenery grows ever more secluded.

(By Baryak Pu) She learns to comb her loosened hair and tries on a new skirt; the news is that the auspicious time for our meeting is this very spring. Because she wishes to appear beautiful, her heart grows restless.
Confused. He asks those nearby for the correct direction. (Green Rain on the Banana Leaves) Turning back, he reaches the Ninth Stage amidst the dust;
the layered passes of Jiange open wide and clear. In the humble alley, he does not ride a golden horse;
returning home, he wears his tattered robe once more. (Arrow Peak’s Reality)
One day, while Xiangyan and Yangshan were making cakes at Mount Gui, the Master said, "At that time, our late teacher Baizhang personally realized this principle.
Yangshan and Xiangyan looked at each other and asked, "Who could answer this question?
The Master said, "There is one who can answer it. Yangshan asked, "Who is it? The Master pointed to the water buffalo.
He said, "The Way, the Way. He told one of them, "Go fetch a bundle of grass," and the other, "Go fetch a bucket of water.
When they had placed these before the oxen, as soon as the oxen began to eat, the Master said, "In this way, in this way; not in this way, not in this way. Both men then prostrated themselves.
The Master said, "At times it is bright; at times it is dark.
Hanxiu Qian remarked, "When the strings vibrate, one distinguishes the melody; when the leaves fall, one knows autumn. This belongs to Master Miu-shan and his son.
Yet, within the gate of the patch-robed monks, there is still a lack of awakening. Why? It is not the hand of the monk Seng-yao; it is merely laboring over painting in vermilion and green."
Another verse:
The steamed buns and the water buffalo reveal the fundamental principle; Face-to-face transmission makes the Way flourish ever more.
Guests from beyond the transformation are fundamentally distinct; Do not mistake a blade of grass for a celestial hero.
Master Guishan ascended the hall. "The bitter cold of mid-winter is an annual occurrence; as the movement of the sun’s shadow shifts, what is the nature of this matter?
Yangshan stepped forward, stood with his hands clasped, and remained there. The Master said, "I knew well that you would not be able to answer this question.
He then looked toward Xiangyan. Xiangyan said, "I am uniquely able to answer this question. The Master repeated his previous question, and Xiangyan also stepped forward.
He stood before him with his hands joined in *añjali*. The Master said, "Fortunately, I encountered the Son of Silence (Jizizi), who does not understand.
Ruiyan Yun'en remarked, "Miaoxi was about to lead his two disciples toward a time of frozen ice and aged snow to hold a family banquet.

They feasted on bear paws and the peaks of Mount Diao, their appetites fully satisfied; the sounds of pipes, strings, and tortoise-drum resonated through the clouds and heavens, witnessed by those far and near."
Everyone looked on with admiration and delight. Yet, when it came to the division of the family estate, they remained as estranged as those of Wu and Yue.
[The Master] strikes the whisk and says: "At first, one only spoke of the length of the thatch; only after burning it did one realize the ground was uneven. Wushi Dao said:
"The father and two sons of Mount Huangbo have set up a stage for a puppet show; they have played it out with such ferocity that there is no good way to bring it to a close. But tell me—"
That is the place where he delivers the decisive blow. Each of the two men stands with hands folded behind their backs; outside the gate, the sand basin, the well, and the stones run about.
It makes old Guizhi Huishan laugh to death as he turns southward to look at the Big Dipper. Kongyousheng said:
"Although the father and son of Mount Gui were harmonious in sound and resonance, with their striking and singing occurring simultaneously, when one examines them closely, they are both..."
To sit upon the tip of a hundred-foot pole is for each person to recognize but a single speck; this cannot avoid the laughter of bystanders.

Had Mingjue been asked at that time, "The bitter cold of midwinter is an annual occurrence; how is it with the shifting movement of the sun's course? he would simply have said, "Today the wind is somewhat stiff.
Then he would have requested, "Venerable Sir, please return to your quarters. Had one been able to utter such a word, that would be the lineage of Miu and Yang.
The wind will certainly not be so desolate.
As the movement of the sun’s shadow shifts, what of the matter? Thread comes and thread goes, surely a source of confusion.
Woven into Sichuan brocade of a thousand kinds of ingenuity, it does not go beyond that single shuttle from of old. (Lan’an Shu)
A single pole with a line catches two golden fish; Unstirring the clear waves, their intent is uniquely distinct.
Slanting the straw raincoat to cover them behind, Only the bright moon remains, filling the rivers and lakes.
(Shixi Yue) An arrow silently pierces the shadow of the red sun; The pair of hawks have already fallen from the emerald clouds. One knows not that Li Guang lacked the profound mystery.
"Excellent! Look toward where the bowstring was released.
(Xianji Yun) Miaoxi asked Yunguan, "Is it true that you have long been with Yaoshan? He replied, "It is true.
The Master said, "What is the mark of a great man at Yaoshan? He replied, "It exists after nirvana. The Master said, "How can it exist after nirvana?"
Yangshan said, "Water cannot wet it. Yanque then asked, "I wonder, what is the Great Man’s mark of Baizhang?
The Master replied, "Majestic and dignified; brilliant and resplendent. Before sound, there is no sound; after form, there is no form.
A mosquito on an iron ox—there is no place for you to alight."
Tiantong Hua said: "The two venerable masters describe the marks of a great man; how is this different from pointing to a deer and calling it a horse?
Someone asked Guizong, "What are the marks of a great man at Huqiu? To which he replied: "Nine times nine, a hundred times a hundred; half blue, half white. Pingyang Min said:
"The two venerable masters pointed to a deer and called it a horse; Master Ying'an took a tortoise and turned it into a turtle."
Each received three blows of the staff. Someone asked, "How are the marks of a great man like those of Tiantong? He tore open his chest and said, "Majestic and august;
distinct and clear. Sixty kalpas across three lifetimes—one might realize it, yet one would not even know it."
When Guishan saw Liu Tiemo approaching, he said, "Old cow, you have come. Tiemo replied, "Tomorrow there is a great assembly at Tiantai for a vegetarian feast;
will the Master go as well? The Master then threw himself down into a reclining posture, and Tiemo immediately departed.
Jingci once said: "The old fellow Guishan had, throughout his life, a backbone so straight it could not be bent.
Yet he was pushed over by Liu Tiemo; even until now, he cannot get up. If you wish to help him rise, please each offer a turning word.
The assembly remained silent, whereupon [Jingci] drove them all away at once with his staff. Zhongfeng Ben said: "Guishan..."
Mount Shishuang was pressed down by Liu Tiemo with a single squeeze; he wanted to rise, but he could not. Liu Tiemo was pushed over by Guishan with a single shove;
he wanted to stay, but he could not. If Master Ben were to pass judgment in this manner, how many people would be biting off their own thumbs behind his back?
Boshan Lai said: "The ridge mountain rises clouds; the main mountain rains down. The ladle divines."
Listening to empty sounds; when one is drowsy from heat, there is much delirious chatter. Even if the bow is broken and the arrows exhausted, one is still not a true master.
If you wish for those of the same breath to seek one another and those of the same sound to respond to one another, look at this herd of water buffaloes.
He laughed again and said, "Their nostrils are all in the hands of Boshan. Guangjiao Yu said: "When Liu Tiewo came, it was not because they were not enemies that he did not..."
“Gathering at the head. Old cow, you have arrived! To invite a thief and ruin the household. Tomorrow is the Great Assembly feast at Tiantai Mountain;
will you, Master, go there as well? What kind of soup are you sucking out of a sesame cake? He assumes a reclining posture and then departs.
“The rain has ceased and the clouds dispersed; the vast sky is wide open. A pair of mandarin ducks cannot be captured in a painting. Yuan’an Yu said: “Miaoyan was struck by an iron [bolt].”
One question from Mo [Zhaozhou] was enough to leave him lying face down in the street; even if oxen or horses were to trample over him, he would not care at all.
But tell me, will you go to the Great Assembly Feast or not? Come back tomorrow and we shall see.
Once he rode his iron steed into the heavy city; when the imperial decree was proclaimed, the six kingdoms were heard to be purified. Still grasping his golden whip, he asks the returning traveler:
"In the deep of night, who walks with me along the Imperial Street?
(Cui Feng Xian) Having achieved victory in a hundred battles, he grows old in the Great Peace. Wandering at ease, who dares to vie with him? His jade whip and golden horse remain idle in the end.
The sun, the bright moon, and the pure breeze enrich one’s entire life.
(Tiantong Jue) The host has no virtue and the guest has no spark; amidst the flash of a stone-fire, lightning flies.
Dying together and living together, sharing both gain and loss—how many can truly know this mind? (Zhong’an Kong)

Cloud-nests, dreams severed; the moon’s brilliance shines in autumn. The Jade Maiden turns her body across the Ox and Plow constellations. Casting off the flower-crown, she returns to her old retreat.
On the dark path and the bird-track, there is no room for gathering.
(Zuan Jian) Together we enjoy this time of peace and prosperity when the Way is secure. When meeting, one never unfurls the spear or banner. As the occasion requires, simple rice and clear tea.
Outside, lying exhausted or walking idly—who knows how many there are?

(Wuzu Fan) Releasing both and gathering both, exhausting the roles of host and guest; the lutes and songs play together in the "Spring at the Jade Tower. Drunkenly supported, the golden pavilion and pearl curtains are silent;
the fragrance of flowers remains deep within the dew. (Tianzhang Yu)
Suddenly grasping the shadow-grass to probe the wind, he turns his body directly beneath it—altogether different. The four seas are tranquil and clear, heaven and earth are still;
the General’s intent does not lie in his carved bow. (Lang Shan Yu) When the eight directions have achieved their merit, the Imperial Way is level.
For long, the carved bow has hung idly in the quiet courtyard. Last night, a gust of wind swept across the sandy embankment.
Wild geese—mistakenly thought to be the sound of frontier alarm horns.
(Zudeng Shao) On Mount Míu, while ascending the hall, a monk came forward and said, "I beg the Master to preach the Dharma for the assembly.
The Master said, "I have already exhausted you thoroughly. The monk then bowed.
Xuefeng Cunen heard this and said, "The ancients possessed such a heart of compassionate intimacy.
Xuansha Shibei said, "That old fellow on the mountainhead has missed the point of the ancients' affair. Xuefeng asked, "Where did he miss it?
Xuansha said, "When Muzhou was questioned by that monk, he was reduced to total fragmentation. Yuan'an Yuanwu said, "You must know that before Muzhou even ascended [the hall]..."
By the time he entered the hall, he was already utterly exhausted. Falingyin said, "Yuan'an was a master of the Way.
When a monk asked Muzhou, "What is the true person of Baizhang? the Master descended from his meditation seat and stood with his hands clasped.
The monk asked, "What is the true person of the Master? and the Master sat back down.
The face of Baizhang’s cat; the eyes of Guishan’s ghost. Seeing people, it merely smiles in vain; handling objects, it does not know their names.
(Songyuan Yue) Sparse shadows sway in the moon over the plum blossoms by the river; deep and light, a secluded spring arises in the garden of Langyuan. A gust of warm breeze leaks through them all.
Leaking. A fragrance fills the heavens as it sends the *youjin* (wandering essence).
(Complete Transcender of the Patriarchs) An old woman applies makeup, dotting her lips with vermilion. She displays her own fine spirit before others.
Her frowning brow and cold smile are exactly like [the Buddha’s], yet she pays no heed to the onlookers who cover their noses. (Shifan Yan)
Guishan said to the assembly, "So many people like this have attained only the great potential, but not the great function.
Yangshan raised this matter and asked a hermit at a hut at the foot of the mountain, "The old man on the mountain head spoke thus; what was his meaning?"
The Master said, "Please try to bring it up again. Yang attempted to bring it up once more, but he was tripped over by the abbot.
Yang returned and reported this to the Master, who laughed heartily.
Xiaoyan Bao said to Bi Muishan, “Jizi, do you require one more kick? Lian’an asked, “Everyone says that Yangshan was kicked by the hut dweller;
yet they fail to realize that Yangshan possessed the skillful means of a thief who never gets caught.
Although the hut dweller gained the advantage, he could not avoid having his lips and skin split by laughter. Old man Xiaoyan!”
"To speak thus, you see only the sharpness of the tip of a needle. Now tell me, how far apart am I from those old masters?
He then laughed heartily.
Guishan asked Yangshan, "Setting aside the matter of the present for a moment, what about the matter of antiquity? Yangshan folded his hands.
He stepped forward. The Master said, "That is still just a matter of the present. As for matters of antiquity, how is that? Yang bowed and withdrew to stand behind him.
The Master said, "You have wronged me; I have wronged you."

Zhaojue Qin said: "Although Yangshan was skilled at advancing and retreating to illuminate the past and present, he nonetheless had to drink the broth from within Huibian’s sesame cake and seek oil by pressing sand. Even so, tell me: what was the meaning behind Yangshan’s gesture of joining his palms?
If you can understand this, your journey as a pilgrim is complete; if not, I, this old monk, have never [attained it]."

"I have let you all down; from now on, it is you all who have let this old monk down. Fang’an Xian said: "Yangshan advances forward and retreats backward, penetrating the ancient and clarifying the present. Why did Muzhou say that both sides were mutually yielding? He then offered this verse:

Advancing forward, retreating back, Penetrating the ancient, clarifying the present— Why did Muzhou say they were mutually yielding? If you can discern this meaning, Then you will see the two elders’ true intent. If you cannot yet comprehend it, The ancients have already been deceived by you.
We meet at the head of the Jin River; together we ascend the wine tower. Having mastered medicine, one suffers little illness; knowing one’s lot, one harbors no great sorrow.
How profound is the intent of this meeting between teacher and disciple! Suddenly, at the opportune moment, he asks about past and present. With hands joined, he steps forward and then retreats;
having passed through a hundred refinements, the true gold is revealed. (Benjue I)

Tearing asunder past and present, there is only this one self. Within the imperial transformation of the five lakes and four seas, the myriad phenomena of the forested universe are neither bent nor extended.
In this matter, who can share in life and death? (Yunlin Lu).
While Yaoshan was seated, Yangshan and Xiangyan were standing in attendance. The Master raised his hand and said: "Those who act like this nowadays..."
"Few," [said the Master]. "Those who do not act thus are many. Yanguan moved from east to west; Xuanzang moved from west to east.
The Master said, "This causal connection will be like gold thrown upon the ground thirty years hence.
Xuanzang said, "It must also be through the Master’s proclamation that this comes to pass. Yanguan said, "Even now, it is not lacking. The Master said, "Shut your dog’s mouth!"
The Elephant King lets out a sigh; the Lion bellows with a roar. He crouches upon the earth and sweeps across the void, shifting the stars and changing the Dipper.
He cuts off the tongue in its tracks and shuts the dog’s mouth. Once thrown to the ground, it rings like gold; the winding Yellow River is clear through to the bottom.
(Nantang Jing) A troop of golden-maned lion cubs, together they roam and play in non-action. Simultaneously they "peck" and "tap," knowing the pivotal moment.
Transformation: The phoenix turns and the dragon coils—how truly marvelous!

(Fundamental Awakening I) Waiting for my lord to arrive, the moon has already set in the west; we exchange greetings of cold and warmth, yet he is as drunk as mud. At the fifth watch, where do you wish to go?
Mounting his horse to leave the gate, the crows cry out in the night. (Still Window Illumination)
One day, Guishan pointed to the fields and said to Yangshan, "That end is so high; this end is so low.
Yangshan replied, "In fact, it is this end that is high and that end that is low.
Guishan said, "If you do not believe me, simply stand in the middle and look at both ends. Yangshan said, "There is no need to stand in the middle, nor should one dwell at either end."
The Master said, "If it is so, look at water. "Water can level things," [Dao]yang replied. "Water has no fixed nature either;
it simply levels itself higher where there is high ground and levels itself lower where there is low ground. Thereupon, the Master desisted.
Longchi said, "The discourse between Master and Disciple, Miu and Yang, is but a small plot of ground.
At the very beginning, there was some clarity; yet when pressed to the very limit, they could not help but end up in embarrassment. Now tell me:
was it Miu Mountain who was embarrassed, or was it Yang Mountain? If anyone can determine this, they will see the high and low of that small plot of ground."
"Not difficult. Erxianman said, "The perspectives of Master and Disciple at Mount Gui were biased and one-sided. When Jingqing heard this at the time, he simply replied:
"Since I came here, my hands have never been stained by mud or water; sitting and watching, the harvest is more bountiful than last year."
While Shitou was seated, Yangshan entered. The Master then interlaced his two hands into fists and showed them to him.
Yangshan performed a woman’s bow. The Master said, "So it is, so it is."
The beautiful maiden, eighteen years of age, is in the full bloom of youthful charm. She performs a single song and dance of the *Zhazhi* before the hall.
Only Wulang understands her elegant demeanor; no one else says her willow-like brows are so lovely.
(Cishou Shen) The lotus moon shines within her breast; the willow-branch wind blows across her face. At midnight, before the courtyard, the *Zhazhi* dance continues.
Dance. At dawn, the sleeves of her gauze robe were damp with rouge.
(Xinwen Ben) While [Baizhang] was seated in the Dharma Hall of Mt. Mui, Yangshan entered. The Master said, "Ji-zi, what has your successor in the lineage been doing lately?
He replied, "Many people are harboring doubts about this matter. The Master asked, "What about you, Ji-zi?"
He said, "As for Huiji, when weary he simply closes his eyes; when vigorous, he sits in meditation. That is why I have never mentioned it.
The Master said, "Reaching such a state is indeed difficult to find. He replied, "According to what Huiji sees, it is merely like this."
"Not even a single word can be applied. The Master said, "Even you cannot do so for a single person. [Yangshan] said, "Since ancient times, all sages have been exactly like this.
The Master said, "There are many who will laugh at you for answering in such a manner. [Yangshan] said, "Those who understand the laughter are my fellow practitioners.
The Master asked, "As for the matter of 'coming forth,' what is it? Yangshan circled the meditation seat once.
[He] circled [the seat]. The Master said, "Tearing asunder past and present.

Jiangshan Qin said, "When the strings vibrate, one distinguishes the melody; when the leaves fall, one knows autumn. From antiquity to the present, it has always been a matter of hitting the mark and striking the core."
The "Bird Path" and the "Mysterious Road" allow for the intimate journeying of father and son; yet, were one in a thicket of thorns, there would still be a lack of awakening.
What serves as proof? Consider, for instance, when Yangshan circumambulated the meditation seat once; Muzhou said, "He has rent asunder past and present."
If one is a monk with clear eyes, one cannot be deceived for even a single point.
Among the successors of the Zen school, where they close their eyes to sit in meditation, they strike a ball on level ground; one must urgently fix one's gaze upon it.
Lifted twice, it was picked up; struck thrice, it could not be held. When it was finally held, it rolled back toward the goal as before.
(Stone Creek Moon) Miaoyan asked Yangshan, "How do you understand the wondrous, pure, and luminous mind? He replied, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth."
[The monk pointed to] the sun, moon, and stars. The Master said, "You have grasped only their phenomena. The monk asked, "What did you ask just now, Reverend?
The Master said, "The wondrous, pure, and luminous mind. The monk asked, "Can it be called a phenomenon? The Master said, "So it is; so it is."
Huanglong Si said: "When the lute and song harmonize and the rhythm and beat follow one another, one must concede this to the father and son of Letan and Guishan.
But as for the wondrous, pure, and luminous mind, even after sixty kalpas across three lifetimes, you have not yet seen it in a dream."
The wondrous, pure, and luminous mind: a single phrase is entirely true. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth;
sun, moon, and stars—exposing one’s liver and draining one’s gall, they illuminate the past and present. If you are not deluded within this, the entire world is golden.
(Xuedou Zong) Once, when a monk asked Master Baizhang Huaihai, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? the Master held up his whisk. Later...
A monk went to Wang Changshi’s residence and recounted the previous conversation. Wang asked, "How did those brothers there deliberate?
The monk replied, "They clarify the mind through form and manifest the principle by means of objects. Wang said, "That is not the way.
You, Venerable One, had better return quickly to Mount Gui. I have sent a letter for the Master. Upon receiving the letter, the monk hurried away.
The Master opened the letter and saw a circular symbol (maṇḍala) within which was written the character for "sun.
The Master said, "Who knew there was a fellow with true understanding a thousand li away? Yangshan, standing in attendance, remarked, "Even so, he is still just an ordinary man.
The Master asked, "And what about you, my son? Yangshan drew a circular symbol and wrote the character for "sun" within it.
He wiped it away with his foot, whereupon the Master laughed heartily.
The Southern Star and Northern Dipper suddenly shifted their positions; the four seas and nine provinces boiled like a cauldron.
King Prasenajit’s nose touched the heavens; Ruci Tathāgata’s feet trod upon the earth. (Baoning Yong)
Holding up the whisk and sealing it with white paper: who among those traveling a thousand li knows of a true friend? Travelers, do not let the road be your enemy;
the four seas and five lakes lie within the realm of the King’s transformation.
(Bieping Yin) Once, a monk asked Master Guishan: "From the sages of antiquity down to the present day, what is the meaning of the Master's intent?"
The Master asked, "What is this thing right before your eyes? He replied, "Is it not simply this very thing? The Master said, "Which one?
He replied, "The one that just now responded to you. The Master said, "You intend to go for which one? Do not cause trouble."
Jiangshan Qin said: "The question was too precarious; the answer was too leisurely. Both failed to reach a resolution.
Because a monk asked Muzhou Daoyuan, "What is the Way? the Master said, "A mindless state is the Way. The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "It is better that you understand this very 'not understanding. The monk asked, "What is this 'not understanding'? The Master said, "Just..."

"It is you; it is not anyone else. He spoke again: "People of the present age simply take that which is directly realized but not intellectually understood as being precisely your mind and precisely your Buddha.
If you seek a single bit of knowledge or understanding from the outside and take that to be the Way of Chan, there is no connection whatsoever;
this is called 'carrying manure in,' not 'carrying manure out. It defiles the field of your mind."
"Because the Way is not the Way.
Yuehuan Qian said, "If it were entirely like this from Baizhang Huaihai, there would be no use for it all one's life. Listen!
This monk is impertinent. He struck his staff once and said, "To let him off is unacceptable."
"Delivering charcoal in the snow is enough to bring joy; adding salt to the sauce is even better.
Often one follows along with words and turns them over, yet remains like a frog’s stride rolling through the mud.
(Dong-sou Ying) When Guishan was instructing the assembly, saying, "Each of you, present what you have realized," at that time there was the Venerable Zhihe.
He came forward and paid his respects. The Master said, "At this very moment, when you are neither thinking of good nor thinking of evil, return to me, Reverend Zhi, your original face.
Zhi said, "At this very moment, it is where I lay down my body and life."
The Master said, "Do you not fall into emptiness? He replied, "If I were to see any emptiness into which I could fall, how could it ever be the place where I surrender my body and life?
The Master said, "When you have reached this point, why do you not ask? He replied, "When I have reached this point, [I do not ask]."
He also did not see any Upādhyāya to consult. The Master said, "Your merit is thin; you cannot support my school. Hanhui Qian said:
"If one does not open the Dragon Gate, how can one know the transformation of the three surges?
If one is not lost in the belly of the fish, how can one rest in the divinity of the Eight Arrays? When Muzhou met this monk on the road, he could not avoid being torn to pieces.
Why is this? Where the level marshes end, there are green mountains; the traveler lies even beyond those green mountains. Again, he recites:
"Casually casting my line at the official ferry, I have long sought an old friend beyond the willows. Having finished our talk, I withdraw the line as evening falls;
you are in Eastern Lu, while I am in Western Qin."
Guishan asked Yangshan, "Regarding the incident of Baizhang’s second visit to Mazu where he held up his whisk—what was the intent of these two venerable masters?
Yangshan replied, "This was the manifestation of the function of great capacity.
The Master [Guishan] asked, "Mazu produced eighty-four spiritual friends; how many attained great capacity, and how many attained great function? Yangshan replied, "Baizhang."
Dadu attained the Great Function; Huangbo attained the Great Utility. All others were merely teachers who preached and exhorted. The Master said: "It is so, it is so.

When the family prospers, filial sons are born; when a state achieves hegemony, it possesses strategic ministers. As for the fist striking the mouth—before one has reached that state, there will be no descendants."
Longmen Yuan records: Miaoshan asked Yangshan, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From the fields. The Master said, "How many people are there in the fields?
Yangshan thrust his spade into the ground and stood with his hands folded behind his back. The Master said, "There are many people on South Mountain mowing thatch. Yangshan pulled [the spade] out.
The spade then departed.
Xuansha Bei said, "Had I seen it, I would have kicked the spade over. Jingqing Huifu, when asked by a monk, "What was the meaning of Yangshan’s planting of the spade?
replied, "A dog carrying an imperial edict; the feudal lords clear the way. Xuansha [kicked]...
"What is the meaning of 'turning over the mind'? Qing said, "The boat cannot be saved; break the scoop. "What is the meaning of Nanshan mowing the thatch?
Qing said, "Li Jing, the Third Elder, has long served in the ranks of battle. Cui峰 Xian said:
"The various quarters all claim that the story of planting the spade is extraordinary, which is much like following the heterodox and pursuing the evil. According to my own view, as for Yangshan..."
Upon being questioned by Guishan, Yangshan was so utterly at a loss that he was as if bound by ropes of his own making, falling ten points short of death.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Yangshan only managed to grasp one peg. Do you all have another way of understanding this?
Jingshan Guangzhao said, "The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom. The common people use it daily yet do not know it. Therefore, the ruler...
"Your Way is rare indeed. Tian Ning Qi said: "Fortunately, there was no trouble;
otherwise, that old fellow Miaoxi would have recited a single mantra until heaven spun to the left and earth turned to the right. Tiantong Wu said:
"At that time, Yangshan should have waited for him to ask how many people were in the field before leaving. This would not only have cut off Muzhou’s entanglement, but also—"
He taught him that he could not find the tip of his own nose. Yufan Yu said:
"Xuedou says that when Yangshan was questioned by Guishan, he was so utterly at a loss that he was left with nothing but to bind himself with no rope—ten parts dead. Do you know Yangshan?
'Strolling casually along a path beneath the flowers, startled is the oriole in the treetop. Zifuku Kō said: "The *zhijiu* bird comes to nest; an empty hole brings the wind."
All of these arise through having something upon which to rely. If this is so, the ocean of meaning is boundless and the dark mechanism is formless;
even if Linji and Deshan were there with their staffs and shouts, they would have no use for them. Tell me, where does the point of benefit or harm lie? Have you not heard it said:
"On South Mountain there are many people cutting thatch"?
The Way is exhausted; when the father and son of Mt. Gui planted their spades together, they still carried the traces of war.
To this day, a single well shines like a mirror; occasionally, there are ripples even without a breeze.
(Huanglong Zhen) In old age, I feel my passions grow as I think of my descendants; now I am ashamed that the family lineage has been established. You must remember the Southern Mountain.
Verse: Carving our bones and etching our flesh, we together repay his kindness.
(Tiantong Jue) The golden whip strikes the dragon’s lair; it spits mist and grasps clouds as it emerges from the sea gate. The vast ocean is sucked dry and sent upward into the heavens;
only thunder and lightning remain, filling the mountains and rivers. (Foxin Cai)
The bandits’ fires meet just at the fifth watch; the manifest loot need not be contested. In the darkness, all is divided among them;
when dawn breaks, each goes their own way.
(Wuzhun Shanfan) Day after day he comes three or five times; sometimes he is joyful, sometimes he is angry. Change your head and face—do not doubt.
Adorned with it, one was originally a man beneath the pointed eaves of his cap.
(Xutang Yu) Half the slope is wind and rain, half the slope is sunshine. The fisherman’s song drifts through the autumn wilds, its melody pure.
How many pleasure boats float upon the stream? How few recognize the sentiment within the song? (Haizhou Ci)
Yangshan once asked Guishan, "What is the meaning of the [Buddha’s] coming from the West? The Master said, "A magnificent lantern.
Yangshan said, "Is it not this very thing? The Master said, "What is this very thing? Yangshan said, "A magnificent lantern.
The Master said, "As expected, you do not understand."
Presented face-to-face, it is bestowed upon him; this clear meaning has no east or west.
With strength in his wrists as heavy as a thousand *qun*, who would say his whole body is mud and water? (Xueyan Qin).
When Shishuang Qingzhu was at Baizhang, the head monk Sima Tuotuo asked him about the "wild fox" story: "How do you understand it? The Master—
He shook the door panels with his hand three times. The head of the monastery said, "You are too crude. The Master replied, "The Buddha-dharma is not a matter such as this.
Cause and effect proceed together—who knows them? Vast and boundless, the four seas have many diverging paths; lifting one's head, one forces forth the newborn."
The Moon. Following the example of Master Zhang, he painted on her azure brows.
(Buddha-mind Talent) When spring arrives, the hundred flowers bloom; where is that rosy countenance? Piteous are the colors within the garden, yet they do not enter the mirror.
(Longmen Yuan): Once while traveling through the mountains, Guishan sat upon a large flat rock. Yangshan stood in attendance. Suddenly, a crow dropped a red persimmon before him.
Yangshan picked it up and presented it to the Master. The Master asked, "Where did you get this? Yangshan replied:
"This is what is moved by the Master’s virtue," [said] Yaoshan. "The Master divided half with Yangshan, saying: 'My son, you must not be without your share.
