Xuansha Bei said: "Mount Gui was pinned down by Mount Yang for one sitting; even until now he cannot rise."—Tiantong Wu.
It is said: Xuansha only knew that Miaoshan was pinned down; he did not know that Yangshan had his throat choked by half a persimmon from Miaoshan, so that to this day he cannot even breathe.

A crow dropped a persimmon before the Master; he asked, "What brings you here?"—the matter was perfectly clear. Each took half, as sweet as honey. If one does not understand this now, when will it ever be?
(Fenyang Zhao) The lineage of Muzhou and Yangshan is manifest throughout ancient and modern times;
the meaning of father and son meeting is most profound. When the fruit ripens and its fragrance wafts, the crow takes it in its beak.
[The words] arrive. Squeezing from here and pulling from there, they seem to cross at the chest. To understand the ultimate point of these two people:
when the mid-autumn moon sets, it reflects in the heart of the pond.
(Dongshan Cong). Miaoshan asked Yangshan, "Ji-zi, speak quickly; do not enter the realm of darkness. Yangshan said, "I believe..."
“Nor do I establish [anything],” he said. The Master asked, “Do you establish it because you have faith, or do you fail to establish it because you lack faith?
Nanquan said, “It is simply I myself; whom else could I possibly believe in? The Master said, “If that is so, you are a śrāvaka of fixed nature. Nanquan said, “I do not even see a Buddha.”
A single cry of a cold wild goose flies southward; chrysanthemums bloom by the eastern fence, bearing the morning frost. The traveler in a foreign land longs for his native home;
the west wind whistles, how desolate and chilling! (Tieji Xin) On one occasion, Yangshan asked Muzhou:
"If hundreds of thousands of myriad objects should all come at once, what would you do? The Master said: "Green."
"It is not yellow. Long is not short. All phenomena abide in their own respective positions; it is no concern of mine. Yang then paid his respects.
Yue Xin Bao remarked separately, "The Master has skillfully explained blue, yellow, long, and short."
While sitting, Guishan pointed to his feet and said to Yangshan, "Throughout the twelve periods of the day, you have been supported and carried by these;
you must not fail them. Yangshan replied, "In the past, at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Garden, they spoke only of this.
The Master said, "Not yet—say more. Yangshan said, "When it is cold, providing them with socks is not considered going too far."
Luan Yuan said: "Although Yangshan did not fail him, he nonetheless had not yet understood the meaning of Muzhou’s intent.
Were it today, I would give him thirty blows of the staff and drive him out."
Guishan addressed the assembly: "A high-minded traveler must stride boldly amidst sounds and forms; only by sitting and reclining amidst sounds and forms does one truly attain it.
At that time, Shushan Ren, who had newly arrived, stepped forward and asked, "What is the phrase that does not fall into sounds and forms?
The Master held up his whisk. Shushan said, "This is a phrase that falls into sounds and forms. The Master lowered the whisk.
The Master returned to the abbot’s quarters. Because his realization was not yet in accord with that of Xushan, he took his leave of Xiangyan.
Xiangyan said, "Why do you not stay for a while? Xushan replied, "I have no affinity with the Master. Xiangyan asked, "What is it about our karmic conditions that does not accord?
Try citing it for me. Xushan cited their previous conversation. Xiangyan said, "I have a saying. Xushan said, "Please tell me it. Xiangyan said, "When words are uttered, they are not..."
[The Master] said, "Sound! Form! Before it, there is no object. Shu remarked, "It turns out there was someone here all along.
He then entrusted Yan with the words, "In the future, when you have a place to stay, I shall come to see you," and then departed.
That evening, the Master asked Yan, "Is that short *jñānika* who asked about sound and form still here? Yan replied, "He has already left. The Master said, "I told you so."
"What was it? Yan said, "I once spoke with him. The Master said, "Try to recount it for me. Yan said, "I told him:
'When words are uttered, they are not sounds; when forms appear, they are not objects. The Master asked, "What did he say? Yan said, "He deeply approved of me.
The Master laughed and said, "I thought this short fellow had some merit, but it turns out—"
"It is simply right here. This fellow, in the future, even if he has a dwelling place where there is no firewood to burn near the mountains and no water to drink near the rivers—Tiantong Huihua said:
"In this world today, seek out one who speaks words that are not sounds and whose presence precedes forms without being an object."
It is like digging through the earth in search of the sky; how much more so when one must also understand the words of Master Guishan!

Nevertheless, one must strictly avoid "piercing the tortoise shell" or "beating the roof tiles. Longxiang Xin said: "Among the assembly, everyone debates and says that Guishan employed his supreme fangs and claws.
It is a pity that Shushan lost one of his eyes. What they do not realize is that it was actually Guishan who lost [his eye]."
One eye was, however, seen through by Shushan. When Zhongfeng speaks thus, do you all accept it?
Baoning Miao said: "The Master’s words for the sake of others do not issue in vain.
Yet, since Shushan could not cut off his own tongue, how could Ying’an avoid following the heterodox and pursuing evil? O monks, here in my place, I let loose one..."
The tracks. Fallen into a heap of sounds and forms, they block off the vital thoroughfare, leaving them open to censure from all quarters.
While Yaoshan was sitting, Yangshan asked him: "After the Master passes away, if someone asks about the Dharma-way of the late teacher, what shall I say?"
"How do you respond? The Master said, "One bowl of congee, one bowl of rice. Yangshan said, "If someone ahead of you does not agree, what then?
The Master said, "A master monk. Yangshan then prostrated. The Master said, "Do not misquote it when meeting people."

The *Huihai Yiyu* states: "From antiquity to the present, how many people have offered words such as 'severe yet without majesty' or 'reverent yet without ritual form,' or have simply gripped their staffs crosswise or raised their fists?
If it were merely like this, how could one know the place where father and son reach mutual accord?
Today, I, this mountain monk, also wish for everyone to know it together," and he then recited a verse:
Do not distinguish between self and other; self and other are no different. A weary fish rests in a shallow pool; a sick bird perches upon the reeds.
Hesitating and unable to advance, with mud on one's shoes, how can one obtain the single scroll of a Master’s book?
Guishan asked Yangshan, "Throughout the entire day we have been discussing with you; what kind of matter has been accomplished?
Yangshan drew a line in the air. The Master said, "If it were not for me, you would surely have been deluded by him."

The *Yulangu Xu* says: "Everyone claims that in the lineage of Miu and Yang, father was compassionate and son was filial; yet upon careful examination, it turns out they were ultimately like family members wielding spears against one another.
For instance, when Miu-shan said, 'Had it not been for me, he would have surely been deluded by his own son,' what was the meaning of this?
Upon the river in a small boat, the wind and waves are perilous; the decrepit old fisherman is simply a master of his craft."
All day long they deliberate on the words of the ancient Buddhas; at that moment, a single stroke became a grievance.
To this day, Miaoshan still remains—do not say that the lineage has been severed of its descendants.
(Foyin Yuan) Though father and son are close, they compete in deliberation; how could one believe there are swords and spears within their chests? At that moment, a single stroke was drawn.
Severed. The entanglements throughout the realm shall never arise again.
(Jianweng Jing) One day, when Guishan saw a wild fire, he asked Dawu, "Do you see the fire? Dawu said, "I see it.
The Master said, "From where does it arise? Dawu replied, "Apart from walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, please ask me another question."
Even the heavenly fires reach the infinite horizon. At the very moment they arise, one must still discern the master.

When the film over the pupils in the eyes has vanished, the entire world before one is free from empty flowers. Old Daowu is truly worthy of praise: the monk who drew water returns to the temple beneath the forest;
the man waiting for a boat stands on the sand at the river’s edge. (Fodeng Xun)
Where does this raging wildfire arise? Purple smoke and crimson flames instantly consume one.
One must know that within sitting, reclining, and walking, seeing it is no different from using it intimately.
(Shixi Yue) Once, when Ziguo came to visit Miaoshan, the Master pointed at the moon to show him. Ziguo brushed it away with his hand three times. The Master—
He said: "It is not that you do not see; it is simply that your way of seeing is too coarse. Hanxiu Qian said:
"At Mount Huai, the cold light extends for ten thousand miles; at Ziguo, the bright moon is a single orb.

Since both ways of seeing are equally luminous, why did he further say it was 'too coarse'? A jade stone meets its true worth only when it encounters a skilled craftsman; a poem attains its full resonance only after repeated recitation.
He saw the artisan and again composed a verse:
"A solitary light shines afar, reflecting across the vast sky; A single path of pure radiance remains the same for all eternity. It is simply that Chang’e’s heart has not yet turned her gaze here;
She still laments that she herself dwells within the Palace of Broad Cold."
While sitting in the Dharma hall, Guishan saw Yangshan passing before the abbot’s quarters. The Master said, "If you were my late teacher Baizhang, you would have to receive a severe beating.
Yangshan asked, "What about today's matter? The Master replied, "You might as well shut your two pieces of skin [your mouth].
Yangshan said, "This kindness is difficult to repay. The Master said, "It is not that you lack talent; it is simply that I, this old monk, am advanced in years."
Mai said, "Today I have personally seen the venerable elder Baizhang. The Master asked, "In what phrase did you see the former master?
Mai replied, "I do not say that I saw him; it is simply that there is no distinction. The Master said, "From beginning to end, you are a true adept."
Lin’gao Yu said: "The simultaneous pecking and hatching; the arrowheads meeting point-blank—Master and Son of Miu and Yang may indeed be called true connoisseurs.
Nevertheless, for a monk with clear eyes, he knows where the blow lands even before it is raised."
A monk once asked Guishan, "What is the white ox on the open ground? The Master said, "Chit, chit.
The monk asked, "What does it eat? The Master said, "Eat, eat.
The white ox was born as a white ox; when it manifests, it is majestic and imposing—do not seek it elsewhere. It is I who cannot conceal its reality.
Verse: Directly beneath, it is clearly a single head.
(Bānyuá Róu) The white ox is out in the open field, beyond all barriers. Wherever it lies, it is at ease; wherever it rests, it is leisurely.
It grazes on water and grass as it pleases, fully satisfied with their sweetness. Pure ghee emerges, nourishing the fertile fields. (Fényáng Zhāo)
A jade-horned ox with frost-white hair stands barefoot upon the earth; its traces are manifest throughout the human realm and the heavens.

It is not like the one on the Snowy Peaks who roars constantly, nor like the one at Mount Mui who was gathered in daily. Coldly inhaling the moonlight, it leaves no shadow; it wanders freely through lands as numerous as motes of dust.
Suddenly, a cowherd ascends the summit of Mount Sumeru and points out which end of heaven and earth is the "other. (Dongshan Cong)
In the open field, the white ox raises the question; responding to conditions with "chit-chit," his teeth are cold.
Not knowing what it is that he drinks and eats, he chews and chews until the vast ocean is dried up.
(Tiantong Ju) *Zongjian Fali*, Volume 39.
*Zongjian fali*, Scroll Forty,
Compiled by Jiyun Tang;
Fifth Generation Below Dajian.
Chan Master Huiji Zhitong of Yangshan in Yuanzhou (a successor of Guishan Lingyou): A foreign monk arrived from the air. The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
He replied, "From India. The Master asked, "When did you leave there? He replied, "This morning. The Master said, "Why so late?
He replied, "I was traveling through the mountains and enjoying the scenery. The Master said, "Your playful display of supernatural powers is indeed not lacking."

"Upādhyāya, you must return the Buddha-Dharma to this old monk before it will be possible. [The master] said, "I came specifically to the Eastern Land to pay homage to Mañjuśrī, yet I have instead encountered a 'lesser Śākyamuni.
He then produced a Sanskrit manuscript on *bīja-patra* leaves and gave it to the master; having paid his respects, he ascended into the air and departed.
From this time on, he was called "Little Śākyamuni.
Donglin Zong said, "Both the Great and the Little Yangshan have been doused over the head with two ladles of foul water by him.
At that time, under Mount Jiyun, there was naturally a direct command; why was it not put into practice? Tell me, what is it?"
The Correct Command: "Tut! Huanglong Xin said, "Big or small, Yangshan was thoroughly hoodwinked by this monk.
He went so far as to produce a *pātra* with Sanskrit script and apply a layer of paste over it. Now there is yet another extraordinary monk who arrives from the air at the gate of Yunyan;
he calls him out to come and wash his feet. Letan Zhen said, "It is a pity that Yangshan let this fellow slip away. At that time..."

If it were Bao Feng, I would have seized him immediately. I would have ordered the *vina* to strike the bell before the Sangha Hall to assemble the community, and having charged him with a formal statement of offense, I would have driven him out. After all, the Buddha-Dharma does not cater to human sentiment.

Since he calls himself an Arhat—one whose taints are exhausted and whose holy life is established—why does he not return home to sit in peace? Instead, he merely continues to travel among mountains and enjoy the waters. —Zhaojue Qin
It is said: "To drive away the oxen of the plowmen and to snatch the food from hungry people—this is what those who serve as the 'fangs and claws' of the Buddhas above do.
Yet when they reached the presence of Yangshan, they were left staring with eyes wide open and mouths agape.
Why? A crane may have its nine-fold gao, yet it cannot spread its wings; a horse may lack the thousand-li stride, yet it vainly pursues the wind. Daopei Tai said: "Yangshan merely..."
To know how to advance forward to pursue the deer, yet not realize that one’s own body has fallen into a snare—this monk has coincidentally formed a meaningful phrase;
he truly possesses the breath of a *chan* practitioner. If anyone can understand this, I grant you permission to pull the tiger’s whiskers backward.
Far removed from the roads of Western India, he travels a long way; he personally heads toward China to play with the ocean tides.
If you wish for a pure breeze to arise beyond the gates, I shall pull him back and give him four more strokes of the rattan cane.

(Nanhua Bing) A blink of the eye in the West; a raising of the eyebrows in this land. This land is the West, and the West is this land. With the outgoing breath, a thousand layers and a hundred folds; with the incoming breath...
A single thought-moment lasts ten thousand years. Zen, Zen. The Jambū tree stands on the southern edge of the sea.
(Nantang Jing) When Yangshan was residing at Dongping, Guishan sent him a letter along with a mirror. The Master ascended the hall, held it up, and said:
"Tell me, is this Guishan’s mirror or Dongping’s mirror? If you say it is Dongping’s mirror, yet it was Guishan who sent it."
"Come here. If you say this is the mirror of Mount Gui, it is currently in the hands of Dongping. If you can speak [the truth], I shall keep it;
if you cannot, I will smash it. The assembly remained silent. The Master then smashed it.
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said: "I ask you, Master, to explain the principle further. He suddenly snatched [the staff] away and broke it.
Holding it up clearly, he illuminated right and wrong; no one among the assembly could open their lips. It is like selling goods with no one to buy them;
in the end, they must return to their original owner. (Dongshan Ceng)
Guishan’s Ancient Mirror, held up by Yangshan: The sun rises in the east, the moon sets in the west. In its sudden fall, no one knows who has picked it up;
The autumn wind rustles, the grasses grow lush and green. (Baoning Yong) An eighty-year-old matron learns to paint her brows;
Her graceful air rivals that of her youth. Were it not for the bright mirror, how could she distinguish the beautiful from the plain?
Ugly! Everyone says it takes no effort for rouge and powder to apply. (Shangfang Yi) I say:
when brought forth to pose this question, how is it that the entire assembly is left utterly bewildered?
Had it not been for being struck once and shattered into a hundred pieces, one would surely have become a resentful ugly wife in the human world. (Xichan Jing)

Yangshan once dreamed that he went to Maitreya’s Inner Court and occupied the second seat. A venerable elder struck the gavel and said, "Today, the one on the second seat shall preach the Dharma. The Master rose, struck the gavel, and said, "The Mahāyāna Dharma transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations. Listen closely, listen closely! The assembly then all dispersed. Upon waking, he related this to Guishan, who said: [Guishan said: "That was not the true second seat; it was the true first seat. Yangshan asked, "What is the true second seat? Guishan replied, "If you wish to know the true second seat, you must go to the place where there is no 'one' and no 'two. Yangshan said, "I understand. Guishan said, "How do you understand it? Yangshan said, "It is like a person with a single eye looking at the moon. Guishan said, "You have only attained half of it. Yangshan said, "I understand. Guishan said, "How do you understand it? Yangshan said, "It is like a person with two eyes looking at the moon. Guishan said, "Now you have attained it entirely. Later, when Yangshan was about to pass away, he told his disciples, "When I was at Mount Gui, I attained half of it; now I have attained the other half. He then composed a verse: "The Great Way is originally complete; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will wander for ten thousand miles. The myriad phenomena are originally empty; Why seek them elsewhere? If you seek them elsewhere, You will fall into the pit of views. The Buddha-nature is originally pure; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be far from the source. The mind-ground is originally level; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be lost in the weeds of discrimination. The Way is originally without words; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be caught in the net of speech. The Dharma is originally without form; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be bound by the traces of images. The patriarchs are originally without teachers; Why seek them elsewhere? If you seek them elsewhere, You will be trapped in the cage of lineage. The Buddhas are originally without names; Why seek them elsewhere? If you seek them elsewhere, You will be confined in the prison of titles. The self is originally without a master; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be led astray by the path of others. The Way is originally without a gate; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be blocked by the barriers of thought. The mind is originally without a dwelling; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be lost in the labyrinth of delusion. The realm is originally without a center; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be adrift in the sea of birth and death. The body is originally without a soul; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be entangled in the web of existence. The world is originally without a foundation; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be submerged in the mud of samsara. The truth is originally without a sign; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be obscured by the clouds of ignorance. The essence is originally without a trace; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be swept away by the current of phenomena. The source is originally without a beginning; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be caught in the cycle of time. The ultimate is originally without an end; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be lost in the maze of views. The absolute is originally without a duality; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be divided by the distinctions of subject and object. The fundamental is originally without a root; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be uprooted by the winds of passion. The nature is originally without a mark; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be stained by the dust of attachment. The reality is originally without a boundary; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be confined within the limits of space. The liberation is originally without a door; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be locked in the prison of form. The awakening is originally without a teacher; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be deceived by the shadows of illusion. The transmission is originally without a lineage; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be severed from the root of the Dharma. The practice is originally without a method; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be distracted by the paths of expedience. The fruit is originally without attainment; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be separated from the state of Buddhahood. The Way is originally without a name; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be lost in the mists of convention. The truth is originally without a word; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be silenced by the barriers of language. The mind is originally without a thought; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be bound by the fetters of consciousness. The body is originally without a form; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be constrained by the limitations of matter. The world is originally without a location; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be tossed about in the whirlpool of existence. The self is originally without a substance; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be hollowed out by the void of emptiness. The Dharma is originally without a teaching; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be bewildered by the proliferation of doctrines. The patriarchs are originally without a person; Why seek them elsewhere? If you seek them elsewhere, You will be separated from the heart of the ancestors. The Buddhas are originally without a land; Why seek them elsewhere? If you seek them elsewhere, You will be alienated from the realm of the Tathagatas. The Way is originally without a path; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be wandering in the wilderness of views. The mind is originally without a ground; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be sinking in the mire of delusion. The realm is originally without a field; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be lost in the expanse of the ten directions. The essence is originally without a core; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be scattered by the winds of change. The source is originally without a beginning; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be cut off from the flow of the Dharma. The ultimate is originally without an end; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be trapped in the cycle of birth and death. The absolute is originally without a duality; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be split by the opposition of subject and object. The fundamental is originally without a root; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be severed from the source of the Way. The nature is originally without a mark; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be obscured by the veil of ignorance. The reality is originally without a boundary; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be confined within the limits of the mundane. The liberation is originally without a door; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be locked in the cage of the senses. The awakening is originally without a teacher; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be deprived of the light of wisdom. The transmission is originally without a lineage; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be estranged from the succession of the patriarchs. The practice is originally without a method; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be distracted by the methods of the provisional. The fruit is originally without attainment; Why seek it elsewhere? If you seek it elsewhere, You will be removed from the
[The Master] said, "You have already ascended to the rank of a sage.
The teacher then bowed. Wuishan Xiu said: "To explain the meaning according to the text is not without merit.

Suppose, however, there were a true adept in Maitreya’s assembly who, as soon as [the teacher] spoke the words 'Mahāyāna Dharma,' cut him off before the sound had even faded, saying: 'Close those two flaps of skin! This is not so.
I merely wish to cut off Yangshan’s drowsy talk, lest it cause later generations to speak dreams within dreams.
Langye Huijue said: "Tell me, do the holy assembly approve of Yangshan or not? If they approve, they betray Yangshan;
if they do not approve, they fall flat on their faces on level ground. Today, I shall not spare my eyebrows and will speak for all of you."
"Broken! The Mahāyāna Dharma transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations.

If you were to present this to those in other quarters, they would understand it in such a way that they would enter hell like a shooting arrow. After Master Tiantong Jue finished citing the koan, he said:
"The Jade Maiden vaguely stirs her mechanism at night; The silken threads emerge one by one from the loom’s navel. The azure waters and blue sky fall into total function; Snow and moon..."
A single color of cold clarity confuses all; O virtuous practitioners of Zen, even when your full effort fails, you remain deluded by that single color.

How can you realize it so as to attain correspondence? Temporarily hanging up the soiled robe, one says, "This is the Buddha"; but when one puts on precious and regal garments again, who is it that is called by that name?
Dongchan Guan said: "When the Venerable One struck the gavel and the assembly dispersed, it left people with lingering doubts.
It was only after they were splashed with the second ladle of 'evil water' that they finally came to their senses—but even then, it was late.

Take, for instance, the Mahāyāna Dharma, which transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations; the Way has already been fully explained. Do you all recognize Yangshan? Baoren Xiu.
Daguang said: "If Daopei had understood how to turn the light back upon itself, Wansong would have had no place to set his feet.
Is there anyone who is perfectly clear while dreaming and wide awake while intoxicated? Tiantong Wu said: "How great was Yangshan, yet he thrust his head into a glue pot!
When the Venerable One struck the gavel and said, 'Now it is the second seat who shall preach the Dharma,' Yangshan’s forehead was shattered to pieces."
At that time, he shook his sleeves and departed, leaving the entire assembly of venerable monks in doubt. Yet he continued to strike the wooden gavel;
he did not stop for even a single pebble.

In a dream, he donned his cassock and visited the elders, with the forest of patriarchs sitting solemnly to his right. When it came to practicing benevolence, he did not yield the mallet to anyone else.
Roaring the fearless lion’s roar of the Dharma, his mind is as calm as the sea, his courage as vast as the heavens. The shark sheds tears; the oyster releases its pearl from its bowels.
Who knows that these delirious words leak my secret mechanism? The long-browed one must surely laugh at the family’s disgrace.
Transcending the four propositions and severing the hundred negations—the illness of Master Mazu and his son need no longer be treated. (Tiantong Jue)
Discussing emptiness within a dream is truly marvelous. How can one transcend the hundred negations and the four propositions?
At that time, he was able to wield the command of Magadha; why must one strike the bell once more within the hall?
(Benjue I) Once, when Master Yangshan was asked by Layman Pang, "I have long heard of Mount Yang; why do you hide [yourself] upon my arrival? The Master held up his staff.
He raised his whisk. The Duke said, "Exactly so. The Master asked, "Is it facing up or facing down?
The Duke then struck a pillar and said, "Even though there is no one here, I must have the pillar bear witness. The Master threw down his whisk and said, "If you go to other places..."
"Feel free to bring this up.
Yinzheng Cen said, "The great and small Mount Yang were completely flustered by Master Pang's single squeeze; their hands were busy and their feet were in disarray.
But as for the layman giving the pillar a blow—how is that? When the whale swallows the ocean water to its depths, the coral is revealed."
Branches.
Two eights make sixteen; counting from the beginning, they are still insufficient. He gathers them and scatters them in disorder before the steps;
the ground is covered everywhere with round patches of green moss. (Baizhang Yuanwen)
A thief stealing a thief’s goods is truly extraordinary; a master hand lets his companion know. Today, they are caught together with the stolen loot;
gaining an advantage is actually losing one. (Baoning Yong) He fears not the overturning of valleys or the collapsing of mountains;
the Yellow Emperor’s precious mirror stands upon a high pedestal. Having gained the ox, he returns the horse; both are non-existent.
[He] loses. Leave it to the current of time to guess wildly.
(Qingshan Xiu) Once, when Yangshan returned to Weishan to pay his respects, Weishan asked:

"Since you call yourself a good spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), how do you distinguish between those who come from all quarters—those who know [the Way] and those who do not, those with a teacher and those without, and those who are scholars of the doctrine?"
"Mysterious Learning (Xuanxue). You, my son, try to explain it to me. The Master said, "Huaiji has a point of verification.
Whenever I see a monk come, I simply hold up my whisk and ask him, 'Do you hear what the various quarters are saying about this, or not? He also said, 'Let us set this aside for a moment.'"
"What do the venerable elders of all quarters think? Guishan sighed and said, "This one is a true fang-toothed tiger from the ancestral school.
Zizhunduan said, "Guishan creates trouble where there is none; out of pity for a three-year-old child, Yangshan accepts the void and receives the guest."
Echoes! To dally with ugliness and act out absurdities, neither can escape being ridiculed by others.

Had there been a man among the assembly at that time who, upon seeing him raise his whisk, had stepped forward to snatch it away and departed with a great shout, even though Master Guishan and his son possessed fangs and claws throughout their entire bodies, they would have had to retreat three thousand miles.
Yangshan went to Yantou. Yantou raised his whisk; the Master spread out his sitting cloth. Yantou picked up the whisk and threw it behind him;
the Master draped the sitting cloth over his shoulder and departed. Yantou said, "I do not approve of your letting go;
I only approve of your taking it up."
One up, one out; one release, one gathering. Yangshan’s handling of danger was even more extreme than Yantou’s.
It was not merely rowing the boat back with the wind; he nearly capsized the fishing vessel.
(Duanqiao Lun) While Yangshan was sitting, a monk asked, "Does the Master know how to read and write? The Master replied, "I manage to do so. The monk then...
The monk circled to the right once and asked, "What word is this? The Master drew a cross on the ground.
The monk then circled to the left once and asked, "What word is this? The Master changed the cross into a *swastika* (卍).
The monk drew a circle and held his hands out as if an asura were supporting the sun and moon, asking, "What word is this? The Master then—
He drew a circle surrounding a *svastika*. The monk then assumed the posture of Lohitya. The Master said, "So it is, so it is.
This is that which all Buddhas protect and keep in mind. You are thus, and I am also thus. Guard and maintain it well for yourself.
The monk prostrated and departed, soaring into the air.
Baoneng Xiu said: "Yangshan’s 'ten characters'—he has annotated them and he has explained them through.
Why do you still require all this 'gruel-and-rice' flavor from later on? At that time, when asked whether the Master could read, why not have said, 'I have always been illiterate'?
Look again: how would he have handled it? Xiaoyan Bao said: "Big and small Yangshan are nothing but mud and water."
[The Master] divided [the staff]. The attendant waited as the Master assumed the posture of Lohitya; he struck him across the spine and said, "You wild fox spirit!
Why do you act like this? Have you not heard it said: 'What is true is difficult to conceal; what is false does not flourish'?"

The void of the Dao’s circuit has not yet been filled; the hand that seals emptiness has not yet taken form. It wondrously operates the celestial wheel and the terrestrial axis, densely weaving the martial warp and the civil woof.
Releasing and gathering, it stands alone yet moves in tandem. When the mechanism is triggered at the dark pivot, the azure sky flashes with lightning;
when the eyes merge with the purple light, stars are seen in broad daylight. (Tiantong Jue)
Seated, he cuts off heaven and earth; his true eye is clear. He overturns the ravines and topples the mountains without ever being startled.
From of old, upon the vast and open thoroughfare, who would fear a traveler knocking at the door at night? (Lian’an asked.
One day, while Yangshan was sitting, a monk came to pay his respects and stood with his hands folded toward the east.
He looked at the Master with his eyes. When the Master lowered his left foot, the monk moved to the west side and stood there with palms joined.
When the Master lowered his right foot, the monk moved toward the center and stood there with palms joined. When the Master drew both feet in and sat down, the monk prostrated.
The Master said, "Since I have resided here, I have never struck a single person. He then took up his staff and struck him; the monk soared into the air and departed.
Falin’s verse says: "What a fine blow! A pity it was too late.
In this thatched hut, rustling, I dwell among the white clouds. An old friend comes from afar with sincere intent; Greeting and formalities have all been set aside.
Unable to avoid the cup of tea, I offer it to you for now. (Nansou Mao)
Prince Jin blew the *sheng* flute, harmonizing with the cry of the phoenix; Flower buds danced beyond the clouds in light robes. Together they performed melodies throughout all quarters;
The radiant light of the jade tree filled the purple and blue heavens.
(Juehai Qing) Looking left, one sees a thief; looking right, one sees a demon. To look directly at them is not so different from this. I do not know where my staff has gone.
Falling into a pit. Every night in the Western Heavens, one looks across the Autumn River.
(Sanzong Zang) Yangshan asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "The South. The Master picked up his staff and said, "Do they speak of this there?
The monk said, "They do not. The Master said, "If they do not speak of this, do they speak of that? The monk said, "No."
He did not speak. The Master said, "Go to the hall. The monk then departed. The Master called out, "Virtuous One!
The monk responded. The Master said, "Come closer. The monk stepped forward. The Master then struck him.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "If Yangshan had not spoken these subsequent words, how could one have recognized the man?
Once, when an Indian monk came to visit him, the Master drew the shape of a half-moon on the ground.
The monk stepped forward, added a circle to it, and then rubbed it away with his foot. The Master extended both hands; the monk brushed his sleeves and departed.
Jizang happened to encounter a guest with pierced ears; once he had used half a month [with him], it was as if he were with you.
When the monk added another half-month, Jizang departed abruptly, yet said, "I have personally met a little Śākyamuni.
(Benjue I). Yangshan asked a monk, "Where are you from? He replied, "Youzhou. The Master said, "Do you still think of that place?"

"No," he replied. "I am constantly thinking. The Master said, "That which is able to think is the mind; that which is thought about is the object. Within those [objects], there are towers, pavilions, groves, gardens, and crowds of people and horses.
When you turn back to reflect upon the source of this thinking, are there still all these various things present? He replied, "At this point, I do not see anything at all.
The Master said, "Your understanding still remains within the stage of intellectual belief (xin-wei). Only when one reaches the stage of realization (ren-wei) is it truly attained.
[The monk] said, "I have not yet reached that position. The Master asked, "Aside from this, is there another meaning or not?
The Master said, "To say there is another or there is not is already inadequate. [The monk] asked, "Having arrived at this point, what is it?
The Master said, "Based on your understanding, you have only attained one mystery. You may take your seat and put on your robe; look for yourself hereafter."
Without exterior yet all-encompassing; unobstructed yet profound. Gateways and walls rise tier upon tier; locks and bolts multiply layer after layer.
Wine is ever flowing so that guests lie prostrate; food is so abundant that farmers collapse from fullness. Suddenly bursting forth into the void, the wind strikes against the wondrous garuḍa;
trampling over the azure seas, the thunder ushers in the roaming dragons. (Tiantong Ju)
For both ordinary beings and sages, there is no divergent path at all. Reflecting back upon that which is being reflected upon, how few people truly know it?
If the spring breeze does not reach the Peach Blossom Spring, the leaves will still fall and the flowers will still bloom in their own time.

(Cishou Shen) In the fifth month, during the great rains, the abbot’s quarters were constructed; in the sixth month, amidst the great heat, the Master was invited. Whether walking or sitting, sweat drenched [the body].
Body. Regretting that in my youth I failed to emulate the masters.
(Juelang Sheng) Within his eyes, mountains and rivers are not seen to exist; he wears his robe backward, revealing both elbows.
Seeking fragrance by the banks of the Si River on a spring day, he sings aloud beneath the blossoms, tipsy from village wine. (Qiaozhi Yu)
Yangshan asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Youzhou. The Master said, "I was just looking for news from Youzhou.
What is the price of rice there? The monk said, "I happened to pass over its market bridge and kicked down its beams."
Baoning Yong said, "I grant you thirty blows. Baoshang Bai said, "Big or small, Yangshan leaves his head behind while his tail does not follow.
This monk has already leveled the eighty-li city of Youzhou; even with his staff, Baoshang was still unwilling to let him pass."
Yangshan asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Mount Lu. The Master said, "Have you ever been to Wulao Peak?
He replied, "I have not been there. The Master said, "Then you, Reverend, have never traveled the mountains."
Yunmen Wenyan said, "These words are all due to compassion; they are talk that descends into the weeds.

Guishan Xiu said, "People nowadays all say, 'It is because of compassion that there is talk that descends into the weeds. They know only how to grasp at the moon, but do not realize the depth of the water.
Had Yunmen been careful with his lips at that time, I wonder how later generations would have discussed it?"
Huanglong Xin said: "Yunmen and Yangshan had only the intention to accept the jade; they lacked the resolve to cede the city.
Little did they know that this monk had already comprehended it all at once. Today, Huanglong is merely practicing the 'medical treatment for a dead horse'."
He then took up his whisk and passed it to the monk; as the monk reached out to receive it, Yunmen struck him.

Guishan Zhe said, "Yangshan may truly be said to have outshone those before him and surpassed those after him. Although Yunmen grasps the essential principles and hammers all monks under heaven, [he still falls short]."
But alas, it is like stirring up waves where there is no wind. Do you all recognize this monk? He came directly from Mount Lu.
Huanglong Zhen said, "Yangshan has already lost his nostrils; Yunmen further adds a footnote—what remedy is there for that?
I, however, am not so. "Where have you recently come from? "Mount Lu. "Have you ever been to the Five Elders Peak? "No."
[When asked if he had been there, Yunmen] replied, "I did go. I simply told them to cook fragrant rice in a separate steamer to offer as an offering to this man. Tiantong Jue said:
"Although Yunmen recognized the inner depths of Yangshan, alas, he only knew one thing and not the other.
But tell me, what was Yangshan’s intention? His boundless elegance is too weary to be peddled; it is better to avoid being pointed out by others as a fine lad."
Sir, you emerge from the weeds and enter the weeds; who can fathom your search? Layer upon layer of white clouds; the red sun shines brightly. Looking to the left, there is no flaw;
glancing to the right, one is already old. Do you not see? Cold Mountain Man went out too early. Returning after ten years, he could not forget.
When coming, there is the Way. (Cui-feng Xian) How does emerging from the weeds compare to entering the weeds? Entering the weeds with one’s whole body is an act of compassion.
Yangshan extends his hand and follows him away; even until now, he remains at the crossroads. (Ben-jue Yi)
If you wish to recognize Mount Lu’s Five Elders Peak, in what place therein would they not meet? A tongue without bone turns according to others;
an iron kettle for boiling tea is not the same as a small cauldron.
(Cishou Shen) Once, when an official came to Yangshan, the Master asked, "What office do you hold? He replied, "I am a *tui-guan* (Assistant Official). The Master held up [his finger].
Fuzi said, “Can you still push this one away? Lian’an asked, “Dangerous.
Zifu Yu said, “Everyone says that the official only knows how to push other officials aside while forgetting himself;
little do they realize that Yangshan had already tested this worldly fellow to the very marrow of his bones. Samaitrui said:
"Officer, why do you not say, 'The Master has exerted himself in his activities'? Observe again what kind of artifice Yangshan employs.
At the end of summer, Yangshan went to inquire after Master Muzhou. Muzhou asked, "While you were down below, what were you occupied with?
The Master replied, "Huiji was down below tilling a patch of fallow land and sowing a basketful of millet. Muzhou said, "You..."
“This summer has not been spent in vain,” [Nanquan] said. The Master (Guishan) then asked, “I wonder, what were your duties during this summer retreat, Reverend?
Guishan replied, “One meal at midday; one sleep after nightfall. Nanquan said, “Reverend, this summer has also not been spent in vain.
Having finished speaking, he stuck out his tongue. Guishan said, “Ji, why do you thus harm your own life?”
Taisuī Zhe said, "Yangshan’s eye illuminates the four quarters of the world, yet when he arrives before Dayuan, he ends up falling flat on his face on pure ground.
Dayuan may be called one who has fulfilled the conditions for raising a son, yet he cannot avoid being a subject of gossip for later generations.
Donglin Yan said, "Nowadays, monks gather in groups of hundreds and thousands, passing through winter and summer and wasting their years in vain; this is a profound insult [to the Dharma]."
The ancients said: "Donglin was not examining the former sages; Yangshan was showing off his brilliance too much; his sticking out his tongue only achieved half [the point].
Tiantong Jue said: "When young, one should exert effort; when old, one should let the mind rest. This entire summer has not been spent in vain.
Why did Yangshan stick out his tongue after he finished speaking? If you can examine this and see through it, misfortune will not enter those who are cautious."
The Gate of the House. *Tianbao Shu* says: "On Mount Gui, poison was administered amidst the wine cups and dishes;
on Mount Yang, spears and halberds were brandished in the midst of laughter and talk. Do you understand? Two humpbacked camels meet face-to-face;
nowadays there are no upright people in the world. *Jingshan Xiu* says: "Clearing a patch of fallow land to plant a basketful of millet; the guest comes forth."
The prisoner’s mouth: one meal at midday and one sleep after nightfall. The rabbit does not leave its burrow.

As soon as Master Muzhou and his disciple Yangshan see each other, they immediately begin to beat the drum of speech. Even if they were to speak until the heavens rain down four flowers and the earth shakes in six ways.
How can silence be better than this?
This elder is honored both for his years and his virtue. His home is rich with poetry and books beyond compare. He eats his fill and sleeps soundly, having no concerns;
yet he comes to rattle the bowl and play with his grandchildren. (Bieshan Zhi)
I have cleared a patch of fallow land and sown a basketful of millet. Turning my head for a leisurely glance, the mountains are blue and the waters are green again.
All day long I take but one meal; after nightfall I stay but one night. When weariness comes, I stretch out my legs and sleep—this is enough for a thousand and ten thousand needs.
Coming together in the eighth and ninth months, by the hedge, the yellow chrysanthemums spread in profusion.
(Xichan Xu) Having opened a patch of field, one has sown a basketful of millet.

When Bian He presented his jade three times to the King of Chu, had he not met a man who recognized its true value, he would still be weeping at Jingmen to this day. One meal at noon, one gruel in the morning; [this is] the severance.
The strings must be mended with phoenix glue; for "Yangchun" and "Bai-xue," there are those who understand their true sound. The mountains remain ever green and the waters ever lush.

(Xin’an Chou) When the wine has run dry and guests wish to depart, do not continue to play the *konghou*. The young lord has already whipped his horse away, leaving me alone to harbor the sorrows of this night.
As Yangshan was walking along carrying his staff, a monk asked, "What is that in the Master's hand?
The Master held it behind his back and said, "Do you see it? The monk was speechless.
Tiantong Wu, on behalf of the monk, clapped his hands and said, "Today I have recognized the Master.
Yangshan entered the monks' hall together with Attendant Lu. The official asked, "Are all these many monks merely those who eat gruel and rice, or are they monks who practice Zen?
The Master replied, "They are neither those who eat gruel and rice..."
"Monk," [the official] said. "Nor is he a Zen monk. [The official] asked, "What is he doing here? The Master replied, "Your Honor should ask him yourself.
Falinyin spoke on his behalf, saying, "He has been thoroughly exposed."
The one who comes to inquire has a reputation that is not at all praiseworthy; how many dragon-elephants (āryas) are there in the Cloud Hall?
Within the sandalwood forest, there is never any impurity; how could the ordinary folk of hasty conduct easily fathom it?
(Benjue I) Yangshan pointed to a snow lion and said to the assembly: "Is there anyone who can pass through this form?"
Yunmen Wenyan said, "At that time, had it been appropriate, I would have pushed him over right then and there. Cui峰 Xian said, "Yunmen only knew how to push him over;
he did not know how to lift him up. Langye Huijue said, "I ask you all now: how far apart are 'pushing over' and 'lifting up'?
Then, picking up his staff, he said, 'It presses past the eyebrows and the nostrils,' and let out a great laugh."
He then threw it down. Jingci Chang said: "To push it over is wrong; to prop it up is also wrong.
Is there anyone who can pass through this color? Nantang Yu said: "Yunmen pushed it over; Cui峰 propped it up.
Even if one were to pass through this color, they would still not be a golden-maned lion. Baolin Xiu said: "One instance of pushing it over, one..."
Then he helped him up. In other schools and different sects, this would not be permitted.

However, in the tradition of the Dongshan school, one must know that there is a time for right and inverted, and when one rises, it is precisely the moment of falling. Only after that can rising and falling be simultaneous, such that neither rising nor falling is established.
[The Master said: "Go buy yourself some straw sandals and travel on foot for thirty more years. Gu Nanmen remarked: "Three old men!"
Although Han increased his wisdom through these events, he had not yet stepped upon the pivotal bolt of the higher realm.
What is the pivotal bolt of the higher realm? "After the sun has risen, it is all a scene of embarrassment. Xuedou Zheng said: "This whole lot of fellows!"
In total, they are turned by the Snow Lion. Falinyin said: "Even now, this is not lacking.
One fall and one rise—this is the Snow Court Lion. He is cautious in avoiding transgression while cherishing benevolence; he is courageous in action while discerning righteousness."

Clear light shines upon the eyes, as if one were lost in one’s own home; with clarity and brightness, one turns the body, yet falls back into the station. For the patch-robed monk, there is nothing to rely upon.
Dying together, living together—what "that" and what "this"? The warm news breaks through the plum blossoms, and spring arrives at the cold branches;
the cool breeze sheds the leaves, and autumn clarifies the turbid waters. (Tiantong Jué)
Last year in Lingnan, the plum blossoms were like snow; this year in Jibei, the snow is like plum blossoms. Amidst the flurry of them, people vie for the sight within their warm chambers;
who would pity the celestial fragrance as it settles upon the green moss?
(Yiran Ji) When a monk asked Yangshan, "Does the Dharma-body understand how to preach the Dharma? the Master said, "I cannot say it."
Another person said he could explain it. [The Master] asked, "Where is the person who can explain it? The Master then pushed out his pillow.
When Guishan heard this, he said, "Jizi is using the business of the sword's edge."
Jingshan Hongdao said: "Miaoyan Shan shunned his son’s ugliness; Yangshan pushing out the pillow was already a slip.
To further attach a name to it and call it 'the matter on the edge of a sword' misleads those who merely mimic the words.
They then proceed in this manner, receiving echoes in place of substance and passing them along. Although Miaoxi borrows water to offer flowers, the principle remains as it is."
There is no crookedness or severance. Right now, let there not be anyone who comes forward with partiality or refusal. I wish to question you:
when one pushes out a pillow, does that truly serve as the Dharma-body preaching the Dharma? Tiantong Huo said:

"If this were a matter of the blade's edge, how could Jizang have ever known how to use it? Or if someone asks whether the Dharma-body understands how to preach the Dharma, one should likewise respond...
The Way cannot be spoken; where is the person who can speak it? It is simply said: "Three lifetimes, sixty kalpas. Lingyin Yue said:
"Miaoyan displayed his brilliance for a while, but he did not realize he had lost one eye.
When someone asked Yefu, "Does the Dharma-body understand how to preach the Dharma? he immediately kicked him in the chest, knocking him down, and told him to get up.
"Come and become a man who is free and easy! Tianning Qi said: "This monk asked about the Dharma-body preaching the Dharma;
he did not even realize he had missed it. Yangshan pushing out the pillow—when had he ever seen such a thing before?

Great as Master Moshan was, he took a mistake for a match and treated it as a matter on the edge of a sword. He tied it all together into a bundle, weighed it on a scale, and it came out at eight [units]."
Two and a half *jin* differ not at all in weight. Had he, at that moment, as soon as the question "Does the Dharma-body preach the Dharma?
was asked, simply taken long strides back to his quarters, would he not have been a transcendent master, sparing the patch-robed monks of the world from further criticism?
Yangshan Qian said: "The Dharma-body preaching the Dharma has already been transmitted within the very question itself. He then pushed out his pillow.

My son, you need only believe, accept, and put it into practice. Although this old man of Mt. Huai has divided the text into sections and chapters, as for the main text itself, I dare say I do not know where its true meaning lies.
The Dharma-body preaches the Dharma; with the eyes of flesh one perceives objects. Great wisdom appears as folly; great eloquence appears as stammering.
Picking up a winnowing fan, he threshes elsewhere; pushing out a pillow, he reveals the sleeping bed. On the edge of a sword, he emits a ray of light.
(By Yue Tang Chang) Hiding his body from the eyes, no one sees him; a drowsy fellow comes, and he looses an arrow. From this point on, the whole earth is filled with the blowing [of the wind].
Mao. Without touching it, one does not violate the division of the courtyard (Yunlin Lu). Yangshan asked Official Lu:

"I have heard that you, Official, attained enlightenment through the study of the sutras; is this so? He replied: "It is so. Because I was studying the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, I attained a point of entry by realizing how to enter nirvāṇa without severing the afflictions. The Master [said]: *Note:

Zhushi held up his whisk and said, "As for this very thing, how does one enter? Lü said, "Even the word 'enter' is not necessary.
The Master said, "The word 'enter' is not for you, Langzhong. Lü then rose and departed.
Qingliang Qin said, "Tell me, for what kind of person is this character 'enter' intended? He also said, "Langzhong, do not be troubled.
Cui峰 Xian, when the whisk was raised, spoke differently, saying, "The whisk has now reached my hands."
Furthermore, in a later conversation he said: "I took you for a mere worldly man.
Now that life and death and nirvana are as easily turned over as one’s hand, and the true eye has opened wide, both are seen to be non-existent; you walk alone upon the Great Path."
In every speck of dust there is right concentration; in every fragment they drift chaotically—the plum blossoms upon the crags. In every branch they dance freely—the willows by the stream.
(Shimen Cong) Once, when Officer Liu questioned Yangshan, asking, "May I hear the principle of realizing the mind?
the Master said, "If you wish to realize the mind, there is no mind to be realized. This absence of a mind to be realized is called true realization."
The mouth faces the nostrils, leaving no space between; the eyes cover the beard, possessing an ancient style. The painted bones bear eighteen flowers;
casually cast out, they fill the basin with red. (Huikang’s Verse) Yangshan was once asked by Guishan:
"In the forty fascicles of the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, how many fascicles were spoken by the Buddha, and how many were not?"
"This is the teaching of Māra. The Master said, "It is all the teaching of Māra. Guishan withdrew. The Master followed after him and said, "I was clumsy in my response just now;
the Master is still like grass on the peak of a piled-up rock. Guishan said, "I grant you that your eyesight is correct."
Jiang Tianquan said: "When Guishan said, 'I will stop,' did he approve him or not? When you were granted the words, 'Your eyes are correct,' did he approve him or not?
You bright-eyed monks must not swallow the dates whole."
While Yangshan was sweeping the floor, Guishan asked, "Dust cannot be swept away; emptiness does not arise of itself. What is this 'dust that cannot be swept away'?
Yangshan swept the ground once with his broom. Guishan asked, "What is this 'emptiness that does not arise of itself'?
Yangshan pointed at himself and then pointed at Guishan. Guishan said, "Dust cannot be swept away; emptiness..."
"It does not arise from itself. "Apart from these two paths, how would you do it? The Master then swept the ground once with his broom, and then pointed to himself and then to Moshan.
The wondrous function is fully raised; the fundamental essence is manifest. The reputation of father and son fills the Great Tang.
With empty hands, he grasps a pair of brooms, yet from the midst of the midnight, he emits a beam of light.
(Hongding Jiao) Once, when Wei Zhou requested a gāthā from Muzhou at Mount Gui, Muzhou said: "Presented face-to-face, it is still..."
"This is a dull-witted fellow! How much more so when it is expressed through paper and ink! Wei then approached the Master and requested instruction.
The Master drew a circle on a piece of paper and wrote: "To know it through thinking falls into the second head; to know it without thinking falls into the third head."
The traces of majestic sound are fundamentally without mark; silent and vast within the misty rain.
How many times have I gazed upon it amidst the mountain colors—half submerged in the blue sea, half suspended in the void.
(Hongding Jiao) Once, when Yangshan was asked by Guishan, "If someone were to suddenly question you, how would you respond? the Master said:

Jing霜 said, "It still carries consciousness within it. He further asked Caoshan, "Regarding the dragon’s roar from within a withered tree," Caoshan replied, "The life-force (bloodline) is not severed.
He asked, "Regarding the eyes within a skull," Caoshan replied, "They have not dried up. Jing asked, "I wonder, is there anyone who can hear it?
Caoshan said, "Throughout the entire world, there is not a single person who does not hear it. Jing asked, "I wonder about the dragon..."
"Dragon's Roar—what chapter or verse is this? Shanshan replied, "I do not know what chapter or verse it is either; those who hear it all perish.
Xuansha Yanben commented on the first statement, saying, "The dragon roars from a withered tree.
Shending Yuanxin said, "Shishuang has been consistently beating people down, making his living within the realm of reality. He then cited Caoshan’s words and concluded, "Understand it in this way."
"Excellent. Zhaojue Qin said: "When mindfulness does not differ and the mind does not deviate, one can leap over the five ranks of sovereign and minister and transcend the three poisons of ignorance.
Thus, one may cause flowers to bloom upon withered trees and blow the pitch-pipe within cold crags. Look at those three old masters:
one penetrated the leakage of words, one penetrated the leakage of sentiment, and one penetrated the leakage of views."

Leakage. If you can investigate and examine this thoroughly, you may walk alone upon the profound barrier. Do you understand this clearly? Do not linger by the cold crags where strange grasses turn green;
sitting amidst white clouds, the pivot of the mechanism will remain unrefined. Jingshan Gao said: "Can you all discern this?
If you cannot discern it, Miaoxi will not begrudge his eyebrows and shall explain it for you. Xiangyan penetrated it.

The leakage of speech: one is killed by being bound by language. Shishuang penetrated the leakage of emotion; he was killed by being driven by emotional consciousness. Caoshan penetrated the leakage of views;
he was killed by being deluded by seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing. This has been clearly stated; let those with eyes discern it.
Tianning Qisong said: "The old man Miaoxi sits with his whole body within the three kinds of leakage, yet he is not constrained by those three leakages.
Even so, if you wish to see the Ancient One, he is truly far away.
Why is this? He has no business corrupting the sons and daughters of others. Tiantong Juexian said: "The King resides within the gate; the minister does not."
[The Master] went out the door. Baoneng Xiu said: "Tiantong is able to express immeasurable Dharma-gates as a single phrase;
sometimes a single-character Dharma-gate could not be fully recorded even with the ink of the ocean's waters. Do you recognize Tiantong’s place of settled ease?
A solitary crane often keeps company with the water; auspicious clouds, having no concerns, never leave the mountain."

"The dragon’s roar from a withered tree is the true seeing of the Way; the skull, though devoid of consciousness, has its eyes first opened. When joy and consciousness are exhausted, the news is exhausted;
how can one distinguish the clear within the turbid? (Cao Shan Ji). Xiangyan’s "One-Legged Verse" says:
"The child pecks and the mother pries open [the egg]; the child awakens and the mother’s shell is gone. When both mother and child have perished, it should..."
The conditions are not mistaken. When the companions sing in harmony, Miaoxin calls it "the single-legged.
Yunmen Xinyun says, "The child pecks and the mother strikes"—let us grant this for now. But when "the child awakens and the mother's eggshell breaks," where do you seek it?
When both mother and child have perished, the conditions respond without error. Since both mother and child have perished, which one is it that responds without error? Tell me!
By what principle does this work?
A single-legged Xiangyan locks away ten thousand layers. Layer upon layer of brocade is sealed by white clouds.
Within this, mother and child have no life at all; even the mechanism of "pecking and hatching" is deaf. (Yunmen Xian)
Layer upon layer, one by one they are shattered. On level fields and shallow grasses, encounters are easy to find.
Suddenly emerging from the crest of a thousand peaks, the earth is silent and people are rare—there is nothing to meet. Only Xuansha understands this meaning;
he suffers from blindness, muteness, and deafness all at once. (Chaozong Ren)
The seven apertures were bored open and Chaos died; the nine suns were shot down and the universe turned black.

A lotus fiber toppled the five Mount Sumerus; a needle’s eye released wings that strike the void. Who fully understands this mechanism of the simultaneous peck and hatch? Alone-legged Xiangyan understood how to take a double step.
Having kicked through ten thousand layers of golden locks, he stands as before in his boots upon the water. (Tianli Zhen)
At the third watch, when the night is deep, form and shadow forget each other upon the pillow and quilt.
Having gained Vzhou’s single-legged bed, where can Zhongqi find a true connoisseur?

Chan Master Hongyin of Mount Jing in Hangzhou (a successor of Guishan Lingyou) was asked by a monk: "What is it like when one suddenly passes away like ashes?
The Master said: "That is still the achievement of ordinary people. The monk asked: "After that achievement, what is it like? The Master said: "The farmer tills the field but does not sow.
The monk asked: "Ultimately, what is it like? The Master said: "The grain ripens, but it is not brought down from the threshing floor."
Tiantong Hua said: "The incense has grown cold in the Phoenix Hall; the snow-nest is frigid at night. A bright moon fills half the window, and a harmonious atmosphere mingles in the air.
At such a moment as this, tell me: does Guizong have any share of meeting with Jingshan?
Setting aside for a moment whether they see each other or not—does this monk who asks such a question possess the eye of wisdom? If he does not, then listen to Yunmen."
Wearing a seamless robe from Tibet; birds nest upon branches that sprout no buds.
Beating the drum and playing the lute, we meet as two kindred spirits. For nine years no one recognized him; how many times did he cross the shifting sands?
(Baoning Miao) A spiritual sprout is not a thing that prospers a family; auspicious grass, on the contrary, becomes a sign of a nation’s ruin.
How much better it is for an old farmer to forget the Emperor’s labor, strolling idly with a drumming belly, rejoicing in the remainder of his life. (Pin Jixiang)
Hongxian was asked by a monk, "What is long? The Master said, "Even the Ten Sages cannot measure it. The monk asked, "What is short?
The Master said, "It would not even fill the eye of a gnat. The monk did not accept this and departed.
He reported this to Shishuang, who said, "It is simply because you are too close to the literal reality. The monk then asked Shishuang, "What is long? Shishuang said, "Not..."
A twist and turn. [The student] asked, "What is short? Zhaozhou said, "In the game of Shuanglu, there is no calling out the colors.
"Pushing aside the weeds and observing the wind to ask about the traveler's journey is but a weary trek to listen to empty sounds.
Look at the colors on the board for both paths; walk freely even atop a hundred-foot pole. (Hongding Jiao)
Chan Master Shenyi of Dingshan in Chuzhou (a successor of Guishan Lingyou) was once questioned by Bishu: "Without falling into numbers and quantities, please, Master, speak.
The Master held up his prayer beads and said, "Are these 'falling' or 'not falling'? Bishu replied, "The round beads have three holes; this is something people of the time know.
He then requested, "Please, Master, complete the previous dialogue. The Master struck him. Bishu brushed out his sleeves and departed. The Master said, "Three..."
Ten years later, he went away beating his breast and weeping aloud. After Shouzhu settled at the monastery, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"Thirty years ago, I was thoroughly deceived by Dingshan; it was no small matter."
Cui Feng Xian said: "Dingshan’s 'using'—it is indeed used, yet how perilous it is!
Pishu’s 'knowing'—he knows, but he simply lacks the eye that discerns the Dharma. Gunan Men said: "Everyone says that Pishu was deceived by Dingshan;
little do they realize that Dingshan himself was led by Pishu until his very sinews and bones were moved. Can you all discern this? If you cannot discern it..."
