A thousand-year-old cypress pierces the blue sky;
With each return of spring, its verdant beauty seems to flourish. It does not obstruct the passage of those who come and go.
The Way: Clouds turn and rain falls; green courtyards shrouded in mist.
(Suan Ding) Chan Master Fanduan of Yanqing in Xiangzhou (a successor of Guishan Lingyou). A monk asked:
"When an earthworm is cut in two and both ends move, in which end does the Buddha-nature reside? The Master spread out both hands.
Dongshan Jia gave a different response: "Right now, as you ask this question, on which side does it reside?
Xiaoyan Bao gave a different response: "Simply call out, 'Venerable! If the monk responds, then say, 'It truly resides on which side? Huiyun Cheng gave a different response:
He struck him immediately upon hearing his voice.
Zhaozhou Mihuang (the successor of Guishan Lingyou) asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Yaoshan. The Master said, "How has the old fellow at Yaoshan been lately?
The monk said, "He is very much like a single piece of solid rock. The Master said, "Is he so serious?
The monk said, "There is no place for you to pick him up. The Master said, "It is not only Yaoshan; Mihuang is also like this."
"Mo. The monk stepped forward, looked around, and stood there. The Master said, "Look, look! Even a stubborn rock moves! The monk then departed.
Cui-feng Xian said, "The 'giving' and 'taking away' were as observable as rice and flour; yet, alas, he died without being mourned.
Zhao-jue Qin said, "Cui-feng’s subtlety was as fine as rice powder; his coldness was like ice and frost. Nevertheless, one sees only..."
"The point of a needle is sharp. According to my view from Mount Jiangshan, this is simply Mihe catching a rat and smashing an oil jar.
Tiantong Hua said: "Is this monk not one who possesses the eye [of insight]? It is unbearable that Yaoshan’s single piece of stubborn rock is being peddled everywhere.
Had it not been for Mihe’s profound discernment of the subtle nuances, he would have nearly suffered confusion."
Rice mixed with a stubborn lump of stone; how many travelers do not recognize it? Yet when a monk sees it for the first time, he cannot help but take south for north.
(Wuqian Zhe) When Mihe was returning to his hometown, an old master asked him:
"The moon has set, the well-rope is broken; people of the time call it a snake. Not yet—what about you?
Shen asked, "When the Seven Masters see the Buddha, what do they call him? The Master said, "If there were a perception of a Buddha, that would be the same as being a sentient being.
Su said, "A peach pit from a thousand years ago."
Fayan, at the place where there was a vision of the Buddha, said separately, "What season is this? Fadeng asked separately, "The one you call it is not.
Jieyan Xiu said, "I have not seen him for a long time; as expected, having grown old, he has become a spirit.
When Mihe went out the door, he learned a 'palm-slap' Chan. Why does he not unfold [his wings] now?"
He came to use [the rice].
He mixed it with the rice and sent a monk to ask Yangshan, "Do people of the present day still rely on awakening? Yangshan said, "Awakening is not non-existent;
however, how can one avoid falling into the 'second place'? The Master deeply approved of this.
Touzi said, "Qingyun. Yangshan spoke thus; did he thereby avoid falling into the trap himself?
If he avoided it, there is still one person who is utterly unwilling to accept it. If he did not avoid it, he likewise falls into the second category.
Although Mihe may have accepted him, does he himself still possess a way to emerge? If you can examine this through and through, [you will see] the two men...
It is like ice melting and a fortress crumbling. Otherwise, do not act with such haste. Letan Qing said: "Mihe’s deployment of the gate was deeply affirmed;
Yangshan’s entry into principle and profound discourse—yet even the 'first head' has not yet been realized.

Tiantong Hua said: "Mihe wielded the hammer and tongs of his own fundamental share; Yangshan displayed the business of the sword's edge. These two elders, regarding the proclamation of the teaching..."
Within this gate, one may truly be called honorable. Yet, in the school of the patch-robed monks, all are men who deserve a beating.
One asks a person at the peak of the Verdant Valley: though he points to the mountain’s end, one has not yet found rest.
Although this spares one from having to issue a further decree, how does it compare to the spiritual sprout that never violates the spring? (Touzi Qing)
At the edge of the second head, awakening shatters delusion. One must quickly let go and cast aside the fishing trap. Effort that remains unexhausted becomes a redundant appendage;

the wise find it difficult to know, for they only realize it after biting their own heels. The old hare weeps with autumn dew upon the ice-disk; the crow shivers in the evening wind beneath the jade tree.
Brought forth, Daoyang discerns the true from the false; without a single blemish, the white jade disc is precious. (Tiantong Jué)
A thousand awakened ones say there is no sorrow; yet those who claim to believe have already encountered the "second head. After the cold food festival, mountain flowers lie in silence;
the evening sun sets in the west while the waters flow east. (Longmen Yuan) One should regret not being able to return to one’s native mountains;
having returned, one still finds oneself at odds with old friends. Turning back to reflect, one finds leisure and ease throughout the four seas.
One day, [Mihuo] asked: "Where is there a border that is not within the imperial domain? (Fruo Ruozhen) said:
"When rice is mixed with [the grain], it is because of the monk. He asked: "Since ancient times, have the sages of the highest caliber attained the true principle?
The Master said: "They have. He asked: "As for this true principle, how is it attained? The Master said: "At that time, Huo Guang sold a counterfeit silver city."
[The monk] asked, "Who composed this treaty document for the Shanyu? He replied, "I, so-and-so, am simply at a loss for words.
The Master said, "This is like teaching a person on level ground to act as a guarantor."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Mihu was a great spiritual friend. Jingshan Daowu raised the case of the letter of agreement and asked:
"Who wrote this? He said: "If Jingshan had been that monk at the time, he would have uttered a turning word to block the old fellow's mouth.
But tell me, what word would he have uttered? After a long silence, he said: 'If it were easy to obtain, one would simply act.'"
Looking on with indifference:
The fishing line in hand is wound and then let out. A small boat ripples across Lake Dongting. Suddenly, a violent wave rises up from the void;
gathering it back in, there is not a single skill left behind. (Yuepo Ming)
Chan Master Cihui of Jiufeng in Fuzhou (a successor of Guishan Lingyou) once followed Guishan as he ascended the hall.

Guishan said, "All of you have attained the great capacity, but you have not yet attained the great function. The Master then withdrew and left. Guishan called out to him, but the Master did not look back.
Guishan remarked, "This man is fit to be a vessel for the Dharma."
Baofu Zhan said: "It is vaguely like a melody; one loses what follows while forgetting what precedes. Gaoshan Ji said:
"When Jiufeng withdrew his body and departed, was that a great function or not? Guishan said, "This son is fit to be a vessel for the Dharma"—was this a reward for him or a punishment?
Cen Master Yuankang (a successor of Guishan Lingyou) once went to visit Shilou. As soon as Shilou saw him, he drew up his feet and sat down.
The Master said, "How perfectly complete your dignified demeanor is! Shilou asked, "What did you just see?
The Master replied, "I have been pointlessly led astray by someone. Shilou said, "It must be like this before it can be called true seeing. The Master said, "How bitter!"
"How many people have been deceived? Lou then rose from his seat. The Master said, "You have seen it, but you have not moved.
Lou said, "I have exerted all my strength, yet I cannot bring myself to emerge from samādhi. The Master clapped his hands three times.
Nanquan Yuan said: "No one in the world can judge the right or wrong of these two fellows. If you could judge them, you would be a fellow student of theirs.
Their mastery of bestowing and withholding is total; though they travel the same road, they do not dwell in the same marketplace. A lion cub does not eat the leftovers of a vulture."
Objects—how can one willingly drool out of petty attachment? (Master Faju of Zhufeng;
Chan Master Fayu of Sanjiaoshan in Qizhou, successor of Guishan Lingyou). During a period of chaos, a military commander entered the mountain and, brandishing a blade, asked:
"Monk, what treasures do you possess? The Master replied: "The treasures of a monk are not appropriate for you."
[The monk] asked, "What treasure is this? The Master let out a thunderous shout. The ringleader did not realize it and struck him with his blade.
Longtang Zhu said: "That ringleader was much like a blind Persian; how could he have discerned a true treasure? Sanjiao was not skilled at deep concealment;
having not yet met another, he hastily opened his fist. Both were at fault. At that time, [the Master] should have waited for him to say—"
"What kind of treasures are these? he asked. [The Master] replied, "I have a fine broken-legged cauldron, a 'pin' (品) shaped hearth, a bottomless alms bowl, and a noseless straw sandal.
If you find them useful, take them as you please; let him know the flavor of our monkhood.
One can never say whether he might set down his yakṣa heart and suddenly manifest the face of a bodhisattva."
The hermit-monk truly delivers the fierce man; with one shout, he clearly distinguishes the precious from the common. Do not say that the leader of the thieves is someone else;
the sharp blade held at the front is used with personal intimacy.
(By Tianmu Li) Chan Master Shuangfeng of Fuzhou (a successor of Guishan Lingyou): When Yangshan asked him, "What is your realization these days? the Master—
Yangshan said, "According to my own realization, there is not a single dharma that can be taken as an object of the mind. Yunyan said, "Your understanding still remains within the realm of objects.
Yangshan said, "I am simply like this; what about you, elder brother? Yunyan said, "Do you have no one who can know that there is not a single dharma that can be taken as an object of the mind?
When Guishan heard of this, he said, "In the future, Jizi will cause people to die of doubt."
The servant went away. Tiansheng Zhe said:
"The first arrow was still light; the second arrow was deep. Limitless commoners were submerged in the mud. Dongchan Yue said:
"To wield skillfully, one need not have a frost-bladed sword; to be able to play, why necessarily require jade strings?"
Jizang’s *Treatise on the Two Peaks* discusses views; it causes those who hear it to fall into ever-deepening doubt.
When meeting others, he is unwilling to speak even three words; how could he possibly cast away his entire heart?
(Benjue I) While Wang Jingchu, the Palace Attendant of Xiangzhou, was attending to official business, Master Mi arrived. The Attendant picked up his brush.
He showed it to him. Baizhang said, "Can you still discern emptiness? The official threw down his brush and entered his residence. Baizhang became suspicious.
The next day, he sent Drum Mountain’s master of offerings to enter and probe the official's intentions; Baizhang also followed him there, hiding behind a screen to eavesdrop.
When the master took his seat, he asked, "What words did Master Baizhang have yesterday?"
They did not see each other again. The Official said, "A lion bites a man; a hound chases a clod of earth. Upon hearing these words, Huimi understood his previous error.
He immediately came forward and laughed heartily, saying, "I understand! I understand! The Official said, "Try explaining it to me.
Huimi said, "Please, Attendant, demonstrate it. The Official held up a single chopstick. Huimi said, "This wild fox spirit! The Official— [laughed].
[The Master] said, "This fellow is thorough.
Wei-shan Zhe said, "Although Master Mi was like this, he only attained one peg. Chang-shi said, "This fellow is thorough.
[Zhe continued,] "It is very much like looking down from a tower and knocking down the tower. Da-mei, however, was not so; although Chang-shi was a layman...
In the Han dynasty, the brush held the power of life and death. Master Mi was a man of great learning in his region, yet he could not escape its confines.
At that time, you should have waited for him to set down his brush and simply said to him: "I have always harbored doubts about this fellow."
Yingshan Yin said: "The Attendant may truly be called one with iron eyes and copper pupils.
Not only did he cause Master Mi to harbor doubts, but he could also put all people under heaven to doubt. Nevertheless, at that time, he let him off too easily.
He should have waited for the 'wild fox spirit' to withdraw his body and depart; why? Because he wanted to make him doubt until he reached the very bottom."
The host of the guest has already had a path through; the tip of the brush is no mere judge of empty space. Once more the power of Heaven is wielded at the end of the chopsticks;
all the sages are made to fall before it. (Chijue Chong) The wheel of function moves with ease upon the pearl-board;
the wondrous point lies entirely at the tip of the brush. Held upright, it remains as it was, yet it is released.
Below. A divine blade, its precious edge cold as it leans against the heavens.
(Yanxi Wen) The Attendant [Wang] and Linji arrived at the Sangha Hall. The Attendant asked, "Do these monks in this hall read the sutras?
Linji said, "They do not read the sutras. The Attendant asked, "Do they practice meditation? Linji said, "They do not practice meditation. The Attendant said:
"You do not read the sutras, nor do you practice Chan; what exactly are you doing? Yangshan replied, "Ultimately, it is all intended to lead one to become a Buddha or a Patriarch.
Linji said, "Gold dust is indeed precious, yet when it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract. Linji continued, "I took you for a mere worldly man."
Touzi Tongbie said, "How can you, sir, value the ears while despising the eyes? Jingqing Daofu spoke on his behalf, saying, "Lately, we have been throwing bricks to draw out jade.
Weishan Xuanzhe said, "Attendant Wang may truly be called a gentleman of the Confucian gate and a master craftsman of the Chan gate.
Were it not for his brilliant and precise discernment, how could he have so clearly distinguished right from wrong? Baizhang Fenggan said:
Linji truly possesses only one eye. Yuan Tong, however, is not so; though gold dust is precious, when it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract.
I took you for a mere worldly man. "Great assembly, try to judge this! Thus said Jingshan Gao.
Linji’s spirit was like that of a king; wielding the Vajra King’s precious sword, he roamed freely throughout the land.
Whenever he casually encountered an official, they were reduced to ruins like crumbling walls or melting ice. Tianning Qi said: "Where has Linji’s 'Blow-off-the-Hair Sword' gone?
If it were brought forth, what would there be [to fear]? When the Attendant came out of the cave himself, there was no rival hand; he gained the upper hand over others."
This place is already spacious enough for others. Lin'an asked: "When these two elders meet, they are as clear as the bright sun and as vast as the great void.
As they push and shove one another, the local scenery of their original ground is fully revealed.
Were it not for such people, how could such words be spoken? Is there anyone here among this assembly of monks who recognizes them? Water does not wash water.
Gold does not trade for gold. With body horizontal, he faces the universe. Who is this kind of person?
A rare occurrence, both mundane and supramundane. To reveal it, one must rely on a person of transcendent capacity.
Using only the hands that mend the robes and season the soup, he turns the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata. (Jingshan Gao)
One step higher than the last; one stride wider than the last. Before those with clear eyes, it is still but a public proclamation. A phoenix does not settle on a wutong tree.
(Songyuan Yue) When the matter reaches the state of no-mind, one does not act with guile.
That crows are black and cranes are white still invites doubt; had it not been for personally seeing the Yellow-head [Bodhidharma].
Old man! How would you dare leak this secret to anyone? (Xutang Yufu) The Attendant Chang went to visit Muzhou.
One day, Muzhou asked, "Why have you come so late? The Attendant replied, "I was watching the horses play polo, so I came late.
Muzhou said, "Is it people playing polo, or horses playing polo? The Attendant said, "People playing polo. Muzhou said, "Then the people are exhausted."

The Master asked, "Is the pillar tired? The official said, "It is tired. The Master asked, "Is the horse tired? The official said, "It is tired. The Master asked, "Is the pillar tired? The official was at a loss.

Upon returning to his private residence, he suddenly attained realization in the middle of the night. The next day, he went to see the State Preceptor and said, "I have understood the matter from yesterday.
The Preceptor asked, "Is the pillar tired? The official said, "It is tired. The Preceptor then gave his approval.
Watching others on horseback playing with a ball, I did not realize that this morning I had entered the monastery late.
The snow has cleared from the official road and spring is at its finest; the river plum blossoms are intent upon inspiring a poem.
(Lan’an Shu, sixth generation under Dajian)
Chan Master Guangmu of Xitai on Mount Yang in Yuanzhou (a successor of Yangshan Ji): A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
The Master said, "You have no Buddha-nature."
Official horses have never been restricted from anywhere; they may gallop as they please along the southern roads and west of the streams.
For a hundred *li* along the mountains, postal stations are established everywhere, with light flowers carpeting the horses' hooves at every turn.
(Ping Jixiang) Chan Master Jingtong of Mount Huo in Jinzhou (a successor of Yangshan Ji): When the Master first visited Yangshan, Yangshan sat with his eyes closed. The Master...
Lifting up his right foot, he said, "It is so, it is so. The twenty-eight patriarchs of India were like this;
the six patriarchs of China were like this; the Master was like this; and Jingtong was like this.
Thereupon, Shangu raised [his staff] and struck him four times with the rattan. Because of this, he called himself "The Great Chan Practitioner of the Four Rattan Strips under Mount Jiyun."
The Buddha. Cui峰 Xian said: "Yangshan’s willow staff has not yet reached the point of breaking. Why did he only strike four times?
One must be a man who cuts through nails and severs iron before this can be achieved. Cuiyan Zhi said: "These four strikes of the willow staff must also not be treated as such."
"A meeting for rewards; one must not hold a meeting for punishments. How do you understand this now? Zhaojue Qin said:
"The union of teacher and disciple is like a mustard seed rolling into a needle's eye. For a time, they borrow a path to pass through, yet they cannot avoid mutually obstructing one another.
Why did Cui峰 say that although the staff had not yet reached the point of breaking, he struck only four times? What kind of juice are you seeking in a sesame cake?"
Furthermore, it is said: "One must be a man who can cut through nails and sever iron to succeed. This is very much like following the heterodox and pursuing evil.
Píngyáng Mǐn said: "Do you wish to know where these four cane strokes fall? One stroke hitting the twenty-eight patriarchs of India is just like this;
one stroke hitting the Sixth Patriarch of this land is just like this; one stroke..."
"Striking him with a single cane—so it was with the Master; striking such-and-such a person with a single cane—so it was with me.
Gentlemen, do you approve of this judgment of mine? If you do, not only will Yangshan be buried, but where would his great Chan-Buddha be?
If you do not approve, how can you swallow the whole枣 (jujube) at once? Here, too, one must truly..."
Only a man who can cut through iron and sever nails will attain it;
at the foot of Mount Jiyun, four rattan whips were used. How perilous it was—then one might have had one’s waist broken!
It is laughable that those who came later called themselves fierce generals; they knew only how to speak empty words of Huo Qubing. (Yingxuan Zun)
In the land of India and in China alike, all are sealed with certainty; there is not even a hair’s breadth of discrepancy.
Eyes askance and nose straight—this resounds throughout the world. A single mouthful of leftover soup will keep one from hunger forever.
(Baoning Yong) Beneath Mount Jiyun, four creeping vines; breaking through Tongguan, a single path opens. Like cranes, like clouds, heaven and earth...
Outside. Like dragons and phoenixes in the misty clouds.
(Yuantong Xian) When a robber encounters a formidable opponent at home, his loot is lost and he has no other recourse. A mountain cane whip that pierces to the bone forces him to submit;
yet it is turned back to become a flower pressed against his face. (Huan’ou Ti)
Jingtong arrived at Mount Huo and announced himself, saying, "I am a great Chan Buddha from under Jiyun Peak, known as 'The Four Twisted Vines of the World,' come to pay my respects.
Master Huo called for the *vina* (chant leader) to strike the bell. The Master strode away.
Cui Feng Xian said, "Although this fellow was able to change according to the occasion, alas, he has a head but no tail.
Zhao Jue Qin said, "This fellow carries the 'winter melon seal' of Yangshan about on his shoulders, flaunting it before others.
Had it not been for Huoshan, he would have nearly been defiled. Even so, it is a pity that the command was carried out only halfway. At that time, it should not have been used."
He called for the *karmadāna* (Vina), saying, "Seize him properly and give him four more strokes of the rattan cane! Let this fellow remain in doubt for thirty years.
Zhengguo Xing said, "These two fellows have thunderous sounds, yet not a single drop of rain."
There was a reason for lifting his foot on the spot; four strokes of the rattan were not enough as recompense. Again, he went beneath the gate of Mount Huo;
though his discernment of the occasion was sufficient, it lacked elegance (the grace of Kṣitigarbha).
Having endured the strokes of the rattan, he wanders at leisure; yet before reaching the secure barrier, he will not rest. Beating the drum and striking the bell—both are [the sound of liberation].
Command: To know the opportune moment and recognize shifting conditions—who can rival you?
(Yuantong Xian) At the sands of Zi Ling, the current rushes like a bowstring; he catches a yellow fish, a *shu-xiang-bian*.
Holding it up in the marketplace, he repeatedly asks for its price, yet no one values it at half a coin. (Fuxin Cai)
Jing Tong asked a practitioner, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master then performed a prostration.
The practitioner said, "Why does the Master bow to an ordinary person? The Master replied, "Do you not see that it says, 'Revere and honor your disciples'?"
Gold beaten into brass chopsticks; white jade carved into ivory combs. The black-lacquered Kunlun monkey has many skills;
he picked up a luminous pearl from the sea.
(Cishou Shen) Before the fragrant grass falls, one falls by oneself and rises by oneself. All in all, it is most senseless; it has deceived poor Old Lady Wang.
(From *Yuntao Zheng*) Zen Master Guangyong of Nanta on Mount Yangshan in Yuanzhou (a successor of Yangshan Huiji). When a monk asked, "What is the essential meaning of Caoxi?
the Master said, "A single lock enters the cold void."
Layered peaks and ridges pierce the cold sky; The pagoda is locked in deep clouds, its majesty inexhaustible. The sound of pines from a thousand ages arrives with melody;
The mountain stream for ten thousand years flows on without trace.
(Touzi Qing) Nantuo returned to visit Yangshan. Yangshan asked, "What have you come to do? The Master replied, "To pay my respects to the Abbot."
Mount said, "Did you see the Master? The Master replied, "I saw him. Mount asked, "How does the Master compare to a donkey?
The Master replied, "When I saw the Master, he did not even resemble a Buddha. Mount asked, "If he did not resemble a Buddha, what did he resemble?

The Master replied, "If there were anything to which he resembled, how would that differ from a donkey? Mount was greatly startled and said, "Both ordinary and sage are forgotten; all affective attachments have been exhausted."
"The body is exposed. I have tested people with this for twenty years, and none have reached a definitive resolution.
You must take responsibility for it. Baeryam Pu said: "Everyone says that father and son are like space merging with space, or water poured into water;
yet they claim that Yangshan lacked the 'spicy hand' to drive the plow and seize the food at the very end. From my perspective as a monk, however, it was actually Yangshan who possessed it."
This is malicious. Why? When one encounters a trap of brocade on the path, even a wise person finds it difficult to forget. As the *Jingde Chuandeng Lu* says:

"Yangshan was not right to be so greatly alarmed and treat this as a minor anomaly, sealing it for him head-on. At that time, had he waited for [the monk] to say, 'If there is something similar, how would it differ from a donkey?
he should have then let out a thunderous shout and sent him away. Had he done so, the Dharma-lineage of Muzhou and Yangshan would not have reached its present state."
While the Master was warming himself by the fire at the South Pagoda, a monk came to visit him. The Master said, "A single word exhausts the entirety of the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
The monk then asked, "What is this one word? The Master thrust his fire tongs toward the side of the brazier and then withdrew them back to their original place.
A single phrase brings forth the ten thousand phenomena; Mahākāśyapa silently closed his heavy gates. At that first moment, the patch-robed monk slightly opened his eyes;
he stuck his chopsticks into the side of the brazier as if they were being consumed by fire.
(Touzi Qing) Nantang asked a monk: "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas; I wonder, does Mañjuśrī himself have a teacher?"
The Master said, "It exists whenever conditions meet. The monk asked, "What is Mañjuśrī? The Master held up his whisk.
The monk said, "Is it not simply this? The Master lowered the whisk and stood with his hands folded.
Baoshou said: "Mañjuśrī certainly has a teacher, but simply no one dares to speak of it.
Even if Nanta were to uphold this point in such a way, it would suffice for him as the teacher of the seven Buddhas;
yet if we discuss Mañjuśrī’s teacher, even I, this old monk, would only have to hang my mouth on the wall."
Once, when a monk asked Nan-ta, "What is the jewel of the Dharma-body? the Master said: "The hundred-tongued bird has not yet ceased its chatter upon the branch;
how could the phoenix deign to roost together with it?"

Pines grow by the crags and cranes rest securely; phoenixes emerge from the Vermilion Mountains and join the flock of *luan* birds. Even facing the wall, one still falls short regarding matters outside the hermitage;
why does Vimalakīrti trouble himself with such excessive discourse?
(Touzi Qing) Chan Master Wuzhuo Wenxi of Hangzhou (a successor of Yangshan Huiji), having attained sudden realization of the mind through his studies under Yangshan, was commanded to...
He served as the *zhuzuo* (steward). Manjusri once appeared above the rice-pot. The Master took his rice-stirring paddle and struck him, saying, "Manjusri is Manjusri;
Wenxi is Wenxi. Thereupon, Manjusri spoke this verse: "The bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip;
The sweet melon is sweet from stem to end. Having practiced for three great kalpas, I am yet despised by this old monk."
The *śakara* eye opens at the crown of the head; having attained awakening, there is no need for a teacher to come again. Strike down the rice pot and cease reciting verses;
in the practice of cultivation, one must know that calamity is the womb [of enlightenment].
(Xiang Tianqing) Sitting idly, he cuts off the myriad mountain peaks; under bright moon and clear breeze, he sleeps through the years. By the corner of his hut, the mountain stream flows on.
[He] cut it off. The fisherman safely reached the gate. (Zicheng followed.
Master Mili of Hongzhou (who succeeded Jingshan Yin) gave a turning word, saying: "Nothing surpasses this. At that time, a monk asked:
"I do not yet understand—what is it that nothing surpasses? The Master said: "It does not go beyond this. Later, that monk asked Chang...
Qing asked, "Why do you not speak of this? Qing said, "What do you intend to call it?
There is no need to discuss such matters at this time. Having completely cast aside my former livelihood, I have transcended and no longer cling to old haunts.
For a thousand ages, the wind of benevolence shall establish the imperial foundation. (Pei Feng Ze)
The Ancient Chan Master Shuangfeng of Fuzhou (who had previously succeeded Shuangfeng) arrived at Shishuang. One day he took his leave.

As Shishuang was about to escort him to the gate with a whisk, he called out to the attendant Gu just before they parted. The Master turned his head back; Shishuang said, "If you intend to grasp it, you are already mistaken.
If you grasp it, you are deviant. Do not even try to form a conceptual understanding of 'neither intending nor not being. Unless one knows that there is [the Truth], one cannot know."

"Go, go! Farewell, farewell! The Master responded with an assent and immediately set out. Later, while on his journey, a monk asked him, "At that time, when Shishuang spoke thus, what was his underlying meaning?
The Master said, "He was simply trying to prevent me from falling into the attachment of right and wrong."
Xuánjué said: "Tell me, does he understand Shíshuāng’s meaning, or not? Fālínyīn said: "How could he have even dreamed of Shíshuāng?
The young master of Luoyang is intoxicated by luxury; he gazes only at the flowers, not at the green mountains. If a pine-clad temple could but retain [the spirit]..."
"Stay! This old monk would not begrudge you a cup of tea.

(Zibo Ke) Chan Master Ribao of Zifu in Jizhou, the seventh generation descendant of Dajian (Huineng), whose lineage was passed to Xita Mu, once drew a circle when Minister Chen Cao visited him. The Master drew a circle.
Yuanxiang drew a circle. Yaoshan said, "I have come this way already without any advantage; why do you need to do this?
The Master placed a dot in the center of it. Yaoshan said, "I took you for a merchant captain from South India. The Master then returned to his quarters and closed the door.

Cui峰 Xian said, "Chen Cao possesses only one eye. Wuquan Zhē said, "Although Zifu is the furnace of one's true nature, how can he withstand Chen Cao, who is already refined pure gold? Do you wish to know Zifu?
He casually casts a single hook, startling the dragon of the azure depths. Lingyan Chu said, "Cui Feng’s critique is such that his elbow..."

The arm never bends outward; yet they fail to realize that when the Minister (Shangshu) cleared away the white clouds, he was seeking a true friend, and when Zifu opened the blue peaks, he was skillfully responding to the incoming stimulus.
Both were masters of their craft, yet they could not help but follow the old patterns and imitate the models.
"Round and round the pearls swirl; the jade chimes ring out. Carried by horse and donkey, they board an iron boat. Entrust this to the carefree traveler of the seas and mountains:
when fishing for the giant turtle, he casts down a single coil of line. He further said: "The monks of the world cannot leap out [of this].
(Cui-feng Xian remarked: "A mirror reflects a mirror; a thief recognizes a thief. How can one bear to add more grit to the eyes? Do you not see Zhong-ni and Can-zhen?"
Wenbo Xue (Enlanrong). When a monk asked Zifusi, "What is the meaning of 'a single mote of dust entering right concentration'? the Master made the gesture of entering meditative absorption.
The monk said, "What is the meaning of 'arising from the samādhi of all motes of dust'? The Master replied, "Whom are you asking?"
Lingxi Yu said: "I, this mountain monk, do not say it so. What is 'a single mote of dust entering right concentration'?
He raised his fist and said, "This is a fist. "What is 'all motes of dust arising in samādhi'? He then struck him straight across the mouth.
Longtang Gu rephrased the former words, saying: "Whom are you asking? Then he rephrased the latter words and instead made the gesture of entering meditative absorption.
Zifu asked a monk, "What was the meaning of the ancients raising their mallets or brandishing their fly-whisks? The Master said, "The ancients were like that.
The monk asked, "But what about raising the mallet or brandishing the fly-whisk? The Master then gave a shout and sent him out.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "What kind of eyes do these ancients have? A monk said, "Master, even in a donkey’s year, would you ever understand?
Yunmen then called to the monk, "Come here, come here! As the monk approached, Yunmen struck him across the mouth with his whisk.
"The topknot jewel is the clouds. Here, it is not so. When the ancients raised their mallets or竖 (uprighted) their fly-whisks, what was their intent? It is said:
"Frequently calling for 'Xiaoyu' is originally a matter of no concern; one simply wishes for the husband to recognize the sound.
If this monk were one who, seeing the horns, knows the ox, he would surely be able to reveal a glimpse of his own insight.
When Zifu first opened the hall at Geyu, he sent a pair of socks to Hu. Hu then wrote the character "fire" (huǒ) and sealed it back.

Upon seeing this, the Master knitted his brows and remained silent for a long time. Later, when Monk Luyuan drew a circle, Hu said, "In the kingdom of Kuśinagara, they personally carried out this command."
Tigers, great beasts, and snakes with turtle-noses—those who have long gathered together are all enemies. Though they share a single mountain, they still divide their own boundaries;
they spit venom, brandish their fangs, and wag their tails with a flourish. (Jiàn-ān Yí) Sharing the clouds and rain, they occupy the Lake of Dongting;
from its seventy-two peaks, the waters overflow and shimmer. Amidst the moonlight, the fishermen’s fires rise as they sing the "kuǎnnǎi" song.
[The wind] rises; the breeze gently bathes the waves as a small boat drifts across.
(Suan Ding) Chan Master Huiqing Bajiao of Yingzhou (a successor of Nanta Yong) ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said:
"If you have a staff, I give you a staff; if you have no staff, I take your staff away."
The Master leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.
Guizong Zhe said, "Daguang is not like this. When you have a staff, I take it away from you;
when you have no staff, I give it to you. Daguang acts in just this way. Do you all understand?"
"Is it used? If a person can use it, then Deshan’s vanguard and Linji’s subsequent command are present.
If it cannot be used, then let it return to its original owner. Touzi Qian said: "If a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will surely have immediate anxieties.
Tiantong Ju said: "If you have it, everything has it; if you lack it, everything lacks it. This is simply up to the person themselves."
"Taking away—what does it have to do with the plantain tree? At such a time, what is your staff? Baofeng Wen said: "O Assembly!
When buying and selling with cash, do not let others deceive you. Do you know? Whether there is profit or loss, one does not leave the marketplace.
Tiandong Jie said: "The old fellow Bajiao has privately set aside the property of the Sangha."

The accounts of past errors have already run their course. This has caused descendants of later generations to add further knots upon the joints of the staff, thereby insulting the ancestral tradition.
At Jing Mountain, everything is starkly bare; if it exists, I do not give it away; if it does not exist, I do not take it away.
"Why is it so? He took up his staff, struck the ground once, and said: "When the power is in one's hand, wait and see when the command is carried out. Wushi said:
"To bestow where there is already something is truly like adding flowers to brocade; but what about taking away where there is nothing?
Ultimately, how do you explain this? After a long silence, he said: "Next year there will be new branches again, but they will only further disturb the spring breeze."
[The discourse] was not yet finished. Yuyan Meng said: "This old fellow has plenty to spare where it is wide, but lacks enough where it is narrow.
It is not so here: when you have a staff, you cannot lift it with both hands; when you have no staff, you cannot set down even your own body.
Shending Ze said: "A single coin buys a pair of straw sandals; there is nothing extraordinary about it."
"Specifically, it is simply that people are not permitted to wear them. Why? Because the Dharma is thus. (He lets out a shout. Shengkeyu said:
"Do you all still know the application of the plantain tree? One may preserve another’s ten thousand acres of fertile fields, yet one cannot avoid being personally destitute with not a single coin.
Gushan Gui said: "The Fifth Patriarch used the story of the staff to request instruction."
Baoyun said: "Clouds upon clouds—do you understand? Add a little where there is too much; subtract a little where there is too little. Why is this?
The secret instructions of the immortals are not transmitted even between father and son. Master Baoyun is much like one who stakes one coin for the sake of a profit of ten thousand;
he does not realize that it is like a skilled gambler who grows poorer day by day. This old man says: 'Add a little where there is too much.'"
If you reduce it slightly in one place, it will naturally be exactly right everywhere. This fellow’s method of calculation saves immense effort.
Do you all wish to understand? He then offered this verse:
Add much and subtract little; do not engage in bartering. When taxes are shifted or commuted, they are increased threefold. Throughout one's life, there is no need to instruct one's children;
once they have fallen into error, they will naturally understand.
Existence and non-existence, past and present—these are two heavy barriers. For a Zen practitioner with the true eye, it is difficult to pass through them.
If you wish to traverse the Great Road to Chang’an, do not listen to the Kunlun man as he speaks of coming and going.
(Touzi Qing) Unfurling leaves no trace; rolling up leaves no mark. At midday, amidst a clear sky, a thunderclap roars. The patch-robed monks are startled and lose their way.
Gods wail and ghosts cry—how can one know the limit?
(Chengtianzong) You must give it to him face-to-face; he will not snatch it from behind your back. Suddenly at midnight, he transforms into a dragon and departs;
black rain and dark clouds split the earth with thunder. (Xutangyu)
The southern branch faces the warmth, the northern branch is cold; Though one kind of spring breeze, it manifests in two ways. I entreat you, do not blow the flute atop the high tower;
Let us all remain here to gaze upon them leaning against the railing.

(Shan Xiaoze) Eighteen beauties dot their brows with azure pigment; Paired by pairs, they have finished painting and drape their robes askew. Their graceful bearing is such that people find them hard to forget.
Behold! Zhang Chang’s toil was but in vain as he gazed toward the purple curtains.

(Falin, rhyme category 2) Existence and non-existence, granting and taking away—herein the school’s tradition is established. A chilling radiance, majestic and cold; who can share in its like? The third-tier waves rise high; where shall one go?
In vain they brandish twin swords to determine male and female.

Bajiao addressed the assembly: "It is like a person walking along who suddenly encounters a ten-thousand-foot-deep pit ahead, while a wild fire presses from behind, with thorny thickets on both sides. If he moves forward, he will fall into the pit;
if he retreats, the wild fire will burn his body; if he turns aside, he will be obstructed by the thorny thickets. At that moment—
At such a time, how can one avoid it? If you can avoid it, you must possess a way to emerge from the situation;
if you cannot avoid it, you are a man who has fallen and died.
Guangyin Biaoyun said: "The old fellow Bajiao has exposed you all and caught you red-handed.
Is there still any blood beneath your skin, you lot? After a long silence, he said: "If it were Ling Xingpo, she would surely have cried out to Heaven!"
Bajiao was asked by a monk, "When a thief comes, one must strike; when a guest comes, one must welcome. But what if both guest and thief arrive at once?
The Master said, "In the house there is a pair of worn-out straw sandals. The monk asked, "As for those worn-out straw sandals, are they still fit for use?
The Master said, "If you take them away, it will be ominous before and inauspicious after."
Zifu Guang said: "To seize them with a double pivot and open them wide with a single stroke—anyone who is but a petty peddler will see their defenses melt away like ice and crumble like tiles.
When a monk asked Bajiao, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya? the Master said: "First, you must not ask; second—"
"Do not rest. [The student] said, "I, a student, do not understand. The Master said, "This shall be our third meeting.
Do not ask about Vimalakīrti lying ill in the city; Luoshan is empty, merely wasting away his own time.
There is no difficulty at all in crossing the shifting sands; do not listen to the oriole singing in that forest. (Touzi Qing)
One does not ask, nor does one rest; one must directly recognize that hook-tip.
Returning again and again to meet him, one rolls an embroidered ball amidst the waves of a rushing torrent.
(Lan’an Xu) Bājião said: "At the age of twenty-eight, I went to Yangshan to visit Nantá. I saw him ascend the hall and say:"
"You all—if you are true men—should have roared like a lion the moment you emerged from your mother's womb; would that not be well?
Under these words, my body and mind were stilled, and I remained there for five years."
Chengtian Yi said: "Bajiao only knew how to instruct others to let out the lion’s roar;
he did not realize that he himself was spitting out much wild fox saliva, which to this day makes people cover their noses. Yongning Ding said:

"At that time, had there been someone in the assembly who, upon hearing such a presentation, stepped forward from the crowd and said: 'For a monk traveling on pilgrimage like you, Master, to eat [such food]...'"
One must also guard against choking on water.
Under the Eighth Generation of Dajian (Dajian Huineng), Chan Master Zensui of Zifu in Jizhou (Dharma heir of Zifu Bao) was asked by a monk: "What is the song of the ancient buddhas? The Master said:
He made this [mudra] sign and showed it to him:
"One song, two songs, deep in the night’s talk; pine wind and rain pass over the mountain ahead. Pity the jade of Bian, separated from Mount Jing;
who is the true connoisseur to retrieve it and return it? (Touzi Qing)
Zifu ascended the hall. Seeing Zifu from across the river, [a monk] turned back as soon as he saw the monastery flagpole; he deserves thirty blows to his heels.
How much more so for one who actually crosses the river! At that time, as soon as a monk stepped forward, the Master said, "He is not fit to converse with."
Horses gallop through the clouds over a thousand trees of blossoms; fish swim beneath the water for ten days.
The eyebrows on his brow have already flown past; behold now, Baizhang’s jade light surges forth.
(Longhua Xiang) Chan Master Jiche of Bajiao Mountain in Yingzhou (a successor of Bajiao Qing). A monk asked: "There is a person who does not abandon birth..."
"Upon death, one does not realize nirvana. The Master replied, "I do not carry [the corpse]. The monk asked, "Why do you not carry it?
The Master said, "This old monk has a rough knowledge of what is good and what is evil."
Tiantong Jue said: "Although Bājiǎo recognizes good from evil, he still cannot drive the plowman’s ox or snatch food from a starving man.
If someone were to question Changlu today, I would strike him with the sound of my voice. Why is this so? Because from the beginning, he has never recognized good from evil.
Dongshan Ying said: "Although Bājiǎo recognizes good from evil, it is very much like adding insult to injury after becoming drunk."
Cup. Those who wish to live cannot be monks. Tiantong does not recognize good from evil; this is like driving away the plowman and seizing his food.
Even if one is a monk who lives on, he cannot avoid wounding his blade or injuring his hand. If someone asks about Xinfeng, simply say to him:
"A sharp sword does not slay the dead. If he is a true patch-robed monk, you may rest assured that he will have a different way of life.
A hundred-year-old child comes out the door, his whole body red and raw, covered in dust. He walks freely through the fire upon a cool ground;
those who understand have no cause to dare approach him.
(Touzi Qing) Chan Master Yuan of Bajiao Mountain in Yingzhou (a successor of Bajiao Qing) ascended the hall and said: "The night of the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world..."
"Come here, and let this old monk roll you all together into a single mass and hurl it to the summit of Mount Sumeru.
Śakra, enraged, will seize it and smash it into fine dust. O Venerable Elders, do you feel a headache yet?
After a long silence, he said, "Do not fail to recognize pain and itchiness. Take care."
In the deepening autumn, everywhere the hibiscus is in full bloom. Some hang toward the west, some toward the east.
There is no need to let the wind and rain envy them; across the high plateau, the fallen petals cover the paths in crimson.
(Pingxiang) *Zongjian Fali*, Volume 41.

Compiled by Jiyun Tang;
The Third Generation Descendants of Dajian.
Chan Master Tianhuang Daowu of Jingzhou (dharma successor of Cunyi) went to visit Shitou. He asked, "Setting aside concentration and wisdom, by what dharma do you instruct people?
Shitou said, "In my place here, there are no servants; what is there to set aside? The Master asked, "How can one understand this?
Shitou said, "Can you grasp empty space? The Master said, "If that is so, then it does not depend on the present."
The Master said, "You have come. He asked, "I do not yet know from where you have come—early or late? The Master replied, "Daowu is not a person from 'that side.
The Master said, "I already knew where you had come from. The Master [Zhaozhou] said, "Why does the Master frame someone with evidence that does not exist?
The Master said, "Even though it is so, how ultimately will you instruct those who come after?"
The man said, "Tell me, who is the 'person of the future'? At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.

Jingshan Daowu Gao asked, "What have you realized? Mingyin Hui said, "At that time, Shitou should have waited for him to say, 'In that case, I do not follow from today,' and struck him with a blow right between the eyes, sparing him from following that [path]."

Regarding "the extremes": the person in front and the person behind are entangled in a web of complications and fail to understand. Ancient *Hangzhou* said: "The clouds have no mind as they emerge from the mountain peaks;
the birds, weary of flying, know it is time to return. How could one avoid such threefold and fourfold reversals? Only when the feet are firm and steady can one attain stability.
The path of Stonehead is slippery and the gate before it is high and steep; originally, it was a case where acceptance and refusal were incomplete.
If one were merely a descendant of another house, they would be but a vague and indistinct likeness; the Buddha-Dharma would not have reached the present day.
Tianhuang Daowu, before he attained enlightenment, lived beside Longtan when he was still unordained, making his living by selling cakes.
He offered ten cakes daily to his teacher, who accepted them. Each time, the teacher would set aside one cake for Daowu, saying, "I bestow this upon you as a protective blessing."
Xin said, "This was brought by me; why do you instead give it back to me? The Master replied, "It was brought by you;
returning it to you—what fault is there in that? Consequently, Xin attained realization and subsequently left home to become a monk.
What was to come will not fail; Longtan’s firm questioning leaves no room for confusion. How many have since vied with one another over words and phrases?
The spring birds warble as they scold the falling blossoms.
(Fenyang Zhao) Seeing the Stone Head atop Mount Nanyue, he returned at once to the ancient shore to consort with the sand gulls. In vain did he divide the Hu-bread into incense.
The bait. It draws forth the golden dragon onto the straight hook.
(Foguo Bai) Holding it back and sending it forth, circling in a ball; the shade it provides for descendants is not cold in its intent.
How does this compare to leaving it whole at that time, so that future generations may view it? (Wuzhun Fan)
The bright pearl of Hepu has been reclaimed from Hepu; the shadow of the black dragon briefly reflects in the floating mirror-light.
Had it not been for the mist snatching it up and the clouds lifting it away, how could one have seen the long river pouring its hundred tributaries?
(Lingtong Ting) One’s native land was never separated by the ends of the earth; having boarded the boat, one has arrived home at once. Let us lift the solitary sail and look around for a moment.
Gazing afar, the green mountains remain as before, shrouded by white clouds.
(Zifuxu) The Fourth Generation under the Great Mirror:
Chan Master Chongxin of Longtan in Lidezhou (Succeeded Tianwu). One day he asked Wu: "Since I first arrived..."

Baizhang said, "I have been instructed in the essentials of the mind. Huairang replied, "From the moment you arrived, there has never been a time when I did not instruct you in the essentials of the mind.
Baizhang asked, "Where did you instruct me? Huairang said, "When you brought tea, I accepted it for you;
when you brought food, I received it for you; when you bowed in greeting, I lowered my head. Where was I not instructing you?"
The Essential Mind. Master Baizhang bowed his head. Huineng said, "If you see, see directly; if you deliberate, you are already mistaken. At that moment, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
He then asked, "How does one maintain this state? Huineng replied, "Roam freely according to your nature; be relaxed and expansive in accordance with conditions."
"Simply exhaust all ordinary sentiments;
there is no separate 'sage's understanding. Xigyan Bao said: 'Longtan asked thus, and Tianhuang answered thus.

If you can truly understand this, then 'ordinary' and 'sage' are mere empty names, and 'delusion' and 'awakening' are both superfluous words. If you do not understand, do not let a blind donkey follow the great crowd.'"
Nanshan Baoyun said: "The great and small devas are usually as firm as a nail being driven home, yet when pressed by this fellow, they immediately level their heights and conform to the low ground.
Even so, if one speaks of the essential heart, we are still separated by a ford."
Leaving the white robe to throw oneself upon a teacher is a matter of noble hardship; offering tea and inquiring after one’s welfare are performed with total personal devotion.
To needlessly recount the affairs of three years again would make even the street vendor selling cakes laugh himself to tears.
(Baizhang Yuanwen) Light as a willow fluff, yet heavy as a mountain—pointing it out clearly in every movement. He pulls off his cloth robe in the wind.
Floating away. Plowing and tilling for livelihood, one knows no leisure. (Sān-fēng Zàng) Honor and favor bind the body;
the traveler’s dream is far. When the orioles call in the inner palace, one immediately longs for home.
On the day of returning with jeweled horses and tinkling bells, in the second month, the spring mountains are entirely covered in flowers. (Zhè-ān Fàn)
Flowers and grasses wind and curl; the waters are a deep azure. At dawn, the ponds, clouds, and trees blend together. In Master Acheng’s house, there is a girl with yellow hair;
she plants tender mulberry trees everywhere and teaches how to raise silkworms.
(By Lingting Ting) Longtan came to visit Deshan. He went straight up to the Dharma Hall and said, "I have long heard of Longtan, but now that I have arrived..."
[Shishuang] came; the pond was not seen, nor did the dragon appear. The Master said, "You have come personally to Longtan.
Deshan remained silent. Cui-feng Xian said, "Taking a mistake for a mistake. Yun-feng Yue said, "The great Deshan has been drowned in a vat of minced meat.
Huang-long Xin said, "When Cui-feng spoke thus, was it because Deshan took a mistake for a mistake?"

A mistake. Longtan takes the mistake and makes it right. Those who recognize good and ill fortune must know the place of departure; those who have not yet passed through the barrier should also discern this.
Do you understand thoroughly? Even if you manage to plant it, it will not be timber for a great beam.
Dongshan Yan said: "Longtan may be called one riding a thief’s horse to pursue a thief. Tiantong Wu said: "Longtan did not see the dragon."
[The Master] said, "He is not manifest. Why then do you say the Son of the Dharma came in person? It is very much like trying to fit a square block into a round hole.
Where, then, is the place where he came in person? Falin Yin spoke on behalf of Deshan, saying: "You have deceived me! You have deceived me!"
The vast and deep pool receives all streams; in vain one holds fragrant bait and casts a golden hook.
Wind and clouds gather, thunder rolls—surely you must wonder why the Dragon King does not show his head.
(Baoning Yong) Having personally reached the dragon pool, the dragon is not seen; the dragon of the pool is not within the pool. Under the blue sky and bright sun, the clouds arise.
Rain. For a thousand ages, all have laughed at Old Master Ye. (Foguo Bai):
With a mouth like a blood-basin and fangs like swords, he has exhausted the world’s pivotal secrets yet cannot boast of them;
having personally arrived at Longtan, the dragon did not appear—this time he has lost the flowers before his eyes. (Xinwen Ben)
The pool is not seen; the dragon does not appear. You must personally reach the dragon pool and give a living testimony.

Do not emulate those who merely receive echoes and grasp at shadows, or those who sit by a stump waiting for a hare, devoid of the capacity for adaptive response. To know the capacity for adaptive response: when the cup is knocked to the ground, the saucer shatters into seven pieces.
(Tanyuan Yan) The abyss is not seen;
the dragon does not appear. The whole body is already within the Hall of the Empty King. Returning from a dream, one suddenly hears the dawn oriole singing;
the spring wind has blown away all the peach petals. (Huanshan Ning)
One night at Longtan, while Deshan was standing in attendance, the Master said, "It is deep in the night; why do you not go out? Deshan said, "I take my leave," and then departed.
He returned, saying, "It is dark outside. The Master lit a paper lantern and passed it to him. As Deshan reached out to receive it—
The Master blew it out again. Dàoxiàn attained great enlightenment and immediately prostrated. The Master asked, "What have you seen?
Dàoxiàn replied, "From this day forward, I shall no longer doubt the tongues of the old monks throughout the world.

On the following day, the Master ascended the seat and said, "In that assembly there is a man whose teeth are like sword-trees and whose mouth is like a blood basin; with a single blow of his staff..."
Without looking back, he will one day stand atop a solitary peak; my Way shall thus proceed.
He piled the mountain’s commentaries and sub-commentaries before the Dharma Hall, raised a torch, and said: "To exhaust all profound dialectics is like placing a single hair in the great void."
Exhausting the pivotal mechanisms of the world is like casting a single drop into a vast abyss; he then burned [the texts].
The mutual overcoming of light and darkness is not worth mentioning. A hair’s breadth of understanding is not yet intimate. When the paper lamp suddenly goes out, the eyes emerge.
The Great Tang is shattered—there is not a single person left. (Baizhang Yuan)
At one time, a waterfall falls before the cliff; at midnight, the golden sun shines upon the palm of the hand.
Opening his mouth wide to display his spirit and resolve, with whom does he traverse the world together?

(Baoning Yong) Light and dark reflect one another, yet the matter remains vast and obscure. Who knows that the divine light bursts forth from behind the crown of the head? All things are thus cut through, severing all manifold distinctions.
The Road: Reaching one’s native village in the north, south, east, and west.
(Da Hong Sui) When light and darkness are distinguished, time is fixed and movement arises; where the firelight extinguishes, the source of its origin is seen.
After Longtan cut off the flow of words, the Buddhas and Patriarchs continued their scolding from solitary peaks without ceasing. (Zhao Jue Zong)
A whirlwind sweeps through, parting the misty haze; a thousand peaks emerge, emerald and towering.
Startled monkeys and resentful cranes have long been cast away, yet at midnight before the mountains, they are called back home.
(By Shangfang Yi) Mist rises from the dragon pool as the old dragon roars; it terrifies the white-browed tiger of the South Mountain. Without disturbing the waves, he seizes the turtle.

Bi Nan-tang Jing: His features are sharp and prominent, his spirit like a rainbow. Wearing a hundred-knot robe and a tattered head-wrap, he has failed the imperial examinations year after year throughout the Divine Land.

Yet, because of a single arrow that pierced the willow, in his old age he was enfeoffed as a Marquis on Horseback. Luo Yue Ying: His features are sharp and prominent, his spirit like a rainbow. Wearing a hundred-knot robe and a tattered head-wrap, he has failed the imperial examinations year after year throughout the Divine Land.
Yet, because of a single arrow that pierced the willow, in his old age he was enfeoffed as a Marquis on Horseback.
Opening the mouth, no teeth are seen; extending the hand, no palm is seen. At midnight they suddenly meet; the entanglement grows ten thousand fathoms long.

(Xue’an Jin) Having personally reached Longtan, he already cast his hook in darkness. Deep in the night, who shares a stroll through the Imperial Street? The paper lantern is blown out; the smoke of the barbarians has ceased.
Rest. Sitting and cutting off the four hundred prefectures of the Central Plains.
(Tianmu Li) Meeting suddenly and unexpectedly, there is no need for a third word; as soon as the foul mouth opens, one hears the local dialect.
The paper lamp is extinguished, yet its meaning remains; the azure dragon is not permitted to lie in the green depths. (Puweng Xian)
Chan Master Xuanjian of Deshan in Dingzhou (dharma heir of Longtan Xian), the fifth generation descendant of Dajian, addressed the assembly: "Tonight, I will not answer questions.
Anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows of the staff. At that time, a monk came forward and bowed; the Master struck him immediately. The monk said, "I have no words."
[The monk] had not yet asked why the Master struck him. The Master said, "Where are you from? [The monk] replied, "A man from Silla.
The Master said, "Before you even stepped onto the ship's railing, you deserved thirty blows."
Fayan Yi said, "The discourse between the Great and Small Deshan is split into two separate pieces. Deshan Mi said, "The Great and Small Deshans have the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake.
Cui峰 Xian said, "Although these two venerable elders were skilled at cutting the long to patch the short."
"To abandon the heavy for the light—yet even this would not suffice to see the old fellow Deshan. You do not realize that Deshan wields the sovereign authority beyond the pass;
he possesses the sword that, if one hesitates to strike when it is time to sever, will fail to avert chaos. Do you recognize the Korean monk?
He was merely a blind fellow who ran headlong into a pillar. Bajiao Che said, "It is like treating a dead horse with medicine."
Langye Jue said, "How is it that Deshan is like treading on spring ice? Even so, it is like a cat playing with a mouse.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "People of this age all say that Deshan made good use of his 'household tools. If you understand it in such a way, have you ever even dreamed of it?
I, this mountain monk, say: Deshan was pushed by this monk until he was utterly reduced to shattered tiles and melted ice."
"Even so, nowadays it is truly difficult to find even a single venerable elder. Zhao of Mount Guishan said:
"Deshan was much like a world at peace where armor is polished and spears are sharpened; this monk did not spare his own life as he pressed against the white blades.
Fayan said: "He split the words of the teaching into two pieces; it was much like medicine and disease treating one another. Yuankui said: "A dragon's head..."
A snake’s tail. It is also like failing to distinguish between gold and brass. Cui峰 said, "A blind fellow who bumps into a pillar; he cuts off the flow of all streams.
Is there anyone now who can act as a patron for this monk from Silla? Come forth and meet with Dayang! He then held up his whisk and said:
"Depart, depart on the road to the Western Heaven; it stretches for more than ten million miles! Wuzu Yan said: [The text concludes with the citation of Wuzu Yan's remark.]
"I, this mountain monk, have already met Deshan. When he says, 'Tonight I will not answer a word;
anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows,' you should simply say, 'I do not ask a question, nor do I take a blow.
Do you think that accords with Deshan? To reach this point, one must be a true person. Huanglong Qing said, "Although it was indeed Cui..."
Fenggan held up the Patriarch’s staff and commanded it to "sit and cut off the entire realm. He only knew how to look forward and could not look back.
This monk came forth with such dignity—where did he strike the pillar? Is there anyone who can discern this?
If you can discern it, not only will you vindicate the Silla monk, but you will also see that your own eyes are clear. If you can discern it...
It does not emerge. It is not only that the Silla monk struck the pillar; every single monk throughout the entire earth emerges and strikes the pillar.
Nantang Jing said: "The old man Deshan is silent yet alert; Fayen is perfectly clear, precise, and vivid.
The Six Tactics and Three Strategies are his military patterns and civil classics. The Silla monk has the 'bing' but lacks the 'ji'."
Ding. Danxia Chun said: "Everyone says that as soon as this monk stepped out, Deshan struck him;

yet at the end, he said, 'Had you not even stepped onto the boat's railing, I would have given you thirty blows. This is where the story is split in two; it is where the dragon’s head meets the snake’s tail.
To understand it in such a way is much like a blind man feeling an elephant—not only have you never dreamed of seeing Deshan yourself," [but you have also missed the point entirely].
You yourself have not yet fully attained the eye of study and inquiry. You do not realize that Deshan’s strategic prowess is complete in both civil and martial arts:
when he lets go, the wind sweeps across the vast fields; when he holds fast, the stars fall from the azure sky.

Thus, while you greedily seek to uphold the orthodox lineage and ascend step by step, if you observe carefully, you have been looking only at the faults of others and have been unable to reflect upon yourself.
As for this monk’s mistake: had he been a true adept at that time, even if Deshan were possessed of eyes and hands all over his body, he would still have had to drop his staff.
Have you not heard it said: "For a great man to pluck the tiger's whiskers is not considered beyond his capacity"?
Since this monk lacked the skill to seize the pearl from the black dragon, he allowed Deshan’s command to be carried out only half-fully.
"Is there anyone among this assembly who will clear the injustice for the Silla monk? If so, please overturn the meditation seat and shout to disperse the crowd!
Here at Danxia, we do not follow Deshan’s practice of using power to bully others; instead, we gave him half the monastery to dwell in. Why was this so?
It is because I deeply lament that in these degenerate times, a single capable leader is difficult to find. If one does not have a true teaching to offer, how can one be extraordinary?
The beast hides its claws; the horned and crested spirit-bird guards its plumage. Zhaojue Qin said: "Deshan was much like a Golden Wheel-turning Sage King, alone presiding over the realm.

Throughout the four quarters and the eight directions, there were none who did not submit. In his casual distribution of edicts and issuance of commands, he achieved the effect of grass bowing and wind blowing.
Had it not been for this monk, how could one have witnessed the majesty of his killing and enlivening, his capturing and releasing?"
His authority is sovereign and his Dharma-eye is perfectly clear. Although Cui峰 (Cui Feng) directly pointed and raised the single word, he was able to uphold Deshan;
yet, while he could indeed uphold the final phrase, he did not uphold the initial phrase. But what is Deshan’s initial phrase?
When the great garuḍa wishes to spread its wings to touch the heavens, who takes note of the surging clouds across the six directions?
Huguo Yuan said: "This fellow relies too heavily on his power to deceive others. I wish for everyone to know my own perspective on this matter:
had that monk been a true man at that time, when the other asked, 'Where are you from? he would have overturned the meditation seat and walked out immediately.
Even if Deshan’s teeth were like sword-trees and his mouth like a blood-basin, he still would have had to [yield]."
"He retreated three thousand li. Why? Because those who know the Dharma are afraid. Jingci said, "This monk was like one who thrusts his bare flesh against a white blade;
it would not have been easy to withstand him. Had he been a true man at that time, when the master said, 'Tonight there will be no answering questions;
anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows,' he would have immediately overturned the meditation seat and shouted for the assembly to disperse."
He snatches away Deshan’s staff and executes the true command; even if Deshan were at the height of his full capacity, he would still have to retreat three thousand li.
Fushan said, "Under Deshan’s gate, the grass falls as the wind blows. Yet, how could Fayen Yuanming fail to let him pass?
Although Cui峰’s methods of granting and seizing are worth observing, and his alternations of suppression and encouragement follow a standard, one must see these two...
"Even the Elder Master (Lao Su) is not yet acceptable. [Deshan] picks up his staff, draws a line, and says: "At the river, the land of Wu ends;
beyond the shore, the mountains of Yue abound. Yunju Zhuang said: "The various quarters can only support the strong; they cannot support the weak.
Tonight, Jing Mountain wishes to settle this injustice. With teeth like sword-trees and a mouth like a foundation stone, one must acknowledge that old fellow Deshan. If..."
This distinguishes the eye of a monk, yet it still lacks awakening. At that time, as soon as this monk stepped forward, he said directly:
"I will not ask a question tonight; I simply wish to meet the Master face-to-face. If he were to strike with his staff, the monk would have seized it and given him a shove.
"Not only does he sit and cut off Deshan, but he also avoids the punishment of Cui-feng. Is this not a truly spirited monk?

[The Master] picks up his staff, strikes it once, and says: "A crane in the Nine Gao has difficulty spreading its wings; a horse that lacks a thousand-li stride vainly pursues the wind. Da-wei Lun said:
"If I were a monk from Silla, as soon as I saw Deshan open his mouth, I would have laughed 'He-he'!"
He laughed loudly and departed. Daci Xun said, "Old man Deshan has had his nostrils pierced by this monk with a broken tethering rope behind his back.
Do you understand? This mountain monk is not here to support the weak or suppress the strong; I simply wish to point out a place of entry for all of you.
He struck the ground with his staff and said, "The moon is dark, the frost is thick; the hair on one's bones stands on end."
"Cold! A crane perches ten thousand feet high, letting out a single cry. He gives a shout. Dongta Xi said: "Deshan holds the rank of General Gan in his grasp;
he has freedom over life and death. Yet, alas, there are two commands in one assembly—where is the true master?

If Changxi had encountered this monk, as soon as the monk came forward to bow, he would have returned directly to his quarters. Not only would this have left the messenger-monk tongue-tied, but it would also have been a fine way to handle the situation."
Lest we fail one another through mutual negligence, Dun’an Ding said: "Deshan spread an iron net that covered the heavens, thinking none would dare to flap their wings;
yet they encountered a hawk from Silla who pierced through it with a single stroke. Tell me, where exactly was it pierced?
If you can discern this, you may join in cheering for this monk; if you cannot discern it," [the verse continues].
Come forth! Do not fail the Master Deshan.
Having personally obtained the hand of Ren Gong, he drew two hooks with a single, clear line.
As soon as the golden-scaled fish that has pierced the net begins to play in the water, the angler pulls in the line from the bank. (Foyin Yuan)
The General’s command sweeps away dust and smoke; the Imperial Edict circulates, proclaiming its virtuous grace.
The young lord knows only to sing "Both Drunk," yet at nightfall he is captured alive.
(Baofeng Zhao) Transversely grasping the Mo-ye sword beyond the gate, who dares to challenge his heavy encirclement? How laughable is that monk from Silla!
The Son: The total functioning that shatters the enemy is radiant.
(Gufo Min) Holding high the ancestral seal, he settles all within the world; who would dare face his presence to inquire of good or ill fortune?
Were it not for this monk from Silla, how could the pure wind have been stirred for a thousand ages? (Dayi Zhe)
The great smelter melts the gold; a sudden clap of thunder startles the spring. Grasses and trees flourish and bloom; their radiance renews itself daily.
Without expending the slightest effort, he captures the celestial qilin. With full majesty, he masters life and death with ease; his brilliance shines through the ages like the moon.
