You say, "Does Miaoxi still have a transgression? A cangue upon his head and shackles upon his feet. Jiashan Yu spoke on behalf of the monk, saying:
Fortunately, I know that the Master is a true adept.
Distant lands are not permitted to offer rare treasures; In secret, he summoned only the instruction to present lychees. Han Wudi’s jade peach could never compare to these;
It was a waste to have Liu An make him a thief. (Haizhou Ci)
Laughing at that parrot who mimics human speech, it flies back and forth from the north branch to the south branch.
At the very end, how could it know the strength of the wind? It is broken, its feathers falling with a *shān-shān* sound.
(Zhuofeng Yuan) When Xuefeng was at Dongshan, Shan said, "Upon entering the gate, you must have something to say; you cannot simply say, 'I came early.'"
[The monk] entered. The Master said, "I have no mouth. [The monk] said, "Even if you have no mouth, at least return my eyes to me.
The Master stopped there. Changqing Ling said, "I respectfully withdraw."
There was a monk living in a hermitage at the foot of Xuefeng Mountain who had not shaved his head for many years. When someone asked him, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
the monk replied, "The stream is deep and the handle of the ladle is long. Hearing this, the Master (Yunmen) took a razor in his sleeve and went to visit him in person.
As soon as he saw the monk, he said, "If you have attained the Way, I shall not shave your head. The monk immediately washed his head and knelt before the Master, who then shaved him.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Although the Hermitage Master was forged from cast iron, how could he avoid the essential tongs and hammers of Xuefeng?
Had he been merely superficial at the beginning, how could his deeds have so startled heaven and moved earth? Do you understand? His golden arrowheads were seasoned through a hundred battles;
his iron whip possessed great strength, yet he lamented having no enemy. Liran Wen said: "The Hermitage Master wanted to obtain the opportunity."
It was appropriate. Yet, in the end, he lost one point to Xuefeng. Shengfa Faying said, "Xuefeng loved to seek advantage;
from beginning to end, he was exposed by the Hermitage Master."
The Old Man Xuefeng, showing his compassion, consented to visit him. On the tip of a single hair, he distinguished dragons from snakes.
One must know that this does not lie outside the reach of verbal expression; it is a total, natural flow of the true lineage.

(Dongshan Yuan) Xuefeng asked a monk, "I have heard it said that you, Venerable Sir, once came as a celestial messenger—is this true? The monk replied, "I dare not say so. The Master [said]: *Note: The final character "師" (shī) indicates the end of the Master’s verse or commentary.*
The monk said, "I have come to resolve this very matter. He replied, "Admiring your virtue and wisdom, how could I have feared the mountain passes?
The Master said, "You are still drunk; get out! The monk then departed. The Master called out, "Virtuous One! The monk turned his head back. The Master asked, "What is this?"
The monk also asked, "What is it? The Master said, "This lacquer bucket. The monk was speechless. The Master looked back at Jingqing and said, "What a fine monk you are!
You have fallen right into this lacquer bucket. Jingqing said, "Does the Master not settle the case according to the facts?
The Master said, "It is something I use constantly. But what if someone were suddenly called upon and replied, 'What is it?'"
[The student] said, "What about that 'lacquer bucket' he spoke of? The Master said, "How can you say that? It forms no principle at all.
The student said, "He reached me in such a way; you say it forms no principle. The Master said, "I reached him in such a way;
you say it forms no principle. The student said, "Both were moments of 'in such a way. Why is it that between them there is one who attains and one who does not?"

[It is] attained. [Dongshan] said: "I have not seen it taught that the supreme flavor of ghee is prized by the world; yet when encountered by such people as these, it instead becomes a poisonous drug.
Cui峰 Xian (Cui-feng Xian) said: "Look at how father and son meet; their words and spirit accord with one another. Those who know this would say their bones are ground to powder."
This debt of gratitude is difficult to repay. Those who do not understand say that he was supporting the high and suppressing the low, or intimidating people at a moment of peril.
Whether it be deadly poison or sweet nectar, this serves as a mirror for a thousand years. Do you understand? You lacquer bucket! Shigan Hui said:
"Xuefeng leaked his secret at every turn. This monk bumped into it and struck against it; even if he were called back, he would still be as pitch-black as lacquer before him."
Xuefeng had been given a silver folding chair by the Military Governor of Min. A monk asked, "How should the Master repay such offerings from the Great King?
The Master struck the ground with his hand and said, "Beat me lightly."
A monk asked Shushan, "What was the meaning of Xuefeng saying, 'I strike you lightly'? Shushan said, "A radish tucked into his hair;
the tail hangs down level with his heels."
Because he was asked how to repay the kindness of one's lord, he raised his staff and withdrew it completely, taking his seat at the vital ford.
If wind and waves stir at the prow of the boat, the flowing sands fill the eyes and no person is seen.

(Fenyang Zhao) Not knowing what to use to repay the sovereign’s grace, the wind rises upon the rivers and lakes, leaving ripples in the water. A single ancient sail catches the inspiration of the moment.
Go! With whom do you go hand-in-hand past the Heavenly Gate?
(Baoning Yong) Receiving offerings—both sides are equally illusion. Facing the critical moment, why not spare your eyebrows and whiskers?
You know well that there is no skill beyond this; *tu!*—you old blind donkey from Qianzhou! (Baoye Yuan)
Xuefeng asked a monk, “Where are you going? The monk replied, “I am going to the communal work. Xuefeng said, “Go.

Yunmen Wenyan remarked, “This is merely recognizing people by their words. Tiantong Juexian said, “Do not move it; if you move it, you will receive thirty blows of the staff. Yunmen’s statement that this is ‘recognizing people by their words’ is like painting legs on a snake.
—Shishou Fang *Note: The term "shisu shiren" (隨語識人) refers to a pedagogical method where the teacher discerns the student's realization based on their spontaneous verbal response.*
It is said: "The old fellow Xuefeng mostly started from a causal circumstance; let us not investigate what has already passed.
Even if Tian Tong were to act in this manner, how could it merely be a case of raising one's voice to stop an echo? One must simply accept thirty blows oneself before it will do."
Xuefeng asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Zhejiang. The Master said, "By boat or by land?
The monk replied, "I have not traveled by either route. The Master said, "How then did you get here? The monk replied, "What obstacle could there be?
The Master struck him and drove him out. Ten years later, the monk returned. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Hunan. The Master said, "The lake..."
"How far is it from here to Nanyue? [The monk] replied, "It is not separated. The Master held up his whisk and asked, "Is it separated by this?

[The monk] replied, "If it were separated, then I would not have arrived. The Master then struck him and drove him out. Later, after the monk had settled elsewhere, he would insult anyone he encountered.
A fellow practitioner of the Master’s went specifically to visit him, and when the monk recounted the previous conversation, the fellow practitioner rebuked and scolded him.
He explained it for others, and the assembly wept with grief at that time. He would often burn incense and pay remote prostrations during the middle of the night.
Gao Feng Miao said: "This public case is somewhat similar to Deshan’s overturning of the bowl.
If you can see it in Deshan’s bowing his head, you will understand the intent behind Xuefeng’s strike; if you can see it in Yantou’s refusal to assent, then [you will understand]."
One understands the monk’s intent to scold at the point where Yantou reveals it in secret;

one understands the monk’s intent to have his companion point it out at the point where Yantou claps his hands; one understands the monk’s intent to weep at the point where Yantou grants him a prediction;
and one understands the monk’s intent to pay homage from afar at that same point. Today, Xifeng brings forth these two venerable elders.
I have bound them all together into a single bundle and cast them before you. It is easy to see the two elders;
it is difficult to see Xifeng. Why? Because they have eyes but no ears; they sit by the fire in the sixth month.

Horns upon his head, he goes and returns; in the snowy courtyard, twice the battle banners unfold. Before the army, he does not err in the General’s command; yet though heroes emerge from the nine realms, they remain there.
Though they emerge from the nine realms, there is a secure barrier; until one penetrates this secure barrier, they have not seen enough.
On the tip of the staff there is an eye as bright as the sun; if you wish to recognize true gold, look for it within the fire. (Fodeng Xun)
I have heard it said that Mount Min abounds in *gu*-poisons; though one employs a thousand methods and a hundred schemes, there is no way to avoid them.
Since the "soul-accelerating ghosts" already dwell within the cup, only when one’s life is surrendered to them will one find rest.

(Xu Tang Yu) One who possesses the raw jade labors in vain only to suffer the amputation of his feet; one who offers a pearl rarely fails to evoke the dragon’s radiance. How can one cast away such yellow gold?
Seal. For now, follow the fish and birds as they bathe in the Canglang River; do not let it slip away. Cease your pointing and breaking.
Let the true evidence be exposed in broad daylight.
(Ningyuan’s place: A silver lamp illuminates the azure window; when the oil is exhausted, it still radiates light. As the dying embers fade with each tug, the ink-blackened wick rests upon the bed.
(3. Jifu) Xuefeng was once asked by Sansheng, "What does the golden fish that has passed through the net eat? The Master said, "I will tell you as soon as it comes out of the net.
[Sansheng] said, "Even the 'head-word' of fifteen hundred virtuous teachers is not enough."
The Master said, "The affairs of this old monk’s abbotship are many.
Baofu Zhan said, "Contention is insufficient; yielding is more than enough. Cui峰 Xian said, "It is a pity he let him off.
He should have been given thirty blows; not even a single blow should have been spared. Truly, such a master is rarely encountered. Chengtian Zong [said]: [As above].
It is said: "To cast a net that covers the heavens, one must be Xuefeng; to enter deep into the tiger’s den, one must be Sansheng.
Some fellows say that Xuefeng was within the net and Sansheng was outside the net. Alas, alas! This deeply wrongs the ancients.
Were it not for these two masters, they could not have roamed freely throughout the world. Yangqi Zhe said: "Sansheng is acceptable."
It is said that at Longmen, ten thousand fathoms high, one is accustomed to being a guest;
at Xuefeng, it was as if Mengchang’s gate were open—how could he fear a distinguished visitor? Baofeng Wen said: "Excellent! Excellent! Joyful! Joyful! It is just like a hawk."
"Do not be startled. Baoning, however, was not like that. "What does a golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eat? I will tell you once you have managed to get out of the net.
[Baoning] did not even recognize the "critical phrase" (huatou) of the Great Master of fifteen hundred disciples.
Thereupon, [Zhaozhou] seized his staff and drove him out through the triple gate. He then said, "This is truly a source of great joy; it is just like a tiger—do not move!"
[Zhen] said: "All you Chan masters, how does Baoning’s 'happiness' compare to Sansheng’s 'happiness'? Is there anyone here who is truly happy?
Come forward and let us settle this. After a long silence, he said: "I take him by the hand and pull, but he will not enter.
Jingshan Gao said: "One person is as coarse as a mountain; another is as fine as rice flour. Although their coarseness and fineness differ, when weighed on a scale, they are light."
Precisely so. Today, Jingshan gives you a true and sincere announcement: you all must strictly avoid "drilling the tortoise shell" or "beating the roof tiles.
Furi Zhe said: "The conduct of Sansheng was extraordinary; Xuefeng was accustomed to seizing such opportunities.
One pressure and one nudge—their functional application was their specialty; one release and one withdrawal—their arrowheads struck the mark. The dragon ascends the vast ocean; the crane dances."
Danyuan: "Though each displayed his own strategies, when scrutinized, it was like planting thorns on level ground;
even now, after all these years, they remain largely unweeded from within the thickets. Is there anyone here now who can weed them out? Sanxing and Xuefeng are beneath your feet.
If not, do not speak of a golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net—even a mud-scorpion cannot be said to have done so."
"It is so. The *Dandu Yiyun* says: "Because of practicing with arms swinging, the wind fills the sails. This is the path of the patch-robed monk;
how could it be within the bells and chimes of an ancient temple? Is it not the case that an old Mahā who has shrunk his feet stands ten thousand fathoms high against clay gods and earthen Buddhas?
Fifteen hundred mangy dogs gnaw at a withered stump; here and there, one or two swift hawks circle."
The clever hare, however, allows the leopard to establish its majesty, which can then be relied upon in the shadows; the dragon gains the clouds, whereby its transformations become divine.

A good spiritual friend, encountering such a person, fails to recognize the principle of "responding with voice and seeking through breath," instead spending his days by the side of the long meditation couch facing yellow-mouthed śrāmaṇeras, wielding staffs and shouts, mistaking the cry of a crane for the song of a nightingale. This is truly a great sorrow for the man of ambition.
How extraordinary! Nevertheless, this mountain monk still has thirty staffs with which to strike Sansheng. Why?
When we are hungry, we should seek food from Xie Renzu; there is no need for the rice of Tao Hunu.
A golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net—do not say it lingers in the water. It stirs the heavens and the earth, shaking its mane and wagging its tail.

A thousand-fathom whale rushes forth as great waves surge; with a single roar, thunder shakes and a pure breeze arises. As the pure breeze rises, who among those in heaven and on earth knows how many such there are?

(Cuifeng Xian): An aged fisherman sits upon his fishing platform; golden-scaled dragons surge forth, drumming the waves as they come. The sea-gate is vast and empty, yet he casts his net; with a single thunderclap, heaven and earth are opened. (Zhenjing Wen): An aged fisherman sits upon his fishing platform; golden-scaled dragons surge forth, drumming the waves as they come.
The sea-gate is vast and empty, yet he casts his net; with a single thunderclap, heaven and earth are opened.
Seizing the waves and grasping the clouds, its momentum is startling; a sudden rain across the void pours like an overturned basin.
Had it not been for the releasing of the Huaihe sluice-gates, the tide-head at the Nine Bends would never have settled.

(Shangfang Yi) Within the cave there are no clouds, yet another world exists; the peach blossoms are like brocade, the willows like cotton wool. The immortals do not concern themselves with reckoning winter.
Summer. The rocks crumble and the pines wither; this is one year.
(Wuzu Yan) A swift hawk soars toward the heavens; a cold rooster sleeps at dawn. Shedding all habitual nests and lairs, neither slow nor fast is partial.

When the life-root is severed, let go in the moment of urgency; when the hands and feet are right before you, strike while they are relaxed. When a drop of water turns to ice, do not fail to recognize it. Planning from within the tent.
The vastness of the ocean is encompassed within the curtains. Have you not seen? The golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net has a new livelihood;
the head monk’s affairs are so many they bring laughter to one's death.
(By Yuetao Chang) As the first waves arise, clouds and thunder send them forth; leaping with majestic vigor, behold the Great Function. Clearly, the "burning of the tail" marks the crossing over.

At the Dragon Gate, the magnificent whale is unwilling to linger in the pickle jar. A matured man does not startle the multitude; accustomed to facing great adversaries, he has no fear from the outset.
Floating freely, he is as light as five *liang*; yet towering, he is more than a thousand *jin* in weight. His lofty fame spans the four seas—whom else could it share?
Standing firm like a pillar, he is unmoved even by the eight winds. (Tiantong Juexian)
The song-board beats in time with the city watchtowers; clear songs compete on the painted boats. As the boat travels through the night on the sands, my aging eyes see nothing but boundless expanse.

(By Yang Xi Sen) Xuefeng received one tangerine and one orange each, sent by the King of Min as a mark of his favor, and dispatched a messenger to deliver them. He wrote a letter inquiring: "Since it is..."
[The Emperor asked: "The colors are generally the same; why are the names different? The Master returned the tangerine with its original seal intact.
The Emperor again sent a messenger to question Xuansha. Xuansha then covered it with a sheet of paper.
Tuyin said: "The feet of these two elders were not planted firmly on the ground; they were deluded by those two tangerines and both failed to escape being ridiculed by the King of Min.
Falin Yin said: "Had I seen them at that time, I would have simply called out to the messenger.
Once he responded, I would have told him to go back and describe the situation clearly."
Bring forth the tangerine; there is no need for doubt. For an iron ox to be bitten by a mosquito must be sheer folly.
Even King Min has not yet understood the Master’s intent; I ask Xuansha to strike him once more with the awl.
(Yanshou Hui) Clearly distinguish the tangerine and do not confuse it; offer flowers and borrow water to discern the dragon from the snake. A single sheet of white paper covers it all.
Understood! To spare the world from raising arms and weapons.
(Yezufuan) A single color, yet two different names; a paper covering cannot deceive the eyes of the multitude.
When the Old Man Xue first sent it back, King Min had not yet ceased his doubts. (Hengchuan Gong)
Xuefeng addressed the assembly: "The entire earth is this gate of liberation; yet, even with hands extended to pull one in, no one enters.
At that time, a monk came forward and said, "Master, you cannot blame me. Another monk said, "What is the use of entering?
The Master then struck him.
Cui Feng Xian said: "Among these three, one person receives salvation. If you cannot discern this at all, how many people are there on level ground?
Longchi Chuan said: "It is just like those two monks who both understood [the teaching].
Yet, when they arrived here, why was it that one received a blow of the staff while the other did not? Miaojue Hui said: "The old fellow Xuefeng is oppressing and pressuring people."
"What is it? [The Master asked. "Since you have arrived here, why is your nose in another's hand? After a long silence, he said:
"Gazing greedily at the moon in the sky, one loses the oar in one's hand. Falin Yin said:
"As for these two monks speaking in such a manner, did they enter the gate or not?"
The great earth is a gate of liberation; the Buddhas of the three periods swallow it all in one gulp.
Thinking Xuefeng had something extraordinary, you have come to deceive my fine descendants.
(Lan’an Shu) Once, while on a work assignment, Xuefeng was carrying a bundle of rattan himself when he encountered a monk on the path and dropped it down. The monk—
He was about to take hold of him when the Master gave a single kick and sent him tumbling down. Upon returning, he related this to Changsheng, saying, "I just now kicked that monk;
it felt truly exhilarating. Changsheng said, "The Master must first replace that monk in the Nirvana Hall before you can feel such satisfaction."
Cui Feng Xian said: "Changsheng is much like a family member dying in the east and a family member in the west helping with the mourning;
he too deserves a kick. Baizhang Yuan said: "Xuefeng wins five hundred outside the gate, but loses one thousand within the house.
Fushan said: "This monk took a kick from Xuefeng; a small gain met with a great opportunity. Changsheng took [the kick]..."
Cui-feng’s single kick brought disaster upon his own house; they were all men of the Nirvana Hall. Ruiyan Yun said:
"This monk ate Cui-feng’s single kick and saw ghosts in broad daylight; Changsheng ate Cui-feng’s single kick and became an immortal on level ground.
Master Fushan, great as he was, missed the mark by no small amount. Nantang Yu said: "Xuefeng was indeed a master of descending..."
The slope does not move; a swift opportunity is hard to encounter. Were it not for Changsheng, one would have labored in vain without merit.
Nevertheless, how does Xuefeng’s single kick compare to Xuedou’s single kick? Kai-xian Jin said, "Great and small, Baiyun has missed much.
Little did he know that while Xuefeng lost five hundred outside, he won one at home."
A Hook: Darkly casting fragrant bait upon the river’s edge, He truly catches a golden-scaled fish to bring home.
Had it not been for the swift reeling in of the line, He would have nearly lost it to the heron. (Shangfang Yi)
Xuefeng and Xuansha were beside a bamboo fence. Xuansha asked, "Is there Buddha-dharma even here by the fence?
The Master said, "There is. Xuansha asked, "How so? The Master shook the fence once. Xuansha said, "I do not see it that way."
The Master said, "And what about you, my son? He replied, "Pass through the head of the bamboo splints.
Guangrun Rong said, "If someone asks, 'At this very moment, is there still Buddha-dharma or not? what would you say? He replied, "There is.
"How is there? He said to him: "Internally, nothing is emitted; externally, nothing is admitted."
Father and son walk hand in hand into the old garden; Passing by the short fence, they lean on their bamboo poles. In the thick mud there are thorns, yet no one sees them;
Only when they step upon them do they realize their feet are pierced.
(Lan’an Shu) Xuefeng ascended the hall and, raising his whisk, said: "This is for those of middling and lower capacities. A monk then asked: "Suddenly—"
When a superior person arrives, how do you respond? The Master also raised his whisk. The monk said, "This is for those of middling or inferior capacity.
The Master then struck him.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "I am not like Xuefeng, who beats upon complications. He then took up his staff and said, "This is for..."
When people of middling or inferior capacity suddenly encounter a person of superior capacity coming toward them, what then? [The Master] strikes. Huguo Yuan said:
"In the house of a patriarch, there is seizing and releasing, there is killing and giving life. If one were to rub an itch on the head of a snake, it would not be like this either.
He took up his staff and said: "This [staff] is for people of middling and inferior capacity. But when suddenly encountering a person of superior capacity coming toward them—"
"How so? [The Master] replied, "I simply do not engage in the entanglements of Yunmen.
Chexi Chong said, "Although Xuefeng and Yunmen wield the power of killing and giving life with great spirit, when scrutinized, they are still merely adding branches where there were none.
According to Chexi’s own view," he then held up his whisk and said, "I shall take this very thing and universally provide for all."
Whether high, middle, or low, people may unfurl [the banner] as they please; they may take it up as they please. At every place, the vital pass is cut off;
each individual stands like a wall ten thousand fathoms high. But when one of those who have entered this midst comes, what then?
"The hearts of the ten thousand nations are intoxicated as they taste the great cauldron; together we shall lead each other’s hands up to the high terrace. — Yuanzhao.
Sansheng said: "Xuefeng held up his whisk; when Yunmen asked him a question, he struck him. I, Ciweng, am not like that.
If an eminent superior person were to suddenly encounter me, what would I say? I would simply say: 'Go! You are not the right person.'"

Lightning strikes faster than one can cover one's ears. To drive in the stake, one must act with urgency. If the water is deep and the stake’s base is long, the sound of thunder will rise up on all sides.
Picking up the staff, he does so for those of middle, lower, and superior capacity; yet he lets them pass without striking.
Once the people of Qin entered the Peach Blossom Spring, their descendants have been immortals for generations. (By Chang of Yuet Tang.
While at Guoqing Temple, Xuefeng held up his alms bowl and asked a presiding master, "If you can speak, I will give you this bowl.
The master said, "This is a matter concerning the transformation-buddhas. The Master said, "You have not even become a servant to a presiding master yet."
[The host] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Ask me and I will tell you. Just as the host was about to prostrate, the Master tripped him over.
Later, the host related this to Yunmen, saying, "It took me seven years before I finally saw [the truth]. Yunmen said, "It took you seven years before you finally saw it?
[The host] replied, "Yes. Yunmen said, "You will need another seven years before you truly attain it."
Cui Feng Xian remarked regarding the matter of the transformation Buddha, "I only fear that you will leave the Master at a loss.
At the end, he added separately, "The bandit has been utterly defeated. Falin Yin said, "Wait for him to say, 'Only after seven years shall I see it,' and why not immediately give him a bowl?"
Xuefeng was once asked by the King of Min, "I intend to build a Buddha hall; what do you think of that?
The Master said, "Great King, why not build a Hall of the Empty King? The King said, "I request the Master to strike me. The Master extended both hands.
Yunmen Wenyan said: "In one stroke, forty-nine.
The son of the Empty King’s palace. Xuefeng spread his two hands, adding: "The old man of Shaoyang, in one stroke, forty-nine."
Always facing south, one gazes at the Northern Dipper.
(Jue of Ji'an) Once, while Xuefeng was gathering firewood with the community, he encountered a monk on the road;
he then threw down a piece of wood and said, "The entire Tripitaka speaks only of this."
Zhēnrú Zhé said: "The entire Great Canon of Teachings does not speak of this. Tiānníng Qí said: "What is this very thing?
Let aside for a moment whether it is spoken of or not; where do you all see these two elders? Zhōngyuè Nén held up his whisk and said:
"If you lift it up, it is 'Thus have I heard. If you let it down, it is 'Believing and accepting, we shall practice.'"
At every place, green willows are fit for tethering horses; at every household gate, one penetrates to Chang’an.
The great road is as level as the palm of a hand, yet it is difficult for people of this age to set foot upon it.
(Cishou Shen) The waters of the Ru flow toward the east; the waters of the Chu come from the south; all return to the great ocean, where salt and fresh share the same flavor.
A patch-robed monk who possesses the eye at the crown of his head—try to discern its depth therein.
(Fóxìng Tài) *Zōngjiàn Fálín*, Volume 44; *Zōngjiàn Fálín*, Volume 45.
In the *Jiyun Tang* [Collection],
it is recorded that when Xuefeng sent the Elder Nanji forth from under the Sixth Patriarch Dajian, he performed a woman’s bow. Nanji folded his hands and responded, "Yes, yes."
The Master struck his forehead with his hand and returned home.
Falinyin said: "Xuefeng saw Nanji; Nanji did not yet see Xuefeng. When seeing off guests, one should provide according to the means of one's household;
by sending them off with full sincerity, one avoids giving rise to doubt. Yet, one is instead favored with a heavy burden of excessive courtesy."
A Gift. Folding his hands, he knows from afar that [the monk] is returning at dusk.
(Touzi Qing) Once, when a monk asked Xuefeng, "What is the first phrase? the Master remained silent for a long while. The monk reported this to Changsheng.
Sheng said, "This is the second phrase. The Master ordered the monks to ask, "What is the first phrase?
Sheng said, "Heaven! Heaven!
Gufeng Xiuyun remarked, "The two elders shed tears like this because their hearts are pained; yet as for the first phrase, it has not yet been reached."
In a dream, Xuefeng led two hundred followers to the place of Master Fuyang. He asked, "May I stay at your monastery to spend the summer retreat?
Fuyang took his staff, drew a line on the ground, and said, "If you cannot step over this, then speak. The Master was speechless.
The *Longchi zhuan* says: At that time, Xuefeng should have simply said lightly, "I know your compassion, Master.

He then summoned the assembly and told them to take up residence as they pleased. This would have been like floating down the river in a narrow robe or selling a cloth trouser—nothing could have stopped him.
Xuefeng addressed the assembly: "I have already met you at Wangzhou Pavilion; I have already met you at Wushan Ridge;

I have already met you before the Sangha Hall. Later, Baofu asked Ehu, "Setting aside for a moment the meeting before the Sangha Hall, where did you meet me at Wangzhou Pavilion and Wushan Ridge? Ehu strode away.
Fangzhang. Fubian then entered the Sangha Hall.
Cuifeng Xian said: "The two elders were indeed correct; they only knew that Xuefeng let go, but they did not know that Xuefeng held fast.
Yunju Qi said: "As for these two venerable masters, tell me, did they understand or not? When they met face-to-face..."
[They] met face to face. Jianfu Can said: "The old man Xuefeng has already exhausted the salt and vinegar.
Nowadays, when monks enter the gate, ascend the hall, and meet their host, they stubbornly clasp their hands at their chests and further seek instruction on a 'place of seeing.
To chew bitter gallroot with its roots intact is not yet the ultimate suffering. Wushi Dao said: "Xuefeng laid out [the path]."
A vast net spread across the heavens to catch phoenixes and dragons. Baofu and Ehu have, for no reason, run right into it;
to this day, they cannot emerge from it. Is there anyone now who can pass through? [He] strikes the meditation staff and says:
"Sparse, yet nothing leaks through. Yuan-an Yu said: "I ask the Master to go down to the Nirvana Hall. Fa-lin Yin said:
When these two great elders meet in this manner, when have they ever even dreamed of Xuefeng?
At Wangzhou, Wushi, and before the hall, they meet and encounter one another ten thousand times over;
yet it is only at Gao’an and Baofu that their meeting allows for such shifting and changing. (Fenyang Zhao)
Lotus fibers draw in whales and turtles; a needle’s point rolls as mustard seeds are cast. At Wàngzhōu and Wūshí Lǐng, before a note is even sung, the response is already given.
The Great Táng beats its drum and Xīnluò performs its dance; face-to-face presentation, yet they do not see one another.
(Yuánwù Qín) Deep within the hall, there have long been two or three; originally there is nothing, so what more could there be? When the deluded see this, they give rise to joy.
Joy! When the makers meet, their faces are full of shame.
(Longmen Yuan) Gazing afar at Wuzhi Peak before the Sangha Hall, they take long strides and bow their heads across the great thousandfold world.
If one is a cub of the man-eating lion, turning over does not depend on the tips of blades of grass. (Yiweng Ru)

The lingering cold remains in the mountain stream, while color blooms upon the pines; The slanting sun at the stone gate brings spring to the tips of the grass. Clouds and mist do not forbid the coming and going;
Let us inquire: how many people are there in the monks’ hall? (Lingyan Chu) To till the land one needs oxen;
to travel the road one needs horses. Originally, this was not Zhang San; why then call him Li Da? After a long silence...
"Clouds, alas! (The monk steps forward.
A single verse of the *Li Sao* stirs the courts of Chu; the Three Xiang and Seven Lakes are all filled with sorrowful sentiment. The sound of resentment shall endure for a thousand ages;
one simply pours forth one’s loyal heart to its very depths. (Yingzhang Jie)
My heart is truly most sincere; I have laid bare my innermost feelings to tell you all. Yet you, a man of boundless kindness, do not understand me;
leaning against the railing, I waste my thoughts in silent brooding.
(Tianjie Min) One day, while burning fire in the monks' hall, Xuefeng closed both the front and back doors and cried out, "Help! Put out the fire!"
"Extinguishing the Fire. Xuansha took a piece of firewood and threw it through the lattice window. The Master (Shishuang Qingzhu) immediately opened the door.
"Burning logs until they glow red-hot, warming the whole body; the joy is difficult to contain—a spring fills the entire house.
Had it not been for Layman Xie coming to join the fire, who would have known there was someone freezing outside the gate? (Shilin Gong)
Xuefeng was performing communal labor to clear a field when he saw a snake. He lifted it up with his staff and called to the assembly, saying, "Look!
Look! Then, with a blade, he cut it in two. Xuansha tossed the staff behind him; the assembly was all struck with astonishment. The Master said, "How magnificent!"

Jiashan Yu said: "Xuefeng and his son are in a state of desperate urgency; they are merely playing with a dead snake. They do not realize that when the law is fully applied, there are no subjects left.
Do you know of the one who leaves open a single thread? When the vast ocean has been fished out and the fishing boats return at dusk, a single pure song arises from a secluded heart.
Jiashan Ren said: "The old man Xuefeng and his son play with a live snake as if it were dead."
The Old Man of the Mountain played with a dead snake as if it were alive. If Yao-feng had seen the snake, he would have beaten the grass to startle it.
Once, when a monk was prostrating, the Master struck him five blows. The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie?
The Master struck him another five blows and shouted him out.
Cui Feng Xian said, "I have never entangled myself in complications with anyone. The first five blows were like the sun shining upon the world;
the latter five blows were like clouds rising to bring rain. If you can discern this, I shall likewise give you five blows.
Wuwei Shou said, "This monk’s forehead is pressed to the ground, yet his transgressions fill the heavens. Xuefeng was lenient toward him, yet he still does not know his own guilt. Once again—"
This is an unforgivable transgression. To further claim that "the sun shines upon heaven" or that "clouds rise and bring forth rain" is to delude later generations. What does this mean?

"Having once suffered the bitterness of snow and frost, one is startled even by the falling of willow blossoms. Dongchan Guan said: "The nature of emptiness is spontaneous; the nature of directness is natural."
This is not like Cui Feng’s deception of people. Of the monks struck by Xuefeng with the first five blows, one bowed;
of those struck by the latter five blows, the other had committed no fault. Tell me, is it so or not? If you say it is, what need is there for your eyes? Jia-shui Qian said:
"Xuefeng was much like a golden-winged garuḍa cleaving the sea to seize and swallow the dragon straightaway. Xuedou has misjudged the ancients.
The man bought straw sandals again and set out on his journey. Tell me, where did his fault lie? If you cannot discern this, you shall receive five blows of the staff as well.
Meiweng Gaō said: "For the first five blows, the mouth should be closed and not opened; for the latter five blows, the mouth should be opened and not closed.
If this is so, one has a share in receiving the blows; if it is not so, Xuefeng shall eat them himself."
It is attained. Why? A man of the forest binds himself with a fine rank; a person of meager fortune is not enriched by windfall wealth.
Though the first arrow is light, the subsequent arrow is deep; once it leaves the bowstring, life itself perishes.
Only upon waking and being pricked again by the golden needle does one realize that the former ailment was no light matter. (Haizhou Ci)

One pluck fills the air with sorrow, silencing the wild geese; A second stroke brings forth lamentation, weeping for the spring cuckoo. This sentiment no one understands; The east wind carries it ten thousand miles away.
(Tie-rong Xuan) Xuefeng asked a monk, "What is your name, *sāriputra*? The monk replied, "Xuánjī. The Master said, "How much do you weave each day? The monk replied, [silence].
"Not a single thread hangs [upon you]. The Master said, "Go to the meditation hall. As soon as the monk had walked three or five paces, the Master said, "Your kashaya has fallen to the ground.
The monk turned his head back; the Master then struck him.
Skillfully weaving a spiral pattern, not a single thread is revealed. Borrowing your shuttle to manifest the entire mechanism;
when a single fine line is applied, it is like brocade—only to be struck in the face by a wild wind.
(Hongding Jiao) Once, while the assembly was in session at Xuefeng, a monk said "Zhenzhong" (take care) and departed. The Master said, "If everyone were like this monk..."
The monk asked, "How much mental effort and strength does this save? Xuansha said, "If you, Master, receive people in such a manner, you will blind the eyes of the entire city of Min.
The Master asked, "And what would you do? Xuansha said, "I would simply give him thirty blows of the staff.
The Master said, "In the future, no one will be able to deal with you."
The two go together on their original mission; they travel straight to the capital where profits are doubled.
Regardless of heaven and earth, or how bright the stars and moon may be, they gather it all up and marry it to the East Wind.
(Yongning Ding) Chan Master Gao Tingjian of Xiangzhou (a successor of Deshan Jian): When he first visited Deshan, he joined his palms from across the river. Gao—
Sheng said, "I do not understand. Shan beckoned him with a fan, and the Master immediately attained enlightenment; he strode off crosswise and never looked back.
Jingzhao Daoyuan said, "Gao Ting strode off crosswise; I grant that he was a clever monk. But if one were to..."
To say that he was a dharma heir of Deshan is not yet permissible. Why? Because he still remains on the opposite bank of the river from Deshan. Tiantong Ruyi said:
"All quarters claim that with a single glance between master and disciple, the 'cracking' and the 'pecking' occur simultaneously.

But what connection is there? Do you wish to see Deshan at Gaoting? He then descended from his seat. Tianning Weiqing said: "Among the assembly, some discuss this, saying that Gaoting saw [the truth]."
Deshan would not speak with others but simply departed. Thus Miaoxi said, "He is still separated from us by the river.
Have you ever dreamed of Gaoting? [The Master] picks up his staff and says, "One should have called him back and given him a beating.
Now tell me, was this a reward or a punishment? Qingshan Xiu says: "Jingshan’s alternating raising and striking is like drawing one's bow after the thief has already fled."
Nowadays, people have spent twenty or thirty years at the gate of intellectual knowledge. Since they are no longer separated by a river, how should they proceed?
One knows the strength of a horse when the road is long; one sees the true heart of a person after many years.
Meeting upon the river, they asked about staying; master and disciple were like needle and magnet, instantly attuned.
Dingguang beckoned from afar at Jingu; Zhiyi nodded his head in the dark at Jiangling.
(Dahong Su) Deshan stares with eyes wide open inside a coffin; Gaoting hides his body within stagnant water. How many heroic spirits have they deceived!
Han: Mistaking mountains and rivers for one’s own eyes.
(Muzhou of Shaoshi) Leaving the White Emperor Castle at dawn amidst colorful clouds, he returned to Jiangling from a thousand li in a single day.
The cries of monkeys on both banks never ceased, yet the light boat had already passed ten thousand layers of mountains. (Juyin Xuan)
Gao Ting was once visited by a monk from under the guidance of Jia Shan. As soon as the monk prostrated himself, the Master struck him. The monk said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects;
why do you strike me immediately? The Master struck him again and drove him out. When the monk returned and related this to Jia Shan, Jia Shan asked, "Do you understand?
The monk replied, "I do not understand. Jia Shan said, "It is fortunate that you do not understand. Had you understood, it would have been Jia Shan [who was at fault]."
[The monk] was speechless.
Tiantong Hua said: "Gaoting, for a time, could not restrain his impatience; yet how could he help it? He let the staff pass too quickly.
Had that monk been a true man at that moment, let alone Gaoting or Jia Shan—even Master Bodhidharma himself would have been unable to act."
"Come forth! I shall also cut you into three pieces. Why? Because a family prospers through filial sons, and a state achieves hegemony through strategic ministers.
Jingci Ming said, "Gaoting and Jia Shan each established their teaching styles with perfect appropriateness;
however, one among them was slightly off the mark. Tiantong speaking thus is like a tea jar from Gong County.

Chan Master Shiyuan (d.u.), the seventh-generation descendant of Da Jian, was a successor of Yantou Huo. He resided at Ruiyan in Dancheng. Sitting upon a large rock all day long, he appeared as if he were an ignorant fool.
Every day he would call out, "The Host! and when there was a response, he would say, "Be alert! Be alert! Hereafter..."
"Do not let others deceive you. Later, a monk visited Xuansha. Xuansha asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "Ruigyan.
Xuansha asked, "What words or phrases did he use to instruct his disciples? The monk recounted the previous conversation. Xuansha said, "In one sense, it is all a matter of playing with the spirit;
yet, it is truly extraordinary. He then asked, "Why did you not simply remain there? The monk replied, "He has already passed away. Xuansha—
He asked, "Now, would you still be able to respond? The monk had no reply.
Cui-feng Xian said, "Alas! Alas! Bao-ning Yong spoke on behalf of the monk, saying, "Why does the Master not hear me when we face one another?
Yun-ju Yuan said, "All the patriarchs under heaven have provided words for this monk."
It is like when someone in the eastern house dies and those in the western house offer their condolences;

even if Ruiyan were to emerge from within himself, it would still be but staring eyes from inside a coffin. Zhaojue Qin said: "The cold pool of Baizhang reaches its depths; the moon is in the heart of the waves at a thousand fathoms.
Rock pines lean against the heavens, and wind arises in the secluded valley. It is utterly majestic in its solitary standard and serene in its refined bearing."
When the moon leaves the azure pool, its reflection remains in the path of the clouds; thus, one passes right by what is before one’s face.
At that time, had this been a man of true mettle, upon hearing [Xuansha] say, “Can you still respond to it right now? he would have immediately let out a shout.
This would not only have cut off the vital ford of Xuansha, but would also have avenged the old master Ruiyan. Daming Zhi said: “I exhort you...”
"Let us drink another cup of wine; once we pass the Yang Pass to the west, there will be no old friends. Jingshan Xiu said: "To startle the multitude, one must be a man of heroic spirit;
to overcome the victor, one must be a lion cub. This monk only knows how to transmit words and deliver messages;
he cannot turn back and leap from the precipice. Not only has he missed Ruizhan, but he has also missed Xuansha. Ruizhan.
Yunwen said, "The Patriarch’s play with this one case can truly be called transcending the present and surpassing antiquity. Yet, he only managed to be a son who guards the family estate.
Here, one must cast open a single eye; not only to inherit the ancestral legacy, but to break through the tower and leap over the hearth.
Do you understand? A flash of lightning cannot reach it; a spark of fire is hard to pursue. The rabbit's path is not where the Great Elephant roams. [He then recited: "The rooster..."
Is millet ever the food of the phoenix? (A shout.

Calling out oneself and responding to oneself is already being wide awake; one is not deceived by others, for the principle is not slight. The fragrance of the white lotus in the pond has not yet ceased;
the mountain colors before the eaves are green throughout the four seasons. (By Baiyang Shun)
Suīyán constantly calls out, "The Host! It soars forth from the highest peak of Mount Sumeru. The great earth is overturned, yet there is no place to find it;
A single melody of wind and song resounds within the painted pavilion.

(Tiānyī Zhé) Those who study the Way do not recognize the Real, Simply because they have long been identifying with the spirit. Throughout immeasurable kalpas, they have wandered through birth and death.
The Source. The deluded call this the "original body" (no gate opens).
Before the wind, a single melody stirs feelings of parting; its tune is ancient, and no one can join in the harmony.
Singing it oneself and pouring for oneself, one drinks alone; even to this day, one remains unawakened. (Bieshan Zhi)
Deliberately staring at a skull to see ghosts, rising and falling by one’s own hand while feigning alertness—how many truly brilliant men have been deceived!
How few are there who can look right through to the very liver and entrails?
(Tianzhangyu) A string of cassia seeds, rhubarb, and *huanglian*—who has ever known such coolness in their innermost being? Two lines upon Xue Tao’s stationery...
Tears. Sent to those across a thousand mountains and ten thousand waters.
(Jueju Yun) At the peak of Guangwu Mountain, the sun’s shadow grows low; one cannot bear the birds crying in the green willows. Their every note awakens the traveler from Jiangnan;
the orange and citron trees are in bloom as I prepare for our parting. (Sixiu Wen)
One call, one response; rising by oneself and falling by oneself. How laughable is Ruiyan—when will he ever reach an end?
(Three circles) Ruiyan arrived at Jia Shan. Shan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Wo Long.
Shan said, "When you came, had the dragon already risen? The Master stepped forward and looked around. Shan said, "To apply moxa on top of a healed scar!"
[The master] sighed. The teacher said, "Venerable sir, why do you trouble yourself so much? Yangshan ceased his activity.
Weishan Zhe said, "Although Ruiyan was fierce and imposing, he could not avoid being excluded by the clear waters of Jiaoshan."
Jingshan Hongdao said, "If it were not for shooting the stone tiger at Lantian, I might have nearly killed General Li by mistake.
Ruiyan Yunwen said, "These two venerable masters push and shove one another like those skilled at wielding the Great Saber (Taie), who do not injure their own hands."
However, there are places where it reaches and places where it does not.
When Shuigan visited Yantou, he asked, "What is the fundamental principle? Yantou said, "Movement. The Master said, "What is it when there is movement?
He replied, "It is not the fundamental principle. The Master pondered this deeply. Yantou said, "If you agree with this, you have not yet shed the root."
"Dust! If you do not consent [to let go], you will sink forever into birth and death.

At these words, the Master attained realization. Dongta Ming said: "Using gold to trade for gold; the earthen jar is not left behind when it breaks upon the well-rim. Using a wedge to extract a wedge;
how could the water jelly ever separate itself from the shrimp? Even if Ruiyan’s lacquered bucket were swift, it would still be something a gentleman might enter."

Cunyan said: "Although that old fellow Yantou had the ability to 'open a path through the mountains and build a bridge across the waters' whenever he encountered them, alas, he lacked the hand to 'snatch away the food and drive the plow. If someone were to ask him today, 'What is the fundamental constant principle?
he would strike them across the spine with his staff. If they asked further, 'How is it when there is movement? he would say to them: 'The waves rise three times high and the fish transform.'"
"O Dragon! The deluded person is like one bailing out water from a pond at night.
A perfect pearl is not pierced; a great block of jade is not carved. What the Daoist practitioner prizes is the absence of sharp edges and corners.
Cast away the path of 'acceptance,' and root and dust become empty. Entirely free of dependence, one lives with vivid clarity. (Tiantong Jue)
A monk asked Ruiyan, "How can one deliberate so as not to fall into stages? The Master said, "It cannot be arranged. The monk asked, "Why can it not be arranged?
The Master said, "From the beginning, it has had no stages. The monk asked, "I wonder what rank or position it occupies?
The Master said, "It does not sit in the Hall of Universal Radiance. The monk asked, "Does it still transform and guide through principle? The Master—
It is said: His fame resounds throughout the three realms; where would he not be honored at court?
Layer upon layer of moss and lichen, yet purple qi abounds; the moon enshrouds the cinnabar cassia as the night stretches long. Beyond the era of Vipaśyin, the wheel of gold turns;
incense wafts from the forbidden palace as ten thousand nations pay their respects. (Xuchunyan)
Deep clouds lock the layered cliffs at midnight; the handle of the Dipper slants across as the moonlight fades.
Purple vapors swirl and condense before the break of dawn, while the myriad realms bow their heads to listen to the voice of Yao.

(May you, O Master, daily) not manifest the precious seal to discern the winds that come. This is far removed from the deeds of ancient wheel-turning kings; shifting positions and seizing the opportune moment, he restores the Correct Dharma.
Transformation: The eight regions of the barbarian lands all returned to the source. (Treading upon the white lotus.
Chan Master Daoxian of Luoshan in Fuzhou (a successor of Yantou Quanhuo) was invited by the King of Min to open the hall.
As the Master ascended the seat, he gathered up his *saṃghāṭī* robe and said, "Take care," then immediately descended from the seat. The King of Min stepped forward, took his hand, and said:
"How does this assembly on Vulture Peak compare to today? The Master said, "I thought you were but a common man.
Unable to restrain his amusement on the spot, he fully displayed his family style with a single roar. Though the paper and ink are as vast as mountains, they cannot record it all;
let the patch-robed monks cease seeking it within the realm of meaning. (Dongshan Cong)
An *udumbara* flower appearing in this world is most difficult to see; its extraordinary fragrance drifts in the cold morning breeze.
Were it not for the World-Honored One casting his compassionate gaze upon it, it would be treated as nothing more than a wildflower or weed by the roadside.

(From the *Bǎoyèyuán*) Beneath the seat of Mount Sumeru lies a tortoise; through the long passage of years, its shell has become most sacred. Yet, on this cool ground, it is being bored through by someone.
The Cavity. Where in the hexagram-text is the "Complete Person" (Zhengren) to be found?
(Shuangfeng Cun: A single path straight as a bowstring; for a thousand ages there shall be no peer. Even if there were the mechanism of the "gnawing arrowhead," the skull would be reduced to powder.

(Shaku Dōan) Rōzan, because of Baofu’s question, recalled how a monk once asked Yantou: "In the midst of the vast turmoil of the mundane world, how does one discern the host? Yantou replied, "A copper sand-pan filled to the brim with oil. "What is the meaning of this? the teacher asked. Baofu responded by calling out, "Great Master! (Dashi). Rōzan said, "Baofu! Baofu responded. Rōzan said, "He has already fallen into the weeds. Rōzan then said, "If you can speak like this, you will not fall into the weeds. He further said, "The ancients had their own ways; they did not rely on words and phrases. They were like a great general who, when the enemy army approaches, immediately strikes with his sword. If you do not strike at that moment, you will surely fall into the weeds. He then quoted the verse: "The great general wields the sword; / The enemy army is struck down. / If you hesitate for even a moment, / You will surely fall into the weeds. Rōzan said, "This is the way of the Buddhas and patriarchs. It is not something to be grasped through intellectual understanding. If you understand it through intellectual understanding, you are like a person who, having been struck by a sword, falls to the ground and dies. This is what is called 'falling into the weeds. If you can turn the sword around and strike back, you will not fall into the weeds. This is what is called 'the great general wielding the sword. "Agreed," he said. The Master remarked, "A monkey has entered the Dharma hall. The Master then asked Mingzhao, "If someone were to ask you now, what would you say?
Mingzhao replied, "An arrow piercing the shadow of the red sun."
Jingshan Daokai said: "A monkey enters the Dharma hall; an arrow pierces the shadow of the red sun.
Two ancient sages shoulder snow together to fill a well. He gave a shout. Tianning Weiqing said:
"If I were Luoshan, when he asked such a question, I would also give a shout. Now tell me: which was Tianning’s shout and which was Jingshan’s?"

Are these the same or different? When Layman Luo first visited Shishuang, he asked: "What is it like when arising and ceasing never cease? Shishuang replied: "You must become cold ashes and withered wood;
you must go where a single thought lasts ten thousand years; you must go where the universe is contained within a lid; you must go where there is pure clarity, utterly free of a single speck."
The Master did not attain realization. Later, he went to visit Yantou, who shouted, "Who is it that arises and ceases? At this, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Baen Xiu said, "If it were Wansong, he would have stopped right after the shout. Jingshan Xiuzhi said, "To kill a person, one must use a sword that kills.
Zifuhui said, "The great ocean does not harbor a corpse; the point of a needle does not admit a mosquito."
The two great elders have held up [the Way] for a thousand ages, each illuminating the other. Nowadays, people fall into error by clinging to words and phrases.
Which one possesses the living eye? Which one lacks the living eye? This is why they fail to accord with it, and why it is set aside.
Not only do they fail to recognize the two great elders, but they also fail to recognize Luoshan.
Chopping through the old tangles; smashing the foxes’ den. The leopard sheds its mist to change its pattern; the dragon rides the thunder to transform its bones.
*Du!* What is this thing that flickers so restlessly between arising and ceasing? (Tiantong Jue) Who is it that arises and ceases?
Strike at the nest and seize the plunder. Slay the blind turtle; rescue the lame tortoise. (Shaliu Huiguang)
Arising and ceasing without pause—who can understand this? A single strike upon the occasion penetrates the heavy barrier.
East and west are both the Road to Chang’an; vast and unconfined, one goes and returns of one’s own accord.
(Wuzhun Fan) Cold water sprinkled on boiling soup—the tongue does not leave the mouth. How pitiful, old Yantou; his compassion became a fault.
Majestic is the Lung-hsiang steed;
valiant is the tiger-like transformation. He overturns the military dispatches without resorting to expedients; the triple encirclement is successfully broken.
The siege of the firm city has ended; having returned in triumph, he lights his lamp to gaze upon his sword.

(Tianshui Guang) The forest is dark and the grass rustles in the wind; the General draws his bow by night. At dawn he seeks his white-feathered arrow, only to find it buried within the notch of a stone.
(And so, I am clumsy and dull-witted. In a dream I caught a thief; when my eyes opened, he lay by my pillow. A burst of laughter—how needlessly did I trouble myself!
Though it was needless, do not be negligent. A thousand fathoms of frosty cliffs strike one with chilling cold. (Mok-rik-jik)
Luo Shan was at He Shan. As he was seeing off his companion, Elder Ju, to the door, the Master took up his staff and thrust it forward once.
Ju had no reply. The Master said, "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; a single horse gives birth to twin foals. Later, a monk cited this to Shu Shan.
Shu Shan said, "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; a single horse gives birth to three tigers."
In spring there are a hundred flowers; in summer there is heat. In autumn there are cool breezes; in winter there is snow.
If there are no idle matters hanging upon the mind, it is truly a fine season for humanity.
(Zhao Tang I) Without treading the path before the gate, spring returns and another year passes. Fallen blossoms cover the ground in red; fragrant grasses stretch green to the heavens.

One day, Luoshan asked Yantou, "For thirty years you have been at Dongshan, yet you did not approve of Dongshan—is that so?
Yantou replied, "It is. Luoshan said, "Does this not mean that you are a successor of Deshan?"

"Furthermore, you did not approve of Deshan. "Is that so? Tou said, "It is so. The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment your lack of approval toward Deshan, as for Dongshan—where was he deficient?
Tou remained silent for a long while and then said, "Dongshan was a fine Buddha;
it was simply that he lacked radiance. The Master then bowed in worship.

Baiyan Fu said: "When the opportunity arises, he points directly face-to-face; when face-to-face, the opportunity is seized with agility. Huanzhu Huo may indeed be said to have thoroughly mastered this principle;
yet, being presented with a three-foot hat by Luoshan, he seemed as if he did not understand it at all.
One with an iron forehead and copper head; one with three heads and six arms. Both borrow the nostrils of others, yet they give vent to their spirit for Dongshan.
(Nanyuan Sheng) Refusing to acknowledge a master throughout the Great Tang, Luoshan’s prostration was a mistaken deliberation. Dongshan is a fine Buddha; people find him difficult to fathom.
How shameful! From the crag of shame and remorse, Yantou emits light. (Wan’an Yan) The strategist who lost the battle’s plan was no ordinary man;
the Dragon Spring on his tongue launched a secret assault from the shadows. How could he have known that as the fires of his hearth diminished, his troops grew ever more formidable?
To this day, one wonders how many heroes he has slain. (Xue Qi Jing)

Luo Shan, because of this, asked the Venerable Wuzhen: "As for Yantou’s saying, 'Dongshan’s Buddha is simply without light,' I do not know what deficiency Dongshan had that he was told he was without light. The Master called out, "Zhen! Zhen responded.
The Master said, "Truly, it is a fine Buddha; it is simply without light. Zhen asked, "Why did the Great Master dismiss him [by saying he was without light]?"
Wuzhen spoke of a story. The Master said, "Where is the place where Old Teacher Chen set you straight? Speak quickly, speak quickly! Wuzhen was speechless.
The Master struck him thirty blows and drove him out. Wuzhen reported this to Zhaoqing. For an entire summer, Zhaoqing scolded him;
at the end of the summer, he came personally to question the Master, and Wuzhen recounted the incident clearly. Zhaoqing then prostrated himself in repentance.

I say: To blame the Great Master for speaking beyond the categories and uttering startling phrases is a grievous error. Deluded practitioners of Chan merely point and comment; yet, it is perfectly clear that this Buddha is without radiance.
Under these words, those who misunderstand the school are left in vain confusion. Fortunately, there is Zhaoyin of Qingsi;
for one summer he has clarified what was muddled and erroneous. Once the realgar is applied, he writes his hidden sorrows to the wise.
(Fóxìng Tái) A single drop can raise waves ten thousand fathoms high; a man’s livelihood need not be much. Look at Wang San from the western neighbor!
Sister-in-law: "Used to borrowing my mother-in-law’s shawl, she now bows directly to her.
(Tong Qiuyu) Luo Shan was staying in a hut on Mount Dayu. At that time, a monk took his leave to go to Shushan.
The Master said, "I have a letter for Shushan; may I give it to you? The monk stepped forward and said, "Please, I request it. The Master pointed with his hand toward the top of his head.
He then extended his hand and said, "How do you deal with this? The monk had no reply. Later, the monk went to Shushan and raised this story in the hall.
One monk asked, "Do you understand this story? The assembly had no reply. The monk said, "No one in the world can do anything about Great Ridge."
Wishing to entrust it to a postal messenger to be sent ahead of spring, The words were repeated with earnest care, the intent growing more intimate.
Yet it was mistakenly gathered up by a bystander; The distant mountains remain as ever, steep and azure.
(Bójì Jiàn) Chan Master Cóngfàn of Xiāngxī in Fúzhōu (a successor of Yántóu Huì). When a monk from Gǔshān arrived to pay his respects, the Master said: "How is it that you..."
"Are you not a monk from Gushan? He replied, "I am. The Master said, "Why does the pearl on your forehead not appear?
The monk had no reply and abruptly took his leave. As the Master saw him off at the gate, he called out, "Elder! The monk turned his head. The Master said, "Your belly is full of Zen.
The monk asked, "What kind of mental activity is yours, Master? The Master simply laughed loudly.
Yingshan Yin said: "This monk has lost his integrity in front and uprooted himself from behind. Why did Xiangxi let him pass at this point?
After a long silence, he said: "One must also know that there is a blade within the smile."
While Chan Master Shengshou Yan of Fuzhou (a successor of Yantou Huo) was mending his robes, a monk came to visit him. The Master held up the robe to show him, saying:
"This mountain monk has a single robe; I display it for all to see. The two strips of cloud-patterned cloth are divided; do not let the needle and thread be exposed.
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk had no reply. The Master said: "What have you been doing for so long?"
Yingshan Yin said on behalf [of the Master]: "Broken! Broken!
Old and heartless, I am too weary to speak of Chan. Raising up the monk’s robe to reveal the priority of the pivot—those two clouds and waters remain even now;
throughout the ages, no one has been able to mend them whole. (Xuejian offered this.)
Do not find fault with this old family tradition; its principles have never been lacking. Throughout my life, my heart has remained as one piece—how many people in this world know it?
(Meibai Yi) How could my words be considered excessive? My true nature has always been difficult to repay. For the most part, it returns to his very bones and marrow.
Separate. "The spirit of elegance truly does not reside in a sable fur cloak.
(Zhuofeng Yuan) Chan Master Hui-leng of Changqing in Fuzhou (a successor of Xuefeng Cun) was strolling with Baofu.
Baofu asked, "An ancient said, 'At the summit of Mount Miaofeng. Is this perhaps it? The Master said, "It is indeed so, but it is a great pity."
A monk asked Gushan about Changqing’s statement, “What was the meaning of saying this?
Gushan said, “If Master Sun had not spoken these words, one could say that skulls would cover the fields and white bones would stretch across the mountains.

Cui峰 Xian said, “Today, as we travel the mountains with this fellow, what do we seek? He added, “In a hundred or a thousand years, it will not be said that they are entirely non-existent; they truly are.”
"Too little. Lian'an Wang said, "The level field and shallow grass barely reveal his style; this is like drinking wine only when meeting a kindred spirit.
Even upon close examination, it still lacks half. Tiance Zhou said, "A slap across the mouth would have been appropriate."
If you can fix a single eye here, I allow that he may meet [the Master] amidst the level fields and shallow grass.
On the solitary peak of Miaofeng, the grass grows lush; who can clearly grasp it and receive it? It is not for those like Master Sun to discern its true end.
How many know that the skull has fallen to the ground? (Cui Feng Xian)
Eighty-four thousand, not just one by one; within the seven golden mountains, the seas flow on.
The summit of Mount Sumeru is as level as the palm of a hand. Who takes up the long pole to fish for the giant turtle?
(Cangtang Qing) Hand in hand we walk together—whom can we accompany? Before our eyes, who beholds Mount Sumeru? Clouds and mud do not separate the path we have come.
The Path. Entrusted to sons and grandsons, look at it everywhere.
(Fuxincai) Changqing ascended the hall and said: "When everything has been swept clean and put in order, you come forward and seek me out.
I strike you once across the back. If there is a blow that reaches you, you must feel shame; if no blow reaches you, you..."
Furthermore, where would you go to understand this?
Cui-feng Xian said: "Cui-feng does not say so. However, it has been thoroughly cleaned and tidied up. You must come forward and seek me out;
I shall strike you across the spine with a blow of my staff. If that blow reaches you, you will be grievously wronged; if it does not reach you..."
"I strike you! I level my account with you. But if you understand it in such a way," said Huanglong Qing.
"Changqing only knows how to be disjointed and bloated; he does not know the source of the Way. Cuifeng spreads out vines and pulls at branches;
he cannot avoid drifting with the waves. Baofeng, however, is not like this. Having cleared everything away until it is pristine, come forward and simply say: 'Do you understand?'"
"Go back to the hall. Even so, one must still have *saindhava* (salt) before it will do. Tiantong Jue said:
"Eating the monastery’s rice with a dead mouth and stretching out one's legs to sleep on the long benches—those who know shame are difficult to find."
Do you still know where Changqing’s staff fell? Thunder opens the hibernating burrows; lightning sears the tail.
It draws forth the towering head and horns. Tianning Qi said: "Among the assembly, some deliberate, saying: 'If one sits upon a pure ground, one must clear away all clutter.
To come forward and seek [the truth] is to deserve a beating. To seek is the illness; the staff is the medicine."
According to the path of Cui Feng, if a single staff reaches you, you will immediately suffer defeat; if no staff reaches you, he treats you as an equal.
Little do they realize that these two great elders—one digs the earth to create a pit, while the other levels the well and blocks the stove.
Everyone desires to bring about Great Peace through effortless means, yet alas, they instead meet with ridicule and laughter.
Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind upon this long ago, yet until this very day he has not attained the wondrous. Gunan said: "I, Gunan, am not like that.
Having swept everything clean and put it all away, you must come right forward; I shall strike you across the spine with a blow. If one blow reaches you, you will be spared."
Hide yourself away in a clean place; not a single blow shall reach you. You must understand for yourself how to make a living.
When a monk asked Changqing, "What is the True Dharma Eye? the Master said, "Having a vow, one does not scatter sand."
Baofu Zhan said, "One must not scatter sand anymore. Cui峰 Xian said, "A true master must certainly manifest the fundamental share [of the Dharma] to be seen;
one must not scatter sand. Furthermore, who among you is a person with the true eye who cannot be deceived?
Come forth and speak before the assembly! If you cannot speak it, Cui Peak will point it out for you one by one."
"With eyes open, it is right; with eyes closed, it is also right. Gu Nanmen said: "Changqing was cautious and fearful;

Baofu fed the ox from upstream; Cui峰 mixed mud and water. Although all of them applied the eye for the sake of the assembly, Gu Nanmen can nonetheless provide a substitute phrase to further pierce through [the meaning].
If you people wish not to be deceived by others, you must simply not rely on yourself."
Enough of this concealing.
How can the mountain of the power of vows be considered worthy of praise? Hiding their bodies yet revealing their shadows, they are as numerous as hemp seeds.
Had it not been for Baofu’s own direct witnessing, who would believe that Master Ling had scattered sand once more? (Bao Ye Yuan)
Changqing was once asked by a monk, "What is the speech that accords with the sages?
The Master said, "Because of your question, my mouth has become as straight as a carrying pole. The monk asked, "Why is it so? The Master replied, "What did you just ask?"
Zhaojue Qin said: "It is so, it is so. It accords with the occasion without error. Yet, how unfortunate that this causes such great alarm over a trifle!
Or when someone asked Daolin, he simply replied: "Master Zhi was no ordinary monk; the scissors were right there on the head of his bed."
Changqing said, "If it were all like today, the Old Barbarian would have cause for hope. Baofu said, "If it were all like today, the Old Barbarian would be utterly hopeless.
Baoci then asked, "To speak in such a way—is this a statement of mutual recognition, or is it not?"—Huanglong Nan.

Yunmen said, "It seems as it always has today; at Caoxi, the stream has been cut off. Tiantong Jue said, "The wealthy lament that a thousand mouths are too few; the poor regret that a single body is too many.
Yunjuzhuang said, "When the Old Barbarian had hope, gold was tested by stone; when the Old Barbarian had lost all hope, jade was tested by fire.
He struck his whisk and said: "One year’s spring has already passed; the terraces and pavilions are filled with lush green shade."
The heavens are high as wild geese soar into the clouds; the earth is solemn as crickets enter the grass to cry out.
It is entirely within the landscape of autumn, while the traveler’s sorrows follow the sentiments of a foreign land. (Dong-sou Ying) During the Changqing era, a monk asked:
"When a wild sheep hangs its horns from a branch, what then? The Master said: "A fellow of the weeds. [The monk] asked: "Hanging..."
"After the horn, what then? The Master said, "A chaotic clamor. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, what then? The Master said, "Before the donkey's business has departed, the horse's business arrives."
Cui Feng Xian said, "I would rather have my body shattered into fine dust than ever blind the eyes of a single sentient being.
Changqing added, "There is something more to this; even if a stag’s antlers have not yet emerged, it is like gazing toward one's hometown from ten thousand miles away.
Nantang Yu remarked, "If Changqing had answered in such a manner, he would have blinded the eyes of all people in the world."
Cui峰 said, "I will never let a single being's eyes go blind; from ten thousand miles away, one gazes toward the home pass.
Changqing entered the hall and said, "When meeting a fellow traveler on the path, they pass each other with shoulders touching; the lifelong task of study is then complete."
Cui峰 Xian said: "It is so, it is so. But if the needle cannot pierce and the wind cannot enter, what use is there?
Zhaojue Qin said: "Meeting a fellow traveler, they pass each other shoulder-to-shoulder; the lamp-post and the lantern together bear witness to the oath. Gunan Men said:
"Familiar faces fill the world, but how many can truly know the heart? Qianyuan Chang, having finished citing these, said: "And now—"
"What serves as the verification of the Way? [The Master] picks up his staff and strikes once, saying:
"Holding a hoe with empty hands, Meeting on the road, we pass each other arm-in-arm. Raising the eyebrows—do not let the moment slip away!
Throughout your life’s study, what have you clarified? Once awakened, it takes not even a single kṣaṇa. (Benjue I)
Changqing was once asked by a monk, "In the Western Heaven, they use a wax man as a test; I wonder what is used here as a test? The Master said, "An iron pill.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The large ones are large; the small ones are small."
Suiyan Yun said: "Changqing’s answering the question in such a manner was like greedily watching the wild geese in the clouds while losing sight of the boat at the ferryhead.
Each member of this assembly of mine considers themselves to be clutching the jewel of the divine serpent or cradling the raw gem of Mount Jing."

Furthermore, regarding such a critique, is there anyone who remains dissatisfied? After a long silence, he said: "If one attempts to reach it with the calculating mind, it will ultimately be difficult to realize;
the adept must be startled in secret."
Changqing was asked by a monk, "When there is a question and an answer, the roles of host and guest are clearly defined; but what is it like when there is neither question nor answer?
The Master said, "Everyone they meet says it would be best to retire from office, yet among those beneath the forest trees, not a single person has ever been seen."
Everyone says my mind has come to rest; But when questioned, where is there ever any ground? Words contradicting the heart—deceiving oneself;
In the swift river of karma, one drifts along at will.
(Zhimen Zu) Once, a monk asked Changqing, "How can one attain freedom from doubt and delusion? The Master then extended both hands. The monk...
He did not speak. The Master said, "Ask me again, and I shall tell you. The monk asked once more. The Master sat with his shoulders bared. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "How do you understand this? He replied, "Today the wind has risen.
The Master said, "Speaking thus does not settle one's understanding. What essential point among the ancients and the moderns can equal this?"
"Congratulations! If you can bring it forth, I will allow you to be the host of this dialogue. The monk simply stood there. The Master then asked, "Where are you from?
He replied, "A man from the north. The Master said, "Having traveled three thousand li from north to south, why are you practicing such falsehoods?
The monk was speechless.
When the hand is extended, ten thousand fathoms crumble; the dried river has no water, and the moon does not come.
If you have doubts, ask Master Pang separately: "Who accompanies the stone woman at Huangmei?
(Touzi Qing). Changqing asked a scholar, saying: "In Buddhism, there is that which sentient beings use daily yet do not know. Confucianism also says:"
"The common people use it daily without knowing. Not knowing what? Cui said, "They do not know the Great Way.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "Truly they do not know. Baoshou Xin said, "Changqing knows how to let go, but does not know how to gather it back in."
Yunmen’s “releasing what was not bound” means that even if you do not act in this way at all, you can only be made to carry straw sandals for the new monk.
Changqing ascended the hall; once the assembly had gathered, the Master dragged out a monk and said, "The assembly, prostrate to this monk!"
He spoke again: "This monk has a most profound depth; he has just instructed the great assembly to prostrate. The assembly was speechless.
Half a straw raincoat amidst misty rain, the morning wind is cold. In shallow waters, why bother casting down the fishing rod? Having caught a blind turtle, he uses it in vain as bait;
Suddenly laughing, he enters the marshy shallows of the *liǎohuā* flowers. (Baiyu Si)
The arrow that pierces the willow at a hundred paces when drawn; it shoots through the void in seven or eight shards.
Piteous indeed, one who mends the imperial robes finds no patron; in vain he forges the golden needle within the flames.
(Suyam Min) Changqing took up his staff and said, "If you recognize this, the business of a lifetime of study is finished."

One must diminish its majestic radiance. When meeting with the Sangha, proceed with gentle courtesy. This mountain monk’s perspective is what I wish everyone to know together:
What is this source? As for that source—strike him across the back with a staff, and he will awaken immediately, tearing asunder past and present.
Gunanmen said: "Cui-feng, too, let it pass. What is this source? As for that source—wait."
For thirty years, he struck [his disciples] on the spine with his staff as soon as they spoke. Why? Because what is true is difficult to conceal; what is false does not flourish.

Like a mirror or a placid lake, the azure depths are profound and still; though vast and boundless, one has never reached its source. Only the masterful hand of Wang Wei could capture this in a painting:
a single dot forms a dragon, complete in both places. (Baoning Yong)
The ice ridges snap the locks at the mouth of the Chang River; no one is seen coming along the bird-path. A gust of wind sweeps through the cultivated bamboos;
on the jade balustrade, the snow piles high. (Xinwen Ben) The spring source rolls on, its expanse boundless;
it is clear and still, as level as an opened mirror. Two places become dragons from a single drop.
Ink. How many have exchanged their very eyes? (Bao Ye Yuan) When one family has business, a hundred households are busy.
One invites the ridicule of others for being both too short and too long.
Yet I envy the gentleman on Mount Taihua, who throughout the year remains silent, beyond the reach of deliberation. (Shui Yue Ying)
