"You simply take the staff; I intend to put these words into practice.
Cui-feng Xian said, "In that case, you are relying on power to deceive others. But how can it be that a matter does not arise in isolation?
If this monk had been able to be cautious from the beginning and guard against the end, the staff would have had to be taken by Jing-qing himself."
Jingqing asked a monk, "What is that sound outside the door? The monk replied, "The sound of raindrops. The Master said, "Sentient beings are inverted;
they lose themselves and pursue external objects. The monk asked, "How about you, Master? The Master said, "I have not lost myself.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'not having lost oneself'? The Master said, "It is still easy to manifest one's person; it is difficult to speak from the standpoint of total liberation."
Huanglong Xin said: "To speak of 'difficult' or 'easy' is but to turn further away from seeing oneself. To ensure one does not lose sight of oneself, what sound would you call it right now?
Langye Jue said: "It may be attained, but it is very much like falling into a pit on level ground.
Fayun Xiu said: "Everyone knows the phrase for 'leaving the body. But as for the phrase for 'shedding the body,' can anyone say it? (After a long silence)..."
"In times of difficulty, one sees the mind of a true man. Yuansou Duan said: "Jingqing has years but no virtue; he loves to seek advantage for himself.
This monk was chasing after appearances and seeking out sounds, so he deserved to suffer humiliation. At that time, when Jingqing asked, 'What sound is that outside the eaves?
he should have simply let out a shout. Or perhaps, having said 'How about this? How about that?', he should have shaken his sleeves and departed. Even if—"
Jingqing had the means to capture him alive and in hand, yet it was of no use.
Shengfa Fa said, "Although Langye understood how to bend the straight into a curve, he certainly did not know what kind of sound this was.

Lian’an Guang said, "If the furnace is not hot, the stubborn ore is difficult to melt. At that time, had he waited for him to say, 'How about you, Master? [Langye] would have struck him across the back with his staff."
A blow of the staff! This does not merely sever the monk; it is rather a matter of head and tail being perfectly aligned.
When the sound of rain drops falls in the empty hall, even a master finds it difficult to respond. If you claim you have entered the stream, you still do not understand as before.
Whether it be so or not, rain falls in torrents across the southern and northern mountains.

(Cui-feng Xian) Outside the gate, between the eaves, the sound of dripping rain: sentient beings, in their inversion, pursue deluded emotions. How pitiable that they fail to realize the place where they themselves are not deluded;
though they emerge from the body, their essence remains unclarified. (Yue-tang Chang)
The sound of raindrops on the eaves is distinct and perfectly clear. If you are a traveler who has not yet returned home, it is all in vain to strain your ears to listen.

(By Baiyang Shun) Outside the gate, the sound of raindrops remains as before. No matter how skillfully one may speak of myriad things, how can they compare to reality? Throughout my life, I have cast my heart and courage toward others.
They gaze at one another as if they were strangers.
(Wan’an Yan) The young girl speaks like one who is dazed; all day long she has no heart for the loom.
She has transformed into a stone upon Wangfu Mountain, unaware of when her husband will return. (Yuejiang Yin)
Autumn rains drip through half the window as the night watch draws to a close; they disturb the beauty, leaving her sleep restless.
Who can share this solitary longing? Amidst the mist, it disperses into the waves of Lake Dongting.
(Yuanjian Jing) When Jingqing asked a monk, "How do you understand Zhaozhou’s story about drinking tea? the monk left. The Master said:
"A monk from Handan was learning the Tang gait.
Cui Feng Xian said, "This monk was not a person from Handan; why was he learning the Tang gait?
If you can discern this, I will give you some tea to drink. Nantang Yu said, "Jingqing personally saw that this monk was indeed a person from Handan."
Why did Cui峰 say "It is not"? He took up his staff, drew a stroke, and said: "Many have mouths but do not get tea to drink.
When a monk asked Jingqing, "Is there still Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year? the Master said, "There is. The monk said: "If so..."
"What is the Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the New Year? The Master said, "The Primordial Beginning inaugurates the reign;
all things are renewed. The monk said, "Thank you, Master, for your answer. The Master said, "Jingqing loses ground today.
Another monk asked Mingjiao, "Is there still Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the New Year? Mingjiao said, "No. The monk said, "Every year is a good year; every day is a good day."
Jiurui asked, "For what reason, then, is there none? Miaoyan said, "When Zhang Gong drinks, Li Gong gets drunk.
Jiurui remarked, "Old and decrepit as you are, you have a dragon's head but a snake's tail. Miaoyan replied, "Today Mingjiao has suffered a defeat."
Zhaojue Qin said: "If you say there is, you lose; if you say there is not, you lose. Where does the contradiction lie?
Today, if someone were to ask Chongning, 'Is there still Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year?
simply say, 'It is not in either of these two extremes. If they then ask, 'Why is it so? simply say, 'Chongning loses today,' just as the ancients did."
"Are people the same or different? Jingshan Gao said, "The two venerable masters—one stands atop the highest peak without revealing his head;
the other walks upon the deepest ocean floor without getting his feet wet. This is so, yet it cannot be said that there is not some degree of confusion here.
Suppose someone were to ask me, Upāsaka Gao, today: 'Is there still Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year?'"
There is none. He simply said: "Today, a troupe of servants in the tea hall is performing village songs and communal dances, playing with spirits and ghosts.
This so provoked the indignation of Dianxiong (Pointing to His Chest) that he hurled the Bowl-Mountain Peak.
It was cast beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, startling Kauṇḍinya so with terror and alarm that he fell backward, mounted his pillar, and leaped away."
The board-carrying Chan practitioner has his nostrils stuffed; he has crashed into Tianzhu Peak in Shuzhou.
The mountain deity of Anle Mountain, unable to restrain his impatience, comes forth, grabs him by the chest, and says:

"Venerable One, since you claim to be an Arhat who has emerged from the dust and toil of the twenty-five realms of existence within the three worlds and transcended birth-and-death with its limited segments, why do you still possess so much ignorance?"
This was one question. Unable to overcome his shame (*mala*), he retreated to the third seat inside the Buddha Hall and sat there.
As before, he patted his chest and ribs, saying, "In the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am honored. He said to himself, "Stop! Stop!
When the Venerable Gaofeng asked him about the Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year, why did he keep performing somersaults in the void? It was merely empty talk.
[He] deceived the people. After a long while, he said, "Upādhyāya Gao has lost ground today.

Tianning Qi said, "Whether there is Buddha-dharma or no Buddha-dharma, both Great Elders Jingqing and Miaojiao have sat squarely at the head and cut it off; they do not permit later generations to speculate upon it.
Miaoxi uses the mouth of empty space to wag his broad and long tongue, sweeping across the three thousand great thousandfold world-systems."

The *tathatā* of the Buddhas of the present and future, as well as that of sentient beings—ordinary and sagely, yin and yang, cold and heat, and all the calculations of increase and decrease—are bound together into a single phrase.
Herein, rolling up and unrolling are unimpeded; gathering in and letting go are free. What does it matter whether it is the beginning of the new year or the end of the old?
"Way has it; Way lacks it. Who dares to look directly at this? If you reach the gate of Tianning, you must still undergo further examination.
"In my youth, I once decided the battle lines between dragons and snakes; now in my decline, I sing like a young child. Dajue Sheng said:
"One person says 'it exists,' another says 'it does not exist. Both lose their advantage; they are bold and coarse of heart."
He realized there were thirty staffs and bestowed them all upon him at once. Now tell me:
do they belong to the side of Jingqing, to the side of Mingjiao, or to the side of the two monks? If you can discern this, you may walk hand-in-hand with the ancients.
Regarding the New Year Dharma: the answer is "it exists. For the month with fewer days, it remains as before—the twenty-ninth.
The jade dragon snaps the golden bridle and lets out a great roar amidst the clouds.
(Lan’an Shu, 2) Regarding the New Year Dharma: the answer is "it does not exist. If you understand this, you remain as before on the halfway point. Who will take up the small boat in the clear night?
Flute. Under the bright moon, he plays across Lake Dongting.
From a cup of seven treasures, he pours grape wine; upon golden-flower paper, he writes verses of *Qingping*.
In the quiet palace courtyard, no one sees him as he idly takes up the King’s jade flute and plays. (Xinwen Ben)
A secure and secret field, where spiritual powers are played; at the New Year of the Buddha-Dharma, both "existence" and "non-existence" lose their advantage.
All things are uniformly equal to empty space—how could one allow for the establishment of a fixed point? The wind upon the grass carries out the Patriarch’s command;
who says that when the thunder ceases, its resonance does not continue? (Yuánwù Qín)
In the New Year, the Buddha-Dharma spreads its true breeze; it makes one laugh at the old man on the street celebrating the year’s end.
Where can one go when the three-tiered waves are high? In vain do they try to determine the male and female with a pair of swords.
(Xuetang’s Verse) With oars for following the wind and oars for against the wind, as the waves surge and the billows crash, one’s spirit grows bolder. One song does not know heaven and earth.
(Qiao) To this day, people still admire such refined poetic style. (Byu-ran Pu) Small talk is hard to fathom during the days of plum rain;
in a single day, the weather shifts from sun to shade several times. The paper windows beneath the eaves dry and then get wet again;
the stone path before the gate grows damp and then dries once more. (Un-am Ryang)
Carving stone and boiling seawater—both can bring wealth to a nation. Though such hegemonic achievements may be said to be accomplished, they are by no means the measure of a true King.
(Liaorishao) When a monk asked Jingqing, "Is there still Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year? the Master replied, "There is. [The monk] said, "If so..."
"What is the Buddha-dharma of the New Year? The Master said, "In the first month of spring, it is still cold.
Jianmen Yong said, "Jianmen does not say so. If someone were to ask, 'What is the Buddha-dharma of the New Year?'"
"Looking toward the Way, it is still cold in the early spring. Xiangdao said this. Xian of Gushan asked, "Since these two statements are essentially the same, why is there a difference between them?
[Xiangdao] replied, "It is certainly not that one does not know the seasons and thus fails to reveal the spring light; however, as for the Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the New Year..."
Neither had they yet dreamed of such a thing.

Jingqing asked a monk, "What is that sound outside the gate? The monk replied, "The cry of a magpie. The Master said, "If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata."
Hearing sounds and seeing forms are not hearing and seeing; seeing forms and hearing sounds are what constitutes seeing and hearing.
If you wish not to incur karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma.
(Wan’an Yan) Once, when a monk asked Jingqing, "The sound-before-words is most wondrous; I ask the Master to point to its ultimate destination," the Master replied, "Xu You did not wash."
[The monk] said, "Why is it like this? The Master said, "It is as if your feet are still tied. [The monk] said, "I am just like this;
what about your own intention, Master? The Master said, "Without cause, the wild geese arrive at night, startling the autumn from the rear pond."
A whirlwind raises the dust; falling flowers flow with the stream. Before the sound, it is exquisite and beyond all reach. Startled, the autumn arrives at the rear pond;
Xu You did not wash his ears. Her features rival those of Xi Shi; she opens her lips but does not show her teeth. (Fang’an Xian) Jingqing asked Lingyun:
"The matter of traveling on pilgrimage is great; I beg the Master for guidance. Lingyun said: "In Zhejiang, rice is made of..."
"What is its price? The Master said, "Had it not been for Daowu, you would have ended up understanding it as the price of rice.
Daguishou said, "Lingyun was only able to let it go; he could not bring it back. Had it not been for me, you would have ended up understanding it as the price of rice.
Why did you not ask him further, 'How do you understand it? If he had attempted to respond, [you should have] immediately given him a blow."
He struck him with the hot iron bar.
Because of this, Jingqing was asked by a monk, "When a student 'sputters,' I ask the Master to 'peck. Does it still come back to life? The Master said, "Does it still come back to life?
He replied, "If it did not come back to life, it would be ridiculed by others. The Master said, "That too is just a fellow of the weeds."
Cui Feng Xian said, "If monks possess such extraordinary matters, and if even one or two of them can unfold this together with one another,
then the ancient sages did not appear for nothing. Cheng Guocheng remarked, "This fellow Jingqing is much like someone who confesses his own guilt before he has even been struck."
The ancient Buddhas had a family tradition; when they responded to the challenge, they met with censure. Mother and child do not recognize one another—whom does the pecking and the hatching coincide?
The pecking has already awakened, yet the shell remains heavy and meets with a blow. The reputation of the monks of the world is far-reaching.
(Cui-feng Xian) The mechanism of pecking and hatching is transmitted without error; the precious mirror of Huangdi stands before the hall. All myriad conditions are exhausted, buried in the mud.
The earth: the four seas are clear and calm, the moon is in the sky. The hammer of one’s own fundamental portion must forge; the furnace and bellows of one’s own house must be refined.
When meeting, do not ask about those who study the profound mystery; from here to the Western Heaven is eighteen thousand *li*.
(Fojian Qín) River-eyes and sea-mouths, nails driven into iron tongues. A rooster nesting in a phoenix’s nest is simply not a duck. Even if one were to "crack" and "peck" together—
At the same time, one cannot avoid a direct thrust to the head.

(Fóxìng Tái) The spring light is refined away, not permitted to linger; Only when the frost-flakes turn half-white does one know shame. With staff in hand, he meets again the mirror of the clear lake;
The water-bull returns once more to roam amidst the grasses.
When Jingqing was staying in his hermitage, a practitioner came and slowly approached his rope bed.
Taking up the whisk, he held it aloft and asked, "I call this thing a 'whisk,' Master; what do you call it?
The Master replied, "It is not possible to further assign names or establish words. The practitioner then threw down the whisk and said, "What is there to die for?"
Urgent! Mingzhao Qian spoke on his behalf, saying: "Dying to live, gasping for breath. Baoshou Fang said: "The practitioner is indeed a true master.
It is a pity that the Hermitage Master let him go at that time; had he not let him go, one can be certain the practitioner would have seen to his own retribution."
There is a share in this grace.
Once, when a monk asked Jingqing, "What is the source of the Great Way? the Master said, "It flows forth from here;
it flows forth from here. It flows on endlessly, day after day. Gigantic waves surge a thousand fathoms high, yet who knows there is not a single drop?"
(No Standard Model) Jingqing ascended the hall and remained silent for a long time. A monk asked, "How should one sing the Patriarchal Song? The Master said, "Carrying a drunk man home.
The monk said, "If that is so, then you have let the Master down. The Master said, "A fierce tiger does not eat the flesh of its own prey."
Dajue Sheng said: "Although Jingqing’s methods of 'bestowing' and 'seizing' are worth observing, they are like adding more wine after one has already become intoxicated.
Dajue does not do so. If someone asks, 'How should one sing the Patriarchal Song? he would direct them toward the Way, saying, 'A person of great capacity.
If that were the case, it would mean failing the Master. One must know the proper etiquette. Now tell me, is this the same as Jingqing’s approach, or is it different?"
One day, Jingqing struck the bell himself in front of the Sangha Hall and said, "Xuansha has reached the bottom; Xuansha has reached the bottom.
A monk asked, "What did Xuansha say? The Master drew a circle. The monk said, "If one had not practiced long, how could one know it was like this?
The Master said, "To lose money and then suffer for it."
Cui Feng Xian said, "I nearly had Caizhou broken. Wenyuan Qinquan said, "There is a hard thorn in the soft mud.
Gunan Men said, "Although this monk was skillful at exposing Jingqing's flaws, as for the city of Caizhou—it has been broken down long ago.
Falin Yin said, "I want to ask Gunan: since Caizhou has already been broken..."
The provincial capital: "Bring back my Wu Yuanji!
Casting a single bait straight into the heart of the waves, the silken-scaled fish leaps from the billows onto the hook.
It nearly snaps the line at the tip of the pole, drawing onlookers down from the fishing platform. (Shixi Yue)
Jingqing asked a monk, "What is that sound outside the door? The monk replied, "It is the sound of a snake swallowing a shrimp.
The Master said, "I thought all beings were suffering; it turns out there are even more suffering beings."
Yongning’s Bell-Cauldron says: "If you are a truly outstanding monk, you should step forward and say:

'It would not be out of place for me to take thirty blows of the staff on behalf of the Master; this would not only cut off Jingqing’s tongue, but also manifest that one's own head is upright and one's tail is straight.'"
"I thought that sentient beings suffer; yet there are even more suffering sentient beings. It is easy to get along when meeting one another, but it is difficult to live together as human beings.
(Wan’an Yan). National Teacher Shenyan of Xingsheng Monastery at Gushan, Fuzhou (a successor of Xuefeng Cun), went to visit Xuefeng. Xuefeng recognized his karmic affinity.
When [Fengxue] was mature in his understanding, he suddenly rose and seized him, asking, "What is this? The Master attained clear realization;
yet he forgot even that realization, doing nothing but waving his hand back and forth. Fengxue asked, "Are you engaging in intellectual reasoning? The Master replied, "What reasoning could there be?
Fengxue examined his understanding and, finding it complete, patted him in confirmation.
Jingshan Xiu said: "As soon as the Sleeping Dragon stirs, the Vermilion Phoenix soars.
Suddenly seized by Master Zeng by the chest, his lifelong path is abruptly exhausted. Without cause, he raises his hand and flicks it lightly;
he laughs himself down at the Great Summit of the South. (Zhuyu Jian)
Gushan addressed the assembly: "If one discusses this matter, it is like a single-edged sword. A monk asked, "The student is a corpse; what is the sword?
The Master said, "Drag out that corpse! The monk responded with an assent, returned beneath his robe and bowl, packed up, and departed.
That evening, the Master asked the Head Seat, "Is the monk who spoke those words still here? [The Head Seat replied,] "He left immediately."
[The monk] departed. The Master said, "I would give him twenty blows.
Yunju Qi asked, "If this monk was unwilling, what fault did Gushan commit? If he was willing, why did he depart immediately?
He further said, "Gushan’s staff both rewards and punishes him. Cui峰 Xian said, "In all quarters..."
Jindao said, "Gushan has lost one of his eyes. Little did he know that beneath a heavy reward there must be brave men.
Even so, it cannot be avoided that for a moment they are all buried together.
Dongchan Guan said, "This monk brings out a corpse and makes it move as if alive. Gushan possesses a fine sword, yet it still lacks sharpening."
Baoshou Fang said: "Everyone says that Gushan’s staff is excellent; it is a pity, however, that it was too late. [The monk asked: "What is the sword?
[Gushan] struck him across the spine twenty times and drove him out. If you act like this, you have not even dreamed of Gushan. Gunan Men said:
"This monk concealed his edge while wielding his sword, yet he was struck by Gushan’s twenty blows until his corpse lay ten thousand miles away. Although it was thus..."

This was so; bystanders laughed at it. Bahe Shun said: "All who speak of this say that the monk refused to strike Gushan, yet they do not realize that Gushan already had a sword hanging at his gate—a corpse already lying ten thousand miles away. It is a pity that at the end he added twenty blows of the staff;
one sees this as drawing a bow after the thief has already passed."
A verse by Gushan says: "Directly beneath, it is still difficult to comprehend; Seeking through words, it becomes even more remote.

If one discusses Buddhas and Patriarchs, They are, quite unexpectedly, separated by the ends of the earth. He raised this to question a monk, saying: "How do you understand this? The monk was speechless.
Later, the monk said to his attendant: "I do not understand; please provide a substitute phrase for me. The attendant said: "The Master..."
"What do you say? You are still as far away as the ends of the earth. Upon hearing this, the Master called to his attendant and asked, "Did you provide that monk with words on his behalf?
The attendant replied, "Yes. The Master then struck him and expelled him from the monastery.
Kaixian Jin said: "Gushan and his attendant were not discreet in their conduct; they were completely exposed by this monk in one fell swoop.
Yet Kaixian also said: 'Directly beneath, it is still difficult to comprehend; following words only makes it more remote.
If we speak of Buddhas and Patriarchs, they are suddenly separated by the ends of the earth. How, then, do you all understand this?"
The State Preceptor’s foster son is too compassionate. How does entering the weeds compare to emerging from them?
Shooting the sacred arrow that reaches the ninefold heavens, it remains, as before, a vast distance across the sky.
(Shixi Yue) On the occasion of ascending the hall, Guishan delivered this statement: "Under the gate of Guishan, one must not cough. At that time, a monk coughed.
[The monk] made a sound like a sneeze. The Master said, "What are you doing? He replied, "I have a cold.
The Master said, "A cold is fine. Langye Jue said: "The thunder was great, yet there were no drops of rain at all. Yungai Ben said:
"Although Gushan used a 'probing pole' and 'shadow-grass' [to test him], he could not help but take the crooked for straight. Daolin, however, would not do so. How could one have a cold?"
Wind. In the mountains there are no other medicines; outside the gate there are green pines. Guangjiao Yu said:
"Gushan dangles his hook in the four seas, yet this monk drags his hem at Longmen. Although he does not employ fists or kicks, he nonetheless has a documented lineage."
People everywhere say that at Drum Mountain, the dragon had the head but lacked the tail;
they do not realize, however, that this monk was pushed by Drum Mountain into a deep pit at Baizhang, where he remains until this very day, unable to raise his head. Chengshan Jia said:
Gushan held fast to his borders and did not permit even half a person to pass through; why, then, did he let this monk go? Have you not heard it said:
"A lion does not eat the remains left by a vulture; a swift falcon does not strike a rabbit already lying down"?
A single arrow across the vast void reaches the nine-layered city; the old man Xue’s lineage style still resounds with vigor.
It is said that when the imperial court issues its decrees, no one at all is permitted to pass through there. (Xutang Yu:
The thunder rolls on and on, yet not a drop of rain falls; in vain they speak of the General’s strategic skill being lax—who can recognize the subtle maneuvers of Sun and Wu?
Measuring it—sometimes extended, sometimes coiled—it is entirely dependent on the conduit.
(Yongjue Xian) Beneath a ten-thousand-fathom cold pool, a single hook descends; the water’s light is so clear and cool it presses upon the eyes.
No scaled dragons are seen as they surge through wind and waves, yet a blind turtle stubbornly thrusts its head out. ([Zhao]an Pu)
Chan Master Lingcan of Cuiyan in Mingzhou (a successor of Xuefeng Cun) ascended the hall and said: "For an entire summer, I have been talking here and there with you brothers.
Look—do Cuiyan’s eyebrows still exist? Changqing said, "They grow. Yunmen said, "The barrier.
Baofu said, "The thief’s heart is fearful. Cuiyan Zhi said, "Exerting one's utmost strength for the sake of the assembly; yet disaster arises from within."
The Private Gate. Yungju Yuan said: "Cuiyan knew it was wrong yet committed the offense; though the amnesty has passed, he is not pardoned.
Yunmen presses him for the subsequent action, adjudicating the crime according to principle. Do you still recognize Changqing and Baofu? A man from Puzhou delivers a thief."—Zhaojue Qin.
Yunmen said: "Cuiyan has cut off the tongues of everyone in the world; there is nowhere for them to chew or peck. Changqing gained wisdom through this incident;
Baofu was one who recognized the essential with the essential; Yunmen settled the case based on the facts.

Although these masters vied with one another in responding according to the ancestral style, have they truly been able to cut off Cuiyan’s heels? Without following in his footsteps, try to say something! Jianfu Xing said: "Cuiyan..."
Opening his eyes, he urinates on his bed; the question is where the answer lies. Yunmen loses his money and incurs punishment; the answer is where the question lies.
If the question is not where the answer lies, and the answer is not where the question lies, Donghu’s staff pierces through the Great Elephant of Jiazhou.
You all, lift up your sitting cloths and perform the ritual of *pravāraṇā* within the land of Japan! —Chengtian
The Master said: "The entire earth is the single eye of Cuiyan; what more need be said of being 'in' or 'out'?
It reaches the point where the venerable masters of all quarters exhaust every artifice, yet they cannot escape the circle.

Thus Baofu said, 'The mind of a thief is always apprehensive,' which is precisely to fall into his trap. Yunmen said, 'A barrier!'—this is much like struggling for strength within a dream. Long... (text continues)
Auspicious clouds arise. Understanding arises following words. But as for Senior Monk Zong, what then? [He] took his whisk and drew a circle, saying:
"Entrusted to the carefree guest of the sea and mountains; when fishing for the giant tortoise, drop a single circle.
Daming Tai said: Baofu said, "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive; only those on the same path know. Changqing said, "It arises."
...and so forth. To follow the words and give rise to understanding—Yunmen called this "shutting off. It blocks the throat. If someone were to ask, "And what about Daomiao?
[Yunmen] would take up his staff, strike once, and say, "Threaded all through on a single string. Baolin Xiu said: "A skilled thief is not known even by ghosts and spirits.
Since he has been seen through by Baofu and Tiantong, Cuiyan was no good hand at it; he was truly outdone."
"I do not know how many great masters like Yunmen and Changqing were all at once pierced through their nostrils by Cuiyan’s single tuft of eyebrows.
Jingshan Xiu said, "Cuiyan was also selling flour with the chaff still on it," and further remarked,
"A whole crew of unperforated iron hammers."
Cuiyan’s demonstration to his disciples is peerless through the ages; to respond with the character "Pass" (Guān) is to lose one's money and incur punishment.
Old and decrepit Baofu finds it difficult to suppress or exalt; Cuiyan prattles on incessantly—clearly a thief. With a flawless white jade, who can distinguish the true from the false?
Changqing and Xiang’an knew each other intimately; their eyebrows have grown. (Cui Feng reveals them.
Zuozai and Baofu carry the cangue and pass the indictment; they have grown. Changqing is lost to truth and pursues delusion; Yunmen shuts his door.
The moon over the autumn river; old and decrepit is Cuiyan. His eyebrows are above his eyes.
(Huanglong Xin) A golden mallet, its blood-red hue piercing through the cloud-robe; his authority beyond the threshold is bold and majestic.
Having smashed the mountain-demon’s cave, he casts his line for whales and turtles in the depths of the azure pool. (Nantang Jing)
With a crossbow of ten-thousand-jun power, whom does one shoot? Before the arrow has even left the string, the target’s life is lost.
This brings misfortune upon the blind turtle, who loses the floating wood; it is like wishing to bathe in fire amidst golden dust.
(I’an Kwon) possesses a thief’s mind and a man’s courage; clearly and decisively, he responds to every stimulus. Even Baofu and Yunmen would hang their heads in shame before him.
Deceptive lips—Cuiyan and Changqing. Eyebrows as green as jade reflecting the eyes—Du the Chan monk. What limits are there?

He stubbornly claims that meaning and phrasing must be swept away all at once; he buries himself while swallowing his breath and stifling his voice, and he brings disgrace upon the ancestral school by facing a wall and carrying a wooden board. (Tiantong Jue)
Where the spring breeze arises, one borrows a blade to cut through water; suppressing it here and uplifting it there, how can such emotion be restrained?

Seeking a deceptive encounter with the hope of catching ten birds, piercing the willow-leaves without sparing a single arrow—though these may be turned in an instant to conceal their function, every one of them is a son of a wealthy man who wears no trousers. (My companion!)
Cuiyan was invited by the Abbot to attend a meal at the lecture hall. The Master said, "I have a question for you; if you can answer it, you shall have the meal.
He then picked up a sesame cake and asked, "Does this possess the Dharma-body? The Abbot replied, "It possesses it.
The Master brought the cake to his mouth and said, "In that case, you are devouring the Dharma-body. The Abbot was speechless.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "I specifically thank the Master for descending to honor this empty assembly. Tianye Zhou’s commentary says, "Those who recognize the debt of gratitude are few;
those who betray it are many. Mingyin Huai’s commentary says, "I did not expect that even a master of our school would hold such a view."
Chan Master Jiaoran Changsheng of Fuzhou (a successor of Xuefeng Cun) was asked by Xuansha:
"I observe that the Tathāgata does not come from the past, does not continue into the future, and does not abide in the present. How about you, Elder?
The Master said, "Let me pass, and there will be a place for me to speak. Xuansha said, "Since I have let you pass, how do you speak? The Master remained silent.
The monk asked, "To whom do you entrust this teaching? The Master said, "I do not entrust it to the Abbot. The monk said, "I knew you would be making your living inside a ghost cave.
Chou of Chongshou offered a different interpretation, saying, "What do you call the Tathāgata?"
Pairs of jade trees, brilliant and flawless, Are not like the reeds and rushes by the autumn river. On a clear night, they play together beneath the moon;
Deep into the night, they still perform the "Plum Blossoms Falling" melody.
(Jian’an Yi) Changsheng was asked by a monk: "The ancients said that ignorance is itself Buddha-nature, and that afflictions need not be eliminated."

"What is ignorance that is itself Buddha-nature? The Master, his expression suddenly stern, raised his fist and scolded him, saying, "Today this monk is going to be beaten! "How is it that afflictions need not be eliminated?
The Master seized the man's head with his hand and said, "This monk creates such karma for others!"
Jianfu was like a cloud; Changsheng’s response was much like following another’s footsteps. Jiuyi Kai said: "This monk digs a pit to wait for his own burial;
Changsheng stretches out his neck to await the axe. If this were the Buddha-nature of ignorance..."
[He will] wait another three lives and sixty kalpas.
Zen Master Zhifu of Ehu in Xinzhou (a successor of Xuefeng Cui) was once asked by a monk: "Does a filial-defiant son still receive his father’s inheritance?
The Master said: "Though he may have his own way of managing it, he cannot avoid wounding himself."
Jiang Tianquan said: "This monk was merely borrowing food to get others to eat it, which caused Guyang’s mouth to remain open, unable to close. Nevertheless, this monk is a master."
Casting away gold as if casting away mucus, he whistles long to sustain his livelihood.
Once entering the river current, his entire body is within the pure and white.
(From the *Chanzong Jianfa Lin*, Volume 46)

The Seventh Generation Descending from Dajian [Huineng].
Chan Master Hongtao of Anguo in Fuzhou (a successor of Xuefeng Cui) cited the inscription for the National Teacher, saying:
"When it is attained within the mind, even *eranda* trees become sandalwood; when it is lost in its essential meaning, even nectar becomes a garden of thorns."
He said to a monk, "A single word must encompass both the meanings of gain and loss. How would you say it?

The monk raised his fist and said, "One cannot call this a 'fist. The Master did not approve. He also raised his fist and said, "It is precisely because one calls this thing a 'fist' [that it is so]."
Cui峰 Xian said, "A fellow who binds himself with no rope; he does not even recognize his own fist.
Dabei Xiu said, "Cui峰 An-guo was entirely lofty and beyond the mundane world, yet when facing the enemy at the front line, he merely followed the ranks.
Tiantong Hua said, "If you can see through Cui峰, you will see that An-guo is a dragon’s head and a snake’s tail."
Tail. If one’s vision is not penetrating, *eranda* will become a sandalwood tree, and nectar will become a thornbush garden.
Dong Chan Guan said: "This monk could not clamp the mouth of An Guo; An Guo could not stop the censure of Cui Feng;
and Cui Feng could not escape the critique of Da Miao. Pity this group of fellows—they cannot even stand up to one person."
Xuánjué asked, "What is it? Dàiyún said, "I require a phrase that possesses both the meanings of gain and loss.
Xuánjué simply said, "Stop. Why was this so? A single drop of a lion’s milk scatters ten *hu* of donkey’s milk.
Nántáng Yù said, "I am not like Ānguó, who discussed gain and loss with a single word and two meanings. He took up his staff and said, "This staff of mine can kill."
There is life within killing, and killing within life; sometimes killing and life occur simultaneously, and sometimes they do not.

If you can employ this skillfully, there is nothing—whether mundane or supramundane—that is not prepared for you; thus, you may observe the interplay of letting go and seizing, and the freedom of rolling up and unfolding without hindrance.
If you cannot so employ it, you are merely a fellow who binds himself with no rope at all. —Xiaoyan Bao (Xiaoyan Baoshou)
Cui Feng said: "The feet of Da'an Guo have not even touched the ground. Gunan said: "An Guo is one who falls down by his own rising.
If you call it a 'fist,' do you say he loses? It cannot be called a 'fist. Do you say he gains?
Precisely because you call it a 'fist,' if you run about on the basis of gain and loss, what end will there ever be?"
Although the strings may be moved to produce different melodies, they ultimately do not escape the circle of this old man. After all, how is it? He spreads his hands and says:
"One must quickly turn one's eyes to look at the immortal."
Chan Master Kexiu of Dongyan in Yuezhou (a successor of Xuefeng Cun):

Once, after Yunmen had been there for several days, as soon as he went up to pay his respects, the Master came down and asked, "Where have you been? Yunmen replied, "I went to attend upon [the Buddha]."
The Master said, "Why are you running about in such disorder? Yunmen said, "I was away for a moment. The Master said, "Where have you been?
Cui-feng Xian commented separately, "He deserves thirty blows of the staff. Cheng-tian Yi said, "What does Yunmen mean by 'for a moment'?"

He was not there at that time; he had been running about in disorder outside the gate all day long. Although Dongyan had lived at home for many years, he did not even know where his own dwelling place was.
The Venerable Fu of Taiyuan (a successor of Xuefeng Cun) was initially lecturing on the Dharma-body of the Three Virtues at Guangxiao Temple in Yangzhou.
Because a Zen practitioner laughed, he ceased his lectures for ten days; he sat upright within his chamber, practicing quiet meditation to withdraw his mind and collect his thoughts.
From the first watch until the fifth watch, he suddenly attained awakening upon hearing the sound of drums and horns. He knocked on the door of a Zen practitioner. The practitioner asked, "Who is it?
The Master replied, "It is I. The practitioner rebuked him, saying, "I have been instructing you to transmit and uphold the Great Teaching and to preach the Dharma in place of the Buddha!"

"Why did you come home last night drunk and lie down in the street? The Master replied, "Dharma Master, I have been lecturing on the sutras for some time now, twisting the nostrils of my own biological parents.
From this day forward, I shall never dare to act like this again. The Dharma Master said, "Go for now;
let us meet tomorrow. Thereupon, the Master ceased his lectures and traveled extensively throughout all quarters.
A single melody of the *Shanyu Fengyin* (Hunting the Hunnic Chieftain) extends far; where Master Fu hears it, the notes are *gong* and *shang*.
To this day, every night, travelers from Yangzhou listen in vain at the tower’s edge as the sound breaks their hearts.
(Benjue I) Who blows the painted horn by the river city? A single melody of the "Plum Blossom" is heard across the shore. The lingering wine has just begun to clear as the golden censer...
Cold. The moon still shines bright upon the branches of the *haitang* tree.

(Lan’an Shu) Qinsheng has entered the vast ocean; the Grand Historian roams the famous mountains. From now on, along the roads outside Yangzhou City, strict orders shall prohibit the gates from opening early. (Huījī Xī)
In the desolate southern land, I lodge in a solitary city. My traveler’s dream drifts on as I sleep deeply. A single blast from the painted horn startles me awake;
the cuckoo cries out beyond the shadows of the flowers. (By Yuan’an Wei) Tāiyu went to study under Xuefeng.
When Xuefeng heard of his arrival, he gathered the assembly. Upon reaching the Dharma Hall, the Master looked around at Xuefeng.
He then went down to attend to the administrative affairs. The next day, he went back up to pay his respects and said, "I offended you, Master, yesterday.
Feng said, "Knowing it was such a matter, let it rest."
When a monk asked Yunmen Wenyan, "Where is the point of offense? Yunmen struck him. Cui峰 Xian said, "What is the use of striking hundreds of thousands of people?
Only when the entire world has been struck with the staff can Xuefeng be truly established.
But tell me, what kind of eye does Elder Fu possess? He further said, "One thousand five hundred people..."
"Good friend! Upon being glanced at by Old Fu, Xuefeng immediately hoisted his banner of surrender.
By the next day, he said, 'Knowing it was such a matter, I shall simply leave it at that. Indeed. Yunju Shun said, "The Great Xuefeng was once more deluded by Upādhyāya Fu;
even this very Upādhyāya Fu is one who carries his own shackles through the trial. Chengtian Zong said, "He only knows..."
One does not know the second; yet they fail to realize that Xuefeng was already winning the battle a thousand miles away while sitting in his tent, planning his strategy.
Although Upādhyāya Fu presented his lifelong insights, he remained within Xuefeng’s circle.
Nantang Yu said: "Eye meets eye; mind knows mind. Yunmen then struck him. Upon the staff there is an eye as bright as the sun.
Cuiyun said, "What use is it to beat out hundreds of thousands of pieces? To recognize true gold, one must look at it in the fire.
Farin Mi asked, "Where did Elder Fu commit an offense? Xuefeng said, "If you know it is such a matter, then leave it at that. But tell me, what matter did he know?
General Li Guang was peerless throughout past and present. Penetrating deep into the enemy's camp, he preserved his life and avoided harm;
without raising a blade, he achieved small victories, and his illustrious reputation remains celebrated at the frontier to this day.
(Haoyin Xin) His inner spirit is like a rainbow as he ascends the Dharma Hall; binding a calf to the fence is exactly appropriate. If one says he has offended the Elder Harmony...
Furthermore, upon the snow there is no cause for frost to fall again. (Chengyan Yu) From Taiyuan he went to Touzi.
Touzi said, "I have long heard of the Venerable Fu of Taiyuan; could it be you? The Master made the gesture of clapping his hands.
Touzi said, "The old monk has been caught. The Master then departed. Touzi said, "Wait and let the various quarters pass judgment."
"Look! The Master turned his head. Zizhi struck him immediately.

Xuansha Bei said, "Was it not Touzi who invited this upon himself? Baiyan Fu said, "Although these two elders were direct in hand and swift in eye, how could they avoid mutually humiliating one another?"
Taizhen asked Gushan, "Before one's parents were born, where was the nose? The Master said, "Brother, you speak first.
Taizhen said, "Now that you are born, tell me, where is it? The Master did not agree. Gushan then asked, "How about this?
The Master said, "Bring me the fan in your hand. Gushan gave him the fan, and the Master questioned him again.
The Master shook his fan and did not respond. Since Fushan could not fathom this, he struck the Master with a single punch.
Zhaojue Renqin said: "Chongning was not like that either. Before one's parents were born, where were the nostrils?
Just slap him right across the mouth!"
"Before one's parents were born, where was the nose? All the veteran masters of the monastic groves are ignorant of this 'phrase for concealing the body.
Although Gushan saw the occasion, he could not avoid propping up the gate; his fanning [the air] was excessive. Yuanfu was merely playing with trivial household utensils."
The spring colors are deep within the mountains; flying flowers fall in countless numbers.
(Fohuiquan) At the head of Gaoyuan Rapids, all is shattered into a hundred fragments; before Xianggu Peak, the eyes are blurred with rheum. I dare say that Gushan has no nostrils;
the monastic groves have laughed heartily for a thousand ages. (Zhengtang Bian)
Come well to view Mount Lu from all eight sides; its precipitous cliffs and flowing streams together reveal their countenances. Clouds hang across the valley mouth like torn cotton wool;
they will not allow the weary bird to return with a single cry.
(Master Mei Gaō) When Dayuan went to attend the invitation of the Great King at Gushan, Xuefeng saw him off at the gate. Upon returning to the Dharma Hall, he said:
"A holy arrow shoots straight toward the nine-layered city. The Master said, "He has not yet reached the mark.
Feng said, "He is a man of thorough penetration. The Master said, "If you do not believe me, wait until I go to examine him myself.
He then pursued him to the middle of the road and asked, "Elder brother, where are you going? Feng replied, "I am going to the nine-layered city."
The Master asked, "What if you suddenly encounter an encirclement by a threefold army? Sanshan said, "He has his own path that reaches through the heavens.
The Master said, "In that case, would he not have left the palace and lost the hall? Sanshan said, "Where is there that does not permit one to be honored?"
The Master shook out his sleeves and turned back. Feng asked, "How was it? The Master said, "A fine sacred arrow, broken in mid-flight.
He then recounted the previous conversation. Feng then said, "He has something more to say. The Master said, "That old frozen fellow!"
"There is still a trace of local sentiment remaining. Guishan Zhe said: "There has been much deliberation among the assembly. Some say that as soon as one asks, 'Where are you going?
one should strike right here; not striking is where the holy arrow breaks. Others say: 'What if one suddenly encounters being surrounded by a threefold army?'"
"Excellent shot! Not hitting the mark is where the sage’s arrow breaks. To engage in such theoretical discourse is not only to deceive others, but to deceive oneself as well.
Do you wish to understand? Zhāng Xiāng once seized the "Jade of the Linked Cities," yet the Lord of Qín remained at ease and brought about peace.
Bǎofēng Wén said: "Wait until he says, 'What an excellent arrow!'—then break it in mid-flight and ask him, 'Tell me...'"
"What was it? Before he could raise [his staff], Baoning struck him with a painful blow. First, this ensured that Master Fu would henceforth become a monk of genuine caliber;
second, it sharpened the edge of the "sacred arrow"; third, it established him as a true patriarch of the Chan school to serve as a guiding eye for future generations.
"Venerable practitioners, is this right or not? Baoning Yong thus responded to Drum Mountain.
The Record says: "Master Fu, I also know you are an evil man. Jingshan Daokai asked:
"Where did the holy arrow break? Someone said: "Gushan’s failure to answer his question was where the holy arrow broke."

To criticize that "Gushan was not right to explain the principle; this is where the sage’s arrow broke," is not only a failure to understand Gushan, but also a failure to understand Elder Fu. Little do they realize that Elder Fu was, in fact, nothing but a thief.
Having suffered a total defeat before Mount Gu, he came to Xuefeng to uproot the very foundation [of his delusions].
This is much like hawking goods from Yangzhou while standing inside one's own house. Had it not been for Xuefeng’s marks of a great man, where would this thief have found a place to hide?
At that time, it was a pity he let him go; it became an unresolved koan.
Is there anyone here now who can avenge the ancients? Come forward and I will ask you: where exactly did the holy arrow break?
Tianning Qi said: "The holy arrow of Gushan has shot deep into the nine-layered city, full of martial spirit.
Yet Fuzhao Zuoshi instead says the arrow is broken; he attributes the crime to another and imposes that guilt upon himself.
Miaoxi says that Fuzhao Zuoshi is a rogue who returned from before Gushan with a defeat upon his shoulders—riding the thief’s horse to kill the thief. How extraordinary!
Heaven! Oh, Heaven! Generally speaking, nothing arises in isolation. At that time, Xuefeng merely dangled that single "sage-arrow" of his, which caused him to invite thieves to plunder his house.
Had he clenched his teeth and remained steadfast, who would have dared to stir up waves where there was no wind?
Even if the entire world were transformed into hemp, bamboo, and reeds to become monks, they would still not be able to pass the test of Gushan.
As for the opening of the mouth: Tianning was not disparaging the ancients. What is the "sage’s arrow"? It is a stalk of latrine grass;
throw it onto a heap of refuse. If you further ask where it breaks, do not let your hand fall into boiling water.
In the Cavern of Heaven there are no walls and the moon has no obstruction. The Master Who Pays Homage to the Dipper knocks his teeth together.
The wind shakes the ancient altar, and pine seeds fall; it knocks off the paper cap from his head, tilting it askew.
(The Mirror of the Transcendent) The Azure Youth double-reins his jade steed as it neighs. His pale white spring robe is encircled by a green sash. Returning at midnight beneath the flowers—
Past. A golden whip strikes down the falling crimson petals. (From "Brief Notes on Bamboo Huts," No.
2) Within the ninefold city, it is not distant at all; shot through layer after layer, the arrows are more than double.
Suddenly encountering the place surrounded by the three armies, there is clearly a path leading straight to the heavens.
Mouth engaged in human affairs, the head pokes out; immediately one turns over and enters the thieves' den.
It was not that he knew for certain before the wind; both have leapt into the nest of right and wrong.
(Yunmen Cheng) The river is vast and empty, the water leaves no trace. On both banks, the reeds laugh at the bright moon. A single blast from the long flute startles the birds at rest.
The wild geese cause people’s fishing sentiments to be filled with regret.
(The mountain forms and the waves. A man from Taiyuan was managing the bathhouse at Xuefeng. One day, Xuansha arrived. Xuefeng said, "There is a little mouse here;
it is currently in the bathhouse. Xuansha replied, "I shall wait to examine this for you, Master. He then went to the bathhouse.
In the quarters, he saw the Master drawing water and said, "I have come to see you, Senior. The Master replied, "We have already met. He asked, "In what kalpa did we ever meet?
The Master said, "Why are you dozing off? The monk then entered the abbot’s quarters and reported, "I have already fathomed him.
Feng asked, "How did you fathom him? The monk recounted the previous conversation. Feng said, "You have been robbed by a thief."
Liyuan asked, "The Venerable Fu briefly displayed his sharp edge, yet he was pinned down by Xuansha. Xuefeng, in the end, possessed the marks of a great man;
it is no mistake that he was a spiritual teacher to fifteen hundred people. Is there anyone [who can respond]?
Can you discern it? The secret instructions of the immortals are not transmitted even between father and son.
The elephant king and his offspring follow one another; those on the bank watch as hoof meets hoof. They eat the fragrant grass delicately until they know fullness;
returning, they do not wait for the sun to set. (Xutang Yu)
Born into the same family as paternal aunts, maternal aunts, and sisters, they apply powder and rouge to ascend the mat.
When the blazing midday sun arrives, their entire bodies are drenched in sweat, making them loathsome to behold.
(Shiyu Fang), the eighth generation under Dajian.
Chan Master Huiji of Mount Huanglong in Ezhou (Xuánquán Yànsì). A monk asked, "What is it like when the wind is calm and the waves are still?
The Master said, "A five-liang weight hanging from the top of a hundred-foot pole."
At the top of a hundred-foot pole, five *liang* hang down; across the desolate sands and boundless wastes, one lets oneself be blown by the wind.
How pitiable are the countless travelers on the Canglang River, who still clutch their compass needles to determine where they shall return.
(Shilin Gong) A monk asked Huanglong about the meaning of Chan, and the Master replied, "To slander is its meaning."

Xuedou said: "To say that the Buddhas of the three periods are slanderous, that the twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven are slanderous, that the six generations of patriarchs of the Tang land are slanderous, that the old monks throughout the world are slanderous, that those in all quarters are slanderous, and that this mountain monk is slanderous—if among these there were one who was not slanderous, would there be such a person?
Though one might discourse on the profound and speak of the wondrous as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, how could it compare to the [two]..."
Feng said, "Slander is intimacy. Tianning Qi said: "If someone were to ask Nanhu, 'What is the meaning of Chan?
tell him, 'Praise is its meaning. Now tell me: is it the slander that is right, or is it the praise? If you see with your eyes, you are blind; if you hear with your ears, you are deaf;
if you speak with your mouth, you are mute; if you think with your mind, you are at a loss. Ten-thousand-foot rocks are buried in snow at the edge of the sky; the cave gate—"
The ice broke several pine trees.
When Huanglong first attended Yantou, he asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Yantou said, "Do you know how to save steamed cakes?
The Master replied, "I do. Yantou said, "For now, go and save the steamed cakes. Later, when he arrived at Xuanquan, he asked [the same].
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Quan picked up a stalk of soapberry and asked, "Do you understand?
The Master said, "I do not understand. Quan set down the soapberry and made a gesture of washing clothes.

The Master then prostrated himself and said, "I now know that the Buddha-dharma has no other [essence]. Quan asked, "What principle have you seen? The Master replied, "I once asked Yantou about this."
Tou said, "Do you still understand saving rice cakes? Saving rice cakes is simply resolving stickiness.
When the Master held up the soap nut, that too was resolving stickiness. Therefore it is said there is no difference. Quan laughed heartily, and the Master subsequently attained realization.
Huanji said to Jiyun: "If Xuanchuan had not laughed later, he would have nearly brought disgrace upon Yantou.
Although Huanglong’s single laugh caused him to cast off his horns and hooves, he still could not escape being led by the plow and dragged by the harrow."
Chan Master Mingzhao Deqian of Wuzhou (a successor of Luoshan Xian) asked Guotai:
"The ancients said that Jushi attained a reputation surpassing all others simply by reciting three lines of incantation.
How would you remove those three lines of incantation for him, so that he might attain a reputation surpassing all others? Guotai held up one finger. The Master said, "It was not because of this..."
"Every day he struggles to recognize the guest from Guazhou.
Letan Qing said, "Mingzhao recognized only the guest from Guazhou, yet he did not recognize Guo Tai.
Even if he had recognized him, he still would not have dreamed of Old Juzhi."
Mingzhao was unwell. Guotai came to inquire after his illness. As soon as he entered, the Master said, "A-ye! A-ye! Elder Shishu Shen, save this old monk!
Guotai asked, "What is there for the Master to save? The Master raised his head and looked at him once, saying, "Ei!
Those eyes are dark and piercing; you are still that same old Zen Master Shen from before. Thus it was.
He turned his body away and faced the wall, never to see him again.
Jingshan Yin said: "If Mingzhao had not turned his body and faced the wall, what face would he have to show Guotai?
Even a single illness was beyond his control; how much more so the coming and going of birth and death?"
Mingzhao was once asked by a monk, "Of the seven cubs born to a tiger, which one has no tail? The Master said, "The seventh one has no tail.
Langshan Yu said, "Since the question has its source, the answer likewise shares that same ground. But tell me, is the seventh one a tiger or not?"
This is a tiger. If you can certainly escape, I grant you leave to roam freely across the world. Otherwise, do not attempt to make a living off its tail;
a tailless beast is difficult to approach. To draw near is to bring about the loss of one's life. Only if you can master the tiger yourself may you hope for safety.
The Head. Naturally the head is straight and the tail is also straight. (Gushan Gui) Seventh:
When the wildcat has lost its tail, its breath from devouring oxen is already enough to boast of. The monastic communities clamor and dispute over their lips and mouths;
how many travelers will actually reach home? (Jingshan Gao)
The seventh child has no tail; blue eyes and a yellow head, laughing until his chest splits open. He is accustomed to baring his claws and fangs right before one’s face;
with a single roar, a pure breeze arises. (Làngshānyù) While Mingzhao was tending the brazier, a monk asked:
"There is no dharma before the eyes, yet the intent lies before the eyes; it is not [simply] before the eyes."
The Dharma is not something that can be reached by the ears or eyes. Which phrase is the guest, and which is the host?
The Master pointed to a fire and said, "Can you pluck out a single eyebrow from within this for me?
[The monk] replied, "Not only would I lose my life, but all the people in the entire world would lose their lives. The Master said, "Why do you come to court with your hair in a topknot?"
Jingshan Gaofeng said: "This monk has a head but no tail; Mingzhao has a tail but no head.
If anyone can speak so that both head and tail are perfectly complete, I, Yunmen, will give you my staff. Tianning Qisong said:
"They do not understand how to pull out the eyebrows from within the fire, nor do they know which of these four lines is the guest and which is the host. How wondrous!"
Master Miyun said, "Master Xixi has a head but no tail; Master Mingzhao has a tail but no head.
Even if one could utter a phrase from Master Miaoxi that is perfectly complete in both head and tail, Tianning’s staff would still not let him go.
Yuan'an Meng said, "Not meeting a village ahead and not catching up with an inn behind—fortunately, at least the fire-bowl remains."
Mingzhao went to the place of Elder Tan. Tan said, "In the study of the Way, one must go to where the whole person is, and one must also go to where the half-person is.
Mingzhao then asked, "I do not ask about where the whole person is; what is meant by 'where the half-person is'? Tan had no reply.
Later, he instructed his junior monk to ask Mingzhao about it. Mingzhao said, "If you wish to know..."
"Where is the 'half-person' located? He too is merely a fellow playing with lumps of mud. Tiantong Hua said:
"I have heard that the One-Eyed Dragon indeed possesses only one eye. Suddenly, a monk comes forward and asks:
"I do not ask about the location of the 'one person'; what is the location of the 'half-person'? [The Master] then strikes him across the back.

"Strike! Ask again: 'Where is the one person located? and he immediately drives him out in the middle of the night. Why? Because once you have started, do not stop halfway. Song Ruyi said: "From afar, the mountain has color; from nearby, the water makes no sound. Now tell me:

is this place where the one person is, or is it where half a person is? He took up his bamboo staff, struck once, and said: [The Master] struck. [The Master] was eating powdered-rice gruel. The Master said, "Foolish man! You are as hard to kill as one beaten with a staff. When the evening came, [Zhaozhou] recounted this to several Zen guests.
The Master stepped forward and said, "I hope you have been well? Zhaozhou said, "Today, I shall give this very monk two slaps! An attendant, Seito, said, "There is no need to slap him;
how would you speak from within the innermost core? The Master replied, "From within the innermost core."

"Speak! Speak! Taoyao had no reply. The Master said, "I shall bind all of you together at once, tie you into a single bundle, and hang you upside down beneath the urinal. Come see me tomorrow; take care."
Tiantong Jie said: "I have always told people that all day long, amidst vast surging waves, one scoops up water and splashes it about, yet not a single drop wets the body.
This was because Mingzhao had stepped upon that 'little bit' [of the fundamental]; thus he naturally employed it with ease.
It is a pity that his edge was not sharp enough, leading to so much entanglement. Had it been Huazang..."
Seeing that the other had said, "Originally it was just flour-rice," Mingzhao struck him twice on both cheeks, leaving this fellow to harbor doubts for thirty years.
One day, as Mingzhao was traveling to Baoning, he encountered Baoning along the way. The Master then asked, "Brother, are you..."
Among his fellow practitioners on the path, one pointed to his own nose and said, "This thing obstructs me; I cannot penetrate it.
Could you remove it for a moment? Ning replied, "How long has the Master been here? The Master said, "Alas!"
"By now you have caused me to lose a pair of straw sandals," he said, and then turned away.
Guo Tai spoke on his behalf, saying, "Not only this person, but even all the Buddhas could do nothing about it. The Master asked, "Why do you compare yourself with others?"
Chengtian Yi said: "Mingzhao merely teaches people how to pluck away another's nostrils, yet he does not realize that he himself has lost so many eyebrows.
Mingzhao was once at the residence of High Official Gao when the Master (Xun) saw a hanging portrait of Maitreya; the Master pointed to it.
Maitreya Buddha called out, “Hermitage Master! The master responded, “Yes. The Master said, “Has this fellow still not attained thorough penetration? The master was speechless.
The Master said, “Is it not bitter even when yellow myrobalan is boiled with its very roots? Later, Guo Tai took his place and simply joined his palms, saying, “Excellent, excellent!
The Master said, “The Abbot may stay in the hermitage as a neighbor to him, but that is all.”
[The Master] said: "His heels do not touch the ground; Mingzhao was indeed able to discern this. Nevertheless, it is so, it is so.
To pluck jade blossoms to insert into the cloud-like tresses—alas, the fair lady ultimately does not look. For no reason, the young gentleman’s hair stands on end."
Precious! The autumn waves ripple and turn as the mind remains at ease. (Suan Ding) Mingzhao went to visit Master Shengguang.
As soon as he stepped across the threshold, Shengguang extended his foot. The Master said, "Your tricks are exhausted," and with a sweep of his sleeves, he departed.
Chengtian Yi said: "Mingzhao displayed his brilliance for a time, yet he brought about his own defeat. Although Shenguang exhausted all his skills, he sat and attained peace.
When Mingzhao ascended the hall and the assembly had just gathered, he immediately said: "The wind at the peak is somewhat stiff; this is not where you can find a place to settle yourself."
"Go back to the warm room and deliberate there," he said, and then returned to the abbot’s quarters. The assembly followed him to the quarters.
The Master said, "As soon as you reached the warm room, you were already nodding off," and with his staff, he struck them all at once, dispersing them.
Jianfu Can said, "The wind at the peak is somewhat harsh; let us return to the warm room to deliberate. There was bait on the hook. The assembly followed him to the abbot’s quarters.
"Yellow gall is not yet bitter," he said, but as soon as they reached the warm room, they were seen nodding off, so he struck them all at once with his staff and dispersed them.
"A pity that gold is treated like dung and soil," he added, and further remarked, "Mingzhao’s vanguard has taken action."
The Hall has since been swallowed up by others; it is a pity that there was no one among the assembly at that time.
Had they then heard the words, "First return to the warm room to deliberate," they would have all dispersed at once, leaving this old fellow unable to return to his quarters as he desired.
Within the hall, it was exceptionally cold and piercing; who among the multitude dared to face it head-on?
One sees only the western wind scouring the earth, yet who knows that a single leaf stirs with the onset of autumn? Depart for a warmer place; stop and wait, for no one will plug your throat for you.
You must know that the Great Emperor’s achievements were vast: both sides of the Grand Canal were reclaimed at once. (By Fo-hui Quan)
When the head of the wind is cut off, advancing is difficult; As monks travel together, they are not easy to observe. Before reaching Tongguan, the sky has already dawned;
It is unbearable to turn back and gaze toward Chang’an.
(Kai Fu Ning) When the wind at the head grows harsh, it is hard to stand firm; As soon as the warmth returns, one falls into a daze. Yet I laugh at Mingzhao for his idle expenditure.
Force! To arbitrarily arrange two places—(Gushan Gui)—is already a stiff and perverse head.
To further bury oneself in a warm place, only to leave behind traces for a thousand ages, is to have eaten Luoshan’s white rice in vain. (Jieshi Peng)
The monkey and the soft-shelled turtle cannot part ways; summoned and sent away, all suspicion and doubt are severed.
Yet when the conversation reaches the point of paradox, once again the heart and liver are not brought along.
(Ji’ān Dà) Chan Master Dàkuáng of Zhāoqìng in Quánzhōu (a successor of Chángqìng Lèng), while leading the community in carrying mud, halted midway and leaned upon his staff.
Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Is it the mud above the cave or the mud below the cave? The monk replied, "The mud above the cave. The Master struck him with a staff.
He then asked another monk, who said, "The mud below the cave. The Master likewise struck him with a staff.
He then asked Mingzhao, who dropped his mud-sack, stood with his hands folded, and said, "I ask the Master to discern this for me. The Master then desisted.
Jingshan Daokai said: "Although Zhaoqing had indeed put it down, how could Mingzhao bear it?
Had Yunmen seen him set down his mud-sack and say, 'I request the Master’s discernment,' he would have struck him across the spine with a blow. See how he would have settled the matter!
Tianning Weiqing said: "At Guoqing, the talented are noble; in a wealthy household, the children are spoiled."
Zhaoqing asked Changqing, "What is the meaning of your daily clamor with words? The Master replied, "If one does not work for a day, one does not eat for a day.
Changqing said, "In that case, you are sharpening your bow and tempering your arrows. The Master said, "I am waiting specifically for Weichi to arrive.
Changqing asked, "After Weichi arrives, what then? The Master said, "I will let his sinews and bones cover the ground."
His eyes bulged; Qing then went out.
The *Six Tactics* and *Three Strategies* are ancient enough to boast of; without moving a blade, one sees a true master. In the lion’s den there are no other beasts;
when it comes to benevolence, one does not yield, as if having no father. (Xuejian Feng)
Chan Master Baoci Guangyun of Fuzhou (a successor of Changqing Ling) asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Wolong.
The Master said, "How long have you been there? He replied, "I have spent the winter and passed the summer there. The Master said, "The Dragon Gate has no guests who stay overnight."
"Why was there no other beast in that Lion’s Den for so long? The Master said, "Try making a lion's roar.
He replied, "If I were to make a lion's roar, there would be no more Master. The Master said, "Out of consideration for you as a newcomer, I let you off with thirty blows."
Cui峰 Xian said, "Strange! O practitioners of Zen, if one proceeds with impartiality, neither side is harmed; yet if one adheres strictly to the command, both are in peril.
Can you still discern this? Gunan Men said, "Let us set aside this monk for a moment.
But if one were to strictly adhere to the command, how many blows of the staff would Baozi deserve? Qinghua Yan said, "The host examines the guest; the guest..."

They are able to see the master; one might say both are masters of their craft. If it were this mountain monk, I would simply continue to exhaust the Dharma, regardless of whether there are any subjects left.
As the *Renwang jing* (Benevolent Kings Sutra) says: "At the end, I shall give you thirty blows. Is this a reward or a punishment?

Chan Master Baowei Xiaowu of Baoen Temple in Wuzhou (a successor of Changqing Huiheng) was once asked by a monk: "When the waves surge and the cauldron boils, arising must be the manifestation of the absolute reality.
I wonder, what was the intention of the ancients? The Master rebuked him. The monk said, "If that is so, then it is not sequential.
The Master said, "Your words have fallen into error. He added, "My words have also fallen into error; how will you deal with this?"
Life arises. The Sangha remains silent in response.

A single path of green sedge enters the depths of the clouds; on steep cliffs, rosy clouds rise over the forest at dusk. I intend to employ my inner talent to repay that which lies beyond the mundane world;
the traces of the immortals, Ruan and Liu, are but a vain pursuit. (Suan-an Ding)
The Layman Wang Yanbin (who had met Changqing Hui-leng), Grand Tutor of Quanzhou, entered the Buddha Hall of Zhaoqing.
Pointing to an almsbowl, he asked the hall attendant, "What is this bowl? The attendant replied, "It is a Bhaisajyaguru bowl. The layman said, "I have only heard of the Dragon-subduing bowl.
[The attendant] said, "Wait until there is a dragon, and it will descend. The layman said, "What if one suddenly encounters a dragon coming, seizing the clouds and clawing through the waves?"
"How is it? [Yunmen] asked. [The attendant] said, "He does not even look back. The scholar said, "The talk has fallen away.
Yunmen Yan, addressing the temple director separately, said, "When you are reborn in heaven in a future life, do not let me down.
Xuansha Shibei addressed him separately, saying, "Even if you exert all your supernatural powers, where could you go? Baofu Zhuan addressed him separately, saying, "Take refuge."
Regarding the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, Baizhang always maintained a separate stance by making the gesture of overturning his alms bowl.

Guishan Zhe said, "The temple director only knows how to look forward and does not know how to look back; while the Great Minister’s divine majesty was fully displayed, the temple director’s bowl remained overturned.
At that time, had Daowu seen him and asked, "What about when he comes seizing the clouds and grasping the waves? [Daowu] would have lifted up the bowl and said, "All finished."
"By your supernatural power, even if the Eight Great Dragon Kings were to come, they could do nothing but display their majesty and plead for mercy.
Baeryam Pu added: "If I had been there, I would have pointed at the sky and said, 'Release him to go forth as rain across the heavens.
Then I would have pointed at the bowl and said, 'Do not forget that you came from within this. "If the Hall Master had applied such a move at that time, he would have surely [gained the upper hand]."
The Grand Tutor took his place with his knees bent in the proper manner.
When the Grand Tutor arrived at Zhaoqing to partake in the tea ceremony, the Senior Monk Lang and Mingzhao were holding the tea kettle when they suddenly tipped it over.
The Grand Tutor then asked, "What is that beneath the tea stove? Lang replied, "It is the Spirit Who Supports the Stove. The Grand Tutor said, "If that is so..."
"Why did the spirit holding the incense burner overturn it? Lang said, "To serve an official for a thousand days and lose him in a single morning.
The Master (Shishi) shook his sleeves and departed. Mingzhao said, "Dharma Seat Lang has eaten the meal of Zhaoqing, yet he goes out to seek wild roots elsewhere.
Lang asked, "What about you, Dharma Seat? Zhao said, "A non-human being has found its opportunity."
Cui Feng Xian said: "At that time, he should have simply kicked over the tea stove. Wu Shan Zhe said: "Grand Councilor Wang was much like Zhuge Liang seizing the jade;
his hair bristling with rage. Mingzhao was likewise unable to restrain himself, finding it difficult to seize such a favorable opportunity.
If Da Mei had been in the position of Layman Lang, when asked why he turned [the stove] over, he would have simply laughed 'He-he'."
A great laugh. Why? Because he saw it but did not take it; though he thought of it, it was a thousand miles away. Yingshan Yin said:
"Wang Taifu is like the needle on a scale, with the weights clearly distinguished. Nevertheless, he was outwitted by Zhaoqing Mingzhao."
Tell me, where was he defeated?
Because of this, when Changqing cited Xuefeng holding up a whisk to show a monk, the monk immediately stepped out.

The halberds at the gate—whether they are intended as such or not, they stand firm like mountains. At the third watch of the night, one passes through the secure barrier; loyal words do not shrink from weeping before the wind.

"I have asked, yet you did not know"; "I have answered, yet you still do not understand. The moon is cold, the wind is high; ancient crags and frosty cypresses. How laughable, meeting [him] on the road!

(Mingjue Xian) Mountain flowers are like brocade, the water is like indigo; clouds rest upon high peaks, the moon is in the pond. Two earthen oxen fight and enter [the gate].

Mountain flowers like brocade, waters like indigo; Emerging from heaven and earth, revealing no face. I once trod the path by the banks of the Wuling Creek;

Chan Master Xing’ai of Baima Monastery in Xiangzhou (he was a successor of Yuan of Baidiao) was asked by a monk, "What is the matter that lies beyond the Dharma-body?
The Master replied, "A shrimp at the bottom of the well swallows the moon."

A master of hand has never avoided others; lightly picking up the Iron Kunlun, even with the strength of the eight-armed Nala, what kind of pivot could turn his body?
(Pingxiang) Zen Master Dazhu, second generation (successor of Huanglong Ji), asked a monk, "Where have you set out from? The monk replied, "From Min. The Master said:
The Master said, "How brilliant! The monk replied, "I thank you for your instruction. The Master said, "How pitiful! The monk bowed.
The Master said, "When I speak thus, where does it land? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "If he has no wound himself, do not inflict one upon him."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Whenever a master speaks, his words do not issue in vain. Since this monk has come from Min, what excellence is there?
To thank the teacher for his instruction—what indignity is there? Do you see the paradox? If you see it..."
Only then can one believe that the Daoist jujube tree is upon the mountain monk’s whisk. This is raising waves where there is no wind; it is gouging a sore on healthy flesh.
If this is not yet the case, then this old monk’s transgressions fill the heavens. Falin Yin said: "A person of immeasurable capacity has been turned around by the flow of words."
When the monk was about to take his leave, Master Zao asked him, "If you arrive at various places and someone asks you about the Dharma-way here, how will you answer?
The monk said, "I will speak when I am asked. The Master said, "Where is there a Buddha who has no mouth?"
The Master said, "It is 'only this'—is it not difficult? The monk brandished his whisk and asked, "Do you see it?
The Master replied, "Where is there a Buddha without eyes? The monk said, "It is 'only this'—is it not difficult? The monk circled the meditation seat once and departed.
The Master said, "You are well able to respond. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "I do not recognize you, old man. The monk said, "What is the use of recognition?"

Zhaojue Qin said, "The jujube tree has a mouth but is like one mute; this monk has eyes but is like one blind.
He walked once around the meditation seat—the defeated general—then struck the meditation seat three times, his bow broken and his arrows exhausted.

Huanglong said, "Fierce! The Master said, "Not fierce. Huanglong said again, "Fierce! The Master said again, "Not fierce.
Huanglong then struck him, whereupon the Master attained realization.
Chengtian Yi said: "Huanglong’s 'hasty' strike was ultimately nothing but blind censure and reckless blows.
That Heishui attained enlightenment because of it—I dare say he still lacks true clarity."
A hundred-foot pole stands tall, floating amidst the clouds. Once, fragrant bait was offered to twelve oxen. Fortunately, a scaled dragon now surges through the waves;
this time, the golden hook has not been cast in vain. (Kerū Kō)

When looking, one does not see; it is dark and murky. How is it that this is one's own radiance? [The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying:
"The kitchen, the storehouse, and the main gate. He further said: "Better not to have such 'good things' at all."
Yuan-an Yu said: "Yunmen’s two substitute lines—one is picking out stars from within the water; the other is spreading a net atop the mountain.
Beating the drum in the land of Great Tang and ringing the bell in the land of Silla—there is no connection between them.
Please return to the hall for tea. Lingyan Chu struck his staff and said: "The kitchen, the storehouse, and the mountain gate—all are opened wide with a single blow!"
The ladle is large and the bowl is small; let everyone examine this at their own leisure. Ultimately, where does the radiance reside?
It is not said: "To open the mouth is an error; to conceive a thought is to deviate"?
Shining forth by itself, it stands alone in solitary brilliance; for you, I have opened a single thread. When the flowers fall, the tree has no shadow; when one looks, who does not see?
To see or not to see—riding a cow backward, one enters the Buddha Hall. (Cui-feng Xian) Utterly shrouded in darkness, there is no need to look;
it supports the heavens and supports the earth, a vast expanse of black. At the triple gate and the kitchen storehouse, they are ever-present.
Right. A single path, pines and wind fill the courtyard with cold. (Baizhang Yuan) Beyond the night-bright curtain, a thousand peaks are exquisite;
before the phoenix-mirror stand, ten thousand phenomena differ. Erasing traces and extinguishing footprints, not a grain of dust is established.
Who is the Buddha hall? Who is the incense kitchen? Striking out, one produces the five-colored marrow of the phoenix; smashing it, one [reveals] the dragon’s pearl.
The Dragon’s Bright Moon-Jewel (Wenyu Qín):
Each person possesses their own luminosity; when looked for, it is not seen, shrouded in darkness.
When the mountain gate and the kitchen storehouse are kicked over, at that moment light and dark are clearly distinguished. (Weixiao Yan)
Scenery renews itself nearly ninety times; Flowers fall and bloom—the body within a dream. Everyone says tomorrow is the first day of the month;

Shan took the lantern and placed it inside the Buddha Hall; he then took the mountain gate and placed it atop the lantern.
