Lingyin Li said: "Although Yunmen’s announcement was thus, it was a manifestation from within the concealment of the blade;
here, however, it is not so. Within the four modes of deportment, amidst the ten thousand phenomena, there is a treasure hidden in the very presence of the sun.
[He strikes once with his staff and says: 'Do you understand? The Sea God knows its preciousness but does not know its price; he leaves it for the world to illuminate.'"
Night. Anjing said: "Yunmen speaks in such a way to display his eccentricities and delude the masses. Here in my place, it is not so.

Look at the ancient shore. Who is there holding a fishing rod? The clouds drift slowly; the waters stretch vast and wide.

The lacquer bucket was unpleasant, so he requested that it be moved aside.

A single mani jewel is cast before you; it is simply that this monk does not know how to make use of it. Do you understand?
On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, heaven and earth open for all eternity. Having once ascended the Peak of the Golden Wheel, no other mountains are worth counting.
The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month: riding a donkey without beating the drum; the spring breeze brings forth the hundred grasses, adding fresh earth to the graves.
(Zhenjing Wen) A single melody of Shaoyang, its ancient tune pure and clear; over many years, wood and stone have transformed into essence. As it is passed on to others in Guangling, who is there?
Remaining here, one retains the cry of the cuckoo under the bright moon.

When meeting a swordsman on the road, what then? The person in the steamer carries his head and flees south. (Beita Zu)
The "hair-cutting" precious sword need not be drawn; its pure radiance bursts from the scabbard, piercing the Dipper and Ox constellations.
Though fully manifest in daily life, people do not see it. Yunmen’s patriarchal word shall repay you.
(Yunxi Gong) Three feet of autumnal light are hidden within the scabbard; when meeting a true adept, the blade’s edge is revealed. Now, the smoke of war fills the four seas.
Silence. Without unfurling the red banner, he returns to his native land.
(Yuantong Xian) When a monk asked Yunmen, "What is the single path of Yunmen? the Master said, "Intimacy."
Falin’s *Yinyun* says: "The two paths are now clear.
Yunmen’s path is direct; his eyes admit no dust. Since the era of war and strife in the Five Dynasties, how many have seen such peace? (Yang Wuwai).
Yunmen’s single path is level and smooth; one may walk at will, east or west, setting down one’s feet.
Behold well the place where the mist breaks through the green willows, where peach blossoms along the ravine vie with the warbling orioles.

A monk once asked Yunmen, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The single word that pierces through.
Tianning Qi said, "How about Tianning? He took up his staff, struck the meditation seat, and said, "I almost let the prisoner remain in confinement and the wisdom grow."
He uttered a single word, yet it was not quite right. Suddenly turning his head, he said, "Zhang San Li Si.
(Jingshan Daoyuan) When Yunmen was asked by a monk, "What is the 'blow-off-hair sword'? the Master replied, "Skelter. He also said, "Scatter."
"Who says it is a 'hair-cutting sword'? Yunmen’s bones can be known. Once power is in one's hand, only then will the time for the decree to be executed be seen.
(Zhenjing Wen) Yunmen asked a monk, "What sutra are you studying? The monk replied, "The *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*. The Master said, "Your meaning has fallen into error. The monk asked, "How so?"
"Where does this monk fall into error? The Master said, "Take him away yourself.
Zhongfeng Ben remarked: "Adding frost to snow; adding shackles to manacles. Face-to-face, there is no partiality; stars and constellations are shifted.
Do you wish to know where this monk fell into error? Wait thirty years and then see."
A monk once asked Yunmen, "How many years of age are you, Master? The Master said, "Seven times nine is sixty-eight.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Since you do not understand, I shall reduce your age by five years for you."
Foji said: "The Great Master Yunmen’s presentation of the School of the Patriarchs during his lifetime was indeed magnificent;
yet it cannot be said that he did not indulge others to the point of losing his virtue. I, this mountain monk, am not like that.
If someone asks me how old the Master is, I simply say, 'The same age as this staff. If they then ask how old the staff is, I strike them across the back."
A single blow—take it for granted that this brings lifelong joy. Nevertheless, it is still the way Cold Mountain speaks.
When a monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the rain falls continuously and does not stop? the Master said, "Zha! (A sharp, piercing sound).
Tiantong Jie said: "A single note from Yunmen encompasses heaven and earth; the ocean surges with waves, and Mount Sumeru stands towering.
[Suddenly] picking up his staff, he struck it once and said: 'The Great Master Yunmen has no place here to draw breath.
Now tell me, where is Wugu’s 'living human eye'? [Again] striking the staff, he said: 'After long rain, suddenly the sun shines.'"
Qingdi Ning, Hanshan claps his hands, and Shide is filled with joy. To understand it in such a way is like driving a nail into dry land or enduring rain that never clears.
Yunmen says, "Zha! The sun spreads its wings; the dragon retracts its scales and fins. Is this due to the season, or is it the Buddha-dharma?
To conjecture about an arrow hitting two targets is in vain; the pupils in one's eyes are already covered by drooping brows.
(Fo-zhi Yu) Yunmen’s single note:
a hair-piercing blade, its luster shining through the scabbard. Were it not for Zhang Hua, all that blinking of eyes would be in vain. (Yue-bo Ming)
The clay man slays the wrathful dragon; the snow-white blade leans high against the heavens. White waves surge over the mountain peaks;

The Master took up his staff and said, "Zen!
When a crow caws, it is a crow; when a magpie caws, it is a magpie. It is naturally understood; it is not learned from others.
This lame monk lets one move pass by. Raising the staff, he blew upon his lips: *guan guan*, which is still superior to the singing of the partridge in the third month."
*Gu Mei Jiu* (Pouring Fine Wine): The cuckoo urges one on, "It is better to go home.
When a monk asked Yunmen, "Is it true that the Buddha-dharma is like the moon in the water? the Master said, "In the clear waves there is no path through.
The monk asked, "From where did you, Master, obtain this? The Master said, "If you ask again, from where would it come? [The monk asked: "At such a time as this..."

He has lost by one move. But tell me, where exactly was he defeated? Xiangyan Bao took up his staff and said, "If you can understand these three turning phrases, you will not only walk alone across the crimson heavens; you may become a teacher to all people under heaven."
If this is still not clear, I shall briefly provide a commentary and refutation. One phrase is the true wind standing like a wall; one phrase cuts off the tongue;
one phrase is the yellow millet dream upon receiving the pillow. Commentary has been completed; the explanation has been fully revealed.

Do you recognize the old man of Shaoyang? He wields the divine compass of the South with marvelous mastery; he who can turn heaven and overturn the mountains—whom can he share his secret? By Xiu of Qing Shan.

All understood. The layered passes and mountains reveal ever-new radiance.

(Zhandang Zhun): Pervading the entire realm, nothing is hidden; the clear waves are serene and still. Exchanging blows to meet the occasion, the arrow-points meet directly.

Section on Guan (Wenyuan Qinqu). Yunmen addressed the assembly:
"Medicine and illness treat one another. The entire earth is medicine; which of these is the self?
The entire earth is medicine; how could past and present be so mistaken? Close the door and do not build a carriage; the thoroughfare is naturally vast and open."
Mistaken, mistaken! Even the nostrils that pierce through the vast heavens have been pierced through.

(Cui Feng Xian) With the left eye one sees not the mountains and rivers; with the right eye one sees not the sun and moon. It reaches the point where when the hundred flowers bloom, each and every one shall be distinguished for you. (Bai Yun Tuan)
When medicine and disease do not counteract one another, why is it necessary to involve the entire earth? [Geyin] instead mocks Old Yunmen for having lost his mother-born nose.

Leaves and paths crisscrossing, one attains freedom; the sturdy gate’s bolt turned, the wondrous is fully gathered. Within this, the secret meaning is difficult for people to comprehend;

(Heshan Fang) Ten-thousand-fathom Dragon Gate, its momentum leaning against the void; from the hanging cliff, hands are cast off to distinguish fish and dragons. People of the age look only at the fishing line.

thus, for a thousand ages, the wind of sorrow is stirred. (Shushan Ru)
Giving and taking proceed together to determine right and wrong; Shao-yang’s application is too solitary and precarious.
If this monk possessed the diamond eye, the Zhao jade and the city of ten thousand houses would both return as one path.

When Yunmen was asked by a monk, "What is the matter that lies beyond the Dharma-body? the Master said, "It would not be difficult for me to tell you what lies beyond.

"Set that aside for a moment. How do you understand the Dharma-body? The monk replied, "Just so, just so.

In his hands. Truly, one has no way to ascend to heaven and no door to enter the earth. Yet Cuifeng wishes to advance further. Do you understand?

The fragrance fills his gauze robes and his belly is full of strategy; his entire body is graceful and without a single flaw.

Raising his hand, he grasps the Southern Dipper; shifting his body, he leans against the Northern Polestar. Looking out from beyond the heavens, who is this kind of person?

Silent. The embroidered robe still bears the scent of musk.

Dragons coil and tigers crouch; trees grow in layered tiers. Its momentum reaches the floating clouds and yet collapses of its own accord.

in the land of Great Tang, the drum has not yet been struck. Pleasure within suffering, suffering within pleasure—who says that gold is like dross?

How many such fellows from villages of three houses are there, busily trying to catch catfish upon a tree? (Cishou Shen)
When Yunmen arrived at Gao-hu, he heard the Master enter the hall and say: "Do not say that those who have not yet attained realization are constantly in a state of anxious agitation;
even those who have attained it, who clearly know where they are going, are still in a state of anxious agitation.
After the Master descended from the hall, Yunmen asked the Head Seat, "What was the meaning of the Master’s words just now? The Head Seat replied, "Anxious agitation."
"Pressing against the ground. The Master said, "The Head Seat has lived here for a long time; his hair is white and his teeth are yellow—this is the kind of talk he makes.
The monk asked, "And what about you, Senior? The Master said, "If you wish to speak, then speak. If you see, then see. If you do not see, do not speak recklessly.
The monk asked, "As for what you said, 'pressing against the ground,' how is that? The Master said, "Head."
[The Master] placed a cangue upon [the monk's] head and shackles upon his feet. [The monk] said, "In that case, there is no Buddha-dharma.
The Master said, "This is the realm of the great beings Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra."
Taisu Zhè said: "In general, one who 'cleanses the weeds to observe the wind' must be such a person.
Yunmen may truly be called a thunderbolt from a clear sky, a roll of thunder in a drought; it is enough to cause the souls of those for a hundred li to tremble with terror.
Have you not heard it said: 'To startle the multitude, one must be a man of heroic spirit; to overcome the victor, one must be a lion’s cub'? Huanglong Xin said: "Yunmen is like a chisel."

"Driving in a stake into the ground. The head seat used a knife to gouge out the air. Even if one were to drive in both the stake and the knife simultaneously, one would still not escape having a cangue placed upon the head and shackles upon the feet.
Baoshang said, "Yunmen was much like pressing his sword at the Hong Gate; his spirit charged through the ox and the dipper.
At that time, even if there had been generals as numerous as clouds and ministers of state as dense as rain, they could only have done nothing but fold their robes in submission."
Why? The eye is empty; who in the universe could oppose it? Three feet of Dragon Spring sword—its light makes the gallbladder chill.
Yunmen addressed the assembly: "The halved, the split, and the three-needle case—where is the nostril?
Bring it forth for me, one by one, and let us see. He spoke on their behalf, saying: "High, middle, and low."
Jingshan Daokai said: "Leaning on the gate, lurking by the door, they dally with their spirits.
In years past, I once knocked at the pass of Muzhou. To betray righteousness and forget kindness—treat it as a trivial matter. I hear that the Wu dialect has been completely transformed;
Their speech is now entirely that of the barbarians from Guangnan. (Xutang Yu)
Yunmen asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come to pay respects at the stupa. Yunmen said, "You are mocking me.
The monk said, "I truly have come to pay respects at the stupa. Yunmen said, "Then you do not even observe the five precepts."
Baofu Zhan said, "The wise do not reproach the foolish. Fenyang Shao said, "Each other is left standing there, rendered dull.
Yunmen addressed the assembly: "When my staff transforms into a dragon and swallows up heaven and earth, from where do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth come?"
Tongxuan Qi said: "Yunmen’s single-period arrangement is undeniably fresh; yet, when scrutinized, it is still like one who embraces stolen goods while crying out for innocence.
Lingyin Li said: "Yunmen is much like having hidden away the moon of the Chu heavens, yet leaving behind the stars of the Han lands.
Here, it is not so. [He] picks up his staff and says: 'The staff has already secured the universe.'"
[He said: "To whom have the mountains, rivers, and the great earth been entrusted? He struck the ground once and said: "When one person rejoices, ten thousand people depend upon it.
The staff swallows up heaven and earth; it is in vain to speak of rushing through the peach-blossom waves. Those who burn their tails do not rely on seizing [the fish].
Clouds seize the mist; why must those who bask in the sun lose their courage and souls? It has been grasped. Whether you hear it or not, you must remain free and unburdened;
do not continue to be muddled and confused. Seventy-two blows were lightly pardoned, but one hundred and fifty are difficult to let you off with. (Cui-feng Xian)
Having nurtured the transformative material of Huanglong, suddenly there is a clap of thunder on level ground.
Intending to show it face-to-face to others, he swallows the universe and spits it back out.

The eyes have pupils and the skin has blood; one must truly have a trace of a mark for every blow.
Do not let the "cat-spirit" and the "white ox" mock you; right now, serving intimately, there are no descendants.

A mountain that is nearly complete does not advance even a single basket of earth; old and decrepit Yunmen sits and reaps the benefit. He is one who hooks the giant tortoise and the great whale.
His skillful means were lofty. Having long been accustomed to descending into the sea and traversing the waves, he could freely exercise his mastery in releasing slowly or drawing in swiftly.
Floating house, drifting abode—how carefree and unmoored!

Kuai Pingsheng’s insight was also correct for his study of the Way. Tianning Qi said, "Great and small Yunmen were both exposed by the steward.
Falin Yin said, "When you scold me, I’ll let you have your bundle; when you spit at me, I’ll let you have your splash of water."
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when all-encompassing wisdom penetrates without obstruction? The Master said, "Sweeping the floor and pouring water;
the Duke has arrived. Sweeping the floor and pouring water;

A laugh. What prevents the blue eyes from opening specifically? (Cishou Shen) Sweeping the floor and splashing water—the Duke arrives.

he possesses the talent to serve as a general or minister among men. (Shui'an Yi)
The All-Knowing One’s penetration is without obstruction. Sweeping the ground and splashing water—the Lord has arrived.
Meeting face-to-face, seizing the opportunity like a flash of lightning, Hanshan claps his hands and laughs heartily.

A student came forward and asked, "When one has truly reached such a state, what then? The Master said, "From where could illumination be established?

it does not belong to Śākyamuni’s discourse on the orthodox or the deviant.
Once, a monk who was a lecturer came to visit Yunmen. After some time had passed, the monk said, "Before arriving at Yunmen, it was just like the new moon;
once I arrived, however, it became all crooked and bent. The Master, knowing this, summoned him and asked, "Did you say that?
The monk replied, "I did. The Master said, "Very good. Let me ask you: what is the new moon? The monk then—
The monk struck his forehead and made the gesture of gazing at the moon. The Master said, "If you continue like this, you will lose your eyesight in the future.
Ten days later, the monk returned. The Master asked again, "Do you understand now? He replied, "I do not yet understand. The Master said, "Ask me."
A monk then asked, "What is the newly risen moon? The Master replied, "It is curved and crooked. The monk was at a loss.

Langye Jue said, "Tell me, does the Buddha-dharma still have spiritual efficacy? Suppose someone were to ask this now..."
"What is this newly born moon? [The monk] replied, "It is the sound of the wooden board being struck before the Dharma Hall.

once you are fully satiated, you will naturally forget all hunger. (Tieshan Ren)
Cloud Gate ascended the hall, held up his staff, and said: "Ordinary people truly say it exists; those of the Two Vehicles analyze it and say it does not exist;
Pratyekabuddhas call it illusory existence; Bodhisattvas regard its very substance as emptiness.
But for us monks, when we see a staff, we simply call it a staff. When walking, just walk; when sitting, just sit. Do not disturb it."
Jingshan Daowu said: "I am not like Yunmen, who digs a hollow in empty space. He suddenly took up his staff and said:
"This staff does not belong to existence, nor does it belong to non-existence; it does not belong to illusion, nor does it belong to emptiness. He struck the ground once and said:
"Ordinary beings, those of the two vehicles, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas—all turn toward this very place. Each, according to their own capacity, fully attains its use. Only..."
Within the realm of the patch-robed monk, this staff acts as a source of harm and an enemy. When you wish to walk, you cannot walk; when you wish to sit, you cannot sit.
Take one step forward and you are made to lose your way by the staff; take one step back and you are pierced through the nostrils by the staff.
Is there anyone here now who does not find this bitter? Come forth and meet the staff! If there is no such person, [then the staff remains].
"Next year there will be new shoots again; the spring wind’s vexation shall never cease. Tianning Qi said: "Ordinary people should not give rise to the view of existence.
Those of the Two Vehicles should not give rise to the view of non-existence. Pratyekabuddhas should not give rise to the view of illusory existence.
Bodhisattvas should not give rise to the view that things are empty in their very essence. One must not let this pass. This old fellow Yunmen is greedy."
Watching the white waves, he loses his oar; he brings all the patch-robed monks of the world into trouble, causing them all to fall into the circle of the staff.
This cannot be let pass; it would be best to bury him whole in a single pit.
How can one say that the Two Vehicles and Bodhisattvas have reached their end? When will the Buddhas and ordinary people finally rest?
Worldly affairs are simply settled by the way of public justice; the human heart is difficult to keep like a flowing river.

Courage follows the cataracts as they end; The mind flies with the waves as they subside. When the boatman reports the cataracts have ended, Mind and courage return at once. (Gufeng Yuan)
The spring colors have no high or low; the flower branches have their short and long. Though the Taihang Mountains are perilous paths, people continue to travel them as before.
(Shuzhong Yun) Yunmen ascended the hall and said:
"When light does not penetrate through, there are two kinds of illness. In all places one is not clear, and before one's eyes..."
There is something; it is one. Furthermore, it penetrates and transcends all dharmas, yet it is an empty, indistinct state that resembles the semblance of having something;
this too is light that has not been fully penetrated. Moreover, the Dharmakāya also has two kinds of illnesses:

reaching the Dharmakāya and yet clinging to it as a dharma, failing to forget one's own views, and still remaining seated within the realm of the Dharmakāya—this is one. Even if you manage to penetrate through this...

When the mind realizes its identity with the essence, it cuts off the disease-root of the flowing stream; when one reaches the source and forgets emotions, one mirrors the scene of the non-self.
Only those who have manifested bodies beyond the limit of Avidyā (Wei-yin), those who sleep soundly at the crossroads of the marketplace, can be examined and treated.
Otherwise, do not mistake a daily malaria for a case of *shanghan* (febrile cold).
The myriad phenomena of the universe stand majestic; Transcending them leaves no trace to obstruct the eye. Who has the strength to sweep away the traces at his gate?
Hidden within the breast, a natural sentiment arises of its own accord. A boat lies across the wild crossing, reflecting the autumn’s azure;

The flower-moon shadows shimmer along the celestial street. Intoxicated by the eastern breeze, I lean alone against the balustrade.
After the morning court has ended and the ninefold palace is silent, the six palaces still adjust their robes and caps.

The *Qǐgāngzōng* states: "Deshan’s three phrases for instructing disciples—'Śākyamuni has not even a single word'—spare you the trouble of forced interpretation.
Śākyamuni and Bodhidharma are no match for him. 'Encompassing heaven and earth' is the Sun; 'cutting off all streams' is the Fragrant Elephant."
Following the waves and drifting with the currents—like floating duckweed. A single arrowhead pierces the three barriers;

clearly, this is the path behind the arrow. When Deshan ascended the hall, he said: "Study only the living word; do not study the dead word. If you can realize it beneath the living word, you will remain unobstructed for eternal kalpas.

The monk said, "In that case, I am not mistaken. The Master then struck him.
The *Qigangzong* states: "This mountain monk has re-examined this case. The two houses are harmoniously integrated;
mundane and supramundane are enjoyed as one. Do you understand? Simply investigate the 'dead word,' do not investigate the 'living word. If you can realize it beneath the dead word,"
Eternally across kalpas, there is no obstruction. A single speck of dust is a Buddha-land; a single leaf is a Śākyamuni—this is a living phrase.
Raising an eyebrow, blinking an eye, pointing a finger, or holding up a whisk—these are living phrases. The mountains, rivers, and the great earth, without further ambiguity—this is a living phrase.
If someone asks, "What is a dead phrase? one replies, "The Persian looks up at the sky. If it is so, then one has not erred. However...
There are utterances that possess no real meaning at all.

I laugh at myself, now old and lacking such spirit; let the clouds and birds fly about as they please.

Rest. Remembering the *shébù* partridges crying in Jiangnan (Changling Zhuo).
Having escaped the body of a frontier garrison soldier, he comes instead to steal the sight of spring in the imperial gardens.

Not knowing, he instead asks the moon at the edge of the sky. The School of Deva, the School of Deva: beneath the red banner, a pure wind arises.

Not only does this save us from one more blow of the staff, but let us see how Old Man Mingjiao rises. He said again, "Dangerous!

Sitting for long becomes weary, yet it is also peaceful and joyful.

(Fujian Qin) To seize [the mind] at the place where all news is cut off is to let it run away within form and shadow. It is simply because one is too lazy to question one’s own descendants that one wishes to wear the formal robe backward.
Sitting for long becomes weary; the rank is already high, but upon rising, one loses the marks of humanity and heaven. There is none.
Only those who can recognize the white tuft [of hair] are permitted to enter.
(Chang of Yuet-tang) Once, when a monk asked Xianglin, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? the Master replied, "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountain."
Zhaojue Qin said: "To bring up one is to clarify the three; this is the aperture of the patch-robed monk. A thousand differences follow a single track; it is the fundamental tongs and hammer.
Although this is so, Daolin does not think so. If someone were to ask about the matter beneath the patched robe, he would simply say:
'Cotton wrapping a magnetized stone; iron encasing a lump of clay. Tiantong Hua said: "When Xianglin spoke thus, he was like a rat."
"Entering the ox-horns. If someone asks about the matter beneath the patch-robes of the Returning-to-the-Source (Gui-zong) school, he simply says to them:
"Next year there will be new branches; the spring wind, though vexing, has not yet ceased. Pingyang Min said: "When the Patriarch spoke thus,"
This, too, cannot avoid the fault of grasping for what comes before while losing what lies behind. If someone were to ask me, this mountain monk, I would simply say:

"A single breath remains silent, yet it contains all phenomena; where could the myriad spirits fail to find their impartiality? Gunanmen said: "Xianglin practices the spring mandate in winter; Cuifeng tears from the east to patch the west.
If you wish to understand the matter beneath the patched robe, each of you must seek it out for yourselves. Ling.
Yan Chu said: "Dongshan was not like this. If someone were to ask such a question, he would simply say: 'Movement gives rise to wind. Now tell me: which is it?
Is it the one at Xianglin, or is it the one at Dongshan? If you can discern this, then Dongshan’s life is in your hands;
if you cannot discern it, then your lives are in Dongshan’s hands. He then cast down his staff.
Zhaozhou said, "The one who carries his life comes to the hook. Tianjing Xin said, "Where Cui峰 drags through mud and carries water, he chops nails and cuts iron;
where Zhaojue chops nails and cuts iron, he drags through mud and carries water. Do you all know how Xianglin acts for the sake of others?
A dog runs off with a dry bone in its mouth."

In the twelfth month, the mountains are set ablaze; ten thousand kinds and a thousand varieties [perish]. The crane perches on the pines, chilled by the cold; the man stands in the snow, frozen by the frost.
Bodhidharma did not understand—what a great difficulty, what a great difficulty!
(Cui-feng Xian) In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains; two luminaries appear at the edge of the heavens. Xiang-lin never understood it; he sat in vain at the Jianmen Pass.
(Foyin Yuan) In my later years, winter has arrived with bitter cold; The leaves of the thousand trees are now falling away. Blazing wild fires leave no flowing streams;
It must be that they follow the wind across distant mountains. (Shangfang Yi)
The great elder of the forest speaks Chan with ease; he does not hang Chan upon the surface of his lips.
Valleys deep and mountains remote, empty and without form—where can anyone call out so that the resonance is not perfect?
(Tiantong Jué) The nest knows the wind; the burrow knows the rain. How pitiable is Xie Sanlang, rowing his boat all alone under the moon. (Wenshu Neng)
Under the patched robe, one tends the fire; the mountain is ablaze. In the twelfth month, poverty pierces to the very bone. How laughable that the spreading flames have not yet ceased;
the eyebrows are scorched crimson and the face is parched.
(Tiantong Jing) In the twelfth month, the fire burns the mountain; heaven is vast and earth is wide. Sadāprarudita Bodhisattva suffers; throughout the market, he sells his heart and liver.
(Qiaoyuanquan) Xianglin was asked by a monk, "What is the livelihood of a patch-robed monk? The Master said, "Plowing fields in one's ears;
plowing fields in one's ears, with smoke filling the mouth. Zhong Kui can dance the eighteen beats; Zhang Lao rides the raft up [the Milky Way]."
Nine Heavens. (Wuan Quan) When a monk asked Xianglin, "Who is the master of ten thousand acres of fallow fields? the Master said, "Look, look; the twelfth month is ending."
The embroidered ball is tossed before the painted hall; its wondrous turning is impartial, its essence naturally perfect.
If you truly wish to perform deeds upon the edge of a sword, you must once again meet old Yunmen. (Shi Ming) Look, look! As the twelfth month draws to a close, how is the matter of daily life?
The wealthy loathe that a thousand mouths are too few; the poor lament that a single body is too many.
(Chun-na Qing) Xianglin was once asked by a monk,
"What is the single lamp inside the room? The Master said, "Three people testify that a tortoise becomes a turtle."
Suiryak Yun said: "The three men have taken a tortoise and turned it into a turtle; each has a tongue in its mouth. When the occasion arises, they cannot discern the wind coming from;
even when drinking water, one must guard against choking. Old Xianglin was able to lead and uplift [others], yet the true lamp illuminating the world was completely blown out. *Hah!* (A shout)."
When six ears conspire, the matter does not succeed. Speaking directly reveals the heart of one with sincere intent. Who comes to flicker the lamp-flame within the chamber?
A child with white hair has newly grown whiskers on both temples.
(Touzi Qian) The brilliant, pure light pervades the world; there is nowhere to hide it. Sound cannot be cast out; how could form manifest it? Cut through the nail right where it is.
Cutting through iron. Eradicating the tracks and byways of past and present, he rises far above Linji and Deshan.
Three people take a tortoise for a turtle; how extraordinary! Each time one drinks water, one chokes. (Zhaojue Qin) Three people take a tortoise for a turtle;
at the bottom of the well, the mud-ox’s breath is choked. Even if one’s eloquence were like a cascading river, there would still be reason [to fail].
It is difficult even to clear one’s name; a solitary light shines on high, ever bright and pure.
(Fóxìng Tàiyīn) Three people testify that a tortoise is a turtle. Amidst the fierce flash of a stone-fire, smoke rises from beneath the earthen ox;
an wooden horse bites iron in its mouth. Separately, separately! Where could there be heat when frost flies in the sixth month? (Cāngyán Huī)
A monk asked Xianglin, "Why does the delicious flavor of *amṛta* turn into poison? The Master said:
"Paper is in demand at Dujiang;
to the west of Jinxi, the misty waves are green. After the fresh rain, the lichees ripen on the mountain peaks; by the side of Wanli Bridge, there is much wine."

Chan Master Shouchu Zonghui of Dongshan in Xiangzhou (Successor of Yunmen Wenyan). Initially, he visited Yunmen. Yunmen asked him about his recent [practice].
"Where did you depart from? The Master said, "I crossed at Cha. "In what place did you spend the summer retreat? The Master said, "In Hunan. "When did you leave there?
The Master said, "Last autumn. "I grant you thirty blows," [the Master continued]. "Where does the fault lie? [the monk asked].
"The fault lies in going directly to Jiangxi and Hunan in such a manner," [the Master replied]. At these words, the monk attained sudden enlightenment.

Cui Feng Xian said: "Yunmen’s presence was like that of a king; when pressed, it would melt away like ice dissolving. Had he acted according to the mandate at that time, his descendants would not have come to such an end. Baizhang Yuan said:
"Great Yunmen, upon being questioned by Dongshan, found himself so utterly at a loss that sweat broke out on his forehead and glue formed in his mouth. Baoning Yong provided another [verse]:

The King of the Sky, his countenance majestic, A single word from the Mountain Cave, and he is struck dumb. If he had followed the command then and there, His lineage would not have been severed today.
Yunmen’s later words say: "You blind fellow! I thought you were a person. He then struck him. Tiantong Jie says:
"Yunmen was too generous in letting go and too stingy in gathering back. At the end, he was so earnest; why not have given him his proper share of fodder?
Dongshan’s awakening in this way was also like 'divining with a ladle while listening for an empty sound.'"—Lingyin Yue.
It is said: "Everyone everywhere claims that father and son met their opportunity and struck simultaneously, like a chick pecking at its shell and the mother from without.

Little do they know that Yunmen’s true command was not being exercised; instead, he rolled about in a patch of weeds, causing Dongshan to lose his nostrils so that, to this day, there is no place to find them.
Fushan said: "When you hold fast to heaven and earth, Buddhas and patriarchs have no path for entry; when you let go..."
In rivers and seas, fish and dragons find their way to swim and play. The old man Yunmen was indeed extraordinary. Cui峰 said, "Yunmen’s bearing was like that of a king;
once pressed, [his defenses] would melt away like ice and crumble like tiles. What did he know of good and evil?
Had he enforced his command at that time, he would have blinded the eyes of all people under heaven. Tianjing Xin said, "The mountains are high and the waters are deep; the clouds..."
To act like a bird in flight is acceptable at the Cloud Gate, but not at the Well of Heaven. Why? A house is not wealthy simply because it has no stagnant goods;

one releases the hawk upon seeing the rabbit. Because of this action, the arms dangle. When the bare bones are exposed in poverty, whether square or round, one is truly rich and noble—thus, three blows of the staff are bestowed.
Still hesitating, he struck again and only then recognized the sharpness of the awl’s point. Beyond the solitary mechanism of the single-legged staff, even clear-eyed monks do not yet understand it.
(Yuánwù Qín) From of old, the Great Way leads straight through the Chang’an;
at every step, one must look with eyes that see. At the five-li mark, one knows only how to return the five.
After many miles, only at the end does one realize the difficulty of the path ahead.
(Failing to wither away,) he sits firm as an old ox in Shaoyang. Suddenly, beyond the lakes of Jiangxi, there is a response. At that time, the iron barrier was raised high;
it was not necessarily that the Yellow River would not flow backward. (Baofeng Xiang)
Mistaken words in mutual exchange—guilt cannot be escaped. To let him off with three blows makes him fret and fume.
He sends that rice-bag off toward Jiangxi, raising the price of rice in Luling even higher.
(Zhongfeng Edition) Once, when a monk asked Dōngshān, "What is the Buddha? the Master said, "Three pounds of hemp."
Mingjiao Kuan said: "To the south there are bamboos; to the north there are trees. Tianbao Shu said:
"It might still be tolerable for a rope to grow from hemp, but how can one endure a snake growing upon that rope? He gave a shout and said: "A single path traveling back and forth through Chang'an."
A five-colored painting of an ox’s head, its forehead marked with gold. On a spring morning in the second month, all the farmers take it as their model.
At the Cold Food Festival, they celebrate the New Year; three or five hundred pieces of iron cash are spent.

(By Fuyan Ya) With sidelong glances he reads Sanskrit characters; with clicking tongue he recites mantras. He blows on the fire with a long, pointed bundle of straw; wood fills the hearth and smoke rises.

(The Great Fool Zhi): The golden crow is urgent; the jade hare is swift. How could a skillful response ever involve a slight or a touch? Unfolding the task and meeting the opportunity, one sees Dongshan.
The lame turtle and the blind tortoise enter the empty valley. Flowers cluster thickly; brocade clusters thickly. Bamboo from the south and wood from the north.
I recall Master Lu of Changqing, who understood that one should laugh and not weep. (Cui Feng Xian) How can one distinguish the hemp-skin?
Waxing snow brews tea to soothe your intoxication. Yet there is a path where travelers have not yet arrived;
wild flowers smile, and the old branches embrace spring. (Fa Chang Yu)
A leap year once every three years is known to all; yet there are those who are coarse and fail to keep track of the time.
Last night the geese returned as the desert passes grew cold; a piercing wind blew through the branches of the moonlit trees.
(Touzi Qing) A single slice of newly risen moon, like a蛾眉 (yumei—crescent) painted across the azure sky. The fish in the water avoid the hook; the birds beyond the clouds guard against the bow.
(Yuanxian Zun): Clouds rise as the thousand mountains awaken;
the wind rises high as the ten-thousand trees turn autumnal. Beneath the waters of Stonehead City, waves beat upon the fishing boat. (Fohui Quan)
In the third month of Jiangnan, it is the day of the partridge; after the rain, the scenery of all peaks is fresh.
Having traveled to the ends of the earth, one understands the ways of the world: to buy shoes, one must have plenty of bright coins.
(The Third Patriarch) Donkey tails, pig heads, and ox tracks—three catties of hemp skin reveal the secret message. Master Zhì’s staff-tip holds a pair of scissors.
A foot. From time immemorial, when rain falls, the steps become wet.
(Yùquán Liǎn) Life and death have always been entirely within one’s own power; the weapons and armor of the three frontiers are gathered in at once.
Who would have known that without employing any strategic maneuvers, one could sit and pacify the four hundred prefectures of the Central Plains? (Dā’ān Zhuāng)
A dragon-scaled, single-horned green *qilin*, with golden eyes emitting light like fresh lightning;
though it cannot be detained by golden chains or jade railings, it has flown up to the Purple Palace of the Heavens during the night.

(By San-yi Yu) I ask the Buddha: "Three pounds of hemp. Eyes meet face-to-face, hands even more so. Planting trees atop a tiger’s head; burying a person upon the *taisu* (the year’s presiding spirit).
(The Han-Guan Parable) A monk asked Dongshan, “What is the Eye of the True Dharma? The Master said, “A paper wick with no oil.
Dongshan Yan remarked, “It is not that Dongshan has nothing; it is simply that he is too frugal. If someone were to ask me today, I would simply say: [a lamp with no oil].
Facing the Way, one is blind. Why? It is simply because they must correspond to one another.
Dongshan, the master craftsman, was a bit more discerning; he tested the true adept with a paper wick without oil. Old, decrepit Chan practitioners have eyes like needles;
they speak of Chan and speak of the Way as frequently as hemp seeds. (Cuiyan Zhen)
A paper wick without oil is truly marvelous; no one knows it is unfit for picking up. Turning back, he remembers the path he came by;
under the moon, he strides home with confident feet. (Wuzu Yan) Dongshan ascended the hall:
"Words do not unfold the matter; speech does not meet the occasion. Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases..."
"Deluded! Can you still recover? Within the domain of you monks, you must possess the eye that discerns dharmas to reach this point.
As for Dongshan speaking thus, he too has a fault. But tell me, where does the fault lie?"
Yuan'an Yu said: "In a night dream, I had an inauspicious omen; I inscribed it upon the wall. When a gentleman reads it, it is transformed into a great auspiciousness.

A thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions are resolved through seizing the opportune moment; at such a time, the enlightened master is present.
Though the Northern Dipper hides its body and there are words, few know the news that transcends the crowd.

Once awakening comes, not a hair’s breadth of effort is required—it is like a cricket swallowing a large tiger amidst the flames.

"How do you deliberate upon this? As Fandeng hesitated, the Master struck him with his sitting mat and returned to the assembly.
Furizhi remarked, "Fayan possesses the marks of a great man; Fandeng is but a petty fellow. Senior Dharma Master Shen was accustomed to finding such openings.
Had he been under the gate of Long’an, none would have been permitted to move at all. Why? Because those who recognize the Dharma stand in awe."
The soundless great ocean surges with waves reaching the heavens; at the Yanzu Mound, it rages as if howling. The seasoned fisherman sits idly watching;
he would startle the people of this age with the height of the crests.

(Pingyang Min) In the military camp, talk of tigers stirs as battle clouds open; wishing to emulate the former masters, one’s hands are tied. As spears and halberds are just deployed, victory is divided.
Defeated. Riding backward upon the enemy’s horse, he seized the standard and returned.

(Yuanzhiyuan) To pierce the willow leaves at a hundred paces requires subtle skill; deploying such mastery in every direction is rare in this world. Among these, a single arrow is difficult for others to learn;
having shot through the heart of the flower, he returns with the prize. (Xueqijing)
A kind of innate, peerless talent; seizing the moment, he brings forth wind and thunder.
With the sharp edge of his rhetoric, he overturns all eight directions at once, winning him the planting of palace flowers throughout his hair.
(Meishan Yuan) Fengxian and Master Ming arrived at the Huai River and saw a man pulling a fishing net; there was a fish within the net.
He broke through. The Master said, "Brother Ming, you are truly brilliant! You are just like a true monk.
Ming said, "Even so, it would have been better had I not run headlong into this net at the beginning. The Master said, "Brother Ming, you still lack awakening.
It was not until midnight that Ming finally realized this.
Jingshan Daowu said: "As for what Upāsaka Ming has realized, tell me: is it within the net or outside the net? Yuan'an Yuanwu said:
"Once bitten by a snake, one fears rotten grass for three years. Xidun Chao said:
"One must know that the words of the ancients were not spoken in vain. But tell me, where was his lack of realization? If you turn toward..."
"Let my lord issue an order to search for him; you must strike until the staff breaks. If he gives some vague, delusive answer, do not stop even when the staff is broken.
Aside from these two possibilities, is there anyone who knows where these two men have gone?
He then laughed heartily and said, "They have entered! They have entered!"
How magnificent! With one leap he penetrates the deep abyss; a thunderclap pursues him, but he goes away and does not return.
One must laugh at those who "burn their tails" at the Dragon Gate—still, they remain with their foreheads marked amidst the waves.

(Jingshan Gaofeng) Leaping high across the vast waves, he passes through the heavy barrier; roaming at his pleasure, he calls out but cannot bring him back. How pitiable are those who sink quietly into the ditches and ravines!
How could one know the ocean is vast? Let it be as it is in its leisure.
(Xiu of Qing Shan) A single stroke of a fisherman’s song amidst the rain on the reeds; startled egrets fly into the autumn mist. Previously, I was a captive official wandering through Chang’an;

now, by fortune, I walk at ease along the clear shores. O Su Gong, O Su Gong, friend with whom I shared a bond as deep as a severed neck—how can I repay you but with these words written upon the grass?
To know oneself. (The Three Proper Basins) Li Yuanjun fashioned the jar;
Shang Jun established the penal code. This is to apply the very methods of a person to treat that person’s own body.
(Qiyou Chan Master of Nan Yue Banruo Monastery [Yunmen Wenyan’s successor]; Xidun Chao) A monk asked: "In India, they used a wax figure as a test.
I wonder, what do you use as a test here in this land? The Master said: "A Korean person wearing straw sandals."
Picking up a tortoise’s hair, one laughs heartily; with a single blow, ten thousand layers of locks are opened.
Even if a wax figure were as frozen as ice, what would it matter? It is no more than a person from Silla wearing straw sandals.
(Kusan Mirror) Chan Master Jingqin of Shuangfeng in Shaoyou (a successor of Yunmen Wenyan) addressed the assembly: "To take a step forward is to lose sight of principle; to retreat..."
"To take even one step is to lose the matter. Even if you remain in a state of total stillness, you are no different from the insentient.
A monk then asked, "How can one avoid being like the insentient? The Master said, "Moving and acting.

The monk asked, "How can one avoid losing the matter while remaining deluded about the principle? The Master said, "Take one step forward, then take one step back. The monk bowed, and the Master said, "Go!"
When someone came with such an understanding, the Old Monk did not approve of him. The man said, "I beg the Master to point it out directly. The Master then struck him.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Like a hawk seizing a sparrow, like a falcon catching a pigeon—this is the subtlest of the subtle, the most wondrous of the wondrous."
A step forward, one does not lose sight of the principle; a step back, one does not fail in the facts. This is what is meant by "within suchness, there is non-suchness;
within non-suchness, there is yet suchness. Within this, there is a final stroke that outshines the past and transcends the future.
Shuangfeng was asked by a monk, "When Piṇḍola accepts offerings throughout the four worlds, does he reach them all?
The Master said, "It is like the moon entering the water. The monk asked, "How is it that he acts without confusion?
The Master said, "Jade dew hangs before the Hall of the Bright Moon; pearls sparkle within the Crystal Palace."
Blended yet unmixed, its essence is eternally empty; snow and moon intermingling their light—nothing can compare.
Responding to myriad circumstances without hindrance, a single cloud moves freely, rolling up and unfolding.
(Zide Hui) Chan Master Wutong Ji of Beichen in Qi Prefecture (a successor of Yunmen Wenyan) asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Huangzhou."
The Master asked, "Where were you during the summer retreat? The monk replied, "At Zifu. The Master said, "With what did you provide for that merit?
The monk replied, "A case of double meaning. The Master said, "But how can it be when it is in the hands of Beichen? The monk said, "If it is in your hands, then take it back.
The Master struck him. The monk was dissatisfied; the Master followed him out and drove him away.
Cui峰 Xian said, "How extraordinary! This monk truly possesses a composition that surpasses his teacher. Do you know this monk? He only knows how to pursue what is ahead and cannot look back.
Had he been in Cui Feng’s hands, even if the staff were broken, he would not have let him go.
Nantang Yu said, "One does not stop at half-measures; to strike a man, one must have an iron fist."
Chan Master Huanglong Zan of Meizhou (a successor of Yunmen Wenyan) asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Xianglin.
The Master said, "How long have you been there? The monk said, "Six years. The Master said, "When the World-Honored One was at the Snow Mountains for six years, he realized unsurpassed Bodhi.
What have you accomplished during your six years at Xianglin? The monk was speechless. The Master [said]: "..."
It is said: "A fellow who moves his kitchen to eat his own meal.
Baoshou Xin says: "According to Huanglong’s judgment, this monk is not worth a single coin. Yet, if one looks closely, he is not without merit.
But tell me, where lies his merit? One sees only the vast expanse of the waves; one does not even realize it is Lake Dongting."
Shen. Chan Master Chenggu of Jianfu in Ruzhou (a successor of Yunmen Wenyan). A monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “No, no.
Again he asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, “No, no.”
A man from the north happens to meet a man from the south. He asks him how he eats lychees. Before his mouth has even opened, he has already fallen into error;
let me repay him with the two words "sweet" and "fragrant. (Wuwen Can) An iron cauldron floats on the waves to catch the giant sea monster;
a silver lamp with moldy flowers intoxicates one with spring wine. Do not be surprised that the fragrance lingers when the curtains are drawn.
The Duck: For generations he has held the imperial brush, possessing the "phoenix feathers" (of literary talent).

(Xiangweng Yun) He cuts off the flow of a thousand rivers so they do not leak away. His vision surpasses Buddhas and Patriarchs; his spirit swallows the oxen. Where the world’s edge ends, there is no more warfare;
from the myriad villages, the sounds of stringed songs rise up from painted towers. (Xue'an Rui)
The Ninth Generation Descendant of Dajian, Master Baohua of Lianzhou (Succeeding Baiyun Xiang), asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from Dayong.
The Master said, "What has been happening at Dayong lately? The monk said, "Lately, they have managed to brew a jar of soy sauce. The Master then called out to him.
A novice brought a bowl of water and offered it to the monk for him to see his reflection.
When he opened the door, what did he see? The spring colors filled the level forests; rejoicing that a noble guest had arrived, he played the zither and struck the lute.
Chan Master Wenshu Yingzhen of Dingzhou (a successor of Deshan Mi). A monk asked, "The myriad dharmas return to the One; to what does the One return?
The Master said, "The Yellow River has nine bends."
Questioning the Dharma to its ultimate cause, where does it return? The Yellow River flows through waves of azure ripples.
One must know that beyond the clouds, atop a thousand peaks, there stands a numinous pine tree, cold with dew.
(Touzi Qing) The path ends and the crags break off; there is no door for entry. Fortunately, the mountain elder points out the source. The nine-bend Yellow River is clear and transparent.
The bottom. Who knows that this is a separate heaven and earth?
(Lan’an Xu) Nine bends cannot be viewed with a sidelong glance; who understands the waves as he steers the boat? Mañjuśrī once displayed his hand that turns heaven;
it was enough to dry up the myriad streams of the Tidal Source. (Muguan Yong)
A monk asked Mañjuśrī, "What was the meaning behind the ancients' gesture of hanging down one foot? The Master said: "Sitting for too long leads to fatigue;

as soon as the letter is sent, one returns in haste. Hanging down one foot is a response that follows in the footsteps of those who came before. Who understands that sitting for too long leads to fatigue?"
All at once: "Like snow falling on a red furnace, they naturally commune with one another.
(Touzi Qing). Zen Master Qin of Nanyue Nantai (a successor of Deshan Mi). A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said: "An inch of tortoise hair weighs seven catties.
In ordinary speech one does not meet anyone; to speak is to wound the truth, yet it seems too intimate.
Disregarding that the phoenixes have ceased their song within the flames, he startles the stone tiger, who secretly gives rise to anger. (Touzi Qing)
A marvel erupts from within the stone; the Iron Woman grapples the clouds and dances the sun. How many times have we heard the cascading waters fly down the cliffs and ravines?
To this day, the sorrowful resentment remains without explanation.
(Tianqi Ruchi) Lingcheng Sansheng (Baoling Jian’s successor). When Master Yin Kuan asked, "Where have you come from? the Master replied, "The water is clear, the moon [is reflected]."
Manifesting himself, Kuan said, "Very well, let me ask you this. The Master said, "A short jacket is not dyed black. Kuan said, "Go drink tea;
the sea and sky are vast and wide—a single cry of autumn. It cleaves the reflection on the clear river, which flows backward.
On the verdant ridges of Hengyang, the moonlight divides; only the traces remain, causing one to grieve. (Ssuan-an Ting)
One day, Lingcheng went up to the hall to pay his respects to Master Kuang. Kuang said, "It has been several days since you, the Senior Monk (Zuozhang), arrived;
have you been at ease? Lingcheng replied, "Spinach makes a fine soup. Kuang said, "This fellow has true resolve.
Lingcheng said, "The character for 'king' (Wang) does not take a dot. Kuang clapped his hands and laughed heartily.
"An object picked up beside the Wind and Rain Pavilion; Meeting people, he calls out to sell a night-bright pearl.
Though it is brilliant and strange as it is tossed and hurled about, There is still cause for apprehension even amidst laughter while brandishing a sword.
(Jian’an Yi) Master Jie of Wuzhuo in Qizhou (Shuangquan Kuansi), because of Yujian’s verse on Yunmen’s "The Northern Dipper is hidden," [composed this].
Shenhui said: "The Northern Dipper concealing its body is the very act of exalting it; from this, the Dharma-body is revealed in full majesty.
Yunmen has deceived his own followers until the present day, leaving them to measure it in vain. Now, let us ask about the intent behind his verse."
Jian then opened his eyes and looked at him. The Master said, "If you understand it in this way, Yunmen is not worth a single coin, and you yourself would have lost both eyes.
Jian indeed came to pass exactly as he had been told; in his later years, the Master also lost one eye.
Juefan Hong said: "The way people today recklessly speculate on the words of the former masters, thereby misleading future generations, should serve as a slight warning.
Zhongfeng Ben said: "'The Northern Dipper conceals its body'—this was not something even Yujian’s verse could express;
even Wuzu Jie would have had to stand behind him with palms joined. That he lost his sight in his later years was also [a consequence of this]."

Excellent! Master Hong remarked that such is the karmic retribution for falsely slandering one’s own ancestral lineage: "Do not let the intellectual learning of the common schools bury the heart-mind of the Patriarchs.
Once, when a monk asked the Fifth Patriarch, "What is the Buddha? the Master replied, "Treading upon a scale-weight, it is harder than iron."
Treading upon the scale-weight, as hard as iron; the bewildered Chan practitioners have not yet glimpsed it. On Mount Erdong, fire-clouds arise;
in the sixth month, heavy snow falls from the long sky.
(Yunfeng Yue) Walking at ease amidst the red dust, no one asks about its length or brevity. Returning when the day is about to end, a sliver of moon illuminates the vast waves.
(Tianning Lian) The cowherd returns home riding his ox backward; the bright sun in the city does not cease until late.
Treading upon a scale-weight, hard as iron—how could he have known the boatman would head for Yangzhou? (Fotu Xun)
The Fifth Patriarch asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "From the Eastern Capital. The Master said, "Have you seen the Emperor?
He replied, "Every year, once, he goes out to the Jinming Pool. The Master said, "If there is reason, it may be excused; if there is no reason, it cannot be tolerated."
"Go out! Zhenru Yuan said:
"This monk has come directly from Dongjing. When he responded in such a manner, did he see the Son of Heaven or not?
When the Fifth Patriarch spoke thus at the end of his teaching, was he rewarding him or punishing him?"
The Fifth Patriarch was once asked by Zhimen: "I do not ask about the passing of summer and the arrival of winter; what is it like when meeting beneath the forest trees?
The Master said, "Listening to the jade water-clock before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion. Zhimen said, "But what can be done? The Mountain of the Lord is high, while the Mountain of the Altar is low."
The Master said: "Striking a golden bell atop Mount Sumeru;

silver waves surging from the highest peaks; red dust rising from the deepest ocean floor. The golden bell and jade water-clock answer one another in acridity, leaving the vast world of people in a state of doubt.
Were it not for a true master, who could pass through these barriers? Only by holding the whip and looking back can one truly understand."
The four seas are good neighbors. Have you not seen how Zhongni and Wenbo Xue met beneath their overturned canopies—how truly marvelous!
(Yuǎnwù Qín) Listening to the jade water-clock before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, one strikes the golden bell atop Mount Sumeru; the Great Spirit lifts his hand, yet there is no more to it.
My son! He split apart the myriad layers of Mount Hua (this is the awakening of the hermitage).
Hares and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have no horns. Cut off to the last hair and the last filament, as vast as mountains and peaks.
Like the rhinoceros at the Ox-Island, he parts the waves and billows of the ocean floor; like the swords uniting at Yanping, they scatter as rain and hail across the clear sky. Be silent! Be silent!
Waving the hand across the river, there is one who understands; why wait for the awakening that comes from a single night at Caoxi?
(Xiaoyin Yun) Chan Master Zhimen Guangzuo of Suizhou (a successor of Xianglin Yuan). A monk asked: "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water?
The Master said: "The lotus flower. The monk asked: "What is it like after it has emerged? The Master said: "The lotus leaf."
Tiantong Jue said: "The numinous tortoise has no lines; the empty shell need not be drilled.
The lotus flower and its leaf tell you to know: once it has emerged from the water, it is the same as when it was not yet emerged.
Ask the old man Wang north of the river and south of the river—once a doubt is resolved, another doubt is resolved. (CuiFeng Xian)
Smoke enshrouds the greenery beyond the balustrade; the wind shakes the fragrance of every stalk in the pond. Thank you, O woman who washes silk, for not plucking them;
you have left them in the rain to shelter the mandarin ducks. (Cishou Shen) Lotus flowers and lotus leaves share the same pool;
year after year, their petals and leaves are green interspersed with red. The spring waters ripple with clarity and purity.
At the bottom, a single cry of a bird in the wind of the fifth watch.
(Zhang Wujin) The lotus leaves are round, holding up emerald canopies; The lotus flowers are radiant, vying for their crimson makeup.
Their fragrance transcends all categories, yet no one offers it; Once more, they follow the warm breeze across the wild pond. (Yungeng Jing)
Master Zhimen ascends the hall: "If there is even a single dharma, Vairocana falls into the rank of ordinary beings;
if the myriad dharmas are non-existent, Samantabhadra loses his realm. At such a time as this, where does Mañjuśrī emerge?
If he cannot emerge, the golden-maned lion’s waist will break. Fortunately, there is a full plate of rice; do not wait until it is seasoned with pepper and ginger."
A thousand *qīng* of fertile fields were claimed as one’s own; for nine out of ten years, they underwent the vicissitudes of the tides. Now, putting forth his hand, he invites others to buy them;
the entire root and source are entrusted to those who truly understand the trade.
(Fenxiang) A monk of Zhimen asked, “What is the essence of *prajñā*? The Master said, “An oyster containing the bright moon. [The monk] asked, “How about...”
This is the function of *prajñā*. The Master said, "A rabbit is pregnant.
Cui-feng Xian said, "Not only does it hold fast to the world, but it also brings peace and stability to the state.
If you are well able to investigate and contemplate this, then please walk alone across the crimson sky. Gu-nan Men said, "What is the essence of *prajñā*? Blind."
People see only darkness. What is the functioning of prajñā? When the loom stops, the shuttle halts. O assembly, why must you seek it out with such deliberate effort?
It is fortunate that you may sit securely within your own home. Do you understand? Had I known earlier that the lamp was fire, how much longer would it have taken for the rice to cook?
A single expanse of empty stillness, beyond all conceptualization— From this, humans and devas see emptiness arise. The oyster holds the bright moon; how deep is its intent!
It has once waged war against the Chan school. (Cui-feng Xian) The oyster holds the bright moon;
the autumn waves are cold. The hare conceives the fetus; the night spirit is chill. The brilliant, pure light becomes one.
A single fragment. You must turn your head and observe it well. (Fojian Qin) The jade hare conceives within her womb;
the oyster holds the bright moon. The timing is precisely the Mid-Autumn Festival. A single luminous pearl rolls upon the jade platter;
thoroughly without flaw, its radiance is pure and brilliant. (Cishou Shen)
The moon reflects in the crystal pitcher, suddenly shattered; whose rabbit is it that does not carry a fetus? The pure light is scattered and difficult to contain;
brooms fly about, yet they cannot sweep it away. (Yunlin Lu) Zhimen was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Tread through straw sandals and walk barefoot. The monk asked again. [The Master replied: "Tread through straw sandals and walk barefoot."
"What is the matter beyond the Buddha? The Master said, "On the tip of the staff, one lifts up the sun and moon.
Cui-feng Xian said, "A thousand soldiers are easy to find, but a single general is hard to seek.
Xiao-yan Bao said, "One phrase clarifies three phrases; three phrases clarify one phrase. This belongs to him, Zhi-men. As for Cui-feng speaking thus, where does it lie?"
The monk is at Zhimen; try to settle it and see for yourself. Tanglian said: "One step wider than the last, one move higher than the last.
Old baldy Zhimen—this too is a great mistake. What is his point of error?"
When a gentleman speaks, his words are like a nail driven into wood.
He tramples through straw sandals and walks barefoot; when a patch-robed monk reaches this state, there is no fixed pattern.
With the tip of his staff, he carries the sun and moon, roaming freely throughout the nine provinces and the four seas. (Zhenru Zhe)
The gate of wisdom truly captures the ancestral style. Yunmen lets loose his broad and long tongue: great wisdom appears as if ignorant, great skill seems as if clumsy.
Though one exhausts every effort, the mystery remains unfathomed; do not pile up earth upon level ground, and do not drive stakes into empty space. (Tiantong Jue)
On the tip of his staff he carries the sun and moon; hiding his body within the Northern Dipper, how extraordinary!
The ocean of three thousand worlds is deep and dark, yet a single point of snow emerges from the new furnace.

(Nantang Jing) Having trampled through straw sandals, he runs barefoot; the indignation in his breast pierces the Ox and Dipper constellations. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, he strikes the golden drum.
The Bell: A Lion’s Roar in the Midst of a Hundred Battlefields.
Master Xiang of Lotus Flower at Tiantai (Fengxian Shen’s successor) held up his staff and said, “When the ancients reached this point, why did they refuse to stay?
No one in the assembly could answer. He then said, “It was because their progress along the path lacked power. He spoke again:
"How, ultimately, is it so? Holding his staff across his shoulder, he said: "Carrying my knotted staff slung over my shoulder, I look not back at people;
I go straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
Zhaojue Qin said: "He deserves thirty blows as well. It is simply because he carries a wooden board on his back;
his cheeks can be seen from behind his head. Do not associate with him. Can you all discern the Master of the Hermitage? His heels have not even touched the ground.
Tiantong Jue said: "He is brought in but not brought out. A man who dwells in the mountains in his true colors. Sida swallowed all Buddhas; Puhua..."
"The Eye does not see Samantabhadra. Now tell me, where does the sickness lie? [He suddenly picks up his staff and strikes once, saying:
"In public, even a needle is not permitted; in private, a carriage and horse may pass through. Baoshou Xin said:
"The lotus-staff has already stirred up and disturbed the three thousand great thousandfold worlds. Do you know it yet? It has now transformed into a dragon. Can you subdue it?"
"Eh! Dust in the eyes and earth in the ears; though there are a thousand peaks and ten thousand crags, he refuses to stay.
Fallen flowers and flowing water are vast and boundless—raising his eyebrows, where has he gone? (Cui-feng Xian)
Wandering aimlessly amidst the flash of a stone-light; Linji’s “white-handed” theft has no peers.
He overturns Mount Hua and Mount E’er until the heavens turn black—who knows that his body is upon the imperial tower?

(Wuan Quan) He enters straight through a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks; the willow flowers fall away as the apricot blossoms turn red. His entire body is mud and water, yet he is utterly without [stain].
The Master stands to one side, robes trailing through the clouds as the dawn bell tolls.
(His companion) raises his cloud-flute and plays it in reverse; once the melody ends, tears soak his robe. Who would have known that it turned into the "Yuyang" mode?
Amidst bitter rain and chilling winds, the sound grows even more mournful. (Guanzhi’s principle)
Ten li of yellow clouds darken the white sun; The north wind blows geese as snow falls in profusion.
Do not worry that there will be no one who knows you on the road ahead; Who in all under heaven does not recognize you?

(Byan-’phur rgyang) A young lord in brocade robes strolls through the imperial streets; Along both sides of the road, peach blossoms are endless to behold. How many times he has ascended to the heights and leaned upon the parapets!
The eyes see that the mountains and rivers no longer hold the autumn of the Han palace.

(Falin-yin) Chan Master Huiyuan of Deshan in Dingzhou (a successor of Yunmen Wenyan’s lineage through Shuangquan Yu). A monk asked: "The three-month summer retreat for restraining the feet is now complete;
what is the ritual for the *pravāraṇā* (self-indulgence) ceremony? The Master said: "A monkey chasing a butterfly, taking nine steps."
After a pause, [the student] asked, "What is the meaning? The Master showed him with this verse: Two children carry a wooden drum;
The one on the left beats it, the one on the right dances. In a single instant, they manifest hundreds of thousands of forms; I show them clearly to you—take heed and remember!
Ruayan Yun said: "The answer has been given; the verse has been composed. Yet, this monk still refuses to nod his head in agreement.
Seeing this as an injustice on the road, Ruayan felt he must meet with Deshan. With self-indulgence upon him today, he places a flower right before his face.
One phrase settles the confusion: the monkey chases the butterfly; the butterfly flies away, nowhere to be found—empty.

He sat in meditation in the midst [of the assembly]. Like threading a needle at the bottom of the sea, he suddenly took up his staff, looked left and right, and said, "Is there anyone among you who would celebrate and praise because of this meal?
He struck the ground once and said, "Do not let your idle scholarly interpretations bury the mind of the Patriarchs."

A monk asked, "There is already firewood on the mountain; why are you carrying it away? The Master set the wood down on the ground and said, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not understand. The Master [said]: [The Master] said: "If you can see the firewood as the mountain, then you have attained the Way. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "If you can see the mountain as the firewood, then you have attained the Way. The monk asked, "How can one attain the Way? The Master said, "If you can see the Way as the mountain, then you have attained the Way. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? Three parts of the day have already passed as two; how could the turtle ever run out of the jar? **Explanation:** This passage is a commentary on a verse by Xuedou Chongxian. The first two lines describe a state of non-duality where distinctions between directions vanish and the natural world remains untouched by human artifice. The third line depicts a figure in a state of total relaxation and freedom. Daopei critiques Xuedou for providing a "dizzying" (mingxuan) remedy that exhausts the practitioner's mind. He then offers his own commentary, noting that time passes swiftly and that the essence of reality is never lost, just as a turtle cannot escape from its jar. The phrase "three parts of the day have already passed as two" suggests the rapidity of time, while the final image implies that the fundamental nature of things is always present and cannot be lost.

I do not envy the distant scenery of Chang’an; by the waterside and beneath the trees, my life’s vocation is complete.
Serenely, I possess another kind of leisurely governance: sitting daily atop the tower, I count the falling petals.

Chan Master Chenghao of Yiqian in Jingmen (successor of Beita Guang)—while a monk was entering the room, there was a dog nearby.

A Verse on the Dharma-body Beyond the Jade Spring: One night the rain poured down in torrents, Knocking down the grape arbor.

The administrators, heads of departments, and laborers were all called upon for communal work; Those leaning leaned, those propping propped— Propping and leaning until daybreak. As before, how pitiable they are!

who would believe that, facing the wind, it suddenly becomes circuitous? (Shiyu Fang) The traveler’s road south of the mountains winds and turns;

[He] left. At the head of the fence hung an embroidered waist-skirt.

"How much does the gourd-drinker weigh?"东坡 (Sōngp'o) had no reply.

Two and a half catties—altogether in one's own hands. Even so, it is still necessary to help up Yüan-ch'uan.
It simply depends on how heavy that shout of his was; how many people cannot utter it? Even if they could, you would give them another shout.
Ching-shan Hsiu spoke on behalf [of Yüan-ch'uan], saying: "He has still not cleared the scale-pan. P'ing-yang Min.
It is said: "Everyone says that although Zizhan possessed ten thousand scrolls within his breast, it did not take a single shout from Yuquan for them to melt away like ice and crumble like tiles.
Yet they fail to realize that Yuquan’s walls and moats were not secure;
with a mere slight pressure from him, Zizhan was completely exposed. O Assembly, please examine this: where exactly was he exposed? If you cannot identify it,"
He could not avoid being completely seen through by the worldly official. Tianjie Shengdai said, "The grass-robbers have suffered a great defeat.
Guangjiao Yudai said, "This fellow was caught on the first cast."

Yuzan said: "Snow, snow—flakes upon flakes, without distinction. It continues down until the twelfth month, and then proceeds as before through the first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth, and eleventh months of the following year without ceasing.
Let it freeze them to death and starve them to death; this will spare them from their wild and incoherent talk."
Miyin said: "This is neither an insult nor a praise. It surpasses Linji and Deshan, yet it is not like Yunju’s 'Arhat.
Tell me, what was Yquan’s intention? After a long silence, he said: 'If only the snow would melt away.'"
Spring arrives naturally.
On the Winter Solstice, Master Yüquan ascended the hall. As the movement of the sun’s shadow shifts, the coarse cloth trousers are a brilliant crimson. Do not wonder why they are unwashed;
there is nothing to replace them.
Dian Niu wanders through the clouds; at both the Great and Small Yuquan, waves arise without wind.
Yunyan saw injustice on the road and brought it down with a single blow, shattering it to pieces. He then cried out loudly, "Look at his feet!
Jianfu Can said, "At that time, had I been there, I would have said to him: 'Stop showing off so much!'"
Boasting of wealth and status; selling out one's own poverty. Killing a person may be excusable; groundless conduct is difficult to tolerate.
(Wu Zhunfan) To follow the vermilion and paint the crows is not yet enough to speak of; to follow the crowd in learning the clouds of calligraphy is but a waste.
Now it is even more unbearable in its disorder; smearing and waving wildly, it is intolerable to hear. (Yin Rucheng)
One woman marries one man; one horse mounts one saddle. The green mountains naturally grind through the ages;
the flowing water has never left the azure sands.
(Yun’an Liang) Chan Master Huailian of Dajue at Yuyang Mountain in Ningbo (a successor of Ledu Tangcheng under Wuzu Ke) ascended the hall and said: "The bright day..."
Ascending in the east, the white sun sets in the west; as swift as a game of *touhu*, it flashes across the vast void. A divine dragon takes flight in a single leap, penetrating the boundless;
yet its slender scales still leap within the mud. Amidst the spiritual flames, do not linger or settle. A three-year-old child wears his hair in four-cornered tufts. *Chan*.
Where the gauze robes hang, the autumn mist is thin; as the thatched door first opens, the wild waters are clear.
Finding contentment, let us cast down the three-footed hook; the bamboo blinds are rolled high, revealing a single peak of green.
(Fenxiang) Chan Master Yihuai of Tiantai Monastery in Yuezhou (successor of Xuedou Xian), upon accepting the invitation to Shanshan, ascended the hall for the opening address. (2)
For ten years I have joyfully admired this mountain. Today, I am glad that the conditions have finally converged.
Though I, this mountain monk, have not yet reached it, my body has already arrived here. Yet when I actually arrive at this mountain, Mount Sōan will be within my own body.
Shifting the body and changing the step, the old Tianyi [Huikai] does not spare his eyebrows—who knows him?
If today you clarify the affairs of that very day, the partridges cry out as spring warms in Jiangnan.
(Cishou Shen) When a monk asked Tianyi, "What is it like when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? the Master said, "It supports the heavens and props up the earth. The monk said:
After being ground down, what is it like? The Master said: "Within the shadows of the setting sun, there is no hiding one's body;
supporting the earth and propping up the heavens, this is the total manifestation of function. Within the shadows of the setting sun, there is no hiding one's body.
Sometimes sitting alone on the peak of a solitary mountain, in profound stillness, one still hears the frequent sound of falling leaves. (Songyuan Yue)
Tianyi ascended the hall and said: "A wild goose flies across the vast sky; its shadow sinks into the cold water.
The goose has no intention of leaving a trace, and the water has no mind to retain the shadow. If you can be thus, only then will you understand how to act among those of different species.

There is no need to shorten the crane or lengthen the duck, nor to level mountains or fill valleys. Let it go, and there are a hundred uglinesses and a thousand clumsinesses; bring it back, and one is still cramped and constrained."
Earnestly, I employ it; I dare to vie with the Eight Great Dragon Kings in wealth. If I do not employ it, it is altogether not worth half a penny. *Chan*.
The wild geese cry out as they fly through the high, cold clouds; their shadows fall upon the chilly river, yet they remain unaware. The river water is without sentiment, and the geese have no—
The mind acts among different kinds in this very way. (One Original Enlightenment) A lone wild goose in the vast sky cries out in autumn.
The Persian offering jewels has a nose like a hook. The wind sweeps white clouds back to distant peaks;
At twilight, the moon hangs from the tips of the willow branches. (Wan’an Rou)
Tall bamboos and lofty pines suffice for the four eaves; when the moon is bright and the wind is still at night, the curtains hang down.
A wooden bed and earthen stools are perfectly suited to one another; with a single turn of the body upon awakening, willows and cicadas cry out.
(By Yuan Yafu) The headless boatman sails down to Yangzhou, chasing the waves and following the wind to the very ends of heaven. This is simply the spirit and interest of the helmsman.
"Excellent! Even where there is no elegance, there is elegance. (Muan Mi) Tianyi addressed the assembly: "The ancients said:
'Upon the mountain of the five aggregates is a single expanse of emptiness; entering and exiting through the same gate, we do not meet.
For immeasurable kalpas we have lived in rented houses, yet in the end we do not recognize our own master. There was an old man..."
Xiu said, "Since you did not recognize him, whom did you ask when you first rented [the room]? To handle it in such a way is far-fetched. Why?
You must know that on the road of the dead there is a place where the living emerge; on the road of the living, there are countless dead.
Which is the road of the living where there are countless dead? And which is the road of the dead?"
This is the place where people on the road find their true origins. If you can examine this with clarity, you will cast off the cap of dripping fat and strip away the stinking cloth tunic.
Jingshan Daowu said: "The ancient Buddha Tianyi’s words are beautiful, yet they are not yet perfect. Let the discerning patch-robed monks try to distinguish them for themselves.
