(Nantang Jing) Tianyi said, citing the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: "If one sees that all marks are no-marks, then one sees the Tathāgata. This is the Dharma-eye.
[The monk] said: "If one sees that all marks are no-marks, then one does not see the Tathāgata. The Master said:
"If one sees that all marks are no-marks, where then are the eyes? This statement contains two points of defeat.
Who can see that all marks are no-marks? Seeing and not seeing must both be investigated.
If one penetrates thoroughly through these two points of failure, only then will one see Gautama.
(Benjue I) Tianyi addressed the assembly: "When the hundred limbs have all crumbled away, one thing remains eternally numinous. When the hundred limbs crumble away, they are all..."
Returning to the earth. Where does that one thing, eternally spiritual, find its rest? Nan Tang Jing said:
"Where does that one thing, eternally spiritual, find its rest? The vast sky clears of clouds and the azure heavens are wide.
Innumerable flowers fill the lotus palaces and Buddha-fields; raise your eyebrows and observe them closely. Tian Qi Rui said: "As for observing..."
"None. What do you call 'one thing'? [He] gave a shout. Nengrenjian said: "Nantang’s speaking in this way is fit only for entering the Buddha, not fit for entering the Māra.
As for my own view, I wish for all of you to know it together: 'One thing is eternally efficacious; where can it be placed?
Turning the body, one treads upon the full moon; the mountains of knives and trees of swords must be shattered. Hot!"

Where is this one thing that has long been numinous placed? Within it lies a phrase—allow whom to investigate it? Clouds withdrawn and mist dispersed, the autumn sky is still;
ten thousand miles of moonlight, a single sphere of jade.

the roof broken, one sleeps gazing at the stars.
"Bones thin and skin withered, clothes are torn; deep in the night, the roof broken, one sleeps gazing at the stars. "The crown of the head does not possess the *kāla* [the temporal bone]."
Eyes! Do not ask about the Chan of the Patriarch who came from the West.
(One’s original enlightenment) reveals its hidden form without one’s own awareness; how can it be endured when the roof collapses and shadows fall away?
Sleeping among the clouds and啸 (shouting/singing) at the moon is truly extraordinary; who else has such a spring breeze to carry down? (Gloss by Kegyū)
Rigid, gaunt bones pierce through the cold and warmth; the roof is broken, the stars sparse, revealing the crown of the head.
As soon as the black-lacquered lantern blinks its eyes, one transforms into a flying *kūn* at midnight in the Northern Ocean.

[The student] asked, "What is the meaning? The Master said, "Even if it were Pāpīyān, he would still knit his brows. [The student] said, "Thank you for the instruction, Master.
The Master said, "From India to this land.
Gushizang said: "Master Yi washing himself while clutching the bridge pillar—while it is not that he does not hold the rope and let the boat go, one must..."
Furthermore, those who lack the eye of a man of the Way wait for others to ask, "What is Buddha? before they cut down the carrying pole.
What is the underlying meaning? A yakṣa pointing at a ghost; thanking the teacher for his instruction. The well is deep and the rope is short—how pitiable!
Chan Master Fachang Yiyu of Hongzhou (the successor of Beichen Xian) asked the two head seats, Ying and Sheng:
"I wish to build a Dharma hall here; tell me, what is the appropriate course of action? Ying said, "The thief is the petty person.
The Master said, "Zi of Shaowu moves and immediately emits the stench of excrement. Ying said, "It has weathered the frost."

Pai said, "Where would you, you donkey-headed fellow, put it? Sheng said, "I leave it to you to beat the bricks and smash the tiles.

The Master said, "When a member of the eastern household dies, the members of the western household offer their condolences. Ying said, "Seeing it on the road..."

These three old men have indeed seen much of the world. Yet, as for the Dharma Hall, it has never been finally settled. Why? This year...
"When the Tai-sui (Year Star) is directly ahead, one must encounter Wu and Ji.

He sought a National Teacher who had no Zen; as soon as there was even a hair's breadth of involvement, he would execute him. It is laughable that this monk extended his hand.
In this matter, the Way has no partiality; there is simply no seeing of imbalance.

"Be careful not to startle the snake. Yanguan said, "Do not try to smear mud on others. The Master said, "And what are you doing, poking your head into a glue pot?

Shengshou extended both hands. Yanyue said, "A shrimp cannot leap out of its basket. Shengshou said, "Do not attempt to compare a three-inch candle to the brilliance of the great sun.
Yanyue said, "But what can be done? The public case is right here. Shengshou said, "Disciples of Zen who create disorder are as numerous as hemp and millet."

Lotus-pickers sing songs of lotus-gathering; Oars and poles, paired together, glide upon the deep blue waves. In that single matter which touches the human heart, To this day there remains a mystery upon the river.

Carrying my staff, I stride out through the pines; In every place, the peach blossoms are fragrant and rich. This brings me to mind the old master Lingyun of old.

The scholar said with delight, "I request your presence immediately. The Master replied, "The four elements of this mountain monk are fundamentally empty; the five aggregates do not exist.

Píngyáng Mǐn said: "Fóyìn forgot the hook while coveting the bait; Dōngpō used his cleverness and ended up being clumsy.

Would that not have made the elegant Scholar Sū appear truly outstanding? Tiānjiè Shèngdài said: "If you act like this, then you will be caught by me."

In vain you boast of nimble hands used to pilfering gates; the ramparts and fortifications remain as solid as mountains. Though every stratagem is exhausted, there is ultimately no door through which to enter.

(Yuechuan Yin) Chan Master Fajian of Jiangshan, Jinling, the twelfth generation descendant of Dajian Huineng (Yunju Shunsu). A monk asked: "What was the intent behind the First Patriarch’s wall-gazing?"
"What? The Master said, "Supporting heaven and propping up earth. [The student] asked, "What is it like when one goes directly in this manner? The Master said, "Falling to seven, falling to eight.
He asked again, "What was the intent behind the Second Patriarch standing in the snow? The Master said, "Every three years there is an intercalary month."
[The questioner] asked, "Why did he transmit the Dharma and pass on the robe? The Master said, "Village wine is enough for anyone to buy.
Baiyan Fu remarked, "There is resonance within Jiangshan’s words; its bestowal and seizure are worth observing. Truly, it is fit to be the eyes of gods and humans."
An encounter once in ten thousand ages. Here, however, it is not so. What was the intent behind the First Patriarch’s facing the wall?
"Sifting for fish and shrimp on level ground. What is it like when proceeding in this manner? "When the waves at Caoxi are like this, countless ordinary people sink beneath them.
What was the intent behind the Second Patriarch standing in the snow? "Piercing the brain and entering the glue-pot. Why was he given [the Dharma]?
The Dharma was transmitted with the robe. If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci hell, do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata.
Chan Master Jiebi Furi of Hangzhou (successor of Liaoyuwang) was asked: "What is the Seal of Vairocana? The Master said:

Yet it is little known that ancient script is difficult to clarify; thus, this monk meets [the truth] as if he had not met it at all.
Fengguo was not like this. What is the Vairocana Seal? Not a single stroke is added to the text. If you practitioners do not understand, how can you possibly understand?"

Fire-trees reach toward the heavens, shining through the night; Wandering youths, do you know where to return?

Yuantong addressed the assembly: "Sitting in cold meditation at Shaolin for nine years was ultimately seen through by Shen Guang.

Within the cave, one vainly prolongs the years and months;
the world can be made to match an ancient mirror. To seek discernment within words is itself delusion; where white clouds arise, the green mountains are beautiful.
At dawn, as before, the moon sets in the west. (Xiang Tianqing)
The worlds of the ten directions are a single mirror; looking at one’s form within the mirror is not yet the truth.
When you touch your own nostrils and realize, "This is me," only then will you see the person of original nature.
(Lan’an Shu) A bolt of plain silk has just been woven; its length and breadth are perfectly suited to the lover’s heart. A pair of mandarin ducks calls out in the autumn.
Water: Even if there were the monk Zhiyao, he could not paint it.

(Clouds, banks, and peaks)—without cause, a clear breeze rises from level ground. It sways the dense shadows of flowers, casting them deep. At night, leaning against the river tower, I gaze idly toward the horizon;
the *huqia* flute has blown past the eastern sea gate. (Zhengfan Kai)
When Xuansha traveled south, the people of Putian County staged a hundred varieties of performances to welcome him.
The following day, the Master asked the Elder Xiaotang, "Where did all that clamor go yesterday? Xiaotang lifted up a corner of his cassock.
The Master said, "It is like trying to catch a fish with a net; there is no connection."
Fayan Yi said, "Yesterday there was quite a commotion. Qingliang Qin said, "Today it is even more laughable.
Guishan Zhe said, "Daopei does not do it this way. If someone were to ask me, I would simply snap my fingers once."
If a monk comes forward and says, "I expect there is no connection," Huanglong Xin would instead approve of him. Why?
Because for a great man, even plucking a tiger’s whiskers is his rightful duty. But tell me, where does the point of profit or loss lie? Huanglong Xin said:
"To uphold and establish the vehicle of our school, it must be an elder like Xiaotang; why did Xuansha say, 'He is tossing and turning, there is no connection'?
I do not think so. If someone asks me, I simply say: "The heavens share the white clouds at dawn;
the water flows with the bright moon. Zhaojue Qin said: "If someone were to ask me, I would simply say, 'It starts all over again. If he..."
The Way is not something to be grasped or discarded; it has no point of contact. [If you try to grasp it,] I strike you across the spine with my staff.

Why? "The waves at Caoxi are just like this; countless ordinary people sink beneath them. Boshan Lai said: "To test water, one uses a tongue; to test water, one uses a staff. One discerns true gold amidst a blazing fire;
one recognizes the Son of Heaven in the midst of a bustling market. Recognize the old monk beneath his *kāṣāya*—this is Xuansha."
This person of Little Pond—though he may cover it over with a lid, his mouth is bitter while his heart is sweet.
There is yet more to come: hiding a boat in a mountain ravine at night, or rowing upon a clear source. Fish and dragons do not yet know that water is their life;

a broken chopstick may as well stir it about for a moment. Old Man Little Pond, Third Master Xie: the seal covers the arrow-point; the probe-stick tests the shadow-grass. He withdraws and contracts. Old Man.
The tortoise nests; the lotus plays. Flower-scaled fish sport among the algae.
(Tiantong Jue) Today is silent and still; yesterday was noisy and clamorous. When the wind ceases, the flowers still fall; where the birds cry, the mountains grow more secluded.

(North Gorge Jian) A guest amidst the flowers, an immortal within the wine. Returning to the Jade Pass in autumn, he does not come back in spring. Falling petals and warbling birds in chaotic profusion;
mountain windows and cave doors in silent stillness. Who in these gorges knows of human affairs? From afar among the crowds, one gazes upon the empty clouds.
*Shan* (Iron Face Xuan). Xuan Sha asked Jing Qing:
"The scriptures state that for a Bodhisattva, not seeing a single dharma is a great fault.
Now tell me, what dharma do they not see? Jing Qing pointed to a pillar and said, "Is it this dharma that they do not see?"

The Master said, "In this region of Zhejiang, you may eat as much clear water and white rice as you wish; yet you have not even dreamed of the Buddha-dharma. Tong’an Xian commented on Jingqing’s words, saying, "I know that the Master does not act rashly. Cui-feng Xian said:

[The Master said,] "In this region of Zhejiang, you may eat as much clear water and white rice as you wish; yet you have not even dreamed of the Buddha-dharma. Tong’an Xian commented on Jingqing’s words, saying, "I know that the Master does not act rashly. Cui-feng Xian said:
Both the Great and the Small Jingqing were thoroughly deceived by Xuansha. Had I been there at the time, I would have simply said:
"The prediction on Vulture Peak has not yet reached this point. Guishan Zhe said: "Had it not been for Jingqing, one would almost have forgotten what came before and lost track of what followed.
Why? Because unless one meets someone else, the fist will never be opened. Tiantong Jue said: "At that time, Jingqing..."
Answering in such a manner—did Xuefeng’s final words accord with this or not? Thus it is said, "Jingqing has long since ceased dreaming of the Buddha-dharma";
one must be a fellow practitioner of Xuefeng to truly understand. Tiantong Huo said: "Jingqing let loose his stubbornness;
even a Buddha could do nothing for him. Had it not been for Xuefeng seeing through him, he might well have been trapped by a pillar."
[He] swallowed it whole. Tiantong Jue said: "When these two venerable masters met unexpectedly, it was very much like children playing;
where were the Buddha-dharma and their own bodies and minds? Having finished citing the words of Ying’an Hua, he gave a shout and said:
"If one were to cause tears to fall frequently, even the vast ocean would have to dry up."
The old man Xue’s lineage is noble and his offspring flourish; he is further able to value the sacred bonds of kinship.
Though his management of the household affairs resembles that of others, there are those among them who fall for wine and stray into the weeds.

(Xutang Yuyuan) A subtle mechanism sets a deep pitfall; sharp blades clash with rapid fury. No one recognizes the merit of the sweating horses, yet we shall once more discuss his epoch-making achievements.

(Dong-sou Ying) Thread goes and silk comes, stitched together closely and thickly. Every word is precise, the underlying sentiment profound. A bystander sees through it; it is difficult to conceal or hide.
Even feigning a look of anger, one cannot get through with insults. (Hai-zhou Ci)
Owl-lipped and quail-tongued, they speak in local dialects; though their hearts share the fragrance of orchids, their minds are as cold as a snow-bladed sword.
Flowers fall before the courtyard as jade dew flies; the *xuan* and *chi* pipes are blown toward the moon for one to behold.
(By Xiangweng Yun) A man beyond the world roams beyond the world: a lion of the West River, a ball of Lingnan. His refined elegance is inexhaustible, yet his innermost heart remains.
Song: Hand in hand, we descend once more from the Jade Tower. (Cold Pines Tune) Xuan Sha was asked by Jing Qing:
"I am a student newly entered into this forest; I beg the Master to point out a path for me to enter.
The Master said, "Do you hear the sound of the Yan River water? He replied, "I hear it. The Master said, "Enter through here."
Wuzu Yan said: "If you have truly attained entry, you may roam freely in all four directions and eight facets.
If it is not yet so, you must by no means depart from this very place. Jingshan Gao said: "If you wish to truly attain entry, you must directly depart from this very place.
Tiantong Jie said: "These three great elders were all merely contending at a crossroads, rubbing one wooden bucket against another."
"There is a place of great joy. As for me, a mountain monk, it is not so; I do not even like to hear the word "entering.
Tianning Qi said: "What kind of place is this? Whether one leaves or does not leave, whom else would you ask?
I recall those days by East Creek, when flowers bloomed and leaves fell; how many times I intended to cast gold to fashion a Zichqi! Jing.
Tingzong said: "The three great elders shifted the strings to a different tune; their instances of granting and revoking are worth observing.
Yet, had they acted according to the proper command, they could not have avoided receiving thirty blows of the staff. Why? At midnight the great sun shines; when the sky is bright, the head falls."
Heaven-born son of Kunlun with azure eyes, possessing skills that surpass others yet remaining unaware of them himself. How many times the black winds have overturned the great ocean;
amidst the waves he emerges and submerges, sporting at ease.
(Baizhang Yuan) Wind-blown fragments of jade, snow upon a thousand peaks; rain-dripping rock-flowers, spring across ten thousand lands. One can listen to the flowing waters of Yanxi.
Mind. The murmuring stream flows all day long, yet there is no hearing of what is heard.
(Luo Han Nan) In his final years, Xuansha entrusted this to Jingqing; turning back to hear, one listens to the sound of the river’s flow.
Now that ears have been washed in the Canglang River, who is willing to step to the current and cleanse their cap? (Min Gufo)
A stream of cold springs flows beneath the emerald peaks; Xuansha called him forth for the sake of the true mechanism.
Although Jingqing entered through hearing, how could flowing water ever wash away right and wrong?
(Tieshan Ren) Once, a monk asked Xuansha: "I have heard the Master say that the entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl."
"Jewel. The student asked, "How can one understand this? The Master said, "The entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl.
What is there to understand? The monk then desisted. On the following day, the Master asked him again, "The entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl;
how do you understand this? He replied, "The entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl."
"How do you apply this? The Master said, "I know you are making your living inside a ghost cave.
Baoci then said, "Both of us speak in this same way; why does yours, however, turn out to be a ghost cave?
Cui峰 Xian (Cui Peak Xian) offered a different interpretation of Xuansha’s words, saying: "In other quarters this may be acceptable, but here it will not do."
Once, while the assembly was in meditation, Xuansha heard the sound of a swallow and said, "He speaks deeply of the true reality (*dharmatā*) and skillfully expounds the essential teachings.
He then descended from his seat. At that time, a monk requested further instruction, saying, "I do not understand. The Master replied, "Go away!
Who would believe you?"
The purple swallow flies back, circling the painted beams; It does not refuse to empty its belly and pour out its heart. A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them;
Once more it follows the oriole over the low wall. (Benjue I) My humble office drives me north and south;
I have long pined for the dust of the traveler’s road. Amidst the misty rain and smoke, I deeply recall the spring of my old garden.
(Extended Life and Wisdom) Once, a monk asked Xuansha, "What is the student's own self? The Master said, "What use is there for your own self?
Yunmen Wenyan remarked, "A person of immeasurable capacity has been turned around by the flow of words. The monk then asked, "What is [the self]?"
Regarding the student’s own self: The Gatekeeper said, "Suppose suddenly someone on the road calls out, 'Monk, come to the meal!

You too will get some food to eat according to your lot. Baoshou Xin said, "Tell me, was it this monk who turned back within the flow of the words, or was it Xuansha who turned back within the flow of the words? If there is reason, what use is a loud voice?"
In my whole life, I have never dreamed of the Southland; it is truly vexing that people speak of the partridges. Though I am clothed in brocade, I cannot yet return to my native land;
I seek the imperial capital within a mere village of three households. (Huàn jì tíng) The kinship between father and son is no different from other kinships;
separated from the body yet adhering to it, they are entirely in accord. If one were to treat this with even the slightest sense of formality as a guest—
Wait. It makes the bystanders with their cold eyes laugh to death.
(Guanchuzhen) Once, when a monk asked Xuansha, "What is the pure Dharma-body? the Master said, "Dripping pus."
Baizhang Yuan said elsewhere: "The stench of excrement perfumes the heavens. He also said:
"A child born by transformation upon a lotus leaf—every drop of it is festering pus. "On a fishing boat, the family style is revealed;
people only look at the fishing line, failing to see the red smartweed facing the reeds. (Tianyi Huai)
Drops of pus, golden light; the entire Dharma-body revealed in full majesty. On the banks of the Jiaolu River he once manifested transformation;
a single-leafed fishing boat drifts upon the vast and boundless.
(Yang Wuwai) The pure Dharma-body is beyond compare; after illness, it remains as before, dripping with pus. Wild geese cry out, severing the autumnal light.
Old age. A single red leaf drifts down. (Lan’an Shu) Drop by drop, the entire body is festering pus.
Not a single speck falls to the east or west. If one says this is not for those who know the sound, they cannot avoid being blown by the wind into a different tune. (Gao Feng Miao)
Xuan Sha ascended the hall. When the assembly had gathered, he drove them all away at once with his staff.
Turning back toward his attendant, he said, "Today I have reached a realization that was perilous—like being shot by an arrow into hell.
The attendant replied, "I am glad the Master has returned to human form once more."
Cuiyan Zhi said: "Whether it be Great Xuansha or Little Xuansha, they have not reached the village in front nor arrived at the shop behind.
How, then, can one find the path of liberation? Daowu Zhen said: "Whether it be Great Master Zhi or Little Master Zhi, you are merely one-sided and withered.
Daowu is not so; of Xuansha and his attendant, each possesses a single eye. Yunju Shun said: "This..."
He said to the assembly, "It has been reduced to a pulp like mud. How do you understand this? The Mountain Monk says:
The attendant was not a matter of words. Xuansha was merely seeking sandalwood in a thicket of brambles. Dongchan Guan said: "How great!
Xuansha’s very life is in the hands of the attendant."
Xuansha said: "Before the face of a deceased monk is precisely bodhi encountered at every glance; it is the divine light from ten thousand miles, the mark behind the crown.
Tianyi Huai said: "Setting aside for a moment the case before the face of a deceased monk, what about that which is behind a living person? It is this—
What is it? Right here, it is simply Xuansha: "Every sight is entirely true; the words are not far-fetched. Before the deceased, one personally attests to this;
there is no partiality and nothing to be obscured. The monastic communities are vast and clamorous, vying with one another in their chatter, as if trying to grasp at empty space.
Illusory flowers. (Fenyang Zhao) Setting aside the matter before the deceased monk, how does one encounter [him] behind the living?
Since the breaking of Yunnan, it has been until now that the northern frontier is opened. (Benjue Yi)
Once, when Guishan was being prodded by Attendant Guang, he said, "If you, Uncle, can penetrate Zen, I shall take my iron boat and sail it into the sea.
After Guishan had established his monastery, he sent a letter to ask Guang, "Have you yet taken your iron boat and sailed it into the sea?"
Fayan Yi said in his place, “The Master would never act in such a way. Fenyang Zhao said, “You see only the sharpness of the chisel’s tip;
you do not see the squareness of the chisel’s head. Qingliang Qin said in his place, “I ask the Master to disembark from the boat.
Zhiti Ai said, “Xuansha is merely a poor man thinking of his old debts. Yunju Yuan said, “Zen has never even existed.”
[He] attained it. What use is there in deliberating over old matters? Suddenly he was moved by that iron boat;
what could Xuansha have done about it? Huelinben said: "Yesterday I passed through Silla. Yunjuzhuang said:
"Critiques from all quarters are not few, yet they can only support the strong and cannot support the weak. Today I have long examined this."
It does not depart from its original state. How could one dare say that Xuansha was led astray by the attendant Guang? It is simply impossible to provide a definitive analysis.
After all, how is it? When the government has no fixed regulations, one follows the private conventions of the people.
Xuansha said: "The divine light of ten thousand miles is the mark behind the crown; when it has vanished from the crown, where can one look?
The matter is already accomplished, and the intention is already at rest. This trace of arrival is pervasive wherever it touches. A wise person, upon hearing this, should extract it with vigor;
do not wait until in an instant you have lost your head."
Divine light shines from behind his crown, illuminating the boundless. How could the narrow confines of ten thousand *li* suffice to describe it?
If you ask for the ultimate meaning of Xuansha’s intent: the skull is cold at midnight under a frosty sky.
(Benjue I) While Xuansha was sitting, he saw a single white spot on the ground before him. Pointing at it with his staff, he asked an attendant monk:
"Do you see? He replied, "I see. The Master asked this three times, and he answered three times. The Master said, "You see me, and I see you.

If you see, why do you say you do not understand? Fenggang Miaoyun said: "To see is to see; to understand is to understand. There is no further doubt. Now tell me, what is this single point of white?"
"What exactly is this? Puzhi Long said, "This monk has gained a pair of eyes, while Xuansha has lost one nostril."
Your seeing is my seeing; it is fully manifest. Only after breaking through the thicket of thorns does one know there is no front or back.
Let this single point penetrate from ancient times to the present. Before black and white were yet distinguished, where could one discern anything?
Xuan Sha once encountered the Tripiṭaka Master Śīlabhadra, who was skilled at distinguishing various sounds. King Liu invited him to put this to the test.
The Master struck a bronze incense burner with an iron fire-tongs and asked, "What sound is that? He replied, "The sound of bronze and iron.
The Master said, "Great King, do not allow yourself to be deceived by a foreigner."
Fayan Yi said in his turn: "The Great Master has long received the offerings of the Great King. Qingliang Qin said in his turn: "On the contrary, it is the Master who is deceiving the Great King.
Cui峰 Xian offered a different version, saying: "The Great King should increase his faith and respect.
He also offered another version, saying: "Do not deceive a foreigner. Jingyin Cheng said: "Since it is not the sound of copper or iron, it is profound."
Xuan Sha asked, "What sound did you call that? Thus, while the Tripitaka Master only knew how to cross the water, he failed to notice his clothes were getting wet;

Xuan Sha was particularly adept at framing others, yet what can one do? The state has its laws. Now tell me, how does the Tripitaka Master’s deception of the Great King compare to Xuan Sha’s deception of the Great King?
Tiantong Juo said: "When principle accords, the spirit responds; the poor man finds the treasure within his garment."

When emotions are obstructed, one becomes a mere object; thus, the Great Strength Man lost the pearl from his forehead. The Tripitaka Master could only understand what was before him and failed to look behind.
Do you still know? To falsely accuse another of a crime and then impose that very crime upon them. Pogong Miaoxiu said: "How great and small were Xuansha’s attachments to 'ability' and 'inability.
At that time, he fortunately encountered this Great King Liu. Had he been a truly authentic monk, [he would have acted differently]."
This is surely a moment of exposure.
Before the sound, it stands alone; originally it has no name. At the guest-halls of Chu and the towers of Qin, one sells away one’s very self.
A pity that the flower-viewer stands until old age, unaware that spring has already passed beyond the village ahead. (Tian’an Sheng)
Xuan Sha addressed the assembly: "The World-Honored One said that he possessed the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye and entrusted it to Mahākāśyapa;
this was like speaking of the moon. Cao Xi held up his whisk; this was still like pointing at the moon. At that time, Gu Shan stepped forward and said, "The moon is here!
The Master said, "This fellow is looking for the moon right from me. Gu Shan did not agree, and returning to the assembly, he said, "He said..."
"I seek the moon within it. Cui Fengxian said:
"Xuansha and Gushan were like two generals arraying a million-man battle formation, yet they merely threw tiles and stones at one another to strike.
If there were a monk capable of discerning this, he would know that the entrustment of the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye has its rightful place. — Huguo.
Yuan said: "Xuansha and Gushan each expound their own principles, yet for the most part they do not recognize the moon.
Do you all wish to recognize the moon? Fortunately, there is no place where it shines partially; there are simply those who have not yet understood.

Gunanmen said: "Xuansha lures people into breaking the law; Gushan buys a hat to fit a head. Had it not been for Cuifeng’s clear discernment of the situation, [the error] would likely have persisted."
Whether you accept it or not, is there any monk present right now who does not accept it? I want to ask you:
what do you call the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye?
Xuan Sha said, "If we discuss this matter, it is like a plot of land whose boundaries have been demarcated and sold to various people;
there remains only the tree at its center, which still belongs to me, the old monk."
Fochuan’s commentary says: "Since the boundaries of the four directions have already been demarcated and the contract for the sale finalized, why does the tree in the center still belong to Xuansha?
'Ten thousand matters rest with the Old Teacher; the tree still belongs to you. The butcher Guang'e attains Buddhahood; the Second Patriarch [cuts off his arm]."
The Great Master repays his debts.
(Gushan Gui) The ancestral fields and gardens of the Buddhas and Patriarchs have all been sold; not a single boundary on the four sides has been left behind.
Alas, there still remains the central tree, which continues to disturb the spring breeze without ceasing. (Jingshan Gao)
The grandfather’s fields and gardens all belong to me; how could the fruit of the central tree come from another?
To uproot it with its branches, leaves, and roots—to see one’s descendants, their resolve must be far-reaching.
(Duan’an Yan) Xuan Sha once pointed to the gate above; the Chan practitioners of the four seas have not yet ceased their efforts. Only the Son of Heaven of the Han dynasty...
Noble. The banner of the envoy returned from Xingyi under Gaixia in Pengcheng.
(Jiangshan Ai) When Xuefeng passed away, the assembly requested Xuansha to preside over the funeral rites. On the third morning, he gathered the assembly to serve tea.
The Master then picked up a single tea bowl before the spirit and asked, "The Great Master was alive when..."
"You say: 'Now, how would you say it? If you can say it, then the former master was not at fault;
if you cannot say it, the fault lies with the former master. He asked this three times, but the assembly remained silent.
The Master then smashed the bowl to pieces and returned to his quarters.
Zhongta asked, "On what basis did Sha ask you how you understand it? Ta said, "What fault was there in my late teacher? Sha then turned his back to the wall.
Ta went out; Sha called to Ta again. Ta turned his head. Sha said, "How do you understand this?
Ta then turned his back to the wall. Sha desisted. Xiaoyan Bao said: "At that time, there was a monk who, as soon as he saw him—"
When he spoke thus, [Xuefeng] overturned the tea table, so as not to leave unresolved matters for his ancestors that would bring calamity upon his descendants.
Once, Xuansha visited the Master of Sandou Hermitage; as soon as they met, the Master said, "Do not take offense, but I have been living in the mountains for many years and have no sitting mat.
The Master asked, "Everyone has one; why does the Hermitage Master have none? [The Master] replied, "Sit down first and eat."
Tea. The Master said: "The Abbot has always been here.
The paths leading to and from the hermitage intersect; step by step they follow one another’s tracks. The mountain is remote and the years many, so no one arrives;
a stream flows through the valley, nourishing the tall pines. (Shuai’an Cong)
When Xuansha saw Gushan approaching, he drew a circle. Gushan said, "No one can get out of this.
The Master said, "I knew you would go about your business in the wombs of donkeys and horses. Gushan asked, "And what about you, Preceptor?
The Master said, "No one can get out of this. Gushan said, "If that is how you speak, Preceptor, then I..."
Jiashan asked, "Why did he say he could not speak? The Master said, "I have it; you do not.
Cui峰 Xian said, "He only knows how to greedily gaze at the white waves, yet he fails to realize that he has lost the oar in his hand.
Yunfeng Yue said, "Whether one can speak or cannot speak, both remain within Xuanzha’s circle. Now, what shall we do?"
"Having emerged from its circle. Zhaojue Qin said: "This is truly a single path; only those who have realized it know it.
It reaches such a state that it exhausts heaven and earth and spans ten thousand ages without shifting; it consumes the kalpa-stone and empties the mustard-seed city without end."
Even those who have passed through the barrier must still keep their eyes open; only then will they succeed.
It is all the same at such a time—why then do you say, "I have attained it, but you have not"? By all means, avoid making your livelihood within the wombs of donkeys and horses! Jingyin Cheng said:
"In the monastic communities, there are often those who understand this by taking it to mean that Drumshan had not yet reached the realm of Xuansha. However...
Do people recognize these two elders? Have you not heard it said that they both emerged from this very source? Nanhua Bing said:
"To twist the nostrils and exchange the eyes—if one lacks such a skillful hand, how can one uphold the lineage of the School?"
"Even so, it is simply laughable. One must laugh for thirty years. But what is there to laugh at?
I know full well that you are making your living in the belly of a donkey or a horse. Dongchan Guan said:
"At that time, had I been Drum Mountain, when Xuansha also said, 'Everyone fails to produce this,' I would have immediately replied: 'Master, you originally thought otherwise.'"
There is a point of superiority here: it was not merely to fulfill his prior merit, but rather to meet with Xuansha within the wombs of donkeys and horses.
Tiantong Jue said: "Xuansha was much like one who relies on power to deceive others and uses strength to oppress the weak.
It was because he could shift the focus and bring it forth that both were alike; why then did he say, 'I have attained it, you have not'?"
What is true is difficult to conceal; what is false does not flourish. Baoen Xiu said:

"People of this age love to go to the celestial palaces and pure lands, yet Drum Mountain (Gushan) does not love the wombs of donkeys or horses. People fear falling [into such states], yet Xuansha did not fear them.

Therefore, he lowered his voice and bore his own spirit, looking down upon others and walking with a stride. He possessed the power of a lion that cannot be deceived; do you still believe in Tiantong’s protection?"
Have you realized it? Amidst the dust, one can act as the master; beyond transformation, one comes as a guest of one’s own accord.
The adept should seek the medicine for those without illness; where could a horse’s belly or a donkey’s womb be placed?
On that day at Gushan, what a pity—that his nostrils were plucked away by someone. (Benjue I)
One night, a cold sound came within my dream; at dawn, I put on my sandals and went to its source.
I hope that in the height of summer I shall pass by here once more, cast off my lotus robes, and sleep upon the rocks.
(Haeju Ji) The Great Way trusts in all-encompassing tolerance; its abundant grace never ceases. My scales leap in the Dragon and Phoenix Pond; I wield my brush within the Purple Palace.
(Tie Rongxuan) One night, while Xuefeng and Dizang were conversing with the Abbot until late, the Master said, "The attendant has closed the door with the bolt.
How can you get out? Dizang said, "What do you call a 'door'?"
Cui-feng Xian took his leave of Di-zang; at that time, Di-zang said, "Be careful," and Xian departed immediately.
Qing-liang Qin took his leave, saying, "Preceptor, do you wish to rest? Xuan-sha said to Xue-feng, "I am now going to employ the Great Function. Preceptor, what will you do?"
Feng threw three wooden balls out simultaneously. The Master made a gesture as if striking a shield.
Feng said, "Only when you were personally at Vulture Peak could you act like this. The Master replied, "This too is my own affair."
Yingshan Yin said: "The father acts and the son carries on; truly he has succeeded to the family estate. Yet, he cannot avoid being mentioned on people's lips.
Huiyun Sheng said: "Look at this father and son; they are remarkably similar. They dance in step, one following the other, their notes and scales in perfect harmony.
However, if we speak of the Great Function, only when the Elephant Bone Rock is cast aside can one grant him a share in the understanding of the teaching."
When Xuansha saw three newly arrived monks, he personally struck the work-call drum three times and returned to his quarters.
After the newcomers had performed their formal salutations, they also struck the work-call drum three times and entered the Sangha hall.
A long-resident monk came forward and said, "The newcomers have slighted the Master. The Master replied, "Strike the bell to assemble the assembly for an examination. The great assembly gathered.
The assembly gathered, but the newly arrived monk did not go forward. The Master ordered an attendant to go and summon him.

As soon as the newly arrived monk stepped out of the Dharma Hall, he struck the attendant once on his back and said, "The Master calls for you. When the attendant reached the Master’s quarters, the newly arrived monk returned to the hall.
Later, Jiu-zhu asked, "Master, why did you not examine the newly arrived monk? The Master replied, "I have already examined you."
The case was concluded.
Zuian Yin said, "It is a pity that this monk was let off so easily," and then offered this verse:
Xuan Sha clearly repairs the mountain path; the newly arrived monk secretly passes through Chen Cang. Traveling by night, they do not meet; at dawn, they part ways.
Together we reached Xianyang; strict were the commands, and regulations were enforced according to the statutes. Clearly, the four seas are as clear as a mirror;
where else could one seek a frontier?
The sun sets on the southern side of Mount Sumeru, while it is precisely the fifth watch of the night in the continent of Uttarakuru. Most bitter is this: that what is good is Silla.
Guest: "Hazy and dim, as if still walking in a dream.
(Yuan Jieying) Once, when a monk asked Xue Sha, "What is the matter that is most intimate? the Master said, "I am Xie Sanlang."
Originally a guest upon a fishing boat, By chance I shaved my beard and hair and donned the *kāṣāya*. I cannot remain within the ranks of Buddhas and Patriarchs;
Last night, as ever, I lay among the reeds. (Cui-feng Xian) He personally extends this definitive inquiry to you:
Do not compare it to the transmission from Liusha to Shaoshi. Last night, the wild geese returned to the Twin Peaks.
Later, he thanked his family members and stood before the bright moon.
(Touzi Qingsu) In this season of late autumn, a land of water and clouds, where a thousand acres of reeds have not yet been touched by frost, the river scenery is not sold in fragments;
it is bestowed all at once upon Xie Sanlang. (Zuyin Ming)
Whispering reeds reflect the flowing river; A lone sail and solitary oar drift upon a small boat. I pay no heed at all to the fine rain and slanting wind;
My single mind rests only upon the tip of my fishing rod. (Xiaowenkān) The long pole has no bait, the fishing line is light;
Slanted against the bow of the boat, the autumn moon is bright. A horizontal flute—this is not for those who are ordinary men.
Meeting! One blows for oneself and listens to oneself. (Meigu Yue) Xuansha said:
"In the bell there is no sound of the drum; in the drum there is no sound of the bell. Bell and drum do not intersect;
every phrase is without before or after."
Taking the head as the tail; falling down by oneself and rising by oneself. Dwelling in a fisherman’s village, his clothes woven from reeds and rushes.
(Tianye Zhoushou) When Changqing Ling arrived, Xuansha asked him, "Setting aside the medicinal taboos, how do you speak?
Ling said, "Why do you act so foolishly? The Master said, "The model of Xuefeng Mountain comes here to gather food; here, the sparrow lets it go."
"Excrement.
Chengtian Yi said, "Xuansha only knew that Changqing’s sparrow was dropping dung; he did not know that his own excrement was so foul it perfumed the heavens.
If you wish to eliminate this medicinal taboo, it will take sixty kalpas across three lifetimes."

Chan Master Guichen (Dizang), of Luohan Monastery in Zhangzhou, the eighth generation descendant of Dajian Huineng and successor to Xuansha Shibei, asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the South.
The Master said, "How is the Buddha-dharma in the South? The monk replied, "It is full of bustling discussion. The Master [said]: *(Note: The provided text ends abruptly at the Master's response.)*
[The monk] said, "How does it compare to my planting fields here to earn my own food? [The Master] said, "What can you do about the three realms?
The Master said, "What do you call the 'three realms'?
Wuwei Zhe said, "Pure poverty brings long-lasting joy; turbid wealth brings much anxiety. Baolin Xiu [commented on] "earning one's own food": [it is like] "planting fields here."
The text below says: "If that is so, then it is not only the case for the South. Boshan Lai said: "This monk is entangled in the three realms;
he brings disgrace upon the Chan practitioners of the Southern Land by failing to eliminate his worldly airs. Is there anyone now who can truly meet with Dizang?
You must first cast away your plow, rake, and hoe before you can succeed. Daci Yan said: "How great [and yet how small]!"
Dizang’s saying, “Planting fields to buy rice,” leaves people with no choice but to harbor doubts for no reason. At the end, however, he asks, “What do you call the triple world?
which is like having a dragon’s head but a snake’s tail. The *Renwang jing* (Benevolent Kings Sutra) says that Dizang’s family style is no less than that of the ancient Buddhas;
truly, such a person is encountered once in a thousand years. Yet, when pressed by this monk, he was brought straight to his knees.
[The assembly] was left in disarray. Falingyin said: "Dizang may indeed be called one who is clear in reproaching others but ignorant in reproaching himself.
If this monk were a true master, when [Dizang] asked, 'What do you call the three realms? he would have simply laughed heartily."
Look at what other tricks Kṣitigarbha might perform:
he tills the fields to earn his meal. Who can discern this within words? Afternoon meal-bell strikes; true gold has never lost its luster.
(Yunfeng Yue): Plowing the fields to earn one's meal, one must wait for it to come. The profound mystery is left to be conjectured at will. Upon the shadowless tree hang the sun and moon;
how many people here have their hearts turned to ash? (Min Gufo)
All manner of doctrines and explanations are merely forced constructs; transmitted from mouth to ear, they become fragmented and disjointed.

Plowing fields to earn one’s meal is a matter of daily life, something those who have not reached full realization do not understand. When one has fully realized through practice, one knows there is nothing left to seek; like Zhang Liang, one ultimately does not prize the rank of a marquis.
Forgetting artifice, one returns to the company of fish and birds, washing one’s feet in the autumnal mists and waters of the Canglang River. (Tiantong Jue)
Planting fields and eating fine rice; satiated, one lies down with legs stretched long.
Taking the three realms and placing them on the left side—this drew forth the old, ancient fellow Longya, who held a broken wooden ladle in his hand. (Wuzhun Shanfan).
When Dizang, Changqing, and Baofu entered the prefectural city and saw a screen painting of peonies, Baofu said, "A truly fine..."
[Daowu] held up a peony flower. Qing said, "I hope you do not mistake this for a flower. The Master said, "What a pity, a single flower!
Baoci then asked, "Regarding the words of these three venerable elders, is there any distinction between the intimate and the distant?
As for Dizang speaking thus, where does he land? Huanglong Xin said, "According to the insights of these three men, one person transcends [the others]."
The Buddha transcends the patriarchs. One person benefits both self and others; another deceives himself. He then asked the monk, "Tell me, who is it that deceives himself?
The monk said, "Do not let your eyes deceive you. Long said, "From here, go further to a place where it is deep night, quiet, and utterly deserted.
Only then can you go together with him to deliberate."
Dizang was gazing at the moon and said, "The clouds move; there is movement. The rain falls; there is movement. A monk said, "It is not that the clouds move; it is the wind that moves.
The Master said, "I say that neither the clouds move nor does the wind move. The monk asked, "But just now, Master, you also said the clouds move. The Master replied, "Who is at fault?"
The wind rises and the tree’s heart trembles; clouds arise and the nature stirs up dust. If you understand today’s affairs, you have obscured the person of original nature.

(Lóngjì Xiū) If one were to grasp at objects, one would enter the ford of delusion; as long as there is even a hair’s breadth of it, it is but dust. Do not fail to believe that in the past there was no form.
Appearance: Seeking knowledge externally is not the truth. (Qing of Caotang) Clouds arise within the cave;
the wind stirs through the forest, creating sound. If you understand today’s matter, half a pound is eight ounces.
(Shangfang Peak) Dizang asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Qinzhou. The Master said, "What have you brought with you?
He replied, "I have brought nothing. The Master said, "Why do you speak falsely before the assembly? The monk was speechless. The Master—
He then asked, "Is it not true that parrots come from Qinzhou? The monk replied, "Parrots come from Longxi.
The Master said, "That is not much of a difference.
Weishan Zhe said, "This monk has come directly from Qinzhou; why does he speak such falsehoods before the assembly? He wishes..."
Do you understand? To be a guest without courtesy brings disgrace upon the host with its muddied waters.

When one comes to ask about the "perfected wind," responding to the occasion is not yet skillful. Failing to turn back after three attempts, it makes the mouths of the patch-robed monks laugh until they crack.
Starving, one encounters a king’s banquet yet cannot eat; when will the misty waters of a hundred cities come to an end?
(Dàbiàn Quán) The east wind smiles through the flowers, bringing forth spring’s radiance; bees and butterflies at the branches pursue only the fragrance.
A single cry from the cuckoo amidst the hanging green shadows—none know how long the path home may be. (Yuǎn’ān Ān)
Once, while Jizang, Fayan, Shaoshou, Hongjin, and three others were gathered around a brazier to ward off the snow, Jizang cited the *Zhao Lun* (Treatise of Zhaoming) to the passage:
"Heaven and earth share the same root as I. Jizang asked, "Are the mountains and rivers the same as you, venerable sir, or are they different?
Fayan said, "Different. Jizang held up two fingers. Fayan said, "The same. Jizang again held up two fingers.

The Master pointed [at a stone] and immediately departed. As Yan was taking his leave, the Master saw him off at the gate and said, "Upādhyāya, you usually say that the three realms are mind-only and all phenomena are consciousness-only.
Now tell me: is this stone under our feet inside the mind or outside the mind? Yan replied, "It is inside the mind.
The Master said, "What kind of reason is it for a traveling monk to place a piece of stone inside [his mind]?"
His heart was troubled; his eyes were distressed, and he had no way to respond. He then set down his bundle and sat beneath the mats to seek a resolution.
There are many ways to deliberate upon sameness and difference, yet how has this old fellow ever raised his tongue? From ancient times to the present, it has been impossible to carry it away.
A pair of spiritual swords lean against the cold of heaven. (Baoning Yong)
Cease contending with yourself and the mountains and rivers; there is nothing to be done when you stir up the weapons of war.
Behold the General deploying his martial strategy: with two cold swords, he settles dragons and snakes.
(Yemufu Stream) How many kinds of talk are there at the head of the furnace? How can one observe oneself at that very moment? Arise directly and display your skill!
Two. The mountains, rivers, and the great earth are pitch black.
(Xutang Yu) Dizang asked a monk, "While you were at Zhaoying, was there any extraordinary news? Try to recount it. The monk said, "I dare not misquote.
The Master said, "What is the matter of ultimate reality? The monk said, "Why does the Master [ask]?"
Thus it was. The Master said, "That monk has fallen into a trap.
Chengtian Yi said, "Although this monk from Zhaoqing has not yet uttered his extraordinary news, he has already startled the multitude and raised the crowd's eyebrows.
Dizang only knows that the other man has fallen into a trap; he does not realize that his own tongue has already been trailing on the ground."
Once, while Jizang was with Zhongta attending Xuan Sha, Xuan Sha struck Zhongta with a blow of his staff and said, "Is it in terms of name?
Is it in terms of essence? Zhongta did not respond. Xuan Sha then asked the Master, "How do you understand this?
The Master replied, "That monk received a blow of the staff and does not know where it came from."
Regarding the "True Clouds of Samādhi," as for the central pagoda, those who do not know where the single blow comes from—does even Kṣitigarbha know?
Do not say that Kṣitigarbha does not know; I dare guarantee that even Xuansha did not know it either.
When Dizang was performing the memorial feast for Xuansha, he invited Master Ba’en to partake of the medicinal food (yao-shi).
As Ba’en looked at the place of offering, he did not see a portrait there, so he asked the Master, "Do you have a portrait? The Master gestured with his hand and said, "Look!"
En said, "It turns out there was never anything real. The Master said, "It is very much like not looking at it at all.
With brows like willows and faces like flowers, she is too weary to comb and wash herself. Who says she is not as beautiful as when she first married?
Idly facing her neighbors, she draws the jade thread; with the golden needle, she embroiders a pair of yellow orioles. (Jian’an Yi)
Zen Master Huizhou Jizhao of Anguo Monastery on Wolong Mountain in Fuzhou (a successor of Xuansha Shibei) ascended the hall and said:
"The circumstances of our daily meals here are for the sake of you, my brothers; yet they are ultimately not constant. If you wish to attain the essential point,"
Rather, it is the mountains, rivers, and the great earth that reveal the Way to you. Since that Way is eternal, it is also ultimate.
If one enters through the gate of Mañjuśrī, all insentient things—earth, wood, tiles, and pebbles—assist you in triggering the awakening.
If one enters through the gate of Samantabhadra, one arrives without moving a step. If one enters through the gate of Avalokiteśvara, [one...]
All sounds and echoes—frogs and earthworms—assist you in triggering the mechanism. Through these three gates of expedient means, I show them to you.
It is like taking a single broken chopstick and stirring the waters of the great ocean, so that the fish and dragons may know water as their very life. Do you understand?
If you lack the eye of wisdom to examine this with discernment, then no matter how many hundreds of clever and ingenious methods you employ, they will not lead to the ultimate realization.
Langye Jue said: "Though it be a good cause, it brings about an evil fruit. Baoning Yong said:
"O assembly, whether you are struck or bumped from the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, above, or below, you are unaware and unknowing; where does the fault lie?"
After a long silence, he said: "With rouge and powder, it is easy to become a beautiful woman; without money, it is difficult to be a fine gentleman.
Jianfu Xing said: "According to my own assessment, Master Anguo, you do not even know where your own life and soul have ended up."
"Even a single broken chopstick would not suffice here. Is there no one who snatches food from the tiger's mouth?
If there is none, this mountain monk cannot help but apply another cauterization upon the existing burn scar. [He] struck the meditation seat and descended.
Dongchan Guan said: "Once An-guo was feeding a baby with rice in his mouth. Unaware that those watching him felt revulsion, he asked the Head of the Monastery (Yuanzhu):
'The former Master said, "The entire ten directions of the world is this very body of true reality.
Do you see the Sangha Hall? The Head replied, 'Master, do not let your eyes deceive you. The Master said, 'The former Master has passed away.'"
The transformed flesh is still warm. Fālín’s *Yīnyún* says:
"Both the Great and the Small Ān-guó are in a state of extreme urgency; this monk has exchanged his very eyes for them. He is ten parts away from death;
even if there were Lu or Biàn, they could only fold their hands in helplessness. Thus, he busily lets go and gathers back—how could this be skillful?
Is this what is meant by "acting"? Nevertheless, it is not necessarily that An-guo’s intention was good.
The Chan Master Qiruan of Dazhang Mountain in Fuzhou (a successor of Xuansha Shibei) was asked by a monk: "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them? The Master said:
"When the tally arrives, the decree is executed. The monk said: "In that case, will you not be bound away by birth and death?"

The Master said, "A-ye, a-ye. Yingshan Yun said, "This old fellow acts so foolishly that even the Lord of Yama must fold his hands in submission. Nevertheless, you must still put him to the test before you can truly have it."
*Zongjian Faling*, Scroll 53 and Scroll 54,
compiled by Jiyuntang.
The Ninth Generation Descendant of Dajian [Huaihai]:
Chan Master Fayan Wenyi of Qingliang Monastery in Jinling (Succeeded by Luohan Chen). While traveling on foot, he was detained by rain at Dizang Monastery and consequently went to visit him.
Dizang asked, "Where are you going? The Master replied, "I am traveling on pilgrimage. Dizang said, "Traveling..."
"What about the matter of the feet? The Master said, "I do not know. [The student] said, "Not knowing is most intimate. The Master attained realization.

Now, though one may be as learned as he was then, when all subtle dust is shed, one arrives at "not knowing. Whether short or long, let there be no cutting or patching; whether high or low, it is naturally held level.
The family’s abundance or scarcity is used according to the occasion; the field is leisurely and full of trust.
With every step you move, you clearly betray those two eyebrows from thirty years ago of wandering as a pilgrim.

(Tiantong Jue) Coming from the south and going to the north, all are in a state of frantic toil; throughout the day, amidst dust and smoke, there is nothing to be done. With a confident stride, one tramples the path of fragrant grass;
according to circumstance, one borrows a glance at the many falling flowers. Two rows of eyebrow-arches span the autumn moon; a pair of celestial ponds soak [the world].
The Jade Shuttle: Best not to know where its horns end; Where can one find the riddle when turning around?
(Bāng Wǒlǚ) The horns are distinct, yet turning them distorts the truth; Master Yègōng was too old and indolent to capture the spirit.
One day, breaking through the wall with thunder and lightning, Surely there will be a wondrous immortal to paint in the pupils. (Tán Jírěn)
With a majestic and towering air, he emerges from the forbidden city; in his eyes, nothing can withstand his true intent.
Who would have known that a single spark in a cold place burns forth eyebrows arched in an eight-character formation? (Wuyi’s Commentary):
The elixir of the immortals is without error, yet the matter of turning iron into gold remains distant. It is not like the quicksilver of medicine found in these present times.
[He] gathered his head and spoke in vain of cinnabar.
(Jun Huidu) Fayan was at Dizang’s [monastery]. One day, he presented what he had seen. Dizang said, "The Buddha-dharma is not like this.

The Master said, "My words are exhausted and my principles are spent. Dizang said, "If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, everything is already fully accomplished. At these words, the Master [attained realization].
Upon hearing these words, he attained great enlightenment.
A full platter of pure nectar was set forth; once it reached the mouth, it caused one’s life to perish instantly.
Having died and returned to life, one cannot be deceived—only sighing in regret that one has wandered the crossroads searching for a lost sheep. (From the *Shouchang Jing*)
The Dharma-eye [Dongshan Liangjie] asked this because Subhūti Fang had come from Changqing. The Master raised an ancient verse by Changqing and questioned him:
"What is the body that stands alone, revealed amidst the myriad phenomena? Subhūti Fang raised his whisk. The Master said, "How can you understand it in such a way?
He asked, "How about you, Master? The Master said, "What do you call 'the myriad phenomena'? He replied, "The ancients."
A man asked, "Do people not negate the myriad phenomena? The Master said, "Within the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. What is there to say about negating or not negating?
Only after these words did the man attain awakening.
Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. Each time we meet, we are more intimate. East, west, south, and north—all are the transformation of our Sovereign.
Do not laboriously seek the ferry crossing in Jiangnan.

(Fushan Yuan) Seeing the Buddha through the departure of thought, breaking through the dust to bring forth the scriptures. The family dharma is already manifest; who establishes a formal gate? Day after day, the boat moves on.
The river’s ripples are pure; spring follows the green burn-marks upon the grass. Whether you stir them or not, listen attentively.
The three paths have fallen into ruin, yet you may return at once; the pine and chrysanthemums of years past still breathe their fragrance.
(Tiantong Ju) Rain washes the pale red of the peach buds tender; the wind shakes the light green willow filaments delicate. A single river of autumn water reaches the heavens.
Emerald green. On both banks, the *liǎo* flowers smile alongside the white water lilies.
(Complete with both aspects) Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. At dawn, the rooster’s cry scatters the stars across the sky. The mute cowherd sits steady upon his ox’s back;
a single blast from the iron flute clears the universe.
When Huayan asked Hui-chao, "What is the Buddha? the Master said, "You are Hui-chao.
Jin-su Yuan remarked, "Huayan’s response like this can truly be called 'treating an illness without needing medicine carried on a donkey.
If one can play music, why necessarily use strings of jade? This monk attained enlightenment; he was indeed a fine person. Yet, when examined closely, there is still [something left].
The matter lies here. But tell me, what matter is it? *Cluck!* This is the bottom line of Xuansha.
"The spring breeze of the Jiang region cannot stir it; the partridge cries deep within the flowers. When the waves of the third stage are high, the fish transforms into a dragon;
yet the fool still scoops water from the night pond. (Cui Feng Xian)
Traveling over treacherous precipices, one asks of the difficulty of the road; someone asks about the northern village or the southern.
In Chang’an, there are countless people coming and going—how many can pass through the pass without their bells?
(Touzi Qing) The wooden man travels a thousand li; the swift horse does not move its hoof. As the setting sun rests upon the southern lands, it neighs toward the north because of the wind.
(Chengjue Yi) For wondrous function, there is no need for a frost-sharpened blade; to be able to pluck, why must it be with jade strings?
In the afternoon of a bitter winter, at the third watch of the night, sitting idly and sleeping idly when the clouds disperse. (Cuiyan Zhen)
With a single large coin, one buys a steamed rice cake; having eaten it into one's belly, one is immediately no longer hungry.
(Baizhang Yuanwen) When the slightly sour plum first produces its kernel, the oriole grows old and the flowers wither—traces are already ancient. One night, the southern wind shifts the *dou*.
Handle. The willows by the morning smoke have no concern for spring.
(Zhengtang’s Discernment) Asking about Chang’an from within the Han-yuan Hall, it points directly to the person, chilling to the very bone. The ground lacks vermilion and turns to red earth;
the granary has not a grain of rice, only overturned husks. (Songtao’s Extensive Commentary)
When a monk asked Fayan, "What is a single drop of water from the Cao source? the Master replied, "It is a single drop of water from the Cao source.
Tiantong Jie said, "Fayan brandished his banner in the midst of a hundred-battle field; he could not avoid being laughed at by bystanders."
Suddenly someone asks, "What is one drop of water from Cao’s Spring at Lingyin? Point directly to them and say: "A mixture of excrement and urine.
One drop of water from Cao’s Spring is clear and still; it flows out through a thousand rivers, utterly free of the sound of waves. How many have wandered and played within the great ocean?
Vast and boundless, he wanders around the waterside (Baizhang Yuan).
A single drop of water from the Cao source—this is where the waves arise. Peach blossoms flow out from within the grotto;
the fisherman’s boat sleeps through the night amidst the reeds. (Yang Woei-wei)
A single drop from Cao’s spring flows in an extraordinary current; it enters the vast blue sea, crowning the nine provinces.
Though several times he cast his hook amidst perilous waves, it is never heard that he lost his fishing boat.
(Cao Tang Qing) To receive an ox from one person, yet return a horse to another—how precious is the source at Cao! One must know the propriety of this. Thunder rolls and surges.
The ocean waves arise. Who understands cutting off the current and going down that way? Going down that way, at midday one strikes the third watch.
(Chan Master Shao) A single drop from the Cao source stirs up billows and waves; ten thousand streams return to the sea to vanish. If you say that Qingliang has something else...
The essential point is this: it does not hinder what happens today or tomorrow.
(Qi Yinghua) When Fayen answered the previous words, the attendant Tiantai Shao attained sudden and complete enlightenment.
He then reported his realization to the Master, who said: "In the future, you shall be a teacher to kings, causing the ancestral Way to shine with great brilliance. I—"

It is so. A single drop of water from the source of Cao; mutual abuse is merely adding thorns to a bundle. The quail and the magpie chirp in vain, while the steed Huailou has already traveled a thousand li.
(Yuekuqing) The white clouds have dispersed and the azure sky is high; the moon sets into the heart of the waves, reflecting jade sprouts. O fisherman upon the river, cease your aimless drifting;
a cold wind suddenly arises, sharp as a blade.
Fayan was once asked by a monk: "I have heard it said in the teachings that 'from the root of non-abiding, all dharmas are established.
What is this root of non-abiding? The Master said: "Form arises before there is substance; names arise before there is naming."
Boshan Lai said: "Before form had arisen and before names had emerged, tell me, from where did the myriad phenomena come?
If you let this pass, it will not do. He gave a shout.
No trace remains; all news is cut off. White clouds have no root; what color is the clear breeze? It disperses the canopy of heaven without artifice, and sustains the earth with effortless power.
It penetrates the profound source of a thousand ages and establishes the model for the myriad phenomena.
In every speck of dust, the worlds converge—everywhere is Samantabhadra. Wherever the gates of the pavilions open, in every instance is Maitreya. (Tiantong Jue)
It has leaked away. In spring it does not bloom; in winter it does not store snow. A pair of earthen oxen chew the ancient moon—how trivial!
Where can form and name discuss this withered stump? (My companion,) from of old, the message beyond that shore is difficult to transmit;
even if it were transmitted, one would still be stuck in the realm of achievement. Are you willing to believe that a single hexagram-line penetrates all change?
Abiding in the place where sprouts do not bud, he rolls the spring wind upon his branches.
(Huaiqinghai) Fayen asked Elder Jue, "Did you come by boat or by land? He replied, "By boat. The Master said, "Where is the boat now?"
He said, "The boat is in the river. The monk withdrew. The Master then asked a bystander, "Do you say that the monk who just now spoke possesses the eye of wisdom, or does he not?
Boshan Lai replied: "The void has no colors; the great ocean has its waves. Baoren Xiu acted as the bystander.
The monk said, "The bandits have passed; now they are mustering their troops. Yishan Nu said, "Thread comes and line goes without revealing a single sharp edge.
Were it not for a state of clarity in one's vision and mastery in one's application, how could such a thing be possible?
Nevertheless, if you interpret this as 'Buddha-dharma,' you will bring disgrace upon those two elders, making them worth not even half a coin."
Water does not wash water; gold is not traded for gold. One perceives the color of the coat to obtain the horse; one plucks the silk strings to delight in the zither.
From the binding of cords to the drawing of trigrams—how many such matters there have been! The true and pure heart of Pangu has been utterly lost.

(Tiantong Jue) In times of prosperity, one constantly hears the sounds of the Great Odes. The *Yuanhe* harmonizes the musical laws as the phoenix nests in the forest. Without cause, the melody ends and the strings are stilled.
Later, as he was moving about, a mind of killing and destruction suddenly arose.
(Xinglang Xiong) Fayen asked Master Xiu: "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth. How do you understand this?"
[The student] said, "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth. The Master said, "If you understand it in this way, how can you attain it?
[The student] said, "I am just like this; what about you, Elder Brother? The Master said, "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth."
Xiu then performed a prostration.
Dongchan said, "The Master of the Mountain responds in such a manner; why do you not accept it?
When Xiu subsequently requested instruction from Fayan, he likewise replied with those same words. Tell me, where does the confusion lie? If you can see through this point, [you will understand].
"I grant you one eye. Wuzu Jie distinguished this as the "Dharma Eye" and struck him across the back.
Baoning Yong said, "Master Xiu, why did you not say at that time, 'Even understanding it in such a way, how could it be right?
Jingshan Gao said, "The two elders' discourse was continuous and dense, like drawing out thread from silk; they supported the legacy of Dizang."

As for their lineage style, one might say it fills the eyes with light. Yet, if one were under the gates of Deshan or Linji, one would still have to buy straw sandals and go on pilgrimage before it would do.
Why? Because a difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds apart. From where could such news have come? Tianning Qi said:
"Those two old fellows did not understand the turning phrase. If someone were to ask Tianning today—"
He said to him: "Yesterday someone asked this very same question; I gave them thirty blows and drove them out of the monastery. Baoyuan Xiu said:
"If Wansong had seen Fayan say that at the time, how could it have been otherwise? He would have said, 'I have long heard that the Master possesses such a pivotal teaching.
Otherwise, he would have simply waved his hand and departed, surely cutting off everyone at once. Bo.
Shanlai said, "Fayan’s hook catches people in a place beyond doubt. But tell me, how many magical arts does he possess? When the king speaks, it is like a single thread;
when it issues forth, it is like a thick cord. Hexu Qian stepped forward and said on his behalf, "The Master, it turns out, originally possesses other great strengths."
In those days, the Six Kingdoms were already at peace; having enjoyed peace for some time, they knew nothing of war.
Master Xiu devised the "Long Snake" formation, and everyone in the world understood the nature of life and death.
(Foyin Yuan) Shicheng asked his fellow practitioner with intimacy: "Without speaking of east or west, he pointed directly south. The two paths of light and dark pass back and forth.
The road winds and twists indistinctly through mist and mists.
(Baoning Yong) When a fly sits upon the scale pan, it immediately tilts; the weights of ten thousand generations shine upon what is unbalanced.
When the smallest fraction of a grain is seen with precision, in the end it yields to the fixed star of the scale. (Tiantong Jue)
A single path as straight as a string; the message of eternal peace has been delivered. Myriad realms all bring tribute; the four seas have seen the embers of war extinguished.
(The Room Opens) Two blades clash like flashing lightning; the Vajra cuts through iron as if it were soft mud. Turning one’s head, one tramples the mountain passes to dust.
The Moon. It has not yet escaped being planted again upon the eyes and eyebrows.
(Xuedui Zhao) Fayen addressed the assembly: "If you recognize this bench, there will be more than enough room all around."
Yunmen Wenyan said, "If you recognize the bench, heaven and earth are vastly different. Cui峰 Xian said, "A vast marsh hides the mountains;
a thick mist can subdue the leopard. Jianfu Hui said, "Recognizing the bench, one sees it is made of nanmu wood.
Yuantong Xiu said, "Recognizing the bench, its four legs touch the ground. Letan Qing cited Fayen and Yunmen.

Cui Feng finished speaking and said, "These three fellows all rely on their own views; they have two divergent paths, clear and obscure, and have not escaped being mere hearsay—like the moon in the water.
Huang Long, however, is not like this: 'Pervading beyond heaven and earth, unfolding before the sun and moon.
Jingshan Daokai said, "If you recognize the bench, it is easy to shave your head and wash your feet. Even so, it is still wrong."
There were many who understood this. The *Longchi Chuan* says: "If you recognize the bench, study further for thirty more years;
upon returning, do not say it is still just a bench. Yunmen Cheng said: "Recognizing the bench—there is precisely something more to it."
Lingxi Yu said: "Fayan knows how to let go but does not know how to pull back; Yunmen knows how to pull back but does not know how to let go.
Tianyi meets with a stumble on level ground—these are all merely leaning upon grass and clinging to wood. How can they compare to this: 'Dragging my staff, I watch the clouds rise;
idly listening to two or three notes of the yellow oriole'?"
I know not how to repay Your Majesty’s grace. Clouds rise over the rivers and lakes, ripples form upon the waves.
A single sail, riding its momentum, departs; With whom will it pass through the Celestial Gate?
(Baoning Yong) One is not so, two is not yet accomplished. A magpie cries amidst falling flowers and flowing waters. In the quiet courtyard, rain disperses as night draws on.
A crescent moon rises once more from the bottom of the sea.
(Xiang Tianqing) When a monk came to pay his respects, the Master pointed toward the curtain. Shortly thereafter, two monks went together to roll it up.
The Master said, "One gains, one loses.
Huanglong Qing said, "Fayan held the Mohe sword in his hand; killing or giving life was left to the occasion. The two monks both went to roll up the curtain simultaneously.
Tell me, which one wins and which one loses? Do you understand? "Mundane affairs are best settled with impartiality;
the human heart is difficult to align with the full moon. Lian’an asked: "Fayan stuck his head out, and the two monks chased after the clod of earth.
Even if they were swift and nimble in their retreat, they could not avoid taking a tumble on level ground. Baiyang Le said: "The eight characters are laid open; the eyebrows..."
A flat nose and straight [features]—no sinews in the eyes, a lifetime of poverty. For ten thousand ages and ten thousand kalpas, one can only remember them in vain.
Fayen said, "One gains, one loses. Is there anyone who can distinguish this? He struck the meditation staff and said, "The mountain monk’s mouth is too narrow."
Dowpeak Zhenju finished quoting Li’an’s words and said, "If not for these two monks stepping forward, it would have been almost a laborious effort without merit.
Nevertheless, do you know where one tumbles on level ground? One arrow, two targets."
The pine is straight and the thorn is crooked; the crane is long and the duck is short. To the world of Fuxi and Huangdi, both order and chaos have been forgotten.

In its stillness, it is like a dragon hidden in the abyss; in its freedom, it is like a soaring bird breaking its tether. Why then do the patriarchs come from the West? Gain and loss, right and wrong, are all mixed together.
Like a reed-boat turning through the empty air with the wind, or a vessel cutting across the current to reach the shore—within this, there is the clever patch-robed monk.
Behold the skillful means of Qingliang. (Tiantong Jue) An old general holds aloft his white jade whip; the two colts gallop away with elegant grace.
Those who debate and measure gain and loss throughout antiquity look in vain before the evening rain on the western mountains. (Zhengtang Bian)
On the Seventh Night, the magpies cross the Milky Way to build their bridge; the young maid threading needles toils in vain.
The traveler on the raft beside the Shiji rock now faces white surging waves upon the level slopes.

(From "Shijian Le") Pointing toward the peaks, the scenery for the gaze is secluded; lotus flowers are carved as if emerging from the autumnal waters and sky. Most pitiable is that single streak of misty haze.
Excellent! It causes the traveler’s two eyes to be obscured. (The middle line corresponds to the rhyme.
A single leaf falls from the green paulownia tree atop the bright pavilion. A pair of wild geese fly south, roaming upon the sea. Gain and loss are discussed only as matters of a thousand ages;
who can truly recognize the autumn of the Han palace? (By Zhai’an Fan)
Fayan was asked by a monk, "Who arrives first before the hall of the ancient Buddha? The Master replied, "He who does not move a step.
Zifu Guang said, "Fayan answered the question in such a way that he leads those with a vast, wandering karmic consciousness to sit in a place where they are soulless and destined for death.
Before the hall of the ancient Buddha, they will dream of it only after the year of the donkey. Nevertheless, who ultimately is this person?"
Arriving first. Few reach the ancient Buddha hall before the Ox-Head Hell-Warden.
To meet him is difficult; he possesses the mechanism of a flashing lightning bolt. A dragon in stagnant water is ultimately no sage.
Startled awake, it remains as before with eyes clouded by rheum. (Tianyi Huai)
Fayan addressed the assembly: "Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, all is brilliantly clear, without so much as a single thread of hair.
If there were a single thread of hair, it would simply be a single thread of hair."
Qingliang Qin said: "If there is even a single thread, it is not a single thread. Shuian Yi said:
"The moonlight last night was most excellent; today, the autumn mountains inspire boundless emotion."
Fayan was once asked by a monk, "What is the matter from kalpas of dust ago? The Master said, "It is exhausted in this very moment.
The matter of kalpas of dust is entirely contained within this present moment. The Patriarch did not understand; he sat facing a wall in silent contemplation.
(By Yang Wuwe) Spring ends and summer begins; suddenly autumn arrives. I ask those white-haired elders in Chang'an: on what day will you have a hundred thousand pieces of gold girded at your waist?
Guan said: "Riding the wind and the crane up to Yangzhou.
(Yishan De) Fayan held up an incense spoon and asked, "This cannot be called an incense spoon; after all, what shall it be called?
A monk said, "An incense spoon. The Master did not approve. Twenty days later, the monk finally realized his error.
Mist and water stretch far away, growing ever more distant; the frosty wind blows sternly, separating one from the ends of the earth.
Even if you were to recognize the fragrant ladle, it would still guarantee that this fellow has not yet arrived home.
(Chu’ān Pǔ) Fǎyǎn asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from Sīzhōu to pay homage to the Great Sage. The Master said, "The Great Sage..."
"Will he emerge from the stupa this year? He replied, "He will. The Master then asked a monk standing nearby, "Do you say this monk has ever been to Sizhou? The monk likewise had no reply.
Fushan Yuan said: "This monk reached Sizhou, but he simply did not see the Great Sage.
Dochang Quan said: "This monk saw him; he indeed saw the Great Sage, but he simply never recognized Fayen.
Dongchan Guan said: "This monk reached Sizhou, he saw the Great Sage, and he recognized Fayen; it is simply that..."
