When he went to seek him himself, the head was nowhere to be seen. Baolin Xiu said, "This group of fellows has their illness deep-seated in the vital organs;
they only look at saying that the monk was not seen, but who knows that it is actually they themselves who do not recognize the monk?
When someone came forward and said, "The Master is merely supporting the weak and not the strong," Baolin struck him immediately upon hearing these words. Tell me, was this an affirmation of him?
To accept it:
the wondrous, perfect golden ground is utterly free of even the finest dust. One who arrives should contemplate the true formless. Do not say that the Mysterious Gate is difficult to approach;
lift your head and you are already among those within the pagoda. (Chengtian Zong)

While in the process of opening a well, Fayuan asked the assembly, "If the spring source does not flow, it is obstructed by sand. But as for the Way-eye (daoyan) not flowing, what is it obstructed by?
The assembly had no reply. [Fayuan] provided the answer on their behalf: "It is obstructed by the eye."
The Fifth Patriarch Jiao said, "Fayan was much like one who could not save his boat and so smashed the bailer. If it were I, Jiao, I would not do so.
When a spring does not flow, it is obstructed by sand; but as for the eye of the Way not flowing, what is it obstructed by?
I would simply tell him it is obstructed by the Way itself. This not only causes him to attain sudden awakening in that very moment, but also serves as a testament for all time.
“Leave this eye.
Dharma-Eye ascended the hall. When the three rounds of drums had ceased, the assembly crowded upward. Matters of the Buddha-dharma and human affairs were all settled at once.
Huiwen Ni said: "When the three rounds of drums have ceased and they have all come crowding forward, the staff is not here;
I shall give them thirty blows with the handle of a broom. Píngyáng Mín said: "Fayan used a hook; Huiwen used a chisel. This mountain monk neither hooks you nor chisels you;
let me set you free for a while so that you may watch until it cools. He then said: "When the three rounds of drums have ceased, they come crowding forward."
"Up until now, the text below is long; we shall leave it for another day. Falin-yin said: "When the three rounds of drums have ceased, they all crowd upward.
What a miserable fellow! What bowl are you looking for?"
Fayan heard the sounding of the vegetarian fish-drum and asked the monks, "Do you hear it? "If you heard it just now, you do not hear it now;
if you hear it now, you did not hear it just now."
Falin’s *Yinyun* says: "The Dharma-eye is largely like celebrating a feast;
one listens with ears as if deaf and speaks with a mouth as if mute. As for the tongue of the Dharma-eye, what is real and what is false? (Wuzhuo’s General Summary).
Regarding the monk’s question, "How can one penetrate the two characters 'sound' and 'form'?", Fayen called out to the assembly, saying, "All you venerable ones..."
[The Master] sat. Now tell me, has this monk penetrated it yet? If you understand where this monk was asking, then penetrating sound and form will not be difficult. Tiantong Jue said:
"From the past until now, one has failed to realize it only because the 'house-thief' is difficult to guard against. To be clear and distinct right here—now, look toward..."
Staying overnight in a thatched hut, Fengge Miaoyun said: "Brightly repairing the plank road, secretly crossing at Chen Cang.
Yuan'an Yulu said: "On level ground, there are countless dead people. Lanmo Daoyun said: "This monk sleeps crosswise amidst sounds and forms;
having been deceived once by Fayan, he is unable to take even a single step forward. Turning to look at the assembly, he said: "Do you still..."
Do you know that those who wear the Dharma-eye have been deceived by the Sangha?
He asked in person to seek a way through; the master directly pointed out the darkness for him. Suddenly his eyes and ears awoke from a spring dream;
the warbling of the oriole and the chatter of the swallow are all perfect penetration. (Da Hong Su)
Sound and form are both but two words; yet for the patch-robed monk, they are sand in his eyes. Amidst the Yellow Crane Tower, a jade flute is blown;
in the fifth month, plum blossoms fall upon the river city.

(Cishou Shen) Having once washed one’s ears in the azure mountain stream, ten thousand gullies and a thousand crags turn the path ever more secluded. Most especially so when the moon is bright and the wind is still.
Night. A single long cry of laughter as the sea gates turn autumnal. (Lian'an asked.
Chan Master Hongjin of Qingxi Mountain in Xiangzhou (a successor of Luohan Chen) asked Master Xiu:
"If one clearly understands the principle that birth is non-birth, why is one still transmigrated by birth and death? Xiu replied: "The bamboo shoots have finished."
[The bamboo] was finally finished as a bamboo pole; it is now being used as bamboo strips. "Can you still obtain it? The Master said, "You shall realize it for yourself in the future.
[Daoshao] said, "My insight, Shaoxiu, is only this much. What is the meaning of the Abbot's intent?
The Master said, "This is the Director of the Monastery’s room; that is the Head Cook’s room. Daoshao then bowed in thanks.
Advancing into old age, he clearly reached Mount Wutai; Master Xiu was truly a man who came from Min. The *vinaya-dhara* and the temple head face one another at the gate;
when their names are mentioned, they cause people’s two eyes to open wide.
(Zhengjue Yi) Vast and unattached, lofty and unrestrained, his homeland is peaceful and settled where few men dwell. With such slight strength, he shares [his realization].
The Stages. Vast and boundless, body and mind are cut off from right and wrong. When right and wrong are cut off, one stands alone in the Great Square, leaving no tracks.
(Tiantong Jué) King Mu followed the Queen Mother; before the steps, he listened to the white clouds. The attendants did not recognize him at all, yet they still presumed it was Bingfen.
(Liutingting) The pillar has been pregnant for years; as the time for delivery approaches, her life hangs by a thread.
Suddenly, a jade girl emerges from its side, causing all the guests at the high hall banquet to fall over with laughter. (Zhiyinghua)
Chan Master Shaoshou, Abbot of Longji Mountain in Fuzhou (a successor of Luohan Chen), addressed the assembly: "The dharmas of ordinary people are fully present, yet ordinary people do not know them.
The dharmas of sages are fully present, yet sages do not understand them. If sages were to understand them, they would be ordinary people;
if ordinary people were to know them, they would be sages. These words possess one principle and two meanings. If a person..."
If you can discern this, there will be no hindrance; you will have a point of entry into the Buddha-dharma. If you cannot discern it, do not say that you have no doubts.
Huanglong Qing said: "Master Xiu only knows how to spread his nets and set his snares, yet he does not realize he has fallen into the trap himself. You must...
"Have you escaped the body? This also contains one principle and two meanings. If a person can discern this, they will fall forever into the Avīci Hell.
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "It is easier to refine iron into gold and jade than it is to exhort people to eliminate their right and wrong.
Jingci Daoyi said: "Even if there were a path of entry, what could it accomplish? An ordinary person remains an ordinary person; a sage remains a sage."
If one is thus, one is a sage. But tell me, when both the ordinary and the sage are forgotten, how do you express it in a single phrase?
Holding a scripture, leaning against a pine tree, he stands; smiling, he asks the guest, "From where have you come?
Mianjie struck his staff and said: "One does not know; two does not understand. East, west, south, and north, all are drenched in rain. Tianning Qi said: "Master Xiu."
"What is familiar is difficult to forget. This is like bamboo shoots sprouting in winter in a foreign land. Longchi said: "It is not so at Longchi.
Ordinary people possess the Dharma of the sages, yet ordinary people do not know it. Sages possess the Dharma of ordinary people, yet sages do not realize it.
If sages were to realize it, they would no longer be sages; if ordinary people were to know it, how could they remain ordinary people?"
"In this very moment, as I, an old monk, have thus brought [you] down, is there still any discrimination? He lets out a shout and says:
"When meeting one who has attained the Way on the road, do not respond with speech or silence."
The ordinary is entirely the holy, and the holy is entirely the ordinary. Investigate the reality and abandon names; penetrate directly beneath.
When one is vast, clear, and transcends the realm of both ordinary and holy, the wordless child speaks incessantly.

(Lingyuan Qing) Eradicate the entanglements of manifest proclamations; there is no need for "zhi-hu-ye-zhe" (the particles of formal discourse). Even if you are thoroughly proficient in the meaning of every phrase, you cannot avoid—
To call a donkey a horse. (Wan’an Yan) The Peak of Fusion rises ten thousand fathoms high;
before a word is spoken, one’s feet already ache. If one does not go forth amidst the drifting clouds, how could one know the chill of the stars?
Longji’s verse says:
If you wish to recognize the path of liberation, All phenomena do not reach one another. The eyes and ears cease seeing and hearing;
Sounds and forms are in a vast, tumultuous uproar.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Sound does not reach the ear; form does not reach the eye. When sound and form intersect, the myriad dharmas manifest.
Tell me, do you still tread upon the path of liberation or not? If you do not realize this meaning, your cultivation will be nothing but bitter toil."
Longji’s verse says: "When the beginner has not yet entered the Way, they must not be caught up in a clamorous bustle. Realize it amidst the tolling of the bell;
be overturned amidst the beating of the drum. Tianmu Li said:
"Master Xiu may truly be said to have no interference between the five notes and six pitch-pipes; it is indeed beautiful."
Alas! For now, you are buried alive amidst the dust of sounds; to this day, you cannot emerge from it. Why? Xuan Sha said, "The bottom has been reached.
Longji said, "When it is a pillar, one does not see the pillar; when it is not a pillar, one does not see the pillar. Right and wrong have already departed. This is "is."
"Not taking it from within the scriptures.
Jingshan Hongdao said, "Tsk! This is starting all over again. Tianning Weiqing said, "Master Liu Xiushan has little understanding of the teachings;
even his 'extraordinary' insights are merely the views of a lecturer. He has not yet dreamed of our monk."
The old patriarch was present. When seeing a pillar, he simply called it a pillar; when seeing a lantern, he simply called it a lantern.
Do not touch them; if you touch them, you shall receive thirty blows of the staff.
If you can point it out, this is like moving flowers while butterflies follow; if you can point it out, this is not like carrying water from the spring or returning with the moon.
"Is" is good; Zhengzhou pears surpass Qingzhou dates. "Is not" is good; the Elephant Path leads into the Penglai Isles. Even "is" has no connection [to the truth].
Treading upon a scale-weight, hard as iron—even "is not" has no connection. The Vajra sword cuts directly through the head.
A-he-he! Do you understand? When one knows few things, afflictions are few; where one recognizes many people, disputes are many.
(Qu’an’s own verse:
A great-feathered arrow at the waist of a fierce warrior—once drawn, its single shaft settles the Celestial Mountains. Heaven and earth are unified, as pure as...
Mirror. There is no need for flying letters or closing the gates again. (Huishí Qí) Longjì said:
"Two breakings do not constitute one; the single Dharma eternally endures. If a person understands 'one' and 'two,' they will suffer in the depths of saṃsāra for eons."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Master Xiu is like a sky-reaching long sword, its divine majesty awe-inspiring;

where it is level and smooth, it stands as steep as a thousand fathoms, and where it stands as steep as a thousand fathoms, it is level and smooth. Although this is so, he has only spoken half the truth.
This mountain monk is not like that: two broken, one is not formed; even the single dharma does not remain; neither one nor two is made."
[The student] says: "For eternal kalpas one undergoes sinking and drifting;
hearing does not transcend sound, and seeing does not go beyond form. Pointing to the east, one speaks of the west; taking the south for the north. (Gulin Mao) Longji said:
"The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are only the awakening of the nature. Originally there is no person who is deluded or awakened; it is merely..."
"It must be resolved today.
Tianning Qi said: "Since there is neither delusion nor enlightenment, what is there to resolve? 'From of old, no one has recognized the merit of his labor;
he simply wishes to re-examine his epoch-making achievements.'"
Longji asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Cuiyan. The Master said, "What words or phrases did Cuiyan use to instruct his disciples?
The monk said, "He usually says, 'When you go out the door, you meet Maitreya; when you enter the gate, you see Śākyamuni. The Master said, "How can he speak in such a way?
The monk then asked, "And how about you, Master? The Master said, "When you go out the door, whom do you meet?"
"What do you see upon entering the gate? A monk had an awakening at these words.
Jianfu Hui said, "Though you have won one battle of glory, you have lopped off a pair of feet. Now tell me, does this fall on the side of the guest or the side of the host?
If you can determine this, then in sorrow you share the grief and in joy you share the delight. Shan... [text fragment]
The Sangha is not like this. Upon exiting the gate, there are the mountains of Wu and the waters of Chu; upon entering the gate, there are the Buddha Hall and the corridors.
If there happens to be a monk who comes forth and asks, "What is the Master’s meaning? one may grant that he possesses a single eye. Xichan Xu said:

As for this, it is not that the realization of the Sangha is non-existent; yet, alas, one has not yet encountered the ultimate truth. It is like being bewitched by demons under the clear blue sky and bright sun.
Longji, with his head white and teeth yellow, speaks such words as these. Lan’an, however, is not so: "Leaving the gate, the bamboo path is unweeded;
entering the courtyard, the square pond reflects the cold."
Longji was asked by a monk, "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder: will this [reality] be destroyed or not?
The Master said, "It is not destroyed. The monk asked, "Why is it not destroyed? The Master replied, "Because it is identical to the great trichiliocosm."
Question: "If one carves out the heart? Answer: "It is like splitting open the belly. Turning the body within the words—what need is there for haste?
When the kalpa-fire blazes together with the great trichiliocosm, the entire mechanism remains unmoving while the sword’s edge whirls. At the peak of Longji Mountain, the dragon sheds its bones;
in the heavens of Yama, the drum stirs the surging rapids.
Having ears, one does not hear what lies beyond the window; before one’s eyes, how could there be any mechanism of difference or sameness?
By chance, I encountered an old man from the Three Families; his speech was entirely humorous and unrestrained.

(Tian'an Sheng) Chan Master Xuanliang of Dongchan Temple in Fuzhou (a successor of Bianhong Xi under Xuefeng Yicun). A monk asked: "Fundamentally, there is neither delusion nor enlightenment. For what reason..."
"Why is it that there are Buddhas and sentient beings? The Master said, "Your words have fallen.

Yingshan Yun said, "Tell me, was it this monk’s words that fell, or was it Dongchan’s words that fell? Chengtian Yi said: [The Master said,] "Your words have fallen. Yingshan Yun asked, "Now tell me: did this monk’s words fall, or did Dongchan’s words fall? Chengtian Yi said:
This person was attempting to press ahead with his journey under the moonlight according to the *Mahāsāṃghika* Vinaya, when he inadvertently fell into the water with his whole body.

Although Dongchan was able to follow the direction and point out the way for him, he nonetheless lacked the strategic mastery of a true patriarch. At that time, had he been asked such a question, he would have struck him with his staff and driven him out.
He simply causes them to give rise to devotion toward the Buddha, so that at the point where delusion and awakening are suddenly empty, they establish a separate way of life.

Under the tenth generation of Dajian (Mazu), there was National Teacher Deshao of Tiantai Mountain in Taizhou (who succeeded Fayen Yi). Because a monk asked him: "Having just left the Master of the Peak of Clarity..."
[The monk] entered the room and sat in the Prajñā-dharmacakra. "Today, we request a word from the Master regarding our house style. The Master said, "In what way have you failed?
The monk said, "If it is so, then the thunderous voice shakes the realm of heaven and earth; there is not one person who does not receive its grace.
The Master said, "Fortunately, you have not yet understood; do not stick out your head. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Stick out your head!"
"That is not correct.
Huguo Yun said: "The National Teacher’s response in this manner certainly reveals the ancestral style of the Buddhas and Patriarchs;

nevertheless, that monk was not yet willing to nod his head. If someone were to ask me, 'Please give us one phrase regarding today's ancestral style,' I would say: 'Today's ancestral style is like a great dragon emerging from the sea.'"
He simply said: "Tiantai is eighteen thousand *zhang* high; morning and evening, mist and clouds seal it from all eight sides.
When Tiantai first visited Longya, he asked: "The majestic and honored one—why can one not approach him?
Longya said: "It is like fire meeting fire. The Master said: "What if water suddenly encounters it? Longya said: "Go! You do not..."
Understand my words.

To harbor a treasure while lost in one’s own land—how great a mistake! To cast a pearl only to meet a drawn sword, then turn back again. The spring breeze knows not of the blooming or falling of flowers;
the flowing water remains as it was, passing through ten thousand mountains. (Píngyáng Mín)
Tiantai was asked by a monk: "The ferry and oars have both been set aside; how can one reach the other shore? The Master said: "I congratulate you on your life's work;
you should be able to find rest right now. Within the great thousandfold world-system, there is not so much as a single hair-tip. Xiang Yu long ago would have agreed at Xianyang."
Standing, a single breeze of imperial grace pervades the eight hundred prefectures. (Yuan’an Fang) Tiantai addressed the assembly:
"The green creepers wind their way straight up to the summit of the cold pine; white clouds linger lightly, appearing and disappearing within the vast void.
All phenomena are fundamentally at rest; it is only people who create their own clamor."
These [teachings] are bestowed out of compassion for you. His tongue drags upon the ground as his speech rolls like thunder. Entanglements fill the earth, yet no one prunes them;
in the spring wind, all is once again in disarray. (Zhuwu Jian) Tiantai addressed the assembly:
"The summit of Tongxuan Peak is not of this world. Outside the mind there is no dharma; the eyes see nothing but green."
Shan said: "Hearing this single verse, Fayen was able to establish our school.
Jingshan Daoyuan said: "The Fayen school was extinguished precisely because of that one verse. Zhaoqing Zuting said: "Heaven does not cover it;
earth does not bear it; there is nowhere to hide the body. The water is naturally green, the mountains are naturally blue; yet even a single hair obstructs the eye. Only...
"The summit of Tongxuan Peak is not of this human world. But tell me, what place is it? "A single petal of falling blossoms flies;
ten thousand realms return to spring. Tiantong Wu said: "At New Tongxuan, it is not so. Today I open another path:
the summit of Tongxuan Peak is indeed the human world. It is only because you fail to realize it that you mistakenly take the green mountains for it. *He!*
With a single shout, he asked, "Do you still understand? Then he descended from his seat.
Singing and sleeping beneath the thatched eaves, drunk and then awake again; Mount Junshan remains ever green between his two brows. His entire family pays no heed to matters of rise and fall;
they do nothing but share the clouds and occupy Lake Dongting. (Wuwen Can)
Outside the mind, not a single dharma has ever existed from the beginning. The National Teacher’s point of view was not yet intimate.
If you say that the green mountains filling one’s eyes are it, by clinging to them, you merely produce more dust in your own eyes.
(Wu-yin-jian) Chan Master Taiqin Fadeng of Qingliang in Jinling (a successor of Fayen Yi) asked a monk: "What is the Patriarch?"

A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Master’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Neither east nor west. The monk did not approve of this answer, so he asked again, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master replied, "Neither east nor west. The monk attained realization.
The ancestral intent from the West knows neither east nor west; Monkeys and birds, in the depths of spring, cry out as they embrace the trees.
How many travelers gaze on in vain longing? The green mountains stand solitary and high, the white clouds hang low.
(Baoning Yong) Neither east nor west—a single phrase held up in its entirety. Soft as raw iron, hard as rotten mud. One has not yet mastered the art of casting a needle.
Washing the bowl with water; scraping the film, one uses the golden probe once more. Clouds lock the home mountain, the path home is cut off;
turning the head, one laughs instead at the cuckoo’s cry.

(Kentang Chong) When Qingliang opened the hall, this mountain monk originally intended to dwell in the mountains to hide his ineptitude and spend his time tending to his illness. However, due to [the circumstances of] the Master...
The Master had a kōan that he had not yet resolved. He called out, "Come forth and settle it with me! At that time, a monk asked, "What is the kōan that the late master did not resolve?
The Master struck him and said, "If the patriarch does not resolve it, the calamity falls upon his descendants.
The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie? The Master said, "The fault lies with me; the calamity falls upon you."
Cuiyan Zhi said: "To exert one's utmost effort for the sake of the assembly, yet the calamity arises from within one's own gate. Yunfeng Yue said:

"This old fellow’s display of bestowing and withholding for a time seems to outshine the past and surpass all that came before; yet when pressed to the limit, he once again leaves his head as a dragon while his tail is like a snake."
"Now, is there anyone who can act as the master for Qingliang? Zhaojue Qin said: "The Dharma-lamp extends throughout the realm;
he wields the power of killing and giving life beyond the threshold. His majestic authority is such that his spirit awes the multitudes and his wind-penetrating standard stands alone.
This humble monk’s lowly ambition and original intent have always been thus. I have come forth today solely because my late Master Wuzu possessed this ready-made [treasure]."
The public case is presented for the assembly to hear. Let there be someone who does not spare their very life to come forward and test it.
If there is none, I shall not avoid picking it up and playing with it myself. (He lets out a shout and strikes the whisk, then descends from his seat. Tiantong Jue said:
If this monk were a true man, he would have come forth and overturned the meditation seat;
not only would he have found a way for himself to emerge, but he would also have spared his ancestors from leaving unfinished business that brings calamity upon their descendants. Dongchan Guan said:
"When a thousand-jin bowstring is drawn, one must think of a fierce battle; when an inch of iron is in hand, one fears only having no foe. Since this monk did not begrudge coming forth...
"Good people! Having set aside [worldly concerns] to attend to the principle, you simply remain as you are; you merely smear it over.
That is why Master Qingliang’s public case remains unresolved to this day. Yangshan Qin said: 'To cross the hearth and establish the household'—this is the standard of Fadeng."
A skilled hand may be at fault for failing to understand its own nature, thereby bringing calamity upon its ancestors. The New Guardian Saint wishes to resolve the public case of his former master;
there is another person present. But tell me, who is it? He then lets out a sneeze. Gunanmen said:
"Fadeng can indeed be called one who guides others with modesty, bending an inch to straighten a fathom. I, however, am not so. The entire world..."
It has never been hidden. Although one may occupy the solitary peaks and highest summits, one has never failed to dwell in the depths of the waters and clouds;
when, then, has one ever lived in seclusion? The Original Teacher is present now, eating and defecating as usual—what unresolved koan could there be?
Since this is so, why do you call out before everyone’s faces today? The ancestral lamp continues its flame, shining without end.
Provided that the hook catches the scaled dragon, The autumn deepens and crimson leaves fall from the groves. Under the moon, the fisherman straightens his rod and line;
His small boat does not stay overnight in the reed cove, But rows across the golden waves, drifting at will. (Snow of Auspiciousness)
In her old age, she conceived the desire to remarry; Skillfully applying rouge and powder, she tries to sell her fading youth.
She laughs at that fallen, foolish young gentleman Who has needlessly diminished his vital spirit by ten parts.
(Zi Qinghao) Regarding the question asked by the monk Qingliang, "What is the profound, secret meaning of the Westward Journey? the Master said, "Suffering."
Profound feelings cannot bear the distance of this desolate village. In vain I roll up the bamboo blinds and lean alone against the gate. The wind is cold upon the river as autumn draws to a close;
Faint mist and sparse rain break the soul. (Shout and turn the wheel:
Withered trees are sprinkled with blossoms—a spring beyond the kalpas. Where there are no traces, one dares not hide the body. Riding backward on an iron horse, he blows the transverse flute.
The Flute. A single melody, its tune spontaneously renewed.

(Miaoye qi) Moss seals the forbidden palace as the sound of the watch-drums fades. The whistling golden wind pierces the body with cold. In the still night, a single wheel of frost-moon shines bright;
A jade-like person leans against the balustrade, lost in sorrow. (Yizhi hua)
In this inn, the lamp’s shadow lingers in desolation; Where does the lone ape cry out at night’s deep? When I ponder these matters, they are truly pitiable;
Though I tune the jade zither, my longing remains unspent. (Wei Zhongjing) The myriad sounds return as the wind sweeps through ten thousand ravines;
After the rain, the color of the grass enters the lattice windows. How many things on the tower top stir the heart?
The matter, however, lies within a single leaf of the *wútóng* tree.
(Zōng Lángyuè) Chan Master Xuánzé of Bǎo'ēn Monastery in Jīnlíng (a successor of Fǎyǎn Yì) initially asked Qīngfēng, "What is the student’s own self?
Fēng replied, "A child of fire comes seeking fire. Later, he visited Fǎyǎn, who asked him: "What..."
[The monk] asked, "Where do you come from? The Master said, "From Qingfeng. [The monk] asked, "What words did Qingfeng have? The Master recounted the previous conversation.
Yan said, "How do you understand this, Senior Monk? The Master said, "'Bing' and 'Ding' belong to fire, yet one seeks fire further;
it is like seeking oneself by means of oneself. Yan said, "Even if you understand it thus, how can that suffice? The Master said, "I simply understand it this way."
"I do not yet understand, Master; how is it? The Eye said, "Ask me, and I shall tell you. The Master asked, "What is the student's own self?
[The Eye] replied, "A child of the fire-element (丙丁) comes seeking fire. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
Gao Feng said, "As for this koan, from ancient times until now, finding someone who understands it without error is like picking out the moon from among the stars.
Take, for instance, the former head monk who attained enlightenment under Fayan’s words; yet, even so, he was not merely following the vermilion.
Let those with true insight try to discern this. Xuanzhao Yuan said, "Fayan was certainly acting according to the situation..."
Ko Da-jie truly possessed the ability to "feign an attack on one state while actually striking another. Thus, the monastery supervisor attained a sudden awakening.
Yet, alas, he was like one who thrusts his head into a vat of glue. Nevertheless, it is easy to see Fayen, but difficult to see Qingfeng.
The first weighing recorded eight *liang*; upon re-weighing, it was exactly half a *jin*. Upon whom does the fixed scale-point (*dingpansheng*) rest?
To contend over a mere hair’s breadth is truly lamentable. (Baizun) Once again I fall drunk before the Jade Tower;
my hair is disheveled, my hairpins askew, and my speech is wild with laughter. Most vexing is this heart-rending sorrow.
In this place, borrow my wife’s robe to pay respects at her mother-in-law’s birthday.
(Wanshan Ning) On this very day last year, within these same gates, Human faces and peach blossoms reflected each other’s redness. I know not where those human faces have gone;
The peach blossoms remain, smiling at the spring breeze. (Huatang Yan)
On the day Xuan opened the hall, both King Li and Fayen were present in the assembly. A monk asked, "The dragon roars and mist rises; the tiger howls and wind is born.
I know this to be a matter concerning the transcendence of the world, yet why is it that I do not understand it upon reaching this point? The Master said, "Understand it well!
The monk raised his head to look, and the Master likewise looked at Fayen, whereupon he withdrew his body and entered the assembly. Fayen [did the same].
Yanguan was startled and his expression changed; he turned his gaze toward the abbot’s quarters and ordered an attendant monk to summon the monk who had asked the question.
Yanguan said, "Regarding the question you asked just now, I will grant that you possess one eye.
Why did you not prostrate before the assembly of devas and humans to cover your tracks? He then struck the sitting mat once. Three days later, the monk vomited [blood].
[The Master] passed away while emitting light.
Shendingi said: "As for this public case, when the Way is exhausted and the mystery is reached, it is like pushing a boat downstream—right where one is, the joints fall away.
Fayan’s 'pitying his son for not being ugly' is like pulling up the roots in the dark. To discuss the matter in such a way shows you do not yet know the ancients. Shendingi.
Without sparing his own eyebrows, he pierced through for him. Striking the staff once, he said: "Do you want to recognize this monk?

He carries dry firewood on his back and meets with a wild fire. Striking the staff again, he said: "Do you want to recognize Fayan? Clouds and thunder escort him as he transforms into a soaring dragon.
[The character for "muttering" (爾)] Xuanze set down his staff and said: "Water returns to the great ocean, and the waves and billows subside. Clouds...
Reaching Cangwu, the atmosphere is serene. Again he offers this verse:
A spirit-attendant at his elbow, he brandishes the Dragon Spring sword; He sweeps away the smoke of war and returns in triumph.
Having won glory that illuminates the universe, His heroic fame is transmitted through the halls of state, past and present.
One day, Chan Master Huiming of Baoen Temple in Hangzhou (a successor of Fayan Wenyi) was visited by a newly arrived monk. The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
The monk replied, "Chengdu. The Master said, "Venerable, since you have left Chengdu to come to this mountain, Chengdu is deficient of you, while this place has a surplus of you.
If there is a surplus, then phenomena exist outside the mind; if there is a deficiency, then phenomena are within the mind."
[The monk’s] response was incomplete. When he had finished explaining the principle, he remained silent and did not ask for further instruction.
The assembly had no reply. Dongshan Ying spoke on his behalf, saying: "Even if I were to explain the principle thoroughly, it would ultimately never be as good as that of the Master.
Chengtian Yi said: "Although Baoyuan has exhausted the explanation of the principle, he himself cannot even account for it."
Chan Master Daqian (Dafayan Yi’s successor), the founder of Yongming Temple in Hangzhou, first visited Fayan. Fayan asked, “Aside from your formal inquiries, what sutra are you studying?
The Master replied, “The Avatamsaka. Fayan asked, “Under which category are the six aspects—totality, particularity, sameness, difference, formation, and disintegration—subsumed?
The Master replied, “All phenomena, both mundane and supramundane, are fully endowed with these six aspects.”
[Zhaozhou] asked, "Does emptiness possess the six characteristics? The Master had no reply. [Zhaozhou] said, "Why do you not ask it?

The Master then asked in return, "Does emptiness possess the six characteristics? [Zhaozhou] replied, "Emptiness. Thereupon, the Master attained enlightenment. [Zhaozhou] asked, "How do you understand this?
The Master replied, "Emptiness. Zhaozhou approved.
Empty, empty—no front and no back. Picked up, it suddenly becomes two pieces.
Carried to the foot of Nanping Mountain, few have seen it through the ages, through the ages. Do you wish to see it? (With the whisk, he draws a circle and says:
"The golden crow flies up onto the crystal palace. (Duanqiao Lun)
Yongming asked Fayuan, "In the Vinaya it is said that hearing the sound of hairpins and bracelets through a wall constitutes a violation of the precepts.
Yet, we currently see gold and silver mixed together and crimson and purple robes crowded side by side. Is this a violation of the precepts or not?
The Master said, "What an excellent point of entry! Fayan said, "In the future, you will have five hundred disciples in woolen robes, who will be held in high esteem by kings and lords."
Tianning Qi said: "If you truly can enter, it is like adding flowers upon brocade; if you cannot enter, it is like having grit in your eye.
Guangxiang De said: "Fayan wished to pluck a single eyebrow from within the fire, but since that was impossible..."
He succeeded; yet Yongming was skilled at "striking from within the nest," which is certainly worthy of praise. Nevertheless, he only understood how to look ahead and failed to look behind.
Zu Dengshao said: "Yongming was like a fragrant elephant crossing a river—cutting through the current and passing over.
He was indeed a master hand, yet he could not avoid being buried alive by Fayan."
The springtime light is stored separately within a single golden jar; I intend to learn the "Partridge" song of Jiangnan. In vain I grasp flower branches to beckon the Stone Maiden;
though she leans sideways and does not fall, she must be supported upright. How many are ugly and dull, and how many are beautiful?

Having traversed famous mountains and market towns alike, I can do nothing but lament that my family is poor and has long been beset by misfortune; I borrow my mother-in-law’s robe to bow for her birthday. (Shi Yu Fang)
For the most part, when there is no mind, one simply rests. What use is this gold to trade for brass? Amidst a thicket of a hundred flowers, the face of a beautiful woman;
a single smile, and all who look on nod their heads in approval.
(Tian Yue Zhou) Wen Jun, lightly adorned, happens to tend the furnace; the jade bowl glimmers with waves of amber. The young gentleman’s refined elegance fills his two eyes.
Jùn: Without having tasted fine wine or gazed upon beautiful maidens, (Chāo of Xidùn) says:
The talented scholar of Luoyang is accustomed to spring excursions; Willow paths and flower streets are all at his disposal. He further recalls passing over the bridge by West Lake:
Wherever one has wealth, how can one not be elegant and refined? (Lín of Rénzǐ)
Chan Master Qingsong of Lingyin in Hangzhou (a successor of Fayan Wenyi) asked a monk, "Do you understand the Buddha-dharma?
The monk replied, "I do not. The Master said, "Are you truly not understanding? The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "Go for now;
come back at another time. The monk said, "Take care," and departed. The Master said, "This is not the principle."
A jade artisan has stored a pitcher of clear ice; With both hands he presents it, luminous and solid. He grasps it with his hand as if it were a *ruyi* scepter and smashes it all to pieces;
The lingering shadows of the sun wind around the eaves of the hall.
(By Xueyin) Chan Master Congyi of Tiansheng Mountain in Xiangzhou (a successor in the line of Qingxi Jin) once said while at Xiuyuan: "Do not say..."
He understood the Buddha-dharma, yet there was no one to be found who could even raise a koan for him. When Master Yuan heard of this, he remained silent.
One day, as the Master was ascending the Dharma hall, Yuan called out, "Congyi! The Master raised his head; Yuan said, "Wrong. The Master then walked two or three steps.
The Head of the Monastery said, "Wrong. The Master stepped forward. The Head said, "Just now there were two wrongs: was it the Senior Monk who was wrong, or was it I, the old man Siming?
The Master replied, "It was Chongyi who was wrong. The Head said, "Wrong, wrong! He then said, "Senior Monk, stay here for the summer retreat;
we shall deliberate together on these two wrongs. The Master, refusing to accept this, departed. After he established his own monastery, he spoke of this every day.
He recalled the previous conversation, saying: "When I was traveling on foot, I was driven by a fierce wind to Ruizhou.
There, the Elder of West Yuan examined me and made two consecutive mistakes. He even detained me for the summer retreat, intending to deliberate with me.
I did not say that I was mistaken at that time; rather, I already knew I was mistaken when I set out for the South."
Shoushan Nian said, "Based on Tianping’s understanding, he has not even dreamed of Xiyuan. Why? Because the story remains.

Zhaojue Qin said, "People nowadays, upon hearing him say that [Tianping] had already gone astray even before setting out for the South, immediately begin to speculate, saying, 'Before he had even begun his pilgrimage, he naturally did not have so many Buddhas.'"

This is the Way of Dharma-meditation. Yet, when it comes to traveling on pilgrimage and being deceived by various quarters, one must not, before having traveled, call the earth heaven or call the mountains water.

Fortunately, there is not a single speck of such a thing. If you all simply act with such vulgar, worldly interpretations, why not buy a piece of cloth for a hat and wear it together? What use would that have? The Buddha-dharma is not like this.
Regarding this principle, Jingshan Daoyuan said: "Tianping’s likeness is indeed a likeness, yet it is not yet the truth. Why? Because he was too hasty in rushing toward his goal.
At that time, as soon as he heard, 'Stay here for the summer retreat and I will deliberate with you,' he made two mistakes.
One should have seized him and said: 'I do not decline to stay for the summer retreat, but how shall we deliberate regarding those two mistakes? Wait—"
Yi hesitated to deliberate. He overturned the meditation seat and departed.
This not only brought joy to his entire life, but also cut off the tongues of everyone in the world. Longxiang Yin, having finished citing Xuedou’s verse, said:
"Regarding this public case, there are many in the monastic community who discuss it but few who reach a definitive judgment. Today, Zhongfeng shall judge it for you all. [One person.]
The Abbot stole from the monastery himself; one person sold the thief and released him, while another knew of it but did not report it.
Each was given thirty blows of the staff. Why? Because if an error is committed quickly, it is easy to correct; if it persists for long, it is difficult to remedy. Wuzu Gang said:
"Even if one had the iron of the nine provinces, it would be difficult to forge these two blunders. Falin Yin said: "At that time, Xiyuan was waiting for him."

The Way arises from the interplay of waves; thus, he struck him with a severe blow to prevent this fellow from being entangled and tripped up for a lifetime within the vines of conceptual proliferation.
Those who follow the Zen school are fond of frivolity; though they come with their bellies full of inquiry, it proves useless. How truly pitiable and laughable is Old Tianping!
He then said, "I regretted my travels at the start. A mistake, a mistake! Xiyuan’s pure wind suddenly melts it away. He spoke again:
"Suppose a monk were to come out and say, 'Wrong!'—how would Xuedou’s 'wrong' compare to Tianping’s 'wrong'? (Cui Feng Xian) Holding the mooring line while letting the boat go;
sticking to the old tuning pegs while adjusting the strings. Distant water cannot save against a near fire; how can a short rope draw from a deep spring?
The old man of T'ien-p'ing was too hasty and careless; he made two mistakes and regretted his travels. The vast earth stretches on endlessly, bringing grief that kills the spirit;
with no strength in one's eyes, one remains poor for a lifetime.

(Yuanwu Keqin) Having brought forth those two mistakes, in the end nothing was accomplished; following this, the paths to the south and north diverged, and later, exhausting all efforts, he could only explain them away.
Verse: Half longing for you, half resenting you. (Qingyun Na) Last night the western wind suddenly blew fiercely;
the peaches and plums in the entire garden were all blown down. The traveler seeking blossoms came vying with others to gather them, yet there was nowhere to grasp them.
Searching everywhere across the ground, they were of no use at all. Turning my thoughts back, I remember the calyxes upon the red and white branches. From time to time...
Raising it up, one forgets the dispute; speaking of it before others is a great error. Regret your wandering travels; within the old papers of a thousand years, one must compound the medicine.

(Qiming’s Mirror) It is easy to call for a snake, but difficult to drive it away. Look closely at the sharp edge of the encounter. If not a single thread is fully penetrated, even a mere inch remains.
Separated by a thousand mountains. A mistake, a mistake! Difficult, difficult! Countless old fishermen have lost their fishing rods.

(By Hansong Cao) Chan Master Yanshou Zhijue of Huiri Yongming Temple in Hangzhou, the eleventh generation descendant of Dajian (Mahādarśana), and successor to Tiantai Shaokang, was visited by two monks. Because of these two monks' visit:
He then asked the head of the assembly, "Have you ever been here before? He replied, "I have. He asked again, "Has the second senior monk ever been here before?

He replied, "He has not. The Master said, "One has gained; one has lost. A short while later, an attendant asked, "I do not know for certain which of those two monks was the one who gained and which was the one who lost. The Master said, "Do you recognize these two?"
The monk said, "There is none. The Master said, "In the same pit, there is no different soil.
Qinghua Yan said, "Where things are laid out flat, one does not encounter the edge of the blade; where one tests a person, how could many words be used?
It is intolerable that these two monks, for no reason, involve their attendant and cause him distress. Tiandou Wei said, "The Yellow River has nine bends, yet it is not..."
If there is no source, even a *keng-nan* tree a thousand feet tall has no root.
The entire system established during the Yongming period would not have been possible were it not for its deep foundation and distant source. However, let us set aside the attendant for a moment.
At that time, when the two monks said, "We know the Master has seen Tiantai," how did you respond?
"Arriving or not arriving—either one gain or one loss. It is not arsenic, yet it is rock honey. With no eyes upon the tip of the tongue, how can one eat it?
Just as the attendant was about to inquire for the definitive meaning, do not blame those in the same pit for having no different soil;
before the lightning has been withdrawn, the thunderclap crashes. (Chijue Chong)
Huìrì was asked by a monk, "What is the essential meaning of Yongming? The Master said, "Add more incense. The monk said, "Thank you for the instruction, Master.
The Master said, "Be glad that there is no connection at all. The monk bowed. The Master then presented this verse:
"If you wish to know the essential meaning of Yongming, Look at the lake before the gate. When the sun shines, radiance arises; When the wind comes, waves are stirred."
Yuan'an said, "And Yun, do you all still see the Patriarch? He struck the ground with his staff and said, "If you wish to discern right from wrong, his face and features are present now.
Before the gate, the lake reflects his countenance like a mirror; facing him, he offers it up on a platter. This is indeed Yongming’s teaching, without a single word left out."
Verse: The wine is rich; one need not drink many cups.

(Xiangtan Yong) Like the sun facing ten thousand acres of blue waves, Like the wind blowing over water naturally forming ripples. To conceive a thought is already to be separated by the cliffs of Yuzhou.
Wherever touched, the wondrous and peerless merit is fully revealed. Wondrous and peerless merit—what more can be said? Tell of the lake’s radiance outside the gate.
"O Lord, within the Mirror of the Source, the myriad phenomena stand in dense array; under one sky of wind and moon, the Six Bridges divide.
(Pingyang Min) Huirui was asked by a monk: "The student has long been at Yongming; why is it that I do not understand the 'house style' of Yongming?
The Master said: "Understand it in the very place where you do not understand."
The house style of Yongming has no separate foundation; the staff carries forth two pieces of emptiness. Last night a wild ox gave birth to an elephant;
this morning the fire at the bottom of the sea glows a brilliant red.
(Pingxiang) Chan Master Zhifeng of Huayan Monastery on Wuyun Mountain in Hangzhou (a successor of Tiantai Shaokang) asked a monk: "Non-action..."
"Serving people. Why, then, is there this "difficulty of the golden lock"? The monk had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying:
"Precisely because it is non-active and without affairs. Luan Yuan said: "The old fellow Wuyun exhausted all his strength to cast a single hook; what a pity that he labored so in vain."
It was without merit. At the very end, he once again unfurled his silken line, yet remained in the realm of non-doubt.
Why did he not wait until the monk was speechless and strike him with thirty blows? Had he done so, it is possible that the monk might have suddenly turned his head at that moment.
Nevertheless, do not say that this monk alone failed Five Clouds; throughout all time and across the world, there have been many who have failed Five Clouds.
When Chan Master Yuan’an of Shangfang at Ruizhu Monastery in Wenzhou (a successor of Tiantai Zhiyao) first read the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he reached the passage:
"When knowledge and vision establish knowledge, this is the root of ignorance; when knowledge and vision have no [established] vision, this is nirvāṇa.
He then broke the phrasing and read it as: "Knowledge and vision establish. Knowledge is the root of ignorance. Knowledge and vision have no. Vision—this is nirvāṇa. At that time...
This has a point of realization that remains unchanging throughout one's life; at that time, he was called An Lengyan. He then spoke a verse, saying:
"It is not something carried from the mountain peak; how could it have been transmitted from Mount Kukkutapāda? Since antiquity, all sages and worthies have been like this."
"It is not that I am tailoring it for you today.
Yingshan Yun said: "Tell me, what is it that he has realized? Is there knowing-and-seeing, or is there no knowing-and-seeing?
Spring grasses are emerald green; spring waters are jade-green waves. As I see you off at Nanpu, how can I bear such grief? (Yanxi Wen)
A monk came forward to pay his respects to Chan Master Huiju of Longhua in Hangzhou (a successor of Shao of Tiantai). The Master said, "What an excellent question!
Ask it according to the Dharma. As the monk prepared to step forward, the Master said, "Again, you have missed the point."
Favor those who hasten to serve; shun those who are intimate. They must be both fierce and docile.
If one were a cub of the golden-maned lion, they would not come here to feign groans and sighs.

(Sixth Snow, Yin) The people of Qin devoured others like silkworms, plotting annexation; they needlessly forced Lord Han to strike the surging sands. To this day, the six states have returned to their rightful lord.
The Way. The Han palace established the custom of bowing to China.
(Zi Qinghao) Chan Master Shishu of Yanfeng in Fuzhou (successor of Tiantai Shaoshan). A monk asked: "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa heard [the Buddha] personally.
At the assembly at Yanfeng, who is it that hears? The Master said: "The questioner is no weakling."
Yingshan Yin said: "This monk’s question was much like holding a torch against the wind—first it burns one's own hand.
Yanfeng’s answer was just like a tavern-keeper selling wine who pours out the cup immediately. After a long silence, he added: "It makes all bystanders laugh to death."
Chan Master Qingxiang of the Nine-Bendings Guanyin Temple in Hangzhou (a successor of Tiantai Shaokong) was asked by a monk:
"In the midst of perilous and evil paths, what serves as the bridge and raft? The Master said: "This very thing serves as the bridge and raft. The monk asked: "What is this? The Master said:
"It strikes right through your nostrils."
Wherever the spring breeze blows, the hundred flowers bloom. Coming thus through the perilous and evil paths, if you wish to know the bridge and the ferry, it is for this reason:
the stone man and the wooden horse conceive in the night. (Sōngwon [Ŭisun]).
One day, when Master Ungju Doji (Dharma-lamp Qin’s successor) was at Hongzhou, Master Choryang said to him: "There is a person..."
A questioner asked, "What is the meaning of my coming from the West? The Master replied, "Neither East nor West.

The Librarian asked, "How do you understand this? The Master said, "Neither East nor West. The Librarian said, "Even if one understands it thus, how can that suffice? The Master said, "Daoqi, it is simply like this."
"Venerable Master, I do not yet understand your honorable intention. The Master replied, "That family already has its own descendants.

The Teacher (Xuefeng) suddenly realized the essential meaning and composed a verse: "Receiving beings and benefiting life—how exquisite! Yet a nephew is ultimately not filial. That family already has its own descendants;
In the future, they shall be used most appropriately."
His own descendants are already here; he has no attachment to his grandfather’s fields and gardens. In a single instant, his livelihood for this life is gone:
what he buys from the east, he sells in the west. (Da Hongen) Suddenly, with a forceful gesture, he points to east and west:
the moon is full over Cangwu, the waters fill the stream. At midnight, the jade-like person remains in a fragmentary dream.
Severing [all ties], leaning against the tower, I alone listen to the cry of a single cock.

Cuiyan Zhi said: "If it were not thus, how could one know that it is thus? Youke Yuan said: "This monk came directly from the hall;

had he waited until [the monk] said, 'Even the Noble Truths are not yet attained,' what levels or stages would there even be? It would have been well to strike him with the staff."
Striking the right sounding-block, he said: "For those standing here, let them take their place at the side. When the old man of Qingyuan arrives here, he will surely have a different way of life.

Xiangweng Yun said: "The mind-essence of Shaoshi was transmitted alone; the true command for patch-robed monks was upheld. When teacher and disciple met, all distinctions between ordinary and sage were forgotten.
It reached the point where the jeweled hall was sealed by clouds, yet its eight sides were transparently clear, as the sun shone upon the frost."
A thousand peaks of cold green in the void; therein lies nothing but the subtle and dense functioning of the spiritual mechanism.

This causes those who examine with superficiality and negligence to frequently fail to ascend the path of his verbal lineage. After all, how is it? Crimson maples shed their leaves as the river and sky break into dawn.
"A thousand-acre expanse of clear river, steered by an iron boat."—Dunyun said, "When a phoenix emerges into the azure heavens, it does not linger over the smoke and greenery of the paulownia trees;

when a crane flies across the blue void, how could it leave its tracks in a cold pool? Although this was a meeting of minds between father and son, there was still lacking that one word at the tip of the branch.

Guo said: "In a place where no one is present, they gaze at one another. It is certain that the old fellow Qingyuan will surely give rise to a heroic spirit.

Not sitting in the Hall of the Empty King over there, how could he be willing to till the fields toward the sun? (Touzi Qing)
Transcendent and solitary, it is difficult to peer at with the orthodox eye; far surpassing past and present, its kind is hard to equal.
Moss seals the ancient halls where no one waits; the moon locks the azure woods where the phoenix does not perch.
(Danxia Chun) Meeting beyond the kalpas, they walk on the other shore; amidst the clusters of numinous sprouts, the iron ox plows. The east wind scatters the thousand crags.
Snow. In the empty sky, cloudless, the solitary moon shines bright. (It becomes a withered tree.

yet if you examine it closely, how much difference is there? (Xueyan Qin)
Barefoot and clad in a straw raincoat, he crosses over distant peaks. When meeting him, one must strictly avoid speaking of the time of Vipaśyin.
He overturns the Terrace of the Qilin, exhausting all traces of effort; he smashes the water-lily flowers, and their reflections sink away. Vast, cold clouds enshroud the mountain summits;
the round, bright moon washes the heart of the waves. The Golden Ox does not eat ordinary grass; at dawn it enters the vast ocean, leaving no place to be sought. (By Baiyu Si)
When people are silent, incense fades, and the scene is desolate. The golden gates are not locked as the night stretches on.
The moon fills the vermilion steps with the colors of a thousand peaks; robes and caps roll in as ten thousand nations pay court.

(By Tianyu Bao) The frost turns the reeds yellow and the moon makes the autumn stream azure. Amidst the water’s lotuses, travelers ply their boats. Spring colors vex the heart, leaving one unable to sleep.
Attained. Returning, the wild geese listen to the high tower. (Nan’an Yi) The crane soars into the Milky Way;
the egret emerges from the reed thicket. There is no fixed order, utterly free from nets and cages. Where the Moon Hall shines, its dignity is profound;
who within the secular world could ever intrude upon it in haste? (Zundao Qi)
Grass obscures the distant steps, cutting off the sound of the imperial carriage. Amidst clouds and trees, the deep green halls are cold.
The bright moon comes of its own accord and departs of its own accord; there is no one left to lean against the jade balustrade.
(Yingzhang Jie) Qingyuan asked Stonehead, "How long has it been since you left the mountain pass? The Master said, "I indeed know you."
"Before long you will leave Caoxi. He replied, "Xiqian did not come from Caoxi. The Master said, "I also know where you are going.
He replied, "Since the Master is such a great person, please do not speak so hastily. The Master then ceased speaking.
A wooden man comes to ask the way to the azure heavens; The stone woman, advanced in years, seems not to hear. Hand in hand they walk together back to their old country;
The evening mountains loom high, locked in heavy clouds. (Danxia Chun) Turning my head, the road to Peach Blossom Spring is no more;
I cannot bear to hold her sleeve as the evening clouds grow dim. The sound of the spring flows deep, coming from the void.

Qingyuan asked Shitou, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Caoxi. The Master raised his whisk and said, "Is there such a thing as this at Caoxi?
He replied, "Not only at Caoxi; even in the Western Heaven, it does not exist. The Master said, "You must not..."
"Have you been to the Western Heaven? He replied, "If I have been there, then I would have it. The Master said, "That will not do; speak further.

He replied, "The Master should also say at least half of it; do not rely entirely on this student. The Master said, "I am not unwilling to tell you, but I fear that in the future there will be no one to uphold it."
Qianhui Yue said: "The old fellow of Qingyuan was adept at striking down soaring phoenixes and skilled at capturing fierce dragons from the bottom of the sea.
Looking closely, he may truly be called a master of a thousand ages. Although Shitou possessed extraordinary strategies, alas, he was ensnared by this old fellow.
Consequently, his descendants of later generations were all brought under his net. Thus it is said:
"Now, is there anyone who can emerge [from this]? After a long silence, he said: "When meeting people, do not err in your speech.
White clouds conceal the jade phoenix; the red sun shines upon the desolate. Where the stars cluster in dimness, the Impartial One presides over the nine heavens."

(Touzi Qing) We meet by the banks of the Jin River; we go hand in hand up to the wine tower. When the song and laughter have ended at the moon’s edge, we turn our heads and board a small boat. (Duan’an Yan)
Who is at the western painted tower? Meeting you, our laughter and talk are low. When we reach home, the spring colors are late;
the flowers fall as the partridges cry.
(By Tuan’an Yi) Qingyuan asked Shitou, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Caoxi. The Master said, "What have you brought with you?"
He said, "Even before reaching Caoxi, it was not lost. The Master asked, "If that is how you apply it, what would you do upon reaching Caoxi?
He replied, "If I had not reached Caoxi, how could I have known it was not lost?"
Lingyan Chu held up his staff and said, "The 'Shang Daren' (The Master of the Upper Realm) knows propriety. You, little students, tell me:

where does the crucial point lie? He struck the ground once and said, "From this moment on, one will not return; yet if one returns, it can be attained. Amidst the misty scenery of the Five Lakes, who could vie for it?"
Lost and not lost—on the road to Caoqi, the travelers are dense. Rain beats down and wind blows, stirring the traveler’s sorrows.

On both banks of the peach blossoms, there are the tracks of oxen; they cross the small bridge, and the returning man finds ease. After the rain has passed over the village ahead, the slanting sun emerges.
At the roadside inn, the wind stirs the bamboo branches, cold; his disheveled green robe remains soaked as ever. (Nan’an Yi)
Regarding the question asked by Qingyuan to the Monk: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? the Master said: "What is the price of rice in Luling?
Boshan Lai commented: "The price of rice, high or low, reflects the verdant hues of Huancui amidst its wondrous peaks; it swallows and spits out Luling, refining the moon."
Flowers bloom upon the jade trees; one must know that the Great Function is boundless and responds whenever there is a resonance.

If one were to discuss the Buddha-dharma at the base of Qingyuan, even sixty kalpas across three lifetimes would not have been enough to dream of it. Cuiyan Zhe said: "Do you recognize where the old fellow Qingyuan stands?
One sees only the imperial wind forming a single expanse; one knows not where the boundaries of territories lie."
The three-eyed tortoise is crimson; the auspicious qilin has a single sharp horn. As it soars through the clouds, evening rain arises; the mountain stream moon brightens the night curtain.
(Fachang Yu) The price of rice in Luling is sharper and fresher than ever; who could discuss it without their lips hanging down? Boundless pure winds arise within the gate.
[Verse by Baiyun Yuan] Outside, cease comparing degrees of intimacy as if measuring pints and pecks.

A grain. Green phoenix trees where ancient phoenixes have grown old. (Yangshan Qin) Since antiquity, Luling has been Jizhou;
to this day, no one can match its price for rice. The green mountains and blue waters remain as they were before;
with the autumn wind, the yellow leaves fall once more. (Fotu Xun)
Piercing through the azure void, pines reach a thousand feet; cutting off the red dust, a stream flows through one valley.
Satiated with food and sleeping soundly, no person may enter; the sun rises in the east and sinks again in the west.

Qingyuan sent a letter to National Teacher Shitou, instructing him to deliver it to National Teacher Huairang of Nanyue, and further entrusting him with these words:
"When you return, I have a small adze for you to use while dwelling in the mountains. When Shitou arrived at Nanyue, before even presenting the letter, he asked: "No—"
"Yearning for the various sages, yet not valuing one's own numinous spirit—what do you think of this? Yuezhou said, "Your question, my son, is too high;
why not ask about what is below? Baotou said, "I would rather suffer in the depths of saṃsāra for eternal kalpas than seek liberation from the various sages."
He then returned. The Master said, "Why have you come back so quickly? Did your letter reach? Daitō replied, "The letter did not pass through, nor did the message reach.
On the day I departed, I was granted by the Master the promise of a 'pickaxe'; I request it now.
The Master lowered one foot, and Daitō immediately prostrated himself.
Xuansha Shibei said: "The great and small Stoneheads were pushed over by Nanyue; to this day they cannot be raised. Cui峰 Xian said:

Cuiyan Zhi said: "When Master Si extended his feet and Shitou prostrated, he simply could not find an axe.

Why then does he hang down one foot? Since he does not seek liberation from the various sages, how [can he attain it]?"
He then prostrated himself. Then, brushing the corner of his sleeve, he said: "Look, look! The adze chops the heavens and earth into pieces, turning them into an eight-cornered grindstone;
it has already chased down the golden crow and the jade hare. Where would the blind turtle and the lame tortoise know of this? Shending Kui said:
"To pass through nine layers of ice on a blade of ice, and to pick up one's whole body upon the edge of a sword—this is truly not bad."

[The Master] struck [him] with his hand. I further questioned Shitou: "Where is this dull axe kept? When you attend court in the morning and seek instruction in the evening, carrying water and hauling firewood, what else do you use?
Unjustly, he burdened Qingyuan with one extra foot; even until now, it cannot be retracted.
He himself was crushed beneath it; even until now, he cannot rise.

The succession of the bone-lineage has been passed down without self-deception; whenever he encounters the field, he is accustomed to winning the silken trophy.
He topples the sturdy fortresses and solid ranks all at once, winning a golden tally with its ancient seal, truly marvelous.

The monk asked again, "I beg the Master for one or two recent sayings. The Master said, "Come forward."
"Come forward. The monk stepped forward. The Master said, "Take this clearly to heart:
when foul water is poured over one's head, one still complains it is too little; when shackles and manacles are added, one never tires of the excess.

The Second Generation under Dajian (Mazu):
Master Xiqian Shitou of Wujie in Hengzhou (Dharma heir of Qingyuan Xingsi).
Once, because Qingyuan asked, "Someone says there is news from Lingnan," the Master said, "There is someone who does not say there is news from Lingnan. Qingyuan said, "If..."
"From where do such great and small scriptural collections come? The Master said, "They all come from here.
"If there is news, it is too much of a burden; if there is no news, it is utterly lost. From this, the great and small scriptural collections emerge;
scattering sand and scattering earth, there is no end to it. Sweet as honey, bitter as gall, bright as the sun, black as lacquer—smash it to pieces!
A wild fox den for a thousand years; ditches filled and ravines blocked, no one recognizes it.
(Yuánwù Qín) No one from home or state sends a letter; traveler, why do you linger so bitterly on your journey?
The spring breeze blows into the famous garden; boundless famous flowers bloom overnight. (Wúyì Lái)

Who can support the depths of the Milky Way? (Ning of Lishan) A star’s flame, hair-tip in size, comes rushing at one's head.
Grasping an axe and hatchet crosswise, one cannot split it open. It stirs up the gods of China. (Mao Tou)
Measuring the depths, it shines uniquely deep into the ancient crags at nightfall.
(Zongkai Yuan) Traversing a thousand miles to seek a solitary trace—only when meeting face-to-face does one see the true function of the occasion.
Yet I envy the arrival of spring in Peach Blossom Spring, where the flowing waters of the stream are filled with red fallen petals. (Langshan Yu)
Because of this, Shitou was questioned by Yaoshan: "I, Wuye, have a rough knowledge of the Three Vehicles and the Twelve Divisions of the Teaching.
I have heard that in the South they point directly to the human mind for the realization of Buddhahood through seeing one's nature, yet I truly do not understand it clearly.
The Master said: "It cannot be so, nor can it not be so; neither 'so' nor 'not so'—neither of these is acceptable. What will you do?"
Shanshan was at a loss for words. He next went to visit Mazu and again posed his former question. Mazu said, "Sometimes I instruct them to raise their eyebrows and blink;
sometimes I do not instruct them to raise their eyebrows and blink. Sometimes those who raise their eyebrows and blink are right;
sometimes those who raise their eyebrows and blink are not right. What do you say to this? At these words, Shanshan attained realization.
Upon realizing this, he prostrated himself. The Patriarch asked, "What principle have you seen that you prostrate yourself?
Shanshan replied, "When I was with Shitou, it was like a mosquito on an iron ox. The Patriarch said, "Since you have realized this, protect and maintain it well."
Fayun Xiu said: "Stonehead’s 'iron hammer with no hole' is truly excellent; it is almost as if he could not entrust [the Dharma] to anyone.
Although Yaoshan went west of the Yangtze River and attained enlightenment, alas, he still suffered a fall on level ground. What support or assistance can there be for him?"

Wuzu Yan said: "When I was among the assembly, I heard you brothers discussing how 'pointing directly to the mind as Buddha' is not permissible, and 'not pointing directly to the mind as Buddha' is also not permissible.
If you speak in such a manner, how can you dare to call yourselves Chan practitioners?
You do not realize that the ancients were both civil and martial, possessing both strategy and tactics. I wish for you all to understand my own perspective."
Everyone knows this: one sees only the surging waves, but does not see the dragon palace within the sea. Daowei Zhi said, "What are you talking about?
When he was at Shitou, it was like a mosquito on an iron ox; even now, how has he ever managed to let anything out?"
Guishan Lingyou said: "The first arrow is still tolerable; the second arrow pierces the person deeply. Youshan added:
"Even if one were to attain enlightenment in this manner, it would still fall into the 'second moon' (a mere semblance). Jingshan Daowu said: "What a fine point of discourse! Who can bring it forth?"
"Though he attained ten parts, I did not yet dare grant him full approval. Xiaoyan Bao said: "Mazu should not have let him off then.
Had he waited for him to prostrate, he could have given him his rightful fodder, ensuring that even an iron ox would break into a sweat all over its body before it was done.
Yishi Yuan said: "At that time, when Shitou was about to ask, why did Mazu not strike him immediately upon the sound of his voice?"

It is not merely a matter of sweeping away the old nests and tracks; it is to directly manifest the wind-and-flow elegance of the teaching itself. If you have not yet attained this, you must first seek understanding within the "tangled vines" of Shitou and Mazu.

If you cannot grasp it at all, you are being far too arbitrary. How could a rustic old man know the vastness of heaven and earth? Even if you were to count on to eighty or ninety, it would still be of no avail.

news from the Central Plains has been received. I have ceased brandishing the three-foot sword; I shall no longer ply the single bow.

who can divide the bright moon between the upper and lower ponds? (Gao Feng Miao)
The stone wall is not mud; the stone jar is not a hairpin. Smash the rhombus-patterned mirror, and there is no image left to apply.

Now, we must walk hand in hand. One must first act thus; only then can one understand how not to act thus. Thereafter, there is no further connection. Do you understand this thoroughly?
In my youth, I once broke through the ranks of dragons and snakes; now in my decrepitude, I listen to the songs of a child.
The young maiden with her hair in two braids and the old woman with snow-white hair; long separated from their home, they suffer in bitter longing.
