how could they hope to ride the wind for ten thousand *li* in pursuit?

(The Dragon of the Emperor). Shitou addressed the assembly: "Words and activities have no connection [to the truth]. Yaoshan stepped forward and said, "It must even reach the point of being beyond words."
Regarding verbal and physical activity, they likewise do not intersect. The Master said, "In my place, a needle cannot pierce it.
Shanshan said, "In my place, it is like planting flowers upon a rock."
Lingyan said, "These two great elders are like mosquitoes trying to bore into a slab of green stone;
they cannot penetrate it at all, which only makes people laugh. Nevertheless, while they exerted themselves for the sake of the assembly, the disaster arose from their own private quarters."
Dunyun said, "Dingyun," and the two great elders spoke thus. Was this to display their wondrous skills and compete for wealth?
Or was it to carve out lands and divide the fiefs? Or did they each possess some other superior quality? Try and say so!
If you can speak it, I grant that you breathe from the same nostrils as the Patriarchs. If you cannot speak it, do not let your idle learning obscure the Patriarchs.
To take oneself as the teacher: at the bottom of the well, the clay ox roars at the moon; amidst the clouds, the wooden horse whinnies in the wind.

Seizing hold of heaven and earth, who can distinguish north, south, east, or west? Straight within the crooked, crooked within the straight; where evenness is required yet not achieved, rely on the scale and the ruler. (Yuánwù Qín)
A wooden man holds a board, striking it amidst the clouds; a stone woman holds a flute, blowing it from the bottom of the well.
One might think they share the beauty of the bright moon equally, yet who knew it would ultimately fall into a heap of right and wrong?
(Only the towering peaks remain. There is this [entanglement] like an iron ox upon a needle; one does not know when the awl will finally cease. Since first drinking from the Western River...
Later, he smiled emptily as he planted flowers before Shitou.
(Huatang Yan) Chan Master Weiyen of Yaoshan in Dingshou, the third generation under Dajian (Huineng), who propagated the Way (succeeding Shitou Xiqian): Initially, he served Mazu for three years.
One day, the Patriarch asked him, "What is your realization these days? The Master replied, "The skin and flesh have fallen away entirely;
there remains only the single reality. The Patriarch said, "What you have attained may truly be called 'harmonizing with the essence of the mind' and 'extending it to the four limbs.
Since this is so, take three strips of bamboo to bind your belly and go dwell in the mountains wherever you please."
The Master said, "Who am I that I dare say I dwell on the mountain? The Patriarch said, "Not so.
There has never been one who acts constantly without dwelling, nor one who dwells constantly without acting. To seek benefit is to find no benefit; to seek to act is to find nothing to do."
"You should prepare a vessel for crossing over; do not remain here long.

The meeting between teacher and disciple is no light matter, yet once the skin and flesh are cast off, they become estranged. Bound together by three strands of rattan, it has become a mere subject of idle talk;
even until now, people have mistakenly fixed upon the weight of the scale."
One day, Yaoshan was sitting on a rock. Shitou asked him, "What are you doing here? The Master replied, "I am doing nothing. Shitou said, "If that is so, then you are sitting idly.

The Master said, "To sit idly is itself an act. Shitou asked, "You say you do nothing; what is it that you do not do? The Master replied, "Even the thousand sages do not know it. Shitou then praised him with a verse: Not doing anything at all— This is the true Way.

The ten thousand things are naturally so; There is no need for cultivation. If you can understand this, You will see the Buddhas of the three times. If you do not understand, You will fall into the pit of birth and death.
It is said: "From the beginning we have lived together, yet I do not know your name; you proceed spontaneously, simply as you go.
Even the sages of antiquity could not recognize you; how could ordinary people in their haste possibly name you?"
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said: "Yaoshan’s dream-telling-dreams are layered upon layers. Miaoxi Gao said: "The object is its true value;
the coin is a full hundred. Yunsong Pin said: "Yaoshan’s eyes look out over the four seas; atop his brow-ridge are one hundred and eight thousand [miles].
Shitou’s feet tread upon the Yellow River; from between his fingers, light radiates as the Ocean-Seal Samādhi. When it comes to pushing..."
Pressed to the limit, he simply said, "I do not know. Since he does not know, after all, what is it that he spontaneously carries along as he walks?
Then, brandishing his whisk, he said: "Happening upon him by chance, I did not expect to see these twin horns; no wonder Moshan called him an ox."

When the profound mystery reaches its ultimate limit, one is naturally free and detached. If you say there are eighteen thousand miles between us, the moon reflects upon the clear river, yet the fish do not see it;
why must the angler cast his trap once more? (Danxia Chun) Moving along with the flow, I am unaware of my name.
Cast a light glance and listen. That greenish-blue upon the water is, after all, nothing but duckweed.

(5th Patriarch Yuan) He cast off the fetters of the Buddhas and patriarchs; vast and open beyond the lines of measurement. Not performing even a single act, he moves with sovereign ease in all directions.
When the ancient mirror faces the stand, it clearly discerns coming and going; when the golden hammer casts its shadow, the iron tree blooms. Thus they proceed together, following the natural course.
One cannot accompany it. Dharma-clouds arise as wind and thunder wherever they go (Yuánwù Qín).
With every step the moon grows cold and the wind rises high; with every stride the mountains grow frigid and the waters deepen. When meeting people, one bares one’s liver and reveals one’s gall;
when encountering righteousness, one cleaves open one’s belly and gouges out one’s heart (Xiètáng Yuǎn).
Sitting at ease or walking idly, a mindless cloud drifts across the mountain ridge. When both the object and its reflection are forgotten, the person does not stand;
from the noon hour, one strikes the third watch.
(Xueyan Qin) Meeting a youth with bifurcated hair whose name is unknown, he blows his iron flute as he walks beyond the ridges. Turning his head, he is suddenly startled by the vast blue sea.
Exhausted. The jade-luan bird flies up; the five clouds level out.
(By Lingting Ting) For a long time, Yaoshan did not ascend the seat. The head monk said, "The assembly has long been longing for the Master’s Dharma instruction.

The Master replied, "Strike the bell! As soon as the assembly had gathered, the Master immediately descended from the seat and returned to his quarters. The head monk followed him and asked, "Master..."
"Just now you promised to preach the Dharma for the great assembly; why then do you not utter a single word?
The Master said, "The sutras have masters of the sutras, and the treatises have masters of the treatises. How can one blame this old monk?"
Langye Jue said: "When Yaoshan descended from his seat, it was not without reason for doubt;

yet when the monastery director pressed him, he lost one of his eyes. Cuiyan Zhi said: "When Yaoshan descended from his seat, the monastery director initially resented that he did not preach the Dharma;
this can be called 'misleading the three armies. Tiantong Jie said: "Cuiyan possessed only a single eye; he truly did not..."
Zhi knew that Yaoshan had returned to his quarters; this was truly "exhausting the three armies. Xuedou Xian said, "What a pity for the old fellow Yaoshan!
He has taken a tumble on level ground, such that no one in the entire world can help him up. Jianfu Huai said:
"Does Yaoshan see the attendant? Does the attendant see Yaoshan? Thirty years hence, should you encounter a master of composition, do not err in your citation.
Wuzu Yan said, "Although he uses himself as a measure for others, how can he avoid revealing his own thievery?
Do you all wish to recognize Yaoshan? He stands leaning against a pine tree, idly holding a scripture, and smilingly asks the guest."
"From where did he come? Kaifu Ning said: "Yaoshan was careful at the beginning and guarded against the end; his Buddha-eye is difficult to fathom.
The Abbot encountered him on a narrow path and, quite casually, let the opportunity slip away. Jingshan Guangzhao, while descending from the seat, said: "There is no small amount of entanglement.
As for saying 'How can one blame the old monk?'—it makes people laugh to death! Xuedou Chong said: "Before the Name of Awesome Sound (Vipaśyin)..."
Beyond the kalpas, who would be willing to join hands and return together? At the crossroads, how many people actually step upon the gold when it is cast down?
I dare ask the assembly: tell me, did Yaoshan ever speak [this], or did he not? If you say he spoke it, you slander Yaoshan;
if you say he did not speak it, you betray Yaoshan. Tell me, ultimately, where does he stand for the sake of others? Liang.
Jiuyun said: "One must know that beyond the clouds, atop a thousand peaks, there is another numinous pine, cold with dew. Zhongfeng Ben said:
"When Yaoshan did not ascend the hall for a long time and failed to utter a single word before the assembly, everyone thought, 'I thought so, I thought so.
Yet at the end, he said, 'The sutras have masters of the sutras; the treatises have masters of the treatises. Ah, it turns out, it turns out! Boshan Lai said: "To receive [the guest]..."
Sentient beings abandon their true nature; being indifferent becomes a burden. When giving and taking provoke one another, do not find it strange.

Furthermore, who would have known that those seeking to hear would instead encounter the cries of chaotic crickets, or that a pristine quality would be troubled by ornate colors? Once pressed by the Abbot, they were reduced to a hundred fragments.
After Gu Nanshan finished citing the words of Cuiyan and Mian, he said: "Although these two elders exerted every effort to support [the Dharma], they were still..."
They possess but a single eye, yet they fail to realize that at Yaoshan’s monastery, one person directs the strategy from within the tent, while another secures victory a thousand miles away.
Nevertheless, Yaoshan only knew how to go; he did not know how to come.
If it were I, upon returning to the abbot’s quarters and seeing the monastery steward asking such a question, I would simply say: "The subsequent text is long; it shall be entrusted to a future day."

Zifu previously said: "Yaoshan finally returned to his quarters; he seemed like a good man, yet as soon as he was lightly pinched by him, he immediately forgot what came before and lost track of what followed. Falinyin said: "Zifu was mistaken in using such terminology."
Little did they know that Yaoshan had already returned to his quarters; they had long since lost what was behind them and forgotten what was before them. After a long silence, he said:
"It seemed like a melody just as it was becoming worth hearing, but was blown by the wind into another tune."
The family law is simple and strict; it is neither two nor three. When the moon comes, it is bright and limpid; when clouds recede from the water, the dew chills the crags.

The true mechanism is attained of itself; who can participate in this wondrous place? This is not merely after Mañjuśrī strikes the gavel; even so, for a thousand ages, Gautama shall remain in his rightful place of honor.
(Tiantong Juo II) A foolish child’s deliberate coin to stop his crying; a fine steed chasing the wind, looking back at its shadow as it strikes the whip. Clouds sweep across the vast sky;
the moon-nesting crane—its cold clarity piercing to the bone, unable to sleep.
A single bright pearl is difficult to price; if one is not a true connoisseur, it is better to cast it away in secret. It is laughable that Yaoshan exerted his efforts in vain;
when the water is clear, the fish appears, yet they do not swallow the hook.
(Cishou Shen) The shop is wide open—do you see it? Why is there more looking at the crowd than buyers? A perfectly polished blade, sharp as a hair.
A sword. It is nothing more than a shuttle on the wall of a potter’s kiln.
(Wuzu Fan) The bell tolls and the assembly gathers at the abbot’s quarters. What a pity to kill the person who has come to request the Dharma. Every dharma is originally not a single dharma;
if you say there is no dharma, then dharmas will entangle your body. (Xiangchuan Hong)
Mountains accumulate within the crevices of the eyebrows; lion cubs are hidden inside the nostrils.
With infinite intent toward the south, north, east, and west—who among these can truly know this mind?
(Gao Feng Miao) A chilling cold wind blows from all eight directions; a single bright sun reflects upon the frosty flowers. In the deep forest, strange herbs loathe the winter.
Cold. Only these courtyard plum blossoms find delight in their leisurely bloom.
(Wei Cen Yin) Since ancient times, the Lady Chang’e has never painted her brows; fools needlessly face her, asking about the remnants of rouge.
She is splashed with foul water again and again, yet she still complains that no rouge is applied. (Yunzhong Feng)
Her topknot binds black clouds, too weary to wear flowers; her short skirt and plain garments are worn as she follows her whim.
The world prizes clever adornment, but who would believe that the true Way flows from one’s own house?
(Sōng-ām Jeong) One peak locks another peak; the path enters Peach Blossom Spring until its momentum is exhausted. Having trodden it all and returned, there is nothing to be found.
The cave entrance is sealed by white clouds. (Falin’s voice) When a monk asked Yaoshan, "What is the supreme treasure within the Way?
the Master said, "Do not be sycophantic. The monk asked, "How is it when one is not sycophantic?
The Master said, "It cannot be exchanged even for an entire kingdom."
Straight as a bowstring, bright as jade; revealing one’s gall and pouring out one’s heart without any detour or crookedness.
Even if the ground were covered in gold, it could not be exchanged for this. It cannot be exchanged. A Persian from the South Sea with a face like ink.
(Fóxìng Tàiyǎn) A hundred thousand green bamboo poles outside the door; three or two plum trees in the courtyard. When guests arrive, do not say you are poor and have nothing to offer.
Wait. How many families are there within the walls of the Pure and Tranquil Gate?
(The Integrity of Cold Pines) Yaoshan asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Hunan.
The Master said, "Is the water in Lake Dongting full yet? The monk said, "It is not. The Master said, "After so much rain, why is it not full?"
Yunyan Cheng, acting on behalf of the monk, said: "It is profoundly still. Dowu Zhi offered an alternative response:
"It is full. Dongshan Jia said: "In what kalpa has it ever increased or decreased? Yunmen Wenyan said: "It is right here."
While Yaoshan was sitting, a monk asked, "What are you pondering so intently? The Master said, "I am pondering that which is not to be pondered.
The monk asked, "How can that which is not to be pondered be pondered? The Master said, "It is not pondering."
Staring blankly, he ponders; there is nothing to be pondered. In the state where there is nothing to be pondered, true pondering occurs.
At the head of Mount Dayu, he meets the Sixth Patriarch; at the inn of Mount Ao, he sees Master Zeng.
(Wuzu Fan) With robes hanging down in dignified ease, what is there to do? Mountains and rivers are unified in a time of Great Peace. Beyond the curtain of night-brightness, the spring breeze blows.
Rising, he lay drunk upon his dragon bed, unaware of anything. (This is the constant cultivation of equanimity.
Youshan asked a monk, "How old are you? The monk replied, "Seventy-two. The Master said, "Is that seventy-two years?
The monk said, "Yes. The Master then struck him.
Caoshan Chang said: "The first arrow is still tolerable; the second arrow pierces the person deeply. At that time, a monk asked:
"How can one avoid this blow? Caoshan said: "When the imperial decree has already been issued, the feudal lords must yield the way."
One day, because Zun Bunan was bathing the Buddha, Yaoshan said, "This one you are bathing from—you can bathe that one as well?
Zun replied, "Bring me that one! The Master then desisted.
Changqing Ling said, "A false dharma is difficult to support. Baoci Su then remarked, "When Changqing spoke thus, was he acting as a guest or as a host?
Among the assembly, this is called 'the words for bathing the Buddha,' and it is also called 'a dual-layered statement. Is it entirely excellent, or is it not entirely excellent?"
Huanglong Nan said: "These two venerable masters, one coming out and one entering in—victory and defeat have not yet been seen.
Thirty years hence, do not err in citing them. Zhaojue Qin said: "Yaoshan’s question was darkly separated by a heavy barrier;
Old Zun’s answer struck both at once with a single blow. One must not merely guard this single path. If someone asks Chongning, 'Can one still bathe [in the Way]? "
"Is it so? he asked, picking up his ladle and saying to him, "What is it like? Tiantong Hua said:
"If Zun Puna had been a true man at that time, when the master asked, 'Can you bathe that [other] one? he would have picked up the ladle and hurled it straight at his face.
Nevertheless, even so, he could not be accused of wronging Yaoshan. Why? Because if you do not enter the tiger's den, how can you seize the tiger's cub?"

Tianbao Shu said: "If I, this old monk, had seen Yaoshan speak in such a manner at that time, I would have scooped up some water and poured it over his head, causing him to melt away like ice dissolving. Qingshan Xiu said: "Yaoshan provided a lateral path to guide beginners;
Puna (Bunna) acted with the courage of one who takes responsibility for the Dharma, and with a single pressure, he finished the matter. If I were Yaoshan..."
Waiting for him to say, "Bring that one here," he snatched the ladle and gave him a scoop right over the head. Why?
Because the water of samādhi is full to the brim; it bathes this stainless person.
Affectionately pouring foul water over one’s head, it draws forth a clear breeze to console the solitude.
Boundless distant mountains cannot be captured in a painting; the lofty pines and tall bamboos stand cold and sparse.
(Tudu Ce) One rain passes, another sun shines; the eyes of the silkworms have opened, and the mulberry buds are green. The magpie calls from the treetop, not yet weary.
It has ended. The hundred-tongued bird and the yellow-black magpie sing together.

(Lan’an Shu) Cherishing the flowers, I rise early to sit in the spring breeze; there is yet another who comes first to dally with the green and red. Hand in hand we go together beneath the blossoms to become drunk;
we do not know how many layers of clouds and moon shadows lie before us. (Meng’an Lü)
A monk once asked Yaoshan, "My own matter is not yet clear; I beg the Master for instruction.

The Master remained silent for a long while and then said, "It would not be difficult for me to speak a single word for you right now, but it would still leave something to be desired; one ought to see it immediately upon hearing it."
If one were to deliberate further, it would instead become my own fault; it is better, then, for each of us to simply keep our mouths shut to avoid implicating one another.

Yongning Ding said: "Yaoshan was merely provoked by this monk; he brought forth all at once his inexhaustible treasure trove of pearls and rare jewels, yet he did not realize that these were nothing more than a fan for the month of December."
A monk once asked Yaoshan, "I have a doubt; I ask the Master to resolve it for me. The Master said, "Come back in the evening and I will resolve it for you.
When the evening assembly gathered, the Master said, "Where is the senior monk who wanted his doubts resolved today? The monk stepped forward from the assembly.
As the Master descended from his seat, he seized him and said, "Everyone! This monk has a doubt," and then gave him a shove. He then returned to his quarters.
He returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Baoci then questioned him, saying: "Tell me, did you resolve his doubt for him, or not? Cuiyan Zhi said:
"To resolve a doubt in such a manner is to add mud upon the earth. Nevertheless, one must not fail the legacy of Yaoshan. Yunju said: [The same].
Yuan said: "The Great and Small Yaoshans were both exposed by this monk. Yuan’an Yu said: "It is nectar, it is poison;
a sword that kills, a blade that gives life. Duchu Wu said: "To seize an elephant, he employs his full strength;
to seize a hare, he likewise employs his full strength. Yaoshan the old fellow was certainly so, but if one wishes to slaughter dragons and slay sea-monsters, he still falls short."
Presented:
Jade medicine and golden branches vie with one another for beauty. A fair lady leans them askew at the edge of her cloud-like tresses.
Alas, not meeting one who understands her worth, she merely sighs in silence as the moon fills the heavens. (Zongmu’s Response)
Yaoshan wrote the character for "Buddha" and asked Daowu, "What character is this? Daowu replied, "The character for Buddha. The Master said, "A talkative fellow!

Yaoshan’s question here is truly worthy of lamentation; the simultaneous resonance of the peck and the hatch is not easily praised. To ask about the Buddha, one must know how to manifest the wondrous.
The Essential Meaning: For the most part, it is because of this that one perceives empty flowers.
(Tingshou Hui) Yaoshan held up a written character for "Buddha" in his hand and asked him, "What do you intend by this? To open his mind, he simply used the character for "Buddha" as his reply;
originally, he had already maintained the five precepts. (Hengchuan Gong)
During a night assembly, Yaoshan did not light the lamp. He gave this instruction, saying: "I have a phrase;
I will tell it to you when a horned ox gives birth to a calf. At that time, a monk said, "The horned ox has given birth to a calf;
it is only that you, Master, do not speak. The Master said, "Bring me a lamp. The monk then withdrew his body and entered the assembly.
Dongshan Jia said, "This monk understands; he simply refuses to prostrate. Qingliang Qian said, "At that time, do not ask for the lamp;
instead, ask him about the bull and the cow. Furthermore, I provide this on his behalf: 'They are twins.'"
Cuiyan Zhi said: "I am not like that. It is a 'special ox' giving birth to a calf; I will not tell you. Why is this so?
If I were to tell you, where else would there be Master Wáng? Fushan Yuan said: "I have a phrase;
I shall speak it when a person without a tongue asks for it. Touzi Qing said: "Tell me, where exactly is this [phrase]?"
As for the principle underlying this monk: if he can explain it, he may clear his own grievance; if he cannot, he will instead be deceived by Yaoshan. Zhaojue Qin said:
"Yaoshan’s casting of the line was intended for the *kūn* and *jing* (the great sea monsters). This monk swallowed the hook and surged over the waves with a thousand fathoms of momentum.
Dongshan’s eye was correct; from a thousand miles away, they shared the same wind. Fadeleng reorganized the banners and flags and readied them once more."
"Armor! But I, this mountain monk, am not like that. There is a single phrase that, prior to the time of Wei-yin, I have already spoken to all people.
If someone asks whether it accords with the bright side or the dark side, I simply tell them: 'When the dragon gets water, his spirit and vigor increase.'"
When a tiger encounters mountain terrain, its majestic ferocity increases. Huanglong Zhen said, "It is like a person writing characters in the dark;
though the characters do not form a complete text, their brilliance is already manifest. Since the brilliance is manifest, why does one not see it when a lamp is lit?
It is not said that 'the thief is a petty person whose cleverness exceeds that of a gentleman'? Yunju Zhuang said, "Big or small, Yaoshan leaves the head and drags the tail."
These people of the Saṃgha know only how to grasp at the moon, yet they fail to perceive the depth of the water. Great assembly, it is like a wild ox giving birth to a calf!
I, this mountain monk, tell you: bring me a single phrase as an answer.
A special ox has given birth to a son; they are quite familiar with one another. Both eyes are a deep crimson, like blue. Though one holds a torch to search for them, no trace can be found.
Everyone, let us all go together to investigate at once. (Longmen Yuan) The General of the Great Tree does not establish merit;
why must his lofty name be listed on the Cloud Terrace? How could it be that he flees from the throne after his task is accomplished?
Praise! Alas for Han Gaozu’s execution of Huaiyin!
(Lingtíng Tǐng) Strong he may be, yet he yields; soft he may be, yet he is firm. Two colors, one tally—snow upon snow.
(Zhìzhōng Shèn) Casting a hook into the four seas to catch the fierce dragon, the lame turtle vies for the lead, intending to reveal its tracks. Yet the thousand-fathom line remains uncast.
Withdrawn. Mountain after mountain remains shrouded by evening clouds.
(The Sound of the Pine String) *Zongjian Faling*, Volume 55; *Zongjian Faling*, Volume 56.
*Jiuyuntang*: Compiled by the Third Generation of Dajian (Huineng), Yashan was reading a scripture.
A monk asked, "Master, you usually do not permit people to read scriptures; why then [do you do so now]?"
[The monk] looked at it himself. The Master said, "I was merely trying to cover my eyes. [The monk] asked, "Can I learn from you, Master?
The Master said, "If you look, even ox-hide will be pierced."
Changqing Ling said, "What fault is there in the eye? Baoci Su then said, "Tell me, does Changqing understand Yaoshan’s meaning, or does he not understand Yaoshan’s meaning?
Xuedou Zong said, "The true mind is unmoving; the ocean of teachings is clear and bright.
When function is attained as suchness, the heavens of principle blaze forth. At this very moment, tell me: is it the scripture, or is it the eye? If you [can] toward this..."
If you see through this thoroughly, there is no further need to follow the tracks of words or pursue delusions at the expense of the truth.
If this is not yet the case, it may still be possible to pierce through an ox-hide; but how many people know that skulls lie scattered all over the ground? Qianhui Yue said:
"Although the old man Yaoshan possessed eyes that surpassed the crowd, he could not avoid following the same ruts as others. At that time, he merely picked up his own head."
He struck him across the face. This ensured that the monk’s lingering doubts were cast off, so that practitioners of future generations would no longer be deceived by old rags of paper.
Nevertheless, though it is thus: the sea is vast, let the fish leap; the sky is wide, let the birds fly.
Blocking the eyes—who can share this vision with Yaoqiao? When the ox-hide is pierced through, the bones and hair shiver with cold.
How many are there across the five lakes and four seas? Densely written characters and sparse lines are all one and the same.

(Baoning Yong) Before the gate, there are naturally a thousand mountains and moons; within the room, there is not a single speck of dust. Even if one were to try to cover it with palm-leaf manuscripts, it could not be concealed.
The Eye. One must know that even pure ground deludes people (becoming a withered tree).
Seeing through the ox-hide, it is penetrated to the very bottom; in the end, there is neither meaning nor text.
When asked, what person's eye can it block? Sanskrit and Chinese are entirely indistinguishable. (Tianmu Li)
If you study by imitating him, it is like truly piercing an ox hide. For years it lies across the desk; the meaning of the characters will naturally become complete.
(Hengchuan Gong) Yaoshan said to Yunyan, "Call the novice monk here for me. Yunyan asked, "What will you do when he has been called?"
The Master said, "I have this broken-legged cauldron that I want someone to carry up and down for me.
[The monk] said, "In that case, I shall lend you a hand, Reverend. The Master then ceased speaking.
Taisu Zhe said, "If Old Man Yaoshan had not encountered Yunyan, his broken-legged cauldron would have become a discarded vessel.
I, Daopei, also wish for everyone to lend a hand to this broken-legged cauldron. Why? Simply to ensure that the ancient style does not fall into ruin.
Tianning Qi said, "When one's insight equals that of the teacher, it diminishes the teacher’s virtue by half; when one’s insight surpasses [the teacher’s]..."
Only then is a master fit to transmit the teaching. At that time, Yunyan was also lacking one move.

Had he waited for [Nanquan] to say, "I have a broken-legged cauldron," and then have him lift it up and carry it down, he would have withdrawn his body and departed immediately. Only after the snow does one know the steadfastness of the pine and cypress;
only when faced with difficulty does one see the heart of a true man. Senglan Rong said: "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. When the Sage acts..."
All things behold it. Yaoshan’s household goods have been entrusted; Yunyan’s heir has exerted all his strength to carry them on.
This may be called passing a vessel of water from one vessel to another, without the slightest leakage.
In years past, this mountain monk also had a broken-legged cauldron; it was already cracked and shattered, having long since been cast away into the heap of refuse. Only this remains...
This is a piece of smokeless firewood; it simply pervades heaven and scorches the earth. Today, I hold it up before you, and it is important that everyone recognizes its presence.
He then takes up his whisk and blows upon it once, saying: "Look, look! The torch of the Vulture Peak still burns today."
"Successive transmission from antiquity to the present," said Master Xiangwun Yun. "The profound and secret dignity is revealed;

turning the mechanism toward the ultimate, authority is distributed to the left and right. If one lets it pass, both are masters of the craft; if one scrutinizes it, neither has reached full realization."
This mountain monk also has a broken-legged cauldron, and I need a courageous man to lift it up and carry it down.
Should someone come forward and say, "I will give the Master a helping hand," you should strike them across the back with a resounding blow of the staff. Do you understand?
Only by raising a child does one truly know a father’s compassion.
Yaoshan provides the head; Yunyan knows the tail. Although the head and tail match one another, they still do not know shame (Ying’an Hua).
Do you wish for us to join hands?
He simply tells them to call the novice monk over; the iron cauldron has no feet and is also without...
[The Master] said, "I hear it. Beneath the wall, in the depths of spring, the leaves of the shepherd’s purse (*rāsnā*) have opened.
(Hengchuan Gong) One day, while Yaoshan was sitting, Daowu and Yunyan were standing in attendance.

The Master pointed to two trees on the mountain—one withered and one flourishing—and asked, "Which is this? The withered one, or the flourishing one? Daowu said, "The flourishing one. The Master said, "Truly so! (Zhao Ran)
"Let it go so that light shines brilliantly everywhere," he said. He asked Yan again, and Yan replied, "That which is withered is it.
The Master said, "Truly, let it be released everywhere so that it becomes withered and plain. At that moment, the novice Gao suddenly arrived; the Master questioned him in the same manner.
Miaoyan said, "Let the withered be withered as it is; let the flourishing be flourishing as it is. The Master looked at Daowu and Yunyan and said, "Not so, not so.
Yellow leaves fallen in the frost become golden coins; a foolish, crying child sees them and is delighted, seizing them to offer to his mother, and everyone says [how wonderful it is]."
Excellent. I do not know who it is that smiles while looking on.
(Haixin) One branch flourishes, one branch withers; yet in their midst, the green leaves grow even more luxuriant. Let the yellow oriole utter its myriad songs as it pleases.
Lest others find fault with us. (Fohuiquan) Applying powder and rouge, then veiling the head— All is pulled by the strings of the puppeteer. The drumhead is broken and the music played to its end;
Gather everyone together and return home. (Baoning Yong)

To speak of the exhaustion of flourishing and withering makes it even more difficult to perceive. The novice monk falls flat at the very tip of speech. The old monk points afar toward where the monkeys cry;
the clouds disperse, the sky is vast, and the moonlight is cold.
(Dizang’s Grace) Three by three, two by two, they are not the same. Hand in hand, they walk step by step into the weeds. Lifting their feet, they step through the embroidery.
Shoes. What harm is there in beating the spring breeze in the month of December?
(Donggu Guang) Yaoshan was once asked by a monk: "In the level fields and shallow grass, herds of wild deer roam. How can one shoot the master within the dust?
The Master said, "Watch the arrow! The monk threw himself down and fell. The Master said, "Attendant, drag this dead man out!"
The monk then ran away. The Master said, "What limit is there for this fellow who plays with lumps of mud?
Cui-feng Xian said, "Though this monk may live for three steps, he must die at the fifth.

Yun-ju Yuan said, "Yaoshan’s crossbow, capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt, does not fire its trigger for a mere field mouse. This monk has stepped out the door with an arrow in him; once dead, he will never again [return]."
"No longer living. Jingci Chang said: "This monk has chased a monkey into the bustling marketplace; Yaoshan has ridden a fierce tiger straight up to the high mountain.
If you try to deliberate upon this as a single point, you will ultimately be subject to scrutiny by others."
Yuan-an Meng said: "It is not easy for this monk to have set up such a question. But when he loosed his arrow, it turned out to be nothing but a dead deer.
Perhaps by some stroke of luck he drank nectar elsewhere and was reborn, so that he did not lose his status as the primal ancestor, King Weyin.
Then, aiming at the empty sky, he drew a bow and said: 'Look at the arrow! Gu-nan Men said: [He]... [continued].
This monk hid his body within the weeds and set up a question-head that he was able to carry through from beginning to end. Yaoshan’s single arrow hit the mark;
yet, alas, the monk who fired it did not die.
The Master Amidst the Dust. Look at this! He lets fly a single arrow and takes three steps. If he remains alive after five steps, he will join the pack in chasing the tiger.
"The true eye has always been entrusted to the hunter," he said aloud. "Look at the arrow! (Cui-feng Xian). Iron cavalry gallops across level ground;
bow and arrow are not yet drawn. What a fine master amidst the dust! Piercing the heart, he heads toward the roadside.

A colt newly emerged from its stable still has a supple waist; a phoenix chick just left its nest still has but slight strength. Having been born with jade hooves, it gallops a thousand li;
having been nurtured with golden wings, it soars through the nine heavens.
(Fojian Qín) While Yushan was reading a scripture, Li Ao, the Regional Inspector of Langzhou, visited him. Seeing the Master holding the scripture with complete composure, he was greatly impressed.
He did not look back. Xu Ao said, "A face seen is not as good as a name heard," and he swept his sleeves and departed. The Master called out to the Prefect; Ao turned his head.
The Master said, "Prefect, why do you value the ears and despise the eyes? Ao returned the gesture and thanked him. He then asked, "What is the Way?
The Master pointed up and down with his hand and asked, "Do you understand? Ao replied, "I do not. The Master said, "Clouds in the sky..."
"Clear blue sky, water in the pitcher. Xu Ao performed a prostration and composed this verse: His cultivated body has taken on the form of a crane;
Beneath a thousand pine trees, he holds two cases of scripture. I came to ask about the Way, and there was no further talk; Clouds in the blue sky, water in the pitcher.
Songyin nodded and said, "I am not like that. When asked what the Way is, I simply say: 'When the state is upright, Heaven's mind is harmonious;
when the officials are pure, the people are naturally at peace. Is there any difference in quality between me and Yaoshan? He leaned on his staff.
Clouds in the blue sky, water in the jar; hand-in-hand with you, we walk through the crimson heavens.
Turning our heads, we do not realize that cold night has turned to dawn; a single mass of red light rises over the sea.
(By Yuantong Xian) The worthy Prime Minister of Longxi ascends Mount Yaoqiao; clouds in the blue sky, water in the jar. When the wind stills and the clouds vanish, the void remains alone.
Dew. The Jade Maidens at the Celestial Gate have never bolted the doors.

(Tianning Lian) Clouds are in the blue sky, water is in the pitcher; the eye’s light follows the finger and falls into a deep pit. The wildflowers by the stream cannot endure the bitter frost and wind;
what need is there to speak of walking the bottom of the profound sea? (Zhang Wujin)
Now there is no meeting face-to-face; in former days, his name was unheard of. One phrase added to three—how can such a composition be read?
(Xiyan Hui) Clouds in the blue sky, water in the pitcher. Throughout my life, I have laid bare my liver and gall toward others. True gold possesses its own true luster.
The price: never mix sand with it when selling to others. (The heart of the Northern Sea) Valuing the ear while despising the eye;
drawing the gold-tipped arrow behind one’s back, looking up at the azure sky—the arrow has already passed beyond the kingdom of Silla.
(Bianshan Qian): "Parting the weeds to gaze upon the wind—what can one do? To find the Way in the deep mountains, one must pass through them.
It is only because the ear is valued and the eye despised that the whole body is led to enter the thicket of weeds. (Duan'an Chang)
While Yaoshan was reading a scripture, Baoyan said, "Master, please stop; it is good for people. The Master set down the scripture and asked, "Is it early or late in the day?
Baoyan replied, "It is exactly noon. The Master said, "There is still this trace remaining.
Baoyan said, "I have nothing, and there is nothing even to be absent. The Master said, "You are far too clever. Baoyan said, "I am simply like this; as for you, Master..."
"What? the Master said. "I am lame and hobbled, a hundred ugly traits and a thousand clumsy ways; I shall simply pass my days thus.
Just now, ascending the green peaks to gaze at the dawn ridges—the mountains are green, the clouds white, and the waters flow vast and deep.
Unaware that within the deep flowers on the opposite bank, one emerges from one layer only to enter another. (Pingxiang)
Once, while Yueshan was planting vegetables with Yuantou, the Master said, "I do not prohibit you from planting;
simply ensure that no roots grow. Yuantou asked, "If you do not allow roots to grow, how will the assembly have anything to eat?
The Master replied, "Do you have a mouth? Yuantou was speechless.
When everyone gathers to eat a stalk of pickled vegetables, it is called the "Stalk of Pickled Vegetables" hell. This is not because one finds it difficult to dwell with others;
it is entirely because the distinction between the ordained and the laity must be clear.
(Shendeng Kui) While Yaoshan and Yunyan were traveling through the mountains, a knife at Yaoshan’s waist made a sound. Yunyan asked, "What was that noise? The Master drew [the knife].
A blade flashed across the mouth in a striking gesture;
the Great Garuda passed alone over the Celestial Pond. The Lion took its cub and followed it to the end; the Kunlun Mountains were struck and the traveler returned to his path.
With one roar, clouds are swallowed and the ten thousand phenomena flee. (Touzi Qing)
When Yaoshan returned from gathering firewood, a monk pointed to the knife at his waist and asked, "What is this thing that makes such a 'mng-bol-bol' sound?
The Master drew the knife and made a cutting gesture; the monk was suddenly enlightened.
It rings out with a *pe-lo-po* sound, completely leaking away. The frost-knife was originally iron from Bingzhou.
Striking the waist of the pillar in front of the hall, fresh blood flows from the crown of the stone man’s head.
(Fazhou Ji) When Yunyan came to visit Yaoshan, the Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Baizhang. The Master said, "What did Baizhang say?"
Regarding the phrase, [Yunmen] said, "Ordinarily I say I have a single phrase that possesses a hundred flavors.
The Master said, "If it is salty, it has the flavor of salt; if it is bland, it has the flavor of blandness; that which is neither salty nor bland is the ordinary flavor.
What is this phrase that possesses a hundred flavors? Yanguan had no reply. The Master said, "What can you do about birth and death right before your eyes? [Yanguan] said, "Right before my eyes..."
"Before this, there was neither birth nor death. The Master asked, "How long have you been at Baizhang? He replied, "Twenty years.
The Master said, "Having spent twenty years at Baizhang, you have not even eliminated your worldly airs."
Having traveled the paths through a thousand peaks until they fade from sight, one only remembers the old cloud-covered hermitage upon returning home.
Greedily seeking the ancient melodies of the Shangu tune, one errs amidst the border *jia* flutes, their single rhyme drawn out long.
(Touzi Qing) Swiftly reclaiming the ancestral fields and gardens, bamboo leads the clear breeze along the source of the stream; thus one recalls those years of carrying a basket on one's shoulder.
The mulberry trees, hemp, chickens, and dogs are all as they were before.
(Nan’an Yi) Chan Master Tianran of Danxia in Dengzhou (a successor of Shitou Xiqian) attended upon Shitou. He served as a laborer for three years.
One day, Shitou addressed the assembly, saying, "Tomorrow, you shall mow the grass before the Buddha Hall. When the next day arrived, the assembly each prepared their tools.
Regarding the spades and hoes: Master Du filled a basin with water and washed his head. He knelt upright before the head [of the image], who saw him and laughed;
he then shaved his hair for him and further preached the precepts to him. The Master covered his ears and departed.
Shitou clears away the weeds to test the heroic;懵懂 (Bengdeng) Danxia’s eyes were not high.
Had he known how to turn his body and walk the living path, he would not have burdened his descendants to this day. (Guyuan says:

At Huilin Monastery, Danxia encountered cold weather and took a wooden Buddha to burn for warmth. The monastery head reprimanded him, saying: *Note: The text provided ends mid-sentence regarding the monastery head's reprimand.*
"How could you burn my wooden Buddha? The Master took his staff and brushed away the ashes, saying, "I burned it to retrieve the *śarīra*.
[The attendant] said, "How can a wooden Buddha have *śarīra*? The Master replied, "Since there are no *śarīra*, take two more statues and burn them.
Thereafter, the temple administrator's eyebrows and beard fell out.
Touzi Qingyuan said, "I do not know how to be a guest; I trouble the host.
Daning Kuan was asked by a monk, "When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, why did the temple steward’s eyebrows and beard fall off? Daning replied, "Thieves do not strike a poor house."
Baoning Yong said: "Setting aside for a moment the fact that the abbot’s eyebrows and beard fell out, did Danxia’s eyebrows still remain?
If you can see this, you will be a fellow student of the ancient Buddhas; if you do not see it, you must by all means avoid denying cause and effect."
Baofeng Wen said: "When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, the head monk’s eyebrows and beard fell off. He suddenly picked up his staff and said, "This is not a wooden Buddha.
He threw down the staff and said, "Who dares to burn you? "If you intend to [burn it], your eyebrows and beard will fall off;
but if you do not intend it, what then? He called out loudly, "Attendant! and picked up the staff. Dongchan Yue said: "The ancients..."
In practice, people today ought to know this: it is like unfurling a great banner; if one executes a guilty person, the whole world submits.
If, however, they are innocent, even the law cannot be applied. Even if a thousand sages were to appear, not a single word could be arranged.
Tiantong Huo said: "The various quarters discuss this, saying that the monastery superintendent suddenly gave rise to a doubting mind."
This led to such a calamity. It is further said that because the abbot did not give Danxia a fire during the cold weather, it resulted in the wooden Buddha being burned down.
Little did they know that by buying iron and obtaining gold, the abbot had experienced a moment of great fortune.
Yunfeng Xuan was once asked by a monk: "Danxia burned the wooden Buddha; why did the abbot’s eyebrows and beard fall off? Yunfeng replied: "One person transmits it."
Wanren said, "The transmission of the void is real. To say 'it is thus' means it does not fall [into categories]. Feng said, "This is a double case. Wanren said, "I do not yet understand;
I specifically request your instruction. Feng said, "Jing, Yuan, Qian, and Ji have brushes stuck in their heads.
Lingyin Yue said, "Great as Danxia may be, he lost an eye in a deep village. The temple administrator is also like this."
Insects gnawing wood may accidentally form characters; yet beneath the gate of Guangxiao, there is no wooden Buddha to be burned.
There is only a single spark of smokeless fire, truly difficult to approach from the side. To aim for it is to have one’s face scorched by its blaze. Everyone must step back and look;
suddenly, amidst the cold ashes, a bean pops—startling heaven and shaking earth, such that even Buddhas and Patriarchs could not save you.
It is so. Fuyan Rong said: "Danxia’s entire body is a great mass of fire.

Not only would his eyebrows and beard fall off if he were to revile others, even if he were to praise them, his eyebrows and beard would likewise fall off. Why is this? Because a man of integrity acts;
he does not fall into the vulgar. Pinyang Min said: "Danxia burned the wooden Buddha; the rhinoceros's horn bears patterns from gazing at the moon."
"Antlers grow; the abbot’s eyebrows and beard fall out; the elephant is struck by lightning and flowers enter its tusks.
[The Master] suddenly picks up his staff, draws a line, and says: "Do not touch it! To touch it is thirty blows! Huangbo Qi said: "Danxia flung forth sparks;
it did not merely bring misfortune upon the abbot, but caused the eyebrows and beards of all people throughout the great earth to fall out. Why is this?"
"When it is cold, all under heaven is cold; when it is hot, all under heaven is hot.
Shen Dingze said, "Everyone says the Abbot has lost his eyebrows and whiskers, yet they do not realize that Danxia has lost his nostrils.
He gave a shout and said, "If you stir even a single hair here, though the cause may be good, it will still bring about an evil result. Jinsu Yuan said, "Danxia..."
"Burning a wooden Buddha—pointless, utterly pointless! The head monk will lose his beard and eyebrows; he suffers it now, he will suffer it in the next life.

Although both sides are perfectly clear, one cannot avoid causing people to harbor groundless suspicions and make hasty conjectures. [The Master] picks up his staff and says, "The wooden Buddha is right here.
He strikes once and says, "It has been burned away. He throws down the staff and says, "Everyone, take good care of your eyebrows! —Nanshan (Fayan Wenyi)
Baoyun said: "Calamity does not enter the door of a careful family. Falingyin said: "The place where the Abbot missed the mark could not be deceived by Danxia;
the place where Danxia missed the mark could not be deceived by the Abbot. Nevertheless, within the way of benevolence and righteousness—"
Moss seals the ancient crags as cold invades the door; The flying are startled by the peril, the running are lost in confusion.
Deep in the night, the fires on the marshes burn against the chill; At dawn, the fisherman’s house is busy with its own doubts.
(Touzi Qing) Snow encloses the mountain gate, frozen and without spring; A single wooden Buddha is split for firewood. Where the eyes move, the eyebrows—
A fall! This constitutes slandering the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma.
(Zhang Wujin) Facing him directly, the upward-tending pivot cannot be concealed; his family style has been bestowed upon others for a thousand ages.
Through layer upon layer of silver mountains and iron walls, he penetrates them all—thankfully, the Abbot of Danxia knew this. (Chu Fang’an)
Striding across private paths, he suddenly attends a public banquet. His *fukutō* (head-wrap) has short ends; his waist-belt boasts a perfect circle.
It is not that he is a groom’s companion come to offer wine; it is merely that he has mistakenly led this youth on in search of a "green felt" (an official post).
(Gyūtō Shō) Peng Zu sought longevity for eight hundred years; Qin Shi Huang ascended the throne yet further sought immortality. Yesterday, upon the Tianjin Bridge—
Too late! Shi Chong still sent off the "Boat for the Poor" himself.
(Wenshu said: "Danxia burned the wooden Buddha; the head monk’s eyebrows and beard fell out. To draw the bow and shoot Weichi, one must have teeth made of gold."
(No-Form Model) In the desolate monastery, the weather is cold; they burn a wooden Buddha. A mass of red flames faces a withered bed. His whole body is warm and steaming all night long.
How difficult it is to make the abbot bear the guilt! (Hyanggwon Gung)
Master Hua discarded gold as if discarding soil; Lord Guan tilled the earth but did not till for gold. A difference of only a hair’s breadth led to such divergent paths;
their high and low standings remain divided to this day. (Chao of Xidun) When the southern mountain burns charcoal, the northern mountain turns red;
what need is there to borrow the power of Yin and Yang’s creative transformation? Its fierce flames reach across the heavens, impossible to avoid.
[He] attained it. He mistakenly taught others; what regret over the wind at the fifth watch! (Falin’s commentary).
When Danxia visited National Teacher Zhong, he encountered the Master while he was asleep. He then asked the attendant, "Is the National Teacher here? [The attendant] said:
"It is right here, right now; it is simply that you do not see the guest. The Master said, "That is far too profound. The monk said, "Do not say that, Venerable Sir;
even the Buddha’s eye could not look and see it. The Master said, "The dragon begets dragon cubs; the phoenix begets phoenix chicks," and then he departed.
When the National Teacher woke from his sleep, the attendant reported the previous conversation. The National Teacher then struck the attendant with twenty blows and expelled him from the monastery.
Upon hearing this, the Master sighed and said, "It is no exaggeration to call him the National Teacher of Nanyang.
Tiantong Hua said, "The attendant was beaten and sent away from the monastery; such a moment has not occurred for a thousand years. As for Guizong, how could he avoid having his eyes burn with envy?"
Although Danxia Gu was indeed a skilled hand, how could he avoid falling into the net of the National Teacher? Can you all discern this?
If you have not yet realized it, it is like grasping a golden whip and asking a traveler returning home: "In the deep of night, who will walk with you along the Imperial Street?"
Jingshan Ce said: "The National Teacher was fortunately sleeping soundly; it was the attendant who broadcasted his family's disgrace.
Had it not been for the many-mouthed Danxia, how could we have seen the National Teacher’s roar? I dare ask the assembly: since the National Teacher was there, why did he not see the guest?
If you can see through this point, not only will you know where the attendant missed the mark, but you will also see your own self."
"Regarding the path of one's origin: although it is thus, do not let idle learning and intellectual understanding bury the mind of the Patriarch.
Tian Qi said, "Danxia knew only the first and did not know the second; the attendant knew only the second and did not know the first.
Both deserve twenty blows of the staff, yet it is a pity they were let off. Now tell me, where does the National Teacher’s eye reside?"
[The Master] said, "I will tell you after you have finished eating the staff. Fengshan Qi said, "Did Danxia ever meet the National Teacher?
Lingfeng Ling said, "Danxia was singing wildly in the green caves; the National Teacher was drunk to the core in the jade pitcher.
Had it not been for the attendant acting so foolishly, how could one have seen the great merit of his labor? Yunzhong Feng.
It is said: "Although the National Teacher was a masterful hand, he was still acting as the host after the dream.
Danxia, being accustomed to pilfering in broad daylight, could not avoid falling into the trap of the attendant. Now tell me: when the attendant receives the staff, is it a reward or a punishment?"
With high pillows upon my ivory bed, I alone forget the passing years. I did not expect spring flowers to fall before my railing.
How regrettable that wandering bees plunder them at will; To this day they chase after them toward the grassy embankment.
(Lin Yaqi) A solitary moon shines; a morning breeze blows. In deep autumn, perilous dew wets the lotus robes. Chaos-stacked are the shadows of willows by the stream.
The fishing boat is unimpeded as it lowers its line once more.
(Lamp of the Great Drama) Lord Song can discern the finest details of autumn hair; he brings forth [the truth] and the soul of Xuanyuan would melt away.
He has severed the three-inch tongue of the Prime Minister; who else dares to speak with such incessant chatter? (Waves of the Brow)
The bald-clawed Old Dragon of Nanyang, with his silk headband and feather fan, moves with ease.
Borrowing but a small portion of the eastern wind, he seeks to witness the merit of the King’s army winning without battle.
(Falin-yin) Danxia went to visit Mazu; on the road, he encountered an old man and a young boy. The Master asked, "Sir, where do you reside?"
The old man said, "Above is heaven; below is earth. The Master said, "If suddenly heaven collapses and the earth opens up, what then?
The old man said, "Heaven! Heaven! The youth let out a sigh. The Master said, "It is not without a father that a son is born.
The old man and the youth then entered the mountains together.
Zhengjue Xian said: "Above is heaven, below is earth; one cannot help but be clever. 'Heaven! Heaven!'—understanding arises following these words.

"This fellow Danxia met with defeat at the hands of the Old Man. Although he finally managed to say 'It is not...'"
"The father does not give birth to the son; this is merely a worn-out leather shoe being forced to stretch.
At that time, seeing the Way as heaven and the world as earth—why not look toward the Way? That wild fox spirit has been right here all along.

At that time, as he waited for him, [the Master] said, "Heaven! Heaven! Why do you not pay three prostrations to the boy?

Changqing Ling asked Baofu, "When one gives food to another to eat, there is a share of merit for the benefactor; why then do you not possess the eye?
Baofu replied, "Both the giver and the receiver are blind men. Changqing asked, "Even when one exhausts their skillful means, does it still result in blindness?"
Fuyun said, "Can you say that I am blind? Baoci then said, "Now tell me, did Changqing understand Danxia’s meaning, or was he merely using his own family wealth?
Bazhao Che said, "Each has one gain and one loss. He also spoke on behalf of the monk, saying, "When there is no shortage to compete over, one yields what is in surplus.
He also spoke on behalf of Danxia, saying, "Both giver and receiver derive no benefit."—Fen.

This leads to the formation of faults; the faults are profound and nowhere to be found. Heaven and earth alike have sunk into the mud.
(Cui Feng Xian) One day Danxia visited Master Pang. Seeing his daughter Lingzhao gathering vegetables, the Master asked, "Is the Layman at home?
The girl set down her vegetable basket and stood with her hands clasped. The Master asked again, "Is the Layman at home? The girl then picked up [the basket].

The basket was taken away. The Master then returned. After a short while, the official came home. The woman recounted the previous conversation. The official asked, "Is Danxia still here? She replied, "He has gone.
The official said, "This is like smearing red earth on a cow's udder."
Taisu Zhe said: "How great was Danxia! He was exposed by the laywoman.

I would have replied, 'It is not without reason that enemies meet. Jiangshan Qin said: "Danxia discerned the ground from its sprouts. It is truly numinous.
Zhao said, "When the words are spoken, the person is known. Letting go of the vegetable basket, it arises right where it is; lifting up the vegetable basket, it is extinguished wherever one goes.
The layman said, "Red earth is smeared on cow's milk; selling Yangzhou inside the house. After all, what is it?
Everyone dispersed, so as to avoid increasing idle talk. Yingshan Yun said, "If Master Pang had not had these subsequent words, he would have almost been [caught]."
Lingzhao has lost her family tradition. As for the saying, "Red earth smeared on a cow's udder"—what is its meaning?
It means not to let bees and butterflies err by mistakenly identifying flowers across a wall. Tianjie Sheng said: "Yingshan missed the ancients.
Although Master Pang was a toothless tiger, his claws were very sharp. Lingzhao was like a phoenix soaring into the sky; she could appear or remain hidden."
Unfathomable! Thus, at Danxia’s place, the autumn light is revealed clearly; at Master Pang’s place, the spring colors are hidden in shadow.
Her garments are plain, her makeup applied haphazardly; with basket in hand and palms folded, she is naturally without artifice. Yet Old Pang still harbors further sorrow;
he would not say that his slave has leaked the fragrance. (Zhang Wujin)

Chan Master Kuang of Changzi in Tanzhou (Heir to Shitou Xiqian). When he first visited Shitou, Shitou asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "From Lingnan. Shitou asked, "In Lingnan, has the construction of the merit-store been completed? The Master replied, "It is complete."
"It has been a long time. It lacked only this 'eye-opening' [consecration]. The Master said, "Do you not wish for the eye to be opened? The Master replied, "I request it at once.
The Head then lifted one foot. The Master prostrated himself. The Head asked, "What principle have you perceived that you prostrate yourself?
The Master replied, "According to what I have seen, it is like a single drop of snow upon a red-hot furnace."
Baoci then said: "When Changzi responded in such a manner, did he possess the eye or not?
If he possessed the eye, why did he ask for it to be opened? If he did not possess the eye, how can you say he had accomplished it long ago?
How do you adjudicate this? Fadeng Qin spoke on his behalf, saying: "The Master may be said to have clouded eyes. Cui峰 Xian said: "He has no eyes."

"What have you seen that you ask whether the merit of the entire shop has been accomplished? This is like driving a stake into empty space.

Addressing the cub of the golden-maned lion: beneath the sandalwood grove, amidst the green sedge—set it down, set it down;
its majesty is naturally complete. One leap, six leaps, eyebrows raised high. Not to be schemed; how many who know? More than three thousand stars have already flown past.
A *li* beyond the heavens, when the pure wind howls; for your sake, I shall suck dry the Western River. *Duḥ!* (Mingjue Xian). Let loose the golden-maned lion;
all beasts leave no trace of their whereabouts. If you wish for its claws and fangs to be fully revealed, you must grasp the rope yourself. (Lan’an Shu).
Yunyan asked a nun, "Is your father still alive? She replied, "He is. The Master said, "How old is he?
She replied, "He is eighty years old. The Master said, "You have a father who is not eighty years old;
do you know him? She replied, "Is it this one who comes thus? The Master said, "This one who comes thus is merely a descendant."
Dongshan Jia said, "Even one who does not come in such a way is still a descendant. Guo of Mount Miao said, "It is not permitted to come in this way;
it is not permitted to come in that way. Ultimately, how is it? After a long silence, he said, "From the beginning there has been no fixed position;
there is no need for forced arrangement. Bai Zhang Le said, "To recognize the father is easy; to recognize..."
For one's descendants, it is difficult; in recent years, our household affairs have been extremely desolate. From a thousand miles away, we look anxiously for news, yet letters are rare.
Yunyan was asked by a monk, "You served Baizhang for twenty years, attending to his robes and bowl; why is it that the lamp of your mind has not been transmitted?
The Master said, "A jeweled crown upon the head. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The sky of the Great Tang."
When Monk Jiugong Qian asked the Emperor of the Underworld, "What is the meaning of the Great Tang Emperor and the King of the Underworld?
Qian replied, "I recall the words of Dongshan. Tianzhi Wei said, "The golden needle secretly pierces; the embroidery reveals layers upon layers of seams."

A jade thread is drawn across horizontally, passing through the ribbed texture to form a corner-knot. This is precisely the profound principle of the great function and great capacity of our late master Yunyan.
Even if Jiufeng had clarified the source beyond the kalpas, what could he have done? For flowers bloom on spiritual sprouts;
spring does not borrow its power. After all, how is it so? The king of geese chooses his own milk; he is inherently no different from a duck.
The jade whip is raised high to strike the golden gate; it draws forth the coral whose price is beyond reckoning.
The ancient Universal Monarch’s full spirit remains whole; without displaying the precious seal, he is naturally honored.
(Danxia Chun) Seated high upon the dragon pavilion, his majesty is peerless. How could a rustic old man ever inquire about the palace gates? Drumming his belly, he knows nothing of Yao or Shun.
With strength, he carries his hoe and leads his calf past the village ahead.
(Yongjue Xian) The vermilion gates encircle the five clouds in layers; reaching these nine peaks is truly difficult to distinguish. How many travelers lost on their way are made to laugh?
With their backs turned toward the dragon towers, they revile the Most Honored One. (Nan’an Yi)
Suddenly halting his horse without cause as he passed through the royal city, he was abruptly greeted by the fragrant breeze of the Imperial Garden’s brilliance.
With a majestic aura and a gait like the flowing melody of a wind-instrument, who would dare to walk the Imperial Street alongside him? (His companions:
His brows arch with eight-colored radiance, his eyes possess double pupils; Buddhas and patriarchs alike must yield to him, for his skeletal structure was born with such sublime distinction.
How profound! How could it be compared to the scattered grains of millet under the clear sky?
(Xiangweng Yun) The numinous flower never waits for spring to bloom; its fragrance beyond the kalpas is peerless. Within this noble station, who can share its entrustment?
A light mist enshrouds the moon as it drenches the moss. (Zongkai Yuan)
Once, when the attendant in charge of the temple returned from visiting the Stone Chamber, Yunyan asked him, "When you went in there, why did you come back so soon?
The attendant had no reply. Dongshan spoke on his behalf, saying, "Someone has already occupied it within."
The Master said, "Why do you go again? Shanshan replied, "One must not let human relations be severed.
Tiantong Jué said: "Bowing the head, one loses the needle; opening the eyes, one finds the thread. The thread has no beginning, yet there is nowhere to measure it."
A needle has no hole, making it difficult to pierce. To reach this point, even the joining of a broken string with *luan*-glue requires the realization of Dongshan.
Once, when a monk asked Yunyan, "What is it like when one is absent for a moment, as if being a dead man? the Master said, "Then you should simply bury him."
It is best simply to bury it; there is no further reliance upon it. Whether in heaven or among men, one may roam at ease and find joy.
One must strictly avoid deliberation that leads onto the path; there is no need to move a finger to open the pavilion.
(Puan Yu) Yunyan addressed the assembly: "There is a man's son who, when questioned, has nothing he cannot explain. Dong...
Shan-chu said, "How many scriptures are there in that other house? The Master replied, "Not a single character.
Shan-chu asked, "How can you have such vast knowledge? The Master replied, "Day and night I never sleep. Shan-chu asked, "May I ask about a certain matter?"
The Master said, "If you can speak it, yet do not speak it.
Tianning Qi said, "If you can speak it, yet do not speak it—how do you understand this? [He continued: "I always regret that when spring departs, there is no place to find it."
Unaware that he had turned and entered therein, Yunyan asked Daowu, "Of the Great Compassionate One’s thousand hands and eyes, which one is the true eye?
The Master said, "It is like a person at night reaching back with their hand to feel for their pillow. [Yunyan] said, "I understand. The Master asked, "How so? [Yunyan] said, "Everywhere."
"The body itself is hands and eyes. The Master said, "You have spoken quite well; you have only spoken to eighty percent of it.
[The monk] asked, "How about you? The Master said, "The whole body is hands and eyes."
Baiyan Fu said: "I do not agree with that. What is the true eye? To say it is 'blind'—if he were to say, 'I understand,' I would ask him:
'Why is it not seen within Yunmen’s pavilion? Why does the matter beyond Tanggongling not come forth when one attempts to deliberate upon it?
I would give him a severe beating. Why? Has it not been said: 'The whole body is hands and eyes'?"
The whole body is it; the entire person is it. Even picking it up, it is still ten thousand miles away. With wings spread, the Peng bird soars through the clouds of the six directions;
grasping the wind, it stirs the waters of the four oceans. What dust and filth suddenly arises? Which hair’s breadth has not ceased? Do you not see?
The netted pearls hang down, their reflections layer upon layer; from where do the hand and eye at the tip of the staff arise? (Cui Feng Xian)

A single aperture, empty and penetrating; on all eight sides, it is bright and clear. Without form and without partiality, spring enters the musical laws; neither lingering nor obstructing, the moon travels through the sky.
With pure, precious eyes and arms of merit, how could his entire body not be such? The hands and eyes manifest before one’s face, revealing the full mechanism;
as the great function unfolds in纵横 (zōnghéng—transverse and vertical), what need is there for hesitation or prohibition? (Tiantong Jué)

Yanjue’s head returns from the mirror; Nanda restores his original body. Not knowing where his hands and eyes arose, he says, "My entire frame remains within a mote of dust. (Buxin Cai) His whole body is hands and eyes;
throughout the world, they have never been hidden. He gropes for his pillow at the head of the bed, turning over in resentment that the night is long.
(Tianning Lian) While Yunyan was brewing tea, Daowu asked, "For whom are you brewing this? The Master said, "There is someone who wants it.
Daowu said, "Why not let him brew it himself? The Master replied, "Fortunately, there is I here."
Exerting all one’s strength from dawn until dusk, one serves the One Person. Filling the cup to the brim, one displays sincere devotion.
Standing in attendance deep into the night beneath the hanging curtains, one dares not move casually through the imperial courtyard.
(Pingxiang) Yunyan asked a monk, "What have you come for? The monk replied, "I have come to converse upon the rock. The Master said, "Does the rock also speak?"
“Even the head is not there. The monk had no reply, so [Dongshan] spoke on his behalf, saying: “He would have nodded his head before even a word was spoken.
Dongshan Ying (Ying) offered this alternative: “How fortunate that the Master has provided verification. Zhengguo Xing (Xing) offered this alternative:
“What is the use of wanting him to nod his head?”
While Yunyan was sweeping the ground, Daowu said, "You are far too busy. The Master replied, "You must know that there is one who is not so busy.
Daowu said, "If that is so, then there is a second moon. The Master held up the handle of his broom and asked, "Which moon is this? Daowu then desisted.

Xuansha Shibei said, "This is precisely the second moon. Changqing Huileng asked Xuansha, "When he turned the broom handle upside down and struck him right in the face, what then? Xuansha stopped short. Luoshan Xian remarked, "Alas!
These two fellows do not know good from bad. This fellow Yunyan has had his hands and feet tied up; how long has he been dead?"
Yunmen Wenyan said, “The slave sees the maidservant’s earnestness. Guishan Zhe said, “Using diligence to compensate for clumsiness.
Baofu Zhuan said, “Yunyan is much like pushing a cart through the mud; every step is laborious.
Cui峰 Xian added a separate comment after the second phrase: “It would have been better to let it pass. Huishan Xing said, “Daowu is level.”
A mound arises from the earth. When Yunyan was walking, he swung his arm; Xuansha said, "That is truly the 'second moon. How thick is your face?
Now tell me, what is the meaning of raising the broom? "A perfect ten of a diamond drill—spread it out before the gate, to whom will you sell it?
Chaomu An said: "One person went first but did not arrive; one person was at the end."
Later, he went too far; he did not touch upon either of the two paths. Where, then, do you all see Yunyan?
"The embroidered mandarin ducks are displayed for you to view, yet the golden needle is not passed on to others. Tianning Qi said:
"Yunyan sets up his broom, and Daowu stops him from leaving—both are merely the 'second moon. Which one is not so preoccupied? This is the One of this night.
"The wheel is full; where is its pure light not present? Xiu of Qingshan said: "If I were Daowu, when asked 'Which month is this?
I would simply say, 'Just so. This would ensure he has no place to put his broom. Xian of Gushan said:
"This group of fellows—Xuansha and Changqing—could melt metal with their collective mouths. It is not that they did not know Yunyan."
My intention is simply this: he must act according to the command. It is not that Xuefeng’s school is wrong;
it is simply that Yueshan’s school is still ten thousand miles away. Boshan Lai said: "Discerning reality at the head of a heap of refuse;
hiding one's body within the handle of a broom. Who cares which month it is—the second or the third? Use what is appropriate when it is needed. Thus spoke Xuansha and Yunmen.
There is a thorn within the words; this is to reward and to punish. Do not disdain the cold of frost and dew; it adds to the exquisite, fragrant scent.
Borrowed for the moment to settle the gate, when its use is appropriate, one simply rests.
The hand that plays with snakes before Elephant Bone Rock—what was done as a child brings shame to know in old age. (Hongzhi Jue)
Acting according to the time and place, one transcends all constraints; when one employs what is appropriate, that is the true household.
Look at the bright moon from the side of the broom; unaware, one suddenly finds matters as tangled as hemp.
(Pingxiang) Chan Master Zongzhi of Daowu Mountain in Tanzhou (a successor of Yaoshan Yan). A monk asked: "What is the Master’s profound [teaching]?"
[The Master] was in the inner chamber. The Teacher descended from his meditation seat and performed a woman’s bow, saying: "Thank you for coming from afar. I have nothing to offer as a reception.
A jade dragon lies coiled in the sea; auspicious clouds rise high. Looking in the four directions, the ten thousand streams return to the source like tides.
When the wooden man comes to ask about the affairs of the Western Palace, he returns with a single peach from the Eastern Garden. (Touzi Qing)
Prostrating deeply and intimately, the rites of three generations are fully observed. If this meaning were not so, would it be merely about jade and silk?

(Wunian Fan) In years of abundance and times of peace, ritual observances are many; meeting one another, we accompany each other with wine and song. Yet, at the banquet, they do not know how to open their hearts.
