"Horns grow. Three days later, while the Master and Yunyan were on the back porch handling needles, Nanquan saw them and asked, "The other day, Zen Master Zhi said, 'Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking of it; if you speak of it, horns will grow.'"
"How do you practice? The Master then withdrew his body and entered the Sangha hall. Nanquan returned to the abbot’s quarters.
The Master came back again to hold the needle. Yanguan said, "Disciple, why did you not respond to the Master just now?
The Master replied, "You are quite clever. Yanguan, failing to grasp it, went to ask Nanquan, "Just now, what was that Zen monk doing for..."
“I am truly unable to respond to the Master. Quan said, “He, however, acts among the heterodox species (*yìlèi*). Yan asked, “What is it to act among the heterodox species?
Quan said, “Have you not heard it said: ‘Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking; if one speaks, horns will grow.
You must proceed by acting among the heterodox species. Yan still did not understand.
Yunju Ying was once asked by a monk, "If one must strictly avoid speaking of it, what then? Yunju said, "These words are most poisonous.
The monk asked, "What is the most poisonous phrase? Yunju said, "A single blow of the staff kills both dragons and snakes. Wulei Quan commented:
To speak in such a manner is much like a sick bird perching on a reed; it utterly lacks the wisdom of transformation. Here, it is not so.

Where wisdom does not reach, one should speak all the more directly: rain sprinkles the flowers upon the crags, wind rises at the corners of the hall; the diagnosis is administered according to the occasion.
Administering medicine according to the ailment; examining the aperture and applying the wedge; untying the glue and removing the bonds. The celestial horse pushes open the Great Gate of Bestowal;
heaven and earth tremble and the stars fall.
Words cannot reach it—this is what we mean by "fellow practitioners. Shaking out his sleeves, he returns to the hall; the assembly then sifts through the sand and gravel.
True gold is beyond discrimination; there is no need for further doubt or lamentation. (Fenyang Zhao) Beneath the adamantine limit lies an ancient skull;
how many people have been crushed by it as they trampled through the blood splashing into the void? Let the bright moon remain behind; you must go on yourself.
A handful [of snow]. How could the cold pines abandon their shroud of white clouds?
(Touzi Qing) Daowu and Yunyan returned to Yaoshan. Yunyan asked, "What is it to walk among those of different species?
Yaoshan said, "I am weary today; wait for another time to come. Yunyan said, "I have come back specifically for this matter."
"Come," the Master said. Yunyan replied, "I shall go for now," and he departed. As Yunyan was leaving, the Master heard that he had not yet attained realization;
unconsciously, he bit his finger until it bled. Coming down, he asked, "Brother Yunyan, when you questioned the Master about that karmic cause, what did he say?
Yunyan replied, "The Master would not explain it to me. The Master then bowed his head.
Hungry, he eats tender grass as he departs for the distant mountains; thirsty, he drinks cold spring water as he turns back from the winding ravines.
Roaming freely across the empty lands of the kalpa, what need is there for evening songs to urge him on?
(Danxia Chun) A turning of the head reveals a distinct mechanism; a side path traversed by few is known to none. In the ancient hall, clouds deepen and wooden clogs find no trace.
[The] traces: "In the spring breeze, the grass grows long as it crosses the front stream.
(Yongjue Xian) Daowu pointed to a *fosang* flower and asked a monk, "How does this compare to that? [The monk] said, "It makes the hairs on my body stand on end.
The Master said, "Ultimately, how is it? [The monk] said, "[It is] something from under Daowu’s gate. The Master said, "Ten li..."

King, Zhaojue Qin said: "Like pouring lacquer onto glue; by examining the shadow, one knows the form. If you do not understand the coming from the right and the going from the left, how can you comprehend the bright casting itself into the dark?
Do you understand yet? A frog leaps up to the Brahma Heaven; an earthworm suddenly crosses the Eastern Sea."
Jingshan Ce said: "If one does not open the doors and windows, how can one know the light of the bright moon?
If one does not float upon the immortal raft, how can one behold the majesty of the Milky Way? Daowu used a wedge to pull out a wedge; this monk uses wisdom to shatter wisdom.

Although they have met by chance along the path, they cannot avoid having three heads and six arms. Do you understand? Out of love for that young man, he has instead turned into a white-haired old man.
Weng. Daowu, because Yunyan asked him, "What is the style of your house, elder brother? the Master said, "What is the use of letting you point it out?
Yunyan said, "How long has it been since that [style] was absent? The Master said, "The roots of the teeth."
There is still a lingering trace of bitterness.
Yongning Ding said: "If you unfold [your mind] with subtle intimacy, you will succeed; yet, if you wish to be a true descendant of Stonehead, you cannot avoid wrinkling your brows as an onlooker."
Daowu was once asked by Shishuang, "If someone were to ask about the ultimate matter after a hundred years have passed, what would you say to them?
Daowu called out, "Attendant! The attendant responded, "Yes. Daowu said, "Fill the water pitcher. After a long silence, he then asked Shishuang, "What did you just ask?
Shishuang repeated his question, whereupon Daowu returned to his quarters. At this, Shishuang attained realization.
Hanging down his hand, he returns the device of the Master; amidst ordinary speech, he unfurls his banners.
As he prepares to inquire further and return to the Abbot’s quarters, one phrase is clear and beyond doubt.

(Danxia Chun) The spring breeze first arrives at the ends of the earth; in the second month, flowers bloom everywhere in the mountain city. From the towers and terraces, the pipes and flutes play a song.
Song: A jade-like person is supported home while intoxicated. (Yunxiu Luan) Daowu said:
"Exaltedness does not lie at the highest peak; wealth does not lie at Fuyan; joy does not lie in heaven;
suffering does not lie in hell."
Miaoxi said: "The high is at the summit; the wealthy are at Fuyan; bliss is in heaven; suffering is in hell. Nantang Yu said:
"One person, standing high on high ground, finds it insufficient to look out; another person, standing low on low ground, finds it more than enough to level the view.
Within the gate of proclaiming the teaching, one may sufficiently behold the splendor; yet within the gate of the patch-robed monks, there still remains a lack of awakening. Dharma.
Linyun said, "Did those two great elders meet each other or not?
Daowu, having been asked by Guishan, "Where have you come from? replied, "I have come from attending to the sick. Guishan asked, "How many people are sick?
Daowu said, "There are those who are sick and those who are not. Guishan asked, "Is the one who is not sick the Venerable Zhi?"
[The monk] said, “Ma. The Master said, “Whether it be illness or non-illness, neither concerns him at all. Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
[The monk] said, “Even if one could speak it, it would have no connection with him.”
Boshan Lai said: "Huairen of Mount Gui and Shangyi of Daowu—though these two elders did not reveal even the point of a needle, they were nonetheless exceedingly clever.
But tell me: who is the one who is ill? Who is the one who is not ill? Who is the one who is not involved? Pingyang Min said:
"If a teacher of the Dharma for fifteen hundred people speaks such words as these..."
This mountain monk would have struck him across the spine with a staff; yet even that one blow has its point of failure. How could the wondrous medicine ever pass the mouth?
Even the divine physician cannot apply his hand. If it exists, it fundamentally is not non-existent; in its ultimate emptiness, it fundamentally is not existent.
It is born without perishing, and it endures without dying. It completely transcends the time before Vipaśyin Buddha.
Walking alone after the void kalpa, he accomplishes peace; as heaven covers and earth supports, the sun flies and the moon runs.
(Tiantong Jué) His supreme countenance excels, yet his form remains unmanifest; dwelling alone in the deep palace, who could know him? Only by chance did he board the raft beyond the heavens.

I regret that I did not tell him so at the time. Nevertheless, even so, he still does not violate the lineage of Yaoshan."
Baoci then said, "When the ancients spoke thus, did they still know there was something [beyond] or not? Yunyan at that time did not understand;
where exactly was it that he did not understand? Cuiyan Zhi said, "Daowu said that Yunyan did not know there was something."
"I regret not having spoken to him at that time. To speak in such a manner—does Dao-wu still know this or not?
When Master Amitābha was approaching his passing, he remarked: "The ancient master Yunyan, at the moment of his departure, put on airs and failed to consider the family's disgrace.
Dao-wu’s talk like this is merely to entice the gentleman with profit. I am not like Yunyan, stringing together these fine, trivialities."

The Fourth Generation Descendant of Dajian:
Chan Master Chuanzi Decheng of Huating, Xiuzhou (Heir to Yaoshan Yan). Because Jiashan had first taken up residence at Heilin.
When Daowu arrived at Yueshan’s hall for the formal sermon, a monk asked, "What is the Dharma-body? Yueshan replied, "The Dharma-body is formless.
The monk asked, "What is the Dharma-eye? Yueshan replied, "The Dharma-eye is without flaw. Daowu let out a laugh.

After the sermon concluded, Yueshan went down from his seat and asked Daowu, "There must have been something incorrect in my response that caused you to laugh. Daowu said, "The Master is of one rank [with me]."
This is the world-transcending [Dharma]. Since there is no teacher yet present, Shanshan asked, "Where is it not right?
I said, "I will certainly not say. He requested, "Please go to Chuanzi at Huating. Shanshan asked, "What is this man like? I said, "Above him is not a single tile;
below him is not enough space to plant a锥 (chui-needle). "If you go, you must change your attire," Shanshan said, and he then dismissed the assembly.
He went straight to Huating. As soon as the Master saw him, he asked, "Virtuous One, in what monastery do you reside?
Shan said, "I do not reside in a monastery; where I reside is not like [a monastery]. The Master said, "If it is not like [a monastery], what is it that it resembles?
Shan said, "It is not a dharma within the present moment. The Master said, "Where did you learn this? Shan said, "It is not something reached by the ears or the eyes. The Master said, "..."
"A single phrase that hits the mark is a tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas. The Master asked again, "A thousand fathoms of dangling line—the intent lies in the deep pool.
When you are three inches away from the hook, why do you not speak? As Shanshan was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him with a pole and knocked him into the water.
Just as Shanshan climbed back up, the Master said, "Speak! Speak! As Shanshan was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him again. Shanshan...
Suddenly attaining great enlightenment, he nodded his head three times. The Master said, "The thread on the tip of the fishing pole is for you to play with;
though it does not disturb the clear waves, its meaning is unique. Daoshan then asked, "When casting the line and throwing the hook, what is your intention, Master?

The Master replied, "The line hangs in the green water; floating, there is the sense of both existence and non-existence. Daoshan said, "Your words carry the profound yet leave no path; your tongue..."

The Master spoke, yet did not speak. The Master said, "The waves of the river have been fished through until at last the brocade-scaled fish is encountered. Shan then covered his ears. The Master said, "So it is, so it is.

For thirty springs you have navigated the perils upon your boat; where the line is cast, it brings life or death to those at the tip of the pole. The cassia trees of the two ridges shall divide for a thousand ages."
The rhyme: The green of the mountains and rivers is renewed in ten thousand ways.
(Touzi Qing) Not violating the clear waves, not casting the hook; how strange, to strike the head of the tortoise right before one's face! A faint spray mists the drizzling rain;
in ten thousand ravines and a thousand streams, the waters flow upstream. (Baoning Yong)
The long pole is cast out, following the waves; the line is reeled in, catching the scarlet-scaled fish.
With a flip of the oar, how free and easy! Turning back, one no longer sees the person of old.
(Foji Yu) Beyond the white clouds on the railing, thoughts drift far and wide. Dense as they are, the golden scissors cannot cut them open. In the secluded cave, one is not bound by golden locks.
The mind, whether moving horizontally or vertically, is unattached as it goes and returns.
(Danxia Chun) When it is three inches away from the hook, how can you speak of it? To hesitate and deliberate is like sand in the eye.
With the moon bright beneath the sail, one carries it back; To whom does its pre-aeonic air and flavor belong? (Zhenxie Liang)
Three inches away from the hook, he snaps the oar once; a hundred thousand pores shiver with cold.
Although both hands have personally delivered it, the point lies in his own nodding of the head.
(Wuji Pai) Without form and without flaw, he immediately turns back his weapon; it was simply because he trusted the mendicant Zhi too lightly. Had he not reached Huating...
Above. A boat oar cast of iron—what can it do for you? (Nansou Mao).
Having spent over thirty years at Yaoshan, how could the livelihood of a ghost-house be transmitted?
Had he not encountered Old Jia Shan at that time, you would have had to patiently prop up a shattered boat. (Qingxi Che).
A single-leafed boat drifts upon the waves; the fishing line stirs the autumn of the vast sky. Who would suffer the pain of a fragrant oar striking their mouth?
The clouds and mountains between the ridges nod in the dark. (Guo Qingliang) Three inches away from the hook, one is already surrounded by obstacles.
As soon as the foul mouth opens, one is separated by the ocean’s edge. One only gains the boundless autumn of the clouds and mountains.
Water. To this day it long reflects the slanting evening sun. (By Gu Yunquan) After the Yangguan Pass was breached, horses left their hooves empty.
Smoke locks and clouds seal the sky as the sun sinks low. When conversation turns to years past, the wind sweeps through the emerald trees;
On broken steles and ancient paths, few have inscribed their names. (By Banzhulü)
Mixing smoke, he casts his line by the autumn riverbank; laughing, he points to the golden-scaled fish leaping straight onto the hook.
With a single stroke of the oar, both ordinary and holy are cut off; with a nod of the head, his entire being sells its own elegance.
(Tiansong Yue) The Boatman instructed Jia Shan, saying: "From now on, you must ensure that where you hide your body, there are no traces; where there are no traces..."
"Do not hide your person in the traces of the world. For twenty years I was at Yaoshan, clarifying only this matter.

Now that you have attained it, do not dwell in cities, prefectures, or villages hereafter. Go instead into the deep mountains and, by the side of your mattock, seek out one or two others to carry on the lineage;
do not let it be severed. As Shanshan took his leave and walked away, he frequently looked back. The Master then—
He called out, "Disciple! Shan turned his head. The Master raised his oar and said, "You thought there was something else. Thereupon he capsized the boat and passed away.
Changlu Liao said: "The oar-head is turned; the stars of the Milky Way shine. The boatman has kicked it over; heaven and earth grow dark."
He raised his whisk and said: "This is that which is dry, white, and utterly pure on the side of the mattock.
Do you know that which leaves no trace and cannot be hidden?"
Jiashan realized his mind beneath the oar; what need to worry about body or name as he capsized the boat?
The fisherman who dangles his line at Huating, ancient and modern, makes one sigh with sorrow upon the misty waves of the river.
(Zhaojue Zong) Not violating the clear waves, his intent is naturally distinct; though his mouth opens and eyes stare, he still hesitates. The fishing boat has capsized, leaving no trace.
Traces: The setting sun and autumn wind battle the reeds and rushes.

(Fotuoxun) With no trace for the body to hide, there is nothing further to conceal. When the whole being is without dependence, it is immediately present. The ancient mirror does not need polishing to reflect itself;
Thin mist and dew moisten the autumn light.
Jiashan does not reside on a single oar; the bright moon and reeds are cold night after night. Who says the news from Huating has been cut off?
The autumnal colors remain vivid upon the rivers and mountains. (Explanatory Verse: A single boat at the bend of green willows;
where the golden scales are caught, it is difficult. The deep waters of the Long River harbor resentment; it was not right to kick over the boat.
(Xiyuan Hui) Where the body is hidden, there is no trace; The numinous bird dwells atop the shadowless tree. Where there is no trace, do not hide the body;
On the sproutless branch, the spring flowers break forth. There is a reason for this— Who can discern it? At daybreak, the western wind blows gently.
Pine needles scattered along a single path (Donggu Guang);

In the courtyard of song and dance, they move to the rising and falling rhythm. The shuttle of the brocade-embroidered words twists and turns as one gazes upon them. Lately, the autumn waters of Dongting have filled;
An ancient sail, favored by the wind, has passed through a thousand bays (Xueguan Yin).
On a night of the thirtieth day, the moon shone brightly. I went to inspect the rice paddies when a thief came to steal the seedlings.
On top of the jumping board, he flipped over and clamped his head between my legs. I gave him a firm tug, and it turned out to be none other than a monk (Chaozong Ren).
He kicked down the vast void and terrified the son of Śakra; the thunderbolt’s decree was put into motion, its spiritual power extending thirty thousand *li*.
(Drink from the River and Sea) Amidst the cries of the Du-yu bird, spring grasses flourish. The Wang-sun is nowhere to be seen; my efforts are in vain. Most grievous is this bitter loneliness.
All news has been cut off; the waters ripple on. Upon the coral branches, the moon-marks are fresh. (The Oath Stone Rests)
The spring colors wither as I depart from Luoyang; under the bright moon, sparse shadows fall upon the eastern wall. How many times last year did I see the swallows before the hall?
Now they fly again, circling the painted beams. (Dan Yanxun) The Boatman had a verse that said:
"A thousand-foot fishing line hangs straight down; A single ripple stirs, and ten thousand waves follow."
The night is still and the water cold; the fish do not take the bait. The boat returns empty under the bright moonlight.
The songs of the girls of Qinzhou are so bitter; Hearing but one note, my tears fall like rain.
If only they had met a Han Emperor who showed them favor, Dong Xian’s breath would have been choked and he could not have spoken. (Fushu)
The Boatman’s Verse says: For thirty years I have roamed the seas; The water is clear, the fish appear, yet they do not swallow the hook.
When the fishing rods are worn out, I plant new bamboo; Without calculating the labor, I rest as soon as it is convenient.
Baizhang Xue said: "I am not like that. For several decades I have roamed these mountains; the grass is deep, the forests are dense, and the herds of beasts are thick.
In a casual sweep, I cast down a net that covers the heavens. There are golden-maned lions, and there are monkeys too. But tell me, what use is a monkey?
Ordinarily it performs a somersault, provoking the bystanders to laugh incessantly. (He looks to the left.)
The Master said: "Is there no golden-maned lion? Come forth and display your fangs and claws!

I sigh every time for the fisherman who is accustomed to casting his line; he always moors by the stream where reeds reflect his form. When asked by others, he does not speak, but merely nods his head.
Fearing that the fish might be startled away, he does not answer those who call to him. (Haizhou Ci)
Chan Master Huisheng of Pishu in Xuanzhou (a successor of Yaoshan Yan) was once visited by Dongshan. The Master asked, “What have you come for?
Dongshan replied, “I have come to attend upon the Master. The Master said, “If it is for the sake of attending upon me, why do you need to move these two flaps of skin? Dongshan was speechless.
Upon hearing this mention, Caoshan said: "The one son has personally attained it;
from the beginning, father and son have never been apart. Why trouble the stone woman with further questioning?
Last night, on the shadowless tree in the cold crags, a horizontal branch fell deep within the white clouds. (Danxia Chun)
Chan Master Baiyan Mingzhe of Ezhou (a successor of Yaoshan Yan) once asked Dongshan and his senior teacher Mi when they arrived, "Where have you recently departed from, Venerable?
Dongshan replied, "Hunan. The Master asked, "What is the surname of the Military Governor?"
He said, "I have no surname. The Master asked, "What is your given name? He replied, "I have no given name. The Master asked, "Do you still attend to affairs?
He replied, "There are naturally corridors and screens. The Master asked, "Do you still come and go? He replied, "I do not come and go.
The Master said, "How can it be that you do not come and go? Shanshan shook his sleeves and departed. The next day, the Master entered the hall and summoned the two senior monks (shangzuo).
[The Master] said, "Yesterday, when we spoke face-to-face, our words did not accord. I have been uneasy all night long. Now I ask you, Senior Monk (Shangzuo), to offer another word.
If it satisfies my mind, I shall open the gruel and stay with you to pass this summer retreat. Dongshan said, "Please, Reverend, ask.
The Master said, "As for that which neither enters nor exits—how is it? Dongshan said, "It is too noble. The Master [said], "... (The text here implies the Master's approval).
Thus, they opened the gruel to pass the summer retreat. Zhaojue Qin said:
"The interplay of the Correct and the Deviant is intended only for perfect integration; direct engagement with the situation honors only what is noble and dignified.
Dongshan observed the capacities of his audience and acted accordingly; when Baiyan’s principle was superior, he followed it. Although this is so, as for those at Jiangshan:

One must develop a distinct eye and perspective; at that time, when he says, "I do not understand," one should immediately apply pressure and say, "He does not understand you, and you do not understand him. I ask you: what words should be spoken here?
"If there were someone who could attain it, even this mountain monk would not serve the congee; he would simply hand over a whisk made of tortoise hair.
If one cannot attain it, study for another thirty years. Tiantong Jie said: "Brightly cast, darkly met; brilliant and penetrating on all eight sides."
One must not strike the head; there is a path for turning the body. Under the Caodong school, one may truly behold the splendor.

But as for the descendants of Linji—if they were here, even if the staff were broken, they would not let it rest. At that time, seeing that he did not know his own surname, [Linji] would have struck him once across the spine.
If you can turn your body here, not only will you be invited to share the gruel, but you will also be settled beneath the bright window.

Incense has faded and people are silent; all is profound stillness. Moss covers the vermilion courtyard as the bright moon shines.
Entering the room, he is too weary to sit upright in the hall; leaving the door, he is still too lazy to descend the steps.

The vital energy (qi). Upon the jade steps, the chill is piercing; how could this be for the sake of fame? Good elder brother! Good elder brother!
For an entire summer, the pines and winds are inexhaustible; his whole body is uniquely suffused with imperial fragrance.

(With Fengzhi) The musical scales of lü, lǚ, gōng, and shāng shift with marvelous harmony. "Dūyú" and "Xǐqǐ" [expressions of joy] prevail in this sagely and enlightened era. We together revere the Heaven of Yao and the Sun of Shun.
Wearing [the cap], I instead envy Chao and You, who knew nothing at all.

it does not receive the spring breeze, yet flowers bloom of themselves. (Touzi Qing)

The novice Gao built a hut on the southern slope of Mount Yao. One day, he came to pay his respects, coinciding with a rainstorm. Mount Yao asked him:

In one gate there is no affair, yet he dabbles in eccentricities; heedless of his entire body entering the mud and water, he still leaves his private belongings in total disarray, leaving nothing but spring trees warbling yellow orioles.

bamboo tubes slant downward until they reach the tea kettle. (Bianwen Xin)
Chan Master Wuxue of Chuiwei in the Zhongnan Mountains of Jingzhao Prefecture (a successor of Danxia Ran).
Longya asked, "Since arriving at your Dharma seat, Master, I have attended your teachings on many occasions, yet I have never received even a single teaching or instruction. What is your intention?

Fayan Yi said, "The Patriarch has come. Cui峰 Xian said, "These two old fellows have been pierced through by this monk;

One day, Cuiwei was walking up and down in the Dharma Hall when Touzi stepped forward, prostrated, and asked, "Regarding the secret intent of the West, how does the Master instruct people?
The Master paused for a short while. Touzi said, "I beg the Master to grant me an instruction."
The Master said, "Do you want another ladle of foul water? The student then bowed in thanks. The Master said, "Do not try to evade.

Once I struck upon the question of the Western Arrival at Cuiwei; as he paused in his walking meditation, his great compassion was manifest.

(Shuian I) A lion emerges from its den; a black dragon enters its lair. Raising its eyes, a wind arises; the brains of all beasts are split open. Yet it still flaunts its claws and fangs.

(Touzi Qing) To accept this as it is, one is not a son who can uphold the lineage. Standing there, until what year will you find the way to turn? The wind drives the sail’s shadow across the sea gate;
at the ferryhead, there still remains one waiting for the boatman. (Huanji Ting)
When a monk came to visit Zen Master Xingkong of Xiaoyi Temple in Jizhou (who was a successor of Danxia Ziran), the Master extended his hands to show him.
The monk stepped forward and then withdrew. The Master said, "Your parents have both passed away, yet you show no sign of grief.
The monk laughed heartily. The Master said, "I shall offer a funeral lament for you shortly. Thereupon, the monk performed a somersault and departed.
He comes out. The Master says, "Heaven! Heaven! Jingshan Qin said:
"When both hands are spread wide, one sees only the sharp point of the awl; when advancing forward or retreating backward, the sharp-pointed awl is not seen.

He laughs heartily; within the laughter there is a blade. He cries out "Heaven! again and again; the bow is broken and the arrows are spent. Now tell me: *Note: This is a Zen dialogue concerning the paradox of the "awls" (the two hands and their point).*
Ultimately, how is it? After a long silence, he said: "If one does not cross the bridge together, how can one believe that the bridge flows while the water does not?
Faling Yin said: "Neither of them has understood."
Xiaoyi came to pay his respects to the Master. When the formalities were concluded, the Master asked, "Going on like this, is there still any principle of the Buddha-dharma?
Xiaoyi replied, "I am at a loss for words. The Master said, "And what about me, old monk? Xiaoyi said, "I am certainly no adept.
The Master then leaned back and pressed his palms together; the monk likewise pressed his palms together. The Master then clapped his hands three times.

[The monk] went down. The monk [Baizhang] swept his sleeves and departed. The Master presented this verse: "The crow does not go before; the hare does not follow behind. How many people here run about in bewilderment?

Advancing, he does not go forward; retreating, he does not stay behind. Moving through both the head and tail and the middle, the barbarian monk claps his hands and laughs heartily.
This has never occurred here in this land, nor in the Western Heaven. (Fujian Qín) Entering the forest, he does not stir a blade of grass;
entering the water, he does not ripple a wave. Having already reached the original source, his tongue is tied and there is no further fault.
If you are a seeker from afar, you must grasp the final word (the Great Perfect Wisdom).
Day turns to night; beginning, middle, and end. The golden crow flies; the jade hare runs.
To be utterly bewildered and silent at this point is entirely like a shrimp leaping out of its basket. (The Moon over Stone Creek)
When Master Xiantian of Changsha (successor of Dachuan) was visited by Master Piyun, as soon as he entered the abbot’s quarters, he asked:

"How do you know the moon has fallen into the cold pond? The Master said, "Even this much is hard to find. [The monk] asked, "Is it not when one has not yet seen it?
The Master gave a shout. Yunzhu opened both hands. The Master said, "To falsely accuse others—what limit is there to that?"
Clouds covered his ears as he went forth. The Master said: "This fellow has met his death;
throughout his life, he was accustomed to clear-sightedness and recognized the head of the battle clouds. With both hands he brandished his halberd, fighting without ceasing.
If worldly affairs were judged with impartiality, this general would have returned to be enfeoffed as a marquis. (Juexiangjian)
The makers meet face-to-face, arrow meeting blade; within it, all is dense and compact, not even a breath can pass.
You must cherish your eyebrows well, lest your entire body fall into the weeds.
(From *Zhuyou Jian*) When Xiantian was visited by a monk from Silla, as soon as the monk unfolded his sitting mat, Xiantian seized him and said: "Before you had even departed your own country..."
"Bring me one phrase from the Way. The monk was speechless. The Master then pushed him out, saying, "He asked for one phrase, yet he spoke two.
Guangyin Biao said, "Where are those two phrases spoken by this monk? Can anyone analyze them? Xiantian was struck dumb.
"You failed to discern it; you could not analyze it. You have brought shame upon the Immortal and the Celestial.
Songting Yan said, "Fojian said, 'I see only the sharpness of the chisel's point, but I do not see the squareness of the chisel's head. He could not avoid deliberating over gain and loss.

Dayuan said, 'To sell gold, one must meet the person who buys gold; accept this as a single verdict. Where I, this mountain monk, see it, I wish for all of you to know it together. [He struck the desk.]
Holding up his staff, he said: "The sword that kills, the blade that gives life—let those with eyes discern it.

Even if the physician Lu could raise the dead, who would know that death is final and life never returns? (Sōjaku Shō)
The immortal Xian Tian was about to bow as he entered for audience with the Master. The Master said, "You wild fox cub, what have you seen that you prostrate yourself?

Xiantian said, "Today I have forgotten what came before and lost track of what follows; I say that as long as one attains the moment, one will never compensate for past losses.

The Master said, "How could it not be so? Xiantian asked, "Who would find this sweet? The Master laughed heartily and said, "Far, far indeed! The monk looked around in all directions and then departed.
Gao Feng Miaoyun said: "One question and one answer; there is guest and host. Everyone says both are masters of the Way.
However, according to my own inspection, while that monk is still passable, Xiantian makes people laugh to death."
The wisdom of Marquis Wu and Grand Marshal Zhong is towering and lofty. He seized territory and served the King with but half a cup of wine.
Why was it that the mountains and rivers could not be unified? It was simply because each person relied upon their own extraordinary talent.
(By Fur of Byeon'amsa) When the monk Sŏngchon arrived from Nakpyŏng Hermitage, the Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Namche. The Master said, "Do you still..."

The Master said, "The most painful thing is that which has not yet rested. The monk asked, "Tell me, what is it that has not yet rested?

The Master said, "Once we have met face-to-face, one forgets fame for a thousand years. Luofu shook his sleeves and departed. The Master remarked, "What limit is there to one who possesses the hand that handles a dead snake?"

Xiantian came to pay his respects to the Master. As soon as he spread out his sitting mat, the Master said, "There is no need for greetings;
give me back the principle before patterns and traces had yet appeared. The monk said, "I have a mouth, but it would be fine if it were silenced.

The Master struck him.
Who among the generals could surpass this? It was not easy for the monk Chusan to engage in such refinement. A dragon’s head with a snake’s tail—bow and arrow broken.
Thirty strokes of the black staff were no more than enough. (Benjue I)
When fist and kick correspond, the orthodox and the eccentric each have their own arts; yet alas, at the very end, they fall short, for a single mechanism obscures its own mystery.

The Daoist came forward and prostrated, saying, "I thank the Master for guiding me. The Master struck him.

He then threw down his staff and returned to his quarters.
Guishan Zhe said: "Had it not been for the old fellow Sanping, one would have nearly used intellectual reasoning to cut this matter short.
One does not see that Shigong said, 'For thirty years with a single bow and two arrows, I have shot down only half a sage. Indeed."
The Three Verses on Leveling state: "This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing; there are no further sounds or forms to present to you.
If one understands this point, there is nothing at all; how could essence and function be hindered by being divided or undivided?"
Tiantong Jue said: "Directly meeting, there is no point of contact. The six gates are not closed; the four crossroads are devoid of tracks.
The entire world is radiance; the whole body has no front or back. At such a time, what is it?
When the shuttle-head is unattached to the warp and weft, the patterns run wild and the meaning is naturally distinct."
Sanping asked Dadian, "Do not point east and draw west; I beg the Master to point directly.
Dadian said, "A stone man crouches at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou. The Master said, "That is still pointing east and drawing west.
Dadian said, "If you were a phoenix chick, you would not seek it there. The Master bowed. Dadian said, "Had you not received the latter phrase, the former talk would have been in vain."
Difficult to perfect.
This is the thorough, compassionate heart of a grandmother. Do not seek it from that side; father and son must meet in accord. Without cause, one enters the wild weeds. (Yuánwù Qín)
A monk asked Master Běnkōng of Mǎjié Mountain (who was a dharma successor of Dàdiān Tōng): "Setting aside all present words and phrases, I ask the Master to point directly to the original nature.
The Master said, "How much time has it been since you lost your source? The monk said, "I have now received the Master’s instruction.
The Master said, "If I were to instruct you, I would be the one who has lost my source. The monk asked, "What then is the case?"
The Master presented this verse: "The mind is the essence of nature; nature is the function of the mind. Mind and nature are one and the same—who distinguishes them, who shares in them?
To seek the source outside of delusion is merely to find it difficult to penetrate. From antiquity to the present, ordinary beings and sages alike are like illusions, like dreams."
Fojian Qin said: "The question was not in vain; the answer was not established for nothing. As soon as one follows the turn of the words, ten thousand mountains appear face-to-face.

Although there is gathering and releasing within the subsequent verse, alas, it is marred by the erroneous deployment of names and phrases. I, this mountain monk, shall once again pass judgment on it.
He then offered this verse:

"The mind is fundamentally not mind; its nature is fundamentally not nature. When both mind and nature are forgotten, who is deficient and who is redundant? Aging and decay are fundamentally empty—like applying moxibustion to seek out a disease.
To delude oneself regarding the source by seeking it externally is to betray both the ordinary and the sage."
The nature of the mind has always been one in essence from the beginning; where existence and non-existence are empty, it penetrates the true void.
Those of past and present who wander outside of reality and remain deluded regarding the source—when spring enters the gardens, everything turns red everywhere.
(Tudu Ce) Benkong ascended the hall and said: "In these very activities and movements, can you still accord with the original patriarch? If..."
"It can be attained. There is no principle of wasting even a single moment throughout the twelve hours of the day.
If it cannot be attained, then drinking tea and conversing are often called 'tea-talk' (chàhuà). A monk then asked, 'How can one avoid this so that it does not become mere tea-talk?
The Master said, 'Have you even recognized your own mouth yet? The monk asked, 'What is the mouth? The Master replied, 'Two pieces of skin.'"
He did not understand. [The monk] asked, "What is the original patriarch? The Master said, "Do not rely on your father or mother in front of the assembly.
[The monk] said, "The assembly has departed with joy. The Master said, "Try to point out the nature of the assembly for me."

The monk bowed. The Master said, "He often says that 'one nature is all natures'. As the monk was about to offer a word, the Master said, "You have brought to naught the eyes of your lifelong pilgrimage."
Do not be in a hurry when practicing Chan and studying the Way; every movement and turn is the touch of the Patriarch. Though the mouth is right before the face, it is still not seen;
drinking tea and engaging in clear conversation, the principle is difficult to penetrate. It is like the flavor of salt in water; the glue and blue pigment within color are truly not empty.
If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not use intellectual understanding to slander the ancestral wind. (Nantang Jing)
Chan Master Ben Sheng (Dadian Tongsi) held up his staff and said: "If I lift it up, you immediately apply conceptual reasoning to the time before it was lifted.
If I do not lift it up, you immediately exercise your mastery over the time when it has been lifted."
"Tell me, where does this old monk act for others? A monk stepped forward and said, "I dare not arbitrarily create complications.
The Master said, "I know you, Dharma brother, do not go beyond the bounds. The monk said, "Where it is low, leveling it leaves something remaining;
where it is high, observing it reveals a deficiency. The Master said, "To add complications upon complications. The monk was speechless. The Master [continued]:
[The Master] said: "To cover one's nose while stealing fragrance is to invite only transgression.
Cui Feng Xian said: "This monk is indeed skilled at critical inquiry; yet, alas, his bow is broken and his arrows exhausted.
None of this compares to our own founder, the master of the school. When he raises [his staff], heaven turns and earth revolves; one must simply fold one's hands and surrender."
When one lets go, it is like grass bowing before the wind; one must surely withdraw the entire body to remain far from harm. Do you see where the Original Birth was acting as a human being?
Holding up his staff, he said: "Peace itself was brought about by the generals; yet they were not permitted to witness that peace."
Gunanmen said: "Both Bensheng and Cuifeng were true masters who exerted their full strength for the sake of others.
Yet, alas, they were burdened by too many complications. It would have been better if this monk had cut them off all at once. Why? Have you not heard it said:
'Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind on it long ago, yet until this very day he has not attained the wondrous'? [He] threw down his staff and asked: 'What is this?'"
When Emperor Xianzong welcomed the Buddha’s śarīra into the inner palace for veneration, it emitted a brilliant light at night.

At the morning court audience, the Emperor inquired about this, and all the ministers offered their congratulations, claiming it was a response to the Emperor’s sagely virtue. Only Wen Gong did not offer his congratulations.
The Emperor questioned him, saying, "All the ministers offer their congratulations; why alone do you, Your Excellency, not congratulate me? Wen Gong then replied in a subtle manner: [text truncated]
"I have previously read Buddhist scriptures. Furthermore, the light of the Buddha does not possess characteristics such as blue, yellow, red, or white;

this is merely the light of dragon deities providing protection. When the Emperor asked above, "What is the light of the Buddha? the official had no reply, and was consequently demoted for his offense.

Xuedou Xian spoke on his behalf, saying: "Your Majesty has cast down your celestial discernment from on high. Wanfeng Wei said: "When the Emperor welcomed the Buddha’s śarīra, it manifested light of five colors.
Within the crevice of his eyebrows, it shone through antiquity and rises to the present. Yueyu said: "The Buddha-light is neither blue, yellow, red, white, nor black;
to see it is to fall into deviance. It is a pity that Han Yu failed to provide a response at the end. If one were to ask Mount Songshan about the Buddha: [The text concludes here.]
"Guang, what is it? He then sighed twice. He further composed a verse:
"The Emperor and the Dharma King emit their constant radiance from their mouths; they unify heaven and earth—this land and the Western Realm."

Chan Master Shandao of the Stone Chamber in Tanzhou (a successor of Changzi Kuang) would, whenever he saw a monk approach, simply raise his staff and say, "All Buddhas of the three periods of time are entirely dependent upon this.
Few were able to attain a profound resonance with these words.
When Changsha heard of this, he remarked, "If I were to see him, I would immediately have him put down his staff and convey another message. Sansheng took up this [instruction].
The words were met with a retort. The Master recognized them as the "Longsha" speech. Hearing that Sansheng had missed the mark, Xingshan went personally to Shishi.
Upon seeing him arrive, the Master hid in the rice-pounding room to pound rice. Xingshan said, "It is not easy for an attendant to receive guests; this poor monk finds it difficult to digest.
The Master replied, "A bowl that pierces through the heart will hold what you bring; a bottomless platter shall receive it."
"The child should take it away. Why speak of its being difficult to digest? Xing then desisted.
Zhaojue Qin said, "Shishi set up this point of inquiry; it was indeed solitary and lofty. Had it not been Changsha, how could he have attained the opportune moment?
Nevertheless, they only knew 'it is thus,' but did not know 'it is not thus. He then raised his staff and said, "The past..."
The Buddhas of the past do not act thus; the Buddhas of the present do not act thus; the Buddhas of the future do not act thus.
If you say in general, "I have set down my staff," I know you are merely one who parrots the words of others.
When there is a spark of vital energy, bring forth a single phrase! Tianning Qi, acting on behalf of Xingshan, said: "How can you take the property of the Sangha and put it into your own pocket?"
"Used for the lower part of the robe and bowl. Baoen Xiu said: "One is a cotton-wrapped stone; the other is an iron-encased lump of mud.
To let go is like the *gui* and *zhang* jade vessels in the temple; to hold fast is like the swallows in their hall.
He took up his staff and said: "To be thus is not it; not to be thus is not it either. To put it down or not to put it down—neither is it."
Zhuo struck the desk once and said: "The sky-reaching long sword strikes terror into people with its coldness. Huiyun Cheng, acting on behalf of Xingshan, said:
"Be careful not to let your belly burst from overeating. Tianpei Jian said: "If there had been a true monk at that time who saw such a statement..."
Facing forward, he cried out, "Heaven! Heaven! This left Shishi with a face full of shame, having no place to retreat.
One night, while Shishi and Yangshan were gazing at the moon, Yangshan asked, "When this moon is crescent, where does its round form go?
When it is full, where does its crescent form go? The Master replied, "When it is crescent, the round form is hidden."
"When it is round, the pointed aspect is present.
Yunyan Cheng said, "When it is pointed, the round aspect is present; when it is round, there is no pointed aspect.
Daowu Zhi said, "When it is pointed, it is not pointed; when it is round, it is not round. Buyuan Wu said, "Yangshan is building a pavilion out of thin air."
A stone chamber was constructed on the site to serve as a platform; thus, the single school of Bodhidharma was reduced to nothing more than swept-away dust.
