Guest of the white clouds, companion of the green mountains; within this station, borrow function to observe the mutual exchange. The bottomless platter is held aloft with a turn of the hand;
the heart-piercing bowl is filled with food for the whole body. (Tiantong Jue) When there is a companion, one comes;
earth opens and heaven unfolds. Cold light emerges once more from its sheath; the ancient road is free of even a speck of dust. Myriad phenomena...
The myriad phenomena join their palms; Mount Sumeru dances with its jagged peaks amidst the Three Terraces.
(Seal of the Most Ample) Dongshan visited Weishan and asked, "Recently I heard the story of National Teacher Huizhong regarding 'insentient beings preaching the Dharma.
I have not yet fathomed its subtle meaning. Weishan said, "I have it right here as well, but it is simply rare to meet someone capable of receiving it. The Master said:
The Master requested instruction from him. Guishan said, "The mouth born of one's parents shall never speak for you, my son.
The Master asked, "Are there others who, like me, have long admired the Way? Guishan said, "From here, going toward Lingling, there is a man of the Way at Yunyan.

If you can brush aside the weeds and catch a glimpse of his wind, he will surely be one whom you hold in high esteem. When the Master arrived at Yunyan, he asked: "What is the absence of [duality]? (Note: The text ends abruptly with "Wu").
The Master asked, "When one speaks the Dharma for insentient things, what kind of person can hear it? Yunyan said, "Insentient things can hear it. The Master asked, "Does the Master hear it as well?
Yunyan said, "If I were to hear it, you would not be hearing me speak the Dharma. The Master asked, "Why is it that I do not hear it?
Yunyan held up his whisk and said, "Do you hear it now? The Master said, "I do not hear it. Yunyan said, "I..."
"You have not even heard the Dharma being preached by sentient beings; how much less so the preaching of the Dharma by insentient things?
The Master asked, "In what scriptures does the preaching of the Dharma by insentient things appear? Yunyan replied, "Have you not seen it said in the *Amitābha Sūtra*:

'The waterfowl and the trees all recite the Buddha's name and the Dharma'? The Master attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "How wondrous! How wondrous! The preaching of the Dharma by insentient things!"
Inconceivable! If one listens with the ears, it will ultimately be difficult to understand; only by hearing sound with the eyes can one truly know.
Xueqiao Xin said: "How extraordinary! How extraordinary! The insentient preaching the Dharma is inconceivable.

In the space of a finger-snap, the stone tiger bites and kills the green-field rooster. Xiaoweng Ying remained silent for a long while and then said: "Lianfeng goes to imitate her [the beauty's] frown."
"How truly marvelous! How truly marvelous! The insentient preaching the Dharma is inconceivable. A wooden ladle leaps into a water bucket;
it bites into the handle of a fan with a creaking sound. I ask the assembly: what is this news? Suddenly, he gave a sneeze and said: "Achoo!"
Today I have caught a cold. When the insentient preaches the Dharma, the sentient listen; when the sentient preach the Dharma, the insentient depart. This is not a casual or empty interpretation:
the mountains, rivers, and great earth are far too talkative. Every person possesses that which is non-corresponding; the pillar and the lantern face toward it.
"Speak! (Daguai Zhi). "Excellent!
The myriad phenomena are all treasures; every thing and every object manifests the family jewels.
To those who do not recognize them, they are but weeds. (Nantang Jing).
Dongshan took his leave of Yunyan. Yunyan said, "After this parting, it will be difficult for us to meet again.
The Master said, "After this parting, it will be difficult for me not to see you, Reverend."
High and lofty, the solitary peak shrouded in mist; beyond the kalpas, the path of concealment and manifestation is impassable.
At midnight, the message turns at the mountain pass; it has nothing to do with spring colors, yet the dark fragrance is thick.

(Zhengtang Bian) A crane emerges from its silver cage and soars into the azure firmament; the phoenix has no place to perch, and the well-locust tree stands empty. Though the Lord of the East may possess two eyes, [he cannot see].
My son, you have not yet beheld the eight-colored eyebrows of Yao.
(Lingtong) Dongshan was about to take his leave of Yunyan. As he was departing, Dongshan asked, "If, after a hundred years, someone were to ask me, 'Can you paint a true likeness of the Master?
how would you respond? Yunyan remained silent for a long while and then said, "It is just this. The Master hesitated; Yunyan said:

"Venerable Upādhyāya, in undertaking this matter, you must be extremely careful. The Master was still beset by doubt. Later, while crossing water, he beheld his reflection and attained great enlightenment.
He spoke a verse, saying: "One must by all means avoid seeking it from others; It remains far removed and estranged from me. Now I go forth alone; Everywhere I encounter It.
It is now precisely myself; I am no longer It. He should... [The text continues with further verses.]
One must understand it in this way; only then can one accord with suchness.
Its essence and measure are beyond effort and do not fall into the present. Though the stars shift and the constellations change, how could they be like a revolving wheel?
Though the calendars of many years are of no use, should one offend against them, the entire lineage shall surely be extinguished. (Zhengtang Bian)
The merit of the earth is such that the state acknowledges him as a subject; yet, without the authority over even a foot of soil or a single person, he returns his entire being to his father.

(Tan Jiren) To see the reflection is to meet the person, yet it is not the person itself. Upon arriving home, why need one send a letter via wild geese? The morning breeze blows through the plum blossoms.
A dream: fragrant mist lightly moistens the antennae of the powdered butterflies; the moon ascends the pearl curtains. It is exactly midnight.
At dawn, the jade water-clock announces the passing of the watch. Before the window, the Qin mirror leaves no trace of foxes; in the forbidden palace, there is no one—dare anyone dare to trespass?
(By Baiyu Si) The Cowherd and the Weaver Maid gaze at one another, separated by only a few paces across the Milky Way. Tonight, there are no clouds to part them.
Severed. When seeing it, it remains as it was; its appearance is distinct at another time.
(Dufanguo) Clearly, the news reveals the total mechanism. A divine light ten thousand feet tall shines from behind the head.
Cast aside both "this" and "that. In the third month of Jiangnan, the partridges cry. (Yunchanghan)
Jade trees cast long shadows over the gates of the golden hall; green lattices and blue locks encircle the traces of incense. Since time immemorial, no one has seen the Wheel-Turning King;
though the precious seal is not displayed, his majesty remains all the more sublime.

(Ning of Lishan) For many years I have wandered like a gourd, lying amidst the deep clouds. Amidst intoxication, I hear the golden pipes and silver flutes. In the autumn colors, I once again roam beneath the mountain.
On the road, by the marshy banks where white artemisia grows, I have encountered you.
(Zha’an Fan) The primal breath is still and the universe is vast; as black and white first diverge, a single path appears subtle.
Treading upon and shattering the shadows of the void before the kalpa, the heavens and seas leave no ground for established rules. (Zudeng Shao)
Dongshan later enshrined Yunyan’s portrait. A monk asked, "The former master said, 'It is just this.
Is it not so? The Master said, "It is. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "At that time, I nearly misunderstood the former master's intent.
The monk asked, "I wonder if the former master was aware of this or not? The Master said, "If he were not aware of it, how could he have spoken thus?"
The Way. If one knew it existed, how could one be willing to speak thus?
Changqing Ling said: "Since you know it exists, why do you speak thus? He also said: "Only when raising a child does one come to know a father's compassion."
Who would dare speak thus? At the fifth watch, the rooster cries and the home-grove dawns. Who would be willing to speak thus? For a thousand years, the crane and the green pine grow old together.
The precious mirror is clear and bright, testing the orthodox and the biased; the jade mechanism turns and shifts, observing both simultaneously.
The gate-style is greatly stirred, and its measured steps are continuous; father and son transform and flow through, their fame and light vast and grand. (Tiantong Jue)
It cannot be described, nor can it be painted. The evening sky is vast and empty—how could this be mere human sentiment?
Mad monkeys howl as the mid-autumn moon turns; from afar, a solitary peak stands alone as clouds drift across it.

(By Gyeongok Hyeon) The ways of the world are vast and boundless, and the fish and wild geese have gone silent. One must rely entirely on the mute to deliver the message. When meeting people, do not speak even a fraction of it.
[The Master] said: "In the end, there is no heart of resentment. (At Ningyuan) Dongshan ascended the hall and said:
"There is a person among a thousand or ten thousand people who does not turn his back on anyone, nor does he face anyone.
Tell me, what kind of countenance does this person possess? Yunju Ying stepped forward and said: "I, this humble one, shall attend the hall."
"Go. Under "Zifu is vast; what face would he have? it says: "Seven concavities and eight convexities. Under "Entering the Hall," it says:
"He has only attained a single peg. It further says: "The Hall of Vacant Whiteness opens; the pearl curtain hangs. Facing every direction without partiality—those who recognize this [will see it]."
Who is it that can withdraw with such swift ease? Yet even so, it remains difficult to join companions for a common return. Thus, what was the ultimate intent of Dongshan?
"The golden needle and double lock are both prepared; the narrow path conceals the whole. Muan said: "To see Dongshan is easy;
to see Yunju is difficult. What is the ultimate point? Several tall bamboos stand before the window.
Green. Several peach trees reflect their redness upon the water.
When a monk asked Dōngshān, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? the Master replied, "A single stalk of thatch after the fire."
When burned by wild fires, it becomes ever more new; even now its smoke and flames cannot be quenched by rain. Red lotuses on dry land obscure the sun and moon;
rootless trees grow tall, their verdant leaves forming shade.
(Touzi Qing) The spring breeze blows, stirring the green waves to sway; countless boatmen follow the ocean tides. One sees only the river gulls flying white.
Waves! How could one know the bright moon is in the clouds and sky? (Kumu Cheng) Skillful response follows the current;
the wondrous meaning is profound. Clearly, a single arrow hits the red heart. This was not the eye of Yi Ji facing the fray;
before one’s face, the Iron Mountain rises ten thousand fathoms high. (Fozhi Yu)

Dongshan addressed the assembly: "At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, when you brothers go east or west, you must go to a place ten thousand *li* away where there is not a single inch of grass.
He further asked, "But how does one go to such a place where there is not a single inch of grass ten thousand *li* away?
Later, Shishuang said, "Stepping out the door, it is all grass. A monk reported this to the Master [Dongshan], who said, "Great!"
"How many people can there be within the land of Tang?
Dayang Xuan said, "Even if one does not step out of the gate, it is still a sea of weeds. Tell me, where should one go and what should one practice?
Do not linger by the cold crags where strange weeds turn green; sitting amidst white clouds, the essence of the school is not yet perfected. — Yuan (Complete)
Tongshan said: "Everyone, how would you express the phrase right beneath your heels at this very moment?
If you say, 'Ten thousand miles, not an inch of grass,' I allow you to have seen Dongshan. If you say, 'Stepping out the door is already grass,' I allow you to have seen Shishuang.
If you say, 'Even not stepping out the door is a vast expanse of grass,' I allow you to have seen Dayang."
"In general, one cannot speak of it. Yet, I grant you that you have seen Yansheng. Why? 'Only a fine breeze comes upon the mat;
no idle words fall into the human world. Baizhang Yuan said: "If you see the Hermitage Master, you see Dongshan.
If you see Dongshan, you see the Hermitage Master. It is easy to see Dongshan, but it is difficult to see the Hermitage Master."
This is difficult; one does not see the Way. "The clouds atop the ridge have no leisure; the water at the bottom of the ravine is too busy.
Guishan said, "Chopping nails and cutting iron; opening wide the profound barrier above. His words are true and his speech sincere;
he points directly to the essential path for people. But how do you understand it? 'As soon as he goes out the door, there is grass. Thus did Shishuang speak.
Shangfeng spoke thus: "None of you must touch it; if you do, you shall receive thirty blows. Jingshan Gao said:
"A single drop of a lion’s milk scatters ten bushels of donkey’s milk. Xueyan Man said:
"Although these three old fellows speak with one voice, they cannot avoid bumping heads and knocking foreheads. Why? Because one of them has opened his mouth."
They cannot be joined. One person has raised their foot high and cannot put it down; another has bolted the door shut and cannot get out. Wángshān was not like this:
throughout the ten directions there is nothing that is external; everything is entirely within a single mote of dust.
Within a single mote of dust there is nothing that is internal; yet it pervades the ten directions. This mere mote of dust must be exhausted to the very limit, for even that cannot be found.
"Facing that place, one installs the gate; where does one enter the grass? Do you understand? Cease encroaching upon the autumn grasses of Dongling;

please look at the lotus of Shushan in midwinter. Gushan Xian said: "Dongshan speaking in this manner is much like a phoenix of auspicious virtue not perching on common trees, or a golden dragon not remaining in a cold pool. It is turning function into position, and turning position into function."
The merit is not non-existent; yet, upon examination, it is merely like a monkey climbing a tree, abandoning one thing to grasp another—it is not the work of a master.
Furthermore, what is the place of the fundamental allotment? After a long silence, he said: "The fishing boat has reached the banks of the Xiao and Xiang rivers;
stifled by breath and weary, I ask the white gulls. Baizhang Xue said: "I, this mountain monk, am not so. Brothers," [he continued].
"Going east, going west—you must go directly to where flames burst forth from the frozen river. But as for that place where flames burst forth from the frozen river, how does one go there?
After a long silence, he said: "The rabbit-horn staff carries the sun and moon; the tortoise-hair rope binds empty space. Lingyin Li said:
"Dongshan only knew how to clarify the position by borrowing function; how could he have known that moss grows upon the Jade Palace?"
Although Shishuang was able to shift positions and seize the opportune moment, he had not yet returned to the path to restore the subtle mystery.

Even if one were to simultaneously advance in both function and position—like mushrooms sprouting from rotten wood—or simultaneously conceal both function and position—like snow freezing a red furnace—the Buddha-Sun must still ask:
how does one proceed toward that place where five horses do not neigh and a single ox does not drink?
Stepping out the gate, one is utterly bewildered; ten thousand miles away, nothing has come, nor is anything yet complete.
If you wish to know the path leading from the gate back to your home mountain, the evening smoke lightly locks it in a vast expanse of green.
(Fohuiquan) Before the courtyard, yellow leaves fall in chaotic profusion; beneath the steps, patches of moss resemble patterns of brocade. Let the wild grasses outside the door grow as they will.
Green. A stone man treads upon the clouds of the sea-mountains. (Jingyin Cheng) Grass stretches on and on;
look for yourself at what is inside the gate and outside the gate. It is easy to set foot within a thicket of brambles, but difficult to turn one’s body beyond the curtain of night-brightness.
Look, look—how many kinds there are! For now, follow the old trees in their shared cold and emaciation; soon, you shall go forth with the spring breeze.

Entering the scarred burn site—(Tiantong Jue)—the void and mysterious bird-path is cut off from even the finest speck of dust; the jade palace is empty, locked with green moss. The shuttle hangs on the wall as it flies through the autumn;
the aged oysters of the vast blue sea all harbor embryos within. (Zu’an Jian)
I see you off on a single horse out from the Imperial Capital; You will tread across the desolate wilds where not a blade of grass remains.
Once you have passed beyond the Great Unity Pass, He will return to you the numinous talisman tucked behind his elbow.
(Yinyuan Qi) Dongshan gave this instruction: "Only those who know there is one above the Buddha have a share in the discourse. A monk asked, "How is it?"
"This Buddha is a person above [the ordinary].
The Master said, "Not a Buddha. Baofu Zhan said, "A Buddha is not [this]. Yunmen Wenyan said, "He cannot be named; he cannot be described; that is why it is called 'not'.
Fayan Wenyi said, "It is a provisional designation called 'Buddha. Tiantong Juexian said, "These two venerable elders..."

"How much has been removed? It is simply like the characters '刁' and '刀', or the confusion between '魚' and '魯'. Reaching this point, one must employ a mechanism beyond kalpas and release an arrow before the wind.
Only by possessing such an eye can one take full responsibility with a horizontal body and accept the task with hands cast loose.
Can you discern it? It is easy to distinguish snow from powder, but difficult to distinguish soot within ink. Jingshan Gaofeng said: "The Two Honored Ones..."
"Venerable sir, you have been maintaining this 'matter above the Buddha' for so long; let us proceed slowly. I, however, am not like that.
What is the matter above the Buddha? [I] would simply seize my staff and strike him across the spine, sparing him from hiding and evading within the realm of the Buddha."
Baoneng Xiu said: "I would like to ask Dongshan: Does one who is above the Buddha still have a portion for answering questions?
Dongming Ji, having finished citing Yunmen’s words, said: "Great as Yunmen was, he still held such a view.
Had I been there at that time, I would simply have let out a cold laugh."
A monk once asked Dongshan, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master replied, "It is much like the 'shock-of-the-cock' rhinoceros horn. Jiacao said:
"Drawing the precious sword horizontally, he cuts away the spirits of the bamboo and trees; grasping the dark pearl in his palm, he illuminates the entire realm of Zhongzhou and Chixian.
This credit belongs to our ancient ancestor Dongshan. As for the great significance of the Buddha-dharma, this distant descendant does not dare to speak."
"Following what is not right yet making it appear lustrous—why is this? If one were a child of the phoenix, would they ever seek it elsewhere?
Dongshan wrote the character "Buddha" (佛) on a fan; when Yunyan saw it, he wrote the character "not" (不) over it. The Master (Dongshan) then changed it to the character "wrong" (非).
When Xuefeng saw this, he removed them all at once.
Xinghua Jang spoke on his behalf, saying, "I am not as good as you. Baiyang Shun said, "If I were Dongshan, I would simply say to Xuefeng, 'You are not of my kinsmen.
Tianbei Yuan said, "Dongshan and Yunyan have raised a mound out of level ground;
the old fellow Xuefeng gained wisdom through this event. Zhigu Sheng said, "A character is changed after three transcriptions—how can one avoid becoming a crow?"

Thus is the horse completed; this is what is meant by the two venerable elders. Although Xuefeng was skilled at following the red and filling in the ink, it cannot be said that he was not right under Deshan’s gate;
yet under Dongshan’s gate, one still remains separated by a ford. Why? Because they are like the *Zhou* script of Grand Historian Shi and the regular script of the Two Wangs.
A monk asked Dongshan, "When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them? The Master said, "Why do you not go to a place where there is neither cold nor heat?
The monk asked, "What is the place where there is neither cold nor heat? The Master said, "When it is cold, let the cold kill you;
when it is hot, let the heat kill you."
Touzi said, "Tongyun, you are almost going that way. Later, Langye Huijue remarked, "Go into the Sangha Hall.
Yunju Shun said, "Langye, great as he was, made such a show of coming and going. As for this mountain monk, it is not so."
"What is the place where there is neither cold nor heat? "In the three months of winter, one faces the warm fire;
in the nine months of summer, one takes the cool breeze. Baofeng Wen said: "If you all can understand this, you may freely exercise your spiritual powers;
at all times, cold and heat will not interfere with you. If you cannot understand it, then simply pass through the winters and summers within the realm of cold and heat."—Huanglong Xin.
Yun said: "Dongshan strikes at the collar from the sleeve; he digs out the lapel from under the arm. Yet this monk could not bear it.
Now, suppose someone comes forward and asks Huanglong—how would you deal with him? After a long silence, he said: "For practicing meditation, one need not necessarily seek mountains and waters;
extinguish the fire in your heart and you will be cool of your own accord. Shangfeng Cai remarked: "Dongshan’s single phrase can truly be called..."
Host and guest intermingle; the orthodox and the deviant intersect. Where do you all turn to avoid this now?
When there is nothing to do, go up the mountain and take a stroll. I ask you, people: do you understand? Letang Zhun said:
"When acting for others, even ice is warm; when not acting for others, even fire is cold. Yangshan Qin said: "Although Dongshan..."
"Head straight, tail straight—this is simply because the nostrils have fallen into the hands of this monk. Wushi said, "Dongshan possesses only the sword that kills;
he lacks the sword that gives life. Suppose someone were to ask, "When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them?
He would also say, "Why not go to a place where there is neither cold nor heat? But where is that place where there is neither cold nor heat?
He said to him, "When it is cold, I burn you to death, O teacher; when it is hot, I freeze you to death, O teacher. Why is this? 'In the three winters, the heat blazes;
in the nine summers, the snowflakes fly. Qinghua Yan said, "The old man Dongshan was like one handing over the *maṇi* jewel-king directly to an ordinary person.
Had that monk had any sinew in his eyes, he would not have been withered by the three winters alone."
Exquisite as a tree in full bloom. Training and guiding throughout the nine months of summer, snowflakes fly;
with hands hanging down, he is like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. Why must the "Correct" and the "Deviant" be contrived?
In the ancient palace of lapis lazuli, the bright moon shines; yet the clever dog merely paws at the steps in vain. (Cui Feng Xian)
There is no place free from cold and heat; how can one sing and respond [to them]? When hot, seek the cool; when cold, turn toward the fire.
You talkative old master—what a display of shamelessness! Everyone wishes to escape the ordinary stream, yet in the end they return to sit within the coals.
(Quandao) Look within: there is neither heat nor cold. Directly beneath, the vast ocean is drained dry. I say that even the giant tortoise can bow its head.
I laugh at you, playing with your hook and line on the sandy shore.

(Tiantong Jue) When hot, it kills with heat; when cold, it kills with cold. Cold and heat have never been of any concern. Having traveled to the ends of the earth, one understands the ways of the world;
the old man wears a hat made of mulberry bark. (Zantang Zhun)

Seeking refuge from heat and fleeing the cold, they inquire about right and wrong; yet few know that one does not depart from cold and heat. Coming forth from the very center, there is no turning back or evasion;
within these words the blade is concealed, and those who can discern it are rare. A snowy day in the midst of summer; fire-clouds fly.
Blown by the wind and scorched by the sun, O Dujie Li (Yeshu Chuan).
The bell at the painted pavilion has subsided behind the bright gauze curtain; the *wú-tóng* trees faintly reflect the slanting crescent of the moon.
The jade-dreams of the *hái-táng* blossoms lie in disarray; the wind strikes the moored boat, raising spray upon the waves.

(Sānyí Yú) At the reed-bay, the fishing boat rests amidst the clear blue waters; drinking alone by the Xiāng River, I gaze upon the bright moon. Dewdrops fall upon the *fú-róng* lotuses as human traces fade away.
Mysterious. The flute is blown at midnight, its name unknown. (Zhà'ān Fàn) Brilliantly responding to the vital energy, it leaves no lingering sentiment.
Brightness and darkness intermingle as killing and giving life proceed. At dawn, the green ridges open to reveal the face of the red sun;
in the wind, white artemisia drifts as the fishing boat lies athwart. (Wèizhōng Fú)
Dongshan was once asked by a monk, "Among the three bodies, which one does not follow the count? The Master said, "I have always been most earnest about this.
Later, someone took this question to Caoshan and asked, "The late master said, 'I have always been most earnest about this. What does that mean?"
Cao said, "If you want my head, cut it off. He then asked Xuefeng, who struck him with his staff and said, "I too have been to Dongshan.
Chengtian Zong said: "One turn of phrase brings peace to the seas and clarity to the rivers; another turn of phrase leaves the wind high and the moon cold. One...
"Tell me, who would ride the thief’s horse to pursue the thief? Try to discern this for me.
Suddenly, if a monk comes forth and says, "It is not like this at all," one might grant him that he possesses a single eye. Jingshan Daowei said:
"With such entanglements as these, you have not yet dreamed of those three old fellows. He added: "Why not apply a needle to the *gāohuáng* (the vital point between the heart and diaphragm)?"
Boshan Lai said: "Nearby, one may not lean upon it; distant, one may not carry it away. Pushed, it does not move forward; pulled, it does not retreat.
To Dongshan, this was like an iron stake. As for those who discern rare treasures, gather dragon pearls, seek out uncut jade, or pursue lapis lazuli—how could they ever speak of this?
One must transcend words and phrases; only then can one truly encounter it. —Ji’an
Lü said: "When these three great elders speak in this manner, although each displays their own strengths, it is still like ink staining a black robe at the end of the night.
What is the ultimate meaning? I have always been earnest about this: when the clouds disperse, the mid-autumn moon shines."
"I must take off his head. Of the three eyes of Maheśvara, one is upright. "I too have come from Dongshan.
Before the courtyard, the iron saw dances the Three Terraces. Bian-shan analyzes it thus; tell me, is there still a way for him to benefit others?
He plants his staff and lets out a shout, saying: "Holding a night-bright talisman in hand, how many know the dawn? — Guangyin Biao
It is said: "These three old fellows are held together by a single hand; their sincere hearts are laid bare, much like the treasure sword of Fengcheng being hurled right before one's face.
Yet those who recognize this kindness are few. This monk was not only deaf but also blind;
he missed the opportunity at Dangyang. Is there anyone now who does not miss it? "Who can recognize the Magistrate who closed the gate? On the riverbank..."
The immortal elder has gone and does not return. Shouchang Qi said: "I have always been earnest about this.
A girl with horned hair has missing teeth; if you want her head, chop it off and take it away. Inauspicious matters are avoided by all under heaven.
I too once went to Dongshan, yet I was not willing to bury my body in one place. Today I clearly raise it up again for you: the cuckoo cries, urging the plowing."
In the deep trees, every cry urges the farmers to their toil as blood flows; do not wait until autumn arrives and the official levies are scarce.
Not entering the world, not following conditions—when the kalpa-vessel is empty, there is a family tradition. White arums, a gentle breeze, the evening on the autumn river.
A single band of smoke as the boat returns to the ancient shore.
(Tiantong Jue) The jade whip is raised and heaven and earth are stilled; the Imperial Way is impartial, manifesting supreme dignity.
When the imperial carriage points its direction, the General’s strict command allows for no exception. (Zhengtang Bian)
I have often been pressed by this matter; it is both laughable and tragic that I must speak of it to you. Wherever the oriole sings, the warm breeze arises;
yet upon the traveler’s brow, the snow of sorrow does not melt away. The willow brows are fine, the flower-like countenance is joyful, and fragrance wafts beyond the clouds at this season.
(Yuan’an Yun)

The profound secrecy of the Ninefold Palace is difficult to fathom; who would dare approach the Sacred Countenance with even a hint of negligence? A single scroll of vermilion writ emerges, borne by the Phoenix;
the myriad phenomena of the universe vie with one another to pay homage to Heaven.

(Ningyuan District) Amidst the sound of the quiet whip, the imperial carriage approaches; looking out in all directions, clouds of incense reach the upper dais. As the imperial carriage turns within the deep palace, the intimacy is palpable.
[The Master] was at [a place]. Following the teachings, his martial prowess was utterly crushed. (This refers to Jian-sou.
When Dongshan was about to take leave of Ping of Xingshan in Jingzhao, Ping asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "Following the current, there is no fixed destination.
Ping said, "Is it the Dharmakāya following the current, or the Saṃbhogakāya following the current? The Master said, "I do not interpret it in either of those ways."
Shennan patted his hands.
Baofu unfolded his arms and said, "Dongshan has his own separate house," and then spoke differently: "How many people have you found?
Weizhi Kai said, "If one were not striking the water with three thousand [feet] or gathering the wind at ninety thousand [li], it would not be easy to answer this question. As for..."
Xingshan clapped his hands, saying, "This is reward; this is punishment.
Dongshan, because of an old master who held up the corner of his *kāṣāya* and asked, "Was there this [nature] even before one's parents were born?
the Master said, "Is it not present right now? The old master shook his head.
Shifting positions to seize the opportune moment is even more difficult to find; returning to the source is again wondrous—how could it be merely conventional?
At the mouth of the Xinfeng Cave, waves surge and roll; one must sweep them away until they are dried up to the very bottom.
(Zhengtang Bian) A monk, while ill in the Yanshou Hall, wished to see the Master. The Master then went to him. The monk said:
“Master, why do you not save the sons and daughters of others? The Master said, “What kind of sons and daughters of others are you?
He replied, “I am the son and daughter of a family of great icchantikas. After a long silence, the monk asked, “When the four mountains close in, what then?
The Master said, “I, this old monk, have also once passed beneath the eaves of a house. The monk said, “To turn back? The Master said, “To turn back.”
"Are they mutually interpenetrating or not? The Master said, "They are not mutually interpenetrating. The monk asked, "Where should I, this disciple, go?
The Master said, "Go into the midst of the parched grain fields. The monk let out a single sigh and said, "Take care," whereupon he sat down and passed away.
The Master struck his head three times with his staff and said, "You only know how to go like that; you do not know how to come back like this."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Generally speaking, for a traveler on foot, the most essential thing is precisely to achieve a state of total transcendence.

Since this monk was already a man or woman from a family of great icchantikas, until the four mountains pressed in upon him and his hands and feet were in a frantic scramble, had it not been for Dongshan possessing great compassion and letting out a 'thread of the Way' to provide him with a level ground, how could he have ever gone forth in such a manner?"

Therefore, the ancients said: "At the moment of death, if even a single hair’s breadth of dualistic thought regarding sagehood or ordinariness has not been exhausted, one cannot avoid entering the womb of a donkey or the belly of a horse.
It is just as Dongshan said: "I have also passed beneath the eaves of people's houses and into their fields of millet.
The cauldrons obstruct the four mountains; they do not obstruct the four mountains. At this point, one must truly be like a bucket.
Only when the foundation is stripped away can one attain it. But tell me, what was Dongshan’s intention? The golden rooster pecks through the lapis lazuli egg;
the jade hare pushes open the gates of the azure sea.
Only understanding how to go thus: "Sandbirds nest by night in the trees of the azure isles. Not understanding how to come thus: "The stone sprout pierces through the moss of the ancient path.
Do not say that the *kūṇī* and *jīng* have no wings; today I have personally returned from the bird-path.

(Tiantong Jue) When holy measure and ordinary sentiment are both exhausted, there is no road for turning back, yet the matter remains non-existent. Passing beneath the eaves of the house, one traverses the millet fields.
Inside. A single path through the belly of a horse and the womb of a donkey.

(Moon over Shixi) It is easy to ascend high with level steps; it is difficult to let go from the void. If, indeed, the holy and the ordinary are swept away like a flash of lightning, how could going and staying be mutually related?
Clouds unfurl and roll across the horizon; the moon waxes and wanes over the vast waves. All the private belongings within one's eyes have been washed clean.
All is exhausted; the pure breeze reaches the eight directions as he walks with ease.

(Ascending the Heavenly Shore) Within the grain fields and terraced fields, his departure is perfectly clear. He strides freely through the forest of swords and mountains of knives. Do not let the snow and moon cause you to lose sight of their single color.
Secretly shifting the misty boat, he ascends the sandy islet. (Peaceful and Remote Ground)
A monk asked Dongshan, "If one wishes to see the Master’s original teacher, how can this be seen?
The Master said, "If our years and teeth are similar, there will be no obstruction. As the monk was about to offer a reply, the Master said, "Do not follow the previous track;
ask another question. The monk was speechless.
Yunju Deng, acting on behalf of a monk, said: "If that is so, then you do not see the Master’s original teacher.
Changqing was asked by a monk: "What is it that resembles the teeth of a year-old calf? Changqing said: "The ancients spoke thus;
what else would you seek here, O *śrāmaṇera*?"
The curtains rolled up, he sat amidst the azure peaks on his double-wheeled seat. His entire being was unadorned by the garment of original nature.
As the dewdrops fell upon the lotuses and the autumn fragrance faded, he felt ashamed to raise his slender brows in response to the setting sun.
(Pingxiang) Once, while Dongshan and Head Seat Tai were eating fruit during the winter festival, Dongshan asked: "There is a thing that reaches upward..."
"O Heaven! It hangs down to support the earth; it is black as lacquer. It is constantly within the midst of movement and function, yet it cannot be grasped within that movement and function.
Tell me, where does the fault lie? Tai replied, "The fault lies within movement and function. The Master then called his attendant and had him remove the fruit table.
Wuzu Ke said: "Tomorrow morning, offer it again for the King of Chu to see. Tongan Xian, regarding the phrase "Where does the fault lie?", said:
"I do not know. Langye Jue said: "If it were not for the old man Dongshan, how could he have discerned this?
Nevertheless, even so, there is still one move missing. Weishan Zhe said: "Do you all understand?"
As for Dongshan’s point of arrival—if you do not know it, you will likely interpret it in terms of right and wrong, gain and loss. This old monk says:
this fruit is not only something the Head Seat may not eat; even if all the people in the entire world were to come, they would not be able to look upon it with a correct eye.
Yungai Ben said: "Although Dongshan possesses the tongs and hammer for shattering empty space, he lacks..."
This is a means of patching up [the teaching]. Waiting for him to pass through it while it is in active use, he simply says, "Please, Head Seat, eat some fruit.
If Head Seat Tai were a true monk, even after eating it, he would have to spit it out. Guo of Mt. Mushi said:
Dongshan treats the worthy as lowly; the Head Seat has no way to vindicate his reason. This mountain monk, seeing such injustice on the road, wishes to clear his grievance.
At that time, had I seen him ask such a question, I would have simply said: "The prediction at Vulture Peak has not yet reached this point."
While he was about to deliberate, [Dongshan] took up a fruit and hurled it straight at his face.
Not only did this block the throat, but it spared later generations from giving rise to groundless conjectures. Jingci Chang said:
"Although Dongshan withdrew the fruit table, he nonetheless could not block the mouth of the Head Seat Tai. Zhaojue Qin said: "Everyone says that the Head Seat Tai’s arrowhead was sharp."
They do not support one another; this is why they met with Dongshan’s censure and stripping away.
Later, Master Zhao of Mount Gui said, "As for this fruit, let alone the Head Seat being unable to eat it—no one in the entire world would even dare to look at it directly.

When the true command of a master is put into effect, the ten directions are cut off; there is a phrase that settles heaven and earth, an eye that distinguishes dragons from snakes—this is truly difficult.
[The Master] said, "At that time, had he been a truly spirited monk capable of pulling a tiger’s whiskers, when [the Master] asked, 'Where does the fault lie?
he would have picked up the fruit and said, 'What, after all, do you call this, Reverend Father? Waiting for him to hesitate, he would have thrown it straight at his face.
Why? Because when one has spirit, one adds to that spirit; where there is no elegance, one creates elegance."
Baoning Moshan said, "Everyone says that Dongshan saw only the sharpness of the chisel's tip, but did not see the squareness of the chisel's head.
Why do you suppress and distort people so? Others say that Master Tai did not get to eat the fruit; however, if he could not, then no one in the entire world could eat it either.
Those who succeed are few, while those who ruin others are many. Yet they fail to realize that Dongshan possesses the turning of the biased and the correct."
They do not infringe upon one another’s footing. Even if you say it does not reside within active functioning, you still cannot eat his fruit.
After a long silence, he said: "Where do the flowing waters and yellow leaves come from? A cow with crows perched upon it passes through a distant village.
Gunanmen said: "To see Dongshan is easy; to see Head Seat Tai is difficult."
Who among us does not have a share of Dongshan’s fruit? To withdraw the tray was a wondrous turning of the pivot.
Tonight, for your sake, I shall lightly break it open: a sleeping cat beneath a peony flower.
(By Mingji Zu) Dongshan brought disgrace upon his family tradition; the Head Seat buried his own self. A pair of mandarin ducks are embroidered together, a marvel for all ages.
Unable to support it. (Yuan’an Yan) It supports heaven and earth, black as lacquer. Day and night indistinguishable—what thing is this?
Picked up and cast into a pit of filth, the lotus flower in the fire wafts its fragrance. (Xutang Yu)
On the return journey, he again wondrously displays his full capacity; his great function is majestic and beyond all command.
Grasped with both hands, it is entirely of one color; at midnight, the golden sun soars through the heavens.
(Falin Yin) Dongshan asked a monk, "Which one is your true master? The monk replied, "The one currently responding to you. The Master said:
"Alas, alas! In these times, all people are like this. They take only those who follow behind the donkey or the horse to be themselves;
that the Buddha-dharma is sinking is a sign of this. If one has not yet clarified the 'host within the guest,' how much less so the 'host within the host'?
A monk asked, 'What is the host within the host? The Master said, 'Disciple, speak for yourself.'"
[The student] said, “When I say ‘So-and-so,’ that is merely the guest within the host. What is the host within the host? The Master said, “To speak thus is easy;
to maintain continuity is very difficult. He then presented this verse: “Alas, I see the practitioners of the Way nowadays, Countless millions who only recognize the gate.
They are just like those entering the capital to pay court to the Holy Sovereign, Who have reached no further than the Tongguan Pass.”
Stop! Guest among guests, with brows unknit and eyes devoid of muscle, you toil in foreign lands seeking a true friend, yet you have lost the priceless treasure within your robes. (Fushan Yuan)

The Guest within the Host: Exerting all one’s strength to seek him, no location can be found. In years past, there was still something of him to be seen; today, who knows, for his eyes are both blind? The Host within the Guest:
My house is vast and expansive, truly difficult to describe. In what is sought, there is no stinginess, nor is there high or low; noble and base are one and the same.
The path is level and smooth;
he is the Lord among Lords. His golden palace is adorned with the seven treasures without deficiency, and a thousand sons constantly surround his holy countenance.
When the various heavens do not submit, he raises his wheel of power.
A lifetime of concerns knotted into my brow; dust flies across my face as my hair turns autumn-gray.
In truth, I have no skill for venturing forth; alas, today’s road is poor and filled with sorrow.
(Hongzhi Jue IV) Day after day I trade for profits of ten thousand gold; at dawn, I seek news of home upon the ancient path. Clearly, I have received word from my venerable parents.
How steadfast! Alas, it is difficult to rely upon hearts of joy and fear.
As the bugles blow atop the palace towers and the six streets are bright, the General of the Golden Horse emerges from the Forbidden City. His authority beyond the borders is truly well-established;
he does not harm social customs, and thus there is natural peace and prosperity.

The Immovable Golden Wheel possesses the fullness of ten thousand virtues; upon the imperial throne, moss has grown thick as the court ranks have not yet assembled. The tabooed name at the head is forbidden throughout the realm;
who would dare to approach it with even a hint of transgression against the Sacred Countenance?
Wandering to the ends of the earth through many springs, my studies have been in vain and my merits have brought only increasing poverty.
Though I have traversed the vast depths of the ocean of practice, the sky of ultimate meaning is so expansive that it admits no dust.

(Discerning the Four from Qingzhou) With tattered robes and emaciated bones, nothing remains but bare skin; alone he stabilizes the realm, radiating the light of primordial antiquity. Within the three-foot scabbard, he executes the treacherous.
A sword; a hundred scrolls of recommendation for the worthy within a bag.
The whip is still at the vermilion steps as the nine palaces open; ten thousand miles of rivers and mountains, utterly free of a speck of dust.
Casting off the official robe and donning a straw hat, every voice cries out only, "He comes from over there!"
Layer upon layer of deep locks on the purple mist peaks; in ancient caves, dragons cry as the mists deepen. The wooden woman sings of returning amidst crimson flames;
the stone man strides forward seeking one who understands.
Dongshan was once asked by a monk, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "The head is three feet long;
the neck is two inches long. He then had his attendant take this statement and ask Sansheng. Sansheng pinched the attendant's hand.
The Master approved of this.
Wenfeng Yuyun said: "To have so wonderfully attained the living path for turning around that belongs to the lineage of patch-robed monks—this must be credited to Old Man Xinfeng.
Although Sansheng was able to communicate through secret signs, he ultimately lost by one move.

If someone were to ask today, 'What is the meaning of having a head three feet long and a neck two inches long? I would tell them: wait until your four feet are firmly planted on the ground, and you will see for yourself."
Yet there is a point of clarity. Xueyun said: "Finding a stratagem within the Iron Ring Mountains; withdrawing from the tip of an ox horn.
Although Sansheng was skilled at guiding according to the occasion, he was still like a blind donkey following a herd. Now, if someone asks Xiongshan, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa?
I would say to them: "The children have not yet woken from their sleep; do not raise your voice too early."
Dongshan said: "In this age of the Dharma-ending period, many people possess only dry wisdom. If one wishes to verify what is true and what is false, there are three kinds of 'leakage':
First is the leakage of views: when the spiritual capacity does not leave its station, one falls into a sea of poison. Second is the leakage of sentiment:
when one is stuck in preferences for this or that, one's perspective becomes biased and withered. Third is the leakage of speech: when one pursues subtlety, one loses the fundamental source."
The faculty of discernment is obscured from beginning to end; turbid wisdom flows on and turns.
The wooden man on the ridge lightly opens his mouth; the stone woman by the stream darkly nods her head.
How laughable that Li Bai of old, last night, again stayed overnight upon a fishing boat. (From *Letam Zhao*)
The world’s most exquisite and secluded mountains and streams— Who can join hands with me to wander them together? Turning my head, I suddenly hear the cry of the cuckoo;
Laughing, I point toward the white clouds: "Go back and rest.
(Sentiment) In years past, I was once a seeker of Zen; I knocked at every profound gate and exhausted the essential veins of the Way. At the end of the night, ink-stained robes turn black.
The shirt: Speaking to others, one says their mouth is narrow. (Verse:

Having attained the principle of profound emptiness, one follows the luminous nature into extinction. Were it not for the exhaustion of effort and power, how could one avoid serving the King of Space?
(Three Homages with Virtue) Ultimate stillness encompasses all sounds;
the spiritual source cuts off all currents. How could one know the meaning of the "comprehensive inclusion" if not by seeking it beyond the "correct" and the "partial"?
Relying on words, divine understanding arises; it merely stirs the sentiments of delusion and awakening. The primordial numinous tree roars, and a rain of flowers creates a cold brilliance.

The rotted *ke* tree has turned to stone for a thousand years; in the moon pavilion, the fragrance of the void is uniquely profound. Alas, one cannot bear the bitterness of lingering attachment to white clouds;
the phoenix and crane have not yet been mounted to ascend to the celestial court. (Tán Jírěn)
Ten thousand men are released from the garrison to return to their villages; they rely on the kindness of neighbors to the west for food and lodging. Their parents' graves lie far before their eyes;
at night they light pine torches to illuminate the traces of the woodcutters.
A man of principle does not seek the rank of marquis; sweeping the path and supporting the flowers, he has full freedom. Yet he is further worn out by the flower-gods to the point of death;
his resentment toward spring is not yet ended when he now grieves for autumn.
What is the use of donkeys carrying and horses hauling medicine? Once the illness has reached the vital organs (gao-huang), how can it be pursued?
Most lamentable is that today there are many masters of the craft, yet they cannot drive their needles into the painful spots for others.
(Shengkeyu) When a monk asked Dongshan, "What is the self prior to the empty kalpa? the Master said, "A white bird enters..."
Reeds in bloom.
Beat away the yellow orioles; let them not sing upon the branches. For when they cry out, they startle my dreams, preventing me from reaching Liaoxi.
(Zhengtang’s Commentary)
One night during a formal assembly at Dongshan, the Master did not light the lamp. A monk came forward to pose a question, then withdrew.
The Master ordered his attendant to light the lamp and called for the monk who had just asked the question to come forward.

As the monk approached, the Master said, "Bring me two or three ounces of flour to give to this venerable elder. The monk brushed his sleeves and withdrew. From that moment, he attained awakening and subsequently renounced everything he possessed.
He provided robes and provisions and held a vegetarian feast for three years. Later, he took leave of his teacher. The teacher said, "Go well.
At that time, Xuefeng was standing in attendance and asked, "As for this monk who has taken his leave, when will he return? The teacher replied, "He only knows how to go once."
Not understanding this, he returned to the hall and passed away while sitting beneath his robes and bowl.
Feng reported this to the Master, who said, "Even so, he is still three lifetimes behind me."
At noon in the cave, it strikes the third watch; travelers immediately vie for the path.
Aside from the recluse Chen of Mount Hua, who among those walking does not carry with them right and wrong?
(Cishou Shen) Once, while Dongsan was visiting a sick monk, the monk asked, "What is it like when fire and wind disperse? The Master said, "When they came."
"There is not a single thing. When departing, let it be as it may. He asked, "What can be done about this debility?
The Master said, "You must know that there is one who does not fall ill. He asked, "What is this one who does not fall ill? The Master said, "If you awaken, there is not a single inch;
if you do not awaken, you are separated by a mountain slope. He asked, "Is it permissible to speculate regarding what lies ahead? The Master said, "Though it is as black as lacquer."
Established in the present moment, after the dispersal of fire and wind, one entity remains eternally numinous: the golden land of the Buddha-realm, the white jade courtyard of heaven.
Do not speculate on what lies ahead; wherever you go, remain alert and aware. When the single thought-moment is pure, even the human world will be at peace.
(Nantang Jing) Dongshan was unwell.
A monk asked, "Master, regarding this illness, is there anyone who does not fall ill? The Master said, "There is. The monk asked:
"Does one who is not ill still look upon the Master? The Master said, "The old monk has his share of looking at him. [The monk] asked, "How is it when the Master looks at him?
The Master said, "When the old monk looks at him, he does not see that there is any illness."
Boshanlai said: "The Gate of Non-duality opens; the Sun-face and Moon-face are both unlike anything else.
Dongshan’s chronic ailment cannot be mixed with it, nor can it be categorized as uniform—it is like skillfully diagnosing an illness while within the illness itself.
This monk has sinews in his eyes and blood beneath his skin; for him to see Dongshan is not difficult."
Casting off the stinking skin-bag, one turns the red flesh-ball over; the nostrils are straight at the head, and the skull is dry beneath.
The old physician no longer sees his lifelong ailment; meeting the young child, the difficulty is found nearby. When the wild waters grow thin, the autumn floods have receded;
where the white clouds are severed, the old mountains are cold. You must cut it off completely; do not be negligent. When everything is exhausted and there is no more effort, you will arrive.
Position: Standing alone and towering, you do not share a single platter with me.
(Tiantong Jue) Treading through reed marshes and willow bends, his life’s journey points only to the ancient crags. Where the divine path turns, the white clouds are severed;
though the hundred birds do not come, the spring is still cold. (Fulfilling the position)
Dongshan was once asked by a monk, "What is the father of the green mountains and white clouds? The Master said, "That which is not dense and dark.
The monk asked, "What is the child of the white clouds and green mountains? The Master said, "That which cannot distinguish east from west.
The monk asked, "What is it that the white clouds lean upon all day long? The Master said, "One cannot depart from it. The monk asked, "What is the green... [The text ends here.]
The mountain master did not know at all. The Master said: "It is he who does not look back.
The river flows and the night spirit linger; wind sweeps the reeds as they fly with snow. The stone woman is accustomed to riding the golden phoenix’s dance;
the wooden man joyfully mounts the jade dragon’s return. (Frequent Auspiciousness)
Dongshan went to visit Xingping. As soon as he spread his sitting mat, Xingping said, "Do not prostrate before an old man. Dongshan replied, "I am prostrating before that which is not an old man.
Xingping said, "He does not accept prostrations. Dongshan said, "He has never been prostrated to."
He is not an old man; he does not bow, nor does he receive offerings. Before the world of Vīraṇa, and after the crown of Vairocana, he holds fast within the jar where the days are long;
touched, the green serpent roars from within its case. A skilled physician earnestly warns his patient: taking medicine is not as good as abstaining from food. (Tiantong Jue)
Noble and majestic, he stands apart from the crowd; sitting alone in the deep palace, he faces the slanting rays of the setting sun.
Though others may claim not to know him, how can the family’s disgrace be tolerated once it has been heard outside?
(Ningyuan Di), *Zongjian Faling*, Volume 59.
*Zongjian fali*, Scroll Sixty,
Compiled by Jiyun Tang;
Fifth Generation after Dajian (Huineng).
Dongshan was once asked by a monk: "Regarding the saying, 'Constantly and diligently wipe away [the dust], do not allow it to gather,' why is it that one does not obtain his robe and bowl?
The Master said: "Even if one were to say, 'Originally there is not a single thing,' one still would not deserve to obtain his robe and bowl.
Tell me, then, who deserves them? The monk offered ninety-six responses, none of which accorded with the truth. At the end—
Later, [Zhaozhou] said, "Even if you were to bring it here, he would still not accept it. Only then did the Master consent.
Cui峰 Xian said, "Since he does not accept this eye, what he brings must surely be blind. Do you see the patriarch’s robe and bowl?
If one enters the gate at this point, they are handed over with both hands—not only at the head of Dayu Ridge."
"One person cannot lift it up. Even if the entire nation were to come, one would simply take it away slowly.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "In total, they do not deserve his robe and bowl; rather, they study together with the ancient Buddhas. But tell me, whom are they studying with?"
Tiantong Jue said: "Changlu does not say it this way. You must bring it forth. If you do not bring it forth, how can you know that it is not received?
That which is brought forth must surely be the eye; that which is not received is truly blind. Do you understand? Illuminating everything, the essence has no dependence;
the entire body merges with the Great Way. Gunan Men said: "Dongshan follows when the principle is long. *Cui*... [text ends]
Fengjue says, "One reveals three. Now, since it was not accepted when brought forward, how is it that everyone else wears it horizontally or vertically at all times?
Is this robe a robe or not a robe? One day, passing through the hall, it gets wet twice;
is this bowl a bowl or not a bowl? If it is, why did Dongshan refuse it? If it is not, where have the Patriarch’s robe and bowl gone? Right now—
What, then, is this daily practice and upholding? If one enters the gate in this manner, why wait for the two hands to hand it over or for the struggle at Mount Yung?
One can take it for granted that the descendants of Huangmei will spread throughout the world. Shengfa said:
"These two great elders expounded the teaching thoroughly, yet they could not avoid each seeing only one side. Shengfa is not like this. If there were someone who..."
"If it were to come, it must be received; if it were not to be received, it would certainly not come. That which comes is not the eye, and that which is not received is not blind.
Do you still see the patriarch’s robe and bowl? 'The moon in the empty realm over the ten-thousand-year-old azure pool—only after repeatedly stirring and searching will you finally know.
After Lingyin Yue finished citing the words of Cuiyan, he said: 'When one reaches the river...'"
The land of Wu has come to an end; across the river, the mountains of Yue abound.
The Patriarch’s robe and bowl were left behind in vain leisure; he did not accept them, yet his eyes remained unopened.
Who would believe in the events of the distant Putong era? How could they have been transmitted from Mount Lingyin? (Benjue I)
Dongshan was once asked by a monk, "Master, you usually teach people to practice the 'bird-path. What is the bird-path? The Master said, "Not meeting a single person.
The monk asked, "How does one travel it? The Master said, "One must simply have no private self beneath one's feet. The monk asked, "..."
"Suppose one were walking the path of birds; would that not be one's original face? The Master said, "Disciple, why are you so upside-down?
He asked, "In what way am I upside-down? The Master said, "If you are not upside-down, why do you call a servant 'master'?
He asked, "What is the original face? The Master said, "Not walking the path of birds."
Liran Xuang said: "Not walking the bird-path is the original face. Why then, in ordinary circumstances, do you only teach people to walk the bird-path?
Tell me, what was Dongshan’s intention? After a long silence, he said: "To cross a river one must use a raft;
once the shore is reached, one leaves the boat behind. Fengshan Qi said: "Recognizing rank and understanding the distinction between noble and humble, one naturally wears the cap."
One’s shoes should not be worn upside down, nor should one be unwilling to waste money or grain. In this present age, people’s perspectives are muddled;
they cannot distinguish gold from brass because they have lacked great ambition from the start and have settled for such perversity.

Furthermore, tell me: what is the true countenance of one who does not travel the path of birds? After a long silence, he said: "I shall not refuse to tell you: it is also very difficult to maintain continuity."
The ancient path stands serenely leaning against the vast void. To travel the profound way remains a journey over precipices and crags.
Though not ascending the "Bird Path" may be considered subtle, when examined closely, one has already encountered the Way at every turn.
(Danxia Chun) Shooting down the crow from the summit of the ten-thousand-fathom peak, its wings unfold like the azure waves of the *Hetu* diagram; among them, how many are the primordial beings?
The characters record exhaustively all past accounts of *feng* and *shan* sacrifices.

(Tan Jiren) Not traversing the "Bird Path," the imperial wind sweeps vast and wide. What does a weary old back know? Drunk and fallen upon the celestial street—what contribution has the Emperor’s power had for me?
A cup of wine shall amuse me in my old age. Old I am, indeed; yet I lack something good: I do not measure up to the man from the eastern village.
O Great Lady of the King! (Molizhi) Though one possesses the art of riding on the void, Penglao Island remains far away. If you wish to see the Lord of Guya, you must descend from the Purple Sky.

Descending from the Purple Abyss, bidding farewell to the celestial breeze, jade blossoms and precious grasses grow in dense clusters. Who would say that the old moonlight and wind of the immortal lord have ceased?
At the eastern window, the red disk of the sun still hangs. (The central seal) The verse of Dongshan says:
Greed, anger, and ignorance—how utterly ignorant they are! Fortunately, this morning I have come to recognize them. As I walk...
Strike! As soon as you sit, strike! Entrust this to the Mind-King and examine it with care. For immeasurable kalpas, you have remained unliberated.
I ask you three: do you know or not?
Shending Yin said: "I am not like that. Greed, anger, and ignorance are truly without consciousness. Throughout the twelve periods of the day, let them be as they will.
Walking, they go; sitting, they follow. Entrusted to the mind-king, what could one possibly do with them? Since immeasurable kalpas past, they have been fundamentally liberated;
why need one further ask whether they are known or unknown? Zibo Ke said: "Refine your own mind; use the tongs and hammer with fierce intensity."
It is secret. One must be like Dongshan, whose coughing, waving of arms, joking, laughter, and reprimands were all nothing other than the samādhi of liberation.
This is returning it to Shendeng. Nevertheless, had Shendeng not been forged and tempered within the furnace and bellows of Dongshan, how could he have attained such ease?
Dongshan did not strike Shendeng; rather, he perceived a sign upon the ground. From [therein...]
"You beat me this morning and hammer me this evening; I dare say that your greed, anger, and ignorance remain as unsubdued as ever, even if it were to take a donkey's age.
If you can discern [the truth] here, I will grant that you understand the Tathāgata-dhyāna. But as for the Patriarchal Zen, you are still ten thousand li away from the frontier."
Dajue Sheng said, "To speak in such a manner—if one were under Dajue’s gate, I would have broken the donkey’s waist and not let it pass.
Why? Since there was already the integrity of the King who yielded his throne, why dispute the purity of washing the ears?
Nevertheless, even so, one must be a person of substance before this can be achieved. Xuetang Xuan said, "These two old fellows—one is a forced master."
The Master said: "One person drifts along with circumstances; yet, for now, they do not fail to serve as a compassionate vessel across the sea of suffering.
If you reach the gate of Houshan, you must by no means mention it. Should you mention it, I shall break your donkey’s back. Why?
Because within the royal treasury, there is no such blade. Yunlin Lu said: "Shisou also could not let him off the hook—greed, hatred, and delusion."
Who does not know? To take a tortoise and certify it as a soft-shelled turtle is his doing; to carry snow to fill a well, or to strike fire that burns one's own eyebrows.
If you wish to drive a single nail into the Mind-King, it is difficult to hide even within the pores of a lotus fiber; where else, then, could one stand to be a "fore-knower"? It is also said:
if you proceed from the words of Dongshan to resolve the matter, when it is cold, it is cold throughout heaven and earth. If [you proceed] from...
If you are enlightened through the words of Shending, you will be sent forth to heat up all under heaven.

He hurriedly went out, thereby avoiding using evenness to report back on unevenness; such behavior invites loathing. Qinghua Yan spoke on his behalf, saying:

It is not a jade tablet, nor is it a ceremonial scepter. Turning back, he enters straight into the Azure Dragon’s cave.

Even "Tàipíng" (Great Peace) is thus a mere *tāla* tree; ultimately, he has not left the nest.
How much less can one endure such idle chatter before those with clear eyes? (Fojian Qin)
Shishuang was once asked by the Senior Monk (Upādhyāya) Jinming of Xuzhou, "What is it like when a single hair pierces through all the holes?

The Master said, "You must wait until after ten thousand years. Jinming asked, "And what about after ten thousand years? The Master said, "If you wish to pass the imperial examination, let yourself pass;
if you wish to excel among the elite, let yourself excel. Later, Jinming asked Jingshan Yin. Jingshan said, "Let the brilliance be as it is."
"You, Guanghua. As for bearing fruit, let it be up to you to bear fruit.
[The Master] said: "Shishuang stares with eyes wide open from within his coffin. Do not say that Jinming lacks the eye."
The sun is warm and the breeze gentle; spring is at its finest. The noble youth gallops his horse to roam the upper forest.
The cold scholar, yet unenrolled, clings to his old blue felt mat. Flowers fall and flowers bloom—all is but sorrow.

(By Sheng Fapu) Chan Master Jianyuan Zhongxing of Tanzhou (a successor of Daowu Zhi) was attending upon Daowu when they went to a donor’s home to offer condolences. [The following verses describe this occasion.]
The Master tapped the coffin and asked, "Is he alive or dead? I replied, "He is alive; I will not say he is dead.
The Master asked, "Why do you not say? I replied, "I will not say; I will not say.
As we were returning along the road, the Master said, "Master, you must speak for me today. If you do not speak, I shall strike you! I said, "Strike!"
[The Master] immediately struck him, saying, "I do not say. The teacher then struck him again and said, "Go back to the monastery; I will send you away. Later, the teacher attained realization.

When he encountered my passing, he went to Shishuang and raised this dialogue to request further instruction. Shishuang said, "Have you not heard it said: 'I do not say he is born, nor do I say he dies'?
At these words, the teacher attained great enlightenment.
Yunju Yuan said: "Shishuang is adding a point to an arrowhead; even if he were to wake up a thousand Jianyuan, it would still be of no use.

Had I waited until he finished his statement, I would have struck him with a heavy blow and driven him out. Not only would this have made me a patriarch of the world, but it would also have cleared the grievance for Daowu.
Wuzu Yan said: "Today Baiyun is filled with indignation and cannot remain equanimous; I must bring this to a decisive end."
This is a public case (gong'an). First, Daowu did not understand how to act as master of himself; second, he was unable to adapt to circumstances and enter the secular world.
At that time, had he been asked whether one is born or dead, he should have simply said, "Wait until we return to the monastery, and I will tell you.
Had he been able to grasp this statement, a clever fellow would have given it a decisive kick, sparing Great Master Daowu a beating with his fist.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Daowu threw his body across for the sake of others, pointing directly to the root-source of birth and death.
Jianyuan went personally to the Treasure Mountain, yet he missed it right before his face.

Were it not for the deep roots planted in the past by the adamantine true nature, how could one suddenly turn the light back upon oneself amidst the shallow grass of the level field and see where Daowu exerted his effort to assist? For now, let us consider this."
"What is the place where Dao Wu exerts his effort to assist others? Jingshan Hongzhi said: "I will not say it for the living, nor will I say it for the dead.
Two layers of legal cases, all brought before me in a single indictment. A sharp blade, polished to a glint, cuts through the essential points.
Cast off the 'vulture-stink' robe; discard the 'grease-smeared' cap. Seated upon the great throne, his spirit is vast and majestic. He gave a shout.
Tianning Qi said: "Life? Death? To stir a thought is already to deviate from the truth. Not speaking—do not speak! Where would you go to seek it?
Dragging out the nostrils, smashing the skull: ten thousand strings of cash wrapped around the waist, riding a crane up to Yangzhou.
When there is spirit, add more spirit; where there is no elegance, there is elegance nonetheless."
The hairless chain rattles at both ends; the flawless green jade is offered three times.
To meet with the chopping off of one's feet instead is utterly groundless—who would have thought that upright speech would seem as distant as its opposite?
(Fóxìng Tái) The front head falls into a trap; he takes a blow in the dark. A poisonous hand scratches him where it itches; a heron flies amidst the snow.
Not seen. A single silver pitcher hangs from the tip of a tree branch.
(Chengtian Zong) When casting the hook at the head of a rapids, the scarlet-tailed, patterned fish still hesitates.
Suddenly leaping out from within the vast waves, it seizes the mist and grasps the clouds, making the universe seem low. (Tiantong Hua)
The invitation has been issued to its limit, yet he cannot be called back; In vain it causes tears to soak the cold ashes. Leaning on the tower, I suddenly hear the "Liangzhou" melody;
Who would have thought the frontier *jia* flute would play the "Falling Plum"?
(Huishan Hai) One day, Jianyuan took up a spade and went to Shishuang’s Dharma Hall; he walked from east to west, and from west to east.
Dongshuang asked, "What is it? The Master said, "I am seeking the sacred remains of the former master. Dongshuang said, "The vast waves surge and the white billows reach the heavens;
what sacred remains of the former master are you seeking? The Master said, "This is precisely where one must apply effort.
Dongshuang said, "In this place, not even a needle can penetrate; what effort could there be? The Master took up his spade, slung it over his shoulder, and departed.
Taoyuan Fu spoke separately, saying: "The sacred remains of the former master still exist. Mingzhao Qian said: "Do not say 'what'—what other words could he have used as a substitute?
He replied: "A heron speaks like a crane. He also acted on behalf of Jianyuan, immediately throwing down his spade and saying:
"Shallow water has no fish. Qinglong Si said: "These two elders may truly be said to be of the same lineage and shared the same thread. Shou...
At the moment of release, look closely: it has still not been utterly severed. If you wish to achieve this utter severance, do not trouble yourself seeking the spiritual remains of the former master;

the misty radiance overflowing the eyes spans from antiquity to the present. It is laughable that those holding spades merely exert their strength—how much better it would be to clasp hands together and open one’s chest in mutual accord!
Rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have none. To sever a hair-tip, to sever a hair-fiber: it is like a mountain, like a peak.
The golden, numinous bones remain even now; amidst white waves flooding the heavens, where can they be placed? A single sandal returned to the West—once lost (Cui Feng Xian).
All day long leaning against the gate and resting by the tower; how many times has the bright mirror reflected her combing her hair? From this moment on, she serves only Pan Lang.
Later, he too failed to recognize his shame before others. (Baoning Yong) At that time, bitter words were never spoken;
only after awakening did one begin to seek out the spiritual bones. Over the Lian River, the cold moon and rain fall desolately;
the floating clouds have dispersed, and the sky is as clear as if swept clean. (Meng’an Xin)
In life, one never encountered a true知音 (zhīyīn—connoisseur); after death, one can only seek the sacred remains in vain.
Where can it be sought right before one's eyes? Let the golden chain float or sink as it will.

Huguo Yuan said: "In inquiry, one must inquire truly; in seeing, one must see truly. To speak even so much as a hair’s breadth of its beginning or end is entirely self-deception.
Suppose someone were to ask me today: 'Why do you strike with a shout? I would simply say: 'Gold has its own price;

A single phrase for the occasion rings like jade; inside and out, its brilliance fills the eyes with cold clarity. One never dwells within the realm of no-outflows;

The jeweled sword gathers dust as the universe finds peace; in the Great Tranquility, there are no affairs of war to discuss.

[The monk asked,] "What is the Dharma-eye? The Master said, "The Dharma-eye has no flaw. When the monk returned, he reported this.
"It resembles me. I said, "This fellow has only now finally attained thorough understanding.
Yuyang Xueyun said, "Thirty years ago he sold the ox to buy the horse; thirty years later he sells the horse to buy the ox."
If one is of an extraordinary caliber, one will certainly not turn within the flow of another’s discourse. Do you see? The Dharma-body is formless;
the Dharma-eye is flawless.
