Tian Qi said: "The spirit’s power is such that it is sovereign even within tiger dens and demonic palaces; its application is so subtle that nothing can obstruct it from the ends of the earth to the furthest reaches of the sea.
To let it loose, it spreads like stars across the high heavens; to seize it, it vanishes like clouds swept away by the wind.
Since antiquity, it has been said that a bright spear is easy to dodge, yet a hidden arrow remains difficult to guard against. Like the gnawing of a tiny mouse, people do not perceive the pain."
"If a person attains this realization, they traverse horizontally across the eight directions. Dazhu said: "Observe how these masters meet; their spiritual sparks butt against one another.
As the song grows higher, the response becomes steeper. They are brilliant on all eight sides—how free and easy!
Nevertheless, do you know where this monk was secretly wounded by the poisoned arrow? Zudeng Shao said: "The golden needle operates in secret; within it..."
He did not meet the sharp edge of the blade; he returned it to Jia Shan. In establishing himself, he was as unashamed as a jade thread;
he drew it crosswise from his sleeve, utterly forgetting continuity. This must have been Master Yue; his display and entrustment were without deviation, truly a master of the craft.

When meeting others, he would not deign to brandish spears or dance with battle-axes. Alas, in the end, he was struck by Jia Shan’s hidden golden scalpel; its poison has entered his very marrow to this day. It should be...
At that time, Daizhen, like a lion cub capable of a great roar, overturned the meditation seat and swept his sleeves to depart.
Not only did he cut off Jia Shan’s tongue, but it was also seen that the master and disciple had a firm basis for their relationship.
While Jia Shan was engaged in communal labor, the Rector ordered Furu to deliver tea. Furu said, "I have come solely for the sake of the Buddha-dharma;
I have not come to deliver tea. The Rector said, "The Master has sent me to invite the Senior Monk.
Furu replied, "The Master may do as he pleases," and then took the tea to the place of work. Seeing the Master there, he shook his tea bowl to make a sound, but the Master did not respond.
Jingzhao Daoyi said, "Three or five bowls of strong tea; the meaning lies at the edge of the mattock. The Master said, "The pitcher has the posture of pouring tea;
how many bowls are there in the basket? Daoyi said, "The pitcher has the posture of pouring tea; there is not a single bowl in the basket. He then poured the tea.
The assembly all gazed at him with their eyes. Daoyi said, "The assembly is looking up expectantly; I beg the Master for a word."
The Master said: "If you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it; carry it home in a bottomless basket. Jue said:
"Holding a night-bright talisman in one's hand, how many know when the dawn breaks? The Master called to the assembly: "Someone has already arrived! Go back!
Thereupon he presided over the communal labor.

Wan’an Yan said: "To clarify one's own nature, to display a lofty mechanism, to carve out a separate path of life at the edge of a precipitous cliff, to distinguish dragons from snakes and capture tigers and rhinoceroses, and to offer *amṛta* (clarified butter) amidst a thicket of poison—only then can one be like a lid fitting its box or a mustard seed entering a needle’s eye.
This was the point where guest and host were in accord for Jia Shan that year. As for me, the mountain monk, what more is there to say?"
Born. If you encounter a recluse on the road, do not have them cast a golden statue of Zi-qi.
If you meet a dead snake by the way, do not strike it down; you must cast away the bottomless basket.
Often, matters arise from idle talk; do not treat idle talk as if it were merely idle talk. (Pak Ong-hyeon)
A man carrying a wooden board has no constraints; he would rather starve to death on Mount Shouyang than swear never to eat the grain of Zhou.
(Xutang Yu) Jiashan ascends the hall: His movements do not pass beyond his door; his dwelling does not nest in a hollow. His eyes do not look toward other positions;
his feet do not tread upon other positions. The six gates are not closed; there are no tracks at the four crossroads. His study does not pause at midday; his intent...
Establishing the Mystery: For a thousand kalpas, the eye does not borrow from the tip of the tongue; for ten thousand kalpas, the tongue does not look to the clarity within the eye.
This sublime faculty requires no sharpened edge. If you reach this point, what matter is there? "The thread on the tip of the fishing pole is played by you;
without disturbing the clear waves, the meaning is naturally distinct."
The moon sinks into the blue sea, yet the dragon does not hide; Mist locks the azure Wugu, yet the phoenix remains unknown.
Beyond the kalpas stand the dense, shadowless trees; They cast shade from branches that have not yet sprouted.
(Danxia Chun) Once, a monk asked Jia Shan, "What is a phrase of resemblance? The Master said, "The lotus leaf is round and round, as round as..."
The Mirror: "The tips of the water chestnut's corners are as sharp as awls. Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "The wind blows the willow catkins like flying balls; the rain beats the pear blossoms like fluttering butterflies."
Yangshan Qian said, "Although Jia Shan was indeed not unresponsive to the monk's intent, he was nonetheless exposed by that monk.
It was not so with Yangshan. What is a 'concordant phrase'? 'The lotus leaf is round and round, as round as a mirror;
the water chestnut horn is sharp and sharp, as sharp as an awl. The student does not understand: 'The wind blows the willow catkins like a flying ball; the rain beats upon the pear blossoms.'"
The butterfly flies; in the end, it is something quite distinct. Tianning Qi said:
"Jiashan’s response was like adding flowers upon brocade—like bamboo and peach blossoms intertwined. It simply has not yet touched upon the fundamental matter.
Today, if someone asks, 'What is a phrase that is similar? I would say to them: Do not take Zhidu’s crane and call it the work of Wang Xizhi."
E’o. Yulang Xu said: "I, this mountain monk, am not like that. If someone were to ask, 'What is a phrase of resemblance? I would simply say to them:
'A sandbag hangs on the wall—no need to think of food. The reflection of a bow sinks into the cup—do not mistake it for a snake.'"
A monk from under the guidance of Jiashan went to Shishuang. Upon entering the gate, he said, "How do you do? Shishuang replied, "Not necessary, Venerable Sir.
The monk said, "In that case, take care," and departed. He then went to Yantou. Upon entering the gate, he again said, "How do you do?
Yantou then sighed twice. The monk said, "In that case, take care," and as soon as he turned to leave, Yantou—
[The monk] said, "Although he is a junior monk, he was also able to manage and uphold [the teaching]. That monk returned and reported this to the Master.
The next day, the Master ascended the hall and called out, "Monk, you who came from Shishuang Yantou yesterday, come forward.
The monk came forward as instructed and related the previous conversation. When the monk had finished speaking, the Master asked, "Does the assembly understand? If no one speaks, I, the old monk..."
"Without sparing even his eyebrows, he went on to say: 'Although Shishuang possesses the sword that kills, he lacks the sword that gives life;
Yantou, however, possesses both the sword that kills and the sword that gives life.'"
Baiyan Fu said: "Shishuang and Yantou already had it; Jiashan has let it go.
As for this monk, it cannot be denied that he is indeed a clever practitioner. However, he was not right to suffer a defeat at the hands of Jiashan.
Had he been able to guard his beginning and protect his end at that time, when [Jiashan] said, 'Recite the previous story according to the Dharma,' he should have simply—"
He overturned the meditation seat. Even if one were to appoint this fellow from Jia Shan as a salt-and-iron magistrate, he would still not have attained it.
When Jia Shan was serving as the head cook at Mount Gui, Mount Gui once asked, "What vegetables are we eating today?
The Master replied, "Two years under the same spring. Mount Gui said, "Attend well to your duties. The Master replied, "The dragon dwells in the phoenix’s nest."
Tiantong Jie said: "The handle is in one's hand; seizing or relinquishing is according to the occasion. When struck and tested, a hundred flavors are complete.
Within this, there is only one flavor missing. Tell me, is it oil or is it sauce? If you can discern this, then the merit of Huazang’s efforts will not have been in vain.
Tianjie Sheng said: "As soon as this fellow Jia Shan encountered that single laugh, his three oars opened his eyes."
"Come! he said, and immediately his breath swallowed up all directions. "Nevertheless," he continued, "in your daily practice, have you ever bitten into the two years being one spring?
He let out a shout and said, "Drive away that stone tiger!"
Meeting by chance, I ask about the monks' congee; it cannot be compared to the offering of fragrant rice at the hermitage garden.
Purple qi follows the vermilion phoenix through the night; the golden dragon coils around the branch of the moon at dawn.
(Touzi Qing) After the rain, the moss on the Dragon Court is moist; at the end of night, the candles in the Golden Hall are first red. The palace ladies play refined music for the Ascending Peace.
Song: Beyond the Prohibitions, laboring in vain; yet his hearing and sight remain sharp.
(Da Hongyu) Nestled within the dragon’s lair and the phoenix’s roost, two years pass as one spring. The fragrance of osmanthus flowers drifts thickly; on level ground lies the azure cloud.
(Grand Bounty) The purple mist lowers as the curtains hang at the Yellow Gate; holding the vermilion edict, he descends the vermilion courtyard. A fragrant breeze wafts to welcome the jade pendants;
how could one from beyond the secular world dare to pry? (Peaceful Distance)
Jiashan was once asked by a monk, "Regarding the twelve divisions of the teachings and the meaning of the patriarchs' intent, why does the Master not permit people to ask about them?
The Master said, "They are my sitting cloth. The monk asked, "By what Dharma does the Master instruct people?

The Master said, "In empty space, there is no path for a needle to hang upon; you, sir, are in vain exerting the effort of twisting thread. He asked again, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "Yes."
"No," the Master said, "the descendants of Jinxu, the true body of Śarīra, and the profound discourse on the Ungraspable—
these are the den of wild foxes."
Ulcerous sores and worn-out paper are far too coarse; painting the void is entirely unfit. How could a fierce flame allow even a mosquito to alight?
A mad monkey vainly covets its own shadow in the sky. The divine blade brushes away the coral moon; the mechanism of the "Hu-ping" cake transcends the discourse of Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Turning stones into gold is easy for those who meet the Immortal; teaching people to eliminate right and wrong is difficult. (Dajue Sheng)
The wind and sun shine brightly; fowl and dogs live in simplicity. The stratagems of Sun and Wu were laid out like a chessboard.
Wu Ding’s road-cutting first destroyed Shu; the ten-thousand-li walls early lost Qin. Dust is cleared away and the single board is a deep, lustrous pearl;
The mechanism of life stirs, and the waves of the four seas flow on. The universe is swept clear, free from blemish or shadow; Flowers laugh and orioles sing—spring is everywhere. (Yuan’an Fǔ)
Yao and Shun hung their robes; ten thousand nations basked in spring. In the Great Peace, there was no business of war.
With jade whips and golden horses, they were idle all day long; with bright moon and clear wind, they were rich for a lifetime.
(Three circles) When Jiashan was about to pass away, he left this final instruction: "The branch of Shitou will soon be extinguished. Luopu—
[The monk] said, "Not so. The Master asked, "Why? He replied, "That other house already has its own green mountains.
The Master said, "If it is truly so, then our school shall not fall into decline."
Yuanwu Keqin said: "The single branch of Shitou owes its survival to Lopu; those who cause our school to fall are to be pitied.
As for Jia Shan’s later words, it is like selling silk at a reduced price—his descendants will all end up as commoners. Zudeng Shaoyan said:
"Jia Shan habitually swallowed Buddhas and patriarchs and overawed all quarters. Even on his deathbed, he still put on such airs and postures."
It was not merely by the power of one arm that the Master of Many Words emerged; eventually, he could not even enter the Nirvana Hall.
Chan Master Lingzun of Qingpingshan in Ezhou (a successor in the lineage of Cuiwei) was once asked by a monk: "What is the Mahāyāna?"
The Master said, "A well-rope. [The monk] asked, "What is the Small Vehicle? The Master said, "A money-rope.
[The monk] asked, "What is outflow (āsrava)? The Master said, "A strainer. [The monk] asked, "What is non-outflow (anāsrava)? The Master said, "A wooden ladle.
[The monk] asked, "How is it when you present yourself face-to-face? The Master said, "Hand it over to the steward."
Tianning Qi said: "I, Yongzuo, do not avoid the censure of all quarters; I must add a point to an arrowhead.
Even if one were to shatter the Great Tang Empire, not a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma could be found."
A bamboo sieve and a wooden ladle; strings of cash and a well-rope—this is the manifest family style, a vast and open way of life.
Let your livelihood go forth, trusting in conditions as they come; where else could the Buddha-dharma be applied? There is no need for contrivance, simply follow along as it is;
naturally, the mind-ground is ever peaceful and joyful. (Tiantong Jue)
The outflows of the two vehicles strike against the King of Emptiness; after the snow has fallen, how can one endure the midnight frost?
(Zhang Wujin) The colander and wooden ladle, the string of coins and the well-rope—beating tiles and divining with tortoise shells are but vain calculations. Only the Qilin...

A Single Horn. (Nanhua Bing) Gently striking the sandalwood clappers to join the warbling of the oriole, her voice checks the drifting clouds as it flows in winding turns. Sung a thousand times, yet parted a thousand times;
it leaves people still longing for that "Little Liangzhou. (Zhongmu Ying)
At the beginning of the Qingping era, Chongxian first visited Cuiwei. He asked, "What is the essential meaning of the West?
Cuiwei said, "Wait until there is no one here, and I will tell you. After a long while, the Master said, "There is no one; please, Preceptor, speak.
Cuiwei stepped down from his meditation seat and led him into the bamboo grove. The Master spoke again, "There is no one; please, Preceptor, speak. Cuiwei pointed to the bamboo and said:
"One pole is so long; that pole is so short. The Master had a slight understanding, yet he had not yet reached full penetration.
Later, when he went out to reside at Da Tong, he raised this matter and said to the assembly: "The former master went into the mud and into the water;
it was simply that I did not understand."
Father and son meet; their intent is already manifest. Why must we discuss the heat and cold of status? He points out the affairs of the ancestral home with earnest care;
having traversed the desolate wilderness, they speak of its length and breadth.
(Dahong Su) At every turn, the earth is buried with iron thorns; passing through at midnight, one does not yet perceive the difficulty. When dawn breaks, the heels are wounded by them.
[The monk] was overturned. Only then did he realize he had passed through the Iron Gate Barrier.
(Xuedang’s Verse) When Qingping was asked by a monk, "What is the house style of Qingping? the Master said, "A peck of flour makes three steamed buns."
The sound falling across a thousand mountains is also true; the drifting clouds and the night spirit are yet distinct.
One who seeks the traceless ground where no path exists need not ask about the vast city on Mount Kongtong.
(Pín Jíxiáng) Chan Master Dàtóng of Tóuzi Mountain in Shūzhōu (a successor of Cuīwēi): A monk asked, "What is the ten-fold body?"

The Taming Master descended from his meditation seat and stood. Again, [the questioner] asked, "How far apart are the ordinary and the sage? The Master likewise descended from his meditation seat and stood.
Cui-feng Xian said, "Regarding this koan, there is no one among you who does not know it thoroughly. If it were presented in such a manner, the patch-robed monks of the world—"
The entire assembly was preoccupied with discussing the Du family. Did Cuifeng have any further excellence? Try raising this for the great assembly:
how far apart are the ordinary and the holy? Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there. "What is the Ten-Body Tamer? he asked.
Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there. "Tell me, is this the same as what was raised previously, or is it different?
If you say they are the same, I grant you, Elder, one eye. If you say there is something extraordinary about it, I likewise grant you, Elder, one eye.
Furthermore, let us open another path: how far apart are the ordinary and the sage? I ask you, Elder, to provide a turning word."
[The Master] said: "What is the 'Tamer of the Ten Bodies'? Please, Senior Monk, offer a turning word.
Not only will you have visited Touzi, but you will also come to know the excellence of Cui峰. If you simply say, 'I descend from the meditation seat and stand,' then cherish your eyebrows!
Wuzu Yan said: "If someone were to ask me this, I too would descend from the meditation seat and stand."
"What? I shall instead rely on painting a cat. Once I have devised the plan, I will tell you. Jingshan Gao said:
"Touzi descended from his meditation seat and said: 'Today I shall proclaim it for you. You fellows who trail behind donkeys and horses—be most careful not to take this up in a confused manner.
Gao Feng Miao said: "One turn of phrase is as far apart as heaven and earth; one turn of speech is the very standard."
Regarding the words: Gu Nanmen said, "Touzi was a fine Ten-Body Tamer, yet he was bitten by Cui Feng until he cried out in a hundred ways.
If anyone were to ask this, simply say: "It is placed upon the mouth."
Water flows from Kunlun, its waves continuous; heaven is high and earth vast, with beautiful forests and peaks. As the meditation seat slightly lowers, clouds and mountains vanish;
sages and ordinary beings leave no trace, as seas and mountains grow cold.
(Touzi Qing) An old woman bows low to serve her parents-in-law; rising up, she struggles to avoid a face smeared with grime. She forces her cloud-like hair to stand high...
Wan: "Can you even block the eyes of those standing beside you?
(Baizhang Yuanwen) He loves to dangle his fishing line by the riverbank; in the depths of the azure pool dwell fine fish.
It is not that there is no fragrant bait on the hook—how can this fellow catch them? (Changling Zhuo)
The Jade Deer, horned, departs the Milky Way; the Golden Phoenix, clutching flowers, descends from the painted pavilion.
The rustic old man does not disdain the young lord’s intoxication; together they join hands to wander the Imperial Street.
(Shui’an I) The silver moon emerging from the sea is utterly free of dust; a gentle breeze stirs, mingling with the sound of the mortar. The crystal curtain moves as the rose...
[The verse says: "Let go! A fragrance strikes the nose as it fills the entire courtyard. (Mu-tang recites:
Regarding the case where Touzi was asked by Zhaozhou, "When a person who has died the great death comes back to life, what then?
The Master said, "He is not permitted to travel by night; he must arrive at dawn. Zhaozhou said, "I am already white as a monkey; you are even blacker than a monkey."
Tiantong Zhao said: "The two venerable masters possessed only a single eye.
To have eyes while alive is the same as being dead; why need one examine the 'medicinal taboos' of a master?
Even the ancient Buddhas said they had never reached it—none know who can scatter the dust and sand. (CuiFeng Xian)
From the dead he returns to life, his teeth bared; when dawn breaks, he must have already gone on ahead.
In whose private villa, amidst the pond, does a pair of mandarin ducks dwell—so exquisite they cannot be captured in a painting?
(Baizhang Yuan) From the void is born an iron ox; its horns and head are distinct, truly marvelous. It tramples through the depths of the clear pool.
The moon; at the end of the night, he was led through the snow to return home.
(Changling Zhuo) I suspect it is the essence of a thousand-year-old azure jade, transformed into a single slab of autumn-water bone. The Sea God wished to protect it but could not;
suddenly, one day, the head of a giant turtle lifted it up. (Zhengtang Bian)
The mustard seed city and kalpa-stone are exquisitely exhausted at their origin; the living eye illuminates the vast void within the world. Not permitted to travel by night, one arrives at dawn;
the news of home is not yet willing to be entrusted to the crane or the fish.
(Tiantong Jue) A venomous snake emerging from its cave has horns upon its head; a fierce tiger crouching on a cliff has a naturally striped body. Strike the golden drum behind the skull.
[The sound of] a stone chime. Before dawn had broken, he was sent out through the pass.
(Longchi Zhen) When a monk asked Touzi, "What is it like when the moon is not yet full? the Master said, "Swallow three or four."
[The monk] asked, "After it is full, what then? The Master said, "Vomit up seven or eight.
Tiantong Jie said, "Swallowing and vomiting—when calculated, there is nowhere for them to land. If you wish to see a jester, look no further than Huang Fanchoe.
Nanshan Bao said, "I, this mountain monk, am not like that. What about when the moon is not yet full?"
The entire world is this radiance. After the full moon, what then? With his whole body facing no direction, tell me:
how far is he from Touzi? Touzi said, "How do you all deliberate upon this? If you can speak, [then you have it]."

Before the Peak of Tranquil Abiding, mist and clouds cover the earth; along the Path of Caoxi, sun and moon turn as one wheel. If there is anyone who does not understand, I shall provide another verse for you:

"Once, when the moon was full and once when it was waning, I asked the old man; A stone tortoise holding its young leads forth the pure breeze. Yesterday morning, the wooden horse [galloped] within the deep pool."
Pass beyond. Treading out the golden crow, it turns crimson at midnight.
Swallowing is easy; spitting it back out is difficult. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, the celestial wind is cold. Last night at the third watch, it was as bright as day.
I know not who leaned against the balustrade to gaze together.
(Buddha-nature Tai) The thirty-six constituent elements have all turned to ashes; Only a pair of withered eyes remain.
Placed amidst the deep night of the nine-fold thoroughfare, They create light where there was no light. (Xiaoyan Bao)
On his way, Touzi encountered Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou asked, "Are you not the master of Mount Touzi?
The Master replied, "I have come to receive an offering of tea and salt money. Zhaozhou returned to his hut first; later that evening, he saw the Master returning from carrying oil himself.
Zhaozhou said, "I have long heard of Touzi; having arrived here, I see only an oil-seller.
The Master said, "You see only an oil-seller, yet you do not recognize Touzi. Zhaozhou asked, "What is Touzi? The Master lifted up an oil jar and said, "Oil, oil."
Nantang Jing said: "Zhaozhou is a master smith; his furnace and bellows require the smelting of gold to be refined through a hundred trials.
Touzi’s fundamental tongs and hammers cannot help but be used along the way. Do you wish to see where these two elders land? Ten years of bitter toil, no one asks;
in a single day, fame is known throughout the world. Boshan Lai said: "He strides upon the hoofbeats that chase the sun, cutting off [the path]..."
The rushing and converging waters: they are either Zhaozhou or Touzi; they are either Touzi or Zhaozhou. It is like a skilled player of Go who perceives several moves ahead;
the response must depend on the immediate situation, where things naturally fall into harmony. Do you recognize these two elders?
Coming down through the Iron Ring Mountains, I meet you at the crossroads. By chance, I carry a bottle of oil;

who would think it was out of greed for its slippery taste? Providing for guests according to one’s means, whether in plenty or scarcity, I do not envy the high towers from my own flat-roofed house. (Huatang Yan)
Touzi was once asked by a monk, "Master, having resided on this mountain, what realization or realm do you possess? The Master said:
"A girl with horned hair has white strands of hair;
a girl with horned hair has white strands of hair. Amidst a mass of fierce flames, flakes of snow fly. Who else could possibly dwell upon a mountain in such a manner?
**Draft:** Vagrant clouds and flowing waters do not return the same way.
(Baiyun Yuan) Before the Huaye Pavilion, spring is at its peak; Misty willow catkins dance in the clear sky. Having finished tossing the gold coins, she has no strength left for coquetry;
She leans smilingly against the winding balustrade. (Lan’an Shu)
"Regarding the question on the realm of dwelling in the mountains: 'The girl with twin braids has already turned grey. Without meeting face-to-face, do not seek further understanding;
white clouds fly over the old mountain crags. (Tianmu Li) Because of this, Touzi was asked by a monk:
"When the spring rain falls heavily, why do the hundred grasses not sprout? The Master said: "Because they have already been cut down. (Touzi)
"The plantain tree grows just like this. He asked again, "What is the mystery within the mystery? The Master said, "Last year it was the fifth day of the fifth month;
this year it is the same. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "It is not a matter of identity or difference; who speaks of before and after?"
A monk asked, "What is the second moon? The Master said, "In mid-spring, it gradually warms. The monk asked, "What is the first moon?
The Master said, "In early spring, it is still cold."
Early spring is still cold—this is the first month. Mid-spring gradually warms—this is the second month.
If there are no worldly affairs hanging upon the mind, it is truly a fine season for humanity. In Jiangnan and the two circuits of Zhejiang, the spring is cold and the autumn is hot.
(Mong-an Yue) When a monk asked Touzi, "Is there anything extraordinary within the entire Tripitaka? the Master said, "Evolve."
Yunyan’s new version says: "To manifest and enter the Great Treasury of Teachings. Zhaojue Zhenqin said: "When the illness has been cured, there is no need for a donkey to carry the medicine.
Jingshan Dahui said: "There is no lack of 'manifesting' and 'entering,' but these two great elders were truly extraordinary."
[This is] a special case. "Even in sixty kalpas of three lifetimes, one has not yet dreamed of it. Shilin then said:
"The monastic community deliberates and all say that Dahui did not approve of those two elders. If you hold such a view, even in sixty kalpas of three lifetimes, you have not yet dreamed of Dahui."
Sudden and gradual, partial and perfect; provisional and real, emptiness and existence. These words nail one’s iron tongue shut.
River-like eyes and ocean-like mouths—this single path of pure voidness extends through past and present. An octagonal millstone rolls in empty space.
(Zhaojue Qin) One out, one in; half-closed, half-open. A weary crane perches on a cold tree; a mad monkey howls atop an ancient terrace. If you wish to know:
A most extraordinary matter! One should thoroughly tear one’s straw sandals [to pieces].
(Muan Yong) When a monk asked Touzi, "What is the one great matter of causes and conditions? the Master said, "The Minister Yin has invited me to open the hall."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Among the ancient Buddhas of the Tiantong lineage, Touzi was renowned for his extraordinary discernment and his mastery of the practical application of the unadorned Way.
Observing how he casually handled matters, one sees that Buddhist teachings and worldly affairs were seamlessly integrated.
Nevertheless, it is a pity that his realization was not particularly expansive. Today, if someone asks Tianning, 'What is this one great matter?'"
"Conditions. Thus, when the Way-Hand grasps the Golden Wheel, it clears the four seas; may the Sage’s person endure for ten million years.
Qingshan Xiu said: "What is Touzi’s point of reality? If someone were to ask me this, I would simply say:
'In the morning I watch the clouds in layers; in the evening I listen to the water murmuring. Tiantong Muan said: "Foguo’s eye covers [all others]."

The Five Heavens encompass all existence within their breast. According to his lifelong arrangements, whenever he uttered a single word or issued a single command, he sought to reach upward to the celestial canopy and penetrate downward through the wind-circle of the earth. Today, this mountain monk does not dare to suppress his majestic brilliance;
yet upon closely examining these words, they cannot help but seem trivial—achieving results by relying on another. Daofeng, however, was not like this. How is it that he was so great?
The causal conditions of the matter. As it was said before: "A few notes of yellow birds outside the green mountains; they monopolize the splendor and act as its masters.

A single hair has always drawn ten thousand pounds of weight; bearing the full burden, one meets the person of the present moment. With the hands and eyes of the whole body, one picks up and handles [the matter] again:
the withered tree blooms, and spring comes to the great earth. (Longxiang Yin)
A monk asked Touzi, "Caoshan points to the moon; Vulture Peak speaks of the moon. What is the true moon?
The Master said, "Last night at the third watch, it turned toward the west."
Falin’s Verse on Sound: "Why not give him his proper fodder?
Last night at the third watch he turned toward the west; At dawn, he moves spontaneously by the flowering stream.
Lifting his head, he does not recognize that perfect sphere— To whom shall these boundless pure breezes be entrusted? (Cishou Shen)

Heavy. The moon sets and the icy cold presses in; my hair grows thin.

Touzi, Touzi! The wheel of his spiritual mechanism turns without obstruction. Letting go one, he gains one; here and there are the same.
Piteous are the countless people who play with the tide; in the end, they return to die within the waves. Suddenly they are alive: the hundred rivers flow backward in a tumultuous roar.

When a monk asked Touzi, “What is it like when one goes out the door and does not see the Buddha? the Master said, “There is nothing to be seen.

Following skillful means, Maitreya does not dwell in the Tuṣita palace. (Luan Yue)

Chan Master Runu of Mount Daofang in Huzhou (a successor in the lineage of Cuiwei) was once asked by a monk, "How can one attain the nature of hearing such that it does not follow conditions?
The Master said, "Listen! The monk bowed. The Master said, "A deaf man singing a Hu tune;

"Standing from within emptiness, fire burns toward the water.

Standing amidst the thicket of sounds and forms, one perceives through hearing and seeing; worldly affairs follow conditions day after day in their bustle.

The Master replied, "Daoying. Dongshan said, "Why do you not speak from the perspective above? The Master said, "If it is from the perspective above..."
This is not called "receiving the Way.
Tianmu Lü says: "When these two great elders met in their ordinary daily interactions, they asked and answered with all their might, seeking to illuminate the singular path of nobility.

"This is a matter of ascending. "From here to the capital, there is still a journey of half a month remaining.

Yunju was once asked by Dongshan, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from treading upon mountains. Dongshan asked, "Which mountain is fit to dwell on?
The Master said, "Which mountain is unfit to dwell on? Dongshan said, "In this way, the entire country is occupied by you, O Śramaṇa!"
Lei Chan also asked this. The Master said, "Not so. Lei Chan said, "Have you not found a way of entry? The Master said, "There is no way.
Lei Chan said, "How then can you meet with me, the old monk? The Master said, "If there were a way, I would be separated from the Master by a lifetime.
Lei Chan said, "This son of mine will later be held by neither a thousand nor ten thousand people."
Qingshan said: "When masters meet, it is like a pearl rolling on a platter; the pearl rolls and the platter rolls, moving freely and without obstruction.
How can this be compared to those who strike ice to seek fire or climb a tree to catch fish? Today, if someone comes to this mountain, I shall ask:
'Do you come by way of a path, or do you come without a path? If you say you come by way of a path, you do not accord with Yunju."
This refers to having no path by which to come; it does not accord with Dongshan. Whether there is a path or no path, Qingshan says that both are blocked.
But tell me, how can one accord with the meaning of the ancients?
Master Nangye grasped Master Cheong’s hand and asked him: "There being no path, how were you able to reach this place? I suspect our karmic ties from three lifetimes have not yet been exhausted;
we still lack one more spring together to view the flowers. (Nangye) He inquired after the springtime: "How many layers of blossoms are there?
Mist and clouds occupy every peak wherever they reach. Once a traveler has returned from his journey, [he knows the truth].
Later, at the secluded mountain lodge, the midnight bell tolled (from the *Zixian ji*).
At Yunju, while a monk was reciting a sutra inside his room, the Master asked through the window, "Reverend, what sutra are you reciting?
He replied, "The Vimalakīrti Sūtra. The Master said, "I am not asking about the Vimalakīrti Sūtra; what sutra is it that you are actually reciting?"
The monk attained awakening through this.
Tiantong Huo said, "What a pity that this monk was buried alive by Yunju in the midst of wild weeds.
If you all can definitively emerge from this, you may settle yourselves beneath the bright window; if not, feel free to strike the bricks and beat the tiles as you please.
Questioning the Sūtra but not questioning the mindfulness of Vimalakīrti—does one see the bottom clearly through mindfulness?
If you wish to enter the ocean of dharmas as numerous as motes of dust, a single word will manifest it; there is no need for much.

(Tianzhang of Yuezhou) Setting sail with a favorable wind, one was about to reach Yangzhou, when the wind shifted, the bow turned, and the current flowed backward. Steering the rudder depends entirely upon the three elders.
With power, one reaches the shore in an instant—there is no need for worry. (The Dharma-hall is like) Mount Sumeru;
its peak is not seen. The great ocean is deep; its bottom is not seen. One sifts through dust and stirs up clouds of earth, yet finds no place to seek it.
Turning one’s head, one bumps into one's own ground. (Nantang Jing)
A monk asked Yunju, "What is the teacher of all Buddhas? The Master shouted, "You field-hand! The monk bowed.
The Master said, "How do you understand this? The monk replied, "That old monk! The Master said, "So, you don't understand after all.
The monk went out dancing. The Master remarked, "A beggar begging for food from the edge of the stage."
Zhaojue Qin said: "To discern the opportune moment and distinguish between fortune and misfortune requires an eye capable of shifting and turning;

to remain unmoving is for sprouts to grow right where one stands.
The affairs of doorways and thresholds differ in a thousand ways; though one has exhausted them all, one has not yet reached home.
Before the Hall of the Bright Moon stands a tree without shadow; on a night of severe frost and snow, it blooms in full flower.
(Danxia Chun) Upon the budless branch, the numinous blossom unfolds; ten thousand purples and thousands of reds vie with the evening glow. Drunken butterflies and wandering bees have no place to go.
Seeking it out, who would have known that spring colors pervade the ends of the earth? (Rhyme:
*yin*) The Iron Ox does not graze on the grass by the fence; The clever hare has never left its burrow.
If one can exhaust the present moment, Then even iron walls and silver mountains are no more than a trifle. (Lan’an Yu)

The monk asked, "How is it that when one emerges from the earth, one is wealthy and noble? The Master said, "It may exist within the midst of nothingness."
Relying on others for hire is ultimately not one's own; planting mulberry and hemp oneself yields more, even if sparse. In worldly affairs, nothing is better than doing well according to one’s lot.
I have casually transcribed the *Huangting jing* to exchange it for the "azure geese" (the calligraphy of Wang Xizhi).

This too has been excerpted. Now tell me, Minister, do you understand? Even if you were to understand it, it would still not be your own family treasure.

Kāśyapa did not conceal it; he cast his body across and took sole responsibility for it. The meaning of these words is clear and distinct; from ancient times to the present, it has been revealed in full majesty.

the solitary moon disc borrows a womb. (Nantang Jing)

Snow covers the thousand mountains, obscuring the paths and crossroads. The solitary peak remains unwhite, towering and majestic.
Though the young lords of the Five Tombs may swell with pride, the wild old man meets them without a frown.

(By Pung-hyeon Hyeon) They cannot be mixed; their kinds are not uniform. The six lines wind and turn to reveal the double *li* trigram. Deep into the night, one looks down upon the thousand mountains turned white.
It is not that those within [the school] do not know;
(Stone Creek Moon) within their words, both sides carry the profound and mysterious. They all attempt to distinguish the correct from the biased within their speech.
They bring shame upon the single imperial post road, which lies vast and submerged before the bright moon. (Steep Bank Xiang)
Caoshan asked Jinfeng Zhi, "What have you been doing? He replied, "I have been building a house.

The Master said, "Is it finished yet? He replied, "This side is finished. The Master said, "What about that side? He replied, "I shall inform the Abbot on the day the work begins. The Master said, "So it is, so it is."
Whirling the adze until it becomes wind—this was the marvel of Master Shi. Towering over the ravines like Qiao and Song, they possess the form of great beams and pillars.

Discerning the mark within the essence, knowing the pivot beyond all measure: on this side and that side, every step is flawless; moving across the board without fixed destination, they are like brilliant, falling pearls. (Yungeng Jing)
Caoshan addressed the assembly: "All those in various quarters merely hold fast to their own standards;
why not give them a turning word so that they may be free from doubt? Yunmen then asked, "Why is it that one does not know what exists in the most profound and subtle place?
Caoshan said, "Precisely because it is so profound and subtle, one does not know it. Yunmen asked, "How should one approach such a person? Caoshan said, "Do not look toward it."
"Approach closely in the dense place. [The student] asked, "When one does not approach closely in the dense place, what then?
The Master said, "Only then do you understand how to approach. The student responded, "Yes, yes."

Caoshan said, "Attaining it is not as good as not attaining it. The monk asked, "What is it like when not attaining it? Caoshan said, "It is like a person who has lost their way. The monk asked, "What is it like when one has attained it? Caoshan said, "It is like a person who has found their way. The monk asked, "What is it like when one has neither attained nor not attained? Caoshan said, "It is like a person who has neither lost nor found their way. The monk asked, "What is it like when one has both attained and not attained? [The student] asked, "Is it that there is no such thing as 'borrowing' its use? The Master said, "The very moment you speak of sitting is itself its use.
One cannot shift mountains or block the sea while speaking of Chan or speaking of the Way and yet call that 'use.'"
"Do not say that the principle of clarity and emptiness is mere reunion; if you say it is clarity and emptiness, you will lose your very body.
It was the eyebrows that once asked the eyes: how could the black pupil see itself? (Benjue I).
Once, when a monk asked Caoshan, "What thing in the world is most precious? the Master said, "A dead cat's head is most precious."
It is said that the head of a dead cat is most precious. The Master said, "No one will offer a price.
Tiantong Jue said, "Caoshan’s merchandise does not enter the marketplace; even upon careful inspection, it is not worth a single coin."
"When Cao Shan encountered the lowly, he made them noble; here, when I encounter the noble, I make them lowly. Tell me, is there any contradiction here?
Baoyuan Xiu said, "A household is not wealthy if it has no goods for sale. He further said, "The World-Honored One held up a flower;
Jushi (Clodpate) pointed his finger. Tell me, are these the same as a dead cat's head, or are they different?"
Foul-smelling, red and putrid, it is unfit for human touch; The slightest contact leaves the body stained with blood.
Why is it that no one offers a price? It is because this is not a treasure of the world.
(Danxia Chun) In the thatched hall, the door has long been shut against wind and rain; Snow-melted and cloud-steamed, years pass uncounted. This stagnant wares cannot bear the current market price.
Encountering it on the street, displayed as a stall, one is met with disdain.
(Tianyu Bao) People know how to add brocade upon brocade; who recognizes the opulence of the cold crags? The wind sweeps over the stone rills, every stream a string of jade;
the snow adorns the plum branches, every tree a cluster of blossoms. (Miman Ke)
When Caoshan heard the sound of the bell, he said, "A-ye! A-ye! A monk asked, "What are you doing, Master?
The Master replied, "I have struck my own heart. The monk was speechless.
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said in his place: "The heart of a thief is naturally timid. Jingshan Xiu said: "The thief confesses of his own accord. Baoshou Fang said:
"What limit is there for this fellow who dabbles with his spirit? He should be banished to another land."
Qinghua said: "A man of immeasurable capacity, yet he dandles the sons and daughters of others amidst sounds and forms.
Hearing the bell, he calls to the assembly and strikes at my own mind; the idle words of this wanderer intoxicate me even deeper.
That one who attained perfect penetration at the Śūraṅgama Assembly was the King of Righteous Dharma, Avalokiteśvara. (By Banyarou)
A monk asked Caoshan, "What is the master of the Dharmakāya? The Master said, "It is said that there is no one in Qin.
The monk asked, "Is this not so? The Master said, "Behead him! (Zhan).
Baizhang Le said: "Relying on the gate and leaning against the door, one seeks the master and questions the servant.
As for Caoshan’s utterance of the word 'sever' (*zhàn*), tell me, what was his intention? He gave a shout and said: "I thought there was no one here. Do not say I did not speak!"
Caoshan asked a monk, "What are you doing? The monk replied, "Sweeping. The Master said, "Are you sweeping before the Buddha or sweeping behind the Buddha?
The monk said, "I am sweeping both front and back at once. The Master said, "Then bring me my sandals."
The Fifth Patriarch Jie spoke on his behalf: "What kind of mental activity is the Master's?
Only one who recognizes the squareness and roundness of his capacity can understand him. When he asks, "Is sweeping the ground compassion?
he sweeps away both the preceding and the succeeding moments at once; this too is seizing its secondary function. (Fenyang Shao)
A monk asked Caoshan, "What is it like when the spirit-clothes are no longer worn? The Master said, "Mount Ceng’s period of mourning has ended.
The monk asked, "After the mourning has ended, what then? The Master said, "Caoshan loves to get drunk on wild wine."
Baoneng Xiu said: "Cao Shan is sometimes drunk, yet he is lucid within his intoxication; sometimes he is sober, yet he makes no distinction between day and night.

This is because his 'Yellow Millet Dream' has been severed and his domestic attachments have been forgotten. This is why Xinfeng could say that wherever he looked there were only wild forests, and that for years he had lived in leisurely abandon.
Yet, after the filial duty is fulfilled, what is it ultimately like? The four seasons are rich with spring."
The refined elegance of wine and objects;
a household of purity and clarity, utterly unmatched by its neighbors. For years locked away, it admits no dust. Where the light turns, the waning moon is cast down;
when the hexagram lines divide, the month of Yin begins anew. With filial devotion fulfilled, one encounters spring; with steps of intoxication and wild song, one lets them fall.
Wiping his brow, with disheveled hair he wanders aimlessly—who cares for him? In this era of peace and no affairs, he is a man intoxicated by wine.
(Tiantong Jue) The spirit’s bed emerges from the house, a joyful countenance abounds; in western villages and eastern hamlets, songs are sung freely.
Unaware of the decree of the Emperor of Great Peace, he constantly tunes the "Snow Song" amidst the mountain crags. (Guiguo Xian)
Unfastening my sash, I have returned home with nothing to do; Intoxicated by Zhongshan wine, I find it easy to evade Qin. With hair disheveled and legs sprawled, I am a man of carefree decline;
I laugh as I watch the children plant willows anew. Leaning idly on my staff, I walk along the clear ford; The wind carries falling flowers as the spring flows with the water. (Qingyun Qi)
A monk asked Caoshan, "What is a lion? The Master said, "No beasts can approach it. The monk asked, "What is a lion cub?
The Master said, "One who can swallow its parents. The monk asked, "Since no beasts can approach it, why is it instead swallowed by its cub?
The Master said, "Have you not heard it said that when the son roars, the patriarchs flee?"

When both father and son have perished, [the student] asked, "What is it like after they have perished? The Master said, "The whole body returns to the father. [The student] asked, "I do not yet understand:
when the Patriarch has perished, where does the father go? The Master said, "That place also perishes. [The student] asked, "Why did you previously say that the whole body returns to the father?
The Master said, "It is like a prince who is able to accomplish the affairs of an entire kingdom."
Baoshou Fang said: "Do you wish to understand the meaning of the whole body returning to its father? When great functions manifest together, one forgets both contact and avoidance;
who else is there to determine killing or giving life in response to the occasion? Shouchang Cun said:
"Since both subject and object are exhausted, from where could the descendants underfoot possibly meet their ancestors?"
A monk asked Caoshan, "Who is it that brandishes a sword within the borders of the kingdom? The Master said, "Caoshan. The monk asked, "Whom do you intend to kill?
The Master said, "I would kill everyone. The monk asked, "What if one suddenly encounters one's own biological parents? The Master said, [I would still kill them]."
The Master said, "What do you choose? [The monk] said, "But what can one do about oneself? The Master said, "Who can do anything to me?
[The monk] said, "Why not kill yourself? The Master said, "There is no place to apply the blow."

A precipice of ten thousand fathoms—this is Caoshan. With a majestic and formidable presence, he sits at the ancestral pass. Grasping his Mohe sword crosswise, he issues the full command of the True Order;
throughout the realm of Great Peace, he slays the dull-witted and the stubborn.
(Fóxìng Tàiyán) Caoshan was once asked by a monk who recounted the dialogue between Lùhù and Nánquán regarding Nánquán’s surname. Nánquán said, "My surname is Wáng. Lùhù said:
"Does the King still have attendants? Quan said, "The four ministers are not obscure. The monk asked, "In what position does the King reside? Quan said, "Moss grows upon the jade palace.
A monk asked, "What is the matter with 'moss growing upon the jade palace'? The Master said, "He does not occupy the central throne.
[The monk] asked, "When the eight directions come to pay court, what then? The Master said, "He does not accept the ritual prostrations. [The monk] said, "If that is so..."

[The monk] asked, "Then what is the use of coming to court? The Master said, "Those who disobey shall be executed. [The monk] said, "Disobedience is the duty of a subject; I do not yet know what Your Majesty’s intention is.
The Master said, "The Chief Councillor has not received the Imperial decree. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then the merit of governing the realm belongs entirely to the ministers and counselors.
The Master said, "Do you still understand the Imperial intention? [The monk] said, "One outside the secular world does not dare to deliberate upon it."
The Master said: "So it is, so it is.
When moss grows upon the jade palace, one truly has no place to dwell. The four ministers have no way to offer their sagacious counsel; the old farmer knows this—by whose power does he receive it?
As the breeze warms, his song falls upon the wild plow. (Shilin Gong)
The golden ducks' incense has faded and the night-watchers' water-chimes linger on; deep within the jade palace, purple moss grows.
The high heavens hold a moon that illuminates a thousand gates, yet upon the Great Way there is no one—only I walk alone.
(Shifanyan) Caoshan asked Senior Monk Jiang: "The Buddha’s true Dharma-body is like empty space; it manifests forms in response to things."
"The moon in the water. [The student asked,] "How do you explain the principle of the response? He said, "It is like a donkey looking down a well.

The Master said, "You have explained it quite well, but you have only captured eighty percent of it. [The student asked,] "And how about you, Teacher? The Master said, "It is like a well looking down at a donkey."
Boshanlai said: "The brilliance of a noble scholar and the manner of a poet are here perfectly integrated; there is no further depth to be found.
Caoshan’s guidance transcends the ordinary, like performing a somersault down from the crest of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff—one cannot reach up to grasp it."
It is not merely the Three Mysteries and Five Ranks; truly, the skulls of Buddhas and Patriarchs have all been pierced through.
*Ei!* Words that emerge have never been fully perfected; if there is speech, it must be free from mundane sentiments. The Jade Maidens by the river laugh aloud;
the stone men on the ridge listen with their ears pricked. (The Withered Tree is Complete.)
The donkey gazes at the well; the well gazes at the donkey. Wisdom encompasses all without limit; stillness contains all with abundance.
Who can discern the seal behind the elbow? No books are stored within the house. The shuttle-head is unattached to the warp and woof; the patterns run wild and free, their meaning uniquely distinct.
(Tiantong Ju) The donkey gazes at the well; the well gazes at the donkey. A gourd grows upon the leaves of a winter melon. If you cannot understand, do not hesitate. It is settled.
On the plate of stars, not even a grain’s weight is left.
(Wuan Quan) Killing and giving life applied together—truly a master at work. A sword dances in mid-air, its movements dense and frantic.
If the two eyes were to miss by even a hair’s breadth, it would turn into acres of mustard flowers. (Tanjirnin)
Tearing down the eastern fence, patching up the western wall—through ten thousand kalpas, they remain of one and the same substance. To mistake the head for its reflection is to lose one’s nostrils;
yet, they are not lost. Above, below, and in the four cardinal directions, there is no peer to compare.
(Di Hui Lu) When a monk asked Caoshan, "What is it like when the five ranks respond to guests? the Master said, "Which one are you asking about right now?"
A monk said, "I have come from the position of partiality; I request that the Master receive me within the position of correctness.
The Master said, "I will not receive you. The monk asked, "Why will you not receive me? The Master said, "I fear you would fall back into the position of partiality.
The Master then asked the monk, "As for this non-reception—is it a reception of the guest or not? The monk replied, "It has already been a reception of the guest."
The Master said: "So it is, so it is.
In the moon, the jade hare conceives in the night; in the sun, the golden crow broods over its egg at dawn.
A dark-lacquered Kunlun man walks through the snow; turning his body, he shatters the lapis lazuli bowl. (Danxia Chun)
Thus he dwells in peace within the state, like the Elephant before the Emperor. Beyond the curtains of the night’s clarity, no news is conveyed.
The golden cock crows, shattering the dream of the jade man; the hues of dawn linger before the brocade curtains.

(The Ancient Sage) Deeply silent and soundless, he bows to the Supreme Honored One. As soon as there is a trace of movement, he is no longer present. At midnight, when no one hears the palace watch, [the silence remains].
Leakage. When the moon rises, the pear blossoms close their gates deep within. (Yiranji) Caoshan was asked by a monk:
"When a child returns to his father, why does the father not acknowledge him at all? The Master said, "It is only right that it should be so.

The monk asked, "Where then is the affection between father and son? The Master said, "Only then is the affection between father and son truly established. The monk asked again: [The text provided ends here.]
"What is the debt of gratitude between father and son? The Master said, "A blade or an axe cannot cleave it open.
Tiantong Jue said, "The emerald curtain hangs down; the imperial decree has not yet descended. The purple silk screen is closed; sight and hearing cannot penetrate it."
A transgression as slight as a hair’s breadth. When the moon rises at the night door, one takes a step in secret; the crane flies out from its silver cage. Do you know?
Shedding the body within the single color, there is no lingering shadow; not sitting in the same wind, one avoids falling into the great [trap]. Baoen Xiu said:
"Stepping back to court the sovereign, turning the body to approach the father. Caoshan has exerted his utmost strength to uphold this and emptied his bag to hand it over. Heaven!
A child, at night by the bright curtain outside the Hall of the Empty King, borrows the proclamation from a tongueless person and receives the mandate through an earless person.
This is still merely the matter of the moon rising beside the night door; how do you speak the phrase "the crane emerges from the silver cage"?
"Hardly has it spread its wings in the nine ravines, yet it vainly pursues the wind for a thousand li. Miaoye Qi said, "Moss grows in the jade palace;

the crane emerges from its silver cage. It lies only within the realm of ordinary daily conduct—how regrettable that those who recognize this grace are so few. After a long silence, he said, "It is also very difficult to maintain continuity."
An axe cannot cleave it open; the numinous mechanism is free from a speck of dust. A pure breeze sweeps away the lingering snow; harmonious breath brings spring back.
(Taidu Yun) A curtain of emptiness and stillness closes the deep palace; the ancient mirror is profound and dark, revealing no form. Turning one’s step to return, there is truly nothing to be seen.
Bian: The moon enshrouds colored mists as it locks the vast sky.
(Ningyuan Di) Directly beneath, one utterly forgets the dignity of the ancestors; who would begrudge discussing kinship through intellectual understanding?
Let the dust of the six kingdoms settle, and you must believe that Heaven and Earth serve but One Man. (Luyan He)
Densely packed, the golden scissors cannot cut it open; the smoke has subsided in the ancient cauldron, submerged in cold ashes.
At night’s deep, there is ultimately no one to attend; who outside the door is fit to set foot within?
(Pingxiang) When a monk asked Caoshan, “Why can unmoving grass conceal a fragrant elephant? the Master said, “O *śramaṇa*...”
Li Xing was a poet. He also said: "Ask Caoshan what it is:
A single cloak of mist and rain upon the eyes of spring; In every place, willows hang over fishing boats. The wooden man sleeps so deeply he knows not the dawn;
The stone woman holds her lamp beneath the autumn clouds beyond. Autumn beyond the clouds—answering with a hidden mechanism. Before the wind, the southward journey has already been lost."
Wild geese; after the rain, they resemble once more the single hook of the moon.
(Tian’an Sheng) The mountains stretch on and on, and the waters flow on and on. The willows hang down so supple, a perfect place to moor the boat.
Where the stars and constellations shone with brilliance last night, I often wondered if the bright moon had filled the entire blue isle. (Ni Shan Wei)
Caoshan addressed the assembly: "Do not travel the path of the mind; do not don the garment of the original source. What need is there for 'just so'?
Most certainly avoid 'before birth. Baiyan Fu said:
"Great indeed is Caoshan’s fear of the blade and avoidance of the arrow! But Baoshou would not have it this way. He then recited: "Love..."
When walking along the path of the mind, one constantly wears the garment of original nature. What prevents suchness? It does not obstruct that which has not yet arisen.
"Great assembly, if you rely on Caoshan, you will affirm Baoshou; if you rely on Baoshou, you will affirm Caoshan. Is there anyone among you who stands out as exceptional?
Try to offer a different phrase. After a long silence, he said: "If there were no lifting of the tripod or pulling of the mountain..."
Strength! A black steed from a thousand li is not easily ridden.
Before Mount Fankuo, I met Du Fu; he wore a bamboo hat as the sun stood at its zenith. I asked him why he had become so thin since we last parted;
it was simply because of the toil of composing poetry in the past. (A rare and magnificent poem.)
Born into a wealthy and noble family, how could one know the poison of wealth and nobility? It was not only Xu You who was deluded;
there was also the even more deluded Chao Fu (Qie Chu Ne).
When a monk asked Caoshan, "Who is it that constantly emerges from and submerges within the sea of birth and death? the Master said:
The second month, [a monk] asked, "Is there no seeking for liberation? The Master said, "There is indeed seeking for liberation; it is simply that there is no path.
The monk asked, "What kind of person can receive him? The Master said, "One who is bound by shackles and fetters."
Shending said, "To cast off the precious and don the coarse, to wear shackles and be bound by cangues—this is the everyday meal of every monk's household.
Yet when suddenly called upon, they do not turn their heads; these are board-carrying fellows who cannot be confined. Do not vainly claim this is Caoshan."
Even if a thousand Buddhas were to appear in the world, they would only have the means to withdraw. Nevertheless, tell me:
did Caoshan point the way while at Dangyang, or did he honor the whole body? Do you understand? A single breath speaks not, yet it contains all forms;
where do the myriad spirits offer thanks for this impartiality?
Appearing and disappearing according to the teachings for the second month; a single hair’s breadth of attachment leaves the karma of the three paths.
This causes people for a thousand ages to remember Hanshan: "The old road cannot be returned to for ten years; yet if one can return, it is a solitary iron bar stretching ten thousand miles.

(Yi gui gui). Caoshan addressed the assembly: "Ordinary sentiment and holy views are golden chains. On the profound path, one must employ mutual interpenetration (*huigu*). As for taking [the Way]..."

Regarding those who subsist on right livelihood, they must possess three types of "falling" (duo). First, wearing fur and bearing horns; second, not severing sound and form; third, not receiving food.
Choubunuo asked, "Wearing fur and bearing horns—what kind of falling is this? The Master said, "This is the falling of the category.
"Not severing sound and form—what kind of falling is this? The Master said, "This is the falling of following. "Not receiving food—" [The Master said, "This is the falling of non-attachment."]
"This is a profound fall. The Master said, "This is a noble fall.
With horns mingled in the mud and dust, this very body is clearly revealed. On the banks of fragrant grass and green willows, where is there that does not proclaim its nobility?"
(From *Lèiduō*, Baizhang’s Third Case) The monkey cries under the frosty night moon;
The flowers smile at the spring of Qinyuan. Amidst the vast expanse of red dust, Every single thing is the old friend.
(Falling into Following):
In the painted hall there are no locks or keys; who would dare to step across its threshold? Do not wonder why there are no overnight guests; from the very beginning, no one has been seen there.
(Falling into Noble Dignity).
In the midst of chaos, activity and rest are one and the same; it is like snow placed within a silver bowl. If you wish to be different from an ox, how would you differ from an ox?
(Liu Duo; Juefan Hong, No. 3) All that is heard is unheard;
all that is seen is fundamentally nothing. If you seek to sever sound and form, a wooden puppet shall attain Buddhahood.

(Falling accordingly,) one is born into the family of a sovereign; what further nobility could there be? One should naturally wear precious and imperial regalia; looking upon these, what cause for alarm or wonder is there?
(The Noble and Honored Fall).
It is fitting to unite with the original mind and eliminate every worldly concern. Throughout the ten directions and all sand-grain worlds, the Great Vairocana turns his head;
on both banks, the greenery is lush. He smiles and points, asking: "Do people of this age recognize him or not? (Senshō Tetsumitsu).

Amidst the halls of song and pipe, he strikes the gavel of stillness; though the banquet is splendid and radiant, he does not raise an eyebrow. The Great Being of Perfect Penetration has nothing more to say.
A technique: when the mind is absent in one place, both places are deficient;
in the four directions and eight corners, there is no mutual recognition. Sitting alone in vast stillness, how could there be any limit? Suddenly, a clear breeze carries a distant fragrance;
in the air, several petals of flowers lie scattered in disarray.
Caoshan asked Elder De: "In which sutra does it say that when a Bodhisattva is in meditative concentration, he hears an elephant crossing a river?
De replied: "It appears in the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*. The Master said: "Did he hear it before entering concentration, or did he hear it after?

De said: "This is your teacher’s own flow [of words], Master. The Master said: "You speak quite well, indeed; yet you have spoken only half. De asked: "How about you, Master? The Master said: "The rapids."
Reaching down to grasp it—Qíhuā points toward the falling plum branches; jade-pressed, it extends horizontally for twelve feet.
Who would believe that amidst the biting cold of night, the ethereal souls of fragrance drift as they play the flute in the caverns? (Qìngshān Dǐng)

Chan Master Kuangren of Shushan in Fuzhou (successor of Dongshan Jia), the sixth generation descendant of Dajian Huineng, was once asked by a monk: "What is the teacher of all Buddhas?"
The Master said, "Why do you not ask the old fellow from Shushan? The monk had no reply.
Only by raising a child does one know the compassion of the parent above; the words of a relative have no flavor, yet outsiders harbor doubts.
If you wish to exhaust the deepest reaches of the vast blue sea, listen to the "Fisherman’s Song" and do not be deluded. (Touzi Qing)
The stone dragon sprouted wings and suddenly soared upward; from its mouth it spat forth tens of millions of layers of yellow clouds.
The great earth, mountains, and rivers were all shrouded in mist, leaving people with no way to distinguish the stars.
(From *Qianzhishen*) Shushan had a monastery official build a funerary pagoda for him. When the pagoda was finished, the official informed the Master. The Master asked, "How much [did it cost]?"
The Master gave three coins to the artisan. The patron said, "Everything depends on you, Reverend.
The Master asked, "Shall I give three coins to the artisan? Shall I give two coins to the artisan? Or shall I give one coin to the artisan?
If you can say something [to resolve this], I will build the pagoda for you myself. The patron was speechless. Later, he recounted this to Daling Xian. Xian said, "Is there anyone who..."
"Can you say it? The Master said, "No one has been able to say it yet. Ling said, "When you return, tell Shushan:
'If you give three coins to the craftsman, the Master will certainly not obtain the pagoda in this lifetime.
If you give two coins to the craftsman, the Master and the craftsman will join hands together. If you give one coin to the craftsman... [The text ends here].
A man was working for a master craftsman when his eyebrows and beard fell out. When the master returned, he reported this to the Teacher (the Master).

The Teacher assumed a dignified demeanor, looked toward the Great Ridge in the distance, and prostrated himself from afar, saying: "I thought there was no one; it turns out the Great Ridge has an ancient Buddha emitting light that shoots all the way here.
"Even so," he added, "it is like a lotus flower in the month of December. Later, the one from the Great Ridge heard of this and said: "I acted in such a manner..."
"The Way is also like a tortoise hair three feet long.
Fushan Yuan said: "Shushan used a chisel to strike the earth; Daying used a knife to carve the void.

Although these two ancient worthies applied their chisels and knives in error, people of the present day find it difficult to match them. Why? Because within their subsequent words there is both 'striking' and 'carving'."
"Kill! Even so, it is like losing money in a river and searching for it in the river. Cheng Tianzong said:
"What is there to say about 'tortoise hair three feet long' or 'lotuses in the twelfth month'? All such things are merely rolling in the grass while still wearing one's clothes.
Even if you were to categorize and arrange matters here into threes and fours, explaining them with such brilliant clarity, you have not yet seen the Patriarch’s true eye in a dream. I...
At that time, had one seen Shushan speak thus, one would have simply said, "Not even a single coin.

Had he waited for him to further expound upon principles, one would have immediately overturned the meditation seat and demolished the memorial pagoda, leaving this old fellow without a place of reliance for the rest of his life.
Why is this so? Because only by knowing gratitude can one understand how to repay it. Baenlun said: "Today, Lin..."
"Furthermore, Master Quan, it requires a specific approach. If you give three coins to the artisan, you will certainly not obtain a pagoda in this lifetime.
Why? Because it would be laborious yet fruitless; he would become intoxicated by wine and negligent in his work.
If you give two coins to the artisan, you and the artisan will join hands together; neither will be at a loss, and there will be no outstanding debt."
"If one were to give a single coin to a craftsman, it would cause that craftsman's eyebrows and whiskers to fall out.
Everyone knows that Shushan did not pluck out even a single hair; do you also know where Linquan makes such a judgment? A drunkard’s mouth is a measureless bushel."
Slicing and stir-frying in leisure; barbarians brawling in strife. When the wine has sobered and the cool moon fills half the window, the lamp flickers dimly—what else is there?
Wuzu Gang said: "These too are the seventy-two suspicious tombs of Cao Mao."
A clear breeze stirs the fishing boat; The sails hoisted, the waves rise to strike the heavens. How laughable, the glistening scales vying to play in the water;
In the end, they are all pulled by the fishing line. (Danxia Chun) Having received the elegant style, she transmits it to the powder-painting youth;
In a single day, three times she skillfully applies her makeup. Changing her head and face, no one [recognizes her].
Shi Yuan was originally Li Erniang of the Eastern Village (Fujian Qin).
She dug up the communal land belonging to the Sangha of the ten directions; for three coins, she exposed the remains of corpses.
Though Luoshan the Ancient Buddha was efficacious and miraculous, he could not avoid having his own body buried in one place (Jingshan Gao).
I have always loved the jade-like beauty with her smiling, azure eyes; yet her voice and form are ever separated by a sandy islet.
Who says the Yellow River does not roll on today? Its waves, though windless, harbor no lingering sentiment. (Three Verses, Chongjue Kongsan) Annoyingly, the cowpen was opened last night;
the person at the head of the ridge called, but did not return. I trouble you to tell this to the Western Mountain.
The moon does not shine upon the cold ashes of a solitary lamp.
(Two *wen*) When practicing causes, one must distinguish the resulting fruits; a jeweled pagoda soaring into the void costs but a single *wen*.
If you wish to understand the ultimate meaning of Shushan, the ancestral patriarchs of our house reside in Bingfen. (One *wen*)
Thump, thump, the drum. The spring of the second month. At dawn, with wind and waning moon, one sacrifices to the River God.
On this Qingming day, the ghosts here are countless; how many are the souls severed upon the road?
(Xueqiao Xin III) Smoke drifts fine and thin; the willow branches are fresh. It is the weather for those who drink, the Jade Tower Spring. Butterflies flutter and soar outside the empty courtyard.

Citing the deity within the wistaria flowers, who possesses the power of transformation—how could its shadow be so light? It is clear that this thing is a spirit-demon; its entire body is pure white, as if made of jade.
Not a single speck of sentiment for your house;
the stupa is crystalline, transcending all bounds and new. Its layered ridges meet at the summit, even more rugged and imposing.
On the top of the flagpole, five *liang* of silk flutter—how many who are rushing toward their goal are made to laugh to death! (Xuechan Bai)
A monk once asked Shushan, "What is the meaning of winter's arrival? The Master said, "The capital produces great yellow [rhubarb]. Gunan said:
"If someone were to ask me, 'What is the meaning of winter's arrival? I would tell them: 'Xinghua’s lotus shells are good for planting fire.
Now tell me, how far apart are these two ancient masters? If you all treat this as a mere worldly discourse,"
The Buddha-dharma has not yet been glimpsed even in a dream; yet you continue to deliberate upon the Buddha-dharma. Even across thousands of miles, what ultimately is it?
You must know that beyond the distant mists and waves, there is another way to deliberate.
The capital produces great yellow; where it is ripe, it is most difficult to forget. Dao-wu constantly performs a dance; he was originally just Xie Sanlang.
(Dan-xia Chun) When asked about matters of winter’s arrival: "The capital produces great yellow. For the sake of one grain of rice, he loses six months of rations."
(Mimian Jie): In the capital they produce great yellow [turmeric]; seeing the thief, one sees the stolen goods. The bamboo staff transforms into a dragon and departs;
the fool bails out the night pond. (Songyuan Yue)
As the movement of the sun’s shadow shifts and the days grow longer, the silent youth deliberates within himself.
Although this is not something a divine immortal has applied, it is the foremost prescription transmitted from across the sea.
