"Building a carriage while the door is closed; fitting the parts together when the door is open. These two venerable masters may be said to have accomplished their work spontaneously, with the beginning and end corresponding perfectly.
However, if we discuss matters that transcend the Dharmakāya, all such efforts are merely like lashing a boat to a post and rowing it—dare I say they have not even dreamed of the truth.
"Is there anyone here now who wishes to understand? He then made the gesture of rowing a boat and said: "Beyond the mountains are more mountains; beyond the pavilions are more pavilions.
When will the singing and dancing at West Lake ever cease? The warm breeze intoxicates the travelers. He then let out a shout and said: "Hah!"
Had it not been for this one shout, he would have nearly said, "Mistaking Hangzhou for Bianzhou.
His eyes look toward the southeast, yet his intent lies in the northwest. He turns the pivot of heaven and overturns the axis of earth.

Above the Dharma-body and within the realm of the Dharma-body, there has been a spirit of rare and heroic breath for five hundred years. Like glue and lacquer meeting, like arrows supporting one another, Mount Nan rises.
Clouds and rain over the northern mountains (Yuanwu Qin).
Verdant and interlacing within the caverns of pine and creeper, the tall bamboo stands transcendent as a thing beyond all things.
Do not compare the tall bamboo to the lofty pine; it does not equal the lofty pine’s aged wind-bone. (Fojian Qin)
Shushan visited Xiangyan at a time when Xiangyan was presiding over the assembly. A monk asked, "When one does not admire the various sages and does not prize one's own spiritual nature, what then?

Xiangyan replied, "All myriad functions cease; even the thousand sages cannot carry one away. Shushan, standing in the midst of the assembly, let out a sound like retching and said, "What kind of words are these?
Xiangyan immediately descended from his seat and called to him, saying, "That was my response to this monk just now."
"There must be something wrong, which has led to my uncles being reproached by you. I do not know where the fault lies.
The Master said, "When the myriad functions have ceased, there is still something remaining. Though the thousand sages did not carry it with them, it was nonetheless obtained from others.
How can you say there is no fault? Yan said, "I ask the Master to speak for me. The Master said, "If I am to make you speak, you must first pay me the courtesy due to a teacher."
Only then did Yanguan attain realization. He prostrated and repeated his previous question. The Master said, "Why do you not say that 'acceptance' and 'agreement' cannot both be total?
Yanguan said, "If it is acceptance, what is there to accept? If it is agreement, with whom is one agreeing? The Master said, "Acceptance is accepting the thousand sages;
agreement is agreeing with one's own numinous spirit. Yanguan said, "If my teacher, the Junior Uncle, speaks thus, then in the future [the teaching] will be overturned."
"I have been away for thirty years," [the Master] said. Later, the Master indeed acted exactly as he had previously recorded.
Afterwards, the Master asked Jingqing, "When one says 'yes' or 'no,' they cannot be total. How do you understand this? Jingqing replied, "The whole is contained within 'yes' and 'no.
The Master asked, "If they cannot be total, then how? Jingqing said, "Within this, there is no path of 'yes. The Master said, "Now, at last, you satisfy this sick monk's mind."
Zifu Guang said: "Xiangyan’s one lift and one strike produced a brilliant luster. It is indeed excellent;
however, it is a pity that he did not use the staff of a monk. Had he used the staff at that time, thirty years would not have been necessary.
Nevertheless, I still wish to ask everyone: regarding Xiangyan’s final statement, 'In the future, you will vomit for thirty years,' was this truly Shushan’s fruit?"

"Is this a miraculous manifestation of the Buddha-dharma as the prophecy foretold, or is there some other underlying principle? After reflecting for a long while, he clapped his hands and laughed loudly, saying:
"Once Ziqi is dead, there is no one who understands the music; how could I not break the strings of Boya's zither?"
A blade does not cut itself; a finger does not touch itself. The crane is white, the crow is black; the pine is straight, the thorn is crooked.
As soon as a speck of dust with its shadow appears, it is entirely cast off, leaving no trace. "I am willing not to preserve it; I grant it not to establish.
A single piece of pure light shoots toward the Dipper and Ox stars; in heaven and on earth, one attains freedom. (Wenyu Qin)
Cutting through the flesh to see the bone; stripping away the meat to seek the core. Threads depart as silks arrive; spirits emerge and ghosts vanish.

There has never been a gap so slight as a hair’s breadth, yet it seems as if fire and water were separated. For thirty years I have vomited my guts out upside down, until my forehead was willing to touch the ground;

only then did I satisfy the intent of this sick monk. I see only the benefit of heading westward; cherish these words from my entire life to instruct future generations. These words of bitter frustration, once spat out, are swallowed back again.
(Muchunmen) Shushan held a wooden snake in his hand. When someone asked, "What is that in your hand? the Master raised it and said, "A daughter of the Cao family."
Tianmu Li said: "The wooden snake in my hand was the daughter of the Cao family; her beauty was extraordinary, yet her malicious intent was difficult to restrain.
He took up his staff and said: "Now she has manifested herself on the South Mountain; who dares to look at her as she brandishes it upside down?
He threw it down and said: "Watch out for your life!"
In separation, one’s face is not as smiling as a flower; in the sorrow of parting, it is difficult to find anything like the heartless bamboo.
Because others spoke of the daughter of the Cao family, my illness of longing was drawn deeper.
(Cishou Shen) In my old age, I have lost all sense of reason; I call a wooden snake the daughter of the Cao family. If I do not yet encounter one surnamed Pan...
Lan: Generally speaking, no one is willing to grant permission.
(Tianyu Bao) Shushan asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Xuefeng. The Master said, "When I arrived previously, everything was insufficient;
is it sufficient now? He replied, "It is sufficient now. The Master said, "Sufficient for porridge, sufficient for rice."
The monks remained silent.
A single official road stretches out level and smooth; Countless travelers pass along it at their leisure. Do not say that because the ground is level there is no danger;
One must know that even on level ground there are deep pits. (Cishou Shen)
Shushan arrived at Jiaoshan. Jiaoshan ascended the hall. The Master asked, "I have heard your words: 'Before one's eyes there is no dharma; the meaning lies before one's eyes.
What, then, is the dharma that is not before one's eyes? Jiaoshan said, "The night moon flows with radiance; the clear pool has no reflection.
The Master made a gesture of overturning the meditation seat. Jiaoshan asked, "What about you, Layman? The Master said, "Before one's eyes there is nothing."
The Dharma is utterly ungraspable. Master Shan said: "Look at this one warrior!
Upon the eight-flowered ball, he embroiders the red banner; on the hundred battlefields, he grasps it with his bare hands.
Having returned to his country with a song of victory, the hero has won and made this a time of peace. (Wuliangshou)
The numinous talisman and the dagger are hidden within the scabbard; entering alone into the heavy encirclement, his courage is bold.
Alas, because the commander-in-chief can kill or give life, others' stratagems are all in vain.
(Jia-shui Qia) Shu-shan was asked by National Teacher Yao: "Whose realm is this, with its hundreds of folds and thousands of layers? The Master said: "Left."
Twisting reed ropes to bind the ghost-child;
a hundred coils, a thousand layers, as if wishing to inquire all around. Shushan answered with a total liberation from form.
At that time, who among the assembly understood? It was so direct that the waters of Jiangxi flowed backward. (Touzi Shu)
Shushan was once asked by Lingquan: "Regarding the saying that 'a withered tree produces flowers,' this begins to accord with others.
Is this a phrase of this side, or a phrase of that side? The Master said, "It is also a phrase of this side. Lingquan asked, "What is a phrase of that side?
The Master said, "A stone ox breathes forth the mist of the three springs; a spiritual sparrow does not perch in the shadowless forest."
The vast ocean is calm when the wind ceases; the mist clears and the water’s hue holds the moon in its emptiness.
A single band of cold radiance—how can one look upon it without end? Who can discern within this the dragon shedding its bones?
(Danxia Chun) Mist locks and clouds seal the body in vast fusion; since there is no path within, how could it be traversed? A sacred spring gushes forth, free from partiality.

Chan Master Qian of Qinglin in Suizhou (third generation successor of Dongshan Jia). Whenever there was a new arrival, he first ordered them to carry firewood three times before they were permitted to enter the hall for formal practice.
There was a monk who did not comply and asked: "Within these three turns..."
[The monk] did not answer. [The Master asked,] "How is it outside the three turnings? The Master said, "The Iron Wheel-turning King’s decree within the realm.

The vast river is clear and transparent, reflecting the moon’s brilliance; yet this pervasive purity before one's eyes is not yet home.
I ask: where does the fisherman’s boat go? At nightfall, as always, it rests among the reeds. (Danxia Chun)
The Three Elders silently turn the rudder; the solitary boat turns its head at night. Reed flowers are snow upon both banks; misty waters are autumn across the river.
The wind’s force supports the sail so one travels without rowing; the sound of the flute calls one down to the moonlit isles.

(Tiantong Jue) After Zhang Jian, there was none whose madness surpassed his; the "Grass Script" was passed down as a calligraphy of the immortal in intoxication. Broken halberds and short spears were entirely... [not present].
Looking back, clouds and mist still rise from the pages today.
(Tian'an Sheng) Chan Master Zhendong of Longya Mountain in Hunan (a successor of Dongshan Jia) first visited Dongshan and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Dongshan said, "When the waters of the Dong River flow upstream, I will tell you. The Master...
Having awakened to its essential meaning:

in the ancient source there is no water; how could the moon arise? A single stream flows westward from the brim, dividing into many branches. On the *Xi* Ridge, the inquiry into Bear’s Ear has ceased;
in the Snowy Courtyard, speak no more of Shaolin Spring. (Touzi Qing)

Cave-water has no cause to flow upstream; it flows back only because it sees the suffering of others. The intent of the Patriarchs who came from the West is truly without intent; when deluded thoughts and the frantic mind cease, all is at rest.

(Hengchuan Hong) Longya asked Cuiwei, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s intent? Cuiwei said, "Bring me my meditation board. The Master [said]: The water in a cavern has no reason to flow against the current; It flows back only because it perceives the bitter urgency of others. The ancestral intent that came from the West is truly without intent; When delusive thoughts and the frantic mind cease, one simply rests. (Hengchuan Hong) Longya asked Cuiwei, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s intent? He replied, "Bring me my meditation board. The Master said:
He then passed over the meditation board; as soon as [Linji] caught it, he struck him. The Master said, "I will let you strike me, but there is no meaning of the Patriarchs in it.
He then asked Linji, who said, "Bring me the meditation cushion. The Master then passed the cushion over to him.
Ji received him and struck him immediately. The Master said, "As for striking me, you may strike at will; however, there is still no meaning of the Patriarch.
Later, while residing [there], a monk asked, "When you were traveling on pilgrimage, you questioned two venerable elders regarding the meaning of the Patriarch.
I wonder, did those elders truly understand it? The Master said, "They understood, indeed they understood; yet, there was still no meaning of the Patriarch."
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said, "The Ancestor’s Earth-Resident Star is right at his head. He also said, "The Master has such a long face.
Shimen Cong said, "Longya may be excused as long as no one presses him; but as soon as he is pressed by a single patch-robed monk, he loses an eye.
Cui-feng Xian said, "Linji and Cuiwei know only how to let go, they do not know how to gather in. I—[say]: [They are both wrong.]

At that time, had it been Dragon Tooth (Longya), he would have waited for [the monk] to ask for the meditation cushion and the Zen board; having picked them up, he would have immediately hurled them at his chest.
Guishan Zhe said, "These two venerable seniors may truly be called masters of the fundamental division.

Dragon Tooth’s way was one of 'plucking the grass and observing the wind,' providing a model and a mirror for later generations. Although his conduct while residing there was indeed clear, fundamentally, he lacked [true realization].
The intent of the Patriarchs was as follows: regarding looking ahead and behind, or administering medicine according to the illness, Longya was certainly not lacking in this regard.
Daowei, however, was otherwise. When asked, "Have these two venerable masters attained clarity yet? he struck him across the back with his staff.
This not only upheld the two venerable masters but also did not fail the one who had come to inquire. Zhaojue Qin said: "Longya’s coming to study was crude and reckless."
He remains in a state of indistinctness. Although he looks back and forth, how can he avoid revealing his shadow while hiding his body?
Since there is no meaning from the Patriarchs here, what is the use of seeking clarity? If you can discern it within this, I, this mountain monk, will give you my staff;
if you cannot discern it, I shall pierce through your nostrils all at once. Boshan Lai said: "This fellow Longya..."
"A secondary iron backbone, straight and rigid to the very end; even to break open the Great Tang Empire, it is difficult to find a man whose head is upright and whose tail is straight.
Gunanmen said: "These three old men move their toes from within their boots.
Although Cuifeng speaks on behalf of Longya, he sees only the sharpness of the chisel-head and not the squareness of the adze-handle.
"□, you did not prostrate before the Shanyu; from beginning to end, you followed only the protocols of the Han Emperor.
Only after the snow has fallen does one know the resilience of the pine and cypress; only when faced with difficulty is a true man revealed.
(Fóxìng Tàiyī) "The carriage is yoked to a green dragon, yet he cannot ride it; everyone says the Master is a fool. Within the thick mud lies that which injures men."
A piercing thrust. Three times he once set a trap for a tiger (Manna Cheng).
Facing the meditation cushion and the Zen board before Longya, why did he fail to act as a master when the moment arose? His intention was exposed beneath the eyes of Chengshi;
I fear it may now drift away to the ends of the earth. How could a sword be hung in empty space? Yet a raft floats upon the Milky Way. No sprouting.
Grass can unravel the scent-elephant of the treasuries; a bottomless basket can hold a live snake. Today, what obstacles are there upon the rivers and lakes?
For crossing to the other shore, there are boats and carts.

(Tiantong Jue) Great wisdom appears as folly; great skill seems as clumsiness. The uncarved jade hides within the mountain, its luster naturally contained; when the people of Jing embraced it to offer it, it was merely a piece of wood.
He met with the loss of his feet. Old Longya is truly extraordinary—soft as a ball of cotton, yet hard as iron.
He is even superior to that man who once cut off his own tongue.

(Ningyuan District) Once he rode an armored steed through heavy encirclements; he was accustomed to breaking the spirit of titled generals. Now, in his leisure, he dwells beneath the flowers of the Jade Hall.
Walking. It is like hanging a precious sword within the phoenix curtains. (Wearing pure and heroic shoes. *Lungya’s Verse*:
“One reaches famous mountains throughout the world because of one’s feet; through years of hardship, they become worn like socks.
Now that I am old and can no longer walk, I hold in my hand a broken wooden ladle.”
Baizhang Yuan said, "The old man Longya can truly be said to find it difficult to forget what he is familiar with.
Jingshan Daokai said, "Baizhang acting this way is much like judging others by one's own standard. Miaoxi, however, is not so; when the family is poor, one simply prepares vegetarian meals."
"I am too busy to practice cursive script. Tianning Qi said: "This one and that one—let us let all three go at once.
Right and wrong exist all day long; if you do not listen, they naturally cease to be. Gunan Men said: [The same].
I, this mountain monk, am not like that. The famous mountains of the world are under my own two feet; though I have traveled the weary roads in hardship, I have no socks to wear.
Now, as I recall these things, my spirit is deeply pained; my hands are empty, and I have not even a wooden ladle.
Since I have no wooden ladle, with what shall I receive and attend to you all? Today, being weary from human affairs, I wish to sleep; I leave this for you all to chew upon.
A monk asked Longya, "What is it like when the two mice gnaw through the vine? The Master said, "One must have a place to hide oneself before it can be so.
The monk asked, "What is this place to hide oneself? The Master said, "Do you see me yet?"
In the cold moonlight, it lingers upon the distant peaks; ten thousand acres of calm lake are sealed with the light of white silk.
A fisherman’s song startles the herons from the sandbars; they fly into the reeds, their traces lost to sight.
(Danxia Chun) Majestically manifest, yet dense and difficult to see. Though the two mice are clever, they shall find no advantage. The wisteria branch pierces through.
Before birth, the True Eye is manifest; with skillful transformation, Old Longya’s timing was like lightning. When encountering the lowly, he made them noble;
when encountering the noble, he made them lowly.
(Yuánwù Qín) My own spirit is at ease and leisurely; beneath the moon, I gently launch my small boat, drifting off toward the clouds beyond the Fusang tree.
Guest: Even until now, the mountain peak has not yet turned. (Lin Gao Yu) Longya’s Verse:
Studying the Way is like drilling for fire; when smoke appears, one must not stop. One must wait until the golden star manifests before returning home and reaching the end.
Shending Yin said separately: "Studying the Way is like drilling for fire; when you encounter smoke, you may stop.
Do not wait for the golden star to appear, lest you burn your feet and then burn your head. Cuiyan Zhen said: "If we speak of the sudden [enlightenment], Longya is still only halfway there."
If one discusses gradualism, even the Divine Cauldron itself lacks awakening. Ultimately, how is it? This year there are many fallen leaves;
several times I have swept them back home.
When National Teacher Yao asked Longya, "When heaven cannot cover and earth cannot support, what then? the Master [Longya] said:
[Shao] said, "The Way is such as this. [The Master] asked this seventeen times in succession. The Master said, "If I had explained it to you, you would have cursed me away long ago.
Later, when Shao was residing at Tongxuan Peak, while in the midst of bathing, he suddenly realized the meaning of the previous conversation.
He assumed the full ritual decorum, faced the Master, and prostrated himself, saying, "Had you revealed it to me back then, I would not be where I am today..."
[Zhaozhou] definitely scolded him.

Xufeng Zhuo said: "Everyone stands upon the earth and reaches toward heaven. Yet there are those whose gravity exceeds that of the heavens and earth, such that even heaven and earth cannot cover or contain them.
Hehe! Misfortune and blessing have no gate; one invites them for oneself."
An iron ship floats in the center of the great ocean; following the waves, the surging billows reach the heavens.
Reaching the shore with a favorable wind, no one recognizes it. Since time immemorial, north of the river, they have used iron coins.
(Donggu Guang) When a monk asked Longya, "What did the ancients obtain that they then ceased [to strive]? the Master said, "Like a thief entering..."
An empty room;
a solitary pine and wild cranes cry at the humble gate. Snow fills the cold forest, heard as night falls. This single life has nothing at all;
it does not hinder the mountain stream and clouds beneath the crags. (By Kumukcheong)
Like a thief entering an empty house. Two fives make ten. A broom suffers from a headwind. A scale-weight frequently coughs.
*Du!* Urgently, as by the decree of the Law!
(The Root of Heaven) When a monk asked Longya, "How does one apply effort throughout the twelve periods of the day? the Master said, "It is like a person without hands."
[Master] Xingquan [performed a fist gesture]. Yunju Qi said, "Fine words! But how do you understand them? He once asked a monk, "A person without hands—how could they possibly perform a fist gesture?
When he questioned him further about the Buddha-dharma, the monk simply stopped speaking. From this, one can know that [the truth] is revealed.
Puyuan’s explanation is useless; it would be better to carefully grasp the meaning of the ancients.
Daowei Xiu said, "It is so, yet it merely teaches people to make a living within the realm of the aggregates. How can one apply effort throughout the twelve hours of the day?
It is like a person with hands making a fist—how can that even be?"
It is like a handless man wishing to make a fist; who would dare to step forward directly against him?
If one is always thus throughout the twelve periods of the day, there is no need to further inquire about the Patriarch’s Zen.
(Benjue I) Once, when a monk asked Longya, "What is it like when a lion turns back to look over its shoulder? the Master said, "Let the turning back and looking stop for now; you..."
“Does the Way fear Mañjuśrī? He replied, “Not only Mañjuśrī; even the Buddha does not fear him. The Master said, “What can be done about being ridden by Mañjuśrī?
He replied, “That which is ridden by Mañjuśrī is not a lion. The Master said, “As for the matter of the backward leap (*parāvṛtti*), how is it?
He replied, “Its application is without deficiency. The Master said, “This is precisely the matter of the backward leap regarding that which is ridden by Mañjuśrī.”
"How is it? The monk was speechless.
Among all beasts, the lion cub is well able to roar, shaking its full majesty; its wondrous functions are unrestrained as it paws back and forth.
Yet, alas, Mañjuśrī sits upon it; the King of Khotan cannot pull it away, and Sudhana, on the contrary—
A doubt arose: one might think that there is no one in the world who can surpass [the Buddha], yet when one is swallowed by the six sense-objects (ṣaḍ-viṣaya), [one is lost].
(From *Zhimen Kuan*) Once, a monk asked Longya, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "I will tell you when a stone tortoise learns to speak. The monk said, "Does a stone tortoise ever speak? The Master said, "If it did, what would I say to you?"
Tiantong Jue said: "One phrase—looking up at it, it becomes ever higher. One phrase—drilling into it, it becomes ever firmer.
One phrase—beholding it, it is ahead. One phrase—suddenly, it is behind. Can you discern this?
A sincere heart, slice by slice, few know; face-to-face, piled high, rare are those who see."
The stone tortoise speaks not, yet it is a true knower; the earless skull listens in the deep night.
At dawn, it hides within the shadowless tree; though the great sun shines everywhere, it cannot be found.
(Touzi Qing) Who says the turtle cannot speak? Its wondrous words ring out clearly of their own accord, exhausting the teachings of the Western-Come Patriarch.
[The Master] said: "To know this and yet not meet it is in vain. (Benjue I).
Chan Master Qianfeng of Yuezhou (successor of Dongshan Jia) ascended the hall and said: "If you raise one, you must not raise two;
to let go of one thing is to fall into the second. Yunmen stepped out from the assembly and said: "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai, but..."
He was going to Mount Jing. The Master said, "The head cook must not be called for general labor tomorrow.
Langye Jue said, "When the road is long, one knows the strength of the horse; when years have passed, one sees the true heart of man.

Guishan Zhe said, "Qianfeng is skilled at singing, and Yunmen is skilled at clapping. As the singing and clapping follow one another, the ancient style is clear and pure. Is there anyone who can truly appreciate this?"
"Ma! In one hall, the wind is cold and still; through the ages, the meaning remains clear. Cui Feng Xian said:
"Yunmen only knows how to lift with one hand; he does not know how to press down with the other. Is there anyone here who can exert effort together? Try to show your claws and fangs! Yunju Yuan said:
"In Qianfeng’s dream, he closed his eyes and leaped over the Yellow River; upon waking, his body was back on his bed."
Up. Yunmen, after getting drunk, helped someone up onto a tree; when he woke up, they were both back in their seats, having become one mass.
To this day, they cannot be separated. If anyone can discern where they have fallen, I grant you the title of foremost in understanding emptiness.
Yuwang Lian said: "If you raise one, it is as black as lacquer; if you raise two, it is not at all so. Tell me, how is it? After a long silence, he said:
"The drum is beaten in the eastern city, yet the sound echoes in the western city; the flowers bloom within the garden, yet the fragrance wafts outside.
Huguo Yuan said: "To know the tail by the head, and to know the future by the past. If this were not mutually known by both, how could one possibly [proceed] toward..."
"Here, we all put forth one hand together. "It is so; it is so. But alas, there is still one move missing. Jingshan Gao said:
"Qianfeng, while washing his face, felt for his nose; Yunmen, while eating his rice, bit upon grit.
When the two met suddenly, they found out they were old enemies after all. Even so, it is permitted only for the Old Barbarian to know; it is not..."
Xu Laohu said, "I understand. He further remarked, "Both sides are airing their family's private faults; fortunately, there are no bystanders.
Yuwang Guang said, "The eyes are keen and the hands are swift; both are masters of the craft. Yet, when examined closely, they still fall short by one move.
Hongfu, however, was not like this. He said, "If you bring up one, you must not bring up two. To let one move pass is to fall into the second. Suddenly, someone—
[He] comes out. [The Master] strikes him across the spine. Why? To shatter the skull so that all news is exhausted; let the great earth be left in a vast, dark expanse. Tiantong Jue said:
"When sitting and cutting off the ten directions, a thousand divergent paths are severed; when letting loose a single thread, ten thousand streams flow toward the source.
Only when these two venerable masters open up their family style can one truly see the conduct of a monk. Is this truly so? Too...
The Emperor’s decree pervades the realm; the General of Sweating Blood harbors his heart beyond the frontier.

let this talk spread far and wide. Lian’an Zhen said: "One person [stands] atop the peak of a solitary mountain."
"Shaking the shrimp. One person, at the bottom of the great ocean, strikes a rabbit. Even if a skilled hand were to present itself, it would still be washing soil in the mud.

The phrase before the sound is like eyebrows upon a mouth; Buddhas and Patriarchs have never known it from the beginning.
Last night, Kunlun idly spoke a dream: a black-headed man gave birth to a white-headed child.
(Danxia Chun) The spring orchid and the autumn chrysanthemum—each is right for its own season. Where is there no mutual interpenetration? Whom can one blame for dividing the marrow and the skin?
When the wind comes, the crow already senses it; when the dew is heavy, the crane knows it first. If one asks how this can be so, they themselves do not know at all.
(Yuánwù Qín) Boiling the sea to make salt always has its flavor; striking the void to produce a sound is fundamentally without sound. When Kūṇāla bumps into the Persian.
My son, take my hand and walk together along the bottom of the sea.
(Cishou Shen) High towers and beautiful maidens in pairs, each sitting at jade beds by crystal windows. Having embroidered the mandarin ducks, they present them;
the golden needle is deeply inserted into the brocade sachet. (Foxing Tai)
The Persian brings forth Hainan incense; the blind-eyed K'un-lun man debates its worth. The merchant does not understand the tongue of the trilled sound;
he merely observes that two nostrils are long. (Fozhi Yu) Though the rustic gate is set, it has never been closed;
I idly watch the solitary birds as they come and go. Originally intending to escape into the mountains, I have remained here.
Abiding. Abiding in the mountains is called "emerging from among men" (*jiu-mo-yin*).
Qianfeng ascended the hall and said: "The Dharma-body has three kinds of illnesses and two kinds of radiance; you must penetrate each one thoroughly."
"Having just finished my formal prostrations and returned home to sit steadily, you must know that there is still a 'further' opening above this.
Yunmen came forward and said, "Why does the person inside the hermitage not know what is outside the hermitage? The Master laughed heartily.
Yunmen said, "This is still a point of doubt for me, a student. The Master asked, "What kind of mental activity is yours? Yunmen replied, "I also wish for the Master to [instruct me]."
[The Master] said, "You must be exactly like this before you can sit securely. The Gatekeeper responded, "Yes, yes.
Cui-feng Xian said, "If one understands the phrase of praise and blame, it is not necessarily a good cause that brings about an evil result.
Wei-shan Guo said, "Gan-peak creates a mound on level ground; Shao-yang raises waves with the wind. Nevertheless, though water and milk blend together..."
Mud. For a thousand ages, it has been the standard for the monastic groves. Since it is already water and mud mixed together, why is it called the standard for the monastic groves?
If you do not enter the great waves, how can you see the one who plays with the tide? Tiantong Jue said: "If you sit still, the illness lies in the vital organs;

if you employ it, the light does not penetrate through. Even if you were to move freely in all directions, turning a thousand mechanisms, you would still not know that there is a 'hole above'—would you then be able to sit securely? In the end, the moon in a frosty night falls spontaneously."
At Qianxi, the shopkeeper told a man who was testing the gold for purchase that such genuine gold was difficult to find.
The buyer brushed his sleeves and walked away, his face covered in shame and embarrassment, not daring to show anger. (Baizhang Yuanwen)
Discerning the tune by the movement of the strings; asking one and knowing ten. Grasping the hand and lifting the hand; casting glue onto lacquer.
Not seeing what is outside the hut while inside the hut; failing to understand the unperforated iron hammer. In human life, acquaintance values those who truly understand;
water entering water, gold exchanging with gold. (Zhaojue Qin)
Lowering the hook across the four seas to fish for the fierce dragon; beyond the ordinary, he converses in mystery with those who know him.
Meeting face-to-face, he wears his robe and the scholar’s cap; there is no hindrance as they walk hand-in-hand up the high peak.

(Fóxìng Tàiyán) Within the hermitage, one knows not the affairs outside the hermitage; even those with iron brows and copper heads are not like him. He fixes the flower-patterned board and beats the swing.
The Swing. Upon the tiger’s tongue, the *svastika* is inscribed.

(Xiatang Yuan) When the spring breeze has its master, it returns to Jingu Valley; on a snowy night, who arrives at Shanxi? If it were not for those with true discernment, there would be no place to seek it;
how could a man of spirit allow himself to be led by the hand? (Huanji Ting)
When Yunmen arrived at Qianfeng, he said, "I ask the Master to answer me. The Master said, "Have you even reached the old monk yet?
Yunmen said, "In that case, I am late. The Master said, "How so? How so? Yunmen said, "I thought the monkey was white;
it turns out there is also a black monkey."
Baoneng Xiu said: "Yunmen’s lightning flashed across a clear sky; Qianfeng’s thunder rolled across parched earth.

When it comes to releasing both simultaneously and gathering both back in, even a master monk finds it difficult to grasp. Boshan Lai said: "An extraordinary question receives an extraordinary answer.
A swift clap of thunder leaves no time to cover one's ears; a fine steed cannot catch up with the wind. It is a turning that encompasses both the partial and the perfect."
Each carries the means for probing the profound and seeking out the hidden; yet, when examined closely, they deserve a severe beating.
Why? Because they create trouble where there is none. To let them off would be unacceptable. Ou-feng Cheng said:
"Two lacquer buckets have lost their nostrils."
The bowstring and the arrow notch interlock; the net and the pearls face one another. Shooting a hundred targets, every arrow finds its mark; gathering all reflections, every light is unimpeded.
Having attained the *dhāraṇī* of words and phrases, they abide in the *samādhi* of playful sport. Wondrous within this interval, they turn and shift with both partiality and perfection;
it must be thus that they act with sovereign ease, whether vertically or horizontally. (Tiantong Ju)
Once, when a monk asked Qianfeng, "The *Bhagavāns* of the ten directions all share the single path to the gate of nirvāṇa;
I wonder, where does the beginning of that path lie? The Master drew a line with his staff and said, "It is right here. Later, the monk requested further instruction from Yunmen.
Master Nianqi held up his fan and said: "The fan leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens, striking the nostrils of Śakra.
A carp from the Eastern Sea receives a blow, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin. Do you understand?"
Cui-feng Xian, acting on behalf of the monk, gave a shout. There was also a monk who requested instruction from Chang-qing;

Chang-qing said, "Go ask the second seat in the hall. Cui-feng, acting on behalf of the monk, said, "Wrong. Later, a monk asked Cui-feng about this, and Cui-feng said, "Falling into a pit and tumbling down a ravine.
He then provided his own alternative response: "The mind of a thief is always apprehensive. Huang-long Nan said, "Gan-peak’s single occasion of pointing..."
The Path: To bend it is for those of initial capacity; Yunmen, however, opened up its transformations so that later generations would not grow weary.
Daopei Xiu said: "From ancient times to the present, everyone says that Qianfeng established the patriarchs' hall during his summer retreat to open a path for future generations."
Little did they know that the monk’s single question had already left them flustered and at a loss.
Tell me, where does the confusion lie? After a long silence, he said: "It is not in the water, nor is it in the mountains; it lies only within the fluctuations of the human heart.
Baofeng Wen said: "Did Qianfeng even dream of this when he spoke thus? I, this mountain monk, am not like that. I wait for him..."
A monk asked: "If you strike him on the spine and then ask where the path lies, and wait for him to open his mouth before shouting 'Hot!
and driving him out—furthermore, there was Yunmen, who could not distinguish the heterodox from the orthodox; he would pick up his fan and say [something]...
as for fellows like this, who are nothing but a muddling together of mud and water, ten or five of them could be buried right there at a heap of refuse. What is there to it?"
"Too much! Aha ha! Is there pleasure or no pleasure? Is there sufficiency or insufficiency? Now, fortunately, we face green mountains and blue waters.
All such matters have been set aside for a time this year. Let the body and mind rest freely without constraint. Everyone, do not nod off! Nanhua Bing said:
"Qianfeng exhausted his compassion to guide the student at the critical moment; Yunmen skillfully opened up expedient means to confront him directly."
The face triggers the mechanism; it directly causes withered wood to bloom and cold ashes to flare into flame.

But tell me, when the carp of the Eastern Sea is struck once with a staff and the rain pours down like an overturned basin—what matter on the boundary does this clarify? It is like fanning the fire with the wind; not much effort is required.
Lingyin Yue said: "Qianfeng was also like nailing down a post and rowing a boat.
A three-eyed turtle, red as fire; a one-horned qilin, swift as a drill. The Earth-Dweller (Tusuo) wanders at night through Jambudvīpa;
sparks fly from beneath the feet of the clay ox. (Chengtian Zong)
Tearing apart Yunmen’s single-handled fan; breaking off Qianfeng’s single staff. Two or three thousand places of pipes and strings;
four or five hundred lanes of flowers and willows. (Jingshan Gaofeng) Once it enters the hand, one uses it to treat a dead horse;
with *re-spirit* incense, one seeks to raise you from your peril. For a time, he presses out [the realization] that pervades the entire body.
Sweat! Only then can one believe that my family does not spare its eyebrows.

(Tiantong Jue) Dwelling in Peach Blossom Spring, he was already ahead of those who fled Qin. He sought a fisherman to ask for a ferryboat. The roosters, dogs, mulberry trees, and hemp plants all vied in laughter and dance;
they laughed at people who try to scoop up the sky within the water. (Baonuan Xiu)
A beautiful woman rides her horse away toward the eastern valley; suddenly wind and rain arrive, and she takes shelter under a tree. An old woman peddling charms plays with autumn flowers;
who says that six times six is thirty-six? (The Thousand Finger-Seals).
Chan Master Wensui of Qingshan in Lizhou (a successor of Dongshan Jia) was sitting together with Yantou and Xuefeng when Dongshan said:
As he was serving tea, the Master closed his eyes. Dong said, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from entering meditative concentration.
Dong said, "Concentration has no gate; through what have you entered?"
An old master spoke on his behalf, saying, "There are many who understand it in this way.

Cui-feng Xian spoke differently, saying, "At that time, he should have simply pointed at Yan-tou and Xue-feng and said, 'Give some tea to these two sleepyheads! Fa-lin Yin spoke on his behalf, saying, "He should have immediately knocked over the tea service!"
Qinshan was visited by a monk. Qinshan held up his fist and then opened his hand, saying, "When it is open, it becomes a palm;
the five fingers are distinct from one another. He then closed his fist again and said, "Now it is a fist; there is certainly no high or low. Tell me, does Qinshan still allow for deliberation?
The monk stepped forward and also held up his fist. The Master said, "Your doing so is merely being 'without'."
"Opening and closing the Han. Cui-feng Xian said, "I do not do it this way. He then held up his fist and said, "When clenched, it is a fist; there is high and low.
He then opened his hand and said, "When opened, it becomes a palm; there is no factionalism and no partiality. Now tell me, is it better to let go for the sake of others, or to hold fast?
"It is good for people to open up. Kai made the carriage; Wo joined the tracks.
If you say, 'I build the carriage inside my door and join the tracks when I go out,' I know that you are making your living inside a ghost cave. Zhaojue Qin said: "The palm is also a hand;
grasping is also a hand. What are you deliberating about? He then raised one foot and said: "Extending is also a foot; withdrawing..."
This is also the foot. It has neither high nor low; it allows for no deliberation as to whether it is the same as or different from Qianshan.
Nantang Yu said: "Unfolding it is not the palm; grasping it is not the fist. Both ends are completely severed—'A single sword leans against the sky, cold.
Is there still a way to benefit others? He gave a shout and said: 'The west wind blows across the Wei River. It falls.
Leaves fill Chang’an;
those with poetic talent should naturally be close. There is no need for songs or further frowning. The Censor who attends court is not Han Shou;
do not steal his fragrance and bring trouble upon others. (Haizhou Ci)
When a monk asked Qinshan, "What is the house style of the Master? the Master said, "Brocade and embroidery, a silver incense pouch;
the wind blows its fragrance along the entire road. When Yantou heard of this, he sent a monk to deliver a message, saying, "Give this word to Elder Sister Number Eighteen."
"Serve Panglang well. Pingyang Wen said:
"The old man Suí did not obscure the lineage of Dongshan; Master Huò did not violate the tradition of Deshan.
One still wears the garment of original nature; the other still travels the path of the mind. Neither has yet emerged from Cao Shan’s four prohibitions."
Today, someone asked, "What is the house style of the Master? He replied, "Like jade that is precious yet not used;
like簧 (huáng) pipes whose speech carries a touch of sorrow. He looked left and right and said, "Is there anyone here now who can transmit these words? The assembly remained silent.
It is said: "The blood-stained cuckoo's spring has passed again; for your sake, how could I begrudge the loss of my蛾眉 (mei-erh) brows? Lingyan Chu said:

"Qinshan merely sought to flaunt his gallantry, regardless of the fact that [the woman] was left with her soul vanished and dreams broken. Although Yantou strictly adhered to the national laws, what can be done when the offense does not merit a heavy sentence?

If someone asks this mountain monk, "What is the patriarchal style of the Master? [he would answer: "The blood-stained cuckoo's spring has passed again; for your sake, how could I begrudge the loss of my mei-erh brows?"
Faced with the Way, clear knowledge shows you will not reach it; once more he ascends to the top of the small tower. Looking left and right, he says:
"When this mountain monk makes such an announcement, what is his intention? He strikes the bamboo rattle once and says: "Frequently calling for 'Xiaoyu' was originally no matter at all;
it was simply to have the patron recognize the sound. Falin Yin said: "I am not like that. What is the meaning of 'Monk'?"
The Family Style: He struck him across the spine with his staff and, looking left and right, said, "Do you all feel a pain in the crown of your heads?
When the Zen guest Jūryō came to inquire, saying, "What is it like when a single arrow pierces the three barriers?
the Master said, "Let out the master of the barrier and see. The guest said, "In that case, one knows that an error must be corrected. The Master said, "Wait further..."
"When? he asked. [The monk] replied, "A fine arrow; having no place to land, it simply went out. The Master said, "Come here first, Ācārya.
The monk turned his head back. The Master stepped down from the meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Setting aside for a moment the 'one shaft piercing the three barriers'—"

"Try to shoot an arrow for Qinshan and see," he said. As Liang hesitated, the Master struck him seven blows, saying, "Let this fellow who talks nonsense ponder this for thirty years. A monk reported this to Tong’an Cha.
Tong’an said, "Although Master Liang knows how to shoot the arrow, he has yet to hit the mark. The monk asked, "How can one hit the mark? Tong’an said, "The barrier."
"What kind of person is the 'Central Lord'? The monk returned and reported this to the Master.

The Master said, "If Master Liang had understood it in this way, he too would have avoided the mouth of Qian Mountain. Nevertheless, Tong'an did not have good intentions; you must examine this for yourself before you can understand."
Tiantong Jue said: "When it comes like mountains piled up and peaks heaped high, and goes away like ice melting and walls crumbling, then people of this age know it exists.
Let me let out the Lord of Guanzhong for you to see—how should one act? Some say that at that moment one should have shouted; others say one should have struck with the palm.
Yet while such a blind application may suffice for a single occasion, it is still not the Lord of Guanzhong himself. Do you understand?"
Can you grasp it? Not sitting upright in the hall, how can one respond to the dual mechanisms?
For you, I release the Lord of Guanzhong; you who would shoot arrows, do not be reckless!
To take this eye, the ears must go deaf; to lose these ears, the eyes become blind. Pity how a single arrow pierces the three barriers—this is the unmistakably clear arrow.
The Subsequent Path. Have you not seen what Xuansha said? "A great man takes the primordial as the ancestor of mind.
(Cui Feng Xian) Failing to understand the intent of the Chanyu, he sends light chariots out through the Han Pass. Alas, his bow and arrows are spent; he gazes in vain toward Mount Helan.
(Qinshan Lingting) While Qinshan, Xuefeng, and Yantou were at an inn drinking tea, the Master said, "Those who do not know how to turn their bodies and breathe out shall not drink this tea.
Yantou said, "If that is the case, I certainly shall not drink the tea. Xuefeng—
Xuantou said, "So it is with me. The Master said, "These two fellows do not even recognize the *huatou* (the critical phrase).
Xuantou asked, "Where has it gone? The Master said, "An old crow in a cloth bag; though alive, it is as if dead. Xuantou stepped back and said, "Look, look!
The Master said, "Let us set aside Master Huo for a moment; what about Master Cun? Feng drew a circle in the air with his hand.
The Master said, "How could you not ask? Tou laughed heartily and said, "It is far too remote. The Master said, "There are many who have mouths but cannot drink tea.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Although Qingshan understood how to shift his body and breathe, he still did not yet have the portion for drinking tea. Why is that?"
The story continues. Guohu Xinyue said, "Qingshan was much like the Bodhisattva Kṣāntivādin; even as he was dismembered limb by limb, his countenance did not change.
Had the Venerable Xiang been there at that time, he would have smashed the tea set right then and there, at the very first question."
There was no small amount of triviality.
Qinshan, Yantou, and Xuefeng went together to Deshan. When the Master [Deshan] came out and asked, "Tianhuang spoke thus;
Longtan also spoke thus. I wonder, how would you speak, Preceptor? Deshan said, "Try it yourself."
[Shishuang] raised [the case of] Emperor Suzong and said, "Look at the bottom of the Dragon Pond! As the Master hesitated, Shishuang struck him.

Having been struck, the Master returned to the Yanshou Hall and said, "It is indeed so; he has beaten me far too severely. Daowei said, "If you act like this, you shall not be able to say in the future that you have seen Deshan."
Fayan Yi said: "That is exactly it; you have struck me wrong. Wuzu Keqin said:
"Deshan only knew how to beat dead Qinshan; he did not know how to beat living Qinshan. Cuiyan Zhongzhi said:
"Qinshan only looked ahead and did not look behind. How would you now provide relief for Qinshan? Cui峰 Xian said: [He remained silent.]
Qinshan’s establishment of this point of inquiry is truly extraordinary; yet, alas, it is like a dragon’s head with a snake’s tail.

You should try to cite what the Emperor of Heaven (Tianhuang) and Longtan said as their ultimate conclusion. [He] then struck with his sitting mat. For a great man to pull a tiger’s whiskers is also his rightful duty.
Deshan’s command was carried out only halfway; had his command been fully executed, Xuefeng and Yantou would both have entered nirvana.
A man of the Hall. Guizong Zhe said, "Under Deshan, things fell like grass before the wind. Daopi was not like this: when someone asked, 'I do not yet understand;
how would you say it, Master? he struck him across the back with his staff. Now, tell me: who is right, Deshan or Daopi? Do you understand?
Horizontally grasping the Mohe sword, he maintains the full authority of the True Command; in a world at peace, he slays the dull and the stubborn."
Tiantong Hua said: "This is merely half of Deshan’s command being carried out. Did Cuifeng manage to escape it or not?
Since he could not escape, even though he passed through Deshan’s gate at that time, he was still one who ate the staff. Do you see Deshan yet?
He suddenly picked up his staff, struck once, and said: "The thief is a petty person. Gunan Men said: "Cuifeng..."
The mountain peak supports the strong but not the weak. One does not know how that old fellow Deshan, having been squeezed by Qinshan, was forced to pass the matter on to another.
"If you hesitate, I strike!"—he has already tried to treat a dead horse. Had he acted according to his own command, why wait for the words "Tianhuang" or "Longtan"?
As soon as [the opponent] stepped forward, he would have driven them out with a great club; he would have settled dragons and snakes, captured tigers and rhinoceroses.
What fault is there?
This decrepit, mindless veteran of the old school—ancient and modern alike prize him for his total lack of flaw. The single lineage of Emperor Tianhuang is manifested in Longtan;
from it surges forth the spiritual source, yet ten thousand paths diverge. (Fenyang Zhao)

When the white waves surge against one's face, where the staff falls, the source is revealed. Like a divine steed whose ten shadows cannot be overtaken by pursuit, only the auspicious qilin is permitted to stride across the great thousand-fold world. (By Bie Mu Chun).

When Qinshan was visited by a former attendant of Deshan who had come to study with him, as soon as the attendant prostrated, Qinshan suddenly seized him and said, "Do you still find it acceptable at Qinshan?"
“Mountains are not like that either,” [the Master] said. [The attendant] replied, “I regret having stayed so long at De Shan; today I have no words with which to respond.
The Master then let go of his hand and said, “Feel free to respond as you wish. The attendant pushed open [the Master’s] chest and said, “Now listen to me for a moment as I vent my breath.
The Master said, “That may be acceptable under the gate of De Shan, but here, not even a single point is of any use.”
[The monk] said, "For a long time I have relied on Mount Qin, yet it does not accord with human sentiment. The Master said, "This repeatedly clouds the eyes of De Shan. Go to the meditation hall.

Jing Shan Ce said, "When killing people, one does not question them; when questioning people, one does not kill them. One thrusts out the chest and exhales the breath; both sides are but 'Alas, Eight' (Meng Ba)."
Even if one were to have a beginning and an end, it would still be like bailing out water and splashing it back again. Do you wish to recognize Qinshan and this monk?
When Prince Li Shun first broke his straw sandals, he was only thirteen; when Master Li’s leather socks were torn, [he was likewise young].
Qinshan was once asked by Yantou, "What is the true word? The Master replied, "Namo Buddhāya. According to the occasion, there was a question;
according to the occasion, there was an answer. It is neither Chan nor the profound mystery.
Later, someone arbitrarily translated it, taking the Sanskrit and rendering it into Chinese (Tang language). (Tuigeng Ning)
Qinshan was debating the principles of the Dharma with a Daoist. The Daoist established his thesis, saying, "Coarse words and subtle speech alike all return to the primary meaning.
The Master said, "Daoist, you are a slave to the Buddha's house. The Daoist replied, "That is too coarse, sir. The Master asked, "Where, then, is the primary meaning? The Daoist was speechless.
Mutang’s reflection says: "Qinshan’s such discourse on doctrine is merely that of a hero in a chaotic age.
From the standpoint of the Gate of the Patch-robed Monks (nanseng), even his receiving a blow of the staff would not be permitted. Why? Have you not heard it said:
'It is better to take one's head before a wise person than to achieve victory before an ignorant person'?"

The Master said, "Can it be called 'sound'? The monk bowed. The Master said, "Tell me, did I speak for you, or did I answer your question?
If you can understand it here, you will have a point of entry."
Cui Feng Xian said, "Baishui was truly extraordinary; yet, he was merely gazing at the heavens. Since this was neither before sound nor after form, how then did he enter?
Yunju Shun said, "Since Baishui had already entered the weeds, this monk has fallen into a remote village.
Thus, the 'Snow Melody of the Yangchun' is difficult for people of the age to harmonize; village songs and communal dances are found everywhere."
"Attainable. Daopei Xiu said, "Baishui only knows 'horizontal thousand' but does not understand 'vertical hundred.
What is sound that is not sound? Do not pursue its resonance. What is form that is not form? Do not pursue its blue or yellow."
Furthermore, if you follow him toward the sound before and the form after to seek a place to settle yourself, you will naturally have a separate livelihood.
Jingshan Gaofeng said: "Baishui took a string of Yunju’s beads and exchanged them for the eyes of everyone in the world;
yet this monk took a single broken cord and, without raising a weapon, pierced his nostrils through. Yunju was like this.
"The Way. This is indeed so. Yet it cannot avoid being caught in a tangled search. Elder Gaomo, not sparing his own eyebrows, shall explain this through for you all:
Sound is not sound; form is not form. Following after the horse and preceding the donkey; appearing like spirits and vanishing like ghosts. The *xuequ* and *yangchun* melodies do not harmonize;
village songs and communal dances are but a muddled jumble. With the whisk, he struck the meditation seat and said: "This..."
"This one is definitely not sound. He then held up [his staff] and said, "This one is definitely not form. After all, what is it?
He gave a shout and said, "If you do not investigate the source at this very moment, you must wait until the future to question Maitreya.
Guangjiao Yu said, "I, this old monk, usually do not wish to play tricks upon people before sound or after form."
A man and woman of the household; once a profligate, he especially pities the traveler; loving wine himself, he spares the one who is drunk.
Why is it that sound is not sound and form is not form? It is like a stone wrapped in cotton, or a lump of mud encased in iron.
How can it be that sound is not sound? Gold is tested with fire; can it be called "form"? One carries the cangue through the legal proceedings. How is it...?
Form is not form. Not reaching the Wu River, one does not reach the end. Can it be called sound? A repeated word is not worth eating. Now tell me:
when you speak to someone and they answer you, these two parts are different; bring them back to the superior category.
If there is someone who can discern this, the crooked will not conceal the straight; I grant you an entrance. You have misled many people. He spoke again: "The ancients..."
To preach and proclaim in such a manner is called "feeding an infant with chewed rice. You all must, right now, sweep away the clouds of delusion and fully open the sun of wisdom;
you may then arise from within sounds and forms, sit or lie down amidst sounds and forms, and stand upon the spot to see where Master Benren acted for others.
Muchan said: "The old fellow Baishui only knows how to shut his door."
The strategy for making a living lacks the utility of charging headlong into battle;
yet, while that monk possesses the utility of charging headlong into battle, he lacks the strategy of staying behind closed doors to make a living. Consequently, this dialogue remains incomplete.
Today, seeing injustice on the road, I shall go forth to complete it. If someone asks, "What is sound that is not sound? answer by saying: "It pervades."
The realms have never been hidden. What is form that is not form? He replied, "A lightning bolt too swift to be covered by a hand.
If you can distinguish the black from the white within this, then all sounds are the voice of the Buddha, and all forms are the form of the Buddha.
Perhaps it is not so: a magpie comes and speaks upon my head, clouds arise before my eyes.
Form is form and sound is sound; where the new oriole cries, the willow smoke is light. At every gate there is a road leading to the capital;
the three islands stretch across as the sea moon shines bright. (Danxia Chun)

Sound issues from emptiness; form arises from non-existence. Before sound and after form, they swirl in a blur; the interval between them cannot admit even a hair’s breadth. How can they be called "models"?
The majestic, perfect response leaves not a grain of dust behind. What use is laboriously forging in the furnace to distinguish them?
How much better it is to attain the patience of non-arising beneath the staff—its fragrance fills the paths as soon as it is heard and seen. (Yuanwu Keqin)

It is not form; it is not sound. Through the lattice windows, one sees the person holding the needle; by observing the wind and parting the grass, what limits can there be? At the gateway of the household door, one mistakenly takes the provisional for the real. (Rhyme:
*zhēn*) Chan Master Xianqi of Tiantong in Mingzhou (a successor of Dongshan Jia) asked the Venerable Jian:

"When a student stands tall and firm, how does one proceed? 卓卓上 (Zhuozhuoshang) — Rhyme: *shàng* (upward). (Note: This text consists of a poetic verse followed by a recorded dialogue from the *Wudeng Huiyuan*. The final line, "卓卓上," serves as a rhyme marker for the preceding verse.)

The visitor said, "I have come specifically to request instruction from the Master. The Master replied, "In my place, one simply voids oneself; what is there that is particularly outstanding or distinct?
The visitor said, "If you, the Monk, answer questions in such a manner, you had better buy some straw sandals and go on a pilgrimage.
The Master said, "Come closer. Jian approached him. The Master asked, "As for my responding to you in this way, where does the fault lie?"
Jian remained silent. The Master then struck him.
Tiantong Hua said: "Master Qi is indeed a hammer of the fundamental division, yet he has not yet managed to block Tiantong’s mouth.
Although Venerable Jian has deeply entered the inner precincts, he still lacks the eye to pass through the barrier."
Exemplary! It stops as soon as it is excreted. The rat dances the *Santai*; the cat blows the *pi-li* flute.
The tortoise lifts its head and sings a *ba-gē*. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven.
(Chengtian Zong) Xianqi asked a monk, "What is the eye that is unimpaired in its application? The Master said, "Just like being blind."

Ordinary people—blind, deaf, mute, and speechless—are far from the true source. When the eyes resemble the eyebrows, the Way is first approached. Last night the Lord of Spring secretly issued his decree;
where the yellow oriole cries, the green willows are in spring. (Danxia Chun)

Chan Master Jiufeng Puman (successor of Dongshan Jia) of Ruizhou asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Min Province. The Master said, "The long journey must have been difficult.
The monk said, "It was not difficult; as soon as one moves a step, one arrives. The Master asked, "Is there anyone who does not move a step?
The monk said, "There is. The Master said, "How can such a person reach this place? The monk had no reply, and the Master drove him away with his staff.

Dongshan Ying said: "To act for others, one must be thorough; to kill someone, one must see the blood. While this is indeed the sincere, warm-hearted concern of Jiufeng, it is a pity that this monk was not a good guest and troubled his host.
Had he been a true patch-robed monk (nanseng), he would simply have said: [as Dongshan did].
"Master, it seems you have never traveled on pilgrimage. Take it for granted that this staff has another recipient.
Layer upon layer of clouds, layer upon layer of water; his steps never moved as far as Jiufeng.
If one says the journey was difficult after traveling afar, the host is already halfway there. (Xueyan Qin)
Puman asked a monk, "How does one accord with the Way throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said, "Accord with the Way through non-mind.
The monk asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "It is still tolerable to seek mud upon the earth; to seek water within the waves is truly pitiable."
Leading a donkey to drink from the river, its nostrils blowing up waves; on the bank, hoof beats against hoof; in the water, snouts face snout.
(Fang’an Xian): Puman was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of 'non-transmigration'? The Master said, "The bright moon rises in the east; the golden crow sets in the west.
The monk said, "It is not that you, Master, do not understand. The Master said, "When the principle is right, one acts immediately. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
The monk said, "In the way of benevolence and righteousness, what fault is there in performing prostrations? The Master said, "Since his place of origin is not clear, strict orders must be enforced.
Zhu Wencai said, "When the eyes are clear, one can discern even the finest hairs; when the principle is correct, one can distinguish between right and wrong."—Jiufeng.
He has deeply discerned the beginning and end; from head to tail, everything is upright. But as for this monk who prostrates—how is that?
If one does not go deep into the vast ocean, how can one catch the scaled dragon back home?
Puman asked a monk, "What is the indestructible body? The Master said, "It is precisely this. The monk said, "I do not understand;
I ask the Master to point it out directly. The Master said, "Just now, how much did you deviate [from the truth]?"

The indestructible body is precisely the correct; the correct is precisely the indestructible body. Just now, how much twisting was there? It pinched the tip of the nose until it was painful. (Stone Creek Moon).
Zen Master Huicheng of Jingzhao Huayan Temple (successor of Dongshan Jia) served as the *karmadāna* at Luopo. Because of this... [text continues]
He requested that the gavel be struck, saying: "In the upper section they stack firewood; in the lower section they plow the earth. At that time, the Head Seat asked, "What is the Holy Monk doing?
The Master replied, "He does not sit upright in the hall; how could he attend to the dual functions at both ends?"
Letan Zhen said: "Although Huayan’s responses were timely and his application of means was never inappropriate, he only knew how to push the pole with the current;
he did not know how to steer against the wind. Had it been Upādhyāya Zhen at that time, as soon as he saw him say, 'What is the Holy Monk doing?
he would have struck him once with the mallet and said: 'The assembly has finished their communal work; the Head Seat should come forward.'"
The Monastery. Respectfully submitted. Now tell me, why is it so? Have you not heard it said: "When the authority is once in one's hand, behold the time when the command is carried out"?
Zhaojue Qin said: "The pearl drills through nine bends; Xu Jing may indeed be called a master of divine skill. The jade unfastens the linked rings;
I, this mountain monk, shall further provide another path. If someone asks, "What does the Holy Monk do?", simply reply: "Vast and open."
A bright mirror stands upon its pedestal; unmoving, it responds to myriad conditions through form and sound.
When Huayan was at Dongshan, he asked, "This student has not yet seen the path of principle and cannot yet avoid the realm of conceptual consciousness.
Dongshan said, "Have you seen the path of principle yet? The Master replied, "There is no path of principle. Dongshan asked, "From where did you obtain this?"
When Qingshi approached, the Master said, "I am asking you as a student. Dongshan said, "In this way, you must stand where there are ten thousand miles of land and not a single inch of grass.
Qingshi asked, "Is it even permitted to stand where there are ten thousand miles of land and not a single inch of grass?
Dongshan said, "You must simply go in this manner."
Parting the shallow grass, a speckled snake is revealed; its venomous breath steams forth, casting down the evening glow.
There is no help for it, for the beggar’s wiles are different: with a bottomless basket, he carries his load home.
(Suan Ding) One day, Chan Master You of Youqi in Taizhou (a successor of Dongshan Jia) struck the bell and ascended the hall. As soon as the assembly [gathered]...
The assembly gathered. The Master then asked, "Who is striking the bell? The monk replied, "The Rector (Karmadāna). The Master said, "Come closer.
When the monk approached, the Master struck him with his palm and returned to his quarters in the Abbot’s room to lie down.
Touzi said, "Qingyun. Indeed, there have always been those who must flee from the past and present in times of urgency. When one's path is exhausted at the ultimate limit, try asking a bystander.
If you do not recognize their underlying intent, you will surely find yourself caught. Having already engaged in this inquiry, they urgently seek the fundamental reason;
disregarding danger and ruin, they find an excuse for themselves. Though they may gain a small advantage, it is merely injuring others in secret—they are no good at their craft.

Although the monk has indeed suffered this loss, it is because he failed to maintain his own proper station, bringing calamity upon himself; thus, it was not beyond what was expected. Nevertheless, even so, he remains a common man who has been unjustly ensnared in a net.

There is already a witness from another party to attest to this. But tell me, what does this witness testify to? He then said: "When the eastern house has not settled its affairs, the western house suffers the misfortune. He further offered this verse: The eastern house has not brought matters to an end, And the western house receives the calamity. Though the monk has lost his advantage, It is surely his own fault for failing to guard his boundaries. Even so, he is still an ordinary person who has been caught in a trap. There is naturally a bystander with evidence to prove it. But tell me, what does that evidence show? He said: "The eastern neighbor has not finished his business, So the western neighbor suffers the disaster. Then he recited a verse:
Meeting by chance on the road, one asks for the reason; do not immediately offer your heart’s intent in response.
Though the heavy burden may be made to be borne by another, it remains a matter of shame and secret embarrassment.
Pushing a person on level ground, they immediately fall down. Where the Way-man travels, how transcendent is his intent!
Clearly it is known that when the moon reaches the wutong tree, it does not illuminate the wutong tree, but illuminates the azure heavens.

(From *Huanyou Chuan*) Chan Master Beiyuan Tong of Yizhou (a successor of Dongshan Jia) asked Jia Shan: "There is no dharma before one's eyes; where does the meaning lie? (The meaning lies within the eyes.)
"Prior to this, it is not the dharma of the present moment; it is not something reached by the ears or eyes.
"Is this not the Master’s own words? Baizhang replied, "Yes. Mazu then overturned the meditation seat and stood with his hands folded. Baizhang rose and struck him once with his staff.
The Master then went down. Fayan Yi said: "He overturned the meditation seat; why did he not leave immediately?
He had to wait until Jia Shan gave him thirty blows before departing. What was his intention? Yuan'an Meng said: "Jia Shan’s staff was excellent. Only...
This was handed over too late. When [the monk] waited to ask, "Is this not the Master's own words?", he struck him straight across the head.

At that moment, even if Beiyuan had possessed supernatural powers, he would have been unable to react in time. Nevertheless, what was the intention behind Beiyuan waiting for Jia Shan to strike him once before departing?
Once Nongyu has followed Xiao Shi away, the painted portraits remain only as a source of madness for later generations.
Beiyan was at Jia Shan. Seeing the assembly, he said, "Severing the master, one does not fall into a secondary view.
The Master [Xuedou] then stepped forward from the crowd and said, "One must know there is a person who does not keep company. Jia Shan said, "That is still a secondary view.
The Master then overturned the meditation seat. Jia Shan asked, "Old friend, what about it? The Master said, "Wait for me..."
When my tongue was rotting away, I spoke thus to the Master:
"Luxuriant green grasses stir longing for the wanderer; Beyond the willows and beside the tower, the soul is lost in regret. The cuckoo calls repeatedly as the mountain seems about to rain;
Layer upon layer of fragrant mist locks the rustic gate. (Suan-an Ding)
When a monk asked Chan Master Dongshan Daoyuan (who succeeded Dongshan Jia), "If a pure practitioner does not enter nirvana,
and a precept-breaking bhikṣu does not enter hell, what then? The Master said, "When all have been delivered without a trace remaining,
he returns to transcend even nirvana."
Baoshou newly remarked: "What a fine monk! Yet he remains entirely unaware that he has fallen into a pit of shadowlessness, taking this groundless state to be the ultimate realization.
Had it not been for Dongshan’s re-establishment of the bridge and raft, when would he ever have emerged again to see the light of heaven?"
Do you wish to recognize the pure practitioner? He is on the east side. Do you wish to recognize the precept-breaking bhikṣu?
He is on the west side. Do you understand? This too is merely creating trouble where there was none.
The Chan Master Xiandehé of Jingzhao (a successor of Dongshan Jia) lived among the common people in Min. He did not maintain monastic implements nor observe the monastic code.
Wearing a single robe throughout both winter and summer, he would daily gather shrimp and clams along the riverbanks to sustain himself.
At dusk, he would sleep amidst the paper money offerings at the Baima Temple on East Mountain; thus, the local residents called him the "Shrimp-Clam Master. Huayan Jing...
Having heard this, he wished to determine whether it was true or false, so he first hid himself within the paper money.

At the dead of night, when the Master returned, Yan seized him firmly and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied, "The wine table and dishes before the deity.
Yan let go of him and said, "It is not in vain that you and I share the same roots."
Before the altar, a wine tray; an iron ball as large as a fist, struck once and shattered into pieces—worth not even half a coin.

(Wenyu Qin) Before the altar, he tosses paper and asks about the "Coming from the West"; directly seizing the opportune moment, he points to the wine tray. Bare-chested and bare-shouldered, his head and face are revealed.
Rituals: Calamity descends from heaven but does not become a disaster.
(Xiatang Yuan) How pitiable, living amidst piles of paper money! As soon as that foul mouth opens, there is only entanglement.
Having squandered the impoverished livelihood of the ghostly realm, to this day no one passes by the ancient temple. (Dongshan Yuan)
Sifting clams and hauling shrimp, they obscure their own spiritual nature. How can they fit their whole bodies into an ancient temple?
Looking up at that other side, it is a wasteland; what kind of ghostly eyes have they sought for so many years? (Dongye Fu).
Chan Master Juhui of Daguan Mountain in Tanzhou (a successor of Shishuang Zhu), when a monk asked: "As for Bodhidharma, he was..."
“Is it the Patriarch? the monk asked. The Master said, “It is not the Patriarch. The monk said, “If it is not the Patriarch, then why have you come?
The Master said, “It is precisely because you do not realize it. The monk asked, “What is it like after realization? The Master said, “Only then will you know it is not the Patriarch.”
The continuation of the flame at Shaolin is a marvel; on the night of the winter solstice, plum blossoms bloom upon branches after the snow.
Huangbo had a saying in years past: "In the Great Tang Empire, there are no Zen masters.

(Danxia Chun) Directly confronting others, he fully upholds the decree of Shaoshi; failing to respond when the opportunity arises, one passes beyond to Silla. On the Clear Wind Tower, he meets one who understands.
It is already so. There is nothing one can do about stirring up dust and smoke.
(Zu’ān Jiàn) Chan Master Daoyuan of Jiufeng in Yinzhou (a successor of Shishuang Zhu), when asked by a monk, “The patriarchs have transmitted it from one to another; what exactly did they transmit?
The Master said, “Śākyamuni was stingy; Kāśyapa was wealthy. The monk asked, “What does it mean for Śākyamuni to be stingy? The Master said:
[The monk] said, "I have nothing to give to people. [The Master] asked, "What is the wealth of Kāśyapa? The Master said, "Mencangjun within the borders of the kingdom.
[The monk] asked, "Ultimately, what is the matter that has been transmitted? The Master said, "An old man of a hundred years lighting a lamp at midnight."
Within the shadow of stillness, the entire body appears; noble and extraordinary, it naturally transcends all peers. A son born into a wealthy house is especially capable;
at the hour of midnight, the lamp’s light shines upon the neighbor to the west.
(Danxia Chun) The Jade Hall is silent, the mossy courtyard cold; a single expanse of empty concentration, the moonlight chill. From where does the sound of a flute startle the dream?
Rising, he awoke to find the sound of dripping water still lingering.
(Yuanmingzhen) Jiupeng was asked by a monk, "I have heard it said that you, Master, once remarked: 'The various sages who appear from time to time are merely messengers.
Is this so? The Master replied, "Yes. The monk asked, "When the World-Honored One pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward the earth, saying, 'Heaven...'"
"Up above in heaven, I alone am honored. Why, then, is he called a "messenger"? The Master said:
"It is precisely because he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward the earth that he is called a messenger."

The wondrous marks are perfectly luminous and cannot be grasped; the slaves and servants are merely diligent. Pointing to heaven and pointing to earth, they call themselves noble and great—yet they are but messengers transmitting words.
(Danxia Chun) With the gallop of tigers and the stride of dragons, they traverse the vast realm;
their golden resonance and jade-like vibration are by no means ordinary. If you wish to know the profound depth of this nobility...
The Imperial Decree: "The Minister’s seal of authority has not been manifested on the road.

(Guantao Qi) When the envoy transmits the decree, it is done with constant diligence; yet from of old, the Sovereign has never personally inspected the army. For the most part, this is the natural constitution of a ruler’s person;
such instances of him harmonizing the Yin and Yang are rarely heard of. (Tianyu Bao)
A monk asked Jiufeng, "What is the student’s own self? The Master said, "Ask anyone else.
The monk said, "If one accepts it as such right now, what then? The Master said, "Mount Sumeru topped with Mount Sumeru."
One knows one's own heat and cold; who else need one ask about the Patriarch’s intent coming from the West?
To accept it as a whole is to be the whole; atop the summit of Mount Sumeru, one bears Mount Sumeru.

(Stone Creek Moon) Upon arriving at home, there is no need to boast of being the master; with those most intimate, what use is there for formal greetings of cold and warmth? Wearing the heavens and treading the earth, this is the ordinary way.
[This concerns] the matter. To attach even the slightest bit [of conceptualization] is to fall into a position of superiority.
(The seal within the rank. Jiufeng was asked by a monk: "In the West, one who has completed the summer retreat is verified by means of a wax figure.
I wonder, how is it here? The Master said: "His head wears the midnight moon; his feet tread upon golden ground. The monk asked: "Does this person still undergo transformation?"
"No. The Master said, "How can you avoid turning? He asked, "How does one turn? The Master said, "In this very life, we have already heard of the dragon shedding its bones.
Jingshan Xiu said, "If someone were to ask me today, 'Is there anyone here who has attained the Way at the end of summer? I would simply answer:"
The Way is non-existent. Why do you say it is non-existent? Look at the Way: on every person’s brow, the eyebrows cross over the eyes;
on every person’s nose, the nostrils are large and the head hangs down. Now tell me: which is Nine Peaks and which is Mount Jing?
At midnight in the mountain hermitage, the moonlight is deep; With full clarity, one falls away from all merit and achievement.
Pushing aside [the veil], one reaches the upward-opening aperture that pierces to heaven; Layer upon layer of misty peaks, where no person is seen.

(Zide Hui) The golden ground is a perfect circle, the white jade wheel; The azure dragon plays with its shadow as it crosses the ford of clouds. Now, in the Jade Field of the Juyue Mountain, [all is revealed].
[The Master] said, "Externally, the Water-Mother rides a horn-broken qilin.
(Lingtong Ting) When Shishuang passed away, the assembly requested the Head Seat to serve as abbot. At that time, the Master was the attendant;
he addressed the assembly and asked the Head Seat, "The late master said: 'Rest! Cease! Be cold and clear! A single white [robe]...'"
"Refined away—gone from the incense burner of the ancient temple; gone for ten thousand years in a single thought. What matter on the periphery do you clarify?
If you understand, you may serve as abbot; if not, you may not. The Seat-holder said, "I clarify the matter of the 'single color' (monochromatic) periphery.

The Master said, "If that is so, then you have not understood the meaning of the former master. The Seat-holder said, "Just bring the incense. If you go when the smoke of the incense has ceased," the Master said.
"No," he replied. "I do not understand. He then burned incense; before the smoke had even faded, his body suddenly left the seat.
The Master patted the back of the seat and said, "To depart while sitting or to pass away while standing is certainly possible, yet I have not yet dreamt of the meaning of my late teacher."
