Yunju Shun said: "Jiufeng possesses only one eye. Nantang Jing said: "Do you wish to recognize Attendant Qian?
He is simply a fellow who kills people with urgency. Do you wish to recognize the Head Seat? He is simply like saying: 'In early spring it is still cold;
in mid-spring it is gradually warming; in late spring it is increasingly warm. Suddenly someone calls out, 'Venerable Master! and he remains mute, leaving it to him."
"Call out once! If you do not call out once, even when the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month arrives, you will still not have finished.

Kaifufu Ning said, "Now tell me, does the Head Seat understand this or not? If you say he understands, the attendant pats his back and says, 'The late master’s meaning has not yet been glimpsed in a dream.
If you say he does not understand, how can one deny that the Head Seat is truly excellent? Seize this swift opportunity!"
The hand immediately set out. But tell me, where does the benefit or harm lie? Do you understand? "The road is long and the night is deep; do not carry a torch.
Let us all blow it out and walk in the dark. Nanhua Bing said: "To penetrate the barrier of birth and death, one must soar far above the realm of things."

Wielding the sword that kills and gives life, he alone occupies the center of the world. Unless one’s eye of wisdom is clear and penetrating, one cannot avoid leaning on a fence or groping along a wall.

Do you understand? The spring orchid and the autumn chrysanthemum each flourish in their own season. The Jianfu Monastery verse says: "Generally speaking, when it comes to the essential seat of the Dharma, one desires its weight;
yet without weight, one cannot serve as the scale for the Buddhas and Patriarchs, nor act as their claws and fangs. One desires...
As for its benefit: there is no benefit greater than that which can open the way for humans and devas.

Observe how, upon Shishuang’s passing, both the head seat and the attendant each extended a hand to support his school’s fundamental tenets; this truly outshines the past and surpasses the future, something rarely heard of in all time.
If you wish to discern the source of this matter, each of you should please break your bows and arrows and overturn the shooting targets, then come before me.
When monks meet one another, Jingshan Daokai said: "Two unperforated iron hammers; among them, one is the heaviest. Tianning Weiqi said:
"The Head Seat has passed away while sitting; the attendant speaks of yellow and black paths. The former master’s intent lies at the hook's tip;
you must believe that within the curve there is the straight. If it were under Linji’s gate, who would receive thirty blows?"
"Eat! Those who come to speak of right and wrong are themselves people of right and wrong. Baen Xiu said: "The Head Seat carries a one-sided board and has grasped only a single fragment.
At that time, when he saw the Way, [if] he had said, 'In that case, I have not yet understood the late Master's intent,' it would have sufficed for him to say, 'I am not your equal.
This would have left Jiufeng with no place to stand. Have you not seen it said: 'When there is not enough to compete for, yield.'"
This leaves something remaining. Boshan Lai said: "Those who establish well cannot be uprooted; those who debate well appear as if they were mute.
The Head Seat diminished their outward splendor and filled their inner substance; he purified their conduct and provided them with a model. How could the affairs of the abbot be otherwise?
The attendant was far too abrupt and lacked common sense. Do you understand Shishuang’s intent?
Both of them deserve thirty strokes with a broom. Qinghua Yan said: "These two fellows are like people from Wuyue rowing a boat."
"Each is made to stand on one side. The Old Man of Shishuang would certainly not have been willing to nod his head in approval.
Xiang’er Jue said, "Where the Master acts, it is like fire melting ice; he penetrates the barrier of right and wrong, and his total functioning is free from gain and loss.

Everyone says that the Head Seat was stuck in 'one color,' while the Attendant’s realization surpassed his teacher. This can be called losing the essence while missing the source—utterly confused regarding the direction."
How backward! You do not realize that the Head Seat is like a heron standing in the snow—his species is distinct.
The Attendant is like a phoenix soaring through the crimson heavens, unentangled by golden nets. One stands atop the highest mountain peak; the other walks the depths of the ocean floor.
Each came from their respective directions and gathered together within the nine-layered city. Do you wish to recognize these two now?
[He raises the whisk and says: "The dragon lies in the azure depths; the wind is piercingly cold. [He lowers the whisk and says: "The crane returns to the celestial expanse;
its back brushes the heavens."
What in this world is most worthy of lamentation? A seamless iron hammer from the beginning. The furnace cannot smelt it through;
let it be blown by the wind for a thousand ages. (Bao-ning Yong) Bearing horns and clad in fur, a body of a different species;
cold ashes and withered wood—dust in the eyes. Although one has not yet realized the former master’s...
[Danxia Chun: "What can be done? At the moment of departure, one must act with personal resolve. [Shangfang Yi:
"Though a single arrow may settle the Tian Mountains, it is difficult to strike out in the midst of a hundred-battle field.
Do not say that the incense offerings in ancient shrines have ceased; before the deity, there shall always be wine and platters."
The stone man fears not the lion’s roar; upon the summit of Mount Sumeru he performs a somersault.
The vast ocean is exhausted at the third watch; the raw-iron Kunlun runs beyond the clouds.

(Chengtian Zong) One lineage of Shishuang was personally transmitted to Jiufeng. The incense has burned out and he has departed; the true pulse is difficult to penetrate. A crane makes its nest in the moon.
A thousand-year dream. In the snow-covered hut, people are lost in a single hue of function. Sitting and cutting off the ten directions, one still has a mark on the forehead;
take a subtle step and watch the flying dragon.

(Tiantong Ju) A single expanse of void and concentration, utterly free from sentiment; the white clouds disperse as colored mists spread across the sky. Travelers, do not blame me for my haste on the journey.
Swift! Sitting and guarding the cold crag, strange grasses turn green. (Yunyan, because of this:
Ten-thousand-fathom cold pools are clear to the bottom; on a frosty night at midnight, ice is about to form. To fish, one must cast the golden-scaled bait;
pull back the reed curtain toward the bright moon. (Zhengtang Bian)
The plum and the snow contend for spring, neither willing to yield. The poet sets aside his brush, laboring over their appraisal.
Though the plum yields to the snow three parts of its whiteness, the snow must concede to the plum a single measure of fragrance.
(Six Fools’ Wisdom) Jade towers and golden halls lock in the crystalline branches; the Consort vainly exerts her dancing sleeves. Even now, the autumnal radiance is clearly revealed.
Entrusted. Who knows of the hidden spring colors within the darkness?
(Panshi An) One needle, then another needle—determined to probe the depth of the ailment. When a needle strikes the painful spot, the gallbladder and liver are revealed;
only then does one know the heart’s resolve to cut flesh from one's thigh to save another. (Meixi Du)
Jiufeng was once asked by a monk, "Everyone says they come to seek instruction; I wonder, does the Master actually provide salvation?
The Master said, "Do you say that the great mountain has ever lacked a single inch of soil? The monk asked, "When one travels across the four seas in search of the Way, for what purpose is it done?
The Master said, "Yañña lost his head and his mind went mad. The monk asked, "Is there anyone who is not mad? The Master—
He said, "There is. He asked, "What is this state of not being mad? The Master said: "Suddenly awakening on the road with eyes still closed;
a great musical law arising in a cold valley. A complete transcendence that accomplishes salvation; the groves are transformed into flowers and willows—why wait for the spring breeze?"

(Fang’an Xian) The affairs of ten-thousand-li borders cause me constant worry; Yuanming [Tao Qian] cast off his seal and laughed at the title of Marquis. Returning to his native village, he was one with the wind and moon;
What need was there for the toil of life to bend the waist once more? (Xuelun Guo)
A monk asked Jiufeng, "The entire universe is, after all, this single eye. What is the eye of the universe? The Master said, "The universe is within it.
The monk asked, "Where is the eye of the universe? The Master said, "It is precisely the eye of the universe. The monk asked, "Does it still illuminate?
The Master said, "It does not borrow the power of the three luminaries. The monk said, "If it does not borrow [the three luminaries]..."
Guangshi asked, "On what basis do you call this the 'Eye of Heaven and Earth'? The Master said, "If it were not so, there would be countless people seeing ghosts before their own skulls.
As threads come and go, they speak of their inner feelings; hand in hand they enter the brocade thicket, yet in the end, their hearts are filled with boundless tears."

Painful! A single long note from the flute is entrusted to the autumn wind. Mountains layer upon layer; waters flow in succession. With the tip of the brush, one carefully dots the eyes of the dragon.
(Mok-rik-chi) Within this vast universe, there is but a single eye.
Where the light-headed is dark, the dark-headed is bright. If the golden probe were to leave behind even a hair’s breadth [of error], it would be a failure.
Obscured. Grass moves as the wind blows; all are soldiers. (Huatang Yan) There is a path for withdrawing; how can one advance?
Repeatedly picking up [the matter], he cuts through iron and chops through nails. When the envoy’s star shifted three times, the circumstances were finally appropriate;
in stabilizing the state and securing the realm, one sees his maturity. (Pin Jixiang)
A monk asked Jiufeng, "The ancients said, 'Because of the true, the false is established; from the false, the true is manifested. Is this so? The Master said, "Yes.
The monk asked, "What is the true mind? The Master said, "Not eating mixed food. The monk asked, "What is the false mind?
The Master said, "Grasping at conditions and giving rise to inversion. The monk asked, "Apart from these two paths, what is the original substance? The Master—

[The student] said, "The fundamental substance is not separate. [The teacher] asked, "Why is it not separate? The Master said: "If one does not revere the Goddess of Merit, who would loathe the Woman of Darkness?
To distinguish truth from falsehood is like sifting gold from sand; to enter and exit the same gate is to be an enemy from a past life. (Fang’an Xian)

Jiufeng addressed the assembly: "The eternally abiding Dharma-body is neither born nor extinguished. A monk asked, "If it is neither born nor extinguished, why do beings transmigrate through the six realms?
The Master said, "It is because of the mind. The monk asked, "By what skillful means should one realize the Dharma-body?
The Master said, "By uniting the empty mind with the principle of emptiness. The monk asked, "What is it like after realization?"

The Master said, "Let them revolve as they will within the three realms; in vain do you listen to the four modes of birth rushing on. He asked again, "Do you understand? [The monk] said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "Prostrate yourself!"

Refined gold requires a hundred smeltings; after a hundred smeltings, its color does not change. Turning toward the Way values being without mind; when there is no mind, the Way expands. Deeper still:
the autumn night moon, the incense burner’s ashes in an ancient temple. The Dharma-body possesses not a single thing; the mountains stand empty and towering.
(Nantang Jing) Once, when a monk asked Jiufeng, "What is the head? the Master said, "Opening one's eyes, one does not perceive the dawn. The monk asked, "What is the tail?
The Master said, "Not sitting upon the ten-thousand-year throne. The monk asked, "What is it like when there is a head but no tail? The Master said:
"In the end, it is not valued. [The student] asked, "What is it like when there is a tail but no head? The Master said, "Though one is full, there is no merit.
[The student] asked, "What is it like when the head and tail are perfectly matched? The Master said, "The descendants have gained strength, yet those within the room do not know."
Boshanlai said: "Pointing out the living path amidst the marketplace, his tongue does not touch the flesh; manifesting the total holding up of the ultimate, his skull does not touch the heavens.
Though the teeth of Jiufeng are like a shuttle in his loom, he possesses the skillful needlework of a clever wife.
What is most precious is that his descendants have gained strength while remaining unaware within the inner chamber. But tell me, what is it that they do not know?"

Regarding this matter, Lingyin Li said: "Dongshan’s clarity and subtlety harmonize the 'Correct' and the 'Deviant'; the four ministers all serve a single sovereign. Jiufeng distinguishes noble from base within the lineage;
the five sons return their whole bodies to the father. Yet they fail to realize that beyond the limit of Vairocana (Wei-yin), five horses do not neigh;
at the threshold of this present world, a single ox does not drink. Now tell me: when clouds rise over the azure peaks and the wind...
Green duckweed sprouts; withered trees roar like dragons; skulls laugh for joy. And what of it? He then planted his staff and said:
"The moon in the empty realm of the ten thousand ages’ azure pool—only after thrice scooping and stirring can one finally come to know it."

The compass draws the circle and the square draws the rectangle; they employ action and inaction, and concealment and manifestation. They leave the bird dwelling in the reeds at its own devices, while the sheep advancing or retreating bumps against the fence.
Eating the food of others and sleeping on one’s own bed: clouds rise to bring rain, and dew condenses to become frost.

Jade threads meet and pass through the eye of the needle; silk threads remain unbroken as they emerge from the loom’s belly. The stone woman halts her shuttle, yet the night deepens toward midday. The wooden...
The human path turns and the moon’s shadow shifts at its center.
(Tiantong Jue) Regarding this, Jiufeng was asked by a monk: "The ancients said, 'Even those who do not come in such a manner are still but their descendants.'"
"What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The ancients did not speak falsely. [The monk] asked, "What is the descendant who comes?
The Master said, "He still guards the precious treasure. [The monk] asked, "What is the father? The Master said, "There is no house to sit in;
there is no lineage to be established."
The Noble One’s natural state is inherently peerless; though there is a path for the transformation of the body, one traverses it amidst the journey.

Moss seals the ancient halls, making their traces hard to find; his essence blends with all dust, leaving no visible mark. Turning and revolving, both the Chinese and the barbarians reach ultimate transformation;

vast and boundless, things and self are entirely of one wind. The counsels of Shun and the tracks of Yu are but trivial matters—how could they see the Noble One again calculating merit? (Tian’an Sheng)
If one does not stand alone in precariousness, the Way begins to flourish greatly. As soon as one occupies a position of honor and nobility, one falls into the present age.

Who can recommend the wind and moon before the kalpa? The springtime beyond transformation is naturally unknown. Forgetting signs and omens, severing all expedient means—vast and empty, the golden hall overgrows with green moss.
Let the single breath of the Great Transformation turn as it will; why trouble to re-cut the eyebrows upon the eyes? (Yuan’an Fang)
A single curtain of bright moonlight reveals the returning tracks. How can one remain in a cold crag, sealed by strange weeds? Having no ground to plant even a single awl, one still falls into views;
the waters of the Xiang River have not yet been fully exhausted. When the essence and illumination are complete, the position finally ends. Shattering the coral, he laughs at Shi Chong.
If you wish to know the father of the Prince of Birth, the crane soars through the clouds and mists, emerging from its silver cage. (Xuan’an Yue)

The tetherless mud-bull is sought out on the open ground; the cowherd rides backward into the wild weeds. A single blast from the iron flute—autumn fills heaven and earth; amidst the deep mists and clouds, he hangs his robes and wanders. (Yuanzhiyuan) Jiupeng was asked by a monk:

"Why is it that a single stroke of the painting-calamus cannot capture the true likeness of Master Zhigong? The Master said: The tetherless mud-bull is sought out on the open ground; The cowherd rides backward into the wild weeds. A single blast from the iron flute—autumn fills heaven and earth; Amidst the deep mists and clouds, he hangs his robes and wanders. (From *Yuanzhiyuan*, Jiupeng’s section. A monk asked: "For what reason can a single stroke of the painting-calamus not capture the true likeness of Master Zhigong? The Master said: [as above].

[The Master] said, "Xie Sengyou, however, granted that Zhigong [was enlightened]. [The other] asked, "I do not know what kind of person Sengyou had to certify his realization for him to grant that Zhigong was so.
The Master said, "A tortoise bows its head to the pillar of Mount Sumeru."
The beautiful jade of Mount Jing was sought by Bianyi; the supreme treasure is flawless, cutting off all causes for perception.
An iron ox with its calf tramples the blue sea; the stone tortoise that strikes the moon grows long feathers and scales.
(Touzi Qing) Chan Master Jingxin of Yongquan in Taizhou (a successor of Shishuang Chu) was asked by a monk: "What is that which is transmitted?"

[The student] asked about this matter. The Master said: "The dragon spits forth water that grows long; the fish swallow endless bubbles. [The student] said: "I ask the Master to pick it out for me. The Master said:
"Beat the drum and turn the prow of the boat; the oars pierce the moon beneath the waves."
Lingeringly, the half-moon sinks into the cold water; Resplendent, the three stars fall upon the emerald peaks.
In the past, Yunyan once let it slip: "The Prince of the Golden Wheel’s jeweled flower crown.
(Danxia Chun) Yongquan, because Emperor Wuzong had suppressed the Buddhist teachings, was tending cattle at the monastery. At that time, two Zen guests named Jiang and De arrived.
Along the way, they saw the Master riding an ox; not recognizing him, they remarked, "The hooves and horns are quite distinct, yet how unfortunate that the rider cannot see them.
The Master spurred the ox and departed. The two Chan practitioners subsequently rested beneath a tree and brewed some tea.
The Master stepped down from his ox and sat with him. He then asked, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "From over there.
The Master said, "What is the matter of 'over there'? He [Qiang] lifted his tea cup. The Master said, "This is still the matter of 'this side.
What is the matter of 'over there'? Qiang was speechless. The Master said, "Do not say that the rider does not see clearly."
Baoning Yong said to his attendant, Quanji, "When you return to the mountains, explain this clearly.
Baoshou Fang remarked, "Great Master Yongquan seems to have lost ground at the south end and come back to settle matters at the north end.

At that time, he waited for [the questioner] to say, 'The horns are very distinct,' yet how could he help it that the rider did not recognize them? Why did he not dismount the ox and step forward himself?"
Seizing him and saying, "Speak quickly! Speak quickly! if the other hesitates even for a moment, he strikes him across the face with a single palm.
Then he says, "It is well; do not say that the rider does not discern."
Fragrant grasses spread far and wide—how could they change with autumn? The cowherd boy and the white ox roam at ease.
In the midst of the extraordinary, those on the Way find it hard to see; Yet they say he rides an ox without knowing the ox.
(Danxia Chun) One who studies medicine desires nothing more than excellent prescriptions, But after many days, they become mere herbalists. What is truly required is your genuine medicine.
Look! Before others, one cannot avoid being busy at both ends.
(Lisuyan) When Yongquan was visiting Xuefeng, he escorted him to the sedan chair. Once they were inside, the Master said, "This one is carried by four people;
which one is carried by how many? Xuefeng straightened his body and rose up, saying, "What are you saying? The Master asked again.
Feng said, "Xuefeng would not have understood. The Master said, "If you know, then you know; it is simply that you cannot express it.
Yunju Zhuang said, "There is guest and there is host; there is total withdrawal and total release. You must directly recognize Xuefeng of Yongquan."
Whether you have escaped or not yet done so, you must by all means refrain from driving a stake into empty space. Xuánjiàn Héng said:
"Yǒngquán feigned deafness, which was not without a certain pliability; Xùfēng deceived his opponent and did not know how to reduce the number of cooking fires.
If it were Fórì, he would wait for the question, "How many men carry it? and simply say to the four men, "Give one tally to this venerable monk. Observe Yǒngquán!
Furthermore, what course of action should be taken?
*Zongjian Fali*, Fascicle 64; *Zongjian Fali*, Fascicle 65.
Ji Yun Tang Edition.
Compiled by Chan Master Yuanjing (Shizhuang Zhu’s successor) of Mount Yungai in Tanzhou, the Sixth Generation after Dajian (Huineng). A monk asked Shizhuang: "The myriad..."
"If all the doors are closed, I do not ask. But when ten thousand doors are all open, what then? Shuang said, "What about the matter within the hall?
The monk had no reply. After six months, he finally uttered a phrase: "No one can receive him. Shuang said, "To speak, you speak indeed too much;
yet you have only spoken eighty percent. [The monk] asked, "And as for you, Master, how is it?"
"What? Heshang Shuang replied, "No one recognizes him. When the Master heard this, he prostrated himself and requested that Heshang provide an exposition for him.
Heshang was unwilling. The Master then took Heshang by the arm and went up to the abbot’s quarters, saying, "If you do not speak, I shall strike you!"
Shuang said, "It is found. The Master prostrated repeatedly. Shuang said, "No one recognizes him. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "The beginning was not reached; the end went too far. Tiantong Jue said, "In the secure and secret field, one must avoid falling into the realm of effort and achievement.
The garment that clings to the flesh must be stripped away. To discern the essence within the school, one must turn beyond the measure of the mind."
The pivot: one must be meticulous before it can be grasped. The difference within sameness is still clearly tinged with ambiguity;

the sameness within difference is truly difficult to reach its ultimate subtlety. Do you know where Shi-sang and his son shifted their positions? "The jade figure burns her candle and first breaks the dream;
the night is cold, and Qing-nü has not yet ascended the loom. Tian-ning Qi said: "If someone were to ask Yong..."
When the ten thousand households open their gates together, what then? To him he said: "Be glad that you have arrived.
Are you the same as or different from the ancients? Baegam Pu said: "To be entirely without dependence, one must see through to the state where not even an inch of thread hangs;
to be majestic and unassailable, one must exhaust the present moment. Here, a deviation of even a hair’s breadth means that the musical scales will no longer harmonize."
Now, do you know the secure and profound place of Shishuang and his "father" [his teacher]? Beyond the mundane world, how can there be room for calculation or deliberation?

The ancient hall stands with crags opening to reveal the moon, while frost gathers and snow falls upon the pines; their resonance is inexhaustible. Before the stars, a man lies in his chamber amidst a thousand peaks;
even Buddhas and Patriarchs have no way to recognize this fellow. (Touzi Qing)
No one can grasp him; he surpasses Ma Xiangru. Indeed, he comes upon the bridge; he remembers the inscription on the pillar’s head.
No one recognizes him; the chessboard belongs to the drunken woodcutter. Turning his head, the axe-handle has rotted away; even the great ocean has turned to dry land.
(Tiantong Jue) In profound stillness the curtains hang, the jeweled hall is empty; throughout the six palaces, only the sparse patterns of incense smoke are seen.
The Dragon’s countenance is ultimately most majestic and solemn—who would dare lift their eyes to gaze upon him? (A separate, wondrous assembly.)
The Chan Master Yizhan of Mount Zhongnan (a successor of Shishuang Chu) arrived at Xuefeng for several days, after which he went to Xuansha.
Xuansha said, "Regarding this matter, I alone am able to know it. How do you, Elder, understand it?
The Master replied, "One must know that there is one who does not seek to know. Xuansha said, "Why does that old fellow on the mountain head go through all this hardship?"
Cui Feng Xian’s words regarding the distinct boundary state say: "How many under Xuefeng’s gate are like this?
Chan Master Hongjian of Mount Fuchuan (a successor of Shishuang Chu) was once asked by a monk: "When one brings the uncut jade to a master, will the master receive it?
The Master struck the incense altar with his hand. The monk prostrated. The Master said: "That you prostrate is not without merit."
"What is the matter therein? The monk then struck the incense altar. The Master said, "The tongue does not leave the mouth;
the tongue does not leave the mouth. Three times three makes nine. Calculating all the way to the edge of the incense altar, both have fallen behind others."
(Chōdō Shō) Fushan was asked by a monk, "Please speak, Master, regarding that place where hook and mallet do not reach. The Master remained silent for a long while.
The monk said, "The mechanism of a flashing bolt is in vain for one who merely stands and ponders. The Master said, "Try to utter a phrase that transcends the ordinary; speak it! The monk drew near.
The Master stepped back three paces. The Master said, "This is an extraordinary statement. As for the matter at hand right now, how is it?
The monk brushed his sleeves and departed. The Master said, "He is indeed a fellow from Tianjin Bridge."
Zhaojue Qin said: "This monk is like unrefined gold and uncut jade. The great furnace of Fushan has opened wide;

after a hundred smeltings and a thousand refinements, he has become a single Diamond King’s precious sword. Do you understand this thoroughly? He is a man on the Tianjin Bridge, looking with eyes fixed upon the tip of the Northern Dipper."
Fushan was asked by a monk, "What is the offspring of the lion? The Master said, "A fine roar. The monk clapped his hands and said, "A fine hand! A fine hand!
The Master said, "Under the clear blue sky and bright sun, you have been bewitched by a ghost. The monk made a gesture as if to overturn the meditation seat. The Master struck him.
The monk said, "The donkey's business is not yet over when the horse's business arrives. The Master said, "Truly so."
The master said, "This monk took a bowl and filled it with water, intending to compare it to the great ocean.
Ying Shan Yin said, "Had it not been for Fu Chuan, his spirit-talisman would have nearly been snatched away by that monk."
With staff and wood, he performs once more upon this stage; he waits for an adept to appear in the ordinary course of things.
Although the "Snow Melody" is difficult to harmonize with, he laughingly takes up the "Ba Song" and ascends the platform.

(Xueguan Yin) Mountains topple as he spreads his wings like those of a Peng bird; the brooks overflow as he unfurls his scales like those of a dragon. Heaven revolves and earth turns as he shifts leftward.
Yet, right and left shift; wind arises and clouds emerge, exiting from the realm of ghosts and entering the realm of spirits. I too do not know how such numinous wonders can be like this.
Once, while wandering through the profound darkness, I beheld a feathered immortal (a *xiān*).
The Chan Master Hǎiyàn of Zhěmísì on Mount Yúnmén in Yuèzhōu (a successor of Shīshuāng Zhū), when asked by a monk: "How is it? [Hǎiyàn said: "Jièxùxiá. (This refers to the master's response.)

"This is a secret chamber. The Master said, "It is not a place for the tight-fisted. [The monk] asked, "Who is the person within the secret chamber? The Master said, "One who does not sit upon the colored ox.
Yanguan Yin said, "Yanguan would not say it this way. What is the secret chamber? The ten directions have no walls. As it was thus...
Who is this person within the secret chamber? With eight sides completely unobstructed.
This is Chan Master Shizhu of Fengxiang Prefecture (a successor of Shishuang Chu). While the Master was traveling, he arrived at Dongshan.
There, due to the words bestowed by Master Daogyan, it was said: "There are four kinds of people. The first person speaks beyond the Buddhas and Patriarchs, yet cannot take a single step."
[The Master] said: "There is. One person’s practice surpasses that of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, yet cannot be expressed in words.
Another can express it and can practice it. Another cannot express it and cannot practice it. Which one is that person? The Master stepped forward from the assembly and said:
"The one whose practice surpasses that of the Buddhas and Patriarchs but cannot be expressed in words is simply tongueless and not permitted to practice. The one who can express it..."
That which the Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot speak is simply that there is no basis for it, and thus it is not permitted to be spoken.
That one person who can speak and can practice is simply like a lid fitting its box. That one person who cannot speak and cannot practice is like seeking life by cutting off one's own breath;
this is like a child born of a stone carrying a cangue and wearing shackles. Shanshan asked, "What about your own portion, Master?"
Shengshui said, "The Master’s words are comprehensive and penetrating; how brilliantly they manifest! Sanshan asked, "As for Minggong Xiushou on the sea, what about him?
Shengshui said, "Two illusory people meet, clapping their hands and laughing 'he-he'."
The mud ox at the bottom of the sea plows the white moon; the wooden horse in the clouds gallops through the clear wind. The barbarian monk is too lazy to hold his Western bowl;
at midnight he boards a boat and crosses to the east of the sea.
(Danxia Chun) The wooden man blows the double-reed flute atop the ridge; the stone woman plays a short lute by the stream. In every place, all speech is in accord.
The Way. Whose lutes and pipes do not transmit the mind? (By Yu Zunpeng.
The scholar Zhang Zhuo (who met Shishuang Chu) was directed by Master Chan Yue to visit Shishuang. Shishuang asked him, "What is your surname?"
The layman said, "My surname is Zhang and my given name is [矢*出]. Changshou said, "Seeking cleverness, it cannot be found; from where does [矢*出] come?
The layman suddenly attained realization and presented this verse: "Radiant, silent illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges; Ordinary beings, sages, and all sentient creatures share my home.
When a single thought does not arise, the entire body is manifest; As soon as the six sense organs stir, they are obscured by clouds. Severing affliction..."

When afflictions are heavy, the illness increases; even to turn toward True Suchness (tathatā) is likewise erroneous. To flow in accordance with worldly conditions without obstruction, one regards both nirvāṇa and saṃsāra as equal to flowers in the sky.
Jing-shan Gao said: "The donkey chooses a damp spot to urinate."
The decrepit Shishuang knows no taboos; he can bring up the pivotal phrase right before one’s face.
It was only because of that "motherly heart" on that day that it has been passed down through the ages, lingering on the lips of men.

(Fujian Qin) I do not envy those who transmit titles by imperial decree or those who enjoy a fine reputation; they mistakenly take the mountains and rivers for their own eyes. In a single moment, both skill and clumsiness are torn asunder.
Shattered! The heavy illness of the afflictions is eradicated.
(Xiaoweng Kan) Advancing forward, there are precipices three thousand *zhang* high; retreating backward, there are cliffs tens of thousands of layers deep.
Cherish this old man Zhang Zhuo of the Great Tang; his iron hammer, lacking a hole, dances in the spring breeze. (Baoye Yuan)
Chan Master Yuan’an of Luopu Mountain in Lizhou (a successor of Jiashan Hui): Having long served as an attendant to Linji, one day he took his leave.
As Linji ascended the hall, he said, "In the gate of Linji there is a red-tailed carp; shaking its head and wagging its tail, it has gone southward.
I know not in whose pickle jar it will be drowned. After the Master had finished his travels, [he arrived at Luopu].
He went straight to the foot of Mount Jia and pitched a hermitage there. For a year he did not visit Jia-shan. Jia-shan composed a letter and ordered a monk to deliver it.
When the Master received it, he sat down immediately; when the monk unfolded his hands to request [a response], the Master gave no reply.
The Master then struck him, saying, "Go back and report this to the Abbot. When the monk returned and reported it, Jia-shan said, "If that monk had opened the letter, within three days..."
"He will surely come. If you do not open this letter, this man cannot be saved. Three days later, the Master arrived. Seeing the Mountain, he did not prostrate;
instead, he stood facing him with his hands joined at his chest. The Mountain said, "A rooster nesting in a phoenix's nest—these are not of the same kind.
Begone! The Master said, "I have traveled from afar to seek your presence; I beg the Master for a single meeting. The Mountain said, "Before my eyes there is no..."
"Upādhyāya, there is no old monk here. The Master then gave a shout. Xiangyan said, "Wait, wait! Do not be so hasty and precipitate.
The clouds and moon are the same, yet the streams and mountains differ. It is not that you cannot cut off the tongues of all people under heaven," [but...]
"Preceptor, how can you teach a tongueless person to speak? The Master hesitated; Shan then struck him. From this point on, he took [Shan's teaching] to heart.
Xinghua Jiangdai said of Pu: "Just know how to become a Buddha; do not worry about sentient beings. Wuzu Jie came out with Pu’s words, saying:
"Try explaining the principle further," and then he left. Dayang Xuan said in his place: "I want the Master too."
Proof. Cui-feng Xian said: "This fellow is pitiable and tragic; he has rendered Linji ineffective.
Since he says 'the clouds and moon are the same,' I would say 'the streams and mountains are each different. What need is there to say that a tongueless person cannot speak?
With this, he struck him across the mouth with his sitting mat. Had Jia-shan been a man who understood the Way, he certainly would have placed [the mat] beneath a bright window.
[The Master] struck the gavel. Zhaojue Qin said: "Although Cui峰 was like drawing a bow after the thief has fled, he nonetheless cleared Linji’s innocence.

Examining this from the start, his command was carried out only halfway. Had he been able to shoulder the treasury of the true Dharma-eye, as soon as [Linji] said, 'How can one teach a tongueless person to speak?
he would have overturned the meditation seat and shouted the assembly apart—what more need be waited for?"
What is this "arranging beneath the bright window"? He picks it up and goes straight off.

Even if one’s mechanism is like a flash of lightning, one’s eyes like shooting stars, and one’s eloquence like a cascading river, in the end one finds no place to set hand or foot. But tell me, where does the confusion lie? He then said:

Xian. Dongshan Fu said: "At that time, although Luopo had no words with which to respond and no principles by which to justify himself, his ignorance was like that of Goujian’s practice of success—he was ultimately able to sleep on wooden chips and taste gall."
A companionless stone man enters the mountains at night; snow enshrouds his crimson crown as his green robe chills.
He roars, revealing the three peaks’ beauty beyond the kalpas; he holds forth the golden robe to gaze upon the sun.
(Touzi Qing) Shaking its head and wagging its tail, this red-tailed fish has no place to rely and knows how to turn its body; it severs the tongue, yet possesses abundance.
The technique: pulling back the nostrils, wondrously penetrating the divine. Beyond the curtain of night-clarity, wind and moon are as bright as day;
before the cliff of the withered tree, flowers and plants flourish throughout spring. The tongueless man—the tongueless man! Truly upholding the full mandate, one fresh phrase.
Walking alone within the world, clearly and fully aware, let the whole realm rejoice in its happiness. (Tiantong Jue)
The front foot does not find solid ground; the back foot shifts its step. One falls into the thick mud, while bystanders cry out in pity for their suffering.
If one calls out to raise them up, it only brings trouble upon you.
(Shi Yu Fang) Under the Incense Pavilion, he drunkenly inscribed a poem. Favor and disgrace were linked in a single moment. Clouds, moon, streams, and mountains all share in this.
Different. Throughout his life he wandered aimlessly to the west of Yelang.
(San-yi-yu) As the wind rises over the wheat waves, purple lightning flashes; upon the Dragon-leaping Pool, the dawn sun shines bright.
Had he been able to display his valor by drawing his sword at that time, why wait for the thunder to shake the gates of the sea? (Xiao-yue-lang)
Luo Pu was once asked by a monk, "It is said that making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as making offerings to a single mindless man of the Way.
I wonder, what fault do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have, and what virtue does the mindless man of the Way possess?
The Master said, "A single sheet of white clouds spans the mouth of the valley; how many returning birds are utterly lost in their nests?"
Shide is lax and indolent, unaware of the break of dawn; Hanshan is lazy and idle, not knowing when to return home. Before a single word is uttered, the perfect sound is beautiful;
beyond all things, the crescent moon shines upon the three peaks.

(Danxia Chun) The eyebrows of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are curved; there is nothing to realize and nothing to cultivate, yet the eyes are blurred with rheum. Treading upon it, one finds the bottom still unexhausted.
Frozen. At one moment it was recognized as azure lapis lazuli (Fózhì Yù).
The ancient mountains stand towering, locked in cold mist; they refuse to lightly grant the transmission of their heart-mind. A jade maiden seeks the seal of no-words at night;
a stone man points afar toward the moon’s brightness (Zìdé Huī).
Luopu asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Jingnan. The Master said, "There is a person who goes like this;
do you encounter him? The monk said, "I do not encounter him. The Master said, "Why do you not encounter him? The monk said, "If I were to encounter him, my head would shatter into pieces.
The Master said, "Your three-inch tongue is very well-guarded."
When Yunmen Wenyan saw this monk in Jiangxi, he asked, "Is there such a saying? The monk replied, "Yes.
Yunmen said, "Luopu would have retreated three thousand li."
Luo Pu was asked by a monk, "What is it that cannot be contained within the Great Canon? The Master said, "The rain nourishes the three types of grasses to flourish;
a single piece of jade shines by its very nature."
Before Biepyo Rock, the dawn bears the traces of spring; The fragrant breeze occasionally gathers atop the Vulture Peak.
One must know that within the jade image and the vase-stupa, There is another lamp that illuminates heaven and reflects the earth.
(Touzi Qingsu) Once, when a monk asked Luopu, "What is it like when a student intends to return to his hometown? The Master said, "The house is ruined and the people are gone."
"Where will you go when you return? he asked. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then I shall not return. The Master said, "The remaining snow in the courtyard melts under the sun;
who will sweep away the drifting dust within the room? He then presented this verse: "Determined in mind, I return to my home, Boarding a boat to drift upon the Five Lakes.
Raising the oar, the stars and moon vanish; Pausing the rowing, the sun stands solitary. Unmooring the lines, I leave the shore of error."
"Raising the sails, he sets out upon the direct path; having arrived, his home is utterly swept away.
Thus he avoids being a fool within the house. Tian Qi said: "This monk has been solitary and exposed for kalpas, which is why he never forgets it.

Although Luopo’s [ice] has melted and his [fortifications] have crumbled, there is still fear that he might build a palace of jade; though he is freed from external entrapment, he still maintains internal management. He cannot help but..."
I offer one more word: Why? Where the wild geese fly, they do not reach; man is dragged by profit and fame.
On the road to the peaceful land, the journey is empty and far; my longing for home drifts on, beyond the bounds of thought.
When you cast off your hands and arrive home, what will there be? A crystal palace locked with empty flowers. (Danxia Chun)
Lopu was asked by a monk: "When a single hair swallows up the vast ocean, what more can be said therein? The Master replied:
"If a household possesses the White Deer Map, there will certainly be no such monsters."
Baofu Zhan said in parting: "In a home where there is no painting of Bai Ze, such a monster will certainly not exist.

Though there may be a thousand acres of clouds before the crags, within the door there is utterly no lamp at midnight. The perilous peaks stretch as far as the eye can see, beautiful through ancient and modern times;
the slanting light of heaven shines upon the layered emerald heights. (Danxia Chun)
When a monk asked Luopu, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? the Master said:
"Where the green mists cover all, one emerges and hides the tip; when the white moon shines, the azure pool has no reflection."
The myriad flowers have not yet blossomed, but the plum has already split open; The ten thousand trees are withered and falling, yet the cypress grows all the more wondrous.
The clouds are thin, failing to reveal the moon’s reflection through the sieve-like branches;

The mist is light, unable to expose the wind-swaying limbs. (Danxia Chun) Faintly the morning sun hangs upon the bamboo window; Pomegranate flowers beyond the courtyard leave behind lingering fragrance. The curtains are drawn, and the bright sunlight no longer enters.
Leakage. A lingering light smoke locks the painted hall. (The second line is complete.
When Layman Pang rose from his prostrations, Luopu said, "In midsummer it is scorching heat; in early winter it is slight cold.
The Master said, "Do not be mistaken. He replied, "Master Pang is old. The Master said, "Why do you not say 'it is cold' when it is cold, and 'it is hot' when it is hot?"
Nanquan said, "What is the trouble with being deaf? The Master said, "I give you thirty blows. Nanquan said, "Shut my mouth and plug your eyes.
The Master said, "Right now, I shut your mouth; clearly, I plug your eyes. From the beginning, Luopu and Master Pang have never emerged."
Muzhou Carrying a Board: Facing him directly, he fully upholds [the Way], illuminating past and present.
Whether winter is cold or summer is hot, who can discern it? (Lingyuan Qing) Luopu ascended the hall: "Sun Bin is closing his shop today. Any diviners, come forth!
At that time, a monk stepped forward and said, "I request the Master to divine for me. The Master said, "Your father is dead. The monk was speechless.
Fayan Yi clapped his hands three times in response. Jingshan Daokai said, "This monk has lost his luck and killed his own father;
he is now being clapped for by another. One truly knows that misfortune does not come alone. Yet Luopo was skilled at divining, and Fayan was skilled at judging.
If one reflects carefully, both elders have simultaneously revealed their flaws. Having already cast the hexagram, they have obtained "Fire."
The *Fengding* hexagram. Why is it categorized as *Dihuo Mingyi*? Yunmen did not think so. He suddenly took up his staff and said, "Under Sun Bin, the father has been executed.
He struck the ground three times and asked, "Do you understand? Belonging internally to the *Gen* palace, he sought the external image once more.
Again, he struck the ground three times and said, "A thousand spirits and ten thousand numina; ten thousand sages and a thousand spirits—do not follow the crowd!"
[He] strikes the desk once again and says: "Inquiring about good or bad fortune. Jin-su Yuan said: "Lu-pu opened a great divination shop and was skilled at discerning good and bad fortune.
What is regrettable is that this monk did not pay the divination fee; he brings trouble upon bystanders as they clap their hands in laughter.
Today, it is not so here. Sun Bin is closing his shop. If there is a diviner who comes forward—suddenly, a filial son!"
A man from Iwami requested the Master to divine his fate. The Master simply said to him, "Your father is alive. "Venerable ones," [the Master continued], "his father has already died.

Why, then, did he say he is alive? Have you not heard how for seventy-one years his fame was renowned throughout the district? The character of this virtuous man is such that its influence remains as enduring as high mountains and long rivers?"
Lopu was asked by a monk, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?

The Master said, "The sun and moon together with their radiance—who has a separate path? The monk said, "In that case, light and darkness follow different routes, yet right and wrong are of one measure. The Master said:
Simply do not lose your own sheep; why must you weep at the fork in the road?
The moon sifts through pine shadows, high and low among the trees; The sun shines upon the heart of the pond, heaven above and below. The blazing heat of the sky is not yet midday;
The full orb of the autumn night is not known to be round. (Danxia Chun)
When a monk asked Luopu, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? the Master said, "Snow covers the solitary peak, yet the peak is not white;
rain nourishes the stone sprout, and the sprout has just begun to grow."
The dragon roars at the bottom of the sea, moistening clouds and rain; the tiger roars among the trees, clearing the valley breeze.
Do not say that thorns grow everywhere on the road, for how much more so in a poor household where there is little welcoming or seeing off?
(Danxia Chun) Once, when the practitioner of Haxi Daozhe visited Luopo, the Master asked: "Since we parted at Lixi, I have now..."
“How many years have passed? he asked. The Master said, “I still remember the events of long ago. The monk said, “I have heard it said that those who speak of the Way forget all dates and years.
The monk continued, “Master, your administrative duties as abbot are many; allow me to observe you closely for a while. The Master said, “If you strike me, you strike one who understands Chan.
The monk said, “I am capable of receiving such treatment. The Master said, “For you, a practitioner dwelling in the mountains, your own affairs are many.”
Qinglong said this: "The two elders have their host and guest; they have their gathering and their release. Yet when examined closely, they are all merely exposing each other's family scandals.
Today, Bianshan takes a rope made of tortoise hair, ties it into a single knot, and hurls it into the Jewel-Bead Pond to drown them there.
Is there anyone who can save them? If not, I trouble the Elder of Dongchan to do so.
I explain it for you:
such news is extraordinary. From every branch of the moon-orchid tree, a far-reaching fragrance issues. Recently, Chang’e displayed her ingenuity;
with her eyes fixed upward, she embroidered a pair of mandarin ducks. (Danxia Chun)
Luo Pu said to his attendant, "Master Zhao has composed the Four Treatises; they are truly extraordinary.
The Master replied, "Master Zhao is indeed extraordinary, yet he has still not seen the Patriarchs. The attendant was speechless.
Qingliang Qin said, "Where did the Master see the Patriarch? Yunju Xi said, "Where is it that Master Zhao failed to see the Patriarch?
Is it because there are so many words? Furthermore, how many words did Master Zhao have?"
Lopu was asked by a monk, "When many hands sift through gold, who is it that obtains it? The Master said, "The ancient treasure within the fist is not selected by sifting through the sand.
The monk said, "If that is so, then even with hands outstretched, one does not encounter it. The Master said, "Do not mistake the cry of a crane for the song of a warbler."
Seeking gold—how could it depend on sifting through sand? Even touching the stones amidst the waves requires effort.
When the pillar suddenly emits light at the third watch, at that moment, who knows it?
(Danxia Chun) Once, when a monk asked Luopo, "When the various sages come in this manner, with what shall we make offerings? the Master said, "Though the Earth-Dweller..."
Holding a *khakkhara* staff, he is no mere Brahmin;
though spirits visit him in vain, he but clamors on in delusion. His gate and courtyard stand like sheer cliffs, ten thousand fathoms high.

He finely slices the pure breeze to serve as sacrificial offerings, and thinly slices the bright moon to serve as spring wine. In vain he performs the three libations to repay the intentions of those who come; how could one seek even a single coin to purchase such a thing?
Paper burns; there is not a single thing left to offer. Amidst the snow and frost, the blade is held level, its edge sharp enough to shave a hair.
(Tian'an Sheng) When Luopu was approaching his final passing, he addressed the assembly, saying: "I now have a matter to ask you all. If you say this is it—"
"This is placing a head upon a head. "If you say it is not so," [the Master] said, "then you must cut off your head to seek life.
The First Seat said, "The green mountains do not lift their feet; beneath the sun, one does not hang a lamp. The Master said, "What kind of age is this that such talk is made?
At that time, the Senior Seat Yancong replied, "Setting aside these two paths, I ask the Master not to question me further."
The Master said, "Not yet; speak further. Yancong said, "I have not exhausted the Way. The Master said, "I do not care whether you exhaust it or not.
Yancong said, "Since Yancong has no attendant, I have come to respond to the Master myself. The Master then ceased speaking.
That night, he had an attendant call Cong and asked him, "Disciple, today your response was most reasonable. You should have realized this."
The intention of the former master. The Way of the former master: "There is no dharma before one's eyes; the meaning lies before one's eyes.

It is not a dharma of the present moment; it is not that which can be reached by the ears or the eyes. Which phrase is the guest? Which phrase is the host? If you can discern this, I shall entrust you with the bowl and robe.
Yancong said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "You ought to understand. Yancong said, "I truly do not understand."
The assembly gathered. The Master shouted them out and said, "Suffering! Suffering! The next day, another monk brought up the previous conversation and questioned the Master.
The Master said, "The Compassionate Boat does not ply upon the clear waves; at Sword Gorge, it is but labor in vain to release wooden swans."
Baoci then said: "Tell me, does the Head Seat truly not understand? Or is it that he is afraid of seeing the bowl-bag stick to him?
Boshan Lai said: "At the time of his impending passing, he entrusted the karmic seal to his descendants;

his subtle thoughts were heaven-made, and his disposition was naturally distinct. The Head Seat, Master Yan, had a great path for self-actualization—how regrettable that the Elder [did not recognize it]."
It is difficult to grasp through words and phrases; if one seeks it through intellectual understanding, one cannot avoid being like someone who presses a map to find a horse.
Baiting the hook for clouds and catching the moon at the pure ford, old in years and solitary in heart, I have yet to catch a scale.
After returning with a single verse of the *Li Sao*, I am the only one left sober upon the banks of the Miling River. (Tiantong Jue)
The matter beneath the paper robe requires no womb; with hands clasped on a precipice, one is but a babe in swaddling clothes.
At the assembly of Nirvana, the site of enlightenment opens; the Direct Transmission arrives like a crown prince.
(Nantang Jing) For years I have drifted in a fisherman’s boat upon the river waves; the long pole remains in my hand, never idle. Yet, failing to meet the scaled dragon, my labor has been in vain.
With power, he gathers in the fishing line and passes through another bay.
(Yuan Zu Yu) Chan Master Ke Wen of Panlong Mountain in Yuanzhou Prefecture (a successor of Jia Shan Hui) was asked by a monk:
"After a deceased monk has passed away, where does he go? The Master said: "The stone ox follows the ancient road; the night lamp shines in broad daylight."
A bottomless boat sails across the four hundred continents; the moonlight’s reflection falls upon the shallow sands.
The mud-dragons stir the waves, vying for prominence; ten thousand acres of misty billows flow forth unimpeded.
(By Pingxiang) Chan Master Shanhuan Pu of Luojing (a successor of Jiashan Hui) was once asked by a monk: "What is the realm of Shaoshan?"
The Master said: "Throughout ancient and modern times, monkeys and birds cry out; emerald colors are enshrouded by thin mist. [The student] asked: "What is it like to be a person within this realm?

The Master said: "Step back and look. This is the finest realm of Shaoshan: mist enshrouds the light emerald hues. One wishes to paint it, yet cannot finish; monkeys and birds call out, one note after another."
(Shixi Yue) Once, when Zun Bunan came to visit Shao Shan, the Master met him at the foot of the mountain. Zun asked, "Where does the road to Mount Shao lead?
The Master pointed with his finger and said, "It goes toward where the Wuna Peak is green and deep blue. Zun drew near.
The Master seized him by the front and said, "I have long heard of Mount Shao; is it not so? The Teacher said, "It is indeed so. Layman, what business do you have?
He replied, "I intend to pose a question; will you answer me? The Teacher said, "I see you are no son of King Kimnara;
how could you possibly draw a bow to shoot Wei-chi? He replied, "A phoenix flies straight into the misty clouds; who—"
[The student] said, "I fear the wild sparrows in the forest. The Master said, "The painted drum before the hall is for you to strike; try to display your family style as an old monk [would].
[The student] said, "A single phrase transcends beyond the thousand sages; the pine and vines do not equal the full moon.
The Master said, "Even if you go straight out beyond the time of Wei-yin, you are still half a month’s journey short of Shao-shan. [The student] asked, "Where does the fault lie?"

[The student] said, "Your words are extraordinary; people of this age know them. The Master said, "If that is so, then true jade is distinct from the mud, yet it does not brush away the dust of ten thousand affairs.
The student said, "Under the workshop of Lu Ban, one merely applies clever ingenuity. The student asked, "The student only understands it thus;
I do not know what your intention is, Master. The Master said, "At night, the Jade Maiden casts her shuttle and weaves brocade upon—"
Xishi asked, "Is this not the very style of your house, Master? The Master said, "A farmer fashions a jade water-clock;
it is not the work of a master craftsman. Xishi said, "That is still merely literary expression. What is the style of your house, Master?
The Master said, "Lying across the body to face the universe—who is there to show their head? Zun was speechless. The Master then returned to the mountain with him.
As soon as the formal greetings were concluded, the Master called him forward and said: "The *dārala* possesses a spirit that pierces the heavens;
this old monk has a scheme to enter the earth. The *dārala* swallows the vast ocean in one gulp; this old monk carries Mount Sumeru on his back.

The *dārala* comes forward with sword in hand; this old monk awaits him with spear leveled. Speak quickly, speak quickly, regarding the single path that leads upward! [The *dārala*] replied: "Clarity."

[Zhao] pointed to a mirror on a stand and requested, "Please, Master, have a look. The Master said, "I do not look. [Zhao] asked, "Why do you not look? The Master said, "The water is shallow and there are no fish;
it is a vain effort to cast down the hook. Zhenzhou was speechless. The Master then struck him.
Huanglong Xin said, "It is well to strike such fellows as these! Even if one were to kill hundreds of thousands of them, what fault would there be?
Had they been in Huanglong’s hands at that time, even if his staff had broken, he would not have let them go.

Heshan Xun said, "When spreading a net across the heavens to strike the phoenix and snare the dragon, the host carves jade and etches ice; the guest gathers flowers and clusters brocade. When it comes to this...
The pivot does not yield; face-to-face, they vie for precedence. Interlocking corners and spiral patterns exist in mutual preservation and mutual conquest.
Everywhere it is said that a master of hand presents his skill within the hands of another. Is this truly so?

From the perspective of Huirui’s realization, if Zunbuna can be careful at the beginning and guard against the end, he need only wait for Shaoshan to point out the path, and with a swift stride, he will ascend to the inner sanctum. Take care.
Take this and arrange it beneath the bright window. This not only cuts off the tangled vines of conceptual proliferation, but also avoids being caught by others’ hooks and lines.
Why? Because at the point where a single move has not yet been reached, the entire board is filled with empty mental exertion. Tiantong Hua said:
"Master Sijian caused a great deal of alarm and fuss for a time, yet he did not realize that since Shao Shan suffered the lethal blow of Puna, [the matter] remains so to this day."
No one can examine it thoroughly. Tell me, where does the error lie?

Adapting to the times and responding to changes, following things through their cycles of success and failure—whose bird-like spirit could distinguish the male from the female? Before the Marquis of Han met his fortune, he maintained the style of a simple monk;
that he rolled up the Three Qin like a mat was not without strategy. What need is there to recall Kuai Tong’s words of loyalty and righteousness? (Fangan Xian)
Meeting on a narrow path, divine mechanisms are cut off; it is like a crash of thunder combined with a flash of lightning.
It resembles a wild torrent that has undergone a hundred turns. The axe of Ying is applied; the arrow of Ji is set. Even the keen eyes of a hawk and the piercing gaze of a dragon cannot discern them.
As for Sima Xiangru’s chariot yielding to General Yan—let the people of the age judge who is superior and who is inferior. (Luan-yuan Yue)

Vivid green and deep blue, the traveler’s longing stretches afar. With a marvelous display of heroic mechanism, he proves himself a master craftsman. Gathering up his leaning staff, he returns home; thus he avoids having to play the lute under the moon. The monk asked: [The Master continued: "If you can see it here, then you will understand. The monk said: "I do not understand. The Master said: "If you had understood, you would have been like a person who has lost their way. The monk said: "What is this place where right and wrong do not reach? "What kind of phrase is this? The Master said, "A single mass of white clouds does not reveal its ugliness.
Tiantong Jue said, "The entire body shifts and interchanges, avoiding contact with the dignified; withdrawing from one's position to extract the essential, it is appropriately evasive and indirect."
Do you see where Shao Shan was acting for him? He exerted all his strength to push his father into the inner depths. Dongshan Fu said:
"Shao Shan may truly be said to have struck down the moon of the Chu heavens and plucked away the stars of the Han lands; he casually uttered a single phrase."
The blade is sheathed and not revealed. Even when scrutinized, it has not yet been completely severed. Today, if someone asks:
"In a place where right and wrong do not reach, is there still a phrase? Answer directly: "No. Why is there none? Simply say: "The autumn waters and the vast sky are one color;
the setting clouds and the solitary wild goose fly together."
White clouds do not reach the summit of the central peak; The landscape of misty vines fills the eyes with extraordinary beauty.
A single phrase contains the melody of a thousand ages; Amidst ten thousand layers of blue-green, the moon first arrives.
(Touzi Qing) Alone facing the vast ocean, he cuts off all currents; Casually dancing his oars, he casts the golden hook. White clouds do not reveal the misty waves.
Vast and open. A single sound from the transverse flute—heaven and earth turn autumnal.
(Muan Yong) A solitary cloud reveals no blemish; the white cloud-child leans against the green mountain-father. Dewdrops fall upon the crane’s nest as the dream first returns;
a new crescent moon, like a half-hook, rises over ten thousand households. (Jide Hui)
Shaoshan asked Baizhang, "Is this not the talkative Baizhang Yin? He replied, "I dare not say so. The Master said, "How many mouths do you have?
He replied, "My whole body is it. The Master said, "Where do you usually defecate? He replied, "I defecate inside Shaoshan's mouth.
The Master said, "If there were Shaoshan's mouth, that would be fine; but what if there were no Shaoshan?"
"Where is your mouth facing as you defecate? Because [Yunmen] was speechless, the Master struck him.
Yunmen Yan said, "This talk has fallen into the hands of this fellow; I grant you thirty blows.
He also said, "I thought he was a lion cub," and further said, "Today, Shaoshan’s mountain crumbles and its ice melts away. Cui-feng Xian said, "From the beginning, I have had doubts."
Zhaozhou arrives at Shaoshan. Yufan Yu says: "Treading on grass and wounding a snake; provoking fire and burning one's own body. People like this are found everywhere.
Because Chan practitioners have too many mouths, they are driven to the point of being silenced; because Shaoshan has no mouth, he is driven to the point of being choked."
Qinghua Yan said: "Because a white-headed old man has his whole body as a mouth, he cannot bear the single excrement of Shaoshan.
Shaoshan, when asked by a monk, "What is the house style of the Master? replied: "Rootless grass on the absolute summit."
Leaves sway of their own accord without wind;
the solitary peak of the Wondrous Summit is uniquely lush. A numinous sprout born of heaven does not touch the earth; its verdant leaves sway constantly without a breeze.
What need has its fragrant scent to follow the charms of spring? (Danxia Chun)
When a monk rose from his prostrations at Shaoshan, the Master said, "A great material hidden in a humble dwelling.
The monk stepped aside and stood there. The Master said, "You have lost the timber for a ridgepole."
Chengshan Heshan said: "The first arrow is still tolerable; the second arrow pierces the person deeply.
One must know that with hands clasped in prayer, one has already crossed the ford. To advance further is only to drift and sink deeper.
If dull copper were treated as gold, it could only deceive those who have no eyes. (Danxia Chun)
In the third month, the peach-blossom waters fill the shallows; Scales of brocade vie to leap through the Yu Gate.
Unable to restrain the white waves surging to the heavens, They cause the fish to leisurely return with their foreheads marked.
(Jia-shui Qia) Chan Master Lingchao of Shanglan in Hongzhou (a successor of Jia-shan Hui) was asked by a monk: "What is the original essence of Shanglan?"

[The monk] asked about the matter of division. The Master said, "It is not borrowed from the thousand sages; how could it be sought from the ten thousand functions? [The monk] asked, "When there is neither borrowing nor seeking, what then?
The Master said, "Can you not pick it up and place it in the hands of the *śrāmaṇera*?"

A single patch of spiritual luminosity is fundamentally wondrous and perfect; within it, there is neither the orthodox nor the biased. On the auspicious grasses of Treasure Peak, there are no roots or stems;
they do not await the labor of spring, yet their colors are naturally fresh.
(Danxia Chun) When a monk asked Shanglan, "After Sudhana saw Mañjuśrī, why did he then go south? The Master said:
Learning relies upon entering the inner chamber; only then does true understanding begin to flow through. [A monk] asked, "Why did Maitreya instead send him to see Mañjuśrī?
The Master said, "The Way is vast and boundless; it is inexhaustible when encountered by people."
Tianning Qisong said: "The most extraordinary among the extraordinary, the most profound among the profound. To reach the very source and bottom of the Dharma, one must be like Shanglan;
even so, one has still not yet arrived at the gate of the Patriarchs."
The Chan Master of the Four Dhyānas in Yanzhou (a successor of Jiashan Hui) was once asked by a monk: "In the past, there was the saying, 'When invited, one does not turn back.
Now I invite the Master to enter a well; will you go or not? The Master said: "Deep within, there is no other source; those who drink shall have all their thirst extinguished."
The lineage of Caoxi flows from antiquity to the present; Consciousness alone attempts to fathom its depth.
This is the place where the ancients played at will; Though they entered the well, they never sank.
(Danxia Chun) Chan Master Hailu of Taiyuan (a successor of Jiashan Hui): Once, when someone requested that Tripitaka Master Guanding be provided with offerings, [Hailu] spread...
Having taken their seats, the Master sat upon that very seat. At that time, the Dharma Seat Master Yunshe asked, "In what year did you, Preceptor, begin your practice?
The Master said, "Seat Master, come forward. Yunshe approached. The Master said, "As for Kātyāyana, in what year did he begin his practice?
Yunshe was utterly bewildered. The Master shouted, "You bed-wetting ghost!"
Mostly learned from others; a lifetime spent vainly flapping one's mouth.
If you wish to exhaustively fathom this ground of empty luminosity, it was not included even before the Seven Buddhas.
(Danxia [Fu]) Chan Master You of Mount Tiangai in Fengxiang Prefecture (a successor of Jiashan Hui) had a monastery named Wugou Jingguang.
Someone asked, "Since it is already stainless pure light, why did you build a bathhouse? The monk was speechless.
He requested the Master to provide an answer on his behalf. The Master said, "On a night of bright moon in the third autumn month, one does not merely display its full orb."
Although the answer exhausts the profoundest meaning, how can one avoid the fact that the pivotal phrase has not yet been personally encountered?
If you wish to realize that which is fundamentally stainless, you must further enter the water to see the tall man.

(Danxia Chun) Chan Master Linggui of Sanjiao Mountain in Qizhou (who succeeded Qingping Zun). Once, a monk asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: [The text here indicates the beginning of the Master's response].
He said: "Come tomorrow and I shall tell you; I will not speak of it now.

Longing to ask about the affairs of a former dynasty, my heart is wounded. I see only the river flow on, never to return. At the close of day, the eastern wind blows and the spring grasses turn green.
The partridges fly up onto the Terrace of King Yue. (Fin Shijiang)

Chan Master Gantian of Toutingou (Toutingou was a dharma successor of the same lineage). A monk asked: "The father did not seek refuge [in you]; why then did he seek refuge in you, the son? The Master said:
"Is this not the business within another's own house? The monk asked: "Does the relationship between father and son still belong to the realm of effort?
The Master said: "It does not. The monk asked: "If it does not belong to the realm of effort, how is it so? The Master said: "Father and son each act for themselves."
Tuo asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "You and I understand each other:

the dragon returns to the vast, azure waves of the deep pool; the crane roosts in the thousand-year-old pine at the bottom of the ravine. The moon shines upon the thin mist as the autumn colors fade into infinity;
its pure light has already penetrated the jade curtains and windows. (Pingxiang)
While Touzi was wandering the mountains, he saw a cicada shell. An attendant asked, "The shell is here; where has the cicada gone?
The Master took the cicada shell, placed it by the attendant's ear, and made the sound of a cicada. The attendant attained realization.
Light and thin like the shell of a cold cicada, withered and dry like the form of a fallen leaf. Picked up and brought to the side of the ear, it chirps two or three times in succession.
(Nantang Jing) Clearly, one’s feet tread upon the five Sumeru mountains; who would believe such a claim of supernatural power? It is truly not as good as that cicada shell.
A single cry awakens the child who wets his bed.
(Yishan De) Chan Master Weizhen of Niu-tou, Fuzhou (a fellow successor of Touzi). A monk asked, "What is the master’s family style?

"How is it? The Master said, "If you will eat, let you eat; if you will not eat, go as you please.
Yingshan Yun said, "With a heart and liver cast of raw iron, one can strike until they ring with a sharp clang."
