Chan Master Tong’an Pí of Fēngqī Mountain in Hóngzhōu (successor of Yúnjū Yìng), the seventh generation descendant of Dàjiàn. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "The golden rooster carries its chicks back to the Milky Way; the jade hare conceives her fetus within the Purple Microcosm. The monk asked again.
"If a guest were to arrive suddenly, how would you receive them? The Master said, "The golden fruit was plucked by the monkey this morning;
the jade flower was carried back by the phoenix this evening.
Guangfu Qin said, "Guangfu does not do it this way. If someone asks, 'What is the master’s house style? I would tell him:"

Singing "kuan-nai" amidst the clusters of emerald bamboos; Lying in the depths of blue cliffs within the misty vines. Suddenly encountering a guest, how shall one receive them? An unfathomable basket holds the bright moon;
A mindless bowl stores the pure breeze. Jingshan Guangzhen said: "The family style of the same household is indeed strange.
However, Jingshan does not think so. If someone asks, 'How is it? [I would say: The white clouds are not yet dispersed; The green mountains remain as they were."
This is the family style of the Upādhyāya. He simply says: "At the time of the midday meal, there is but a single bowl of rice mixed with curd;

as for the right or wrong of the Way of Chan, he knows nothing of it. When a guest arrives, what will he use to receive them? Steamed buns and noodles. Tianning Qi said: "Moving between the 'Correct' and the 'Biased' without striking a sharp edge;
in the free and easy flow of question and answer, one only clarifies the noble dignity. The Old Man of Tong’an was well-versed in attaining this."
It is convenient. Someone might ask, "What is the house style of the Master? To which he replies, "The alms bowl is full of steamed rice.
"How do you receive guests? "A cup of tea after the meal. Tiantong Muan said, "Tongan is remarkably extraordinary."
The wondrous joy is of a single flavor and ordinary; the家风 (family style) of the ancestors is simply just this. The school of Bodhidharma has been swept away to its very foundations.
Now, if someone asks, "What is the family style of the Master? [the answer is: "Grind thoroughly three thousand grains of castor bean."
Having cast away the five flavors of Chan from all quarters, what is it when a guest arrives? One must change the bones, wash the entrails, and reorganize;
even with eyes and hands functioning throughout the body, one must still practice further. Zimei Zhou said:
"The family style of the same house is exceedingly wealthy and noble, yet it utterly lacks the flavor of a monk. Here, it is not so. Suppose someone were to ask: 'What is the Master’s house style?'"
Feng: "Only facing the Dao, with lush, tall pines spreading their emerald canopies and dense, tall bamboos forming a green wall.
When suddenly a guest arrives, how shall you receive them? At mealtime, cook wild oats; in the afternoon, serve coarse tea. Fengshan Qi said:
"The founding ancestor of Tong’an was as wealthy as Jin Gu and as generous as Meng Chang. Although he may have been showing off his ancestral estate,"
This is merely wind; it cannot avoid wasting the monastery's permanent assets. Should someone ask about the "house style" of Miaoye, tell them:
"I plow through a thousand acres of clouds in the azure void; I enjoy the moon over the green mountains with a single ladle. When guests arrive, with what will you entertain them?
There is only the family meal; there is truly no fragrance of the five flavors.
At midday, smoke gathers as the mountains loom; at the end of night, the sky is pale and the moon is full. In this state of unified, silent illumination, the cold night is long;
luminosity and darkness are perfectly integrated before any sign has arisen.
(Danxia Chun) A sheet of silk is like falling snow, upon which two carp have been formed. If you wish to know what is in my heart, look at the writing within my belly.
(Bafang Xian) Before the white jade steps, the golden phoenix dances; atop the golden hall, the jade rooster crows.
Coming from the center and arriving through the simultaneous—last night the snow was deep and the moon was bright. (Xueyan Qin)
Ancient temple, smoke enshrouds the highest peak; Deep in the night, who is there striking the golden bell? Each sound resonates beyond the *Vaiśvānara* eon;
The stone maiden returns as the moon stands at its zenith. (Wei Cen Yin) The purple curtains hang in the Yellow Hall, the atmosphere extraordinary;
The violet silk canopy is complete with the full family style. Splitting the sandalwood—each fragment is [perfumed].
Incense. Shattered jade and jingling gems; in every speck of dust there is jade. Secretly threading the jade needle, layers upon layers of brocade;
densely packed with golden needles, clusters upon clusters of flowers. Embroidered mandarin ducks fly everywhere; the golden rooster pecks through the lapis lazuli cave.
(By Hansong Cao) The jade gates are deep and silent, with few arrivals or departures; along the imperial street, one sees much green moss creeping in. Though spring light remains before the eaves...
Mèi. Inside the room, there was not the slightest sound of string or wind instruments.
While Huāiqīnghǎi was reading the scriptures at Tóng'ān, he saw a monk come to pay his respects. He then covered his head with the sleeve of his robe.
The monk stepped forward and made a gesture of offering condolences. The Master lowered the sleeve, picked up the scripture, and said, "Do you understand? The monk then took the robe...
He covered his head with his sleeves. The Master said, "Alas! Alas!
Baoshou then remarked, "These two fellows are like veteran generals from renowned clans encountering the descendants of Sun Wuzi;
naturally their maneuvers and withdrawals are worth observing, and their exchanges are precise. Nevertheless, they will only bring laughter upon the guests at the Fishing Terrace."

There was a monk from Tong’an who asked: "To interpret the meaning based on the scriptures is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three periods; to deviate from a single word of the scriptures is to preach like a demon.
What is the principle behind this? The Master said: "A solitary peak rises in remote beauty, unclad by misty vines; a sliver of moon moves across the sky."
The empty sky and clouds are inherently distinct;
the clouds fly high on their own while the waters flow of their own accord. The sea and sky are vast and wide, cradling a solitary boat.
At nightfall, one does not seek lodging in the reed coves, but transcends both the middle and the two ends. (Danxia Chun)
Riding the inspiration of the moment, I come forward in a small boat; drifting east and west, it touches neither bank as the waters flow on.
Behold the moon above the Twelve Bridges—mountain colors and lake light are most profound at night.
(Qingyun Qi) Fallen flowers and flowing water are both heartless; they escort the eastern wind past the city of Luo. A single cry of "kuang-er" rises from the misty peaks.
[The Master] said: "Outside, the wind and light are monopolized; who can compete with them?
(The character for "moon" [月] and the character for "screen" [厂] form the character for "screen" [屛]). Tong’an asked a newly arrived monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Hunan.

The Master said, "Do you know the wind and clouds here at Tong’an that embody the Way, like the floral balustrades of the celestial sphere? He replied, "I know. The Master said, "This is not your realm."

The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "A short-term peddler of firewood merely boasts of his books and sword. As the monk prepared to offer further words, the Master said, "Before the sword and armor are deployed, the thief's true self has already been revealed."
Bai Zhang Le said: "This monk only knows how to hurry along his journey, unaware that he has taken the wrong road.
Tong’an was skilled at responding to the occasion, yet he wasted so much effort in such roundabout ways. Bai Zhang was not like this:

when asked where he had come from, and the monk replied, 'From Hunan,' [Bai Zhang] immediately said, 'Before the sword and armor were even deployed, the thief’s true form was already revealed. This not only allowed the monk to rejoice in his life's realization, but also spared him [further trouble]."
Causing all people’s speech to falter:
Autumn winds enter the sleeves, bones and hair shiver with cold. The gardens and groves are withered and thin, hard to bear looking upon. Already the melancholy mood is tenfold more desolate;
Unable to endure the wind and rain, they are further ravaged. (By Buryan Pu)
Travelers at Nantang find the autumn air fresh and clear; Deep in the night, the wind does not stir over the green duckweed. The lotus flowers, heavy with dew, seem to sleep;
As the moon rises slantwise, the cries of mandarin ducks begin to stir. (Iron Sail Boat) Ascending the hall at the time of his passing in Tong’an:
Before the Many Sons Pagoda, the lineage sons are brilliant; Before the Five Elders Peak, matters are as [if they were]...
"What? After he had raised this three times, no one in the assembly responded. Tong Anzhi stepped forward and said, "The night is bright; outside the curtains, they stand in formation.
Ten thousand miles of songs and chants proclaim a time of Great Peace. The Master said, "One must be such a donkey-man before it can be attained."
Baiyan Fu said: "In the past, when I was at Tong'an, I entrusted the bowl-bag to someone who was not an ordinary person;
even at the very end, I remained most earnest about it. My urgency in seeking a worthy successor has reached its peak.

When Old Zhi responded in this manner, although he did not fail to uphold the essential tenets of the school, I do not yet know whether he truly captured his [Baiyan’s] intention or not. If he had not captured his intention, then...

Furthermore, it is said that this must be a donkey-like fellow who can achieve it. Even if one were to exactly accord with his intent, how could one prevent the fact that thirty generations hence there will be one who refuses to comply?
An old man yearning for his son leans against the Azure Tower; amidst the layers of misty trees, sorrow fills the gaze. When someone comes to meet him, he receives news of safety.
Xin: Hurriedly, he pulls the pearl curtain up onto its hook.
(Tian Duo Si) Who can succeed to the family legacy and carry on the loom and fur? At the end of his life, there is a profound reason for casting down the fishing rod.
Where the bright and the dark meet in mutual resonance, the imperial splendor shall yet flourish for a thousand autumns. (Bai Yan Fu)
Chan Master Huaiyun of Guizong on Mount Lu (a successor of Yunju Deng) was once asked by a monk: "What is it like when the water is cut off and the wheel is stopped?
The Master said: "The millstone does not turn."
Cutting off the water, the wheel stops; the talk is already complete. Borrowing a mother-in-law’s robe to bow for her birthday.
Later generations did not see Old Guizong; they often speculate on the two sides of the stone.
(Foyin Yuan) Performing a somersault atop a thousand-fathom pole, casting a fishing hook into the heart of the great ocean waves. In the end, it returns to his very flesh and bone.
Excellent! Without applying rouge or powder, he is already elegant and refined.
(Nanhua Bing) The great function, sweeping across like a flash of lightning— Even the Śakra-locana eye is still stuck with glue.
On the path of delusion, they scramble for words in their dreams; I recall following him along once more. (Meng’an Xin)
Chan Master Zhang of Mount Xi at Chizhou (a successor of Yunju Ying) was serving as a wood-gatherer under Touzi.
One day, while attending Touzi during tea, Touzi held up his teacup and said, "The myriad phenomena of the universe are all contained within this.
The Master then splashed the tea away and said, "Where are the myriad phenomena of the universe? Touzi remarked, "What a pity!"
"A bowl of tea.
Mingzhao Qian said: "Before Jingshan had even poured the tea, what words should have been spoken to avoid him saying, 'What a pity—that bowl of tea'?"
Chan Master Nihon Kū of Hangzhou (a successor of Yungju Ying) visited Jia Shan.
As soon as he reached the steps before the abbot’s quarters, Jia Shan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Yunju. Jia Shan asked, "Where are you right now?"
The Master said, "I am on the peak of Jia-shan, atop the [Ning*Yi]. The Master asked, "The old monk’s year is in Kan; the Five Ghosts are upon my person.

As the Master was about to ascend the steps, Jia-shan said, "From which of the three jeweled stairways do you ascend? The Master said, "The three jeweled stairways are for the sake of the present age;
as for the single path that goes beyond, I ask the Master to point it out directly. Jia-shan then made a bow, and the Master ascended.
As they were ascending the steps to pay their respects, the Mountain Master asked, "With whom did you travel, Ācārya? The Master replied, "With Old Man Wood.
The Mountain Master said, "Why do you not come to visit this old monk? The Master replied, "The Teacher has his own share of seeing him. The Mountain Master asked, "Where is he?"
The Master said, "It is in the hall. Deshan then accompanied the Master down to the hall. The Master then took up his staff and threw it before Deshan's face.
Deshan asked, "Was it obtained from Mount Tiantai? The Master replied, "It was not born of the Five Peaks."
[Daowei] asked, "Can it not be obtained from Mount Sumeru? The Master said, "It is not encountered even in the Moon Palace.
[Daowei] said, "If that is so, then can it be obtained from others? The Master said, "Even one's own self is already an enemy; what could be made of obtaining it from others?
Daowei said, "A single bean might burst within cold ashes."
Baoshou said, "Master Ben’s one response and one reply have great significance; he truly does not fail as the legitimate son of Yunju.
When pressed with such scrutiny, it is not that his words were split into two parts. At that time, had he been asked where Old Man Mu was, why did he not say, 'I have just arrived and am weary;

When an ordinary person asks, he answers as an ordinary person; when a sage asks, he answers as a sage. [A monk] asked, "What is the 'absence of the grandmotherly heart' after twenty years?
The Master said, "When an ordinary person asks, I do not answer as an ordinary person; when a sage asks, I do not answer as a sage."
Tiantong Jie said: "If Wugu had seen [the monk] at that time, he would have simply let out two cold laughs.
Had this old fellow been enlightened, he naturally would not have fallen into the conceptual trap of 'saint' or 'ordinary person. Baon'en Xiu said:

"Jinpeak may indeed be said to have obtained the upper-grade tongs and does not fall into the nests of contemporary people. Nevertheless, when scrutinized, even so, it is merely falling down by oneself and getting up by oneself."
Shouchang Hao said: "The old fellow Jinfeng was so dense and compact that not even a drop of water could pass through;
yet when he was lax and stubborn, he followed the heterodox and pursued evil. This monk, greedy for the fragrant bait, cannot avoid falling into the nest of the holy and the ordinary.
For hundreds of kalpas and thousands of lifetimes, there will be no way out. Today, Xingguo levels the high and follows the low, buying a hat to fit the head—do not say otherwise."
"It would be better for me, this mountain monk, to speak to you of 'Old Lady Chan,'" he said, and gave a shout. Shiguzi remarked:
"Although Jinfeng possesses the skill to shift the key and change the tune, he still lacks the strategic maneuver to point out flaws and snatch back the jade;
in the end, he cannot avoid leaving things split into two pieces. Here in my own tradition, it is not so: twenty years ago, I had the heart of an old woman. [He] was hungry.
Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty. After twenty years, there is no more "old woman’s heart" (pedantic affectation); one simply eats when hungry and drinks when thirsty.
Once, when a monk asked Jingu Peak, "What is it like when the four seas are at peace? the Master said, "He is still just a man standing on the steps."
The dust and smoke of the four seas have already settled; the bright moon before the window shines cold upon people. No great merit has been granted as a reward for the General;
the precious horse and golden spear are suddenly too dull to behold.

(Danxia Chun) Guests from beyond the transformed realm may rest in peace; the General does not prize the jeweled flower crown. When his task is accomplished, he withdraws from office, leaving nothing behind.
Power! Turning my head toward the world of dust, my hair stands on end and my bones shiver.
(Companion and fellow. Jingu Peak asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from the Eastern Land.
The Master said, "How did you pass through Jingu Peak’s barrier? He replied, "My credentials are clear. The Master said, "Let me see them presented to Jingu Peak. The monk extended both hands.
The Master said, "The Jinfeng Pass has never been crossed by anyone. Yangshan asked, "Can you, Reverend, cross it?
The Master replied, "A Persian eating black pepper.
Yangshan Qian remarked, "To cross the pass, one must have the eye that penetrates the pass; to guard the pass, one must be the person who holds the pass."—Jinfeng.
Unaware of my drowsiness, I was jostled by that monk. Nevertheless, along this vast imperial highway, travelers have never been barred from passing day or night.
While Jinfeng was eating cakes in the Sangha Hall, he picked up a single cake himself and passed it around once from the head of the platform.
When the assembly saw this, they all simultaneously joined their palms. The Master said, "Even if you were to rise with tenfold effort, you would still only have attained half.
Later in the evening, a monk requested instruction, saying, "Today, while distributing the cakes, the Master said one could only attain half. Please [explain this]."
The Master said, "The Abbot has the full Way. He made a gesture of picking up a cake and asked again, "Do you understand? [The monk] said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "Even Jinfeng only attained half of it."
Jinpeng’s honey-cake allows only half; if you want the whole thing, look again in five days.
(Fang’an Xian) Once, when a monk was taking his leave, Master Jinpeng asked, “Where will you go? The monk replied, “I dare not arbitrarily transmit any news.
The Master said, “If you reach other places, take care not to speak of Jinpeng’s way of guiding others. The monk replied, “I have already received your honorable instructions. The Master—
[The Master] said, "Suppose someone were to ask you right now—how would you respond? The monk lifted the corner of his *kāṣāya*. The Master said, "Your agility is inferior to that of the *śrāmaṇera*.
Juyin Xuan remarked, "Great indeed is Jinfeng’s skill in bringing people to their wits' end; yet, upon closer inspection, he was instead..."
This causes the assembly to be confused and distracted. Here in this mountain monastery, matters do not follow a single fixed direction.

For these past ninety days, I have walked and sat together with you all. Now, as the situation leaves me no choice, I shall allow a thread of opportunity to let us discuss the Buddha-dharma for a moment.
Yet, alas, it is not the right time. Nevertheless, tell me: does the mountain monk still [possess it]?
"Is there anyone present?
asked Master Huixia of Caoshan in Fuzhou (a successor of Caoshan Ji). A monk asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world?"
The Master said, "Caoshan is not as good. [The monk] asked, "How is it after he has appeared in the world? The Master said, "He is still not as good as Caoshan.
Wuzu Yan said, "If one observes this from the perspective of worldly truth, Caoshan deserves twenty blows of the staff.
If one observes this from the perspective of the ancestral Way, Baiyun deserves twenty blows of the staff. Nevertheless, there are eyes at the tip of the staff; both men [are struck]."
Among them, one person fully accepted it, while another did not accept it at all. If you can discern this, I grant that you possess half an eye.
Tiantong Juo said: "The Buddha and Caoshan exchange roles as host and guest; whether appearing in the world or not appearing in the world, each possesses a single eye.
There has never been constant movement without stillness, nor has there ever been constant stillness without movement. Do you understand?"
"Ma! How could the profound cavern be constrained by locks and bolts? Transverse and vertical, it does not involve the dualistic mechanism.
Baoren Xiu said: "Caoshan was not as good; he went himself with a flask to buy village wine. It was not as good as Caoshan; he put on his robe and came back to act as host.
Where Tiantong takes up [the case], there is no obstruction. Wansong’s commentary tears it open; how could it hinder its being pressed together? Buddha and...
Caoshan’s master and guest are in harmonious union. Whether appearing in the world or not appearing in the world, his two eyes are perfectly clear and bright.
All day long he is on the road yet never leaves home; all day long he is at home yet never leaves the road. Do you understand? Clouds arise from the mouth of the cave and return to the cave;
dense and secret, they cannot be cut open even by a golden blade. Tianning Qi said: "How great and small is Caoshan’s mouth!"
Sweetheart’s bitterness. If someone were to ask Shoushan, “How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? [Shoushan would say] “Good. “And how was it after he appeared in the world?

[He would say] “Good. He gives him two “Goods”; listen for a lifetime and investigate. Shaokang Hao said: “The perfect harmony of the Correct and the Deviant belongs to the original master of our school.
To clarify the mechanism within, one must have a standard in the moment of encounter. If there is a question,” [he continued,] “...[the response follows].”
The Mountain Monk said: "When the Buddha had not yet appeared in the world, how was it? Water was sufficient and grass was sufficient. After he appeared in the world, how was it?

One was plowing with the plow and dragging the harrow. Why is this so? When the clouds disperse, every house has the moon; when spring comes, flowers bloom everywhere. Falin Yin said: "Shifting function to accord with the position, shifting the position to accord with function;
tearing asunder and squeezing together; the integration of the Correct, the Deviant, and the Perfect. This is the lineage of Caoshan, Tiantong, and Baofeng."
Each of the three great patriarchs had their own particular strengths. Faling provided yet another path. How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world?

You have already seen through this. How was it after he appeared in the world? You have already seen through this. Nevertheless, do not let your idle scholarly interpretations bury the pivotal mechanisms of the masters and ancestors.
The sun hides behind the green mountains as auspicious vapors rise high. The phoenix dwells within the *wú* tree, looking about in boredom.
Without cause, a stone horse passes through the depths of the pool; it startles the mud-dragon, who overturns the ocean tide.

(Touzi Qing) The ancient trees and sacred nests leave the crane’s dream lost in confusion. A white elephant from Mount Kunlun returns riding backward. The water swells like fish scales, and the boat lies across.
The bank. A whirlwind arises and flowers fall upon the path. (Zantang Shen) Caoshan is not as good;
the flower’s root is originally brilliant. He is not as good as Caoshan: the tiger’s body is inherently striped. The climate in Jiangnan is warm.
In the north, the spring chill lingers. A single tangle of willow filaments cannot be gathered; they are draped with mist upon the jade balustrade. (Shi’an Shao) Caoshan is not as good:
he is neither horse nor donkey. Not as good as Caoshan: the tiger does not eat its own stripes. When the dragon roars, the mist rises.

When the tiger roars, the wind grows cold. To those of penetrating insight, it is seen at a single glance; for those of middling or inferior capacity, there are a thousand mountains and ten thousand peaks.
To cure illness, one need not rely on medicine carried by a donkey; to prolong life, what use is the "Nine-Return Elixir"?

(By Xianan Chou) A subtle aura of purity lingers amidst the chill of the Purple Microcosm. Gazing upward, one feels as if the spirit itself were about to vanish. Alas, the colored clouds drift on ever further.
Miao! Deep in the night, I lean alone against the jade balustrade. (A seal-mark in the center:
Ten thousand loads of mist and clouds are enjoyed as a marvel; my two brows hang daily over the hall of the forehead.
Thinking of those who toil on the roadways, how can they compare to planting purple *zhī* fungi in the deep mountains? (Pointing directly south:)
Silver basins filled with snow—their colors are indistinguishable; reeds conceal egrets—their kind cannot be discerned.
Pair after pair of jade-like roosters crow at midnight, together spying upon the purple qi that locks the vermilion courtyard.
(Rulun Zheng) A needle cannot pierce it; an axe cannot split it. The body is a target for arrows; the mouth is the source of calamity. Drunken Caoshan.
Not yet sober from his intoxication, he traveled to Mount Nanyue in the morning and Mount Tiantai in the evening.

(From the *Juyin Xuan*) Once, while a monk was standing in attendance, Caoshan said, "The Way is truly scorching hot. The monk replied, "It is. Caoshan asked, "As for this heat, where would you go to avoid it?
The monk replied, "I would go into the midst of the boiling cauldrons and the burning coals to avoid it. Caoshan said, "But as for that..."
"How do you avoid the boiling cauldrons and the burning coals? He replied, "The manifold sufferings cannot reach him.
Zhaojue Qin said, "Turning the mechanism and shifting the position is indeed a way that penetrates all quarters; it is like a lotus flower in midwinter.
Even so, to cut through nails and sever iron, there is yet another path. If someone were to ask this mountain monk: 'How do you face such heat?'"
"Where do you avoid it? He replied to him: "In the cauldrons and the burning coals.
"How do you avoid it in the cauldrons and the burning coals? He said: "By being burned to death. Now tell me, is there still a way for him to benefit others?
Zifu Lu said: "He provides an intimate grasp; it is perfectly integrated and sovereign—this belongs to Caoshan. Nevertheless, when examined closely,"
There is still a path for the mind to follow. Here, it is not so. If someone asks, "How does one avoid [the suffering] within the cauldrons and the furnace coals?
I tell them: "I know you do not have the faith to believe. Dongshan Du said: "As for the suffering within the cauldrons and the furnace coals, it is beyond description.
Why, then, do you say that 'none of the various sufferings can reach it'? Do you yet understand where the ancients were headed?"

There is none. If one knows that when it is cold, the entire heaven and earth are cold, and when it is hot, the entire heaven and earth are hot—if you can understand it here, you must further know there is a "transcendental keyhole" above this.
If this is not yet the case, you will only know that phenomena pass before your eyes.
Unaware that old age creeps upon one from the head;

a fragment of jade from Kunlun remains moist within the fire. A solitary moon in the azure void is a perfect circle at the bottom of the water. With a single thought, all is serene and free of differentiation;
let the blue seas change into mulberry fields as they may. (Danxia Chun)
Multitudes of sufferings cannot reach it; it is a magnificent realm existing in its own right. All the splendor of wind and light has been purchased at once, without spending a single coin.
(Kuchan’s Mirror) At Tianhua Temple on Lake Hegua, every window and balcony opens facing the water. It is not that they close their doors to ward off the mundane.
Guest: "How many people are there who can truly enjoy their leisure?
(Tianmu Li) "Blinding the three eyes at the crown of the head, they stroll freely amidst boiling cauldrons and glowing coals.
If one says that the various sufferings cannot reach them, where indeed could such a place ever exist? (Shaoshi Mu)
Ten-thousand-fathom crimson cliffs press against the heavens; jagged, wondrous rocks lock in clouds and mist.
Who can be known as one who has forgotten artifice? Casting off all reliance, one attains spontaneity.
(Pointing directly to the south) When a monk asked Caoshan, "What is it like when the four mountains press in from all sides? the Master said, "Caoshan is right in the midst of them."
The monk asked, "Is there still a way to seek it out? The Master said, "If you are already within it, then you must seek it out.
Yingshan Yin said: "Old Cao Shan was so thoroughly pressed by this monk that he stood there and wet himself.
Baiyan Fu said: "To answer in such a manner is very much like contradicting oneself. If I were Cao Shan, I would wait for him to say 'Is there still a way to seek it out?'"
Seeking emergence, there is none; not seeking emergence, why not seek emergence? Yet it is said that he has long been accustomed to its enjoyment.
Chan Master Xuanwu Guanghui of Heshan in Fuzhou (a successor of Caoshan Ji). A monk asked: "What is the West?"
The Master said: "If you do not prostrate, when will you wait for [the right moment]?
The empty hall is silent and the night is cold; carrying a jade lute, one plays it under the moon. If it is not a true connoisseur, it is in vain to lean the ear;
how could the mournful wind and flowing water have anything to do with it? (Danxia Chun)
Chan Master Hongtong of Mount Yuwang in Changning County, Hengzhou (a successor of Caoshan Ji). A monk asked, "What is the patriarchal style of the Master?
The Master said, "My entire body is not worth five copper coins. The monk said, "How utterly poor and destitute you are!"
The Master said, "In ancient times it was thus. [The student] asked, "How did they provide for it? The Master said, "According to the family’s abundance or frugality.
For generations, our family tradition has not cost a single coin; within pure poverty, we are even more poor. We wear clothes and eat food according to what is available;
in every thing and every matter, we use that which is most intimate. (Danxia Chun)
A monk asked Zen Master Xichan of Shuzhou (who was a successor of Caoshan Benji): "What is the state beyond thought and deliberation? The Master said:
"Who has seen the void nod its head at night?"
A single point of luminous clarity is beyond the six gates of perception; it is manifest—what need is there to fix one’s gaze upon it further?
Within this, the message is difficult for people to entrust themselves to; only the empty void nods its head in secret.
(Danxia Chun, *Zongjian Faling*, Vol. 66)
*Zongjian fali*, Scroll Sixty-Seven,
Compiled by Jiyun Tang; The Seventh Generation Descending from Dajian (Huineng).
Chan Master Shoucheng Jingguo of Huguo Monastery in Suizhou (a dharma heir of Shushan Ren) was once at Baoci Monastery in Hunan with Master Huanhua.
While Master Ci was ascending the hall, Huanhua stepped forward and asked, "What is the true suchness of buddha-nature? Master Ci replied, "Who does not have it?
Huanhua did not find resonance with this answer, so he subsequently requested further instruction from Master [Shoucheng]. The Master said, "Who has it? At these words, Huanhua attained realization.
Awakened! Who lacks it? Who possesses it? Within the phrase, there is the mystery. Smashing through the heavy barriers, the Way is manifest.
If you were Ziqi listening to the playing of the lute, would you ever mistake the resonance of the pines for the chirping of autumn cicadas? (Da Hong Sui)
Three in the morning and four in the evening—how little! Four in the evening and three in the morning—how much!
One cannot discern the measure of such quantities; from this, the confusion between existence and non-existence arises. To avoid such confusion: Oṃ suru siri svāhā. (Fóxìng Tàiyīn)
Who lacks it? Who possesses it? This is the Way of the total mechanism (*qianji*). Turning the body beneath a word, one does not remain stuck.
Even if one has not yet awakened, one has already set out on the path; this is to mistake a winnowing basket for an ironing board. A-he-he!
If a person can understand how to ride a donkey backward, they will not spend a lifetime following behind others. (Xiuyan Rui)
When a monk asked National Protector (Huguo), "What is the original mind? the Master said: "The rhinoceros develops patterns on its horn from gazing at the moon;
the elephant has flowers enter its tusks because it was struck by thunder."

A three-legged numinous tortoise scampers along the desolate path; a branch of auspicious grass hangs down amidst the chaotic peaks. Mount Kunlun contains the Jade Mountain, its luster smooth and bright;
the cool hare conceives her fetus, yet the moon knows it not.
(Danxia Chun) Regarding the question asked by a monk, "What is the mark of the Brahma-voice? Master Huguo replied, "A donkey brays in Hebei. "In Henan... [The text ends here.]
The dog barks;

Maudgalyāyana sought the Buddha’s Brahma-like voice, yet though he exhausted his supernatural powers, he could not see its limit. Who can awaken to the braying of the donkey and the barking of the dog?
The perfect sound, vast and clear, is revealed to humans and devas. (Dahong Su)
Huiguo was asked by a monk, "What is one's original father and mother? The Master said, "One whose head does not turn white.
The monk asked, "With what shall I make an offering? The Master said, "Diligently serving rice-less gruel; before the hall, do not inquire after kin."
Stepping out the gate, the entire world lacks a true friend; Entering the door, what fills the eyes is no kinsman. In this empty hall on a cold night, what else is there?
Only the bright moon in the azure sky serves as a neighbor. (Danxia Chun) Silent within the inner chambers, her face is not revealed;
Years have passed without a single hair turning white. With diligent care, she uses only the rising clouds [to tend the fire].
Rice. A stone woman brought it forth, yet he did not accept the meal. (This refers to Sīlánróng.
When a monk asked Hùguó, "What is it like when a crane stands upon a withered pine?

the Master said, "The one beneath the ground has a great deal of embarrassment. [The monk asked,] "During the Huìchāng persecution, where did the Dharma-protecting benevolent spirits go? The Master said:
Two fellows before the mountain gate are utterly ridiculous. A monk asked, "What is it like when a drop of water freezes?
The Master said, "After the sun has risen, they are utterly ridiculous."
Boshan Lai said: "The three *samvara* of Huguo are a seamless whole; even a man with iron eyes and copper pupils could not analyze them apart.
Only those of the same path know this. Who, then, is of the same path?"
Even if you were to know it, it would all be nothing but a display of arrogance. Standing alone like a crane upon a solitary pine, there is no one who can equal such a being.
How could this compare to geese and ducks that dally with flocks of chickens? Having transformed and departed from Liao Yang, there is no trace left behind;
the spiritual tree stands remote and desolate, for the phoenix does not alight there. (Da Hong’s third verse.)

The Dharma-protecting deity before the ancient temple suffered bitterly at the nose during the Huichang suppression; when the time came, heaven and earth exerted their power together, and in the end, the Way was restored to its rightful lord.
Ice forms and drips of water appear; how pure and lofty this matter is! Yet when the sun rises in the east, it is no longer firm. How could mountain streams and ravines keep it?
In the end, it returns to the great ocean to become waves and surges.
Majestic and formidable is his ambition, his hair not yet white with age. A man need not fear failing to attain a marquisate;
rather, he should reflect on the guest who passed down purity and integrity, who washed his ears at the stream’s head and would not drink from the ox’s trough.
(Tiantong Jue) On the day Master Tao renounced office, he lay looking up within his thatched cottage. Who could trade five *dǔ* of rice for the breeze of the north window?
(Cherry Blossom in an Iron Vessel;
Xuan) Zen Master Hui of Huangbo Mountain in Ruizhou (Heir to Shushan Ren). He asked Shushan, "What is it like when one departs in a single kṣaṇa?
Shushan said, "It fills and obstructs empty space. How will you go? The Master said, "It fills and obstructs empty space. It does not...
If one does not depart, the mountain simply ceases to exist and fills all of empty space; it is better not to go, for the limits of past and future are severed and there is no dwelling even now.
Riding backward atop the Buddha Hall, he exits through the mountain gate, then takes that very gate and hangs it upon the pillar. (Lan’an Xu)
Chan Master Guangdeyi of Wancu Mountain in Xiangzhou (a successor of Qinglin Qian). A monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body?
The Master said, "Lacking the strength to ascend mountains or wade through waters; in a thatched door, no one knows the melody."

The essence is wondrous and the profound is explored; one has traversed the entire journey. How can this compare to the extraordinary life of the country elder? Having forgotten effort in daily use, his mind is level and secure;
he avoids serving a sovereign and is thus spared the shock of favor or disgrace.

(Danxia Chun) He does not love the towers of song and wine in Chang’an, but follows only the leisurely joy found in the rustic cottage. When the wind is clear and the moon is bright, his idleness reaches its end.
Day after day, doing nothing but acting like a foolish deer—this is my lot.

(Jiāshuǐ Qiá) I am too lazy to shoulder the anxieties of heaven and earth; it is better to follow my circumstances and ascend to Mount Yingzhou. With the clear breeze and bright moon, there are three people;
amidst the fragrant grass and slanting sun, there is but a mound of earth. Whether dreams are short or long, they are all but dreams; whether sorrow comes or goes, it is all the same.
It brings about sorrow. Who can one rely upon to voice these endless matters of the heart? Before one's eyes, yellow chrysanthemums reveal a different autumn.
(Tie-rong Xuan) Chan Master Xianyun of Shimen Temple in Xiangzhou (heir to Qinglin Qian). A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Riding alone on a thousand-li elephant beyond the mundane world; striking a golden bell beneath ten-thousand-year-old pines."
The moon is dim and hazy outside the night-bright curtains; Riding an elephant, he turns about and strikes the precious bell.
Its vast resonance ascends beyond the three realms; Why does the deaf man still sleep so soundly?
(Danxia Chun) Chan Master Zangyu Kuanghua of Baoci in Tanzhou (a successor of Longya Dun). A monk asked: "When emotion arises, wisdom is obstructed; when thought..."
The variations [in expression] differ. [A monk asked: "When feeling has not yet arisen, what is it like? The Master said, "Separated.
[The monk] asked, "When feeling has not yet arisen, what is it that separates? The Master said, "This lad has not yet met the right person."
Langye Jue said, "Baoci may indeed enter the mud and the water, but according to the gate of the patch-robed monks, he is far, far removed.
Huanglong Xin said, "This is also a case of minor compassion imitating great compassion. This monk is likewise a victim;
he is like a young fisherman who has not yet met the right person. Nowadays, people often interpret this as being about right and wrong, rather than interpreting it as being beyond right and wrong."
"How is this principle? After a long silence, he said: "In the heavens, all stars bow toward the North; among men, no water does not flow toward the East. Kaifu Ning said:
"Baoci has severed the life-vein of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; letting go and gathering back, neither ordinary beings nor sages can fathom it.
Dongchan Guan said: "At the beginning, Baoci opened his eastern pavilion wide; in the end, he used only coarse [teachings]."
Teabowls were prepared for the ceremony. Lianwen asked: "Baoci could truly be said to walk upon icebergs and run upon the edge of a sword;
how can one blame this monk for being a thousand miles away even when face-to-face?"
When the insentient is still separated [from the sentient], how can one pass through? Between a single hair and a strand of silk, the paths are ten thousandfold.
A pity for those who run empty-handed at both ends; they cannot see the fundamental source directly beneath them.
(Baiyun Cuan) Separation: In a cloudless blue sky, thunder crashes. Among the monks of the monasteries, as numerous as rice and hemp, how many are true immortals? Who knows?

The *dàkè* (a type of boat), the ships of Jiangnan, and the junks of Hainan—those who grip the helm and hoist the sails must know the rhythm; following the waves and drifting with the currents, when will it ever cease?
"Letting go, one arrives home with hair already white. (Dahong Sui) "Separated.
"The Indian monk has his ears pierced and his eyes are black. To the west of Dongyuan is Zhaozhou;
in Guanyinyuan, Maitreya is enshrined. (Shi’an Shao)
Chang’e skillfully plays the sheng flute within the moon; The resonance pierces the clear heavens, startling all who see and hear.
Pushing open the jade door, she accidentally loses her footing; Her entire body falls amidst ten thousand layers of clouds.
(Xianan sees: The red flames of peach blossoms dazzle both eyes; In the wind-high painted pavilion, the moon serves as a lamp. Having awakened from sleep, one simply gazes at the mountain colors.
"Excellent! Who would have known that the essence of spring resided in such rugged crags?
(Hyon-am Park) A beauty of eighteen years wanders upon the road; Encountering people on the narrow path, she has no way to avoid them.
She covers her face with a red silk fan, Yet her helpless, coy shyness only makes her all the more charming. (Hyo-am Yook)
Barrier. Striking is not as good as frightening. Human life is empty; wealth is real. (The Parable of the Pass of Han Guan).
In his eulogy for Longya’s portrait, Baozi said: "The sun rises over the connected mountains; the moon is full before the door. It is not that he has no body."
"I do not wish to reveal myself entirely. One day, while Longya was sitting inside his tent, a monk asked, "It is not that you have no body;
you simply do not wish to reveal yourself entirely. I ask the Master to reveal yourself completely. Longya pulled back the flap of the tent and said, "Do you see?
The monk replied, "I do not see. Longya said, "You did not bring your eyes. Later, when the Master heard of this, he remarked, "That old fellow Longya only managed to say half of it."
Yunmen Wenyan instructed a monk to raise [the case], saying, "I will not fail to tell you. When the monk had finished raising it, Yunmen said, "I will not fail to tell you.
Fayan Wenyi commented separately: "He has filled the monastic groves to satiety. Dongchan Guo said:
"Just now Baozi and Longya were walking hand-in-hand past here; they squeezed through the monk's ear-cavities. Why did he not know?"
Chan Master Shenzhe of Hanzhushan in Xiangzhou (a successor of Longya Dun) asked a monk, "Zhang, Wang, Li, and Zhao are not your original surnames.
What is your original surname? The monk replied, "I share the same surname as the Master.
The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment that we share the same surname, what is your original surname? The monk said, "Wait until the waters of the Han River flow backward."
He said this to the Master. The Master asked, "Why do you not say it right now? He replied, "Has the Han River ever flowed upstream?
The Master then desisted. Xinfan Lan said:
"By desisting while holding the pearl, he still remains unsatisfied in his heart. This monk’s virtue is indeed vast."
Mounting a mountain, one’s principle can subdue even a leopard; yet, as for his original surname, he truly never spoke of it.
But tell me, what was his ultimate original surname? [He] gave a shout and said: "There is none in Suzhou; there is one in Changzhou."
Chan Master Yuen of Gusang in Tanzhou (a successor of Daguang Hui). A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "At midnight, a crow wears snow upon its head; at dawn, a mute man returns home with his head in his arms."
Auspicious mists and auspicious smoke lock the Jade Tower; the Prince in his prime enjoys carefree leisure. Upon the Lapis Lazuli Hall he rides the Golden Horse;
before the Bright Moon Hall he rolls the Embroidered Ball. (Danxia Chun) Guming Peak is so lofty its form presses against the heavens;
the clouds are so deep they never reveal its summit. The remaining stele and ancient seal script are difficult to decipher.
While at [the monastery], he suddenly saw the tips of the pines and the full orb of the moon. (Entering the mundane world, he transcends it.
Chan Master Baizhang Shanzang of Jingzhao (a successor of Daguang Hui) was asked by a monk, "What is the Master’s profound depth?
The Master said, "A short man crossing a deep stream."
The white-haired youth possesses even greater wisdom; at the third watch of the night, he crosses the vast and boundless expanse.
He comes and goes spontaneously without interruption, requiring neither boat nor raft.
(Danxia Chun) Chan Master Chengyuan Wuyin of Heshan in Jizhou (a successor of Jiufeng Qian) was summoned by the Prince of Jiangnan.
The Prince asked, "Where have you come from, Master? The Master replied, "From Heishan. The Prince asked, "Where is that mountain?
The Master said, "When people come to pay court at the Phoenix Palace, the mountains and peaks never move."
Yingshan Yin said: "At that time, if Lord Li had said, 'If it is so, then did you send the Master's attendant here?
How would he have responded? Try to provide a substitute answer for He Shan’s reply and see. He then shouted, "Speak! Speak quickly!"
A monk asked Heshan, "To study and learn is called 'hearing'; to transcend learning is called 'the neighbor.
To go beyond these two is called 'true transcendence. What is true transcendence? The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum.
The monk asked, "What is the True Dharma? The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum. The monk said, "I do not ask about 'this mind is Buddha. [The Master said,] "As for..."
"What is it that is neither mind nor Buddha? The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter that transcends this?
The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum."
Dongchan Yue said: "Heshan’s immeasurable meanings and hundreds of thousands of Dharma-gates proceed like the sun and moon being revealed;
how could drifting clouds ever obscure them? Dongchan does not strike this broken drum. When the occasion arises, he transforms like a leopard; seeing a rabbit, he releases the hawk.
This is merely to ensure that each of you understands for yourselves. What is the true transgression? It is truthful speech. What is the truth?"
The Truth. Words as they are. How can that which is neither mind nor Buddha be so? Non-deceptive speech. How can this be the matter of the upward direction?
Non-differentiated speech. These four turning words are like iron caltrops; he who can swallow them whole is a master hand. If you have not yet reached this state, [do not be complacent].
"His words move further and further away from the Way. Fengshan Yan said, "Old man Heyuan was so pressured by this monk that he ended up adding far too many explanatory notes."
First, pulling stones; second, shoveling earth. To trigger the mechanism, one must use a crossbow capable of drawing a thousand *qian*. The Old Teacher of Xianggu once rolled a ball;
how does he compare to Heyshan, who knows how to beat the drum? I inform you: do not be reckless. What is sweet is sweet, and what is bitter is bitter.
(Cuifeng Xian): "Picking up a tuft of cloth requires many words; how can it compare to the single phrase transmitted by He Shan? One beat of the drum resounds through the universe;
a thousand-fathom ice suddenly gives birth to a lotus. (Touzi Qing)
Straw sandals for a crown, pines for hairpins—how elegant and clever is this perspective!
The pure sound remains only beneath the wind-swept eaves; all day long, no one descends the steps.
(Xutang Yu) With Mount Kunlun as the pole and the Yangtze River as the line, with Mount Tai as the bait, he hooks the leviathans. *Du!* How strange is this peach!
The wind and rain lash the flowers in haste; fish and dragons alike are lost amidst the surging waves.
(Zibai Ke) My husband serves at Xiao Pass while I remain in Wu. The western wind blows upon me, and I grieve for my husband. One line of written news brings a thousand lines of tears;
as the cold reaches you, will my clothes still reach you? (Songrumi)
Chanshi Changcha of Tong’an Yuan on Fengxi Mountain in Hongzhou (a successor of Jiufeng Qian) once heard the sound of magpies and said to the assembly, “The joyful magpie cries in the cold cypresses;
the Mind-Seal is transmitted by it. A monk stepped forward and asked, “Why is that necessary? The Master replied, “There is someone among you.
The monk said, “Under Master Tong’an’s gate, the Way is cut off and men are sparse. The Master said, “A Hu man drinks [wine].”
The milkman, on the contrary, marveled at the skilled physician, saying, "Rest, rest! The Master said, "An old crane enters a dried-up pond; not a trace of fish is seen.
Tiantong Jie said, "When the string is moved, the melody is distinct; there is a call and there is a response. The higher the call, the more sublime the response."
In the midst of this, although the sounds of Zheng and Wei were jumbled together, the five notes and six pitch-pipes were all brought forth in their proper order.
Tong’an asked a monk, “If the eye-realm has no light, how can one see? The monk replied, “The Big Dipper turns east and the Southern Dipper shifts west.
The Master said, “It is like a Confucian scholar entering the Grand Ancestral Temple. The monk said, “If that is so, then the Way is cut off beneath Master Tong’an’s gate.”
"The people have departed into the wilderness. The Master said: "Cradling an infant crosswise, he intends to manifest the Imperial Edict.
To Silla, Bohai, Nanyue, and Tiantai—where not even a speck of dust creates an obstruction—how could there be any involvement with coming or going? Turn your head and gather your thoughts."
The gates of liberation have opened; yet, turning back to recall Sudhana, he sought his superior friends, traveling through a hundred cities before knowing when to return.
(Chengtian Zong) When Tongan encountered a newly arrived monk, he circumambulated the meditation seat three times, struck his staff once, and said:

"At the place where neither ordinary beings nor sages reach, I ask you, Master, to speak. The Master snapped his fingers three times. The monk said: "Today, Tongan has frightened me into forgetfulness."
The monk left after making his initial mistake. The Master asked, "Where did you set out from, Ācārya? The monk said, "I take my leave," and departed.
The Master remarked, "A patch-robed traveler of the Five Lakes, a Zen practitioner with a single staff—before you have even reached Tong’an, you will surely be filled with doubt.
The monk turned his head and said, "What I see nearby is not as good as what I hear from afar. The Master said, "In greed for a single cup of wine, he lost the fish in the entire boat."
Zhaojue Qin said: "The entire army, with its ranks of cavalry and infantry intermingled, engages in battle between two arrays—how extraordinary!
Yet, alas, both sides suffer defeat. Heshan Xun said: "Exerting great function, manifesting great potential;

whether coming from the light or meeting in the dark, whether on level ground or in perilous terrain—if they wield the staff that kills or gives life, I shall simply use a lead weight wrapped in cotton. Even if all...
When the eyes are fixed upon it, it is difficult to determine what is this and what is not. Ultimately, how is it? It is truly laughable:
a single unperforated flute, played at both ends with host and guest reversed.
A monk asked Tongan, “What is the house style of the Phoenix’s Roost? The Master said, “The Phoenix’s Roost has no house style.
The monk asked, “Since it is the Phoenix’s Roost, why is there no house style? The Master said, “It does not welcome guests nor wait for visitors.
The monk asked, “If that is so, for what purpose do those from the four seas come seeking here? The Master said, “The meal is already set before you.”

The alms offered by bystanders are swallowed in a single mouth by the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time. Thus, in the deep stillness of the mountains as the moon turns yellow, the light divides behind the crown of the head, dawning through a thousand gates.
Sitting, I watch the spring return to the scorched earth. (Zidehui)
What subtle thoughts dwell in the young wife’s boudoir? In silence, she takes agalloch and sandalwood to dye her embroidered robes.

A monk asked him, "I have traveled far to seek your chamber; I beg for a word from the Master. The Master said, "Under the gate of Sun Bin."
[The monk] spoke in vain, like one divining by tortoise shell, saying, "A name is not bestowed without reason. The Master said, "Go and drink tea. The monk then said, "I take my leave" (*zhēnzhòng*).
The Master said, "Though you have gained one moment of glory, you have lopped off a pair of feet."
Tiantong Jue said: "A fist comes, a fist responds; a kick comes, a kick responds. Fist and kick intersect—whose loss, whose victory?
Shaking its head and wagging its tail, it passes through the strict barrier. Who would believe the words of one whose feet have been cut off?
Nevertheless, there is one point of confusion; try to examine it. Qiaozhiyu said: "Since he is skilled at being the guest, this one is also skilled at being the host."
Master: "When host and guest attain each other, it is certainly so. Why then do you say that although one gains glory in one field, one loses both feet?
Tongan was asked by a monk, "What is the Teacher of Gods and Men? The Master said, "The horns upon his head are not yet complete. His body—
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when the horns have not yet fully emerged atop the head? The Master said, "Not being carried upon [the head].
He asked, "What is it like when the hair has not yet emerged on the body? The Master said, "Not a single thread of silk is hanging."
Baonenglun says: Tong’an turns the mechanism beyond the kalpas and looses an arrow before the wind; he pierces through both sacred understanding and mundane sentiment at once.
This is not merely a matter of splitting the trigger, seizing the nest, and hitting the red heart;

even if one were a monk with hands as nimble as eyes—like the eight-armed Nārāyaṇa—it would still be difficult to grasp. Furthermore, regarding the line "not holding up [the bowl]," he says: "It is already too towering."
Regarding the phrase "not even an inch of thread hangs [upon one]," it says: "There still remains the bare bone. The *Shouchang Jing* states:
"Passing through passes and fords is easy; traversing dangerous pits is difficult. A strategist possesses the ability of foresight; a general relies solely on the power of his martial prowess."

Foreseeing perilous places, one does not tread upon them; certain of securing a superior position, one ascends it high. Without the need for bloody combat, success is achieved, thereby well-preserving the people from the misery of war.
Let the divine mechanisms and subtle calculations proceed; in the end, they are but a hollow display. Do you wish to know the intent of Tong’an?
Suddenly he draws forth the flint that ignites the plains, startling the spirits dwelling in their nests and caves into dispersal.
In the inner palace, behind heavy curtains, the dawn is still cold; On the vermilion steps, the moss is damp, and the ranks have not yet been formed.
Precious incense and phoenix-tapered candles merge into clouds and mist; Silently the curtains hang down, concealing his countenance.

(Danxia Chun) Tattered robes, coarse and ragged, chase the clouds as they fly; From of old, those who recognize them in this world have been rare. Even if it were by the hand of Weixiu, one could not paint it. (Miaoxi)
He stands before the eaves; the stone tigers do not know his intent.
(Companion of my peers) He comes of his own accord to the Jade Palace, too weary for sleep. Upon the purple thoroughfares, who would have the heart to spur him on?
Throughout the eight wildernesses, no one dares to recognize him; yet he is called by others a "Earth-Walking Immortal. (Yichu Yuan)
With ash on his head above, he does not reckon the passing years; indolent toward human affairs, he enjoys leisurely wandering.
Even the Three Sovereigns would not suffice to be called noble and honorable; let the hundred officials be left to harbor their anxieties.
(Gulin Ru) Tong’an asked a monk, "Where have you recently departed from? He replied, "Jiangxi. The Master said, "How is the Dharma-way in Jiangxi compared to here?"
The man said, "I rely on this question to ask you, Master. Had I asked another person, disaster would have ensued.
The Master said, "I was a bit hasty just now. The man said, "I am no infant; it is useless to try to stop my crying with yellow leaves.
The Master said, "I feel pity for the turtle and spare the tortoise; whether to kill or to let live is up to me."
Zhaojue Qin said: "In the house of a patriarchal master, one wields the tongs and hammer of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; it is only right that he act immediately, leaving no trace behind.

A monk asked Tongan, "The student has not yet understood the timing; I request the Master’s instruction.

Chan Master Shandao of Mount Muping in Yuanzhou (a successor of Wen of Panlong) first visited Luopo. He asked, "Before a single bubble has arisen, how does one discern the current of the water?
Luopo replied, "Shift the boat to understand the current; raise the oars to distinguish the waves.

A general of the musical corps rose from his prostrations and, looking toward the horse-landing platform, said: "I do not ask about having sucked dry the waters of the Western River."
"Please ask the Master to swallow the mounting platform. The Master extended his hands and sang: "Wipe it clean and bring it here! The military commander was suddenly enlightened;
he swallowed the mounting platform before the steps. Even if one meets someone with a mouth, it is difficult to open. Do not take offense at this heavy rehandling of the play-cloak.

Chan Master Guangde Zhou of Xiangzhou (the successor of Guangde Yan) was asked by a monk:
