The Master said, "The salt is exhausted and there is no charcoal. [A monk] asked, "When the salt is exhausted and there is no charcoal, what then?

The Master said, "Do not speak of your sorrows to one who is already sorrowful; to speak of them to one who is sorrowful would kill them with grief. (Collected according to the *Jingde Chuandeng Lu*). Jingshan Daokai said:
"The ancients acting in such a manner is called 'washing one's feet and then stepping onto the boat. Yuan-an Yuanwu said: "No..."
This is the ferry-crossing where travelers seek passage; how could one possibly roam through every spring of Wuling?
Though there are rules for gathering and releasing according to the season, the matter of leaving the gate or entering the house remains beyond discussion.
You must reach the roads of Chang’an; do not crouch in the weeds of a deep village. (Xutang Yu)
Guangde was once asked by a monk, "How can one attain the wondrous within the midst of waves? The Master said, "Without employing oars or rudders, and with the bottom removed;
coming and going, one never relies on a life-preserving float."
A single phrase in response is difficult to grasp; the Wheel-Turning King does not transform the land of Jambudvīpa. The waves and ripples of boundless lands are level;
alone he drives the mud ox to plow the moonlight. (Danxia Chun) Guangde was asked by a monk:
"When a fish is in the deep pool, it is hard to avoid the net; when a dragon dwells in shallow water, it is hard to find."
"How is it at such a time? The Master said: "The entire body is as dark as Mount Kunlun; throughout the whole person, there is but a single point of frost.
White clouds are cut off, the body has no reliance; the numinous crane soars upward in flight.
Smoke locks the reeds within the bright moon; the immortal, sightless, returns through the darkness. (Pingxiang)

Chan Master Jingxuan of Taiyang in Yingzhou (in the tenth generation after Dajian Huineng, successor of Liangshan Guan) ascended the hall and said: "At midnight, a black rooster broods over a goose egg."
At dawn it rises, appearing as a stork; its feathers like those of a crane, its claws like an eagle’s, and its body like that of a heron.
Yet it keeps company with crows. Soaring high into the misty heavens, it flies low over the willow banks. Returning at evening, look closely:
it is vaguely like a wild goose amidst the clouds.

Chongxian Qi said: "They cannot be mixed; their categories are not uniform. The Elder Dayang has exhausted his efforts in picking them up and showing them, yet those who encounter a true connoisseur are rare.
Gaoting speaks thus, but how many misunderstand him? They go on to make their living inside a charcoal pit. Baiyan Fu said:
"If a person thoroughly understands this, the three illnesses and two lights will be simultaneously transcended."

Not so. Let me pierce through the veil for you: When the Śūnyatā-deva was struck all over his body until it was crimson and raw, with fresh blood dripping like snow upon the great earth by a handless man wielding a staff of hare’s horn—do you understand this thoroughly?
Even if you were to understand it thoroughly, you would still be a yojana away from seeing the sun.
Dàiyáng ascends the hall: "The towering peaks of Mount Sāgara reach ten thousand fathoms; the path of birds is difficult to traverse. Upon the edge of a sword and thin ice—who can tread this way?
The wondrous phrases of the vehicle of the patriarchs are difficult to express through the pathways of speech. Even Vimalakīrti was silenced;
thus, when Bodhidharma came from the West, he sat facing the wall for nine years before finally meeting one who understood him. Dàiyáng today is likewise without [words]."
End. Take care. A single phrase that does not touch the lips is wondrous; sitting coldly at Shaolin is the ultimate compassion. You must know that this Way is not transmitted through instruction;
standing in the snow, Shen Guang already acted with undue force. (Danxia Chun)
Dayu asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Hongshan. The Master said, "Is the late master still there?
The monk said, "He is. The Master said, "His presence is not lacking; please have him come out so that I may meet him. The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "This one is merely an attendant.
The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Go and drink some tea."
Longchi said with a slight smile: "This monk was carrying a single length of broken rope everywhere, intending to thread it through people's nostrils.
This time, however, he was instead threaded by the old fellow Ming’an, until he was left unable to move or act.

Nevertheless, while the old fellow Ming’an certainly possessed his own strengths under the Dongshan lineage, had this been Linji, the staff would not have been spared even if it were broken to pieces."

Chongxian remarked, "That monk indeed came from Hongshan; it was simply that he misdelivered Hongshan’s words, thereby causing a needless waste of the Sun Temple’s (Tài-yáng) constant supply of tea and soup."
Tanyang asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "A full flask cannot be emptied;
the great earth has no hungry person.
Baoneng Lun said, "Old man Ming'an did not fail the question; he revealed it with his whole heart. This may truly be called 'that which is attained.'"
Extremely simple, yet the manifestation is vast. Danxia said: "Wangxiang was heartless, yet the Yellow Emperor honored him; Bian He possessed wisdom, yet the King of Chu disliked him.
Although these are called words of insight, they are merely adding a point to an arrowhead or driving a wedge into empty space.
Do you wish to recognize the family style of the Ming'an lineage? When hot, enjoy the cool; when cold, turn toward the fire. There is not a single distracting matter hanging upon the mind.
What need is there to distinguish the beautiful jade of Mount Jing? There is no use picking up the dark pearl from the Red Water.
Wangxiang was heartless, yet the Yellow Emperor valued him; Bian He possessed wisdom, yet the King of Chu detested him.

(Danxia Chun) A single range of spring mountains stretches across the dawn sky; the cloud shadows are blurred, as if a painting were unfinished. How wonderful it is, facing the misty waves of the river!
The back. Nángōng Jǐ’s brushstrokes leave fresh traces. (A line of five characters) In the sixth month there are plum blossoms;
in the twelfth month there are lotuses. Soft as iron and stone, yet hard as cotton. In an instant they lie in disarray across the balustrades.
They vex the painter, for their colors cannot be fully rendered. (Zǐfù Jù)

Chan Master Yiqing of Touzi in Shuzhou (Dharma successor of Tanyang Xuan), the eleventh generation descendant of Dajian Huineng. A monk asked: "Master, you have just offered incense to pray for the Emperor’s longevity.
Tell me, how many years does the current Emperor live? The Master said: "The moon embraces the red cassia tree."
Far-reaching. The stars bow to the North Star on high.

The six kingdoms enjoy peace and tranquility; congratulations on this holy year. The pearl curtains are rolled high as the moon shines before them. How could the Golden Wheel be content to sit idly in the hall?
There is no need to strike the still-whip at the vermilion steps. (Danxia Chun)
The Jade Candle opens afar the ten-thousand-li heavens; the spring colors within the Forbidden City proclaim themselves. Clouds rise high and the sun recedes as the auspicious qilin stirs;
the Polar Star and the Milky Way illuminate the evening plains.

(Accompanying my companions: The dew grows cold at the distant Dragon Tower; the stars turn as the celestial vault rises high. Who may draw near to the Sovereign’s countenance? Fragrance stains the jade-embroidered robe.

(Lingtíng Tǐng) A single expanse of empty stillness, utterly free from conditions; The moon-gate stands high above the sky of Emperor Yao. At times, an ancient stone chime strikes beneath the clear frost;
It casts forth a numinous elixir, as large as a fist. (Dèwēi Yù)
Touzi addressed the assembly: "If one discusses this matter, it is like a phoenix soaring into the sky leaving no trace;
or a wild goat hanging from a tree branch—how can one find its tracks? A golden dragon does not dwell in a cold pool; how could a jade hare ever settle within the shadow of a moon disc?
Should host and guest be established, one must shake one's head beyond the kalpa of Wei-yin; yet when questions and answers are presented..."
The Mysterious Path: with the side-mention serving as the chant. If one can act thus, one is still only halfway there. Should you further fix your gaze, there is no need for us to meet.

The water is clear and the moon is full; the man of the Way is sorrowful. Wondrous function has no dependence, and categories cannot be gathered. Beyond the kalpas, it is both correct and biased, and inclusive.
On the road, one discerns spring and autumn upon branches that have not yet sprouted.
(Danxia Chun) Having hewn away the green mountains, he dwells in an ancient cave; where white clouds enshroud him, the waters flow in layers. At night, the bright moon comes to shine upon him;
from a thousand miles away, the cold light passes through as a single mirror. (Pin Jixiang)
Touzi was asked by a monk: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he follow? The Master said:
"Before the time of Weiyin, a single arrow pierced through two layers of mountains. The monk asked: "What is this matter that is transmitted? The Master said:

"It is entirely because of the moon over Huai that it can illuminate the spring of Yingyang. The monk said: "If that is so, then one enters the water and sees the tall man. The Master—[remained silent].
The monk said, "I only know that the jade of Jing is extraordinary; how can one discern the heart of the King of Chu? The monk bowed, and the Master struck him with his whisk.
Baolin Lun said, "When this monk asked in such a manner and Touzi answered in such a manner, it was a discernment of the essence within the school, beyond the reach of ordinary measurement."
A turning point. One might say that the facts exist as a box and its lid meeting; the principle should be like the tip of an arrow striking another. Do you understand this yet?
If you are still muddled and superficial, Baoen will speak for you. Holding up his whisk, he said: "Laughing, he grasps the golden needle to thread the broken thread;
with earnest care, he transmits it to his descendants. He threw down the whisk. Chongxian Qi said: "Opening..."
He cleared the borders to expand the territory and abolished the old to establish the new. Old Man Touzi was truly a hero of his generation.
But tell me, where did this single arrow fall? If anyone can say, they may roam freely throughout the world.
Jade flowers bloom upon coral branches; the wind carries their pure fragrance throughout the nine realms.
Do not say that heaven and earth are devious—Shao Yang once saw Mu Zhou come.
(Danxia Chun) Exotic grasses and numinous branches, the wind passes through them in green; the rhinoceros and the moon, both without sentiment. Across the stream, peach and plum trees shed crimson.
All at once, the sails upon the Yangtze River come from Yue, clear and pure. (Companion of my comrades) On the banks of Ying, those who join in the singing are few.
Beside the Terrace of the King of Chu, the snow falls thick and white. A single melody at Canglang dances with the clouds;
one might mistakenly take the Consort of Xiang for the Lady Fu. (Lingting Ting)

Ten-thousand-fathom Dragon Gate, where startling snow-spray erupts; the distant source from the Min River truly cannot be confounded. From of old, the lofty and ancient have differed between the Yangtze and Huai rivers;
this is not a matter of discussing ordinary tributary streams. (By Bairyam Pu) Touzi ascended the hall:
"The vast waves surge and the white billows overflow the heavens. Who will gather the luminous pearl that subdues the sea?"
[He] clapped his hands. After a long while, he struck the ground with his staff and said, "A hundred fragments.
Xiangweng Yun said, "If Touzi had not had these subsequent words, he would have nearly lost his 'palm-jewel.
Nevertheless, it cannot avoid being a scene of total disorder. He then offered this verse:
The pearl from the Vermilion Water turns and penetrates the sun’s radiance; the Dragon King rages and hurls his golden hammer. The cold light strikes and shatters it as the misty waves spread wide;
the formless creature (Wangxiang) encounters again the mechanism of the falling precipice.
Chan Master Qingpou of Xingyang in Yingzhou (a successor of Taiyang Xuan) was serving as a garden head at Taiyang, tending melons.
Taiyang asked, "When will these sweet melons be ripe? The Master replied, "They are already overripe right now. Taiyang said, "Pick out the sweet ones and bring them here.
The Master asked, "For whom would you eat them? Taiyang said, "For those who do not enter the garden. The Master said, "I do not yet understand."
Yang asked, "If one does not enter the garden, will they still eat? Yang said, "Do you recognize him?
The Master replied, "Although I do not recognize him, I cannot help but give it to him. Yang laughed and departed.
Chongxian Qiyun said: "The melons are ripe and the seeds fall away; those who do not enter the garden sit and enjoy the fruit without merit.
When Dayang and his father discerned in this manner, it can truly be said that "the sweet melon is sweet all the way through to its stem."

Entering the garden or not entering the garden—these are all equally the children of slaves. This person has been here from the beginning; the exalted and distinctive one is not here. Not here, where is he?
The wind blows and the clouds cease, transcending the reach of thought and deliberation; on the roads of Chang’an, we do not meet.
In the land of non-arising, it is difficult to exchange or shift positions. *Tut!* (A seal within the station.
Xingyang asked a monk: "When Sagara emerges from the sea, heaven and earth tremble; as for this matter of face-to-face transmission, what is it like?"
The Master said, "When the Golden-Winged Bird King presides over the universe, who among them is the one who emerges? [The student] asked, "What if one suddenly encounters such an emergence?
What then? The Master said, "It is like a hawk seizing a pigeon; you may not believe it now, but only upon verification before the Imperial Palace will you know it is true.
[The student] said, "If that is so, then I shall fold my hands across my chest and retreat three paces. The Master said, "You must..."
Mizhuo’s “Turtle”: Do not wait for further instruction before returning with your forehead marked.
Ba’en Xiu said: "This monk was like Rāhula; he vied for victory when Śāriputra first established the Anāthapiṇḍada Garden.
Yet, although the dragon is surely the sovereign among scaly creatures, it cannot ultimately avoid becoming food for the garuḍa."
Qiaofeng’s wondrous words: "Three times he matched and surpassed [the opponent], soaring into the clouds and mists; with a single phrase he displayed his brilliance, far exceeding all peers.

To provide a definitive resolution for this monk, he truly draws the golden needle through the jade thread. When I, this mountain monk, raise up such a teaching, it is also to clarify the universe and trample upon the surging waves.

He unfolds and expands the vastness of heaven and earth with wondrous skill; his majestic reputation resounds through the imperial court. The myriad states fold their hands in submission, all receiving his transformative influence;
how could the rulers of the "ants and beetles" dare not submit? (Frequent Auspiciousness.
Chan Master Shencheng of Fuyan on Mount Nanyue (Dharma heir of Dayang Xuan) was specifically invited up the mountain by Minister Li to inquire about the Dharma.

"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master pointed to the cypress tree in front of the courtyard. The Official asked this three times, and the Master answered him thus three times.
The Official was delighted and composed a verse: "Appearing and disappearing amidst drifting clouds, filling the vast void; The original true form, it turns out, is not a single speck of dust.
Time and again I have inquired about the meaning of the coming from the West; He only points to that single cypress tree in front of the courtyard."
Falin said: "According to the views of the Venerable Yin, what was attained during the first transmission was already somewhat superior;
yet he waited for the second and third, which is not merely 'ten thousand miles of white clouds. Had it been Tao Yuanming, he would have simply knit his brows and returned home."

In the past, he suffered three defeats in three battles; yet once Duke Huan personally released his prisoners, his hegemonic enterprise was established with a reputation that lasts for a thousand years.
To this day, who does not admire his noble strategy?
(Huishongzhong) The golden hook submerged in the water startles fish and dragons; a three-legged toad surges through the waves. With a single cry of "kuannai," he returns to his own place.
By the riverbank, on a clear night under the moon, he wanders alone.

(Chongxiao Yu) Chan Master Daokai of Ruyi (Furong) at Tianting in Dongjing, the twelfth generation descendant of Great Mirror [Baizhang] (he was a successor of Touzi Qing). He went to visit Touzi and asked: "The Patriarch said..."
"Phrases are like the daily tea and rice of a household. Beyond this, is there any other way to speak for others?
The Master said, "Tell me, within the realm of the universe, does the Son of Heaven still require Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang?

As the Master was about to offer a word in response, the Master [Xuedou] suddenly struck him across the mouth with his whisk and said, "From the very moment you conceived the thought to speak, you already deserved thirty blows. At that, the Master’s mind suddenly opened.
He attained awakening. He prostrated and then departed. The Master said, "Come here first, Ācārya. The Teacher did not look back.
The Master said, "Have you reached the stage of non-doubt? The Teacher covered his ears and went out.
Qixia Chengyun said: "When the lotus flower emerges directly at that moment, does it not cause people to hesitate?

Yet Touzi gently pulls it back, so that one’s entire being is unintentionally exposed. If, at this point, you can stir up waves and create ripples, I guarantee that Touzi will have no choice but to retreat.
Chongxian Qi said: "How brilliant! It is truly like breaking through a wall and soaring into flight. (3)
"Ten blows have been duly administered. Granted, yet when examined closely, there are still thirty blows remaining.

Like wind blowing upon water, like water being blown by the wind; patterns interlacing and spreading—what "that" and what "this"? Wondrously embracing and mutually merging, it is like the resonance of jade and metal.
Fully upholding the true command, it is as lofty as a mountain to be gazed upon. Turning my laughter toward the single sandal returning to the West.
People, without cause or reason, arbitrarily distinguish between skin and marrow.
(Zhuan’an Cheng) A young wife within the inner chambers knows nothing of sorrow; on a spring day, she applies her makeup and ascends the green tower.
Suddenly seeing the color of the willows at the road’s edge, she regrets having taught her husband to seek the rank of Marquis. (Nan’an Yi)
When the arrow flies swift and the spirit moves ahead with joy, the soaring dragon-riders emerge from the celestial pond. Their heroic bearing cannot be bound by others;
though the purple edict commands them to gallop ten thousand miles, it is in vain.
(The Seal Corresponding to the Position) One day, while Fúróng was attending Tóuzǐ as they strolled through the vegetable garden, Tóuzǐ handed his staff to the Master. The Master received it.

He then followed along. The Master said, "It is only right that it should be so. The Master continued, "Carrying the master's sandals and holding his staff for him would not be considered going beyond one's duty.
[The student] said, "There is someone else traveling with us. The Master said, "That other person does not accept the teaching. The student then withdrew.
That evening he asked the Master, "Earlier today, our conversation was not finished. The Master said, "Please ask the Master to bring it up. [The student] said, "At dawn..."
On his birthday, as he was born in the hour of the Dog, the Master came carrying a lamp. The Master’s son said, “Your coming up and going down has not been in vain.
The Master replied, “When one is by the side of a Venerable Abbot, it is only proper to act thus. The son said, “In whose household are there not slaves and servants?
The Master replied, “The Abbot is advanced in years; we cannot do without him. The son said, “How so very earnest!”
Qin asked, "The Master said there is a share in repaying gratitude.
Fengxue joyfully remarked, "Bright light meets dark harmony; jade turns and pearls revolve. Host and guest are in accord, and there is no lack of profound penetration."
Thus, while the exchange of verses at the gate and courtyard is sufficient for one to admire the outward splendor, if we discuss the path that goes beyond, it is still not yet there. Why?
Have you not seen it said: "Over there, he does not sit upon the throne of the Empty King; how could he be willing to till the fields facing the sun?"
Furong ascended the hall. "The Dharma-body is subtle in principle and profound in expression; it transcends the afflictions of beginning and end all at once.
You worthy ones, is there a Dharma-body existing apart from this illusory body? Or is this illusory body itself the Dharma-body?
If you understand it in such a way, you are entirely relying on others to form interpretations, remaining muddled and divided between two paths. [This is] the Dharma-eye..."
Having not yet attained supernormal powers or clarity, one does not see the monk’s question to Jia Shan. [The monk asked: "What is the Dharma-body? Shan replied, "The Dharma-body has no form.
[The monk asked: "What is the Dharma-eye? Shan replied, "The Dharma-eye has no flaw. Now, if someone were to ask, "What is the Dharma-body?
a sheep would immediately lie down on dry ground. If they asked, "What is the Dharma-eye? a donkey would select a wet spot to urinate. Furthermore—
Someone asked, "What is the Dharmakāya? [Jiashan replied,] "Buying a hat to fit the head. "What is the Dharmacakṣus? "Pits, hollows, mounds, and hills.
If one were to examine this through conceptual selection, Jiashan’s approach would merely be the realm of study rather than the profound mystery.
It is like worldly, domestic objects that one cannot let go of; this causes the gate of emotion to remain firmly shut and the fetters of consciousness to be difficult to open. Now...
If the sun did not manifest its proper radiance, how could those who study later know where to turn?
I exhort you all: do not seek the Truth; you must only cease your views. When all views are exhausted, the dark mist will no longer arise;

naturally, the mirror of wisdom will be luminously clear, with nothing else remaining. Do you understand? After a long silence, he said: "You must believe that there is fire within the stone; now, rest."
Turning toward the heavens, one asks the sun;
the Way accords with the ordinary, utterly free from extremes. Why must the traveler endure such hardships? From now on, do not trust the divinations of Sun Bin;
the tortoise shell has no spiritual power, so there is no need to bore into it. (Danxia Chun)
The General secures the realm and stabilizes the state; the Minister of State coordinates the Yin and Yang.
Sitting upright in the Dragon Pavilion, he attends to no affairs; let the four seas rejoice in peace and prosperity.
(Zifuxu) The great artisan is not clever; the great Confucian does not study. Severing the hair-tip, severing the hair-fiber; like mountains, like peaks. The Red Water is without mind.
The pearl was obtained; though Mount Jing possesses wisdom, it remains lost within the jade casing.

(De-wei-yu) Because of his own awakening, Fu Rong asked: "The songs of the Hu family do not fall into the five musical notes; their melody transcends the azure heavens. I beg the Master to blow and sing them.
The Master said: "The wooden cock crows at midnight; the iron phoenix calls when the dawn breaks. [Fu Rong] said: "If that is so,"
A single phrase contains the melody of a thousand ages; those gathered here, like clouds and water, are all connoisseurs of this art.

The Master said, "A tongueless child can join in the chorus. [The monk] replied, "An adept patriarch, the eyes of humanity and the heavens. The Master said, "Stop trying to use those two pieces of skin!"
Kegui said: "The mutual exchange between teacher and disciple has successively stimulated and elevated one another.

There has certainly been no lack of those who have upheld the tradition of the Dongshan school and opened the eyes and minds of humans and devas. But tell me, what is the essential principle of Dongshan? The clear breeze combs the green willows;
the bright moon plays upon the azure woods."
The charred *tóng* is played at night, its tuning-pins distinct; the moon reflects upon the ice-chambered hall as the melody reaches its highest pitch.
A tongueless child is able to join in the harmony, riding an iron phoenix out into the azure heavens.

(Tingshan Chong) The people of Zheng perform the dance, the people of Chu sing the song; the sound winds around the high beams as the *Xuěqǔ* melody is harmonized. All under heaven rejoice to hear the transmission of the Sage.
Zuo. Deep within the nine-layered palace, melancholy stirs in abundance.
(A single pearl atop the head) Autumn mountains and crimson trees reflect upon the riverbank; even now, amidst the autumn wind, one remembers an old friend.
When they finally walk together to their former haunts, they pour out the night’s wine as the moonlight drenches the frost with its fresh radiance. (Zhao’an Fan)
Furong was serving as the kitchen steward at Touzi. Touzi said, "Managing the affairs of the kitchen is no easy task.
The Master replied, "I dare not say it is easy. Touzi asked, "Do you cook the porridge or steam the rice? The Master said, "The laborers wash the rice and light the fires;
the attendants cook the porridge and steam the rice. Touzi asked, "Then what do you do? The Master replied, "Out of the Master’s compassion, I let them have their leisure time."
Chongxian Qi said: "He was deeply trusted and understood; he entered and left without hindrance—Furong has attained this. After thirty years, people will mostly be indolent;
where will one find such a free-spirited fellow? Wenfeng Yu said: "Those who calculate and devise strategies have their own subordinates;
to simply sit with folded hands in non-action, one must return to the Sovereign. Furong’s response in this manner may indeed be called...
You have well grasped the essential meaning. However, when one arrives at the summit of the literary peak, there must still be another way to understand it before it is complete.
Why? Because "The waves of Caoxi are just like this; countless ordinary people sink beneath them."
Facing a formidable foe, he deployed a wondrous formation; with a single light-drawn arrow, he emerged from the heavy encirclement. Of what use were all those weary horses?
Only when the nation prospers does one truly know the majesty of the Emperor’s power.
(Yuan Fufeng) When a monk asked Master Fuyong, "What is the seamless stupa? the Master said, "White clouds enshroud the mountain peak. It ends here.

Although Fuyong’s words are thus densely sewn with needle and thread, from the beginning, the essential point is entirely [missing].
There is none. It is truly difficult to see the seamless stupa. Why? When the moon sets in the frosty sky and night is half spent, who will share this cold reflection in the deep pool?
Layer upon layer, falling in profusion; shadows gather in dense clusters. One must strictly avoid looking with the eyes fixed upon the sun.
Directly beneath, neither existence nor non-existence stands; all is vast white, then again vast black.

(Xueyan Qin) Mist and clouds steam and swirl as it leans against the high void. Being seamless, it has from the start transcended difference and sameness. How laughable that people add further annotations!
Feet. Amidst the moonlight locked by the mist of Kunlun, the shrine of Mount Dai soars high toward the azure mists. The jade carriage riding upon the clouds is rarely seen;
as the ministers bow and throng, the mountain’s countenance is serene, and amidst the cries of "Ten Thousand Years," the blue bird flies forth. (Lingtíng Tǐng)
The willows are lush and green; the peach blossoms are brilliant red. All that enters the range of sight is distant; who can directly recommend it?
A single cry of a dawn oriole from beyond the clouds—ten thousand valleys shrouded in mist, invisible.
(Guyan Yu) Furong was asked by a monk: "Whose song do you sing, Master? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? The Master said: "A golden phoenix."
Dwelling at night beneath the Shadowless Tree, the peaks and ridges have just appeared when they are veiled by sea clouds.
The *Tianmu Lü* says: "Do you see where Old Man Fuyong answered? It is not that he did not say, 'Shaoyang once visited Muzhou.'"
Spontaneous response—how could it be contrived? A single phrase fully encompasses both the hidden and the manifest.
A lingering thin mist enshrouds the ancient path; the solitary peak remains forever unrevealed in its majesty.

(Danxia Chun) The springtime light leaks through, half-hidden yet subtly penetrating; the vital warmth is so pervasive that no garment escapes its touch. Warbling orioles and falling leaves fill the misty village.
Twilight. The forest is still and thickets abound; horse tracks are few.

(Companion and I) In the desert, the wind is high and the solitary wild goose descends. On the marsh isles, the spring is warm and the white crane sleeps. Once gone to my old mountain, news and letters have been cut off.
My gaze reaches the limit of the vast green woods, locked in by the evening mist. (Lü of Meng’an)
Furong was visited by the Imperial Censor Yang Jie, who asked, "How many years has it been since we last parted? The Master said, "Seven years.

In the middle of the night, while lodging in a village field, he beheld the stars and moon shining brilliantly. There was...
The Master returned to present his robe. Yunyan asked, "How do you explain Dongshan’s five ranks of ruler and subject? The Master replied, "In my place, there is not even a single rank.
Yunyan ordered him to attend the hall and said to an attendant monk, "This fellow indeed possesses a point of view, yet he does not recognize the fundamental principle.
Later, when the Master entered the room for instruction, Yunyan had previously instructed an acolyte to...

Human beings are distinguished by their stations. When the Master arrived, he summoned both Shishang and Shizhang. Thereupon, the Master secretly attained the profound essence [of the teaching] and composed this verse:
"The single rank is just revealed, yet the five ranks are distinguished; Ruler and minister are in harmony, and purple clouds gather thick.
The night-bright curtain rolls up, shining without partiality; Layer upon layer of golden halls reveals the Most Honored One. Shishang received and understood this.
Jianfu was like a cloud; Tianyi had not yet penetrated the ultimate barrier above him, and the Great Dharma remained unclarified—this was due to the compassionate heart of the moment.
The skillful hand and ingenious mind are difficult to describe; were it not for Xijiang, it would have been hard to achieve such spiritual resonance.
Yet, was there truly such a thing under the gate of the Patriarchs? Xijiang said: "The single rank has just been manifested."
The Five Ranks. I wish to question him about this. Setting aside the five ranks for a moment, from where does this single rank itself come?

Chan Master Zuanan Zhijian of Xuedou in Mingzhou (16th generation descendant of Dajian Huineng; successor to Tiantong Ruojue), while studying under Cuiyan Zong, was asked by the Mountain (Cuiyan): [The text continues with the dialogue.]
"One who exerts oneself for the sake of the multitude surely has no lack of toil. The Master said, "You must know that there is one who does not toil.
[The monk] asked, "When one cannot remain within the state of honor and nobility, what then? The Master said, "Meeting him at every turn, yet not being recognized. [The monk] asked, "..."
"This is still like a host and guest on the road. What is the 'host within the host'? The Master said, "A flame is extinguished by blowing with the fingers.
Shan covered the Master's mouth with his hand; the Master pushed him away and departed.
Chongxian Qi said: "The two elders are much like those who cannot hold their alms bowls; they falsely claim not to be hungry. Zu’an ascended the hall and said:
"The World-Honored One has a secret word; Kāśyapa did not conceal it. A night of falling flower rain."
The mountain stream flows full with fragrant waters;
the palace borders the Taiye Lake where the azure waves are seen. The summer heat has slightly subsided as autumnal intent abounds.
One night, a gentle breeze rises from the tips of the duckweed, turning the dewdrops over until they cover every lotus in the pond. (Tiefan Zhou)
A dead snake lies across the road, its two red eyes glaring; scorched by the sun and fanned by the wind, its stench fills the city.
Its poisonous breath is unbearable, yet it continues to writhe and dance; to this day, no one travels upon the official highway.

(Xiangweng Yun) The stars shine brightly at midnight, the dew falls vast and clear; Mount Xiang looms high and steep, its majesty impossible to subdue. With a single phrase, he fully upholds the patriarchal legacy.
Command: Let the falling rain make every place fragrant. (De Wei-yu) Bamboo shadows sift through the golden moonlight filling the tower;
as the stars shift and the Dipper turns, they illuminate the azure isles. Suddenly, the faint sound of a lute from a thatched cottage is heard;
one spontaneously plays the pipes and sings, dispersing former sorrows. (Ni-shan Wei)

Chan Master Chang’ung Ru Jing of Tiantong Mountain in Mingzhou, the seventeenth generation descendant of Dajian (Huineng) [and successor to Xuedou Jian]: Having studied under Zu’an at Xuedou, he attained realization while contemplating the "Pine Tree" koan.
He presented a verse, saying: "The ancestral intent from the West is the pine tree in the courtyard; The nostrils are vast and empty."
Facing each other in vast silence. A withered branch falling to the ground, just as it leaps. The bright lattice of pine and ivy laughs and surges upward. He nodded his head in approval.
Throughout his life, he moved through various great monasteries; later, he resided at Jingci. By imperial decree, he was promoted to Tiantong.

Holding up the imperial edict, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The clouds part, and the nine heavens reveal themselves; the sun is seen as a multicolored phoenix bearing it forth. Now tell me, what is it like?"
What need is there for further detail? Swiftly, as per the Imperial Decree!

He thrusts his body into the cavern of the vast blue ocean and plucks the pearl from beneath the chin of the black dragon to return. Its radiance shoots far toward the constellations of Beidou and Niu;
its value is so great that it causes a profound tremor throughout the imperial capital. Even unto this present day, the jade phoenix soars high on its wings.
Set aside that other side; the crystal pitcher glows at night. The jagged cliffs rise high, brushing the Milky Way.
On the ten islands, the spring flowers are in full bloom.
(By Baiyu Si) Zhaozhou seizes it and hands it over for grinding and cooking. This滞貨 (stale merchandise) is highly valued atop Mount Huiri. The spring breeze from the Yellow Gate beckons.
In this place, the Linglong Rock rolls up the rich imperial incense. (The central position accords with it.
Chang’eng ascends the hall: The frost wind howls with severity; the frost leaves fall in desolation. Raising his whisk, he says: "Look!"
There is only Linglong Rock; its towering height seems to rise ever higher. What is called "Tiantong’s滞貨" (stale goods) has today been briefly peddled once.
Is there anyone who will offer a price?
Wenfeng Yuyun said: "When Chang’ung preaches the Dharma in this manner, it is truly difficult to harmonize with such a 'Spring Melody in Snow.
Yet, he has pointlessly labeled it 'stale goods' and demands that others pay its price.
The Spring Melody from before is now regrettable to have been transformed into a vulgar 'Ba-ge' song. Is there anyone who can turn it back? Try and show your strength for Chang’ung!"
When Chang’eng opened the furnace, he ascended the hall, called to the assembly, and drew a circle, saying:
"This is the Tiantong fire-pot. Approach it and you will be burned to death; retreat and you will freeze to death.
Suddenly, if a man were to come forth and ask, "What should be done?"—*thump!*—the fire-pot has moved!
Tianxi Shengyun said, "If I had seen him speak like that at the time, I would have given him a sudden shout right over his head and said,
'This old fellow does not even know his own eyebrows are being burned away!'"
Chang’eng ascended the hall and said: "Lu Xiujing, Tao Yuanming, Mañjuśrī, and Samantabhadra—drawing a single perfect circle, they say:
'We present this petition together. Now tell me, by whose authority is it judged? If it were Confucius, he would have said: 'I have nothing hidden from you.'"

Lotus flowers bloom in the sixth month, their fragrance rising from the water; at the corner of the hall, the warm breeze brings coolness with the night’s fall. Cease your painting; do not engage in idle calculation.
When his work was accomplished, he thought of the immortals and recalled Zi Lang. (A new beginning.

Although Chang’eng sat in the Dharma hall six times, he never spoke of receiving the transmission. When someone requested that he offer incense, the Master said, "I shall wait until I am in the Nirvana Hall to offer it.
When the time of his passing arrived, he indeed offered incense, saying, "Like Jing Xing’s pilgrimage."
For over forty years, I first arrived at Nanyue Lushan, where I lost my footing and fell into a pit. This incense must now be offered up;
it would be a grave neglect of my late Great Master Xuedou Zu’an.
Longtang Zhiyun said: "The Great Ancestor Chang’eng was buried alive by Xuedou in a jade pit, leaving him with grievances that could never be redressed.
Thus, he was unable to speak his mind three times and twice over; it was only at the very end that his wrongs were finally vindicated.
Why is this? Even if one possessed the lute of Boya, it would still be difficult to transcribe the heart’s innermost song."

The Eighteenth Generation Descendant of Dajian (Dajian Huineng), Chan Master Jue of Lumen in Xiangzhou (a successor of Tiantong Jing), visited Chang’ung. He encountered him as he was ascending the hall for formal instruction.
"A single black plum is like its original form; a spider weaves a web to catch a dragonfly. The dragonfly loses two of its wings—how laughable!"
"Eating a plum while biting an iron nail. The Master could not help but laugh and say, "Had I known earlier that the lamp was fire, how much longer would it take for the rice to cook?
Later, he received the seal of transmission and went forth to reside at Lukmon Temple.
A solitary wheel of brilliant purity amidst a throng of elephants; The inverted pendent moonlight reflects upon the dragon’s pool.
A single roll of white silk surges above the waves; The four seas are clear and still, yet the billows strike the heavens.
(Suan Ding) Seek him everywhere, yet you do not see him; In years past, he distressed me as the wild geese conveyed his letters. Now, we meet upon a narrow path.
[The Master] said: "Casting off [all concerns], roam the ends of the earth and let your ignorance run free.
Lumen addressed the assembly: "The entire great earth is the student’s single volume of scripture;
the entire universe is the student’s single eye. With this eye, one reads this scripture, never ceasing for even ten million billion kalpas."
Baoen Xiu said, "It is not easy to read and contemplate. Yuan'an Meng said, "At this very moment, where there is the scripture, there are no eyes;
where there are eyes, there is no scripture. When you raise your intention to read, it immediately becomes interrupted.
Baoen said, "It is not easy to read and contemplate. [The Master] exclaimed, "Bah! Why such drowsy talk? Longtang Zhu said, "If you look, your eyebrows will fall off; if you read..."
A flower blooms on a pestle.
When Lu-men asked Pu-zhao, "What is the single eye of the student that encompasses the entire universe?
the Master said, "You are obstructed by a single volume of scripture. As Zhao was about to respond, the Master shook his hand and said, "Not fast enough, lacquer!"
The bucket. By means of this, one attains the meaning beyond words.
Tianjie Shengyun said: "Setting aside for a moment the fact that Lumen was accustomed to seizing such opportunities, tell me: what is the meaning beyond words?
When the cup is dashed to the ground, the saucer shatters into seven pieces."
Lumen addressed the assembly: "The horns of an ox need not exist; yet their existence does not hinder anything. The horns of a hare need not be absent;

yet their absence is not permitted. Why? In the affairs of the world, it is only when one finds the circumstances to be excusable that they do not obstruct the principle, however difficult that principle may be to accommodate."
Lightening his body, he descends the steps with slow strides; brushing against the spring breeze, he is moved by emotion.
Turning his leisurely form back toward the cave-palace, the moon shines bright as the golden hall grows cold and still.
(Pingxiang) The nineteenth generation descendant of Dajian.
Chan Master Puzhao Xibian of Qingzhou (a successor of Jue of Lukuan) addressed the assembly: "To realize before the sound is to fall into the present age;
to take up after the phrase is to lose one's head and mistake it for a reflection. What is the self prior to the empty kalpa?"
Yuan-an Yu said: "The Way is not difficult; I fear only falling into the ways of the present age. Long-tang Zhu said:

"The Elder of Qingzhou upholds the ancestral principles of the Dongshan school, revered and looked up to by all under heaven. He opens wide the eastern gate to welcome guests, yet he does not forget the inner chambers of the imperial palace.
Do you wish to recognize your own self prior to the empty kalpa? After a long silence, he said: 'From the beginning, there has been no rank or position.'"
Who dares to forcibly arrange it? Baizhang Yuan said: "The poor are at ease, while the wealthy toil.

The mountains and rivers of the great earth are complete as auspicious images. To seek fire from the element of fire (Bing-Ding) is to reiterate a redundant intent. Melting snow in a red furnace is not a matter of ordinary sentiment;
the blue peaks and the vast waves are the most wondrous mystery. To climb a tree to catch fish is ultimately an error; to mark the boat to find a lost sword is surely [futile]."
In vain. Once the noble steed *Huailiu* caught sight of the shadow of the whip, he endured his impatience and pursued the wind across the nine heavens.
(Linquan Lun) The vast sky is clear, as if washed by heaven; along both banks, red peach and white plum trees stand in stillness.
Having crossed the bridge, one walks upon the road; the partridge cries out amidst the deep flowers. (Beiming Zhan)
In the precipitous ravine, the flowing spring freezes and ceases its flight. The bamboo blinds roll up as the moon reveals my frosty robes.
Last night in the solitary village, I heard the flute; at dawn, its clear melody fills the misty heights.

(From *Chao Ming Kao*) A single orb of autumn moon reflects upon the Xiao and Xiang rivers. The fisherman’s small boat drifts upon the vast, boundless expanse. Along both banks, the reeds and flowers seem like a night of mist.
Snow. A few cries of wild geese chill the Canglang River. (Jieshi Gong) Qingzhou addressed the assembly:
"I do not ask about discerning the host within the guest; what is the host within the host?"
Lord of Lords. The Jade Palace and Heavenly Countenance dwell in the Purple Abode; the moon bathes the vermilion steps, its shadow deep and still.
Infinite colored clouds veil the corridors and eaves. Communication is blocked; even looking, one finds nothing. To whom can this clear matter be told? (Linquan Lun) Qingzhou addressed the assembly:
"At midnight it is perfectly bright; at dawn, nothing is revealed. Why is it said that black and white have not yet appeared?"
The first watch: this is still the "partial" within the "central.
At the jade steps of the ceremonial hall, they await the dawn in the cold; Slowly the handle of the Dipper turns across the balustrade. The quiet whip first sounds as the palace screens open;
Fragrant mist and pearl curtains are difficult for the eyes to pierce. Deep in the palace, the shadows are vast and profound; Truly, the news is hard to transmit. (12)
The gates of the nobleman’s mansion remain unbarred; beside the wall, the flowers are silent while the birds’ songs clamor. This is truly not the world of men.

(Zong Yuanyuan) Silk curtains and jade banquets—past events now laid bare. The dock flower, still clinging to its stem, alone stirs the soul with grief. Within the palace of the King of Shu, the moon shines at the third watch;
it is no longer for those who whisper secrets of the mortal world. (Jue Yinyuan)
The inquiry from Qingzhou: There is praise for it that words cannot exhaust; where there are no words, the mind is naturally clear.
This would be to tear asunder empty space; were it not so, it would be the livelihood of ghosts. At the point of ultimate certainty, Master, speak a single phrase!
Yuan'an Yu said: "A skeleton with protruding bones. He also said: "Turning one's back and drawing a golden arrow. Baizhang Yuan said: "Do not pretend to be deaf.

Ducks are short and cranes are long; pines are straight and thorns are crooked; Li Bai’s plum blossoms are red and peach blossoms are pink; mountains are green and waters are blue. To respond to vinegar in such a manner."

A thousand feet, ten thousand feet—contentment. In the meditation hall, beneath a single pillow, one indulges in the sweetness of sleep; only then does one truly believe that there is no way for honor or disgrace to enter.

(Linquan Lun) A precious steed with an ornate saddle emerges from the imperial precincts; the golden whip points afar as scattered red petals fly. Who takes up the short flute to sing the song of spring?
A single note of the *gong* and *shang* scales sinks into the subtlest depths. (Gongtang Shu)
Qingzhou Yin asked Da Mingbao, "It transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations; I pray that you, Master, will point directly to the meaning of the Westward Transmission.
The Master said, "Yesterday someone asked this very same question and was beaten out. He asked, "How about today?
The Master said, "How can you be so insensitive to pain and pleasure? On the following day, Mingbao paid his respects. The Master said, "What a pity!"
"Granted. The staff was broken. Mingzhidu broke into a sweat.
Wenfeng Yu said, "One push, one probe; there is letting go and gathering in. We must acknowledge these two elders; they did not fail in their skill as masters of the hand-eye.
Some say it is like a red-eyed man bumping into a firebrand; even so, it does no harm to grant him permission."
[The Master] said, "If you were truly a Great Enlightened One, you would still not have even dreamed of it.
Qingzhou asked, "When both extremes are purely not established and the Middle Way need not be settled,
tell me, where can one encounter the ultimate point?"
Yuan of Yufan said: "Pitiful are the bones by the Indefinite River; They are all but people from dreams within a spring chamber.
The sun rises over Junshan as the morning mist withdraws; A mirror of empty clarity reflects autumn above and below. Reeds and sedges suddenly fly, clouds suddenly rise;
How many kinds of bright colors dwell upon the azure isles. (Bījaśrī)
Qingzhou asked: "When returning to one's original state and shifting positions, one must wear horns and don fur. Is it permissible to call such a being an animal? Yuan-an Meng said:
"The Lady Nüwa was unaware of the grief over the lost kingdom; across the river, she still sang the 'Hou Ting Hua'."
Qingzhou asked: "In every thought-moment Śākyamuni appears in the world; at every step Maitreya descends to be born.
Why is it that as soon as one directs the mind toward them, one errs, and as soon as one stirs a thought, one deviates?"
Yuan'an Meng said: "The wealthy lament that a thousand mouths are too few; the poor resent that a single body is too many.
Baizhang Yuan said: "Sweet melons are sweet; bitter melons are bitter."
Chan Master Yunwai Xiu of Tiantong in Mingzhou (the fifth generation descendant of Tiantong Jue, dharma heir of Zhiguang Ju) ascended the hall and said:

"Within the bustling dust of the marketplace, there is the Buddha-dharma of the bustling dust of the marketplace. Within the deep mountains and rocky valleys, there is the Buddha-dharma of the deep mountains and rocky valleys.
Yesterday, when this mountain monk went out through the city gate, [I encountered] the Buddha-dharma of the bustling dust of the marketplace."
At that time, I forgot all about it. Upon returning to Twenty Li of Pines and Clouds, I immediately beheld the Buddha-dharma within the deep mountains and rocky valleys.
Venerable assembly, tell me: what is the Buddha-dharma within the deep mountains and rocky valleys?
White clouds linger and drift, appearing and disappearing amidst the vast void; green creepers wind their way upward to the very summit of the cold pine trees.
Longtang Zhu said: "In the deep mountains, the Buddha-dharma has been fully manifested, one by one, beyond the clouds.
But tell me, what is the Buddha-dharma within the bustling marketplace of the red dust? The pavilions stretch across the lakeside villas as the plum blossoms play amidst the clearing snow;
music is performed in the military camps, mingling with the melodies of the frontier flutes. Furi Xi said: "The old fellow beyond the clouds seeks..."
Ordinarily, one swallows the entire universe with a single breath; yet when it comes to the two words "Buddha-dharma," one immediately splits them into two separate pieces.
With me, An, it is not so: the bustling marketplace and the red dust of the world are themselves the deep mountains and rocky cliffs;
the deep mountains and rocky cliffs are themselves within the bustling marketplace and the red dust of the world. Therefore, at the peak of Mount Taibai, I mix mud and water together—Chang’an.
The marketplace stands ten thousand fathoms high like a sheer cliff. At the place where it stands ten thousand fathoms high like a sheer cliff, one’s entire body merges with the water and mud.
When merging with the water and mud, one is suddenly and decisively standing ten thousand fathoms high like a sheer cliff. Tell me, what excellence did Long’an possess that he was able to be thus?
Zhuo leaned on his staff and said: "One sees only the imperial wind forming a single expanse; one knows not where the boundaries of territory lie. Falin Yin said:
"Within the deep mountains and rocky cliffs, the Buddha-dharma belongs to those beyond the clouds. Within the bustling markets of the red dust, the Buddha-dharma belongs to the dragons and elephants.
When these two places are joined together, they form a single expanse; yet this must be achieved by the Sun of the Buddha. And so it is.
As for "The Way is like a forest," what is it like here? Holding a scripture in hand, leaning against a pine tree, he smiles and asks:
"From where have you guests come?
Tiantong offers this statement: "Today Tiantong has died a great death. How will you save him?"—Tiantong.
"Today I am dying a great death; do not try to save me. Today, Tiantong is dying a great death; who will walk with me?
Regarding the first question, Xuedou commented: "Why try to save him? Regarding the second question, he said: "I invite the Master to eat."
[The Master] ate his rice. On the third occasion, he asked: "The Master goes first; I follow behind. Zifeng Ju finished citing Xuedou’s corroborating words and said:
"One turn of phrase traverses heaven and weaves the earth; one turn of phrase grates jade and strikes gold;
one turn of phrase muddies the clay and blends the water. If anyone can discern among these, I grant that you have attained the Buddha-dharma."
[This is] not so. One must undergo a "great death" before one can attain it.
The Chan Master Daming Bao (succeeded by Puzhao Bian) of Cizhou, twenty generations after Dajian [Huineng], addressed the assembly: "If we discuss this matter, it is like a person making needles."
A thread. Fortunately, every stitch was identical. Suddenly, seeing someone approach, he unconsciously lost the needle and saw only the thread.
He searched here and could not find it; he searched there and could not find it. He said to himself, "If I cannot find it even nearby, how could it have come from afar?
After searching for a long time without success, his mind became weary and confused, so he fell asleep and pulled [the thread].
The robe meets the pillow. Just as one is about to rest upon the pillow, there is a sudden, sharp prick—*kwa!*—and suddenly it is right here.
Yuyan Meng said: "Daming was unable to extract the nails and pull out the wedges for future generations;
instead of acting as one who has settled matters with clarity, he led them toward making a living on the needle-thread. Even if they were to grope their way to it, they would only become more lost."
Recognizing the head by its reflection—though so it may be—after thirty years, every time one drinks water, one chokes.
Through the misty waters of a hundred cities, one wanders in bitter exile; though the gates of the pavilion open, passage is not permitted.
Only Sudhana has seen this for himself: "Virtue-Cloud is not on Mount Miaogao. (Nan’an Yi)
To cherish the bright pearl amidst a heap of refuse, the compassionate heart exhausts itself in many ways. Its brilliant luster may be stirred and taken by anyone;
there is no need to trouble oneself to break open the dragon’s abode.

(A Seal of Position) When the fragrant blossoms have faded in the fourth month of the human world, the peach blossoms in the mountain temple begin to flourish in full bloom. One harbors a long-standing regret that spring departs with nowhere to be found.
[He was] in that place, yet he did not know how to turn and enter into this. (Iron Sail Boat) Daming ascended the hall:
"The treasure-trove of a Wheel-Turning King is like the state of one who is utterly destitute; the waist-belt at a wine shop is like the business of a great wealthy man.
Turning his body around, he bumps into a faceless fellow; where there is a fist, he uses it, and where there is a kick, he kicks."
He then gave a kick. Furthermore, who knows that the tradition of my Dongshan school has a distinct principle of "seizing the tiger’s head and gathering its tail"?
Do you understand? The jade dog travels all night, unaware of the dawn in heaven.
Where the pivot-wheel turns, all obstructions vanish; like lightning flashing and stars racing, one admires the master craftsman.
At the tip of the white-boned tree, the fish’s fan; upon the waves of the azure pool, the bird’s overturned cart.

(To Part from the Herdsman Chun) When the tiger roars on the solitary crag, the green peaks merge; when the dragon sighs in the withered wood, the clouds deepen in the cavern. The reflection of the rhombus mirror falls, leaving no trace.
Trace: At midnight, the autumn light was as cold as ice.

(Fen Jixiang) Chan Master Jueti of Wangshan in Taoyuan Prefecture (the Great Ming Treasure Successor), the twenty-first generation descendant of Dajian, saw a magpie pecking at raw rice on a stand. Thereupon—
He clapped his hands once, and the magpie flew away. Da Ming then struck the Master on the back with his palm.
The Master turned his head around, and Da Ming said, "Was it the magpie that betrayed you, or was it you who betrayed me? The Master was at a loss for words.
Daming said, "It is fortunate that you are a pitiable being; yet, we have instead been mutually neglecting one another. At these words, the Master attained a sudden realization.
For ten years he had served in positions of secret and solemn importance; when he suddenly abandoned his quarters, everyone was filled with suspicion and wonder.

Someone asked Daming, "Where has the attendant gone? Daming replied, "He comes from all quarters and goes to all quarters; why should one take it to heart? [The questioner] said, "I shall go to seek him."
"What is it like to study? Ming said, "If there is the Way, studying will grow its horns; if there is no Way, studying will diminish its majestic radiance.
The entire assembly was then filled with doubt, until later he received the seal of certification.

Longtang Zhiyun said: "With his entire being he offers reverence, yet he does not touch upon its majestic severity. Shifting positions and maintaining the essence, he attains the wondrous regardless of horizontal or vertical orientation.
Whether the Way exists or does not exist, he does not involve himself in either. How do you all understand this? At daybreak he hides within the shadowless tree;
though the great sun shines, it cannot find him."
Reining in his horse to chase the wind’s shadow, he leaves no trace behind; holding his iron arrow upside down, he roams upon its tip.
Let the white blades of the soldiers clash as they meet—whom can rival his merit to be enfeoffed as a Marquis of Ten Thousand Households?
(Zong Kaiyuan) A night of rain in Shanglin hastens the blossoming of flowers; from the branches of the red apricot, the dawn mists disperse. The Lord of the East naturally moves with rectitude.
"Let it be so! Let the spring colors overflow throughout the Imperial House.
(Lingtong Ting) Wushan once elucidated the fundamental tenets of the Dongshan school, saying: "Now that there is a position of supreme dignity, one must clarify the person of supreme dignity.
One must know that the person of supreme dignity does not occupy the position of supreme dignity; only then is it clarified."
Noble does not fall into the ranks of the common.
Baoshou Fang said, "Wangshan’s manner of holding this up still leaves something lacking in clarifying the single path of nobility. Why?
Has it not been said: "Outside the square, who dares to deliberate? Yuan'an Meng said, "How about 'black lacquer'?"
Upon the folding screen, he further transcribed Lu Tong’s “Poem on the Lunar Eclipse”:
At the third watch, the jade hare leaves the Milky Way; At midday, the golden cock crows atop the palace towers. The fragrance in the inner chambers is clear, yet Your Majesty does not sleep;
The four ministers have no ground upon which to present their virtuous counsels. (Jiāshuǐ Jiá)
Spring returns to the Yang Valley and ten thousand flowers bloom anew; the imperial curtains part at the dragon-throne steps, and the realm is clear.
To know the matter of the dragon-sleeve distributing fragrance, one must hear the crane cry in the clouds while the stone tiger is startled.

(By Xian Shantao) The Forbidden Palace does not occupy the central position of the nine ranks; it bends its will to provide expedient means for those to come. Carrying a bamboo pole wherever one goes, one meets the occasion as it arises.
Sporting, I whistle at the moon and chant with the wind as I wander to and fro.

(Yun yi leng) Not occupying the Palace of the Empty King, I am too weary to dwell in the Five-Phoenix Tower. In my ordinary state, I follow my own inclinations; who could rival me in such carefree roaming?
(Zhen Nanhong) Too weary to accompany the court audiences of the four seas; the layered imperial halls are locked with moss. The Golden Wheel is not mounted upon a precious throne;
one may come and go as one pleases amidst the myriad greens. (Bingya Xiang)
With earthen steps and thatched roof, there is nothing contrived; though occupying the supreme honor of the "Nine-Five" throne, he remains unaware of his own majesty.
Abundant is the Heavenly威 (awe) that shakes all beyond the borders—who among the eight directions would dare not turn their hearts like sunflowers toward him?

(Equally illuminating, one sees: Loving the moon, he strolls idly through the bamboo grove; gold sifted from the stream fills the ground as he cleanses himself in the pure breeze. Returning home, he sits cross-legged upon his rush mat.
Above. Tea bowls are frequently refilled; honor and disgrace are empty.
(Muan Mi) The precious hall of the dragon-clouds is beyond all pursuit; the curtains hang thickly, revealing no face. Who can draw near to the imperial majesty at such close quarters?
Let the phoenixes and mandarin ducks line up in white ranks as they may. (Zifou Ju)
King Shan ascended the hall and said, "Is there anyone here who can charge through the current and pass the blade? A monk went from east to west and from west to east.
The Master said, "Before you have won a single round of glory, your two shins shall be cut off. The monk said, "I know that the Master is accustomed to using this device.
The Master said, "The offense shall not be punished twice. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. The monk stuck out his tongue.
The Master said, "Staring with wide-open eyes from within a coffin. The monk said, "Take care," and then departed. The Master said, "What connection is there?

With crimson feet in the vermilion clouds, one knows how to ride the wind. Laughing to oneself, a single cry makes heaven and earth seem narrow;
beneath the moon over Flower Creek, one watches the soaring wild geese. (Xiangweng Yun)
Chan Master Nanyang Xiangyan Chunzhu Wencai (Baoying Yu’s successor), the twenty-seventh generation descendant of Dajian, reached the line in the *Song of Realizing the Way*,
“The illusory and transformed empty body is itself the Dharma-body,” and attained sudden, profound enlightenment.
Yuan’an Yu said: "If you were to awaken here, the day will come when you will wear fur and horns. Longtang Zhu said:

"Without leaving the path beneath the flowers, one immediately sees the spring within the cavern. Do you understand? I, this mountain monk, shall now borrow hands to perform my fists," whereupon he cited Changlu’s ascent to the hall:
"The illusory, transformed, empty body is itself the Dharma-body," and then he performed a dance.
"Do you see? Do you see? If you see in this way, the village wine is delicious by the bridge. He then performs a dance and says, "Do you see? Do you see?
If you do not see in this way, the wild flowers are fragrant on the opposite bank. Now tell me, is there any difference between what Xiangyan realized and what Changlu said?
Lone and perilous, a single sword emerges from Zhao Pass; snow beats upon beard and brow, yet resentment grows ever harder to bear.
Whether moving with the flow or against it, Heaven’s designs are unfathomable; the waters of Jianghuai continue their ceaseless murmur.

(By Xiangweng Yun) Water pierces through stone crevices; clouds lock the mountain nooks. When one is without illness, the phantom flower merely obscures the eyes; when doubt exists, the reflection of a bow becomes a serpent.
Set down the cup. Having seen through it all, go back! Having once been where the gibbons wail through the Three Gorges, even one who is not a man of sorrow feels grief within.
(By Hansong Cao) Xiangyan attained awakening while reading the *Song of Realizing the Way*. He went to visit Huairang to present his understanding. Huairang questioned him, saying:
"Regarding the saying, 'Have you not seen?'—to whom does this refer? The Master said, "Presented face-to-face, there is no turning away or evasion.
Yuan said, "A man who has fallen into a pit or a ditch speaks such words. The Master asked, "How about you, Preceptor?"
Yuan said, "Your mouth is full of nonsense. The Master said, "I have thoroughly seen through you.
The dream returns as dawn breaks; spring fills the painted hall. Plucking a water-lily flower, he knows how to turn his body.
Not believing that his countenance is exactly like mine, He rides his donkey once more across Western Qin. (Gongtang Shu)
When a monk asked Xiangyan, "What is the Dharma-realm of principle? the Master said, "Empty space falls to the ground; shattered to pieces, it forms no pattern.
The monk asked, "What is the Dharma-realm of phenomena? The Master said, "Upon arriving, the house is utterly emptied; one need not be a fool within the dwelling.
The monk asked, "What is the Dharma-realm of the non-obstruction of principle and phenomena? The Master said, "The three winters are barren."
Muxiu: "In the ninth month of summer, snowflakes fly. He asked, "What is the dharma-realm where all things are unimpeded?
The Master said, "The clear breeze accompanies the bright moon; the rustic old man smiles as they draw near."
Chongxian Qi said: "The old man Xiangyan only knew how to point out boundaries and draw lines; he did not realize his entire body was plastered with mud.
This monk understands it immediately—this is indeed understanding. Yet this is merely the wealth and honor found upon paper. As for the four dharma realms, he has not even dreamed of them."

The Great Illuminating Jewel Cloud states: "The Old Man of Incense-Veneration (Xiangyan) was merely looking back toward the subtle path of the school, yet he did not realize his entire body had rolled into the grass.
Although this monk has gained a small patch of ground, he simply does not know how to make use of it. Do you understand the four dharma-realms?"
Seventy-nine, sixty-three, gathered. Son of the Red Emperor.
Three-footed Longquan sword, neither this nor that. Eradicating tyranny to establish the law, the Han fame resounds.
Returning home, they drink together; the Great Wind dances. The Great Wind dances! Before the Hall of the Bright Moon, the elders rejoice. Parting the cloud-sleeves, the dragon flies.
Rain. (Yue Changping) Xiangyan ascended the hall and said:
"Dongshan’s 'three pounds of hemp,' Yunmen’s 'dry dung-peg'—on the large scale, they fill and break through empty space;
on the small scale, they do not even amount to a hair's tip. How strange that the Old Man of the Boat in those days used a long pole to fish through the clear waters."
Jiangyue: "Tonight the moon sets and the pond is empty. Do not, by any means, mistake a tortoise for a turtle. Great assembly, the ancients said, 'We shall meet after the moon has set.
But tell me, what is it that you meet? Dragging his staff backward, he returns to the abbot's quarters."
The wealthy and noble of Chang’an lament the end of spring; they vie with one another to admire the newly blossomed purple peonies.
Separately, there is a jade dish receiving the dew, cool and clear; no one rises to gaze upon it beneath the moon.
(Ping Jixiang) Twenty-eighth generation under the Great Mirror.
Chan Master Yan of Mant’an (Chun-zhuo Cai-si) of Wan’an was profoundly enlightened regarding his doubts and obstructions while reading the *Treasure Mirror Samādhi*.
Later, he ascended the hall and said: "I do not study the way the various quarters speak of Chan so expansively, bewitching the men and women of people’s homes.
A monk came forward and asked, "What was it like when Bodhidharma sat facing the wall? The Master replied, "That was precisely a vast calamity."
[The student] asked, "How can one completely sever this? The Master said, "To twist thistle fibers into rope to bind a ghost-child—one must be such a person.

As for the arrow that severs the throat or the broth of venomous insects, what hindrance is there in touching them? What harm is there in tasting them? Smash it to pieces as one would the [sword] of the Qin era."
The Demon-Exorcising Mirror. Grasping clouds and seizing mist—how could this be ordinary? With a single lift of the jade whip, the golden streets are stilled;
water-sprites and mountain demons have nowhere left to hide.

(By Hansong Cao) With a hawk-like brow, it flies alone with a heart for ten thousand miles. Who would believe its ambition for a marquisate? Its resentment is difficult to restrain. To secure the state, do not easily provoke the frontier.
"An omen. When a matter is grave, one must know that the calamity will be even deeper.

(Xiangweng Yun) Chan Master Niaogai of Shaoshi, the twenty-ninth generation descendant of Dajian (successor of Songting Yan), visited Wan’an. Wan’an said, "If you encounter a dead snake on the road..."
"Do not kill it; take it home in a bottomless basket. This is the fundamental principle of the Dongshan school.
"If you are a reckless Chan practitioner, how could you ever penetrate this? The Master asked, "Is this the 'neither affirming nor negating' [back-and-touch]?
An said, "It would make this mountain monk laugh until his mouth fell off. The Master was at a loss for words. An said, "What kind of bowl are you seeking inside a ghost cave?"
Master Yù felt increasingly uneasy. One day, Wàn'ān ascended the hall and said: "A single word that transcends and stands alone in its own time.
At these words, Master Yù attained sudden, vast enlightenment.

The tortoise shell—when has it ever supported a meditation seat? A dead snake—what need is there to carry it in a basket? For the elixir of immortality, one grain alone suffices; then one may howl at the moon.
Do not raise your voice. Once the snow melts and the land becomes a water-realm, spring will naturally arrive at the mountain city.
Take good care of the travelers: the road is slippery; avoid walking crosswise.
(By Hansong Cao) White clouds over the Fen River in the autumn of the Han era—how many times have I seen the Yellow River flow backward? Treading upon the fallen red petals, do not [be heedless].
Wearied, he returned with only his black sable robe remaining. (Xiangweng Yun) uttered these verses in solemn farewell:
"At eighty-seven years of age, with each exhalation and inhalation, I cast my hands free beyond the Voice of Authority; all is continuous and dense."
This poor fellow, facing death, cannot bear to let go; he vomits out his heart and liver to hang from the treetop. Turning toward that other side, he gazes with sorrowful longing;
the Canglang River flows boundlessly as autumn deepens. (Parting from Mucun).
Thirty generations after the Great Mirror.
When Chan Master Qibin of Shaoshi in the Western Capital (who later changed his lineage to follow Ningran) first visited Ningran, Ningran asked, "Before Bodhidharma had come, how would you practice?
The Master was perplexed by this. One day, upon seeing a *qinfeng* (Qin-seal) locust tree, he attained realization.
He immediately returned to stand in attendance, his body trembling violently. Ningran said, "Qibin, you have realized Chan; why are you so startled?"
While he was still harboring doubts, the Master suddenly said, "Today I have reached this point; it is like picking up a piece of ice from within a red-hot furnace.
He nodded and said, "The secret essence of the Dongshan school resides within your own person."
It would be better to shatter one's body into fine dust than to be a person who fails to fulfill their obligations to others.
One picks up a flake of snow from a glowing furnace; its brilliance is like that of a jade tree in eternal spring.

(Xiangweng Yun) Standing firm, he compels the living snake to transform into a soaring dragon; he stirs the depths of the vast ocean to raise a wind of raw fishiness, raising his head and wearing his horns as he brushes the heavens.
Han: Vomit forth tens of thousands of layers of yellow clouds.
(Jingtang’s tree) All is empty. Ascending the hall: Do not think of good; do not think of evil. The clouds part and the sun rises; there is a road facing the sun.
The donkey looks into the well; the well looks at the donkey. The moon sets and the pond dries up; there is no gate through which to enter.
Frost on the tongue, clouds over the eyes; the stars turn at the southern palisade as he recites with earnest devotion. After the banquet of the jade flowers, his reputation stands far apart;
who among those in the coastal lands does not carry you? (Pín Jíxiáng).
Regarding the monk’s question, "What is the matter prior to the empty kalpa? the Master said: "A tortoise toward..."
Fire. Yuyan Yuan said: "To deliberate and reject is to miss the point. Now tell me, where does the fault lie—on the host or on the guest?
If you can understand this here, only then will I grant that you have realized the matter prior to the empty kalpa. If you do not understand it, then watch as the turtle enters the shell.
Fire. Fengshan Qi said: "On the day of the fifth month at the hour of the horse (noon), red mouths and white tongues are all extinguished.
Regarding Chan Master Wufang Nengjiu (who succeeded Jukong Bin), the thirty-first generation descendant of Dajian Huineng: he visited Jukong, who asked, "Whom have you studied under?"
The Master said, "Before Mount Shaoshi, the wind is still. [The student] asked, "Why does one flower open into five petals?

The Master said, "A hundred pieces of a holeless iron hammer shattered. [The student] asked, "Why do you deceive with empty words? The Master said, "Everyone in the world only knows how to deceive with reality;
not a single person knows how to deceive with emptiness. [The student] said, "You have revealed yourself without being struck. The Master said, "One who is accustomed to using it has no hindrance."
Penetrating the test:

Before the thunder shakes the mountain, the Sleeping Dragon arises; turning clouds and overturning rain, his momentum is layered and deep. Entering the marketplace, he fears not the peril of the great waves;
with a single strike, let the True Eye be made to penetrate. Sharp teeth and a sword-like tongue, its point concealed—his breath swallows heaven and pierces the azure sky.
Heavenly! His heroic spirit was so brilliant that heaven and earth were shaken. A night wind spread the fragrance of ten thousand flowers.
(The Integrity of the Cold Pine) On a moonlit night, the ethereal consort returns, playing her zither. In profound silence, her cloud-belted robes pass through the empty mountains.
This lingering sorrow from the south—tears fall upon the fragrant breeze amidst the lush green mists. (The Recluse of Xiang)
The moon covers the green mountains, grasped in the palm of the hand; dewdrops fall drop by drop onto the golden platter.
Together we partake of the jade-flakes, a flavor beyond the ordinary, as we drink from the fragrant incense while the Purple Pavilion is cold.
(Zong Kaiyuan, 32nd generation under Dajian)

Chan Master Wencai of Moon-Boat (Dingguo was his successor) at Shaoshi Mountain in the Western Capital kept himself in seclusion and studied the *Nian-ti* (Excerpts and Comments) by Wansong on the kōans of ancient masters;
however, he remained as ignorant as if facing a blank wall. One day, he suddenly attained realization and said:

"The style of the Cao-Dong school possesses the skill of weaving 'reversal-pattern' brocade (*huíwén*). It is not merely a matter of fine needlework and thread, nor simply of winding and turning in circular patterns."
As for those who committed fundamental transgressions, he would not dare to accept them as his disciples. Subsequently, they would suddenly turn over a new leaf and leave the monastic precincts;
only after they had studied under Master Wufang and attained great realization was he finally granted their certification.
In spring rain, mountain flowers blaze like brocade; in autumn wind, falling leaves fly like gold. At night’s stillness, the recluse finds joy;
when the monkeys cry, the traveler’s heart is grieved. *Ei!* If one does not casually ascend a high peak to gaze afar, how could one see the depth of the eastern-flowing ocean? (Baiyu Si)
Kicking over the old vat of dregs—*ta*! A smile, the function of the original source. No "night-bright" curtain hangs before the hall;
in the sixth month, the Yellow River freezes to its very bottom. (Standing alone and transcendent,) the merit achieved through bloodshed is truly not deceptive.
Its dragon-splendor is dense and pervasive—who else can surpass it? Ten thousand households in Chang’an sing of the bright dawn.
The Moon. The sound stops the clouds as it returns to the imperial palace; it blows through the forbidden halls.

(Xiangweng Yun) Master Yuezhou addressed the assembly: "When Bodhidharma came from the West, he directly pointed to the One Vehicle Dharma for single-lineage transmission, enabling people to see their nature and become Buddhas.
When it reached my Shaoshi [Mount Song], it was like nine tripods suspended by a single thread. You all must seize this opportunity..."
Your physical strength and vigor are robust; to accomplish this matter, you must exert yourself. Do not let the days pass in idleness.
With not an inch of iron in hand, you have already subdued the demons; the transformation of divine soldiers is merely "grass-sa. If you ask about the pivotal point mentioned above:
it is like a staff from Mount Kunlun stirring the Yellow River. (Huan Yin Qian)
Chan Master Zongshu Xiaoshan of Beijing,
the thirty-third generation descendant of Dajian (Dajian Huineng), whose lineage was inherited by Yuezhou, entered the room of Yuezhou to seek instruction.
After serving in secret for eight years, he succeeded to the seat at Shaoshi. He sighed and said: "Since the passing of my late master, the patriarchal style within the realm has nearly vanished.
An elder once remarked that while the monastic communities are in decline, those who propagate the Dharma are many;
they feign themselves and seek ease rather than urgently providing support. Their collapse could occur with a single step. Although I am ashamed of this entrustment," [he continued].
"What will become of this path of the Dharma? he thought, and so he took charge of it. Later, he went up to the capital and resided at Zongjing.
The terrain was deficient in the southeast, yet the water flowed out naturally, vast and wide; waves surged for ten thousand *qǐng*, a boundless expanse of azure.
It deceives countless foolish men and women, who press down into the mud pit to lay bricks and tiles. (Nan’an Yī)
In the Yingfeng Palace, the Yunhe zither has ceased; rising to listen to the new cicadas, I walk upon the shallow *shā* grass.
For I love how the dewdrops from the Nine Heavens fall, their sound most abundant upon the Ten-Thousand-Year Branches.

(Tiefan Zhou) Brocade curtains and jade groves open beneath the sun; in the crimson court, the talents of the ranked immortals are personally examined. The Transformed Man alone drives his chariot for a thousand years.
The Deer said: "This comes from the summit of Mount Kunlun. (Mount Jade Kunlun).

The thirty-fourth generation descendant of the Great Mirror, Chan Master Shaoshi Huanyou Changrun (Successor of the Zongjing), studied the *Zongjing*. The Mirror raised [the case]: "I am not this now."
