"It is not he; yet, after all, who is it? The Master presented a verse, saying: "If you wish to recognize this person, there is a true report of him:
Formless, he fills the void; with form, he leaves no trace. He has been the teacher of Buddhas and patriarchs;
He shall forever be the standard for heaven and earth. A whisk of tortoise hair stirs a pure breeze; On the tip of a staff of hare's horn shines the bright moon."
When he emerged, Jing again questioned him. The Master said: "The colored phoenix flies, its body turning with ease;
the iron ox runs, its mind always at leisure. Jing said, "Excellent!"
The light of the broken mirror flies forth, needing no external conditions. A golden hairpin is slanted, its jade flower exquisite. Fragrant petals fall to the ground, difficult for anyone to gather;
a colorful phoenix carries them away to the edge of the sun. (By Xiangweng Yun) The drum at Leimen;
the fierce battle at Red Cliff. Opening the precious treasury; smashing the crystalline clarity. The celestial net interlaces and spreads.

Layer upon layer they reflect one another; the luster of the pearls illuminates each other, brilliant and perfectly clear. A staff of rabbit horns picks up a dancing peacock; a rope of tortoise hair binds a bellowing iron ox.
Transverse and vertical, the affairs of coming and going cannot be distinguished; reaching this point, it is difficult to maintain the sentiment of father and son.
One merely desires that merit and achievement be ever manifest in the world, unaware that through these turns the family reputation is being spread. (Hansong Cao)

Chan Master Lingshan Yunkong Changzhong (Dharma successor of Zongjing): When Shouchang asked about the essentials of the Dharma, the Master said, "If you can be diligent and refuse to deceive yourself, this is precisely the practice from beginning to end.

One day, hearing his brothers discussing the meaning of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* with great eloquence, the Master remarked, "If the eye of the school is not clear, it cannot be considered ultimate. Shouchang heard this.
Stupefied and lost, he asked, "What is the Eye of the School? The Master shook out his robes and rose. Later, Chang requested further instruction.
The Master said, "I truly do not know; you must look for it yourself. Later, while at Dayao Shan, Chang attained awakening.

He then entered the abbot’s quarters to communicate what he had realized. The Master said, "It is not that there is nothing to be awakened to, but you must ensure that you can actually make use of it."
Only then can one truly attain it; otherwise, it is merely "mercury-silver Chan.
Yongning Ding said, "Under a heavy reward, there must be brave men. As for that which Shouchang realized—was it mercury-silver Chan, or was it not?"
The oriole on the branch hears [the sound] with tears; new traces of weeping mingle with old ones. For several years, the fish and birds have been silent of news;
today, the mountains and passes weary the soul in dreams.
(Ssan Ding) The thirty-fifth generation under the Great Mirror.
Chan Master Fangan Nian of Dajue Cizhou (successor to Run of Shaoshi) visited Huanchou. Huanchou asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From the North.
Huanchou asked, "How does the Dharma-way of the North compare to that of this region? The Master replied, "The waters branch into a thousand streams, yet they flow from a single source.
One day, while visiting the site where the First Patriarch sat in meditation against a wall, he attained realization and said, "Five-Milk Peak..."
What a wonderful news! Large and small stones, each one touching the ground. He went into the room and presented his realization; Xiu gave him his seal of approval.

Having pierced through iron walls and silver mountains, he has trampled over the seals and pivots of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. The Dharma path flows north and south, and thus it is lush and verdant.
The forest: stones large and small, some laughing, some weeping. Water flows out in ten thousand streams; dew drops upon a thousand bamboo stalks.
The myriad phenomena pervading the world are all but empty flowers. Where else could one open one’s two eyes?
*Tu!* Six times six is originally thirty-six. (Hansong Cao)
A purple steed is turned back by its jade bit; With bold leaps it tramples the peaks’ very crest. Turning its body, it kicks down the rocks before the cliff;
Waves surge from the clear pool as the moon’s chariot wheel turns in autumn.
(Xiangweng Yun) Chan Master Wuming Huijing of Shouchang (Lingshan Zhongsi) asked a monk: "Zhaozhou said, 'The old woman at Mount Tai...'"
"I have thoroughly scrutinized you. "In what way have I been scrutinized? [The monk] said, "Today, you, Master, have failed.
The Master said, "I have been unable to do anything about this for my entire life. Let me teach you well: if you truly understand..."
He brought it up for them to see. As the monk was about to offer a word, the Master struck him with a staff and said, "You fraudulant fellow!
Xiqia Cheng said, "A single case from Mount Tai has snatched away the nostrils of so many people and swapped out the eyes of so many others.
This monk also knew how to feign clarity, yet when the old man produced this bit of firewood, he [was caught]."
He blew upon [the monk] right before him, leaving him with no way to retreat. But tell me, did he know where this one blow landed?
Shouchang said:
"Wading through rain and braving the wind to go; donning the stars and girding the moon to return. He knows not the suffering of his own body; only..."

Fearing that the practice of the gate might be deficient, Zishan Ren said: "Planting rice, one goes out early at dawn; watching the water, one forgets to return at night. The Great Meaning pervades the entire body—who could have any deficiency?"
Shouchang read the *Transmission of the Lamp* and saw the record of a monk asking Xingshan, "What is the Way? Shan replied, "A magnificent mountain.
Shouchang did not understand the meaning of this. One day, while lifting a stone, he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
A single stone outside the city of Guangzhou—how many prefects have tried to move it and failed?
This old monk lifts it up as do those in all quarters: Mengchang crossed the dark Qin Pass by night. Neither gods nor ghosts can fathom it.
For three hundred years this great mountain has stood tall, dominating the entire land of the Great Tang. (Nan’an Yi)
Everywhere the spring breeze blows, the grass grows lush and tall. What was already unbearable to grieve upon becomes even more so.
When the Great Spirit (Guli) split open the road to Mount Hua, the tiger-like power and dragon-like majesty were manifest at that very moment.

Filling the valleys and filling the ravines—what a magnificent mountain! Yet, amidst this, a single stone casually reveals its mottled patterns. Upon the cowherd’s field, the family’s reputation [remains].
Excellent! The elegance of a thousand ages lies in this very moment.

(Yu Kunlun) Chan Master Zhanran Yuancheng of Xian-sheng Yunmen in Yuezhou, the thirty-sixth generation descendant of the Great Mirror [Bodhidharma] (heir to Da-jue Nian), visited Yunqi. Yunqi raised [the following]:
The Master asked about the "Mud Ox at the Bottom of the Sea" kōan from Gao Feng. "Within it, there is one phrase; tell me, which one is it?
The Master pushed out a monk standing nearby and said, "The assembly shall bear witness. Xi nodded his head in agreement.
Yuan-an Meng said: "At that time, these words spread throughout the land, causing Mount Sumeru to tremble and the waves of the great ocean to surge.
The asuras held up the sun and moon in their hands and cried out in a loud voice: 'The distinction between the heterodox and the orthodox is not made;
the fault lies with the bystander monk. Chong-xian Qi said: "To sift through sand to find gold—this still belongs to the hands of the old fellow Yun-men."
This is a swift eye. If it were but a single phrase from within [the teaching], let alone Yunqi, even the old man Gao Feng could not have brought it forth. Why? Let the assembly bear witness.
Yunmen once went to visit Dajue at Zhifengtu. Dajue asked, "Zhifengtu is close to Green Mountain;
the city of the Yue King lies far across the vast blue sea. What is it like then? Yunmen replied, "The moon pierces through the bottom of the pool;
the Persian does not raise his eyebrows."

The questions probe the profound, and the answers dwell in the obscure; golden needles and jade threads, their meanings in perfect accord. The cave gates are locked by mist, difficult to peer through;
even those with iron eyes and copper pupils must shrink back in awe.
(Jia Shui Qia) Carved dragons and spirited steeds endure for a thousand autumns; his talent once moved the Marquises of the day. Today, the vapors of great mists rise anew.
Together we meet in the spring river; Xu Lao has come for his sheepskin robe.
(Lingtíng Tǐng) Meeting in Eastern Yue, how many times have we slept drunk? The bright moon fills the tower by the Mirror Lake.
Our parting lament ends at the Xīlíng Ferry; Willows in the autumn wind, with cicadas on every tree. (Tiěfán Zhōu)
Yunmen once visited Da’guan Ke of Helin on Mount Wutai. They stayed together until late at night, during which time Da’guan asked, "Do you have sufficient faith?
Helin replied, "I have sufficient faith. Da’guan said, "Since you have sufficient faith, I ask that you take this *Lotus Sutra* and throw it into a chamber pot.
Helin did as he was told. The practitioners of other quarters were filled with doubt and alarm. The Master went there to investigate him and asked:
"Is there such a thing as this at He-lin? he asked. He replied, "Indeed there is. The Master said, "Do you believe it? He replied, "I believe it.
The Master said, "Since you believe it, cut off your head and bring it here! He-lin was at a loss for what to do.
The Master said, "You are a vain talker, a guest of Zen! Guo-wen cried out, "Alas! Alas! He-lin will suffer in hell for ten thousand kalpas! Yun said, "..."
The Gate has already spoken a word on this.
Dongming Ji said: "Of these two venerable masters, one possesses the sword that kills but lacks the sword that gives life;
the other possesses both the sword that kills and the sword that gives life."
Once, while Yunmen was with the two masters Zibai and Yuechuan, as well as the gentlemen Huang Shengxuan and Tao Wangling, they were enjoying the moon.
Shengxuan asked about the karmic conditions concerning Mazu and Nanquan enjoying the moon, requesting a word from the Master. The Master said, "You are sitting and I am standing;
I cannot explain it for you. Shengxuan immediately rose and apologized for his error. Yuechuan remarked, "The Hanlin Academician has missed it."
Baizhang said, "My utterances do not reach those of this old man.
The flute has ceased its blowing, yet a sudden sound arises; though the clamor of voices harmonizes with it, none know the true melody. Only the elegant Grand Historian understands the intent;
he halts the refrain to alone capture the heart of the ancients. (Nan’an Yi)
A thousand fathoms of damp mist illuminate the chill upon men; amidst the jumbled green mountains, when can one find peace?
Even more regrettable is the neighbor’s restless sleeplessness, as they gaze toward the distant peaks all at once.

(Mimam Ke) Free from constraints and utterly unburdened, one is carefree and elegant; north, south, east, and west, there is nowhere to grasp. With such spirit, one rolls and unfurls oneself across the six directions.
Yunmen: "The light of his eyes pierces through the four worlds. (De Wei Yu).
When a monk asked Yunmen, "What is the great function? the Master said, "To kill ten million people and not be called a man of impulsive temperament."
Bai Zhang Lebie said, "He has deceived all the people in the world; he cannot be called a man of impulsive nature.
Wozongfu said, "Yunmen possesses only the sword that kills, but lacks the sword that gives life; Bai Zhang possesses only the sword that gives life, but lacks the sword that kills.
If someone were to ask Yishan, "What is the great function? he would simply say, "The treasury of my sovereign."
There is no such blade within. Tell me, how far apart is this from the ancients?

Once, when a monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when an ancient mirror has not yet been polished? the Master assumed a stern countenance and raised his voice to enumerate the monk's past transgressions.
The monk, feigning anger, took his leave. The Master said, "Just polish that one spot. The monk bowed.
The Milky Way is like silver, wind and dew spread wide; A heart full as the heavens is poured out toward you.
It is only because there is no one on this seat who knows me; Thus, the reed flute sounds yet another note in the breeze.
(Nan’an Yi) Deep within the emerald peaks, a dark fragrance drifts; Red mountain flowers bloom, each blossom exquisite. A single sheet of white clouds stretches across the valley.
[The Master] laughed: "He mocks the returning bird that is itself lost in its nest. (This is the integrity of the cold pines.
Once, when a monk asked Yunmen, "What is the perfect circle? the Master said, "A large sesame cake."
Smelting gold and carving jade, the veteran smith’s hammer; pointing directly at the sun, beyond all right and wrong.
Entrusted to the guest from Han who soars across the Celestial Pond, lest their shadow fall upon the Great Perfect Mechanism.
(Zong Zhijian) How does one’s speech compare to one’s practice? Turning over the rubble reveals nothing but gold. Who can compose a song to match the "Warm Spring"?
Tune the iron flute and blow it open amidst the white snow’s song (Xue’an Rui).
One day, after Yunmen had finished ascending the hall to preach the Dharma, he suddenly called out to the assembly, saying, "Is there anyone who wishes to ask a question?"
"If anyone comes out, I shall merely strike the grass to startle the snake. As soon as a monk emerged, the Master said, "Truly, this is a field of karma!
He struck his staff upon the ground and descended from his seat.
Yuan'an Yu said: "This old fellow sought a momentary sense of cleverness and agility, yet he failed to consider that future generations would scrutinize him.
As for this patch of ground, from antiquity until now, how has it ever been pure? It was merely a chance flash of insight, yet he was knocked down by this monk."
Yunmen ascended the hall and said: "This old fellow does not even recognize the basic strokes of a character, yet he forces his way out before others to preach the Dharma.
He misreads 'Zeng Shen' as 'Lu Shen,' and the entire assembly will surely laugh themselves to death. Laugh, laugh, laugh! Within this laughter there is a wondrousness."
If you can still awaken to the meaning within this and pierce through the single aperture at the very head, then tell me: what is this one aperture?
After a long silence, he said: "To move one’s countenance and reveal the ancient path is not to fall into the silent mechanism."
"Mistranscribing Zeng Shen as Lu Shen—Yunmen was far too foolish and complacent. A single aperture right before one’s face illuminates past and present;
why must he raise his eyebrows and let it fall into two or three?
(Muan Mi)" Once, when a monk came to visit Yunmen, Yunmen asked him, "How is your business of traveling on foot? The monk drew a circle.
The Master drew a line through it. The monk struck the desk three times. The Master, however, drew a circle.
The monk struck the desk another three times. The Master then drew three more circles. The monk wiped them away with his hand.
The Master said, "Apart from this, try to utter another phrase. The monk hesitated. The Master then shouted and sent him out.
Dongming Ji said, "This monk was about to complete a mountain nine fathoms high, yet he failed to advance even a single basket of earth.
Jingde Han said, "If I were that monk, I would wait for him to speak, and once he had finished, I would offer another phrase beyond what he said," whereupon he shook his sleeves and departed.

Together they take hū-bǐng (stale cakes) to sell at the street corner; giving and taking proceed with ease, attaining freedom. When the situation changes and the banner is exchanged, merit is finally established;
yet he loses him one move and does not become a marquis. (Shān-cí-jì) Carrying his book-box, he returns to narrate matters in the painted hall;
every word expresses joy that is no less than that of the stars Xi and Shang. But when the conversation reaches the point of personal sentiment...
In this place, a single glance turns the clouds and mountains into a vast, hazy expanse.
(The Sound of the Celestial Drum) Flowers fly from the Moon Cave; lightning flashes across the frosty void. To seize the embryo and change the bones is to preserve the power of transformation.

The dragon roars in the iron tree and the skull dries up; the tiger howls in the golden gale and heaven and earth turn. Since the thunderbolt has already struck behind the head, the sword remains pressed against the gate. I—
Who within the royal treasury can discern it? Picked up, it is cast toward the eastern great river. Myriad streams and a thousand mountains all look up to this source.

(The Assembly for Returning to the Origin) Once, when Yuanwu asked Yunmen about the verse on seeing the Buddha, he asked: "There is no dharma before one's eyes; the meaning lies right before one's eyes. What is its purport?"
The Master said, "I heard that your teacher has left the pass—is this true? He replied, "It is not the Dharma of the present moment; it is not something reached by the ears or eyes.
The Master asked again, "And what of it? The Master said, "Please come out; I wish to maintain silence. Hu then came out.
Meeting on a narrow path, a singular marvel is revealed; clearly, the etiquette of host and guest is not lacking.
Yet, within this, there is something even more erroneous—a truth unknown to those who have not undergone diligent effort.
(Jiegan enters: Phoenix pipes and crane flutes are separated by the colored clouds; one knows not whose house lies beyond the wall. Heavy gates are fast locked, leaving no way to seek it out.
In this place, there are a thousand trees of emerald peach blossoms along the path.

(No dependence or obstruction. The great Peng bird soars upon the wind; the azure dragon emerges from the sea. A single movement of the strings produces a different melody; those looking on have their expressions altered.
Walking together and conversing, they move with spontaneous ease. In Mingzhou, there is a certain "Dull Bagman. (Master Mugong Qian.)
During the day, the thatched gate is not yet closed; when guests arrive at the hall, the jade cup is offered. Cease speaking of how the spring colors of the Chu Mountains are fine;
let the bright moon always remain before the village ahead.
(By Quan Yuezu) Yunmen was asked by a monk, "What is the student's own self? The Master said, "You have no self. The monk said:
"Why does the student have no self? The Master said, "If you had a self, you would not seek it from me.
"Taking up the thorny weeds, they surpass the spiritual blade; Killing and giving life according to the moment, never slackening. Turning Aqingshan upside down, he returns home;
The fragrant plum blossoms drift on the breeze over Ye Creek. (Wei Zhongfu)
Seeking the Way into Peach Blossom Spring, the path grows ever more remote; as the mists and clouds vanish, one asks for the celestial raft.
Not knowing where the remnants of Qin’s dynasty dwell, the mouth of the cave is sealed by clouds that exhale azure blossoms.
(Zeng Xinxiu) Yunmen ascended the hall; suddenly a cock crowed, whereupon he said: "Aha! Elder Golden Cock, for your sake I shall turn the first [dharma-wheel]."
The Dharma-wheel of the fundamental truth of meaning is now complete. What more do you people here seek?

The water-railing is level with the sand; the stone terrace is cold. A clear breeze and fine rain mingle with fragrant scents. Against the wind, one plays the reed flute three times by the river city;
The soul is broken—silk skirts sweep across fallen plum blossoms. (Lingtíng Tǐng)
The flowing water and lofty mountains carry profound meaning. Since Master Qi departed, few have been true知音 (knowers).
Now I speak this to those who observe the wind; it is no ordinary sentiment of parting.
(By Silanrong) Yunmen was asked by General Su Yunpu: "The embroidered mandarin ducks are for you to behold; do not take the gold..."
[The Master] said, "The measure of the needle is like that of a person. What is the golden needle? The Master replied, "When I traveled once through the capital, I did not encounter a single person.
Pu asked again, and the Master said, "The ancient Buddhas have long since passed away."
Chongxian said, "Yunmen’s golden needle is cast in secret; it brings shame upon the solitary embroidery of the mandarin ducks.
When the Minister in his brocade robe walks at night, he does not think of the splendors of his native land. Fengshan said, "The auspicious qilin does not tread upon living grass;

the great Peng bird is ashamed to roost in a chicken coop. As for the mechanism of biting the arrowhead and the verse that startles the multitude—who dares to follow its wind? It is merely the final branch."
The Master scolded his wife severely. "If he is indeed unprincipled," he said, "I shall question him again and give him a blow, leaving this worldly fellow in doubt for thirty-six years."
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it to walk among those of different species? The Master said, "Strike me lightly!
Strike me lightly! The monk said, "I understand. The Master asked, "How do you understand? The monk then brayed like a donkey.
Chongxian Qi said: "Though this monk is skilled at his paces and strides, he still lacks the ability to turn back.
Examining him closely, he is merely one who studies the steps of Tang at Handan. Baiyan Fu said: "Master Yunmen spent his entire life with his eyes and brain perfectly upright."
His spirit was clear and lucid. Without cause, that monk who led him on went about making his living among a pack of blind donkeys and lame horses.
I, your unworthy grandson, am not like that. As for "What is practicing among those of different species? I simply say:
"The head of carpentry," "The head of masonry," "The head of construction," or "The head of stonework. Xue'an Rui said: "To perform Buddha-work among those of different species, one must..."
This was only just attained by Yunmen; he has not yet escaped leading people along with bit and saddle, with no end in sight.
I, however, am not like this. What is "walking among those of different species"? It is the pure *dharmakāya*, the perfect *saṃbhogakāya*, and the hundreds of thousands of millions of *nirmāṇakāyas*.
Turning my steps toward the streams and mountains, my eyes grow twice as clear; where the fallen flowers lie deep, the grasses are lush and green.
Born with the horns of a pair of twins, their traces remain nowhere to be found.

(Zongyuan Yuan) Having turned the pivot of the mechanism at the head of the ancient path, one wanders freely through wild fields and desolate banks. One does not even notice the sound of cicadas on the road.
All things are understood; one also perceives the early autumn heralded by the breeze.
(Zuandaoqi) Having fished out the moon over the Yue River, the jade flute blows away the spring within the caverns. Last night he did not stay overnight in the deep palace;
with a single oar and a fisherman’s song, he passed through Mengjin. (Shanrongbo)
When Yunmen was at Yunqi, he was escorting a deceased monk back to the monastery. He asked the assembly, "Where has the deceased monk gone after his transformation?
A monk stepped forward from the assembly and said, "Thank you, Preceptor, for your concern."
Yuan'an Yu said: "Although the old fellow Yunmen was skilled in expedient means, he still had to substitute for this monk by entering the Nirvana Hall himself.
Once the pivot of the immediate occasion is encountered, it is like building a wall in one place so that both sides are secure; thus, one can evade the sudden rain on this side."
Passing through, one immediately beholds the clear breeze at dawn; turning back, he returns to sing the melody of the Three Rivers.
A resonant, metallic clanging rings out from the depths of the azure sky.
(Wei Xin rises) In this frosty sky, we linger for wine in the joy of old friendship; with silver candles and golden censers, the night is not cold. If you ask of Wujiang since our parting—
Mind. Viewing the green mountains and bright moon within a dream.
(This refers to Sīlana Rong. Yunmen ascended the hall and said: "The crows cry on the front mountain; the magpies chirp on the back mountain. This very thing is ○○."

Deep contemplation is not yet wondrous. It is like a mute person eating yellow bitter ginseng; though they have a mouth, they cannot speak of it. Yunyan said, "Yunmen, that old fellow intends to cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven, yet he does not realize he is merely biting into the red edge of a plum. He then offered this verse: Deep contemplation is not yet wondrous; It is like a mute person eating yellow bitter ginseng. Though they have a mouth, they cannot speak of it. Yunyan said, "Yunmen, that old fellow intends to cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven, yet he does not realize he is merely biting into the red edge of a plum. He then offered this verse: The great matter is right here before you; Why do you go seeking it elsewhere? If you can see through the words of the ancients, Then you will know the source of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Do not mistake the path for the goal; Do not seek the truth within the scriptures. If you can let go of both body and mind, Then you will see the true face of the Buddha. Do not be attached to forms or appearances; Do not dwell on thoughts or concepts. If you can transcend all dualities, Then you will enter the gate of liberation. Do not rely on external conditions; Do not depend on internal cultivation. If you can be free from all attachments, Then you will attain the state of non-attainment. Do not seek enlightenment in the future; Do not dwell in delusion in the present. If you can be at ease in the midst of all things, Then you will realize the ultimate reality. Do not be bound by the teachings; Do not be constrained by the precepts. If you can be free from all limitations, Then you will manifest the great function. Do not seek the Way in the mountains; Do not seek it in the cities. If you can be at home wherever you are, Then you will be a true practitioner of the Way. Do not be concerned with fame or profit; Do not be obsessed with reputation or gain. If you can be content with whatever comes, Then you will live in accordance with the Dharma. Do not be swayed by circumstances; Do not be moved by emotions. If you can remain steadfast in all situations, Then you will be a true heir of the Buddhas. Do not be attached to the past; Do not be anxious about the future. If you can live in the present moment, Then you will be free from all suffering. Do not seek peace in stillness; Do not seek activity in movement. If you can be at ease in both stillness and movement, Then you will be a true master of the Way. Do not be bound by the small; Do not be limited by the narrow. If you can embrace the vast and the great, Then you will be a true vessel of the Dharma. Do not be concerned with the trivial; Do not be distracted by the mundane. If you can focus on the essential, Then you will be a true seeker of the Way. Do not be attached to the self; Do not be attached to others. If you can be free from all attachments, Then you will be a true renunciant. Do not be bound by the world; Do not be bound by the monastery. If you can be free from all bonds, Then you will be a true monk. Do not be concerned with the body; Do not be concerned with the mind. If you can be free from both body and mind, Then you will be a true practitioner of the Way. Do not be attached to form; Do not be attached to emptiness. If you can be free from both form and emptiness, Then you will be a true Bodhisattva. Do not be concerned with birth; Do not be concerned with death. If you can transcend both birth and death, Then you will be a true Nirmanakaya. Do not be attached to life; Do not be attached to death. If you can be free from both life and death, Then you will be a true Arhat. Do not be concerned with the past; Do not be concerned with the future. If you can be free from all time, Then you will be a true Tathagata. Do not be attached to the provisional; Do not be attached to the ultimate. If you can be free from both the provisional and the ultimate, Then you will be a true Mahasattva. Do not be concerned with the small; Do not be concerned with the great. If you can embrace both the small and the great, Then you will be a true Universal Monarch. Do not be attached to the lowly; Do not be attached to the noble. If you can be free from both the lowly and the noble, Then you will be a true Cakravartin. Do not be concerned with the ordinary; Do not be concerned with the extraordinary. If you can be free from both the ordinary and the extraordinary, Then you will be a true Buddha. Do not be attached to the mundane; Do not be attached to the supramundane. If you can be free from both the mundane and the supramundane, Then you will be a true World-Honored One. Do not be concerned with the finite; Do not be concerned with the infinite. If you can be free from both the finite and the infinite, Then you will be a true Samantabhadra. Do not be attached to the conditioned; Do not be attached to the unconditioned. If you can be free from both the conditioned and the unconditioned, Then you will be a true Vajradhara. Do not be concerned with the self; Do not be concerned with the other. If you can be free from both self and other, Then you will be a true Avalokitesvara. Do not be attached to the one; Do not be attached to the many. If you can be free from both the one and the many, Then you will be a true Manjushri. Do not be concerned with the near; Do not be concerned with the far. If you can be free from both the near and the far, Then you will be a true Maitreya. Do not be attached to the beginning; Do not be attached to the end. If you can be free from both the beginning and the end, Then you will be a true Sariputra. Do not be concerned with the cause; Do not be concerned with the effect. If you can be free from both cause and effect, Then you will be a true Mahakasyapa. Do not be attached to the teacher; Do not be attached to the student. If you can be free from both teacher and student, Then you will be a true Ananda. Do not be concerned with the high; Do not be concerned with the low. If you can be free from both the high and the low, Then you will be a true Upali. Do not be attached to the pure; Do not be attached to the impure. If you can be free from both the pure and the impure, Then you will be a true Mahaprajapati. Do not be concerned with the light; Do not be concerned with the dark. If you can be free from both light and dark, Then you will be a true Yasodhara. Do not be attached to the bright; Do not be attached to the dull. If you can be free from both the bright and the dull, Then you will be a true Rahula. Do not be concerned with the wise; Do not be concerned with the foolish. If you can be free from both the wise and the foolish, Then you will be a true Sudhana. Do not be attached to the good; Do not be attached to the bad. If you can be free from both the good and the bad, Then you will be a true Bhadra. Do not be concerned with the right; Do not be concerned with the wrong. If you can be free from both the right and the wrong, Then you will be a true Kasyapa. Do not be attached to the true; Do not be attached to the false. If you can be free from both the true and the false, Then you will be a true Maudgalyayana. Do not be concerned with the real; Do not be concerned with the unreal. If you can be free from both the real and the unreal, Then you will be a true Subhuti. Do not be attached to the existent; Do not be attached to the nonexistent. If you can be free from both existence and nonexistence, Then you will be a true Sariputra. Do not be concerned with the permanent; Do not be concerned with the impermanent. If you can be free from both permanence and impermanence, Then you will be a true Mahakatyayana. Do not be attached to the eternal; Do not be attached to the transient. If you can be free
A phoenix soars atop the Jade Dragon Ridge; pecking and sipping coral, it returns beneath the moon. When it cries out a single note, even heaven is moved;
throughout the layered maritime kingdoms, the robe is transmitted at night.
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is it like when one comes in such a way? The Master said, "Idle chatter. The monk asked, "What is it like when one does not come in such a way?
The Master said, "Idle chatter. The monk asked, "What is it like when one comes in both such a way and not in such a way?
The Master said, "Idle chatter. The monk asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "Idle chatter."
A flute without holes plays across the painted clouds; The plum-blossom melody has been played through to the end, with nothing more to add.
If there were a true connoisseur who could lend an ear, The entire contents of my liver and gall would be poured out at once.
(Xue'an Rui) *Zongjian Fali*, Volume 70.
*Zongjian fali*, Scroll 71, Compiled by Jiyun Tang;
under the lineage of Dajian, the thirty-sixth generation.
Chan Master Wuyi Yuanlai of Boshan in Xinzhou (a successor of Shouchang Jing) attained great enlightenment while on the latrine upon seeing a man climbing a tree.
He went to see Shouchang, who asked, "How have you been lately? The Master replied, "There is a living path, but it simply must not be known by others.
Shouchang asked, "Why must it not be known by others? The Master said, "Not knowing, not knowing."
Hansong Caoyun said: "If one were to discuss the vital path, it is not only that our teachers and disciples cannot bring it forth through their handling;
even if Bodhidharma himself were to arrive, he would be unable to manage it."
The ancient gate opens as I travel at dawn; the wind carries fragrance, lightening my brocade robes. Noble souls speak of the Cangzhou isles;
across the azure sea and empty sky, willow catkins drift. (By Quan Yuezu) As the year draws near its end, the remnants of the final month are unbearable.
I rejoice to see the plum blossoms blooming upon their branches. The young lord in his brocade robes indulges in wild revelry.
Manner. Reining in my horse, I stroll gracefully along the snowy path. One song, another tune; I turn to my old friends. Drunk on village wine, I sleep in blissful ease.
(Nan’an-yi) With jade and silk, they look back toward the imperial capital;
the King of Wusun returns home and no longer claims kingship. In the quiet reaches of the world’s edge, there are no military expeditions.
In battle, the martial spirit is dissolved into the light of the sun and moon.
(Hei Li Zhi) Walking alone upon the empty steps as the dawn light grows faint, the wind rises high and the plants and trees reveal their total functioning.
Turning back, he does not tread the path from whence he came; he wins the pure breeze to fill his sleeves as he returns. (Han Song Cao)

The mountain moon casts its white light across the central courtyard; the recluse, having been drunk, is now just beginning to sober. It is not that he fears the chill of spring, but rather that he grieves at treading upon the shadows of plum blossoms.
(Dàn Dēngqīng) Boshan [received] from Shouchang [the teaching] through the Chan Master Xuánzé’s response to a monk’s question regarding the dragon’s roar raising mist and the tiger’s howl...
The Master spontaneously uttered this verse on the "Wind-Arising Talk on Life": "Killing and enlivening vie for mastery, each possessing its own marvel;
How could the dim-sighted physical eye ever know it? Emitting light, it does not conform to the whims of the age; It follows the old spring wind chasing the horse's hooves."

Qixia Chengyun said: "To overturn the seas and mountains, one must possess talent that rises from the ground; to drive forth thunder and lightning, one must have a composition that reaches the heavens.
This verse by Boshan possesses the talent that rises from the ground, and it contains the composition that reaches the heavens."

It was required that for five hundred years one be renowned in the world. The phoenix danced at Mount Qi; across a hundred thousand *li*, the mind was transmitted. The dragon roared from a withered tree.
Yet, one must also have a distinct place of understanding and realization before it can be attained.

To turn the celestial pivot, one must return to the author; to overturn the terrestrial axis, one must be that person. In such a state, dragons contend and sea-monsters struggle—who would know the suffering of the turtles or the bitterness of the fish?
One clears away the dust of emotional attachments, forging the mundane and refining the sagely; one sweeps the mystical path, where thunder rolls and roars.
"Eh! Behold the imperial wind forming a single expanse; mountains green and waters blue—the ancient world.
(Ciyun Wen) Upon the whisk of tortoise-hair, at the tip of the rabbit-horn staff, the face is turned away; free and easy, how elegant!
(Xingshan Kang) Boshan was asked by a monk, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Red silk. The monk asked, "Is red silk not the Way? (Boshan)
[The Master] said, "It is not the Way. [The monk] asked, "Since it is not the Way, why did you answer with red silk?
The Master said, "Because you asked about the Way, I answered you with red silk."
The wild geese return, soaring high above the Taiye Pond; New blossoms bloom low upon the branches of Shanglin Park.
The light of the year is worthy of appreciation wherever it reaches; Yet the spring colors among men remain entirely unknown.
(Nan’an Yi) In Jiangnan, spring stirs as the first snow melts away; The wind and light are vast and serene, abounding even in the night. The traveler greedily gazes at the heavens.
How could one know that spring’s colors rest upon the tips of plum blossoms?
(Cold Pines’ Integrity) Each time I seek counsel, I am brought closer; from the pavilions, mist and rain brew the warmth of spring. Without cause, they are reflected within the pond;
the ruddy sheldrakes, preening their feathers, enter the painted screen. (Numinous Flames’ Illumination)
Chan Master Huitai Yuanjing of Dongyuan in Jianyang (a successor of Shouchang Jing) attained a realization and presented a verse to Shouchang, saying:
"Once recognized, it is not worth half a coin; How many years have I spent in vain groping for it? All those in this lineage are but deceivers of their own hearts;
What need is there to speak of the Patriarch having a separate Zen? Shouchang said: "Tell me, where exactly is [this 'separate Zen']?"
At the place where Zhaozhou interrogated the old woman, the Master said in a stern voice, "Monk, do not act so strangely.
Chang laughed heartily and said, "If one wishes to reach this critical point in Zen practice, only then will one no longer be caught in others' snares. The Master bowed.
Qixia Chengyun said: "Dongyuan was struck by Shouchang’s cold, sudden blow of the awl. Had there not been the subsequent words, it would have been a disaster, a disaster!
One has dug a deep pit for oneself and is burying oneself alive; with no way to survive, whom can one blame when the calamity arrives? Only by turning over the body can one pick up the lump of mud."
My son, you have mistaken the black pearl for a common treasure.
(From the Writings of Ciyun) With a seven-foot staff, I wander at leisure; striking through rain and beating against the wind, I pass my life. Turning across the stream bridge, I meet an old friend;
suddenly, I snap the sinew of my straw sandals.
In the Eastern Garden, seeing a monk approaching, [the Master] immediately said, "This fellow has lost his soul; what are you doing here?
As the monk was about to respond, he struck him with his staff and drove him away.
A single drunken draught of Cao Shan’s wine atop the Tortoise Head; his ancestral estate is so utterly complete that he knows nothing exists beyond it.
Relying on this very "soul-snatching elixir," he causes lightning and thunder to run backward. Do not run about recklessly! Speak, speak! (Mei Fengren):
Bare bones, two impoverished hands meeting; a worn-out staff-root with a glint of spirit. Sitting completely still, he cuts off the Gate of Ghosts.
The Way requires that one restore the souls of the people of Jambudvīpa.
(Haihui Awakens) Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian of Gushan, Fuzhou (Successor of Shouchang Jing). While the Master was reading the Lotus Sūtra, he reached the passage:
"At that time, I manifested for them a body of pure radiance. He then asked Shouchang: "What is this pure radiance?"
Mingxin stood up straight and firm. The Master said, "Is this all, or is there something more? Mingxin rose and began to walk.

At that moment, the Master suddenly attained great enlightenment, as if casting off a heavy burden. He followed Mingxin into the abbot’s quarters to communicate what he had realized. Mingxin immediately struck him three times with his staff.
He said, "Henceforth, you must not be hasty. He then showed him a verse, saying:

"Even if one were to mount the back of the golden-haired lion, I would still require them to turn themselves over under the staff. The Master wondered why he further required a turning-over under the staff.
Four years later, while passing through Yanjin, he heard a monk reciting a sutra: "At once they coughed and all together snapped their fingers. It was then that he understood.
The two sounds pervade the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions; through this, one thoroughly perceives the sphere of action of Shouchang.
Since picking up the *maṇi* jewel, he has reached the banks of the Yanjin River and emptied himself to the very bottom.
Coming as a bare-boned pauper with not a single thing, his two eyes remain clearly visible beneath his brows. (Juehai Wen)
In the fourth month, the fragrance of new lotuses fills the pond; A gentle breeze blows, permeating the gauze curtains. Startled from the bliss of deep sleep, how joyful is the heart!
If one were to speak of this to the people of this age, how many would understand?

(Ye Zhou Shun) The blue void hangs over the precipice, making flowers bloom before the eyes; One breathes in and out the morning mists and rosy clouds of the three thousand peaks. Within this, the fundamental source is clearly manifest.
The Matter: From outside another's gate, he drives three carts. (Truly lazy and settled! With every step he takes, it rises higher;
who knows that beneath the staff there is no leniency? A dragon lying in wait gains the water and stirs up waves;
a master of the ship crosses the ocean tide in a light skiff. (This is immediate realization.)
These two sounds are spoken with the mouth closed; clear light flickers as the sea-gate opens wide. In a single snap of the fingers, the entire mechanism is revealed;
turning over in one’s tracks beneath the staff, the hair on one's skin stands cold.
(By Ziyu Zhe) The thirty-seventh generation under Dajian [Huineng].

One day, while Master Mingche (a successor of Yunmen Cheng) was with his attendant Maolang Huai by the side of Yunmen, Yunmen said, "The old monk’s four elements are out of harmony; can you cure me? The Master replied, "Heaven!
Heaven! Maolang said, "Why such delirious talk? Yunmen said, "It is better than this one who cannot read."

To ascend to the pure clouds [of enlightenment] while suffering from a terminal illness that is difficult to cure with sedatives is like treating Yunmen’s chest-constricting ailment by merely administering ginseng and atractylodes;
it is no wonder that Yunmen himself used saltpeter and rhubarb.
The azure sky and bright sun stir wind and thunder; clouds lock the green mountains, mists shroud the crags. The spirited birds cry out their "guan-guan" without ceasing;
though eyes are clearly present, they have never been opened.
Master Lao suffered from three concurrent ailments; children vied with one another to bring him *Sanchentang* decoction. It was calculated that he would live for only three more years;
his tears were spent, yet he could not cease weeping for the Azure Heaven.
The Night-Bright Talisman is held before the mechanism; it plunges deep into the surging waves that splash to the heavens.
Even if the leviathans could manifest transformations, once they are hooked, they are hauled onto the fishing boat.
Chan Master Mai-lang Ming-huai (successor to Yunmen Cheng) of Mingyin Temple addressed the assembly: "The oxen and calves of Luoyang eat the tips of the grain stalks;
the fields of Jing and Yi yield only half their harvest. The Śūnyatā-deva dies of an empty belly, while the rivers Yangtze, Yellow, Huai, and Ji flow with long streams of tears."
Having ascended the pure clouds, he clearly used the family tombs of another as a pretext to lament his own inner affairs;
it is fine so long as those who have no connection to them remain unaware, but should he encounter their kinsmen, he cannot avoid making them laugh until they fall to the ground.
A single segment of true wind cannot be painted; blowing clearly and passing silently, it sends you on your way.
The mud ox roars, shattering the moon over the clear pool; the stone horse, spurred with the whip, does not advance a step.
(Tianning Hong) Master Furi Shiyu Mingfang (successor of Yunmen Cheng), while residing at Yunmen, was visited by Huang Duanbo.
A questioner asked, "What about when one comes with clarity? The Master said, "At Ye Creek, I do not permit a small boat to stay overnight.
[The questioner] asked, "What about when one comes in darkness? The Master said, "From here to Qiantang, there is still a crossing to be made."
Qingmen Lin said: "Drawing his precious sword horizontally, he does not even touch its edge;

one must yield to this lay practitioner who manifests the partial and the correct, and grandly expounds the ancestral school, returning it to that measureless old master. Do you all recognize where these two elders have landed?
If you can recognize it, it is just like Yang Xiu seeing the 'Young Lady' (youfu) character—he naturally knows its subtlety at a single glance. Suppose...
If you have not yet understood, listen further to this verse:
A single word that strikes the vital point is even longer than a discourse; White artemisia and red sedges fill the Xiang River. At midnight, the moonlit boat sails with the wind;
It does not touch east or west—how excellent its intention!
The Buddha-Sun asked, based on a monk’s question, "What is the Lord among Lords? The Master said, "I never brought it from Jiangnan.
[The monk] asked, "Why did you not bring it? The Master said, "It is actually thanks to you."
Amidst a profusion of myriad flowers, he buys rustic wine; by the winding river, he moors his fishing boat. Drunk, he carelessly casts his line;
his raincoat hangs askew against the setting sun.

When Master Foji first read the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he reached the passage: "Like you, Mañjuśrī, there is yet another Mañjuśrī," at which point his body and mind, as well as the world, were fused into a single whole.
Later, while ill, he encountered Yunmen’s public address beginning with the word "Let go," which brought him a pervasive sense of joy and liberation.
He presented a verse stating: "If one understands the meaning of extending and retracting at the tip of the pole, releasing life is originally for the sake of the catch."
The fisherman scolded him severely for his pain at the gate. Later, hearing a monk cite the story of Dahui peeling lychees, he suddenly broke into a hearty laugh.

Casting his fishing rod from the summit of a ten-thousand-fathom peak, the lychee is swallowed and spat out, its chill overwhelming all; with smoke-screened robe, bamboo pole, and straw hat, he stands amidst the setting sun.
Outside, the coral and jade platters lie in disarray. (Fine timber) Deep within the reed cove, the moon is at its third watch.
Red smartweed flowers bloom as the river waters turn clear. One cannot bear the guest from the Ruoye Stream;
he has inherited the family trade and continues to uphold the clan’s reputation. (Valley clouds are clear)
The moon reflects in the clear pool, utterly pure; At night’s stillness, the golden-scaled fish swim toward the light.
Suddenly it leaps once, turns its body over— It is a whale amidst the peach-blossom waves.
(Yu Qiao Yu) Because of the wind, the cold gathers; ice forms and there are no ripples. A jade dragon swims and plays within the deep pool. A sudden clap of thunder strikes the azure sky.
In the vast grotto of the dark ocean, he unleashes the great *kūṇ* and *jīng* fish, sucking the sea dry.
(Xueyun Chi) Upon hearing this once, he immediately withdraws his body; having cast down his hook and returned home, there is another spring.
On the tip of his pole, he rolls out infinite meaning; the sky and sea are vast and clear, the moonlight fresh. (Fuxu Gu)
Foji asked, “How can one begin to avoid being defiled? The Master said, “A patrol officer violating the curfew.
Anmei Yuru said, “A white blade is laid across, yet its edge remains hidden; this must be the work of the old master alone. Zishan, however, was not like this.
When asked, “How can one begin to avoid being defiled? he simply said, “A new lotus leaf holding raindrops.”
As the wind stirred, a distant fragrance arose.
The Buddha-Sun asked Bairyam, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Ganzhou. The Master asked, "Where is the Venerable Kōngtóng at this moment?
Bairyam stepped forward, paid his respects, and said, "I humbly wish the Venerable Master ten thousand blessings in your daily life. The Master—
He said, "You are mistaken. The other said, "I knew well enough that you, Master, were accustomed to turning the noble into the lowly.
The Master said, "Mistaken! Mistaken! "Meeting on the broken wharf, we shared our feelings; Taking off his sandals was clearly intended to suppress him.
When the end came and there was nothing more to be done, Out of deep kindness, he could only bestow the immortal scriptures. (Dufangluo)
The Buddha-sun dwells again amidst the heavenly flowers. A monk asked, "The stone parasol has already been withdrawn; the heavenly flowers are spread once more.
I beg the Master for instruction on that phrase which one cannot lift no matter how hard one tries. The Master said, "Brandishing an axe at a master carpenter's gate.

The monk said, "A roar from West River is not yet considered extraordinary; hiding one's body within the Big Dipper is still dull. The Master said, "The oil-selling lady applies water [to her brush]."
Tou said, "If that is so, then you know where gratitude is due, and the price for repaying it is boundless. The Master said, "Everyone, look at this monk!
Wuyi Jie said, "Although this monk is able to look through the hole and drive in the wedge, from beginning to end he still wishes to see the full force of the lift."
This phrase that arises cannot avoid being taken upon oneself as an error. Baoshou’s exertion was not applied; turn after turn, there is a way to emerge.
Examining it closely, it still has not been completely severed. Should someone ask this mountain monk: "The stone city has already been left behind."
Baoshouan arrived again. [The Master asked: "What is the phrase that cannot be lifted even with all one's strength? [The Master] simply said:
"Just look at the moon by the hermit's cliff; last night it shone clearly as it drank from Oxen Creek."
Chan Master Mingyu of Yuyan in Hangzhou (a successor of Yunmen Cheng) was asked by a monk, "What is it like when both parents have passed away?

The Master said, "A fine message indeed. The monk asked, "Is it still necessary to rely on protection and maintenance? The Master said, "When a single speck of film is in the eye, empty flowers fall in confusion."
In the hall above, there is no longer one’s own parent; from the eyes, one brushes away the cataracts and floating flowers.
Having traveled the path of the bright moon through three watches, one crosses the flowing sands across the vast, dark expanse.
(Haiei Xing) Yuan’an asked a monk, “Where are you going? The monk replied, “To Mount Bian. The Master said, “I have a message for you; please take it with you.”
The monk said, "I have attained it. The Master let out a thunderous shout; the monk was at a loss. The Master turned and walked away.
When the monk reached Mount Bian and had finished recounting the previous events, Bian said, "If this fellow were to come here, he could occupy the seat of the First Seat."
Weixin remarked: "Master Yuan'an applied colors within the great void; my late ancestor Baishan found a true connoisseur on his stringless lute.
If it were Upādhyāya Qi, however, it would be otherwise. When the monk said, "I understand," he immediately drew a circle on the ground and sat down.
Not only did this provide the messenger-monk with a place to stand, but it also made the grand message credible.
Penetrating. Why? "Turning one's head, everything belongs to the descendants; the patriarch has never left the gate.
Because his house is wealthy, he is generous with his wealth and knows no stinginess; yet the destitute son, with a branded forehead and no refuge, laments in sorrow.
He wanders alone among his kin and friends, but even as he pours out his innermost feelings, they pierce his cheeks. (Zhao Xian Sheng)
Dragging it off the tip of his nose, he laughs heartily; there is much elegance and refinement in this. Last night a tiger was bitten by a leopard;
at dawn, its former den is nowhere to be seen. (Zhengguan Zhe) Yufan studied under Yunmen.
Upon entering the hall, he took a vow of silence. While he was intensely engaged in *tishī* (mindfulness), Yunmen suddenly entered the hall. High...
Sheng said, "Put it down. The Master involuntarily raised his eyebrows and smiled. Sheng asked, "When the ox in Huaizhou eats the grain, why does the horse in Yizhou have a bloated belly?
The Master said, "Ask the pillar. Sheng said, "As for the tree falling and the vines withering, where ultimately does the phrase return?
The Master said, "The long river tosses white waves. Sheng said, "I still have my doubts about you."
The Master then presented a verse, saying: "Meeting him everywhere, I have recognized him; before Stone Umbrella Peak flows a continuous stream.
The Gatekeeper then pulled at his robe. The Master shook out his sleeves and departed, saying: "Boundless falling blossoms as the spring mountains grow dusk;
returning home by the road, listen to the birds' cries."
Stone Parasol Peak: ten thousand trees in autumn. By the banks of Ye Creek, the venomous dragon roams. Boundless falling petals, boundless spring.
The tree falls and the vine withers; laughter does not cease. (Yu Qiao Yuyu) Thundering the Dharma-thunder, raining down the Dharma-rain.
A crystal cup holds the milk of the Lion King. I am fondly attached to the mountains and waters of the Su Embankment.
Leisurely. On a wind-swept, flowing moonlit night, who is there to converse?
(Qian Yuyu) With a raised brow and a smile, the mind reaches emptiness; Mount Sumeru is brushed aside, leaving no trace. Treading upon the blue seas, it cannot be hidden;
the water of the Caves of Reversal flows eternally throughout the world. (Fu Xugu)
Chan Master Ermi Mingfu of Dongshan (a successor of Yunmen Cheng) was traveling by boat to visit a friend in Deqing when he attained realization upon hearing the sound of a gong.
He reported this to Yunmen, who said, "This is due to the influence of past roots; however, you must still realize that there is a further step beyond.
The Master assented. One day, as Yunmen ascended the hall for the discourse, he said, "Let it go! At these words, the Master suddenly attained full [awakening].
His body cast off its skin. He composed a verse, saying: "Midnight frost is cold and the moon suddenly sinks low; Travelers reaching this point all hesitate.
Turning over, he tramples the path by which he came; Starlight glimmers dot by dot as the handle of the Dipper hangs down."
The sound of the gong startles the dragon from the azure pool; its horns and head towering, the universe is empty. Waves rise upon the two rivers with nothing to conceal them;
within the strains of the lute, the ancestral wind is revealed. (Yu Qiao Yu) Resolving to seek instruction, he forgot both sleep and food;
within the sound of the bronze gong, he realized the perfect and eternal. The moon reflects on the Ya River at the tip of the fishing pole.
Water flows forth, its radiant brilliance filling the Great Tang (how brilliant and magnificent!).
With a single strike of the gong, the mind is suddenly emptied. Before the Hall of the Ancient Mirror, no merit is established.
Only when empty space itself is ground to dust will the guiding principle be settled upon the tip of a single hair (as pure as jade).
To secretly reveal this to the assembly, to establish merit and function while preserving illumination—this is much like climbing a tree to catch fish.

To withdraw the senses and eliminate cleverness—is this any different from milking a bull? Furthermore, it is said: "The Way is not seen, heard, sensed, or known, yet it is not separate from sound, form, voice, or language.
Based on what has been stated above, how, ultimately, should one practice? After a long silence, he said: "When you meet [it] on the road..."
Do not strike and kill the dead snake; take it home in a bottomless basket.
The green mountains are layered upon layer, and the waters flow in depth after depth; tell the traveler that the road is impassable.
It would be better to return to the mulberry and oak groves, where village songs and communal dances provide leisurely joy. (Haihui Xing)
Chan Master Mingyou Xiangxue (successor to Yunmen Cheng) was asked by a monk: "When one has long been stalled and cannot penetrate through, what then?
The Master said: "The prayer beads are in my hand. The monk asked: "When sounds have not yet ceased, what then? The Master said: "A mustard seed. The monk asked:
"When the six windows are not yet stilled, what then? The Master said: "We have already met."
Casually joining hands, they enter the red dust; step by step they follow one another, yet they are not kin.
All day long they cannot part from each other; sometimes they laugh, sometimes they scold.
(By Jie Hongliang) A sea-traveler stands at the edge of the abyss asking for the way; the fisherman answers him point by point. How pitiful that he did not encounter one who can play with the tide.
The hand—until this very day, it remains halfway.
The gears of the mechanism grind and mesh in secret harmony. When the story reaches the point of sorrow, tears well up to flow. A gust of golden wind blows down the leaves;
where on earth does autumn not strike with alarm?
Chan Master Rui Bai Mingxue of Bian Mountain (a successor of Yunmen Cheng) went to visit Yunmen. Yunmen brought up the story of "killing the cat.
At these words, the Master realized there was something beyond conceptual understanding; he tossed out his meditation cushion and said, "With one word, you reach Xuzhou.

Later, while crossing a bridge, Yunmen said, "The mountain stream flows with a gurgling sound; try to speak of it. The Master said, "Striking the void produces a resonance. He struck [the air] and departed.
The wood had no sound. Master Men smiled and nodded his head. Six days later, when the Master heard the sound of the bell, he attained great enlightenment.
The waters of the Yeshui River are clearer than the waters of Mount Pien; Mount Yue is higher than the highest mountains.
Striking the void produces resonance that is heard throughout the great earth; striking wood produces no sound, yet it pulverizes Mount Sumeru. Together, father and son, they transcend.
The national winds flow on. Casting out the meditation cushion, the moon shines upon the mirage-tower. Having traversed every path under heaven, one draws back a single finger.
(Shisong Qian) The furnace fire is evenly tempered;
forging the iron hammer, its weight is never deficient by a single ounce. Carelessly cast forth into the azure heavens.
Go! Strike down the white phoenix from the edge of heaven.
(Choe-am Park) The sound of the bell roars forth like crashing clouds and thunder; the ignorance of kalpas is instantly reduced to ashes.
Stepping aboard the boat, he returns at once; throughout Jambudvīpa, spring blooms everywhere. (Won-gam Da)

Pulao’s roar startles the stars at noon; atop Bai Zhang Mountain, golden spots scatter wildly. Not looking at the blossoming branches where the night moon flows, he instead spreads his stone parasol to shade gods and men.
He lets the oxen loose and brings the horses home—the master of the realm; he strikes the phoenix and nets the dragon—the guests from beyond the transformational world.
Riding backward upon the tiger’s head to gather its tail, where in his lineage is there not constant renewal? (The Lion’s Milk Vessel)
A single strike of the golden bell penetrates Yunmen; striking wood and knocking upon it, one debates beyond the lofty exterior. Water flows over the cross-bridge, its current inexhaustible;
the clear resonance rings out, preserved through all time and eternity.
(Worldly Tune: Guiding) When empty space is pulverized, there is no way to escape; yet it causes the meditation cushion to laugh without ceasing. A single strike of the bell’s sound—Heaven and Earth!
Pure. The bright moon on the treetops, autumn over the Five Lakes. (Transcending the eyes, one is conversant.
When Bian Shan asked about "the matter beneath the garden hut," how is it? The Wall said: "Planting seeds during the Qingming festival."
The Master said, "The Buddha-dharma is not like this principle. [Wuzhuo] said, "Two years and one spring.
The Master said, "You have not yet escaped sound and form. Wuzhuo picked up a jujube from the wall and said, "Can this be called 'form'?
The Master said, "If you do not call it 'form,' what would you call it? Wuzhuo said, "There is one in Qingzhou."
The clash of two blades shows no sign of ceasing; banners flash, bringing sorrow to the seas and mountains. One battle concluded, they return late;
the bright moon and clear breeze fill the imperial tower.
(Zong Kaiyuan) Though the General harbors the will to subdue the barbarians, how can he prevail when the barbarians refuse to surrender? The battle ended and he returned before daybreak.
Dawn. The courtyard is strewn with the wreckage of swords and spears.
(Ciyun’s Inscription) Upon the misty waves, a light boat floats upon the river. I am accustomed to roaming amidst waves that startle the soul.
If one but finds satisfaction at the tip of the fishing pole, There is no need for oars or rudders to sail down to Qingzhou.
Evening *zazen* at Bian Shan: A single-leafed skiff tossing upon the waves; casting the line, one watches for floating coins. Suddenly, a golden-scaled fish appears on the hook;
it does not fail the old fisherman braving the evening mist. Then, with his whisk, he makes the gesture of casting a hook and says:
"Tonight, this mountain monk casts his hook and throws his line. Is there any great *kūn-jing* [whale] here who will risk its life?"
"Come forth and swallow it! At that time, a monk came out and bowed. The Master said, "So, you are just a shrimp.
Le Chan Yao remarked, "He pilots a bottomless boat and casts a net across the heavens; the old fellow is indeed skilled at this.
Yet, when examined closely, it is much like stirring up waves where there is no wind. Although this monk is accustomed to entering the great surges, he should not have been so greedy for it."
With fragrant bait, a single cast brings the fish to the surface. Even if one possesses the form of a golden-scaled dragon, one cannot avoid being content to act as a mere frog.
Had you encountered this mountain monk at that moment, you should have snatched away the whisk and overturned the meditation seat;
then I guarantee that you, old man, would have been left utterly humiliated.
I imagine the clamor of the courtyard gate and the feasting on tripods; the Eastern Pavilion is opened wide to await the eminent and wise.
Had there not been guests who arrived at cockcrow at that time, even three thousand pairs of vermilion shoes would have been in vain.
(Ciyun’s Inscription) When I lived late in my life on Mount Bian at Kongtong, I struck the meditation board and sang east and west. Whenever a monk came to seek instruction, [I would respond].
He also struck the Zen board to indicate this.
Yunyan said, "Vast and spiritual, divinely attuned, wondrously responding without fixed direction. One does not know how many worlds there are within the land of China.
At this very moment, is there anyone who knows where Mount Bian has fallen? The moon sets in the frosty sky."
The night is nearly half over. Who else shares this cold reflection in the clear pool?

Again, I offer this verse: A single stroke of the bell pierces the stars at dawn; I bid farewell at the vermilion steps, no longer attending Your Majesty. From now on, the cold light shall empty the vast fields;
The udumbara flower shall bloom entirely within the fire.
When Layman Yin of Bian Mountain asked, "What is it like when not a single thought has arisen? the Master said, "A stone man wearing an iron hat.
The Layman asked, "What is it like when one has completely forgotten all thoughts? The Master said, "The sun sets at midnight."
Yunyan said, "Master Bianshan intended to strip him of his grease-stained cap and force him to cast off his stinking sweatshirt;
yet he did not realize that on a moonlit night in the still mountains, the empty tears are but the cry of the cuckoo."
Ascending the hall at Mount Bian: Drifting yellow leaves manifest the ancestral style of the Buddhas; wandering clouds reveal the true face of the person here.
How joyful to behold the jewel of the precepts shining brilliantly atop the mountain peaks! A single path of divine light, towering and majestic, pierces through past and present.
Nevertheless, one must further know there is a way to turn the body. But tell me, what is it?
Turning back along the path: the transformative merit returns to oneself, and the zither hall is cold; withdrawing from office to serve the sovereign, the ancient hall is chill.
Yunyan said, "The auspicious clouds gather, and the fragrant clusters all withdraw their splendor; on withered wood, flowers bloom.
While it is certainly true that the spring breeze blows away the ice and moon over the lake beyond the kalpas, if one speaks of the path of turning back, one must let another speak of it.
He finally attained realization.
While visiting Jinsu at Bianshan, as the Master was about to ascend the hall, the Teacher stepped forward from the assembly and gave a shout. Jinsu struck him.
The Teacher shouted again, and Jinsu struck him once more. The Teacher said, "This old fellow has failed! and returned to his place.
The *Fuxian pin* (Chapter on Blessings and Goodness) says: "When black beans have not yet sprouted, how can green and yellow be distinguished?

When a dragon-horse suddenly appears atop a stupa, who can tell odd from even? Once the fruit is the precious seal facing forward, what need is there to manage a thousand differences? The two great elders meet abruptly;
when they reach the point where their horns interlock, it is clear that guest and host are no different. Yet, as Bian Shan said, 'The breach is exposed.'"
It is understood. But tell me, where does the failure lie? When sent forth, it charges straight into the ranks of gongs and drums;
when withdrawn, it rolls up the majesty of ten thousand points.
When Bian Shan was asked by a monk, "What is the inconceivable realm? the Master said, "A snail swallows a great..."
The elephant charges forward, heedless of its head, brandishing the Dragon Spring sword; it cleaves through the void as blood splashes to heaven.
Iron walls and silver mountains are all pulverized; the Vairambha wind rises and the lightning mechanism whirls. (Gongtang Shu)
One day, Bianshan pointed to peach blossoms and addressed the assembly, saying, "Lingyun attained enlightenment upon seeing peach blossoms;
why do you all not attain enlightenment when seeing them? A monk asked, "How was it, Master, when you saw the peach blossoms?
The Master replied, "This old monk has never suffered from blurred vision. The monk said, "What about right now? The Master made a coughing sound.
This old monk has an ailment; go out!
In the past, Lingyun once lost his eyes; now he raises them up to deceive his descendants. When the time comes, a sudden rain will fall, crushing the blossoms;
again one sees the falling petals covering the entire village. (Xue’an Rui)
When Bian Shan arrived at Jinsu, he encountered the occasion of the boat being hoisted. He asked, "What is it like when space pilots an iron ship?
Jinsu struck him immediately. The Master caught the staff and said, "What is it like when waves surge a thousand fathoms high? Jinsu was about to strike again.
He tried to take off his staff, but could not. The Master said, "I knew well that you would find no place to apply your hand.
Xul said, "Tell me, by whose grace and power do you act? The Master snapped his fingers once.
The jade wheel hangs beyond the clouds in the azure sky; The waves of the ten-thousand-li silver river beat against the heavens.
Reeds on both banks, snow on both banks— A small boat should follow the favorable wind back home.
(Xue'an Rui) Ascending the Dharma Hall at Mount Bian: The moon-hook and cloud-bait are constantly cast; In the deep, clear pool, all is still and silent. There is...
At that moment, he went off swallowing the hook amidst the waves; drawing in the line, his joy was high. "O Great Assembly, tell me:
how would you express this single phrase of 'drawing in the line and rolling up the hook'? After a long silence, he said: "Willow branches crisscross within a flower basket;
the street vendor shouts loudly, selling the fresh."
Fragrant bait is cast idly, floating upon the waves; the water is deep and the fish are dense, silently swallowing the hook.
The old fisherman, having attained his purpose, sings as he returns home; the bright moon and reeds fill his fishing boat.
(From the *Chidu zhuan*) Zen Master Zhinyun of Xueguan at Yingshan (a successor of Boshan). When he first visited Boshan, he served in the fodder shed. Because he saw...
While grinding his nose, he suddenly attained realization. He presented a verse, saying: "In the place where we meet directly, there has always been no concealment;
the tongue is originally but flesh—chewing it to pieces does no harm. One day, Shanshan ordered the head monk to ask him:
"What is the eye of humanity and heaven? The Master replied: "Upon the crown of the head. [The monk asked: "Is there still any need for a mirror? The Master...
He said, "The mountain does not see the mountain. He continued, "If you do not hesitate, you will meet a true master. The Master covered his ears and departed.
At the slanting side of the setting sun, the path stretches far away; looking east toward Poyang Lake, the water is like a cart. Where he treads upon the mountains, his sandals shatter;
how many times have the wind and moon fallen upon the plum blossoms? (The rhyme is *yi*.)
Silver mountains and snowy nights form ice-flowers; rubbing his nose, he laughs "he-he" as a master. Yesterday at Lan Pass there was no obstruction;
in the morning sun’s brief flash, it is the edge of the world.
(Chan Master Zhipei: Several times returning home, yet never arriving. Heaven and earth turn and revolve in endless circles. Since trampling the plum blossoms to pieces—
The moon—within its blue-white eyes, it clings to the sand.
(Chongxiao yu) In the square pond, the fine grasses lie as the evening sun slants; from the hidden willow tips, the crows return at dusk.
On one's feet, the straw sandals should be tied fast; would one truly follow the bright moon to tread upon the reeds? (Weixin qi)
The millstone has no feet, yet it runs upside down; he grasps the nostrils but loses the mouth.
He blinds the true eye of gods and men; empty space lets out a great lion’s roar.
