Daomi would never have held such a view. The Master said, "I shall give him thirty blows.
White clouds arise from the bottom of the ravine; a woodcutter passes by the bridge over the front creek. Looking toward the immortal source, there is no other tree;
ten-thousand-foot dragon pools lie furthest west. I charge the travelers to watch for slippery paths; how many will find their footing beyond the heavens?
Clouds obscure the sky; they laugh to death those who lean on the gate or stand by the door, mistaking the cry of a crane for the song of a warbler.
(Nan’an Yi) White clouds rise from the mountain stream, opening wide his two eyes; he vainly claims that finding rest is not communicated. The father-son mechanism is truly perilous and steep;
with thirty blows of the black staff, he proclaims the ancestral style. (Hongji You)
Dānapāramitā ascends the hall: When the season arrives for withered trees and cold crags, the spring breeze stirs the ashes from the ritual tubes.
The stone man claps his hands and laughs aloud; do not mistake the spring ox for a mound of earth.
To ascend loftily into the pure clouds—to act for others in such a manner—is to possess only the sword that kills, yet lack the blade that gives life.
Dan Deng would have it otherwise: the spring ox is merely earth arranged; when the season meets its time, how magnificent!
It wins the east wind arising over the vast fields, and from this point on, the hundred flowers shall bloom in fragrance.
High waves surge through the gorges of Baxia, rolling back smoke and mist as the sun sinks low. On both banks, travelers have not yet returned;
one hears once more the heart-rending cries of the gibbons.
As for the *dānapāramitā*, when a monk asked, "What is 'falling into the category'? the Master said, "A divine rhinoceros gazes at the moon.

The monk asked, "What is 'falling into conformity'? The Master said, "A wooden horse roams through spring. The monk asked, "What is 'falling into nobility'? The Master said, "Sitting, yet not occupying the hall."
Ascending loftily into the pure clouds, he stirred the vast ocean with a single chopstick; if he could thus cause the fish and dragons to know their destiny, then Master Song was not without merit.
Yet, it simply did not satisfy the intention of Master Cao. Looking to his left and right, he said, "In this place, there are three falls."
In the governance of the Great Peace, there is originally no sign; the rustic style of the common folk is anciently and most pure.
They simply attend to village songs and community feasts; who knows of the virtue of Shun or the benevolence of Yao?
(By Tianning Hong) Chan Master Zongbao Daodu of Changqing (successor of Boshan Lai). Because a monk asked: "All Buddhas arise from..."
When this sutra emerges, what is this sutra? The Master let out a thunderous shout.
Who can understand this shout in the midst of the light? The bustling universe is wrongly deliberated upon. Where did the autumn wind come from last night?
The great earth is like a single sheet of silver frost. (Desin)

The wind sweeps away the battle clouds, leaving all clear; the dragon bestows its essence upon the seas and mountains. The rain nourishes the common people, while withered branches and decaying stones remain utterly helpless, vainly expending their affection for the Thunder Lord and the Lightning Maiden.
Chan Master Daoyan of Dufeng Zhushan (a successor of Boshan Liaoyi) once posted three questions to test those who came before him. The first said:
"The path to Dufeng Peak is perilous and the checkpoint is strictly guarded; those who wish to arrive must first present a travel permit."

Traveling by water and land alike to the imperial capital, the cold winds and driving snows are more than one can bear. How could it compare to sitting still until the soles of one's feet are worn through? Only when one attains the Way does one realize the precision of one's own hand and eye.
(Zhengguan Zhe) The green mountains rise steeply and the waters flow long; the emerald bamboos and yellow chrysanthemums flourish in the profusion of autumn.

At this very scene and at this very time, those who attain [this state]— (Chengguan Zhe) The green mountains are rugged and the waters flow on forever; the lush bamboo and yellow flowers bloom in the midst of autumn. At this sight and at this moment, those who attain [it]—
[The Master] said: "A young lord of a hundred years’ wealth suddenly becomes a marquis.
Regarding Chan Master Huizhou (Bozan Lai’s successor), when a monk asked: "Zhengjue said, 'When the stone egg has burst and the tamarisk branches have swept the ground, I shall return.
Now that you have succeeded to his seat, will you not return? The Master said: "I am already here."
[The monk] said, "To charge another with a crime they have not committed and impose punishment upon them. [The Master] said, "If that is so, then the case is closed according to the evidence.
The Master said, "I accept this indictment.
"The stone egg bursts open and the yellow crane departs; The tamarisk branches bow low and the phoenix arrives. White artemisia and red sedges on the autumn river."
Cold. The iron flute plays the "Falling Plum Blossoms" for no reason.
(Haihui Xing) Performing as a play upon meeting the occasion, he displays his heroic prowess. As the two armies clash, his spirit is high.
Now that we have met these days of peace where signs are absent, the battle banners do not move, yet the wine-shop flags sway. (Desi Xin)
The family estate is utterly swept away, reduced to bare bones and poverty; beneath the white clouds of the crags, one shifts one’s form in secret.
Treading upon the bird-path, the void turns; within the brocade of heaven and earth, not a speck of dust remains.
(Chongxiao Yu) When Guhang was ascending the hall at Boshan, a monk came forward and asked: "Before the bell has tolled and before the drum has sounded, is there still a Buddha?"
"Dharma is also non-existent. Shanshan said, "The wooden man blows at the bottom of the well; the stone woman dances by the stream.
The Master asked, "How do you express the 'mysterious phrase within words'? Shanshan said, "Midnight is perfectly bright; at dawn, nothing is revealed."
Master Deshi said: "The lofty peak of Mount Bo stands high; though it stands, its summit cannot be seen. The ancient vessel sails deep within the bottom of the ocean;
though it travels there, its feet remain dry. Even if you wish to inquire about the two characters 'Buddha-Dharma,' you still lack awakening."
In spring warmth, they call to one another as they emerge from the emerald heights; walking at times and sitting at others, they have utterly forgotten to return.
At dusk, a sudden squall of east wind and rain makes it impossible to avoid their entire bodies being soaked through.

(Tandengqing) Bare trees and cold crags are entirely free of a speck of dust; frozen clouds deeply lock in the spring upon the mountain peaks. The ice-like skin of the plum blossom transmits its message.
Faith. A hidden, fragrant scent intoxicates with its chill.
At the high Phoenix Pavilion, the morning light rolls up, cold and clear. The civilization of the Great Antiquity is difficult to behold.
Entering directly into the inner palace, one forgets the bolts and locks; the crimson clouds turn to snowflakes to gaze upon. (Tianning Hong)
Upon hearing a rooster flapping its wings and crowing, Chan Master Daofeng of Boshan Xuejian (who succeeded to Bolu Shanlai) attained great enlightenment and said:
"The embers of the cypress seeds are nearly extinguished; A neighbor’s rooster suddenly lets out a single cry. In years past, I mistakenly mistook the donkey for the well;
Today, I finally know the well is looking at the donkey."
The drum at the watchtower has ceased and my dream has just awakened; suddenly I hear the rooster’s cry and the dawn bell.
Do not say that the well-donkey attained enlightenment from this; only when the well-donkey is cast aside does the mind become empty.
(Not a Mirror on a Stand) Chan Master Xinglang Daoxiong of Yefu (successor of Boshan Lai) was asked by a monk: "How does one leap over the tiger's head and grasp its tail?"
"This is still the old nest and trap of people of this age. How can the myriad streams be cut off and the ten thousand functions be brought to rest?
The Master said, "Regarding what you have asked:
it is like Yezhu shedding the iron shackles from his head; yet, for now, there is no one to bear witness."
Tenfold spring upon the Laolao Pavilion—how can one bear to entrust this sentiment of parting to the riverbank?
Having finished singing the "Yangguan" melody in its three repetitions, he borrows the official willows to see off the traveler.
(Haihui Xing) The peach blossoms along both banks are red as fire; the willow catkins filling the embankments are white as silver. A gust of celestial wind comes from where?
In this place, how much spring remains upon the disarrayed branches?
Master Lang’s skill was practiced; he took advantage of the opportunity to mix cat-tail with cat-food. The hawk that has caught its rabbit has already returned home;
how many dogs have been deceived by a withered stump? (Not a mirror on a stand.)
Chan Master Jue-lang Dao-sheng of Tianjie Monastery in Jinling (the successor of Dong-yuan Jing) was invited by the Prince of Jing to ascend the seat.
A monk asked: "Today the Prince of Jing has prepared a vegetarian feast; is there anyone who can receive the offerings of a sovereign?"
The Master said, "The fragrant wind blows away the withered flowers and rains down new and beautiful ones.
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then even Brahma and Śakra should offer praise. The Master said, "Do not blame me for not leaving my bed."
The purple *fuxi* stone reaches up to the clouds; how could it ever wear horns or shed hair? It would rather refuse than allow the eyes of a single monk to be blinded.
Old Man Lang was off by a mere trifle. Here, however, it is not so: is there anyone capable of receiving the offerings of a king?
There are exquisite pastries and dumplings; eat them quickly and bring them here.
The palace eunuch repeatedly adds to the fragrant incense of the jeweled censer. As the moon sets over the vermilion courtyard, it hangs directly above the hall.
If anyone asks about the affairs of the palace, one who is naturally noble and dignified will lazily refuse to leave their bed. (Haihui Xing'er)
Whether in seclusion or in the bustle of society, many raise their own worth while sighing with self-pity. True elegance does not lie in applying rouge and powder;
it requires only genuine feeling when facing an old woman.
At the Phoenix Pavilion soaring above the clouds, the *shao* music resounds; it draws forth immortal maidens of surpassing grace.
Speaking softly with lingering affection, they return to their grotto-dwelling, where one hears only the drifting resonance of their jade rings and pendants.
(From the *Jinduo wen*) In the celestial realm, he visited Dongyuan. Dongyuan asked, "Have you ever heard of Bo Shan’s preaching of the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra*? The Master replied:
Once, Yuan said, "I have heard it said that Maitreya received his prediction of enlightenment after one more lifetime. What do you make of that?
The Master replied, "There are many who harbor doubts about this. Yuan said, "And you yourself go about in such a manner. The Master was struck by this.

Later, while sitting around a brazier, the Master raised the ancient worthy’s dialogue concerning the "blazing kalpa-fire," noting that some say it destroys [all things] while others say it does not. "What is the meaning of this? Yuan said, "You..."
Furthermore, coming thus—afterward, the Master presented what he had seen throughout his life. Yuan was deeply impressed;
black and white were clearly distinguished within this marvelous and subtle realm. The first move at the head seems difficult to encounter, yet one meets a true connoisseur swiftly before the cliff.
The axe is worn away while the chess pieces are consumed; the view is inexhaustible. (Tingshan Chong)
The tiger roars before the crags, giving rise to solitary pride; suddenly, fresh sprouts emerge from withered wood.
Having personally received the rain and dew throughout all time, one turns a new course of life and blows the jade flute.
(Flower Without Leaves) Once awakened, one must still go forth to meet others; within Mount Wuyi lies a treasure lost to its own home. Who knows that this single way of life—?
Distinct. The dream-pen blooms, and spring fills the great earth.
(Zhìyuán Jiàn) A single word, the mechanism met; the will may now be rewarded. Private wealth exhausted, he becomes even more refined.
Last night, the stone woman laughed aloud; ten thousand miles away, a jade tower embraces the heavens. (Zǐyú Zhé)
Tianjie asked, "What is the meaning that cannot be fully expressed by the teachings of the Great Canon?
The Master said, "Tears flow from a heart of pain. He asked, "And what about the final picking up of the flower? The Master said, "If you want the head, chop it off and take it!"
How lamentable are those who mistake the shadows for the person! They point toward the heavy barrier and yet ask for the ford. Alas, their mouths are born too narrow;
they can only pour forth their very liver and gall at once.
Having cast off the flower crown, he forgot his nobility; yielding to others, he sat amidst the green mists.
The *Mahāyāna-artha-sūtra* explains this with profound clarity; in every word, one perceives the Truth without contradiction.
(Hongdingjiao) One day in the celestial realm, a deity asked a monk: "Poverty last year was not yet true poverty; poverty this year is only then true poverty. You—"
"Daoxiangyan, where do you establish yourself and sustain your life? He said, "There is not even a needle; what life could one possibly sustain?
The Master said, "How can a man who has lost his life roll about in the grass? He asked, "Where is it that he rolls in the grass?
The Master said, "A licorice root used as a horsewhip."
The jade flute is blown repeatedly, awakening the mind beyond kalpas; it calls back withered bones to produce the dragon’s cry. The clouds rise from the azure sea, yet no one understands;
they vainly draw forth the golden waves, piercing through past and present.
(Pujie Long) Treading to pieces heaven and earth, he is utterly free of a speck of dust; where there are no traces, do not hide your body. Within the eye of a gnat, he turns his sinews over.
A single combat: leaping upon his horse and raising his whip, he crossed the Mengjin Ford.

(Chongxiao yu) In times of great peace and no affairs, the frontier generals pass their time; before the Muli beacon tower, they raise the signal banners of their oaths. With a shout, the battle clouds rise to fill the sea;
with a single roll of the war drums, the entire army is broken. (Haibui xing)
In times of great peace, one discusses the clash of arms; across ten thousand *li* of battlefields, not even a blade of grass remains.
If you are one who has long served in the ranks, withdrawing the troops depends on a single roll of the gong.
(Zhengjue Zhe) Chan Master Daolin Daopei of Kaiyuan (the worthy successor of Gushan) ascended the hall and said: "The mark of the invisible crown is perfectly round in every individual."
Full. Why do I manifest while you remain hidden? The Lamp-King’s throne has a share for every person.
Why do I sit while you stand? Do you understand? Before the Mohe sword has emerged from its scabbard, there are thousands of miles of drifting silk;
when casually drawn forth, it severs everything at once.
The bright moon and clear breeze lie beyond the solitary isle; white clouds and flowing waters are west of the broken bridge.
A single expanse of cold radiance is as bright as a mirror; it cannot be mixed with, for its kind is not uniform.
(Chong xiao yu) Ziling deeply reclused on Mount Fuchun, idly holding his fishing line at the azure bay. Shrimp and crabs are sparse in the autumn waters.
Silence. The sky, accompanied by the bright moon, returns with the hook.
(Ciyunwen) *Zongjian Faling*, Volume 71; *Zongjian Faling*, Volume 72.
Jiyungtang Collection:
Venerable Elders (Succession of Dharma unknown).
Chan Master Yunding of Dongshan in Fuzhou. A monk asked: "What is the Master’s daily practice?"
The Master said, "I eat my fill; you suffer from hunger. [The monk] asked, "If it is said that 'dharma after dharma does not reach one another,' then how is this?
The Master said, "Whatever transgressions you commit, I know them all."
Falin’s voice says: "When principle does not rely on location, how would one dare to encroach upon it even slightly?
When the Way is unobstructed, how could there ever be a single thing to act as an opponent or a counterpart? This is Dongshan’s point of view.
If one were to judge this according to the school of Falin, it would be precisely like losing one's way in broad daylight. He then offers a verse:
Beyond the waters and across the mountains, longing pulls at my heartstrings; in dreams of spring, I embroider mandarin ducks. Within this state, every dharma fails to reach one another;
the bright moon still shines upon my native land.
Emeralds and jade lie by the greedy fish banks; Azure coins float and swirl within the green waters.
Rising and falling with the wind, entirely unimpeded— In these frequent moments of leisure, there is a world apart.
(Suan Ding) When a monk asked Yunjing, "What is the meaning of the Master’s single branch of the fly-whisk? the Master said, "Break through cultivation."
The monk said, "In that case, then there has originally been nothing at all. The Master asked, "Who is it that knows there is nothing?
The monk said, "It is the student’s fault. The Master said, "You should reflect upon this further."
Falin-yin said: "Whether it be the Buddha who comes or Māra who comes, he cuts them down. Dongshan ultimately did not know where the whisk came from;
had he let it pass indiscriminately, what would this differ from cutting off a crane’s neck to lengthen a duck’s? Yongning Ding said: "What a fine whisk!
This monk could not lift it up, and Dongshan could not employ it. Yongning is accustomed to acting with straightforwardness; he wishes to—"
It is difficult even to analyze:
clouds lock the azure cliffs, flowers fill the brook. When travelers reach this place, they remain lost on the path. A single cry of a bird emerges from the secluded valley;
it is precisely the moment the immortals face each other in a game of Go. (Haihui Xing)
The officials have dispersed at the heavy gates; seals and insignia lie scattered like blades of grass. A single scrap of paper causes one’s hair to stand on end.
If one wishes to inquire about the affairs within the Hall of the Central Secretariat, they are as chaotic as a thicket of swords and halberds amidst the wild weeds.

(Falin-yin) At the summit of the peak, a ten-fathom lotus blooms in the pond; its fragrant breeze awakens the immortals within the cavern. With their caps askew and sandals turned backward, they roam upon the clouds.
Manifesting thus, he stumbles before sounds and forms. (Suan Ding) Yunzhong asked a monk:
"Dongshan said there is 'one thing that reaches up to heaven and down to earth. I wonder what kind of thing this is? The Master said:
"Carrying an iron yoke and eating an iron staff. [The monk] said: "Heaven and earth turn black; mountains and rivers flee."
The Master said, "A ghost is added before the Hall of King Yama; he lies for a thousand years beneath Mount Beimang. The scholar cried out, "What joy!
What joy! The Master said, "That too is a wild fox swallowing a mouse."

Falin’s *Yinyun* states: "Do not taste the water from a household afflicted by *gǔ* poison. Since Dongshan was unable to peer through the innermost heart of Jiaor, how could he avoid bringing this fellow along for a live burial beneath the gate of Dongshan several hundred years later?

He then offers a verse: Do not taste the water from a household afflicted by *gǔ* poison; If you cannot see through the old fellow’s liver and gall, How can you avoid being implicated for several hundred years? This fellow is buried alive beneath the gate of Dongshan. Furthermore, he offers a verse:
An ancient root emerges from before the thorny crags; though many years have passed, it still bears traces of blood-stained scars. One knows not from where the stench of wind has come;
it vainly seeks to restore its soul within the desolate wilderness.
Severing the thousand rivers, white snow falls in profusion. The crimson-tailed fish sinks into exhaustion, its soul darkly consumed.
At midnight, the old fisherman strikes the sounding pole with urgency; crying out at the break of dawn, he wanders lost upon his path.
(Suan Ding) When a monk asked Master Ding of Gaoyou Prefecture, "What does the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eat? the Master replied:
"Dried dung. Falin says:
"At the top of a hundred-foot pole, one does not know the way to turn the body; one vainly twists the nostrils of the Three Sages.
Before a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, one does not understand the mechanism of reaching down with the hand; one merely blurs the eyes of Yunmen. Today..."
When someone asks such a question, Falin ultimately refuses; he possesses only the heart that accepts the jade. Yongning Ding said:
"The price asked was eight hundred, yet the offer was one thousand. This may be called surpassing all past and present.
In this day and age, ten out of five or two pairs are those who turn their backs on Qin and forget Chu; those who examine the belly and inquire into the heart are few."
Iron walls and silver mountains surge forth; struck once upon the head, they turn to ash.
If the scaled dragon could but sprout its horns, it would burst through the blue sky and send thunder crashing back.
(Haihui Xing) He tramples the Buddha’s steps, his hooves sinking into the earth; where the last red petals drift, they leave their mark in fragrant mud. From the clear waves, a pleasure boat emerges.
My son, look afar; the reeds are all one color, a state of bewilderment.
(The Sound of Dharma Forest) Chan Master Daowu of Foguang at Puzhao Monastery in Zhengzhou wore a white shirt, rode a yellow calf, and played a short flute while wandering through Luoyang.
He once said: "If you say I am an ordinary person, I have come from the rank of the sages. If you say...

If you say, "I am a sage," you are returning to the rank of the ordinary; if you say, "I am neither ordinary nor a sage," you are retreating to a separate place of practice atop the crown of Vairocana.
Falin’s *Yinyun* says: "If a Buddha covets even a single grain of rice, he will utterly waste away all the merit cultivated through kalpas of past practice.
Now tell me, where exactly is the point at which he covets that grain of rice?"
In his hand he holds a seven-foot *langgan* staff; piercing clouds and crossing waters, he is as lively as a dragon.
Sometimes he lifts it atop Mount Rong; cleaving through the blue sky, he never lets go.
(Jian’an Yi) Having fashioned a thatched hut beside the twin trees, he follows the staff as he passes over distant peaks. Do not say that he has no dwelling place.
In this place, withered trees filling the mountains seem to utter dragon-sighs (the sound of the Dharma-forest).
Zen Master Sian Si of Lingyun in Wenzhou ascended the hall for the summer retreat and said:
"With the great perfect enlightenment—ox-horns and horse-horns—I make my monastery, my melon basket, and my vegetable basket."
Falin’s *Yinyun* says: "To overturn that which lies beyond the era of Weiyin, there is not a single trace to be found;
to sweep away everything at the threshold of this present age, not even a vestige of habitual tendency remains. Yet, for all intents and purposes, there is no path by which to emerge."
Frosty leaves fly as the moon fills the sky; Leisurely I tune the brocade zither before the window.
If I wish to find a true connoisseur like Zhou Lang, I intentionally mistune the strings from time to time.
(Ciyun Wen) Clearly, day and night grind away through all ages; Busily, the sun and moon leap like twin balls. One knows not for whom this world exists.
Old age. I have preserved the green mountains to gaze upon within a painting.
(Haihui Xing) I have bound a thatched hut beside a winding creek; I leave only my heart’s concerns to face the green mountains.
Dwelling in seclusion, I take no heed of court affairs; all day long, in silence, I keep the gate shut alone. (Falin Yin)
When Chan Master Sigu Daocan arrived at a place, he made it his business to test and examine others.
Upon passing through Xuedou, he remarked, "This old fellow’s mouth is dripping with water. Xuedou said, "Do you not approve of me, monk?
The Master replied, "Indeed, your mouth is dripping with water. He gave a single strike with his sitting cloth and departed. The temple steward was indignant and pursued him.
When they reached the middle of their journey, he injured the Master’s foot. The Master said, "This was caused by this old man.
One day you must break one of your own feet to repay me. Later, Dou indeed suffered as he had said.

Falin’s *Yinyun* says: "Xuedou was 'water-sifting' (straining water) at the bottom; later he broke a leg to repay him. Daocan was also "water-sifting" at the bottom; the steward broke his leg. But has he yet repaid Xuedou? He then offers a verse: The Master of the Hall was water-sifting at the bottom; The Guest Prefect broke a leg to repay him. If you ask me what this is like— It is like a dog licking its own teeth. The Master of the Hall was water-sifting at the bottom; The Guest Prefect broke a leg to repay him. My poet’s heart is but slightly broader than my wine-drinker’s; though I drink deeply and wield the brush, my inspiration remains undiminished. Cold smoke draws in the rain as it rushes into the chamber;
willow-bows and reed-arrows carry the very essence of my heart.

Anger is not anger; striking is likewise not striking. Receiving an ox from one person and returning a horse to another—like singing a "White Snow" or "Yangchun" melody, the lofty notes have few who can harmonize.
It is clear that these two one-legged ones know the rites. (Planting trees on the mountain.
The Great Master Zhu Hong, known as Yunqi Lianchi of Hangzhou, visited Xiaoyan at Liuxiang to seek instruction.
Yan said, "You have come from three thousand *li* away to instruct me; what instruction do I have for you?

The Master was suddenly enlightened and took his leave to return home. While traveling on the road through Dongchang, he heard the sound of the drum from the watchtower and attained a great awakening.
He composed a verse, saying: "The events of thirty years ago remain suspicious; What marvel was this meeting at three thousand *li*? I burn incense and cast [the dice]..."
The clash between the halberd and the void is but a trivial matter; demons and Buddhas vainly contend over right and wrong.
Chengtian Xing said: "Although Yunqi has attained awakening, alas, he has fallen halfway.
If you wish to return home and sit securely, you must turn your head back and see Xiaoyan once more before you can succeed. Falin Yin said: "Return."
On the southern slope of Mount Ma, he grazed his oxen in the wilds of Peach Forest.
Although he yielded three times when facing south and twice when facing north, he nonetheless attained the empire through military conquest. Once again, let us offer praise.

Having finished my tour of the upper gardens, I arrived at the riverbank; reds and yellows fill my eyes, entering my dreams again and again. When my兴致 (xìngzì) has ended and I return, there is nowhere to be found;
my true hometown does not lie in Western Qin.
When the waters reach Mount Yan, the mind is not upright; One bumps one’s head and encounters a head-wind.
Piteously, the drum of Dongchang is crushed to pieces; All family possessions lost, both hands are empty.
(Ciyun Wen) Outside the gate of Dongchang, the drum beats loudly; Suddenly, the void collapses to the ground. Having picked up a single shard from the red furnace...
Snow. Yet it is the ice of the Yellow River in the sixth month. (Yuyai Yuan) When the Minister Wang Zongmu asked Yunqi, "Last night the mice were chirping and recited the entire Avatamsaka Sutra;

what happens when the cat suddenly appears? Wang was speechless. The Master provided his own verse for him: Snow. Yet it is the ice of the Yellow River in the sixth month. (Yuyai Yuan) Cloud Rest [Monastery] [responded] to Senior Secretary Wang Zongmu’s question: "Last night the mice were chirping and reciting the entirety of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
What happens when the cat suddenly appears? Wang was speechless. The Master provided his own verse on his behalf: Snow. Yet it is the ice of the Yellow River in the sixth month. (Yuyai Yuan)
The Dharma Master fled, leaving behind his lecture desk, whereupon he composed this verse: "The mouse squeaks; the *Avataṃsaka* is clear and distinct. How strange!
Minister Wang, you have been deluded by a beast. A cat suddenly leaps out before the painted hall;
at the head of the bed, the preaching of the Dharma leaves no trace. No trace—this is the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*, the World-Ruling Sovereigns’ Wondrous Adornment Chapter."
First, Falingyin said:
"If one cannot pursue questions beyond the framework [of conventional logic] nor maintain the essence beyond the framework, how can one be considered a skilled practitioner?
This results in kings and dukes dying beneath the words [of the teaching]. Have you not heard it said that, generally speaking, a true master must not..."
It is but a single path. Again, he offers this verse:
The moon in Vairocana’s pavilion is dim and hazy; In every land and every atom, there is no difference or sameness.
How laughable that Sudhana has nowhere to seek it— Its pure light is scattered in profusion against the eastern whitewashed wall.

The western wind stirs sorrow amidst the green waves; the fragrant lotuses have faded, their emerald leaves withered. Returning from a dream in the fine rain, the roosters cry out as the frontier passes far away;
on the small tower, the jade flute is blown until its notes grow cold.
(Suan Ding) Master, layer upon layer, you accompany me through layer upon layer. One night we spoke deeply of the emptiness of the ocean of nature. Twenty-four banners, a level bed.
"Earth. Who knows who struck the bell of the Jade Tower?
(Biancai Hai). At Yunqi, a monk asked: "Can Chan meditation and the recitation of the Buddha's name be harmonized? The Master said:
"If they were two separate things, how could they be harmonized?"
Falin said: "Heaven and earth share one principle; the myriad dharmas are of one suchness. The Great Master has indeed exhausted his realization of this;
it is only that the central pillar of the house still awaits another to come and secure it."
The white plum blossoms on Gushan are not caused by snow; the fragrance arising in the snowy valley is not from plum.
When both plum and snow are forgotten, their noble form is revealed, and a subtle, lingering fragrance comes to invade the senses.
(Ning Shouheng) I divined a secluded dwelling within Taoyuan Cave; there, fowl, dogs, mulberry trees, and hemp abound in abundance. Having gathered Huangjing roots, I grind them with white [snow].
The Art: At once gather the medicinal gourds. (Haihui Xing) Bamboo shoots and ferns fill the mountains;
tea fills the gardens. Scattered before the cliffs, they vie with the evening glow.
Returning from the midnight dream, a single glance reveals that every flavor need not be sought afar. (Falin Yin)
Yunqi’s Address to the Assembly on a New Year’s Day: Today we celebrate the New Year; the seasons have changed once again.
But what was it like yesterday? On the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month.
Falin said: "To take the head for the tail, and to take the tail for the head—unaware that the four seasons shift in secret, how can one concern oneself with the passage of days and months?
To this, I further grant you a broom; make it your livelihood before the gates of the guest houses."
The green mountains stretch out their necks in the sunlight; the clear waters lift their brows at night. Grasping the pen, I judge the void and paint forth the ancient Zhong Kui.
(By Jie Hongliang) The Taoist of Huayang chants over his golden bell; the Master of Ghost Valley blesses his divination tubes. There is only Wang the Great of the Eastern Village.
Brother, my wife burns paper money to send off the Year-End Ghost.

(Haihui Xing) The colors of water and the light of mountains all enter the poem. A flight of wild geese casts their shadows in staggered formation. After drinking, one knows not the narrowness of heaven and earth;
when the moon comes, the plum blossoms shift outside the window. (Falin Yin)
Yunqi once inscribed his own portrait, saying: "Nine out of ten strokes fail to capture the likeness; this vexes the painter to no end.
Perhaps this one comes close enough, so I shall leave it here provisionally as an object of veneration. If you say this is the true likeness, you are still off by two *zhang*.
Not being off by two *zhang*? Thirty blows!"
Ciyun’s commentary states: "Yunqi Daoxuan comes close to this; it is much like trying to judge the density of flowers in the sky or comparing the length of a rabbit's horn. Falin Yin says:

"Even if the confession comes from the prisoner's own mouth, he still deserves thirty blows; yet [the master] only allows half of them to be carried out. He then offers this verse: [Verse omitted as per instructions to provide only the translation of the provided text.]
Three monkeys tossing coins at night; turning them over and over, center and edge are lost.
Forgetting the path back from the cliff’s edge, they vainly distinguish upper and lower heavens beneath the water.
A bald broomstick picked up, skillfully used to paint the brows; Red earth smeared on the lips, making Xi Shi look beautiful. I pity the people of Yue, their smoke and clouds gathering thick;
At the top of Yongcui Tower, they mistakenly recognize her. (Suan Ding) She combs her cloud-like hair and arranges her palace makeup;
In ten turns of spring breeze, nine times her heart breaks. The water lily flower is shattered, yet both reflect [the light]. (Ssu-an Ding)
"Shadow! At once it would put even Du Weiniang to shame. (Huanliu hears this.

Zibo Daguan, the Great Master Zhinao, upon hearing the recitation that "to sever delusive thoughts is to increase one's illness, and to pursue True Suchness is likewise a deviation," was greatly perplexed.
One day during a vegetarian meal, he suddenly attained great enlightenment and said: "It was this which made me..."
Under the guidance of Linji and Deshan, one is awakened by a single slap of the hand; what need is there for "how" or "what"?

Falin Yin said: "That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure. Since it cannot flow forth from the breast, even if one forces open their sleepy eyes, they are merely leaning against the door or standing by the eaves.
By the painting of the Eight Steeds, their fleet hooves leap forth; they overturn their stalls and sheds, casting off their bridles and bits.
Had Bian Que looked upon them at that time, one could surely have had a thousand pieces of gold spent on crafting brocade saddles for them.

(Ning Shouheng) A mad monkey wails for the moon as it clings to an ancient tree; a fierce tiger roars in the wind as it crouches on a precipice. In the human world, there is yet another way to reach the heavens.
The Road. It is not necessary to travel from within this following crowd.
(Ascending with grandeur: Pure wind and bright moon linger together; alone by the stream’s edge, I seek my old haunts. Turning past the crags, I happen upon a smile;
as the sun rises over Fusang, the sea gates are autumnal. (The sound of the Dharma-forest.)
Chan Master Wunian Shendao of Huangbo in Ruizhou was asked by a monk, "Does the fruit of the Way exist, or does it not exist?
The Master said, "To say it exists or to say it does not exist—both constitute slander. The monk asked, "How then may one attain it? The Master said, "Seeking nothing, one attains it.
The monk asked, "What is the essence of the Way? The Master said, "Though my mouth is full, it cannot express it. The monk asked, "The four... [text fragment]
"What about at the time of the great dissolution? The Master raised his fist and said, "This does not belong to the four elements.

Falin Yin remarked: "When grasped, the sea is vast and the mountains are distant; when let go, not even a speck of dust remains. If one can penetrate this, I allow them to study alongside the ancient Buddhas; yet you must further know that there is one person above this. He then offered a verse:

When the four elements disperse, The fist is raised in the void. Not belonging to earth, water, fire, or wind, It is neither existent nor non-existent. If you can see through this, You will be a peer of the ancient Buddhas. But you must still know: There is one person beyond this.
There is no need to laboriously plant crabapples at the bottom of the well; peaches and plums fill the garden, all of them pure gold. Wandering for ten thousand miles, one has not yet returned home;
how pitiable, the bright moon reflecting upon the heart of the waves.
Having traversed ten thousand mountains and myriad peaks, it is difficult to turn one’s body within the shadows of white clouds. For your sake, I shall point out the path beyond the tip of the staff;
you must believe that Kuru is not in the south. (Biancai Hai). Wunian asked a monk:
"The ancients pressed together their throats, lips, and mouths and said, 'Bring forth a single phrase. What about this one?"
"How do you speak a phrase? The Master said, "I have not closed my throat, lips, and mouth; now you, tell me a phrase.
The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Your mouth has been blocked by sounds."
Falin’s *Yinyun* says: "As for this monk being choked by sound and voice, let that be for now. But tell me, you old fellow of No-Thought—have you managed to escape it or not?
An old general guards the frontier pass; the Xiongnu are struck with cold dread. Returning to his native land in times of peace, he writes a formal report of the subduing of the barbarians.
(From the Samādhi-born Pure) Border Pass:
How could one listen to the false crowing of a cock? Chariots and horses pass with a whistling sound, yet are not permitted to proceed. The border official speaks in vain of his extreme severity;
from of old, the seals and passes must be clearly distinguished. (Falin’s Verse)
Chan Master Fangtan Yifeng of Baima Temple in Kuizhou was once asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
The Master replied, "Fire burning at both ends, with smoke at only one."
Falin-yin said: "The great purport of the West—how could the paths be limited to ten thousand? This fellow merely compares them by a tiny fraction;
it simply does not do to fabricate arbitrarily. He then offered this verse:
Whistling in the breeze, a transcendent upon the palm; He idly drapes his twin sleeves as he winds through clouds and mist. With a single high song, heaven and earth darken;
The shadow of the pagoda is inverted, plunging into the sky beneath the waves.

"Longing for plums to quench thirst is too much cleverness. Let the saliva flow in the mouth and cheeks as you swallow and spit; no provisions need be carried on the road, and no doors need be bolted.
Singing songs and drumming their bellies, they fill the entire universe. (Sulan Ding) Yifeng constantly held a small hand-drum (*taogu*) in his hand;
on one side was written the character "Chù" (矗), and on the other side was written the character "Bēn" (犇).
Generally, when responding to the capacities of others, he frequently raised [his staff] and shook it.

Falingyin said: "It is not that there was nothing at all under the gate of Yifeng; however, were this the case today, how would it differ from carrying water to the riverhead only to sell it there? He then offered a verse:
Divine heads and ghostly faces in countless varieties—when brought forth before the assembly, they are no ordinary things. Who can truly comprehend this one song or two?
Yet, with a silk fan, one hides a face flushed with shame.
The divine edge met face-to-face reveals no form; Splatters of blood, scattered like spring rain. Do living beings, dazed and bewildered, know how to return?
How lamentable that morning and evening they lie beneath the green shade.
(Suan Ding) Master Xian of Yang’an at Ehu in Guangxin Prefecture painted a great circle on the wall, within which he wrote:
Do not let it be smeared black; when writing on the outside, do not allow it to mar the white.
If there is anyone who can provide annotations both inside and outside the circle, I will permit you to study the Way. Otherwise, you are all merely full of self-satisfaction.
Falin-yin said: "The orthodox does not establish the profound; the partial does not attach itself to things.
Geyu has exerted all his strength to manifest this, yet who after a thousand years can avoid the fault of being 'dark oneself while making others bright'? Yongning Ding said:
"Geyu has pointlessly drawn lines on the ground to create a prison, seeking to cut off the feet of everyone in the world. Little does he realize..."
Bringing misfortune upon oneself, one falls directly into hell.
Before the Hall of the Bright Moon, the precious mirror opens; there is no ground for arranging the orthodox or the deviant.
How much better it is to host a banquet within the chamber, raising cups and moving the counting sticks while guessing in secret. (Haihui Xing)
It has drunk dry the clear waters of several branches of the Xiang River; far away, the moon’s chariot-wheel begins to shine at night.
Ten thousand bushels of rabbit-light have no place to hide; countless travelers wander within their dreams.
(Falin Yin) Master Yang’an once placed a "Gateless Lock" in his chamber to test those who would come. He spoke in verse: "Transmitted from antiquity..."
The Lock. Rely on your own key of wisdom to open it. If you lack the method for opening the lock, there is no need to come even if we meet.
Falin-yin said: "Tell me, is this a lock with no door, or is it not a lock with no door? He then offered this verse:
Along the road, yellow flowers bloom in every fresh hue; Passersby vainly follow the dust raised by horse hooves. Several times they lose the path they came upon;
Amidst bitter rain, they again hear the frequent calls of the cuckoo.
The gates and walls are ten thousand fathoms high—who can peer within? How many children have entered the chamber and ascended the hall?
If they are one’s own flesh and blood, the family traditions will fall into ruin and be scattered in fragments.
(Suan Ding) The Great Master Deqing of Mount Han at Caoxi in Shaoyou read the *Zhao Lun* until he reached the passage on the Brahmin who left home to become a monk. He said:
He returned with his head bowed. A neighbor saw him and asked, "Is that former man still here? The Brahmin replied, "I am the same man as before, yet I am not the man of before.
Suddenly he had an awakening and said, "Only today have I realized that my nostrils point downward.
Miaofeng asked, "What have you attained? The Master replied, "Last night, two earthen oxen fought and entered the water together. [This continued] until...
Now that all news has ceased, Feng laughed and said, "I am glad you have the capital for staying on the mountain.
Chengtian Xing said, "Although Master Han knows his nostrils point downward, he certainly does not know his eyebrows are above."
Falin-yin said: "The original capital for dwelling in the mountains is certainly not lacking; however, if you wish to see the Brahmin, you have not yet reached that point.
Why did Miaofeng not provide him his proper portion of fodder at that time? He then offered this verse:
Where does the ancient immortal blow his iron flute? With every note, he summons my native land back to me. A hundred years of old dreams are as if only yesterday;
All boundless thoughts are reduced to ashes in this very moment.
Hanshan visited Xiangyan Bao. Xiangyan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From the South. Xiangyan asked, "Do you remember the path by which you came?
The Master said, "Once passed, it is finished. Xiangyan said, "In that case, your place of origin is clear.
The Master then prostrated.
Falin said: "One person is coarse and superficial; the other is dull and ignorant.
Both fellows have their heels kicked up into mid-air, and even until now they have not yet touched the ground."
Traveling south through rugged paths for three thousand *li*, On land there are carriages, on water there are boats.
Though one may pass with clear official credentials, For straw sandals, one must still pay the fee.
(Jian’an Yi) Peach blossoms in the cave drift with the stream; Who is it rowing a light boat therein? The family members suddenly recall those years...
The matter: In the sixth month, coolness arises in the myriad wells; autumn has arrived.
(Falin-yin) As soon as the heel moves, one has already gone astray. Coming from the south, moreover, the road is far.
Even if the place of origin is clear, upon close examination, one has not yet reached home. (Chongxiao-yu)
Chan Master Wengu Guangyin of Zhenji in Hangzhou went to visit Master Zhuan of Longchi. At that time, the Master was warming himself in the sun at the foot of the steps.
The Master asked, "Where is the Master? Zhuan replied, "Just at this moment, he is not here. The Master then prostrated;
Zhuan then ceased his activity and departed.

Falin-yin said: "Regarding 'the eyes of one who possesses them and one who does not' in the context of prostrating before True Stillness—nowadays, teachers and monks do nothing but talk of 'setting the whole platter out,' and they even say this is 'accepting all failures. If you understand it in such a way, how can you possibly succeed?
Yongning Ding said: "To come in such a manner and yet depart in such a manner—if these are the words for leaving the gate, then even if one were to [employ] the four elements..."
Circling about the various continents, have you ever dreamed of this place?
Deep within Penglai, jade forms the screens; the eyes turn green at the boundless misty waves. One knows not where the immortal maidens dwell;
one hears only the rhythmic *ding-ding* of wood being hewn. (Falin’s Verse)
As we parted, our arms were clasped with lingering hesitation; our repeated instructions were imbued with a profound sense of parting.
On the evening return, the mountain paths were slippery; looking back, do you still recognize me, your old friend?
(Suan Ding) Clouds seal the Qin trees, and moss seals the road. From where has this fisherman come to intrude? Across the shore, he calls out with earnest courtesy to the immortal.
"Son," he said, "a crane has just returned from atop the pines.
(From *Ciyun wen*) When Zhenji was about to depart, Daoci escorted him to the gate. Patting the Master’s back, Daoci said, "Old nephew, I still have my doubts about you.
The Master asked, "Doubt what about me? Daoci said, "What is the secret transmission of its meaning? The Master replied: [The text ends here.]
"Today I shall not turn back from Yixing. Master Chi laughed heartily. The Master donned his bamboo hat and departed. Falin Yin said:
"Even if one were to don the hat and depart, it would still be a secret transmission of its intent; this is truly an enigma for all eternity."
Li Bai was about to set out upon his boat when he suddenly heard the sound of songs accompanied by rhythmic foot-stamping on the bank.
The waters of the Peach Blossom Spring pool are a thousand feet deep, yet they do not equal the depth of Wang Lun’s affection for me.
(Haihui Xing) Wild waters shimmering reflect the lengthening of my sorrow; the father and son of the farming household are busy for whom? Their rain-cloaks hang high as the sun sets.
Outside, the wheat is green and the barley is yellow. (Falin’s tone) An old fisherman casts his line by the banks of the Qujiang;
appearing and disappearing amidst the misty waves, he has lost count of the years of spring.
He says of himself that by his solitary boat on the cold waters, he has never encountered a man who remains sober alone. (Dingsheng’s pure [verse])
One day, Chan Master Fasheng of Poshan Cave in Haiyu said to Yan Tianchi, "Last night, Qionglong Mountain nodded its head.
I do not know what you, Layman, would say about it. Do not say that the Buddhas of the three periods have their mouths hanging on the eastern wall;
if you, Layman, are as carefree and unencumbered as this, it will not hinder my being open-mouthed and harmonious."
Hehe. Chengtian Xing said, "Dongwen, you old master, spit blood at people; you have first defiled your own mouth.
Not only will Master Yan find this unbearably bitter, but Qionglingshan cannot help but laugh coldly. Falin Yin said, "Even if one were to sprinkle..."
Sā luo luo du duo he he. The Qionglong Mountain nods its head in agreement. Again, he recites:
White artemisia and red leaves—neither have a fixed time. In dreams, the passes and mountains; the moon arrives late. Chang’an lies a thousand miles away, yet there is no place to dwell.
Dipping my fingertips in blood, I write this autumnal longing.
Wishing to visit old haunts by lake and mountain, I happened upon a noble guest on a small boat. We spoke clearly until the moonlight within the cabin window faded;
perhaps the lake and mountains did not nod their heads in approval. (By Biancai Hai).
At Dajian Temple in Shuntian Prefecture, Chan Master Bianrong Zhenyuan was asked by Lu Wutai: "As for..."
"What is the wisdom of Mañjuśrī? The Master said, "Not following external objects apart from the mind. "What is the practice of Samantabhadra? The Master said, "Harmonizing all states of mind.
"What is the Dharma-realm of Vairocana? The Master said, "The non-obstruction of phenomena in every particular.
Lu sighed in admiration and said, "From this day forward, I understand that the myriad differences are of one essence."
Falin’s *Sound of the Dharma* says: "Liu Wutai only knows that the myriad differences are one essence, but he does not know that the one essence is the myriad differences.
What is the wisdom of Mañjuśrī? Like a blind man feeling an elephant. What is the practice of Samantabhadra?

Habitually loathing the dragging of plows and the pulling of harrows. What is the Dharmadhātu of Vairocana? Having fled from the brothel, one has not yet repaid the wine debt. For now, let him remain in doubt."
Seven years have passed.
A single petal of peach blossoms is as red as fire; The willows along the embankment are as green as mist. When the moon sets over the peach blossoms, butterflies are lost;
In the deep spring of the willows, the cuckoo cries out in grief. (Ding Shengchun)
The three peaks of Mount Hua stand inverted against the sky; for whom do the pure breeze and bright moon return?
Watching idly where wild birds settle in their nests, my gray beard hangs drooping, falling again and again. (Falin Yin).
Master Fuyuan of the ancient Yan Temple in Tanzha, Shuntian Prefecture, went back to visit Kuole. Kuole said, "You have come."
"Yes. "Look at one phrase from the intimate place of the Way. The Master stepped forward and said, "On this day, I respectfully wish the Venerable Master ten thousand blessings.
[The Master] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master replied, "My mouthful of teeth are all bone;
my ears are two pieces of skin. Lezuo said, "When have you ever seen Yuanming? The Master then asked, "How about it?"
"This is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma. Lehe raised his staff. As the Master hesitated, Lehe struck him, saying, "A mouth full of nothing but bones;
ears made of two pieces of skin. Only then did the Master achieve great awakening.
Falin said: "If awakening were located in the sphere of perfect luminosity, one would truly not know that the teeth are bone and the ears are skin.
If awakening were located in the sphere of vast bliss, how could one have ever seen perfect luminosity come into being?"
Planting banana trees amidst the flames of a red furnace, A hundred-foot sprout grows tall and upright.
Sudden rains and wild winds rage throughout the night; Who knows who leans against the high green heavens?
(Haihui Xing) Clouds gather thickly by the Magpie Bridge, The moon is hazy by the River of the Astronomer’s Pole. The ancients shared the autumn from afar.
Regretful sighs; unaware, my entire body is drenched in tears like a rainbow.

(Falin’s Verse) From of old, the warrior’s spirit has been like a rainbow. Barefoot, he swept across the void to the east of the sea. With one hand he grasps the clouds, with the other he brings down rain.
In a stern voice, he rouses the dragon from the azure depths.
Chan Master Yuanliang of Baoding Xiaoshan addressed the assembly: "How could a turtle ever run out of a jar? A shrimp may leap, but it never leaves the measure.
If one lacks a firm and resolute mind when entering the world, one will wander aimlessly through the cycles of the six realms."
Brothers, we have now entered the Mountain of Jewels; is there anyone who returns empty-handed?
If there is, they must receive three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred blows in the evening.
Baonun Chun said: "If you speak of a 'solid heart,' once you have escaped the cycle of the six realms of rebirth, you will enter hell again as swiftly as a shooting arrow.

Falin Yin said: "If you wish to achieve liberation from the cycle of the six realms of rebirth, you must first eliminate the solid heart; only then can it be attained. He then offered this verse: To escape the cycle of the six realms, One must first cast away the solid heart.
Only when this heart is removed Can one truly attain liberation.
Three thousand blows at dawn, eight hundred at dusk; when will the wandering through the six realms ever cease? Mount Bao laughs until he falls over, Huang Fanquo;
how could a turtle ever run away from inside a jar?
With heads scorched, foreheads blistered, and hair disheveled, the true mechanism is expounded in vain as faith fails to penetrate. This is not yet a mouth capable of trapping tigers;
even so, with teeth missing, one cannot engage in the wind.
At that time, Zen Master Yunju Zhuan’u Guanheng of Nankang Prefecture was told by the monk Wen:

“The methods of those in other quarters, though they may be skilled at killing people, will inevitably leave traces of blood. Yet when you, Master, kill people, let alone traces of blood, there is not even a breath left behind.
The Master replied, “You have come once again to defile this sick monk.”
Falin’s Verse on Sound: Do not speak of bloodstains; one has never even touched a blade.
When the Fisherman of Xiao and Xiang meets the Third Lord, If he lets his solitary boat loose at sunset, Be careful of the waters upon the Muro River;
At night, do not dwell deeply on the orchids and fragrant herbs. (Haichui Xing)
Shallow water in a level field—let it rest. Meeting on a narrow path brings more than enough sorrow. Watch where the waders and clams contend;
there is only the old fisherman nodding his head in secret. (Falin’s Verse) Yunju asked a monk:
"What kind of skill did the old woman possess that she burned down the hut? The Master said: "All offerings..."
"Among all forms of sustenance, the Dharma-sustenance is supreme. The attendant said, "The Master has already departed; I do not yet understand what the underlying meaning was.
The Master replied, "A bright spear is easy to dodge, but a hidden arrow is difficult to guard against."
Falin said: "In that case, do you not wrong the old woman? In that case, do you not wrong the abbot?
If you wish for neither to be wronged, why not come and ask Falin? He then offered this verse:
Tall, swaying green willows line the water’s edge; Passersby who reach this place are all left bewildered. The long river is like a single strip of silk, washed perfectly clean;
Who can distinguish the sails of the ships above from those below?

At a roadside inn, the spring breeze lifts the wine banner; travelers rein in their horses, saliva dripping from their mouths. Time and again they wish to drink at this house, yet fear unfastening their sable furs to pay for the wine.
(Dingsheng Chun) Let the white clouds rise and fall as they will upon the green mountains;
following my own whim, I enter deep into the layers of *bìluó* vines. Sleeping in the dew and lodging in the grass, I am utterly without care.
Obstruction. Furthermore, seeing the moon on the mountain peak as a lamp (Iron Mechanism Faith).
When a monk asked Yunju, "What are the two kinds of roots? the Master said, "The nature of fire is scorching; the nature of water is moist."
Falin’s *Yinyun* says: "There are two kinds of roots. Yunju [Dongshan Liangjie] spoke this quite clearly.
If someone were to question Falin about this today, he would simply settle the case based on the facts. Furthermore, he offers this verse:
A favorable breeze and gentle rain pass over the river ahead. Scarlet leaves fall in profusion, carrying their sorrow back home. Awakening from my midnight dream, I cannot bear to look;
The two peaks hang indistinctly, half-suspended in the void.
The nature of fire is dry; the nature of water is moist. Even a monk with clear eyes finds it difficult to distinguish between them.
One gourd and two ladles. A cast-iron caltrop hurled right in one’s face.
(By Yang Mingxu) Yunju was asked by a monk, "What is the eternally abiding true mind? The Master said, "The green mountains rise steeply."
The water flows on forever. [A monk] asked, "How far apart are the true mind and delusive thoughts? The Master said, "The yellow chrysanthemums are in full bloom;
the green bamboos rustle gracefully.
Falin Yin remarked, "Clearly, these words do not distinguish between the biased and the correct, nor do they know what is inverted or deviant. To use them to guide others is a calamity."
Shengfalin’s critique in this manner—do not say it is merely the perspective of an old woman. Deshi Xin said:

"Tearing open the gateway of the face, he alone surpasses all past and present; yet even so, he is still short by a little. As for the two minds of truth and falsehood, he cannot avoid making the pillar burst out laughing."
As the evening sun slants and the wind blows, wild geese play upon the sands; I can do no more than entrust my thoughts to the drifting mists.
I know not whether the mists can truly match my heart, as they divide into a thousand million households across the vast expanse.

(Falin’s Rhymes) The moon reflects upon Dongting Lake where the autumn waters are cold; the azure clouds have dispersed, leaving the heavens of Chu wide and open. The wind is gentle and the waves are still, as flat as—
The palms move as the stars dance within the jade basin;
days grow long and the wind is warm, the willows turn a lush green. Northern geese fly back into the profound darkness.
On the Yuelang Tower, I idly blow my flute, winning a spring heart that fills the entire Lake Dongting. (Xiao of Chian Monastery)
Cuiyan Guxue Tongzhe Chan Master ascends the hall for the opening of the furnace. Cuiyan opens the great forge;
there is not a single piece of firewood or charcoal. With a pair of bare hands and empty fists, he smelts away all mundane sentiments and intellectual interpretations.
But tell me, after they have been completely smelted, what is it like? A cricket swallows a crab amidst the flames.

Falin said: "The provisional establishment of this one period is sufficient to be called the work of a master craftsman. Yet, as for that gold which leaps from the crucible, it naturally possesses a distinct life of its own.
He further composed a verse:
The cicada in the fire swallows the crab; once the nose is pained, one’s heart turns sour.
Throughout past and present, these heroic spirits have needlessly gouged out their own healthy flesh.

A cold wind suddenly rises as the azure sky clears; a few stray clouds pass over the eastern ridges. The white snow makes the mountain valleys cold through the three winters, yet when the sun returns, the great earth blooms with ten thousand flowers in red.
The West River has been sucked dry, not a single drop remaining; throughout the four seas, communication is now severed.
With bare hands, he overturns the lairs of both ordinary beings and sages; even centipedes and crabs all become dragons.
(Biancai Hai) Cuiyan was asked by a monk, "What is one's original face? The Master said, "The stone pedestal before the steps."
The monks prostrated. The Master said, "Look, look! The foundation stone is moving! Faling Yin remarked, "That which moves is the stone; the foundation stone itself does not move.

Nowadays, there is a certain class who borrow the shrimp as their eyes and say, "Guxue borrows an event to clarify the mind, and uses an object to manifest the principle. He then offered this verse: The Master said, "Look, look! The foundation stone is moving! Faling Yin remarked, "That which moves is the stone; the foundation stone itself does not move.
Nowadays, there is a certain class who borrow the shrimp as their eyes and say, "Guxue borrows an event to clarify the mind, and uses an object to manifest the principle. He then offered this verse:
Carrying my staff, I wander alone through mists and clouds; having found the mists and clouds, I no longer think of home. Do not say that the traces of the immortals are nowhere to be found;
it is simply that many fine mountains are hidden by the clouds.
A single blow shatters the cave of spirits; a pungent wind spreads across the earth, chilling those who encounter it.
It stirs the dense forest, making the mountain streams turn azure; on the road home, one celebrates this new sound.

(Suan Ding) Having entered Zhongnan to plant fields of *huoju* roots, I have mistakenly been called an "Immortal of the Cavern. When the spring wine ferments at the jar’s mouth, longevity is attained.
Wine. Drunk all day long, he sleeps upon a stone pillow.
(Huanliu Wen) When Cuiyan was presented with a verse by a monk that contained the line, "The myriad phenomena reveal their true countenance," the Master asked, "What is the true countenance?
The monk replied, "Only after the snowfall does one know the integrity of the pine and cypress. The Master said, "The pine and cypress are themselves among the myriad phenomena."
"How is it that one's true countenance is revealed? He replied, "The entire mechanism is manifest alone. The Master said, "After it is manifest, what then?
He replied, "There is no dharma outside the mind. The Master then struck him.
De’an Xin said, "This monk has a path for his own emergence at every turn; he did not see a master in vain. If...

This is not the essential hammer and tongs of Cuiyan; it cannot withstand examination. Nevertheless, even so, if you arrive at the gate of a true monk, he will not let you off even if his staff breaks.
Chan Master Létán Yuánbái Tōngkě of Jiangxi ascended the hall and said: "A dead snake is treated as a live one and played with;
the daughter of the Cáo family has had a reputation for elegance for a thousand ages. Xuefeng flung down his staff—truly a way to startle people.
Bǎofēng flung down his staff—is there any monk here who wants to be startled? To deliberate upon this on level ground amidst a thousand peaks."
Mutually steep and lofty, each takes its place within the hall.
"Breaking the ancient mirror," Falinyin said: "Even if you were to break the ancient mirror, it would still be like playing with a live snake as if it were a dead one."
A dragon soars through the clouds, its crimson tail lashing; Fragrant winds blow in gusts as rain falls in drifts. Without cause, it stirs the waters of the vast ocean;
Upon level ground, waves surge ten thousand fathoms high.

(Ning Shouheng) Bamboo leaves interlace, a lush green welcoming the eyes; Peach blossoms bloom profusely, their crimson hues adorning the cheeks. The Lord of Spring divides his hands evenly between them.
Entrusted. The ninety days of spring are like a dream. (Falin Yin) Words emerge from the seamless, round sphere;
cast east and west with a mind at ease. A barefoot Persian has just stepped upon it;
his entire body is unaware that his very pores and hair stand cold. (Suan Ding)
Yuanbai ascended the hall and said: "Sometimes my words and phrases are as hard as iron; sometimes my words and phrases are as soft as cotton.
When meeting ginger, they are pungent; when meeting salt, they are salty. But tell me, when encountering the Patriarch Bodhidharma, what are they like?"
The Sanskrit language of the Western Heaven;
the Chinese language of this Eastern Land. Cheng Tianyi said: "Although Lestan has the waves of its deep waters, it lacks the surging billows that reach the heavens.
Falinyin said: "I, Falin, do not think so. When encountering Bodhidharma, what would you be like? Call him over and drag him here!"
Grinding and revolving, she is summoned to pull the plow as she meanders along. Again, she offers this verse:
All day long she has no other business than to skillfully adorn herself, Tying and knotting a "heart-to-heart" hairpin to send to her lord. Does my lord’s heart know it is as mine?
The mandarin ducks bear but empty tears in a thousand rows.
The waning moon sinks low, its chill soaking the pond; Willow shadows on the level bridge reflect in the deep pool. Passersby, do not stand by the railing;
It is precisely the moment when dreams are severed within the inner chambers.
(Suan Ding) Having given away all one’s private possessions to others, One gains for oneself only a life of poverty. Throughout one's travels, one bites at the pig.
A dog. Its teeth and jaws are like iron nails.
Chan Master Ji Cui Weiyi Puzhun addressed the assembly: "Hemp is exchanged for cloth; silk is exchanged for gauze. What is bought is expensive;
what is sold is cheap. Therefore it is said: 'When the cup falls to the ground, the plate shatters into seven pieces. Do not—"

"Movement does not shift it; it neither transmigrates nor changes. Holding up his staff, he said, "If you can directly take this up, I shall divide the Tiger Brook Valley with you and give you half the monastery.
Falingyin said, "Taking this up is not difficult, but I fear that 'half the monastery' might become a point of attachment. Indeed, even old grain and rotten mushrooms [can cause such clinging].
Hemp. To pick it up and display it is not without merit as a skillful hand; yet, were one a true master of the Way, they would simply cover their nose and spit.

The dragon emerges from the sea, its clouds filling the islands; the tiger shakes the forest trees, stirring the roots of the crags. When the rain has ceased and the wind is spent, there is no further trace;
yet the dragon and tiger are summoned to guard the bamboo gate. (Haihui Xing)
The shadows of cassia sway, piercing the Dipper and Ox; willows hang low, tethering the light boat. The passes and mountains stretch to the horizon, unbearable to gaze upon;
white geese and yellow reeds share the same hue of autumn. (Jiannan Yin):
Deep in the mountains, the human realm differs from the city; one gathers fresh firewood and roasts it with its leaves still attached. White clouds fill the chamber, pushing back [the darkness].
[The moon] emerges; half the window reflects the moon, half the window reflects the pines.
(De-shi Xin) Ji-cui was asked by a monk: "Before opening one's mouth, I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: "The east wind blows fiercely."
Wearing a rain hat, the monk stood there lost in thought. The Master said, "The white clouds have already passed over Silla.
Faling Yin said, "Striking a dead sparrow on the ground—this alone is sufficient for a master.
If one tries to seize a hawk in mid-air, one still lacks one essential move. Xuxu said, "This monk has no gate through which to enter. Jicui said, [the same].
There is no gate through which to exit.
The mountain man of Hua-ye sleeps within his cave; the traveler from Tiantai stands by the stone bridge. The straw sandals have been worn through until they break as the dream first awakens;
with a snap of the fingers, we meet again upon the eight-thousand-li road. (By Shouning Heng)
A multicolored phoenix soars into the void; a dark dragon emerges from the cave, passing through the rain.
If one asks for news from within this realm, the white clouds have already passed beyond Silla.
(Falin’s Verse) When the monk Mo Ma-yi-teng asked Layman Lu Wenhai: "In the past, you studied under [masters] before your parents were born..."
[The Master] said, "From before until now, there has been no news. Xianshou said, "You have not yet reached the ground where there is no news.
Yunyan said, "Master, you previously said that 'blue is blue light. What about this? Xianshou said, "I do not speak like that now."
"The Pure Land is black as lacquer.
Falin Yin said, "I am not like that now; it is actually quite fitting to leave Wenguai in a state of doubt.
He then said, "How much difference is there between 'the Pure Land is black as lacquer' and 'blue light from blue'? "
No boats or oars upon the water, no carriages upon the land. Upon the ancient path, frost lies thick and the wild goose’s shadow slants.
One might think that news from one's hometown has been severed; yet, even at the ends of the earth, the plum blossoms remain.
(Haihui Xing) Amidst the cries of the cuckoo, harmony is stirred. Red silk is cut into shreds to lead the guest across. Walking until reaching the stream’s edge, he leans against the railing.
Verse: One wave surges after another. (Jian-nan pronunciation) The East of Lu and the West of Qin each have their own designs;
Their secret plots are solely for deep strategic use. Once the dust and smoke have settled, there is nothing more to do;
The six states dare not invade with joined armies. (Zhengjue Zhe)
An old salt seller encountered a monk on the road who was heading toward Fuchuan. The monk asked, "In which direction does the road to Fuchuan lead?
The old man remained silent for a long while. The monk asked again. The old man said, "Are you deaf?
The monk replied, "What did you say to me? The old man said, "I told you the way to Fuchuan. The monk asked, "Do you understand Chan? The old man said, "Don't."
The monk said, "If one attains Chan, even the Buddha-dharma will come to an end. The old man said, "Try saying it for me.
The old man held up a load of salt and showed it to him. The monk said, "Difficult. The old man asked, "What do you call this? The monk said, "Salt.
The old man said, "What connection does that have [to the matter]? The monk asked, "And what do you call it? The old man replied, "I cannot tell you anymore."
Regarding "Salt," Falin says: "Even if one were to exhaustively comprehend the Buddha-dharma, the burden upon one's shoulders would never have been set down.
Yet, in this present age, it is difficult to find even a single person [who can do so]."
The old man is accustomed to selling private salt; the patch-robed monk asks pointlessly about the capsized boat. Both, their arts exhausted, cannot return;
they remain altogether on the midway path. (Haihui Xing: Mountains are jagged swords, waters are blades;
wind and clouds shift and change, drumming up a tumultuous din. Who can go alone toward Qin River?
Go! Pick it up for me and cover the hairs on my gallbladder.
(Falin-yin) Braving the dew, he holds his pole toward the water’s edge; one layer of misty rain, another layer of spring.
But when he reaches the vast, boundless expanse, he is instead pointed out and ridiculed by bystanders. (Suan-ting)
In her later years, Lady Juezhen of Haotou in Huangyan, Taizhou, established a reception hall for travelers beside Mingyin Monastery in the city.
One monk entered her private quarters carrying his pack and rain hat. Juezhen asked, "Who are you? The monk replied, "I am a wandering monk.
Juezhen suddenly pointed to his feet and said, "Why do you not notice that the cord on your straw sandals has snapped? The monk was speechless.
[The Master] said, “Right. Then he threw out his pack and hat and said, “Here there is no place for you to set foot.

Falingyin said, “This monk was traveling on pilgrimage; Huangyan’s legs were aching. ‘There is no place here to set foot’—thirty blows for this must be personally received by the one who committed it.”
A wooden man carries the moon into the empty valley; a stone woman pierces the clouds to enter the bustling marketplace.
With longing thoughts spanning ten thousand miles across heaven and earth, even now she still remembers Jiangnan.
(Haihui Xing) One body, yet another body of sorrow; the desolation of the mountain passes brings grief that never ceases. News has recently arrived from the frontier that my lord has passed away.
When he arrived, he did not dream again of the "big sword head" (a riddle for "evening," as *dào* means "evening" and *tóu* means "head").
Later, when Elder Kui of Huangyan came to visit Master Zhen, Zhen asked, "I have heard it said that you, Elder, fathered a son last night—is this true?
Kui replied, "But tell me, is it a boy or a girl? Zhen said, "A rooster runs off clutching a lamp."
"A turtle bites the fishing rod.
Faling says: "The faces of men and women—when one awakens to the truth, they are clearly and vividly presented.
Everyone says Minggui was too hasty in his progress; Faling bites down on his teeth and says 'blind,' waiting for future gentlemen to judge. Furthermore.
Verse: Azure waves surge forth, jade orbs roll on; who can understand how to fix the gaze upon the immediate occasion? The boundless autumn light is gathered all away;
as the night draws to a close, one feels only the chill of the morning breeze.
A special cow gave birth to a jade qilin; its radiant auspicious light permeated the four neighboring houses. In haste, she repeatedly consulted the diviners regarding yin and yang;
upon the banana leaves, the green was just beginning to spread evenly.
Zongjian Fali, Volume Seventy-Two
